## GD4436 — Concurrent Decoration launches can publish duplicate permanent public services [conditional]

`Decoration` checks for the public `Decorator` port while inside `Forbid()`, but releases Forbid before loading the theme and classes; it publishes the newly created port later with `AddPort()` (`workbench/c/Decoration/decoration.c:227-262`). Those operations are not one atomic check-and-publish sequence. On ExecSMP, two launchers can run the lookup on different CPUs and both observe no port; on a uniprocessor, one launcher can be task-switched after `Permit()` and before `AddPort()`, allowing another to make the same observation. `Forbid()` is explicitly processor-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:47-50`). `AddPort()` enqueues the node under its list lock but does not reject an existing name (`rom/exec/addport.c:50-75`).

After publication, each process calls `Detach()` and enters a loop whose Ctrl-C branch does not stop the loop (`decoration.c:258-286`). Thus both successful launchers can remain as detached services with distinct public ports carrying the same name. `FindPort()` returns only one matching node, so later name-based reconfiguration is delivered to one instance; the other service remains alive with its prior decoration state and resources. The existing-port branch itself sends a synchronous update to the found service (`:227-245`), but it does not cover the interval before either concurrent launcher publishes.

**Trigger and consequence:** two Decoration launches overlap while no `Decorator` port is registered, both successfully load their classes, and each reaches `AddPort()` after its own earlier lookup found no port. A duplicate permanent task and public port remain; name-based clients reach one matching service and cannot reliably update the other. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `workbench-c-decoration` (the target is in the active `workbench-c` aggregate), on single-CPU or ExecSMP systems; the required launch overlap is conditional. **Confidence:** high for the separated lookup/publication, local-only Forbid semantics, duplicate-permitting AddPort, and persistent service loop; actual overlapping launches were not scheduled. Serialize reservation and publication with a cross-CPU lock and release it on all startup paths, or recheck atomically before publishing. No Decoration process, port, display, or SMP schedule was run; source-only; see the [coverage trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#decoration-singleton-check-publish-gd4436).

## GD4535

**MUIScreen can expunge its library base while the auto-close task still uses it.**

**Indexed summary:** MUIScreen expunge signals its worker but does not wait for it to finish before returning success.

`workbench/libs/muiscreen/muiscreen_init.c:56-96` stores `LIBBASE` in the task's `tc_UserData`, then the worker continues to read the base, its semaphore and its screen list while servicing messages. `libExpunge()` at lines 99-104 only sends `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C` when the message port exists and immediately returns `TRUE`; it does not wait for task termination. Successful expunge permits the generated library cleanup to release the base while the signaled task may still be traversing screens or releasing the semaphore. The worker then dereferences stale base storage. The selected module includes this initializer (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/mmakefile.src:5-13`). Trigger: library expunge while the auto-close task is active; consequence: task use-after-free during teardown. **Confidence: high; interleaving not run.**

## GD4536

**MUIScreen leaks the auto-close task and stack after the worker exits.**

**Indexed summary:** MUIScreen does not free its manually allocated task or stack when the auto-close worker exits.

The initializer allocates the task structure and a separate 4,096-byte stack with `AllocMem()` (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/muiscreen_init.c:25-40`), and initializes an empty `tc_MemEntry` list before calling `AddTask()` (`:29,45`). The worker sets `muisb_closeTask` to NULL and returns after Ctrl-C or when `CreateMsgPort()` fails (`:89-96`), but neither it nor expunge frees the task or stack. The default task finalizer reaches `RemTask()`, whose cleanup frees only allocations linked in `tc_MemEntry` (`rom/exec/remtask.c:169-182`); MUIScreen's separate allocations are not linked there. Thus the normal worker shutdown, and the early exit if message-port creation fails, retain the task structure and stack. This is distinct from GD490's pre-launch failure branch and GD4535's library-base lifetime race. **Confidence: high; worker exit not induced.**

<a id="gd4608"></a>
## GD4608 — `ScalePixelArray()` passes zero scale factors to the generic HIDD scaler

`internal_ScalePixelArray()` zero-initializes `struct BitScaleArgs`, then sets only the source and destination dimensions before calling `HIDD_BM_BitMapScale()` (`workbench/libs/cgfx/scalepixelarray.c:124,186-191`). It never sets `bsa_XSrcFactor`, `bsa_XDestFactor`, `bsa_YSrcFactor`, or `bsa_YDestFactor`, so all four remain zero. The generic HIDD implementation uses those factors in `scale_srcpos()`; its `pos` expression divides by `df` without guarding zero (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4920-4925,4951-4955`). With any nonzero destination width, the first horizontal sample therefore divides by zero; if that path returns, the vertical sampling loop has the same zero denominator. The method is part of the base Gfx bitmap class (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:192`); the only other checked-in override forwards to its superclass (`gfx_cursorfbclass.c:354-359`).

**Trigger and consequence:** call the selected `cybergraphics.library` `ScalePixelArray()` on an HIDD RastPort with nonzero source and destination dimensions, after temporary object allocation and source upload succeed, when the selected bitmap class uses the generic inherited scaler. The zero destination factor reaches integer division by zero, so the scaling call can fault or otherwise fail before rendering the destination bitmap. Set each source/destination factor from the corresponding source and destination dimensions before dispatch. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable CyberGraphX library (`workbench/libs/cgfx/mmakefile.src`) with an HIDD bitmap class using the generic base scaler; the checked-in graphics debug test calls `ScalePixelArray()` with nonzero dimensions (`developer/debug/test/graphics/scalepixelarray.c:252-256`). **Confidence:** high for zero initialization, omitted assignments, and the generic method's unguarded division; runtime manifestation depends on the selected HIDD method and target's division-by-zero behavior. No scaling call, device, build, or runtime fault was exercised; source-only; see the [ScalePixelArray factor trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#scalepixelarray-zero-factor-gd4608).

<a id="gd4631"></a>
## GD4631 — Generic HIDD `MapColor()` loops forever on a 65,536-entry palette

`BM__Hidd_BitMap__MapColor()` iterates the bitmap's indexed color table with `UWORD i` while comparing it to `cmap->entries`, whose type is `ULONG` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4689-4708`; `rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:195-199`). For exactly 65,536 entries, `i` reaches 65,535, increments with 16-bit wrap to zero, and remains less than `cmap->entries`; the loop never terminates. The code does not break when it finds an exact match, so even a color at the start of the table does not avoid the wrap. The base method is registered by the generic Gfx bitmap class (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:188`); the only other checked-in override forwards to its superclass (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_cursorfbclass.c:447`).

The count is reachable through the ColorMap interface: `CM__Root__New()` accepts the `ULONG aoHidd_ColorMap_NumEntries` tag, logs values above 256 only through `D()` and continues to allocate/store the requested count (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_colormapclass.c:68-98`). `BM__Hidd_BitMap__SetColorMap()` installs the supplied map without narrowing its entry count (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:4580-4608`); subsequent palette mapping reads that map's `entries` field. No checked-in caller was found constructing or attaching a 65,536-entry map, so the demonstrated trigger is an external/future HIDD client using these public interfaces.

**Trigger and consequence:** an indexed HIDD bitmap uses a successfully allocated ColorMap with exactly 65,536 entries, and a caller invokes `HIDD_BM_MapColor()` on a color. The base method remains in its table scan indefinitely, so the calling graphics operation/task hangs. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `hidd.gfx`; the ColorMap/bitmap methods are in the generic HIDD interface and no target-specific override avoids the base loop in the checked-in tree. **Confidence:** high for the counter-width wrap and constructor/attachment path; in-tree trigger reachability is not established. Use an `ULONG` loop index or reject unsupported entry counts. No large map, color mapping, build or runtime operation was performed; source-only. See the [full-method and ColorMap caller recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#generic-hidd-mapcolor-65536-entry-loop-gd4631).

## GD4655

**`CoerceMode()` is exported but unconditionally reports that no mode can be selected (documented public API gap; high source confidence, in-tree caller impact unverified).** The selected generic graphics implementation is included by `rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:79`, and `graphics.conf:202` publishes the `CoerceMode()` vector. Its API comment says it determines the best mode for a viewport and returns `INVALID_ID` only when it cannot coerce (`rom/graphics/coercemode.c:32-47`). The entire implementation instead logs “not implemented” and returns `INVALID_ID` for every input (`:58-60`). The source also explicitly lists the function as unimplemented under `BUGS` (`:48-49`), so this is a known incomplete implementation rather than an accidental branch defect. Implement the documented mode selection or remove/clearly gate the vector if this API is intentionally unsupported.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** any client calling the selected generic graphics.library vector with a viewport and target monitor/mode. Repository-wide C/assembly search found no maintained direct caller beyond the generated m68k emulator thunk, which only forwards the public call; external client behavior is not established.

**Consequence:** callers cannot use this exported API to select a coercion mode and receive the failure sentinel regardless of whether a suitable mode exists. No viewport or display mode was queried. **Confidence:** high that the vector is selected and always returns `INVALID_ID`; practical impact depends on external callers. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD4656

**`CloseMonitor()` can lose a concurrent `OpenMonitor()` count update.** `OpenMonitor()` increments the public `MonitorSpec.ms_OpenCount` with `AROS_ATOMIC_INC()` after finding a monitor (`rom/graphics/openmonitor.c:64-85`), while `CloseMonitor()` protects a plain `ms_OpenCount--` with `DisplayInfoDataBaseSemaphore` (`rom/graphics/closemonitor.c:54-62`). `OpenMonitor()` does not take that semaphore, so on ExecSMP the atomic increment can interleave with the non-atomic decrement and the decrement's load/store can overwrite the increment. The shared count can then understate outstanding opens; a later `CloseMonitor()` can report that no open reference exists even though one remains. `MonitorSpec.ms_OpenCount` is explicitly documented as the driver open count (`compiler/include/graphics/monitor.h:43`), and `CloseMonitor()` reports failure when it observes zero (`closemonitor.c:29-35,54-62`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** an ExecSMP build where clients concurrently open and close the same `MonitorSpec`, including calls from separate tasks on different CPUs. The only maintained code that reads the count is `CloseMonitor()` itself; no in-tree concurrent caller was found, so impact is limited to an incorrect public count/close result for external or future clients. Use one shared SMP-safe atomic update or serialize both operations with the same lock. **Confidence:** high for the mismatched update mechanisms and absent shared lock; practical impact is medium because the count has no other maintained consumer. No monitor was opened or closed concurrently; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1269`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1269), complete `OpenMonitor()` and `CloseMonitor()` bodies and maintained field-reference census.

## GD4658

**Explicit `GetSprite(0)` or `GetExtSpriteA(..., GSTAG_SPRITE_NUM, 0)` can hand the cursor sprite to a caller as if it were an independent hardware sprite.** Automatic allocation starts at bit 1 and skips sprite zero (`rom/graphics/getsprite.c:77-95`; `getextspritea.c:70-92`), but both explicit-index branches accept zero and set bit 0 whenever it is clear (`getsprite.c:100-111`; `getextspritea.c:94-106`). `GetExtSpriteA()` additionally marks `ExtSprites` bit 0. No checked-in code initializes or reserves `GfxBase->SpriteReserved` bit 0; the graphics base is clear-allocated by `MakeLibrary()` (`rom/graphics/graphics_init.c:43-48`; `rom/exec/makelibrary.c:105-110`), and the selected graphics initializer has no later assignment to this field. Thus either vector can return zero to an explicit request. In the selected generic `MoveSprite()` implementation, sprite number zero is sent to `HIDD_Display_SetCursorPos()` and all nonzero numbers are ignored (`rom/graphics/movesprite.c:78-101`); the m68k override likewise routes zero to the cursor and nonzero values to chipset sprites (`arch/m68k-amiga/graphics/movesprite.c:80-103`). The m68k `ChangeExtSpriteA()` sends sprite zero to `HIDD_Display_SetCursorShape()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/graphics/changeextspritea.c:80-94`). Thus a caller that treats a successful explicit allocation as an independent sprite can move or replace the system cursor instead.

**Trigger and affected configuration:** an external Graphics API client calls `GetSprite(sprite, 0)` or `GetExtSpriteA()` with explicit `GSTAG_SPRITE_NUM == 0` while bit zero is clear, then uses the returned sprite through a selected display. Automatic `pick == -1` requests are unaffected because they skip bit zero. The public documentation accepts explicit indices 0–7, while the implementation notes say sprite zero is reserved for the mouse cursor (`getsprite.c:35-48`; `getextspritea.c:37-46`). No maintained in-tree allocator caller was found. **Consequence:** the client can interfere with cursor position/shape and does not receive an independent hardware sprite; `FreeSprite(0)` clears the allocation bit without changing cursor ownership. **Confidence:** high for the explicit allocation and cursor routing; practical impact is limited to external callers that assume sprite zero is independent. Invalid picks below -1 also reach negative shift expressions in the allocators and `FreeSprite()`, but those values are outside the documented 0–7/-1 interface and no maintained caller was found, so that case is not promoted. No sprite API call was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1235), sprite allocation bodies and selected movement/change implementations reviewed.

## GD4662

**Empty-destination region copies leak the partial rectangle chunks after allocation failure, and selected layer callers continue with incomplete regions (conditional region-state corruption and memory leak; high source confidence).** `_LinkRegionRectangleList()` saves `prev = *dstptr` once, appends each copied rectangle through `_NewRegionRectangle()`, and on allocation failure only frees the newly appended suffix when `prev` is non-NULL (`rom/graphics/intregions.c:224-250`). For an empty destination, `prev` is NULL, so a failure after successful chunk allocations skips rollback. Each region chunk stores 128 rectangles and a fresh pool supplies 20 chunks (`rom/graphics/graphics_intern.h:48-66,449-460`); with no reusable chunks available, allocation of a further pool can fail after 2,560 rectangles have been appended. The destination pointer has been advanced to the last rectangle, not restored to the first.

`SetRegion()` has this empty-destination case: it clears `dest->RegionRectangle`, stores the new tail only in local `addr`, and returns FALSE without publishing or freeing it when the copy fails (`rom/graphics/setregion.c:66-85`). This loses the region's only head pointer. `_CopyRegionRectangles()` instead advances the destination field itself; when its caller disposes the failed temporary region, `DisposeRegion()` passes that tail pointer to `_DisposeRegionRectangleList()`, whose tail-oriented cleanup releases following chunks but cannot release earlier chunks (`rom/graphics/intregions.h:155-161`; `intregions.c:144-220`; `disposeregion.c:53-72`). `OrRegionRegion()` also uses `_CopyRegionRectangles()` when its second region is empty, then returns FALSE with that destination field pointing at the tail (`rom/graphics/orregionregion.c:56-65`).

Selected hyperlayers code ignores failed region operations in visibility and damage reconstruction, including `DeleteLayer()`'s `SetRegion()` snapshots (`rom/hyperlayers/deletelayer.c:82,99`), z-order unions and snapshots (`movelayerz.c:56,64,100,150,173,225`), and `_ShowPartsOfLayer()` / `_BackFillRegion()` unions (`basicfuncs.c:1102,1286`). These callers can proceed with empty, partial, or malformed region state after an allocation failure; the exact redraw/visibility consequence depends on the geometry and failing operation. Preserve the original head and free all newly allocated chunks on failure, then require callers to stop or restore state when a region operation returns FALSE.

One selected path makes that consequence concrete: when `ChangeLayerVisibility()` makes a layer visible, it clears `l->VisibleRegion` and calls `_ShowPartsOfLayer(l, &r, ...)` (`rom/hyperlayers/changelayervisibility.c:100-127`). `_ShowPartsOfLayer()` unions `r` into that empty destination without checking failure, then builds replacement ClipRects from the resulting region and installs them (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:1100-1120`). If the empty-destination copy exceeds available region chunks after partial construction, the copy helper leaves the destination at its tail and leaks its prefix; the following intersection sees only the tail-linked portion, so the layer can become visible with incomplete ClipRects while the public operation still returns TRUE. The same 2,560-rectangle fresh-pool trigger and free-pool caveat apply; no layer was shown or allocation failure induced.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library region operations and hyperlayers callers when an empty destination must copy/union a sufficiently large rectangle list and region-chunk allocation fails after partial construction. A fresh pool holds 20 × 128 rectangles; existing free chunks can raise the failure threshold. No allocation failure or layer operation was run; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L264`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L264), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L307`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L307), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1111`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1111), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1113`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1113), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1201`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1201), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1818`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1818), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1822`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1822), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1866`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1866), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1872`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1872), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L2559`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2559), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L2740`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2740). The region allocator/copy and listed caller paths were rechecked for this expansion.

## GD4666

**`XorRectRegionND()` dereferences a failed result-region allocation on its empty-rectangle path (conditional null dereference; high source confidence).** When `IS_RECT_EVIL(Rect)` is true, the function allocates a result with `NewRegion()` and immediately passes it to `_CopyRegionRectangles()` without checking for NULL (`rom/graphics/xorrectregionnd.c:61-70`). `_CopyRegionRectangles()` evaluates `&R2->RegionRectangle` before entering `_LinkRegionRectangleList()`, so a failed `NewRegion()` is dereferenced at the call site (`rom/graphics/intregions.h:155-161`). `NewRegion()` returns NULL when its `AllocPooled()`/`AllocMem()` request fails (`rom/graphics/newregion.c:47-64`).

**Consequence and scope:** A memory-allocation failure while `Rect` is empty/invalid causes a null-pointer dereference instead of returning the documented NULL result. The function is declared in the public Graphics vector configuration (`rom/graphics/graphics.conf:236`) and has a generated m68k emulator thunk (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4346-4351`); a checkout-wide search found no maintained C caller, so no in-tree operation is claimed to trigger the path. Add the same `if (ret == NULL) return NULL;` guard used by sibling non-destructive region functions before calling the copy helper. **Affected configuration and trigger:** any build exposing this public Graphics vector, when `NewRegion()` fails and the rectangle satisfies `IS_RECT_EVIL()`. No allocation failure or region operation was run; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1165`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1165), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1770`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1770). The cited function bodies and public vector/thunk were rechecked for this entry.

## GD4682

**ColorMap construction accepts an oversized entry count whose byte-size multiplication wraps on 32-bit builds (conditional undersized allocation and later out-of-bounds access; high source confidence).** `CM__Root__New()` reads `aoHidd_ColorMap_NumEntries` into `ULONG numentries`; values above 256 only produce a debug message, and the constructor continues with that count (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_colormapclass.c:58-79`). It stores the count in `data->clut.entries` and allocates `sizeof(HIDDT_Color) * entries` without checking multiplication overflow (`:94-100`). `HIDDT_Color` is four `UWORD` components plus one `ULONG pixval`, totaling 12 bytes (`rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:177-183`). On 32-bit builds, a count of 357,913,942 (`0x15555556`) makes the allocation expression wrap to 8 bytes, while the logical entry count remains 357,913,942. If that small allocation succeeds, later `CM__Hidd_ColorMap__SetColors()` trusts the logical count and writes a full color into the undersized array without reallocating (`gfx_colormapclass.c:242-277`); getters also accept indexes against that oversized count (`:330-406`).

**Consequence and scope:** A caller that creates the generic HIDD ColorMap with an oversized NumEntries tag can obtain an object whose table is smaller than its advertised count; subsequent valid-by-that-count color access reads or writes outside the allocation. The class is selected by the generic `kernel-hidd-gfx` module (`rom/hidds/gfx/mmakefile.src:4-27`). A checkout-wide search found only the selected bitmap-class and m68k P96 constructors; those use small counts, so no maintained in-tree trigger was established. Reject counts above the supported maximum before storing the count or allocating. **Affected configuration and trigger:** 32-bit builds selecting generic gfx HIDD, a direct HIDD client requesting a count above `SIZE_MAX / sizeof(HIDDT_Color)`, and successful allocation of the wrapped byte count. No large ColorMap was allocated or accessed; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L433`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L433). The class constructor, table methods, color layout, module manifest, and checked-in constructor sites were rechecked for this entry.

## GD4696

**Radeon DrawLine, DrawRect, and DrawPolygon overwrite the GC line pattern instead of testing it (conditional graphics-state corruption and incorrect line rendering; high source confidence).** All three Radeon methods use `if ((GC_LINEPAT(gc) =! (UWORD)~0) || !bm->fbgfx)` (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_bitmap.c:454,552,654`). C parses `=!` as assignment followed by logical NOT, so `!((UWORD)~0)` evaluates to zero: each call writes zero into the shared GC's `linePat`, then takes the `bm->fbgfx` hardware branch whenever that flag is true. The intended non-mutating predicate is present in the parallel Nvidia methods at the same three operation sites (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/nvidiabitmap.c:595,850,922`). `GC_LINEPAT` directly accesses the GC instance field (`rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:434`); the generic GC initializes it to all ones and stores caller-set values (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_gcclass.c:233,279`).

On the Radeon framebuffer path, the selected primitives proceed with hardware commands without using the caller's line-pattern bits, so non-solid patterns are not honored. On the DrawLine fallback path, the generic rasterizer tests the pattern bit for every pixel (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:1648,1689,1744`); after Radeon has set it to zero, it emits no foreground pixels (except opaque background handling). Regardless of which path draws, the GC remains changed after return, affecting later operations that reuse it. The public Graphics `Draw()` vector reaches `HIDD_BM_DrawLine()` with the RastPort GC (`rom/graphics/draw.c:24-36`); the method also remains directly callable through the HIDD API. The Radeon module has PPC-specific build overlays for Sam440 and CHRP/Efika, but the module/package is optional, so this finding does not claim that every such boot image loads it.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** a loaded Radeon HIDD handling any `DrawLine`, `DrawRect`, or `DrawPolygon` call with a reusable GC; on framebuffer-backed Radeon bitmaps the condition also forces the hardware path for any incoming line pattern. No drawing operation or Radeon hardware was used; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1261`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1261), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1276`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1276), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1278`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1278), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1286`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1286). The three Radeon predicates, GC field/set behavior, generic line consumer, `Draw()` caller, and Nvidia counterparts were rechecked for this entry.

## GD4700

**Radeon expunge leaves its managed-memory header linked in Exec's MemList while freeing the driver base that contains it (conditional stale memory-header/callback reference; high source confidence).** When the detected card has usable framebuffer memory, `BitmapInit()` allocates its bitmap and initializes the embedded `sd->managedMem` header, including `MEMF_MANAGED`, allocator callbacks, and `mhe_UserData = sd`; it then links that header into `SysBase->MemList` (`workbench/hidds/radeon/bitmap.c:401-438`). The card initialization path calls `BitmapInit(sd)` after VRAM sizing (`radeon_driver.c:2415`). The header is embedded in Radeon static data (`ati.h:107`).

`ATI_Expunge()` unmaps the PCI framebuffer/MMIO/ROM regions, disposes its PCI object, releases attribute bases, and deletes the pool, but has no operation removing `managedMem` from `SysBase->MemList` (`ati_init.c:309-348`). The selected generic generated `ExpungeLib()` then removes the library node and frees `LIBBASE` when the open count is zero (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1532-1590`). Because the memory header and its callback context are embedded in that base, the Exec memory list retains a node pointing into freed storage. The normal memory allocator walks this list and dispatches `mhe_Alloc` for managed headers (`rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:27-72`), so a later allocation can traverse the stale node and callback/context. Remove the managed header under the same MemList synchronization before unmapping/freeing its owner, and ensure outstanding VRAM allocations prevent expunge or are released.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** a Radeon HIDD build loaded for a supported card with nonzero usable framebuffer memory, followed by library expunge and a later system allocation. Radeon HIDD packaging is optional; this does not claim that every PPC Sam440 or CHRP/Efika boot includes it. No module expunge or allocation was run; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1276`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1276), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1286`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1286). The header publication, sole initialization path, callback owner, ATI expunge, and generated base teardown were rechecked for this entry.

## GD4728

**BarMasking titlebar-shape generation ignores rectangle-insertion failures and can pass a NULL region into `CopyRegion()`.** `RegionFromLUT8Image()` scans each titlebar row and joins consecutive nontransparent pixels into opaque runs (`workbench/libs/decorator/decorimagefuncs.c:546-597`). When a run ends at a transparent pixel, it calls `OrRectRegion()` but ignores the BOOL result (`:577-581`); only the initial rectangle and a run extending to the row's end set the `failed` flag (`:560-561,588`). An intermediate region-allocation failure can therefore leave part of the outline absent while later runs continue to be added. The helper returns this partial region as if complete.

`windecor_windowshape()` caches the returned region and returns a copy for the window (`workbench/c/Decoration/windowdecorclass.c:1873-1899`). Intuition's selected `DefaultWindowShapeFunc()` calls that method, replaces the window's prior outline, assigns the result to `msg->NewShape`, and reports success (`rom/intuition/intuition_misc.c:1192-1217`). Thus a missed intermediate insertion produces and installs an incomplete titlebar mask.

The same path has a sharper allocation-failure case. On a shape change, `windecor_windowshape()` first disposes and clears the old cached shape (`:1875-1884`). If `DNewLUT8ImageContainer()` then fails, it skips cache construction but still calls `CopyRegion(wd->tbarshape.shape)` with NULL (`:1886-1899`). If the container allocation succeeds but `RegionFromLUT8Image()` returns NULL after a checked insertion failure, it stores NULL and makes the same call. `CopyRegion()` allocates an empty region and forwards its input to `OrRegionRegion()` (`compiler/alib/copyregion.c:43-50`); `OrRegionRegion()` immediately reads `R1->RegionRectangle` without a NULL check (`rom/graphics/orregionregion.c:58-61`). If that subsequent `NewRegion()` succeeds, the window-shape update dereferences NULL.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the Decoration window class with `BarMasking` enabled, when a titlebar shape is built or regenerated. An ignored intermediate insertion failure requires a row with an opaque run followed by transparency and a transient `OrRectRegion()` failure; the NULL-region fault requires a failed shape/container operation followed by successful allocation in `CopyRegion()`. **Consequence:** a partial titlebar clipping region, or a task fault while updating the window outline. **Confidence:** high for the ignored result, cache publication, and NULL dereference; manifestation requires the stated allocation-failure sequence. No region allocation failure or window-shape operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD4735

**Concurrent sprite allocation can return the same hardware sprite to two callers on ExecSMP.** `GetSprite()` and `GetExtSpriteA()` mask interrupts with `Disable()`, scan `GfxBase->SpriteReserved`, and set the selected bit with an ordinary read/modify/write (`rom/graphics/getsprite.c:75-113`; `rom/graphics/getextspritea.c:68-108`). The Exec contract states that `Disable()` affects only the local processor on ExecSMP and shared data also needs a spinlock (`rom/exec/disable.c:42-44`). Neither allocator takes one. If two CPUs concurrently request the next available sprite, each can read the same clear bit before either stores it, then both set that bit and return the same index. Requests for different indices can also lose one update because the shared byte updates are not atomic. `FreeSprite()` modifies the same reservation fields under the same local-only exclusion (`rom/graphics/freesprite.c:51-57`).

**Trigger and affected configuration:** overlapping `GetSprite(-1)` or `GetExtSpriteA(..., GSTAG_SPRITE_NUM, -1, ...)` calls from separate CPUs in an ExecSMP build, when the callers compete for an available sprite. The generic graphics.library build manifest selects these implementations; the source defect is specific to ExecSMP, where local interrupt masking does not serialize CPUs. No maintained in-tree C allocator caller was found, so use by concurrent public API clients is the trigger established here. **Consequence:** distinct clients can receive the same sprite number and overwrite or free one another's sprite allocation state; a lost update can also leave a live reservation unmarked. **Confidence:** high for the missing cross-CPU synchronization and interleaving; the concurrent call was not run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1235), full allocator/free bodies and Exec `Disable()` contract rechecked.

## GD4755

**`BltPattern()` mishandles exponent 16 when an area pattern is supplied.** The public `SetAfPt()` macro stores its `n` argument directly in the signed-byte `RastPort.AreaPtSz` without a range check (`compiler/include/graphics/gfxmacros.h:34-38`; `compiler/include/graphics/rastport.h:58-67`). For either `+16` or `-16`, the pattern renderer computes `1L << 16` and stores 65,536 in signed `WORD patternheight` (`rom/graphics/bltpattern.c:163-167`), which narrows to zero on the 16-bit WORD target ABI. When the generic render callback runs, it evaluates `(... ) % patternheight` before drawing (`:35`), so a zero height reaches division by zero/undefined behavior. For `+16` with a non-NULL mask and without `INVERSVID`, the separate solid-pattern test computes `1U << 16`, stores zero in `UWORD rows`, and executes no validation iterations; it therefore treats the pattern as solid and delegates to `BltTemplate()` (`:134-153`), ignoring the actual pattern rows.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library's generic `BltPattern()` area-pattern path on targets with 16-bit `WORD`/`UWORD`, when a caller sets `AreaPtSz` to +16 or -16 and invokes a path that reaches the pattern callback; +16 with a mask takes the misclassification path instead. No maintained `SetAfPt()` caller at exponent 16 was found. The local public header gives no valid exponent range, so whether exponent 16 is valid API input remains unestablished; treat this as a conditional API-boundary candidate until that contract is resolved. **Consequence:** if such an exponent is valid, an unmasked or negative-exponent masked render can encounter modulo by zero, while the positive masked path can draw as though the pattern were solid. **Confidence:** high for these consequences when the stated value reaches the code; low-to-medium that the value is within the supported API contract. No pattern operation or compiler-specific conversion was run; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD4763

**`ChangeVPBitMap()` can report screen buffers safe after a failed viewport rebuild, while the display state remains on an older buffer.** `ChangeVPBitMap()` assigns the requested bitmap to `vp->RasInfo->BitMap`, calls `MakeVPort()` without checking its result, then proceeds to reload the viewport chain and queue both DBufInfo messages (`rom/graphics/changevpbitmap.c:66-105`). The AmigaVideo `MakeViewPort` method can return `MVP_NO_MEM` before replacing the existing copper list when it cannot allocate a new `CopList` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1236-1269`). The graphics caller still queues the safe and display messages, whose VBlank handler replies to them (`rom/graphics/graphics_init.c:163-189`); `FreeScreenBuffer()` waits for the safe reply before releasing an internally allocated bitmap (`rom/intuition/freescreenbuffer.c:65-108`). Intuition's `ChangeScreenBuffer()` also updates `screen->RastPort.BitMap` and returns TRUE without receiving or checking a rebuild result (`rom/intuition/changescreenbuffer.c:74-83`).

There is an additional stale-state path in repeated swaps. `MakeVPort()` saves `vpd->Bitmap` in `PreviousBitmap` only when that field is NULL; later successful swaps leave the original saved object there (`rom/graphics/makevport.c:120-169`). On a subsequent failed rebuild, rollback restores `PreviousBitmap` (`:222-232`). For the HIDD bitmap path used by `AllocScreenBuffer()`, the successful A→B swap clears `VPXF_WRAPPED_BITMAP`; therefore the later B→C attempt does not dispose B in `MakeVPort()`'s failure rollback. If C's viewport rebuild then fails, rollback selects A rather than the bitmap B that had been displayed before the request. `ChangeVPBitMap()` continues into `display_LoadViewPorts()` using that restored VPD, while the raw RastPort/RasInfo fields still identify C. The selected AmigaVideo `ShowViewPorts()` passes the restored VPD to its compositor; `BitMapStackChanged()` rebuilds the visible stack from `vpd->Bitmap` and its bitmap data, so the failed request can leave A as the display state while Intuition has updated its RastPort to C and returns TRUE. This caller trace supports the stale display-state consequence; no actual display transition was run. The guaranteed defect remains that the rebuild failure is ignored and both DBufInfo replies are still produced.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** AmigaVideo on m68k-Amiga, with a visible double-buffered viewport; at least one successful buffer change followed by a later viewport-build failure (for example, AmigaVideo's `CopList` allocation failure). **Consequence:** callers can be told that a buffer is safe and a screen-buffer change succeeded even though the rebuild failed; after repeated swaps, the restored HIDD bitmap can also differ from the previously displayed buffer. **Confidence:** high that the failure is ignored and messages are queued; high that `PreviousBitmap` can remain stale across successful swaps; medium for the resulting displayed image because backend reload behavior after failure is not runtime-verified. No allocation failure, swap, VBlank or display operation was run; source-only.

## GD4764

**Popasl can free an ASL requester while its worker is using it and queue completion against disposed objects.** The open hook starts a separate process with raw pointers to the ASL requester, tag array, application, and Popasl object (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/popasl.c:176-191`). `MUIM_Cleanup` calls `AbortAslRequest()` when `asl_proc` is non-NULL, but does not join or otherwise wait for that process (`:384-390`). There are two teardown windows. First, `AslRequest()` finds and retains the request node/internal structure before allocating common state and opening the window (`workbench/libs/asl/aslrequest.c:77-85,112-121`); it publishes `rn_ReqWindow` only after `OpenWindowTagList()` succeeds (`:207-223`). If cleanup runs during this setup interval, `AbortAslRequest()` sees a NULL `rn_ReqWindow` and returns without cancelling (`workbench/libs/asl/abortaslrequest.c:53-58,103-107`), after which Popasl disposal immediately frees the requester, pool, internal structure and request node (`popasl.c:339-345`; `workbench/libs/asl/freeaslrequest.c:55-68`). The still-running `AslRequest()` can then continue through those freed objects. Second, after a window is published, `AbortAslRequest()` sends a close message and waits only for its reply (`abortaslrequest.c:65-101`); the ASL event loop replies before `AslRequest()` performs requester-specific cleanup, clears `rn_ReqWindow`, frees common state, and returns (`basicfuncs.c:819-825`; `aslrequest.c:302-331`). In either case the worker can continue to queue `MUIM_Popstring_Close` against its saved application and Popasl pointers (`popasl.c:64-72`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected Zune Popasl class when its parent/application is cleaned up while the worker is between startup and window publication, or after the requester window has opened but before the worker has returned from `AslRequest()`, on the normal AROS ASL implementation. **Consequence:** in the setup case, the worker can continue using a freed requester node/internal structure; in either timing window, it may enqueue completion against an application or Popasl object being disposed. Make abort observable before window creation, and join the worker and drain/cancel its completion before freeing the requester or target objects. **Confidence:** high for the publication/abort/free ordering and missing join; the required teardown overlap and resulting invalid access were not run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD4772

**Indexed summary:** Picture scaling divides by zero for a zero requested width or height.

**Source and trigger:** The selected Picture class registers `PDT_Scale()` for `PDTM_SCALE` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/picture.conf`). The method copies the requested dimensions into `DestWidth`/`DestHeight` without validating them, then divides by each value when computing fixed-point scale factors (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1344-1369`). A caller that supplies zero for either requested dimension reaches an integer division by zero. The later `PScale_KeepAspect` branch also divides by the computed scale factor (`:1371-1375`), which can truncate to zero for sufficiently large requested dimensions.

**Consequence and scope:** An invalid or extreme scale request can fault the caller instead of being rejected. This is not limited to external callers: MultiView initializes `pdt_zoom` to 1 and decrements it without a lower bound, then derives dimensions by dividing the original image size by the absolute zoom factor (`workbench/utilities/MultiView/main.c:857,1642-1645`; `misc.c:652-671`). For a 640×480 image, after 480 Zoom Out selections the helper submits a zero destination height; the selected Picture scale method divides by that dimension (`pictureclass.c:1356-1367`). High confidence for the unbounded caller parameter and target division; no zoom or scale request was run.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Picture datatype full-body/public-method pass dated 2026-10-23.

## GD4784 — FTManager publishes a blank font preview after bitmap allocation failure

`fbNew()` does not fail the preview when its grayscale pixel buffer or destination bitmap allocation fails. If `AllocVec(width1 * height, MEMF_CLEAR)` returns NULL, the gray branch is skipped but construction continues with `gray_bitmap == NULL`; if `AllocBitMap(width, height, 8, 0, NULL)` returns NULL, the code likewise continues without a bitmap (`workbench/system/ftmanager/fontbitmap_class.c:160-165,231-256`). The resulting `BitmapObject` accepts `MUIA_Bitmap_Bitmap == NULL`; the selected Bitmap class's draw path checks for a NULL bitmap and returns without drawing (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bitmap.c:49-50,273-275`). `fbNew()` can therefore return a non-NULL but blank preview object. `fiUpdatePreview()` treats any non-NULL object as success, removes and disposes the existing preview, and installs the new one (`workbench/system/ftmanager/fontinfo_class.c:701-724`). A transient allocation failure thus replaces a previously valid font preview with a blank one instead of preserving it or reporting failure.

There is a related unchecked metadata-allocation path: if `AllocVec(length * sizeof(*info), MEMF_CLEAR)` fails, `fbNew()` sets `length` to zero but leaves the bounding-box extrema at `INT_MAX`/`INT_MIN` sentinels (`fontbitmap_class.c:79-90`). It then computes `xmax - xmin + 1` and `ymax - ymin + 1` (`:152-153`), which overflows signed `int` on the supported 32-bit-int targets before the later positive-size test. The resulting dimensions are not defined by C; this failure path can continue into bitmap/object construction rather than cleanly aborting. The precise post-overflow outcome is compiler-dependent and was not reproduced.

**Trigger and consequence:** in the optional FTManager target, a memory-allocation failure during grayscale preview generation can return a blank MUI bitmap object and discard the previous valid preview. Failure of the glyph-info allocation instead reaches signed-overflowing bounding-box arithmetic and can construct a preview with invalid dimensions. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-system-ftmanager` builds; default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation branches, NULL-bitmap acceptance, and preview replacement; high for signed overflow on 32-bit-int targets, with compiler-dependent consequences. Check every required allocation, return failure before publishing a preview, and preserve the old preview when construction is incomplete. No allocation failure, font render, preview replacement, or build was run; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#ftmanager-font-bitmap-allocation-failure-recheck).

## GD4806

**P96 graphics enumerates `.card` libraries without holding references across task switches.**

During `P96GFX__Initialise()`, the code walks `SysBase->LibList` under `Forbid()`, but releases it before initializing each matching `.card` and reacquires it afterward (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_hiddclass.c:1687-1702`). It retains both the current `lib` node and `name` pointer while `Permit()` allows other tasks to run. `P96GFX__InitCard()` then dereferences the library name and stores the raw library pointer in `CardBase`/BoardInfo before calling card-driver vectors (`:1629-1650`); the enumeration loop also uses its saved node to continue. If another task closes the last open reference and the `.card` library's close/expunge path removes it during the unlocked interval, the iterator and/or card initialization can access a removed node, freed library memory, or unloaded vectors. `CloseLibrary()` runs the library close vector while task scheduling is forbidden (`rom/exec/closelibrary.c:68-91`); the checked-in removal path also arbitrates `LibList` with `Forbid()` around the expunge vector (`rom/exec/remlibrary.c:62-79`). Those protections serialize each list mutation, but do not pin the node across P96's `Permit()` window. The P96 HIDD does not open a library reference around enumeration or `P96GFX__InitCard()`. Trigger requires a concurrent final close/expunge of a listed `.card` library during P96 initialization. This is the m68k-Amiga P96 HIDD path; the unpinned lifetime window is source-confirmed, while an in-tree closer that overlaps initialization was not established. **Confidence: medium-high for the lifetime gap, conditional reachability; concurrency not exercised.**

The selected `P96` monitor opens the named card library before opening `p96gfx.hidd`, and its source explicitly says both libraries are deliberately left open because the display driver continues to reference them (`workbench/devs/monitors/P96/p96.c:8-18,129-141`). That path pins the card it asked to load, so its own card is not the final-close trigger. The risk is limited to another `.card` library already present in `LibList` whose last reference is released during enumeration, or to an external caller directly creating this overlap; no in-tree overlapping close was found. **Confidence:** high for the raw-pointer lifetime gap, medium for reachability from an external or additional-card configuration.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L25`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L25).

## GD4817

**Generic JAM2 alpha-template blending never reaches the foreground color at full alpha.** In `JAM2AlphaTemplateBuffered()`, each channel is computed as `background + (foreground - background) * alpha / 256` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:3469-3488`). The alpha input is an 8-bit value, optionally inverted with XOR 255. At the fully opaque value 255, integer arithmetic leaves every channel that differs from the foreground exactly one value toward the background: for a positive delta `d`, `d*255/256` truncates to `d-1`; for a negative delta it truncates toward zero to `-(|d|-1)`. Thus a red/green/blue foreground channel of 0 over 255 yields 1, and a foreground channel of 255 over 0 yields 254. The neighboring `do_alpha()` implementation uses a rounded `/255`-equivalent calculation, confirming that the JAM2 denominator is inconsistent with the 0–255 alpha range (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:2944-2956`).

**Caller path, trigger, and scope:** `BM__Hidd_BitMap__PutAlphaTemplate()` selects this routine when color expansion is not transparent and the GC draw mode is not invert, maps foreground/background colors into 8-bit channel fields, then passes the alpha array and inversion flag to `DoBufferedOperation()` (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:3495-3541`). The public `BltTemplateAlpha()` path reaches the HIDD method through its clipped render hook (`workbench/libs/cgfx/blttemplatealpha.c:86-115`). Any non-background-expanded JAM2 draw with at least one alpha sample equal to 255 (or 0 with inversion enabled) and a foreground/background channel difference triggers the off-by-one result. This affects generic HIDD bitmap implementations that inherit the base method; classes overriding `PutAlphaTemplate()` are outside this implementation. **Consequence:** fully opaque mask pixels retain a one-level contribution from the background in each differing color channel, producing a small but deterministic color error. **Confidence:** high for the arithmetic and generic caller path; no rendering operation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14611`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14611).

## GD4868 — Picture's IFF writer reports success after failed seeks or short writes

**Source:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1633-1644,1741-1801,1833-1892,1904-2058,2078-2081`.

`WriteBytes()` seeks to each absolute output offset with `DTIO_Seek64()` but discards the seek result, then calls DOS `Write()`. It returns zero when `Write()` reports an error or any count other than the requested length. `DT_Write()` ignores every `WriteBytes()` result in both indexed and 24-bit output paths, then clears `IoErr()` and returns `TRUE` unconditionally on the normal exit. The public DOS `Write()` contract returns the actual byte count, including `-1` on error (`rom/dos/write.c:27-43`); the shared `DTIO_Seek64()` helper reports `-1` on seek failure (`workbench/classes/datatypes/dtio64.h:71-85`).

**Trigger and consequence:** any failed output seek, failed write, or short write during Picture IFF serialization. A failed seek can cause a later `Write()` to hit the wrong current position; a short/error write can leave a partial file. In both cases the datatype can still report success with `IoErr() == 0`. MultiView's selected `DoWriteMethod()` opens the destination with `MODE_NEWFILE`, calls `DTM_WRITE`, closes the handle, and displays its save-failed message only if the datatype method returns false (`workbench/utilities/MultiView/misc.c:504-543`). Thus a failed or incomplete save may be presented as successful. The Picture datatype target is explicitly defined by `workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/mmakefile.src:4-14`, and `picture.conf:45-46` maps `DTM_WRITE` to this method. A checked-in i386-PC floppy package includes the datatype; default Workbench inclusion is not established by the checked manifests.

**Affected configuration and confidence:** builds that include Picture datatype and invoke its IFF `DTM_WRITE` method, including the checked i386-PC floppy package. High confidence in the discarded seek/write results and unconditional success path; actual I/O failure behavior was not induced. This finding is separate from GD6167's missing indexed mask plane and GD6168's 24-bit BODY offset/FORM-length mismatch. No save was attempted; source-only.

**Surviving review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1758`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1758), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1918`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1918), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L2750`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2750), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L2035`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2035), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3111`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3111).

## GD5085

**Indexed summary:** MUI ARexx dispatch dereferences a failed argument allocation and calls hooks after parser setup allocation fails.

**Source and trigger:** For a templated command, dispatch allocates `len + 2` bytes for `arguments` and immediately copies into it, appends a newline/NUL, and later frees it (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1721-1731,1749`). If `AllocVec()` fails, the copy and writes use NULL. If `AllocDosObject(DOS_RDARGS, ...)` fails instead, the argument vector was never initialized by the later guarded `memset()` (`:1733-1747`), but the code still invokes the command hook unconditionally with that vector (`:1752-1754`).

**Consequence and scope:** Either resource failure can crash dispatch or pass uninitialized command arguments to the hook, depending on which allocation fails and the hook's behavior. The path requires a templated command to be configured, a matching ARexx command received, and the corresponding allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked NULL use and unconditional hook call; hook-side consequences vary. No allocation failure or ARexx message was induced; source-only.

## GD5086

**Indexed summary:** MUI Application Load/Save can pass an unterminated filename to DOS for long explicit paths

**Source and trigger:** Both `Application__MUIM_Load()` and `Application__MUIM_Save()` use a 1,024-byte stack buffer for the path (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:2304-2310,2370-2376`). Their built-in ENV/ENVARC cases use bounded `snprintf()`, but the explicit-name branch uses `strncpy(name, message->name, sizeof(name) - 1)` and never writes `name[sizeof(name)-1] = '\0'`. An explicit path of at least 1,023 bytes therefore leaves the buffer unterminated unless that stack byte happens to be zero. Each method then passes `name` to DOS `Open()` (`:2312,2378`), which consumes it as a C string.

**Consequence and scope:** DOS may read beyond the local array while interpreting the path, and the resulting path may include unrelated stack bytes or fail unpredictably. This affects callers of the public Load/Save methods that provide a custom path at least 1,023 bytes long; the built-in ENV/ENVARC selectors are not affected. The full checked-in `application.c` caller review found no custom-name call site, so the trigger is established by the public method input, not a maintained in-tree caller. **Confidence:** high for the missing terminator and out-of-bounds string consumption; practical result depends on stack contents and DOS path parsing. No file operation was run; source-only.

## GD5087

**MUI Application Save truncates the old file and hides later IFF write failures.** `Application__MUIM_Save()` opens the destination with `MODE_NEWFILE` before allocating or initializing the IFF writer (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:2488-2501`), so opening successfully truncates any existing preferences file. Later `PushChunk()`, the PRHD `WriteChunkBytes()`, `MUIM_Dataspace_WriteIFF`, both `PopChunk()` calls, and `CloseIFF()` do not contribute to the method result; the method always returns zero (`:2497-2535,2541-2548`). The selected DOS IFF stream handler converts a short or failed `Write()` into a hook error (`workbench/libs/iffparse/dosstreamhandler.c:48-55`); `WriteStream()` converts that to `IFFERR_WRITE`, which `WriteChunkBytes()` returns (`basicfuncs.c:392-423`; `writechunkbytes.c:72-81`). A failure after the file has been truncated can therefore leave an incomplete IFF file while the public method reports the same zero result as its ordinary path. `CloseIFF()` is void and only logs a `PopChunk()` failure, so its finalization status cannot repair the method's result (`closeiff.c:69-87`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds including the selected MUI Application class when `MUIM_Application_Save` opens a destination but a later DOS write, seek, or IFF chunk-finalization operation fails. The checked-in LogView caller also ignores the method result (`workbench/system/LogView/logview.c:789`), and external MUI clients can invoke the public method. **Consequence:** the prior saved file may be replaced by an incomplete file and callers cannot detect the failed save through the method result. Preserve the prior file until a complete temporary IFF has been finalized, and propagate serialization/finalization errors. **Confidence:** high for truncation ordering, discarded IFF results, and unconditional zero return; actual file damage depends on the stated I/O failure. No save or filesystem failure was run; source-only.

**Review evidence:** application serializer body and IFF/DOS stream error path in the selected local sources; source-order body review recorded at [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3247`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3247).

## GD5088

**Configdata Save can accept a failed PRHD write and discards later IFF errors after truncating the preferences file.** `Configdata__MUIM_Save()` opens the destination with `MODE_NEWFILE` before writing its IFF form (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:1183-1212`). `SavePrefsHeader()` tests `WriteChunkBytes()` as a Boolean rather than requiring the full `PrefHeader` byte count (`:1161-1173`); the selected DOS stream reports a short/error write as negative `IFFERR_WRITE` (`workbench/libs/iffparse/dosstreamhandler.c:48-55`; `basicfuncs.c:392-423`; `writechunkbytes.c:72-81`), and that negative value is truthy in the helper's `if`. If `PopChunk()` then succeeds, the helper reports success and the serializer continues into Dataspace output even though the PRHD payload was not fully written. Independently, the serializer ignores the return from `MUIM_Dataspace_WriteIFF`, ignores the outer `PopChunk()` result, calls void `CloseIFF()` without checking its logged finalization errors, and returns zero on every path (`configdata.c:1213-1233`).

The selected Zune Preferences `save_prefs()` calls this method for ENV and optionally ENVARC files and ignores its result (`workbench/prefs/Zune/zune.c:657-699`); the method itself provides no failure status. A write/finalization failure after `MODE_NEWFILE` can therefore destroy the prior settings file and leave an invalid or incomplete replacement without a reported failure. Require exact header write length, propagate all nested IFF errors, and write to a temporary file before replacing the existing preferences.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds including MUI Configdata when a save opens its target and a later DOS/IFF write, seek, or chunk-finalization operation fails; the negative-PRHD-return case additionally requires `PopChunk()` to return success after that write error. **Confidence:** high for the truthy negative-error check, ignored status paths, and truncation ordering; the exact malformed output depends on stream failure behavior. No save or filesystem failure was run; source-only.

**Review evidence:** Configdata IFF save body and selected Zune caller reviewed at [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3078`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3078), [`#L3278`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3278); IFF/DOS stream return contract checked in the cited local sources.

## GD5089

**Zune Preferences applies partial, default, or fallback settings after Configdata loading fails.** `Configdata__MUIM_Load()` initializes `res = TRUE`, ignores the return from `StopChunk()`, clears the object's Dataspace before parsing, then loops on `ParseIFF()` without recording its terminal error (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:1242-1271`). `StopChunk()` can fail when `EntryHandler()` cannot allocate or store its local handler (`workbench/libs/iffparse/stopchunk.c:52-64`; `entryhandler.c:73-99`). If that registration fails, the scan has no stop handler for `PREF/MUIC`, so the Dataspace has already been cleared but the `MUIC` chunks are not delivered to the import call. It also ignores the result of `MUIM_Dataspace_ReadIFF()` for each `MUIC` chunk (`:1265-1268`); that method can return `IFFERR_NOMEM` after its temporary-buffer allocation fails (`classes/dataspace.c:197-220`). Once `OpenIFF()` succeeds, handler-setup/parser/read errors therefore leave `res` true. `Dataspace__MUIM_ReadIFF()` has another false-success path: it ignores `MUIM_Dataspace_Add()` results, although Add returns 0 when pooled-node allocation fails (`classes/dataspace.c:93-126,235-237`); it also breaks on a record length larger than the remaining chunk or silently stops at a trailing fragment shorter than an eight-byte record header, then unconditionally returns 0 (`:221-243`). Thus a partially imported Dataspace can be reported as successful even if callers begin checking the method result. The other direct reader caller, `Application__MUIM_Load()`, also ignores the result and imports the records accumulated so far into every window child (`application.c:2386-2450`); selected callers include the Zune settings test and LogView startup (`developer/debug/test/Zune/settings.c:100`; `workbench/system/LogView/logview.c:765`). In `Configdata__OM_NEW()`, a true return for the app-specific ENV file prevents trying the ENVARC file and the global fallback (`configdata.c:578-602`). Missing Dataspace entries are later supplied by the Configdata getters/default tables and synchronization path (`:304-360,614-628`), so the resulting object can combine values imported before failure with defaults for the rest.

The selected Zune `main_open_menu()` path constructs Configdata, explicitly calls `MUIM_Configdata_Load()` for the chosen file, ignores its result, applies the object through each page's `MUIM_Settingsgroup_ConfigToGadgets`, and calls `test_prefs()` (`workbench/prefs/Zune/zune.c:630-662`). `test_prefs()` saves the current page values to `ENV:zune/<appname>.prefs` (`:610-612,669-702`). A malformed/truncated IFF, Dataspace buffer/node allocation failure, or malformed trailing record can thus apply partial/default preferences and persist them over the ENV settings. The ordinary `MUIM_Application_Load()` path can likewise import an incomplete record prefix because the Dataspace reader reports the malformed tail or failed Add as success and Application Load ignores the reader result. There is a second failure edge at this same caller: when the selected file cannot be opened or `OpenIFF()` rejects it, `Configdata__MUIM_Load()` returns FALSE before clearing the object's existing Dataspace (`configdata.c:1245-1256,1272-1279`), but `main_open_menu()` still applies that preloaded app/global fallback through the pages and calls `test_prefs()`. Thus an unavailable or non-IFF selected file can silently apply and persist fallback settings as if the selected file had loaded. At startup, the same false-success result for an app-specific ENV file also suppresses recovery from a valid ENVARC/global file before `load_prefs()` applies ConfigToGadgets (`configdata.c:578-602`; `zune.c:578-601`).

Check and propagate `StopChunk()`, `ParseIFF()`, and `MUIM_Dataspace_ReadIFF()` errors, preserve the previous Dataspace until a complete load succeeds, and allow constructor fallback after a failed file parse. **Affected configuration and trigger:** selected Zune Preferences or MUI Configdata builds when an opened IFF load terminates with a parse error, a `StopChunk()` handler registration fails after the clear, or a `MUIC` Dataspace import fails after the clear, or the Zune Open-menu's selected file cannot be opened/initialized as IFF; the menu ignores the FALSE result and applies/saves partial, default, or preloaded fallback settings. Separately, app-specific ENV parse failure can suppress ENVARC/global fallback. **Confidence:** high for the ignored `StopChunk`/parser/import errors, Dataspace clear ordering, failed-open preservation, fallback condition, and Zune apply/save sequence; the particular malformed file, missing selected file, or temporary-allocation failure is conditional. No preferences file was imported and no allocation or I/O failure was induced; source-only.

**Review evidence:** Configdata constructor/load and Zune callers rechecked at [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3278`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3278) and the source-order MUI/Configdata inventory.

## GD5090

**MUIS_AllocPubScreenDesc dereferences its result when descriptor allocation fails.** The function stores `AllocMem()`'s result in `psd` and immediately uses it without checking for NULL. When `src` is non-NULL, `CopyMem(src, psd, ...)` writes to the failed allocation; when `src` is NULL, the default name/title copies and subsequent field assignments dereference `psd` (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/allocpubscreendesc.c:51-71`). The routine therefore faults instead of returning NULL on memory exhaustion, before any caller can recover.

This affects both branches. `MUIS_ReadPubFile()` passes a populated local descriptor (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/readpubfile.c:93`); PSI also calls the default branch from the palette preset action (`workbench/prefs/PSI/editpanel_class.c:387`) and the populated branch from screen copy/list construction (`screenpanel_class.c:152`; `screenlist_class.c:63`). The callers' later NULL checks cannot protect against the write inside the allocator helper. The API's expected allocation-failure behavior should be to return NULL without dereferencing it, allowing the callers to handle failure.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting MUIScreen and any caller invoking `MUIS_AllocPubScreenDesc()` while its `AllocMem()` fails. **Consequence:** task fault in the caller before it can handle allocation failure; the original allocation failure is not propagated. **Confidence:** high for both branches and caller reachability; actual memory exhaustion was not induced. Source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5090`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5090).

## GD5091

**Configdata dereferences a failed list-node allocation while loading public-screen preferences.** `Configdata_LoadPubScreens()` first receives an allocated descriptor from `MUIS_ReadPubFile()`, then allocates a list node with `AllocVec()` and immediately stores the descriptor in `psNode->ln_Name` without checking the result (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:1331-1337`). If the node allocation fails while a descriptor is being loaded, this dereference faults. `Configdata__DisposeDescriptors()` has already cleared the existing list before the file is read, and the newly returned descriptor is not freed on this failure path.

This loader runs after a successful Configdata preference load (`configdata.c:1287-1289`) and as the filesystem notification method for the public-screen preference file (`:601-614`). Configdata is the selected builtin class; MUI Window later queries the descriptor list when a named public screen cannot be locked (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:459-468`). Thus memory pressure during a file containing at least one readable descriptor can fault the task during load or notification, rather than leave the list empty/partial and continue. The list-node allocation must be checked, and the descriptor released if insertion cannot proceed.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting MUI Configdata/MUIScreen; `MUIS_ReadPubFile()` returns a descriptor and the subsequent `AllocVec(sizeof(struct Node), MEMF_CLEAR)` fails during the load or notification path. **Consequence:** task fault; the descriptor returned by the reader is also left unfreed on the failing branch. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation, failure ordering and selected call paths; no allocation failure or notification was induced. Source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5091`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5091).

## GD5092

**MUIS_OpenPubFile leaks acquired IFF/DOS resources on setup failure.** The function allocates an `IFFHandle`, opens the named DOS file, and opens the IFF parser in sequence, but its failure exits return NULL without unwinding resources acquired earlier (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/openpubfile.c:54-90`). If `Open()` fails, the allocated IFF handle is not freed. If `OpenIFF()` fails, both the IFF handle and open DOS stream are retained. In `MODE_NEWFILE`, failures from either `PushChunk()` or the exact-size `WriteChunkBytes()` check likewise return NULL while the IFF and DOS stream remain open; a successfully pushed FORM or PRHD chunk may also be left unclosed. `MUIS_ClosePubFile()` cannot clean these cases because callers receive only NULL and invoke it only for a returned handle (`closepubfile.c:47-57`).

Checked-in callers include Configdata public-screen loading, PSI ScreenList load/save, and Zune SystemPrefs loading (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:1331`; `workbench/prefs/PSI/screenlist_class.c:150,183`; `workbench/prefs/Zune/systemp.c:88`). Each conditions its normal read/write and close sequence on a non-NULL result. Repeated failures can therefore retain file handles and IFF allocations; write-mode setup failure can additionally leave a newly truncated or partially initialized file, which is tracked separately under the save-path finding.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting MUIScreen and calls to `MUIS_OpenPubFile()` where an acquired stage fails: file open after `AllocIFF`, `OpenIFF` after file open, or write-chunk/header setup after opening a `MODE_NEWFILE`. **Consequence:** leaked IFF handle and/or DOS stream, with partially initialized output possible on the write path. **Confidence:** high for the missing cleanup and selected caller handling; no file or IFF failure was induced. Source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5092`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5092).

## GD5093

**PSI can report public-screen preferences saved after IFF finalization fails.** `ScreenList_Save()` sets `result = TRUE` after `MUIS_OpenPubFile()` succeeds and keeps it true when every descriptor write succeeds. It then calls the void `MUIS_ClosePubFile()` and returns `result` without observing finalization status (`workbench/prefs/PSI/screenlist_class.c:174-202`). The close helper calls `PopChunk()` for write handles, then `CloseIFF()`, `Close()` and `FreeIFF()`, but discards the `PopChunk()` result and exposes no status (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/closepubfile.c:47-57`). A failed final chunk write/closure can therefore leave the public-screen file incomplete while ScreenList_Save reports success.

The PSI finish and Save As callers both discard ScreenList_Save's return value (`workbench/prefs/PSI/mainwindow_class.c:57-68,179-189`), so neither path can surface even ordinary descriptor-write failure to the user. On finish, PSI proceeds to quit immediately after the save calls. This is distinct from failure to write an individual descriptor, which does set `result = FALSE` in ScreenList_Save; this finding is specifically the unobservable close/finalization result.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** PSI builds using MUIScreen; public-screen save setup and descriptor writes succeed, but `PopChunk()` during `MUIS_ClosePubFile()` fails while finalizing the file. **Consequence:** incomplete/invalid saved file can be reported as successful internally, and the selected GUI callers discard even the returned status. **Confidence:** high for ignored finalization status and caller behavior; a finalization error was not induced. Source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5093`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5093).

## GD5096

**PSI's public-screen list display treats the fixed-width Name field as an unbounded C string.** The IFF reader accepts an exact-size `MUI_PubScreenDescArray` and copies all 32 bytes of `Name` into the descriptor without requiring a NUL terminator (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/readpubfile.c:61-70`; `fileformat.h:31-39`). The selected PSI display hook then appends `desc->Name` with `strcat()` to a 34-byte static buffer (`workbench/prefs/PSI/screenlist_class.c:112-117`). If a loaded descriptor's Name and adjacent fixed-width fields contain no terminator, `strcat()` scans beyond the Name array and writes the resulting string past `buf1`; a two-byte underline/bold prefix reduces the buffer's available name space further.

The short read/record-size checks in `MUIS_ReadPubFile()` do not validate string termination, so a complete fixed-size IFF record with unterminated fields reaches the list construct/display path. `ScreenList_Load()` inserts each returned descriptor into the MUI List (`screenlist_class.c:144-167`), whose registered display hook is `ScreenList_DisplayFunc` (`:330-335`). The source supports this conditional malformed-record failure; ordinary names written by PSI are expected to be terminated, and the trigger requires a file whose fixed-width string fields do not contain an early NUL.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** PSI/MUIScreen builds loading a full-size public-screen record with unterminated fixed-width string fields; the list display hook renders that descriptor. **Consequence:** out-of-bounds string read and write beyond the display buffer, with possible corruption of adjacent static state. **Confidence:** high for missing validation and unsafe display operation; malformed input is conditional and no file was loaded. Source-only. Validate/terminate each fixed-width string at the reader boundary and format the display into a bounded buffer.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5096`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5096).

<a id="gd5097"></a>
## GD5097

**MUIS_ClosePubScreen discards autoclose tracking and reports success when Intuition refuses to close a screen with windows.** After finding the public screen, the helper calls `PubScreenStatus(..., PSNF_PRIVATE)` but ignores its result, removes and frees the screen's node from `muisb_autocScreens`, then calls `CloseScreen()` without checking its BOOL result (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/closepubscreen.c:73-95`). `PubScreenStatus()` returns zero and leaves the screen public when visitor windows remain (`rom/intuition/pubscreenstatus.c:57-73`). Independently, `CloseScreen()` returns FALSE when `screen->FirstWindow` is non-NULL (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:105-113`). MUIScreen nevertheless sets `retval = TRUE`.

For a screen created with `AutoClose`, removing the tracking node before a failed close prevents the MUIScreen close task from retrying it: that task only checks screens still present in `muisb_autocScreens` (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/muiscreen_init.c:78-88`). If visitor references prevent privatization, the screen remains public; if privatization succeeds but another window still blocks close, it remains private. In either case, the discarded tracking leaves the screen open after its windows close. The worker has a second path to the same failure: after a zero-visitor signal it checks only `FirstWindow`, removes/frees the tracking node, then calls `CloseScreen()` (`muiscreen_init.c:72-88`). If another task acquires a public-screen visitor reference after the signal but before this check, `FirstWindow` may be NULL while Intuition's `CloseScreen()` rejects the close because `psn_VisitorCount` is nonzero (`rom/intuition/unlockpubscreen.c:78-105`; `rom/intuition/closescreen.c:331-348`). Later `UnlockPubScreen()` signals the worker again when the count reaches zero, but the AutoClose record is already gone. PSI's selected Close action treats MUIS_ClosePubScreen's return as success and does not beep (`workbench/prefs/PSI/screenpanel_class.c:215-223`); its CLI close path also reports success from the helper (`workbench/prefs/PSI/psi.c:378-383`). This is separate from GD5098's concurrent list-node lifetime race in the same helper.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting MUIScreen; either `MUIS_ClosePubScreen()` is called on an `AutoClose` screen with a window still open, or the AutoClose worker processes a zero-visitor signal after a new visitor reference arrives while no window is open. **Consequence:** the screen remains open and loses its AutoClose tracking; depending on visitor references it remains public or becomes private, while the explicit close helper reports success. **Confidence:** high for the ignored status values, tracking removal, and helper's success result; no screen/window operation was run. Source-only. Preserve AutoClose tracking until `CloseScreen()` succeeds and propagate failure. Also handle `PubScreenStatus()` failure before treating the screen as private.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5097`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5097).

## GD5098

**MUIS_ClosePubScreen uses a PubScreenNode after releasing the list lock that protects it.** The function walks Intuition's public-screen list under `LockPubScreenList()`, saves the matching `PubScreenNode *`, then calls `UnlockPubScreenList()` before using the node again (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/closepubscreen.c:58-67`). It later dereferences `pubscrnode->psn_Screen` for `PubScreenStatus()` and again for autoclose lookup and `CloseScreen()` (`:73-87`). Intuition's `CloseScreen()` acquires the same public-screen list semaphore and removes and frees the node while holding it (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:147-155,331-348`).

If another task closes the same public screen after MUIScreen releases the list lock but before its next `pubscrnode` access, Intuition can free the node in that interval. MUIScreen then reads the freed node to obtain `psn_Screen`; two concurrent `MUIS_ClosePubScreen()` callers can also both retain the same node from their initial lookup. The selected PSI close action calls this helper (`workbench/prefs/PSI/screenpanel_class.c:217-221`), and PSI's CLI close path calls it as well (`workbench/prefs/PSI/psi.c:378-383`). Keep the list lock across the protected node use or copy/refcount the screen under a lifetime mechanism that prevents concurrent removal.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting MUIScreen and Intuition; another task successfully closes/removes the matching public screen after `UnlockPubScreenList()` and before MUIScreen's subsequent node dereference. **Consequence:** stale-node read and potentially invalid screen pointer passed to Intuition; exact result depends on the interleaving and memory reuse. **Confidence:** high for the lock/lifetime mismatch and freeing path; the race is conditional and was not scheduled or run. Source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5098`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5098).
