## GD5151 — OpenSBI GOP conversion drops bits from non-contiguous component masks

The OpenSBI EFI stub accepts `EFI_GOP_PIXEL_BITMASK` and copies the firmware's red, green, blue, and reserved masks without checking that each mask is contiguous (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/efi_stub.c:700-705`). `krnFillVBEFromGOP()` converts each mask to the VBE size/position representation through `krnFBMask()` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_startup.c:323-340,356-365`). That helper counts only the run of set bits starting at the lowest set bit; any later set bits after a zero are discarded from the representation. `bootloader.resource` reconstructs a contiguous mask from only the resulting size and position (`rom/bootloader/bootloader_init.c:194-215`), and EFIFBGfx uses those reconstructed masks to advertise the framebuffer pixel format (`rom/hidds/efifbgfx/efifbgfx_support.c:37-45`; `efifbgfx_displayclass.c:78-92`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the UEFI GOP reports a `PixelBitMask` mode with a non-contiguous color or reserved mask, and OpenSBI captures that current mode. The VBE compatibility record no longer describes all mask bits; EFIFBGfx then advertises a different packed pixel format, so rendered component values can be misplaced or lost. **Affected configuration:** RISC-V64 OpenSBI using the EFI framebuffer HIDD, conditional on the firmware's current GOP bitmask layout. **Confidence:** high for the lossy mask conversion and downstream use; whether a particular firmware mode supplies such a mask is not established by checked-in board data. No GOP mode or framebuffer was exercised; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5152 — OpenSBI EFI framebuffer treats low-depth direct-color pixels as palette indices

The EFI stub accepts GOP `PixelBitMask` modes down to an 8-bit pixel width: its mask-span loop stores `bpp` as the smallest whole-byte width covering all component masks (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/efi_stub.c:698-725`). Startup publishes those masks as a VBE `VMEM_RGB` mode (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/kernel/kernel_startup.c:345-365`). For any captured depth at or below 8 bits, however, `initEFIFBGfxHW()` discards the supplied channel masks and substitutes 8:8:8 masks (`rom/hidds/efifbgfx/efifbgfx_support.c:37-53`), and `EFIFBGfxDisplay__Root__New()` advertises `vHidd_ColorModel_Palette` based on `depth > 8` (`rom/hidds/efifbgfx/efifbgfx_displayclass.c:74-88`). The selected EFI framebuffer implementation's `DACLoad()` is a no-op because it assumes GOP is truecolor (`rom/hidds/efifbgfx/efifbgfx_support.c:139-144`). In this palette mode, `SetColors()` updates the superclass ColorMap and its private DAC buffer, then calls this no-op upload (`efifbgfx_bitmapclass.c:168-207`). `UpdateRect()` ultimately copies the bitmap's one-byte-per-pixel buffer directly to the firmware framebuffer (`efifbgfx_bitmapclass.c:210-220`; `efifbgfx_support.c:102-138`).

**Trigger and consequence:** GOP supplies a direct-color `PixelBitMask` mode whose masks fit in one byte per pixel and OpenSBI keeps that mode. EFIFBGfx treats each source byte as a palette index, but the firmware interprets the same byte as packed direct-color component bits. Updating the software palette cannot change the firmware's direct-color interpretation, so displayed colors can disagree with the requested ColorMap colors. The HIDD's advertised palette behavior does not match the scanout format. **Affected configuration:** RISC-V64 OpenSBI with EFIFBGfx, conditional on a low-depth direct-color GOP mode. The ordinary GOP RGBX/BGRX formats are 32-bit and do not trigger this case; no checked-in board evidence establishes a low-depth GOP mode. **Confidence:** high for the differing color-model selection and no-op palette update; firmware-mode reachability is conditional. No framebuffer mode or palette operation was exercised; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5167

**PSI builds an EditWindow title by concatenating an imported fixed-width screen name without bounds.** `ScreenPanel_Edit()` passes `desc->Name` from the selected public-screen descriptor as `MUIA_EditWindow_Title` (`workbench/prefs/PSI/screenpanel_class.c:80-97`). `EditWindow_New()` copies a localized title into `wtitle[PSD_MAXLEN_TITLE + 20]`, appends a space, then uses unbounded `strcat()` with that tag value (`workbench/prefs/PSI/editwindow_class.c:24-28,59-63`). The public-screen file reader copies all 32 Name bytes without checking for a NUL (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/readpubfile.c:61-70`). A malformed record with unterminated Name and adjacent fixed-width strings can therefore make `strcat()` read beyond the Name field and append more than the remaining title buffer capacity. The PSI Copy action is a second unsafe sink: it duplicates the selected descriptor, then `strcpy(namebuf, new->Name)` copies an unterminated fixed-width name into `namebuf[PSD_MAXLEN_NAME]` with no bound (`workbench/prefs/PSI/screenpanel_class.c:147-160`). A 32-byte nonterminated Name followed by nonzero Title bytes therefore overruns this stack buffer before the bounded `stccpy()` call. The Copy button is connected directly to this method (`:324-327`), and loaded records enter the same ScreenList through `MUIS_ReadPubFile()` (`screenlist_class.c:144-167`).

These are distinct consumers from GD5096's list display hook: the title is built when the user opens Edit, while Copy performs an unbounded stack-buffer copy. The 148-byte title destination allows ordinary names; the copy action overflows as soon as the fixed-width Name lacks a terminator. Both require an imported record with malformed fixed-width text, which the reader currently accepts without validation.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** PSI/MUIScreen builds; load a full-size public-screen record with a nonterminated Name (and nonzero following field for the title overrun), then open Edit or press Copy on that descriptor. **Consequence:** out-of-bounds read and title-buffer write in Edit; out-of-bounds read and stack-buffer overwrite in Copy. **Confidence:** high for both unbounded operations and selected caller routes; malformed file contents are conditional and no file/window was opened. Source-only. Validate imported strings and use bounded copies for display, title, and duplicate-name construction.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5167`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gd5167).

## GD5170 — MUI Window sleep restores the wrong minimum width

**Finding:** On the first sleep transition, the MUI Window class saves the native window's `MaxWidth` into both `wd_SleepMaxWidth` and `wd_SleepMinWidth` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:3282-3309`). On the final wake transition it passes those saved values to `WindowLimits()` as the restored minimum and maximum (`:3312-3335`). The minimum argument should come from `Window->MinWidth`; instead it becomes the previous maximum.

Intuition's selected `WindowLimits()` implementation changes `MinWidth` only when the current `Window->Width` is at least the requested minimum, and returns FALSE without changing that field otherwise (`rom/intuition/windowlimits.c:74-80,105-106`). MUI ignores that return. Thus, when the old maximum exceeds the current width, the temporary sleep minimum remains in place after wake; when it does not, the old maximum is installed as the minimum. In either case the original lower resize bound is not restored, so a user can be prevented from narrowing the window to its configured minimum.

**Trigger and scope:** an opened window with a native render window has distinct original minimum and maximum widths, receives `MUIA_Window_Sleep=TRUE` on its first sleep-count transition and later `FALSE` on the final transition, and passes the normal saved-height guard (`wd_SleepMaxHeight > 0`). The class is in muimaster's default `CLASSES` list (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:60-89`); application-level sleep iterates its windows and forwards the attribute (`classes/application.c:1204-1217`). Checked-in callers include PSI application-level sleep around screen editing/file requests and direct window sleep in TextEditor, VMM, HDToolBox, AROS TCP syslog, disk-image GUI and QuickPart. A caller census found the paths paired, including the VMM task selector close-request wake; nested disk-image requesters balance through the sleep counter. The effect depends on the window's original limits and size; no window operation was run.

**Confidence:** High for the incorrect saved field and failure to restore the original minimum; the visible resize restriction is conditional on the configured limits. **Suggested correction:** save `Window->MinWidth` into `wd_SleepMinWidth`.

**Review evidence:** [`sleep/wake implementation and Intuition limit trace`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mui-window-sleep-wake-minimum-width-gd5170); [`maintained-caller pairing census`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mui-window-sleep-all-maintained-callers-pairing-gd5170). Source-only; no build or runtime behavior was exercised.

## GD5179

**OpenScreen leaves a freed screen published when MakeVPort fails.** The synchronous open action first inserts a public-screen node, publishes the screen through `IntuitionBase->FirstScreen`/`ActiveScreen`, and may assign `DefaultPubScreen` (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:2433-2471`). It then sets `msg->Success` false if `MakeVPort()` returns an error, but still calls `AddResourceToList(screen, RESOURCE_SCREEN, ...)` (`:2476-2500`). The caller copies that failure into `ok`; its rollback frees the color map, layers, bitmap and finally disposes the `IntScreen` (`:2303-2310,2317-2399`). That rollback does not unlink the public node, repair the screen chain/default pointer, or remove the embedded resource hash node. `ScreenClass__OM_DISPOSE()` only releases decoration state and delegates to the superclass (`rom/intuition/screenclass.c:46-79`); it does not repair these publications. This failure path also bypasses `CloseScreen()`'s public-node/resource/screen-chain removal (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:331-351`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** any selected Intuition build when opening a screen reaches `MakeVPort()` and it returns a nonzero error, such as a display-mode rejection or a display/copper-list allocation failure. **Consequence:** global screen and resource lists retain links into the freed screen, and a public-screen node can retain `psn_Screen` pointing at the freed object; subsequent screen traversal, public-screen access, or resource lookup may dereference stale memory. Unpublish and unlink the screen before disposing it on the failed-open path. **Confidence:** high for publication-before-failure, unconditional resource-list insertion, and disposal without matching unlink; manifestation requires a failed `MakeVPort()` during an otherwise initialized OpenScreen. No screen open or failure was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5184

**Finding:** Several preferences clients retain a borrowed public-port pointer after `FindPort()` without protecting the port through `PutMsg()`. On ExecSMP, the owner can remove and free the port on another CPU in that interval; the sender then posts through a stale `MsgPort *`. If the port is removed but not yet freed, a late message can instead arrive after the manager has stopped servicing its queue. Either outcome can leave the sender waiting indefinitely; the freed-port case also passes stale storage to Exec IPC.

**Evidence and trigger:** Preferences Editor uses this sequence in `find_prefs()`, `find_jano()`, and `send_jano()` (`workbench/prefs/Editor/PrefsPort.c:28-42,65-78,84-95`). Jano Editor uses it in `find_janoed()` and `send_pref()` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:437-452,479-492`). The optional VMM preferences app has the same gap in `AllowVM()` (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/config.c:17-45`): it looks up `VMPORTNAME`, allocates a request and signal, then enqueues and waits without holding `Forbid()` across lookup and send. `TryToQuit()` can remove the public port after `ExitPossible()` (`workbench/system/VMM/VM_Manager.c:169-198`); the manager then leaves its message loop and cleans up the port (`VM_Manager.c:650-676`; `VM_Manager_Init.c:1085-1102`). If `AllowVM()` enqueues after the manager has decided to quit, the request is not acknowledged; if cleanup deletes the port first, `PutMsg()` dereferences the stale port while touching its queue (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-95`). This VMM case applies only when the optional VMM manager is built and running far enough to publish its port. The owners remove and free their public ports during cleanup (`workbench/prefs/Editor/PrefsPort.c:99-108`; `workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:495-500`; `workbench/prefs/Editor/JanoPrefs.c:570-574`; `workbench/tools/Edit/Jed.c:119-124`). `FindPort()` releases its port-list read lock before returning (`rom/exec/findport.c:50-59`); `RemPort()` removes under the list lock, while `DeleteMsgPort()` frees the object (`rom/exec/remport.c:49-64`; `rom/exec/deletemsgport.c:48-56`). `PutMsg()` then dereferences the supplied port to enqueue the message (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-95`). The optional VMM command-line clients have the same lifetime gap despite wrapping lookup/send in `Forbid()`: `VMMStat` (`workbench/system/VMM/tools/VMMStat.c:36-53`) and `VMMUsageCLI` (`tools/VMMUsageCLI.c:41-55`) call `FindPort()` and `PutMsg()` in one local critical section. `TryToQuit()` can remove `VMPort` on another CPU (`workbench/system/VMM/VM_Manager.c:169-198`), and final cleanup deletes it (`VM_Manager_Init.c:1085-1102`); Exec documents `Forbid()` as processor-local on ExecSMP (`rom/exec/forbid.c:52-60`), so those clients are not pinned against cross-CPU teardown. If a request is sent after the manager stops consuming, the clients wait forever for their reply signal; if teardown frees the port first, the sender passes the stale pointer to `PutMsg()`. Their `Forbid()` does serialize the lookup/send against same-processor scheduling on uniprocessor builds. These are legacy standalone VMM tool sources; their makefiles offer explicit targets, but no selected AROS parent-manifest edge was established for them. `C:GfxControl` has the same caller-side lifetime gap: `Start()` obtains the public `GfxControl` port with `FindPort()` and later sends its `ADBA` message through that pointer (`workbench/c/GfxControl.c:139-164`). A concurrent `ADBA` invocation can wake `PatchTask`, which calls `RemPort()` and `DeleteMsgPort()` after `WaitPort()` (`:95-103`), while the other invocation is between lookup and `PutMsg()`. The latter can then enqueue through the freed port. This extends the same conditional ExecSMP interleaving to the optional `workbench-c-sh` command; it is not a separate root cause.

**Affected configuration and confidence:** Confirmed source-level lifetime gap for the listed clients on ExecSMP builds if owner shutdown overlaps the lookup-to-send interval; the VMM instance is optional and conditional on a live manager. The callers also omit the `Forbid()/Permit()` protection required by the `FindPort()` contract on non-SMP builds; task-preemption overlap there is plausible but not established for every call path. Confidence: medium, because the queue-stop and stale-pointer interleavings follow from owner and sender ordering, but no concurrent shutdown was run. No IPC or task was exercised.

## GD5191 — MUI Area cleanup can dereference a freed timer request after rearm allocation fails

`Application__MUIM_AddInputHandler()` allocates a `timerequest_ext` for timer handlers and stores it in the embedded input-handler node's `mln_Pred`; if allocation fails, it returns TRUE without installing a request or clearing that predecessor (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1474-1502`). `Application__MUIM_RemInputHandler()` later reads `mln_Pred`, calls `CheckIO()`/`AbortIO()` and `WaitIO()`, then frees the request, but does not clear the stored pointer (`:1508-1527`). The selected Area timer callback removes the completed request, changes `ihn_Millis` to 50, and immediately adds the same embedded node again (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.c:2127-2138`). If this rearm's allocation fails, the node retains the pointer to the request just freed. Later `Area__MUIM_Cleanup()` sees nonzero `ihn_Millis` and calls `RemInputHandler()` again (`area.c:1601-1617`), which passes that freed pointer to `CheckIO()`; `CheckIO()` dereferences `io_Flags` immediately (`rom/exec/checkio.c:48-59`). On an initial timer registration failure, the add method also returns TRUE without a request, and a later removal interprets the unset predecessor as a request.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting the MUI master library and Area class, when timer-enabled Area input is used and a timer-request allocation fails, followed by handler removal or Area cleanup. RelVerify input uses this path (`area.c:1753-1766`). **Consequence:** removal reads an absent or freed request and can fault or operate on reused IORequest storage. Clear the predecessor and registration state when removing a request; propagate failed registration so callers can avoid later removal. **Confidence:** high for ignored allocation failure, stale predecessor retention, the cleanup caller, and the immediate CheckIO dereference; allocation failure and cleanup were not induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5227 — Graph records a timer handler as installed when its allocation fails

Graph sets `GRAPHF_HANDLER` before calling `MUIM_Application_AddInputHandler()` in both the live `MUIA_Graph_PeriodInterval` setter and `Graph__MUIM_Setup()`, and ignores the method result (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:331-342,425-441`). The application method allocates the timer request internally; on allocation failure it skips `SendIO()` but still returns `TRUE` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1474-1502`).

**Trigger:** The optional Graph.mcc class is built and used with a nonzero period, and timer-request allocation fails during setup or when periodic mode is enabled.

**Effect:** Graph retains `GRAPHF_HANDLER` although no timer is running. It then suppresses later registration attempts while the flag is set, so periodic samples stop. During cleanup it sees both periodic and handler flags and calls `MUIM_Application_RemInputHandler()` for the node that has no valid request (`graph.c:545-559`), reaching the invalid-request cleanup described in GD5191. A selected in-tree client is SysMon's processor graph, which constructs Graph with a 1000 ms period (`workbench/system/SysMon/processor_graph.c:110,177`); the class itself is optional and SysMon's run-time presentation depends on the shipped Graph.mcc module.

**Confidence:** High for the caller's unchecked registration and false installed flag; conditional on Graph.mcc being present and timer allocation failing. The invalid request passed to cleanup is covered jointly with the generic MUI allocator/removal path in GD5191. No timer allocation failure or graph update was induced; source-only.

## GD5229

**IntelGMA treats failed graphics display registration as successful initialization.**

The PCI enumeration callback sets `sd->PCIDevice` before configuring the device (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_init.c:329-333`), programs the initial mode with `G45_LoadState()`, then discards the status returned by `AddDisplayDriverA()` (`:417-444`). After enumeration, `G45_Init()` reports success based on `sd->PCIDevice` being non-NULL (`:500-505`), so the startup caller publishes `sd.IntelG45Class` and leaves the process resident (`intelgma_startup.c:251-295`) even if graphics.library rejected the display registration.

`AddDisplayDriverA()` can fail before driver setup with `DD_NO_MEM` or `DD_ID_EXISTS`, or return `DD_DRIVER_ERROR` when `driver_Setup()` cannot instantiate the graphics class (`rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:166-175,180-181,270-297`; `rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:326-385`). Each failure occurs after IntelGMA has programmed the initial mode, so startup still reports success while graphics.library has not accepted the display driver. The generic API can also return `DD_IN_USE` after a boot-display handover refusal, but that trigger is not established for IntelGMA: its `Root.New` forwards attributes to the graphics superclass without consuming `DDRVA_Handover`, unlike the Nouveau class (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_hiddclass.c:520-535`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:421-435`). **Trigger:** an IntelGMA-supported device is found and one of the applicable pre-setup or class-instantiation failures occurs after `G45_LoadState()`. **Scope:** IntelGMA monitor startup with the selected graphics.library. **Confidence: high for ordering and ignored result; failure was not induced.**

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L69`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L69). The previously recorded overlap with an ignored registration result is now traced to this `AddDisplayDriverA()` call.

## GD5277

**Indexed summary:** MUI can dereference a NULL command table while dispatching an ARexx message.

**Source and trigger:** Setting `MUIA_Application_UseRexx` enables creation and publication of the ARexx port independently of `MUIA_Application_Commands` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:582-586,710-727`). When a message arrives, dispatch assigns `cmd = data->app_Commands` and immediately evaluates `cmd->mc_Name` in the loop condition without checking whether the command table is NULL (`:1707-1713`).

**Consequence and scope:** An application that enables ARexx but supplies no command table can dereference NULL when any message is dequeued from its published ARexx port. Supplying a command table or leaving ARexx disabled avoids this path. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked state and dereference; it requires a received message on a successfully created port. No ARexx message was sent; source-only.

## GD5278

**Indexed summary:** MUI invokes templated ARexx command hooks when ReadArgs rejects the arguments.

**Source and trigger:** Once a matching command with a non-NULL template is found, MUI calls `ReadArgs()` but does not test its return before invoking the configured hook (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1721-1747,1752-1754`). A syntactically invalid or incomplete argument string can therefore make `ReadArgs()` return NULL while the hook still runs with the zero-initialized argument vector.

**Consequence and scope:** The command hook receives arguments that failed the declared template validation and may treat absent or invalid operands as valid values, potentially performing an unintended application operation. This applies to configured templated commands receiving arguments rejected by `ReadArgs()`; parser-allocation failure before vector initialization is separately covered by GD5085. **Confidence:** high for the ignored parse result; application-level effect depends on hook behavior. No command was sent; source-only.

<a id="gd5330"></a>
<a id="gd5330-vgagfx-cursor-erasure-reads-past-a-smaller-displayable-bitmap"></a>
## GD5330 — VGAGfx cursor erasure reads past a smaller displayable bitmap

`erase_mouse()` builds an inclusive `Box` whose right and bottom coordinates are `mouseX + mouseW` and `mouseY + mouseH`, one pixel beyond the cursor's drawn extent (`arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_displayclass.c:392-405`; `draw_mouse()` iterates exactly `mouseW` columns and `mouseH` rows at `:338-389`). `vgaRefreshArea()` clips that box against `disp_width` and `disp_height`, but does not clip source reads against the bitmap's `width` or `height` (`arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_support.c:445-480,515-679`). The bitmap constructor preserves requested bitmap dimensions separately from mode dimensions and allocates `bpr * height` bytes; it permits a displayable bitmap smaller than the mode, and visibility setup explicitly clears the uncovered display area (`arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_bitmapclass.c:48-91,265-288`). `SetCursorPos()` clamps the cursor origin to the bitmap edge (`vgagfx_displayclass.c:295-317`), so a subsequent cursor erase at the bottom edge of a smaller bitmap can make `vgaRefreshArea()` read source rows beyond the allocated bitmap. The extra inclusive column can also extend reads past the logical row width.

**Trigger and consequence:** select a displayable VGA bitmap smaller than its physical mode, place the cursor at its bottom or right edge, then cause a cursor move, visibility change, or shape replacement that erases the old cursor. The source refresh reads beyond `VideoData`; at the bottom edge it can read beyond the allocation, while the extra column can read into row padding or the following row. **Affected configuration:** VGAGfx selected on i386-PC or x86-64-PC with a displayable bitmap smaller than the selected mode. **Confidence:** high for inclusive-end mismatch, physical-only clipping, and the smaller-bitmap path; no bitmap or cursor operation was run. Use `mouseX + mouseW - 1` / `mouseY + mouseH - 1` and clip the source rectangle to bitmap bounds before refreshing. Source-only.

## GD5366

**IntelGMA `PutImageLUT` dereferences an optional missing lookup table on framebuffer bitmaps.** The IntelGMA bitmap class overrides `moHidd_BitMap_PutImageLUT` (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_bitmapclass.c:2197-2199`). When its instance has `bm->fbgfx` set, the method reads `msg->pixlut->pixels` without checking whether `msg->pixlut` is NULL (`:1571-1584`); this occurs before the later scratch-allocation fallback. If the LUT structure exists but its `pixels` member is NULL, the accelerated 32-bit path indexes `colmap[*line++]` (`:1588-1628`). The generic bitmap superclass explicitly supports either a NULL LUT or a NULL `pixels` table, treating input bytes as pixel values (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:3924-3951`). The override therefore does not preserve the superclass method's accepted no-LUT case.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** a build that includes/selects the optional IntelGMA driver and calls `HIDD_BM_PutImageLUT` on an IntelGMA framebuffer-backed bitmap with `msg->pixlut == NULL`; a non-NULL LUT with `pixels == NULL` also faults if the framebuffer path, accelerated product range, and scratch allocation all select the indexed conversion loop. The active `workbench-devs-common` aggregate selects monitors, and the x86-64 PC monitor route selects the PCI monitor set containing IntelGMA (`workbench/devs/mmakefile.src:21-27`; `workbench/devs/monitors/mmakefile.src:4-13`). A repository-wide search found no checked-in IntelGMA call that supplies a missing LUT; external HIDD clients are the established remaining trigger scope.

**Consequence:** the method can dereference NULL while converting the source image, instead of using the generic superclass's raw-pixel fallback. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked dereference, override registration and generic fallback; medium for occurrence because no in-tree caller was found passing a missing LUT to this optional driver. No bitmap, HIDD method or hardware was used. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5367

**`WritePixelArray8()` cannot represent a clipped 32,768-pixel row width in its HIDD call.** The public vector takes signed `WORD` endpoints and documents the input row width as `xstop - xstart + 1` (`rom/graphics/writepixelarray8.c:16-25,30-45`). A caller can request the full representable coordinate range `xstart=0, xstop=32767` on a bitmap at least 32,768 pixels wide. The rectangle remains `0..32767` after bitmap clipping (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:101-140,1064-1088`), but `wp8_render()` stores `MaxX - MinX + 1` in a signed `WORD`, then passes that width to `HIDD_BM_PutImageLUT()` whose method signature also uses `WORD` (`gfxfuncsupport.c:680-691`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:3892-3893`). A signed `WORD` cannot represent the positive width 32,768.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library builds when `WritePixelArray8()` is called on a bitmap at least 32,768 pixels wide with a rectangle spanning `0..32767` horizontally. Such a row is consistent with the public endpoint and buffer-size contract; no checked-in caller uses this width. **Consequence:** the width passed to the HIDD is target/compiler-dependent and cannot faithfully represent 32,768; on targets that retain the low 16 bits it becomes negative and the generic HIDD `PutImageLUT` rejects it (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:3924-3940`), so the requested row is not written. Other conversion results can cause a truncated row or target-specific behavior. **Confidence:** high for the signed-width mismatch; medium for the exact manifestation because out-of-range conversion behavior depends on target/compiler. No wide bitmap or pixel-array call was used. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5421

**Indexed summary:** `WaitTOF()`'s shared waiter queue races on ExecSMP and retains a stack node if another task removes its blocked waiter.

`WaitTOF()` links a stack-local `Node` into the shared `GfxBase->TOF_WaitQ`, sleeps for `SIGF_SINGLE`, then removes the node (`rom/graphics/waittof.c:51-63`). Both queue mutations are protected only by `Disable()`, which explicitly masks interrupts only on the calling CPU in ExecSMP builds (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-60,85-93`). The VBlank handler concurrently traverses the same queue with `ForeachNode()` and calls `Signal()` on each node (`rom/graphics/graphics_init.c:163-200`); the macro fetches `node->ln_Succ` only after the loop body (`compiler/include/exec/lists.h:195-201`). On SMP, `Signal()` can make a waiter runnable on a different CPU and call `KrnScheduleCPU()` for its affinity (`rom/exec/signal.c:350-386`). That waiter can remove its node and return from `WaitTOF()` while the CPU 0 interrupt is still traversing, leaving the handler to read `ln_Succ` from a node whose stack lifetime has ended. Two callers on separate CPUs can also interleave their `AddTail()` pointer writes and corrupt or detach queue links.

There is a distinct cancellation path even without SMP: while a task is blocked in `WaitTOF()`, another task can call the public `RemTask(task)` API. `Wait()` sets the target to `TS_WAIT` before switching away (`rom/exec/wait.c:92-103`), and `RemTask()` rejects only `TS_INVALID`, `TS_TOMBSTONED`, or `TS_REMOVED` states, so it accepts that waiting target (`rom/exec/remtask.c:71-75`). It removes the task from scheduler lists, runs `CleanupETask()`, and frees every entry in its `tc_MemEntry` list (`remtask.c:91-105,115-128,165-181`); task creation places the stack allocation in that list (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:250-251`; `compiler/include/exec/tasks.h:62`). `WaitTOF()`'s stack node is not the task's scheduler node and is not registered for cancellation, so `RemTask()` leaves it linked in `TOF_WaitQ`. The next VBlank traversal reads the freed stack node and passes its stale task pointer to `Signal()` (`graphics_init.c:194-197`). This can disrupt the next TOF traversal or task signaling. The trigger is a caller removing a task while it is waiting in `WaitTOF()`. The selected `security.library` includes a root-only `secKill()` vector that calls `RemTask(task)` for a non-process target (`rom/security/mmakefile.src:29`; `rom/security/secKill.c:30-62`), so a maintained in-tree removal entry point exists. A repository-wide search found no `secKill()` client and no direct `WaitTOF()`/`RemTask()` pairing, so no checked-in caller is shown selecting a task in this state; the trigger remains conditional on a public-API caller. It applies to any selected graphics.library build with an active VBlank server, including the verified Raspberry Pi package. This removal path is separate from GD5421's ExecSMP queue interleavings but shares the same missing waiter-lifetime cleanup.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** an ExecSMP AArch64 Raspberry Pi 4/5 build with the selected graphics.library and timer resources. The package manifest selects both (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:97-118,213-218`), and the AArch64 kernel includes `kernel_execsmp` (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/mmakefile.src:20-30`). BCM2711/2712 scheduler ticks cause `INTB_VERTB` only on CPU 0 while other cores remain schedulable (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/platform_bcm2711.c:184-195`; `platform_bcm2712.c:292-302`). A repository-wide direct-call census found maintained calls in Blanker, Editor/Jed and popupmenu, plus developer calls in `2View` and `truecolorpens`; `AROSBootstrap` also calls it twice but is confined to the m68k-Amiga target. Blanker and Jed are under disabled aggregate tool edges (`workbench/tools/commodities/mmakefile.src:20`; `workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12`), popupmenu has a separate explicit library target, and both graphics test and `2View` are developer targets (`developer/debug/test/graphics/mmakefile.src:22-33`; `developer/demos/2View/mmakefile.src:7-16`). No caller edge into the standard Raspberry Pi package was found. The finding therefore remains conditional on a client calling this public vector in the selected ExecSMP configuration. **Consequence:** concurrent callers can corrupt the TOF queue or strand a waiter; the interrupt can also read a returned waiter's expired stack node. **Confidence:** high for the unsynchronized shared-list operations and cross-CPU wake path; the exact interleaving and resulting failure were not exercised. No waiter, VBlank event or SMP schedule was run; source-only.

## GD5422

**Indexed summary:** ExecSMP callers can race VBlank while enqueuing DBufInfo swap completions, losing a pending reply or leaving an already completed buffer record linked.

`internal_QueueDBufInfo()` pushes a `DBufInfo` onto the shared singly linked `dbuf_pending` head by writing `dbi_Link1` and then the head pointer, under `Disable()` only (`rom/graphics/graphics_init.c:205-212`). The VBlank server concurrently removes due entries by writing through `link` to `dbi_Link1` or the head, then clears the removed entry's link/count and sends both replies (`:163-192`). On ExecSMP, `Disable()` masks interrupts only on the local CPU (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-60,85-93`), so it does not serialize a caller on another CPU with the CPU 0 VBlank server.

For example, with due entry A at the head, CPU 0 can read A, CPU 1 can set new entry B's link to A, CPU 0 can unlink A and clear A's link, and CPU 1 can then publish B as the head. B now links to A even though the interrupt has completed A. On a later VBlank the cleared count makes A immediately due again, so it may be traversed and replied twice; the original caller may already have consumed its safe reply and freed the DBufInfo. With a different ordering, CPU 0's head update can overwrite CPU 1's new head and drop B, so B's completion messages are never sent. Intuition's `ChangeScreenBuffer()` calls `ChangeVPBitMap()` and later `FreeScreenBuffer()` waits for the safe reply before releasing the screen buffer (`rom/intuition/changescreenbuffer.c:74-83`; `freescreenbuffer.c:65-108`), making a lost request capable of blocking that cleanup indefinitely.

There is also a producer-versus-producer ordering with the same missing queue lock. `ChangeVPBitMap()` holds `ActiViewCprSemaphore` only through the viewport rebuild, releases it at `:98`, and calls `internal_QueueDBufInfo()` afterward (`:70-101`). Thus two concurrent direct callers can each leave the semaphore-protected section and overlap the local-`Disable()` head insertion on different CPUs. Both can read the same old head, then the later head store hides the other caller's record. The current in-tree direct callers were enumerated in the coverage ledger; this additional trigger applies when clients invoke the public vector concurrently and does not depend on VBlank removing a node during insertion.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** an ExecSMP build with graphics.library VBlank service active, when a new `ChangeVPBitMap()` enqueue races with VBlank removing an already-due pending node. The AArch64 Raspberry Pi 4/5 package selects graphics.library and timer (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:97-118,213-218`), and its BCM2711/2712 timer causes `INTB_VERTB` on CPU 0 while other cores remain schedulable (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/platform_bcm2711.c:184-195`; `platform_bcm2712.c:292-302`). The normal `ChangeScreenBuffer()` wrapper reaches the enqueue while holding Intuition `LockIBase` (`rom/intuition/changescreenbuffer.c:74-81`), but the VBlank handler takes no such lock and the graphics queue only uses local `Disable()`, so that wrapper lock does not exclude the race. A second concurrent enqueuer is not required; direct public `ChangeVPBitMap()` clients also reach the queue. **Consequence:** a swap can lose its safe/display replies or a completed DBufInfo can remain linked and be processed again, causing a wait to hang or a stale record/message-port access. **Confidence:** high for the unsynchronized queue writes and both source-level interleavings; no SMP interleaving or resulting failure was run. No screen buffer or VBlank was exercised; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5438 — MUI Group reports success when a dynamically added child fails setup

`Group__MUIM_AddObject()` first inserts the child into the Group's Family list and increments `num_children`, then, when the Group is already set up, calls `DoSetupMethod()` for the child but discards its return value and unconditionally returns `TRUE` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:250-299`). The Family insertion itself links the child before returning success (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/family.c:213-238`). This differs from `Group__MUIM_Setup()`, which checks each child's setup result and returns `FALSE` when setup fails (`group.c:1027-1078`).

**Trigger:** An application adds a child to a live/set-up Group (`OM_ADDMEMBER`, `MUIM_Group_AddTail`, `MUIM_Group_AddHead`, or `MUIM_Group_Insert`) and that child's `MUIM_Setup` returns false. `DoSetupMethod()` forwards that result (`workbench/libs/muimaster/support.c:72-78`).

**Effect:** The caller receives insertion success and the child remains in the Family list and counted as a member, although setup did not complete. The Group's later membership, layout, and cleanup walks still encounter it. A concrete in-tree dynamic caller is Cycle's `UpdateEntries()`, which adds newly created Text pages to its page Group (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/cycle.c:291-325`); the failure condition depends on the child class's setup path and is not claimed to occur for ordinary Text pages.

**Confidence:** Medium. The unchecked failure and retained membership are explicit. The practical effect depends on the child class's setup-failure cleanup contract; the specific selected Text caller establishes the dynamic-add path, not that Text setup currently fails. Source-only; no setup failure was induced.

## GD5439

**MUI Dataspace Clear frees entries without unlinking them from its list.** `Dataspace__MUIM_Clear()` saves each node's next pointer and frees the node from the pool, but never calls `Remove()` and never reinitializes `data->list` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/dataspace.c:129-145`). The MinList head and neighboring links therefore continue to refer to freed pool storage after the method returns. Subsequent `Find`, `Add`, or `WriteIFF` traversals follow those stale links; `Add` first walks the list looking for a replacement ID before appending its new node (`:93-126,147-164,246-276`).

The selected Configdata load path exercises reuse directly: after opening and initializing a preference IFF, it calls `MUIM_Dataspace_Clear()` and then parses `MUIC` chunks into the same Dataspace (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:1252-1265`). A nonempty prior Dataspace can therefore leave the next import traversing freed nodes; depending on pool reuse, the walk can fault, miss/replace the wrong entry, or corrupt list state. The other in-tree Clear call is Dataspace disposal with an externally supplied pool (`dataspace.c:83-90`); the object is then destroyed, so this path does not independently establish a subsequent traversal. `MUIM_Dataspace_Clear` remains a public method, so external callers that reuse the object have the same defect.

Unlink each node before freeing it, or reinitialize the MinList after all nodes have been released. **Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI Configdata reload after the Dataspace already contains entries, or any public Dataspace Clear followed by a list operation. **Consequence:** later traversal reads freed node links and may fault or corrupt preference records/list state. **Confidence:** high for the missing unlink/reinitialization and selected reload sequence; exact manifestation depends on pool reuse and was not reproduced. No Dataspace reuse or preference reload was run; source-only.

**Review evidence:** Dataspace full-body and Clear/reuse path are recorded at [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3363`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3363); the selected in-tree Clear caller census is recorded at the latest Dataspace caller recheck in that ledger.

## GD5440

**MUI Gauge repeatedly scales its stored current value on every OM_SET.** Gauge construction divides the initial `MUIA_Gauge_Current` by `MUIA_Gauge_Divide` once (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/gauge.c:52-80`). `Gauge__OM_SET()` then divides `data->current` unconditionally after processing its tag list, even when the update changed only `Max` or `InfoText` (`:104-198`). The stored value has already been scaled, so each unrelated update scales it again; integer division can progressively reduce it to zero and lower the displayed bar/text. For example, the selected Zune MUI debug test creates a vertical Gauge with `Current=30`, `Max=50`, and `Divide=2`, and its `NumericSetMax()` later changes the maximum in response to the editable maximum field (`developer/debug/test/Zune/test.c:48-50,1508-1526,2313-2315,3847-3853`). Its initial current is stored as 15; a max-only update scales that to 7, and another max-only update can reduce it further.

Scale only a newly supplied raw Current value, or keep the raw value separately and derive the displayed value without mutating it on unrelated attribute updates. **Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI Gauge users with nonzero `MUIA_Gauge_Divide` who update Max, InfoText, or another attribute through OM_SET without also supplying a fresh Current value; the selected debug test provides a concrete Max-update path. **Consequence:** the gauge current and formatted value drift downward after unrelated updates. **Confidence:** high for the unconditional repeated division and the cited caller. No Gauge or UI sequence was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5449

**MUI Levelmeter ignores its public Label attribute.** The public Levelmeter header declares `MUIA_Levelmeter_Label` as a V11 set/get `STRPTR` attribute (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/levelmeter.h:15-16`), but the private instance data has only the background pen and previous needle angle (`levelmeter_private.h:4-8`). `Levelmeter__OM_NEW()` forwards the incoming tag list to the Numeric superclass without storing the label (`levelmeter.c:56-69`); the Levelmeter dispatcher has no OM_SET or OM_GET case and forwards those methods to the superclass (`:423-442`). Its draw method paints a label background and frame but never draws label text (`:351-403`). A source search found no checked-in caller setting this attribute, so the defect is limited to public/custom clients rather than a demonstrated in-tree screen.

Implement storage, Set/Get handling, and rendering for the declared attribute, or remove the unsupported public declaration if the API is not intended to provide a label. **Affected configuration and trigger:** builds that select Levelmeter as a muimaster built-in or build the standalone `workbench-classes-zune-levelmeter` target (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:52,372-378`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/mmakefile.src:274-280`), when a client supplies or queries `MUIA_Levelmeter_Label`. **Consequence:** setting the advertised label has no visual effect and querying it does not return the configured string. **Confidence:** high for the declared attribute and missing storage/dispatch/rendering; no checked-in caller uses it. No Levelmeter object or GUI was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5472 — PanelGroup does not reconcile tracking after Group membership changes

PanelGroup initializes its private panel list and scans children once in `PanelGroup__OM_NEW()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panelgroup.c:175-235`). `PanelGroup__MUIM_PanelGroup_ScanPanels()` adds recognized children to that list and updates the count, but it does not remove tracking nodes for children that are no longer in the Group (`panelgroup.c:411-441`). PanelGroup's dispatcher handles its custom methods and Group change notifications, but does not intercept inherited `OM_ADDMEMBER`/`OM_REMMEMBER` or the Group Add/Remove methods (`panelgroup.c:946-977`).

**Trigger:** A client changes a PanelGroup's children after construction through inherited Group membership methods and then uses PanelGroup state/collapse/expand or drag-reordering operations without separately reconciling the private panel list.

**Effect:** Newly added Panel children are absent from `panel_list`, so bulk collapse/expand and panel state queries do not manage them consistently. Removed panels remain represented by nodes containing their old object pointers; bulk collapse/expand iterates those nodes and invokes `SetPanelCollapsed()` on the stored object (`panelgroup.c:515-623`). If a removed Panel is disposed before that operation, the retained pointer no longer denotes a live Panel object. `MUIM_PanelGroup_RemovePanel()` can remove a node, but ordinary inherited Group removal does not call it (`panelgroup.c:488-510`).

**Scope and confidence:** Medium. The missing reconciliation is explicit and the Group subclass exposes inherited membership operations. The reviewed checkout contains no in-tree dynamic PanelGroup child mutator, so the trigger is limited to clients that mutate membership after construction; no claim is made that a selected in-tree caller reaches it. Source-only; no GUI operation or disposed-child use was run.

## GD5521

**`GetGBuffers()` does not check the size multiplication used for a Bob's save buffer.** It first computes `Height * Width * 2` into signed `long memsize` and allocates that amount for `ImageShadow`, then multiplies the same signed value by `Depth` and passes it to `AllocMem()` for `SaveBuffer` (`rom/graphics/getgbuffers.c:84-103`). If double buffering is requested, the resulting value is reused for `DBuffer->BufBuffer` (`:114-125`). `VSprite.Height`, `Width`, and `Depth` are signed `WORD` fields with no dimension-range guard in this function (`compiler/include/graphics/gels.h:85-87`).

**Trigger and consequence:** On a target with 32-bit `long`, positive values `Width=32767`, `Height=8194`, and `Depth=8` make the first request 536,985,596 bytes, then make the signed `memsize *= Depth` operation exceed `LONG_MAX` (mathematical result 4,295,884,768). Signed overflow is undefined in C; therefore the source establishes an unchecked, unrepresentable size calculation, but does not by itself establish a deterministic wrapped allocation size for a selected compiler. If that target/compiler produces the ordinary two's-complement wrapped value (917,472), successful allocation makes `GetGBuffers()` return TRUE with a SaveBuffer far smaller than the required extent; the double-buffer copy is similarly undersized when `db` is TRUE. Later Bob save/restore may then access beyond that allocation. `FreeGBuffers()` repeats the same signed multiplication when freeing these buffers (`rom/graphics/freegbuffers.c:76-100,110-119`), so cleanup size is also not reliable after overflow.

This requires an extreme but representable public `VSprite` geometry and a 32-bit-`long` build. The only repository references beyond these two bodies are generated m68k emulator ABI thunk definitions and the function-vector table (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3041-3047,7545`; the corresponding `FreeGBuffers` thunk is at `:3608-3614,7609`); no maintained source call site invoking either API was found, so current in-tree reachability is not established. **Confidence:** high that the unchecked signed multiplication overflows for the stated dimensions on 32-bit-`long` targets; conditional for the undersized-allocation and later overrun consequence until the selected compiler's overflow behavior and an external caller are established. No allocation, buffer use, or runtime behavior was tested; source-only.

## GD5522

**VMM can leave its main preferences window asleep when the task-selector window fails to open.** The Add Task menu action calls `BuildTaskList()` (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/mui.c:341-343`). That function sets `WI_Window`'s `MUIA_Window_Sleep` to TRUE, populates and sorts the selector list, then requests `MUIA_Window_Open=TRUE` on `WI_TaskSelect` without checking whether it opened (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/task_page.c:414-445`). The only paths that wake the main window are the selector's close-request notification (`mui.c:150-152`) and the successful-entry hook (`task_page.c:466-471`).

The selected Zune/MUI `WindowOpen()` implementation can return FALSE when setup, root-object setup, or `DisplayWindow()` fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:3757-3795`); the `MUIA_Window_Open` setter calls it but discards that result (`:3158-3166`). The window's open state is separately queryable and is set only after successful display (`:3421-3423`; `WindowOpen():3795-3797`). Thus a failed task-selector open leaves the main preferences window's sleep count incremented, with no selector close-request or selection hook to decrement it. The main window remains unresponsive until another path explicitly clears sleep or the application exits.

**Trigger and consequence:** While VMM's preferences main window is open, choose Add Task and have task-selector setup or display fail (for example, the selected `OpenWindowTags()` call returns NULL in `DisplayWindow()`). The task list build completes, but the selector stays closed and the main window remains asleep. Applies to the VMM MUI preferences target using the selected in-tree Zune/MUI implementation. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked failure and unmatched sleep increment; the failure is conditional on GUI setup/window creation returning failure. No GUI window or failure was induced; source-only.

## GD5523

**Changing `BUTTON_Transparent` after the first render leaves the button bevel's cached transparency stale.** `Button__OM_SET()` forwards tags to `button_set()`, which updates `bd_Transparent` but does not invalidate or update an already-created `bd_BevelImage` (`workbench/classes/reaction/button/buttonclass.c:249-255,83-85`). `Button__GM_RENDER()` creates that bevel image only when the cache is NULL, passing the current transparency value once (`:318-328`); later renders reuse it (`:331-342`). The selected bevel image stores `BEVEL_Transparent` during setup and its render handler uses that stored field to decide whether to erase/fill the interior (`workbench/classes/reaction/bevel/bevelclass.c:37-59,345-378`). By comparison, changing `BUTTON_BevelStyle` explicitly disposes the cached bevel so it is recreated with the new setting (`buttonclass.c:57-64`).

**Trigger and consequence:** Construct and render a button with a non-`BVS_NONE` bevel, then set `BUTTON_Transparent` through `OM_SET` and render it again. `bd_Transparent` changes, but the existing bevel image retains its original value, so the interior continues to be erased/filled when transparency is enabled late, or remains unfilled when transparency is disabled late. The effect lasts until the bevel cache is otherwise discarded or the button is disposed. Applies to Reaction `button.gadget` with an active bevel image; a repository search found no checked-in dynamic setter caller, so current application impact is not established. **Confidence:** high for stale cached state and visual mismatch; public API reachability is conditional on clients changing the tag after initial render. No GUI or render was run; source-only.

## GD5524

**Reaction `button.gadget` accepts `BUTTON_AutoButton` but does not render the selected built-in glyph.** The public header defines `BAG_*` built-in glyph types and identifies `BUTTON_AutoButton` as their selector (`compiler/include/gadgets/button.h:43,66-78`). `button_set()` stores the value in `bd_AutoButton`, and `OM_GET` returns it (`workbench/classes/reaction/button/buttonclass.c:54-56,274-276`), but the render path draws only `bd_Glyph` (`:420-427`). A complete implementation search finds no use of `bd_AutoButton` outside its store/get path and no mapping from the `BAG_*` values to images.

**Trigger and consequence:** Create a Reaction button with `BUTTON_AutoButton` set to a defined glyph type, then render it. The value is retained and queryable, but no glyph is drawn unless the caller separately supplies `BUTTON_Glyph` or `GA_Image`. The checked-in OpenURL preferences source uses `BAG_UPARROW` and `BAG_DNARROW` for four list-reordering buttons (`external/openurl/raPrefs/OpenURL.c:224-233,278-287,329-338`), so those controls lack their requested arrows when using this implementation. **Confidence:** high that the tag is accepted but ignored by rendering; the specific OpenURL visual effect depends on that optional external target using this class at runtime. No GUI render was run; source-only.

## GD5525

**Reaction `button.gadget` disposes `BUTTON_Glyph` as a BOOPSI object even though the public tag accepts a plain `struct Image *`.** The public declaration describes `BUTTON_Glyph` as a single-plane `struct Image *` (`compiler/include/gadgets/button.h:30`). `button_set()` stores the supplied pointer (`workbench/classes/reaction/button/buttonclass.c:51-53`), and `Button__OM_DISPOSE()` unconditionally passes it to `DisposeObject()` (`:227-244`). `DisposeObject()` dispatches `OM_DISPOSE` on the supplied pointer; it does not free an ordinary Image allocation according to its type (`rom/intuition/disposeobject.c:57-65`). The button also draws the pointer as an `Image` through `DrawImageState()` (`buttonclass.c:420-427`).

**Trigger and consequence:** Give a button a valid caller-owned or statically allocated classic `struct Image` through `BUTTON_Glyph`, then dispose the button. The class dispatches a BOOPSI dispose method against storage that the API does not require to be a BOOPSI object; this can fault or corrupt memory, and violates the normal caller ownership of a plain Image. Passing a BOOPSI image object may happen to be compatible, but the documented type does not require one. The checkout contains no direct `BUTTON_Glyph` caller, so reachability is through external clients. **Confidence:** high for the ownership/type mismatch; exact failure depends on the supplied Image storage and adjacent object-dispatch state. No object was created or disposed; source-only.

## GD5526

**Picture layout frees the source even when it cannot create the transparency mask.** With `PDTA_FreeSourceBitMap` enabled, `DT_AsyncLayout()` calls `CreateMaskPlane()` and discards its Boolean result, then unconditionally calls `FreeSource()` and marks the layout complete (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1003-1012`). For transparent-color images, `CreateMaskPlane()` returns FALSE if the mask allocation fails, the source pixel format is not one byte per pixel, or scaling is active (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/colorhandling.c:579-603`). `FreeSource()` releases and clears `SrcBuffer` (`:396-409`). A later `PDTA_MaskPlane` query retries mask creation, but cannot succeed without `SrcBuffer` (`pictureclass.c:464-467`; `colorhandling.c:579-585`).

**Trigger and consequence:** Layout an image whose BMHD says `mskHasTransparentColor` with `PDTA_FreeSourceBitMap=TRUE`, then encounter mask allocation failure or a mask-ineligible configuration such as non-1:1 scaling. Layout still sets `Layouted=TRUE`; the source is gone and the mask remains NULL. The selected `render_on_rastport()` recognizes the transparent-color BMHD, queries the mask, and draws nothing when it is NULL instead of taking the opaque-blit branch (`pictureclass.c:630-648`). Thus the object can report successful layout but later render no image; retrying mask creation cannot recover it. The public `PDTA_FreeSourceBitMap` setter enables this behavior (`pictureclass.c:326-328`); a maintained Wanderer background caller explicitly requests source release and scales before layout (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindowbackfill.c:471-485`), though that caller consumes the resulting bitmap directly and does not itself establish the masked-render consequence. **Confidence:** high for unconditional source release and NULL-mask rendering; actual mask failure depends on allocation or the selected source/scaling configuration. No datatype layout or render was run; source-only.

## GD5527

**Picture datatype rendering drops alpha on destinations shallower than 15 bits.** The PNG datatype marks RGBA/gray-alpha images as `mskHasAlpha` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/png/pngclass.c:388-399`). During Picture layout to a low-depth screen, `DT_AsyncLayout()` selects the colormapped conversion path (`pictureclass.c:935-947,974-981`); `RemapTC2CM()` skips the alpha byte while remapping RGB into the destination bitmap (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/colorhandling.c:699-702,747-771`). At render time, `render_on_rastport()` uses `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` only when destination depth is at least 15 (`pictureclass.c:609-627`). For shallower targets, its mask branch recognizes only `mskHasMask` and `mskHasTransparentColor`, not `mskHasAlpha`, then falls through to `BltBitMapRastPort()` (`:628-660`). The converted bitmap therefore has no alpha information for that opaque blit.

**Trigger and consequence:** Render a PNG or other truecolor alpha Picture object onto a destination bitmap below 15 bits. Partially and fully transparent pixels are written as ordinary colormapped RGB pixels rather than composited over the destination; transparent regions overwrite what was behind them. This applies to the build-selected Picture datatype and to PNG alpha inputs when the optional `workbench-datatypes-png` target is included (its aggregate edge is commented out in `workbench/classes/datatypes/png/mmakefile.src:4-14`). The behavior is in the public Picture render path (`DT_Render()` and `DTM_DRAW`, `pictureclass.c:667-716,2190`). **Confidence:** high for alpha-byte omission and the low-depth opaque-blit path; exact visual output depends on input alpha and destination contents. No image was decoded or rendered; source-only.

## GD5528

**PNG palette import treats the sole partially transparent palette entry as fully transparent.** The decoder counts entries whose tRNS alpha is not 255 only when `num_trans > 1`; it converts the palette to RGBA only when that count exceeds one (`workbench/classes/datatypes/png/pngclass.c:293-317`). Later, any palette tRNS table with at least one entry is represented in the Picture BMHD as `mskHasTransparentColor`, and `bmh_Transparent` is set to the first entry whose alpha is not 255 (`:417-440`). Picture's mask builder then compares palette indices for equality with that value, producing a binary transparent/opaque mask (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/colorhandling.c:586-629`). The mask renderer uses that binary mask (`pictureclass.c:630-647`).

**Trigger and consequence:** Load a palette PNG with exactly one non-opaque tRNS entry whose alpha is between 1 and 254, and render it through Picture. Because the decoder does not convert the single-entry palette to RGBA, the selected palette index becomes fully transparent in the generated mask; its partial opacity is lost. The maintained MUI `GetImageFromFile()` path loads Picture objects, checks their BMHD, and obtains `PDTA_MaskPlane` for the screen-backed bitmap (`workbench/libs/muimaster/datatypescache.c:377-440,173-234`); its image renderer uses that mask (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/image.c:503-505`). The PNG module manifest does not define `PNGDATATYPE_ALWAYS_ARGB`, so the palette-preserving path above is the selected default; a build defining that macro takes a different conversion path. Applies to the PNG datatype target and Picture mask path; the active `workbench-datatypes-complete` aggregate includes PNG, and `workbench-classes-complete` selects that aggregate (`workbench/classes/datatypes/mmakefile:4-20`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/png/mmakefile.src:6-14`; `workbench/classes/mmakefile:4-6`). **Confidence:** high for the partial-alpha-to-binary-mask conversion; visible blending depends on the caller rendering over a nonuniform background. No PNG was decoded or rendered; source-only.

## GD5529

**PNG direct-access retains all unknown chunks when the caller requests selected chunk types.** When `chunkstoread` is non-NULL, `PNG_LoadImageInternal()` first calls `png_set_keep_unknown_chunks(png_ptr, 3, 0, 0)` and then adds each requested type (`workbench/classes/datatypes/png/directaccess.c:218-241`). The selected libpng target is 1.6.58 (`workbench/libs/png/mmakefile.src:3-5`). In libpng's API, `3` is `PNG_HANDLE_CHUNK_ALWAYS`, and `num_chunks == 0` sets the default for all unknown chunks; the subsequent positive-count calls only set per-type policy. The [libpng manual](https://github.com/pnggroup/libpng/blob/libpng18/manuals/libpng-manual.txt) documents that this retains unknown chunks as raw data. After `png_read_end()`, the loader copies only names present in `chunkstoread` into caller storage, then destroys libpng's read structures (`directaccess.c:390-455`).

**Trigger and consequence:** Call a PNG direct-access entry point with a non-NULL list of desired chunk names and decode a file containing other unknown chunks. Libpng allocates and retains every unknown chunk during parsing, even though the wrapper later copies out only the requested types. The extra data remains allocated until `png_destroy_read_struct()` and can raise peak memory use or cause an otherwise unnecessary allocation failure for files with large or numerous unrequested chunks; it is not returned persistently to the caller. The maintained icon reader requests only `icOn` for the first embedded PNG (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjPNGio.c:317-328,363-367`), so unrelated unknown chunks in that image exercise the extra retention path. Applies when the separately buildable PNG datatype and libpng 1.6.58 target are included. **Confidence:** high for the all-unknown retention setting and selection-only copy-out; practical impact depends on unknown-chunk volume and available memory. No PNG was decoded; source-only.

## GD5532

**Workbench WindowDecor dereferences a NULL per-window buffer for standalone directional system images.** `SysIClass__IM_DRAW()` builds `wdp_UserBuffer` as zero when its RastPort has no layer window (`rom/intuition/sysiclass.c:388-411`). For `LEFTIMAGE`, `UPIMAGE`, `RIGHTIMAGE`, and `DOWNIMAGE`, ordinary rendering (neither `SYSIFLG_NOBORDER` nor `SYSIFLG_GADTOOLS`) dispatches `WDM_DRAW_SYSIMAGE` to the screen's window decorator (`sysiclass.c:571-579,675-683,780-788,886-894`). The selected Workbench `windowdecorclass` handles that method in `windecor_dispatch()` (`workbench/c/Decoration/windowdecorclass.c:2033-2034`). `windecor_draw_sysimage()` maps these four types without setting `checkok`, then immediately evaluates `&wd->dts->dts_Elements[elemid]`; its later `if (wd && ...)` guard occurs only after this dereference (`windowdecorclass.c:791-792,851-866,878-885`).

**Trigger and consequence:** Draw one of those four system images through `DrawImage()` using a RastPort with no `Layer->Window`, with the standard decorated rendering flags. The caller supplies a NULL per-window user buffer, and the Workbench decorator dereferences it before rendering, causing a NULL-pointer fault. This is conditional on the Workbench WindowDecor class being selected for the screen and the image taking the decorated system-image path; no claim is made for GadTools, no-border rendering, or RastPorts associated with windows. **Confidence:** high for the source-level NULL dereference and dispatch conditions. The caller and class paths were traced; no draw was run, so this is a source-only candidate.

## GD5534

**Reaction button.gadget mishandles the documented `BUTTON_TextPen` sentinel and cannot select pen 0.** The public tag is a `LONG` and documents `-1` as the default `TEXTPEN` value (`compiler/include/gadgets/button.h:31`). `button_set()` casts the tag value to `UWORD` (`workbench/classes/reaction/button/buttonclass.c:71-72`), and rendering treats any nonzero `bd_TextPen` as the literal pen index; zero instead selects state/prefs/default pen logic (`buttonclass.c:355-365`). Thus the documented `-1` becomes 65535 and is sent to `SetAPen()`, while explicit pen 0 cannot be requested. The class data is zero initialized by the BOOPSI instance allocation, preserving default selection when the tag is omitted.

**Trigger and consequence:** Create or update a Reaction button with `BUTTON_TextPen` set to its documented `-1` sentinel, or set it to `0` intending pen 0, and draw text on a RastPort. The sentinel is used as pen 65535 rather than `TEXTPEN`; explicit zero falls through to the class's default pen selection. The exact visible result of an out-of-range pen depends on graphics implementation and color-map depth; the API-level pen selection is incorrect. A repository search found no maintained in-tree use of this tag, so the issue is limited to external/public API clients. **Confidence:** high for cast, branch, and documented contract mismatch; no button was rendered, source-only.

## GD5535

**Reaction button.gadget accepts text style, fill/background pen, and text-padding tags without applying them.** `button_set()` stores `BUTTON_SoftStyle`, `BUTTON_BackgroundPen`, `BUTTON_FillTextPen`, and `BUTTON_FillPen`, but the selected class's rendering path does not read those fields. For `BUTTON_TextPadding`, the setter explicitly does nothing (`workbench/classes/reaction/button/buttonclass.c:45-46,68-81`; stored fields in `button_intern.h:42-49`). The header declares the tags, though unlike the pen tags it gives no further behavioral comments (`compiler/include/gadgets/button.h:32-33,42,53`). Text rendering uses its own state/prefs/default selection and the bevel image handles the frame/fill (`buttonclass.c:337-365`).

**Trigger and consequence:** Pass any of these tags to a Reaction button and draw it. Text style and the fill/background color choices do not affect output, and enabling text padding has no effect. This is limited to clients that expect these declared attributes to configure the button; no maintained in-tree caller was found. Because the header provides no contract detail for `BUTTON_TextPadding` and `BUTTON_SoftStyle`, those two are weaker compatibility candidates than the explicitly typed pen attributes. **Confidence:** high that the class accepts but does not consume the values; intended compatibility is uncertain for tags without documented semantics. No button was rendered, source-only.

## GD5536

**Reaction button.gadget declares integer, bitmap, and animation attributes that the class does not implement.** The public header groups `BUTTON_Integer`, `BUTTON_BitMap`, and the `BUTTON_Anim*` tags under “Additional attributes defined by the button.gadget class,” with types indicating a numeric value, bitmap, animation enablement, image arrays, frame count, and frame index/adjustment (`compiler/include/gadgets/button.h:25-26,46-56`). The selected `ButtonData` has no corresponding fields (`workbench/classes/reaction/button/button_intern.h:33-54`), and neither `button_set()` nor the render method handles those tags (`buttonclass.c:35-85,337-431`). As a result, creation/update tags are ignored and cannot configure those declared features.

**Trigger and consequence:** Supply one of these attributes when creating or updating a Reaction button and expect the named numeric, bitmap, or animation behavior. The class does not retain or act on the supplied value. No maintained in-tree user of these tags was found. The header does not define finer behavior (for example, bitmap ownership or frame-update rules), so this is retained as a qualified public-interface completeness/compatibility candidate rather than a claim about those unspecified details. **Confidence:** high that the selected class ignores the declared attributes; uncertain whether every declaration is intended to be supported by this implementation. No gadget operation was run, source-only.

## GD5538

**MUI Window render info leaves `MPEN_MARK` at pen 0, so mark-pattern presets use the wrong foreground.** The MUI default pen table assigns `MPEN_MARK` the system `HIGHLIGHTTEXTPEN` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/muimaster_init-aros.c:84-86`; enum in `mui.h:276`). Window setup calls `InitRenderInfoPens()`, which obtains and stores the other pens but has no assignment for `MPEN_MARK`, then publishes `mri_PensStorage` as `mri_Pens` (`classes/window.c:368-409,517`). The window class instance pool is created with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`rom/intuition/newobjecta.c:108-115`), and the `MUI_RenderInfo` is embedded in that instance (`classes/window.c:80`), so the omitted slot remains zero. Pattern rendering uses `mri_Pens[MPEN_MARK]` as the foreground for `MUII_MARKSHINE`, `MUII_MARKHALFSHINE`, and `MUII_MARKBACKGROUND` (`imspec.c:80-82,792-798`).

**Trigger and consequence:** Open a MUI window whose background uses one of those three mark-pattern presets. The pattern renderer selects pen 0 for the foreground instead of the configured `HIGHLIGHTTEXTPEN`, changing the pattern's appearance. Other image patterns do not use `MPEN_MARK`. This affects the selected MUI implementation independent of screen depth, though the visible color depends on the screen's pen mapping. **Confidence:** high for the initialized default, missing render-info assignment, and three pattern consumers; no window was opened or drawn, source-only.

## GD5539

**MUIMaster can leave its preference-created custom screen open when the Application is disposed.** When a window has no explicit screen and the app preference contains a screen mode ID, `SetupRenderInfo()` opens and stores a shared `mgi_CustomScreen` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:420-440`). During `Application__OM_DISPOSE()`, each child window is removed via `OM_REMMEMBER` before it is disposed (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:847-870`). `Application__OM_REMMEMBER()` first calls `MUIM_DisconnectParent()` and only afterward removes the window from `app_WindowFamily` (`application.c:1455-1466`). The window disconnect closes an open window (`window.c:3595-3615`), leading through `WindowClose()` to `MUIM_Window_Cleanup()` (`window.c:3840-3869`). `CleanupRenderInfo()` checks `MUIA_Application_WindowList` at that point; because the last window is still listed, it does not close `mgi_CustomScreen` (`window.c:652-676`). After the list removal and child disposal, `Application__OM_DISPOSE()` has no custom-screen close path (`application.c:847-1030`).

**Trigger and consequence:** Configure a MUI application with a non-default screen mode preference, let its window open on the preference-created custom screen, then dispose the application while the window remains in its window family. Closing that final window during disposal runs cleanup before it is removed from the list, so the cleanup retains the custom screen; disposing the application then discards the global-info owner without closing it. The screen remains open after the application and window are gone. This applies to the path where MUIMaster itself opened the screen; caller-supplied screens are not included. **Confidence:** high for the source ordering and missing final close; no application was run or screen opened, source-only.

## GD5580 — failed Group setup leaves its Area event handler linked for a retry

A Group's `MUIM_Setup` first calls the Area superclass setup, which installs the Area event handler when input mode or context-menu handling is enabled and sets `MADF_SETUP` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.c:1565-1568,1589`). Group then sets up its children. If one child fails, it cleans previously successful siblings and returns `FALSE`, but does not clean up the Group object itself (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:1027-1069`). `WindowOpen()` responds to root setup failure by calling `MUIM_Window_Cleanup`, whose implementation cleans Window render/background resources but does not call `MUIM_Cleanup` on the root object (`window.c:3767-3772,4046-4059`).

The Area event-handler node therefore remains linked in the Window's `wd_EHList`. `WindowOpen()` retry runs Group/Area setup again, and Area calls `MUIM_Window_AddEventHandler` with that same embedded node. The Window method unconditionally reinserts it via `EnqueueByPriAndAddress()` (`window.c:273-293,3994-4005`); no duplicate-membership check or prior removal occurs.

**Trigger:** A Window root Group (or a nested Group whose failed setup propagates to the root) has an Area input handler registered, a child `MUIM_Setup` returns `FALSE`, and the caller retries opening the Window without first successfully cleaning the failed root tree.

**Effect:** Setup bookkeeping and event-handler membership remain from the failed attempt. Re-inserting the same list node can corrupt the Window handler list; later event traversal or removal then operates on damaged links. Groups without an Area event handler, and failed setup without a retry, do not reach this duplicate-insertion path.

**Confidence:** High for the missing cleanup and duplicate insertion path under the stated conditions. The resulting list-link corruption follows from reinserting an already-linked intrusive node; no failed setup or retry was induced. Source-only.

## GD5589 — MUI retains a replied AppMessage pointer in a get-only attribute

For each AppWindow message, the Application input loop passes the `AppMessage *` to the target object through `MUIA_AppMessage` and then immediately calls `ReplyMsg()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1816-1823`). Notify's `OM_SET` stores that pointer in per-object attribute data, while `OM_GET` returns the stored pointer without clearing it (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/notify.c:409-415,465-481`). The message is owned by the AppWindow sender again after reply, so it may be reused or freed while the MUI object continues to expose the old address.

**Trigger:** A client queries `MUIA_AppMessage` after the synchronous notification dispatch has returned, or otherwise retains the returned pointer beyond the AppWindow message callback/reply.

**Effect:** The attribute can return a pointer to a message whose lifetime has ended; dereferencing it can observe reused contents or invalid storage. The selected in-tree consumer, ImageAdjust's AppMessage hook, receives the pointer during synchronous notification and therefore does not establish a late-query path (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/imageadjust.c:64-72,709-718`). This finding is limited to clients that query or retain the get-only attribute after dispatch.

**Confidence:** High for pointer retention and reply ordering; external-client dependent for an invalid dereference. Source-only; no AppMessage was delivered or retained at runtime.
