## GD5689 — QuickPart loses free-space nodes when ranges merge

`QPPartitionContainer__MUIM_QPart_ccPartitionContainer_AddFree()` updates an existing free node and sets `addFree`/`addObj` false when the incoming range overlaps or meets it; after that it neither links the incoming `FSNode` nor adds its child object to the MUI group (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:362-414`). The selected Delete action allocates a new node and child object, then passes them to this method (`QP_ccApp.c:416-441`). On a successful merge, neither allocation is freed or transferred, so the bookkeeping node leaks and a successfully created child object is left unattached and undisposed.

There is also a selected partition-scan consequence. `AddPart()` can mark the initial free-space node for deletion when a partition starts fewer than 512 sectors after the container start (`QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:245-277,267-270`). If at least 512 sectors remain after the partition, it creates a trailing spacer and passes it to `AddFree()` before removing the marked node (`:273-277,353-356`). Because `AddFree()` does not skip `PCCN_Delete` nodes, it merges the trailing spacer into the still-linked initial node, then `AddPart()` removes that node. The incoming trailing spacer was not linked, so the free tail disappears from QuickPart's list and display; the new spacer allocations are also left without disposal. This occurs during the selected partition-table scan, before user edits.

A separate failure case remains qualified: if the child `NewObject()` in the Delete action returns NULL and the range does not merge, `AddFree()` stores the node and calls `OM_ADDMEMBER` with a NULL child (`QP_ccApp.c:422-441`; `QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:405-412`). The model/UI divergence is direct, but MUI's handling of that call is not established here.

**Trigger and consequence:** in QuickPart, either delete a partition whose freed range meets an existing free node (temporary node/child leak), or scan a table whose partition begins fewer than 512 sectors from the container start and leaves at least 512 sectors at the tail (the marked initial free node is removed after absorbing the tail spacer, so the tail is no longer represented). **Affected configuration:** the `AROS` Workbench aggregate selects `workbench-tools`, whose active MetaMake dependency includes `workbench-tools-quickpart` (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`). **Confidence:** high for the merge-time leaks and for the scan-path lost-tail state; practical scan trigger depends on partition geometry. Skip nodes marked for deletion and either transfer or dispose of incoming node/object ownership on every merge. No GUI, partition table, allocation failure or delete operation was run; source-only.
## GD5690

**Indexed summary:** Zune Preferences Save As can overflow its filename buffer when appending `.prefs` to a near-maximum selected path.

**Source and trigger:** The selected Zune Preferences target includes `zune.c` (`workbench/prefs/Zune/mmakefile.src`). Its Save As hook calls `aslfilerequest()` with a static 1,000-byte `filename` buffer, then appends the six-character suffix plus NUL using unbounded `strcat()` whenever the chosen full path does not contain the substring `.prefs` (`workbench/prefs/Zune/zune.c:711-724`). The helper copies up to 498 bytes each for directory and filename and calls `AddPart(fullname, filepart, 998)` into that same 1,000-byte destination (`workbench/prefs/Zune/zunestuff.c:21-29,47-52`). A selected path that fills the helper's permitted output length and lacks `.prefs` therefore exceeds the destination when the suffix is appended, writing beyond `filename`; the append happens before the `configdata` NULL check. **Confidence: high** for the bounds mismatch: the selected `AddPart()` implementation accepts outputs up to 997 path characters plus NUL when called with size 998 (`rom/dos/addpart.c:119-143`), while appending `.prefs` needs seven additional bytes including NUL. The exact requester interaction was not run. The suffix test also accepts `.prefs` anywhere in the path, but that is separate from this bounds finding.

**Review state:** Re-established from the selected Save As hook and helper's explicit output-length contract. Source-only; no file requester or save operation was run.

## GD5692

**Indexed summary:** BoingIconBar can discard remapped icon images when its first screen lock fails but window creation succeeds (conditional placeholder icons after a screen transition; medium source confidence).

**Source and trigger:** `ReadPrefs()` first locks the public screen and calls `LayoutIcon()` on loaded icons while that lock is valid, then unlocks it (`workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/iconbar.c:767,820-837,863-867`). `OpenMainWindow()` performs a separate `LockPubScreen(NULL)` attempt (`:1405`). If this second attempt fails, its result leaves `MyScreen` NULL; with `Icon_Remap` enabled, it still passes that NULL to `LayoutIcon()` for every current icon (`:1497-1505`). In the selected icon library implementation, `LayoutIconA()` frees each image's cached bitmap/remap resources, clears `ni_Screen`, and returns TRUE for a NULL screen (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:97-129`). `OpenMainWindow()` then independently calls `OpenWindowTags()` with `WA_PubScreenName, NULL` (`iconbar.c:1508-1518`). The selected `OpenWindow()` implementation performs another `LockPubScreen(pubScreenName)` for that tag and fails only if this separate attempt also lacks a screen (`rom/intuition/openwindow.c:581-603,640-643`); therefore a transient availability change between these calls can let the window open after the earlier failed lock has discarded the screen-specific icon caches. The window-open path does not remap icons again before drawing them (`iconbar.c:1541-1555`). The screen-reset restore caller also runs `ReadPrefs()` before `OpenMainWindow()` (`:1877-1891`), so it contains the same two-attempt sequence. **Affected configuration:** `AUTOREMAP`/`Icon_Remap` enabled; `ReadPrefs()` maps icons successfully, the subsequent `OpenMainWindow()` lock fails, but its later `OpenWindowTags()` lock succeeds. **Consequence:** toolbar icon rendering can lack the cached screen-specific remapped imagery until a later successful `OpenMainWindow()` remaps it. **Confidence: medium-high** for the separate lock attempts and cache invalidation; the necessary transient interleaving and visual result were not reproduced.

**Review state:** Candidate re-established from selected source and its screen-reset caller. Source-only; no screen transition or rendering was run.

<a id="gd5694"></a>
## GD5694 — MUI Window snapshot leaves alternate Y uninitialized before config serialization

**Source and trigger:** `Window__MUIM_Snapshot()` initializes the window ID, current geometry, alternate X, alternate width, and alternate height, but assigns `winp.x2 = 0` twice and never assigns `winp.y2` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:4444-4469`). It passes the automatic `struct windowpos winp` to `MUIA_Application_SetWinPos`. `Application__OM_SET()` copies all eight coordinate fields, including `y2`, into the application's saved window-position array (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1024-1060`). When configdata saves window positions, it obtains the array and byte count and copies that range into the dataspace with `MUIM_Dataspace_Add()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:884-906`); the record size includes the uninitialized field (`application.c:1273-1290`). Thus an MUI application that snapshots an open window and subsequently saves its configdata serializes the indeterminate 16-bit `y2` value. **Affected configuration:** MUI applications using window snapshot and configdata persistence. **Consequence:** the saved window-position record contains a nondeterministic alternate-Y word; current restore reads only `x1/y1/w1/h1` (`window.c:824-841`), so no live-window geometry consequence from `y2` is established. Initialize `winp.y2` (and retain the intended alternate-dimension semantics) before storing the record. **Confidence:** high for the uninitialized assignment and copy-to-dataspace path; no config save was run.

**Review state:** Rechecked the complete value flow from snapshot through application storage to dataspace serialization and compared it with restore reads. Source-only; no MUI application or config save was exercised.

## GD5695

**Indexed summary:** StartDragSelect can miss an asynchronous-layout startup and report success while the layout process is active.

**Source and trigger:** `StartDragSelect()` checks `DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC` and sets `DTSIF_DRAGSELECT` while holding the object's `si_Lock` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/startdragselect.c:74-84`). `DoAsyncLayout()` instead acquires the library-wide `SEM_ASYNC`, then sets `DTSIF_LAYOUT | DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC` without acquiring that object lock (`workbench/libs/datatypes/doasynclayout.c:152-174`). If the two public operations overlap and layout sets its flags after StartDragSelect's check, StartDragSelect returns TRUE despite the layout process having started. The async worker later waits for `si_Lock` before executing the layout method (`doasynclayout.c:48-56`), so the operations use different locks for the check/publication boundary.

**Consequence and scope:** A caller can be told drag selection started while an asynchronous layout is queued or active, despite the API's documented requirement that selection only start when no layout process is working. This can leave selection enabled during geometry updates. The checked-in MultiView caller invokes StartDragSelect from its Mark menu (`workbench/utilities/MultiView/main.c:1568-1587`), and selected ASCII layout uses DoAsyncLayout (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/asciiclass.c:165-181`), but no checked-in execution path establishes that those calls overlap across tasks. Treat the interleaving as a conditional API-level race, medium confidence; no schedule or GUI operation was exercised.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), StartDragSelect/DoAsyncLayout locking recheck dated 2026-10-24.

<a id="gd5696"></a>
## GD5696 — AmigaGuide can miss a resize at asynchronous layout completion

**Source and trigger:** In the external AmigaGuide process path, `AGMT_LAYOUT` holds the outer gadget's `si_Lock`, clears `DTSIF_NEWSIZE`, performs `DTM_ASYNCLAYOUT`, checks `DTSIF_NEWSIZE`, and exits the loop when it is clear; it then clears `DTSIF_LAYOUT` before releasing `si_Lock` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/process.c:268-286`). The resize path in `GM_LAYOUT` instead holds `ag_ASyncLayout`: when it sees `DTSIF_LAYOUT`, it sets `DTSIF_NEWSIZE` and signals the worker, otherwise it queues a layout and sets `DTSIF_LAYOUT` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/amigaguideclass.c:614-636`). The worker does not acquire `ag_ASyncLayout` around its final NEWSIZE check and LAYOUT clear. If a resize reaches the worker after its final clear check but before its `DTSIF_LAYOUT` clear, the resize sets NEWSIZE and is treated as covered by the running worker, but that worker does not loop again. The resize's dimensions can therefore lack a completed layout/viewport-metric refresh until a later layout request. `dtm_asynclayout()` derives visible and total viewport metrics from the current domain and content attributes (`amigaguideclass.c:844-953`). **Affected configuration:** AmigaGuide datatype objects using the external asynchronous layout process and receiving a resize in this narrow completion interval. **Consequence:** viewport metrics and scrollbar state can remain based on the earlier layout until another layout occurs. The existence of the unsynchronized check/update window is supported by source; actual resize timing and user-visible duration were not reproduced. **Confidence:** medium-high for the flag protocol and missed-update interleaving; runtime scheduling and UI effect remain unverified.

**Review state:** Rechecked the producer, worker loop and metric publication path, including the distinct semaphores protecting resize submission and worker execution. Source-only; no layout or resize was run.

<a id="gd5698"></a>
## GD5698 — failed Intuition opens overwrite timer setup resources on retry

**Source and trigger:** `IntuitionOpen()` performs timer setup only while `TimerBase` is NULL. It assigns a newly created port directly to `TimerMP`, then an `IORequest` directly to `TimerIO`, and returns FALSE if port creation, request creation, or `OpenDevice(TIMERNAME, UNIT_VBLANK, ...)` fails (`rom/intuition/intuition_init.c:427-449`). These failure returns do not delete the new request or port, close a partially opened device, or clear the fields. Exec `OpenLibrary()` returns the result of the library open vector directly (`rom/exec/openlibrary.c:89-99`); a NULL result does not invoke `CloseLibrary()`. A later `OpenLibrary("intuition.library", ...)` retry enters the same `!TimerBase` block and overwrites those fields with newly allocated resources. Repeated failures can therefore strand earlier ports and requests; a failure followed by success also leaves the failed attempt's resources unreachable through the stored pointers. **Affected configuration:** Intuition library open attempts that reach timer initialization after earlier open stages succeeded and encounter timer setup failure, with a subsequent retry. **Consequence:** allocated timer message ports and I/O requests from failed attempts are leaked; timer-device failure itself does not establish an open device handle, while any failure after a successful open would also need a matching close. Free/clear partial resources on each failure path before allowing retry. **Confidence:** high for the missing local cleanup and overwrite sequence; no allocation/device failure or retry was induced.

**Review state:** Rechecked the complete timer setup block and its retry guard; `TimerBase` is assigned only after `OpenDevice()` succeeds, so each earlier failure leaves retries enabled. Source-only.

## GD5701 — withdrawn: unselected Nouveau HIDD and unsupported I²C slave feature

The Nouveau HIDD is not selected by the current checkout's active package manifests: the only references to `workbench-hidds-nouveau` in the top-level and PC driver metatarget files are commented-out entries (`workbench/mmakefile.src:41`; `arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:10`; `arch/all-pc/mmakefile.src:8-12`). Its own manifest exposes the target but defines it through optional `#MM` metarules (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:22-28`). The source-level behavior also documents the unsupported case: `i2c_new_client_device()` unconditionally returns `ERR_PTR(-ENODEV)` with the comment “no slave drivers exist here” (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_i2c.c:196-200`). The GF4 TMDS-slave probe calls `nouveau_i2c_encoder_init()` without checking its result (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/dispnv04/dfp.c:625-654`), but the candidate did not establish a defect in a selected configuration or a contract requiring off-chip slave-encoder support. Withdrawn from the active findings index; retained here as an out-of-scope/unsupported-feature disposition, not a confirmed bug. Source-only; no hardware or display operation was run.

<a id="gd5702"></a>
## GD5702 — IControl USE/SAVE truncates preference files and discards export errors

**Source and trigger:** In command-line `USE` or `SAVE`, `Prefs_HandleArgs()` opens `ENV:Sys/IControl.prefs` with `MODE_NEWFILE` before calling `Prefs_ExportFH()`; `SAVE` does the same for `ENVARC:Sys/IControl.prefs` (`workbench/prefs/icontrol/prefs.c:258-282`). `MODE_NEWFILE` creates or truncates the target. The exporter initializes `retval` to FALSE and sets it TRUE only after writing the PRHD and ICTL chunk payloads completely; allocation, IFF setup/push, and short/failed `WriteChunkBytes()` paths leave it FALSE (`prefs.c:132-216`). The IFF API returns negative errors or the positive byte count written (`workbench/libs/iffparse/writechunkbytes.c:32-55`), and IControl treats short writes as failure. However, `Prefs_HandleArgs()` ignores both exporter results, closes each handle, and returns TRUE (`prefs.c:260-284`); `main()` also discards the handler result (`workbench/prefs/icontrol/main.c:34-39`). **Affected configuration:** IControl command-line `USE` or `SAVE` when an export allocation or IFF/DOS write fails after the destination has been opened. **Consequence:** the prior preferences file has already been truncated and can be left empty or partial, while the CLI reports no export failure; `SAVE` can additionally leave ENV and ENVARC copies inconsistent if only one export succeeds. Export to a temporary file and replace the destination only on complete success, and propagate/report the failure. **Confidence:** high for truncation-before-export and discarded error status; no I/O failure was induced. The interactive PrefsEditor export path is separate and returns `Prefs_ExportFH()`'s Boolean to its caller.

**Review state:** Rechecked the command-line caller, file-open modes, exporter return conditions, IFF short-write semantics, and separate interactive caller. Source-only; no preference file was written.

<a id="gd5703"></a>
## GD5703 — IControl leaks the prior current-directory lock on Workbench icon-read failure

**Source and trigger:** When launched from Workbench with more than one startup argument, `ReadArguments()` advances to the dropped-file argument, switches the process directory to `wa_Lock`, and stores the prior directory lock returned by `CurrentDir()` in static `olddir` (`workbench/prefs/icontrol/args.c:28-42`). If `GetDiskObject(wa_Name)` fails, it displays an error and falls through to return FALSE (`args.c:61-73`). `main()` calls `FreeArguments()` only inside the `if (ReadArguments(...))` branch (`workbench/prefs/icontrol/main.c:34-72`), so this failure bypasses the routine that restores `olddir` (`args.c:76-80`). DOS process teardown unlocks the process's current directory (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:964-965`), which is the Workbench argument directory after the change; that does not release the separate saved prior lock. **Affected configuration:** Workbench launch with `sm_NumArgs > 1`, a nonzero `wa_Lock`, nonempty `wa_Name`, and an unreadable/missing DiskObject for the dropped path. **Consequence:** the original current-directory lock is left unreleased when IControl exits. Restore the old directory on every path after `CurrentDir()` succeeds, including the icon-read error path. **Confidence:** high for the missing cleanup path and distinct lock ownership; no Workbench drop or failing icon read was run.

**Review state:** Traced `CurrentDir()`'s return contract and process teardown's current-directory unlock against the IControl caller and early return. Source-only.

<a id="gd5707"></a>
## GD5707 — Picture datatype source-buffer size wraps before PNG scanline copies

**Source and trigger:** `AllocSrcBuffer()` rounds the chunky row stride to 16 bytes with `MOD16(width * pixelbytes)` and allocates `SrcWidthBytes * height` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/colorhandling.c:316-331`). On 32-bit builds, `ULONG` and `IPTR` are 32-bit. For a PNG with width 65,535, height 16,385, and RGBA output (`pixelbytes == 4`), the aligned stride is 262,144 bytes and the product is `2^32 + 262,144`, which wraps to 262,144 for `AllocVec()`. The dimensions fit the Picture `BitMapHeader`'s UWORD width and height fields. The selected PNG decoder sets those header fields from IHDR (`workbench/classes/datatypes/png/pngclass.c:245-260,413-415`), reads each scanline, and calls `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY` with the full PNG width and one row (`pngclass.c:515-538`). On the first row, `PDT_WritePixelArray()` allocates the wrapped source buffer and copies 262,140 bytes; on the next row it computes destination offset `SrcWidthBytes` and copies another 262,140 bytes beyond the 262,144-byte allocation, with no extent check (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1093-1150,1185-1207`). The i386 PC floppy package selects both `picture.datatype` and `png.datatype` (`arch/i386-pc/boot/floppy/mmakefile.src:55-60`). **Affected configuration:** 32-bit builds including these datatypes and loading an RGBA PNG with dimensions whose aligned row stride times height wraps to an undersized positive allocation; the dimensions above give a concrete arithmetic case. **Consequence:** subsequent decoded scanlines are copied outside the Picture source buffer, corrupting adjacent memory or faulting. Reject multiplication overflow before allocation and validate each requested pixel-array rectangle against the allocated source dimensions. **Confidence:** high for the 32-bit arithmetic, allocation extent and selected PNG caller; no image was loaded and allocator success for the 256 KiB request was not induced.

**Review state:** Traced PNG IHDR/header publication, transformation to four-byte RGBA rows, first and subsequent scanline calls, Picture buffer allocation and copy offsets, and the selected i386 floppy manifest. Source-only.

<a id="gd5708"></a>
## GD5708 — AreaEnd polygon fill can fail to terminate at WORD_MAX Y

**Source and trigger:** `AreaDraw()` stores signed `WORD` coordinates (`rom/graphics/areadraw.c:67-75`), so Y=32767 is representable. `AreaEnd()` derives inclusive bounds from the recorded vertices, verifies the TmpRas capacity, and calls `areafillpolygon()` (`rom/graphics/areaend.c:88-90,106-110,130-155,185-195`). Both polygon rasterization paths use an inclusive `WORD y <= bounds->MaxY` loop (`rom/graphics/areafill.c:118,151`). A minimal public-API trigger is `AreaMove(rp, 0, 32766)`, followed by `AreaDraw()` at `(1,32766)`, `(1,32767)`, and `(0,32767)`, then `AreaEnd()`. These coordinates survive `FIX_GFXCOORD` unchanged and close into a 2-pixel-wide, 2-row polygon. Its aligned TmpRas requirement is only four bytes, so a normal small scratch allocation passes `AreaEnd()`’s capacity check. The loop reaches 32767 and increments the `WORD` to 32768, which is out of range for the signed type. On the project's ordinary two's-complement narrowing behavior this becomes -32768, which still satisfies the inclusive comparison, so the loop cycles instead of returning. `AreaEnd()`'s subsequent `BltPattern()` is reached only after the rasterizer returns (`areaend.c:149-169`). **Affected configuration:** callers submitting an Area polygon with maximum Y=32767 and sufficient TmpRas; the manifestation depends on target/compiler narrowing behavior. **Consequence:** `AreaEnd()` can remain in polygon rasterization indefinitely and never blit the completed area. The earlier claim of writes beyond the planar destination bitmap is withdrawn; this path supports nontermination only. No maintained in-tree caller at this coordinate was found. **Confidence:** medium for the inclusive loop and two's-complement manifestation; no compiler-specific run or oversized AreaEnd call was performed.

**Review state:** Rechecked coordinate narrowing, AreaEnd bounds construction and TmpRas size gating, both inclusive loops, and the post-rasterization BltPattern call. Source-only.

<a id="gd5709"></a>
## GD5709 — OS 3.5 icon writer reports success when IFF chunk finalization fails

**Source and trigger:** For non-PNG native icons, `__WriteIcon_WB()` serializes through `WriteStruct()` and `IconDesc` (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:396-405`). The selected `ProcessIcon35()` hook passes the write-mode operation to `WriteIcon35()` and returns its Boolean (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjio.c:966-999`). `WriteImage35()` sets `ok = TRUE` after successful header/payload writes, calls `PopChunk(iff)` without checking its result, and returns `ok` (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobj35io.c:863-893`). `WriteIcon35()` sets its overall `ok` TRUE when image writers succeed, then ignores the final `PopChunk()` for the enclosing `FORM ICON` and returns that unchanged status (`:998-1015,1059-1068`). `PopChunk()` can fail while seeking to patch an unknown chunk size, writing that size, seeking back to the end, or writing an alignment byte (`workbench/libs/iffparse/popchunk.c:77-131`). `WriteStruct()` propagates the special hook result (`compiler/arossupport/writestruct.c:274-287`), so a TRUE from `WriteIcon35()` reaches `__WriteIcon_WB()` and `PutIconTagList()`. The `MyDOSStreamHandler` propagates short DOS writes and failed seeks as errors (`diskobj35io.c:71-78`). Thus a payload-complete write followed by a chunk-finalization failure can still return TRUE through `WriteIcon35()` and the selected `PutIconTagList()` caller. `PutIconTagList()` opens ordinary icon output with `MODE_NEWFILE` and uses the writer's Boolean as its success result (`workbench/libs/icon/puticontaglist.c:124-155`); the prior file may already be truncated/replaced by an incomplete IFF icon. **Affected configuration:** icon saves using the OS 3.5 IFF writer (non-PNG native icon data), where payload writes succeed but a later chunk seek/backpatch/pad/flush fails. **Consequence:** callers can be told the icon save succeeded even though the output IFF has incomplete chunk lengths or padding. Check and propagate every `PopChunk()` result before returning success. **Confidence:** high for the ignored return path and IFF failure modes; no seek/write failure or icon save was induced.

**Review state:** Rechecked the writer selection, stream handler error conversion, nested and outer chunk finalization, and `PutIconTagList()` result propagation. Source-only.

<a id="gd5710"></a>
## GD5710 — OS 3.5 icon serialization leaks its allocated IFFHandle

**Source and trigger:** `WriteIcon35()` returns early for missing native image data or preserved extra-image data. Otherwise, for a native icon with image/ARGB pixels and `ni_Extra.Size == 0`, it calls `AllocIFF()` and, if that allocation succeeds, initializes and opens the handle for IFF output (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobj35io.c:898-955`). Every path after this allocation falls through to `return ok` without calling either `CloseIFF()` or `FreeIFF()` (`diskobj35io.c:1059-1068`). The caller's `CloseIcon()` closes the DOS file but has no access to the lost IFF handle (`workbench/libs/icon/puticontaglist.c:124-155`). `AllocIFF()` allocates the internal `IFFHandle`/default context storage, and the IFFParse API documents `FreeIFF()` as releasing it (`workbench/libs/iffparse/allociff.c:20-31,48-54`; `freeiff.c:20-22,45-63`). **Affected configuration:** OS 3.5 IFF serialization of native icons with image or ARGB data when `ni_Extra.Size == 0` and `AllocIFF()` succeeds; preserved PNG/extra-data copy-through and no-image early returns do not enter this allocation path. **Consequence:** each such save retains the IFF handle and its associated context allocations for the process lifetime. Close the IFF stream state and free the handle on all post-allocation paths. **Confidence:** high for the unmatched allocation and absent cleanup; no icon save was run.

**Review state:** Compared the writer's complete post-allocation exits with the selected caller's DOS-file cleanup and IFFParse allocation/free implementations. This resource leak is distinct from GD5709, which concerns unchecked chunk-finalization status. Source-only.

<a id="gd5711"></a>
## GD5711 — short 32-bit .otag files trigger an out-of-bounds header read

**Source and trigger:** `OTAG_GetFile()` obtains the `.otag` file length `l`, allocates `sizeof(struct OTagList) + l`, and reads `l` bytes into the trailing `data` member (`workbench/libs/diskfont/bullet.c:85-107`; `OTagList` is two pointers followed by `ULONG data[1]` at `diskfont_intern.h:78-83`). On 32-bit builds, `sizeof(struct OTagList)` accounts for `data[0]` but not `data[1]`. For a 0–3 byte file, the later `otaglist->data[1]` comparison reads four bytes beginning at the end of or beyond the requested allocation (`bullet.c:109-112`). The first identifier comparison can already set `ok = FALSE`, but the second `if` executes independently, so the short-file case still performs the out-of-bounds read before `OTAG_KillFile()` rejects the list. Outline-font descriptors reach this loader through `ReadFontDescr()` when `ContentsID == OFCH_ID` (`workbench/libs/diskfont/af_fontdescr_io.c:72-95`). **Affected configuration:** 32-bit builds loading an outline-font descriptor whose companion `.otag` file is 0–3 bytes long. **Consequence:** the parser reads beyond the allocated tag buffer while rejecting the file; the read has undefined behavior and may fault, but no value corruption or later use is established. Reject files shorter than the two-word header before reading either word. **Confidence:** high for the allocation/layout boundary and unconditional second-word access; no short file was loaded.

**Review state:** Rechecked the 32-bit `OTagList` layout, allocation size, both header checks, and `ReadFontDescr()` caller. This is distinct from GD2819, which covers unbounded tag-pair scanning after the fixed header; no consolidation is needed. Source-only.

## GD5712

**Indexed summary:** A `.font` descriptor with two bitmap entries and 65,535 outline-size records can wrap diskfont.library’s combined `UWORD` entry count to zero; directory enumeration then exposes a cleared zero-size outline entry and omits the declared sizes.

**Source and trigger:** `ReadFontDescr()` reads the bitmap-entry count and outline-size count as `UWORD`s, allocates an array for their sum, then increments `fdh->NumEntries` (also `UWORD`) for each outline size not already represented by a bitmap (`workbench/libs/diskfont/af_fontdescr_io.c:64-102,211-256`; field declarations at `diskfont_intern.h:85-89`). With two bitmap entries and 65,535 outline-size records, if those records contain both bitmap sizes and each of the other 65,534 possible distinct `UWORD` sizes, the loop appends 65,534 entries and the total 65,536 wraps `NumEntries` to zero. The allocation is sized from the original bitmap count plus outline count, so this case does not itself show an undersized array write. `ReadFileEntry()` then copies zero attributes, reserves the special outline attribute, and increments its count to one (`diskfontfunc.c:105-147`). That attribute is in the zeroed allocation and receives no Y-size assignment there. The directory iterator returns it as the sole item (`diskfontfunc.c:978-1030`), which `AvailFonts()` copies into its output (`availfonts.c:120-133,174-220`).

**Affected configuration:** Any build using this diskfont implementation when scanning an OFCH `.font` with the stated counts and size set. The exact file is unusually large and crafted; no repository-selected font was shown to meet the trigger.

**Consequence:** The affected file is represented in disk-font enumeration by a single zero-size outline entry; its bitmap and declared outline sizes are omitted. No memory overwrite is established by this count-wrap path. **Confidence:** high for the integer wrap and resulting enumeration behavior; trigger availability in installed fonts is unverified.

**Review state:** Re-read `ReadFontDescr()`, `FreeFontDescr()`, `ReadFileEntry()`, the directory iterator, and `AvailFonts()` data flow. The zero-size item follows from the cleared special attribute and the one-entry OFCH handling. Source-only; no descriptor was loaded and no runtime behavior was exercised.

## GD5713

**Indexed summary:** FreeType’s glyph bitmap allocation failure is treated as a missing glyph, and diskfont continues building a proportional font with zero metrics and no character data for that glyph.

**Source and trigger:** `RenderGlyph()` initializes the map width to zero, then returns without setting an error when allocation of `bitmap.rows * bitmap.pitch + 1` bytes fails (`workbench/libs/freetype2/glyph.c:183-185,227-235`). `GetGlyph()` turns the zero-width map into `OTERR_UnknownGlyph` and returns NULL (`:367-373`). Diskfont’s `OTAG_GetGlyphMaps()` ignores the return code from `ObtainInfoA()` and continues; if other glyphs were obtained, it accepts the font (`workbench/libs/diskfont/bullet.c:418-455`). In the proportional-font path, `OTAG_CalcMetrics()` leaves cleared zero `CharKern`/`CharSpace` slots for a missing non-space glyph (`:613-661`), and `OTAG_MakeCharData()` leaves its cleared character-location entry and bitmap data untouched (`:785-814`; arrays are allocated cleared at `:511-536`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** diskfont opening an OFCH font whose `.otag` selects the FreeType2 engine, when the `GlyphMap` object allocation succeeds but its per-glyph raster bitmap allocation fails and at least one other glyph remains available.

**Consequence:** the font can be accepted with a missing glyph; proportional text using that character has zero advance and no glyph pixels, so subsequent characters can shift left. The builder does not fail the font or retry that glyph. **Confidence:** high for the failure propagation and zero-initialized proportional metrics; memory exhaustion and its visible rendering effect were not induced.

**Review state:** Re-read the FreeType render/GetGlyph/ObtainInfo path and the diskfont glyph-map, metrics, and character-data consumers. Separated this raster-buffer failure from GD9835, which is the distinct NULL dereference when allocation of the `GlyphMap` object itself fails. Source-only.

## GD9691

**SDL mode enumeration applies the fullscreen flag as a truth test on surface flags.** The `SDL_ListModes()` call passes `surftype | LIBBASE->use_fullscreen ? SDL_FULLSCREEN : 0` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_hiddclass.c:235`). Because conditional `?:` has lower precedence than bitwise OR, this evaluates as `(surftype | use_fullscreen) ? SDL_FULLSCREEN : 0`; when true it returns only `SDL_FULLSCREEN`, dropping the requested surface-type bits. With hardware-surface support (`surftype == SDL_HWSURFACE`), this asks for fullscreen modes even when the user did not request fullscreen. Conversely, when fullscreen was requested, the expression still omits `SDL_HWSURFACE`. Later, `SDL_SetVideoMode()` combines the requested surface flags with `SDL_FULLSCREEN` only when `use_fullscreen` is true (`:539-545`), so the enumerated modes can be filtered against different flags from those used to create the actual display.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional SDL HIDD on an SDL backend reporting hardware-surface support. `startup.c` initializes `fullscreen` to false and sets it only from the icon `FULLSCREEN` tooltype or CLI switch (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/startup.c:150,198-205`). Thus the default launch takes the windowed path, but the precedence error passes `SDL_FULLSCREEN` whenever `surftype` is nonzero. If that host returns different windowed and fullscreen mode lists, valid windowed modes can be omitted from the HIDD enumerator. **Consequence:** users can lose otherwise available windowed display modes. **Confidence:** high for the precedence/flag mismatch and default startup state; exact host mode-list differences were not exercised. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9692

**SDL color expansion uses its temporary row buffer without checking allocation failure.** `SDLBitMap__Hidd_BitMap__BlitColorExpansion()` allocates `msg->width * sizeof(ULONG)` bytes into `srcline` but never checks the result before passing it to `HIDD_BM_GetImage()` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_bitmapclass.c:601,610-647,663-696`). The generic `BM__Hidd_BitMap__GetImage()` writes pixels through the supplied output pointer in its Native path (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:2665-2718`), so allocation failure for a nonempty transparent or opaque expansion reaches a write through NULL.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional SDL HIDD when the obsolete public `BlitColorExpansion` method is invoked for a nonempty region and its row-buffer `AllocMem()` fails. The method is documented as obsolete and no checked-in direct caller was found. **Consequence:** the drawing operation can fault instead of failing cleanly. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation and generic output write; conditional on external or future method use and allocation failure. No allocation or draw was attempted; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5714

**SDL reports graphics-driver startup success when its display object cannot be created.** In `SDLGfx__Root__New()`, the driver object is created by the superclass, then the method calls `OOP_NewObject()` for `LIBBASE->display`. Failure leaves the zero-initialized display pointer NULL, but the method still returns the non-NULL graphics object (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_hiddclass.c:295-320`). `driver_Setup()` accepts that graphics object; if `aHidd_Gfx_DisplayDefault` is NULL, it only logs that no display was exposed, then returns TRUE (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:349-374,400-408`). `AddDisplayDriverA()` therefore reports `DD_OK`, and `sdl_Startup()` treats that as success and registers the class resident (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/startup.c:131-140,276-283`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional hosted SDL HIDD (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/mmakefile.src`) when the HIDD display object's allocation or construction fails after the graphics object succeeds. **Consequence:** the monitor reports successful startup and remains registered without an SDL display; the already registered SDL keyboard/mouse drivers are not rolled back. **Confidence:** high for the ignored NULL display and success propagation; runtime allocation failure was not induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5715

**SDL graphics HIDD construction dereferences unchecked pool allocations.** `SDLGfx__Root__New()` does not check `CreatePool()` before its subsequent `AllocPooled()` calls (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_hiddclass.c:78,230,253`). The selected `AllocPooled()` implementation dereferences the pool header before allocation (`rom/exec/allocpooled.c:77-93`), so a failed pool creation reaches an invalid pool access. Later results are also unchecked: a failed `synctags` allocation is indexed when `nmodes > 0` (`sdlgfx_hiddclass.c:253-264`); a failed per-mode tag allocation is written at indices 0–6 for any listed mode no larger than the current display (`:255-270`); and failed `modetags` allocation is written at index 0 regardless of mode count (`:272-286`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional hosted SDL HIDD when memory pressure causes the pool or one of these tag-array allocations to fail during graphics-driver construction. **Consequence:** construction dereferences or writes through NULL/invalid storage instead of returning a clean driver-creation failure; exact fault manifestation depends on allocator and target behavior. **Confidence:** high for unchecked results and subsequent dereferences/writes; no allocation failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5716

**SDL color expansion uses a four-byte destination stride for 24-bit pixels.** In the `bytesperpixel == 3` cases of `SDLBitMap__Hidd_BitMap__BlitColorExpansion()`, the code indexes the row as `((Uint32 *)p)[x]`, while `PUTPIXEL24` writes only three bytes at the supplied address (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_bitmapclass.c:634-642,683-690`; macro at `:300-308`). The next destination pixel should begin three bytes after the previous one, but this code advances four bytes. For widths greater than one it leaves gaps, misplaces the expanded pixels, and the final write can extend beyond the active row into padding or the next row.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional SDL HIDD with a 24-bit/three-byte destination surface when a client invokes the obsolete HIDD `BlitColorExpansion` method for a region wider than one pixel. The public method description says graphics.library no longer uses it; repository search found no checked-in direct caller. **Consequence:** incorrect color expansion and possible row-boundary overwrite for the conditional external-call case. **Confidence:** high for the address-step mismatch; in-tree reachability is unestablished. No bitmap was drawn; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5717

**Opaque SDL color expansion uses the source Y coordinate as its X coordinate on 16-bit surfaces.** In the opaque `bytesperpixel == 2` branch, `HIDD_BM_GetImage()` receives `msg->srcY` for both its X and Y origin (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_bitmapclass.c:674-680`). The neighboring transparent 16-bit case and the opaque 1-, 3-, and 4-byte cases pass `msg->srcX` as the X origin (`:623-630,665-672,683-697`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional SDL HIDD with a two-byte destination surface when a client invokes the obsolete `BlitColorExpansion` method with `srcX != srcY`; no checked-in direct caller was found. **Consequence:** opaque expansion reads the wrong source columns and paints incorrect foreground/background pixels. **Confidence:** high for the argument mismatch; in-tree reachability is unestablished. No bitmap was drawn; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5721

**SDL startup failure after input registration leaves drivers linked to disposed classes.** `sdl_Startup()` registers keyboard and mouse driver objects through `HIDD_Input_AddHardwareDriver()` before calling `AddDisplayDriverA()` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/startup.c:97-106,128-140`). If display registration returns an error, `sdl_Startup()` returns FALSE without removing either driver. Its only `HIDD_Input_RemHardwareDriver()` call is in the earlier `!msdriver` branch (`:112-126`). `HW_AddDriver()` stores each successful instance in the shared subsystem's driver list (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:173-200`); only `HW_RemoveDriver()` unlinks and disposes it (`:266-300`). The caller then quits SDL, stops the event task, and disposes the generated keyboard/mouse classes without unregistering those instances (`startup.c:275-307`). Class disposal frees the class dispatch tables and class object (`rom/oop/basemetaclass.c:500-522`; `rom/oop/rootclass.c:137-150`), while the shared driver list still retains instances whose class pointer refers to that metadata. `HW_EnumDrivers()` can later return those retained instances to callers (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:353-375`), so later attribute/method access can dispatch through freed class metadata. The separate VBlank-server lifetime during event-task removal is GD2620.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional hosted SDL HIDD when keyboard and mouse driver creation succeeds but `AddDisplayDriverA()` fails. **Consequence:** startup reports failure but leaves globally registered input instances tied to disposed classes; later enumeration/use can follow stale class metadata. Unregister both drivers before disposing their classes. **Confidence:** high for the registration, missing unlink, class-metadata disposal, and retained list entry; later use is conditional, and no display-registration failure or post-failure enumeration was induced. Distinct from GD5714, where a missing display object is incorrectly reported as success. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5722

**SDL startup leaks a graphics.library reference when input setup fails.** `sdl_Startup()` opens `graphics.library` and returns early if either input subsystem/driver setup fails (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/startup.c:89-91,97-126`). That failure branch removes a keyboard driver if one was created and disposes the temporary input HIDD objects, but it does not close `GfxBase`; `CloseLibrary()` appears only on the later path after display registration (`:138`). The comment in the outer startup routine says these libraries are manually opened because they must survive the `main()` return (`startup.c:156-157`), so returning from this helper does not transfer or discharge the reference.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional hosted SDL HIDD when `graphics.library` opens but keyboard or mouse HIDD/driver creation fails. **Consequence:** the failed startup retains one graphics.library open reference; repeated retries can accumulate references. Close the library on the input-setup failure path as well. **Confidence:** high for the unmatched successful open and early return; no input allocation failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5723

**SDL startup failure cleanup omits the display HIDD class.** The startup routine creates `xsd.displayclass` before creating the bitmap/input classes and entering `sdl_hidd_init()`/`sdl_Startup()` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/startup.c:228-245,257-277`). If a later step fails, the rollback disposes the keyboard, mouse, bitmap and graphics class objects but never disposes `xsd.displayclass` (`:297-307`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional hosted SDL HIDD when display-class construction succeeds and a later class initialization, SDL HIDD initialization, input setup, or graphics-driver registration step fails. **Consequence:** the display meta-class object remains allocated after the command reports startup failure. Dispose the display class on each post-construction rollback path. **Confidence:** high for the created object and omitted cleanup; no startup failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5724

**Unmapped SDL key symbols retain a release-bit sentinel (currently masked by GD10087).** `sdl_keymap_init()` initializes every SDL symbol slot to `0xff` and overwrites only symbols listed in its mapping table (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/keymap.c:139-150`). The SDL event task dispatches both key-down and key-up events (`event.c:102-109`), and the keyboard HIDD ORs `IECODE_UP_PREFIX` on key-up (`sdl_kbdclass.c:64-75`). Since `0xff` already contains that bit, after the producer supplies the HIDD event's `flags` and `code` fields correctly, an unmapped symbol would be emitted as raw code `0x7f` with the release bit set for both host transitions. `MapRawKey()` rejects codes at or above `0x78` (`compiler/include/devices/inputevent.h:98-100`; `rom/keymap/maprawkey.c:90-95`). In the current little-endian SDL path, however, `sdl_kbdclass.c` assigns the byte through `kbdevt`; GD10087 causes keyboard.device to read code zero, so this `0x7f` behavior is masked and is not claimed as the present delivered code. Ignore unmapped symbols or explicitly map supported symbols when correcting the event construction.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional hosted SDL keyboard HIDD, for a host key symbol absent from the static mapping table. **Consequence:** once the event-layout defect GD10087 is corrected, both transitions for that symbol would become release notifications for communication code `0x7f`, rather than being ignored. **Confidence:** high for the sentinel and bit operations; this specific downstream effect is conditional on correcting GD10087. No SDL event was injected. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5725

**SDL mouse wheel button events are emitted as button transitions with no button code.** The selected SDL event task collects mouse-button events and forwards both button-down and button-up records to `Hidd_Mouse_SDL_HandleEvent()` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/event.c:73,88-99`). In SDL 1.2, vertical wheel movement is represented by mouse buttons 4 and 5. `SDLMouse__Hidd_Mouse_SDL__HandleEvent()` maps left, right and middle buttons, but its default branch assigns `vHidd_Mouse_NoButton` while preserving the event's Press or Release type (`sdl_mouseclass.c:77-108`). It therefore sends no `vHidd_Mouse_WheelMotion` event or wheel delta for those wheel-button transitions. The HIDD mouse event contract says NoButton describes simple motion, while wheel deltas are carried in `x`/`y` for WheelMotion (`rom/hidds/mouse/mouseclass.c:41-62`). The selected X11 backend demonstrates the intended translation of Button4/Button5 to WheelMotion with signed vertical deltas (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11_mouseclass.c:142-168`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the optional hosted SDL HIDD when the host reports a vertical wheel as SDL 1.2 button 4 or 5 events. **Consequence:** consumers of the AROS mouse HIDD receive no wheel-motion event; instead they receive invalid no-button press/release events. Map wheel-button input to `vHidd_Mouse_WheelMotion` with a signed `y` delta and ignore the synthetic release. **Confidence:** high for the AROS event dispatch, field mapping, and HIDD contract mismatch; SDL host input was not run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5726

**VESA graphics construction failure removes an unregistered reset callback.** `VESAGfx__Root__New()` obtains the partially constructed HIDD from its superclass and next tries to create its display object. It initializes and registers the embedded `ResetInterrupt` only when that display creation succeeds (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_hiddclass.c:65-86`). If display creation returns NULL, the failure branch immediately coerces the HIDD through its Dispose method (`:88-93`). `VESAGfx__Root__Dispose()` unconditionally calls `RemResetCallback()` on the instance's reset node (`:98-104`), although this failure path never called `AddResetCallback()`. Generic `root_new()` allocates and clears the complete instance (`rom/oop/rootclass.c:107-128`), leaving both links in the unregistered node NULL. `RemResetCallback()` forwards it to `Remove()` (`rom/exec/remresetcallback.c:45-49`), which dereferences the predecessor and successor without checking whether the node is linked (`rom/exec/remove.c:45-64`). The rollback therefore dereferences NULL instead of disposing the partially created HIDD cleanly.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** i386-PC and x86-64-PC boot packages select `vesagfx` (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:75`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:68`), and the module manifest selects this class implementation (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/mmakefile.src:4-17`). The trigger is failure to construct the VESA display object after the VESA HIDD instance was created. **Consequence:** allocation-failure rollback can fault in `Remove()` and fail to return cleanly. **Confidence:** high for the unmatched registration/removal path and NULL links; no allocation failure or boot was induced. Only remove the callback if it was registered, or use a rollback path that skips callback removal. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5727

**EFI framebuffer construction failure removes an unregistered reset callback.** `EFIFBGfx__Root__New()` creates the HIDD instance through its superclass and then tries to create the display object. It initializes and registers `data->ResetInterrupt` only when display creation succeeds (`rom/hidds/efifbgfx/efifbgfx_hiddclass.c:63-84`). If display creation returns NULL, the constructor immediately coerces the partially created HIDD through its Dispose method (`:86-90`). `EFIFBGfx__Root__Dispose()` unconditionally calls `RemResetCallback()` on that instance's reset node (`:96-101`), although the failed constructor never added it. The generic root constructor allocates and clears the whole object instance (`rom/oop/rootclass.c:107-128`), so the unregistered node's successor and predecessor fields are NULL. `RemResetCallback()` passes the node to `Remove()` (`rom/exec/remresetcallback.c:45-49`), and `Remove()` dereferences its predecessor and successor without checking that the node is linked (`rom/exec/remove.c:45-64`). The failure cleanup therefore dereferences NULL before the partially constructed object can be disposed normally.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the `efifbgfx.hidd` target when its display object allocation/construction fails after the framebuffer HIDD instance has been created. The RISC-V64 OpenSBI boot package includes `efifbgfx` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:109-119`), and the module manifest selects this implementation (`rom/hidds/efifbgfx/mmakefile.src:4-17`). **Consequence:** the constructor's allocation-failure rollback can fault in `Remove()` instead of returning cleanly. **Confidence:** high for the missing registration/removal pairing and NULL list links; no allocation failure or boot was induced. Track whether the reset node was registered before removing it, or route constructor rollback through cleanup that only removes installed callbacks. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5728

**Finding:** When the generic GFX histogram class is constructed for a bitmap, its fast-method cache requests `PutPixel` as the bitmap's `UnmapPixel` method and requests `PutPixel` as both histogram methods. In the selected method layout, the latter offset resolves to `FindColorEntry`, so histogram insertion never calls `AddColorEntry`. The constructor therefore dispatches each unmap request to the bitmap's pixel writer with an `UnmapPixel` message, then repeatedly searches an initially empty histogram and never inserts colors. The generic ChunkyBM and PlanarBM pixel writers do not check coordinates; the mismatched message fields can cause unintended bitmap writes, including outside the backing bitmap, depending on the bitmap implementation and the narrowed pixel/pointer values. The histogram remains empty even when those writes do not fault.

**Trigger and scope:** An external caller constructs the selected `CLID_Hidd_BMHistogram` for a bitmap. The class is selected in `rom/hidds/gfx/mmakefile.src`; no in-tree constructor caller was found. All four `USE_FAST_BMH*` switches are enabled in `gfx_intern.h`.

**Evidence:** `gfx_histogramclass.c:53-60` caches the wrong method offsets and `:64-80` uses them in the constructor's full bitmap scan. `gfx_intern.h:607-617` sends an `UnmapPixel` message through the cached method; `:621-648` similarly constructs distinct Find/Add messages. `gfx.conf:518` defines `PutPixel(WORD x, WORD y, HIDDT_Pixel pixel)`, while `:540` defines `UnmapPixel(HIDDT_Pixel pixel, HIDDT_Color *color)`. `gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:107-139` computes a backing-buffer address directly from the supplied coordinates; `gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:356-385` likewise computes a plane offset without coordinate validation. Histogram `AddColorEntry` inserts the node at `gfx_histogramclass.c:118-140`; `FindColorEntry` only writes its output pointer on a match at `:143-184`. With an initially empty list and Add misdirected to Find, no entries are created.

**Confidence:** High for the method mismatch and empty-histogram consequence; the extent of the unintended bitmap write depends on the selected bitmap implementation and runtime address/format values. No constructor operation was run. Source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L450`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L450) and the detailed recheck below.

## GD5729

**Finding:** `Sync__Root__Get()` attempts to return `PixelTime` in picoseconds, but its `aoHidd_Sync_PixelTime` case falls through into `aoHidd_Sync_PixelClock` and overwrites the result with the raw clock in Hz (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_syncclass.c:347-358`). For every nonzero clock, a `PixelTime` query therefore returns the wrong attribute and unit. The same case divides by `pixelclock / 1000`; a nonzero clock below 1 kHz makes that divisor zero before the fallthrough.

**Trigger and scope:** A caller queries the generic GFX sync HIDD's obsolete but still declared `aHidd_Sync_PixelTime` attribute (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:731`). The generic class is selected in `rom/hidds/gfx/mmakefile.src`. `parse_sync_tags()` accepts `aHidd_Sync_PixelClock` directly without a minimum-frequency check (`gfx_syncclass.c:555-559`), so a sub-kHz nonzero clock can reach the divide-by-zero path. No in-tree PixelTime getter was found; the observable wrong result is conditional on an external getter, and the sub-kHz divide requires such a supplied mode value.

**Consequence and confidence:** High confidence that every nonzero PixelTime query returns PixelClock instead, and that 1–999 Hz reaches a zero divisor in the getter. No query or mode was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5730

**Finding:** The generic DMEnum's recursive `querymode()` allocates the final ModeID array at its terminal recursion frame, using `mq->numfound + 1` entries for all matches plus the invalid-ID sentinel (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:175-204`). It does not check `AllocVec()` before advancing the returned pointer and writing that sentinel. On allocation failure, pointer arithmetic on NULL is undefined and the sentinel store writes through the resulting invalid address. This happens even when there are zero matching modes because the function still allocates the one-element sentinel array.

**Caller path and scope:** The selected public `DMEnum__Hidd_DMEnum__QueryModeIDs()` enters this recursion for generic mode queries (`gfx_dmenumclass.c:749-809`). The graphics.library `display_Setup()` caller checks for a NULL result only after the method returns (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:76-80`), which cannot handle the earlier sentinel write. The generic DMEnum class is selected by `rom/hidds/gfx/mmakefile.src`; architecture-specific P96 and AmigaVideo enumerators override this method on their own targets and have separate query implementations.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** A display using the generic GFX DMEnum and a mode-ID query whose terminal result-array `AllocVec()` fails. **Consequence:** invalid pointer arithmetic and a sentinel write through a failed allocation while enumerating modes; the caller cannot receive the documented NULL failure cleanly. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation and store. No allocation failure or query was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5731

**Finding:** CursorFB's `CFB_REMOVE_ALL` helper uses the fixed rectangle `[-16384, 16383]` on both axes when deciding whether to hide the software pointer before an operation with unknown bounds (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_cursorfbclass.c:60-67`). `GfxDisplay_CursorIntersects()` compares this rectangle with the current cursor rectangle and returns false when they do not overlap (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:296-307`). The mouse position and stored cursor position are signed `WORD`s (`compiler/include/devices/inputevent.h:34-42`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_display.h:50-55`), so positions above 16383 remain representable. For example, a cursor whose left edge is 16384 or greater is outside the helper's test rectangle and is not removed.

**Affected operations and consequence:** The helper is used by polygon draw/fill, text draw/fill, bitmap clear, and bitmap scale (`gfx_cursorfbclass.c:303-359`). If one of these operations modifies pixels under a displayed cursor at a coordinate above 16383, CursorFB forwards the operation without first saving/removing the pointer; the operation can overwrite the cursor image, and the later render bracket is skipped because `inside` remains false. This is conditional on a display/bitmap path that permits such pointer coordinates and on the operation touching the cursor.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** The generic CursorFB wrapper is used by the selected generic graphics HIDD. The hosted SDL driver imports SDL_ListModes() widths after checking only that they do not exceed the current host width (arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_hiddclass.c:235-268); the shared sync class defaults HMax to the selected HDisp (rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_syncclass.c:133-144). The X11 driver likewise copies host hdisplay values directly into mode tags (arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11gfx_displayclass.c:286-335). Thus, when either hosted backend exposes a mode at least 16,385 pixels wide or high, a cursor at signed-WORD coordinate 16,384 through 32,767 can be visible outside CFB_REMOVE_ALL's bracket. The headless HIDD caps width and height at 16,384 and does not reach this range (rom/hidds/gfx/headless/headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:37-38,234-241).

**Scope and confidence:** The hard-coded intersection range and its missed coordinate range are certain; the source confirms optional hosted mode paths do not impose the 16,384 limit, while an actual trigger depends on the host advertising such a large mode and the operation touching the cursor. No display or drawing operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5732

**Finding:** The generic bitmap HIDD's `DoBufferedOperation()` allocates a scratch buffer sized for up to 16 KB of pixels. If that allocation fails and more than one line was requested, it retries with a one-line buffer; if the retry also fails, it returns `FALSE` without processing any pixels (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:79-124`). Four callers discard that result and leave explicit TODO comments for their missing fallback: `PutTemplate()` (`:3315-3358`), `PutAlphaTemplate()` (`:3483-3541`), `PutPattern()` (`:3809-3880`), and `PutTranspImageLUT()` (`:4088-4114`). Those HIDD methods return `VOID`, so callers receive no indication that the requested drawing was skipped.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** This affects bitmap classes that inherit these generic methods and receive a positive-width/height request when its scratch-buffer allocation attempt(s) fail. It does not apply to `PutAlphaImage()`, whose caller checks the result and runs a per-pixel fallback (`:3097-3130`), or to ChunkyBM's separate `PutTemplate()`/`PutPattern()` overrides (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:756-870`). `PutTranspImageLUT()` is also used by the selected graphics.library text path (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:750`).

**Consequence and confidence:** The affected operation silently leaves the destination unchanged for the requested region, even though the public operation has no failure result. High confidence in the ignored allocation failure and missing fallback; manifestation requires the stated allocation failures and an inheriting bitmap class. No allocation failure or drawing operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

<a id="gd5733"></a>
## GD5733

**Finding:** ChunkyBM's `PutAlphaImage()` stores the source and destination row skips in signed `WORD`s (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:439-440`). Both the BGR032 and RGB16_LE branches compute `src_step = msg->modulo - msg->width * 4` and add that signed value after consuming each row (`:447-495,498-557`). `HIDD_BM_PutAlphaImage()` defines `modulo` as `ULONG` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:3004-3005`), so a valid source stride can produce a skip outside the signed 16-bit range. For example, width 1 and modulo 40,000 produce a 39,996-byte row skip; on supported targets where conversion to `WORD` wraps to 16 bits, the stored skip becomes negative and subsequent rows read from the wrong source location. `dst_step` is narrowed the same way for sufficiently wide destination rows.

**Caller and affected configuration:** CyberGraphX `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` accepts a `UWORD srcmod` and forwards the stride and clipped rows to `HIDD_BM_PutAlphaImage()` (`workbench/libs/cgfx/writepixelarrayalpha.c:37-47,116-128`). `AllocBitMap()` maps the CyberGraphX `PIXFMT_RGB16_LE` special format to `vHidd_StdPixFmt_RGB16_LE` (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:26-38,285-296`), which selects ChunkyBM's RGB16_LE branch. The same source-stride trigger is selected on Raspberry Pi ARM-native VCGfx builds: `vcgfx_hidd.h` defines `VC_FMT_32`, `vcgfx_pixfmts.c` registers BGR032, and both VideoCore bitmap classes inherit `CLID_Hidd_ChunkyBM` without overriding `PutAlphaImage()` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/vcgfx_hidd.h:29`; `vcgfx_pixfmts.c:22-59`; `vcgfx.conf:53-80`). The parent package selects `vcgfx` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/mmakefile.src:36`). Thus a 40,000-byte public source modulo with a narrow multi-row write also reaches the affected BGR032 loop on that selected target. The destination-step narrowing remains conditional on a sufficiently wide destination row.

**Consequence and confidence:** Rows after the first can consume source pixels from the wrong address, producing incorrect alpha-blended output and potentially reading beyond the caller's intended row data. The narrowing is certain; the wrap result is implementation-defined in C and the specific negative value applies to supported targets with 16-bit two's-complement conversion. No bitmap operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5734

**Finding:** PlanarBM's Copy-mode `FillRect` fast path writes every non-null bitplane and never consults `GC_COLMASK(msg->gc)` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:443-502`). The graphics.library adapter sets that GC mask from `rp->Mask` for bitplane destinations (`rom/graphics/graphics_inline.h:82-89`), and `SetWriteMask()` updates `rp->Mask` (`rom/graphics/setwritemask.c:48-49`). The generic FillRect fallback draws scanlines through the generic per-pixel method, which applies `GC_COLMASK`; the optimized PlanarBM override therefore changes the expected masked-write behavior.

**Caller and trigger:** `RectFill()` obtains the RastPort GC and dispatches `HIDD_BM_FillRect()` through `fillrect_render()` (`rom/graphics/rectfill.c:68-101`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:330-337`). With a planar bitmap, `SetWriteMask(rp, 1)` followed by a Copy-mode `RectFill()` should change plane 0 only. The fast path instead writes the selected foreground pen's bit into every allocated plane for each covered pixel, including planes excluded by the write mask. The override applies only when the bitmap is non-null and GC draw mode is Copy; other modes call the superclass.

**Consequence and confidence:** Unselected color planes are corrupted by ordinary clipped rectangle fills on planar RastPorts with a partial plane mask. High confidence in the mask propagation and its omission from the selected fast path. No bitmap or fill was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5735

**Finding:** `create_std_pixfmts()` initializes the standard-format pointer table to NULL, then records each newly created format in `csd->std_pixfmts[]` before linking it into `pflist`. If creation of a later format fails, `delete_pixfmts()` disposes the linked objects but does not clear their table entries (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_init.c:172-207`). `GFX_ClassInit()` ignores the helper's FALSE result and continues with cursor-wrapper and hardware-root setup; it can still return success if those later steps succeed (`:270-328`).

**Caller path and consequence:** `DMEnum__Internal__GetPixFmt()` returns a table entry for a valid standard format without checking that it is non-NULL or live (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:1321-1335`). Generic bitmap creation, pixel conversion, display setup, and ChunkyBM conversion call this lookup (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:2608,2740,2904,4405`; `gfx_displayclass.c:1003`; `gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:415,684`). If standard-format construction fails after one or more entries were installed, earlier entries point to disposed objects and later entries remain NULL. A subsequent lookup can therefore pass a stale object to OOP methods or fail to provide the requested format, depending on which table index is used.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** The generic GFX HIDD is selected by `rom/hidds/gfx/mmakefile.src`. Trigger requires a standard-format object allocation failure partway through `GFX_ClassInit()`, followed by successful cursor-wrapper initialization and hardware-root registration, then a consumer lookup of an affected format. **Confidence:** high for cleanup leaving table entries and the ignored status; manifestation depends on later initialization succeeding and a caller using one of the affected entries. No allocation failure or lookup was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5736 (withdrawn duplicate)

Withdrawn as a duplicate of [GD6139](#gd6139), which documents the same empty palette-to-palette conversion helper and includes the directly accessible differing-format `CopyBox` caller. GD6139 is the retained finding; do not count GD5736 as a separate defect.

## GD5738

**Finding:** The generic GFX `CopyBox` wrapper protects at most one display. It selects the destination display whenever the destination is a CursorFB-wrapped bitmap, otherwise it selects the source display; then it uses that display's cursor state for both source and destination intersection checks (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1252-1310`). `GfxDisplay_CursorIntersects()` only reports an intersection when the bitmap equals that display's currently composited cursor bitmap (`gfx_displayclass.c:296-307`). For wrapped source and destination bitmaps owned by different displays, the source cursor check therefore uses the destination display and does not remove the source display's cursor.

**Caller and trigger:** The selected graphics.library blit helper dispatches to `HIDD_Gfx_CopyBox()` for a HIDD bitmap copy (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:642-650`); the public `BltBitMap()` path reaches this helper through the RastPort/bitmap copy support. Trigger requires a cross-display copy with a CursorFB-wrapped source and destination, where the source display currently has its cursor drawn over the source rectangle. The implementation unwraps both operands and performs the copy while only the chosen display's cursor semaphore is held. The software cursor is part of the source framebuffer pixels, so the copy reads and transfers the cursor image as if it were application content.

**Consequence and confidence:** The destination can receive a stale copy of the source pointer; later pointer movement or source redraw can expose the copied pointer image. High confidence in the one-display selection and bitmap identity check; manifestation requires the cross-display wrapped-bitmap configuration and source cursor overlap. No display or copy operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5739 (withdrawn; API semantics unestablished)

`HIDDT_Color` contains red, green, blue, alpha, and `pixval` fields (`rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:174-183`). `AddColorEntry()` stores the complete structure, and `GetEntryColor()` returns the complete structure, but `FindColorEntry()` compares only red, green, and blue (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_histogramclass.c:118-140,143-184,188-198`). Thus two entries with equal RGB and different alpha resolve as the same entry if a caller expects alpha to be part of histogram identity.

**Disposition:** Withdrawn as a bug candidate on 2026-10-25. The public `Hidd_BMHistogram` interface declares method signatures but does not state whether alpha participates in entry identity (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:597-600`). A repository-wide exact-symbol search found no direct maintained method caller beyond the class's own constructor, whose fast-method dispatch is independently broken and already tracked as GD5728. The implementation fact that lookup compares RGB only is therefore not evidence of a violated contract or a maintained alpha-merging defect. Retain this note as a source observation, not an active candidate. No histogram operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5740

**Finding:** The extended `AllocBitMap()` tag parser handles `BMATags_Friend`, `BMATags_Depth`, `BMATags_Clear`, `BMATags_NoMemory`, and `BMATags_DisplayID`, but has no case for the documented `BMATags_Displayable` tag (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:196-230`). The public contract says the tag controls displayability and defaults to `BMF_DISPLAYABLE` (`allocbitmap.c:128-131`). Instead, the HIDD-selection decision uses only the original `flags` (`:237-246`), and the HIDD `aHidd_BitMap_Displayable` attribute is also derived only from `flags` (`:323-326`).

**Trigger and consequence:** For a low-depth extended-tag request with `BMATags_Displayable = TRUE`, no displayable flag, and no other HIDD-forcing option, the function can take the plain-bitmap path; the returned bitmap is not displayable despite the explicit tag. Conversely, `BMATags_Displayable = FALSE` cannot override `BMF_DISPLAYABLE`; the HIDD path still runs and receives `Displayable = TRUE`. This conflicts with the tag's documented override/default behavior and the stated restriction that non-displayable bitmaps cannot be used as custom bitmaps or `RasInfo` bitmaps (`allocbitmap.c:163-166`).

**Scope and confidence:** This affects callers using the public extended tag-list form. A maintained C/header search found no in-tree `BMATags_Displayable` caller, so caller impact is external. High confidence that the parser ignores the tag and that both explicit override cases follow the flags instead. No bitmap was allocated. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5741

**Finding:** `AllocRaster()` accepts `ULONG width` and `ULONG height`, then allocates `RASSIZE(width, height)` bytes (`rom/graphics/allocraster.c:16-23,54`). `FreeRaster()` accepts the same dimensions as `UWORD` and passes `RASSIZE(width, height)` to `FreeMem()` (`rom/graphics/freeraster.c:16-24,53`). The public prototypes retain this width mismatch (`rom/graphics/graphics.conf:122-123`).

**Trigger and consequence:** On the 32-bit `ULONG` interface, allocate a one-row raster with width 65,536. `RASSIZE(65536, 1)` is 8,192 bytes, but the width parameter to `FreeRaster()` converts to `UWORD` zero; `RASSIZE(0, 1)` is zero. `FreeMem()` treats zero-byte frees as a no-op (`rom/exec/freemem.c:64-66`), so this valid `AllocRaster()` result is leaked when freed with the same requested dimensions. Other out-of-range dimensions can also be narrowed, but this report claims only the exact zero-size leak case.

**Scope and confidence:** High confidence in the signature mismatch and zero-size no-op consequence. A checked-in caller census found no `FreeRaster()` use with dimensions above `UWORD`; the trigger is available to external callers of the public vector. No raster was allocated or freed. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5742

**`ScaleLayer()` reports failure even when its layer-shape callback completes.** The public Layers vector calls `ChangeLayerShape()` and then returns `FALSE` unconditionally (`rom/hyperlayers/scalelayer.c:78-88`), although its function contract says `TRUE` means success and `FALSE` means failure (`:50-55`). In the ordinary one-ClipRect path, the callback returns the layer's non-NULL `shaperegion` (`:111-115,147-156`); `ChangeLayerShape()` treats that nonzero hook result as acceptance and returns the previous shape (`rom/hyperlayers/changelayershape.c:100-118,248`). A completed callback therefore still yields a false status from `ScaleLayer()`.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** callers of the selected `layers.library` vector when `ScaleLayer()` completes its callback. The vector is in the Layers manifest (`rom/hyperlayers/mmakefile.src:44`; API declaration in `layers.conf:52-55`), and `layers` is included in the base library package (`rom/mmakefile.src:140,146-149`). The only checked-in direct calls are in the optional `developer/demos/winshape.c:197,206`; they ignore the return value. **Consequence:** public callers that use the documented result to detect failure receive `FALSE` after a completed operation and may report a failed scale or take failure cleanup. No checked-in caller demonstrates that consequence. **Confidence:** high for the unconditional result and contract mismatch; external caller impact is conditional. No layer was scaled; source-only.

## GD5743

**`AllocSpriteDataA()` returns a cleared pointer bitmap when generic HIDD scaling cannot allocate its scratch buffers.** For an HIDD source bitmap, `AllocSpriteDataA()` uses that bitmap as the destination's friend and requests a same-format, eight-bit `BMF_CLEAR` destination (`rom/graphics/allocspritedataa.c:194-210,242-253`). If that allocation succeeds, it calls the public `BitMapScale()` and then publishes the destination in `sprite->es_BitMap` without checking whether scaling wrote any pixels. `BitMapScale()` has a `void` interface (`rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c:42-48`). Its generic HIDD dispatch calls `HIDD_BM_BitMapScale()` and then updates the destination regardless of whether the method completed (`:125-131,211-220`). The generic bitmap implementation returns immediately if allocation of `srcbuf`, `dstbuf`, or `linepattern` fails, before writing destination pixels (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4928-4949`). The clear destination therefore remains blank, yet `AllocSpriteDataA()` returns it as a successful sprite.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** callers creating pointer sprite data from an HIDD bitmap, when the destination bitmap allocation succeeds, the selected bitmap class uses the generic HIDD scaler method, and one of its three scratch allocations fails. The checked-in Intuition `PointerClass` caller accepts a non-NULL sprite and proceeds to `CreateSharedPointer()` (`rom/intuition/pointerclass.c:103,119-149`). When that pointer path installs its default colormap, palette entry zero is zero-initialized while entries 1 onward receive pointer colors and alpha (`:128-139`); a cleared indexed destination contains index zero, so this path produces a fully transparent pointer image. This is conditional on using the default colormap path; a source-provided colormap can give index zero different semantics. **Consequence:** a transient memory-pressure failure can make pointer creation report success while the newly created pointer is blank (typically invisible with the default palette). **Confidence:** high for the unchecked void scaler result and the generic-method no-write allocation exits; medium for the user-visible pointer effect because it depends on the selected HIDD class and palette path. This is distinct from GD77's general `BitMapScale()` failure-reporting behavior. No allocation failure or pointer creation was induced; source-only.

<a id="gd5744"></a>
## GD5744

CyberGraphX coordinate entry points accept unsigned `UWORD` coordinates (and some, such as `ProcessPixelArray()` and `ExtractColor()`, accept `ULONG`), then narrow them into signed `WORD` rectangles or HIDD pixel/blit coordinates. `struct Rectangle` itself stores all four coordinates as `WORD` (`compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:45-51`). Representative paths include `WritePixelArray()` and `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` constructing such rectangles (`workbench/libs/cgfx/writepixelarray.c:183-188`; `writepixelarrayalpha.c:107-112`), `ReadPixelArray()` and `ExtractColor()` doing the same (`readpixelarray.c:133-147`; `extractcolor.c:92-119`), and `WriteLUTPixelArray()` forwarding destination coordinates to the `WORD`-coordinate `WritePixels8()` path (`writelutpixelarray.c:117-123`). Other reviewed affected entry points include `MovePixelArray`, `FillPixelArray`, `InvertPixelArray`, `ReadRGBPixel`, `WriteRGBPixel`, and `ProcessPixelArray`; their individual file rows in the coverage ledger record the parameter and narrowing paths.

**Trigger and consequence:** A caller supplies a coordinate above 32,767 for a bitmap/window that actually supports dimensions beyond that range. For example, destination x = 32,768 narrows to −32,768 when stored as a `WORD`.
