## GD5905

**IconList leaks a temporary date string when the date field cannot render text.** `RenderEntryField()` allocates a concatenation buffer for `INDEX_LASTACCESS` and formats the date/time into it (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Classes/iconlist.c:914-921`). It returns early if the resulting string is empty (`:927-928`) or if `TextFit()` returns zero for the available field dimensions (`:966-969`). The only `FreeVec(text)` is at the function end (`:1013`), so neither early return releases the allocated date string.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** detail/list mode with the Last Access column enabled; render an entry whose formatted date/time is empty or whose column height/width permits no character to fit. **Consequence:** one temporary allocation leaks for each affected redraw. **Confidence:** high for the allocation and bypassed cleanup paths; no date-column render was performed. Source-only.

## GD5906

**graphics.library treats a displayless HIDD as a successful driver setup.** `driver_Setup()` accepts a non-NULL result from `HW_AddDriver()`, then looks for the driver's display list or default display. If neither is exposed, it only logs the condition and still returns TRUE (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:369-415`). If `display_Register()` is called, it is also `void` and ignores a NULL result from `display_Setup()` (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:366-410`); `display_Setup()` can fail when a required framebuffer bitmap cannot be created and frees only its monitor-display record (`:159-204`). `AddDisplayDriverA()` converts only a FALSE `driver_Setup()` result to an error (`rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:281-297`).

There are selected paths into this false-success result. The explicitly built LinuxFB HIDD can expose a display object whose required graphics.library framebuffer bitmap cannot be created. IntelGMA can fail to construct `sd->display` but still return its graphics HIDD; its DisplayDefault getter then yields NULL, and rejecting the NULL display in the compositor does not make the driver constructor fail (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_hiddclass.c:551-572,595-598`; `intelgma_compositorclass.c:426-443`). `G45_Init()` treats the already-set PCI-device pointer as success and the startup caller publishes the class and stays resident (`intelgma_init.c:500-505`; `intelgma_startup.c:251-283`).

The same generic path is reached by HeadlessGfx if its root object is created but its default display object is not: `HeadlessGfx__Root__New()` stores the root object, attempts `OOP_NewObject()` for the display, and returns the root object even when that attempt returns NULL (`rom/hidds/gfx/headless/headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:295-307`). The generic Gfx HIDD getter supplies NULL for DisplayDefault (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:856-880`). During boot-queue replay, `driver_ReplayBootQueue()` interprets the resulting TRUE from `driver_Setup()` as success and frees the queued entry (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:296-323`); the failed HeadlessGfx display is therefore not retained for retry. The RISC-V OpenSBI boot manifest selects this HeadlessGfx target (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:51`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** any `AddDisplayDriverA()` caller whose constructed HIDD exposes no usable display or whose display setup fails. Selected examples are LinuxFB and IntelGMA under their stated allocation failures; the selected RISC-V OpenSBI HeadlessGfx boot path requires default-display construction to fail after its root object succeeds. **Consequence:** callers can be told setup succeeded without a usable display; on the HeadlessGfx boot-queue path, graphics.library also discards the only retry entry. In LinuxFB, the HIDD and AddDisplayDriver configuration remain retained with its framebuffer mapping and descriptor; in IntelGMA, startup remains resident after programming its initial mode but registers no display. Propagate display setup failure and remove the HIDD/configuration when no display was registered; keep failed boot entries queued. **Confidence:** high for the success propagation, the three source paths and the HeadlessGfx queue retirement; occurrence requires the stated construction/allocation failures. No display registration, allocation failure or boot replay was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5907

**Display-driver removal omits the callback's registered userdata argument.** `SetDisplayDriverCallback()` saves the callback and its registered `userdata` in the graphics display-chain head (`rom/graphics/setdisplaydrivercallback.c:74-79`). When a display is enabled, `display_Enable()` calls the callback with that value and stores the callback's return value in the per-display `mdd->display_userdata` field (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:334-340`). On removal, the first argument is correctly the stored per-display object, but `display_Expunge()` also passes that same per-display object as the third `userdata` argument (`graphics_display.c:241-243`); the documented contract requires the original value supplied to `SetDisplayDriverCallback()` (`setdisplaydrivercallback.c:35-49`). Pass `CDD(GfxBase)->mdisplay.display_userdata` as the removal callback's third argument. **Affected configuration and trigger:** a private Graphics API client registers a callback with non-NULL userdata and needs that userdata during a display-removal notification. The only checked-in caller is Intuition's `DisplayDriverNotify()` (`rom/intuition/intuition_init.c:300`), whose removal branch ignores its third argument and disposes the first argument (`rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:50-76`), so no current in-tree failure was established. **Consequence:** another callback client can lose its registered context during teardown and may use the per-display return object as if it were that context. **Confidence:** high for the argument mismatch; impact is conditional on a private API client consuming userdata during removal. No callback or display removal was run; source-only.

## GD5908

**Display-mode lookup and bitmap creation can race display removal and dereference freed state.** `FindDisplayInfo()` walks `GFXPRIVATE_MONITORFIRST`, then scans the selected driver's embedded `modes[]` array without obtaining `displaydb_sem` (`rom/graphics/finddisplayinfo.c:54-84`). `NextDisplayInfo()` similarly reads the display list and mode records without a shared lock (`rom/graphics/nextdisplayinfo.c:55-91`). `GetDisplayInfoData()` accepts the raw handle returned by `FindDisplayInfo()` and dereferences its driver and mode fields before querying the HIDD objects; when given a handle it does not revalidate that the handle remains registered (`rom/graphics/getdisplayinfodata.c:149-176`).

The writer path removes the display under the exclusive `displaydb_sem`: `display_Expunge()` unlinks it, disposes the display/compositor/framebuffer objects and frees the mode-record allocation (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:221-275`; the boot handover caller is `rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:251-284`). Its refusal check only protects displays with an active viewport or front bitmap; it does not pin an undisplayed boot-mode display for a concurrent enumerator. Thus a concurrent iteration can retain a handle while a native graphics-driver registration performs the expunge, then pass the stale handle into another `GetDisplayInfoData()` call or continue walking the freed list/mode array. The selected ScreenMode Preferences caller has this multi-call sequence: it obtains `id` from `NextDisplayInfo()`, stores `handle = FindDisplayInfo(id)`, then makes separate name, display-info and dimension queries using that same handle (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/smselector.c:103-121,135-165`). This is not limited to cold-start enumeration: the optional monitor Wrapper accepts CLASS/LIBRARY from its icon tooltypes or CLI, opens a missing HIDD library, and calls `AddDisplayDriverA()` (`workbench/devs/monitors/wrapper/wrapper.c:60-100`), providing a maintained on-demand registration path that can overlap an open ScreenMode selector. Intuition's selected `OpenScreen()` path is another multi-call consumer: it obtains a `DisplayInfoHandle` with `FindDisplayInfo(modeid)` and reuses it for separate dimension and display/monitor queries (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1104-1109`). If that mode belongs to an inactive boot display being removed during on-demand registration, these queries can dereference the detached handle before screen creation finishes, extending the race to ordinary `OpenScreen()` callers. The same unpinned lifetime reaches `AllocBitMap()`: its `BMATags_DisplayID` handling obtains a raw mode handle and saves `dh->drv`/`dh->id` (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:219-226`), then later calls `HIDD_Display_CreateObject(drv->display_obj, ...)` (`:341-348`). PSI provides another selected retained-handle path: its `DispIDlist_New()` iterates `NextDisplayInfo()` and inserts each ID through `MUIM_List_InsertSingle()` (`workbench/prefs/PSI/displayidlist_class.c:116-118`); the selected MUI List implementation calls the construct hook for inserted entries (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:2983-3018,3070-3079`). `DispIDlist_ConstructFunc()` retains the handle from `FindDisplayInfo()` across separate Name, Display, and Dimension queries (`displayidlist_class.c:57-84`), so list construction can likewise use a detached handle during display removal. `OpenScreen()` passes its selected mode ID through that tag (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1225-1238`). If handover expunges the inactive boot display between lookup and bitmap creation, the allocation can use the freed driver record and disposed display object.

The core `MakeVPort()` path also retains this unpinned state: for a non-HIDD planar bitmap whose `GetVPModeID()` returns `INVALID_ID`, it derives the PAL/NTSC mode ID and stores `dih->drv` from `FindDisplayInfo()` (`rom/graphics/makevport.c:84-92`). It later dereferences `mdd->display_obj` in `HIDD_Display_CreateObject()` to wrap the bitmap (`:147-153`), with no display-database lock or lifetime pin spanning the lookup and use. If the corresponding inactive boot display is expunged during that interval, this maintained graphics-library path can pass a freed display object into bitmap construction. This is the same raw-handle/removal race, not a separate finding.

Serialize all display-mode readers and bitmap construction against removal, or provide stable copied/reference-counted mode and driver state across `FindDisplayInfo()`, `GetDisplayInfoData()`, and `AllocBitMap()` use. **Affected configuration and trigger:** Graphics builds with runtime boot-display handover, when a task enumerates or queries a mode while native HIDD registration removes the corresponding inactive boot-mode display. Selected maintained examples are ScreenMode Preferences and PSI, which reuse handles across name/display/dimension queries; Intuition `OpenScreen()`, which reuses one across dimension and display/monitor queries and then passes the mode ID to `AllocBitMap()`; and `MakeVPort()` wrapping a non-HIDD bitmap with a PAL/NTSC mode while that inactive boot display is removed. **Consequence:** the caller can read freed mode records or query disposed HIDD objects, disrupting mode enumeration, bitmap construction, or screen creation; bitmap allocation can also dereference the freed driver record or display object. **Confidence:** high for the unlocked readers, exclusive unlink/free path and selected retained-handle callers; the concurrent timing and exact manifestation are conditional. No mode enumeration or handover was run. Source-only.

## GD5910

**`SetRGB32()` writes past the fixed HIDD pixel translation table for an out-of-range color index.** The public `SetRGB32()` contract says a color index outside the valid range is ignored (`rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:67-81`). The ColorMap-side `SetRGB32CM()` call does validate `n < cm->Count` (`rom/graphics/setrgb32cm.c:61-76`), but `SetRGB32()` unconditionally proceeds to `internal_SetRGB32Colors()` (`setrgb32.c:116-124`). That helper calls `HIDD_BM_SetColors()` and then, for a HIDD viewport bitmap, writes each `colors[i].pixval` to `HIDD_BM_PIXTAB(bitmap)[first + i]` without checking the bitmap table extent (`setrgb32.c:14-53`). `AllocBitMap()` allocates this translation table as exactly `AROS_PALETTE_SIZE` entries (256) for displayable HIDD bitmaps (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:417-426`; size `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h:109-110`). Therefore `SetRGB32(vp, 256, ...)` on such a viewport attempts the first byte-pixel write beyond the table even though the ColorMap update itself rejects the index. `LoadRGB32()` reaches the same helper using its caller-provided `first` and `count` (`rom/graphics/loadrgb32.c:87-103`); its allocation-fallback loop also reaches `SetRGB32()` for each computed index (`:74-85`). `SetRGB4()` provides another route to the same unchecked write: its public contract says an out-of-range color index is ignored, but its signed `WORD n` is forwarded directly to `SetRGB32()`'s unsigned `ULONG n` (`rom/graphics/setrgb4.c:20-42,61-69`). A negative invalid index is converted to a large unsigned value and rejected by the ColorMap setter, but still reaches the unbounded HIDD pixel-table access. No checked-in negative-index `SetRGB4()` caller was found. Later caller tracing did establish maintained positive invalid-index paths through Intuition: GD9937's SetIPrefs offset sends indices 256–259 on an 8-bit Workbench screen; GD9938's depth-four pointer-color decoder produces indices 0x8009–0x800B; and GD9939's one/two-plane sprite-base underflow produces indices 65531–65535. Those caller-specific calculations remain separate findings, while GD5910 records the shared unchecked HIDD pixel-table write they reach. Add a shared `first + count` bounds check before the HIDD table write, while preserving the documented no-op behavior for invalid color indices. `LoadRGB4()` is another route to the same write: its positive caller-supplied `count` controls conversion and it calls `internal_SetRGB32Colors(vp, hidd_colors, 0, count, ...)` after allocation (`rom/graphics/loadrgb4.c:64-99`); if that allocation fails, its per-entry fallback calls `SetRGB32()` (`:67-79`). Thus `LoadRGB4(vp, colors, 257)` also reaches pixel-table index 256 on the affected viewport. Checked-in LoadRGB4 callers use screen-derived `numColors` or fixed 16-entry counts; none above 256 was found. `GetRGB4()` has the related negative-index read recorded separately as GD5768. **Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library configurations using a displayable HIDD bitmap with its 256-entry pixel table, when either a caller supplies an invalid index/range to `SetRGB32()`, `LoadRGB32()`, or `LoadRGB4()`, or the selected Intuition paths in GD9937, GD9938, or GD9939 produce an out-of-range index under their stated screen/depth conditions. **Consequence:** an out-of-bounds write can corrupt adjacent memory. **Confidence:** high for the public no-op contracts, signed-to-unsigned conversion, exact table allocation, unchecked write, and the three selected Intuition caller paths; the stated display/depth conditions remain conditional. No palette operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD5911

**`ExtendFont()` leaks an unlinked hash node when building an extension fails.** For a font with no existing extension hash entry, `ExtendFont()` allocates a `tfe_hashnode` and marks it new before attempting to allocate the extension (`rom/graphics/extendfont.c:72-99`). It only inserts that node into the hash table after the extension, cloned tag list, and any required chunky color-font buffer have all succeeded (`:101-125`; `rom/graphics/fontsupport.c:79-97`). If extension allocation fails, `CloneTagItems()` fails, or `colorfontbm_to_chunkybuffer()` fails, the cleanup frees any allocated extension/tag data but never frees the newly allocated node (`extendfont.c:110-140`). Because the node was not inserted, `StripFont()` cannot find it to reclaim it (`rom/graphics/stripfont.c:61-80`; `fontsupport.c:102-123`). A later `ExtendFont()` retry for the same font misses the unlinked node and allocates another one, so repeated failures can leak one node per attempt. Selected callers include diskfont conversion, which propagates extension failure, and resident-font matching in `OpenFont()`, which continues without extension tags when `ExtendFont()` fails (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfont_io.c:442-469`; `rom/graphics/openfont.c:76-80`). A caller or client retry can then allocate another node. Free the new node on every failed build path. **Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library when `ExtendFont()` is called on a font without a hash entry and extension/tag/color-buffer allocation or color-font conversion fails. **Consequence:** a small `tfe_hashnode` allocation is permanently lost per failed attempt; repeated retries can accumulate the leak. **Confidence:** high for the allocation/link/cleanup mismatch; allocation failure was not induced. No font operation was run; source-only.

## GD5912

**`AndRectRegion()` can leave the list head inside a rectangle chunk, so cleanup leaks the head chunk.** While clipping a region, the function unlinks non-overlapping rectangles and, if the first surviving rectangle is in the middle of a chunk, publishes that interior rectangle as `Reg->RegionRectangle` without normalizing it to the chunk's first rectangle (`rom/graphics/andrectregion.c:108-141`). Each rectangle's `Counter` still records its slot within the 128-entry chunk (`rom/graphics/graphics_intern.h:48,58-67`). Later `_DisposeRegionRectangleList()` frees the chunk containing its start node only when `Counter(RR) == 0`; for an interior start it advances to the next chunk and frees only subsequent chunks (`rom/graphics/intregions.c:180-213`). Thus, if clipping removes an earlier rectangle but retains a later rectangle in that same first chunk, `ClearRegion()` or `DisposeRegion()` leaves the head chunk allocated (`rom/graphics/clearregion.c:54-58`; `disposeregion.c:52-60`). A maintained path is `ScrollRegion()`, which calls `AndRectRegion()` on a temporary region and then disposes it (`rom/graphics/scrollregion.c:68-88`). Preserve a chunk-base head when publishing the clipped list, or make list disposal free the first chunk even when the start node is interior. **Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library when a region has multiple rectangle entries in its first chunk and `AndRectRegion()` clips out an earlier entry while retaining a later entry in that chunk, followed by region cleanup. **Consequence:** one rectangle-chunk allocation remains leaked for each affected region cleanup; repeated use can accumulate leaked region memory. **Confidence:** high for the interior-head and cleanup mismatch; the required region shape was not constructed. No region operation was run; source-only.

## GD5913

**Opposite-direction `ClipBlit()` calls can deadlock while locking layers from different screens.** When source and destination are distinct layers in the same `LayerInfo`, `ClipBlit()` first takes the shared `LayerInfo` semaphore so callers acquire both layer locks in one order. For distinct `LayerInfo` objects, it skips that ordering lock, then obtains the source layer semaphore followed by the destination layer semaphore and holds both for the full blit (`rom/graphics/clipblit.c:113-128,275-279`). `LockLayerRom()` blocks on each layer's semaphore (`rom/graphics/locklayerrom.c:51-67`). The public entry documentation says `ClipBlit()` copies between one RastPort and another and handles layered and non-layered ports (`rom/graphics/clipblit.c:43-48`); it imposes no same-screen restriction. Two tasks concurrently calling `ClipBlit(A→B)` and `ClipBlit(B→A)` for layers on different screens can therefore each hold its source layer and wait indefinitely for the other's. Unlocking occurs only after the blit returns (`clipblit.c:275-279`). Use a system-wide layer ordering rule or otherwise acquire multiple layer locks in a stable order. **Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library with two distinct layers whose `LayerInfo` pointers differ, when concurrent clients issue opposite-direction `ClipBlit()` operations. No checked-in call-site pair establishing that exact cross-screen interleaving was found; the affected path is permitted by the public two-RastPort API and remains conditional on caller concurrency. **Consequence:** both blit tasks can remain blocked on layer semaphores, preventing either operation from completing and leaving those layers unavailable to other users. **Confidence:** high for the inconsistent lock order and blocking acquisition; no concurrent blit was run. Source-only.

## GD5914

**`TextFit()` applies numeric bounds that its contract says to ignore when an extent is supplied.** The function documentation says `constrainingBitWidth` and `constrainingBitHeight` apply only when `constrainingExtent` is NULL (`rom/graphics/textfit.c:34-45`). However, `TextFit()` always rejects the entire request when `constrainingBitHeight < rp->Font->tf_YSize` (`:73`), and in the character loop it always rejects a character when the numeric width is exceeded (`:106-107`), even when a non-NULL extent supplies the actual bounding box. A caller that supplies a valid extent large enough for the text but passes zero or stale numeric limits therefore gets zero or a truncated character count and a zero/short `textExtent`. **Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library clients calling `TextFit()` with non-NULL `constrainingExtent` and numeric width/height values smaller than the text's required dimensions. The checked-in direct callers pass NULL for the extent; the TextEditor `TextFitNew()` wrapper also forwards its caller's extent, but its checked-in callers pass NULL; the non-NULL case is exposed by the public `TextFit()` API without a maintained caller in the reviewed slice (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/NewGfx.c:87-108`). **Consequence:** text is omitted or clipped despite fitting inside the supplied extent, causing incorrect layout/cursor-fit decisions for affected clients. Ignore the numeric limits whenever `constrainingExtent` is non-NULL. **Confidence:** high for the documented contract and unconditional checks; no non-NULL call was run. Source-only.

## GD5915

**`BltClear()` leaves the final byte unchanged for odd contiguous byte counts.** In the generic implementation's direct-count path, it clears complete 32-bit words and, for a two-byte remainder, one 16-bit word; a one-byte remainder is never written (`rom/graphics/bltclear.c:61-73`). The selected m68k Amiga override rounds the byte count down to a word count and submits only those words to the blitter, likewise omitting an odd final byte (`arch/m68k-amiga/graphics/bltclear.c:26-31,54-64`). The API's flags text says bit 1 selects row/bytes-per-row mode, but the following `bytecount` description reverses those modes and separately mentions even counts, so the exact documented odd-count contract is internally inconsistent (`rom/graphics/bltclear.c:27-35`). The finding is limited to callers using the implementation's contiguous direct-count mode with an odd byte count; no checked-in call does so. The reviewed in-tree paths pass even sizes: bitmap allocation uses `RASSIZE()` with an even row stride, Flood uses `WIDTH_TO_BYTES()` rounded to an even byte count per row, and the benchmark passes 32,000 (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:506-532`; `rom/graphics/flood.c:166-176`; `compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:43`; `rom/graphics/graphics_intern.h:286`; `developer/debug/test/benchmarks/graphics/amigademo.c:356-359`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** a caller uses contiguous direct-count mode and passes an odd byte count. **Consequence:** the final byte retains its previous contents, so the requested memory block is not fully cleared. **Confidence:** high for both implementations' odd-byte behavior; medium for contract applicability because the local parameter prose conflicts with the flags description. No odd-sized clear was run; source-only.

## GD5916

**Color-font conversion narrows row geometry and can either skip reads or overrun its chunky buffer.** `colorfontbm_to_chunkybuffer()` sets `width = tf_Modulo * 8`, `height = tf_YSize`, and allocates `width * height` bytes in 32-bit `ULONG` arithmetic (`rom/graphics/fontsupport.c:130-139`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:39-43`). It then passes the wide geometry through `InitBitMap()`'s `UWORD` width and `ReadPixelArray8()`'s `WORD` coordinates (`fontsupport.c:144-157`; `rom/graphics/initbitmap.c:19-22`; `rom/graphics/readpixelarray8.c:40-49`). For `tf_Modulo=16385` and `tf_YSize=32767`, width is 131,080 pixels and the product wraps from 4,295,098,360 to 131,064 bytes. `InitBitMap()` truncates width to 8; `ReadPixelArray8()` truncates `xstop` to 7 and sets a 16-byte output row stride (`initbitmap.c:63-68`; `readpixelarray8.c:100-123`). Its row callback writes 8 pixels per row at that stride (`readpixelarray8.c:21-32`), so the final row reaches byte 524,263, well past the 131,064-byte allocation. `ExtendFont()` invokes this conversion for non-antialiased color fonts (`rom/graphics/extendfont.c:110-116`). A second, lower-size failure follows from the same unchecked geometry handoff: `tf_Modulo` and `tf_YSize` are UWORD fields (`compiler/include/graphics/text.h:25,35`), and `ConvDiskFont()` copies these fields and allocates/copies color-font plane data using `tf_YSize * tf_Modulo` without imposing a width cap (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfont_io.c:149,159,210,287-295`). With `tf_Modulo=4097` and `tf_YSize=16`, the source row width is 32,776 pixels and each selected plane needs 65,552 bytes. `InitBitMap()` narrows that width to UWORD value 8; the `ReadPixelArray8()` call narrows `xstop=32775` to a negative WORD on the common 16-bit target ABI. Its `xstart > xstop` check then returns zero before reading pixels (`readpixelarray8.c:100-111`). The helper ignores that return, and because `AllocVec()` requested `MEMF_CLEAR`, extension succeeds with an all-zero chunky color-font buffer (`fontsupport.c:138-157`; `extendfont.c:110-121`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library when extending a real color font with `tf_Modulo=16385`, `tf_YSize=32767` (or another geometry where the `ULONG` product wraps while the narrowed read still writes beyond the allocation); this extreme example requires about 512 MiB of character-plane data per selected plane. A separately representable 32,776-pixel-wide font row (`tf_Modulo=4097`, `tf_YSize=16`) reaches the zero-result/blank-conversion path if accepted by the font loader. The loader fields can encode it and no source-side maximum was found, but practical availability of such fonts is unverified. **Consequence:** the extreme case lets `ReadPixelArray8()` write beyond the chunky buffer, potentially corrupting adjacent memory or faulting; the smaller case silently produces an all-zero converted color font. Validate geometry and use checked, padded allocation arithmetic before conversion, and check the pixel-read result. **Confidence:** high for the integer truncation and output bounds; medium for the smaller case's path after loader parsing, and low-medium for practical reachability of either oversized font because no maintained caller/font establishing one was found. No font or allocation was created; source-only.

## GD5917

**Compositor registration accepts an unregistered method interface when a class advertises the compositor class ID.** `compositor_Install()` obtains `IID_Hidd_Compositor`'s attribute base, then calls `OOP_GetMethodID(IID_Hidd_Compositor, 0)` and rejects only a zero result (`rom/graphics/graphics_compositor.c:29-42`). `OOP_ObtainAttrBase()` creates an IID-table bucket with `methodbase = (ULONG)-1` when no method interface has been registered (`rom/oop/obtainattrbase.c:79-106`). `OOP_GetMethodID()` finds that bucket and returns `methodbase + methodOffset`, so for offset zero the result is `ULONG_MAX`, not zero (`rom/oop/getmethodid.c:59-77`); the compositor install check therefore accepts the failure sentinel. `AddDisplayDriverA()` routes any class matching `CLID_Hidd_Compositor` into this installer (`rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:172-178`). If that class lacks a registered compositor method interface, installation stores it and reports success. Later `compositor_IsBMCompositable()` and `compositor_SetBMCompositable()` form method IDs by adding offsets to the invalid base (`graphics_compositor.c:75-97`); the compositor interface defines validation and enable at offsets 4 and 5, yielding IDs 3 and 4 instead of registered compositor methods (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/include/compositor.h:37-45`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** a compositor class is passed to `AddDisplayDriverA()` with the compositor class ID but without a successfully registered `IID_Hidd_Compositor` method table. The checked-in Compositor startup registers a method descriptor before adding its class (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_startup.c:35-52,84-95`), and the checked AmigaVideo/Nouveau/IntelGMA compositor definitions also declare the interface; no in-tree malformed registration path was found. **Consequence:** graphics.library accepts an invalid compositor class and later dispatches bitmap validation/enable calls using unrelated method IDs, leading to incorrect method behavior or failure. Reject `ULONG_MAX` (and ensure the method base is initialized) rather than testing only for zero. **Confidence:** high for the sentinel arithmetic and install check; low-medium for practical reachability because the trigger requires a malformed or partially registered compositor class and no checked-in caller supplies one. No class registration or compositor dispatch was run; source-only.

## GD5918

**Hardware ranges ending at the CPU address-space boundary are treated as non-overlapping.** `driver_RangesOverlap()` checks half-open ranges with `abase < bbase + bsize && bbase < abase + asize`, using `IPTR` arithmetic without checking endpoint overflow (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:176-193`). If two reported ranges both end exactly at the address-space limit, each endpoint wraps to zero. For example, on a 32-bit target, base `0xfffff000` with size `0x1000` represents the final 4 KiB; comparing that range with itself makes both strict comparisons false after wrap, and the function reports no overlap. `driver_FindBootDisplay()` uses this result to decide whether an incoming native driver is about to take over the boot display's hardware (`graphics_driver.c:220-245`); `AddDisplayDriverA()` exposes the range array through `DDRV_HWRanges`, whose entries are CPU address ranges (`compiler/include/graphics/driver.h:29,40-48`; `rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:50-64`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** a boot-mode and incoming driver report valid mapped CPU ranges whose half-open endpoint is exactly `UINTPTR_MAX + 1` (or otherwise overflows `IPTR`) and which overlap. The matched ranges are then treated as disjoint; if no other range pair overlaps, the boot driver is not selected for handover and may remain active while the incoming driver takes ownership. The selected Nouveau caller constructs up to six ranges from each PCI BAR’s CPU-translated start and resource length, then passes them to the finder before probing the card (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:267-315,435-444`). This confirms that the comparator receives PCI aperture ranges, but the checked-in tree does not establish a BAR whose translated half-open endpoint reaches the address-space boundary. The EFI framebuffer ranges reviewed so far likewise are not shown to reach it. **Consequence:** a boot display can be left active over hardware the new driver is taking over, potentially leaving the old display path using remapped or reprogrammed resources. Use overflow-safe interval comparisons. **Confidence:** high for the wrap and comparison result; low-medium for practical reachability because no selected in-tree caller supplies such a range. No range comparison, handover or driver registration was run; source-only.

## GD5919

**`MakeVPort()` frees a temporary ViewPortExtra without releasing its allocated viewport data on failure.** When the viewport has no existing graphics node, `MakeVPort()` allocates and associates a temporary `ViewPortExtra`, marks it `VPXF_FREE_ME`, and sets `own_vpe` (`rom/graphics/makevport.c:91-107`). It then allocates `HIDD_ViewPortData` into `vpe->DriverData[0]` (`:109-112`). A later failure can occur when wrapping a planar bitmap fails or `HIDD_Display_MakeViewPort()` returns an error (`:132-166,200-215`). On error, the function calls only `GfxFree(&vpe->n)` for a newly-created node (`:238-243`). `GfxFree()` unlinks and frees the `ViewPortExtra`, but does not free its `DriverData[0]` (`rom/graphics/gfxfree.c:69-111`). The normal cleanup in `FreeVPortCopLists()` does release `HIDD_ViewPortData` and an owned wrapped bitmap (`rom/graphics/freevportcoplists.c:60-92`), but it can no longer find the node after `GfxFree()` removes it from the association table. If a wrapped planar bitmap object was created before `HIDD_Display_MakeViewPort()` fails, the error rollback disposes it only when `vpd->PreviousBitmap` is non-NULL; a newly-created VPD has no previous bitmap, so that owned object is also abandoned (`makevport.c:159-166,218-243`). The selected `OpenScreen()` caller marks the open unsuccessful on a nonzero result but continues publishing the screen and does not call `FreeVPortCopLists()` on this path (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:2476-2500`), so it does not reclaim these temporary allocations. There is also an in-tree path with a pre-associated VPE: `OpenScreen()` allocates one and attaches it to the ColorMap with `VTAG_VIEWPORTEXTRA_SET` (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1485,1542-1545,1590-1594`; `rom/graphics/videocontrol.c:73-75,391-395`). `MakeVPort()` then finds this node, leaves `own_vpe` false, but allocates `HIDD_ViewPortData` before attempting the display setup (`rom/graphics/makevport.c:97-114,218`). No allocation failure or viewport setup was induced; source-only.

**`VideoControl()` returns success when given no tag items, contrary to its documented result.** The function initializes `res` to zero and sets it to nonzero only while processing an unknown tag in the loop (`rom/graphics/videocontrol.c:62-66,394-397`). Return an error when no tag item was processed. **Confidence:** high for the documented contract and return path; practical impact is limited to callers that submit no items, and no maintained empty-list caller was found. No VideoControl call was run; source-only.

## GD5922

**`OwnBlitter()` does not serialize shared owner state across CPUs on ExecSMP.** The routine reads and writes `GfxBase->BlitOwner` and inserts its stack-local waiter node into the shared `BlitWaitQ` while using only `Disable()` (`rom/graphics/ownblitter.c:68-81`). Exec documents that `Disable()` masks interrupts only on the calling processor in ExecSMP builds and requires a spinlock to protect data from parallel access (`rom/exec/disable.c:55-60`). Two CPUs can therefore both observe `BlitOwner == NULL`, publish different owners, and return as though each has exclusive access. Queue insertion/removal and `DisownBlitter()`'s empty-check/head-read/signal sequence also lack cross-CPU protection (`rom/graphics/disownblitter.c:72-82`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** an ExecSMP system where tasks on separate CPUs concurrently call `OwnBlitter()` while ownership is free, or manipulate the waiter list concurrently with `DisownBlitter()`. **Consequence:** multiple callers can believe they own the blitter at once, allowing unsynchronized blits; waiter nodes/signals can also be lost or corrupted under concurrent queue changes. Protect the owner and waiter list with an SMP-safe lock while preserving interrupt-context constraints. **Confidence:** high for the missing cross-CPU synchronization and documented `Disable()` semantics; practical impact depends on an ExecSMP target/client using the shared blitter API. Checked-in direct hardware blitter users are m68k-specific, and no parallel API call was run; source-only.

## GD5923

**QBlit/QBSBlit queues have no consumer on selected targets other than AmigaVideo.** Both public vectors append nodes to `GfxBase` queues; on an empty pair they also call `OwnBlitter()` before publishing the first node. The only in-tree code that reads and drains these queues is the AmigaVideo `gfx_blit` interrupt handler (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_chipset.c:1171-1228`; repository-wide queue-field census). The queue-start code in each vector is otherwise a comment; a synthetic interrupt is requested only under `(AROS_FLAVOUR & AROS_FLAVOUR_BINCOMPAT) && defined(mc68000)` (`rom/graphics/qblit.c:72-100`; `qbsblit.c:69-97`). The default `amiga-m68k` configure path sets `aros_flavour="standcompat"`, which includes `AROS_FLAVOUR_BINCOMPAT` (`configure.in:2273-2280`; flavour mapping `:4594-4597`); thus its selected AmigaVideo handler receives the first-node kick and the earlier idle-Amiga trigger does not apply. On other selected Graphics.library targets, no queue-draining worker or interrupt handler is present, so queued callbacks have no in-tree service path. The public API documentation promises the callback when the blitter is ready and says blitter operations are simulated when hardware lacks a blitter (`qblit.c:36-58`; `qbsblit.c:35-57`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** a caller uses `QBlit()` or `QBSBlit()` on a selected target that builds the public vectors but has neither the AmigaVideo queue consumer nor an equivalent platform worker; the queue remains unserviced even after first-node insertion. A repository-wide call census found no maintained native C caller; generated m68k emulator thunks are present (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3180-3185,3210-3215`) but the emulator library is not selected by the aggregate ROM edges in this snapshot (`rom/mmakefile.src:10,89,121`). **Consequence:** the callback remains pending, the first queue's `BlitOwner` is not released, and callers awaiting completion can stall; later `OwnBlitter()` calls can remain blocked. Provide a queue consumer for each supported target or make the vectors reject/complete unsupported requests consistently. **Confidence:** high that only AmigaVideo consumes the queues in-tree and other selected targets have no consumer; practical impact is conditional on external or future API calls. The default `amiga-m68k` compatibility build is excluded from the no-kick case. No queue, blit, interrupt, emulator call, or build was run; source-only.

## GD5924

**Selected caller/reachability recheck (expanded 2026-10-24):** The generic mode enumerator iterates pixel formats inside each sync mode and preserves the driver's pixel-format tag order (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:175-256`). A concrete selected path is the RISC-V OpenSBI Headless HIDD: its boot manifest selects the module and its manifest builds the `Headless` monitor loader (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:51`; `rom/hidds/gfx/headless/mmakefile.src:4-24`). With default tooltypes, the monitor passes no fixed depth; Headless defaults `MAXDEPTH` to 24 and registers the ascending 8-, 16-, and 24-bit formats at its single sync mode (`headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:136-145,187-218,254-277`; `disk_startup.c:43-48,91-107,145-175`). Its inherited `NoFrameBuffer=FALSE` maps to `vHidd_FrameBuffer_Direct` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:756-770,861-870`), and graphics.library creates a default framebuffer for direct modes (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:149-170,413-429`). All Headless formats share the configured width and height, so the chooser sees equal pixel areas: it records the first 8-bit mode, advances `best_depth` for 16 and 24 bits, but its strict `res > best_resolution` check never replaces the selected mode. The resulting default framebuffer is 8-bit despite the selected 24-bit mode. `Headless`'s separate `NominalDepth` setting controls later screen-mode selection and does not alter this enumeration order or framebuffer chooser.

The other selected multi-format tables checked here are depth-descending in Radeon, NVIDIA, Nouveau, SAGA, VideoCore, and Intel GMA. P96 and AmigaVideo enumerate lower depths first, but their HIDDs report `NoFrameBuffer=TRUE` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_hiddclass.c:726-738`; `arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:797-808`); SAGA also reports no framebuffer (`sagagfx_hiddclass.c:385-400`), so these do not reach this default-framebuffer chooser. Other enumerators supply one format per mode or a single framebuffer format. This narrows the confirmed selected in-tree trigger to the default RISC-V OpenSBI Headless monitor configuration; other public HIDD orderings remain a conditional API surface.

**The default framebuffer chooser can keep a larger lower-depth mode after finding a higher-depth mode.** `get_best_resolution_and_depth()` updates `best_depth` whenever the current mode reaches that depth, but only updates the selected mode when pixel area exceeds the single `best_resolution` accumulated across all depths (`rom/graphics/dispinfo.c:34-61`). For example, if a 24-bit 1920×1080 mode appears before a 32-bit 1280×720 mode, the first mode sets `ret` and `best_resolution`; the second raises `best_depth` to 32 but cannot replace `ret` because its resolution is lower. The helper therefore returns a 24-bit mode despite the available 32-bit mode. `display_FBCreate()` calls this helper when creating the default framebuffer and documents its intent as selecting the highest resolution at the best available depth (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:413-429`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the build-selected RISC-V OpenSBI Headless HIDD/monitor when registered with default `MAXDEPTH` and no `FORCEDEPTH` tooltype; its 8/16/24-bit modes share one resolution and are registered in ascending depth order. Other public HIDDs can trigger the same defect if they provide lower-depth formats first and create a direct or mirrored default framebuffer. **Consequence:** graphics.library creates an 8-bit default framebuffer even though the selected Headless display supports 24-bit modes. Choose maximum depth first, then maximum resolution among modes at that depth. **Confidence:** high for the chooser and selected Headless source path; runtime mode registration and framebuffer creation were not exercised. No mode enumeration or framebuffer was run; source-only.

## GD5926

**`WeighTAMatch()` computes font-size distance after converting unsigned sizes to signed words.** `TextAttr.ta_YSize` is a `UWORD` (`compiler/include/graphics/text.h:72-78`), but the matcher casts both operands to `WORD` before subtracting and calling `abs()` (`rom/graphics/weightamatch.c:72-74`). Thus UWORD values 65535 and 0 become -1 and 0, giving a computed difference of one instead of 65,535; the function can assign a near-perfect size score to a radically different font. Conversely, sizes 32767 and 32768 narrow to 32767 and -32768, producing a computed distance of 65,535 and an immediate zero score although their actual difference is one. The returned score is used to rank in-memory and diskfont candidates (`rom/graphics/openfont.c:76-82`; `workbench/libs/diskfont/opendiskfont.c:97-140`; `diskfontfunc.c:1352-1377`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** a public caller requests or a font advertises a `ta_YSize` above `WORD_MAX`; bitmap and outline candidate matching both pass through this matcher. **Consequence:** diskfont can reject the closest available size or prefer a much less suitable candidate. Compute the difference in an unsigned or wider type without narrowing first. **Confidence:** high for the casts and arithmetic; practical impact is limited to unusually large UWORD sizes, and no such font search was run. Source-only.

## GD5927

**`WeighTAMatch()` can make a large size mismatch outrank closer in-memory fonts.** When the requested size is smaller than the target size, the matcher computes `sizediff << 7` and stores it in signed `WORD sizematch` (rom/graphics/weightamatch.c:95-103). For an upward difference from 256 through 511, that product is outside the signed WORD range; on the selected two’s-complement targets it narrows to a negative value. With no style mismatch, the initial score is 32767, so subtracting the negative penalty produces a value above 32767 which narrows again when assigned back to signed `WORD matchweight` and returned (:57-58,100-105). The selected `OpenFont()` caller receives this result into an unsigned `UWORD match`, then compares it with signed `WORD bestmatch` and can select the candidate as a high positive weight when it is visited after a closer same-name candidate (rom/graphics/openfont.c:55-56,65-84); the integer promotions on the selected 32-bit and 64-bit targets preserve that unsigned value in the comparison. This gives a concrete in-tree consumer for the wrapped score without requiring style differences. Diskfont’s separate selection variables are signed WORD; its path can still accept a positive score when style penalties reduce the base enough; style scoring is at rom/graphics/weightamatch.c:73-86, and diskfont selection is at workbench/libs/diskfont/opendiskfont.c:97-140 and diskfontfunc.c:1352-1377.

**Trigger and consequence:** on a two’s-complement target, an in-memory font with the requested name has a size 256–511 pixels larger than the requested `ta_YSize`. If visited after a closer same-name candidate, its narrowed negative result is converted to a high unsigned score by `OpenFont()` and can replace that candidate; if it is the only same-name candidate, it can be returned despite the large size mismatch. On diskfont selection, the previously identified positive-score case additionally requires enough style-mismatch bits to be cleared that the narrowed penalty leaves a positive signed score. **Affected configuration:** graphics.library’s selected `OpenFont()` path on targets with two’s-complement WORD narrowing; the candidate size and font-name match must meet the conditions above. **Confidence:** high for the arithmetic and caller conversions on selected targets; practical reachability depends on unusually large in-memory font sizes, and no font search was run. Calculate the penalty and final score in a wider signed type, rejecting out-of-range penalties before returning a WORD. No font search was run; source-only.

## GD5928

**Reinitializing a user copper list leaves its count at capacity and may leave the active cursor on an old extension list.** When `UCopperListInit()` sees an existing first buffer, it sets `FirstCopList->Count = FirstCopList->MaxCount` and rewinds only `FirstCopList->CopPtr`; it does not reset `ucl->CopList` to the first list (`rom/graphics/ucopperlistinit.c:59-65`). If the active list is the first list, the first subsequent `CBump()` increments Count past MaxCount, so its equality check never triggers a new segment and the cursor advances beyond the original buffer (`rom/graphics/cbump.c:56-99`). If a previous fill left `ucl->CopList` on an extension segment, reinitialization leaves the active pointer there and does not reset that segment's Count/CopPtr either. The `CMOVE`/`CWAIT` macros write at `CopList->CopPtr` and only then call `CBump()` (`compiler/include/graphics/gfxmacros.h:51-53,92-103`; `rom/graphics/cmove.c:55-61`; `cwait.c:57-63`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** a client reuses an already initialized `UCopList` after writing instructions, especially after it has grown beyond the first segment, then emits more instructions. No maintained macro caller was found. **Consequence:** the new list can append to stale instructions or write past a copper-instruction buffer instead of starting from a clean list. Reset the active list, all reused segments' cursors/counts, and the link sentinel consistently. **Confidence:** high for the incomplete reset and count boundary; public-client exposure only, with no list reuse run. Source-only.

## GD5929

**Copper-list growth allocation failure leaves the void macros able to write beyond the full instruction buffer.** `CBump()` increments Count before checking whether the current segment is full. When it reaches `MaxCount`, it tries to allocate an extension node and then its ten-instruction buffer; either failure returns without advancing the current cursor or reporting an error (`rom/graphics/cbump.c:56-81`). `CBump()` returns void, as do `CMove()` and `CWait()`, and the public `CMOVE`/`CWAIT` macros write an instruction before calling `CBump()` (`compiler/include/graphics/gfxmacros.h:51-53,92-103`; `rom/graphics/cmove.c:55-61`; `cwait.c:57-63`). If the caller continues after the failed growth, its next instruction overwrites the last valid slot; the next bump increments Count beyond MaxCount and advances the pointer, and a subsequent instruction writes out of bounds. When the node allocation succeeds but its instruction-buffer allocation fails, the empty node remains linked in `Next`; `FreeCopList()` later traverses and frees that node, and Exec `FreeMem(NULL, 0)` is a no-op (`rom/graphics/freecoplist.c:50-63`; `rom/exec/freemem.c:64-66`). Ordinary continuation increments the still-active segment's Count past MaxCount, so the linked empty node is not selected on a later `CBump()` in this path; no NULL-cursor retry consequence is established. **Affected configuration and trigger:** a client fills a user copper segment, extension allocation fails, and it continues emitting instructions without an externally available failure indication. No maintained macro caller was found. **Consequence:** silent instruction loss followed by out-of-bounds writes. An error-reporting/status mechanism and safe rollback are needed before callers continue. **Confidence:** high for cursor/count state after either allocation failure and the conditional subsequent out-of-bounds writes; impact requires a public client to continue building after the void call. No allocation failure or copper list was run; source-only.

**Radeon on-screen bitmap allocation failure frees the failure sentinel as a VRAM offset.** `ATIOnBM::New` initializes `bm->fbgfx = TRUE` and stores `AllocBitmapArea()`'s result in `bm->framebuffer` (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_bitmap.c:102-112`). `BitmapAlloc()` returns `0xffffffff` when no contiguous framebuffer range is available (`workbench/hidds/radeon/bitmap.c:460-488`). It then calls `bmclr()` with `ptr >> 10` as the bit offset; `bmclr()` advances the allocation bitmap pointer by `bitoffset >> 5` before writing (`bitmap.c:135-165`). No bitmap, VRAM allocation failure or hardware was exercised; source-only.

**Radeon 15-bit alpha blits store fully opaque source pixels as black.** In the `bm->depth == 15` path of `ATIOnBM::PutAlphaImage()`, `destpix` is initialized to zero. **DisplayAlert can perform an unaligned word load on m68k for a valid multi-line message.** Its documented input format stores each line as a two-byte X coordinate, one-byte baseline, NUL-terminated text, and one continuation byte; a nonzero continuation byte starts the next record immediately, with no padding (`rom/intuition/displayalert.c:35-43`). `requester_makebody()` reads the coordinate using `*((UWORD *)s)` (`rom/intuition/requesters.h:143-151`), then advances over the coordinate, baseline, text terminator, and continuation byte (`:152-155`). Source-only.

Source-only.

## GD5962

**X11 framebuffer setup never frees the allocated class-hint structure.** `x11gfx_onbitmap.c` calls `XAllocClassHint()`, fills the fields with static strings, and passes the structure to `XSetClassHint()` without releasing it (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11gfx_onbitmap.c:175-182`). A complete search of the file finds no corresponding `XFree(classhint)`. The Xlib API specifies that `XAllocClassHint()` allocates the structure and that callers free it with `XFree()`; `XSetClassHint()` sets the property but does not take ownership ([XAllocClassHint/XSetClassHint documentation](https://xorg.freedesktop.org/archive/X11R7.5/doc/man/man3/XSetClassHint.3.html)).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** each successful hosted X11 window setup reaches this class-hint allocation. **Consequence:** the host-side class-hint allocation is leaked per window setup. The string fields point to literals, so the missing release concerns the allocated structure. **Confidence:** high for the local missing release and documented Xlib ownership; no X11 window was created. Source-only.

## GD5963

Source-only.

## GD5964

**X11 PseudoColor icon drawing never releases allocated colormap cells.** In `init_icon()`, each icon pixel on a PseudoColor visual calls `XAllocColor()` and uses the returned pixel, but the function never records allocated pixel values or calls `XFreeColors()` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11gfx_onbitmap.c:593-609`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** hosted X11 with a PseudoColor visual; icon creation reaches pixels for which `XAllocColor()` succeeds. **Consequence:** the persistent X11 client retains each allocated cell reference, including repeated references to the same color; repeated window/icon creation can exhaust available colormap allocations. **Confidence:** high for the allocation loop, missing release, and Xlib ownership/counting contract; no PseudoColor display or icon creation was run. Source-only.

## GD5965

**X11 initialization rollback can leave the host-clipboard port published after its event task exits.** The X11 event task signals its parent that startup succeeded, then calls `x11clipboard_init()`, which creates `hostclipboardmp` and publishes it under `HOST_CLIPBOARD` with `AddPort()` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11.c:407-411`; `x11_clipboard.c:70-83`). The event task's exit cleanup deletes only `x11task_notify_port`; it does not `RemPort()` or delete `hostclipboardmp` (`x11.c:680-687`). Thus, if the worker has published the clipboard port before this rollback, the named port remains discoverable with its owning task gone.

There is a scheduling window because the worker publishes the clipboard port after signaling the parent. **Consequence:** clients that find and send requests to `HOST_CLIPBOARD` can enqueue work with no event task to service or reply to it; a later startup may also encounter the stale published name. **Confidence:** high for publication and missing shutdown removal; conditional reachability depends on the startup interleaving and class-initialization failure, neither was induced. Source-only.

## GD5966

**X11 clipboard selection writes omit INCR transfers and acknowledge property writes without checking their outcome.** For `XA_STRING`, the handler computes a request-size threshold but leaves the size condition commented out and has an unconditional `if (1)` branch; it passes the entire clipboard buffer to one `XChangeProperty()` request and has the INCR path marked TODO (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11_clipboard.c:448-477`). ICCCM's selection-owner conventions require large selection data to use INCR and require the owner to confirm that storing the property did not fail before sending a confirming SelectionNotify ([ICCCM Large Data Transfers](https://xorg.freedesktop.org/releases/current/doc/xorg-docs/icccm/icccm.html#large-data-transfers)).

Source-only.

## GD5967

**X11 shared-memory initialization accepts the `shmat()` failure sentinel as a valid mapping.** After successful `shmget()`, `init_shared_mem()` stores `shmat()`'s result and checks only `NULL != shminfo->shmaddr` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11_xshm.c:148-160`). Source-only.

## GD5969

**X11 HIDD startup calls `HW_AddDriver()` on objects that do not implement the `HW` interface, so startup fails before registering input drivers.** `X11_Startup()` constructs `CLID_Hidd_Kbd` and `CLID_Hidd_Mouse`, then calls `HW_AddDriver()` directly on those objects (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/startup.c:65-83`). OOP returns zero when an object lacks the requested method/interface (`rom/oop/metaclass.c:752-799`). Therefore `kbdriver` is NULL, the mouse call is skipped, and the `!msdriver` branch makes startup return FALSE (`startup.c:75-104`). On this failure return, neither successfully constructed input object is passed to `OOP_DisposeObject()`; likewise, if only one `OOP_NewObject()` succeeds, the partial-construction failure branch closes `graphics.library` and returns without disposing the successful object (`startup.c:62-70`). Source-only.
