## GD5984

**IntelGMA registers its graphics driver even when creation of the display HIDD meta-class failed.** Startup creates `sd.IntelG45DisplayClass`, but only sets its `UserData` on success and does not include the result in the later initialization gate (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_startup.c:205-218,224-253`). After `G45_Init()` succeeds, it registers `sd.IntelG45Class` through `AddDisplayDriverA()` (`:251-265`). When graphics.library instantiates that class, its `Root::New` calls `OOP_NewObject(sd->IntelG45DisplayClass, NULL, displaytags)` (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_hiddclass.c:542-554`); with a NULL class and class ID, `OOP_NewObject()` returns NULL (`rom/oop/newobject.c:76-84`). The HIDD `Root::New` nevertheless returns its successfully constructed graphics object, and the compositor constructor rejects the NULL display and returns NULL (`intelgma_compositorclass.c:412-445`). `driver_Setup()` accepts the HIDD instance even if it exposes no display, while `G45_Init()` uses `sd->PCIDevice` as its success criterion (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:369-402`; `intelgma_init.c:500-505`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** IntelGMA monitor startup when display-class allocation fails but subsequent required class creation and hardware initialization succeed. **Consequence:** startup can remain resident after reporting success, although graphics.library has no registered display for the driver and compositor creation failed. Treat display-class creation as required and unwind on failure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked class result and caller chain; allocation failure was not induced. Source-only.

## GD5985

**IntelGMA startup leaks its display meta-class when later initialization fails.** Startup creates `sd.IntelG45DisplayClass` after `sd.IntelG45Class` and before bitmap, I2C and compositor meta-classes (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_startup.c:205-247`). On the failure path, nested cleanup disposes the compositor, I2C, bitmap and graphics classes, then releases attribute bases, but never disposes `sd.IntelG45DisplayClass` (`:274-294`). Any subsequent failure after display-class creation—for example a later meta-class allocation failure or `G45_Init()` returning false—therefore leaves that meta-class object and its OOP resources allocated after startup returns and closes its libraries. The successful driver path intentionally stays resident and is not the leak case. **Affected configuration and trigger:** IntelGMA monitor startup when display-class construction succeeds and any later required class or hardware initialization step fails. **Consequence:** retained OOP meta-class resources after failed startup; repeated failed attempts can accumulate those resources. Add the display class to the failure unwind in dependency-safe order. **Confidence:** high for allocation and asymmetric cleanup; failure was not induced. Source-only.

## GD5986

**IntelGMA's 3D CopyBox path checks the source bitmap's graphics-memory flag twice and can send a system-memory destination address to the GPU.** The eligibility condition is `!(bm_src->fbgfx && bm_src->fbgfx)` instead of requiring both `bm_src` and `bm_dst` to be graphics-backed (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_copybox.c:97-115`). Distinct-bitmap CopyBox calls this helper and falls back to the superclass only when it returns FALSE (`intelgma_hiddclass.c:880-903`). Displayable bitmaps use `AllocBitmapArea()` and set `fbgfx = TRUE`; non-displayable bitmaps can instead use ordinary `AllocMem()` and set `fbgfx = FALSE` (`intelgma_bitmapclass.c:100-110,165-190`). Once admitted, the 3D path programs `bm_dst->framebuffer` directly as the GPU color target (`intelgma_copybox.c:230-252`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** supported IntelGMA generation-3 chipsets, distinct source/destination bitmaps, source graphics-backed, destination system-memory-backed, supported source/destination pixel widths, and a CopyBox geometry accepted by the 3D path. **Consequence:** GPU commands use a CPU system-memory pointer as the destination surface address; the intended software fallback is skipped, so copy results are invalid and may access an address not mapped for GPU use. Require `bm_dst->fbgfx` as well as `bm_src->fbgfx` before issuing commands. **Confidence:** high for the duplicated predicate, allocation classes, caller selection and target address; GPU behavior was not exercised. Source-only.

## GD5987

**IntelGMA's Gallium batch-buffer destroy callback passes a winsys pointer read from its freed batch object.** `IntelGMA_WS_BatchbufferDestroy()` derives `gmabatch` from the callback argument, frees its CPU map and graphics allocation, then frees `gmabatch` before evaluating `gmabatch->iws` for `IntelGMA_ReleaseBuffers()` (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_galliumclass.c:454-470`). The helper reads `iws->buffer_is_busy` while traversing cached buffers (`:198-225`). The selected callback implementation ignores its first `iws` parameter, and several other call sites deliberately pass zero (`:403,589,836`); those zero callback arguments do not cause this finding. The destroy path instead has to dereference the indeterminate `gmabatch->iws` to fetch the callback pointer. It holds `UnusedBuffersListLock` before calling the helper, and `AttemptSemaphore()` nests when the current task already owns the semaphore (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:164-202`), so the cache traversal is reachable when the unused-buffer list is nonempty. **Affected configuration and trigger:** an IntelGMA Gallium batch-buffer destroy callback, with a nonempty unused-buffer list and a target that exercises the optional Gallium interface. The callback is exposed to the linked Mesa integration; no in-tree call to this exact destroy callback was found, so the call sequence is conditional on that integration. **Consequence:** evaluating `gmabatch->iws` after freeing `gmabatch` can supply an indeterminate object pointer, and the helper then reads its callback field, causing invalid access or a fault during destruction. Save `iws` before freeing the batch object and pass the saved value. **Confidence:** high for the source-order lifetime defect and helper dereference; the external callback trigger and runtime manifestation were not exercised. Source-only.

## GD5988

**IntelGMA's Gallium batch-buffer constructor mishandles both CPU-map and graphics-memory allocation failures.** After `CALLOC_STRUCT()` succeeds, the constructor allocates `batch->base.map` with `MALLOC()` but never checks that result; it then requests graphics memory and returns NULL directly if that allocation fails (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_galliumclass.c:264-292`). If CPU-map allocation failed but graphics allocation succeeds, `IntelGMA_BatchBufferReset()` immediately calls `memset()` through the NULL map (`:119-127,288-290`). If graphics allocation fails, the already allocated batch object and CPU map are not freed before returning NULL (`:270-278`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** IntelGMA Gallium batch-buffer creation when either allocation fails. **Consequence:** CPU-map failure can fault during constructor reset; graphics-memory failure leaks the CPU map and batch object. Check both allocations and unwind whichever succeeded before returning failure. **Confidence:** high for ordering, unchecked NULL and missing unwind; no allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

## GD5989

**AmigaVideo native-mode enumeration dereferences a failed mode-node allocation.** `addmodeid()` allocates a `NativeChipsetMode` and immediately writes its fields and links it into the list without checking the result (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:263-276`). The display HIDD's `Root::New` calls `addmodeid()` for every standard mode it advertises before registering the mode tags (`:360-402`), so a single node-allocation failure reaches `m->width` and faults during mode enumeration. The selected AmigaVideo startup registers this HIDD through graphics.library (`startup.c:34-48`; selected in `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:158,375`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** m68k AmigaVideo HIDD initialization when the `NativeChipsetMode` allocation fails for any enumerated mode. **Consequence:** NULL dereference aborts HIDD construction/driver setup instead of returning a usable mode list or a clean failure. Check each allocation and unwind the partial list. **Confidence:** high for unchecked allocation and immediate dereference; memory failure was not induced. Source-only.

## GD5990

**AmigaVideo can orphan its display service task when shutdown and redraw signals arrive together.** `DisplayServiceTask()` waits for `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C | SIGBREAKF_CTRL_F` and switches on exact equality with each single signal (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_compositorclass.c:516-532`). Exec `Wait()` returns the entire intersection of pending signals with the wait mask, then clears all bits in that mask before returning (`rom/exec/wait.c:128-137`). If redraw and shutdown are both pending, neither `case` matches and both signals are consumed; the loop does not set `svcdie`, clear `csd->svcTask`, or close its `IntuitionBase`.

The shutdown sender is the compositor's `Root::Dispose()`, which signals `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C` and immediately calls superclass disposal without waiting for the worker (`amigavideo_compositorclass.c:117-127`). The redraw sender is `gfx_vblank_attachbm()`: when a non-interlaced display is asked to attach an interlaced bitmap, it sends `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_F` to `csd->svcTask` so the service worker will call `RethinkDisplay()` (`amigavideo_chipset.c:1327-1335`; worker branch at `amigavideo_compositorclass.c:521-525`). This interrupt-side event can race with compositor disposal. On the combined-signal path the worker loops back into `Wait()` after the compositor object has been disposed; it retains its task and open Intuition-library reference. Since the disposed object's `housekeeper` pointer is lost and the worker did not clear the shared `csd->svcTask`, later teardown cannot reliably signal that old task, and a newly created compositor can overwrite `csd->svcTask` with another worker.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** selected m68k AmigaVideo compositor after its housekeeper task has started, when a VBlank redraw request and compositor disposal cause both control signals to be pending at the same `Wait()`. **Consequence:** the shutdown request is lost, leaving an orphan service task and an open Intuition-library reference; later display rebuild notifications may continue to target the orphan until `csd->svcTask` is overwritten. Handle bits independently and give shutdown precedence, then join or otherwise confirm worker exit before releasing its owner state. **Confidence:** high for combined-bit consumption and exact-match fallthrough; the scheduling window and resulting resource leak require the described overlap. No disposal, VBlank signal or task schedule was run; source-only.

## GD5991

**AmigaVideo uses an uninitialized overlap adjustment when revealing same-mode hidden screens.** In the downward-move reveal loop, `adjust` is assigned only when the moved bitmap and an obscured candidate have different interlace modes (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_chipset.c:1665-1685`). If their modes match and `toptmp < topvis`, `gfx_vblank_attachbm()` can successfully make the candidate visible; the code then reads the uninitialized `adjust` to set `topvis = toptmp - adjust` (`:1687-1703`). That threshold determines whether later, higher-priority obscured screens are also reattached during the same scan. The missing same-mode value should account for the candidate's own `copld.extralines + 2`; only cross-mode cases scale that quantity by two or one-half.

The active path starts when an AmigaVideo bitmap's position changes: `AmigaVideoBM` updates its `topedge` and calls the compositor's `BitMapPositionChanged` method, which stores the bitmap in `csd->updatescroll` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_bitmapclass.c:265-280`; `amigavideo_compositorclass.c:479-491`; `amigavideo_chipset.c:1143-1146`). The VBlank handler later invokes `gfx_vblank_doupdatescroll()` (`:1795-1824`). Its branch `bm->updtop < bm->topedge` is the downward-move path; it scans higher-priority obscured screens and updates the visibility threshold after each successful attachment (`:1665-1704`). `gfx_vblank_attachbm()` accepts a candidate only after its visible height exceeds one line (`:1358-1367`), so the uninitialized adjustment affects later screen decisions only if an attachment succeeds and another candidate remains to be checked.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** selected m68k AmigaVideo HIDD when a bitmap is moved downward, a higher-priority obscured screen becomes visible, that screen has the same interlace mode as the moved bitmap, and another obscured screen is considered afterward. **Consequence:** the next overlap threshold depends on an indeterminate stack value, so later hidden screens can be wrongly revealed or left obscured and the compositor's screen stack/copper fragments can disagree with the intended overlap. Initialize `adjust` for the same-mode case (to `bmtmp->copld.extralines + 2`) before using the threshold. **Confidence:** high for the uninitialized read and caller conditions; which later screens are misclassified depends on the indeterminate value and screen geometry. No scroll, reveal, or VBlank update was run; source-only.

## GD5992

**AmigaVideo writes a null-derived startup copper list when its chip-memory allocation fails.** `initcustom()` allocates one 200-byte chip-memory block for the null sprite and 46 copper instructions, but does not check `AllocMem()` before deriving `copper1` from the result (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_chipset.c:1962-1964,2039`). If allocation returns NULL, the integer offset sets `copper1` to address `0x10`; every `COPPEROUT` expands to two stores through the cursor (`amigavideo_intern.h:13-15`), so the startup instruction writes target low addresses beginning at `0x10` rather than allocated copper storage. The code subsequently publishes the invalid list pointers in `GfxBase->LOFlist`/`SHFlist`, `custom->cop1lc`/`cop2lc`, and `GfxBase->copinit`, then enables display DMA (`amigavideo_chipset.c:1966-2028,2035-2037`). The copper list has a fixed nonzero size: 46 instructions, or 184 bytes (`:2039`); the allocation also reserves the 16-byte sprite preamble.

This runs during the selected m68k AmigaVideo HIDD startup, before driver registration (`startup.c:34-48`; selected ROM and module payloads at `arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:158,375`). `initcustom()` returns `VOID`, so startup cannot observe or roll back allocation failure. Interrupt servers and the blitter vector are also installed before this allocation (`amigavideo_chipset.c:1915-1950`); their separate lifetime on a later module-init failure is GD5993.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** m68k AmigaVideo HIDD startup when the 200-byte `MEMF_CHIP` allocation fails. **Consequence:** CPU stores target the null-derived low address range instead of the copper buffer; if execution continues, the driver also publishes those invalid addresses as copper lists and enables DMA. The exact fault or low-memory effect depends on the machine's address mapping and was not reproduced. Check allocation success and unwind/restore the chipset before publishing the list or enabling DMA. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation, null-derived target and subsequent publication; hardware-specific outcome remains untested. Source-only.

## GD5993

**AmigaVideo failed initialization leaves interrupt callbacks referencing freed module memory.** `AmigaVideo_Init()` calls `initcustom()` before it attempts display-driver registration (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/startup.c:34-48`). `initcustom()` publishes the VBlank server with `AddIntServer()`, installs `gfx_blit` into the system blitter vector with `SetIntVector()`, and registers/enables the CIA timing callback `gfx_beamsync` (`amigavideo_chipset.c:1915-1950`; callback bodies at `:1171-1185,1266-1290`). It then initializes the chipset and returns without an unwind path.

A later `AddDisplayDriver()` error makes `AmigaVideo_Init()` return FALSE (`startup.c:44-52`). This is a real failure path: `AddDisplayDriverA()` can return `DD_NO_MEM` when allocating its `gfxdriver_data` record fails, or `DD_DRIVER_ERROR` when `driver_Setup()` cannot instantiate the HIDD (`rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:181-183,284-292`). The module's failed-init machinery does call its registered expunge set (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:42-69`), but AmigaVideo's only expunge callbacks release OOP attribute bases or do nothing; neither removes the VBlank/CIA servers, disables those sources, restores the prior blitter vector, nor frees the handlers' chip state (`amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1680-1688`; `amigavideo_bitmapclass.c:359-369`; exhaustive local call search found no `RemIntServer`, `RemICRVector` or vector restoration). Genmodule then frees the library base and returns NULL (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1158-1180`). The VBlank and CIA server data point into that base, and their code plus the blitter callback code are in the failed module; the blitter vector is stored in the still-live graphics.library base. A later interrupt can therefore call freed code or dereference freed module data.

The ignored `Init_AmigaVideoClass()` return is one way to reach the later driver-setup failure, but GD5993 is the missing rollback after `initcustom()`'s interrupt publication; it is separate from GD5992's unchecked copper/sprite allocation, which can corrupt memory before registration is attempted. **Affected configuration and trigger:** selected m68k AmigaVideo HIDD, when `AddDisplayDriver()` fails after `initcustom()` has installed the handlers, including its driver-record allocation failure path. **Consequence:** active interrupt registrations retain code/data addresses from a module base that failed-init cleanup frees, risking a fault or memory corruption on subsequent interrupt dispatch. Remove/disable the handlers and restore the prior blitter vector before returning init failure, or defer publishing them until registration can no longer fail. **Confidence:** high for the registration, failed-init expunge/free ordering, and absent teardown; the post-failure interrupt dispatch was not run. Source-only.

## GD5994

**AmigaVideo copies a dummy interlace copper list through an unchecked allocation.** `initvpicopper()` allocates chip memory only when `ViewPort->DspIns->CopSStart` is NULL, then immediately passes that pointer to `CopyMemQuick()` without checking the allocation result (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/chipset.h:48-69`). The helper copies `MaxCount << 2` bytes and derives several `bm->copsd` pointers from the returned destination. A normal AmigaVideo viewport has a nonzero list size: `MakeViewPort()` sets `MaxCount` from `get_copper_list_length()`, which returns at least 2,000 bytes (`amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1151-1170,1214-1260`; `amigavideo_chipset.c:486-494`). `CopyMemQuick()` performs word-copy loops through its destination and has no NULL check (`rom/exec/copymemquick.c:58-88`), so an allocation failure leaves the copy target NULL and the subsequent copper pointers are derived from an invalid base.

The helper is reached from two selected paths. In the VBlank path, `gfx_vblank()` handles a pending `updatescroll`; `gfx_vblank_doupdatescroll()` can expose a hidden non-interlaced bitmap in an interlaced display and call `gfx_vblank_attachbm()`, which invokes `initvpicopper()` before linking the interlace fragment (`amigavideo_chipset.c:1317-1389,1614-1703,1795-1824`). The bitmap's normal non-interlaced `MakeViewPort()` path explicitly frees `CopSStart` and sets it NULL, so the later dummy allocation is expected (`amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1151-1170`). The compositor's stack rebuild has the same non-interlaced-bitmap-on-interlaced-display call at `amigavideo_compositorclass.c:287-300`.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected m68k AmigaVideo HIDD (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:158,375`), when a non-interlaced viewport must be represented in the interlace copper list and the `MEMF_CHIP` allocation for its dummy list fails. **Consequence:** the code copies a nonempty list to a NULL destination and publishes derived invalid pointers; the VBlank caller can do this from interrupt context, disrupting display update and potentially corrupting low memory or faulting according to the target mapping. Check allocation success and abort/roll back before copying or linking the interlace fragment. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation, nonzero copy size, and selected caller conditions; the exact hardware failure effect was not reproduced. Source-only.

## GD5995

**P96Gfx crashes while disposing an 8-bit bitmap whose palette allocation failed.** In the bitmap constructor, a failed palette allocation sets `ok = FALSE` before the bitmap is allocated or linked into `cid->bitmaplist` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_bitmapclass.c:337-343,345-356`). The failure path nevertheless invokes the class's `Root::Dispose()` method (`:368-373`). Disposal unconditionally calls `Remove(&data->node)` after freeing bitmap storage (`:399-409`), but the zeroed node was never linked. Exec documents that `Remove()` requires a node already in a list and directly dereferences `ln_Pred` and `ln_Succ` (`rom/exec/remove.c:24-31,54-65`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** P96Gfx bitmap construction for depth-8 formats when the 768-byte palette allocation fails. **Consequence:** cleanup passes an unlinked, NULL-linked node to `Remove()`, causing invalid memory access during error handling instead of returning a clean construction failure. Track whether the node was linked or avoid list removal for pre-link failures. **Confidence:** high for allocation ordering, constructor cleanup, and the Exec precondition; no allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

## GD5996

**P96Gfx dereferences unchecked allocations while constructing a card HIDD.** When the `.card` supplies a board name, `P96GFXCl__Root__New()` allocates `p96gfx_HWName` and `p96gfx_HWResTmplt` and passes both results directly to `sprintf()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_hiddclass.c:337-344`). It also allocates the resolution, sync-tag, pixel-format-tag, and display-mode-tag arrays without checking any result before filling them (`:355-407,411-519`). These arrays are populated from the card's reported resolutions and supported pixel formats; the selected initialization caller enters this constructor for each discovered card with registered resolutions (`:1820-1841`), and reports failure only if construction itself returns failure. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected m68k P96Gfx HIDD with a named `.card` board or a card requiring mode tags, when any corresponding allocation fails. **Consequence:** a NULL write in `sprintf()` or while filling a required tag array interrupts driver construction instead of unwinding cleanly. Check each allocation and route partial acquisition through cleanup before using it. **Confidence:** high for unchecked results and immediate writes; no allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

## GD5997

**P96Gfx dereferences a failed mode-node allocation while registering display modes.** After querying the superclass display-mode enumerator and mapping a returned mode to a P96 resolution, `P96GFXCl__Root__New()` allocates an `RTGMode` node and immediately writes its fields and links it into `cid->rtglist` without checking the allocation (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_hiddclass.c:581-630`, especially `:621-627`). The constructor's existing mode-enumeration loop otherwise skips unsupported or duplicate modes, so allocation failure is a separate path from those normal skips. **Affected configuration and trigger:** P96Gfx card HIDD construction when a supported enumerated display mode maps to a P96 resolution and allocation of its `RTGMode` node fails. **Consequence:** NULL dereference during mode registration, aborting construction rather than leaving the card with a recoverable incomplete mode list. Check the allocation and either unwind or skip the mode consistently. **Confidence:** high; the returned pointer is dereferenced before any guard. No allocation failure or mode enumeration was run. Source-only.

## GD5998

**P96Gfx dereferences a failed VRAM allocator-header allocation during initialization.** For every discovered card with a nonempty resolution list, `P96GFX__Initialise()` marks initialization successful, records the reported VRAM base and size, allocates a `MemHeader`, then immediately fills its fields and the first `MemChunk` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_hiddclass.c:1741-1774`). The allocation result at `:1767` is not checked. **Affected configuration and trigger:** selected m68k P96Gfx initialization with at least one card reporting resolutions, when allocation of that card's VRAM `MemHeader` fails. **Consequence:** NULL dereference during initialization after the card has been selected; the HIDD cannot complete initialization cleanly. Check the allocation and unwind the card's initialization before accessing the header or VRAM chunk. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked result and immediate writes; no allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

## GD5999

**P96Gfx keeps operating after its cursor color-map object failed to construct.** The graphics-HIDD constructor creates `data->spriteColors` with `OOP_NewObject()` but does not test the result before continuing to register the display (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_hiddclass.c:533-579`). The hardware-cursor path later uses this field: true-color cursor conversion calls `P96GFXCl__PickPen()`, which queries three entries through `HIDD_CM_GetColor()`, and the P96 cursor-pen method calls `HIDD_CM_SetColors()` on the same object (`:1145-1165,1267-1274,1369-1378`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** P96Gfx cards advertising a hardware sprite, if cursor color-map object construction fails and a cursor-shape or cursor-pen update follows. **Consequence:** cursor handling passes a NULL object into color-map methods and can fault instead of reporting construction failure or falling back to a software cursor. Check construction and either fail the HIDD or disable the hardware-sprite path with a valid fallback. **Confidence:** high for unchecked construction and later use; the exact behavior of the color-map method on NULL was not reproduced. Source-only.

## GD6000

**P96Gfx abandons discovered card records and mode lists without freeing them on initialization failure.** `P96GFX__InitCard()` adds successfully initialized cards to `csd->foundCards`, then populates each card's resolution list (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_hiddclass.c:1641-1653`). If every discovered card has an empty resolution list, the initialization loop skips them and leaves `retval` false (`:1741-1745`); the failure branch calls `P96GFX__FreeCardCIDList()`, whose body is empty (`:1777-1783,1624-1627`). The same empty cleanup helper is called when obtaining any required OOP attribute base fails after card discovery and VRAM-header setup (`:1809-1817`). The abandoned records own `cid`, `boardinfo`, optional `vmem`, and any resolution/mode allocations already made; `P96GFX__FreeCID()` is the local release path for the card and board-info allocations, but is not used here (`:1615-1622`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** P96Gfx initialization where cards are discovered but none yields resolutions, or where a required OOP attribute-base acquisition fails after discovery. **Consequence:** card records, board-info buffers, and any per-card allocator/resolution/mode allocations remain allocated after the module initialization attempt fails. Implement list traversal that frees each card and its owned lists, while respecting any resources already published to Exec. **Confidence:** high for the empty failure cleanup and unreleased per-card allocations; no failed initialization was induced. Source-only.

## GD6001

**A later Decoration theme reload can read the freed initial decorator record.** Startup assigns the first `LoadDecoration()` result to the global `basedecor` and installs it with `ChangeDecoration()` (`workbench/c/Decoration/decoration.c:249-272`). Every reload message calls `LoadDecoration()` before `ChangeDecoration()` and `LoadDecoration()` consults `basedecor` to copy its three class pointers (`:110-127,313-319`). The global is not updated to the replacement. When `ChangeDecoration()` replaces the initial record, Intuition schedules its removal only if its screen reference count is zero; after removal, the service handles `MAGIC_DECORATOR` by calling `DeleteDecorator()`, which frees the record (`rom/intuition/changedecorationa.c:64-75`; `rom/intuition/decoration.c:130-150`; `workbench/c/Decoration/decoration.c:321-323,86-90`). If the initial record has been freed before another reload, that reload reads `basedecor->base` through a dangling pointer.

Clear or replace `basedecor` as part of decorator retirement, or use the current live decorator as the class source. **Affected configuration and trigger:** Decoration service after startup, if a replacement retires and frees the initial zero-reference decorator and a subsequent theme reload arrives. If screens still reference the initial record, the stale-read trigger is deferred until those references are released. **Consequence:** use-after-free while copying class pointers; later behavior depends on the reused contents. **Confidence:** high for global publication, reload read, conditional async retirement and free; exact manifestation is allocator-state dependent. No theme reload or screen lifecycle was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6002

**Deleting a Decoration theme record leaks its three tag arrays.** `LoadDecoration()` allocates separate five-entry arrays for `nd_ScreenTags`, `nd_MenuTags`, and `nd_WindowTags` and fills them with the per-class user-buffer, image, config and theme tags (`workbench/c/Decoration/decoration.c:118-160`). `DeleteDecorator()` frees the theme and the enclosing record but never frees any of those arrays (`:86-90`). It is used both when a loaded theme fails before tag creation and, for successfully installed records, after Intuition retires the decorator and sends the service its destruction message (`:110-115,321-323`; `rom/intuition/decoration.c:130-150`).

Free the three arrays in `DeleteDecorator()` after Intuition has finished using the record. **Affected configuration and trigger:** any successfully loaded Decoration record that reaches `DeleteDecorator()`, including a replaced theme with no remaining screen references. **Consequence:** three small tag arrays remain allocated per retired record. Allocation failures while constructing these arrays are a separate GD6003 issue. **Confidence:** high; allocation and use are explicit and no release exists in the repository's cleanup path. No theme lifecycle was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6003

**Decoration dereferences failed tag-array allocations while loading a theme.** After obtaining a theme, `LoadDecoration()` allocates three five-entry tag arrays, then immediately assigns each result to a local pointer and writes element zero (`workbench/c/Decoration/decoration.c:118-137`). Failure of any one allocation therefore leads to a null write; the function has no allocation-failure check or cleanup/NULL return for these arrays. Both startup and the service's theme-reload message call this function (`:249,312-319`), so either path can fault under memory pressure.

Check all three arrays before populating them, release any successful partial allocations and the theme, then return NULL for the callers to handle. **Affected configuration and trigger:** Decoration startup or a subsequent theme reload after `DTLoadTheme()` succeeds, when allocation of any tag array fails. **Consequence:** null dereference during decorator construction rather than a recoverable load failure. **Confidence:** high; each result is directly dereferenced with no intervening guard. This is separate from GD6002's leaked arrays on successful object retirement. No allocation failure or theme load was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6004

**Decoration startup leaks its private port and loaded theme record when class construction fails.** `main()` opens the libraries and creates a private message port before calling `LoadDecoration()` and constructing the screen, menu, and window classes (`workbench/c/Decoration/decoration.c:207-258`). The only cleanup after these nested attempts closes the libraries and command arguments; it does not delete the port or the loaded `DecorationDecorator`/theme record when `LoadDecoration()` or any class constructor fails (`:330-339`). The success path adds the port to the public list and enters the detached service loop, but on the failure path the port was never published and still has no `DeleteMsgPort()` call.

Use one startup unwind path that frees any successfully created classes, calls `DeleteDecorator()` for the loaded record, and deletes the private port before closing libraries. **Affected configuration and trigger:** startup after `CreateMsgPort()` succeeds, if theme loading or any of the three class constructors fails. **Consequence:** retained private message-port resources; when a theme record was already loaded, its record and theme remain allocated as well. Partially constructed class objects are released by the existing nested cleanup when applicable. **Confidence:** high for the missing port and record cleanup; the trigger depends on the relevant load/class failure. No startup or allocation failure was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6005

**A tiled Decoration menu dereferences a failed tile-info allocation.** `LoadMenuConfig()` sets `MenuIsTiled` when any `TileLeft`, `TileTop`, `TileRight`, or `TileBottom` setting is present (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themeconfig.c:136-154`). During `MDM_INITMENU`, `menudecor_initmenu()` allocates `md->img_menu_ti` and immediately writes all four fields without checking the result (`workbench/c/Decoration/menudecorclass.c:164-180`). Intuition dispatches this method for pulled-down menu bars, menus, and submenus (`rom/intuition/menutask.c:919-938,1217-1233,1380-1398`); those callers clear-allocate the decorator's user buffer, so the tiled flag causes this local allocation path rather than an uninitialized pointer.

Check the `TileInfo` allocation and fail menu decoration initialization cleanly. **Affected configuration and trigger:** any selected theme config that enables menu tiling, during menu initialization when the `TileInfo` allocation fails. **Consequence:** null dereference in menu setup; caller does not receive a graceful initialization failure. **Confidence:** high for the parser gate, allocation, immediate writes, and selected caller path. No menu initialization or allocation failure was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6006

**Each successful highlighted menu background render leaks its temporary image container.** In `menudecor_renderbackground()`, the `HIGHITEM && md->di` branch allocates a new image container, copies the highlighted item, applies the tint, and draws it to the RastPort, but never calls `DDisposeImageContainer(di)` on that temporary (`workbench/c/Decoration/menudecorclass.c:138-162`). The distinct source/menu background `md->di` is retained until `menudecor_exitmenu()` and disposed there (`:223-234`); that cleanup does not own or reach the local highlighted copy.

Dispose the temporary container after drawing, including any error paths after allocation. **Affected configuration and trigger:** themed menu rendering when `HIGHITEM` is set, `md->di` is non-NULL, and `DNewDecorImageContainer()` succeeds. **Consequence:** one image container and its associated image storage remain allocated per such render, allowing memory use to accumulate with repeated highlighted redraws. If the temporary allocation fails, this particular leak does not occur. **Confidence:** high; the successful allocation path has no release before return and the menu-exit cleanup handles a separate pointer. No menu redraw or allocation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6007

**Per-screen decoration image remapping dereferences unchecked allocation results.** `ObtainScreenTheme()` applies `CreateDecorImageContainerMatchingScreen()` to each theme image and does not abort when a remap fails (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themescreen.c:20-74`). In that helper, failure to allocate the output container is followed immediately by `out->ok = FALSE`; failure to allocate the subimage decision table is followed by writes into it when image data exists; and failure to allocate the filename is followed by `strcpy()` (`workbench/libs/decorator/decorimagefuncs.c:402-437,448-497`). On the truecolor/alpha path, an opaque subimage also causes unchecked `CreateRastPort()` and `AllocBitMap()` results to be dereferenced/passed to `WritePixelArray()` (`:478-497`). These are separate allocation-failure routes within the same remapping helper; ordinary missing or unconvertible images can instead produce a non-NULL `ok == FALSE` placeholder and are not this finding.

Check allocations before use and propagate remap failure through `ObtainScreenTheme()` with cleanup of already-created images. **Affected configuration and trigger:** screen theme acquisition in Decoration or Appearance preview when any listed remap allocation fails; the RastPort/bitmap subpath additionally requires remapped image data with at least one fully opaque subimage. **Consequence:** null dereference during screen-theme acquisition, preventing graceful handling of memory exhaustion. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked uses and selected call path; each requires the corresponding allocation failure. No screen, preview, or allocation failure was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6008

**A zero Decoration theme `BarHeight` causes division by zero while Intuition sizes a title gadget.** `LoadSystemConfig()` initializes `DecorConfig.BarHeight` to zero and leaves it zero if the theme directory cannot be locked or its `System/Config` omits `BarHeight`; a parsed value is accepted directly through `GetInt()` without a nonzero check (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themeconfig.c:268,317-322,367-369`). `LoadConfig()` returns this configuration, and `DTLoadTheme()` accepts the theme when its image set loads (`themeconfig.c:492-511`; `theme.c:28-48`). Decoration passes the theme's config to the window-decoration class (`workbench/c/Decoration/decoration.c:148-160`), whose `windecor_getdefsizes()` marks close/MUI/popup/snapshot/iconify/lock/depth/zoom gadgets as title gadgets. For a valid gadget image, if the reference font height exceeds the configured bar height, it scales the gadget height and divides by `data->dc->BarHeight` (`windowdecorclass.c:1733-1778,1816-1859`). With a zero value, the division at `:1858` is undefined and the requested gadget sizing can fault. Intuition dispatches `WDM_GETDEFSIZE_SYSIMAGE` from its system-image sizing path (`rom/intuition/sysiclass.c:239-245`), so this is reached during ordinary window gadget sizing.

Reject or replace zero `BarHeight` with a safe default before creating the window decorator. **Affected configuration and trigger:** a selected Decoration theme whose `System/Config` is missing or sets `BarHeight = 0`, with at least one valid title-gadget image, when Intuition requests that gadget's size. The nine checked-in theme configs all specify positive `BarHeight` values, so this pass found no trigger in the bundled themes; custom or incomplete theme directories remain affected. **Consequence:** division by zero during title-gadget sizing. **Confidence:** high for the default, parser, data flow, and divide; reachability is conditional on a custom/incomplete theme and a valid gadget image. No theme was loaded and no window was opened; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6009

**Decoration title-cache allocation failure is passed to `strncpy()`.** After a titlebar bitmap is rendered, `DrawPartialTitleBar()` calls `CacheTitleBar()` (`workbench/c/Decoration/windowdecorclass.c:693`). When the window has a nonempty title whose length differs from the cached length, `CacheTitleBar()` frees the prior title copy and assigns `AllocVec(len + 1)` to `cached->title`, then immediately calls `strncpy(cached->title, window->Title, len)` without checking the allocation (`:206-228`). Allocation failure therefore passes NULL as the destination for a nonzero-length copy.

Keep the existing cache until a replacement allocation succeeds, and skip or invalidate the copy safely on failure. **Affected configuration and trigger:** any decorated window using this titlebar cache when its first nonempty title is cached or its title length changes, and the replacement allocation fails during a border redraw. **Consequence:** null destination passed to `strncpy()`, causing a fault in the redraw path. Same-length content changes do not allocate a replacement. **Confidence:** high for the changed-length gate and unchecked nonzero copy; occurrence requires allocation failure. No redraw or allocation failure was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6010

**Decoration's bar-masking shape path dereferences a failed scaled titlebar image.** When the window's titlebar height differs from the theme's `BarHeight`, `DrawShapePartialTitleBar()` calls `DScaleDecorImage()` and assigns its result to `img_winbar_normal` (`workbench/c/Decoration/windowdecorclass.c:356-411`). If `ScaleDecorImage()` cannot allocate the outer `DecorImage` container, it returns NULL (`workbench/libs/decorator/decorimagefuncs.c:268-287`). The subsequent unconditional `WriteTiledImageShape()` call dereferences `di->ok` before checking tile dimensions (`windowdecorclass.c:266-276,414-425`), so this shape-generation path can fault. (Failure of the inner scaling allocations instead faults inside `ScaleBuffer()` and is tracked separately in GD6016.) The path is reached from `windecor_windowshape()` when `BarMasking` is enabled and a titlebar shape is regenerated (`:1873-1891`); Intuition invokes that method through the default window-shape hook during shape creation/update (`rom/intuition/intuition_misc.c:1192-1222`).

Check the scaled image result before passing it to the tile writer, and retain a valid fallback shape on failure. **Affected configuration and trigger:** Decoration themes with `BarMasking` enabled, a valid `img_winbar_normal`, and a window whose border-top height differs from configured `BarHeight`, when the outer scaled-image container allocation fails. **Consequence:** null dereference during window-shape generation. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked result and caller path; allocation failure is conditional. The regular titlebar rendering path has a separate null-image guard in `DRenderElement()` and does not establish safety for this shape writer. No allocation failure or shape update was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6011

**Truecolor frame rendering can read a failed gradient-column allocation.** `windecor_draw_winborder()` allocates a `Height * 3` source column and passes it to `DFillMemoryBufferRGBGradient()` without checking the result (`workbench/c/Decoration/windowdecorclass.c:963-974`). For a truecolor RastPort, any positive left, right, or bottom border is then sent to `DHorizRepeatBuffer()`. That helper allocates its expanded destination buffer and returns if that allocation fails; if it succeeds, it reads the source column at `buf[(offy + yi) * 3]` without checking whether `buf` was allocated (`workbench/libs/decorator/drawfuncs.c:809-847`). Thus the null read requires the later destination allocation to succeed.

Check the source allocation before filling or passing it to the repeat helper. **Affected configuration and trigger:** gradient border rendering on a truecolor screen, with at least one nonempty frame side, when the source-column allocation fails but the later expanded blit-buffer allocation succeeds. Indexed-color rendering's helper fills with a pen and does not read `buf`; the helper also returns without reading it if its own destination allocation fails. **Consequence:** null-pointer read while constructing a border blit buffer. **Confidence:** high for the conditional path and missing check; requires the stated allocation ordering. No allocation failure or border draw was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6012

**Decoration theme loading dereferences failed config allocations before its caller can handle failure.** `LoadConfig()` allocates a cleared `DecorConfig`, then immediately writes `dc->ThemePath`; it next allocates that path buffer and immediately passes it as the `strcpy()` destination (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themeconfig.c:492-501`). If the config allocation fails, the first write dereferences NULL; if only the path allocation fails, the copy dereferences NULL. `DTLoadTheme()` checks the `LoadConfig()` return and has cleanup for a normal NULL return, but these failures fault inside `LoadConfig()` before it can return (`workbench/libs/decortheme/theme.c:28-43`).

Check both allocations and unwind through a NULL return before using their results. **Affected configuration and trigger:** any caller of `DTLoadTheme()` when allocation of the config object or its `ThemePath` buffer fails; checked-in callers include the Decoration application and Appearance theme preview (`workbench/c/Decoration/decoration.c:110`; `workbench/prefs/appearance/themepreview.c:123`). **Consequence:** null dereference during theme loading instead of a recoverable load failure. **Confidence:** high; both unchecked allocations and their immediate dereferences are explicit. No allocation failure or theme load was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6013

**Malformed Decoration theme settings can pass a null-derived pointer to numeric parsers.** `SkipChars()` stores `strstr(v, "=")` and unconditionally increments the result (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themeconfig.c:20-25`). The menu and system parsers select recognized settings by their leading key text and then call `GetInt()`, `GetIntegers()`, `GetTripleIntegers()`, or `GetColors()` without first requiring an equals sign (`themeconfig.c:136-174,336-456`). For example, `BarHeight 25` matches the `BarHeight ` branch and reaches `GetInt()`; because no `=` exists, `SkipChars()` increments a NULL pointer, which is undefined behavior, and `GetInt()` passes the result to `atol()` (`:27-32,367-369`). The other helpers likewise pass that result to `sscanf()` or their numeric conversions. `LoadConfig()` does not validate the syntax or reject the theme (`:492-511`), and the `Decoration` command accepts a caller-supplied theme path (`workbench/c/Decoration/decoration.c:170,192,249`).

Check for `=` and reject malformed settings before calling the conversion routines. **Affected configuration and trigger:** `decoration.library`/`decortheme.library` consumers when a selected custom theme's `Menu/Config` or `System/Config` contains a recognized numeric setting without `=`. Bundled themes were not established as triggers in this pass. **Consequence:** undefined pointer arithmetic followed by numeric parsing through the invalid result; the parser may fail or fault, depending on compiler and runtime behavior. **Confidence:** high that malformed recognized lines reach the null-result increment and conversion; exact manifestation is implementation-dependent. No config file was modified or parsed at runtime; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6014

**A zero-width menu source tile can trap Decoration in an endless render loop.** `LoadMenuConfig()` marks a theme tiled when it parses any `TileLeft`, `TileRight`, `TileTop`, or `TileBottom` setting, without checking those values against the loaded background image dimensions (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themeconfig.c:136-154`). `InitMenuSkinning()` copies those values into `TileInfo`, and the menu decoration passes that tiling data to `DRenderMenuBarBackground()` for the pulled-down menu-bar draw path (`workbench/c/Decoration/menudecorclass.c:176-183,185-199`). `TileImageToImageMenuBar()` computes the center source width as `src->w - TileLeft - TileRight` and passes it to `DrawTileToImage()` with destination width `dest->w - TileRight` (`workbench/libs/decorator/drawfuncs.c:203-224`). With a custom theme where `TileLeft == src->w`, `TileRight == 0`, and `TileTop > 0`, the top-strip call has source width zero, positive destination width, and positive height. `DrawTileToImage()` sets `dw` to that zero source width, then loops while `width > 0` subtracting `dw` and adding it to `dx`; neither value changes, so the render never returns (`drawfuncs.c:172-200`). The menu-bar destination height is expanded to at least the top-plus-bottom tile caps before this call, so the renderer's cap-height check does not prevent this case (`menudecorclass.c:188-199`; `drawfuncs.c:214-219`).

Reject tile dimensions that leave a zero-sized source region, or make the tile loops return when a source step is zero. **Affected configuration and trigger:** Decoration/decortheme consumers using a custom tiled theme whose menu background has zero-width center region (or another zero source step) while the corresponding destination region is positive. The trigger is configuration- and image-specific; no bundled-theme trigger is claimed. **Consequence:** the menu background draw does not return, stalling the caller during menu rendering. **Confidence:** high for the zero-step loop and conditional path; no theme or menu draw was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6015

**Theme image loading dereferences unchecked path and filename allocations.** `GetImageFromFile()` computes a path-buffer size, calls `AllocVec()`, and immediately passes the result to `strncpy()` and `AddPart()` without checking for failure (`workbench/libs/decorator/decorimagefuncs.c:302-324`). After opening and decoding an image and allocating its `DecorImage`, it makes a second unchecked `AllocVec()` for `di->filename` and passes that result to `strncpy()` (`:335-340`). Either allocation can return NULL under memory pressure, producing a null destination dereference. The second failure also leaves the picture datatype object and image container without the normal cleanup at `:379,382`.

`LoadImages()` calls `DGetImageFromFile()` for each system and menu asset (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themeimages.c:27-69`); `DTLoadTheme()` reaches `LoadImages()` for the caller-supplied theme path (`workbench/libs/decortheme/theme.c:28-41`), and the selected Decoration command passes its `PATH` argument into that loader (`workbench/c/Decoration/decoration.c:170,192,249`). Thus the unchecked allocation is on the ordinary theme-load path, not only an unused helper.

Check each allocation before copying and unwind the open picture and image container on later failure. **Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting `decorator.library`/`decortheme.library` and a theme load where either `GetImageFromFile()` allocation fails. **Consequence:** the caller can fault during theme loading; failure of the filename allocation additionally bypasses local cleanup. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocations and downstream copy calls; no allocation failure or theme load was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6016

**Image scaling dereferences failed output and sample-table allocations.** `ScaleBuffer()` independently allocates a scaled pixel output and a per-destination-column `linepattern`, without checking either (`workbench/libs/decorator/decorimagefuncs.c:74-94`). For positive scaling dimensions, it immediately derives `lastscaledlineptr` from `scaleddata`, writes indexes through `linepattern`, and copies rows through the output pointer (`:90-128`); failure of either allocation therefore causes a null-pointer access inside the helper. `ScaleBuffer()` is called by `DScaleDecorImage()` for screen/image scaling (`decorimagefuncs.c:268-287`) and by `BltScaleDecorImageSubImageRastPort()` for scaled drawing (`workbench/libs/decorator/drawfuncs.c:96-111`). The former's later `di->data == NULL` check cannot handle these failures because `ScaleBuffer()` does not return safely from them. The exported `DScaleBuffer()` also directly exposes this implementation (`decorimagefuncs.c:140-150`).

Check both allocations before pointer arithmetic or writes, and free any successful partial allocation on failure. **Affected configuration and trigger:** callers scaling an image to positive destination dimensions when either `AllocVec()` for the scaled output or the line-pattern table fails. This includes Decoration titlebar remapping/drawing and clients of the public `DScaleBuffer()` API. **Consequence:** null-pointer access during scaling rather than a clean NULL return or skipped draw. **Confidence:** high for both unchecked allocations and immediate uses; occurrence requires allocation failure. No scale operation or allocation failure was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6017

**Low-color screen-theme remapping drops the only reference to each successfully loaded picture datatype object.** `CreateDecorImageContainerMatchingScreen()` first loads a LUT-specific picture, or falls back to the original image, and stores the returned object in `out->o` (`workbench/libs/decorator/decorimagefuncs.c:435-457`). When the source image also has pixel data, the following `if (out->data != NULL)` block unconditionally sets both `out->mask` and `out->o` to NULL (`:468-470`), overwriting the object pointer without disposing it. `DisposeImageContainer()` can dispose the picture only through the surviving `di->o` field (`:155-173`). The screen-theme owner later disposes every remapped image through `FreeImages()` (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themescreen.c:82-90`; `themeimages.c:72-105`), but that cleanup cannot reach the overwritten object. The loss occurs once for each image whose low-color Picture load succeeds and whose source container has `data != NULL`; truecolor remapping skips the Picture-load branch, and a missing/failed Picture load does not create this leak.

Dispose the loaded Picture object before clearing the field, or preserve it in the returned image container so normal disposal can release it. **Affected configuration and trigger:** low-color screen-theme acquisition where a remapped theme image has source pixel data and `LoadPicture()` succeeds for its LUT or fallback image. **Consequence:** the Picture datatype object and its associated resources remain allocated after the remapped screen theme is released; repeated screen-theme acquisition/release can accumulate leaked objects. **Confidence:** high for the overwritten owner pointer and unreachable normal disposal path; no screen theme was loaded or released. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6018

**A one-value Decoration title-bar setting produces a negative source-image offset.** `GetIntegers()` sets the first output to `-1` when `sscanf()` parses exactly one value (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themeconfig.c:34-56`). The parser uses this helper for title-bar settings such as `BarPre`, `BarTitleFill`, and the other bar segments (`:372-396`); `InitThemeElements()` copies the resulting offset and size directly into each `DE_TYPE_TILED_TITLE` element (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themeelements.c:38-46,60-76`). The render path passes `de_SrcOffset` to `WriteTiledImageTitle()` (`workbench/libs/decorator/decoratorelement.c:57-64`), which forwards it as `xSrc` to the blitter (`drawfuncs.c:552-580`). If scaling is needed, the blitter adds that negative value to `di->data` to form `srcptr` (`drawfuncs.c:91-100`). If source and destination dimensions match, it passes the negative source x coordinate to `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` (`:109-118`); that API takes an unsigned source coordinate, so `-1` becomes a large positive offset. Both branches can read outside the source image buffer. The regular rendering path is reached while Decoration draws a window titlebar (`workbench/c/Decoration/windowdecorclass.c:598-623`); the Preferences preview also calls `DRenderElement()` on these parsed elements (`workbench/prefs/appearance/themepreview.c:235-249`).

Reject a one-value setting or define a nonnegative default source offset before constructing the element. **Affected configuration and trigger:** a custom theme config with a one-value title-bar segment setting and a positive segment size, followed by rendering/scaling that element. Checked-in themes use two values; this is a malformed/custom-config trigger, not a claimed bundled-theme failure. **Consequence:** rendering reads before or beyond the source pixel array and can produce invalid pixels or fault. **Confidence:** high for parser assignment and source-coordinate propagation; the precise effect depends on the selected drawing branch and buffer layout. No theme was loaded or rendered; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6019

**Decoration border shading dereferences an unchecked RastPort clone.** `RectShadeFunc()` enables the line-buffer path for multi-pixel clip rectangles: it allocates `outline` when width or height exceeds one, then calls `CloneRastPort(rp)` and immediately writes `dstRp->Layer = NULL` without checking the result (`workbench/libs/decorator/drawfuncs.c:946-1030`). The selected `CloneRastPort()` implementation explicitly returns NULL when its `AllocMem()` fails (`compiler/arossupport/clonerastport.c:16-24,48-56`). Thus, when the line buffer allocation succeeds but the subsequent RastPort allocation fails, shading faults at the Layer assignment. If the line-buffer allocation itself fails, this code takes the direct-RastPort path instead, so that allocation failure does not trigger this particular null dereference (`drawfuncs.c:1000-1028`).

The hook is reached by `ShadeLine()` when gradient shading is disabled and the source image is valid (`drawfuncs.c:1188-1220`); Decoration calls it for multiple window-border segments during window rendering (`workbench/c/Decoration/windowdecorclass.c:1005-1022`). Check the clone before setting its Layer field and fall back to drawing into the supplied RastPort or abandon that shaded segment cleanly. **Affected configuration and trigger:** Decoration image-based border shading over a clip rectangle wider or taller than one pixel, with the line-buffer allocation succeeding and `CloneRastPort()` allocation failing. **Consequence:** null-pointer write in the clipping hook during window-border rendering. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked dereference and documented allocation failure result; no shade hook or allocation failure was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6020

**A negative Decoration title-bar tile size makes the title renderer loop without progress.** `WriteTiledImageTitle()` rejects zero source or destination widths, but not negative `sw`; with positive destination width, its loop sets `ddw = sw`, skips the `w < ddw` clamp, then subtracts the negative `ddw` from `w` and adds it to `x`. The remaining width therefore grows each iteration instead of reaching zero (`workbench/libs/decorator/drawfuncs.c:552-580`). The scaled blit normalizes the negative source width to the full source subimage and returns, so it does not stop the outer loop (`:77-100`). A negative `BarTitleFill` size can reach this path: the config parser stores signed values without validation (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themeconfig.c:34-56,385-386`), `InitThemeElements()` copies it into the title element (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themeelements.c:38-46,74-75`), and Decoration calls `DRenderElement()` with positive measured title-text width when text is present (`workbench/c/Decoration/windowdecorclass.c:620-623`; `decoratorelement.c:57-64`). Other title segments can reach the same loop when their negative configured size is paired with a positive fill/destination width. Checked-in theme configs contain no negative title-bar sizes; this is a custom/malformed-config path.

Reject negative tile sizes while loading the config or make `WriteTiledImageTitle()` return for `sw <= 0`. **Affected configuration and trigger:** a custom theme with a negative title-bar tile size and a render call that supplies positive destination width, such as a visible window title with negative `BarTitleFill`. **Consequence:** the Decoration rendering task remains in the title tiling loop and does not complete the window draw. **Confidence:** high for the loop arithmetic and selected caller; no custom theme was loaded or rendered. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6021

**AboutAROS dereferences failed pool allocations while formatting build labels.** `AboutAROS__OM_NEW()` creates a pool, then allocates `str_buildtype` and immediately formats into it with `sprintf()` without checking the result (`workbench/system/AboutAROS/aboutaros.c:210-233`). Builds defining `BUILDCPU` also allocate `str_buildcpu` and immediately format it without a NULL check (`:242-244`; the selected target adds `-DBUILDCPU` in `mmakefile.src:15`). `AllocPooled()` is documented to return NULL when allocation fails (`rom/exec/allocpooled.c:14-28`). The `str_abi` allocation is also unchecked in the source, but the selected `ArosInquire()` implementation currently returns `AROS_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR == -1` (`rom/aros/arosinquirea.c:31,221-222`), so the allocation branch is not reached in this tree and is excluded from the active trigger.

Check each pool allocation before formatting and dispose of the pool on constructor failure. **Affected configuration and trigger:** AboutAROS object construction when the pool exists but allocation of `str_buildtype` fails, or, in `BUILDCPU` builds, allocation of `str_buildcpu` fails. **Consequence:** null-pointer write in `sprintf()` while constructing the AboutAROS application. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocations, `sprintf()` destinations, and current ABI-major exclusion; requires allocation failure. No application or allocation failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6022

**AboutAROS leaks its constructor pool if MUI application construction fails.** `AboutAROS__OM_NEW()` creates a pool before constructing its application and child objects (`workbench/system/AboutAROS/aboutaros.c:210-212,253-412`). The pool is stored in instance data only when `DoSuperNewTags()` returns a non-NULL object (`:414-423`); `AboutAROS__OM_DISPOSE()` deletes it through that field (`:452-458`). If `DoSuperNewTags()` returns NULL, the constructor returns NULL without deleting the pool, and the selected `main()` caller simply skips its execute/dispose block (`workbench/system/AboutAROS/main.c:32-41`). No surviving object exists to receive `OM_DISPOSE`, so the pool remains unfreed after the failed construction.

No application construction failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6023

**FTManager dereferences a failed serialized-tag-buffer allocation.** `fiWriteFiles()` allocates `write_tags` with `malloc(nr_tags)` and immediately assigns the first serialized tag through `dest = write_tags`, without checking for NULL (`workbench/system/ftmanager/fontinfo_class.c:844-852`). The tag list is populated before this call by `fiSetOTags()`; it always includes required entries such as `OT_FileIdent`, `OT_Engine`, and `OT_Family` (`:576-622`). Thus, when the output file opens, the indirect-data buffer allocation succeeds, and the later serialized-tag allocation fails, the first `dest[0]`/`dest[1]` store faults. The path is used by both the GUI install method and the CLI (`:727-738`; `workbench/system/ftmanager/cli.c:337-343`). This allocation is distinct from the checked indirect-data buffer allocation at `:803-805` and from GD6024's failure to report output errors.

No allocation failure or font installation was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6024

**FTManager reports successful font installation after output files fail to open or write completely.** `fiWriteFiles()` prints a message if either the `.otag` or `.font` output cannot be opened, but it does not record the failure and returns `1` unconditionally (`workbench/system/ftmanager/fontinfo_class.c:741-879`). For `.otag`, it ignores both `Write()` results; a short or failed first write can leave the tag records incomplete, and the second write can leave the indirect data truncated. If the indirect-data `malloc()` fails after opening the file, the function closes the empty `.otag`, continues to the `.font` file, and still returns success (`:792-861`). It also ignores the four-byte `.font` `Write()` result and `Close()` status (`:873-878`). The GUI method returns this value from `MUIM_FontInfo_WriteFiles` (`fontinfo_class.c:915-917`), which the Install button dispatches (`fontwindow_class.c:100-103`). The CLI calls the same function but discards its result and then returns `RETURN_OK` (`workbench/system/ftmanager/cli.c:337-351`), so failed opens and incomplete writes are reported as command success there as well.

Propagate open, allocation, write-count, and close failures to the GUI method and CLI exit status, and remove or clearly reject incomplete outputs. **Affected configuration and trigger:** FTManager GUI install or CLI output when a destination cannot be opened, any `Write()` fails or returns fewer bytes than requested, or the `.otag` indirect-data allocation fails. **Consequence:** the user or caller can receive success despite missing or corrupt font metadata/data files; the CLI exits successfully after either output failure. **Confidence:** high for unchecked results, unconditional return, and the selected CLI caller; no file output or I/O failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6025

**Long FTManager path or output-name arguments leave stack strings unterminated, then pass them to string and path routines.** In the CLI copy path, `ttf_source[256]` receives at most 255 bytes from the caller's `TO` argument with `strncpy()` but gets no explicit terminator before `AddPart()` (`workbench/system/ftmanager/cli.c:169-170,221-230`). `AddPart()` calls `strlen(dirname)` when joining a relative filename (`rom/dos/addpart.c:102-129`), so a 255-byte-or-longer directory value makes it scan beyond `ttf_source` looking for a NUL. Separately, `get_basename()` copies 255 bytes from `OUTFONT` or an extensionless source basename into `basename[256]` without writing a terminator when the input is at least 255 bytes (`cli.c:59-81`). In `fiWriteFiles()`, `path[256]` is filled with `strncpy()` capped at 230 or 250 bytes but likewise receives no explicit terminator; the `target_dir` branch then passes it to `AddPart()`, and both branches pass it to `strcpy(name, path)` before appending an extension (`workbench/system/ftmanager/fontinfo_class.c:741-759`). These calls can read past the local source arrays; `strcpy()` can also write past `name[256]` if the unterminated scan continues beyond that destination's capacity. The CLI exposes the relevant `OUTFONT`, `FONTDIR`, and `TO` arguments and accepts an input filename (`cli.c:169-170,221-230,250`). The GUI name field is limited to 50 characters and passes no target directory to `fiWriteFiles()`, so this report does not claim that the GUI path reaches these length triggers (`fontinfo_class.c:256-260,727-738`).

Bound accepted lengths, explicitly terminate only after proving the source fits, check `AddPart()` results, and construct output paths without relying on unterminated fixed buffers. **Affected configuration and trigger:** FTManager CLI with a `TO` or `OUTFONT` value of at least 255 bytes, an extensionless input basename of at least 255 bytes, or a `FONTDIR` value of at least 230 bytes passed to `fiWriteFiles()`; path concatenation can also produce an unbounded/overlong filename. The GUI name control is capped at 50 characters and is excluded from this trigger. **Consequence:** out-of-bounds string reads and possible stack-buffer overwrite while constructing the copied-font or `.otag`/`.font` paths. **Confidence:** high for the missing-termination paths and selected string-helper calls; exact memory effect depends on adjacent stack bytes and path lengths. No long path or output name was supplied; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6026

**FTManager leaks earlier GUI initialization resources when a later initialization stage fails.** `Init()` opens `codesets.library`, initializes FreeType, then creates four custom MUI classes in sequence (`workbench/system/ftmanager/ftmanager.c:75-98`). A failed FreeType initialization returns immediately after the Codesets library has been opened. If a later class creation fails, the earlier successful classes and both libraries remain initialized. `Cleanup()` contains the corresponding class deletions, `FT_Done_Library()`, and `CloseLibrary(CodesetsBase)` (`:53-68`), but `ftmanager_gui()` returns `RETURN_FAIL` directly when `Init(TRUE)` returns false and never calls it (`:170-174`). The same early return means no rollback of any earlier stages. Failure of the first Codesets `OpenLibrary()` itself acquires no such resource and is not the leak trigger.

Route every failed initialization stage through cleanup that releases only resources successfully acquired, or unwind each stage before returning. **Affected configuration and trigger:** starting the GUI with `codesets.library` available, followed by FreeType initialization failure or failure to create any later custom class. **Consequence:** the failed launch leaves library references and, for later class failures, previously created custom classes allocated; repeated failed launches can accumulate these resources. **Confidence:** high for the acquisition order, direct failure returns, and missing caller cleanup; the precise retained internal state depends on which initialization call fails. No launch or initialization failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6027

**VMM Preferences overflows its menu path buffer with a long selected drawer and uses an incomplete path when composition fails.** Both `MenuOpen()` and `MenuSaveAs()` allocate `char path[80]`, then copy the ASL requester's `fr_Drawer` into it with unbounded `strcpy()` (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/menus.c:7-27,36-59`). The ASL drawer gadget permits up to 1,024 characters plus its terminator (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqhooks.h:38-39`; `filereqhooks.c:878-891,1772-1777`). Thus a drawer of 80 or more bytes writes past the local array before `AddPart()` runs. There is a separate boundary case when the drawer itself fits in 80 bytes but the combined drawer and file name does not: `AddPart()` returns `DOSFALSE` without changing `path` (`rom/dos/addpart.c:127-140`), but both callers ignore that result and pass the unchanged drawer path to the config reader/writer. The reader displays its no-config-file requester if opening that directory fails (`config.c:239-244`). Save As attempts `MODE_NEWFILE` on the directory path; if `Open()` fails, `WriteConfigFile()` returns FALSE and the menu ignores that result, so the failed save has no error indication (`menus.c:59`; `config.c:383-400`).

Use a buffer sized for the selected path or reject a drawer that does not fit before copying; check `AddPart()` and surface its failure instead of using the incomplete path. **Affected configuration and trigger:** VMM Preferences Open or Save As with either a drawer of at least 80 bytes, or a shorter drawer whose combined path exceeds the 80-byte buffer. **Consequence:** the long-drawer case overwrites the stack buffer; in the combined-path case the reader attempts the directory as the config filename and shows its open-failure requester, while Save As may fail to open the directory and then silently discards the false result. **Confidence:** high for both source paths and the AddPart unchanged-on-failure contract; directory-open failure is conditional on the selected filesystem's `Open()` behavior. No long drawer, overlong combined path, or menu action was exercised. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6028

**VMM Preferences copies a long paging-file name into an 80-byte config field.** The file-name gadget is created with `KeyString(0, 256, 'f')`, whose macro sets `MUIA_String_MaxLen` to 256 (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/memory_page.c:228`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/macros.h:147-151`). When saving the configuration in file or pseudo-part mode, `WriteConfigFile()` obtains that string and copies it with `strcpy()` into `CurrentConfig.PartOrFileName[80]` (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/config.c:388-398,434-451`; `workbench/system/VMM/shared_defs.h:343-363`). `ValidSettings()` checks only for a nonempty name, not its length (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/mui.c:199-217`). Thus a selected or typed filename of 80 or more characters overflows this field. `CurrentConfig` is an automatic `struct VMMConfig` in `WriteConfigFile()`; a name near the gadget's 256-character limit extends past the struct and can overwrite neighboring stack storage as well as the trailing configuration fields. Partition-device names take the separate `ST_PartName` path and are not the trigger described here.

Bound the file name to the 80-byte field (including its terminator) before saving, or enlarge and version the serialized configuration field. **Affected configuration and trigger:** saving VMM preferences with paging device set to file or pseudo-part and an `ST_FileName` value of at least 80 characters. **Consequence:** overwrite past `PartOrFileName`, corrupt configuration fields and, for sufficiently long values, adjacent stack storage during config save. **Confidence:** high for the 256-character gadget limit, unchecked copy, and 80-byte destination; no long path or config save was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6029

**VMM Preferences cleanup removes and drains an unregistered, partially initialized commodity port after signal allocation fails.** `InstallAsCommodity()` allocates `ExtCxPort` without clearing it, initializes only `PrefsTask` and `ShowSignal`, then calls `AllocSignal()` before initializing the embedded port fields, message list, or publishing it with `AddPort()` (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/aloha.c:63-94`). If `AllocSignal()` returns `-1`, the function returns FALSE immediately (`:73-76`). The selected caller then calls `CloseAll()` (`main.c:160-168`); because `ExtCxPort` and `CxParams` are already non-NULL, cleanup reaches `UninstallAsCommodity()` (`main.c:70-80`; `aloha.c:143-162`). Cleanup then also uses the uninitialized `mp_SigBit` and `ln_Name` fields in `FreeSignal()` and `FreeVec()` (`aloha.c:158-161`).

Track explicit port initialization/publication state and only remove/drain/free fields that were initialized; initialize the message list before any cleanup can inspect it. **Affected configuration and trigger:** VMM Preferences startup when `CxParams` and `ExtCxPort` allocations succeed but `AllocSignal(-1)` fails before port initialization/publication. **Consequence:** cleanup operates on uninitialized list links/message-list state and signal/name fields, so startup failure can fault or corrupt list state instead of unwinding cleanly. **Confidence:** high for the allocation/publication ordering and unconditional cleanup path; no signal exhaustion or startup failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6032

**VMM Preferences continues with an invalid show-window signal after `AllocSignal()` fails.** The GUI startup path assigns `AllocSignal(-1L)` directly to `ExtCxPort->ShowSignal` and does not check for the `-1` failure result (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/main.c:173-174`). `CloseAll()` treats `-1` as the unallocated sentinel during cleanup, but successful GUI setup proceeds to form `WaitMask` with `1L << ShowSignal`, and the event loop checks the same shift (`mui.c:484,519`). **Workbook opens Info with no lock, so Info displays `SYS:` as the selected object's location.** Workbook's icon Info method calls `WBInfo(BNULL, my->File, NULL)` with the icon's fully qualified file path but no parent lock (`workbench/system/Workbook/wbicon.c:318-325`). `WBInfo()` forwards both values as Workbench startup arguments (`workbench/libs/workbench/wbinfo.c:61-68`). ## GD6049

**Info can overwrite a completed scan's NULL process marker with a stale process pointer and spin forever on exit.** Before launching a size scan, Info sets `scanState = SCANRUN`, then assigns the result of `CreateNewProcTags()` to `scanProcess` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/Info/main.c:1385-1404`). Info's shutdown path sets `SCANDIE` and busy-jumps until that field becomes NULL (`Info/main.c:1425-1431`); the completed worker will not clear it again, so shutdown can spin indefinitely. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
