**Source and trigger:** `NetPrefs_Bootstrap()` scans `PROGDIR:NetModules`, but `LoadNetModules()` returns silently when the directory cannot be locked and ignores individual `OpenLibrary()` failures (`workbench/prefs/network/netpeditor.c:863-912,938-947`). The bootstrap does not require any protocol handlers to have registered. The IPv4/IPv6 module startup callbacks register their handlers only after their window classes initialize successfully (`Modules/IPv4/ipv4_init.c:30-46`; `Modules/IPv6/ipv6_init.c:30-46`). Separately, `RegisterProtoHandler()` allocates the registry node and silently does nothing if `AllocMem()` fails (`netprefs_library.c:134-157`). The entry point ignores the bootstrap result and continues into `InitNetworkPrefs()` (`main.c:31-42`).

When parsing an interface line, `ReadNetworkPrefs()` offers each non-core token to registered protocol readers; if no handler claims it, parsing continues without preserving that token or creating its protocol-address node (`prefsdata.c:1137-1154`). During writing, `WriteNetworkPrefs()` emits protocol tokens only by looking up each stored address node's handler and calling its writer (`prefsdata.c:383-393,429-453`). `SaveNetworkPrefs()` writes the resulting configuration to both `ENVARC:AROSTCP/db/interfaces` and `ENV:AROSTCP/db/interfaces` (`prefsdata.c:1005-1022`). Thus a readable source configuration containing `IP=`, `NETMASK=`, `GW=`, `IP6=`, `PREFIXLEN=`, or `GW6=` can lose the settings for any protocol whose handler was unavailable during that read; a subsequent SAVE overwrites the target configuration without those address tokens. A partial registry loses only the affected protocol family. The same loss can occur after a handler's address-node allocation fails while reading, but that allocation-failure path is not needed to establish this finding.

**Consequence and scope:** Silent loss of interface address configuration on SAVE or GUI Save/Use, with possible impact to the next stack startup. The Network Preferences application and IPv4/IPv6 modules are optional build targets (`workbench/prefs/network/mmakefile.src:21-27,52-78`); no claim is made that a normal installed target has a missing module. Concrete triggers are an absent/unopenable/incomplete `PROGDIR:NetModules` set, protocol window-class initialization failure, or registry-node allocation failure. This is distinct from GD6162, where failed PAWinClass creation leaves a stale global base and a later bootstrap falsely reports success. Confidence: high in the token-loss and overwrite path; conditional on handler unavailability. Source-only; no module failure or configuration write was induced.

## GD6158

**Summary:** Network Preferences returns its editor object without initializing its instance data when no protocol window is registered or a required auxiliary window fails to construct.

**Source and trigger:** `NetPEditor__OM_NEW()` first creates the main PrefsEditor object, then constructs protocol sub-windows and the separate interface, tunnel, host, wireless, and server windows. `protoCount` starts at zero and increases for registered protocol handlers (`workbench/prefs/network/netpeditor.c:1270-1283`). The instance-data population and notification setup are guarded by `self != NULL`, all five auxiliary windows being non-NULL, and `protoCount > 0` (`:1621-1626`). If the main object exists but this guard fails, the method skips all assignments to `NetPEditor_DATA` and nevertheless returns `self` (`:1621-1626,2009-2010`). The zero-handler case is directly reachable when module discovery/registration fails as in GD6157; failure to construct one of the separate windows is the other stated trigger.

The standalone app passes `NetPEditorObject` as `WindowContents` and proceeds when the application object is non-NULL (`workbench/prefs/network/main.c:48-70`). Its Setup method unconditionally uses the instance pointers for list/image operations, attaches the auxiliary windows, and calls `NetworkPrefs2Gadgets()` (`netpeditor.c:2013-2044`). If setup returns, the PrefsEditor Save and Use methods also call `Gadgets2NetworkPrefs()` using the same uninitialized fields (`:2095-2105,2132-2142`; `Gadgets2NetworkPrefs()` first reads `netped_interfaceList` at `:551-565`). A zeroed instance would still yield NULL object pointers; the source does not initialize these fields on the failing branch.

**Consequence and scope:** The interactive Network Preferences editor can dispatch MUI methods through missing or invalid object pointers during Setup, and may likewise fail if Save/Use is reached. This is separate from GD6157's loss of address tokens during headless/config saving and GD6162's stale global registry base. The main object must survive construction while one of the guard conditions fails; no claim is made for failure of the main object itself. Confidence: high that the constructor returns an uninitialized instance on the stated path; the precise MUI failure symptom is source-inferred. Source-only; no MUI allocation failure or GUI operation was induced.

## GD6159

**Summary:** Network Preferences reports successful import and export while ignoring the supplied file handle; export can create or truncate an empty file.

**Source and trigger:** `NetPEditor__MUIM_PrefsEditor_ImportFH()` never reads `message->fh`; it calls `NetworkPrefs2Gadgets()` from the already loaded in-memory settings, runs the DHCP mode update, and returns TRUE (`workbench/prefs/network/netpeditor.c:2154-2167`). `NetPEditor__MUIM_PrefsEditor_ExportFH()` returns TRUE without writing (`:2169-2177`). The inherited PrefsEditor filename methods open an import file in `MODE_OLDFILE` and pass its handle to ImportFH, and open/create the export destination in `MODE_NEWFILE` before passing the handle to ExportFH (`workbench/classes/zune/prefseditor/prefseditor.c:319-365`). `MODE_NEWFILE` therefore truncates an existing destination or creates a new one before this no-op succeeds.

**Consequence and scope:** A user-triggered Import reports success but leaves the current preferences unchanged; Export reports success after leaving an empty file at the selected path. PrefsEditor Revert also uses ImportFH on its backup handle, so its import step likewise ignores backup content before the inherited revert path exports the current in-memory values (`prefseditor.c:384-406`). The finding concerns the Network Preferences PrefsEditor Import/Export/Revert methods; headless `FROM`/`SAVE` argument handling is separate. Confidence: high from direct method bodies and inherited file-open callers. No file was imported or exported; source-only.

## GD6160

**Summary:** Network Preferences can silently lose IPv4/IPv6 address records when copying or rebuilding an interface's protocol-address list fails allocation.

**Source and trigger:** The interface-list construct hook copies the whole interface, resets its protocol list, then calls `ProtoAddr_CopyList()` without a success result (`workbench/prefs/network/netpeditor.c:188-206`). `ProtoAddr_CopyList()` frees the destination first, then allocates one node per source node and silently skips any failed `AllocVec()` (`workbench/prefs/network/protocols.c:163-177`). The `NetworkPrefs2Gadgets()` path inserts each global interface into this list (`netpeditor.c:671-694`), so an allocation failure during list construction leaves that editor row with an incomplete address list. Later `Gadgets2NetworkPrefs()` frees each persistent interface's original list and replaces it with a copy of the possibly incomplete editor row, again ignoring allocation failures (`:551-583`). Save and Use call this routine before writing/applying the settings (`:2095-2105,2132-2142`), making the omitted addresses persistent or active.

A second unchecked path is `proto_build_list()`: it creates a fresh list and ignores `ProtoAddr_FindOrAdd()` returning NULL for a configured slot (`:528-549`; `protocols.c:141-152`). This builder is used by interface Apply and tunnel Apply before the new list row is inserted (`netpeditor.c:2529-2538,2579-2595`). `ProtoAddr_CopyList()` then performs another best-effort copy through the list construct hook. Allocation failure can therefore omit a configured protocol node at either build or copy time; the tunnel path can lose its IPv6 endpoint node.

**Consequence and scope:** One or more configured protocol-address records can disappear from the editor's copied interface and then replace the original records when Save or Use synchronizes the list. A failed copy can also make tunnel settings lack their IPv6 node. Other interface fields are copied separately and are not the claimed loss. The trigger is memory allocation failure during list insertion, address-list rebuilding, or synchronization; the code has no error propagation or rollback for these node allocations. Confidence: high in the partial-list behavior and propagation; conditional on allocation failure. No allocation failure or settings operation was induced; source-only.

## GD6161

**Summary:** Network Preferences rewrites a valid IPv6 `/0` prefix as `/64` and accepts out-of-range prefix values that the stack later clamps.

**Source and trigger:** The IPv6 editor accepts digit characters for the prefix but does not constrain the value to the IPv6 range (`workbench/prefs/network/Modules/IPv6/ipv6_win.c:66-73`). Apply stores the numeric gadget value directly in the signed `LONG pa_prefix` (`:139-157`). The config reader parses `PREFIXLEN=` with `atol()` and performs no range check (`:302-306`). The writer treats any zero prefix as the unset/default sentinel and emits 64 (`:244-249`); the Show method does the same when populating the editor (`:119-126`). Therefore a manually configured valid `/0` is displayed and saved as `/64` after load, or is changed to `/64` on save even when no editor interaction occurs.

Negative and greater-than-128 prefix values are also retained and emitted by the preferences module. The selected AROSTCP stack caller obtains the value from `PREFIXLEN` and passes it to `setprefixmask6()`, which clamps values below zero to zero and values above 128 to 128 before constructing the mask (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/bsdsocket/kern/amiga_netdb.c:627-640,458-471`). Thus the supported consequence established here is invalid persisted settings and a mismatch between the saved value and the effective stack prefix; no out-of-bounds mask write or stack memory corruption is claimed.

**Consequence and scope:** A valid default-route prefix `/0` cannot round-trip through Network Preferences and becomes `/64`. Out-of-range values can be accepted from the UI or config, remain in the written settings, and be silently applied by the AROSTCP stack as `/0` or `/128`. The issue is specific to IPv6 manual-address configuration. Confidence: high from the preference parser/editor/writer and selected stack clamp. No settings file, editor, or stack was run; source-only.

## GD6162

**Summary:** A failed `PAWinClass` initialization leaves Network Preferences with a globally published empty registry base, preventing later bootstrap attempts from retrying module setup.

**Source and trigger:** `NetPrefs_Bootstrap()` creates and initializes the registration base, stores it in the process-global pointer with `NetPrefs_SetBase()`, and only then calls `PAWin_InitClass()` (`workbench/prefs/network/netpeditor.c:922-938`). If `MUI_CreateCustomClass()` fails, `PAWin_InitClass()` returns FALSE while `PAWinClass` remains NULL (`protocols.c:327-334`). The failure path returns NULL but does not clear `g_NetPrefsBase` (`netprefs_library.c:205-215`). On the next call, `NetPrefs_Bootstrap()` sees the non-NULL global base and returns it at the initial guard, before retrying `PAWin_InitClass()`, registering `PAWin.Class`, or calling `LoadNetModules()` (`netpeditor.c:924-927,937-959`).

The standalone entry point ignores the first bootstrap result and continues to read preferences or perform headless SAVE/USE (`workbench/prefs/network/main.c:31-42`). In GUI mode its later `NetPEditor__OM_NEW()` calls bootstrap again (`netpeditor.c:930-934,963-966`), receives the stale base as success, and proceeds without protocol handlers; the zero-handler constructor path is separately described by GD6158. In headless mode the registry remains empty while protocol config tokens are parsed and saved, as described by GD6157. These are downstream manifestations of this stale-base state, not additional claims in this finding.

**Consequence and scope:** A transient `MUI_CreateCustomClass()` allocation/setup failure during the initial bootstrap poisons the process-global bootstrap state: that run cannot initialize protocol plugins on retry. GUI setup consequently lacks protocol windows and handlers; headless preference processing can discard protocol settings. This is conditional on the shared class creation failure. Confidence: high in the global-state and early-return path; the class-creation failure itself is not induced. No GUI, allocation failure, or config write was run; source-only.

## GD6163

**Summary:** Network Preferences exits with a successful process status when command-line SAVE or USE fails.

**Source and trigger:** `SAVE` and `USE` are supported command-line switches (`workbench/prefs/network/args.c:11-25`). `SaveNetworkPrefs()` and `UseNetworkPrefs()` return specific `ErrorCode` values for default-file copy, preference writes, wireless/mobile setup, server writes, and stack/device restart failures (`prefsdata.c:1005-1036`; enum in `prefsdata.h:57-67`). However, `InitNetworkPrefs()` has a `void` return type and discards these results in both branches (`prefsdata.c:1646-1671`). `main()` ignores the bootstrap result as well, calls `InitNetworkPrefs()`, and reaches `return 0` regardless of the requested headless operation's outcome (`main.c:31-42,78-82`).

**Consequence and scope:** A shell script or caller cannot distinguish a successful headless SAVE/USE from a failed write, failed default-file copy, or failed network restart by the process status; the operation can also have performed some earlier writes before a later step failed. The trigger is invocation with `SAVE` or `USE` plus any returned error from the corresponding operation. This concerns command-line headless status reporting; GUI methods separately display their `ErrorCode`. Confidence: high from the result-returning operations and the discarded result path. No filesystem/device failure or command invocation was induced; source-only.

## GD6164

**Summary:** Network Preferences does not close the locale reference it opens during startup.

**Source and trigger:** When `LocaleBase` is available, `Locale_Initialize()` opens both a catalog and the current locale (`workbench/prefs/network/locale.c:40-55`). `OpenLocale(NULL)` returns the current locale and increments its `il_Count` under the locale semaphore (`workbench/libs/locale/openlocale.c:178-191`). `Locale_Deinitialize()` closes the catalog but never calls `CloseLocale(locale)` (`workbench/prefs/network/locale.c:57-60`). `CloseLocale()` normally decrements an opened non-default locale's count and releases it when eligible (`workbench/libs/locale/closelocale.c:48-72`). The leak is relevant when the current locale is a non-default locale; the locale library intentionally ignores closing its default-locale object.

**Consequence and scope:** Network Preferences leaves one extra reference to the non-default current locale after its app task exits. If that locale is later replaced, the retained reference can prevent the old locale object and its associated resources from being reclaimed. The trigger requires `LocaleBase` to be open and a non-default current locale; no effect is claimed for the default locale path. Confidence: high in the unmatched acquire/release; downstream reclamation depends on a later locale change. No locale change or process run was performed; source-only.

## GD6165

**Summary:** The ILBM datatype discards indexed BODY mask planes, leaving Picture's masked RastPort render paths without a mask and without a fallback blit.

**Source and trigger:** For non-HAM ILBM, `ReadILBM()` calls `ReadBitMapPic()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ilbm/ilbmclass.c:568-589`). The reader allocates the destination bitmap at the color depth only (`:118-120,144`) and publishes only `PDTA_BitMap` (`:200`). For uncompressed BODY data it advances over each extra mask row without storing it (`:157-173`). For ByteRun1 it decodes `totdepth` planes into a row buffer but copies only the `bmh_Depth` color planes into the bitmap (`:175-195`); the extra decoded mask plane is not retained. This applies when the ILBM BMHD says `mskHasMask` and is separate from transparent-color masking.

Picture's `PDTA_MaskPlane` getter calls `CreateMaskPlane()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:464-468`). That helper creates a synthesized plane only for `mskHasTransparentColor`, not `mskHasMask` (`colorhandling.c:579-632`), so the retained `MaskPlane` remains NULL for this ILBM input. In `render_on_rastport()`, the `mskHasMask` branch obtains that NULL plane and invokes `BltMaskBitMapRastPort()` only when it is non-NULL; it has no ordinary bitmap-blit fallback (`pictureclass.c:630-648`). The selected Picture class reaches this renderer through both `GM_RENDER` and `DTM_DRAW` (`:716,1500`).

**Consequence and scope:** Indexed ILBM images whose transparency is supplied by a BODY mask plane are not drawn by these Picture RastPort render paths, including ordinary and ByteRun1 compressed bodies. This does not claim failure for `mskHasTransparentColor`, for which Picture synthesizes a mask, or for HAM's separate RGB conversion path. Confidence: high in mask-plane loss and selected draw-path behavior. No image was loaded or rendered; source-only.

## GD6167

**Summary:** Picture `DT_Write()` preserves `mskHasMask` in the ILBM BMHD but omits the corresponding mask plane from BODY and its declared size.

**Source and trigger:** The selected Picture class dispatch exposes `DTM_WRITE` through `picture.conf:45-46`. `DT_Write()` copies `bmh_Masking` into the file BMHD without checking or retrieving `PDTA_MaskPlane` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1682-1700,1784-1790`). Its `bodySize` and FORM size count only `bytesPerRow * numplanes * height` (`:1703-1706,1744-1747`). In the indexed path (`numplanes <= 8`), it writes each row's `numplanes` bitmap planes and never writes an extra mask plane (`:1809-1810,1857-1871,1883-1893`). Therefore, when the source BMHD uses `mskHasMask`, output metadata says the BODY has a mask plane while the BODY size and data contain color planes only.

**Consequence and scope:** The exported ILBM is internally inconsistent and does not preserve its source transparency mask. A reader that follows the BMHD mask declaration will interpret the color-only BODY as including additional mask data, so the saved image cannot reliably round-trip. The verified path is indexed Picture output at 1–8 planes with `mskHasMask`; no claim is made here about the separate 24-bit writer or other `DT_Write()` defects. Confidence: high from the emitted BMHD, BODY length, and plane loop. No file was written or reloaded; source-only.

## GD6168

**Summary:** The Picture 24-bit `DT_Write()` path places BODY eight bytes beyond the end declared by the FORM size.

**Source and trigger:** For a 24-plane picture, `DT_Write()` sets `numcolors=0`, `iffOffset=40`, and declares `FORM` size `bodySize + 40` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1715-1718,1744-1756`). After the fixed header, the BMHD chunk ends at absolute offset 40. An ILBM BODY chunk should therefore start at 40: its four-byte ID, four-byte chunk size, then data beginning at 48. The 24-bit writer instead sets `offset=(numcolors * 3)+48`, writes the BODY ID at 48 and size at 52, then advances to BODY data at 56 (`:1896-1916,2053-2058`). The BODY data ends at `56 + bodySize`, while the declared FORM ends at `8 + (bodySize + 40)`, which is `48 + bodySize`; the data extends eight bytes beyond the declared FORM.

The selected Picture class maps `DTM_WRITE` to `DT_Write()` (`picture.conf:45-46`). This path is taken for 24-plane Picture objects with a writable file handle; the NULL-handle capability probe returns before serialization (`pictureclass.c:1651-1657`).

**Consequence and scope:** The generated 24-bit ILBM has an eight-byte gap where the BODY chunk should begin and a FORM length that excludes the final eight bytes. Consumers that honor FORM boundaries may not see a complete BODY chunk; the output does not reliably round-trip as an ILBM. This is separate from GD6167's indexed mask-plane omission. Confidence: high from absolute writer offsets and declared length arithmetic. No file was written or reloaded; source-only.

## GD6169

**Summary:** `AddDisplayDriverA()` leaks its allocated per-driver configuration on rejection, setup failure, successful setup with no registered display, and final display teardown.

**Source and trigger:** The function allocates `struct gfxdriver_data` before parsing parameters or checking monitor-ID collisions (`rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:181-194,236-279`). If the requested ID range is already occupied, it sets `DD_ID_EXISTS`, skips setup, releases the semaphore, and returns without freeing `cfg` (`:270-279,281-297`). If `driver_Setup()` fails, the function likewise maps the error to `DD_IN_USE`/`DD_DRIVER_ERROR` and returns without freeing the allocation (`:284-297`). Setup can fail if the HIDD cannot be instantiated or if the boot queue entry cannot be allocated (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:369-399,401-413`).

On successful setup, `display_Register()` stores the same config pointer in each display record's `display_cfg` (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:366-384`). If the HIDD is created but exposes no display, or all `display_Setup()` attempts fail, `driver_Setup()` still returns TRUE and no display record retains `cfg` (graphics_driver.c:372-394; graphics_display.c:366-410); this registration-success discrepancy is separately tracked as GD5906. When a registered display is removed, `display_Expunge()` frees its `monitor_displaydata`, and when the last display for that HIDD is removed it removes the driver object, but it never frees the associated `display_cfg` (`graphics_display.c:221-275`). A source-wide search of the graphics core finds no `FreeMem()` for `gfxdriver_data`.

**Consequence and scope:** Each rejected or failed registration leaks one config allocation. A successfully registered driver also leaks its shared config when its final display is removed, and successful driver-object creation without a registered display leaves an unowned config allocation. Repeated duplicate registrations, failed hotplug attempts, or driver remove/re-add cycles can accumulate these small allocations. Multi-display drivers share one config, so cleanup must occur only when no display or boot-queue entry references it. Confidence: high from the allocation, pointer publication, and complete teardown path. No registration, allocation failure, or display removal was induced; source-only.

## GD6170

**Disk-started HeadlessGfx boot registration retains a stack tag list for deferred driver creation.** `HeadlessGfx:Disk` builds `attrs[6]` in `main()` and fills it from the icon's MAXDEPTH, FORCEDEPTH, WIDTH, HEIGHT and DEPTH tooltypes (`rom/hidds/gfx/headless/disk_startup.c:51-52,89-115,141-172`). It passes that local array to `AddDisplayDriverA()` together with `DDRV_BootMode=TRUE` (`:53-57,174`). `AddDisplayDriverA()` parses the separate driver-policy `tags`, then calls `driver_Setup(cfg, attrs, FALSE, ...)` and returns after releasing the display-database semaphore (`rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:168-234,281-297`). Because the driver is boot-mode and `force` is false, `driver_Setup()` allocates a queue entry and stores `attrs` as `boot_attribs` without copying its contents (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:401-414`). `main()` then returns, ending the lifetime of the stack array (`disk_startup.c:177-190`). Later, `BestModeID()` or `NextDisplayInfo()` can replay the queue; replay passes the saved pointer to `HW_AddDriver()` (`rom/graphics/bestmodeida.c:254`; `nextdisplayinfo.c:64`; `graphics_driver.c:296-323,326-370`). The HeadlessGfx root constructor reads the supplied list with `GetTagData()` to configure depth and nominal dimensions (`rom/hidds/gfx/headless/headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:186-201,232-255`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the disk-started `kernel-hidd-gfx-headlessgfx-monitor` path (`rom/hidds/gfx/headless/mmakefile.src:5-14`), when icon tooltypes add one or more attributes and the boot entry is replayed after `main()` returns. The OpenSBI boot manifest selects the HeadlessGfx target (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:51`); the resident startup path passes NULL attributes and is not affected.

**Consequence:** the deferred constructor reads through an expired stack pointer. Intervening stack reuse can replace the configured values or the `TAG_DONE` terminator, so depth/geometry settings become indeterminate and tag scanning may continue beyond the former array. Copy the attributes into queue-owned storage and release that copy on replay success, retry removal, or queue teardown. **Confidence:** high for the stored pointer, stack lifetime, and later constructor read; the resulting stale values or scan extent depend on stack reuse. No monitor, icon configuration, or replay was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6171

**Consolidated into GD5906 (2026-10-25).** This was the HeadlessGfx instance of graphics.library accepting a constructed but displayless HIDD as successful and freeing the replay entry. The specific constructor and boot-queue trace is now included in GD5906; no separate finding is counted.

## GD6172

**`BeginUpdate()` dereferences a failed visible-damage region allocation.** After constructing `damage_region`, `BeginUpdate()` requests a second temporary region by intersecting `l->VisibleRegion` with that damage (`rom/hyperlayers/beginupdate.c:101`). `AndRegionRegionND()` returns NULL when its initial `NewRegion()` fails or when allocation of the result rectangle list fails (`rom/graphics/andregionregionnd.c:52-84`). `BeginUpdate()` immediately passes the unchecked result to `AndRegionRegion()` (`beginupdate.c:101-102`); the latter reads `R2->RegionRectangle` before any NULL check (`rom/graphics/andregionregion.c:53-55`). This happens after `BeginUpdate()` has locked the layer and before it reaches its normal cleanup and success return (`beginupdate.c:68-70,131-139`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting the `kernel-layers` module (`rom/hyperlayers/mmakefile.src:13-24,71-73`; the ROM aggregate and RISC-V OpenSBI image include it at `rom/mmakefile.src:22-27,96-110` and `arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:34-44`). The failure occurs when `BeginUpdate()` has constructed `damage_region` but allocation fails while creating its visible-damage intersection. `BeginUpdate()` is exported in the selected Layers API (`rom/hyperlayers/layers.conf:27`) and the selected Intuition `BeginRefresh()` caller invokes it after locking the layer (`rom/intuition/beginrefresh.c:90-106`). This is distinct from GD5775, where `BeginUpdate()` returns FALSE and the Intuition caller's failure cleanup/pairing is the issue.

**Consequence:** NULL is dereferenced in region intersection, so the update can fault while the layer remains locked. Check the intersection result before passing it to `AndRegionRegion()` and unwind the region and layer-lock state. **Confidence:** high for the nullable allocation result, unchecked call, and dereference; occurrence requires region-result allocation failure. No allocation failure, refresh or layer operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6173

**Hyperlayers dereferences failed region intersections in several locked operations.** `AndRegionRegionND()` returns NULL when it cannot allocate its result region or required rectangle list (`rom/graphics/andregionregionnd.c:52-84`). Three Hyperlayers consumers do not check that nullable result before using it:

- `_ShowLayer()` passes the result to `AndRegionRegion()`, whose `R2->RegionRectangle` access dereferences NULL (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:1136-1137`; `rom/graphics/andregionregion.c:53-59`). It then walks `r->RegionRectangle` (`basicfuncs.c:1139-1142`). The selected `CreateLayerTagList()` caller invokes `_ShowLayer()` before releasing the layer-info lock (`rom/hyperlayers/createlayertaglist.c:370-376`).
- `_InternalInstallClipRegion()` passes its result to `AndRegionRegion()` and then to `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()`/`DisposeRegion()` (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:1428-1436`). Public `InstallClipRegion()` calls this helper while holding the layer lock (`rom/hyperlayers/installclipregion.c:62-68`).
- `CollectPixelsLayer()` dereferences `_r->RegionRectangle` for a simple-refresh layer, and later passes `_r` to `ClearRegionRegion()`, which dereferences its first argument's bounds (`rom/hyperlayers/collectpixelslayer.c:78-79,84-112,235-236`; `rom/graphics/clearregionregion.c:52-59`). This is reached for a visible non-root layer when its parent bounds overlap the requested region (`collectpixelslayer.c:84-98`), while both layer-info and layer locks are held.

The sibling `_BackupPartsOfLayer()` and `_ShowPartsOfLayer()` check this helper's result before using it (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:1036-1040,1103-1106`) and are not part of this finding. `BeginUpdate()` has its own unchecked second-intersection path under GD6172; ClipRect-pool and backing-bitmap failures are separately covered by GD6174 and GD6175.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Hyperlayers builds when allocation fails during one of these visible-region intersections: layer creation/show (`_ShowLayer()`), public clip-region installation, or pixel collection for an overlapping visible layer. **Consequence:** the NULL region is dereferenced before the operation can unwind; the selected call paths hold layer locks, and layer creation or clip/refresh processing can be interrupted with those locks held. Check the helper result and unwind the caller's region and lock state. **Confidence:** high for the nullable return and unchecked consumers; occurrence requires region/result allocation failure and the stated path. No allocation failure, layer creation, clip-region install or pixel collection was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6174

**Finding:** Hyperlayers dereferences failed ClipRect pool allocations while building layer clip lists.

`_AllocClipRect()` first reuses a per-layer spare node, but when that list is empty it returns `AllocPooled(lb_ClipRectPool, sizeof(struct ClipRect))` directly (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:313-333`). `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()` does not check that result before writing its bounds, `lobs`, and `Next` fields (`basicfuncs.c:418-429`). `_ShowLayer()` has a separate direct `AllocPooled()` call and immediately writes the returned pointer's bounds and `lobs` (`basicfuncs.c:1139-1155`). The pool's successful creation during library initialization does not guarantee later allocations succeed (`rom/hyperlayers/layers_init.c:28-33`).

The shared builder is used by `BeginUpdate()`, `_BackupPartsOfLayer()`, `_ShowPartsOfLayer()`, and `_InternalInstallClipRegion()` (`rom/hyperlayers/beginupdate.c:111-115`; `basicfuncs.c:1040,1106,1431`). These operations publish or consume the generated list. The public clip-region wrapper holds the layer lock across `_InternalInstallClipRegion()` (`rom/hyperlayers/installclipregion.c:62-68`); `BeginUpdate()` also runs under the layer lock. `_ShowLayer()` is reached during `CreateLayerTagList()` while the layer-info lock is held (`rom/hyperlayers/createlayertaglist.c:370-376`). Before this call, `CreateLayerTagList()` has already inserted the new layer into the layer-order links (`:280-310`); the pool allocation is unchecked, so NULL is dereferenced before the caller can reach `UnlockLayers()` and return. The path does not reach the function's earlier `failexit` cleanup, either.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Hyperlayers, when a layer operation needs a new ClipRect, its spare-node list is empty (for `_AllocClipRect()`), and the pool allocation fails. `_ShowLayer()` always allocates directly from the pool for each generated rectangle. **Consequence:** NULL dereference during layer creation/show, update, visibility backup/show, or clip-region installation; the locked caller cannot complete its normal cleanup. Check allocations and unwind any partially built list and lock state. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked dereferences and call paths; occurrence requires pool allocation failure. This is distinct from GD6175, which concerns a ClipRect whose backing bitmap allocation fails. No allocation failure or layer operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6175

**Finding:** Hyperlayers does not handle failed refresh backing-bitmap allocations before copying from or to the missing bitmap.

There are two affected refresh paths. For simple-refresh layers, `_CopyClipRectsToClipRects()` allocates a backing bitmap when `backupmode` is true, stores the result in `_cr->BitMap`, assigns it to `destbm`, and calls `BltBitMap()` without checking for NULL (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:721-747`). `ChangeLayerShape()` and `MoveSizeLayer()` reach this path with `backupsimplerefresh=TRUE` (`rom/hyperlayers/changelayershape.c` and `movesizelayer.c`; see caller traces in the coverage ledger).

For smart-refresh layers, `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()` stores an unchecked `AllocBitMap()` result in a hidden ClipRect (`basicfuncs.c:431-439`). Its selected callers include `_BackupPartsOfLayer()` and `_ShowPartsOfLayer()` (`:1040-1053,1106-1117`), which install the resulting ClipRect lists for later layer transitions. `_ShowLayer()` has a similar unchecked allocation (`:1213-1220`); its sole caller, `CreateLayerTagList()`, ignores its return (`createlayertaglist.c:370-371`), and `_ShowLayer()` continues and returns TRUE (`basicfuncs.c:1226-1246`), leaving construction successful with any hidden ClipRect's failed bitmap still missing. `_CopyClipRectsToClipRects()` can use a newly allocated hidden bitmap as the destination for an overlapping copy (`:625-640,721-747`), or create a hidden ClipRect without storage in its non-overlap backup path (`:932-939`). Later `_ShowPartsOfLayer()` selects a hidden ClipRect's `BitMap` as the source and passes it to `BltBitMap()` (`:826-839` and subsequent copy). In the selected graphics implementation, `BltBitMap()` evaluates `IS_HIDD_BM(srcBitMap)` / `IS_HIDD_BM(destBitMap)` before any NULL guard (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:123`; the macro reads a bitmap field in `rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:632`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Hyperlayers simple-refresh or smart-refresh operation when a required `AllocBitMap()` fails. The simple-refresh case reaches the failed destination in the same backup call; smart-refresh can fail during creation/backup and reach the NULL source on immediate copy or later reveal/exposure. **Consequence:** NULL bitmap dereference during `BltBitMap()` in refresh backup or restore. Check the allocation before publishing the ClipRect or copying, and unwind or preserve a valid refresh state on failure. **Confidence:** high for unchecked allocation and selected NULL-sensitive copy paths; occurrence requires bitmap allocation failure and the described refresh transition. This is distinct from GD6174's ClipRect-node allocation failure. No allocation failure, refresh, exposure or blit was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6176

**Finding:** `CollectPixelsLayer()` constructs malformed callback fields for requested pixels that remain on the screen background.

After walking the layer stack, `CollectPixelsLayer()` sends one callback for each rectangle left in the requested region (`rom/hyperlayers/collectpixelslayer.c:262-289`). In this path it assigns `_rect.MinX` to `cplm.xSrc`, then mistakenly assigns `_rect.MinY` to `xSrc` again, leaving `ySrc` uninitialized. It assigns `_rect.MaxY` to `yDest` instead of the top coordinate and never initializes `minterm`. The public message layout confirms these are independent `LONG` fields (`compiler/include/graphics/clip.h:146-157`). A callback that copies the reported source rectangle therefore reads from the wrong coordinates, and the unset fields have indeterminate values.

The sole maintained in-tree caller found is the Lens demo. Its callback returns immediately when `cplm->bm == NULL`, as it is for the screen-background path, so it does not demonstrate the bad fields in-tree (`developer/demos/lens.c:109-117`). The function is exported through the Layers API; external clients that consume background callbacks can observe the malformed message.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Hyperlayers, when `CollectPixelsLayer()` receives a region with any pixels remaining after layer traversal, such as a requested area extending onto screen background. **Consequence:** consumers receive invalid source/destination coordinates and an indeterminate `minterm`; background pixels can be copied from the wrong location or processed unpredictably. Initialize each message field from the corresponding rectangle edge and define the background bitmap/minterm contract. **Confidence:** high for the field assignments; practical impact depends on an external callback processing `bm == NULL`. No callback or pixel operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6177

**Finding:** `CollectPixelsLayer()` drops requested pixels when they intersect a visible superbitmap layer.

For each visible non-root layer whose parent bounds overlap the request, the function intersects the request with `l->shape` and dispatches pixels for simple-refresh or smart-refresh layers (`rom/hyperlayers/collectpixelslayer.c:84-98,104-223`). The `IS_SUPERREFRESH(l)` branch is empty (`:228-230`). Execution nevertheless continues to `ClearRegionRegion(_r, r)` and disposes `_r` (`:231-236`), removing those pixels from the unprocessed region. The final screen-background callback handles only what remains (`:262-289`), so it cannot recover pixels already subtracted for the superbitmap layer. The public function describes collecting all pixels within the requested region and calling the callback for found areas (`:44-57`); the function is exported in the selected Layers configuration (`rom/hyperlayers/layers.conf:63`).

The maintained Lens demo is the only checked-in C caller found; its selected usage starts from a normal window layer and does not exercise superbitmap handling (`developer/demos/lens.c:202-204`). The finding therefore concerns the exported API when called with a region intersecting a visible superbitmap layer; no in-tree caller demonstrates that specific use.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Hyperlayers; a caller requests pixels in a region that intersects a visible `LAYERSUPER` layer. **Consequence:** the callback is never told about those intersecting pixels, and the function removes them from the remaining region as if handled. A caller collecting/copying the requested area receives incomplete pixel coverage. Implement the superbitmap callback mapping or preserve those pixels for a defined fallback. **Confidence:** high for the omission and subsequent subtraction; practical impact depends on a caller using the exported function with a superbitmap layer. No superbitmap or callback was exercised; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6178

**Finding:** `MoveSizeLayer()` does not handle failure to construct the replacement shape region.

After acquiring the LayerInfo lock and removing the current clip region, `MoveSizeLayer()` constructs `newshape` with `NewRectRegion()` (`rom/hyperlayers/movesizelayer.c:77-80,117-123`). The helper returns NULL if `NewRegion()` fails or if adding the rectangle fails (`rom/hyperlayers/intregions.h:48-63`). The caller does not check the result: if a shape hook exists it can pass `newshape` to `AndRegionRegion()` (`movesizelayer.c:124-157`), and it unconditionally takes `&newshape->bounds` for `_TranslateRect()` (`:159-160`). It therefore cannot take the documented FALSE-on-out-of-memory return. The failure also occurs after the old clip region was removed and, for simple-refresh layers, after setting the temporary avoid-backfill flag; control does not reach the normal clip restoration or `UnlockLayers()` (`:96-108,433-438`).

`MoveLayer()` and `SizeLayer()` directly return `MoveSizeLayer()` and document FALSE for out-of-memory (`rom/hyperlayers/movelayer.c:30-44,63`; `sizelayer.c:26-43,63`). Selected Intuition move/resize paths call `MoveSizeLayer()` and ignore its result, then update the Window's stored geometry (`rom/intuition/windowclasses.c:100-112,140-151`; more callers at `:700-736,1018-1028`). If the NULL dereference were converted to a normal failure without caller changes, those callers would still need to avoid publishing geometry inconsistent with the layer; currently the immediate failure prevents normal lock/state cleanup.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Hyperlayers, when `NewRectRegion()` fails during `MoveSizeLayer()` due to region or rectangle-list allocation failure. **Consequence:** NULL dereference while the LayerInfo lock is held, with the prior clip region removed and the normal unlock/restore path skipped; the advertised allocation-error return is not honored. Check the region result and restore clip/backfill/lock state on failure; propagate and handle the FALSE result in callers that update window geometry. **Confidence:** high for the NULL path and lock/clip state; occurrence requires allocation failure. No move, resize or allocation failure was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6179

**Finding:** `ChangeLayerShape()` dereferences a failed allocation for the layer's clipped shape.

`ChangeLayerShape()` acquires the LayerInfo lock, backs up visible pixels, and disposes the currently installed `l->shape` before allocating its replacement with `NewRegion()` (`rom/hyperlayers/changelayershape.c:71-93,128-135`). If `NewRegion()` fails, it assigns NULL to `l->shape`; the failure branch merely skips the rectangle initialization. The function then intersects the requested `l->shaperegion` with `l->shape` when one exists (`:143-144`), and unconditionally takes `&l->shape->bounds` for `_TranslateRect()` (`:146`). Thus a normal allocation failure dereferences NULL after the old clipped shape has already been disposed. The only unlock is after the main operation block (`:246`), which is not reached after the dereference.

The API is exported as a Layers vector and is called by Intuition's `ChangeWindowShape()` path and Hyperlayers' `ScaleLayer()` (`rom/intuition/changewindowshape.c:92-109`; `rom/hyperlayers/scalelayer.c:78`). Intuition serializes its caller with the screen refresh lock, but that does not handle the failed region allocation inside the layer operation. The public API returns the previously installed shape rather than a success Boolean, so the allocation failure also has no documented error return path.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Hyperlayers, when `NewRegion()` fails while `ChangeLayerShape()` constructs its clipped `l->shape`. **Consequence:** NULL dereference with the LayerInfo lock held after the old clipped shape was discarded; layer shape state is left incomplete and the caller cannot receive normal completion. Allocate the replacement before discarding the old region, check all region-operation results, and unwind with a documented failure result. **Confidence:** high for the failure branch and dereference; occurrence requires region allocation failure. No layer shape change or allocation failure was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6180

**Finding:** `ChangeLayerShape()` leaves `cutnewshape` empty, so it can skip visibility reconstruction for layers overlapped only by the new shape.

The function initializes the local `cutnewshape` to an empty region and never writes to it; its only later operation is `ClearRegion()` (`rom/hyperlayers/changelayershape.c:74-80,242`). After installing the changed shape, the visibility-rebuild loop decides whether to clear and recompute each visible layer's `VisibleRegion` by testing overlap against `cutnewshape.bounds` or `cutoldshape.bounds` (`:189-199`). Because `cutnewshape` stays empty, a visible layer whose area is newly covered by the changed layer, but does not overlap the old shape, fails this test. The loop takes the `SetRegion(&r, _l->VisibleRegion)` branch instead of clearing that layer's visibility and rebuilding it through `_ShowPartsOfLayer()`.

The selected public path is `ChangeWindowShape()`, which calls `ChangeLayerShape()` under the screen refresh lock (`rom/intuition/changewindowshape.c:92-109`); Hyperlayers' `ScaleLayer()` also calls it through a shape hook (`rom/hyperlayers/scalelayer.c:78-85`). Thus the trigger does not depend on a hypothetical direct internal call: it occurs when a supported shape change newly covers visible pixels that were not covered by the prior shape. The local `cutnewshape` needs to represent the added visible area (for example, new visible shape minus the old visible shape) before it gates the rebuild.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Hyperlayers; a visible layer's shape changes to newly cover part of another visible layer, and that covered area does not intersect the old shape. **Consequence:** the other layer's `VisibleRegion` and associated ClipRect/visibility state are not rebuilt for the newly covered area, leaving stale layer visibility information and risking incorrect redraw/copy behavior. Populate and use the added-shape region when selecting layers for visibility reconstruction. **Confidence:** high that the region is never populated and the rebuild is gated by it; consequence follows for the described newly covered geometry. No shape change or display operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6181

**Finding:** Selected Hyperlayers operations ignore `SetRegion()` allocation failures and continue rebuilding layer state from incomplete regions.

`SetRegion(src, dest)` copies the source bounds, reuses/copies destination rectangles, disposes any excess destination list, then allocates any missing rectangle nodes. If those allocations fail, it returns FALSE after the destination has already been changed and may contain only a prefix of the source rectangles (`rom/graphics/setregion.c:25-39,58-86`). The selected Hyperlayers callers below ignore that result and use the destination as though the copy completed:

- `ChangeLayerVisibility()` copies a front layer's `VisibleRegion` into temporary `r`, then uses `r` for `_ShowPartsOfLayer()`; when making a layer invisible it also snapshots `VisibleRegion` into `r` before backing/restoring the lower layers (`rom/hyperlayers/changelayervisibility.c:109-127,159-181`). For simple refresh it ignores the copy into `DamageList` before intersecting and scheduling that damage (`:129-145`).
- `DeleteLayer()` snapshots the removed layer's visible region into `r`, then uses that region while restoring lower-layer visibility and ClipRects (`rom/hyperlayers/deletelayer.c:77-119`).
- `MoveSizeLayer()` ignores copies into its new-shape and visibility temporaries, then uses them in intersection, visibility reconstruction, and backfill (`rom/hyperlayers/movesizelayer.c:180-181,236,340-361`).
- `ChangeLayerShape()` ignores copies of old/current visible regions and uses the results to back up pixels and rebuild layer visibility (`rom/hyperlayers/changelayershape.c:89-93,148-149,193-219`). At line 148, if the replacement shape needs more rectangle nodes than the existing `visibleshape` and allocation of the missing suffix fails, `SetRegion()` has already assigned the full bounds and copied the common prefix before returning FALSE. The following parent intersection and visibility/backup traversal use that partial destination. The selected Intuition `ChangeWindowShape()` caller then invokes `CheckLayers()`, whose body only redraws already flagged layers and does not reconstruct shape geometry (`rom/intuition/changewindowshape.c:92-109`; `rom/intuition/inputhandler_actions.c:103-119`). This is a concrete `ChangeLayerShape()` instance of this existing GD6181 root cause, not a new finding.
- Z-order helpers ignore region copies when seeding the `show`/`r` regions used for backing and restoring layer visibility (`rom/hyperlayers/movelayerz.c:64-100,150,217-231`).
- `CreateLayerTagList()` ignores copies that seed the new layer shape and visible-region state (`rom/hyperlayers/createlayertaglist.c:312-337`). The exported `IsLayerHiddenBySibling()` query also ignores its copy into temporary `r` before intersecting and deriving its Boolean result (`rom/hyperlayers/islayerhiddenbysibling.c:78-97`).

These are selected production Hyperlayers sources; the APIs are reached by Intuition layer visibility/deletion/move/resize and shape operations, in addition to the exported Layers query. The affected effects vary by call site, but the common failure is a partially copied or empty region being treated as complete, which can omit refresh/backfill work or leave visibility and damage calculations incomplete. This is separate from GD6173's `AndRegionRegionND()` NULL result and GD6186's failed in-place region subtraction.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `kernel-layers`, when a `SetRegion()` call needs additional `RegionRectangle` storage and allocation fails. **Consequence:** the operation continues with mutated, incomplete destination state; visibility, backing, damage, or query results can be wrong, and the public layer operations do not propagate the copy failure. Check the return at each call site and unwind or preserve the old region before continuing. **Confidence:** high that the helper can return FALSE after partial destination mutation and that these selected callers ignore it; concrete state/rendering impact requires allocation failure at a listed copy. No allocation failure or layer operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6182

**Finding:** `CreateLayerTagList()` leaks its internally allocated shape region when later layer construction fails.

The constructor creates an owned `shape` with `NewRectRegion()` before allocating the `IntLayer` (`rom/hyperlayers/createlayertaglist.c:131-135,179-200`). If the layer allocation fails, it enters `failexit` with `l == NULL`; that cleanup has no reference-based branch to dispose the still-owned local `shape`. If the layer allocation succeeds but construction of `DamageList`, `VisibleRegion`, or `visibleshape` fails, the same cleanup disposes those auxiliary regions and frees `l`, but never disposes `l->shape` (`:208-215,380-392`). The failure occurs before publication/insertion into the layer list, so the caller receives NULL and cannot recover the internal region.

The shape-hook's `layershape` is supplied by the caller and is a separate pointer; this candidate is limited to the constructor-owned `shape` created by `NewRectRegion()`. The public TagList and non-TagList creation wrappers reach this constructor (`rom/hyperlayers/createupfrontlayertaglist.c:93`; corresponding behind wrapper and hook wrappers).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `kernel-layers`, when `CreateLayerTagList()` successfully creates `shape` but the later `IntLayer` allocation or any of the three auxiliary `NewRegion()` allocations fails. **Consequence:** the shape region allocation is leaked on each failed construction attempt. Dispose the owned shape on every failure exit, while preserving caller ownership of `layershape`. **Confidence:** high for both failure paths and omitted disposal. No allocation failure or layer construction was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6183

**Finding:** `MoveLayerInFrontOf()` can dereference a NULL front link when the requested layer is already frontmost.

The public contract says `layer_to_move` should be placed directly in front of `other_layer` and `other_layer` will be behind it (`rom/hyperlayers/movelayerinfrontof.c:30-48`). If the moving layer is already ahead of `other_layer`, the wrapper's sibling scan sets `toback = FALSE` and still calls `_MoveLayerToFront(layer_to_move, GetFirstFamilyMember(other_layer))` (`:78-93,101-119`). When the moving family is already at the front of the sibling list, `GetFirstFamilyMember(layer_to_move)->front` is NULL. `_MoveLayerToFront()` nevertheless unlinks it by immediately writing through `first->front->back` (`rom/hyperlayers/movelayerz.c:126-144`), causing a NULL dereference instead of treating the already-satisfied ordering as a no-op.

Intuition's `MoveWindowInFrontOf()` calls `MoveLayerInFrontOf()` for the primary window layer, and may also call it for the border and requester layers (`rom/intuition/movewindowinfrontof.c:85-105`). It serializes these operations with the screen refresh lock, but the ordering no-op case remains valid and can reach the helper.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Hyperlayers; `MoveLayerInFrontOf(A, B)` is called with compatible sibling layers where A is already frontmost and B is behind it. **Consequence:** NULL dereference in `_MoveLayerToFront()` before it can return TRUE, disrupting a public layer reorder or Intuition window ordering call. Add an early no-op return when the requested relative order is already satisfied, and guard detach links before relinking. **Confidence:** high for the wrapper branch and NULL link under the stated list order. No reorder or window operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6184

**Finding:** `UpfrontLayer()` can reorder a hidden parent family without repairing visibility when its temporary region allocation fails.

`UpfrontLayer()` selects a same-priority placement and calls `_MoveLayerToFront()` while holding the LayerInfo lock (`rom/hyperlayers/upfrontlayer.c:71-78,97-126`). In `_MoveLayerToFront()`, a visible layer uses its existing `visibleshape` as `backupr`; for a hidden layer, the helper walks its family and allocates a temporary region when it finds a visible descendant (`rom/hyperlayers/movelayerz.c:158-180`). If `NewRegion()` fails, `backupr` remains NULL. The entire backup and visibility-reconstruction block is conditional on `if (backupr)` (`:185-235`), but after skipping that block the helper still detaches/relinks the family and returns TRUE (`:238-252`). The region is required here because a hidden parent has no own visible shape to use for the descendant family.

Intuition reaches this path through `WindowToFront()` and through title-bar reveal operations (`rom/intuition/windowtofront.c:96-99`; `showtitle.c:107`; `inputhandler.c:2738-2739`). Those paths serialize screen refresh, but allocation failure still permits the list reorder without the associated visibility/ClipRect repair.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Hyperlayers; an `UpfrontLayer()` request selects a real reorder for a hidden parent whose family contains visible descendants, and `_MoveLayerToFront()` cannot allocate its temporary `backupr` region. **Consequence:** the family is moved in the layer list while descendants' visible regions and ClipRects are not reconstructed for the new order; the operation returns TRUE with stale visibility state. Abort before relinking or preserve/rebuild visibility using an allocation-safe path. **Confidence:** high for the branch and continued relink; occurrence requires the stated family topology and allocation failure. No allocation failure or layer/window reorder was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6185

**Finding:** `_MoveLayerBehind()` dereferences a failed hide-region allocation after detaching the layer family.

`_MoveLayerBehind()` creates `hide` with `NewRegion()` but does not check it (`rom/hyperlayers/movelayerz.c:14-20`). It immediately detaches the family from its old list position (`:22-34`), then uses `hide` while accumulating hidden shapes and testing overlap (`:43-77`). If the allocation failed, this path dereferences NULL at `&hide->bounds` in the backup loop; where a visible same-parent sibling is encountered, the earlier `OrRegionRegion(..., hide)` also receives NULL (`:55-56`). The family has already been unlinked, and the function has no failure cleanup/relink branch.

The helper is reached for actual reorder requests from both `BehindLayer()` and `MoveLayerInFrontOf()` (`rom/hyperlayers/behindlayer.c:65-90`; `rom/hyperlayers/movelayerinfrontof.c:101-115`). Both wrappers hold the LayerInfo lock across the helper call. The no-op cases return before calling it; the failure requires an actual move. **Affected configuration and trigger:** Hyperlayers, when one of those public operations requires moving a family behind another layer and `NewRegion()` fails in `_MoveLayerBehind()`. **Consequence:** NULL dereference after the family is detached, leaving layer-list topology incomplete and the LayerInfo lock held by the interrupted caller. Check `hide` before unlinking, or restore the original links and release locks on failure. **Confidence:** high for the allocation, unchecked consumers, and ordering of detachment before dereference. No allocation failure or layer reorder was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6186

**Finding:** Hyperlayers ignores allocation-failure returns from in-place region Boolean operations and continues with stale region contents.

The in-place `AndRegionRegion()` and `ClearRegionRegion()` build a temporary result; on failure they return FALSE without replacing the destination (`rom/graphics/andregionregion.c:53-87`; `clearregionregion.c:58-89`). `XorRegionRegion()` likewise preserves its destination if its temporary Boolean construction fails (`rom/graphics/xorregionregion.c:57-105`). Selected Hyperlayers callers ignore these returns:

- `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()` ignores XOR/AND results, then flips the `invisible` state and builds ClipRects for the next partition (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:456-476`). If a complement fails, the next pass can use the old partition and misclassify or duplicate clip area.
- `_BackupPartsOfLayer()` ignores `ClearRegionRegion(hide_region, l->VisibleRegion)` and immediately intersects the region to build replacement ClipRects (`basicfuncs.c:1027-1056`). On failure, the old visibility remains and its hidden pixels may be reintroduced into the rebuilt ClipRect list.
- `ChangeLayerVisibility()` and `DeleteLayer()` ignore AND/Clear results during visibility and damage reconstruction (`changelayervisibility.c:83,116,137,181,197`; `deletelayer.c:102,117`). Their subsequent show/backfill passes proceed using the old destination region, so newly exposed/hidden areas or refresh damage can be omitted or retained incorrectly.
- `CollectPixelsLayer()` ignores `ClearRegionRegion(_r, r)` after sending callbacks for the current layer (`collectpixelslayer.c:231-236`). If subtraction fails, `r` remains unchanged; lower layers or the final background pass can send callbacks for pixels already delivered, duplicating collected areas.
- `IsLayerHiddenBySibling()` ignores the AND result after a successful `SetRegion()` copy (`islayerhiddenbysibling.c:84-97`). If the intersection allocation fails, `r` still contains the copied sibling region and the query can report overlap/hidden when the visible shapes do not intersect. The selected Intuition system-gadget path uses this answer to choose `WindowToFront()` or `WindowToBack()` (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_support.c:579-591`). Its separate ignored `SetRegion()` result is covered by GD6181.
- `_InternalInstallClipRegion()` ignores `AndRegionRegion(l->shape, r)` after obtaining `r = AndRegionRegionND(l->VisibleRegion, region)` (`basicfuncs.c:1414-1418`). If the ND intersection succeeds but this in-place shape mask fails, `r` remains the visible-region/clip-region intersection. `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()` then creates its first visible ClipRect partition from that unmasked region (`basicfuncs.c:1420-1426,397-420`), so a nonrectangular layer can receive clip rectangles outside its shape. The public `InstallClipRegion()` path reaches this helper (`installclipregion.c:62-66`). The separate case where `AndRegionRegionND()` itself returns NULL remains GD6173.
- `BeginUpdate()` ignores both in-place shape-mask results after its damage intersection (`rom/hyperlayers/beginupdate.c:101-115`). If `AndRegionRegion(l->visibleshape, visible_damage_region)` fails, the destination retains the prior `VisibleRegion`/damage intersection; when a custom `shaperegion` is present, failure of its second mask similarly retains the unmasked region. The routine then passes that region to `_CreateClipRectsFromRegion()` and publishes its result as `l->ClipRect`, so the active draw clip can include damaged pixels outside the visible/custom layer shape. This requires the allocation-backed Boolean operation to fail on an overlapping, nontrivial shape; the separate NULL result from `AndRegionRegionND()` remains GD6172.
- The simple-refresh backfill block in `_CopyClipRectsToClipRects()` ignores `AndRegionRegion(l->visibleshape, dr)` after clipping `dr` to layer bounds and `VisibleRegion` (`basicfuncs.c:967-1004`). If this final shape mask fails, the preserved `DamageList` region is passed rectangle-by-rectangle to `_CallLayerHook()` including portions outside the custom visible shape (`:987-1004`). This call is reached from `_ShowPartsOfLayer()` during layer reveal with `backupmode == FALSE` and `addtodamagelist == FALSE` (`:1109-1120`). The finding is limited to the failed final mask; a later successful intersection would narrow the region.

These are allocation-failure paths in the selected `kernel-layers` implementation. The failure can leave stale visibility, incomplete or shape-unmasked ClipRect/damage state, backfill callbacks outside the visible shape, duplicate pixel callbacks, or a false sibling-overlap answer, depending on the caller. This is separate from GD6181's ignored `SetRegion()` copies, GD6173's unchecked NULL-producing ND intersection, and GD4662's separate ignored region-union failure in z-order handling.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `kernel-layers`, when an in-place region operation needs temporary `RegionRectangle` storage and allocation fails in one of the listed paths. **Consequence:** the operation continues as if the requested Boolean mutation succeeded, using the destination's prior contents; the observable effect depends on the caller as above. Check operation results and abort or preserve/restore caller state before publishing rebuilt visibility, ClipRects, damage, or callback results. **Confidence:** high for return semantics and ignored results; each effect requires allocation failure at that operation and the stated geometry. No region allocation failure, callback, visibility change, or layer operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6187

**The layer debug test reads `SuperBitMap` from a layer after successful deletion has freed the layer struct.** The interactive `deletelayer()` command calls `DeleteLayer(0, layers[i])`, then immediately reads `layers[i]->SuperBitMap` and may free that bitmap (`developer/debug/test/layers/layerstest.c:224-235`). `freelayers()` repeats the post-delete dereference during shutdown (`:83-94`). On success, `DeleteLayer()` unlinks the layer, calls `_FreeLayer(l)`, and returns TRUE (`rom/hyperlayers/deletelayer.c:136-150`); `_FreeLayer()` frees the Layer allocation (`basicfuncs.c:171-205`). The test's ordinary create commands do not request child layers, so its normal table entries have no descendants and can take this successful delete path.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable `test-layers` utility, when quitting with a created layer or using `dl` on a created layer. **Consequence:** the test dereferences the freed Layer struct to fetch `SuperBitMap`; if it was a superbitmap layer, the subsequent bitmap free also uses data fetched through that stale pointer. Save the bitmap pointer while the layer is alive, then delete and release it using the layer API's ownership rules; do not inspect the Layer after a successful delete. **Confidence:** high for the successful-delete lifetime sequence and ordinary root-child construction; no layer deletion was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6195

**Indexed summary:** GD6195 — compositor disposal leaks per-instance library references and its graphics context.

**Source and trigger:** `Compositor::Root::New` opens `graphics.library` and `intuition.library`, stores them in the instance, then creates a GC through `HIDD_Display_CreateObject()` (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:1003-1018`). Both normal display removal and constructor-failure cleanup dispatch `Root::Dispose`; its complete body only calls the superclass (`:1026-1036`; selected caller `rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:245-248`). It does not close either opened library or dispose the instance GC.

**Consequence and scope:** Each compositor object that reaches these acquisitions retains the library open references and GC after disposal. The same leak occurs if GC creation fails after the library opens, because `Root::New` invokes this disposer on its failure path. Applies to the explicit software compositor target when instantiated by graphics.library. High confidence in the acquisition/cleanup mismatch; no object lifecycle was run.

## GD6196

**Indexed summary:** GD6196 — compositor construction succeeds without the Intuition base required by bitmap-stack handling.

**Source and trigger:** `Compositor::Root::New` stores the result of `OpenLibrary("intuition.library", 50)` but its success test checks only `GraphicsBase`, the display and GC (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:1003-1023`). Later, `BitMapStackChanged` processes viewport entries by calling `HIDDCompositorFindBitMapScreen()`, which immediately reads `IntuitionBase->FirstScreen` (`:1111-1190,95-105`). Graphics.library invokes this compositor method through its selected stack-update wrapper (`rom/graphics/graphics_compositor.h:18-31`).

**Consequence and scope:** If the Intuition open fails while the other construction requirements succeed, creation still returns a usable compositor object; its first nonempty bitmap-stack update dereferences a NULL base. This is conditional on library-open failure and a subsequent stack update. High confidence in the unchecked result and dereference; no open failure or stack update was induced.

## GD6197

**Indexed summary:** GD6197 — Sound datatype playback cursor time truncates after 71 minutes.

**Source and trigger:** The AHI cursor worker computes elapsed microseconds as `now.tv_secs * 1000000UL + now.tv_micro` into an `ULONG`, then scales it to a sample position (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:3641-3655`). The pause path stores the same multiplication in `cursorElapsedAtPause`, also `ULONG`, and resume reconstructs a `timeval` from that truncated value (`:3601-3605,3828-3861`).

**Consequence and scope:** Because `ULONG` is 32-bit, elapsed microseconds wrap after about 4,295 seconds (71 minutes 35 seconds). Continuous cursor position then jumps backward, and pause/resume after that interval loses the elapsed time. For finite-cycle playback, the cursor's cycle-limit calculation is affected only when the configured total duration exceeds this range; shorter playback reaches its limit before wrap. Applies when timer-device cursor tracking is available. High confidence in the narrowing and arithmetic; no long playback was run.
