<a id="gd6262"></a>
## GD6262 — GEMImage shifts by an unchecked file depth before rejecting unsupported formats

**Severity / confidence:** Low severity, high confidence for the source-level undefined operation; the resulting behavior depends on the compiler and target.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3437`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3437).

**Affected configuration:** The optional `gemimage.datatype` target selected by `workbench/classes/datatypes/gemimage/mmakefile.src`, when built and installed with its GEMImage descriptor. The trigger is an image header whose depth is at least the width of the promoted `int` type (32 on AROS builds using 32-bit `int`).

`OMNew()` reads the file-controlled depth into `bitmap_header->bmh_Depth` as a `UWORD` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/gemimage/gemimage.c:261`). Before validating the subformat or supported depths, it evaluates `1 << bitmap_header->bmh_Depth`, stores the result in the narrower `UWORD colour_count`, and passes that value to `SetDTAttrs()` (`:274-289`). A shift count equal to or greater than the width of the promoted left operand is undefined in C. The later original-format switch rejects unsupported depth values at `:333-360`, but it is reached only after the shift and bitmap-allocation attempt.

**Consequence:** A malformed image with an out-of-range depth reaches undefined behavior in the parser before its intended format rejection. The checked source does not establish a particular memory effect or successful image creation.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/gemimage/gemimage.c:261-289,333-360`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/gemimage/mmakefile.src:9-12`; `workbench/devs/datatypes/GEMImage.dtd:1-10`.

<a id="gd6263"></a>
## GD6263 — 8SVX parser reads the fixed VHDR layout without checking property length

**Severity / confidence:** Moderate severity, high confidence. The read extent is fixed by the parser's structure and exceeds the stored property allocation for short VHDR chunks.

**Affected configuration:** The `workbench-datatypes-8svx` datatype module selected by `workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/mmakefile.src`, when built and installed. The trigger is an otherwise parsed 8SVX FORM containing a VHDR property shorter than 20 bytes and a BODY chunk.

`Read8SVX()` registers `(ID_8SVX, ID_VHDR)` as a property, parses the file, finds the property, and checks the current BODY chunk (`workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/8svxclass.c:98-129`). It does not check `vhdr_prop->sp_Size`. It casts `sp_Data` to `struct FileVoiceHeader *` and reads all seven fields at `:132-152`; that structure is 20 bytes (`:40-49`). IFFParse's property handler allocates exactly `cn->cn_Size` bytes and stores that value in `sp_Size` (`workbench/libs/iffparse/prophooks.c:123-148`). Thus a shorter VHDR leaves some or all of the fixed-layout reads outside the property buffer; a zero-sized property also supplies a NULL `sp_Data`.

The resulting fields are consumed before the body-size check and sample allocation (`8svxclass.c:169-205`), so a short property can also supply invalid sample metadata to subsequent validation and Sound datatype setup.

**Consequence:** Reading a short VHDR accesses bytes outside its stored property buffer and may fault or produce invalid header values. No claim is made about a specific adjacent allocation or a particular system-level outcome.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/8svxclass.c:40-49,98-152,169-205`; `workbench/libs/iffparse/prophooks.c:123-148`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/mmakefile.src:6-13`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L2253`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2253).

<a id="gd6264"></a>
## GD6264 — Sound datatype divides by an unchecked zero sample rate or period

**Severity / confidence:** Low severity, high confidence. The input triggers are a malformed/nonconforming zero-rate VHDR or a public Sound datatype client supplying a zero period/frequency.

**Affected configuration:** The `workbench-datatypes-8svx` module selected by `workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/mmakefile.src`, for a VHDR at least 20 bytes long, zero compression, and a sample count that passes the BODY-size check; and the explicitly buildable `workbench-datatypes-sound` target for public callers that set zero-valued `SDTA_Period`, `SDTA_Frequency`, or `SDTA_SamplesPerSec` tags.

`Read8SVX()` copies the two-byte, file-supplied `vh_SamplesPerSec` into the Sound `VoiceHeader` without validating that it is nonzero (`workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/8svxclass.c:145-146`). After compression and sample-count checks, it allocates and reads the sample data, then forms the `SDTA_Period` tag value as `709379 * 5 / vhd->vh_SamplesPerSec` (`:169-205`). C evaluates that division while constructing the arguments to `SetDTAttrs()`, before the Sound superclass can process the tag. Independently, the Sound superclass converts `SDTA_Period` via `Period2Freq()` without checking zero (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:973-976,145-150`), and stores `SDTA_Frequency`/`SDTA_SamplesPerSec` directly into its `UWORD Frequency` field (`:1038-1042`; `classbase.h:58`). `Sound_GET()` later divides by the stored frequency for `SDTA_Period`, and for `SDTA_ReplayPeriod` when the sample length is nonzero (`:1169-1172,1332-1344`).

**Consequence:** A qualifying zero-rate 8SVX file reaches integer division by zero during object construction. A public client can independently reach division by zero by setting a zero period, or by setting a zero frequency and requesting the period or replay-period attribute. No further system-level effect is inferred.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/8svxclass.c:145-146,169-205`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:145-150,973-976,1038-1042,1169-1172,1332-1344`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/mmakefile.src:6-13`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/mmakefile.src:1-13`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3441`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3441) and the [Sound datatype zero-frequency pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-zero-frequency-pass-gd10462).

<a id="gd6265"></a>
## GD6265 — 8SVX sample-count wrap accepts a truncated sample

**Severity / confidence:** Low severity, high confidence. This requires malformed sample counts whose 32-bit unsigned sum wraps to a value that fits the BODY chunk.

**Affected configuration:** The `workbench-datatypes-8svx` datatype module selected by `workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/mmakefile.src`, when built and installed. The trigger requires a full VHDR, zero compression, nonzero sample rate, and enough BODY bytes for the wrapped count.

`Read8SVX()` adds the file-supplied `ULONG` one-shot and repeat counts into `ULONG samplesize` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/8svxclass.c:133-140,175-183`). AROS defines `ULONG` as unsigned 32-bit (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:39-43`), so the addition wraps modulo 2^32. The subsequent `samplesize > cn->cn_Size` check sees only that wrapped value; the parser allocates and reads that many bytes, then publishes it as `SDTA_SampleLength` while the Sound object's `VoiceHeader` still holds the original counts (`8svxclass.c:185-205`).

For example, one-shot `0x80000000` plus repeat `0x80000001` wraps to one. With a one-byte BODY and otherwise valid VHDR fields, the size check passes, and the parser publishes a one-byte sample despite the header's much larger declared count. Sound playback paths use the stored `SampleLength` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:2927-2930,3114-3115`), so this is accepted truncated data rather than an access past the allocated sample.

**Consequence:** A malformed 8SVX file can be accepted with a sample length inconsistent with the VHDR counts, causing playback and other consumers to treat the declared sample as only the wrapped prefix. This finding does not claim an out-of-bounds access.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/8svxclass.c:133-140,175-205`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:39-43`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:2927-2930,3114-3115`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/mmakefile.src:6-13`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3443`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3443).

<a id="gd6266"></a>
## GD6266 — ASCII layout reports success after line-record allocation aborts

**Severity / confidence:** Low severity, high confidence. The trigger is memory-pool exhaustion while a layout is being rebuilt.

**Affected configuration:** The explicit `workbench-datatypes-ascii` target, when built and used with the selected Text superclass. The failure requires a document/layout that needs another line record after the pool cannot satisfy `AllocPooled()`.

During a requested layout, `Ascii__DTM_ASYNCLAYOUT()` removes the existing line records before rebuilding the list (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/asciiclass.c:304-312`). When a new record allocation fails, it sets `abort = TRUE` and stops the line-building loop (`:367-421`). The completion path does not test `abort`: it writes the partial `total` and `max_linelength` into the text special-info geometry and, when no Ctrl-C signal was received (`bsig == 0`), publishes those values through `NotifyAttrChanges()` and clears `DTA_Busy` (`:491-529`).

The Text superclass renderer traverses the resulting line list (`workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:424-437`), and its viewport/scroll handling uses `DTA_TotalVert` (`:2427-2428,2902-2910`). Thus consumers see a completed layout whose line list and scroll extent omit the unbuilt remainder; the old full layout has already been discarded.

**Consequence:** Under memory pressure, ASCII documents can be displayed and scrolled as if a truncated layout were complete until another layout is explicitly requested. This is a rendering/state correctness issue; no memory-safety consequence is claimed.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/asciiclass.c:304-312,367-421,491-529`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:424-437,2427-2428,2902-2910`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/mmakefile.src:9-12`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3221`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3221).

<a id="gd6267"></a>
## GD6267 — ASCII layout reads past an exact-length buffer ending in CR

**Severity / confidence:** Low severity, high confidence for the out-of-range read; a visible failure depends on the memory immediately following the supplied buffer.

**Affected configuration:** The explicit `workbench-datatypes-ascii` target used with the selected Text superclass. The trigger is a caller-supplied `TDTA_Buffer`/`TDTA_BufferLen` pair whose final in-range byte is carriage return and whose allocation ends at that byte.

The ASCII layout loop checks `buffer[i]` for CR while `i < bufferlen`, then unconditionally reads `buffer[i + 1]` to test for LF (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/asciiclass.c:314-325`). When CR is the last byte in the caller's declared buffer, that read is one byte beyond the supplied extent. The Text superclass's setters store `TDTA_Buffer` and `TDTA_BufferLen` directly without copying or appending a terminator (`workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:2477-2485`), so the superclass does not establish an extra readable byte for this caller-supplied case.

The normal text-file loading path is excluded: `LoadText()` allocates `size + 1` bytes and writes a newline sentinel at `buffer[size]` (`textclass.c:312-328`). No checked-in caller was found that passes an exact-length custom buffer to this ASCII class; the finding is scoped to clients using its public Text buffer attributes.

**Consequence:** Layout accesses one byte beyond the caller-supplied buffer and may fault or make the final CR handling depend on unrelated adjacent data. No further effect is inferred.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/asciiclass.c:314-325`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:2477-2485,312-328`; `compiler/include/datatypes/textclass.h:23-30`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/mmakefile.src:9-12`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3221`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3221).

<a id="gd6268"></a>
## GD6268 — ASCII datatype rejects an empty file accepted by its Text superclass

**Severity / confidence:** Low severity, medium confidence. The source behavior is clear; whether empty ASCII documents are required to be accepted is not explicitly documented in the checked-in API contract.

**Affected configuration:** The explicit `workbench-datatypes-ascii` target when used to load an empty file through its selected Text superclass. This does not establish that the default datatype detector selects ASCII for an empty file.

For a zero-byte file, the Text superclass accepts `size == 0`, allocates one byte for the buffer, reads zero bytes, writes a newline sentinel at index zero, sets `TDTA_BufferLen` to zero, and returns the object (`workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:304-338`; `DTIO_Read64` uses `Read()` with length zero at `workbench/classes/datatypes/dtio64.h:90-103`). The ASCII subclass then retrieves the non-NULL buffer and zero length but requires both `buffer && len`; it reports `ERROR_REQUIRED_ARG_MISSING`, disposes the object, and returns NULL (`workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/asciiclass.c:52-103`).

The rejection therefore does not indicate a missing buffer or a failed file read: it is caused by treating a valid zero-length buffer as absent. The base Text path otherwise provides a representable empty document. Because the source does not explicitly promise empty-document support for the ASCII subclass, this remains a low-impact compatibility candidate rather than a high-confidence defect.

**Consequence:** Callers explicitly loading a zero-byte file as ASCII receive object-creation failure even though the Text superclass loaded it successfully.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/asciiclass.c:52-103`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:304-338`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/dtio64.h:90-103`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/ascii/mmakefile.src:9-12`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3221`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3221).

<a id="gd6269"></a>
## GD6269 — Binary layout publishes full height for a partial line list after allocation failure

**Severity / confidence:** Low severity, high confidence. The trigger is line-record pool exhaustion during the initial layout.

**Affected configuration:** The explicit `workbench-datatypes-binary` target and its Text superclass. The failure requires a nonempty buffer and an `AllocPooled()` failure while generating the hex/character rows.

`Binary__DTM_ASYNCLAYOUT()` computes the expected row count from the full buffer length before rebuilding the line list (`workbench/classes/datatypes/binary/binaryclass.c:256-266`). The initial-layout path first removes every existing row (`:276-284`), then appends one row per 16 bytes. If a row allocation fails, it sets `abort = TRUE` and stops the loop (`:286-361`). The completion code does not test `abort`: it stores the precomputed full `lines` count in `si_TotVert` and notifies clients with that full total and `DTA_Busy=FALSE` whenever `bsig == 0` (`:371-414`).

The Text renderer walks the actual line list (`workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:424-437`), while its vertical view/scroll calculations consume `DTA_TotalVert` (`:2427-2428,2902-2910`). After allocation failure, the displayed rows therefore end early while the published total still describes the full buffer; the removed old list is not restored.

**Consequence:** A binary listing can appear to have completed layout with missing rows and a full-height scroll range after memory-pool exhaustion. A later layout may rebuild it; no persistent data loss is claimed.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/binary/binaryclass.c:256-266,276-361,371-414`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:424-437,2427-2428,2902-2910`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/binary/mmakefile.src:1-12`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L2263`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2263).

<a id="gd6270"></a>
## GD6270 — Binary layout overflows 32-bit row-width calculations for large buffers

**Severity / confidence:** Low severity, high confidence for the arithmetic boundary; displayed offset corruption depends on compiler treatment of signed overflow.

**Affected configuration:** The explicit `workbench-datatypes-binary` target on a 64-bit `IPTR` build where `dos64.library` opens successfully and memory is available for a text buffer larger than 2 GiB. The shared Text loader permits lengths below `0xFFFFFFFF` when they are addressable (`workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:312-328`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/text/support.c:22`).

`Binary__DTM_ASYNCLAYOUT()` stores the rounded-up row count `(bufferlen + 15) / 16` in signed 32-bit `LONG lines` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/binary/binaryclass.c:221,256`). For `bufferlen > 0x7FFFFFF0`, `lines` is at least `0x08000000`; each `lines * 16` expression in the offset-width tests at `:258-264` then exceeds signed `LONG_MAX`, invoking signed-overflow undefined behavior while selecting `offsetlen`. The formatter later writes only `offsetlen` hexadecimal digits of the row byte offset (`:302-306`), so a wrapped result can select too few digits and make large row addresses misleading.

At the upper end, the round-up itself is unsigned 32-bit arithmetic: `bufferlen + 15` wraps for lengths above `0xFFFFFFF0`, so the reported `lines` count can be far below the actual rows (`:256`). The layout loop also advances 32-bit `ULONG i` by 16 (`:287`); if it reaches the final partial row at offset `0xFFFFFFF0` and continues successfully, the increment wraps and the loop condition remains true. Allocation failure exits through GD6269's partial-layout path.

**Consequence:** Large but accepted buffers can produce undefined offset-width calculations and incorrect/truncated displayed byte offsets. Near the upper limit, row-count arithmetic can report a wrong total, and a fully successful traversal may wrap its loop counter. These paths require multi-gigabyte input and the stated 64-bit/DOS64 configuration; no runtime behavior was reproduced.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/binary/binaryclass.c:221,256-266,287,302-306`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:312-328`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/text/support.c:22`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:38-39`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L2263`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2263).

<a id="gd6271"></a>
## GD6271 — PNM dimensions are truncated for Picture allocation but not for pixel copies

**Severity / confidence:** Moderate severity, high confidence. A PNM height above 65,535 truncates in the Picture header while the loader continues using the full parsed height.

**Affected configuration:** The explicit `workbench-datatypes-pnm` target with its selected Picture superclass. The trigger is a PNM image dimension above the `UWORD` range, with otherwise valid pixel data and successful allocations.

`LoadPNM()` parses `Width` and `Height` into wider `long` variables and checks only that they are positive (`workbench/classes/datatypes/pnm/pnmclass.c:186-207`). It assigns them to `BitMapHeader` fields, which are 16-bit, without range checks (`:240-246`). The decode loops and pixel-array calls continue using the untruncated `Width`/`Height` values (`:258-358` and the corresponding binary PNM paths).

The Picture superclass sizes its source buffer from the truncated header (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1148`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/colorhandling.c:316-326`), then copies `pbpa_Height` rows and `pbpa_Width * pixelbytes` bytes per row without checking the destination rectangle against that allocation (`pictureclass.c:1182-1206`). For example, a validly encoded P3 image with width 1 and height 65,537 sets `bmh_Height` to 1 and allocates a one-row source buffer; on the second decoded row, the Picture copy begins at row offset one and writes beyond that allocation.

**Consequence:** Large PNM dimensions can make the loader's pixel writes extend beyond the Picture superclass's truncated source buffer. This finding concerns only the PNM-to-Picture copy path; it does not claim a particular adjacent object or further system outcome.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/pnm/pnmclass.c:186-207,240-246,258-358`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1148,1182-1206`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/colorhandling.c:316-326`; `compiler/include/datatypes/pictureclass.h:140-150`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L2268`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2268).

<a id="gd6272"></a>
## GD6272 — ASCII PNM accepts EOF as a pixel sample

**Severity / confidence:** Low severity, high confidence. The trigger is a truncated P2 or P3 file whose header is valid but whose sample data ends early.

**Affected configuration:** The explicit `workbench-datatypes-pnm` target for ASCII grayscale P2 and ASCII color P3 inputs. Binary P4/P5/P6 decoding is not covered by this finding.

`ReadNextInt()` skips whitespace but does not test EOF before computing `c - '0'`; when the first sample read encounters EOF it returns `-49` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/pnm/pnmclass.c:45-64`). It also does not validate that the token characters are decimal digits. The P2/P3 loops use its return value directly, scale by `MaxVal`, store the result in `RGBBuffer`, and call the Picture superclass without checking the input read status (`:299-357`).

For example, a P2 file declaring a 1×1 image and `MaxVal=255` but containing no sample data gets `curcol == -49`; scaling and conversion to `unsigned char` stores 207. The row is passed to `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY`, and the load path can complete successfully instead of rejecting the truncated file. The same EOF result is reused for missing P3 channels.

**Consequence:** Truncated ASCII PNM images can be accepted with invented pixel values instead of reporting a short or invalid sample stream. This is limited to parse correctness; no additional memory or system effect is inferred.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/pnm/pnmclass.c:45-64,299-357,520-526`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/pnm/mmakefile.src:1-12`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3457`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3457).

<a id="gd6273"></a>
## GD6273 — PNM sample scaling divides by an unchecked zero MaxVal

**Severity / confidence:** Low severity, high confidence. The trigger is a nonconforming P2, P3, or P5 header with `MaxVal=0` and at least one sample.

**Affected configuration:** The explicit `workbench-datatypes-pnm` target. P2/P3 ASCII and P5 binary grayscale paths are affected; P6 is excluded because it does not scale channels by `MaxVal`.

`LoadPNM()` parses `MaxVal` from the header and rejects only values greater than 65,535; it has no lower-bound/nonzero check (`workbench/classes/datatypes/pnm/pnmclass.c:212-235`). P2 and P3 normalize sample values using `curcol * 255 / MaxVal` (`:299-339`). P5 does the same for one-byte and two-byte channels (`:420-457`). A zero maximum therefore reaches integer division by zero during pixel decoding, before the row is passed to the Picture superclass.

**Consequence:** A P2, P3, or P5 image with zero `MaxVal` reaches undefined arithmetic rather than being rejected as an invalid header. No further system-level effect is inferred.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/pnm/pnmclass.c:212-235,299-339,420-457`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/pnm/mmakefile.src:1-12`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3459`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3459).

<a id="gd6274"></a>
## GD6274 — P6 decoding ignores MaxVal and always consumes 8-bit RGB rows

**Severity / confidence:** Low severity, high confidence. This affects valid P6 files whose samples are not already 8-bit values scaled to 255.

**Affected configuration:** The explicit `workbench-datatypes-pnm` target for binary P6 PPM input. The parser accepts `MaxVal` values from 1 through 65,535, but this decoder does not use the field.

`LoadPNM()` parses and accepts `MaxVal` up to 65,535 (`workbench/classes/datatypes/pnm/pnmclass.c:212-230`). In P6 mode, it reads exactly `Width * 3` bytes into the RGB row buffer and forwards them unchanged as `PBPAFMT_RGB` (`:479-503`). PPM uses one byte per channel when `MaxVal < 256`, with channel values scaled to `MaxVal`; larger maxima use two-byte big-endian samples. The P6 path neither scales lower-MaxVal channels to 0–255 nor reads/combines two-byte channels when `MaxVal >= 256`.

For `MaxVal=100`, a channel value of 100 is forwarded as 100 rather than full intensity 255. For `MaxVal=256` or greater, the row read consumes only the first `Width * 3` bytes of the `Width * 3` two-byte samples; those bytes are then grouped as unrelated 8-bit RGB channels, and later rows begin at the wrong position in the sample stream.

**Consequence:** P6 images with non-255 maxima are rendered with incorrect colors; 16-bit-channel P6 images are also decoded with the wrong channel and row alignment. This is a pixel-decoding correctness issue.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/pnm/pnmclass.c:212-230,479-503`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/pnm/mmakefile.src:1-12`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3461`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3461).

<a id="gd6275"></a>
## GD6275 — GIF decoder uses codec state after `DecodeInit()` fails

**Severity / confidence:** Moderate severity, high confidence for the NULL dereference on codec-allocation failure; malformed-header failure behavior depends on the uninitialized state and is not specified further.

**Affected configuration:** The explicit `workbench-datatypes-gif` target when loading a GIF with an image descriptor. Triggers include codec-state allocation failure or a rejected/short LZW minimum-code-size input.

`DecodeInit()` assigns the `AllocVec()` result to `gifhandle->codecvars` and returns `-2` when allocation fails (`workbench/classes/datatypes/gif/codeclzw.c:133-139`). `LoadGIF()` logs but ignores that result, then calls `DecodeLines()` unconditionally (`workbench/classes/datatypes/gif/gifclass.c:419-424`). `DecodeLines()` immediately assigns `d = gifhandle->codecvars` and reads `d->eof_code` (`codeclzw.c:158-173`), so allocation failure passes a NULL codec pointer into a dereference. `DecodeEnd()` is also called unconditionally and reads through `codecvars` (`:243-249`).

`DecodeInit()` can also return before `init_table()` on a truncated code-size read or an out-of-range minimum code size (`:140-155`). In those cases the codec allocation exists, but its fields used by `DecodeLines()` have not been initialized; the caller still proceeds. The later unchecked decode-result/partial-image path is tracked separately as GD6276.

**Consequence:** Under codec allocation failure, GIF loading dereferences NULL decoder state instead of returning an allocation error. On rejected/short LZW initialization input, the decoder proceeds with uninitialized state rather than rejecting the image.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/gif/codeclzw.c:133-155,158-173,243-249`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/gif/gifclass.c:404-424`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/gif/mmakefile.src:1-14`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L2273`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2273).

<a id="gd6276"></a>
## GD6276 — GIF loader publishes the full image after incomplete LZW decoding

**Severity / confidence:** Low to moderate severity, high confidence. The trigger is a truncated or malformed image-data stream after successful decoder initialization.

**Affected configuration:** The explicit `workbench-datatypes-gif` target when loading an image whose LZW stream ends early or returns a decode error.

`LoadGIF()` allocates `width * height` bytes for `linebuf` with `AllocMem(..., MEMF_ANY)`, without clearing the buffer (`workbench/classes/datatypes/gif/gifclass.c:404-418`). It then stores each `DecodeInit()`, `DecodeLines()`, and `DecodeEnd()` result in `ret`, but never branches on any result (`:419-424`). `DecodeLines()` can return early on a code/read error or when decoded output exceeds the allocated line buffer (`workbench/classes/datatypes/gif/codeclzw.c:173-188,214-220`). It also returns success on the GIF end code without checking that `linebufbytes` reached zero (`:173-175,239-240`).

Regardless of these outcomes, the loader sends the full descriptor width and height to `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY` (non-interlaced `gifclass.c:441-460`; interlaced `:463-503`). The Picture superclass therefore consumes the whole line buffer even when only a prefix was decoded; the remaining bytes retain uninitialized allocation contents.

**Consequence:** A truncated or invalid GIF can be reported as loaded with corrupted or indeterminate pixels in the undecoded portion, rather than returning a decode error. GD6275 separately covers failed initialization and invalid codec state.

**Source-only evidence:** `workbench/classes/datatypes/gif/gifclass.c:404-424,441-503`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/gif/codeclzw.c:158-188,214-240`; `workbench/classes/datatypes/gif/mmakefile.src:1-14`.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3465`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3465).

## GD6277

**Indexed summary:** GIF raw save proceeds after encoder errors and reports failed output as success.

**Source and trigger:** `SaveGIF()` stores each `EncodeInit()`, `EncodeLines()`, and `EncodeEnd()` result in `ret`, but does not branch on any result (`workbench/classes/datatypes/gif/gifclass.c:676-682`). If `EncodeInit()` fails its codec allocation, it leaves `codecvars` NULL and returns -2; `EncodeLines()` then dereferences that pointer while processing a nonempty image (`workbench/classes/datatypes/gif/codeclzw.c:291-296,317-331`). If initialization instead fails while flushing the minimum-code-size byte, it returns -4 before initializing the encoding table, yet line encoding still proceeds. During line/end encoding, `write_code()` reports a failed subblock flush as -2, but `EncodeLines()` and `EncodeEnd()` ignore its return values (`codeclzw.c:254-286,317-356`). Finally, after writing the GIF trailer, `SaveGIF()` ignores the result of its last `SaveGIF_EmptyBuf()` call and returns TRUE (`gifclass.c:692-696`); that helper returns FALSE when `Write()` writes fewer bytes than requested (`gifclass.c:85-100`). Raw `DTM_WRITE` forwards this result to its caller (`gifclass.c:723-735`).

**Consequence and scope:** A codec allocation failure on a nonempty image can lead to a NULL codec-state dereference; other encoder or destination-write failures can leave incomplete or invalid output while raw `DTM_WRITE` reports success. Applies when the optional `workbench-datatypes-gif` target is built and raw GIF saving encounters one of these failures. High confidence from the unchecked return paths; no allocation failure or destination write was induced.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3467`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3467).

## GD6278

**Indexed summary:** HTML construction can dereference a NULL page during failure cleanup.

**Source and trigger:** `Html__OM_NEW()` initializes `data->page` to NULL. If the text buffer is missing, `CreatePool()` fails, or `call_parser()` fails, the constructor calls `CoerceMethod(..., OM_DISPOSE)` before returning failure (`workbench/classes/datatypes/html/htmlclass.c:248-285`). `Html__OM_DISPOSE()` unconditionally passes `data->page` to `layout_free()` (`:294-307`), and `layout_free()` immediately reads `page->ldata` without a NULL check (`workbench/classes/datatypes/html/layout.c:68-75`). The parser helper returns failure without publishing `data->page` when `parse_init()` or later initialization fails (`htmlclass.c:61-88`).

**Consequence:** The cleanup path dereferences NULL instead of unwinding the partially constructed datatype object. The failure can occur during ordinary object construction when required buffer attributes are absent, or under pool/parser allocation failure. The `workbench-datatypes-html` manifest is an explicit optional target; the defect applies when that module is built and its constructor is used. High confidence from source ordering; no allocation failure or object construction was induced.

## GD6279

**Indexed summary:** Overlong HTML tags or entities write a terminator past a stack buffer.

**Source and trigger:** `parse_tag()` allocates `str[MAX_Tag_Length + 1]`, then accepts normal characters in a loop with the inclusive bound `i <= MAX_Tag_Length`; after the loop it writes `str[i] = '\0'` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/html/parse.c:706-729`). `escape_to_char()` uses the same inclusive loop and terminator pattern with `str[MAX_Esc_Length + 1]` (`:616-651`). The maxima are computed from the longest checked-in tag/entity names during parser setup (`parse.c:141-146,285-319`; `tables.c`). A tag or named entity one character longer than its table maximum fills every stack-buffer slot and leaves `i` one past the last slot, so the terminator write is out of bounds. The parser reads input length-bounded from the selected Text datatype buffer.

**Consequence and scope:** Parsing such a document writes one byte outside the local name buffer and can corrupt adjacent stack state before construction returns. Applies when the optional `workbench-datatypes-html` target is built and parses a document containing a too-long tag or entity name. High confidence from the loop bounds and VLA size; no HTML input or runtime behavior was exercised.

## GD6280

**Indexed summary:** HTML layout dereferences a missing line node after allocation failure.

**Source and trigger:** `linelist_store()` returns NULL when `AllocPooled(data->mempool, sizeof(struct Line))` fails (`workbench/classes/datatypes/html/htmlclass.c:184-208`). `layout_text()` assigns that result to `ldata->oldline` but still advances its x position and continues (`workbench/classes/datatypes/html/layout.c:409-431`). When a subsequent segment wraps or ends a line, `new_line()` passes `oldline` to `linelist_addlf()` (`layout.c:290-305`); that helper unconditionally dereferences the pointer at `htmlclass.c:211-218`. The parser produces linebreak and block-end segments for ordinary document structure (`workbench/classes/datatypes/html/parse.c:229-243,915-925`).

**Consequence and scope:** A transient pool allocation failure during HTML layout can turn into a NULL dereference on the next line-ending path instead of returning a partial-layout error. Applies to the optional HTML datatype target when a document layout encounters pool exhaustion. High confidence from the unchecked return and caller sequence; no allocation failure or layout was induced.

## GD6281

**Indexed summary:** HTML parser treats string-pool allocation failure as end of input.

**Source and trigger:** When fewer than ten bytes remain in the current text pool, `copy_text()` calls `strpool_expand()` and returns zero if allocation fails (`workbench/classes/datatypes/html/parse.c:510-531`; `strpool_expand()` at `:339-348`). `parse_do()` interprets any zero return from `copy_text()` as normal termination and breaks, then unconditionally returns TRUE (`:168-218`). `call_parser()` therefore continues through `parse_end()` and `layout_init()` and publishes the page on success (`workbench/classes/datatypes/html/htmlclass.c:61-90`). If the pool expansion fails after earlier content was parsed, the page is accepted with the remaining input omitted.

**Consequence and scope:** A memory-pressure failure can make HTML construction succeed with silently truncated document content rather than report an incomplete parse. Applies to the optional HTML target when its text pool needs to grow and allocation fails. High confidence from return-value handling; no allocation failure or document parse was induced.

## GD6282

**Indexed summary:** AmigaGuide node layout reads before empty text spans.

**Source and trigger:** On every successful `ParseNode()` pass, the finalization path unconditionally calls `AllocLFLine(cl, obj, pd, text, text)` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/nodeclass.c:1039-1044`). When the pointers are equal, `AllocLFLine()` calls `AllocLine(cl, obj, pd, "", 0)` (`:519-536`). `AllocLine()` checks `text[len-1]` before allocating the line (`:395-405`), so this zero-length case reads `text[-1]`, one byte before the empty string literal.

**Consequence and scope:** Normal AmigaGuide node layout performs an out-of-bounds read during final-line creation; if the preceding byte happens to equal newline, the code also decrements the length to -1 before passing it to `TextLength()`. The path is in the selected AmigaGuide node class. High confidence from the unconditional call and zero-length handling; no guide was laid out at runtime.

## GD6283

**Indexed summary:** AmigaGuide queued triggers dereference a NULL `dtt_GInfo` from MultiView.

**Source and trigger:** AmigaGuide advertises `DTM_TRIGGER` in its supported-method list (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/amigaguideclass.c:66-76`). MultiView's `DoTrigger()` constructs a `dtTrigger` with `dtt_GInfo = NULL` and passes it to `DoDTMethodA()` (`workbench/utilities/MultiView/misc.c:488-499`); maintained keyboard/menu paths call this helper for supported AmigaGuide trigger functions (`main.c:1354-1381,1696-1704`). When the call reaches AmigaGuide in a task other than its worker, `dtm_trigger()` calls `SendAGTrigger()` (`amigaguideclass.c:1038-1049`). That helper unconditionally copies `*dtt->dtt_GInfo` into the queued message (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/process.c:404-417`).

**Consequence and scope:** A supported MultiView trigger can dereference NULL while being queued, before the AmigaGuide worker handles it. This affects the selected AmigaGuide/MultiView integration path. High confidence from the maintained caller and queue implementation; no trigger or GUI interaction was run.

## GD6284

**Indexed summary:** AmigaGuide macro parsing scans past a line-buffer terminator.

**Source and trigger:** `ScanFile()` reads global commands with `FGets(fh, buf, AG_BUFSIZE_LINE)` using a 1,024-byte buffer (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/file.c:296-326`; `classdata.h:35`). `FGets()` reads at most `buflen-1` bytes and always appends NUL, including when EOF or the buffer limit ends a read (`rom/dos/fgets.c:24-28,55-75`). For `@MACRO`, `ParseMacroLine()` scans its body until newline or quote but does not test for NUL (`file.c:129-152`). An EOF-terminated unquoted body, an unterminated quoted body, or a macro line continued beyond a full `FGets()` chunk therefore runs past the terminator. The resulting `ptr-macro` length is passed to `AddMacro()` and used to allocate/copy the body (`file.c:41-51,171-172`).

**Consequence and scope:** Parsing such a macro reads beyond the current line buffer and may copy unrelated following memory into the macro definition or fail while scanning. Applies when the optional AmigaGuide datatype parses a global macro line without a closing delimiter/newline in the current read. High confidence from the DOS `FGets()` contract and parser loop; no guide or macro was parsed.

## GD6285

**Indexed summary:** JPEG XL construction accepts a failed Picture pixel write as a successful decode.

**Source and trigger:** After libjxl reports a full image, `JXL_Decode()` sets the Picture header and calls `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY`, but discards the method result and leaves `error` unchanged (`workbench/classes/datatypes/jpegxl/jpegxlclass.c:142-178`). The selected Picture superclass returns FALSE when it cannot allocate its source buffer (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1102-1118,1148-1150`). `JXL_Import()` therefore sees `error == 0`, sets the object name and returns success (`jpegxlclass.c:228-239`); `JXL__OM_NEW()` returns the object instead of disposing it (`:333-358`).

**Consequence and scope:** If Picture pixel-buffer allocation fails after a successful decode, construction reports a valid JPEG XL object with dimensions but without its decoded pixels, so the failure is hidden from the caller. Applies when the optional JPEG XL target and its external libjxl dependencies are selected. High confidence from the discarded return and superclass failure contract; no decode or allocation failure was induced.

## GD6286

**Indexed summary:** Animation startup dereferences its private state after allocation failure.

**Source and trigger:** During animation object initialization, `DT_InitPlayer()` allocates `struct ProcessPrivate` with `AllocMem()` and immediately writes `pp_Object` and `pp_Data` without checking the result (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:161-168`). The selected animation datatype calls `DT_InitPlayer()` from its `OM_NEW` path (`animationclass.c:1200-1245`). If that allocation fails, the first field store dereferences NULL before the constructor can return an object-creation error.

**Consequence and scope:** Animation object construction can fault under low-memory conditions instead of failing cleanly. Applies to the optional `workbench-datatype-animation` target when the animation class is constructed. High confidence from the unchecked allocation and immediate stores; no allocation failure or object construction was induced.

## GD6287

**Indexed summary:** Animation startup waits forever when a worker fails before its startup flag is observed.

**Source and trigger:** `DT_InitPlayer()` starts the buffer and playback processes, then polls each worker's `PRIVPROCF_RUNNING` flag with `Delay(1)` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:200-240`). It does not check whether either `CreateNewProcTags()` returned NULL, so a process-creation failure leaves the corresponding flag clear and the constructor loops indefinitely. A worker can also start, set `RUNNING`, fail `AllocBufferSignals()` or `AllocPlaybackSignals()`, and clear `RUNNING` before the polling constructor observes the transient (`animationbuffer.c:203-208,359-364`; `animationplayback.c:241-245,344-348`).

**Consequence and scope:** Either failure path hangs animation object construction; callers never receive the object or an error result. This is separate from GD6286's earlier `ProcessPrivate` allocation dereference and from GD6296's later signaling of cleared worker pointers when startup is observed. Applies to the optional animation datatype. High confidence in the unchecked process result and flag ordering; no worker, signal-allocation failure or timing was induced.

## GD6288

**Indexed summary:** Animation direct-render frames self-copy their cache and never become ready.

**Source and trigger:** `cacheFrame()` allocates `frame->af_CacheBM`, assigns it as `rendFrameMsg.Target`, clears the frame flags, and dispatches `PRIVATE_RENDERFRAME` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationframe.c:37-47`). In `DT_RenderFrame()`, the direct-render branch is selected when there are no animation colors or `ANIMDF_REMAP` is disabled (`animationclass.c:522-530`). It chooses `frame->af_CacheBM` as `sourceBM` and blits that bitmap to `msg->Target` (`:530-540`); on the initial cache build those pointers are the same, so the cleared cache is copied onto itself instead of copying `af_Frame.alf_BitMap`. Unlike `DT_RemapFrame()`, the direct branch never sets `AFFLAGF_READY` (`:569-731`). Playback displays a frame only when `GetFrameCacheBitmap()` sees that flag (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationplayback.c:203-210,312-339`). The no-remap route is configurable through public `ADTA_Remap`, including as an object-construction tag (`animationclass.c:1052-1054,1143-1149,1228-1232`).

**Consequence and scope:** On direct-render frames, the decoded pixels are not copied into the cache and the playback loop rejects the frame as not ready, so it is not displayed. Applies when the animation datatype is used with zero palette colors or with `ADTA_Remap` disabled. High confidence from the selected cache producer, render branch and playback gate; no animation or display was run.

## GD6289

**Indexed summary:** Animation remapping dereferences an unchecked high-color output allocation.

**Source and trigger:** In `DT_RemapFrame()`, an allocated temporary scanline is followed by an unchecked `AllocVec(width << 2)` whenever the destination bitmap depth exceeds eight (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:583-599`). The selected caller reaches this method for frames with a color table when `ANIMDF_REMAP` is enabled (`:518-527`). On the non-HAM path, the conversion loop then writes four bytes per pixel through `outline` (`:686-700`); on the HAM path targeting a high-color bitmap, it also writes through the same pointer (`:610-673`). If the output-buffer allocation fails, `outline` is NULL and the first pixel write faults. The cleanup later passes NULL to `FreeVec`, but that is reached only if the earlier write does not fault (`:723-725`).

**Consequence and scope:** A memory-allocation failure while remapping to a bitmap deeper than eight bits can terminate the remapping task through a NULL write. The report establishes the source-level failure path; it does not claim runtime reproduction. High confidence in the unchecked allocation and dependent writes; target formats and allocator behavior were not exercised.

## GD6290

**Indexed summary:** Animation marks a frame ready even when remapping did no work.

**Source and trigger:** `DT_RemapFrame()` performs conversion only inside the condition requiring both a non-NULL target and successful `tmpline` allocation (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:580-585`). It also skips the conversion if either `CreateRastPort()` call fails (`:601-604,718-721`). Regardless of those skipped-work cases, the function then sets `msg->Frame->af_Flags = AFFLAGF_READY` (`:728`). The in-tree `cacheFrame()` caller initializes a new cache bitmap with `BMF_CLEAR`, clears the frame flags, and dispatches rendering (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationframe.c:37-47`). `DT_RenderFrame()` invokes remapping only when both frame and target exist and remapping is enabled (`animationclass.c:518-527`); therefore cache-bitmap allocation failure is not part of this trigger. Playback accepts the resulting ready flag and can return/display the still-blank cache (`animationplayback.c:203-210,312-340`).

**Consequence and scope:** If the scanline or either rastport allocation fails for a remapped frame, the cleared cache can be marked ready and displayed as blank or incomplete. The candidate is limited to those temporary-allocation failures on the remap path. High confidence from the selected cache producer, renderer and playback gate; no allocation failure or playback was induced.

## GD6291

**Indexed summary:** Animation preferences ignore the documented `MATCHCLASS` filter.

**Source and trigger:** The animation preferences format documents `MATCHCLASS` as a case-insensitive pattern that controls whether a line's settings apply (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationprefs.c:46-53`). `ReadENVPrefs()` parses the keyword and, when supplied, the intended `matchstr()` filter call is inside `#if (0)`; `noignore` therefore remains TRUE unless a separate `MATCHPROJECT` token is present and fails its own match (`:183-206`). The selected animation constructor invokes this preferences reader during initialization (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:1234`).

**Consequence and scope:** A preferences line containing only a nonmatching `MATCHCLASS` still applies its `STACK`, `BUFFERTIME`, `BUFFERSTEP` or `NOSKIP` settings to the animation instance. The filter is explicitly disabled in the implementation despite being part of the documented file syntax. High confidence in the ignored-option behavior; no preferences file was changed or loaded.

## GD6292

**Indexed summary:** Animation shuttle handling divides by zero for an accepted zero tick interval.

**Source and trigger:** `ADTA_TicksPerFrame` is accepted directly into the `UWORD` tick interval with no zero check (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:1026-1029`); the constructor's default is positive, and the separate `ADTA_FramesPerSecond` path clamps zero to one before deriving ticks (`:1031-1040,1220-1222`). The public tag is available to object creation and later attribute setting (`compiler/include/datatypes/animationclassext.h:42`; `animationclass.c:1228-1232`). The realtime player hook divides the shuttle time by that interval (`animationplayback.c:73-78`). Realtime dispatches `PM_SHUTTLE` when `SetConductorState()` handles `CONDSTATE_SHUTTLE` (`workbench/libs/realtime/setconductorstate.c:206-222`); this player is registered with that hook during animation initialization (`animationclass.c:133-158`).

**Consequence and scope:** Setting `ADTA_TicksPerFrame` to zero and then shuttling a non-running animation reaches integer division by zero in the callback. The normal default and FPS-derived path do not produce zero; the trigger is the independent explicit tick-interval tag. High confidence in the accepted value and selected callback path; no tag or shuttle event was run.

## GD6293

**Indexed summary:** Animation construction dereferences process state when `ADTA_NumPrefetchFrames` is supplied.

**Source and trigger:** `DT_NewMethod()` zeroes the instance data and applies the caller's attribute list through `DT_SetMethod()` before calling `DT_InitPlayer()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:1210-1211,1228-1232,1244`). `ADTA_NumPrefetchFrames` writes through `animd->ad_ProcessData` (`:1047-1050`), but that pointer is allocated only later inside `DT_InitPlayer()` (`:161-167`). The public tag is declared in the animation class extension header (`compiler/include/datatypes/animationclassext.h:49`).

**Consequence and scope:** Supplying `ADTA_NumPrefetchFrames` in the animation object's construction tag list dereferences the still-NULL process-data pointer before construction reaches its allocator. The same setter called after successful construction is not affected by this initialization-order trigger. High confidence from the zeroed instance, direct setter and later allocation order; no object was constructed.

## GD6294

**Indexed summary:** Animation color-table allocation failures are published and later dereferenced.

**Source and trigger:** For a positive `ADTA_NumColors`, `DT_AllocColorTables()` independently allocates six color arrays and records the requested color count without checking any result (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:337-367`; called by `DT_SetMethod()` at `:1177-1184`). Later, `cacheFrame()` invokes the mapping method when a decoded frame has a color map (`animationframe.c:29-35`). `DT_MapPens()` passes `acd_CRegs` to `GetRGB32()` for a nonzero color count (`animationclass.c:385-395`); the selected `GetRGB32()` implementation writes three values per color through the supplied pointer without a NULL check (`rom/graphics/getrgb32.c:60-69`). In the remaining mapping branches, `acd_Allocated`, both color tables and `acd_GRegs` are also written without checking their allocations (`animationclass.c:420-477`).

**Consequence and scope:** If any required color array allocation fails for an animation configured with a positive color count and a decoded frame with a color map, the mapping path can write through the missing array; the `acd_CRegs` failure has a direct NULL-write path in `GetRGB32()`. No rollback or error is returned from the allocator method, so later rendering is not suppressed. High confidence for the unchecked allocations and concrete consumers; no memory failure or frame mapping was induced.

## GD6295

**Indexed summary:** Animation key-frame setup dereferences a failed allocation.

**Source and trigger:** The `ADTA_KeyFrame` setter allocates `ad_KeyFrame` only when it is not already set, does not check the result, and immediately stores the supplied bitmap through the pointer (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:1019-1024`). The tag is processed by the normal animation `DT_SetMethod()` path and may also be applied to an existing object.

**Consequence and scope:** If the `AnimFrame` allocation fails while setting `ADTA_KeyFrame`, the immediate field assignment dereferences NULL and interrupts construction or the attribute update. This finding is limited to that allocation-failure path; it is separate from the `ADTA_NumPrefetchFrames` construction-order dereference. High confidence from the direct unchecked allocation/use; no allocation failure was induced.

## GD6296

**Indexed summary:** Animation start and removal signal worker pointers after signal setup fails.

**Source and trigger:** Both worker entry points set their `RUNNING` flag before allocating their signal sets, and clear their parent-owned task pointer on exit if signal allocation fails (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationbuffer.c:203-208,359-364`; `animationplayback.c:241-245,344-348`). `DT_InitPlayer()` waits only for the early `RUNNING` flag, so it can return while signal setup is pending (`animationclass.c:200-240`). If setup then fails and the worker clears its pointer, `DT_Start()` signals both worker pointers without testing them (`:1728-1734`); `DT_RemoveDTObject()` does the same for disable signals (`:1252-1276`). The selected Exec `Signal()` implementation dereferences the supplied task pointer (`rom/exec/signal.c:158-172,269`), and its API requires a task pointer.

**Consequence and scope:** Under per-task signal exhaustion after the startup handshake, a later start or object-removal request can pass a cleared NULL worker pointer to `Signal()` and fault. `DT_DisposeMethod()` separately guards each worker pointer, so this report does not claim that path has the same NULL-signal failure (`animationclass.c:1281-1309`). High confidence in the ordering and call sites; no signal exhaustion, start, or removal was induced.

## GD6297

**Indexed summary:** Animation startup uses a failed realtime-player creation as if it succeeded.

**Source and trigger:** `DT_InitPlayer()` stores `CreatePlayerA()`'s result without checking for NULL (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:151-159`). The selected Realtime implementation documents NULL on failure and returns NULL on player-allocation failure (`workbench/libs/realtime/createplayera.c:104-108,127-143`). Animation defaults to immediate playback (`animationclass.c:1216-1219`); its initial layout calls `ADTM_START` when that flag is set (`:1573-1576`), and `DT_Start()` passes `ad_Player` to `SetConductorState()` without a guard (`:1713-1729`). The selected Realtime method immediately reads `player->pl_Source` (`workbench/libs/realtime/setconductorstate.c:83-90`).

**Consequence and scope:** If player creation fails and the animation reaches its initial immediate-start layout or an explicit start request, `SetConductorState()` dereferences the NULL player. High confidence in the failure return and selected caller chain; no Realtime allocation failure or layout was induced.

## GD6298

**Indexed summary:** WebP construction accepts a failed Picture pixel write as a successful decode.

**Source and trigger:** After `WebPDecodeRGBA()` succeeds, `WebP_Decode()` publishes the decoded dimensions and invokes Picture's `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY`, but discards the method result and leaves its local `error` at zero (`workbench/classes/datatypes/webp/webpclass.c:100-125`). The selected Picture method returns FALSE when pixel-format validation fails or `AllocSrcBuffer()` cannot allocate its backing buffer (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1117-1149,1174-1179`). `WebP_Import()` treats a zero error as success, and `WebP__OM_NEW()` then returns the object (`webpclass.c:154-162,170-191`).

**Consequence and scope:** A valid WebP decode whose Picture pixel publication fails can still produce a successfully constructed datatype object with no decoded pixel buffer. Applies to the optional WebP datatype target; the external libwebp decode itself is not implicated. High confidence from the return-value chain; no decode or allocation failure was induced.

## GD6299

**Indexed summary:** WebP save encodes uninitialized pixel data after a Picture read failure.

**Source and trigger:** `WebP_Export()` allocates its RGBA buffer with `AllocVec(..., MEMF_PRIVATE)`, ignores the result of `PDTM_READPIXELARRAY`, and passes the buffer to `WebPEncodeRGBA()` regardless (`workbench/classes/datatypes/webp/webpclass.c:50-64`). The selected Picture reader can return FALSE when the object has no destination mode or cannot provide a source buffer (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1224-1239`). The WebP buffer is not cleared before the read.

**Consequence and scope:** For a positive-size picture whose pixel read fails, the encoder consumes uninitialized or partially filled RGBA bytes and may write a corrupt image while reporting a successful save. Applies to the optional WebP export path. High confidence in the ignored read result and uncleared allocation; no save or Picture failure was induced.

## GD6300

**Indexed summary:** WebP save reports success after a failed or short DOS write.

**Source and trigger:** After a successful encode, `WebP_Export()` calls DOS `Write()` but ignores its return and unconditionally frees buffers and returns zero (`workbench/classes/datatypes/webp/webpclass.c:63-72`). DOS documents and implements `Write()` as returning bytes actually written, zero at end of file and -1 on error (`rom/dos/write.c:27-43,59-73`).

**Consequence and scope:** A failed or short destination write is reported to the caller as successful WebP export, leaving a missing or truncated file. Applies to the optional WebP raw-write path. High confidence in the ignored result and DOS contract; no output error was induced.

## GD6301

**Indexed summary:** WebP save leaks its pixel buffer when encoding fails.

**Source and trigger:** `WebP_Export()` allocates `buffer` before calling `WebPEncodeRGBA()`. It frees that buffer only inside the `size != 0` success branch; when encoding returns zero, control exits the function with `DTERROR_COULDNT_SAVE` and no `FreeVec(buffer)` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/webp/webpclass.c:56-75`).

**Consequence and scope:** Every encode failure after successful pixel-buffer allocation leaks that buffer for the lifetime of the caller's process. Applies to the optional WebP export path; missing headers or the initial buffer-allocation failure do not trigger this leak. High confidence from the local cleanup branches; no encode failure was induced.

## GD6302

**Indexed summary:** WebP decode stores pointers as datatype error values.

**Source and trigger:** On a successful decode, `WebP_Decode()` passes the addresses of its local `LONG level` and `LONG error` variables as tag data for `DTA_ErrorLevel` and `DTA_ErrorNumber` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/webp/webpclass.c:82-86,112-118`). These are scalar datatype error attributes: other selected datatype callers set them with numeric values, e.g. `DTA_ErrorLevel, 1` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/amigaguideclass.c:1345-1346`).

**Consequence and scope:** Instead of setting the successful zero error state, the WebP object receives pointer-address values as its error level and number; later consumers of those attributes can observe nonsensical error metadata. Applies to successful imports through the optional WebP datatype. High confidence in the scalar tag usage and pointer-valued arguments; no datatype error query was run.

## GD6304 — HEIC import reports success after image decoding fails [conditional]

`HEIC_Decode()` initializes `error` to zero (`workbench/classes/datatypes/heic/heicclass.c:41-48`). After a context contains at least one top-level image, it calls `heif_decode_image()` and logs a nonzero `err.code`, but sets no failure value and continues to release the handle and return the still-zero `error` (`:129-170,211`). The selected `HEIF__OM_NEW()` treats a zero result as successful object construction and only disposes the object and sets `IoErr()` for a nonzero result (`:365-390`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a HEIC input passes file/context/image-handle setup but `heif_decode_image()` returns an error. The datatype can return an object as if import succeeded even though the decode branch did not write its pixel data. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected HEIC datatype for file-backed imports, selected through active `workbench-datatypes-complete` rules (`workbench/classes/datatypes/mmakefile`; `heic/mmakefile.src`); successful dependency build requires the external codec sources. **Confidence:** high that the local adapter logs but drops the decode error and returns its initialized success value; which decode failures leave earlier Picture state usable is input-dependent. Propagate a nonzero datatype error when decode fails. No decode or build was run; source-only; see the [HEIC adapter pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2301) and [API contract cross-check](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2303).

## GD6305 — HEIC import ignores Picture pixel-buffer write failure [conditional]

After a successful external decode, `HEIC_Decode()` calls `DoSuperMethod(..., PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY, ...)` to transfer the interleaved pixels into the Picture superclass, but discards the method result (`workbench/classes/datatypes/heic/heicclass.c:141-168`). The selected Picture implementation returns `FALSE` for invalid initial bitmap state, unsupported format, and failed `AllocSrcBuffer()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1102-1149`); it returns `TRUE` only after copying the pixel rows (`:1182-1210`). HEIC's local `error` remains zero on this decoded-image path, and the caller therefore keeps the object (`heicclass.c:43,158-168,211; :381-389`).

**Trigger and consequence:** decoding succeeds, then Picture rejects the pixel write, including when its source-buffer allocation fails. The HEIC adapter still reports successful import and can return a Picture object without the decoded pixels. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected HEIC datatype when its Picture superclass cannot accept or allocate the requested pixel buffer; successful dependency build requires the external codec sources. **Confidence:** high for the ignored Boolean result and local successful return; allocation failure or another rejecting Picture state was not induced. Check and propagate the `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY` result. No image, allocation failure or build was exercised; source-only; see the [HEIC adapter pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2301).

## GD6306 — HEIC import uses the image handle after lookup reports failure [conditional]

The adapter declares `struct heif_image_handle *handle` without initialization, calls `heif_context_get_image_handle()`, and only logs when `err.code` is nonzero. It then immediately passes `handle` to `heif_image_handle_is_primary_image()`, width/height and alpha queries, and `heif_decode_image()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/heic/heicclass.c:99-140`). The checked libheif API contract returns an error status from the lookup; the adapter does not branch away from use of the output on that error (API contract cross-check recorded at [coverage line 2303](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2303)).

**Trigger and consequence:** context parsing reports at least one top-level image, but lookup of the listed image ID fails. If the failed lookup leaves the output unwritten, the following calls use an indeterminate handle and can fault or produce invalid metadata. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected HEIC datatype when libheif returns an image-handle lookup error after reporting an image; successful dependency build requires the external codec sources. **Confidence:** high that the local error branch falls through to handle use; the exact output state and library response are dependency-defined and were not reproduced. Return on lookup failure before using or releasing the output handle. No file, handle lookup, decoder or build was exercised; source-only; see the [HEIC adapter and API contract traces](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2301).

## GD6307 — HEIC import never releases its input buffer or libheif context [conditional]

For each file import, `HEIC_Decode()` allocates `buffer` with `AllocVec(size + 1, ...)` and creates `heifc` with `heif_context_alloc()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/heic/heicclass.c:52-54,77-82`). It passes the buffer to `heif_context_read_from_memory_without_copy()` (`:91`) and does not free the buffer or release the context before returning at line 211. The function releases a decoded `image` only on its success branch and releases the image `handle` only after entering the image-present path (`:141-170`); neither release frees the separately allocated input buffer or context. There is no `FreeVec(buffer)` or `heif_context_free(heifc)` in the selected source file.

**Trigger and consequence:** perform one or more HEIC file imports after the input buffer and context allocations succeed, including imports that later fail. Their retained allocations accumulate across imports and can reduce memory available to the system; buffer size tracks the input file size, with additional context-owned allocations. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected HEIC datatype on successful buffer/context allocations; successful dependency build requires the external codec sources. **Confidence:** high for the unmatched local allocations and absence of cleanup in this function; exact context allocation size and eventual reclamation by external library behavior are not established here. Release the context and input buffer on every exit after allocation, respecting the no-copy API's caller-owned buffer lifetime. No allocation, import or build was exercised; source-only; see the [HEIC adapter pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2301).

## GD6308 — HEIC import advertises 12 header bytes after allocating less [conditional]

`HEIC_Decode()` obtains the file size, allocates `size + 1` bytes when the size is representable, and initializes `headersize` to 12. Its `size < headersize` branch mistakenly assigns 12 again rather than limiting the request to the file size or rejecting the input (`workbench/classes/datatypes/heic/heicclass.c:52-60`). It then requests 12 bytes and checks only whether `Read()` returned `-1`; every nonnegative return, including a short count or zero at EOF, is treated as a complete header and passed to `heif_check_filetype(buffer, headersize)` with length 12 (`:62-67`). The selected DOS `Read()` implementation documents that the result is the number of bytes actually read, zero at EOF and `-1` on error, and forwards the result from the filesystem (`rom/dos/read.c:27-43,59-75`). For file sizes 0–10, the advertised 12-byte extent exceeds the requested `size + 1` allocation; at size 11 the extent fits the allocation but its last byte was not supplied by the 11-byte file read. The file-import caller reaches this path when the Picture object supplies a bitmap header, file handle and `DTST_FILE` source type (`heicclass.c:214-242`); the selected HEIC target defines `HEICCLASS_USESUPPORTPROC`, which invokes the same import routine on its support process (`mmakefile.src:397`; `heicclass.c:365-389`).

**Trigger and consequence:** import a file shorter than 12 bytes, including an empty file, with the HEIC datatype selected. The adapter passes a 12-byte length to the external file-type helper even though the allocation is at most 12 bytes and the file supplied fewer than 12 bytes. If that helper inspects the full advertised extent, it reads beyond the requested allocation for sizes 0–10, or consumes an uninitialized final byte at size 11; this can misclassify the input or fault. The helper implementation is from the external libheif dependency and is not present in this checkout, so the downstream read and its manifestation are not verified. Separately, after the initial size query, the adapter also treats short nonnegative results from its 20-byte MIME read and full-file read as complete (`:69-85`); those conditions require a short read, such as the file changing between size query and read, and the full-file call still advertises the original size to `heif_context_read_from_memory_without_copy()` (`:85-91`). These are included as the same unchecked-read-count pattern, with their external helper behavior unverified.

**Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected HEIC datatype (`workbench/classes/datatypes/mmakefile` actively selects it through `workbench-datatypes-complete`; `heic/mmakefile.src`) when opening a `DTST_FILE` source whose size/read is shorter than the length supplied to libheif. **Confidence:** high that the selected code can allocate less than the length it supplies and ignores short-read counts; medium for an out-of-allocation access or visible decode failure because the external helper body is absent. Reject files shorter than the required probe length or pass the actual byte count, and require exact reads before forwarding a declared input extent. No file, short read, helper, codec or build was exercised; source-only. Supporting call-path and DOS result-contract evidence: [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L2301`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2301), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L2304`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2304).

## GD6309 — HEIC image dimensions are narrowed into 16-bit Picture fields [conditional]

The HEIC adapter assigns `heif_image_handle_get_width()` and `heif_image_handle_get_height()` directly to `BitMapHeader::bmh_Width`/`bmh_Height`, then overwrites them with decoded-image dimensions using the same direct assignments (`workbench/classes/datatypes/heic/heicclass.c:118-120,148-150`). The Picture header declares both destination fields as `UWORD` (`compiler/include/datatypes/pictureclass.h:28-43`), while the locally checked libheif API declares the dimension getters as integer-valued results (API cross-check: [coverage line 2303](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2303)). No range check is performed before narrowing. The resulting header dimensions are then supplied to `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY()` as its width and height (`heicclass.c:158-166`).

**Trigger and consequence:** decode a HEIC image whose width or height exceeds the range of `UWORD` (65,535). The Picture object's dimensions wrap/truncate before they are used to size/copy the pixel array, so the advertised image extent is wrong and the transfer can be rejected or limited to a smaller region. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected HEIC datatype and its Picture superclass when the external decoder accepts dimensions outside the 16-bit Picture header range. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked narrowing and downstream use; external format/decoder reachability for dimensions above the field range was not verified. Reject dimensions that do not fit the Picture header or use a representation that preserves the decoded extent. No large image, decode or build was run; source-only; see the [HEIC dimension/API trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2302).

## GD6310 — HEIC RGBA pixels are not marked as alpha-masked in the Picture header [conditional]

When libheif reports an alpha channel, the adapter switches to `PBPAFMT_RGBA` and requests interleaved RGBA output (`workbench/classes/datatypes/heic/heicclass.c:123-127`). It writes the pixel array but never sets `bmh->bmh_Masking` (`:148-166`). The selected Picture constructor zeroes its entire instance data, including its embedded `BitMapHeader` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:156-178`), and the public `mskHasAlpha` value is 4 (`compiler/include/datatypes/pictureclass.h:84`). For a truecolor destination of depth at least 15, Picture's renderer calls its alpha compositor only when the header says `mskHasAlpha`; otherwise the fallback path uses an ordinary opaque bitmap blit (`pictureclass.c:603-660`). Thus the RGBA alpha byte is stored in the source buffer but the normal high-color render path is not told to composite it. This is distinct from the Picture renderer's separate low-depth alpha limitation (GD5527).

**Trigger and consequence:** import an HEIC image with an alpha channel and render it to a high-color RastPort. Since the zero-initialized Picture header remains unmarked, the high-color `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` branch is skipped and transparent pixels can be rendered as opaque. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected HEIC datatype using Picture rendering on destinations at depth 15 or greater. **Confidence:** high for RGBA selection, zero-initialized masking metadata, and the renderer's conditional; visual impact depends on non-opaque source pixels and was not exercised. Set `bmh_Masking = mskHasAlpha` when selecting RGBA, and preserve that metadata through layout. No image/render/build was run; source-only; see the [HEIC alpha metadata and Picture rendering trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2302).

## GD6316

**GD6316 — VESA and Raspberry Pi framebuffer reset callbacks clear the display without serializing active writers.** Each driver's registered `ResetHandler()` calls `ClearBuffer()` directly (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_hiddclass.c:25-35`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_hiddclass.c:27-36`). `ClearBuffer()` writes across the framebuffer with `SetMem()` and does not acquire the driver's `framebufferlock` (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_support.c:295-310`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_support.c:130-145`). The normal display `Show()`/blanking and bitmap `UpdateRect()`/scroll paths do acquire that lock before clearing or copying pixels (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_displayclass.c:188-218`; `vesagfx_bitmapclass.c:159-161,208-216`; Raspberry Pi counterparts `fbgfx_displayclass.c:193-217` and `fbgfx_bitmapclass.c:159-161,208-216`).

The callback is registered when the HIDD object is created and removed on its disposal (`vesagfx_hiddclass.c:45-89`; `fbgfx_hiddclass.c:40-91`). During ordinary user-mode shutdown, Exec runs reset callbacks one at a time in support tasks and waits for each callback, but it does not stop tasks on other CPUs (`rom/exec/doresetcallbacks.c:31-38,65-80,115-153`). Thus, on ExecSMP, a still-running display client on another CPU can enter a locked update while the reset task performs the unlocked clear. Exec's local interrupt disabling does not supply cross-CPU exclusion. The two writes can overlap, leaving the framebuffer partly cleared or with a mixed frame during shutdown; both operations stay within the framebuffer, and no out-of-bounds write is established.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** x86-64 PC builds selecting VESAGfx and enabling ExecSMP, and AArch64 Raspberry Pi builds selecting fbgfx with the `smp` variant (`arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:63-75`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:220-226`; `configure.in:2195-2198`). The trigger is a reset callback overlapping a live display update on another CPU. **Consequence:** inconsistent/partly uncleared display contents during shutdown; lasting user impact is limited because shutdown is underway. **Confidence:** high for the missing shared exclusion and selected SMP paths; manifestation depends on the overlap and is transient. No reset, display update, or SMP interleaving was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD6317

**X11 and WinGDI startup dispatch input methods on the wrong class objects.** In WinGDI startup, `kbd` and `ms` are instances of `CLID_HW_Kbd` and `CLID_HW_Mouse` respectively, but the mouse is registered through the legacy `HIDD_Input_AddHardwareDriver()` wrapper (`arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/startup.c:66-75`). That wrapper dispatches an `IID_Hidd_Input` method and is documented for `CLID_Hidd_Input` receivers (`rom/hidds/input/include/input.h:112-124`; `rom/hidds/input/inputclass.c:267-287`). `CLID_HW_Mouse` instead derives from `CLID_HW_Input` and provides `HW_AddDriver()` (`rom/hidds/mouse/mouse.conf:27-42`), so the call does not reach the registration implementation; WinGDI sees `msdriver == NULL` and aborts before display registration (`startup.c:73-83`). The keyboard registration immediately before it is valid: `CLID_HW_Kbd` derives from `CLID_HW_Input`, whose `AddDriver` injects the default event callback and consumer list (`rom/hidds/kbd/keyboard.conf:25-40`; `rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:204-237`). But rollback calls `HIDD_Input_RemHardwareDriver(kbd, kbdriver)` on that hardware-subsystem object (`startup.c:74-75`), even though the removal wrapper also requires a `CLID_Hidd_Input` receiver (`input.h:127-138`; `inputclass.c:319-364`). Thus the mouse-registration failure leaves the already-added keyboard driver in the shared hardware subsystem; startup does not call the matching `HW_RemoveDriver()` to unlink it. X11 has the inverse receiver mismatch: it creates `CLID_Hidd_Kbd`/`CLID_Hidd_Mouse` consumer objects but calls `HW_AddDriver()` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/startup.c:75-77`), which requires `CLID_HW` (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:135-160`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** hosted X11 startup, and optional MinGW32 WinGDI startup. WinGDI's current selected path reaches the failed mouse registration after adding its keyboard driver; X11's selected registration calls fail before display registration. **Consequence:** both display-driver startup paths abort; WinGDI additionally leaves a registered keyboard driver behind after returning failure, with its lifetime no longer tied to successful WinGDI startup. Use the `HW_Input` subsystem objects with `HW_AddDriver()`/`HW_RemoveDriver()`, or use the consumer-side legacy methods only on actual `CLID_Hidd_Input` objects. **Confidence:** high for the class hierarchies, method receiver contracts, selected call sequence, and missing matching WinGDI rollback; exact post-failure class-code lifetime depends on the module loader. No build or startup was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
