**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Area frame-characteristics pass and source-order full-body reconciliation dated 2026-10-24.
## GD9425

**Setting an Area context menu after Setup does not register the mouse-button handler needed to open it (conditional lost context-menu input; high source confidence).** The public attribute is settable (`isg`) in the Area interface (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.h:381-382`). During `Area__MUIM_Setup()`, the Area adds its `mad_ehn` to the Window only if `mad_InputMode` is non-none or `mad_ContextMenu` is already non-NULL (`area.c:1565-1568`). `Area__OM_SET()` handles a later `MUIA_ContextMenu` by changing only `data->mad_ContextMenu` (`area.c:690-692`); it does not update `mad_ehn.ehn_Events` or call `MUIM_Window_AddEventHandler()`. The Window keeps delivery handlers in its event-handler list (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:3994-4006`) and invokes those handlers from that list during input dispatch (`:1970-2020`). Therefore, an Area set up with no input mode and no context menu remains absent from the list after a menu is assigned, so its `MENUDOWN` context-menu branch receives no event. Register the handler when the first context menu is assigned to a live Area, and remove it if no other Area input feature needs it.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds including the MUI Area class, when an Area is set up with `MUIA_InputMode = MUIV_InputMode_None` and no context menu, then receives a non-NULL `MUIA_ContextMenu` through a supported runtime Set operation. The repository has no checked-in caller proving that exact transition; external or custom MUI clients can use the public settable attribute. **Consequence:** the assigned context menu cannot be opened through the Area's right-button path until the Area is set up again or some other code registers its handler. **Confidence:** high for the attribute flag, setup gate, setter behavior and Window dispatch list; actual affected clients depend on performing the stated transition. `MUIA_InputMode` is marked init-only (`i..`), so dynamically changing that separate attribute is not included. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Area OM_SET and context-menu input-handler passes dated 2026-10-24.
## GD9426

**MUI Area frame titles bypass their width limit when the Area is narrower than its frame margins (conditional title spill; high source confidence).** `Area_Draw_handle_frame()` computes the available title width as the Area width minus the frame's left/right margins, ten pixels of spacing and the outline adjustment (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.c:1145`). If this signed `int` is negative, it is passed to `TextFit()` as `UWORD constrainingBitWidth` (`:1147-1148`; `rom/graphics/graphics.conf:158`). The negative value wraps to a large unsigned limit, so `TextFit()` can accept the full title rather than rejecting or truncating it (`rom/graphics/textfit.c:73-111,123-138`). The title is centered using that measured width and drawn after the frame clip is removed (`area.c:1150-1151,1188-1228`), so it can extend beyond the Area and visually overlap adjacent content. The final spill remains subject to the enclosing layer or virtual-group clip.

The layout does not guarantee enough width for the title: Area's minimum width is based on frame and inner spacing, not title text, and Group propagates that child minimum to normal layouts (`area.c:855-947`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:1388-1404,1550-1573,1860-1936`). Clamp the available width to zero or greater before passing it to `TextFit()`, and handle the no-space case explicitly.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds including the MUI Area and Group classes, with an Area that has a frame title and a laid-out width smaller than `zframe->ileft + zframe->iright + 10 + addtw`. **Consequence:** the title may render beyond the Area's horizontal bounds instead of being suppressed/truncated; visible overlap depends on the surrounding layer/group clip. **Confidence:** high for the signed-to-unsigned wrap and layout minimum behavior; final visibility is clip-dependent. No layout or drawing was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Area frame-title `TextFit()` and minimum-size reachability passes dated 2026-10-24.
## GD9427

**MUI Area context-menu trigger is declared gettable but is never retained for later reads (conditional stale/missing trigger readback; high source confidence).** The public Area attribute declares `MUIA_ContextMenuTrigger` as `..g Object *` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.h:383-384`). On menu selection, Area obtains the selected `MenuItem` and calls `MUIM_ContextMenuChoice`; its handler sets that pointer as `MUIA_ContextMenuTrigger` (`area.c:1896-1912,2082-2086`). `Area__OM_SET()` has no case that stores this attribute and forwards the tag to `Notify__OM_SET()`, which dispatches notifications but stores only its own supported attributes (`area.c:690-711`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/notify.c:397-455`). On a later Get, Area has no matching case and Notify's getter has no trigger attribute case; both delegate until the root fallback handles it as unknown (`area.c:831-848`; `notify.c:462-513`; `rom/oop/rootclass.c:154-159`). Thus a client can receive the context-menu notification and its item value, but cannot subsequently retrieve that item from the object as the public gettable flag advertises. Retain the most recent trigger in Area instance data and return it from OM_GET, or revise the public contract if the attribute is intentionally event-only.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds with the MUI Area class, after a context-menu item is selected and a client later calls `GetAttr(MUIA_ContextMenuTrigger, ...)`. The menu-selection notification itself continues to carry the selected item; the defect affects clients that rely on attribute readback. The checked-in consumer census found notification-only use, so this consequence is conditional on external/custom callers reading it. **Confidence:** high for the declared getter, transient set/notification path and absent storage/getter; practical effect depends on a client using the documented get capability. No menu choice or attribute query was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Area OM_GET/context-menu-choice and notification caller pass dated 2026-10-24.
## GD9428

**Group `MUIA_Disabled` forwarding changes child nested-disable counts even when the Group's own disabled state does not change (conditional stuck or prematurely enabled descendants; high source confidence).** `Group__OM_SET()` removes `MUIA_Disabled` from the tag list before applying the superclass update, then forwards it to children as `MUIA_NestedDisabled` whenever the attribute is present (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:502-505,566-585,619-633`). It does not compare the requested value with the Group's old local disabled bit. Area represents its own `MUIA_Disabled` bit separately from its nested-disable count: setting `MUIA_Disabled` to TRUE is idempotent, while every `MUIA_NestedDisabled=TRUE` increments the low counter and each FALSE decrements it if nonzero (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.c:559-590`; the getter reports disabled when either contribution remains, `:740-748`). Groups recursively forward the nested tag through `Group_DispatchMsg()` (`group.c:1004-1020`).

Two imbalanced updates follow. First, setting a Group's `MUIA_Disabled` to TRUE repeatedly adds a nested-disable contribution to each descendant on every call, although the Group's own disabled bit changes only once. A later single FALSE removes only one contribution, leaving descendants disabled. Second, when an ancestor has disabled a Group through `MUIA_NestedDisabled`, that Group's own local disabled bit can still be FALSE. A redundant local `MUIA_Disabled=FALSE` nevertheless propagates `MUIA_NestedDisabled=FALSE` to descendants, removing the ancestor's contribution from them while the Group itself remains disabled by its ancestor. Descendant controls can then become enabled while their containing Group remains disabled. Forward only the effective transition of the local disabled bit to children, or track the contributions explicitly so each forwarded increment has exactly one matching decrement.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds including the MUI Group and Area classes with Group child forwarding enabled (the default). The trigger is either repeated TRUE updates to one Group followed by only one FALSE, or a Group disabled by an ancestor receiving a redundant local FALSE update. Appearance Preferences uses runtime `MUIA_Disabled` updates on HGroup option rows (`workbench/prefs/appearance/appearanceeditor.c:385-405,568-603,607-700,1028-1112`), confirming a maintained caller family; the inspected sequences do not establish either exact imbalanced ordering. **Consequence:** descendants may remain disabled after the Group is enabled, or become enabled while an ancestor-disabled Group remains disabled. **Confidence:** high for the local state/count mismatch and recursive forwarding; practical occurrence depends on the stated redundant update sequence. No MUI object or GUI state was changed; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Group `OM_SET` nested-disable and selected Appearance Preferences caller rechecks dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9429

**MUI Area export drops selected-state persistence when Dataspace allocation fails (conditional silent state loss; high source confidence).** `Area__MUIM_Export()` serializes `MADF_SELECTED` for an Area with a nonzero `MUIA_ObjectID`, but discards the result of `MUIM_Dataspace_Add()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.c:2092-2103`). `Dataspace__MUIM_Add()` returns zero when allocating the node fails, before inserting or replacing any record (`classes/dataspace.c:93-126`). The Window export delegates to its root object, and Group export recursively forwards to children; Application Save iterates its windows, calls each Export, then writes the Dataspace without checking those results (`classes/window.c:4535-4541`; `classes/group.c:3471-3474` and its export helper; `classes/application.c:2474-2479,2488-2535`). The resulting preferences file can therefore be written without this selected-state record. On a later load, `Area__MUIM_Import()` leaves the control at its current/default state when `MUIM_Dataspace_Find()` returns NULL (`area.c:2109-2121`). Propagate and handle failed Dataspace additions so Save can report or avoid publishing an incomplete state file.

**Affected configuration and caller:** builds including MUI Area, Dataspace, Window, Group and Application classes. The trigger is a selected Area with a nonzero ObjectID being exported while the Dataspace node allocation fails. The checked-in Zune settings test assigns ObjectIDs to controls and calls `MUIM_Application_Save` (`developer/debug/test/Zune/settings.c:14-22,51-82`); this establishes the save/ID caller pattern, but not an Area-derived control instance at the failure point. **Consequence:** that control's selected state is omitted from the saved file and is not restored by Import; other records can still be saved. **Confidence:** high for the ignored allocation result and missing-record import behavior; occurrence requires Dataspace allocation failure and an identified selected Area. No save, load or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Area Export/Import, Dataspace allocation and Application save caller passes dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9431

**MUI Area leaves its temporary mouse-move handler installed after context-menu opening fails or the Area is hidden (conditional event-consumption regression; high source confidence).** On `MENUDOWN`, Area builds a context-menu object, obtains its `NewMenu`, and assigns `zune_open_menu()`'s result to `mad_ContextZMenu` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.c:1862-1880`). `zune_open_menu()` returns NULL if its allocation, `GetVisualInfo()`, or `CreateMenusA()` fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/menu.c:1510-1535`). Area nevertheless replaces its current event registration with one including `IDCMP_MOUSEMOVE` after that call (`area.c:1882-1886`). If opening failed, the matching `MENUUP` removal/reset is skipped because it is guarded by `if (data->mad_ContextZMenu)` (`area.c:1892-1919`). A second path reaches the same state: `Area__MUIM_Hide()` closes an open context menu and sets `mad_ContextZMenu` to NULL without removing `IDCMP_MOUSEMOVE` (`:1671-1687`). Hiding through settable `MUIA_ShowMe=FALSE` invokes Hide but deliberately skips Cleanup (`area.c:608-630`), so it does not remove the event handler. In either case, the stale handler reaches `event_motion()`, whose normal fall-through returns `MUI_EventHandlerRC_Eat` even when no menu is open (`:1926-1974`). Window event dispatch stops forwarding that input event when a handler returns Eat (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:2416-2431`). Cleanup removes the handler only when Cleanup actually runs (`area.c:1617-1623`). Clear the transient mouse-move registration and restore the button-only mask on every path that closes or fails to open the menu.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds including MUI Area and Window support. The trigger is either (a) an Area receives `MENUDOWN` while inside its bounds, `MUIM_ContextMenuBuild` returns an object with a menu, and `zune_open_menu()` then fails (for example, allocation, VisualInfo, or menu construction failure), or (b) a live Area is hidden with `MUIA_ShowMe=FALSE` while its context menu is open. **Consequence:** subsequent mouse-move events are consumed by this Area handler while it remains registered, preventing later Window event handlers from receiving them; a ShowMe-hidden Area can retain it because that transition does not Cleanup. **Confidence:** high for both paths into the same nonzero event mask/NULL-menu state, the Eat return and Window dispatch stop. No menu-open failure, GUI visibility transition, or mouse event was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Area context-menu open-failure, Hide/ShowMe, and Window event-dispatch passes dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9432

**`zune_open_menu()` leaks VisualInfo when GadTools menu construction fails (conditional resource leak; high source confidence).** The helper first allocates a `ZMenu`, then obtains `visinfo` with `GetVisualInfoA()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/menu.c:1520-1528`). If `CreateMenusA()` returns NULL, the failure branch frees `zmenu` but returns without calling `FreeVisualInfo(visinfo)` (`:1531-1535`). `GetVisualInfoA()` allocates a `VisualInfo` and acquires screen DrawInfo (`workbench/libs/gadtools/getvisualinfoa.c:57-69`); the paired `FreeVisualInfo()` releases both (`workbench/libs/gadtools/freevisualinfo.c:49-53`). Thus each such failed menu construction retains both resources. The earlier allocation/GetVisualInfo failures do not have this leak because no VisualInfo was successfully acquired; the normal path frees it after `LayoutMenusA()` (`menu.c:1537-1538`). Add `FreeVisualInfo(visinfo)` to the `CreateMenusA()` failure cleanup.

**Affected configuration and caller:** explicit `workbench-libs-muimaster` builds (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:91-108,433-440`), when an Area's context-menu open path reaches `zune_open_menu()` and GadTools `CreateMenusA()` fails after VisualInfo acquisition (`classes/area.c:1875-1879`). **Consequence:** the VisualInfo allocation and screen DrawInfo reference are leaked for that failed open; repeated failures accumulate them. **Confidence:** high for acquisition-before-failure and missing paired cleanup. No allocation failure or menu construction was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), menu helper allocation-order and GadTools VisualInfo ownership pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9435

**MUI popup windows silently ignore their requested no-backfill hook (conditional menu redraw defect; high source confidence).** Each of `MakeMenuBarWin()`, `MakeMenuWin()`, and `MakeSubMenuWin()` assigns `WA_BackFill` to `win_tags[7].ti_Tag`, then overwrites that same field with `LAYERS_NOBACKFILL` instead of assigning `ti_Data` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/menu.c:650-652,848-850,942-944`). `LAYERS_NOBACKFILL` is the pointer value 1 (`compiler/include/graphics/layers.h:53`), which is also `TAG_IGNORE` (`compiler/include/utility/tagitem.h:35`). Intuition therefore skips the tag entry, and its `OpenWindow()` default remains `LAYERS_BACKFILL` (`rom/intuition/openwindow.c:100`). HyperLayers treats `LAYERS_BACKFILL` as its default clearing operation, while `LAYERS_NOBACKFILL` intentionally does no backfill (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:125-140`; `dohookcliprects.c:67-72`). The menu code paints each popup's menu contents itself after opening; an exposed/damaged region can consequently be cleared instead of left for that renderer, leaving blank or erased menu pixels until another draw. Set `win_tags[7].ti_Data` to `LAYERS_NOBACKFILL` and leave `ti_Tag` as `WA_BackFill` in all three builders.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** explicit `workbench-libs-muimaster` builds, when an MUI menu-bar, menu, or submenu window is opened and its layer later needs backfill because of damage or exposure. The helper source is selected in the `FILES` list (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:91-108`); the parent aggregate dependency is commented, so default package inclusion is not established here. **Consequence:** the requested no-backfill behavior is absent; visible blanking depends on a damaged/exposed popup region before the menu is redrawn. **Confidence:** high for the tag-field overwrite, `TAG_IGNORE` equivalence and default hook; the visual manifestation depends on the damage/exposure path. No menu window or damage event was created; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI menu-window creation/rendering and full `menu.c` source-order reconciliation dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9437

**Page-mode Group `Next`/`Advance` performs modulo by zero when it has no content pages (conditional undefined arithmetic; high source confidence).** `change_active_page()` starts with `data->num_children` and subtracts one when a Register title group is present (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:164-174`). For `MUIV_Group_ActivePage_Next` and `MUIV_Group_ActivePage_Advance`, it evaluates `(active_page + 1) % num_children` without checking the count (`:188-190`). The Group constructor initializes the count to zero and walks attributes in tag-list order (`:304-352,376-378`). If `MUIA_Group_PageMode=TRUE` is followed by `MUIA_Group_ActivePage=Next` or `Advance` before the first `MUIA_Group_Child`, it reaches the zero divisor during construction; later child tags do not prevent that earlier evaluation. A Group can also reach zero content pages through its supported Remove method (`:762-784`), or by having only a Register title group, which the helper subtracts from the page count. A later OM_SET of Next/Advance reaches the same expression. The public ActivePage attribute is settable/gettable, while PageMode is constructor-only (`group.h:72-92`). Guard the zero-page case before computing the new page.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** explicit `workbench-libs-muimaster` builds. A zero-page Group can trigger the defect either during construction when the ordered tags enable PageMode and request Next/Advance before adding content children, or later when ActivePage is set to Next/Advance after the final content page is removed (also possible for a Register containing only its title child). **Consequence:** the remainder expression has undefined behavior; the result may trap or produce an unusable active-page value depending on target/compiler. The checked-in Register keyboard handler emits Next, but its normal constructor requires labels and builds content pages; no maintained caller was found using the triggering initial tag order or navigating after an empty transition. Those paths therefore remain custom/external-client cases. **Confidence:** high for the zero divisor and constructor/setter paths; in-tree reachability remains unestablished. No page Group was constructed, changed, or navigated; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Group constructor/removal and ActivePage arithmetic pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9438

**MUI 2D Group allocation failure silently omits grid sizing and skips child placement (conditional incomplete layout; high source confidence).** `group_minmax_2d()` frees the prior row array and returns immediately if allocating `row_infos` fails; after a successful row allocation it frees the prior column array and returns if `col_infos` allocation fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:1740-1753`). `Group__MUIM_AskMinMax()` calls this void helper but continues to its normal return without recording or propagating the failure (`:1944-1959,1976-1978`), so the Group's 2D child dimensions are not added to its min/max result. Later, `group_layout_2d()` returns before positioning any children if either array is NULL (`:2685-2707`); its caller does not report that skipped layout (`:2844-2854`). The selected Window open/resize sequence asks the root tree for MinMax and later calls Layout (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:3673-3683,3738-3754`), with no Group allocation-failure status to handle. Thus after either allocation failure, window sizing may omit the grid's child requirements and the children retain their prior or initial positions instead of being laid out. Handle allocation failure explicitly and avoid presenting an incomplete MinMax/layout result as if the 2D pass completed.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds including MUI Group and Window, with a Group configured for 2D row/column layout (the AskMinMax path selects `group_minmax_2d()` unless both dimensions equal one, `group.c:1944-1958`), when either per-row or per-column `layout2d_elem` allocation fails during Window open or resize. **Consequence:** the Group omits its 2D child min/max contribution and later skips placement for every child; visible overlap or stale geometry depends on the previous layout and window dimensions. **Confidence:** high for both allocation returns, the unpropagated AskMinMax path and the NULL-array layout guard; the visual result is state/layout-dependent. No allocation failure or layout was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Group 2D MinMax/layout and Window open/resize caller pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9439

**MUI Group child Setup failure leaves the Group's Area setup state and registrations active (conditional cleanup failure; high source confidence).** `Group__MUIM_Setup()` first calls its superclass, which reaches `Area__MUIM_Setup()`, then calls `DoSetupMethod()` on each child. If a child returns FALSE, Group sends `MUIM_Cleanup` only to preceding children and returns FALSE without cleaning itself (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:1027-1079`). Before returning TRUE, Area Setup has already set `muiRenderInfo`, possibly created owned/selected background resources, registered its mouse-button and requested IDCMP event handlers with the Window, and set `MADF_SETUP` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.c:1526-1595`).

The selected Window caller propagates this failure by calling `MUIM_Window_Cleanup` and aborting open (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:3757-3772`). That cleanup releases the Window background, DnD helper and shared render-info resources, but does not call Cleanup on the root object (`:4046-4059`). Area Cleanup is the code that clears `MADF_SETUP`, removes its event handlers, releases its setup-created Area backgrounds, and clears `muiRenderInfo` (`area.c:1601-1645`). Thus a child Setup failure after the Group's superclass Setup succeeds leaves those Area-level obligations outstanding; the Window's render resources are meanwhile cleaned up. Repeated attempts to open the same Window can re-enter Setup with this stale state, potentially replacing Area setup-resource pointers without first cleaning the previous instances. The concrete resource leak depends on the Group's Area attributes and the child's failing Setup path; the registered handler and setup flag follow directly from the ordering.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI builds with a Window whose root is a Group (or subclass using this method), where Area Setup succeeds and any child `MUIM_Setup` returns FALSE. **Consequence:** Area setup state and registrations survive a failed Window open; Area-owned setup resources may remain allocated, and a retry can repeat setup without matching cleanup. **Confidence:** high for the missing cleanup and surviving state/handler; resource leak and retry effects depend on configured Area resources and child behavior. No failed Setup or Window open was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Group Setup rollback and selected Window failure-caller pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9440

**Horizontal Group minimum and default widths overflow their signed `WORD` accumulators (high source confidence; compiler narrowing behavior applies).** `MUI_MinMax` stores all six dimensions as `WORD` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui.h:159-168`). `group_minmax_horiz()` accumulates each visible child's minimum and default width into `tmp.MinWidth` and `tmp.DefWidth`; unlike its maximum-width path, it does not cap those totals at `MUI_MAXMAX` before `END_MINMAX()` adds them to the Group's output (`classes/group.c:1428-1507`). The build-selected String class accepts `MUIA_String_Columns` as a `WORD` and, for nonnegative values, adds `font->tf_XSize * Columns` to all three width fields (`classes/string.c:547-548,867-896`). Four visible Strings set to 1,125 columns with an 8-pixel font each request 9,000 pixels apiece; the horizontal Group's 36,000-pixel minimum/default sum exceeds signed 16-bit range and is narrowed back to `WORD` without saturation. Window asks the root object for MinMax and uses the resulting values to select and clamp its dimensions (`classes/window.c:3673-3683,2778-2845`). The Group therefore reports an invalid wrapped minimum/default width, which can result in a too-small or otherwise incorrect requested window size.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI builds using signed 16-bit `WORD` and a horizontal Group containing visible fixed-column children whose combined minimum or default width exceeds `WORD_MAX`; the four-String configuration above is one concrete input. **Consequence:** Group MinMax width wraps rather than representing the child sum, so Window's default/minimum sizing uses an incorrect value. **Confidence:** high for the `WORD` fields and unsaturated accumulation; exact narrowing result is target compiler behavior. No layout or window was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Group 1D/2D layout arithmetic and String-width caller pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9441

**Large 2D Group row counts wrap the row-array allocation size on 32-bit targets (high source confidence; target ABI condition).** `MUIA_Group_Rows` is declared as a `LONG` and stored as `ULONG` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.h:93-94`; `classes/group.c:380-383`). `group_minmax_2d()` computes `data->rows * sizeof(struct layout2d_elem)` without a checked multiply before calling `mui_alloc()` (`classes/group.c:1740-1745`). On a 32-bit ABI, `layout2d_elem` occupies 12 bytes, and `size_t`/`ULONG` are 32-bit unsigned values, so the product wraps modulo 2^32. For an empty Group configured with 715,827,883 rows (`0x2AAAAAAB`), the requested byte count wraps to four bytes. `mui_alloc()` is an `AllocVec()` wrapper; `AllocVec()` adds its four-byte size header and accepts this nonzero eight-byte total (`rom/exec/allocvec.c:52-73`). After allocation succeeds, `minmax_2d_rows_pass()` iterates the requested rows even with no children and writes `row_infos[0].weight` at the first iteration (`classes/group.c:1587-1596`). On the described ABI, that member begins eight bytes into the four-byte user allocation, so the first row initialization writes beyond the allocated block.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** 32-bit builds with 4-byte `ULONG`/`size_t`, 12-byte `layout2d_elem`, and an empty 2D Group whose `MUIA_Group_Rows` is set to 715,827,883; more generally, row values whose multiplied allocation size wraps to a small nonzero request. The tag is declared `LONG`, and this value is representable on that ABI. A checked-in source search found only the implementation, declarations, and convenience macros, not a maintained setter callsite; the trigger is therefore through a custom/public MUI client. **Consequence:** the row pass accesses beyond the undersized row array; the explicit empty-Group configuration reaches an out-of-bounds write on its first row. **Confidence:** high for the integer-width arithmetic, allocation path, and indexed write, conditional on the stated ABI and successful tiny allocation. No Group or allocation was created; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Group row-count allocation-boundary and Exec allocator contract pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9442

**Changing live Group spacing stores the new value without recalculating child layout (conditional stale geometry; high source confidence).** Group OM_SET handles `MUIA_Group_HorizSpacing`, `MUIA_Group_VertSpacing`, and `MUIA_Group_Spacing` by updating the stored spacing fields, but does not set `need_recalc` for any of them (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:517-534`). The only `MUIM_Window_RecalcDisplay` call in this path is conditional on `muiRenderInfo(obj) && need_recalc`; `need_recalc` is set for Rows and Columns, not spacing (`:506-524,557-558`). The superclass Area setter does not process the Group spacing attributes (`classes/area.c:470-633`). Group min/max and layout routines consume the updated spacing when next called (`group.c:1435-1438,1524-1528,2309-2474,2685-2757`), so after a spacing-only Set on a live laid-out Group, current child positions and window sizing remain based on the previous spacing until another operation causes recalculation/layout.

The public definitions mark horizontal and vertical spacing as settable/gettable and overall spacing as init/set (`group.h:87-104`). The checked-in Wanderer status-bar path sets overall spacing to zero just before removing a child and adding a spacer inside a Group change batch; that structural mutation provides a separate relayout trigger, so it does not demonstrate the spacing-only stale-layout case (`workbench/system/Wanderer/panel_statusbar.c:529-536`). No checked-in caller was found that sets only the spacing on a live Group.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI builds where a client changes one of these settable spacing attributes on a Group after it has been laid out, without another operation that triggers recalculation. **Consequence:** the stored spacing and rendered child positions/minimum sizing disagree until later layout. **Confidence:** high that this Set path does not recalculate; manifestation requires a live Group and no subsequent relayout. No Set or GUI layout was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Group runtime spacing-setter and relayout caller pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9443

**String construction compares initial contents against an uninitialized buffer (conditional invalid read; high source confidence).** `String__OM_NEW()` collects an initial `MUIA_String_Contents` or `MUIA_String_Integer` value into `str`, allocates the string buffer through `Buffer_Alloc()`, then calls `Buffer_SetNewContents(data, str)` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/string.c:519-533,563-566`). `Buffer_Alloc()` requests `MEMF_ANY`, not `MEMF_CLEAR`, and does not initialize `data->Buffer` for non-secret Strings (`:174-208`). When `str` is non-NULL, `Buffer_SetNewContents()` calls `strcmp(data->Buffer, str)` before writing any bytes or terminator to that allocation (`:228-250`). This reads indeterminate bytes; if the allocation contains no NUL within `BufferSize`, `strcmp()` continues beyond the buffer. If the comparison happens to report equality, the routine returns before copying/terminating the requested contents or updating `NumChars` and `AckBuffer`. The earlier `Buffer_SetNewContents(data, "")` call at line 487 occurs before allocation, so its NULL-buffer guard makes it a no-op and does not initialize the later allocation.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI builds when constructing a String with non-NULL initial `MUIA_String_Contents` or `MUIA_String_Integer`; a non-terminated allocator block is needed for the read to cross the allocation boundary, while an accidental match can skip initialization. **Consequence:** undefined/unbounded string read during object construction, with a conditional early return that leaves the initial value bookkeeping incomplete. **Confidence:** high for the uninitialized comparison and unchecked `strcmp`; exact read distance and early-return manifestation depend on allocator contents. No object or allocation was created; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI String initial-buffer and constructor caller pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9444

**Setting `MUIA_String_DisplayPos` also moves the String cursor and clears selection (high source confidence; API-semantic defect).** The public String attribute is set/get (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/string.h:28-29`). Its OM_SET case stores the supplied value in both `BufferPos` and `DispPos`, clears `MSDF_MARKING`, sets the redraw reason to `MOVE_CURSOR`, and requests an update redraw (`classes/string.c:667-672`). OM_GET returns `DispPos` for this attribute while the distinct `MUIA_String_BufferPos` getter returns `BufferPos` (`:756-762`). Thus an application changing only the display offset also repositions the edit cursor and drops any active selection. On the next draw, `UpdateDisp()` uses the new BufferPos when deciding whether to adjust the viewport, so the requested display position may also be normalized to keep that moved cursor visible (`:950-1029`).

The maintained BetterString subclass has its own `MUIA_String_DisplayPos` setter, which updates its display offset and requests redraw without setting its cursor position (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/GetSetAttrs.c:307-311`); its separate implementation is consistent with display offset and cursor being distinct state. No checked-in call to the base String setter was found, so the direct impact is on clients using the documented settable attribute.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI base String objects when a caller sets `MUIA_String_DisplayPos` while the desired cursor position or selection must remain unchanged. **Consequence:** the cursor jumps to the requested display offset and an active selection is discarded; redraw logic may then adjust the offset around that new cursor. **Confidence:** high for the direct state changes; user-visible impact depends on caller intent. No String object or redraw was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI String display-position setter and drawing pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9445

**String selection endpoints narrow from `ULONG` to signed `WORD` (conditional wrong/empty selection; high source confidence).** String buffers and both cursor/mark positions are `ULONG`, and `MUIA_String_MaxLen` permits a caller-specified positive `LONG` capacity (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/string.c:60-65`; `classes/string.h:38-39`). `Buffer_GetMarkedRange()` copies `MarkPos` and `BufferPos` into local `WORD`s before clamping them against the `ULONG NumChars` (`classes/string.c:363-413`). `Buffer_KillMarked()` uses `WORD` endpoints and a `WORD marklen` for the delete/cut range (`:424-462`). Therefore offsets above `WORD_MAX` cannot be represented. For a string longer than 32,767 characters, a marked range with endpoints beyond that boundary can become an empty or incorrect range; on common two's-complement targets an out-of-range endpoint narrows negative and the helper's lower-bound clamp turns it into zero. Cut/delete then does nothing for a range that appears empty, or can remove text from the wrong portion if only one endpoint is affected. The issue is confined to the selection-range operations; this trace does not establish an out-of-bounds edit.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI String with contents/capacity above 32,767 characters and a selection whose endpoint exceeds `WORD_MAX`; the long-buffer API permits this size, but no checked-in caller with such a buffer was found. **Consequence:** selection queries/rendering and cut/delete can use a truncated or empty range. **Confidence:** high for endpoint narrowing and invalid range representation; exact result depends on target conversion behavior. No String, selection, or edit was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI String selection-range and WORD-offset pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9446

**Secret String construction does not terminate when `MUIA_String_MaxLen` exceeds 65,536 (high source confidence; allocation-success condition).** `MUIA_String_MaxLen` is an initialization-only `LONG`, and `String__OM_NEW()` stores positive values in the `ULONG BufferSize` after clamping only values below one (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/string.h:38-39`; `classes/string.c:541-545`). For secret Strings, `Buffer_Alloc()` allocates both buffers and initializes the secret mask in a loop with a `UWORD` index: `for (i = 0; i < data->BufferSize - 1; i++)` (`string.c:174-208`). At `BufferSize == 65,537`, the bound is 65,536, which a `UWORD` index can never reach: after 65,535 it wraps to zero and repeats. The same nontermination occurs for larger sizes. It happens during construction after both allocations succeed and before `String__OM_NEW()` returns.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** base MUI String with `MUIA_String_Secret=TRUE`, `MUIA_String_MaxLen >= 65,537`, and successful allocation of both buffers. **Consequence:** the task executing object construction remains in the mask-initialization loop and does not complete String construction. **Confidence:** high for the counter/bound mismatch; practical reachability depends on the requested allocations succeeding. No String or allocation was created; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI String caller and setup/cleanup cross-check dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9447

**Numeric ScaleToValue clamps a normalized offset against the absolute scale bounds (high source confidence; nonzero-origin caller condition).** `MUIM_Numeric_ScaleToValue` accepts `scalemin`, `scalemax`, and a scale value (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/numeric.h:35-40`). The implementation first subtracts `scalemin` from the input, but then clamps the result to `[scalemin, scalemax]` instead of `[0, scalemax-scalemin]` (`classes/numeric.c:445-467`). It subsequently multiplies by the Numeric value range and divides by the scale width. For bounds 100–200, every in-range input normalizes to 0–100 and is then clamped to at least 100, so all map to the Numeric maximum. Other nonzero origins produce similarly incorrect mappings; the zero-origin case avoids this particular clamp error. The checked-in Slider, Knob, and Numericbutton callers pass scale minimum zero, so no maintained in-tree trigger was established.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI Numeric clients calling `MUIM_Numeric_ScaleToValue` with nonzero `scalemin`, including custom subclasses or external callers. **Consequence:** scale values map to incorrect Numeric values; with a positive origin the mapping can collapse to the Numeric maximum throughout the scale interval. **Confidence:** high for the arithmetic; direct checked-in widgets use zero origin. No Numeric method or widget input was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Numeric full-body and scale-caller pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9448

**Numeric scale conversions overflow signed LONG intermediates for wide ranges (high source confidence; reachable with sufficiently large Numeric and drawable ranges).** Numeric endpoints and scale coordinates are `LONG`, and `Numeric__OM_SET()` accepts Min/Max directly and clamps only the current value (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/numeric.c:139-146`). `MUIM_Numeric_ValueToScale()` multiplies `(value - min)` by `(scalemax - scalemin)` in signed `LONG` before division (`:501-525`); `ValueToScaleExt()` has the same product after clamping its input (`:530-555`). `ScaleToValue()` likewise multiplies its normalized scale offset by the Numeric range in `LONG`, with a source FIXME warning about overflow (`:445-467`). For example, Numeric range 0–2,000,000, current value 2,000,000 and scale range 0–2,000 makes the ValueToScale product 4,000,000,000, beyond signed 32-bit LONG before division. Slider computes its scale extent from drawable size minus knob length and passes that range to ValueToScale and ScaleToValue (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/slider.c:361-373,520-530`), so a sufficiently wide drawable extent and Numeric range also reach the overflowing product through the maintained widget. Numeric does not reject such endpoint values. The selected keyboard handler also computes `data->max - data->min` in signed `LONG` to choose a step of 1 or 10 (`classes/numeric.c:285-302`). Since the public Min/Max attributes are `LONG` (`classes/numeric.h:68-71`), a range spanning the signed limits overflows in this subtraction as well; on wraparound builds this can select step 1 for an enormous range. Home/End-style `MUIKEY_TOP`/`MUIKEY_BOTTOM` handling also subtracts the current value from the selected endpoint in signed `LONG` before calling Increase (`numeric.c:316-328,371-380`); a range spanning `LONG_MIN` to `LONG_MAX` overflows when moving from one endpoint to the other, before the separate Increase arithmetic covered by GD9449. These remain examples of the same unchecked wide-range arithmetic class and are not counted as separate findings. No checked-in caller with such extreme bounds was established.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** AROS builds with 32-bit signed `LONG`, Numeric range/value and scale-coordinate differences whose product exceeds `LONG_MAX`; direct conversion-method clients can supply such ranges, and Slider can do so when its drawable span and Numeric range are large enough. **Consequence:** signed overflow occurs before division and can produce incorrect scale/value mapping; the keyboard range subtraction can also select the wrong adjustment step. Behavior is compiler-dependent because signed overflow is undefined in C. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked arithmetic; exact result and widget reachability depend on compiler and drawable dimensions. No Numeric conversion or Slider input was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Numeric and Slider scale-conversion passes dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9449

**Numeric increase/decrease performs signed arithmetic before clamping at the configured endpoints (high source confidence; LONG-bound condition).** The public Numeric Min/Max setters accept LONG values without restricting them to a smaller safe interval (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/numeric.c:139-146`). `Numeric__MUIM_Increase()` calculates `data->value + msg->amount` and `Numeric__MUIM_Decrease()` calculates `data->value - msg->amount` in signed LONG before passing the result to `CLAMP()` (`:415-438`). With a range such as `[0, LONG_MAX]`, value `LONG_MAX`, and an increase amount of 1 (or the built-in keyboard step of 10), the addition overflows before clamping; on common two's-complement builds it wraps negative and the clamp can jump the value to the minimum instead of keeping it at the maximum. The inverse applies at `LONG_MIN` when decreasing. The Numeric keyboard handler calls these methods for arrow/wheel changes (`:285-380,383-404`), so the condition is not limited to external direct method calls.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI Numeric and subclasses using the base methods with values/ranges near signed LONG limits, when an increment/decrement crosses a limit. **Consequence:** undefined signed overflow before the clamp; common wrap behavior can jump to the opposite configured endpoint. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked pre-clamp arithmetic; exact result depends on compiler overflow behavior. No Numeric method or input event was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Numeric full-body and scale-caller pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9450

**Slider knob-width sizing can become a nonterminating LONG loop when endpoint-span arithmetic overflows (compiler-dependent; high source confidence).** `CalcKnobDimensions()` reads Numeric Min/Max, then intends to cap ranges above `MUI_MAXMAX` by replacing them with 0–10,000 (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/slider.c:67-93`). The test computes `max - min` in signed LONG without overflow protection. For the accepted endpoints `LONG_MIN` and `LONG_MAX`, that subtraction overflows; on two's-complement wrap builds it evaluates to -1, so the cap is skipped. The following `for (val = min; val <= max; val++)` then traverses the entire signed range and overflows `val` after `LONG_MAX`; with wrapping it returns to `LONG_MIN`, still satisfies the loop condition, and never exits (`:95-105`). This routine is called during Slider Setup and when orientation changes (`:197-202,237-249`), so the condition can stall Window setup or the Set call that changes orientation. More generally, any extreme endpoint pair for which `max-min` wraps to a value not greater than 10,000 can bypass the guard.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Slider with Numeric Min/Max endpoints spanning an overflowing signed-LONG difference, notably `LONG_MIN..LONG_MAX`, when using a compiler/target that wraps these operations as assumed by the loop manifestation. **Consequence:** knob-width calculation performs billions of iterations and then cycles indefinitely, preventing the triggering setup/orientation operation from returning. **Confidence:** high for unchecked arithmetic and loop structure; exact result depends on compiler treatment of signed overflow. No Slider setup or orientation change was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Slider full-body and Numeric caller pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9451

**Slider drawing dereferences the label-copy result without checking allocation failure (high source confidence; draw-time allocation condition).** When the displayed Numeric string is invalidated, `Slider__MUIM_Draw()` frees the prior text buffer, calls `StrDup()` on the result of `MUIM_Numeric_Stringify`, then immediately calls `strlen()` on the returned pointer without a NULL check (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/slider.c:407-415`). The selected `StrDup()` implementation returns NULL when `AllocVec()` fails (`compiler/alib/strdup.c:47-56`). Thus a draw/update after allocation failure dereferences NULL before the Slider can finish drawing; freeing the old buffer first also means the previous label cannot serve as fallback.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** non-quiet MUI Slider when its text cache is invalid and allocation for `StrDup()` fails. Value/range/format updates invalidate this cache (`slider.c:204-210`), as do Slider setup/orientation changes. **Consequence:** the draw path dereferences NULL and the redraw cannot complete. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked failure path; occurrence depends on `AllocVec()` exhaustion. No allocation failure or redraw was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Slider full-body and Numeric caller pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9452

**Runtime Numeric range/format changes relayout the parent but leave Slider knob and label dimensions cached (high source confidence; live-change condition).** Slider computes `max_text_width`, `knob_width`, and `knob_height` in `CalcKnobDimensions()` from the Numeric range and formatted endpoint strings (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/slider.c:67-123`). It calls that routine during Setup and for orientation changes (`:197-202,237-249`). On `MUIA_Numeric_Min`, `MUIA_Numeric_Max`, or `MUIA_Numeric_Format`, `Slider__OM_SET()` clears only its cached offset and current label string; it does not recalculate knob dimensions (`:204-210`). Numeric's setter explicitly requests parent Group InitChange/ExitChange when Min/Max/Format changes, so a live Group can recalculate layout while Slider's AskMinMax continues using the old `knob_width`/`knob_height` (`numeric.c:169-185`; `slider.c:275-303`). If new endpoint text is wider, the label can exceed the knob and the Slider's minimum/default dimensions remain too small; if narrower, it retains unnecessary sizing.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI Slider whose Numeric Min, Max, or Format changes after Setup, especially when formatted endpoint widths change. **Consequence:** parent layout is recalculated using stale Slider dimensions, causing clipped/overlapping label or excess space and incorrect minimum sizing until Slider Setup/orientation recalculates them. **Confidence:** high for the missing invalidation/recalculation and stale AskMinMax input; visible effect depends on changed text width and layout. No runtime Numeric change or layout was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Slider full-body and Numeric caller pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9453

**Numericbutton AskMinMax enumerates every LONG value and loops when the range ends at LONG_MAX (compiler-dependent; high source confidence).** When `needs_to_recalculate_sizes` is true, `Numericbutton__MUIM_AskMinMax()` loops from Numeric Min through Numeric Max, stringifies each value, and measures its text (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/numericbutton.c:137-174`). There is no range cap or overflow-safe terminal condition. Min/Max are settable LONG values and the button re-enables this scan during Setup and when Min, Max, or Format changes (`:64-90,93-115`). A caller census found two checked-in direct Numericbutton users, with ranges `[-30,30]` and `[0,100]`; the `MUI_MakeObject(MUIO_NumericButton, ...)` constructor forwards caller-supplied LONG bounds, but no checked-in call of that constructor was found. The extreme-range trigger is therefore a public-client/configuration path rather than one established in the checked-in direct users. With a range ending at `LONG_MAX`, `val++` overflows after the final iteration; on wraparound builds it becomes `LONG_MIN`, which still satisfies `val <= max`, so the scan cycles indefinitely. Even without reaching the endpoint, very large ranges impose work proportional to every value in the range. Window sizing calls AskMinMax, so the scan can block open/layout after setup or a range/format update.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** build-selected Numericbutton with `needs_to_recalculate_sizes` set and Numeric Max equal to `LONG_MAX`, under compiler/target behavior that wraps signed overflow; large but smaller ranges also cause impractically long scans. **Consequence:** AskMinMax can perform billions of per-value formatting/measurement operations and then fail to terminate on wraparound, blocking the sizing operation. **Confidence:** high for uncapped enumeration; nontermination depends on signed-overflow behavior. No Numericbutton sizing or allocation was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Numericbutton full-body and optional-target selection pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9454

**Custom Prop render buffers leak when a Window closes and reopens (high source confidence; custom-scrollbar configuration).** In the custom scrollbar Show path, Prop allocates two render containers for higher-depth screens, or two bitmaps and a RastPort for lower-depth screens (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/prop.c:865-947`). These resources are freed by `Prop__OM_DISPOSE()` (`:209-234`) and are replaced/freed on a subsequent Show, but neither `Prop__MUIM_Hide()` nor `Prop__MUIM_Cleanup()` releases them (`:467-483,1081-1097`). Window close calls root Hide and then root Cleanup (`classes/window.c:3840-3868`). On the next Setup, Prop assigns NULL to all five resource fields without freeing their prior values (`prop.c:392-406`), losing the only references; a later Show allocates a new set. Each close/reopen cycle therefore leaks the prior custom render resources for that Prop.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** AROS custom scrollbar mode, an on-screen custom Prop that reaches the custom bitmap-render path, and a Window that is closed and reopened while the Prop object remains alive. The exact resource set depends on screen depth and successful allocation. **Consequence:** each reopen can orphan the prior two render containers, or the prior bitmaps and RastPort, consuming memory until process/object teardown cannot reclaim them. **Confidence:** high for the missing Cleanup release and Setup pointer reset; only custom Props that allocated the render resources are affected. No Window lifecycle or allocation was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Prop full-body and Window-border caller lifecycle pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9455

**Removing a live Window-border Prop leaves its pointer in the Window gadget's UserData (conditional stale-object dispatch; high source confidence).** When a window-border Prop is shown, `Prop__MUIM_Show()` stores the Prop object pointer in the Window's vertical or horizontal border gadget `UserData` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/prop.c:986-1013`). On Cleanup, the `usewinborder` branch clears the Prop's local `prop_object` and `gadgetid`, but does not clear the corresponding gadget's `UserData` (`:467-483`). Group removal calls Cleanup before detaching the child (`classes/group.c:762-784`). The Window still owns and dispatches notifications from its border arrow gadgets; on matching arrow-button IDCMPUPDATE, it reads the border gadget's `UserData` and sends `MUIM_Prop_Decrease` or `MUIM_Prop_Increase` if non-NULL (`classes/window.c:1830-1853,1857-1880`). If the removed Prop is then disposed while the Window remains open, the next arrow update can dispatch through the stale object pointer.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Window-border Prop (`MUIA_Prop_UseWinBorder` right or bottom), removed from a live Group/Scrollgroup and disposed while its containing Window remains open, followed by an update from the associated border arrow. The checked-in production use is Wanderer: `IconListview` constructs the right/bottom Props as children of the Window content group (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Classes/iconlistview.c:201-227`), and `IconWindow__MUIM_IconWindow_Remove()` closes the Window, removes it from the application, then disposes it (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow.c:1437-1441`). I found no maintained production path that removes and disposes either Prop while retaining that Window open; the trigger is therefore an API/custom-caller condition, not one established for Wanderer. **Consequence:** if a caller performs the stated sequence, Window dispatches a Prop method through a pointer to a disposed MUI object. The exact post-disposal behavior is not established here. **Confidence:** high for stale UserData retention and the later dispatch path; production reachability is unestablished. No Window, Prop, or input event was manipulated; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Prop full-body and Window-border caller lifecycle pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9457

**Scrollbar leaks its preconstructed Prop when Group superclass construction fails (high source confidence; allocation-failure path).** `Scrollbar__OM_NEW()` creates a Prop object before invoking `DoSuperNewTags()` to construct the Scrollbar's Group superclass (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/scrollbar.c:58-69`). If superclass construction returns NULL, the constructor returns immediately (`:70-71`) without disposing the already-created Prop; the Prop pointer is not yet stored in instance data, so normal Scrollbar disposal cannot release it. Group construction can fail when its internal Family allocation fails: `Group__OM_NEW()` disposes its partially created Group and returns NULL (`classes/group.c:314-326`). Thus a single Prop allocation survives that failure path without an owner.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** selected MUI Scrollbar construction where the initial Prop creation succeeds but Group/superclass construction fails, including failure to allocate the Group's Family object. **Consequence:** the unattached Prop and its constructor-owned allocations leak. **Confidence:** high for the ownership sequence; occurrence depends on the stated allocation failure order. No allocation failure or object was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Scrollbar full-body and Group-constructor failure pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9458

**Scrollgroup uses the content's maximum height as the upper bound for a width clamp, which can suppress a needed horizontal bar (high source confidence; asymmetric custom-child constraints).** In the internal-scrollbar path, `Scrollgroup_Layout_Function()` obtains content min/max dimensions, checks whether a vertical bar is needed, subtracts the vertical scrollbar width from `cont_width`, then recomputes `virt_width` using `CLAMP(cont_width, virt_minwidth, virt_maxheight)` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/scrollgroup.c:133-165`). The upper bound should be the virtual maximum width, already computed in `virt_maxwidth` at lines 140-143. If the width reduction makes `cont_width` smaller than `virt_minwidth` while `virt_maxheight < virt_minwidth`, the local `CLAMP` macro chooses the high bound first when low exceeds high (`support.h:56-57`); this can set `virt_width` below the available width and the later horizontal-bar check at `scrollgroup.c:170-177` fails to show a bar. Example dimensions before chrome: content min/max width 500/1000, min/max height 200/300; available width 520 and height 150; a 40-pixel vertical bar reduces width to 480. A horizontal bar is then required by min width 500, but the erroneous upper bound 300 yields a recomputed width of 300 and suppresses it. The final content layout runs with the reduced width (`:227-229`).

**Trigger:** a Scrollgroup uses internal scrollbars, custom content has minimum width greater than maximum height, and a vertical bar reduces the width below that minimum after the initial horizontal-bar check. The checked-in caller census did not establish this exact layout in a maintained application. QuickPart's pending-operations panel was initially considered a caller because its horizontal operation row has an increasing minimum width, but both the Scrollgroup and its content row specify a fixed height of 60 (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_Main.c:509-517`; `QP_ccOpGrp.c:72-95`); this does not establish the vertical-first condition required by the defect. QuickPart's first drive-pane Scrollgroup depends on dynamic drive-row constraints, which remain unverified. **Consequence:** a Scrollgroup with the stated custom dimensions can omit a horizontal scrollbar while its content minimum width exceeds the viewport, leaving content clipped or inaccessible along that axis. **Affected configuration:** public MUI Scrollgroup clients using internal scrollbars and asymmetric custom-content constraints; no checked-in triggering layout was established. **Confidence:** high for wrong variable and branch logic; conditional impact for callers supplying the required constraints. No Scrollgroup layout was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Scrollgroup full-body, layout-constraint and QuickPart caller pass dated 2026-11-07.

## GD9459

**Scrollgroup minimum-size hook adds scrollbar dimensions in signed WORD without saturation (conditional wrap; high source confidence).** `Scrollgroup_Layout_Function()`'s internal-scrollbar MinMax path stores content/bar dimensions in `WORD maxxxxwidth` and `WORD maxxxxheight`. It selects the larger of the content and the horizontal scrollbar minimum width, then adds the vertical scrollbar minimum width; similarly it selects the larger content/vertical bar minimum height and adds the horizontal bar minimum height (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/scrollgroup.c:56-71`). The `MUI_MinMax` dimensions are signed `WORD` (`classes/muimaster/mui.h:159-168`), and the sums are assigned without a range check. A custom content minimum near `WORD_MAX` plus the opposite-axis scrollbar minimum can exceed signed 16-bit range and narrow to a negative or otherwise incorrect minimum. The hook then returns these fields to Group's sizing path, which treats them as the Scrollgroup's min-size contribution.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Scrollgroup with internal scrollbars and custom child constraints where `max(content_min_dimension, same-axis_bar_min_dimension) + other-axis_bar_min_dimension > WORD_MAX`. Window-border Scrollgroup uses a separate direct-copy branch and is not implicated by this sum. The checked-in caller census found no maintained extreme-size content. **Consequence:** the Scrollgroup reports an invalid wrapped minimum width/height, allowing a Window or parent layout to choose dimensions smaller than the content and scrollbar requirements. **Confidence:** high for the signed-WORD accumulator and absent saturation; manifestation requires custom dimensions near the representable limit and target narrowing behavior. No MinMax calculation or layout was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Scrollgroup full-body, layout-constraint and caller pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9460

**Menu title and enabled changes suppress their own MUI notifications (high source confidence).** `Menuitem__OM_SET()` handles `MUIA_Menu_Enabled`/`MUIA_Menuitem_Enabled` and `MUIA_Menu_Title`/`MUIA_Menuitem_Title` by updating the instance, then changes each matching input tag's `ti_Tag` to `TAG_IGNORE` before calling `DoSuperMethodA()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/menuitem.c:323-350,359-369`). The attributes are declared `isg` in the public class header (`classes/menuitem.h:48-55`). The superclass Notify implementation scans only the tags it receives and calls registered notifications for matches (`classes/notify.c:435-453`); consequently these two attribute changes are not delivered to observers. Menu rebuilding and the application menu update still happen, so the defect is specifically missing attribute notification, not a failed value update.

**Trigger and consequence:** an application registers `MUIM_Notify` for either menu title or enabled state, then changes that attribute with `OM_SET`. The menu state changes but the callback does not run; dependent application state can remain stale. This affects the selected muimaster Menu/Menuitem classes and any client relying on notifications. Checked-in caller review established the class and menu-update paths, but no maintained subscriber was found for these particular notifications. **Confidence:** high that the class filters the tags before Notify; client-visible impact depends on notification use. No notification or GUI operation was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2992), Menuitem and Notify full-body/API pass.

## GD9461

**The public `MUIA_Menustrip_Enabled` attribute is declared but has no Menustrip behavior (high source confidence).** `classes/menuitem.h:17` declares `MUIA_Menustrip_Enabled` as a public `isg BOOL` attribute. The shared Menuitem/Menu/Menustrip constructor and `Menuitem__OM_SET()`/`OM_GET()` contain no case for this tag; `Menustrip__OM_NEW()` delegates to the shared constructor and only marks the instance as a Menustrip (`classes/menuitem.c:185-217,323-369,394-414,431-469`). Thus setting the advertised attribute does not update an enabled flag, and getting it does not return Menustrip state. The class descriptor uses those shared methods, so there is no alternate Menustrip-specific implementation in this module.

**Trigger and consequence:** a client constructs or sets a Menustrip with `MUIA_Menustrip_Enabled` and expects the strip to become enabled/disabled, or queries it expecting the current state. The attribute has no effect/state here, so callers cannot use this public API as declared. The checked-in search found the declaration but no maintained use; impact is limited to clients that rely on the advertised attribute. **Confidence:** high that this implementation lacks handling; exact compatibility expectations should be checked against the intended MUI API version. No MUI object was constructed or queried; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2992), Menuitem/Menu/Menustrip full-body pass.

## GD9462

**A notification callback can free the node that its active dispatch still uses (high source confidence).** `Notify__OM_SET()` walks the object's notification list and synchronously calls `check_notify()` for matching tags (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/notify.c:435-453`). `check_notify()` marks the current node active, calls the registered method with `DoMethodA()`, then clears `nn_Active` after the callback returns (`:341-390`). `MUIM_KillNotify` removes the matching list node and immediately frees it through `DeleteNNode()` (`:579-600`); it does not defer deletion for an active dispatch.

**Trigger and consequence:** register a self-destination notification with `FollowParams=2` and method vector `MUIM_KillNotify, triggerAttribute`, then set that trigger attribute. The callback removes and frees the very node whose `check_notify()` invocation is on the stack. On return, `check_notify()` writes `nn_Active` through the freed node; the enclosing `ForeachNode` traversal also advances using the removed node's list link (`compiler/include/exec/lists.h:195-201`). This can corrupt memory or disrupt notification traversal. The trigger is expressible through the public MUI methods; it does not require another task or an external hook. No checked-in self-removing callback was found. **Affected configuration:** muimaster Notify implementation. **Confidence:** high for the synchronous lifetime mismatch; manifestation depends on allocator reuse/state. No notification was registered or invoked; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L2994), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3084), full-body and direct-trigger recheck.
