## GD9463

**Indexed summary:** MUI Application cleanup dereferences preferences when Configdata construction fails.

**Source and trigger:** `Application__OM_NEW()` duplicates the application base, then constructs Configdata. If that construction fails, it immediately calls `CoerceMethod(..., OM_DISPOSE)` and returns (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:466-478`). The `MUIA_Configdata_ZunePrefs` getter that assigns `mgi_Prefs` is only reached after successful construction (`:479-481`). In disposal, a non-NULL `app_Base` enters the preference-save block and immediately evaluates `data->app_GlobalInfo.mgi_Prefs->window_position` (`:787-793`); there is no validity check. The failed constructor path therefore enters cleanup with a valid base and an unset preferences pointer.

**Consequence and scope:** Application construction can dereference the unset preferences pointer during rollback instead of returning the failed-construction result, when Configdata construction fails after the base has been copied. This is conditional on a Configdata construction failure, such as its own allocation failure. **Affected configuration:** applications using the selected Zune Application class. **Confidence:** high for the constructor-to-disposer state and unchecked dereference; the failure condition is resource-dependent. No object construction or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

## GD9464

**Caller recheck (2026-10-26):** the maintained WandererPrefs path can perform this ShowMe toggle. `_WP_AdvancedViewBackgroundGrpObj` is inserted as a page child of `_WP_AdvancedViewPageGroupObj` (`workbench/prefs/wanderer/wpeditor.c:1620-1626`). The image-spec notification calls `WandererPrefs_Hook_CheckImageFunc()` (`:1884-1890,2080-2087`), which sets the background child group's `MUIA_ShowMe` TRUE for image types 0/5 and FALSE for other types (`:704-710,920-925`). A transition between those image types can therefore cause the false-to-true sequence while the page is inactive, depending on the selected page at the time. This raises the trigger evidence from custom-client-only to a maintained-caller possibility, but does not establish that the user's interaction sequence reaches the invisible-input consequence; confidence remains medium for client-visible impact. No GUI action was run.

**Re-enabling a hidden child of an inactive page can make its controls receive input while the page remains undrawn.** A page-mode Group's `MUIM_Hide` hides only its active child, and its `MUIM_Show` shows only the selected page (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:2896-2945,2949-2985`). Drawing also skips children whose page index differs from `active_page` (`:1350-1367`). But if an inactive page child is first set to `MUIA_ShowMe=FALSE` and then back to `TRUE`, Area's setter handles the second transition independently of the Group page selection: because its parent Group has `MADF_CANDRAW`, it calls `DoShowMethod(obj)` and recalculates display (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.c:608-651`). It does not ask a page-mode parent whether this child is active.

**Trigger and consequence:** a client constructs a page-mode Group, switches away from a page, then toggles one of that inactive page's children from `MUIA_ShowMe=FALSE` to `TRUE`. The child's `MADF_CANDRAW` is restored by `DoShowMethod()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/support.c:80-88`), while the page Group's `active_page` remains unchanged and its draw method continues skipping that child. Area registers its ordinary mouse event handler during Setup with `MUI_EHF_GUIMODE` (`area.c:441-447,1554-1563`); Window's `InvokeEventHandler()` admits GUI-mode handlers when the object has `MADF_CANDRAW` and `MADF_SHOWME` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:1961-1973`). The re-enabled inactive child therefore passes the input visibility gate despite remaining undrawn; keyboard/control-character dispatch also checks those flags without consulting the parent page (`window.c:2348-2373`). **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `group` and `area` in muimaster, including the default class set (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:58-87`). **Consequence:** an invisible page control can receive eligible GUI input, such as mouse-button or control-character events, after this state transition. **Confidence:** high for the source state mismatch and event-gate path; medium for client-visible impact because no maintained in-tree page-mode client was found that performs this exact false-then-true sequence. No object, page switch, attribute update or input event was run; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9465

**MUI Window dereferences a failed system-image allocation when creating border scrollers.** `SetupRenderInfo()` creates the left/right, up/down, and size system images with `CreateSysimage()` when the corresponding optional border scroller is enabled, but it does not check those results and returns success (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:524-548,4030-4035`). `DisplayWindow()` then calls `CreateWindowScrollbars()` (`:799-800`). The right-scroller path immediately reads `mri_DownImage->Width` and then the up/down/size image dimensions; the bottom-scroller path likewise reads the left/right/size image dimensions (`:1231-1247,1281-1299`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a MUI Window enables `MUIA_Window_UseRightBorderScroller` or `MUIA_Window_UseBottomBorderScroller` and any required `NewObject("sysiclass", ...)` fails during Setup. Since setup still succeeds, opening proceeds to border-gadget construction, which dereferences the NULL image pointer before `OpenWindowTagList()`. **Affected configuration:** muimaster builds selecting Window, including the default class set (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:58-87`); the trigger requires the optional border-scroller feature and a failed system-image construction. **Consequence:** window opening faults instead of reporting an allocation/construction failure. Check every image result before creating dependent gadgets and unwind any already-created images. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked results and direct dereferences; occurrence depends on the stated feature and failure sequence. No window, system image or allocation failure was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**Maintained caller check (2026-11-01):** this flag combination is used by normal non-backdrop Wanderer icon windows: `iconwindow.c` sets both right and bottom border scrollers when `isBackdrop` is false (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow.c:681-692`). Wanderer is built as `workbench-system-wanderer-app` from its selected source list (`workbench/system/Wanderer/mmakefile.src:5-21`) and launched by the checked-in Startup-Sequence when present (`workbench/s/Startup-Sequence:157-158`). Additional checked-in caller examples include the Aboutbox and AROS TCP MiamiPanel (`workbench/classes/zune/aboutbox/Aboutbox.c:463`; `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/MUI.MiamiPanel/Classes/muimiamipanel_class_app.c:162-164`). This confirms the affected feature is used by maintained clients; it does not change the allocation-failure trigger or demonstrate a failure at runtime. The report's default muimaster build scope and conditional confidence remain appropriate.

## GD9466

**MUI Window pen setup dereferences a failed computed half-shine or half-shadow specification allocation.** The checked-in AROS initialization leaves both default pen-spec strings empty unless `ZUNE_FORCE_SYSPENS` is defined; that define is commented out (`workbench/libs/muimaster/muimaster_init-aros.c:21,51-53,68-71`). In `InitRenderInfoPens()`, an empty default string selects the computed-color path. If the per-window `hshinespec` or `hshadowpec` is NULL, the code stores `AllocMem()`'s result then immediately writes through it with `snprintf()` without checking (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:383-407`). `SetupRenderInfo()` calls this function during Window setup before returning success (`:517,4030-4035`).

**Trigger and consequence:** under the selected AROS pen configuration, Window setup needs to create a computed half-shine or half-shadow spec and that `AllocMem()` fails. The subsequent `snprintf()` dereferences NULL and faults during setup instead of returning a failed setup result. **Affected configuration:** AROS muimaster builds using `muimaster_init-aros.c` and the ordinary computed-pen configuration; builds defining `ZUNE_FORCE_SYSPENS` take the system-pen branch instead. **Confidence:** high for the selected empty-spec branch and unchecked write; occurrence depends on allocation failure. No window setup or allocation failure was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9467

**MUI Bitmap skips all bitmap blits when its alpha attribute is set.** Both constructor and `OM_SET` store `MUIA_Bitmap_Alpha` and set `use_alpha = TRUE` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bitmap.c:268-271,342-345`); `OM_GET` returns the stored alpha value (`:393-397`). In `MUIM_Draw()`, once a source or remapped bitmap and positive dimensions are available, `use_alpha` selects a branch containing only `// TODO: implement`; it bypasses both the masked and opaque blit branches (`:523-550`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** default `muimaster.library` builds selecting Bitmap (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:60-66`) when a client supplies or sets `MUIA_Bitmap_Alpha` on an object that otherwise has a drawable bitmap. The checked-in attribute definition identifies it as a public MUI V20 settable/gettable ULONG (`classes/bitmap.h:15-16`), but this checkout has no prose defining its precise rendering semantics and no maintained Bitmap caller setting it. **Consequence:** setting the attribute makes this class draw no bitmap pixels; whether all callers expect alpha compositing or another supported interpretation requires confirmation of the external MUI contract. Implement the promised alpha rendering or reject/document the unsupported attribute rather than silently suppressing the bitmap. **Confidence:** high for the no-blit behavior; medium that it violates the public API contract, because the local declaration and TODO do not specify expected alpha semantics. No alpha attribute or draw was exercised. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9468

**MUI Bitmap dereferences a failed transparency-mask allocation during setup.** `remap_bitmap()` reaches the mask path for indexed bitmaps when either a mapping table or source colors is supplied and `MUIA_Bitmap_Transparent` differs from the default `-1` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bitmap.c:47-54,94-98`). After successfully allocating the remapped bitmap, it stores `AllocRaster()` directly in `data->mask` and immediately passes that pointer to `memset()` without checking for NULL (`:82-98`). `AllocRaster()` returns the result of `AllocMem()`, which can be NULL on allocation failure (`rom/graphics/allocraster.c:51-56`). `Bitmap__MUIM_Setup()` calls the void `remap_bitmap()` helper and then returns TRUE without a remapping-failure result to propagate (`bitmap.c:439-449`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `bitmap` is selected in the default `muimaster.library` class list (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:60-66`). The failure is reachable in a checked-in caller: the optional Trident preferences IconList builds five-plane Bodychunk icons with source colors and transparent index 0 (`rom/usb/trident/IconListClass.c:171-190`; program target `rom/usb/trident/mmakefile.src:10-12`). Bodychunk setup creates the source bitmap and then invokes Bitmap setup (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bodychunk.c:336-356`). If remapped-bitmap allocation succeeds but the subsequent mask raster allocation fails, the unchecked `memset()` writes through NULL.

**Consequence:** bitmap setup performs an invalid memory write instead of reporting failure; the normal consequence is a task fault during GUI setup. Check `AllocRaster()` before initializing the mask and unwind the remapped bitmap and line buffer on failure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation result and selected trigger path; no allocation failure, GUI setup, or fault was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9469

**MUI Bitmap reacquires palette pen zero because its remap-cache marker is truncated, then releases it only once.** In the indexed palette-remapping path, the cache is a `WORD`, and the code stores `pen | 0x100` as an acquired marker (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bitmap.c:174-192`). On the next pixel with that source index, `remappixel` is read into a `UBYTE` (`:176-179`), truncating marker `0x100` to zero. The code treats zero as a cache miss and calls `ObtainBestPenA()` again. If the color maps to pen zero, this repeats for every such pixel. `ObtainBestPenA()` increments the shared-pen reference count on each successful match (`rom/graphics/obtainbestpena.c:92-106,149-154`). Cleanup tests the full `WORD` entry but calls `ReleasePen()` only once with its low byte (`bitmap.c:473-484`), leaving the additional acquisitions outstanding.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** default muimaster builds selecting `bitmap` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:60-66`), when an indexed source-color bitmap is remapped without an active mapping table or successful truecolor LUT path, and at least one source index maps to pen zero. A maintained transparent Bodychunk caller supplies source colors and transparent index zero (`rom/usb/trident/IconListClass.c:176-188`); this finding's pen-refcount trigger additionally depends on the selected screen/palette taking the `ObtainBestPenA()` branch. **Consequence:** repeated occurrences of that source color over-acquire pen zero, and cleanup releases only one reference, so palette ownership can remain leaked after the bitmap is cleaned up. Preserve the full-width cache marker when testing cache hits and balance every successful pen acquisition. **Confidence:** high for marker truncation and acquisition/release imbalance once the stated path and pen-zero result occur; no palette or bitmap operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9470

**MUI Bodychunk consumes but discards the supplied mask plane.** For MUIA_Bodychunk_Masking == 1, make_bitmap() includes one extra plane in the input row size and advances over it (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bodychunk.c:148-163), but calls planar2chunky() with only data->depth and writes only those color pixels (:155-176). It never converts the extra plane into a mask or passes one to the inherited Bitmap. With the normal Bitmap default transparent == -1 (classes/bitmap.c:257-260), drawing has no mask and blits the source bitmap as opaque (:523-550). The value 1 is the local mskHasMask datatype value (compiler/include/datatypes/pictureclass.h:81); the independent NList Bodychunk conversion explicitly parses and consumes a mask row for that same enum (workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func4.c:554-583).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting bodychunk and bitmap in the default muimaster class list (workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:60-66) when a client supplies a Bodychunk with MUIA_Bodychunk_Masking == mskHasMask and relies on that plane for transparency without also configuring a separate Bitmap transparent index. **Consequence:** mask bits are lost and masked pixels are rendered as ordinary bitmap pixels, so the image background is opaque. Preserve the extra plane as a mask and pass it into the Bitmap drawing path. **Confidence:** high for the discarded input plane and opaque default rendering; medium for public-client impact because no checked-in direct Bodychunk caller selecting masking value 1 was found and the local MUI header gives no prose semantics. No Bodychunk was rendered; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9471

**MUI Bodychunk uses signed 16-bit dimensions and counters for LONG-sized bitmaps.** MUIA_Bitmap_Width and MUIA_Bitmap_Height are stored as LONG values and make_bitmap() only checks that they are positive (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bodychunk.c:115-120,227-232). It passes data->width to planar2chunky()'s signed WORD width parameter and uses signed WORD for its x/y loops (:29-35,151-175). On AROS targets where narrowing 32,768 to WORD yields -32,768, a valid 32,768-pixel one-row bitmap skips all planar conversion; the cleared chunky buffer is then copied across the destination, producing a blank row. With a one-pixel-wide, 32,768-row bitmap, the signed y counter wraps after row 32,767 and the outer loop continues past the requested height, advancing beyond the correctly sized Body data and issuing writes at negative row coordinates. WORD is signed 16-bit (compiler/include/exec/types.h:58-62). The plain graphics bitmap representation stores width-derived bytes-per-row and rows as UWORD, so these specific dimensions are representable (compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:33-40; rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:494-497).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** default muimaster builds selecting Bodychunk and Bitmap (workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:60-66) when a client supplies positive dimensions above 32,767 and the corresponding valid planar or ByteRun1 Body data. No checked-in direct Bodychunk caller with dimensions above 32,767 was found; the trigger is available through the public LONG width/height attributes but depends on a large external image/client. **Consequence:** oversized width can silently produce incorrect/blank pixels; oversized height can continue processing beyond the declared image and caller-provided body buffer. Reject dimensions outside the signed WORD range or use LONG counters and pass dimensions without narrowing. **Confidence:** high for the narrowing and loop-wrap behavior on AROS's signed 16-bit WORD targets and the representable bitmap fields; no oversized Bodychunk or render was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9472

**MUI ChunkyImage narrows its public LONG row stride to UWORD.** The public MUIA_ChunkyImage_Modulo declaration is a settable/gettable LONG (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/chunkyimage.h:22-23), but the instance field is UWORD (chunkyimage.c:20-27). The constructor and OM_SET store the LONG tag into that UWORD field (:126-128,189-191), and Setup passes the narrowed value to WriteChunkyPixels (:84-86). WriteChunkyPixels uses the stride in its row-offset expression, y * bytes_per_row + x (rom/graphics/writechunkypixels.c:18-24,61-70; rom/graphics/graphics_intern.h:295-296). Thus a valid 65,536-byte stride narrows to zero, causing successive destination rows to read from the same source row. The constructor also uses 0xFFFF as its “unspecified” sentinel and replaces that value with width (:108,141-142), so an explicit valid 65,535-byte stride is indistinguishable from omission.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** default muimaster builds selecting ChunkyImage and Bitmap (workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:60-66) when a client supplies pixel data with a row stride greater than 65,534, or explicitly uses stride 65,535. For example, width 1, height 2, stride 65,536 with distinct row bytes is valid input but is stored as zero. No checked-in ChunkyImage caller supplies MUIA_ChunkyImage_Modulo; maintained constructors use the default width stride. **Consequence:** rows are read from incorrect offsets and the generated image has repeated or otherwise corrupted rows. Store the stride in a LONG-sized field, and use a sentinel that cannot collide with a valid stride. **Confidence:** high for the type narrowing and wrong row addressing under the stated valid input; caller impact is conditional on external/public API use. No ChunkyImage or pixel-array operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9473

**MUI List selected removal can loop forever once the list exceeds 65,535 entries.** List__MUIM_Remove() declares its scan index as UWORD but compares it against the LONG confirm_entries_num (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:2505-2513,2547-2573). For MUIV_List_Remove_Selected, when the count is at least 65,536, the loop advances i through 65,535 and wraps it to zero; because zero remains less than confirm_entries_num, the scan repeats and never reaches the no-selection fallback. Selection at indices above 65,535 is likewise unreachable by this scan. The public removal method is defined to remove all selected entries (classes/list.c:2483-2488). SetListSize and insertion use LONG counts and have no 65,535-entry limit (:532-558,2882-2921).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** default muimaster builds selecting List (workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:60-73) when a client has at least 65,536 entries and calls MUIV_List_Remove_Selected. A maintained caller is BoingIconBar's selected-program removal path (workbench/prefs/boingiconbar/bibeditor.c:260; target declared in workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/mmakefile.src:21), although no evidence establishes that this application's list can reach the required size. **Consequence:** the method spins indefinitely in its caller's task instead of returning; entries beyond index 65,535 are not scanned. Use a LONG scan index or reject list sizes outside the supported index range. **Confidence:** high for the wrap and nontermination on AROS's unsigned 16-bit UWORD type; caller impact requires an unusually large list, and no large list or GUI method was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9474

**MUI Popobject advertises Light as settable but ignores runtime changes.** The class documents MUIA_Popobject_Light as V7 [ISG] BOOL, and OM_NEW stores the constructor value in data->light (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/popobject.c:52-60,253-272). OM_GET returns that field (:352-365), but Popobject__OM_SET() has no Light case and forwards the tag to its superclass (:315-348). The first-open hook uses data->light only when constructing the popup Window, selecting borderless-window tags when TRUE (:168-191). Later changes are therefore neither stored nor applied to an already-created popup.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** default muimaster builds selecting Popobject (workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:78) when a client changes MUIA_Popobject_Light after construction. No checked-in setter caller was found. **Consequence:** MUIA_Popobject_Light reads back the old value and the popup retains its original borderless/bordered style, including when the change is made before the first open. Handle the attribute in OM_SET and update the existing popup window's border properties when it has been created. **Confidence:** high for the [ISG] declaration, missing setter case, unchanged getter state, and one-time window construction; no checked-in caller or GUI mutation was found or exercised. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9475

**MUI Rectangle reports successful Setup after its bar-title text allocation fails, then dereferences the missing text.** When `MUIA_Rectangle_BarTitle` is non-NULL, `Rectangle__MUIM_Setup()` assigns the result of `zune_text_new()` without checking it and then returns TRUE (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/rectangle.c:141-155`). `Rectangle__MUIM_AskMinMax()` and the title-bearing Draw paths dereference `data->ztext->width` and `->height` without a NULL check (`:188-210,281-333`). The selected MUI window-open path runs Setup and then `WindowMinMax()`, which dispatches AskMinMax through its root group (`classes/window.c:3764-3776`; `classes/group.c:1853-1888`). Cleanup itself checks for NULL, so the confirmed failure consequence is the sizing/draw dereference, not teardown. `zune_text_new()` can return NULL when its object or copied-content allocation fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/textengine.c:120-130`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** default muimaster builds selecting Rectangle (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:82`) when a titled Rectangle is set up and either initial ZText allocation fails. **Consequence:** window sizing or title drawing can fault on the NULL ZText. Fail Setup when title-text construction fails, and guard later methods against absent text. **Confidence:** high for selected class, allocation-failure return, successful Setup and selected sizing/draw dereferences; manifestation requires allocation failure. No allocation failure, window or draw was induced; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9476

**MUI Register reports Setup success with missing tab-title text after an allocation failure, then dereferences it during setup or cleanup.** `Register__MUIM_Setup()` stores the nullable result of `zune_text_new()` in each item's `ztext` and calls the null-tolerant bounds helper without checking it (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/register.c:499-503`). Check each allocation and unwind Setup, and make cleanup tolerate uninitialized entries. **Affected configuration and trigger:** default Register class when a tab-title `ZText` allocation fails during Setup; with the non-truncating preference the width loop faults immediately, while with truncation enabled cleanup faults when the successfully set-up object is later cleaned up. **Confidence:** high for the nullable allocation, both unchecked paths and class selection; manifestation requires allocation failure. No allocation failure or GUI lifecycle was induced; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9477

**MUI List hit-testing can loop forever with more than 65,535 zero-width columns.** List__MUIM_TestPos() declares its column scan index as UWORD while data->columns is LONG (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:134,3647-3655). The format parser counts commas into an int and sets the LONG column count without an explicit maximum; DELTA=0 is accepted per column (list.c:618-642,658-719,748). A Display hook that returns empty strings for every column yields entries_width == 0; zune_text_get_bounds() gives empty text width zero (list.c:812-839; workbench/libs/muimaster/textengine.c:554-630). With 65,536 or more columns, zero delta and no bars, hit-testing at mx == 0 makes width_sum remain zero, so mx < width_sum is always false. The UWORD index wraps to zero and the scan repeats instead of returning (list.c:3693-3719).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** default muimaster builds selecting List (workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:60-73) when a client configures at least 65,536 zero-width columns, has at least one entry, and invokes MUIM_List_TestPos at the left content pixel. The method is also reached by maintained hit-test and drag paths (list.c:3785-3792,3848-3853,3901-3912,4007,4124). No checked-in client constructing this extreme format was found. **Consequence:** the caller's task spins indefinitely during hit-testing or a related pointer/drag operation. Use a LONG scan index or impose a supported column limit. **Confidence:** high for the counter wrap and nonterminating condition under the stated format and hit coordinate; no in-tree trigger or GUI operation was found or run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9479

**PSI and Zune leak public-screen descriptors loaded from file.** `MUIS_ReadPubFile()` returns a separately allocated descriptor for each valid record (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/readpubfile.c:50-99`; `allocpubscreendesc.c:47-54`). PSI's `ScreenList_Load()` passes each result through `MUIM_List_InsertSingle()` and loses the original pointer on the next iteration; PSI's construct hook makes a distinct list-owned copy and its destruct hook later frees only that copy (`workbench/prefs/PSI/screenlist_class.c:59-77,144-169,311-315`). The caller-owned descriptor is never released, including when insertion fails.

Zune's `PopPublicScreenStrObjFunc()` also reads these allocated descriptors into its list and never frees them (`workbench/prefs/Zune/systemp.c:88-95`). Unlike PSI, its List has no construct/destruct hooks: the default List construct method returns the input pointer unchanged, and the default destruct method does nothing (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:3071-3087,3095-3110`). Thus the record's `Name` remains usable while the row is present, but each later popup opening clears the list entries without freeing their backing descriptors and then allocates another set. `Popobject_Open_Function()` invokes this hook before each popup open (`popobject.c:193-201`; `popstring.c:178-200`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** PSI when it loads a public-screen file with valid records; or the Zune preferences public-screen picker each time it opens while the file contains valid records. **Consequence:** each record read leaks one `MUI_PubScreenDesc`; repeated Zune popup opens accumulate the allocations. The IFF file still closes after the read loop. PSI can free the original after its construct hook has copied it. Zune should copy each name into list-owned storage with a matching destruct hook, then free the descriptor, or use an equivalent explicit ownership scheme. **Confidence:** high for the allocation and both missing-release paths; no file load or popup was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9480

**PSI can pass a truncated or incomplete path to its file operation.** getfilename() stores the selected drawer and filename in a static 512-byte buffer. It copies the drawer with stccpy() and calls AddPart() without checking its return value, then returns the buffer whenever a filename was selected (workbench/prefs/PSI/mainwindow_class.c:102-158). ASL's file requester allows a 1,025-character drawer path (workbench/libs/asl/filereqhooks.h:38; filereqhooks.c:870-880). stccpy() limits the copied drawer to the destination size, and DOS AddPart() returns DOSFALSE with ERROR_LINE_TOO_LONG when the combined path cannot fit (rom/dos/addpart.c:196-218). PSI ignores that failure and still returns buf; Open and Save As pass it to the load/save methods (mainwindow_class.c:163-187).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** PSI's Open, Append, or Save As requester when the selected drawer plus filename cannot be represented in the 512-byte buffer. **Consequence:** the operation receives a truncated drawer path or a path missing the selected filename, so it may load from or save to a different path or fail against the wrong path. Check both copy and AddPart results, and reject the selection instead of returning a partial path. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked truncation/failure and returned partial buffer; the exact subsequent DOS result depends on the truncated path. No long path or file operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9481

**PSI discards public-screen save errors, and its Finish action quits anyway.** ScreenList_Save() returns FALSE if opening the file fails or MUIS_WritePubFile() fails while writing an entry; it closes an opened file before returning (workbench/prefs/PSI/screenlist_class.c:174-202). MainWindow_SaveAs() discards that return value, and MainWindow_Finish() likewise ignores the results of saving the Use and Save preference files and unconditionally requests application quit (workbench/prefs/PSI/mainwindow_class.c:57-69,179-189).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** PSI when Save As cannot open or completely write the selected file, or when the Save/Use Finish action encounters either failure. **Consequence:** PSI provides no failure result or indication to the user; Finish closes the application after a failed preference save, leaving the intended file absent or incomplete. Propagate the save result and keep the application open or report the failure. **Confidence:** high for discarded results and unconditional quit; no DOS or write failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9482

**PSI's display-mode selector skips its monitor-mask fallback when no exact mode ID exists.** DispIDlist_Set() stores the requested CurrentID and scans its entries with mask initially zero, which compares the full display IDs. The code appears to intend a second pass with MONITOR_ID_MASK to match a mode across monitor IDs, but after the first scan reaches the end, ni is NULL and the method breaks before updating mask and retrying (workbench/prefs/PSI/displayidlist_class.c:141-175). The EditPanel selects a saved descriptor's DisplayID through this attribute and later stores the selected CurrentID back into that descriptor (workbench/prefs/PSI/editpanel_class.c:144,201).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** PSI when editing a public-screen descriptor whose saved DisplayID is not an exact match for any currently enumerated list entry, but a monitor-mask-equivalent entry exists. **Consequence:** the fallback match is not selected; the list becomes inactive, and saving the descriptor can preserve INVALID_ID rather than the corresponding available mode. The fallback intent is inferred from the outer loop that changes mask and the comparison using ~mask; no explicit comment defines the desired fallback contract. **Confidence:** medium for the user-visible mismatch and conditional descriptor result; the unreachable second pass is explicit, but the intended fallback semantics are inferred. No mode list or GUI was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**Palette Preferences dereferences a failed Colorfield pointer-array allocation during Setup.** PEPalette__OM_NEW() sets numentries to the size of a local Colorfield object array, allocates data->colorfieldentries without checking the result, and returns a successfully constructed object (workbench/prefs/palette/palette.c:278-378, especially 347,355-362). ## GD9484

## GD9487

**Palette Preferences does not successfully import ordinary ILBM color maps.** Prefs_ImportFH() first registers a stop chunk for PREF:PALT. When that succeeds, it enters the first branch and scans the IFF input for that chunk; the ILBM:CMAP handler is an else-if and is never registered for this path (workbench/prefs/palette/prefs.c:102-111,159-162). For an ordinary ILBM without PREF:PALT, the scan does not reach the color-map conversion loop. If the first StopChunk registration instead fails and the ILBM:CMAP else-if runs, that branch writes color values but never sets retval to TRUE (prefs.c:161-185,192). PalEditor refreshes its gadgets only when Prefs_ImportFH() returns TRUE (workbench/prefs/palette/paleditor.c:308-321).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable Palette Preferences program when importing a normal ILBM file containing a CMAP chunk. **Consequence:** the advertised color-map import path is skipped in the normal successful registration case; the fallback path, if reached, can modify palette values yet still reports failure and does not refresh the editor. Arrange IFF stop-chunk handling so the ILBM branch is reachable for ILBM input and return success only after a complete import. **Confidence:** medium-high; branch ordering and missing success assignment are explicit, while parser outcomes are inferred from the selected IFF StopChunk/ParseIFF contracts. No ILBM file was imported. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9488

## GD9491

**Indexed summary:** Palette Preferences trusts imported pen-map values as color-entry indexes.

**Source and trigger:** `Prefs_ImportFH()` accepts an exact-size PALT chunk, reads its pen-map words, and for each 8-color value at or above `PEN_C3` subtracts `PEN_C3 - 4`; it does not check the result against the palette's eight map entries (`workbench/prefs/palette/prefs.c:116-155`; `PEN_C3` is `0xFEFC` in `compiler/include/intuition/screens.h:329`). Thus an imported value `0xFFFF` becomes 263. A successful import flows through the selected `PalEditor__MUIM_PrefsEditor_ImportFH()` caller into `PalPrefs2Gadgets()` (`paleditor.c:307-321,284-304`), and `Palette__OM_SET()`/selection callbacks use map values as indexes into the 13-entry palette table (12 colors plus sentinel) and eight-entry screen-pen array (`palette.c:175-199,410-417,621-623`; array lengths from `prefs.h:16` and `paleditor.h:13`).

**Consequence and scope:** Selecting or applying an imported map entry with a value such as 263 indexes beyond the palette's entry array and can also index beyond the pen array before `SetRGB32()`. This can corrupt palette-editor behavior or fault while applying the imported preference. Applies to exact-size PALT files containing out-of-range pen-map words in the optional Palette Preferences target. High confidence in the unchecked conversion and indexed callers; no malformed file or GUI action was run.

## GD9492

**Indexed summary:** Generic indexed-color mapping overflows signed `int` while measuring palette distance.

**Source and trigger:** `colorDistance()` subtracts each `HIDDT_ColComp` after converting it to `int`, squares the signed `int` difference, and sums the four results before returning `ULONG` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4648-4660`). `HIDDT_ColComp` is `UWORD`. Valid `WriteRGBPixel()` values expand 8-bit channels to values up to `0xff00`, and other selected pixel/color APIs can pass `0xffff` (`workbench/libs/cgfx/writergbpixel.c:75-84`; `rom/graphics/setrpattrsa.c:141-155`; `rom/graphics/text.c:725-734`). A component difference above 46,340 overflows a 32-bit signed `int` when squared, before conversion to `ULONG`.

**Consequence and scope:** The indexed `MapColor()` search compares these distances to choose the closest palette entry (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:4662-4704`). On 32-bit-`int` targets, accepted full-range color inputs invoke signed-overflow undefined behavior; on targets with wider `int`, the summed value can still narrow modulo 32-bit `ULONG`. The selected palette pen may therefore be wrong, with exact result dependent on integer width and compiler behavior. Applies to subclasses inheriting the generic `MapColor()` implementation, including the selected generic ChunkyBM and PlanarBM classes. High confidence in the arithmetic and caller range; no color mapping was run.

## GD9493

**Indexed summary:** Generic HIDD line rasterization cannot represent the distance between valid signed-`WORD` endpoints.

**Source and trigger:** `BM__Hidd_BitMap__DrawLine()` receives signed-`WORD` endpoints and stores axis deltas and Bresenham state (`dx`, `dy`, `d`, `incrE`, `incrNE`, and loop index `i`) in `WORD` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:1559-1567,1682-1775`). The public graphics `Draw()` path clips a line to its bounding rectangle and passes the relative endpoint coordinates to this method (`rom/graphics/draw.c:99-140`; `gfxfuncsupport.c:123-140`). When either non-axis endpoint delta is at least 32,768, its absolute value cannot be represented as a positive signed `WORD`. For example, a line from `(-32768,0)` to `(32767,1)` on a bitmap at least 32,768 pixels wide has a horizontal delta of 65,535.

**Consequence and scope:** The narrowed major delta becomes negative and is swapped with the smaller positive delta, so the generic raster loop runs only a short prefix and omits most of the requested line. This is a drawing correctness defect for spans at or above the signed-`WORD` delta boundary, including the public `Draw()` example above. It applies to generic bitmap subclasses inheriting this method; subclasses that replace `DrawLine()` are outside the trigger. High confidence in the narrowing and selected caller path; no line was drawn.

## GD9494

**Indexed summary:** Generic HIDD bitmap row-size rounding wraps to zero for valid maximum-width bitmaps.

**Source and trigger:** `GetBytesPerRow()` rounds `data->width` using a `UWORD width` temporary and the default alignment of 16 pixels (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:849-871`; `BM__Root__New()` default at `:897-899`). For widths 65,521 through 65,535, `(width + 15) & ~15` is 65,536, which narrows to zero in that temporary. For a depth-24 `AllocBitMap()` request, graphics.library selects the generic RGB24 ChunkyBM path (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:242-255,293-310,345-349`; `gfx_displayclass.c:1036-1072`). The ChunkyBM constructor sizes its owned pixel buffer as `height * bytesperrow`; Exec `AllocVec(0)` returns NULL (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:27-82`; `rom/exec/allocvec.c:53-59`).

**Consequence and scope:** The otherwise representable maximum-width depth-24 bitmap fails construction because row rounding wraps to a zero-byte stride and buffer allocation fails. This affects default-stride generic chunky allocations in the stated width range; it does not claim that every display backend uses this generic class. High confidence in the width narrowing and selected allocation path; no bitmap was allocated.

## GD9495

**Indexed summary:** AROS Mutual Exclude dereferences a missing DrawInfo before its constructor can reject the object.

**Source and trigger:** `AROSMX__OM_NEW()` initializes `data->dri` to NULL, then replaces it only if a `GA_DrawInfo` tag is supplied (`workbench/classes/gadgets/arosmutualexclude/mxclass.c:105-113`; tag scan at `:40-66`). It passes the field to a child `SYSICLASS` object as `SYSIA_DrawInfo` (`:133-142`). The selected SystemImage constructor's `sysi_setnew()` reads `dri->dri_Font` before validating the pointer (`rom/intuition/sysiclass.c:115-196`). AROSMX checks for a missing `data->dri` only after `NewObjectA()` returns (`mxclass.c:144-147`), too late to handle the absent-tag case.

**Consequence and scope:** Constructing this optional AROSMX class without `GA_DrawInfo` dereferences NULL in the child SystemImage constructor instead of returning the intended NULL construction result. Its public header does not document DrawInfo as required, and no checked-in AROSMX instantiation was found; external callers can reach the documented constructor. The separately checked GadTools Mutual Exclude class supplies a validated DrawInfo and is not affected. High confidence in the call order and dereference; no object was constructed.

## GD9496

**GetColorMap truncates large entry counts and leaks both color tables on free.** GetColorMap() accepts ULONG entries and allocates ColorTable and LowColorBits using entries * sizeof(UWORD), then stores entries in the UWORD ColorMap.Count field (rom/graphics/getcolormap.c:59-92; compiler/include/graphics/view.h:148-153). For entries=65,536, both table allocations are 131,072 bytes but Count truncates to zero. FreeColorMap() uses Count to calculate both table free sizes, then frees the ColorMap itself (rom/graphics/freecolormap.c:55-74). Exec FreeMem() returns without freeing when byteSize is zero (rom/exec/freemem.c:60-66).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** callers of the public graphics GetColorMap(ULONG entries) API requesting 65,536 entries, provided both table allocations succeed; the API declaration has no stated maximum (rom/graphics/graphics.conf:135-136). **Consequence:** FreeColorMap() leaves both table allocations live and releases the structure containing their pointers, leaking 256 KiB total per map. Reject counts that do not fit Count or store/use a sufficiently wide count for allocation and free. **Confidence:** high; exact allocation size, field narrowing, and zero-size FreeMem behavior are explicit. No colormap was allocated or freed. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9497

**Indexed summary:** Wanderer can dereference a missing icon during drag/drop after icon restoration fails.

**Source and trigger:** `IconList__MUIM_Hide()` frees each entry's `DiskObject` and sets `ie_DiskObj` to NULL (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Classes/iconlist.c:3192-3209`). On the next `MUIM_Show()`, it retries `GetIconTags()` with `ICONGETA_FailIfUnavailable=FALSE` but retains NULL on failure without clearing the entry's visible/selection flags (`:3164-3181`). `IconDrawerList` creates visible orphan `.info` entries as `ST_FILE` with `ICONENTRY_FLAG_ISONLYICON` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Classes/icondrawerlist.c:148-177`).

**Consequence and scope:** With `CREATE_FULL_DRAGIMAGE` enabled in the selected IconList class, dragging a selected entry with a failed icon restore passes its NULL `ie_DiskObj` into `DrawIconOnDragImage()`; `IconControlA(NULL)` leaves the initialized width sentinel unchanged, and the fallback dereferences `icon->do_Gadget.Width` (`iconlist.c:6539-6558,6605-6722`; selected `IconControlA()` behavior `workbench/libs/icon/iconcontrol.c:56-65,457-484`). Dropping onto a visible orphan icon can also dereference the same NULL object while checking whether its type is WBDRAWER/WBDISK (`iconlist.c:6938-6943`). This requires restoration failure after the list was hidden, such as a missing or unreadable `.info` file or allocation failure. High confidence in both unchecked paths; no hide/show or drag/drop operation was run.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3126`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3126).

## GD9498

**Palette Preferences keeps the previous color selection after switching between 4-color and 8-color maps.** The Cycle notification invokes setcolor_func() mode 4, which reads the new mode, changes visibility of fields 4–7, and switches data->penmap to penmap4 or penmap8, then returns without refreshing the active row's mapped color or lastindex frame (workbench/prefs/palette/palette.c:149-175). The current active List row and lastindex remain from the old map. Other selection and map-update paths explicitly read data->penmap[entry] and update the selected Coloradjust color/frame (palette.c:131-147,212-250,518-536).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable Palette Preferences target when switching modes while the active row maps to different palette colors in the 4-color and 8-color maps. **Consequence:** the visible selected frame and Coloradjust value can continue to describe the old mapped color, so subsequent edits may apply to a different color than the user sees as selected. After changing the map pointer, re-run the selected-row synchronization path and update frame/visibility state. **Confidence:** medium-high; the mode handler changes only the map pointer and field visibility, while the other synchronization logic is in separate paths. No GUI mode switch was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9499

**Wanderer leaks each panel spacer removed when a toolbar or status bar is installed.** IconWindow constructs separate top and bottom panel groups, each with an HSpace child stored in its panel data (workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow.c:589-620). When Toolbar setup adds its toolbar, it removes the top spacer with OM_REMMEMBER and clears the only panel-data pointer to it; StatusBar setup does the same to the bottom spacer (panel_toolbar.c:351-362; panel_statusbar.c:385-404). The selected muimaster Group OM_REMMEMBER path hides and cleans up the child, disconnects it, and removes it from the family, but does not dispose it (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:762-789).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Wanderer windows where the optional toolbar and/or status bar is enabled and its extension setup replaces the initial spacer. **Consequence:** the detached HSpace object is no longer in the group tree or tracked by the panel data and is never disposed; enabling both features leaks one object for each spacer. Explicitly dispose the removed spacer after detaching it, or transfer ownership to a tracked field for later disposal. **Confidence:** high for both spacers' construction, pointer clearing, and Group removal semantics. No Wanderer window or panel was created. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9500

**SystemPrefsWindow reports Export with Icon success when writing the exported icon fails.** The Export method first stores the result of MUIM_PrefsEditor_Export in result. If that succeeds and withIcon is true, it loads the default preference DiskObject, changes its tool and tool types, and calls PutDiskObject(prefname, dobj) without checking the BOOL return; it then restores and frees the DiskObject and returns the earlier preferences-export result (workbench/classes/zune/systemprefswindow/systemprefswindow.c:455-519). PutDiskObject documents FALSE on error (workbench/libs/icon/putdiskobject.c:12-53).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Zune SystemPrefsWindow's Export with Icon action when preferences export succeeds, the default preference icon can be loaded, and writing the exported icon fails. **Consequence:** the preferences file is exported but its icon may be absent or stale, while the method still reports success. Fold the icon write result into the returned result and report which part failed. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked BOOL and returned earlier success value; no icon write was attempted. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9501

**SystemPrefsWindow marks the editor changed after an import that failed before changing preferences.** After a selected filename is assembled, the Import method stores the result of MUIM_PrefsEditor_Import in result, then unconditionally sets MUIA_PrefsEditor_Changed to TRUE without checking result (workbench/classes/zune/systemprefswindow/systemprefswindow.c:428-446). The selected Palette editor returns Prefs_ImportFH()'s result and refreshes its gadgets only on success (workbench/prefs/palette/paleditor.c:307-321). For example, an invalid or wrong-sized PALT chunk makes Prefs_ImportFH() return FALSE before copying any values into paletteprefs (workbench/prefs/palette/prefs.c:106-123,156-159).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Zune SystemPrefsWindow with the Palette editor when a selected, opened file fails validation before preference mutation, such as a PALT chunk of the wrong size. **Consequence:** the editor is marked dirty and Save/Use controls can become enabled even though the failed import did not change its settings. Only set Changed after a successful import, or explicitly preserve dirty state when an importer reports partial changes. **Confidence:** high for the unconditional flag update and the stated no-mutation failure path; other importers may partially mutate before returning FALSE, so this report does not claim every failed import is side-effect-free. No import or GUI operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9502

**MUI Colorfield keeps using a fixed pen after its Pen attribute is reset to automatic.** Colorfield's OM_SET releases an owned pen, assigns the supplied Pen value, and sets FLAG_FIXED_PEN when the value is concrete, but does not clear that flag when the value is the automatic sentinel 0xff (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/colorfield.c:215-226). On a later Setup, Colorfield_SetupPen() checks the stale flag and calls SetRGB32() on data->pen rather than obtaining a pen for the current RGB value (colorfield.c:296-324). The attribute documentation says a pen is obtained automatically when not explicitly set (colorfield.c:38-45).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** muimaster's Colorfield class on screen cleanup/re-setup after a caller changes MUIA_Colorfield_Pen from a fixed pen to 0xff. **Consequence:** the gadget continues to claim and program the old fixed pen instead of allocating/releasing an automatic pen according to the new setting; this can overwrite an unrelated screen color and omit the expected pen allocation. Clear FLAG_FIXED_PEN when the sentinel is set and run the automatic setup path. **Confidence:** high for stale flag and subsequent fixed-pen branch; no checked-in maintained caller was found that resets this attribute to the sentinel, so caller impact is conditional on public API use. No pen operation or gadget lifecycle was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9503

**MUI Coloradjust loses hue and saturation when a gradient slider exists without a color wheel.** Coloradjust__OM_NEW() opens the colorwheel and gradientslider gadget libraries independently and creates each child only if its library is available; it permits a gradient child without a wheel child (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/coloradjust.c:215-290). On AROS, support_aros.h defines EXEC_INTERFACE_GET_MAIN as constant 1, so the later check does not reject the object when the colorwheel library is absent (support_aros.h:17; coloradjust.c:301-309). Setup registers GradFunc() for GRAD_CurVal whenever the gradient exists, without requiring a wheel (coloradjust.c:393-407). GradFunc() reads hue and saturation using XGET(data->wheel, ...), then converts the new brightness to RGB (coloradjust.c:178-205). XGET uses GetAttr(), and Intuition GetAttr() returns FALSE immediately for a NULL object (muimaster/macros.h:355-360; rom/intuition/getattr.c:62-80), leaving the initialized storage values at zero rather than dereferencing NULL.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** AROS muimaster Coloradjust when gadgets/colorwheel.gadget is unavailable but gadgets/gradientslider.gadget loads, followed by a gradient value change. **Consequence:** the callback converts brightness with zero hue and saturation, so changing the gradient produces grayscale output instead of preserving the selected color's hue and saturation. Avoid constructing/registering this partial combination or retain and use the last valid hue/saturation when the wheel is unavailable. **Confidence:** high for the zero-value callback inputs and resulting loss of hue/saturation; the prior crash claim is withdrawn because GetAttr() safely rejects a NULL object. The selected Palette caller constructs Coloradjust without requiring the optional wheel (workbench/prefs/palette/palette.c:326-327). No gadget library failure or GUI event was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9504

**An empty vertical MUI PanelTitle divides by zero while drawing.** PanelTitle_Draw() draws only when data->text is non-NULL, then in its vertical-left-title branch computes char_height as data->text_height / strlen(data->text) (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panel.c:666-735). PanelTitle_CalculateTextSize() treats a non-NULL empty string as valid text and sets vertical text_height to character height multiplied by its zero length (panel.c:286-304). Thus a PanelTitle configured with Vertical=TRUE, Position=Left, and Text="" reaches integer division by zero during object drawing.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** muimaster's built-in PanelTitle class when an application supplies an empty but non-NULL title and requests vertical left positioning, then the object is drawn. **Consequence:** the draw method traps or raises undefined behavior at division by zero instead of rendering an empty title. Return early for an empty string or avoid dividing by its length. **Confidence:** high; the guard distinguishes NULL from empty text, and the selected drawing branch divides by the exact zero length. No panel was drawn. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9505

**MUI PanelTitle allocates arrow specs for its old position when Position changes.** In PanelTitle__OM_SET(), the Position case frees existing vector specs, calls PanelTitle_AllocateVectorSpecs(), and only then stores the new position (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panel.c:498-505). The allocator chooses right/up specs for Left and right/down specs for Top based on data->position at call time (panel.c:410-421). After changing Top to Left, the title therefore has no up-arrow spec; after changing Left to Top, it has no down-arrow spec. PanelTitle_DrawArrow() silently skips a direction whose spec is NULL (panel.c:333-377), so the corresponding collapsed/expanded state indicator is not drawn.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** muimaster PanelTitle with Collapsible and DrawStateIndicator enabled, after changing MUIA_PanelTitle_Position between Top and Left and drawing the new state arrow. **Consequence:** one arrow direction is missing because the title retains specs for the previous orientation. Store the new position before allocating orientation-dependent specs. **Confidence:** high for the ordering and missing-spec path; no PanelTitle was repositioned or drawn. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9506

**Collapsible MUI PanelTitle leaks arrow specs on each window reopen.** PanelTitle__MUIM_Setup() allocates orientation-specific vector image specs whenever the title is collapsible (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panel.c:582-606; allocation helper at :398-422). PanelTitle__MUIM_Cleanup() only removes the event handler and delegates to its superclass; it does not call PanelTitle_FreeVectorSpecs() (panel.c:609-616). A later Setup overwrites the stored spec pointers with newly allocated specs, while disposal can clean only the latest pointers (panel.c:468-478).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** a collapsible PanelTitle whose window is cleaned up and set up again, such as closing and reopening the window, before the title object is disposed. **Consequence:** each setup/cleanup cycle leaves the previous arrow specs allocated; repeated reopen cycles accumulate resources until object disposal. Free the specs on Cleanup and recreate them on Setup, or retain them across Setup without overwriting. **Confidence:** high for the unpaired setup/cleanup allocation; zune_imspec_cleanup() is the documented release routine (workbench/libs/muimaster/imspec.h:31-39). No window lifecycle was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9507

**MUI Panel declares a Panel_Draggable attribute that the class never handles.** The public Panel header defines MUIA_Panel_Draggable (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panel.h:21-32), but a full class search finds no use of that tag in panel.c. Panel construction, setting, and getting instead recognize the generic MUIA_Draggable attribute (panel.c:924-944,1124-1142,1208-1218).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** a client using the public MUIA_Panel_Draggable tag to enable or disable a Panel drag handle. **Consequence:** the requested Panel-specific setting is ignored; the generic MUIA_Draggable path remains separately available. Implement and document the declared tag or remove it if it is not part of the intended API. **Confidence:** medium; the header declaration and lack of implementation are explicit, but the header alone does not establish whether this unused tag was intended as a supported public contract, and no maintained caller uses it. No Panel object was created. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9508

**MUI Panel's constructor creates a drag handle for false and can choose its orientation from tag order.** Panel__OM_NEW() handles MUIA_Draggable by unconditionally creating and adding a DragHandle; it never checks tag->ti_Data (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panel.c:924-944). It also passes title_position accumulated from tags already visited. If MUIA_Draggable appears before MUIA_Panel_TitlePosition, the handle is created with the default None position and therefore horizontal orientation; the later title tag does not reorient the already-created handle. Panel_CreateDragHandle() derives vertical orientation only from a Left position (panel.c:270-279).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** constructing a Panel with MUIA_Draggable set FALSE still creates a handle; constructing a draggable Panel with MUIA_Draggable before a Left title-position tag creates a horizontal handle. **Consequence:** false does not disable dragging at construction, and tag order can make the handle orientation disagree with the title. Check the Boolean and parse title position before creating the handle. **Confidence:** high for both constructor paths; no Panel object was created. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9509

**PanelGroup draws the drag marker after a panel even when the drop slot is before it.** CalculateDropPosition() counts only accepted Panel/DragHandle children and returns the current index when the pointer is above a panel's midpoint, meaning insertion before that panel (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panelgroup.c:703-730). DragReport then finds the marker position by incrementing panel_index for each child and, when it reaches new_position, sets drop_mark_y to that child's bottom plus one (panelgroup.c:765-799). The marker is therefore drawn below the target while the requested slot is before it. DragDrop uses that slot to reorder children (panelgroup.c:802-879).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** built-in PanelGroup with DragReordering enabled when a drag is reported above the midpoint of a target panel. **Consequence:** the visual marker indicates a position after the target although dropping inserts at the calculated before-target slot, which can mislead the user during reordering. For simple groups containing only Panels this off-by-side error is explicit; mixed-child groups can additionally misalign because position calculation filters children while marker placement does not. Draw before the target at its top edge when the slot is before it. **Confidence:** high for marker placement mismatch in the all-Panel case; custom mixed-child layouts add an independently identified index mismatch. No drag operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
## GD9510

**PanelGroup single-panel mode does not enforce one expanded panel at initialization or on title clicks.** OM_NEW() parses AllowMultiple and ExpandedPanel, then scans the initial Panel children; the scan records each child's current Collapsed state but does not collapse other expanded panels when AllowMultiple is FALSE (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panelgroup.c:175-235,411-441). At runtime, PanelTitle_Toggle() writes MUIA_Panel_Collapsed directly to its parent Panel (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panel.c:840-850), bypassing PanelGroup's ExpandPanel method, which is where the old expanded panel is collapsed and expanded_panel is updated (panelgroup.c:567-599).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** PanelGroup with AllowMultiple=FALSE and at least two initially expanded collapsible children, or a single-panel group in which the user expands another panel by clicking its title. **Consequence:** multiple panels can remain expanded, and title clicks can leave PanelGroup's expanded_panel and cached PanelNode state out of sync with the actual Panel attributes. Route title toggles through PanelGroup or observe each child's collapsed changes; enforce the invariant after initial scan. **Confidence:** high for the missing initialization enforcement and direct setter bypass; exact GUI result depends on initial child configuration. No PanelGroup was instantiated or clicked. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
## GD9511

**PanelGroup collapse/expand methods can update cached state before the Panel is set up, without changing the Panel itself.** SetPanelCollapsed() calls the Panel setter only when MADF_SETUP is set (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panelgroup.c:149-156). CollapsePanel() and ExpandPanel() nevertheless update the corresponding PanelNode collapsed field, mark states_current TRUE, and complete a group change when the tracked node is collapsible (panelgroup.c:515-559,567-623). Before Setup, the method can therefore report a new cached state while the Panel's MUIA_Panel_Collapsed attribute remains unchanged; the refresh path is suppressed because the cache is marked current.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** calling CollapsePanel(panel) or ExpandPanel(panel) on a tracked collapsible child before the child is set up. **Consequence:** PanelGroup state queries can report collapsed/expanded contrary to the actual Panel attribute, and later layout/setup can preserve the mismatch. Queue the requested state until Setup or update the Panel attribute even before Setup, then keep the cache synchronized. **Confidence:** high for the setup guard and unconditional cache writes; no pre-setup method call or object was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
## GD9512

**Frameadjust dereferences a failed preview-object allocation.** MakeFrameDisplay() returns the result of MUI_NewObject() without checking for NULL, then calls set() and returns that pointer (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/frameadjust.c:139-161). SetAttrsA() rejects a NULL object, so that first helper call returns safely; however, each preview loop immediately passes the result to DoMethod(obj, MUIM_Notify, ...) before OM_ADDMEMBER (frameadjust.c:257-315). The selected DoMethod macro reads OCLASS(obj) after an assertion macro that is compiled out in muimaster (`compiler/include/clib/boopsistubs.h:231-240`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/debug.h:32`), so a failed preview allocation reaches an invalid object dereference there. It does not normally reach Group insertion; Group__MUIM_AddObject() also assumes a non-NULL child, but that is a separate generic contract and not the Frameadjust failure's first crash site (group.c:250-299). Popframe creates Frameadjust as its popup editor child, making this a maintained caller path (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/popframe.c:103-123).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** built-in or separately built muimaster Frameadjust when any MakeFrameDisplay() MUI_NewObject() call fails during construction; Popframe is one selected caller. **Consequence:** construction can fault while adding the missing preview object rather than fail cleanly. Check each preview object before adding it and unwind the partially constructed group. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked result and selected Group NULL dereference; no allocation failure or object construction was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9513 (withdrawn; 2026-10-26)

**Disposition: withdrawn after caller-path recheck.** The earlier candidate said that disposing an open Popframe or Popimage through normal application teardown leaves its popup Window registered in the Application family. That path was incomplete. `Application__OM_DISPOSE()` first removes each main Window with `OM_REMMEMBER` before disposing it (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:862-870`). Family removal invokes `MUIM_DisconnectParent` before unlinking the child (`family.c:274-287`); Window disconnect propagates to its root Group, which recursively disconnects its children (`window.c:3595-3620`; `group.c:832-849`). Both popup classes handle that notification by calling their CloseWindow method, which removes the popup from the Application family before disposing it (`popframe.c:156-185`; `popimage.c:180-211`). Thus the selected normal application/window teardown path clears the popup before either owner's `OM_DISPOSE` runs. The stale-registration case requires direct disposal while the owner remains connected, which is outside the established MUI parent-removal lifecycle; no selected in-tree caller establishing that sequence was found. Removed GD9513 from the active index. No window lifecycle was run; source-only.
## GD9515

**Popscreen retains public-screen name pointers after releasing the screen-list lock.** `PopscreenStrObjFunc()` locks the public-screen list, iterates its `PubScreenNode`s, and inserts each node's `ln_Name` pointer directly into the MUI List (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/popscreen.c:34-43). The List has no construct hook, so `List__MUIM_Construct()` stores that same pointer unchanged (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:3066-3072`). This violates the List API's explicit lifetime contract: without a construct hook, string entries must continue to exist for the lifetime of the List (`list.c:318-320`). Popscreen releases the public-screen-list lock and then compares the retained names with the string gadget contents (popscreen.c:43-62); the List remains available for later popup display and selection. `CloseScreen()` obtains the same list lock before its synchronous removal path and frees the screen's `ln_Name` before releasing it (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:147-155,341-346`). Thus the list lock protects enumeration and removal, but does not extend the stored string's lifetime after Popscreen unlocks it. Another task closing a listed screen in that interval can leave an entry that later comparison, display, or selection reads after free. The maintained PSI Preferences caller uses Popscreen as its screen chooser (workbench/prefs/PSI/screenpanel_class.c:320-326).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the optional muimaster Popscreen class while a public screen is closed after the list is populated and before the List is cleared or rebuilt; the race is possible when screen management and chooser use occur concurrently. **Consequence:** later string comparison, display, or selection can use a freed screen-name string. Copy names into List-owned storage while holding the list lock, and release those copies with the List's destruct hook. **Confidence:** high for the borrowed-pointer lifetime mismatch and CloseScreen free; the concurrent interleaving was not run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9516

**Dirlist drops every entry when a custom filter hook accepts it.** In `ReadDirectory()`, the `data->filterhook` branch builds an `ExAllData` view of each `FileInfoBlock` and calls the hook. A false return skips the entry, as expected for a rejection; a true return falls out of the branch and reaches the end of the enumeration body without incrementing file/drawer counts or calling `MUIM_List_InsertSingle` (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/dirlist.c:209-225, 261-277). The common insertion code exists only in the `else` branch used when no hook is installed.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** built-in or module Dirlist when `MUIA_Dirlist_FilterHook` is set and the hook accepts one or more entries. **Consequence:** accepted entries are absent from the displayed list and the entry counters are not updated; a hook that accepts all entries yields an empty list. Move the common acceptance/count/insertion path after the hook decision. **Confidence:** high for the control flow. The maintained Printer Preferences caller does not set FilterHook; no in-tree caller was found. The hook API's external use was not exercised. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9517

**Dirlist never maintains its NumBytes attribute.** `ReadDirectory()` attempts to set `MUIA_Dirlist_NumBytes` for each accepted file to `data->numbytes + fib->fib_Size` (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/dirlist.c:266-272), but the instance field `data->numbytes` is never assigned or incremented anywhere in the class. `Dirlist__OM_SET()` has no `MUIA_Dirlist_NumBytes` case, while the public tag is declared getter-only (`..g`) (classes/dirlist.c:292-359; classes/dirlist.h:39-40). `Dirlist__OM_GET()` returns the untouched field (dirlist.c:422-424). The directory-change and reread paths attempt to reset this attribute to zero, but do not update the field either (dirlist.c:361-370, 497-510). Thus the getter does not return a directory byte total; additionally, each per-file set uses the same unchanged base instead of accumulating, so any consumer reacting to those set notifications receives individual file sizes rather than a running total.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** built-in or module Dirlist when a client reads `MUIA_Dirlist_NumBytes` or observes its updates while files are enumerated. **Consequence:** clients cannot obtain the documented byte total (the stored getter remains at its untouched initial value, ordinarily zero), and update notifications do not provide a cumulative total. Maintain the instance field by resetting it on directory changes and adding each accepted file size before publishing the attribute. **Confidence:** high for missing field updates and getter behavior; notification behavior was inferred from the SetAttrs path and not observed at runtime. The maintained Printer Preferences caller does not read NumBytes. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9518

**Bitmap cleanup can release palette pen 255 even though color allocation failed.** During indexed-color remapping, `ObtainBestPenA()` may return -1 when no matching or free pen is available. The result is stored after bit 8 is set as a cache marker (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bitmap.c:179-193`), making the cache entry nonzero. Cleanup interprets every nonzero entry as an acquired pen and calls `ReleasePen()` with its low byte (`bitmap.c:473-484`), which is 255 for the failed result. `ObtainBestPenA()`'s failure return is -1 (`rom/graphics/obtainbestpena.c:119-148`); ReleasePen then acts on the supplied color-map index (`rom/graphics/releasepen.c:57-80,147-155`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Bitmap palette remapping on a screen whose ColorMap cannot supply a best pen for a source color, followed by Cleanup, with pen index 255 in range for that ColorMap. **Consequence:** cleanup can release or decrement ownership of pen 255 despite never acquiring it for this bitmap, potentially affecting another user's pen allocation. Preserve a distinct failure sentinel in the cache and release only successful acquisitions. **Confidence:** high for the -1 encoding and unmatched release; the effect on another owner's allocation depends on ColorMap state. Palette exhaustion and cleanup were not run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9519

**Bitmap ignores replacement source bitmaps while an indexed remap is active.** `MUIA_Bitmap_Bitmap` is declared settable/gettable (`isg`; workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bitmap.h:17-18), but `Bitmap__OM_SET()` assigns the new bitmap only when `data->remapped_bm` is NULL (classes/bitmap.c:347-352). While setup has produced a remapped bitmap, setting the public source attribute is silently ignored; `OM_GET` continues returning the old `data->bm` (bitmap.c:399-401). Cleanup frees the remapped output, but does not apply or retain a deferred replacement (bitmap.c:467-471), so a subsequent setup remaps the old source again. The maintained Bodychunk and ChunkyImage subclasses set or clear the inherited source around their own setup/cleanup paths, so this report scopes the defect to direct callers updating the public Bitmap source while remapping is active (bodychunk.c:336-371; chunkyimage.c:244-290).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** muimaster Bitmap when indexed remapping has created `remapped_bm` and a client calls `SetAttrs()` with a replacement `MUIA_Bitmap_Bitmap` before Cleanup. **Consequence:** the new source is discarded without notification or deferred application, leaving the old image visible after later setup. Accept the new pointer and invalidate/rebuild the remapped output safely, or explicitly document the attribute as immutable while setup. **Confidence:** high for the guarded assignment and lost update; no direct in-tree live-update caller was found. No object was set up or changed. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9520

**Indexed summary:** A new async layout can start during worker shutdown and have its live-process flag cleared by the previous worker.

**Status:** New source-revalidated candidate; medium-high confidence. The interleaving follows from the helper's lock/flag ordering; no concurrent schedule was induced.

**Trigger and interleaving:** Worker A clears `DTSIF_LAYOUT` while holding `SEM_ASYNC` and clears `DTA_LayoutProc`, then releases the global semaphore and object lock. Before it clears `DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC`, a second `DoAsyncLayout()` call can see the layout bit clear and take the new-worker branch. It sets both flags, creates worker B, and publishes B's process pointer. A then reaches its unconditional `DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC` clear under `Forbid()`, erasing the marker for B, which may be active or waiting on the object's `si_Lock` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/doasynclayout.c:58-100,152-213`).

The flag publication for B is protected by `SEM_ASYNC`, but A clears the completion flag after releasing that semaphore. On a single-CPU build, a task switch before A enters `Forbid()` is enough for B to publish its flags; on ExecSMP, `Forbid()` is processor-local and does not serialize the two tasks (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-59`).

**Consequence:** `RemoveDTObject()` and `DisposeDTObject()` wait only while `DTSIF_LAYOUTPROC` is set (`workbench/libs/datatypes/removedtobject.c:68-79`; `disposedtobject.c:53-66`). Once A clears the bit, either can remove or dispose the object while B still holds or will use its pointer. This can cause use-after-dispose and asynchronous task failure.

**Affected configuration and caller:** the shared DataTypes library helper and the ASCII, binary, HTML and picture subclass `GM_LAYOUT` handlers, which are the only active checked-in C callers found (`workbench/classes/datatypes/{ascii/asciiclass.c:179,binary/binaryclass.c:189,html/htmlclass.c:371,picture/pictureclass.c:856}`). A repository-wide search also found a disabled direct call in MultiView, its generated m68k emulator thunk, the public vector declaration and a README mention; none adds another active C caller. MultiView reaches the helper indirectly: its Word Wrap menu handler calls `DoLayout(TRUE)` (`workbench/utilities/MultiView/main.c:1681-1693`), and the active `DoLayout()` dispatches `GM_LAYOUT` to the datatype object (`misc.c:593-617`), which the selected subclass can translate into `DoAsyncLayout()`. The helper returns after queueing its worker, while MultiView continues its event loop (`doasynclayout.c:201-218`; `main.c:1299-1306,1770-1772`). Exact module/package inclusion varies by target.

**Remaining checks:** external callers through the public vector, notification reentrancy, and platform scheduler behavior. The checked-in caller census is complete for active C references. Source-only; no build or runtime interleaving was run.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3191`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3191), [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L3196`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3196).

## GD9521

**Indexed summary:** G.72x WAV decoders left-shift negative signed PCM values.

**Source and trigger:** The four selected G.721/G.723 decoder functions return reconstructed samples with `sr << 2` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/wav/g72x/g721.c:143-149`; `g723_16.c:155-161`; `g723_24.c:127-133`; `g723_40.c:147-153`). The reconstruction can be negative when the codeword sign bit is set (`g721.c:141-144`, corresponding `reconstruct(i & signbit, ...)` paths in the other decoders). `sr` is promoted to signed `int` before the shift.

**Consequence and scope:** Left-shifting a negative signed value is undefined in C, even when the resulting mathematical value would fit in `int`. A compiler may therefore generate output that does not preserve valid negative PCM samples. This affects optional WAV G.72x decoding for ordinary negative-valued samples; exact misbehavior depends on compiler optimization and target semantics.
