High confidence in the source-level undefined operation and reachable negative values; no decode or compiler behavior was exercised.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1939`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1939).

## GD9522

**Indexed summary:** WAV IEEE-float decoding converts unbounded samples to signed bytes.

**Source and trigger:** The selected 32-bit and 64-bit float decoders read each sample and directly convert `samp.f * 127.0` to `BYTE`, without checking finiteness or range (`workbench/classes/datatypes/wav/wave_ieee_float.c:28-53`). A malformed float WAV containing a NaN, infinity, or finite sample whose scaled value is outside the representable `BYTE` range reaches this conversion.

**Consequence and scope:** C defines floating-to-integer conversion as undefined when the truncated value cannot be represented in the destination type. The decoder can therefore produce compiler-dependent output for such accepted file contents; no validated sample range prevents this path. Applies to optional IEEE-float WAV decoding of out-of-range or non-finite samples. High confidence in the unchecked conversion and language rule; no malformed file or compiler behavior was exercised.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1939`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1939).


## GD9523

**Indexed summary:** Text datatype dereferences its font after initialization failure.

**Source and trigger:** The selected Text datatype's `_OM_NEW()` calls `InitText(td)` and ignores its return (`workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:2238`). `InitText()` can return zero if it cannot copy the default/requested font name or if both the requested font and the `topaz.font` fallback fail to open (`:246-299`). `_OM_NEW()` immediately dereferences `td->font->tf_YSize` and later reads `tf_Flags`/`tf_XSize` (`:2243-2244`). A failed name allocation or unavailable font/fallback therefore reaches a NULL font dereference during normal object construction.

**Consequence and scope:** Construction can fault instead of failing cleanly when the selected `text.datatype` cannot establish either font. The path also applies to subclasses that construct the Text superclass, including `ascii.datatype`. High confidence in the unchecked return and dereference; the failure combination is conditional. No font failure or object construction was induced.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Text datatype full-body pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9524

**Indexed summary:** Text datatype treats a short FTXT CHRS read as complete.

**Source and trigger:** `LoadTextAsIFF()` sets `buffer_allocated_len` to `pre_size + add_size`, then ignores the result of `ReadChunkBytes()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/text/textclass.c:382-390`). The selected `ReadChunkBytes()` contract returns the actual byte count, which can be short, or a negative IFF error (`workbench/libs/iffparse/readchunkbytes.c:29-52,61-85`). On such a read result, the loader still returns success with the declared length; the allocation is not cleared, so unread bytes are left uninitialized and reported as valid text.

**Consequence and scope:** A truncated or failed CHRS stream can publish partially initialized contents as a successful Text datatype object. Applies to selected FTXT loads, including clipboard loading. High confidence in the unchecked result and length publication; occurrence depends on a short/error stream read. No IFF input was processed.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Text datatype full-body pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9525

**Indexed summary:** Graphics `Text()` leaves the pen unchanged on renderer prerequisite failure.

**Source and trigger:** The Graphics `Text()` autodoc says the current position advances to the position after the text (`rom/graphics/text.c:34-37`). Its antialias renderer returns before the final `Move()` if `OpenLibrary("cybergraphics.library", 0)` fails (`:401-414,553`); its color-font renderer likewise returns if `ExtendFont()` fails (`:559-569,752`). `Text()` dispatches directly to either renderer for matching fonts/depths (`:70-88`).

**Consequence and scope:** Calls using an antialias font on a 15-bit-or-deeper bitmap without the optional CyberGraphX library, or a color font whose extension cannot be established, leave the RastPort cursor at its old position despite the documented API behavior. Medium-high confidence in the source contract mismatch; no library/font failure was induced.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Graphics `Text()` full-body pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9526

**Indexed summary:** DataTypes dereferences a NULL name when a file handle is supplied without a name.

**Source and trigger:** `NewDTObjectA()` documents `DTA_Handle` as usable instead of the `name` argument (`workbench/libs/datatypes/newdtobjecta.c:47-49`). When a file handle is supplied and `name == NULL`, it detects the datatype from that handle and forwards `DTA_Name = name` in the tags used to construct the datatype object (`:159-165,273-275,303-314`). The generic datatype dispatcher finds that tag, then calls `strlen()` on its value for `DTST_FILE` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/class.c:445-456`). Thus a documented handle-only file construction reaches `strlen(NULL)` before the datatype class can use the supplied handle.

**Consequence and scope:** `NewDTObjectA(NULL, DTA_Handle, fileHandle, ...)` can fault during construction instead of creating the object. Applies to file-backed datatype classes using the generic DataTypes dispatcher. High confidence in the direct API-to-dispatch path; no object construction was run.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), DataTypes `newdtobjecta.c` and `class.c` full-body passes dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9527

**Indexed summary:** DataTypes library expunge does not close its message catalog.

**Source and trigger:** `datatypes.library` opens `Sys/libs.catalog` during initialization (`workbench/libs/datatypes/datatypes_init.c:52-61`) and retries on library open if the field is NULL (`:69-85`). Its expunge hook only calls `TryRemoveClass()` (`:93-102`); no path closes `dtb_LibsCatalog`. The locale contract says `CloseCatalog()` decrements the catalog use count and frees/removes it at zero (`workbench/libs/locale/closecatalog.c:25-28,56-69`). After a successful datatype-library initialization and eventual expunge, its catalog reference therefore remains outstanding. Repeated load/expunge cycles can retain another catalog reference each time.

**Consequence and scope:** The locale catalog remains retained after the library that opened it has been expunged, preventing normal catalog cleanup and leaking its associated catalog allocation. Applies when datatypes.library opens a catalog and later expunges; catalog-open failure does not trigger the leak for that cycle. High confidence from the matched open/close ownership contract. No library expunge or catalog operation was run.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), DataTypes library initialization/expunge lifecycle pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9528

**Indexed summary:** DataTypes print-start failures leave the object permanently marked as printing.

**Source and trigger:** `PrintDTObjectA()` sets `DTSIF_PRINTING` before allocating its `PrintMessage` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/printdtobjecta.c:174-181`). If that allocation fails, the function skips the worker-start block and returns `FALSE` without clearing the flag. If `CreateNewProc()` fails, it frees the message but likewise leaves the flag set (`:194-215`). The only clear is at the end of the successfully started `AsyncPrinter()` (`:109-113`). `DisposeDTObject()` waits in a loop while `DTSIF_PRINTING` is set (`workbench/libs/datatypes/disposedtobject.c:53-66`).

**Consequence and scope:** After either allocation or process-creation failure, later print attempts remain rejected and `DisposeDTObject()` can wait forever for a worker that was never started. Applies to calls using `PrintDTObjectA()` when its message allocation or worker creation fails. High confidence in both missing cleanup paths and the disposal wait; no allocation failure or process creation was induced.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), PrintDTObjectA full-body and DisposeDTObject caller pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9529

**Indexed summary:** DataTypes method-table copy underallocates when an existing excluded method is repeated.

**Source and trigger:** Both selected copy helpers subtract one from the unsigned output count for every exclusion entry that matches the source table (`workbench/libs/datatypes/copydtmethods.c:79-91`; `copydttriggermethods.c:86-101`). During copying, however, the source-method loop filters each source entry once if it appears anywhere in the exclusion table (`copydtmethods.c:109-118`; `copydttriggermethods.c:119-128`). For a terminated source table containing methods A and B and a terminated exclude table containing A twice, the count is reduced twice but only A is removed once: the calculated allocation holds one entry, while the output writes B and then its terminator. The API documentation does not require exclusion entries to be unique.

**Consequence and scope:** A redundant exclusion list containing a method present in the source table can cause the helper to write the copied method-table terminator past its allocation. This affects `CopyDTMethods()` and `CopyDTTriggerMethods()` in the selected `datatypes.library`; the only checked-in `CopyDTMethods()` caller passes no exclude list, and no checked-in caller of `CopyDTTriggerMethods()` was found, so the triggering inputs are external subclass-implementor calls. High confidence in the count/copy mismatch for valid terminated lists with duplicate exclusions; no allocation or copy was run.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), method-copy helper pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9530

**Indexed summary:** LaunchToolA closes or leaks its shell-output handle on the wrong SystemTagList paths.

**Source and trigger:** `LaunchToolA()` opens a `CON:` output handle and passes it as `SYS_Output` with `SYS_Asynch = !NP_Synchronous` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/launchtoola.c:101-127`). In the default asynchronous case, `SystemTagList()` starts the shell and returns before its command finishes, but `LaunchToolA()` immediately calls `Close(output)` (`:135`). `SystemTagList()` passes the same handle into the child CLI (`rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:149-150,441-445`; `rom/dos/newcliproc.c:171-173,235-240`) and documents that asynchronous input/output handles are closed when the command finishes (`systemtaglist.c:84-86`). The launcher's close can therefore invalidate the child's still-active output. Separately, if `SystemTagList()` returns -1 because shell creation fails, `LaunchToolA()` returns at `:130-132` without closing the handle it opened.

**Consequence and scope:** Default asynchronous shell launches can lose their output stream before the command completes; failed shell startup leaks the opened console handle. Applies to selected `datatypes.library` `LaunchToolA()` calls for `TF_SHELL` tools, with the early-close path limited to asynchronous launches. The checked-in tree has no direct LaunchToolA caller beyond its public helper relationship; external datatype/tool clients supply the call. High confidence in the handle transfer and branch cleanup mismatch; no tool or shell was launched.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), LaunchToolA/SystemTagList handle-ownership pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9531

**MUI nested clip registration ignores region-intersection allocation failure, allowing drawing outside an outer virtual-group clip.** When `mri_rCount` is nonzero, `MUI_AddClipRegion()` intersects the previously installed MUI region into the new region but ignores the Boolean result (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_addclipregion.c:66-68`). `AndRegionRegion()` builds the intersection in a temporary region and returns FALSE if that construction fails, without replacing or clearing its second input (`rom/graphics/andregionregion.c:56-87`). The caller then installs the un-intersected inner region on the layer and pushes it onto the clip stack (`mui_addclipregion.c:81-95`). `InstallClipRegion()` replaces `l->ClipRegion`; its internal conversion intersects the supplied region with `VisibleRegion` and `shape`, but not with the previous MUI clip (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:1414-1436`).

The nested call is reachable in normal MUI virtual-group drawing: `MUI_Redraw()` builds and registers a clip for virtual-group ancestors (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_redraw.c:58-97`), then a virtual `Group__MUIM_Draw()` registers its child clip and redraws descendants using the same window `MUI_RenderInfo` (`classes/group.c:1334-1387`; the group propagates `MADF_INVIRTUALGROUP` to its children at `:266-278,811-824`). If the inner region is not contained in the outer clip and the intersection allocation fails, descendants draw with only the inner region and can paint beyond the ancestor's clip until `MUI_RemoveClipRegion()` restores the prior stack entry. Check the intersection result and abort clip installation while preserving the existing clip on failure. `MUI_AddClipping()` constructs a rectangular region and forwards it to the same helper (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_addclipping.c:47-73`), so nested rectangle clips share the failure behavior. The in-tree stack uses both APIs from Group, Area, Register, FrameDisplay, ImageDisplay, List and Text; the virtual-group redraw path above establishes a concrete nested caller. `MUI_RemoveClipRegion()` and its `MUI_RemoveClipping()` wrapper ignore the `(APTR)-1` failure sentinel, so failed registration does not itself unbalance the stack; the Area rounded-frame double-dispose on this sentinel is separately tracked as GD9423.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** explicit `workbench-libs-muimaster` builds (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:112,433-439`), during nested region or rectangle clipping when the intersection needs memory and that allocation fails. The module is not selected by its parent aggregate in this tree. **Confidence:** high for the ignored failure, unchanged inner region, layer clip replacement and nested caller path; visible overdraw additionally requires the inner clip to extend beyond the outer clip. No allocation failure or GUI draw was induced; source-only.


## GD9532

**Graphics `Text()` fast-font renderer uses a negative raster stride for long valid strings (high source confidence).** `Text()` accepts a signed `WORD` character count and forwards positive counts to `BltTemplateBasedText()` (`rom/graphics/text.c:31-39,70-88`). For an unstyled 8-pixel font with zero `TxSpacing`, the fast-font path computes `te.te_Width = len * 8` in a `UWORD` and stores the last pixel in the signed-WORD `Rectangle` (`:111-145`; `TextExtent` layout at `compiler/include/graphics/text.h:162-168`). At `count == 4096`, the width is 32768: `te_Extent.MaxX` is 32767, but the subsequent raster-width assignment narrows 32768 to signed `WORD` -32768. Rounding and division then produce `raswidth_bpr == -4096` (`text.c:149-154`).

The renderer allocates the raster using that narrowed width (`:156-162`; `AllocRaster()` feeds it to `RASSIZE()` and `AllocMem()` at `rom/graphics/allocraster.c:54`). In the fast path, each glyph batch computes each scanline as `dst + y * raswidth_bpr` and writes glyph bytes there (`text.c:173-225`). With a normal multi-row font, scanline 1 therefore starts 4096 bytes before the returned raster pointer; later scanlines move farther backward. That is an out-of-bounds write relative to either the allocated raster or a sufficiently large `TmpRas`. At still larger counts the UWORD width itself wraps, producing zero or otherwise incorrect geometry and stride.

**Trigger and consequence:** call the public Graphics `Text()` API with at least 4096 characters, using a fixed 8-pixel font whose glyphs satisfy the fast-path test, no bold/italic style, and zero text spacing. The API documentation places no smaller count limit (`text.c:41-48`). The raster builder writes before the returned buffer and then passes invalid dimensions/stride to `BltTemplate()`, risking memory corruption and incorrect rendering; the final `Move()` also uses the wrapped UWORD text width. The in-tree census found ordinary short Text calls but no call at this boundary; the public API remains directly callable by clients. **Affected configuration:** Graphics library's generic Text renderer when the fast-font predicate applies. **Confidence:** high for narrowing, negative stride and out-of-bounds row address on targets where `WORD` is signed 16-bit (the declared ABI type); no runtime was used to observe allocator behavior. No text was rendered; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Graphics `Text()` full-body and caller pass dated 2026-10-24, plus the 2026-10-24 long-fast-font boundary recheck.


## GD9533

**`ScaleLayer()` discards its existing layer bitmap when replacement allocation fails.** `ScaleLayerCallback()` initializes `bm` to NULL, calls `AllocBitMap()` for the replacement, and never checks the result before passing it to `BitMapScale()` (`rom/hyperlayers/scalelayer.c:104-121,137-151`). `BitMapScale()` explicitly returns without scaling when its destination bitmap is NULL (`rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c:103-104`). The callback then frees the layer's current ClipRect bitmap and installs `bm`, which is still NULL (`scalelayer.c:147-156`). It returns the existing non-NULL shape region, so `ChangeLayerShape()` treats the callback as accepted and proceeds (`rom/hyperlayers/changelayershape.c:100-118`). The layer is left with no backing bitmap after the operation has replaced its previous one. Check the allocation and preserve the old bitmap if it fails.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected `layers.library` `ScaleLayer()` vector (`rom/hyperlayers/mmakefile.src:44`; packaged in `rom/mmakefile.src:140,146-149`) called for a layer with one ClipRect when the destination `AllocBitMap()` fails. The checked-in optional `developer/demos/winshape.c:197,206` is the only direct caller found; external clients may call the public vector. **Consequence:** the layer loses its existing backing bitmap and subsequent drawing or refresh operations cannot use the expected raster. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked NULL allocation, no-op `BitMapScale()` guard, unconditional free/replacement, and accepted callback result; follow-on rendering behavior depends on the caller and layer state. No allocation failure or layer operation was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L457), ScaleLayer full-body and `ChangeLayerShape()` callback pass.


## GD9534

**MUI redraw continues without virtual-ancestor clipping when region allocation fails.** `MUI_Redraw()` starts with no temporary clip and, for an object marked `MADF_INVIRTUALGROUP`, allocates a region with `NewRegion()` for each virtual-group ancestor (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_redraw.c:53-99`). When `NewRegion()` returns NULL, the code leaves `region` NULL and continues; if no later ancestor allocation succeeds, it never calls `MUI_AddClipRegion()`. It nevertheless continues to set the object's ordinary clip rectangle and invokes `MUIM_Draw` (`:101-137`). `NewRegion()` returns NULL when its `AllocMem()` fails (`rom/graphics/newregion.c:63-75`). The same loop can also install only an outer ancestor region if allocation for a nearer virtual ancestor fails but a later `NewRegion()` succeeds.

The selected `change_active_page()` helper calls `MUI_Redraw(obj, MADF_DRAWUPDATE)` after changing and showing a page-mode group (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:163-213`). The selected Group class directly supports `MUIA_Group_Virtual` and marks such a group `MADF_ISVIRTUALGROUP` (`group.c:409-428`; `group.h:106-107`); a virtual parent marks its child `MADF_INVIRTUALGROUP` when adding or connecting it (`group.c:269-278,812-824`). Thus a client can place a page-mode group beneath a virtual group and take this redraw path without the separate `Virtgroup.mui` class. I found maintained uses of virtual groups and active-page changes, but no maintained application source that establishes this exact nested combination; that application-level reachability remains conditional on client layout. If the nearest virtual ancestor is omitted, the nested group's drawing proceeds with only the current layer/window clip; content extending beyond the virtual ancestor's rectangle can be painted outside that group. The code continues drawing instead of reporting or skipping the clipped redraw.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `mui_redraw.c` is selected by `workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:110-129,433-439`; `workbench-libs-muimaster` is included in the active `workbench-libs-complete` aggregate selected by the complete AROS Workbench target (`workbench/libs/mmakefile:9-23,43`; `workbench/mmakefile.src:7-21`). Triggered by a redraw of a virtual-group descendant when its ancestor `NewRegion()` allocation fails (and no later successful region includes that bound), with drawable content beyond the omitted ancestor rectangle. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked NULL result, skipped clip installation and continued draw; visible overdraw depends on the object content and other active layer clipping. No allocation failure or redraw was induced; source-only. This is distinct from GD9531, where a region exists but `MUI_AddClipRegion()` ignores a failed intersection.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI redraw full-body/virtual-ancestor clipping pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9535

**Wanderer AppIcon refresh passes a failed DiskObject duplicate to `LayoutIconA()` (conditional NULL dereference).** When an AppIcon has no existing `IconEntry`, `IconVolumeList` obtains its source DiskObject, duplicates it, and immediately calls `LayoutIconA()` without checking the duplicate (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow_volumelist.c:949-956`). `DupDiskObjectA()` returns NULL if `NewDiskObject()` fails (`workbench/libs/icon/dupdiskobject.c:143-147`), and it also returns NULL after a later duplication allocation failure through its cleanup path (`:170-210,258-308`). The selected `LayoutIconA()` implementation reads `icon->do_Gadget.MutualExclude` before any null check (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:71-84`), so the failed duplicate is dereferenced before IconList's later constructor can reject the NULL `entry_dob`.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** A build/runtime that includes the explicit `workbench-libs-icon` target and the selected Wanderer `IconVolumeList` AppIcon refresh; the failure requires a valid source DiskObject and `DupDiskObject()` to fail while allocating its copy. The selected AArch64 Raspberry Pi package manifest lists `icon` among `PKG_LIBS` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:213`); this does not claim every default Workbench package includes the Wanderer executable. **Consequence:** the refresh faults at `LayoutIconA(NULL, ...)` rather than retaining/skipping the icon or handling allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the NULL-return contract and immediate dereference; occurrence requires the duplicate operation to fail. No AppIcon refresh or allocation failure was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), IconList DiskObject ownership and AppIcon refresh caller pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9536

**`LayoutIconA()` leaves partial screen-layout resources behind when allocation fails.** The routine first tears down the old mapping and sets `ni->ni_Screen = NULL` (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:99-129`), then builds the two image states and publishes the new screen only after both complete (`:206-248,474`). Several later allocation failures return or jump to `exit` without releasing already-built image state: a bitmap failure on the second image can follow a completed first image (`:242-248`); pen-map allocation failure leaves the current bitmap allocated (`:315-323`); temporary chunky-buffer failure frees the current bitmap but leaves the pen map and acquired screen pens (`:325-352`); and transparent-mask allocation failure occurs after bitmap, pen, and chunky-buffer setup (`:363-374`). The common exit only frees `DrawInfo`; the mask-failure branch returns directly and skips even that (`:370-373,476-482`). The dynamic fields are explicitly outside the icon's `FreeList` (`workbench/libs/icon/icon_intern.h:121-129`), but `FreeDiskObject()` tries to release them by calling `LayoutIconA(icon, NULL, NULL)` before freeing that list (`workbench/libs/icon/freediskobject.c:54-67`). Several checked-in callers ignore the `LayoutIconA()` BOOL failure. `GetIconTagList()` returns its icon after calling `LayoutIconA()` and then sets both `IoErr()` and the optional `ICONGETA_ErrorCode` from its unchanged local `error` value (`workbench/libs/icon/geticontaglist.c:345-355`), masking the layout allocation error; `DupDiskObjectA()` returns the duplicate even when image-data activation layout fails (`workbench/libs/icon/dupdiskobject.c:300-307`). Wanderer’s volume-list update duplicates an AppIcon, ignores `LayoutIconA()` failure, and passes the partial duplicate to `MUIM_IconList_CreateEntry` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow_volumelist.c:949-957`). BoingIconBar's `ReadPrefs()` ignores `LayoutIcon()` failure and still marks the icon loaded (`workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/iconbar.c:816-852`); with remapping enabled, `OpenMainWindow()` calls `LayoutIcon()` again before opening its window (`:1497-1505`). Zune's IconImage class ignores the result in both `MUIM_AskMinMax()` and `MUIM_Draw()` and continues to query geometry or draw (`workbench/classes/zune/iconimage/iconimage.c:84-114,117-147`). The icon render debug test checks the result (`developer/debug/test/icon/render.c:48-76`). These production callers can hand out partial state; the later `FreeDiskObject()` cleanup is the concrete leak path. Since NULL already equals `ni->ni_Screen`, cleanup returns at `layouticon.c:96-97` without freeing the partial allocations or acquired pens. A retry with a non-NULL screen instead enters cleanup and evaluates `ni->ni_Screen->ViewPort.ColorMap` while `ni->ni_Screen` is NULL if a partial image has a pen map (`:96-117`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `icon.library` clients laying out palette-mapped icons when an allocation fails after layout setup has started; the mask case additionally requires `TransparentColor >= 0`. Checked-in callers include Workbench Wanderer, BoingIconBar and Zune IconImage paths described above; no particular client is required for the library cleanup leak. **Consequence:** disposing a failed layout can leak screen-specific bitmaps, pen maps, obtained pens, and (for mask allocation failure) the `DrawInfo`; retrying after a partial state with pens dereferences the NULL saved screen while trying to release a pen. **Confidence:** high for the missing rollback and resulting retained resources; high for the retry dereference when a partially built image has a pen map. This is separate from GD9535's unchecked duplicate passed into `LayoutIconA()`. No allocation failure or icon layout was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Icon library duplication/layout full-body and failure-cleanup pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9644

**`LayoutIconA()` retains a freed scaled ARGB buffer across an unmap/remap cycle.** When a high-color screen uses an icon's ARGB image and scaling is needed, `LayoutIconA()` allocates a separate destination in `image->ARGBMap` (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:221-229`). On a later call for a different screen, its cleanup frees `ARGBMap` when it differs from the source `ARGB`, but does not clear the field (`:107-109`). An unmap call with `screen == NULL` then sets `ni->ni_Screen` to NULL and returns (`:127-131`). A subsequent layout to a non-NULL screen does not take the same-screen early return and tries to free the stale `ARGBMap` again before rebuilding the image (`:94-109`). More directly, when the new screen is 8-bit or lower, layout skips the ARGB path and successfully builds the bitmap representation but leaves the stale field non-NULL (`:217-243,474`). `DrawIconStateA()` then tests only that field and passes it to `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` (`workbench/libs/icon/drawiconstate.c:169-176`); the selected Wanderer icon-list renderer calls `DrawIconStateA()` for displayed entries (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Classes/iconlist.c:1185-1193`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `icon.library` clients using a scaled ARGB image on a high-color screen, followed by `LayoutIconA(icon, NULL, NULL)` and then another layout of the same icon to a screen. **Consequence:** the next draw after remapping to an 8-bit-or-lower screen supplies freed memory to `WritePixelArrayAlpha()`; a later remap can also pass the stale pointer to `FreeVec()` again. These use-after-free/double-free paths can fault or corrupt memory. **Confidence:** high for the stale pointer and selected drawing/double-free paths; occurrence requires a dynamically scaled ARGB image followed by a screen transition, with the immediate drawing path specifically applying to a destination screen of depth 8 or less. No icon layout or allocator behavior was run; source-only. This is distinct from GD9536's failure rollback problem.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Icon ARGB unmap/remap ownership recheck dated 2026-10-25.


## GD9537

**`GetIconTagList()` leaves `ICONGETA_IsDefaultIcon` false when it returns a fallback default tool icon.** The output is initialized to FALSE when the tag is parsed (`workbench/libs/icon/geticontaglist.c:106-109`). On an unavailable icon with `ICONGETA_FailIfUnavailable=FALSE`, the identify fallback can return a type default: for an executable file, `FindDefaultIcon()` obtains the `WBTOOL` default and forces that type (`workbench/libs/icon/geticontaglist.c:214-216`; `workbench/libs/icon/identify.c:498-524`). This returns to the outer `GetIconTagList()` call without updating its output flag. Other generic fallback branches also return a built-in icon without setting the flag (`geticontaglist.c:302-310`). The routine's own tag documentation says the output indicates whether the returned icon is a default (`:43-45`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `icon.library`'s selected `GetIconTagList()` path when a named executable has no usable `.info` icon, the caller sets `ICONGETA_FailIfUnavailable=FALSE` and requests `ICONGETA_IsDefaultIcon`, and the identify fallback supplies the system `WBTOOL` icon. The selected `OpenWorkbenchObjectA()` caller uses both tags and passes the result to `HandleTool()` (`workbench/libs/workbench/openworkbenchobjecta.c:73-79,97-109`). Because the stale value is FALSE, `HandleTool()` can take its Workbench-program branch when the fallback icon has no `CLI` tooltype; a true default-icon result takes the CLI branch (`:621-630,688-696`). **Consequence:** the output tag lies about the returned icon and the selected caller can dispatch an executable through the wrong launch path. **Confidence:** high for the output-flag mismatch; medium for the user-visible launch difference, which depends on the fallback icon's tooltypes and the program's launch behavior. No icon lookup or program launch was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), GetIconTagList full-body and selected Workbench launcher caller pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9538

**`FindDeviceName()` ignores its output capacity when copying a DOS device name.** The selected caller supplies a 108-byte stack buffer and passes its size (`workbench/libs/icon/identify.c:418-425`). `__FindDeviceName_WB()` receives that `length` parameter but never checks it: after matching the root lock's handler task to a device entry, it copies the full BSTR name, then appends a colon and NUL (`:659-684`). A 107-byte device name already places the terminator one byte beyond the 108-byte buffer; longer names also overrun during the copy. The DOS `MakeDosEntry()` implementation accepts the full C string length and stores its BSTR length up to 255, without imposing the 106-character limit needed by this caller (`rom/dos/makedosentry.c:55-80`). `AddDosEntry()` checks duplicate names but does not impose a shorter length bound (`rom/dos/adddosentry.c:88-115`), so a DOS client can install a 107-byte-or-longer device name through the public entry path.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `icon.library`'s root-volume identification path when a device entry has a name longer than 106 bytes and its handler task matches the root lock. **Consequence:** copying the device name and suffix exceeds the caller's stack buffer, potentially corrupting adjacent stack data or disrupting icon lookup. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked copy and buffer-size mismatch; medium for occurrence in ordinary system configurations because it requires a long device entry name. No long device name or icon lookup was created or run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), Icon identification full-body and DOS device-name bound pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9539

**The OS 3.5 icon reader does not validate raw image and palette lengths before copying.** `ReadImage35()` allocates and reads exactly `imgsize + palsize` bytes from the `IMAG` chunk (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobj35io.c:285-305`). For raw image format zero it copies `imagew * imageh` bytes without checking that `imgsize` contains that many image bytes (`:318-325`); if the pixel count exceeds the total allocated extent, this reads past the source buffer, and if it falls between `imgsize` and `imgsize + palsize`, palette bytes are consumed as image data. For a raw palette (`HASPALETTE` and `PaletteFormat == 0`), it reads three bytes for each of `numcols` entries without checking that `palsize >= 3 * numcols` (`:332-353`), so a short palette extent makes the loop read beyond the allocated source buffer. The corresponding image dimensions are derived from the file's FACE bytes and can be as large as 256 by 256; the two declared payload sizes are independently file-controlled 16-bit values.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `icon.library`'s OS 3.5 `IMAG` reader for a chunk whose declared image or palette byte count is smaller than the amount the raw-format decoder consumes. The selected `ReadIcon()` path reaches this reader through `ReadIcon35()` (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:279-293`; `diskobjio.c:966-996`). **Consequence:** the parser reads past its allocated chunk-data buffer, and may use unrelated adjacent bytes as image or palette data. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked extents and read sizes; the trigger requires a malformed or inconsistent icon chunk. No icon file was loaded; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), OS 3.5 icon reader full-body and declared-payload extent pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9540

**The OS 3.5 icon reader accepts failed RLE decoding and can publish a missing palette.** `Decode35()` reports an error when the stream does not produce the requested number of entries (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobj35io.c:124-173`), but `ReadImage35()` ignores that result for compressed image data (`:322-330`). Its image buffer is allocated without clearing, so a short decode can still be published with unwritten bytes. For compressed palette data, the reader notices the decode error but sets `imgpal` to NULL and continues to return TRUE (`:355-396`). `ReadIcon35()` then publishes the image and its positive pen count (`:581-610`). The selected loader subsequently calls `LayoutIconA()`, whose palette conversion dereferences `image->Palette[j]` without a NULL check (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:315-336`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** an OS 3.5 icon `IMAG` chunk with nonzero image/palette encoding and an incomplete or invalid RLE stream; the null-palette crash specifically requires a compressed palette decode error and later palette layout. **Consequence:** incomplete image contents may be accepted as complete, while a failed palette decode can make normal icon layout dereference a NULL palette. **Confidence:** high for ignored image decode status and the NULL-palette publication/use path; the trigger requires malformed or truncated compressed icon data. No icon file or layout was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), OS 3.5 icon reader full-body and decoder-result propagation pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9541

**The OS 3.5 icon RLE decoder uses the file-supplied depth in unchecked shifts.** `ReadImage35()` passes the `Depth` byte from the `IMAG` chunk directly to `Decode35()` for every nonzero image format (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobj35io.c:40-50,322-329`). The decoder evaluates `(1 << bits) - 1` without validating the depth (`:124-130`). On AROS targets with 32-bit `int`, depth 32 or higher uses a shift count at least the type width, which is undefined behavior. (Depth 31 has implementation-defined signed-shift behavior and is not included in this undefined-behavior claim.) `WriteImage35()` emits depth 8, but the read path does not enforce that value or another supported maximum.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** OS 3.5 icon reading on AROS targets with 32-bit `int`, for a non-raw image format whose `Depth` field is at least 32. **Consequence:** undefined arithmetic behavior occurs during decoding; no further result is inferred. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked file-controlled shift; the trigger is outside the writer's emitted depth and requires malformed or nonconforming input. No icon file was loaded; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), OS 3.5 icon reader full-body and file-depth shift pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9542

**NewIcon decoding does not check pixel indices against the declared palette size.** `ReadImageNI()` derives a bit width large enough to encode `numcols` (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjNIio.c:174-184`), and stores `numcols` as the number of palette pens (`:174-180`). For palette sizes that are not powers of two, the selected bit width has spare values; for example, three colors use two bits, which can decode value 3. `DecodeNI()` writes each decoded value without checking it against `entries` or the palette count (`:105-113`). The selected `LayoutIconA()` caller later indexes the pen map with each image byte (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:353-355`), where the map has only `image->Pens` entries (`:315-317`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** NewIcon-enabled `icon.library` reading and later layout of an icon whose palette count is not a power of two and whose decoded pixel data contains an unused index value at least `numcols`. The global NewIcon support flag is enabled by default (`workbench/libs/icon/icon_init.c:50`); the classic parser's `ProcessIconNI` hook calls `ReadIconNI()` (`diskobjio.c:1003-1033`). **Consequence:** palette remapping reads beyond the allocated pen-map entries and can select an unrelated pen value. **Confidence:** high for the missing range check and caller indexing; the trigger requires inconsistent NewIcon pixel data. No icon file or layout was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), NewIcon reader full-body and decoded palette-index bound pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9543

**PNG icon loading gives libpng an unlimited memory extent for a file-sized buffer.** `ReadIconPNG()` allocates exactly `filesize` bytes and reads the file into that allocation (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjPNGio.c:338-360`), then `ReadMemPNG()` calls `PNG_LoadImageMEM(stream, -1, ...)` (`:121-132`). The API stores that argument as the memory handle's `ULONG size` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/png/directaccess.c:509-528`); `-1` therefore becomes `ULONG_MAX`. The selected `my_readmem_fn()` checks reads only against that supplied size before copying from the buffer (`directaccess.c:102-114`), not against the actual file length. A truncated PNG whose chunk length causes libpng to request bytes beyond the file can therefore be read past the `filesize` allocation before the datatype rejects or accepts the image.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `icon.library` PNG loading when CyberGfx is available and a malformed or truncated PNG declares chunk data/CRC extending beyond the file. **Consequence:** the PNG parser reads beyond its copied input buffer; parser outcome depends on adjacent memory and may include a fault or incorrect parse result. **Confidence:** high for the mismatch between allocation size and parser limit; trigger requires inconsistent PNG input. No icon file was loaded; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), PNG icon reader and selected PNG datatype memory-reader full-body pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9544

**PNG icon string attributes are scanned beyond their length-delimited `icOn` chunk.** The `ATTR_DEFAULTTOOL` and `ATTR_TOOLTYPE` cases set `val` to the current chunk-data pointer and call `strlen()` without first checking for a NUL within the remaining chunk bytes (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjPNGio.c:430-458`). `chunkdata` is a copy of the unknown chunk payload and `chunksize` is its remaining byte count (`:396-404`); it does not include a guaranteed terminator. The later `chunksize < 0` check cannot catch an overrun because `chunksize` is unsigned. A valid PNG carrying an `icOn` chunk with either string attribute missing its in-chunk terminator therefore makes the parser scan past the allocated chunk payload.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `icon.library` PNG icon loading when CyberGfx is available and a preserved `icOn` chunk contains an unterminated default-tool or tooltype string attribute. **Consequence:** the attribute parser reads outside its copied chunk data and may derive a length/value from unrelated memory before continuing or failing. **Confidence:** high for the unbounded string scan and unsigned underflow check; the trigger requires malformed `icOn` metadata. No icon file was loaded; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), PNG icon reader `icOn` attribute-bound pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9545

**The classic icon reader accepts short or unterminated length-prefixed strings.** `ReadIconString()` allocates the file-supplied `len` bytes without clearing them, then treats only `FRead(...) == EOF` as failure (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjio.c:675-696`). DOS `FRead()` returns the number of blocks read and returns zero at EOF, so a short read is accepted; the function also never verifies that a NUL occurs within the declared length. `AllocMemIcon()` uses `AllocMem()` with the requested flags and does not add termination (`support.c:495-507`). The selected classic icon parser stores these results as the default tool, tool window, or tooltype strings (`diskobjio.c:735-744,785-792,850-876`); Workbench's selected launcher and tooltype lookup subsequently consume them as C strings (`workbench/libs/workbench/openworkbenchobjecta.c:714-718,777-798`; `workbench/libs/icon/findtooltype.c:44-68`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** classic `.info` parsing through `GetDiskObject()`/`ReadStruct()` when the file supplies a length-prefixed string that is truncated or whose declared bytes contain no NUL (`support.c:279-293`). **Consequence:** the parser can publish incomplete/uninitialized string data; later string consumers may scan beyond that string allocation or act on unintended contents. **Confidence:** high for short-read acceptance and missing terminator validation; the later effect depends on the resulting bytes and consumer. No icon file was loaded; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), classic icon serializer full-body and string-read propagation pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9546

**Classic icon writes can report success after default-tool or tool-window serialization fails.** In `ProcessDefaultTool()` and `ProcessToolWindow()`, the write branches call `WriteIconString()` but discard its Boolean result, then return TRUE (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjio.c:746-758,794-806`). The helper reports failure when writing the length or string fails (`:701-713`); `WriteStruct()` propagates false special-hook results (`compiler/arossupport/writestruct.c:274-285`), and `__WriteIcon_WB()` relies on that result to report icon-write status (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:404-415`). Because these two hooks return success anyway, a failed string write can leave a truncated `.info` file while the outer serialization reports success.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** classic icon writing when the icon has a default-tool or tool-window string and the file write fails during that field. **Consequence:** `PutDiskObject()`/the selected writer can report success for an incomplete icon file. **Confidence:** high for the discarded status and hook success path; actual I/O failure was not induced. No icon was written; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), classic icon serializer full-body and write-result propagation pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9547

**Classic icon image dimensions can overflow signed arithmetic while calculating the data extent.** `ReadImage()` reads `Width`, `Height`, and `Depth` from the file into the `struct Image` fields, then computes `size = ((Width + 15) >> 4) * Height * Depth * 2` (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjio.c:425-447`). The fields are signed `WORD`s and the reader does not validate them before the multiplications. On AROS targets with 32-bit `int`, large positive dimensions such as 32767×32767 at depth 32767 exceed the signed range during the calculation, before conversion to `ULONG`; negative dimensions also reach this expression. The selected `ReadStruct()` descriptor reads these values as words and does not impose image limits (`diskobjio.c:184-199`; `compiler/arossupport/readstruct.c:110-114`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** classic `.info` parsing when the file marks a gadget image present and provides out-of-range image dimensions/depth. **Consequence:** signed-overflow undefined behavior occurs in the payload-size calculation; the exact subsequent allocation/read result is not asserted. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked signed calculation on 32-bit-int targets; trigger requires malformed or nonconforming dimensions. No icon file was loaded; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), classic icon serializer full-body and image-extent arithmetic pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9548

**`GetIconTagList()` dereferences a failed DrawerData allocation for disk and drawer icons.** Its final fixup calls `PrepareIcon(icon)` before layout (`workbench/libs/icon/geticontaglist.c:341-345`). `__PrepareIcon_WB()` allocates `do_DrawerData` when the type is `WBDISK` or `WBDRAWER` and the field is NULL, but immediately writes the default window fields without checking the allocation result (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:252-263`). `AllocMemIcon()` returns NULL when either the data allocation or its freelist registration fails (`:495-507`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** `icon.library`'s `GetIconTagList()` path for a disk/drawer icon without existing DrawerData, when the `DrawerData` or freelist allocation fails. **Consequence:** the fixup dereferences NULL instead of returning or preserving the icon. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation and direct writes; occurrence requires allocation failure on that icon path. No allocation failure or icon lookup was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), icon support full-body and DrawerData allocation-failure pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9549

**ARGB-to-paletted icon conversion writes through a failed image-buffer allocation.** When an image has ARGB data but no `ImageData`, `__FetchIconImage_WB()` allocates a one-byte-per-pixel buffer, then unconditionally sets palette metadata and loops over the image area writing through `idata` (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:209-244`). If `AllocMemIcon()` returns NULL, `idata` is NULL and the first pixel write dereferences it. The selected `LayoutIconA()` path calls `FetchIconImage()` when it needs planar image data on a screen path that cannot use the ARGB map (`layouticon.c:218-252`); `IconControlA()` also exposes image-fetching paths.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** an ARGB icon being converted for a non-ARGB/low-depth layout or a selected `IconControlA()` image request, when allocation of its paletted image buffer fails and the image area is nonzero. **Consequence:** conversion dereferences the failed allocation instead of leaving image data unavailable. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked result and write loop; occurrence requires the allocation failure. No allocation failure or layout was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), icon support full-body and lazy image conversion pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9550

**Classic icon writing dereferences a failed DiskObject duplicate.** `__WriteIcon_WB()` calls `DupDiskObject()` and immediately passes its result to `GetNativeIcon()` and later accesses `itmp->do_Gadget` without a NULL check (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:351-362`). `DupDiskObjectA()` returns NULL when its initial object allocation or a later required duplication allocation fails (`workbench/libs/icon/dupdiskobject.c:143-147,170-210,258-308`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** classic icon output through `PutDiskObject()`/`PutIconTagList()` when duplicating the supplied DiskObject fails. **Consequence:** the writer dereferences NULL rather than returning an allocation error. **Confidence:** high for the failure contract and selected path; occurrence requires duplication allocation failure. No write or allocation failure was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), icon support full-body and writer-duplication failure pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9551

**Rejected classic icon writes leak their temporary DiskObject.** After duplicating the input, `__WriteIcon_WB()` returns FALSE with `ERROR_OBJECT_WRONG_TYPE` when the classic icon has no `GadgetRender`, but bypasses the normal `FreeDiskObject(itmp)` cleanup (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:351-364,409-415`). The selected public `PutDiskObject()` wrapper delegates to `PutIconTags()` (`workbench/libs/icon/putdiskobject.c:42-50`), and `PutIconTagList()` reaches `WriteIcon()` for named output (`puticontaglist.c:123-131`).

No icon write was attempted; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), icon support full-body and writer rejection-cleanup pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9552

**ARGB-to-indexed conversion emits a transparent index beyond its pen map.** `__FetchIconImage_WB()` sets `Pens = 17`, uses the 17-entry `ehb_palette`, and sets `TransparentColor = 17`; fully transparent pixels are encoded as index 17 (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:209-220`). `LayoutIconA()` allocates `image->Pen` for exactly `image->Pens` entries, then maps every pixel through `image->Pen[image->ImageData[x]]` before creating the transparency mask (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:317-355,364-383`). Thus a transparent pixel indexes entry 17 beyond the 17-entry map.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** an ARGB icon with at least one fully transparent pixel that is converted to indexed image data and then laid out through the palette-mapped path. **Consequence:** pen mapping reads beyond the allocated map and uses an unrelated byte as that pixel's pen. **Confidence:** high for the produced index, map length and unconditional lookup; trigger requires a transparent pixel and the indexed conversion path. No icon was converted or laid out; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), icon support full-body and ARGB transparent-index caller pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9553

**`ICONCTRLA_HasRealImage2` fetches image data before checking whether the DiskObject is a native icon.** `IconControlA()` initializes `image2` only when `GetNativeIcon()` finds a NativeIcon (`workbench/libs/icon/iconcontrol.c:51-63`), but the `ICONCTRLA_HasRealImage2` branch calls `FetchIconImage(icon, 1)` unconditionally before testing `image2` (`:534-540`). The fetch helper immediately converts the supplied `DiskObject *` to a `NativeIcon *` and dereferences `ni_Image[1]` (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:167-175`). A valid classic/static DiskObject is therefore treated as if NativeIcon fields preceded it in memory.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** callers pass `ICONCTRLA_HasRealImage2` to `IconControlA()` for a valid non-native/classic DiskObject. **Consequence:** the query can dereference memory before the supplied DiskObject instead of returning FALSE for an icon with no NativeIcon select-image data. **Confidence:** high for the missing guard and invalid helper assumption; the exact fault behavior depends on surrounding memory. ## GD9557

**Icon library initialization failure closes required libraries twice.** `icon.library` opens Utility, DOS, graphics, then Intuition. If an open fails, `Init()` closes each earlier successful open on its failure path, but leaves the corresponding `ib_*Base` pointers non-NULL (`workbench/libs/icon/icon_init.c:55-73`). The generated library-init framework sets `initcalled` before invoking the `INITLIB` set and, if it fails, invokes the `EXPUNGELIB` set before expunging the base (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:42-68`). The registered `Expunge()` callback closes every non-NULL required-library pointer (`icon_init.c:76-89`), so the same opens are closed again. For example, if opening `intuition.library` fails, graphics, DOS and Utility each receive a second close; earlier failure points similarly double-close the libraries already opened.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** loading `icon.library` when one of the required libraries cannot be opened after an earlier required open succeeded. **Consequence:** the extra `CloseLibrary()` calls can consume open references owned by other clients and allow a still-used library to be expunged. **Confidence:** high for framework rollback and stale non-NULL pointers; the effect depends on concurrent/other clients holding those library bases. No library load failure was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), icon init and generated library-init rollback pass dated 2026-10-24.


## GD9558

**`FindToolType()` accepts a longer tooltype key that merely starts with the requested name.** The helper compares only `strlen(typeName)` bytes case-insensitively, then advances past `=` only if that exact byte follows; it returns a pointer even when the next character is another key character (`workbench/libs/icon/findtooltype.c:56-65`). Thus requesting `STACK` against `STACKSIZE=...` returns `SIZE=...`, and requesting a flag such as `TINY` can match `TINYNESS`. The public description says the routine finds the supplied type name, which requires a key boundary.

The maintained CLI startup path asks for `STACK` and passes a non-NULL result to `StrToLong()` (`workbench/system/CLI.c:139-143`); a `STACKSIZE=...` entry can therefore be misread as the `STACK` setting. Similar prefix collisions can affect other in-tree device and desktop tooltype consumers. **Consequence:** an unrelated setting is treated as the requested setting, potentially changing startup or device configuration. **Confidence:** high for the prefix match and returned suffix; behavior depends on the colliding tooltype and caller. No tooltype lookup was run.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), icon wrapper/tooltype helper full-body and selected caller pass dated 2026-10-24.

## GD9562

The API only documents the output buffer size; it imposes no corresponding short-input limit. **Consequence:** name processing writes beyond its temporary array before the later output truncation. **Confidence:** high for the buffer size and unbounded copies; no BumpRevision call was run.

The sender can then enqueue through a stale port pointer or wait forever on its private reply port; its held shared lock prevents `RemoveAppWindow()` from obtaining the exclusive lock, so teardown can also stall. **Confidence:** high for the selected caller, teardown ordering, lock ownership, and port-free semantics; manifestation requires the operations to overlap in the stated order. No drop or cleanup interleaving was run; source-only.

**Replacing a displayed MUI image spec can dereference NULL after the spec copy fails.** `Imagedisplay__OM_SET()` frees the old spec and assigns the result of `zune_image_spec_duplicate()` without checking it, then, for an object that is set up, passes `data->spec` to `zune_imspec_setup()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/imagedisplay.c:117-130`). The same unchecked replacement occurs in `Image__OM_SET()` (`classes/image.c:194-207`). `zune_image_spec_duplicate()` returns `StrDup(spec)` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/imspec.c:893-914`), and `StrDup()` returns NULL when `AllocVec()` fails (`compiler/alib/strdup.c:47-56`). In that case `zune_imspec_setup()` passes zero to `zune_image_spec_to_structure()`, whose string path casts it to `s` and unconditionally evaluates `*s` in the type switch (`imspec.c:340-360`). A maintained caller reaches the Image setter after setup: ScreenMode Preferences notifies `ScreenModeAttributes` when the selected display mode changes (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/smeditor.c:168-173`); its OM_SET updates the displayed Image child's spec with `set()` (`smattributes.c:202-215,279-282`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** selected MUI Image or ImageDisplay object already set up, followed by `MUIA_Image_Spec` replacement while `StrDup()` fails; the ScreenMode Preferences display-change path is one concrete Image caller. **Consequence:** a NULL dereference during the setter; the prior spec has already been freed. Check the duplicate result before setup and preserve or safely clear the old image state. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked result and dereference path; allocation failure was not induced. Source-only.

## GD9578

**Reading a Pendisplay RGB color with no valid pen reads outside the colormap.** `Pendisplay__OM_NEW()` initializes the default pen spec to `m0` and sets `data->pen = -1` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/pendisplay.c:43-46`). In `Pendisplay__OM_GET()`, the `PST_MUI`, `PST_CMAP` and `PST_SYS` cases call `GetRGB32(muiRenderInfo(obj)->mri_Colormap, data->pen & 0xffff, ...)` before the later `data->pen != -1` check (`pendisplay.c:225-246`). There are two paths to the invalid read: before `MUIM_Setup`, the Area superclass render-info pointer is NULL (`classes/area.c:1643`; assigned by `DoSetupMethod()` at `support.c:76`); after Setup, `Pendisplay__MUIM_Setup()` stores `MUI_ObtainPen()`'s result without checking it and still returns success (`pendisplay.c:261-274`), while `MUI_ObtainPen()` returns `-1` when setup/acquisition fails (`mui_obtainpen.c:52-60`). In either case the getter passes index `0xffff`. `GetRGB32()` loops through the requested indices without validating the colormap or bounds, and `color_get()` directly reads `cm->ColorTable[index]` and (for newer maps) `cm->LowColorBits[index]` (`rom/graphics/getrgb32.c:62-66`; `color_support.c:87-103`). Colormap table allocation is sized to its `entries` count (`rom/graphics/getcolormap.c:73-91`), so `0xffff` is not a valid pen index. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the built-in Pendisplay class when a caller queries `MUIA_Pendisplay_RGBcolor` on a not-yet-set-up object with a non-RGB spec, or after Setup when acquisition of that non-RGB pen fails. The maintained in-tree getters are not triggers: Imageadjust constructs its two gradient Pendisplays with RGB specs before its initial getter call (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/imageadjust.c:623-637,840-841`), and PSI sets palette Pendisplays to RGB before reading them (`workbench/prefs/PSI/editpanel_class.c:153,210`). No in-tree getter using a non-RGB Pendisplay was found. **Consequence:** before Setup, a NULL render-context/colormap dereference; after failed non-RGB pen acquisition, an out-of-bounds colormap-table read before the getter can return FALSE. Check pen validity and render context before calling `GetRGB32()`, and handle acquisition failure as Setup failure or an unavailable color. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked code paths; medium for repository impact because no maintained in-tree caller establishes the non-RGB trigger. Allocation failure and object queries were not induced. Source-only.

## GD9579

**Disposing a Pendisplay leaves its reference object's notification targeting the disposed object.** When `MUIA_Pendisplay_Reference` is set, `Pendisplay__OM_NEW()` registers an every-change notification on the referenced object's `MUIA_Pendisplay_Spec`, with the new Pendisplay as its destination (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/pendisplay.c:58-63`). `Pendisplay__OM_DISPOSE()` does not remove that notification; its body contains only a comment about the missing cleanup (`:86-96`). The notification implementation retains the raw destination and later calls `DoMethodA(destobj, ...)` when the source attribute changes (`classes/notify.c:341-390`); its `OM_DISPOSE` removes notifications owned by the disposed source, not incoming notifications registered on another object (`notify.c:250-268`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** built-in or external Pendisplay class configured with a reference object; dispose the Pendisplay while that referenced object remains alive, then change the reference's pen spec. PSI is the only maintained direct client found: it assigns palette objects as SysPenField references (`workbench/prefs/PSI/editpanel_class.c:165-170`), but the source review did not establish a PSI teardown sequence where a referenced palette survives disposal of its SysPenField and is then changed. The demonstrated trigger therefore remains public-API use that outlives the destination. **Consequence:** the reference object dispatches a method to an object whose lifetime has ended. Remove the notification while the reference is valid, or otherwise make the notification destination lifetime-safe. **Confidence:** high for registration, missing deregistration, and later dispatch; medium for repository impact because no maintained caller establishes the post-disposal source mutation. No objects or notifications were run. Source-only.

## GD9582

**Balance can lose valid sibling weight during redistribution when a computed per-child weight exceeds signed WORD range.** The public MUI weight tags are declared as `WORD` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.h:421-422,457-458`), while the Area instance stores each weight as `UWORD` (`area.h:495-496`). An ordinary SELECT drag enters `CLICKED` state and registers mouse-move handling (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/balance.c:722-755`); each processed move calls `recalc_weights_all()` with the mouse coordinate (`:784-813,658-665`). The all-siblings path computes group-side totals and deltas in `LONG`, but narrows each old and proposed weight into `WORD w1, w2` (`:465-476,512-519`). The trigger is reachable from valid tag values: for two left siblings at weight 32767 each and one right sibling at weight 1, the left total is 65534 and the complete group total is 65535. At a drag position where the computed left total reaches 65535, redistribution proposes 32768 for one left child. Converting that value to signed `WORD` is implementation-defined; on targets where it wraps negative, the next check treats it as underflow, zeros that child and redistributes the deficit (`balance.c:520-525,554-564`). The next redistribution pass can then zero the remaining left child as well. Thus the issue does not require invalid public tag values, though its manifestation depends on the target conversion behavior. This can produce a materially different set of child weights from the requested divider position. Group layout consumes the changed weights as unsigned values and only treats positive weights as growable (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:1563-1567`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** Balance built into muimaster or loaded as `Balance.mui`; a group with multiple resizable siblings on one side, valid initial weights whose side total exceeds 32767, and a drag that proposes more than 32767 for an individual sibling. The precise failure depends on the target compiler's out-of-range signed-conversion behavior. **Consequence:** a child weight can be zeroed and the residual redistributed, so the group proportions no longer match the drag. Keep redistribution temporaries unsigned/wider and clamp only at the documented attribute limit, with a defined redistribution policy. **Confidence:** medium; the narrowing and negative-weight recovery are direct, and a valid public-tag state reaches the narrowing, but the exact result depends on compiler conversion semantics and drag/layout geometry. No Balance interaction or compiler behavior was run; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

On `MUIA_Radio_Active`, `Radio__OM_SET()` sends `MUIA_Selected` only to the old and new row Groups (`radio.c:154-164`). The nested Image class changes its rendered image state only when its own `MUIA_Selected` is set (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/image.c:180-186`), then passes that state to `zune_imspec_draw()` (`image.c:539-543`). The installer can therefore use “Use existing” semantically while the nested radio glyph remains on the initial option. SysMon is another maintained use. **Consequence:** the radio image states can disagree with `MUIA_Radio_Active`, leaving the prior option visually selected or no programmatically selected option displayed. Set `MUIA_Selected` on the nested image (and keep text/row state consistent) when the active index changes. **Confidence:** high for the object relationships and state dispatch; no GUI interaction was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**Pixmap's RLE decoder does not check compressed or decompressed bounds.** `DecompressRLE()` allocates the expected output size, then consumes run/literal commands using `compressedSize` as a loop counter without checking that the run value byte or literal bytes remain in the input, or that each decoded run fits in the output allocation (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/pixmap.c:360-400`). ## GD9596

**Volumelist computes used-space percentage with overflowing 32-bit arithmetic.** For each volume whose `Info()` succeeds, the display code evaluates `100 * diskinfo.id_NumBlocksUsed / diskinfo.id_NumBlocks` before formatting the percentage (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/volumelist.c:199-207`).
