## GD9601

**Volumelist divides by zero for a successfully reported zero-block volume.** After `Info()` succeeds, `Volumelist__OM_NEW()` computes `100 * id_NumBlocksUsed / id_NumBlocks` without checking the denominator (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/volumelist.c:199-207`). CDVDFS copies the ISO primary volume descriptor's `space_size` into its volume state without validating that it is nonzero (`rom/filesys/CDVDFS/src/iso9660.c:216-253`); its top-level directory constructor only copies the descriptor's root record, and the mount path publishes a DOS volume after that allocation succeeds (`iso9660.c:350-374`; `rom/filesys/CDVDFS/src/device.c:1420-1457`). For such a mounted volume, CDVDFS `ACTION_INFO` sets `id_NumBlocks` from `Volume_Size()`, leaves it zero, sets `id_NumBlocksUsed` to the same value, and returns success (`device.c:789-823`). The selected Volumelist caller locks each DOS volume and calls `Info()` (`volumelist.c:176-211`), so a malformed ISO descriptor that passes the existing mount checks can reach a zero-over-zero integer division. **Affected configuration and trigger:** built-in or standalone Volumelist.mui with CDVDFS available, when an ISO descriptor with zero `space_size` is accepted and its volume is listed. **Consequence:** undefined integer division, commonly a processor exception or class-construction failure while building the list. Reject zero-sized volumes or guard the denominator before calculating the percentage. **Confidence:** medium-high for the unchecked calculation and selected provider-to-caller path; the zero-sized ISO is malformed input and no image or runtime operation was exercised. Source-only.


## GD9602

**IntelGMA startup does not handle failure to allocate its initial mode state or framebuffer.** In the PCI enumeration callback, `intelgma_init.c` allocates `initialState` and `initialBitMap` without checking either result, passes both to `G45_InitMode()`, and clears 640×480 pixels through `initialBitMap + Card.Framebuffer` (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_init.c:421-432`). `G45_InitMode()` writes mode fields through `state` when a clock solution is available, and `G45_LoadState()` unconditionally reads its state argument before touching the hardware (`intelgma_support.c:171-178,284-297`). Therefore a NULL `initialState` reaches a definite dereference at `G45_LoadState()`, even if mode calculation found no clock solution. Separately, `AllocBitmapArea()` explicitly converts graphics-memory allocation failure to `-1` (`intelgma_support.c:543-568`); startup neither checks this sentinel nor avoids the clear loop. Since `initialBitMap` is `intptr_t` and `Card.Framebuffer` is the mapped framebuffer base, the clear-loop address becomes `Framebuffer - 1` (`intelgma_hidd.h:106,148`; `intelgma_init.c:430-432`), and the first 32-bit store starts one byte before the mapping. That can fault at the first store or write across the framebuffer boundary if the preceding address is mapped. These failures occur after a supported IntelGMA device has been selected and can abort startup or fault/corrupt framebuffer memory. **Affected configuration and trigger:** IntelGMA monitor startup on a supported device, if its state-pool allocation or graphics-memory allocation fails. **Confidence:** high for unchecked failure propagation; allocation failure was not induced. Source-only.

## GD9604

**Volumelist truncates displayed capacities above 4 EiB on DOS64.** `printSize()` shifts byte counts of at least 9,999,999,999 by 30 and formats the result after converting it to `unsigned int` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/volumelist.c:20-36`). On DOS64 builds `InfoData` uses UQUAD block counts (`compiler/include/dos/dos.h:176-203`), and `Volumelist__OM_NEW()` computes used/free bytes as UQUAD values before passing both to `printSize()` (`volumelist.c:180-216`). The optional NTFS handler also stores `total_sectors` as UQUAD and returns it through `InfoData.id_NumBlocks` (`workbench/fs/ntfs/ntfs_fs.h:225-226`; `ntfs.c:1092`; `disk.c:57-60`), confirming a maintained wide-count provider path; whether the rest of NTFS supports operating a multi-exbibyte volume is not established. Once either value reaches 2^62 bytes (4 EiB), the GiB count is 2^32 and the cast wraps to zero; larger representable sizes wrap to an incorrect smaller value. **Affected configuration and trigger:** built-in or standalone Volumelist on a DOS64 build when a volume reports at least 4 EiB free or used and the corresponding multiplication remains within UQUAD range. **Consequence:** the free/used capacity column displays a truncated size (4 EiB displays as `0G`). Keep the shifted quantity wide through formatting or format using a UQUAD conversion supported by the target C library. **Confidence:** high for the narrowing and threshold; medium for practical reachability because it requires a multi-exbibyte volume. No such volume or display was used; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9597

**Find can leave its Start/Stop controls claiming a scan is running when no worker started.** There are two creation-failure edges in the same Find launch path. First, `FindGroup__OM_NEW()` ignores a NULL result from `MUI_NewObject(MUIC_Process, ...)` and still returns the group with Start enabled (`workbench/system/find/findgroup_class.c:554-564,589-605`). Pressing Start then disables Start and enables Stop before calling `DoMethod(data->scanproc, MUIM_Process_Launch)`; the selected `DoMethodA()` helper returns zero for a NULL object, so nothing launches (`findgroup_class.c:768-775`; `compiler/include/clib/alib_protos.h:305-317`). Second, when the Process object exists, `Process__MUIM_Process_Launch()` stores the nullable `CreateNewProc()` result but returns TRUE regardless (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/process.c:203-220`; DOS documents NULL on creation error at `rom/dos/createnewproc.c:54-58`). Find ignores that result, and its worker is the only normal path that restores the controls (`findgroup_class.c:731-740`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** standalone Find / Process.mui when either embedded Process-object construction or its worker-process creation fails, such as under memory pressure. **Consequence:** Find presents a nonworking or falsely running scan; when worker creation fails, the Start button remains disabled and Stop enabled indefinitely. Propagate both creation failures and restore/report the UI state. **Confidence:** high for both nullable results and the unchecked UI paths; no allocation or process-creation failure was induced. The parent `workbench-system` aggregation edge is commented in this snapshot, so the Find caller is scoped to builds that explicitly select the standalone target. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9598

**A relaunch can publish a stale task pointer and let the worker observe the previous kill state.** `Process__MUIM_Process_Launch()` makes the worker runnable in `CreateNewProc()` before assigning its returned pointer and before clearing `data->kill` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/process.c:203-218`). `CreateNewProc()` calls `AddTask()` and `Permit()` before returning; its own source notes that a higher-priority child can complete and be freed before the parent resumes (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:543-564`). After a previous Kill, `data->kill` remains 1. If the restarted worker runs first, it can observe the stale kill flag, return from its process method, and set `data->task = NULL` (`process.c:41-53`). The launcher can then overwrite that NULL with the returned pointer to the already-finished task. **Affected configuration and trigger:** Process.mui on SMP or a scheduling path that runs a fast worker before CreateNewProc returns; relaunch after Kill is the direct stale-flag case. FindGroup is a maintained caller that allows Stop followed by Start (`findgroup_class.c:781-787,768-776`). **Consequence:** the new worker may exit immediately, while the Process object retains a stale non-NULL task pointer; later Kill can continue waiting and signal a task whose lifetime has ended. Initialize the kill state before publishing the child and synchronize child completion with task-pointer publication. **Confidence:** medium-high for the ordering and supported runnable-before-return schedule; the exact interleaving was not run. Source-only.

## GD9599

**FindGroup reports a timed-out worker as stopped and re-enables Start.** `MUIM_Process_Kill` returns FALSE when its nonzero `maxdelay` expires while `data->task` is still non-NULL (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/process.c:169-189`). FindGroup calls it with `maxdelay=4`, ignores that result, and unconditionally enables Start and disables Stop (`workbench/system/find/findgroup_class.c:781-789`). Process Launch does nothing while the old task pointer remains non-NULL (`process.c:200-220`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected Find application when a file-system request or per-file scan operation does not finish within one `Delay(10)` interval after the kill request. Because the code increments `delay` by 10 and then compares it with `maxdelay=4`, it times out after that first delay if the worker is still active. **Consequence:** the UI says the search stopped although the worker is still running; another Start appears accepted but launches no new worker, and the old worker may still publish results. Check the Kill result and retain a truthful running/stopping state until termination. **Confidence:** high for the timeout and ignored return paths; the duration of a specific filesystem operation is platform-dependent. No search or stop timeout was run. Source-only.


## GD9600

**Process Kill can signal a NULL or retiring worker task.** `Process__MUIM_Process_Kill()` tests `data->task` in the loop condition and then reads the shared field again as the argument to `Signal()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/process.c:169-175`). The worker concurrently writes `data->task = NULL` immediately before returning (`:41-53`). If that store occurs between the condition and argument read, Kill calls `Signal(NULL)`; Exec's `Signal()` has no NULL guard and dereferences `task` in its CPU-affinity check or task-lock access before any terminal-state check (`rom/exec/signal.c:170-172,269-280`). If Kill instead retains the old pointer, it can enter `Signal()` while the worker is being removed; Exec's state check occurs only after it has already read task/ETask fields, and service-task cleanup later frees the task allocation (`rom/exec/remtask.c:87-154`; `rom/exec/service.c:37-89`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable Process.mui module when Kill or object disposal overlaps a worker finishing naturally or responding to the kill request; the checked-in Find caller reaches Kill through Stop/Cleanup (`workbench/system/find/findgroup_class.c:650-655,781-789`) when Find is explicitly selected as a target. **Consequence:** the NULL read can fault in `Signal()`, while the old-pointer case can read task state during retirement. Synchronize the task-pointer handoff and retain a valid task lifetime through signaling. **Confidence:** high that the field is read twice without synchronization, the worker clears it before task exit, and `Signal()` dereferences its argument without a NULL check; the overlap and resulting fault/retirement access are conditional and were not run. Source-only.

## GD9603

**Radeon successful initialization leaks its timer.device open across module expunge (conditional device-open/resource leak; high source confidence).** `ATI_Init()` opens `timer.device` into the `IORequest` embedded in the library's static data (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_init.c:274-278`). When PCI enumeration finds a supported card, it returns TRUE immediately (`:285-297`) and retains the device for the Radeon `usleep()` helper (`workbench/hidds/radeon/radeon_driver.c:24-34,78,1882-1887,2027,2073`). The only source `CloseDevice()` is in the no-supported-card/failure path (`ati_init.c:298-302`). On successful-module teardown, `ATI_Expunge()` unmaps the card, disposes its PCI object, releases attribute bases and deletes the pool, but never closes `sd->tr` (`:309-348`); the generated library expunge subsequently frees the base containing that request when the open count reaches zero (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1532-1590`). No generated OOP class shutdown closes the timer request.

**Consequence and scope:** expunging a successfully initialized Radeon module leaves its `timer.device` open reference outstanding, so the device's per-open state cannot be released through the Radeon request and the timer device may remain pinned. Close the request/device during the successful expunge path before freeing the library base. **Affected configuration and trigger:** an optional Radeon HIDD module loaded for a supported card, followed by successful library expunge; initialization that fails to find a supported card closes the timer request and does not trigger this finding. No timer device or module lifecycle was run; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L1286`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L1286) and the 2026-10-24 Radeon expunge recheck appended to that ledger. The successful and failed init paths, all Radeon `CloseDevice()` sites, timer helper callers, `ATI_Expunge()`, generated class shutdown, and generated library-base teardown were checked for this entry.


## GD9605

**MonEd can enter its event loop after display setup fails and dereference a NULL or stale window.** `OpenDisplay()` returns `2` when `GetVisualInfo()` fails (`workbench/prefs/MonEd/moned.c:627-628`), but the initial caller treats any nonzero return as success and immediately evaluates `sp_Wnd->UserPort` in `WaitPort()` (`:865-869`); the static `sp_Wnd` is still NULL on this path. If `CreateContext()` returns NULL, its guarded gadget/window setup is skipped and `OpenDisplay()` falls through to `return 1` (`:633-634,761-762`), producing the same bad event-loop entry. The Jump path is also unchecked: after `CloseDisplay()` closes the old window, it ignores the next `OpenDisplay()` result (`:1020-1029`); when setup fails before assigning `sp_Wnd`, it can retain the just-closed window pointer. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-prefs-moned` target (`workbench/prefs/MonEd/mmakefile.src:4-12`), when GadTools visual-info or context allocation fails during initial open or a Jump reopen. **Consequence:** the event loop dereferences a NULL/stale window pointer instead of exiting or reporting setup failure. Make `OpenDisplay()` return a consistent success/failure value, check it at both call sites, and clear the window pointer after close. **Confidence:** high for nullable setup calls, inconsistent return values, and unchecked callers; failure was not induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9606

**MonEd leaks display resources when `OpenWindowTagList()` fails.** Before opening the window, `OpenDisplay()` opens `thinpazfont8`, obtains `MainVisualInfo`, creates a GadTools context and linked gadget list (`workbench/prefs/MonEd/moned.c:590-594,627,633-730`). If `OpenWindowTagList()` returns NULL, it returns `0` immediately (`:738-759`). The initial caller then skips the `if (OpenDisplay())` body and never calls `CloseDisplay()` (`:865-867,1037`), although that routine is the only cleanup for the font, visual-info object and gadget list (`:769-780`). These allocations are therefore abandoned as the process closes its libraries and exits; repeated failed launches accumulate the leaked memory and font reference. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-prefs-moned` target when window creation fails after the font, visual info and gadget list have been allocated. **Consequence:** one process leaks those display resources; repeated failures consume memory and retain the opened font resource. Unwind setup in `OpenDisplay()` on every failure or call a null-safe cleanup path before returning. **Confidence:** high for allocation/cleanup ordering and the missing failure cleanup; no window failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9607

**MonEd's monitor-rate calculation can divide by zero after 32-bit overflow of CLI timing values.** The CLI accepts hexadecimal `TOTROW=0x...` and `TOTCLK=0x...` values, converts them with `xtoi()`, and stores them into the UWORD MonitorSpec fields without range checks (`workbench/prefs/MonEd/moned.c:845-848`; `compiler/include/graphics/monitor.h:35-36`). `UpDateDisplay()` widens those fields into 32-bit `ULONG`s, checks only that both are nonzero, then evaluates `rows * clks * 280` in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic as the divisor (`moned.c:430-442`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:39-43`). The accepted pair `TOTROW=0x4000 TOTCLK=0x8000` makes the mathematical product `2^32 * 35`, which wraps to zero; the subsequent `1000000000 / 0` is undefined and traps on ordinary targets before the monitor update. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-prefs-moned` target with a current monitor, launched from CLI with nonzero timing fields whose product times 280 wraps to zero (the pair above is one accepted example). **Consequence:** the command crashes during display-rate formatting before `UpDateMonitor()` applies the requested timing change. Compute the divisor in a wider type and validate supported timing ranges before storing/updating. **Confidence:** high for the 32-bit operand types, unchecked CLI assignment and exact modular-zero example; no command was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9608

**Icon library's on-demand optional-library opens are unsynchronized and can leak a library reference under concurrent first use.** `DemandOpenLibrary()` tests a shared base field and, if NULL, calls `OpenLibrary()` and stores the returned pointer without a lock or atomic once-initialization (`workbench/libs/icon/icon_intern.h:206-217`). The optional fields are initially zero because the generated library base is allocated with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1090`; fields in `icon_intern.h:177-180`). Multiple selected public calls can reach this helper: for example, `identify.c` probes `DataTypesBase` while identifying file icons (`:89-95,499-505`); icon-library calls are not serialized by the private `iconlistlock`, which protects only icon-list operations. If two tasks make the same first-use call concurrently, both can observe NULL and each successfully open the library; the later store overwrites the earlier pointer. The API calls then use the retained base normally, but `Expunge()` closes only the single stored reference (`icon_init.c:76-89`), leaving one open reference outstanding and preventing clean optional-library teardown. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected `workbench-libs-icon` module when an optional dependency (IFFParse, CyberGfx, DataTypes, or Workbench) is first demanded concurrently by multiple callers. **Consequence:** leaked open reference pins that optional library after `icon.library` expunges; repeated concurrent first-use races can accumulate references. Protect demand-open/store with a per-base synchronization mechanism or an equivalent once-initialization scheme. **Confidence:** high for the unsynchronized check/open/store and single-reference expunge; occurrence requires concurrent first use and successful opens. No library open, concurrent call, or expunge was run; source-only.

## GD9612

**NList, NListtree, BetterString, and TextEditor clipboard shutdown can unload module code while the worker is still executing it.** Each `ShutdownClipboardServer()` sends `SERVER_SHUTDOWN` and waits only until the worker replies to the message; none waits for the worker to exit (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/ClipboardServer.c:332-347`; the NListtree copy has the same shutdown sequence; `workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/ClipboardServer.c:491-505`; `workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/ClipboardServer.c:970-985`). On that command, each `ClipboardServer()` sets `running = FALSE` and replies inside the message loop, then still deletes its port, drops/closes IFFParse resources, logs shutdown, and returns from code in the MCC module (NList/NListtree `ClipboardServer.c:202-230,233-250`; BetterString `ClipboardServer.c:355-404`; TextEditor `ClipboardServer.c:819-879,882-884`). All four classes call `ShutdownClipboardServer()` from `ClassExpunge()` (`nlist_mcc/library.c:176-180`; `nlisttree_mcc/library.c:94-97`; `betterstring/mcc/library.c:143-147`; `texteditor/mcc/library.c:160-165`). Their included MCC startup code proceeds from `ClassExpunge()` through module cleanup and `LibDelete()`, which returns `lh_Segment` for unload after freeing the library base (NList `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mccinit.c:825-855,1022-1054`; BetterString `workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/include/mccinit.c:821-847,1018-1050`; TextEditor uses byte-identical `mccinit.c` logic in `workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/include/mccinit.c:825-855,1022-1054`). If the expunging task resumes after the reply and unloads the module before the worker finishes its tail, the worker continues executing from unloaded module code. **Affected configuration and trigger:** AROS builds of the explicitly selected `classes-zune-nlist-class`, `classes-zune-nlisttree-class`, `workbench-classes-zune-betterstring-class`, or `workbench-classes-zune-texteditor-class` module targets when final close/expunge overlaps the worker's post-reply shutdown tail; SMP makes the overlap possible across CPUs, and scheduler handoff after the reply can also let the caller run first. **Consequence:** the clipboard worker can fetch/execute module code after its segment has been released, risking a task fault or system failure. Join the worker before returning from `ClassExpunge()`, or keep the module loaded until the worker reports that it has exited. **Confidence:** high for the missing exit handshake and post-reply module-code path; the exact unload/interleaving was not run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9613

GD9613. **ScrollRaster and ScrollRasterBF expand negative screen-raster upper bounds to the bitmap's far edge (conditional unintended raster operation; high source confidence).** For a RastPort without a Layer, both functions compare the signed `WORD` upper coordinates after converting them to `ULONG` (`rom/graphics/scrollraster.c:105-108`; `scrollrasterbf.c:103-107`). A negative `xMax` or `yMax` therefore converts to a large unsigned value and is replaced by `width - 1` or `height - 1`. When the other endpoint is also negative but `xMin <= xMax` / `yMin <= yMax`, the caller's rectangle lies wholly outside the bitmap on that axis, yet the range check expands it across the raster. For example, on a 320-pixel-wide screen, `xMin=-2, xMax=-1, yMin=0, yMax=10, dx=1` is expanded to an affected rectangle from x=-2 through x=319. `ScrollRaster()` then fills the far-edge strip and `ScrollRasterBF()` erases it, despite the caller's interval having no bitmap intersection. The attempted `MoveRaster()` copy also passes a negative destination to `BltBitMap()` after its negative-source adjustment (`gfxfuncsupport.c:838-852`; `bltbitmap.c:142-153,244-255`); the generic software path's unchecked negative destination is separately recorded as GD9615, and other backend behavior is not established here. Clamp upper bounds without unsigned conversion and reject or clip a rectangle that has no bitmap intersection. **Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting graphics.library when an external caller uses either public scroll vector on a screen RastPort (no Layer), supplies a negative right or bottom endpoint with ordered endpoints and a displacement smaller than the erroneously expanded extent. The reviewed checked-in console and datatype calls use ordinary nonnegative bounds; no in-tree caller demonstrating this trigger was found. No scroll or raster operation was run. **Confidence:** high for the signed-to-unsigned comparison, expansion, and subsequent fill/erase call; actual retained-pixel movement depends on the selected blit backend. Source-only.

## GD9614

GD9614. **Raster scrolling clears part of the bitmap after an overlapping-copy allocation failure (conditional; high source confidence).** In the no-Layer path, `MoveRaster()` calls `BltBitMap()` for the overlapping source/destination rectangle and ignores its return value (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:838-853`). The Layer path also ignores each blit result: after intersecting source and destination clip rectangles, it calls `BltBitMap()` without checking the result (`gfxfuncsupport.c:951-1019`). With an ordinary visible clip rectangle whose source and destination both use `rp->BitMap`, an overlapping scroll produces the same overlap case in the generic blitter. The generic software `BltBitMap()` implementation allocates a temporary scanline buffer for overlapping copies and returns zero immediately if `AllocMem()` fails (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:299-310`). `MoveRaster()` nevertheless returns `TRUE` (`gfxfuncsupport.c:1031`), so `ScrollRaster()` proceeds to fill the vacated strip with the background pen (`rom/graphics/scrollraster.c:127-140,142-170`), and `ScrollRasterBF()` proceeds to erase it (`rom/graphics/scrollrasterbf.c:124-130,132-165`). For a horizontal overlapping scroll with a nonzero exposed strip, allocation failure therefore leaves the old image in place but overwrites its edge; a vertical or diagonal scroll can similarly erase/fill exposed rows or columns without moving the retained image. **Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting the generic software `BltBitMap()` path for a RastPort with or without a Layer, when its overlapping source/destination copy needs a temporary scanline buffer and that `AllocMem()` fails. The Layer case requires a visible clip rectangle whose copy uses the same bitmap for source and destination. HIDD-specific blit implementations may have different failure behavior; no claim is made for them. **Consequence:** partial scroll state and loss of pixels in the strip that should have been vacated by a successful move. Propagate copy failure from `MoveRaster()` before reporting success so callers do not clear the strip. **Confidence:** high for both ignored-result paths and the generic allocation failure; Layer-path reachability follows the selected same-bitmap visible clip rectangle case. No allocation failure or scroll was induced. Source-only.

## GD9615

GD9615. **BltBitMap does not clip negative destination coordinates before indexing the destination plane (conditional out-of-bounds access; high source confidence).** The generic software path clips a negative source by advancing the destination, but has no corresponding adjustment when `xDest` or `yDest` is negative (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:244-264`). It checks only the destination's far edge (`:270-272`), so a request such as `xSrc=0, xDest=-1, xSize=2` passes the size checks. The pixel loop adds the signed `xDest` to unsigned `x` and passes the result to `copyonepixel()` (`:314-318`); for the first pixel, `xDest` converts to a very large `ULONG`, and `copyonepixel()` uses it as a byte offset into the destination plane (`:341-363`). A negative `yDest` likewise reaches destination row-address calculation (`:291-294`) and can address outside the plane. The HIDD branch also omits low-edge clipping before dispatch (`:142-162`). The selected generic GFX HIDD `CopyBox` method (`rom/hidds/gfx/mmakefile.src:8-25`; `gfx_hiddclass.c:1252-1308`) reaches `copybox_impl()`, whose contract says it performs no coordinate checks (`:930-977`). For same-format chunky bitmaps in copy mode, that implementation calls `HIDD_BM_CopyMemBox8()` (`:1031-1074`); the helper computes `dst_start = msg->dst + msg->dstY * msg->dstMod + msg->dstX` and copies through it without clipping (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapmemblit.c:215-291`). A negative destination origin therefore also reaches a write before the chunky bitmap buffer on this generic HIDD path. P96's selected m68k `CopyBox` override has the same behavior on its CPU transfer path: when either bitmap is outside VRAM and the draw mode is Copy, it calls the inherited `HIDD_BM_CopyMemBox8/16/24/32()` helper with `msg->destX/Y` unchanged (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_hiddclass.c:994-1048`; selected method in `p96gfx.conf:29-30`). That helper derives its destination address from the raw pointer and coordinates without clipping, so the P96 RAM-transfer branch can also write outside the destination bitmap allocation. The build-selected VGAGfx override on i386-PC and x86-64-PC likewise sends `msg->destX/Y` directly to `HIDD_BM_CopyMemBox8()` for Copy mode (`arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_hiddclass.c:156-234`; active package HIDD lists in `arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:74-75` and `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:65-68`). The helper derives its destination pointer from the raw bitmap buffer and coordinates without clipping, so this selected VGA backend has the same conditional out-of-bounds write. VMwareSVGA's Copy-mode path similarly calls inherited `HIDD_BM_CopyMemBox16/24/32()` helpers with unmodified destination coordinates (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/vmwaresvga_hiddclass.c:371-430`); those helpers form the destination address from the raw buffer and coordinates, so the explicitly buildable VMwareSVGA target has the same conditional CPU-copy issue for 16/24/32-bit bitmap pairs. Its parent aggregate edge is commented out (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/mmakefile.src:49-53`), so this is not claimed as a default-image trigger. AmigaVideo's selected m68k override also has no low-edge clipping: `BltBitMap()` forwards negative destination coordinates through `int_bltbitmap()` (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:142-225`), `AmigaVideoCl__Hidd_Gfx__CopyBox()` passes them unchanged to `blit_copybox()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:900-929`), and that routine computes `dstoffset = BytesPerRow * dsty + (dstx / 16) * 2` without rejecting negative origins (`amigavideo_blitter.c:110-159`). For a negative `dsty`, or a `dstx` at or left of the preceding 16-pixel word (for example `dstx=-16` with a positive width that still intersects the bitmap), the resulting plane address is before the bitmap's plane base and is submitted as both blitter C and D pointers (`:205-237`). The fallback superclass is not called because `blit_copybox()` returns TRUE after programming the blitter. Thus the hardware-blitter route also receives an out-of-range destination address. In P96's both-in-VRAM branch, the HIDD passes destination coordinates unchanged to `BlitRectNoMaskComplete()` (`p96gfx_hiddclass.c:1073-1086`), whose implementation invokes a board-supplied function pointer (`p96gfx_card.c:320-327`); no local clip is applied, but the callback's clipping behavior is external to this source tree, so this branch remains unresolved. The NVIDIA override packs destination coordinates directly into the GPU blit command after setting surface offsets and pitches (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/nvidiaclass.c:461-544`), without local clipping; the chip-command clipping behavior is not established by the local implementation, so this branch remains unresolved. Nouveau has a separate, explicitly buildable `Hidd_Gfx::CopyBox` override (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:783-840`; its parent aggregate is commented out at `workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-29`). NV04, NV50, and pre-Blackwell NVC0 helpers submit signed source/destination coordinates without local low-edge clipping (`nv04_exa.c:483-500,223-246`; `nv50_exa.c:1072-1088,286-312`; `nvc0_exa.c:1313-1340,288-315`). The Blackwell branch explicitly clips both rectangles to bitmap bounds (`nvc0_exa.c:1328-1352`). The earlier GPU generations' device-side clipping behavior is not established by this source, so their CopyBox outcome remains unresolved and is not counted as an additional out-of-bounds finding. The X11 and WinGDI overrides similarly forward the rectangle directly to `XCopyArea()` and `BitBlt()` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11gfx_hiddclass.c:197-224`; `arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/wingdi_hiddclass.c:603-634`), while SDL constructs source/destination rectangles and calls `SDL_BlitSurface()` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_hiddclass.c:439-477`). These local methods do not establish their host APIs' negative-destination clipping behavior; those branches remain unresolved. UIKit's override is an empty TODO, and the iOS README says no UIKit display driver is currently provided; it is not counted as a functioning selected graphics backend (`arch/all-ios/hidd/uikit/uikit_hiddclass.c:281-284`; `arch/all-ios/README.txt:9`). The implementation inventory was searched repository-wide; these are the identified `CopyBox` overrides. **Affected configuration and trigger:** callers selecting the generic software bitmap path, the generic GFX HIDD same-format chunky `CopyBox` path, the selected m68k P96 CPU-transfer branch, the selected i386-PC or x86-64-PC VGAGfx branch, the explicitly buildable VMwareSVGA CPU-copy branch, or the selected m68k AmigaVideo hardware-blitter branch, and requesting a blit whose destination begins above or sufficiently far left of the destination bitmap, with a rectangle that still intersects it. Besides direct public `BltBitMap()` calls, maintained internal routes exist through unlayered-screen `ScrollRaster()`/`ScrollRasterBF()` (`rom/graphics/scrollraster.c:97-109,127-128`; `scrollrasterbf.c:95-108,124-125`; `gfxfuncsupport.c:838-852`) and superbitmapped-layer scrolling. `ScrollLayer()` subtracts an unclamped delta from stored offsets, and `SyncSBitMap()` passes `ClipRect - layer bounds - scroll offset` as the destination origin (`rom/hyperlayers/scrolllayer.c:76-79`; `rom/graphics/syncsbitmap.c:64-74`). The optional, explicitly buildable `test-layers` program exposes this route interactively: its `scrolllayer` command reads arbitrary `dx/dy` values and forwards them without range checks (`developer/debug/test/layers/layerstest.c:354-375,1185-1200`); its startup creates a 91x91 superbitmap layer (`:908-921`). For layer 0, scrolling by `dx=-92` advances the stored X offset past the backing origin; the next nonzero scroll calls `SyncSBitMap()` with a negative destination coordinate. Thus this path has a checked-in user-driven trigger in the optional test utility, in addition to the public API and unlayered-scroll routes. **Consequence:** destination-plane or chunky-buffer access can reach before the intended row or bitmap allocation. Clip the destination origin and reduce the source origin and extent before entering either backend. **Confidence:** high for the generic software path and optional `test-layers` trigger, generic GFX HIDD chunky fast path, P96 CPU-transfer path, selected VGAGfx CPU-copy path, VMwareSVGA CPU-copy path, and AmigaVideo plane-offset submission; P96's both-in-VRAM branch and NVIDIA GPU-command branch remain unresolved because their clipping behavior is outside the local implementation. No blit was run. Source-only.


## GD9616

GD9616. **HIDD AllocBitMap crashes for the documented header-only `BMATags_NoMemory` option (conditional; high source confidence).** The public tag contract says `BMATags_NoMemory` suppresses storage allocation and returns a set-up bitmap header (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:133-135`; tag definition `compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:104`). If the requested depth is greater than 8, `AllocBitMap()` selects its HIDD path (`allocbitmap.c:242-246`). With the tag true, parsing sets `alloc=FALSE` (`:215-217`); the HIDD branch leaves `bm_obj=NULL`, does not create a display bitmap, and keeps `ok=TRUE` (`:335-349`). It then proceeds through header setup and unconditionally calls `OOP_GetAttr(bm_obj, ...)` (`:381-390,454-462`). `OOP_GetAttr()` dispatches with `OOP_DoMethod(object, ...)`, and `OOP_DoMethod` dereferences `OOP_OCLASS(object)` (`rom/oop/getattr.c:70-72`; `rom/oop/include/oop.h:95-101`), so this path dereferences the NULL object instead of returning the requested header. **Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library builds using the HIDD allocation branch (for example depth >8) when a caller supplies the public extended-tag list with `BMATags_NoMemory=TRUE`. No maintained in-tree caller of this option was found in the targeted search; the documented public API is the trigger. **Consequence:** the call can fault before returning a bitmap header. Skip the object attribute query and mark/return the header-only representation when no object was created. **Confidence:** high for the null-object dispatch; no allocation or API call was run. Source-only.

## GD9617

GD9617. **HIDD `BltBitMap()` reports eight planes regardless of the bitmap depths and mask (public result-contract mismatch; high source confidence).** The HIDD path computes the minimum source/destination depth (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:137-140`) and rejects an empty request, then dispatches the blit at `:207-216`; after that it unconditionally assigns `planecnt = 8` (`:226-227`). The function documentation says the result is the number of planes actually involved, and the generic software path counts only destination planes with storage that pass the mask (`:280-289`). Thus a successful HIDD blit on a one-plane bitmap with `mask=1` returns 8 rather than 1; the same mismatch occurs when a mask selects fewer planes than eight. The HIDD branch also returns 8 if its cached GC or bitmap-object acquisition fails and no blit is dispatched (`:196-224`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library calls selecting the HIDD path when source or destination is a HIDD bitmap, and a caller observes the return value for a bitmap/mask that involves fewer than eight planes or when HIDD dispatch prerequisites are unavailable. **Consequence:** callers cannot use the return value to determine the number of planes involved and may treat an incomplete or skipped HIDD operation as an eight-plane blit. The reviewed maintained direct `BltBitMap()` call sites discard the return value; no in-tree consequence was established. Return the actual involved-plane count and report failure/no-op consistently with the public result contract. **Confidence:** high that this implementation returns the constant 8 outside the generic path; exact HIDD plane-count semantics for nonplanar display formats and backend failure policy remain open. No blit or HIDD failure was induced; source-only.

<a id="gd9618"></a>
## GD9618

GD9618. **`BestModeIDA()` ignores the public `BIDTAG_GreenBits` minimum.** The API documentation names `BIDTAG_GreenBits` alongside `BIDTAG_RedBits` and `BIDTAG_BlueBits` (`rom/graphics/bestmodeida.c:196-200`), and the mode filter compares `disp.GreenBits` against `args->greenbits` (`:111-116`). However, the tag parser handles RedBits and BlueBits but has no GreenBits case (`:257-294`), leaving `args.greenbits` at its default value of four (`:232-243`) for every call. A requested minimum above four can therefore be under-enforced, allowing a mode with too few green bits; a requested minimum below four can be over-enforced, rejecting modes that satisfy the caller's lower requirement. **Affected configuration and trigger:** callers of the generic graphics.library `BestModeIDA()` vector that supply a `BIDTAG_GreenBits` value other than four; the checked-in `BestCModeIDTagList()` wrapper does not expose or set this tag, and repository search found no maintained direct GreenBits-tag caller, so current in-tree impact is unestablished. **Consequence:** the returned mode may violate the requested minimum or the function may reject an otherwise suitable mode. Parse `BIDTAG_GreenBits` into `args.greenbits` like the red and blue tags. **Confidence:** high for the ignored-tag path; no mode list was queried. Source-only.

## GD9619

**Duplicate of [GD9401](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9401).** Both entries describe the same signed-`WORD` inclusive endpoint narrowing in `BltTemplate()` before shared clipping, which discards a still-visible portion of an edge-crossing request. GD9401 is canonical and additionally covers the matching bitmap-to-RastPort wrappers and maintained caller paths. No separate defect remains under GD9619.

## GD9620

GD9620. **PaletteExtra pen-list traversal can index before its allocation when a shareable palette has more than 32,768 entries.** `ColorMap.Count` is `UWORD`, and `GetColorMap()` accepts an `ULONG` entry count before storing it in that field (`compiler/include/graphics/view.h:148-153`; `rom/graphics/getcolormap.c:43-81`). `AttachPalExtra()` sets the free-list head from the bitmap depth and stores each next index in `PalExtra_AllocList_Type`, which is signed `WORD` (`rom/graphics/graphics_intern.h:71-75`; `rom/graphics/attachpalextra.c:69-113`). At 32,769 entries with a bitmap depth of at least 16, the head is index 32,768. `ObtainPen()` and `ReleasePen()` cast that `UWORD` head to signed `PalExtra_AllocList_Type` when walking the list, yielding -32,768, then use it as an array subscript (`rom/graphics/obtainpen.c:98-126`; `rom/graphics/releasepen.c:74-89`). The allocated arrays begin at index zero, so the first list walk reads before `pe_AllocList`; in `ObtainPen()` this occurs for a specific-pen request that is not the head or when walking a shared list containing a high index. **Affected configuration and trigger:** a caller constructs a ColorMap with at least 32,769 entries, attaches it to a viewport whose bitmap depth is at least 16, then requests or releases a pen through a list-walking path. This is within the representable public `UWORD` count and `WORD` index types, though no maintained in-tree high-entry ColorMap caller was found; OpenScreen caps its palette at 256 entries (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1387-1409`). **Consequence:** palette bookkeeping reads out of bounds and can then make allocation/release decisions from an invalid link. Use an unsigned link type with an unambiguous sentinel or reject/limit counts to the signed-link range. **Confidence:** high for the signed conversion and negative subscript; no pen operation was run. Source-only.

## GD9621

GD9621. **`ObtainBestPenA()` can treat a visibly distant shared color as within tolerance after the distance/free-count product overflows.** The comparison multiplies `best_distance` by the `UWORD pe_NFree` using 32-bit `ULONG` arithmetic (`rom/graphics/obtainbestpena.c:117-125`; `ULONG` is fixed-width in `compiler/include/exec/types.h:39-43`). A reachable trigger uses a 32,769-entry ColorMap and bitmap depth >=16. First reserve the initial free-list head (entry 32,768) exclusively; this leaves 32,768 free entries and a valid head at 32,767. Then call `ObtainBestPenA()` for black to create the only shared pen at 32,767; `pe_SharableColors=32,768` and `pe_NFree=32,767`. Request RGB (105,244,246) under `PRECISION_GUI` (32): `color_distance()` returns 131,077 (`rom/graphics/color_support.c:16-61`), and its product with `pe_NFree` is 4,295,000,059, which wraps to 32,763. The comparison limit is 32² × 32,768 = 33,554,432, so the code considers black acceptable and increments its reference count without trying `ObtainPen()` for a free entry. **Affected configuration and trigger:** a public caller uses a ColorMap with at least 32,769 entries, bitmap depth >=16, one shared pen at an index representable by the signed list link, and many free entries, then requests a sufficiently distant color under a documented precision. Checked-in GUI-precision callers exist, but their maintained screen palettes are small; no in-tree caller combines this count and free-pen state. **Consequence:** the returned pen can have color error far beyond the requested precision, despite free pens being available. Widen the product before comparing. **Confidence:** high for the arithmetic wrap and branch result on the fixed 32-bit `ULONG` ABI; this trigger was checked against GD9620's signed-list boundary but no pen allocation was run. Source-only.

## GD9622 (withdrawn conditional candidate)

**Withdrawn:** the trigger requires `maxpen == -1` on an unattached ColorMap, but the public contract defines `maxpen` as the maximum palette entry and does not document negative sentinel values. Every checked-in `-1` caller supplies a screen ColorMap with PaletteExtra attached. The out-of-bounds behavior for that unsupported input is confirmed, but no supported API trigger was established; do not count GD9622 as an active bug candidate.


## GD9623

**IntelGMA crashes while registering stolen graphics memory if its memory-header allocation fails.** The selected IntelGMA initializer calls `ObtainGfxMemory(sd, 0, virtual, TRUE)` and passes its return directly to `AddTail()` without checking it (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_init.c:324-331`). For `stolen == TRUE`, `ObtainGfxMemory()` does not allocate backing system memory, but it still requires `AllocVec(sizeof(struct MemHeader), MEMF_CLEAR)`; on allocation failure it sets `success = FALSE`, frees the null/partial allocations, and returns NULL (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_memory.c:137-149,176-182`). Exec `AddTail()` immediately writes `node->ln_Succ`, `node->ln_Pred`, and the prior tail links without a null guard (`rom/exec/addtail.c:57-65`). The caller is reached after the selected startup path recognizes a supported Intel PCI graphics device and enters `G45_Init()` (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/intelgma_startup.c:251`; `intelgma_init.c:485-515`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly selected IntelGMA monitor driver on supported hardware, after PCI setup reaches stolen-memory registration, when the small `MemHeader` allocation fails (or the computed available stolen range is rejected). **Consequence:** `AddTail()` dereferences the NULL node during driver initialization, preventing clean initialization and potentially faulting the system. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked NULL result and `AddTail()` dereference; occurrence depends on the conditional allocation/range failure. No allocation failure, driver startup, or hardware was run; source-only.

## GD9624

**GD9624 — Failed graphics.library initialization leaves its embedded font semaphore linked into Exec's public list (conditional dangling-node access; high source confidence).** `GfxInit()` initializes `PrivGBase(GfxBase)->fontsem`, names it, and publishes it with `AddSemaphore()` before allocating `hash_table` and before several later failure points (`rom/graphics/graphics_init.c:59-80,101-119`). The semaphore is embedded in the graphics library base (`rom/graphics/graphics_intern.h:220`). Subsequent failures include the hash-table or optional region-pool allocation, ROM-font allocation, GfxRoot construction, and `driver_init()`. For an `INITLIB` failure, `_set_libinit()` calls the expunge/exit sets and returns failure (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:42-71`); generated `InitLib` then frees the library-base allocation (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1156-1173`). Graphics registers no matching init rollback or expunge handler that calls `RemSemaphore()`; its only init hook is `GfxInit()` (`rom/graphics/graphics_init.c:158`), and `rg` finds no `RemSemaphore` call in `rom/graphics`.

Exec `AddSemaphore()` enqueues the embedded node in `SysBase->SemaphoreList` (`rom/exec/addsemaphore.c:49-64`). `FindSemaphore()` traverses that list with `FindName()` (`rom/exec/findsemaphore.c:51-60`), whose loop dereferences each node's successor and name (`rom/exec/findname.c:82-91`). After the failed init frees the containing base, the public list therefore retains links into freed storage; a later traversal can read freed node/link/name memory, and later list operations can follow the dangling link. `RemSemaphore()` is the public removal operation (`rom/exec/remsemaphore.c:43-56`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** any selected `graphics.library` initialization where `GfxInit()` reaches `AddSemaphore()` and a later initialization step returns failure. This includes the immediately following hash-table allocation failure; the optional region-pool route depends on its build setting. **Consequence:** Exec's public semaphore list retains an embedded node after its storage is freed, making later semaphore-list traversal or mutation unsafe. **Confidence:** high for publication-before-failure, generated base free, and the missing removal path; no init failure or subsequent list traversal was induced. This is separate from GD2346's independently allocated ROM-font leak on overlapping later failure paths. Source-only.

## GD9625

**GD9625 — Failed graphics.library initialization leaves acquired external resources unreleased (conditional resource leak; high source confidence).** `GfxInit()` allocates `hash_table` (`rom/graphics/graphics_init.c:78-80`); when `REGIONS_USE_MEMPOOL` is enabled it can also create a region pool (`:90-99`). Later failure returns include `InitROMFont()` and `driver_init()` (`:103-119`). The failed generated `INITLIB` rollback frees the library base but does not free these independent allocations; Graphics has no matching init rollback handler. The standalone ROM-font allocation is detailed separately as GD2346, and the globally linked `fontsem` node is detailed as GD9624. `GfxRoot` is not counted as a base-owned leak here: `gfx.hidd` creates the `hw.gfx` singleton and registers it under the global hardware root.

`driver_init()` also successfully opens `gfx.hidd` and discards the returned library pointer (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:86-88`), then obtains eight HIDD attribute bases (`:93-101`). Later false returns include missing required attribute bases, missing `CLID_Hidd_GC`/`CLID_Hidd_Gfx` classes (`:103-122`), and failures constructing the software driver/display/object caches (`:123-161`). The function has no paired `CloseLibrary("gfx.hidd")` or `OOP_ReleaseAttrBase()` cleanup; OOP documents that each obtained attribute base should be released (`rom/oop/obtainattrbase.c:35-49`; `releaseattrbase.c:28-40`). Although `graphics.conf` declares `oop` as a relative library and generated rollback closes that reference, `oop.conf` is `noexpunge`; each acquired attribute base separately increments its IID bucket's reference count (`rom/oop/obtainattrbase.c:128-134`). The open-count rollback therefore does not undo those attrbase acquisitions. Some partially constructed display objects/caches are disposed locally; the distinct stale registered-driver case is detailed in GD9626.

The sole `driver_init()` caller is this initializer. The selected generated `INITLIB` rollback frees the failed `GfxBase` after `_set_libinit()` returns false (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:42-71`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1156-1173`), with no Graphics cleanup hook to release these resources. This leak is independent of GD9624's dangling public semaphore node and GD2346's standalone ROM-font allocation.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected `graphics.library` when initialization returns false after the hash table or optional region pool has been allocated; the `gfx.hidd` open-count and OOP attribute-base leaks specifically require `OpenLibrary("gfx.hidd")` to succeed followed by a later `driver_init()` failure. Missing class/attribute registration and object/cache allocation failures are source-level failure paths. **Consequence:** those allocations and references remain retained after the failed library base is freed. **Confidence:** high for the acquired resources and missing rollback; no init failure or reference count was exercised. Source-only.


## GD9627

**Finding:** Generic software `BltBitMap()` copies downward overlapping rectangles in the wrong row order.

**Source and trigger:** The generic implementation loops `y` from zero upward and copies each source row into the corresponding destination row (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:291-319`). Its overlap test only detects overlap between the source and destination scanline address ranges. For an in-place vertical move by one or more rows, adjacent scanlines do not overlap within a single iteration, so it does not save a source row before writing. On the next iteration, the source row may already contain the preceding destination row. `BltBitMap()` explicitly allows `destBitMap` to equal `srcBitMap` (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:55-95`).

**Reachable caller:** `MoveRaster()` invokes this path for a layerless RastPort with the same bitmap as source and destination (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:838-853`). For `ScrollRaster(..., dy=-1, ...)`, it copies the original top row down one row, proceeds to clear the vacated top strip, and returns success; the top-down copy can repeat the first row through the scrolled area. The Layer path also calls `BltBitMap()` for visible ordinary clip rectangles (`gfxfuncsupport.c:1006-1019`). Public ScrollRaster callers include console, text datatype, and Intuition code; this finding concerns the generic software blitter path and does not assert behavior of hardware-specific blitters.

**Consequence and confidence:** In-place downward scrolling can display duplicated/corrupted rows even without allocation failure. High confidence from the row loop and call arguments; no blit or scroll was run.

**Surviving review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md:L426`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L426).

## GD9626

**GD9626 — Graphics HIDD registration can leave stale driver nodes and objects in the permanent global hardware tree (conditional stale-object traversal; high source confidence).** `graphics.library`'s `driver_init()` adds its software `CLID_Hidd_Gfx` object with `HW_AddDriver()` to the `hw.gfx` subsystem, then, if display creation or either object-cache creation fails, directly calls `OOP_DisposeObject()` on the registered driver (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:123-156`). `HW_AddDriver()` allocates a `DriverNode` and appends it to the subsystem's driver list (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:185-199`). Its API explicitly says not to dispose the returned object directly; `HW_RemoveDriver()` is the operation that removes the node, disposes the object, and frees the node (`hwclass.c:157-160,266-295`). Direct disposal therefore leaves the node in the list with a pointer to the disposed object.

The subsystem list is globally reachable. `gfx.hidd` creates its `hw.gfx` subsystem object by adding it to the global `CLID_HW_Root` singleton (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_init.c:319-320`); its `GFXHW__Root__New()` retains the subsystem instance (`gfx_hwclass.c:12-35`), and the HIDD root code states the global root is never disposed (`rom/hidds/hidd/initcode.c:45-53`). `HW_EnumDrivers()` later passes every stored `driverObject` to its callback without checking object validity (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:353-372`). The selected SysExplorer path enumerates the global root, registers `CLID_HW_Gfx` for recursive enumeration, and calls `HW_EnumDrivers()` on that subsystem; its callback then dereferences the returned object's OOP class and queries attributes (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/sysexp_main.c:80-142,165-167,398-406`; `sysexp_library.c:327-332`). After a subsequent successful graphics.library initialization, a SysExplorer hardware scan can traverse the stale entry and operate on the disposed object; the retry ordering and scan are source-supported but unexecuted, as qualified below. The failed `graphics.library` initialization also leaves its direct `gfx.hidd` open reference outstanding (GD9625), so this path does not require unloading the HIDD class code.

There is a second trigger for the same missing-unregistration invariant: `GFX_ClassInit()` registers the `hw.gfx` singleton itself beneath the permanent global hardware root (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_init.c:319-320`), but `GFX_ClassFree()` does not call `HW_RemoveDriver()` for that instance before returning success (`:334-351`). `GFXHW` is the top-level OOP class for this `modtype=hidd` module and is included in genmodule's class list (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:1-12`; `tools/genmodule/config.c:464-489`). The generated expunge path runs the module `EXPUNGELIB` hooks then `_set_libexpunge()`, which calls the class-expunge set (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1557-1573`; `compiler/autoinit/functions.c:75-84`). The generated `GFXHW` class shutdown removes and disposes the registered OOP class (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:146-165`; `tools/genmodule/oopsupport.c:185-212`), while the global root's DriverNode remains. A subsequent global-root enumeration can reach the retained subsystem object after its class has been removed. The only checked-in direct `OpenLibrary("gfx.hidd")` caller is `graphics.library`, which does not close that reference; therefore no selected in-tree last-close/expunge trigger was established for this second case. It remains conditional on a direct client opening and closing `gfx.hidd` without the graphics.library pin.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** (1) selected graphics.library/gfx.hidd when `HW_AddDriver()` succeeds but a later display-object or planar/GC-cache allocation fails. The stale node remains in the global tree, but SysExplorer cannot perform its GUI scan while graphics.library is unavailable: `muimaster_init()` requires `OpenLibrary("graphics.library", 39)` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/muimaster_init.c:56-60`). The concrete later-scan sequence therefore requires a subsequent successful graphics.library initialization before SysExplorer starts. LDDemon can retry a resident library through `FindResident()`/`InitResident()` after a failed load/init (`rom/lddemon/lddemon.c:449-463`), and `InitResident()` adds the library only when its init returns non-NULL (`rom/exec/initresident.c:125-155`); this retry and later scan were not executed. (2) a direct gfx.hidd open/close lifecycle that reaches expunge without the graphics.library open reference. **Consequence:** the first path exposes a disposed OOP driver object through the global subsystem list; the second retains the subsystem instance in the global root after its class is removed. **Confidence:** high for both missing-unregistration paths and consequences; only the first has a checked-in selected caller chain to later enumeration. No allocation failure, library expunge, or SysExplorer scan was induced. Source-only.


## GD9630

**Finding:** TurboPrint source-hook graphics dumps retain `PDERR_INTERNALMEMORY` after successful temporary allocation and row processing.

**Source and trigger:** `Printer_Gfx_DumpRPort()` sets `err = PDERR_INTERNALMEMORY` as a default before allocating the temporary source-hook row and bitmap (`workbench/devs/printer/gfx.c:557-565`). When those allocations succeed, it reads the hook-provided rows and writes them into `src_bm` (`:569-582`), then the common path scales and transfers the output rows (`:594-656`). No assignment resets `err` after successful source-hook setup; `PRS_CLOSE` is called without assigning its result, and the function returns `err` (`:668-671`). The printer device propagates that value to `io_Error` (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:638-659`). The source-hook path is selected for `PRD_TPEXTDUMPRPORT` with the listed chunky/RGB modes (`gfx.c:277-293`) or by the `DRPA_SourceHook` tag (`:316-320`).

**Affected configuration and consequence:** a graphics printer request using a source hook whose row and source-bitmap allocations succeed, and whose subsequent print path runs, can process and attempt to transfer the image but still finish with `io_Error == PDERR_INTERNALMEMORY`. Callers therefore receive a failure result even though the source-hook setup succeeded and output may already have been sent. The code-level status mismatch is high confidence; no in-tree client of the TurboPrint extension was established in this pass. No printer request or allocation failure was run. Source-only.


## GD9631

**Finding:** Printer graphics memory-allocation failures can return success without rendering the bitmap.

**Source and trigger:** After `PRS_INIT` succeeds, the no-source-hook path uses the input RastPort bitmap directly (`workbench/devs/printer/gfx.c:544-545,590-592`). If allocation of the transfer row fails, it only logs a diagnostic (`:597,661-663`). If the row allocation succeeds but allocation of the scaled bitmap fails, it likewise only logs (`:601,657-659`). Neither branch assigns an error to `err`; the function then calls `PRS_CLOSE` without assigning its result and returns the unchanged zero from `PRS_INIT` (`:668-671`). The selected printer device caller copies that value to `io_Error` (`workbench/devs/printer/driver.c:644-659`). The driver module selects `gfx.c` (`workbench/devs/printer/mmakefile.src:3-10`).

**Affected configuration and consequence:** ordinary graphics dump requests without a source hook, after successful printer initialization, when either internal row or destination-bitmap allocation fails. The print loop is skipped, but the device reports success (`io_Error == 0`) despite producing no image rows. **Confidence:** high for the skipped output and unchanged success result; no allocation failure or printer request was induced. Source-only. This is distinct from GD9630, which retains a false `PDERR_INTERNALMEMORY` result on the source-hook path.

## GD9632

**System requester treats `MapRawKey()` buffer overflow as a successful conversion and reads an unwritten byte.** The requester allocates a one-byte `rawbuffer`, constructs an input event with `ie_Qualifier = 0`, and calls `MapRawKey()` with length one before testing the result as a Boolean (`rom/intuition/sysrequest_intern.c:216-230`). The selected built-in default keymap is installed as `DefaultKeymap` during keymap.library initialization (`rom/keymap/keymap_init.c:47-60`). In that keymap, raw key code `0x4c` (cursor up) is marked `ST|S` (`rom/keymap/defaultkeymap.c:105-110`); its unqualified string-table entry selects descriptor zero, whose declared output length is two bytes (`defaultkeymap.c:905-912,631-640`). `WriteToBuffer()` detects that the two-byte result exceeds the one-byte capacity before copying any output (`rom/keymap/maprawkey.c:140-167`; `rom/keymap/support.c:29-37`), and `MapRawKey()` returns `-1` on that overflow (`maprawkey.c:263-264`). Because `-1` is nonzero, the requester enters the branch and compares the untouched `rawbuffer[0]` with its configured true/false response characters (`sysrequest_intern.c:231-247`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Intuition system requester receives raw key code `0x4c` while left-command is held, with keymap.library using its selected built-in default keymap. The requester synthesizes the conversion event with qualifier zero, so the default cursor-up escape string is the concrete two-byte mapping. **Consequence:** the unwritten stack byte can accidentally match the configured true/false response and accept or reject the requester. Require a positive one-byte result before inspecting the output. **Confidence:** high for the selected mapping, overflow return, no-write behavior, and Boolean check; the particular response depends on the stack byte matching a configured character. No requester or key event was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9633

**Disposition:** Withdrawn as a duplicate of GD6073. The unchecked `pg_Gauges` allocation followed by indexed initialization is consolidated into GD6073.

## GD9635

**Decoration marks an image usable after the Picture datatype fails to read its pixels.** `GetImageFromFile()` allocates a cleared `DecorImage` pixel buffer, invokes `PDTM_READPIXELARRAY`, ignores its return value, and unconditionally sets `di->ok = TRUE` (`workbench/libs/decorator/decorimagefuncs.c:335-351`; `NewDecorImageContainer()` uses `MEMF_CLEAR` for the data at `:233-244`). In the selected Picture datatype, `PDT_ReadPixelArray()` returns FALSE if it cannot obtain a source buffer (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1231-1240`); for a bitmap-backed source with no existing chunky buffer, that conversion returns FALSE when `AllocSrcBuffer()` fails (`colorhandling.c:501-516,316-323`). The remapping helper later copies the zero-filled `di->data` and sets the screen image's `ok` flag from the successful destination allocation (`workbench/libs/decorator/decorimagefuncs.c:402-427`), so the image can be accepted and rendered as blank on a truecolor screen.

Check the pixel-array method result and leave the image invalid or fail loading when it returns FALSE. **Affected configuration and trigger:** builds containing `decorator.library`/`decortheme.library` and the Picture datatype, when Decoration loads a bitmap-backed theme asset whose Picture object lacks a chunky source buffer and allocation of the temporary conversion buffer fails; the incorrect `ok` state is observable when the asset is remapped for a truecolor screen. **Consequence:** the theme asset is treated as successfully decoded and rendered from zero-filled pixels instead of reporting/handling the decode failure. **Confidence:** high for the ignored FALSE result and placeholder promotion; requires the described bitmap-source conversion failure and truecolor remap. The Picture datatype target is not in the checked-in default aggregate; it is included by the i386-PC floppy manifest (`arch/i386-pc/boot/floppy/mmakefile.src:55-60`), so this is conditional on builds that include it. No allocation failure, theme load, or rendering was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9643

**Radeon publishes its VRAM MemHeader without the magic required for managed-memory dispatch.** When `Card.FbUsableSize` is nonzero, `BitmapInit()` fills the embedded header's node, sets `MEMF_CHIP | MEMF_MANAGED | MEMF_PUBLIC`, installs `mhe_UserData` and the `mhe_Avail` callback, and appends the header to `SysBase->MemList` (`workbench/hidds/radeon/bitmap.c:401-438`). It never assigns `mhe_Magic`. The HIDD module configuration selects resident auto-init for this module (`tools/genmodule/config.c:812-830`), and Exec `MakeLibrary()` clear-allocates its base (`rom/exec/makelibrary.c:109`), so this field remains zero. `IsManagedMem()` requires both `MEMF_MANAGED` and `MEMHEADER_EXT_MAGIC` (`compiler/include/exec/memheaderext.h:23,49-59`). Exec's `nommu_AvailMem()` therefore takes the ordinary MemHeader branch rather than invoking Radeon `mh_Avail()` (`rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:328-367,384-428`); the clear legacy `mh_Upper`, `mh_Lower`, `mh_First`, and `mh_Free` fields make this published header contribute no Radeon VRAM to CHIP free, total, or largest queries. Set the extension magic before publishing the header, and initialize the legacy fields consistently if they are still needed for fallback compatibility.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional Radeon HIDD on a supported card when detected usable framebuffer memory is nonzero and Exec memory queries include `MEMF_CHIP`; PPC Sam440 and CHRP/Efika have Radeon HIDD build overlays (`arch/ppc-sam440/hidd.radeon/mmakefile.src:5-7`; `arch/ppc-chrp/hidd.radeon/mmakefile.src:5-7`). No memory query or HIDD was run. **Confidence:** high for the omitted magic assignment, clear base initialization, and managed-dispatch predicate; the consequence is limited to Exec's accounting of Radeon VRAM through this MemHeader. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9645

**The vertical Gauge draw path divides by a zero maximum.** `Gauge__OM_NEW()` initializes `max` to 100, then accepts any `MUIA_Gauge_Max` tag without validating it; `Gauge__OM_SET()` also stores a changed maximum without validation (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/gauge.c:45-75,165-175`). The horizontal `MUIM_Draw` branch explicitly returns a zero fill width when `data->max == 0`, but the vertical branch calculates `h = _mheight(obj) * data->current / data->max` without the same guard (`:316-327,346-355`). `current` is clamped to `max` after initial tags and updates, so a zero maximum leaves both values zero but does not prevent the vertical division. The maintained vertical SysMon gauge sets `MUIA_Gauge_Max` to 1000 (`workbench/system/SysMon/processor_gauge.c:53-59`); DiskInfo's vertical gauge relies on the default max of 100 (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/DiskInfo/diskinfo.c:467-472`). The optional Zune MUI debug test (selected by `developer/debug/test/Zune/mmakefile.src:6`) provides a concrete buildable caller: it creates a vertical divided Gauge and updates its maximum from an editable digit string (`developer/debug/test/Zune/test.c:48-50,1508-1526,2313-2315,3734-3745,3847-3853`). The string accepts `0`; `NumericSetMax()` divides that value by `NUMERIC_DIV` and sets the Gauge maximum to zero. OM_SET clamps Current to zero, then the next vertical draw evaluates `0 / 0`. Guard the vertical calculation like the horizontal path or reject zero maxima. **Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting `muimaster`'s Gauge class, when a vertical gauge is constructed or updated with `MUIA_Gauge_Max = 0` and reaches `MUIM_Draw`; the attribute is accepted by the class and the public header declares it as a `LONG` without a positive-only constraint (`classes/gauge.h:23-25`). The optional Zune MUI debug test exposes the trigger through its max field; the checked-in production SysMon and DiskInfo callers use nonzero maxima. **Consequence:** integer division by zero while drawing, causing an architecture-dependent arithmetic exception or task fault. **Confidence:** high for zero-value acceptance, the unguarded division and debug-test setter path; no GUI, object, or exception was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9646

**Panel drag images leak their allocated descriptor on every delete.** `Panel__MUIM_CreateDragImage()` allocates a `struct MUI_DragImage` with `AllocVec()` and returns it even when bitmap allocation fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panel.c:1271-1297`). `Panel__MUIM_DeleteDragImage()` releases `msg->di->bm` but never frees `msg->di` (`:1299-1302`). The sibling Area implementation frees both the bitmap and descriptor (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.c:2246-2254`), confirming the missing ownership release. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9647

**PanelGroup silently leaves a child unmanaged when tracking-node allocation fails.** During `PanelGroup__MUIM_PanelGroup_ScanPanels()`, each accepted Panel child increments a local count and calls `MUIM_PanelGroup_AddPanel`, but the method result is ignored (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/panelgroup.c:426-440`). `AddPanel` returns FALSE when `mui_alloc_struct(struct PanelNode)` fails and otherwise adds the tracking node (`:447-472`). Later collapse/expand/toggle/state operations find and iterate only `data->panel_list` (`:523-553,573-615,629-672`), so that child is never managed; `GetPanelState` reports an untracked child as expanded even if its Panel is collapsed. `ScanPanels` then sets `data->panel_count` to the number of accepted children, masking the missing node (`:438-440`).

This occurs during construction before `ScanPanels` returns. The maintained tutorial uses PanelGroup with multiple Panel children and invokes bulk collapse/expand operations on the sidebar (`workbench/libs/muimaster/tutorial/examples/PanelGroup.c:107-155,36-40`). **Consequence:** the affected child is omitted from bulk state changes and cannot be toggled through PanelGroup methods; querying it returns the default Expanded state. **Confidence:** high for the allocation-failure handling gap and resulting omission; allocation failure was not induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
## GD9648

**MUI class creation failure paths leak acquired superclass references, and built-in lookups fail to retain each returned reference.** When `supermcc` is NULL, `MUI_CreateCustomClass()` obtains `super` with `MUI_GetClass()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_createcustomclass.c:59-64`). For a non-builtin class, `MUI_GetClass()` reaches `ZUNE_GetExternalClass()`, which opens the class library and stores that open reference in `mcc_Module` (`mui_getclass.c:67-74`; `support_classes.c:88-126`). If allocating the `MUI_CustomClass` record fails, the function returns immediately; if `MakeClass()` fails, it frees only the record and returns (`mui_createcustomclass.c:66-76`). Neither failure calls `MUI_FreeClass(super)`, whose external-class branch closes the library reference stored in `cl_Dispatcher.h_Data` (`mui_freeclass.c:55-66`). The successful deletion path does release this superclass reference (`mui_deletecustomclass.c:54-63`). The built-in class factory has the same rollback gap: `ZUNE_MakeBuiltinClass()` obtains a non-root superclass through `MUI_GetClass()` and then calls `MakeClass()`, but if `MakeClass()` returns NULL it closes only the extra muimaster open and never releases `supercl` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/support_classes.c:190-218`). This can also leave an external superclass module open when the failed built-in class names an external superclass.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI/Zune builds creating a custom class by name from an external class library, when either the custom-class record allocation or `MakeClass()` fails after the external superclass lookup succeeds; also, when first creating a built-in class whose non-root superclass lookup succeeds but its `MakeClass()` call fails. **Consequence:** the acquired superclass reference is not released. For external superclasses this leaves the module open and repeated failures can prevent expunge; for built-in superclasses it can leave the superclass reference count elevated. The separate `supermcc` argument path does not call `MUI_GetClass()`; the complete checked-in executable caller search found only the IPv4 and IPv6 Network Preferences window classes, both subclassing the shared `PAWinClass` created with `base == NULL` (`workbench/prefs/network/Modules/IPv4/ipv4_win.c:221-229`; IPv6 `:213-221`; `protocols.c:327-333`). Their normal `MUI_DeleteCustomClass()` cleanup calls `MUI_FreeClass(super)`, whose non-builtin branch calls `CloseLibrary(cl->cl_Dispatcher.h_Data)`; `CloseLibrary(NULL)` is a no-op (`rom/exec/closelibrary.c:71-79`). No separate selected defect is established for those `supermcc` callers.

**Confidence:** high for the missing rollback in both factories; no allocation or class creation failure was induced. These failure paths are conditional and no maintained caller deliberately induces them. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9649

**MUI_RequestA() writes past its button array for requesters with more than 32 gadgets.** The function declares `req_but[32]` with a comment that there should not be more than 32 buttons, then splits the caller-supplied `gadgets` string at each `|` and stores each successful `SimpleButton()` result at `req_but[num_gads]` without checking the index (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_request.c:105,208-233`). `num_gads` is incremented for every segment and is not capped elsewhere. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**Repeated MUI_GetClass() calls do not retain built-in class references.** `ZUNE_GetBuiltinClass()` initializes the built-in class reference count only when it creates a class; when `ZUNE_FindBuiltinClass()` finds an existing class, it returns it without incrementing `cl_Dispatcher.h_Data` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/support_classes.c:223-245`). `MUI_GetClass()` returns that pointer and documents that callers must call `MUI_FreeClass()` when done (`mui_getclass.c:30-50,67-74`). `MUI_FreeClass()` decrements the same counter and, at zero, removes the class and calls `FreeClass()`; Intuition documents that a successful `FreeClass()` frees the class and invalidates its pointer (`mui_freeclass.c:51-78`; `rom/intuition/freeclass.c:75-92,101-106`). The API is obsolete but still exported and used internally. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**A square truecolor gradient at 135 degrees divides by zero.** The image-spec parser accepts decimal angles through `StrToLong()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/imspec_gradient.c:45-67`), and the Zune Prefs slider allows 0–179 (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/imageadjust.c:615-619`).
