At that angle the renderer sets `yw = height`, so for a square draw rectangle `t = -height * vx + width * vy = 0` (`:347-351,375-424`). The per-pixel loop divides by `t` (`:443-464`). The same angle is reachable through the selected image-adjust slider: its hook serializes the value as a `7:` or `8:` spec and applies it to the preview image (`imageadjust.c:84-110,832-840`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** muimaster with CyberGraphX truecolor rendering, when a normal draw of a scaled or tiled 135-degree gradient has equal width and height. The Zune Prefs slider can generate this angle; other callers can also provide it directly. **Consequence:** the renderer executes integer division by zero during drawing, normally causing a task exception or abort on targets that trap it. **Confidence:** high for the selected slider path, integer direction components, zero denominator, and reachable division; no gradient was rendered. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9658

**CursorFB narrows computed bitmap-operation bounds to WORD before testing cursor overlap.** PutImage and other CursorFB wrappers compute the far edge as `x + width - 1` / `y + height - 1`, then pass it through `CFB_REMOVE` to `GfxDisplay_CursorIntersects()`, whose rectangle parameters are signed 16-bit `WORD` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_cursorfbclass.c:54-56,200-213`; `gfx_displayclass.c:296-307`; `gfx_intern.h:389`). The public PutImage method itself uses signed WORD for the origin and extent (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:520`), while bitmap dimensions are UWORD (`gfx_intern.h:183`). An operation beginning near the positive WORD limit can therefore have a valid right/bottom edge above 32767 which narrows back to a negative WORD on the supported two's-complement targets. For example, x=32760 and width=16 produces right=32775; the narrowed right edge compares less than a cursor at x=32760, so the overlap check returns FALSE even though the operation covers it. The selected generic `BM__Hidd_BitMap__PutImage()` accepts the 16-pixel operation, iterates its 0..15 local x range and forwards each `msg->x + x` through the WORD-coordinate `HIDD_BM_PutPixel()` method (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:2787,2820-2823,2852-2855,2889-2893`; `gfx_intern.h:474`). Its first eight pixels, including the cursor at x=32760, remain representable and are written while the cursor stays drawn; later x coordinates narrow at the pixel call. This is sufficient to overwrite cursor backing pixels while the saved-under buffer remains stale. The wrapper also has matching bounded GetImage paths that can include a still-drawn cursor when their overlap endpoint narrows past the cursor. The selected generic graphics library forwards rectangle blits through HIDD PutImage with WORD extents (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:469-472,459-461`). Use a wider coordinate type for intersection bounds or clamp the rectangle without narrowing before testing. **Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics builds using the generic CursorFB wrapper, on a displayable bitmap at least 32768 pixels wide (or high), when a bounded operation starts at 32760 with a positive extent of at least 9 and overlaps the cursor. Cursor rendering clips at the bitmap edge (gfx_displayclass.c:163-173), so a cursor at 32760 can remain visible through pixel 32767 on a 32768-pixel bitmap even though its full rectangle extends farther. The selected generic PutImage path writes the first eight pixels through 32767 before later coordinates narrow, so that visible part can be overwritten while the overlap endpoint has already narrowed negative. No graphics operation was run. **Confidence:** high for the source-level narrowing and selected generic PutImage caller; manifestation depends on the target signed-word conversion and a large bitmap/display. Source-only.


## GD9659

**Deleting a custom MUI subclass closes its supplied superclass library without acquiring that library reference.** `MUI_CreateCustomClass()` takes the superclass directly from `supermcc->mcc_Class` when its `supermcc` argument is non-NULL; this branch does not call `OpenLibrary()` or otherwise retain the superclass module (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_createcustomclass.c:59-64`). The child class stores only the superclass class pointer (`:83-85`), and `cl->cl_Dispatcher.h_Data` is set to the child creator's `base` argument (`:93`). Later, successful `MUI_DeleteCustomClass()` first frees the child class and unconditionally calls `MUI_FreeClass(super)` (`mui_deletecustomclass.c:51-59`). For a non-builtin custom superclass, `MUI_FreeClass()` interprets that superclass's `cl_Dispatcher.h_Data` as an acquired library reference and calls `CloseLibrary()` on it (`mui_freeclass.c:81-86`). But when that superclass was itself created with `MUI_CreateCustomClass(base, ...)`, its `h_Data` is the caller-supplied base, and the child creation path acquired no matching open reference. Deleting the child therefore consumes the parent's owner's library open count. Exec's `CloseLibrary()` dispatches to that library's close vector (`rom/exec/closelibrary.c:44-64`); the generated module close code decrements `lib_OpenCnt` and calls expunge when the count reaches zero with `LIBF_DELEXP` set (`tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1463-1518`). Thus if the owner still relies on its open reference and has requested delayed expunge, deleting the child can unload the parent module while its `MUI_CustomClass` and class are still owned.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** muimaster clients that create a parent custom class with a non-NULL library `base`, then create a child with `MUI_CreateCustomClass(NULL, NULL, parent_mcc, ...)` and delete that child while retaining the parent. The checked-in non-NULL `supermcc` callers are IPv4/IPv6 Network Preferences, whose shared parent class is created with `base == NULL`, so they do not establish this trigger (`workbench/prefs/network/protocols.c:327-333`; `Modules/IPv4/ipv4_win.c:221-229`; IPv6 `:213-221`). No in-tree non-NULL-base `supermcc` call was found. **Consequence:** the parent's library can be prematurely closed, with module unload possible if expunge is pending; subsequent parent-class dispatch or cleanup can use code or state from an unloaded module. **Confidence:** high for the unmatched close in the public API path; no runtime class deletion or module expunge was performed. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9681

**MUI List reports successful setup when an embedded image object's Setup fails.** `List__MUIM_Setup()` iterates the registered `ListImage` objects and calls `DoSetupMethod(li->obj, muiRenderInfo(obj))` without checking the return value, then returns success (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:1761-1798`). List ignores that result and still reports successful setup. The later inherited Bitmap draw checks for a bitmap and skips drawing when it is absent (`classes/bitmap.c:515-555`). **Consequence:** the Trident icon is missing while the List and application continue as though its embedded image setup succeeded; other subclasses may have different consequences, so no broader draw-time fault is claimed. The post-setup `MUIM_List_CreateImage` path also returns its handle without checking the child setup result (`list.c:3229-3250`). ## GD9683

**Finding:** `InitIIH()` writes `MouseBoundsActiveFlag` through `iihdata` after freeing that structure on its failure path.

**Source and trigger:** Whenever `iihdata` allocation succeeds but later setup does not return the handler, control reaches `FreeMem(iihdata, sizeof(struct IIHData))` and then immediately assigns `iihdata->MouseBoundsActiveFlag = FALSE` (`rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:77-89,162-168`). Failure to create the message port, either pool, or both system gadgets reaches this shared tail. The assignment is therefore a write through a pointer after its allocation has been released.

**Affected configuration and consequence:** Intuition input-handler initialization failure after allocating `IIHData`. The write targets freed storage and can corrupt an allocator free structure or memory subsequently reused at that address; exact manifestation depends on allocator state. This is separate from GD5772's pool leak: the use-after-free also occurs on other setup failures, including port or gadget construction failure. **Confidence:** high for the free-before-write ordering; no allocation failure was induced.


## GD9684

**Network Preferences removes live protocol-window objects, then drops custom-class handles after `FreeClass()` refuses to destroy their classes.** `NetPEditor` creates each registered protocol window with `NewObject(ph->ph_WinClass->mcc_Class, ...)` and stores the objects in `data->netped_protoWindows[]` (`workbench/prefs/network/netpeditor.c:1274-1282,1690-1693`). During `MUIM_Cleanup`, it removes those windows from the application (`:2058-2062`) and then calls each loaded protocol module's shutdown hook before freeing the shared parent `PAWinClass` (`:2081-2090`). `Group__MUIM_Remove()` calls `MUIM_Cleanup` on a child and removes it from the group; it does not dispose the object (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:761-781`). `Application__OM_DISPOSE()` later disposes only windows still in `app_WindowFamily` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:847-879`), and NetPEditor has no separate dispose call for its saved protocol-window pointers; these detached instances therefore remain alive during module shutdown. The IPv4 and IPv6 shutdown hooks call `MUI_DeleteCustomClass()` and unconditionally set their `Net4WinClass`/`Net6WinClass` globals to NULL (`Modules/IPv4/ipv4_win.c:232-238`; `Modules/IPv6/ipv6_win.c:224-230`). `MUI_DeleteCustomClass()` only frees its class record and superclass reference when `FreeClass()` succeeds; on failure it returns FALSE and retains both (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_deletecustomclass.c:49-63`). Intuition documents that `FreeClass()` fails while class instances remain alive (`rom/intuition/freeclass.c:28-48`). The caller ignores that failure and loses its only class-record pointer; the parent-class cleanup then also encounters still-live subclass instances/classes.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Network Preferences when IPv4 or IPv6 protocol modules have registered their custom window classes and `NetPEditor` enters `MUIM_Cleanup` with the protocol-window instances still alive. **Consequence:** custom class records and superclass references remain allocated; the detached window objects are not disposed by the group removal path, and their class handles are discarded. The Network Preferences main path exits after application disposal (`workbench/prefs/network/main.c:72-77`), so this is an in-process cleanup leak reclaimed at process exit; no persistence across invocations or module-unload fault is claimed. **Confidence:** high for the failed class free and lost handle given the documented `FreeClass()` contract and selected cleanup order. No app teardown was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9685

**HDToolBox ignores mountlist output errors and can leave a partial file.** The Create Mountlist menu hook opens the selected pathname with `MODE_NEWFILE`, then emits the device/filesystem header and mount parameters through two `VFPrintf()` calls whose return values are discarded; it also ignores `Close()` before optionally copying an icon (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/gui.c:1279-1297,1349-1379`). `VFPrintf()` returns -1 when `FPutC()` reports an output error (`rom/dos/vfprintf.c:40-95`), and the hook discards both results as well as `Close()`'s BOOL result. A failed first or second formatted write therefore leaves the newly created/replaced mountlist incomplete while the hook reports no failure. DOS documents that `Close()` may report a buffered-write error, but the selected implementation overwrites the `Flush()` result with the later `ACTION_END` result (`rom/dos/close.c:19-30,68-72`); the finding does not rely on a close-time flush error being observable. The menu item is enabled for a selected non-table partition and dispatches this hook (`gui.c:1766,1846-1848,2287-2289`). Check both formatted-write results and the close result, and remove or clearly report a partial output file on failure.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable optional HDToolBox program (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/mmakefile.src:20-25`; its parent `workbench-tools` dependency is commented at `:20`) when the user creates a mountlist for a selected partition and a DOS write or final buffered close fails. **Consequence:** an incomplete mountlist remains at the chosen path after `MODE_NEWFILE` has replaced or created it; later use can omit required device or geometry settings, and the user receives no write-failure indication from this hook. **Confidence:** high for ignored error returns and the partial-file path; the trigger requires an output failure. No file, requester or write error was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9686

**HDToolBox passes a freed mountlist pathname to the optional icon writer.** `createml_function()` allocates `pathname`, opens the mountlist, then immediately releases the pathname buffer with `FreeMem(pathname, len)` (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/gui.c:1286-1298`). If the file opened and the default mountlist icon is available, the later icon-copy branch passes that freed pointer to `PutDiskObject(pathname, icon)` (`gui.c:1373-1379`). `PutDiskObject()` synchronously forwards the name to `PutIconTags()` (`workbench/libs/icon/putdiskobject.c:42-50`); the named-output path uses it in `OpenIcon(name, ...)` and, after a successful write, in `Lock(name)`/`FilePart(name)` for Workbench notification (`workbench/libs/icon/puticontaglist.c:124-145`). Keep the pathname alive through the icon operation and check its result.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable optional HDToolBox target (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/mmakefile.src:20-25`) when creating a mountlist while `ENVARC:Sys/def_Mountlist` can be loaded. **Consequence:** the icon writer receives a pointer after its allocation has been freed; depending on reuse of that block, icon creation can fail, use a corrupted pathname, or access invalid memory. Its BOOL result is also ignored. **Confidence:** high for the free-before-use call sequence and synchronous pathname consumption; no mountlist or icon operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9687

**VGAGfx leaks its copied cursor bitmap when graphics-library handover removes the boot display.** `VGAGfxDisplay__Hidd_Display__SetCursorShape()` allocates a private `curs_width * curs_height` pixel copy and stores it in the driver class's shared `mouseShape` state (`arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_displayclass.c:264-287`; state at `vgagfx_intern.h:26-46`). Replacing a shape frees the previous copy, but the VGA display method list contains no `Dispose` override and the display class defines no cleanup method for the current copy (`vgagfx.conf:35-50`; `VGAGfx__Root__Dispose()` also does not free `mouseShape`, `vgagfx_hiddclass.c:120-127`). Graphics-library `display_Expunge()` performs that removal notification and then disposes the HIDD display object (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:241-252`). The VGA boot display is expressly registered with `DDRV_BootMode`; graphics-library handover can expunge it once it is inactive (`vgagfx_init.c:118-136`; `graphics_driver.c:262-283`). Consequently the last copied shape allocation remains allocated when that display is removed; dispose the copy as part of display teardown and clear the saved pointer/dimensions. **Affected configuration and trigger:** i386-PC or x86-64-PC builds selecting VGAGfx as a boot-mode display, with Intuition having installed a pointer shape, followed by another graphics driver handing over the inactive VGA display. **Consequence:** the current copied cursor bitmap allocation is leaked when the display is disposed. **Confidence:** high for allocation ownership, selected monitor-install/removal callbacks and display disposal; occurrence requires the stated boot-mode handover. No pointer shape or display handover was run; source-only.


## GD9688

**X11 cursor-shape updates leak the previous server cursor.** In the selected hardware-cursor path, `X11Display__Hidd_Display__SetCursorShape()` creates a new cursor with `XcursorImageLoadCursor()` and overwrites `data->cursor` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11gfx_displayclass.c:605-637`). The X11 worker then applies the new cursor to every registered window with `XDefineCursor()` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11.c:570-585`). The X11 host-function table has no `XFreeCursor` entry, and no checked-in X11 driver path frees a cursor; teardown eventually closes the shared display connection (`x11_init.c:234`), which releases its remaining server resources only when that connection shuts down. Each successful shape change therefore loses the previous cursor resource while keeping the replacement. Intuition calls this method when installing a new pointer shape (`rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:1954-1955`); repeated pointer changes are thus a maintained route, not only an external method call. Free the prior cursor after all windows have switched, and handle the initial cursor consistently.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** hosted X11 with the selected default `X11SOFTMOUSE=0` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11.h:37`), after a display is created and Intuition installs different pointer shapes while the X11 connection remains open. **Consequence:** one X server cursor resource per successful replacement remains allocated until connection teardown, allowing repeated pointer changes to accumulate server-side resources. **Confidence:** high for the replacement and lack of a release path in the selected driver; server resource limits and eventual operational impact depend on the X server. No cursor update or X11 server resource was exercised; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9689

**X11 display construction leaks the VidMode mode list after copying its entries.** When `OPTION_FORCESTDMODES` is clear, `X11Display__Root__New()` calls `XF86VidModeGetAllModeLines()` and stores the returned `XF86VidModeModeInfo **` in local `modes` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11gfx_displayclass.c:280-288`). It copies each selected mode's fields into the separately allocated `resolution` tags, then frees `resolution` and `mode_tags` on the normal path, but never releases `modes` before returning (`:310-383,446-448`). The allocation is also not released on the mode-tag allocation failure or unsupported-color-model exits (`:358-365,414-425`). No display was created; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9690

**X11 display construction dereferences a failed secondary display connection.** `X11Display__Root__New()` first calls `initx11stuff()`, which opens and retains the driver's primary X connection (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11gfx_displayclass.c:274-278`; `arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11_init.c:127-133`). It then separately calls `XOpenDisplay(NULL)` into local `disp` and unconditionally passes that result to `XDefaultScreen()` (`x11gfx_displayclass.c:282-283`). This is independent of the VidMode option because `XDefaultScreen()` is called before the option check. **Consequence:** the constructor calls into Xlib with a NULL display and can fault or abort display construction instead of returning a clean failure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked call sequence; host connection-failure handling was not exercised. No X11 connection or display was opened; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9693

**MUI custom scrollbar arrows ignore the selected image frame on low-depth screens.** `DrawAlphaStateImageToRP()` advances the raw ARGB pointer for `IDS_SELECTED`, and its high-depth path draws from that adjusted pointer. For screens below 15 bits per pixel, however, it draws from the converted `ni->bitmap` at source coordinate `(0, 0)` for every state (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/image.c:486-507`). `GetImageFromFile()` creates that converted bitmap from the complete image when the selected screen depth is below 15 (`workbench/libs/muimaster/datatypescache.c:398-430`). The Image class treats each prop-arrow image as four horizontal frames: its sizing uses `ni->w >> 2`, while its raw-data offsets select later frames (`image.c:351-358,486-499`). `Scrollbar__OM_NEW()` creates these prop-image children with `MUIA_InputMode, MUIV_InputMode_RelVerify` and `MUIA_Image_Prop` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/scrollbar.c:78-100`); the Image class maps `MUIA_Selected` to `IDS_SELECTED` (`image.c:170-176`). Thus, when a custom scrollbar arrow is pressed on a low-depth screen, the bitmap branch still displays the first (normal) frame instead of the selected frame. Use a state-dependent source X offset for the converted bitmap blit.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI with custom scrollbars enabled, a low-depth screen (below 15 bits per pixel), and a prop-arrow theme image with distinct horizontal state frames; the selected state is reached during the arrow's rel-verify press. **Consequence:** the arrow does not display its selected/pressed artwork. **Confidence:** high for the ignored state offset and caller/state path; no GUI or low-depth display was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9694

**A negative custom-scrollbar tile size makes the Prop renderer loop indefinitely.** `ReadPropConfig()` accepts signed values for recognized tile-size keys through `GetIntegers()`/`atol()` without validating that the parsed sizes are positive (`workbench/libs/muimaster/datatypescache.c:295-310,451-520`). A valid one-value `ContainerHorTile = -1` line, for example, sets the tile offset and size to `-1`. The custom Prop renderer uses that size as `sw` and the positive interior width as `dw` in `WriteTiledImageHorizontal()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/prop.c:666-680`). That helper only rejects zero sizes; with `sw == -1`, it sets `ddw` negative and executes `w -= ddw`, so positive `w` grows and the `while (w > 0)` loop never terminates (`prop.c:520-552`). The vertical path has the same defect for a negative height (`:555-587,638-661`). `dt_load_picture()` accepts `prop.config`/`config` files through `ReadPropConfig()` and marks the result `MODE_PROP` (`datatypescache.c:751-762`); AROS installs `CustomPropRenderFunc` for a custom-scrollbar Prop whose background is such a bitmap (`prop.c:885-920`). Reject nonpositive tile sizes while loading the configuration, and guard the tiling helpers against negative dimensions.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** AROS MUI with custom scrollbar style enabled and a property-image `prop.config`/`config` containing a negative horizontal or vertical tile size, when the corresponding custom Prop has positive interior area and is drawn. **Consequence:** the drawing task remains in the tiling loop and the custom scrollbar render does not finish. **Confidence:** high for signed config acceptance, selected callback wiring, and loop progress; no custom theme was loaded or rendered. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9695

**Hiding a dragged MUI Slider leaves it tracking pointer movement.** When a knob is selected, `Slider__MUIM_HandleEvent()` adds `IDCMP_MOUSEMOVE` to the Window event handler and sets `MUIA_Pressed` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/slider.c:463-475`). Hiding the object only hides its knob image and clears the cached offset; `Slider__MUIM_Hide()` does not remove the handler or clear the pressed state (`:325-338`). The supported `MUIA_ShowMe = FALSE` path sends `MUIM_Hide` but deliberately does not send `MUIM_Cleanup` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/area.c:608-630`), and a hidden child can remain set up in its open Window. Hiding a Group also propagates `MUIM_Hide` to its active/visible children without cleanup (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:2949-2987`), so the same state is reachable by hiding an ancestor. The handler remains on `wd_EHList`: `Window__MUIM_RemEventHandler()` is only called during Slider cleanup or pointer release (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:4011-4022`; `slider.c:257-269,496-505`). Window input dispatch invokes registered handlers based on their event mask without filtering hidden objects (`window.c:2416-2430`). Consequently, subsequent pointer movement still reaches the hidden Slider's `IDCMP_MOUSEMOVE` branch and can change its Numeric value (`slider.c:510-548`); the pointer release path can eventually clear the state, but until then the hidden control tracks input. On show, it may also retain a pressed appearance if release was not delivered to it. Cancel the active drag and remove the mouse-move subscription when hiding, then restore the base event mask and pressed state.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** MUI with the Slider class selected, while its Window remains open; the user begins dragging the knob and application code hides the Slider (directly or through a hidden ancestor) before pointer release. **Consequence:** the hidden control continues to update its Numeric value on pointer movement and can retain stale pressed state until release or cleanup. **Confidence:** high for the registered-handler and hide/event-dispatch sequence; no GUI event was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9701

## GD9718

**Indexed summary:** NListview never attaches its configured initial scrollbars during setup.

**Source and trigger:** `mNLV_New()` initializes `Vert_Attached` and `Horiz_Attached` to FALSE, creates the scrollbar objects, and stores the requested scrollbar modes (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlistview_mcc/NListview.c:570-617`). During `MUIM_Setup`, `mNLV_Setup()` explicitly sets `data->SETUP = FALSE` and calls `NLV_Scrollers()` before delegating setup (`:655-684`). For AROS, `NLV_Scrollers()` sets `safeNotifies = FALSE` because AROS is in the non-AmigaOS branch, then forces both modes to `Always` (`:323-327,346-348,390-392`) and derives the attach bits. But its only application path queues `MUIM_NListview_SetScrollers` only when `data->SETUP == TRUE` (`:443-447`); on this initial setup call the condition is false. `mNLV_Setup()` sets `SETUP` true only after the superclass setup returns, and has no second scrollbar evaluation (`:680-684`). The scrollbar objects therefore remain detached on initial setup, even though this AROS path forces them to always-visible; they are only attached if a later scrollbar-attribute change reevaluates them after setup. **Affected configuration:** NListview on AROS when first set up without a later `MUIA_NListview_Vert_ScrollBar` or `MUIA_NListview_Horiz_ScrollBar` change. **Consequence:** the configured always-visible scrollbars are absent after initial setup, leaving the list without those controls until another attribute update causes the deferred attachment path to run. **Confidence: high** for the setup ordering and missing queue call; no GUI was opened.

**Review state:** Full `NListview.c` body (799 `cloc 2.06` C code lines) reviewed, including constructor, scroller notification/attachment, setup/cleanup, event forwarding, attributes, and method dispatch. Selected class manifest: `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlistview_mcc/mmakefile.src`. Source-only.

Source-only.

## GD9724

**Indexed summary:** NList import reads past a truncated dataspace record.

**Source and trigger:** `mNL_Import()` obtains only the data pointer from `MUIM_Dataspace_Find()`, checks the first `LONG` for `EXPT`, then reads subsequent tags and variable-length fields without knowing or validating the dataspace node's stored length (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc0.c:153-173,225-269`). The dataspace implementation stores arbitrary positive payload lengths with the node (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/dataspace.c:93-125`), and its IFF reader only checks that each payload fits its enclosing IFF chunk before adding it; it does not validate the NList subformat (`:221-240`). The normal application load path imports each child's state from that dataspace (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:2416-2447`). Therefore a truncated/corrupt saved-state item containing the four-byte `EXPT` marker is accepted and `mNL_Import()` immediately reads `nlie[1]` beyond the item. Truncated `WIDT`, `ORDR`, or `SELS` count/value sequences can likewise advance the cursor beyond the payload. **Affected configuration and trigger:** an AROS application with a configured NList object ID loading saved MUI state whose matching dataspace item is truncated or internally malformed but whose payload begins with `EXPT`. **Consequence:** the importer performs out-of-bounds reads; adjacent pool contents can be interpreted as tags/counts and lead to further invalid reads or unintended imported settings. Carry the node length into import and validate each tag's required fields and count before reading. **Confidence: high** for the unchecked reads and the normal truncated-record path; no corrupted settings file was loaded. Source-only.

## GD9720

**Indexed summary:** NList leaks precreated child objects when its Group superclass construction fails.

**Source and trigger:** `mNL_New()` creates an image and a nested custom Group before calling `DoSuperNew()` with that Group as a child (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc.c:352-376`). The selected NList superclass is `MUIC_Group` (`nlist_mcc/library.c:50-56`). AROS `Group__OM_NEW()` first creates its private `MUIC_Family`; if that allocation fails, it disposes the partial Group and returns before iterating the supplied `Child` tags (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:321-326,335-351,415-418`). Therefore the precreated child Group has not transferred to the outer object. NList's failure branch returns NULL without disposing it (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc.c:379-380`); that nested Group in turn owns the earlier image, so the image remains allocated as well. If the nested Group's own Family allocation fails, its supplied image has likewise not been adopted, and NList continues without releasing that image. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlist-class` target when creating an NList object under memory pressure causes either the nested or outer Group's internal Family allocation to fail. **Consequence:** the failed object creation leaks the precreated Group and image objects (or the image when nested Group creation fails). Dispose each locally created object when the next constructor fails before ownership transfer. **Confidence: high** for construction order, failure return, and lack of child adoption/cleanup; allocation failure was not induced. Source-only.

## GD9725

**Indexed summary:** NList copies every parsed formatting position from the first record when its formatting-info buffer grows.

**Source and trigger:** `NeedAffInfo()` grows `data->aff_infos` when a parser requests an index beyond the current capacity. Its copy loop correctly copies each record's string pointer, style, length, and other fields from `[ni]`, but copies `pos` from `data->aff_infos->pos` (record zero) for every destination record (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc4.c:164-202`, especially line 181). Initialization requests `AFFINFOS_START_MAX` 40 entries (`private.h:150`; `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc.c:768`), and the growth rule allocates `40 + 40/2 = 60` records on that first request (`NList_mcc4.c:169-176`). A displayed string or preparse sequence that produces more than 60 affinity records causes a later reallocation while `ParseColumn()` is building its formatting segments (`NList_mcc4.c:337-383,841-853`); `AddSpaceInfos()` can also request growth (`:936`). Later character hit-testing uses the copied positions as source offsets (`FindCharInColumn`, `:1189-1278`), and wrapping stores/advances them to split the underlying row (`NL_DoWrapLine`, `:1417-1514`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlist-class` target when a row/title contains enough formatting, image, tab, or space segments to exhaust the 60-record initial buffer during parsing. **Consequence:** after growth, later segments carry an incorrect source position, so character selection/hit-testing can report the wrong character and wrapped rows can split at the wrong offset. Copy `data->aff_infos[ni].pos` alongside the other per-record fields. **Confidence: high** for the copy-index mismatch and downstream position consumers; no unusually formatted row was rendered or selected. Source-only.

**Review state:** Full 1,757-line `NList_mcc4.c` body read. The growth path and position consumers in parsing, hit-testing, and wrapping were traced; no parser or wrap operation was run. Other standalone NList files and wider client contracts remain partial.

## GD9728

**Indexed summary:** NList's custom copy hooks lose the final character of every returned string.

**Source and trigger:** `CCB_string()` allocates space for `len` output bytes plus a separator and terminator, but its non-escape-filtering branch calls `strlcpy(tmp, str, len)` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func3.c:489-520`). `strlcpy` copies at most `len - 1` characters when given a buffer size of `len`; the following code places the separator/terminator at the returned source length. Both custom hook paths select this branch: the entry hook passes `strlen(display_array[0])` (`:596-603`), while the column hook passes the length returned in `display_array[1]` (`:663-674`). The public contracts require the hook to return its string and its string length (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NList.doc:466-481`), and describe entry-hook string output at `:502-520`. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlist-class` target when copying an entry/column through `MUIA_NList_CopyEntryToClipHook[/2]` or `MUIA_NList_CopyColumnToClipHook[/2]` and the returned length is positive. **Consequence:** the final character of each hook-produced fragment is omitted from the copied string, file or clipboard contents. Pass a destination size of `len + 1` (or copy exactly `len` bytes and terminate explicitly). **Confidence: high** for the size/length mismatch and both selected call paths; no hook or copy operation was run. Source-only.

## GD9733

Add explicit rollback for user-owned initialization resources on every failed `ClassInit()` path. **Confidence: high** for the success/failure ordering and the absence of rollback in the selected template; no initialization failure was induced. Source-only.

## GD9731

**Indexed summary:** Four Zune MCCs can wait forever during initialization when clipboard-server setup fails.

**Source and trigger:** NList, NListtree, BetterString and TextEditor each create the request semaphore and a worker process, send it a startup message, then unconditionally wait on the reply port (NList `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/ClipboardServer.c:261-309`; NListtree `nlist/nlisttree_mcc/ClipboardServer.c:255-309`; BetterString `workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/ClipboardServer.c:420-468`; TextEditor `workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/ClipboardServer.c:899-947`). In each worker, the startup reply is sent only after opening `iffparse.library` (and, on OS4, obtaining its interface) and allocating the worker message port; the failure branches fall through without replying (NList/NListtree `ClipboardServer.c:175-195`; BetterString `:327-347`; TextEditor `:793-813`). Each module calls `StartClipboardServer()` synchronously from `ClassInit()` (NList `nlist_mcc/library.c:143-147`; NListtree `nlisttree_mcc/library.c:83-90`; BetterString `betterstring/mcc/library.c:108-114`; TextEditor `texteditor/mcc/library.c:111-118`). Each target's included `mccinit.c` calls `ClassInit()` synchronously during module initialization (NList/NListtree `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mccinit.c:757-777`; BetterString `workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/include/mccinit.c:753-773`; TextEditor `workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/include/mccinit.c:757-777`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** explicitly buildable AROS targets `classes-zune-nlist-class`, `classes-zune-nlisttree-class`, `workbench-classes-zune-betterstring-class`, or `workbench-classes-zune-texteditor-class` when the child cannot open `iffparse.library`, obtain the OS4 IFFParse interface, or allocate its message port. **Consequence:** the task opening/initializing the MCC remains blocked in `WaitPort()` indefinitely; the request semaphore allocated before process creation also remains allocated on this failure path. Reply with a startup status on every child exit and unwind worker/semaphore state on failure. **Confidence: high** for the unmatched reply and synchronous wait across all four copies; no library, interface, or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

**Review state:** Re-read the NListtree copy and compared the matching worker setup and module `ClassInit()` paths across all four implementations. No process or clipboard operation was run.
## GD9730

**Indexed summary:** NList leaks owned bitmap image resources on cleanup.

**Source and trigger:** `mNL_Cleanup()` deliberately sets `data->SETUP = FALSE` before calling `NL_DeleteImages()` so image removal will not relayout the group (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc.c:1618-1624`). `NL_DeleteImages()` walks the `NList_UseImages` array and calls `NL_DeleteImage()` for each created bitmap image (`NList_func4.c:855-869`). For images tagged `MUIM_NList_CreateImage`, `NL_DeleteImage()` calls `disposeBitMapImage()` (`:789-793`), but that disposer frees planes, mask, obtained pens and the pooled image record only inside `if (bmimg && data->SETUP)` (`:366-404`). Since cleanup has already cleared `SETUP`, it does nothing; `NL_DeleteImages()` then clears the array pointer (`:862-867`), losing the only image-record reference. The public `MUIM_NList_UseImage` contract says NList stores the bitmap/bodychunk object and creates and deletes the image itself (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NList.doc:3466-3498`), so clients need not call the manual delete method. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlist-class` target when a list with a successfully created `MUIM_NList_UseImage` bitmap/bodychunk image undergoes Cleanup (including hide/iconify or teardown) before object disposal. **Consequence:** raster planes and mask are not freed, acquired colormap pens are not released, and the image record is abandoned; repeated setup/cleanup cycles accumulate resources. Separate screen-dependent pen release from unconditional image-memory cleanup, or dispose these resources before clearing setup state. **Confidence: high** for cleanup ordering, automatic UseImage deletion, and the false setup guard; no image or cleanup operation was run. Source-only.

**Review state:** Reconciled the complete `NList_func4.c` image ownership paths with NList cleanup and the public UseImage contract. No image setup or cleanup was run.

## GD9727

**Indexed summary:** NList reports the wrong first selected row in `MUIM_NList_GetSelectInfo` line-selection mode.

**Source and trigger:** `mNL_List_GetSelectInfo()` initializes `res->start` to `1`, then scans selected rows and assigns the first selected index only when `res->start == -1` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func.c:1966-2000`). That condition is unreachable from the initialization. In line-selection mode, the method therefore reports `start == 1` for every selection, even when the first selected row is at another index; with no selected rows it also reports `start`, `end`, `vstart`, and `vend` as 1. The public method dispatches directly to this implementation (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc0.c:664`). The API documentation says `start`/`vstart` identify the first selected row and explicitly requires all four row fields to be -1 when nothing is selected (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NList.doc:2815-2834`); the public result structure has the same field definitions (`include/mui/NList_mcc.h:480-493`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlist-class` target when a client calls `MUIM_NList_GetSelectInfo` while `MUIA_NList_TypeSelect` is line mode, including the empty-selection case. **Consequence:** callers receive an incorrect first-row index, and empty selection is reported as row 1 rather than no selection; clients using the fields to copy, anchor, or display selected rows can act on the wrong row. Initialize `start` to -1 before the scan and preserve the documented empty result. **Confidence: high** for the initializer/condition mismatch, direct dispatch, and documented contract; no selection method was run. Source-only.

**Review state:** Full `NList_func.c` body read; `GetSelectInfo` dispatch and its public documentation/structure were reconciled. No UI operation was run.

**Indexed summary:** NList publishes the row height as its insert-position notification value instead of the affected row index.

**Source and trigger:** When `NTF_DragSortInsert` is delivered, `NL_DoNotifies()` calls `notdoset()` with `MUIA_NList_DragSortInsert` and `data->vinc`; for `NTF_Insert` it does the same with `MUIA_NList_InsertPosition` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc5.c:318-329`). `vinc` is the vertical line height. The public NList docs state that DragSortInsert has the same function/value as InsertPosition and only notifies after a drag-sort move (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NList.doc:799-805,1261-1269`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** an application using the explicitly buildable `classes-zune-nlist-class` target and notifying on either attribute after an insert or successful drag-sort move. **Consequence:** the notification receives a small row-height value instead of the inserted/moved row index; clients that use the trigger value to locate or select the changed row act on the wrong entry. Publish `data->NList_LastInserted` as the notification value, matching the getter and callers. **Confidence: high** for the value mismatch and documented attribute relationship; no notification client or GUI drag was run. Source-only.

## GD9734

**Indexed summary:** NListtree's full-table removal loop reads one pointer past the allocation; that value is immediately discarded.

**Source and trigger:** `NLCreateTable()` rounds capacity to a multiple of 64 and allocates exactly that many node pointers (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:987-1027`). When `NLRemoveFromTable()` finds an entry, it decrements `tb_Entries` and shifts with `j <= table->tb_Entries`, reading `tb_Table[j + 1]` on the last iteration (`:1080-1106`). If the table was full before removal (64 entries in its initial allocation, or a later full multiple of 64), that last read is one pointer beyond the allocated table. Removal reaches this helper through the public `MUIM_NListtree_Remove` method and its RemoveNode2 path (`:2286-2292,7543-7650`); table removals also occur during node moves/exchanges (`:8053-8062,8326-8328`). The API documents removing individual, all, or selected nodes (`docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:2616-2676`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when a sibling list or selected-node table is exactly at its allocated capacity (64, or a later multiple of 64) and a node is removed, moved, or exchanged. **Consequence:** the final copied value is immediately overwritten by the following NULL assignment, so the read does not itself leave an incorrect table entry. It is nevertheless an out-of-bounds source-level read; whether it faults depends on the allocator's adjacent memory mapping and compiler optimization. Bound the shift to `j < table->tb_Entries` after decrementing the count, then clear the last live slot. **Confidence:** high that the source loop indexes one pointer beyond the allocated table for a full-capacity removal; low that this produces an observable fault, because the fetched value is immediately overwritten and an optimizing compiler may eliminate the dead load. No persistent table-state corruption was found in the caller trace. Source-only.

**Review state:** Rechecked `NLRemoveFromTable()`, the public `MUIM_NListtree_Remove` path, and move/exchange callers. Removal decrements the entry count, shifts entries, then clears the final live slot; the out-of-range value is not retained. The full `NListtree.c` body has full-body ledger credit; broader class integration and external caller closure remain open.

## GD9735

**Indexed summary:** NListtree marks nodes selected even when its selected-node table cannot grow.

**Source and trigger:** `NLCreateTable()` stores the rounded requested capacity in `table->tb_Size` before calling `AllocVecPooled()`, and returns NULL on allocation failure (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:987-1027`). `NLAddToTable()` propagates that failure but leaves the old `tb_Table` pointer in place while retaining the larger `tb_Size` (`:1034-1053`). `TreeNodeSelectAdd()` also discards the add result and returns the node as if insertion succeeded (`:1492-1498`). Its callers then set `TNF_SELECTED` and publish selection change (`:10510-10518`; the Remove Selected path also restores the active node this way at `:7631-7637`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when the initial or expanded selected-node table allocation fails under memory pressure. **Consequence:** the immediate operation can mark a node selected although `SelectedTable` omits it. More seriously, failed initial allocation leaves a NULL table with `tb_Size` set to 64; the next insertion sees spare capacity and writes through that NULL pointer. Failed growth similarly advertises the requested larger capacity while retaining the smaller old allocation, so a later insertion can write past it. The failing insertion is not reported by `TreeNodeSelectAdd()`, so its caller still marks the node selected. This can fault on the next insertion and leave selection queries/removals inconsistent. Preserve the old capacity metadata on allocation failure and do not publish selected state after a failed table insertion. **Confidence: high** for the stale capacity metadata, failed insertion and state mutation ordering; allocation failure was not induced. Source-only.

**Review state:** Rechecked the visible selection callback and public method path. `_NListtree_SelectChange()` calls `TreeNodeSelectAdd()` and then unconditionally sets `TNF_SELECTED` and sends `MUIA_NListtree_SelectChange`; `_NListtree_Select()` returns the requested state. `MUIM_NListtree_NextSelected` enumerates only `SelectedTable`, so the failed node is omitted even while marked selected. After failed initial allocation, the next selected-table insertion sees the inflated size of 64, skips allocation, and writes through the NULL table pointer. This is separate from GD9736, which concerns sibling-list tables. No allocation failure or selection operation was run.


## GD9736

**Indexed summary:** NListtree records a larger table capacity before allocation succeeds, so a failed growth can make the next insertion write past the old table.

**Source and trigger:** `NLCreateTable()` stores the rounded requested capacity in `table->tb_Size` before allocating the replacement pointer array; allocation failure returns NULL without restoring the previous size (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:987-1027`). When a 64-entry table needs to grow for a 65th sibling and allocation fails, `tb_Table` still points to the 64-slot array while `tb_Size` now says 128. `NLAddToTable()` reports the failed growth (`:1034-1045`), but public insertion and `InsertTreeNode()` callers ignore the result after linking and displaying the node (`:2561-2586,7129-7253`). On a later insertion, `tb_Entries + 1` is no longer greater than the stale 128 capacity, so `NLAddToTable()` writes the new pointer at `tb_Table[64]`, beyond the old 64-slot allocation (`:1039-1052`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when an at-capacity sibling table's growth allocation fails and a later insertion into that list is attempted. **Consequence:** the table's stored capacity no longer describes its allocation and a subsequent ordinary insertion writes out of bounds; meanwhile the linked-list and indexed table can diverge after the failed insertion. Keep the old capacity until allocation succeeds, and propagate insertion failure or roll back the list/visible entry. **Confidence: high** for allocation ordering, stale capacity, and the later write path; memory pressure and subsequent insertion were not induced. Source-only.

**Review state:** Rechecked `NLCreateTable()`, `NLAddToTable()`, `InsertTreeNode()`, and `_NListtree_Insert()`. Both insertion paths ignore the failed table-add result after inserting the node into the linked/visible tree; `_NListtree_Insert()` then increments `NumEntries` and returns the node. The later-add out-of-bounds write follows from the retained old allocation and inflated capacity. The complete `NListtree.c` body has full-body ledger credit; broader class integration and external caller closure remain open. No allocation failure or insertion was run.


## GD9737

**Indexed summary:** NListtree's AutoVisible Expand mode jumps to the old active row instead of the newly activated hidden node.

**Source and trigger:** In `ActivateTreeNode()`, the Expand branch walks up from the requested node and opens each parent. The loop exits after assigning `tn2 = NULL`, then `GetVisualPos(data, tn2)` returns its not-found value `-1`, which is passed to `MUIM_NList_Jump` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:2182-2225`; `GetVisualPos()` returns -1 for NULL at `:1367-1398`). In NList, `MUIV_NList_Jump_Active` is also `-1` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mui/NList_mcc.h:280-285`), so the jump targets the currently active NList row. The requested node's own visible position is set as NList Active only later in `ActivateTreeNode()` (`NListtree.c:2230-2244`). NList's own `MUIA_NList_AutoVisible` defaults to FALSE (`nlist_mcc/NList_mcc.c:434`) and NListtree does not override it, so it does not correct this jump in the default configuration. The NListtree docs promise that AutoVisible Expand opens parents and scrolls the active entry into view (`docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:253-256`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target with `MUIA_NListtree_AutoVisible = MUIV_NListtree_AutoVisible_Expand`, selecting a node under one or more closed ancestors, while the inherited `MUIA_NList_AutoVisible` remains at its default FALSE. **Consequence:** parent nodes open but the viewport jumps to the previous NList active row (or does not scroll to the newly activated node), leaving the requested active entry offscreen. Compute the target node's visual position after opening ancestors and jump to that position. **Confidence: high** for the NULL/-1 jump, NList sentinel alias, setter ordering, and default auto-visible state; no tree activation or scroll operation was run. Source-only.

**Review state:** Traced the complete AutoVisible Expand branch to the NList jump sentinel, active-index update, constructor default, and public contract. The containing `NListtree.c` body remains under review. No GUI operation was run.


## GD9738

**Indexed summary:** NListtree calls the source node's destruct hook when constructing a duplicate fails.

**Source and trigger:** `DuplicateNode()` passes the existing node's name and user-data pointer to `MUIM_NListtree_Construct` to create a copy. If the construct method returns NULL, the cleanup branch frees the new node/name and then calls `MUIM_NListtree_Destruct` with the original `nodetodup->tn_User` pointer (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:2590-2635`, especially `:2621-2634`). This helper is used by public Copy and by Move with KeepStructure (`:2660-2677,2706-2734,8334-8337,8565-8572`). The documented hook contract says NULL means no new node is added; the paired string destruct hook frees its UserData (`docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:361-403,452-476`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when Copy or Move with KeepStructure attempts to duplicate a node and its construct hook returns NULL, for example because its new user-data allocation fails, while a destructive hook is installed (including the built-in string construct/destruct pair). **Consequence:** the original node remains in the tree but its user data is freed as though the source node had been removed; subsequent tree use or eventual destruction can access or free the stale pointer. Do not call the source node's destruct hook when construction of the duplicate fails. **Confidence: high** for the source pointer passed to the failure cleanup, duplicate call paths, and documented destruct ownership; no failed copy or allocation was run. Source-only.

**Review state:** Read `DuplicateNode()` and traced its Copy/KeepStructure callers plus construct/destruct ownership docs. The `NListtree.c` translation unit remains under review. No copy or allocation failure was induced.

## GD9740

**Indexed summary:** NListtree ignores internal construct/destruct hook allocation failures and can pair a borrowed user pointer with the freeing destruct hook.

Check both hook allocations as one transaction and reject object construction if the pair cannot be installed. **Confidence: high** for the ignored error flag, construct fallback, and destruct ownership; allocation failure was not induced. Source-only.

## GD9742

**Indexed summary:** NListtree has invalid or missing rollback on `OM_NEW` failure.

**Source and trigger:** On AROS, `MUI_NewObjectA()` looks up the custom class and calls Intuition `NewObjectA()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_newobject.c:53-64`); Intuition begins `OM_NEW` dispatch with the class pointer as the `obj` argument (`rom/intuition/newobjecta.c:139-143`). NListtree `_New()` allocates `MemoryPool` and then `TreePool` before invoking `DoSuperNew()` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:5113-5135,5164-5180`). If either pool allocation fails, `obj` is still that class pointer, but the shared failure tail calls `CoerceMethod(cl, obj, OM_DISPOSE)` (`:5306-5312`). The AROS `CoerceMethod()` dispatches any non-NULL object (`compiler/alib/coercemethod.c:51-60`), so `_Dispose()` treats the class object as a NListtree instance and reaches its `INST_DATA`/`DoMethod()` accesses (`NListtree.c:5316-5328; compiler/include/intuition/classes.h:62-64`). If both pools are created but `DoSuperNew()` fails, it overwrites `obj` with NULL; the same `CoerceMethod()` then does nothing, leaking both pools. A third failure path is already visible after successful superclass construction: if the NList version is below 20.130, `_New()` displays a requester and returns NULL directly (`:5208-5226`), skipping the same cleanup and abandoning the object and pools. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when either `CreatePool()` fails before superclass construction, when NList's `OM_NEW` fails after both pools were allocated, or when the created NList superclass is older than 20.130. **Consequence:** the first case dispatches disposal against a class object instead of an instance; the second leaks both pools; the version-rejection case leaks the constructed superclass instance and both pools. Keep local pool ownership until the superclass instance exists, and route each failure through cleanup appropriate to whether an instance was created. **Confidence: high** for the AROS class-pointer dispatch, failure-tail behavior and pool leaks; allocation failures and the old-version path were not induced. Source-only.

**Review state:** Rechecked the AROS `MUI_NewObjectA()` → Intuition `NewObjectA()` class-pointer entry path, all pool/superclass constructor failure branches, the NULL guard in AROS `CoerceMethod()`, and `_Dispose()`'s instance-data accesses. No allocation failure or object creation was run.

Source-only.

## GD9744

**Indexed summary:** NListtree's default clipboard copy mutates node names while trying to strip display escape sequences.

**Source and trigger:** In the default (no custom copy hook) path, `_NListtree_CopyToClip()` copies a node name while removing escape sequences. For an ESC followed by `[` it executes `while (++*s != ']');` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:10058-10072`). `*s` is the character at the source-name pointer, so this increments and writes into the node's name instead of advancing through the sequence. With a typical `ESC [ ...` name it changes the `[` byte and does not strip the remaining sequence as intended; if the name storage is read-only, the copy can fault. The default clipboard handler routes a menu copy to this method (`:6568-6578,10030-10080`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when copying a node whose name contains the display escape sequence format, with the default copy hook selected. **Consequence:** clipboard output retains part of the formatting sequence and the stored node name is modified; read-only name storage can fault during copying. Iterate over the source pointer without writing through it, and bound parsing of the sequence. **Confidence: high** for the incorrect source mutation and default caller; clipboard copy was not run. Source-only.

**Caller and format recheck (2026-10-25):** the selected NList demo contains bracketed inline formats such as `ESC P[1]` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/demo/NList-Demo.c:425-429`), and NListtree's public CopyToClip documentation says its built-in path skips ESC sequences (`NListtree.c:3581-3600`). For `ESC P[1]`, after `s += 2`, `s` points at `[`. `while (++*s != ']')` changes that byte from `[` to `]`, then the next copy begins at `1`, so the node retains a changed name and the clipboard receives the `1]` payload. The normal row context-menu callback invokes this method (`NListtree.c:6568-6578`). `NLTF_DUPNODENAMES` is enabled by default and insertion copies names into the tree pool (`:5142-5147,7111-7119`), so the normal case corrupts the retained tree name; when duplication is disabled, the write can also affect caller-owned or read-only input. This recheck strengthens GD9744's concrete format and caller evidence; no second finding is added. No clipboard operation was run.

## GD9747

**Indexed summary:** NListtree Move and Exchange can reinsert a node into its own descendant list and create a cyclic tree.

**Source and trigger:** `_NListtree_Move()` resolves a caller-supplied destination list/node, removes the source node, then inserts it without checking whether the destination list is inside the source subtree (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:8260-8345`). `_NListtree_Exchange()` similarly swaps parent pointers and inserts both nodes without a cross-ancestry check (`:7990-8110`). Moving a list node after one of its direct children with `MUIV_NListtree_Move_NewListNode_Active` makes the source its own parent; exchanging it with a child can also make it its own parent. The demo exposes both operations. Its Move and Exchange buttons use an ineffective guard: `GetParent()` ignores the supplied node and always asks for the parent of the root list (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/demo/NListtree-Demo.c:251-258`), so the ancestry walk terminates immediately; both guards also repeat the same direction (`:446,527`). A third demo action calls Move with `MUIV_NListtree_Move_Flag_KeepStructure` and has no ancestry guard (`:616-634`); that method path still reuses the moved node and inserts it at the selected destination after its parent-structure handling (`NListtree.c:2660-2699,8334-8345`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when a client moves or exchanges a node against its descendant using the public methods; all three demo actions can submit such a destination, including the unguarded KeepStructure action. **Consequence:** parent/list links become cyclic. The selected renderer's `DrawImages()` recursively follows `tn_Parent` without a cycle check (`NListtree.c:2883-2890,6463`), so drawing an affected node can recurse until stack exhaustion; later tree traversal, removal, or destruction can also fail. Reject descendant destinations before unlinking either node and repair the demo's guards. **Confidence: high** for the method relinking and unsafe demo call paths; no tree mutation or render was run. Source-only.

**Review state (2026-11-01):** Re-ran a checkout-wide C/header search for both method IDs. The only maintained UI callers are three demo actions: Move and Exchange buttons with the broken ancestry guard, plus an unguarded KeepStructure Move action (`NListtree-Demo.c:452,533,633`). `GetParent()` ignores the node argument (`:251-258`), and the two guarded actions test the same direction twice (`:446,527`). The class's four internal Move/Exchange calls are all in built-in drag/drop; `_DragNDrop_DropType()` checks selected-source ancestry against the target through `IsXChildOfListMember()` (`NListtree.c:1237-1250,6096-6114`) before dispatch, excluding descendant targets for ordinary built-in drag/drop. Thus GD9747 remains reachable through the direct public methods and demo actions; no other in-tree external client was found. The demo body is fully read; external callers and broader class/manual integration remain open. Source-only; no method call or tree mutation was run.

## GD9749

**Indexed summary:** NListtree preferences MCP leaks its locale.library reference when AmigaOS 4 interface acquisition fails during class initialization.

**Source and trigger:** `ClassInit()` first opens `locale.library` version 38, then requires `GETINTERFACE(ILocale, ...)` to succeed (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcp/library.c:159-192`). The selected shared startup template defines this macro on AmigaOS 4 as `GetInterface()` and returns failure if the interface is NULL (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mccinit.c:293-300`); the `&&` then skips catalog setup and returns FALSE. The shared `mccLibInit()` failure path deletes the newly-created MCP class and closes its own dependencies, but does not call `ClassExpunge()` (`.../include/mccinit.c:757-785`). `LocaleBase` is closed only in `ClassExpunge()` (`library.c:196-207`), so its successful `OpenLibrary()` reference remains outstanding on this failure path.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly build-selected `classes-zune-nlisttree-mcp` target on AmigaOS 4, when `OpenLibrary("locale.library", 38)` succeeds but `GetInterface(..., "main", 1, NULL)` fails during MCP initialization.

**Consequence:** one locale.library open reference is leaked for the failed initialization attempt. Release `LocaleBase` (and any acquired interface) on the local failure path, or ensure the shared rollback invokes the class cleanup hook after partial initialization.

**Confidence: high** for the conditional open/interface sequence, shared macro expansion, missing cleanup call on rollback, and sole locale release in `ClassExpunge()`; no library load or interface failure was induced. Source-only.

**Review state:** Read the selected MCP manifest and traced this `ClassInit()` failure through the shared startup rollback and expunge cleanup. The finding is specific to AmigaOS 4 interface-acquisition failure. Other MCP callers and generated locale/catalog behavior remain open.

## GD9751

**Indexed summary:** Legacy Listtree continues construction after its per-object pool allocation fails, then calls AllocPooled with a NULL pool.

**Source and trigger:** `Listtree__OM_NEW()` creates the wrapper's backing pool with `CreatePool()` but does not test the result before continuing and returning the object (`workbench/classes/zune/listtree/listtree.c:263-280,317-364`). Every successful object installs `ConstructHook_Proxy` as the required NListtree construct hook (`:344-350`); that proxy calls `AllocPooled(data->pool, ...)` without validating the handle (`:190-207`). Exec's `AllocPooled()` treats its argument as a memory-header pointer and accesses the pool header/requirements (`rom/exec/allocpooled.c:70-93`), so a NULL pool is not a recoverable allocation-failure input.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the build-selected legacy Listtree compatibility class when `CreatePool(MEMF_ANY | MEMF_CLEAR, 16 * 1024, 8 * 1024)` fails during object construction and the caller subsequently inserts a node.

**Consequence:** the object appears constructed, but the first insertion's construct proxy passes a NULL pool into `AllocPooled()`, leading to invalid memory access instead of a clean failed object or insertion. Treat pool creation as required: dispose the partially constructed list and return failure before publishing the object, or make all later operations handle the absent pool. **Confidence: high** for the unchecked pool result and allocator's pool-header access; no allocation failure or insertion was run. Source-only.

**Review state:** Traced the wrapper's object creation, required construct hook, pool allocator call, and selected Exec `AllocPooled()` implementation. The surrounding wrapper and callers remain under review.

## GD9752

**Source and trigger:** In the setup-only `MUIM_List_CreateImage` path, the wrapper obtains the underlying NList image and then allocates its `ListImage` adapter with `AllocPooled()` (`workbench/classes/zune/listtree/listtree.c:750-773`). Check `li` before writing it and dispose `_ret` through NList's matching delete method if adapter allocation fails. **Confidence: high** for the unchecked allocation and immediate writes; no image or allocation failure was run. Source-only.

**Review state:** Traced the legacy adapter allocation and all immediate field/object setup. No image creation was run.

**Indexed summary:** SysExplorer formats a support-module path into an unchecked allocation result.

## GD9754

**Indexed summary:** SysExplorer's registration library dereferences failed allocations while recording modules, bases, and skipped classes.

**Source and trigger:** Three registration paths use allocation results without checking them: `RegisterModule()` copies into `IntModule` immediately after `AllocMem()` (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/sysexp_library.c:82-88`); `RegisterBase()` writes fields into its unchecked `AllocMem()` result (`:94-107`); and `RegisterSkipClass()` writes the name and enqueues the unchecked `AllocVec()` result (`:246-251`). These are used during app/module initialization, including the base and skipped-class registrations from `sysexp_initlib()` (`:312-334`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the build-selected SysExplorer app or support modules when one of these registration allocations fails, such as during startup under memory pressure. **Consequence:** initialization faults instead of reporting registration failure or continuing without the affected registration. Check each result before copying, writing, or enqueueing, and expose failure to callers where registration is required. **Confidence: high** for the unchecked allocation and immediate use; no allocation failure was run. Source-only.

**Review state:** Read the full SysExplorer registration-library body, traced its in-tree initialization callers and confirmed it is in the app target's `BASEFILES`. Broader module registration and shutdown contracts remain open.

## GD9755

**Indexed summary:** SysExplorer leaks caller-owned CPU-page strings after MUI text objects copy them.

**Source and trigger:** In ParseProcessorInformation(), SysExplorer allocates temporary strings for the architecture label and description, each per-core label and model, optional per-core speed, and each CPU-feature block (workbench/tools/SysExplorer/computer_page_cl.c:189-287). Label() constructs a MUIC_Text object with MUIA_Text_Contents set to the supplied string (workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_makeobject.c:270-284); Text__OM_NEW duplicates that contents with StrDup(), and Text__OM_DISPOSE frees only the duplicate (workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/text.c:68-79,121-126). The direct TextObject constructions for CPUInfoStr and CoreSpdStr use the same copy-in path. NFloattext likewise duplicates CPUFeatureStr (workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nfloattext_mcc/NFloattext.c:102-106,159-162). SysExplorer never releases these original allocations after the copies are made. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly selected SysExplorer app when its computer-properties CPU page is built with ProcessorBase available; the architecture strings leak once per page, and model, label, optional speed, and feature strings leak per reported core (speed only when nonzero). Rebuilding the page repeats the allocations. **Consequence:** persistent memory use grows with the number of processors and CPU-page constructions. Free each caller-owned temporary after the receiving constructor has copied it, including all object-construction failure paths. **Confidence: high** for the allocations, copy-in behavior, and absence of caller releases; no GUI or allocation-failure operation was run. Source-only.

**Review state:** Rechecked all string allocations in ParseProcessorInformation() against the selected Label/Text and NFloattext constructors and their disposal ownership. The active AROS Workbench target selects SysExplorer through `workbench-tools` (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/SysExplorer/mmakefile.src:4-5`); runtime launch remains required to trigger the finding. No GUI was opened.
## GD9756

**Indexed summary:** SysExplorer's computer-properties CPU page dereferences unchecked string allocations.

**Source and trigger:** The CPU-page builder stores several `AllocVec()` results and immediately writes through them. The architecture label buffer is passed to `sprintf()` without a NULL check, and the architecture description buffer is likewise used by `sprintf()` (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/computer_page_cl.c:189-203`). The per-core model label/text and feature buffers repeat the unchecked pattern (`:230-244,258-287`); `PrintCPUSpecificInfo()` immediately uses its buffer with `snprintf()` and `strlen()` in the architecture-specific implementation (`cpu_arm.c:38-58` or `cpu_i386.c:37-49`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the build-selected SysExplorer app when the processor resource is present and the computer-properties window builds the CPU page under memory pressure. **Consequence:** a failed buffer allocation can fault while formatting or writing processor information, instead of omitting the affected row or abandoning the page cleanly. Check each allocation and unwind partially created UI objects and strings on failure. **Confidence: high** for the unchecked allocations and immediate use; no allocation failure or GUI operation was run. Source-only.

**Review state:** Read the CPU-page builder and both architecture-specific formatters, then traced the CPU-page caller guard (`ProcessorBase` is required before `ParseProcessorInformation()` runs). No runtime operation was performed.

## GD9757

**Indexed summary:** SysExplorer passes uninitialized CPU-feature storage as a string on non-x86/non-ARM builds.

**Source and trigger:** The CPU page allocates `CPUFeatureStr` with `AllocVec(1024, MEMF_PUBLIC)` and calls `PrintCPUSpecificInfo()` before passing the buffer as `MUIA_Floattext_Text` (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/computer_page_cl.c:276-286`). `MEMF_PUBLIC` does not request cleared memory. For architectures other than x86, x86_64, and ARM, `cpuspecific.h` defines `PrintCPUSpecificInfo` as an empty macro, so the buffer receives no terminator or contents (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/cpuspecific.h:1-19`). NFloattext's copying attribute calls `CopyText()`, which runs `strlen()` on the supplied string (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nfloattext_mcc/NFloattext.c:35-44,102-105,159-162`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the build-selected SysExplorer app on a non-x86/non-ARM architecture with the processor resource present and at least one processor reported, when the computer-properties CPU page is constructed. **Consequence:** the page copies indeterminate bytes as text and may continue reading beyond the 1,024-byte allocation while searching for a terminator. Initialize the buffer to an empty string before the architecture-specific formatter, and have unsupported architectures produce a deliberate fallback string. **Confidence: high** for the empty macro, non-cleared allocation, and downstream `strlen()`; no GUI window was opened. Source-only.

**Review state:** Traced architecture guards through the caller macro and NFloattext's copy routine. This is distinct from GD9756's allocation-failure path and GD9755's normal-use caller-buffer leak.

## GD9758

**Indexed summary:** SysExplorer ATA/AHCI support modules continue startup and call Storage-module APIs after detecting that the required module is absent.

**Source and trigger:** `ATAStartup()` and `AHCIStartup()` obtain `Storage.Module`, display a requester if `GetBase()` returns NULL, but do not return or otherwise disable their startup (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/Modules/ATA/ata_enum.c:103-129`; `Modules/AHCI/ahci_enum.c:106-134`). Both then unconditionally call `RegisterStorageControllerHandler()` and `RegisterStorageBusHandler()` from the Storage module API. The same NULL `StorageBase` is the module base for those generated API vectors; the API definitions are in `Modules/Storage/storage.conf`. `GetBase()` returns NULL when the module is not registered (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/sysexp_library.c:113-135`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the build-selected SysExplorer ATA or AHCI support module is present in `PROGDIR:SysExpModules` while `storage.sysexp` is missing or failed to load. **Consequence:** startup continues into Storage-module vector calls with a NULL base after warning the user, rather than disabling the dependent module; the call cannot reach a valid Storage handler and may fault while dispatching the API. Abort the dependent module's startup after the error, or verify the dependency before invoking its APIs. **Confidence: high** for the unchecked missing-dependency branch and ensuing API calls; no module-load failure was run. Source-only.

**Review state:** Traced both module startup functions through their selected API declarations and the app's base lookup behavior. Module dependency failure is distinct from custom-class creation failure and from OOP attribute-base acquisition OD2399.


## GD9759

**SysExplorer can leave empty hardware nodes marked expandable.** The parent enumeration callback marks a node `TNF_LIST|TNF_OPEN` when its class handler has an enumerator, then clears those flags only if `GlobalCount` did not change during enumeration (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/Modules/Storage/storage_enum.c:84-115`; same logic in `sysexp_main.c:117-137`). Several enumerators advance that counter without guaranteeing a child was inserted. First, `PCIEnumerator_h()` increments it for every PCI device before checking whether the device is a PCI-to-PCI bridge, and inserts a child only for bridges (`Modules/PCI/pci_enum.c:76-89`); a PCI driver with devices but no bridges therefore remains expandable despite having no child. Second, `storageunitenumFunc()` increments it before attempting `MUIM_NListtree_Insert` and ignores the return value (`Modules/Storage/storage_enum.c:151-157`). The ATA and AHCI bus enumerators use the same pattern for storage units (`Modules/ATA/ata_enum.c:76-85,96-100`; `Modules/AHCI/ahci_enum.c:74-87,99-104`). Third, the Gfx module's `addGfxDisplay()` increments the counter before inserting its display node and ignores the result (`Modules/Gfx/gfx_enum.c:56-83`); `gfxEnum()` invokes it for each enumerated display and the registered class handler marks non-base Gfx objects expandable (`:85-127`). NListtree Insert returns zero when its node allocation fails (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:7064-7094,7284-7293`), so a Storage bus, ATA/AHCI bus, or Gfx driver can remain marked expandable even when a child insert fails. **Trigger:** opening the explicitly buildable PCI module on a system with PCI devices but no bridge devices; or enumerating a Storage/ATA/AHCI unit or Gfx display when NListtree cannot allocate its node. **Consequence:** SysExplorer displays an empty expandable PCI-driver or storage/display branch, or omits a child while retaining the parent expansion flag. Base expansion state on successful child insertion, or have enumerators report whether they added a child. **Affected configuration:** SysExplorer builds including the optional PCI, Storage, ATA, AHCI, and/or Gfx modules; their dependencies are commented out of the default aggregate targets (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/mmakefile.src:82-84,112-114,122-124,134-136,145-147,181-185`). **Confidence:** high for the counter/flag paths and NListtree allocation-failure return; no PCI inventory, allocation failure or GUI was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9760

**SysExplorer repeats all PCI bridge entries under every PCI driver.** The class handler invokes `pciEnum()` for each `CLID_Hidd_PCIDriver` object (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/Modules/PCI/pci_enum.c:145-158`). Each invocation creates the general `CLID_Hidd_PCI` object and calls `EnumDevices` with an empty requirements list; the PCI HIDD contract says that this enumerates devices across all buses managed by all drivers (`rom/hidds/pci/doc/pci.en:12-20`; implementation `rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:421-425`). Although `pciEnum()` stores the current driver in `ed_Controller`, the callback never uses it to filter devices (`pci_enum.c:53-60,101-127`). Thus every PCI-to-PCI bridge is inserted under each PCI-driver row. **Trigger:** a system with more than one PCI driver object and at least one PCI-to-PCI bridge, when the explicitly buildable PCI support module is loaded. **Consequence:** bridge entries appear repeatedly under unrelated PCI-driver parents, making the displayed hierarchy inaccurate. Filter enumeration by the current controller/driver or enumerate only that driver's devices. **Affected configuration:** SysExplorer builds including the optional PCI support module. **Confidence:** high for the global enumeration contract and unused controller field; the duplicate display requires multiple driver objects and a bridge. No PCI inventory or GUI was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
