Read a valid object name into an initialized pointer or use a fixed fallback title. **Affected configuration:** SysExplorer builds including the optional PCI support module. **Confidence:** high for the uninitialized value and direct use; exact UI failure depends on the stack value and MUI title handling. No GUI was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9763

**SysExplorer leaks the allocated title string on failed construction and after each disposed Power property window.** `PowerWindow__OM_NEW()` allocates `wintitle` and passes it as `MUIA_Window_Title` (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/Modules/Power/power_window_cl.c:586-602`). Free the temporary on the failed constructor path and release the retained title during disposal after the superclass no longer needs it. **Affected configuration:** SysExplorer builds including the explicitly buildable Power support module. **Confidence:** high for both missing cleanup paths; the construction-failure trigger depends on a later MUI construction failure. ## GD9767

**Zune Text reads past the copied label when its highlighted marker is the final character.** `zune_text_parse_line()` handles `ZTEXT_ARG_HICHARIDX` by advancing `s` twice to underline the character after the marker, then the loop advances it again (`workbench/libs/muimaster/textengine.c:529-543`). If the marker is the final byte of the string, the two advances move from the marker to the NUL and then one byte beyond the allocated copy. `zune_text_chunk_new()` copies a two-byte range starting at the NUL, so `strncpy()` reads the one-past byte (`:254-257`); the parser then advances farther and dereferences the out-of-range pointer in its loop condition (`:500,543`). `zune_text_new()` also receives that pointer and dereferences it in its post-parse newline/terminator checks (`:159-171`). `MUIO_Button` constructs Text objects with `MUIA_Text_HiCharIdx` set to `'_'` and passes the original button label as `MUIA_Text_Contents` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_makeobject.c:358-367`), so a button label ending in the marker reaches this path. **Trigger:** create/layout a Text object with HiCharIdx matching its last content character, including a MUIO_Button label ending in `_`. **Consequence:** parser and caller read beyond the allocated, NUL-terminated text copy; layout or rendering may be incorrect or fail. The source/caller recheck found no confirmed maintained label ending in `_`; the trigger remains available through the Text/MUIO_Button API. Stop parsing when the marker has no following character and keep the source pointer within the string. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `muimaster` Text and make-object support. **Confidence:** high for the out-of-range pointer and reads; no malformed label or GUI was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9768

**Zune menu constructors dereference a failed superclass object allocation.** `Common__OM_NEW()` correctly returns NULL when its superclass `OM_NEW` fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/menuitem.c:167-175`), but `Menuitem__OM_NEW()`, `Menu__OM_NEW()`, and `Menustrip__OM_NEW()` immediately pass that NULL to `INST_DATA()` and write their flags without checking (`:224-254`). **Trigger:** superclass object construction fails while creating a menu item, menu, or menustrip, such as the root object-pool allocation failing. **Consequence:** the constructor dereferences instance data for an object that was never created instead of propagating NULL, so memory pressure during menu construction can break the caller. Return immediately when `Common__OM_NEW()` fails in each wrapper. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the `muimaster` menuitem/menu/menustrip classes. **Confidence:** high for the NULL return and immediate instance-data writes; no allocation failure or GUI was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9769

**MUI_MakeObjectA continues after NewMenu object construction failures, leaking or misparenting entries.** `CreateMenuString()` keeps `menu` NULL when a `MenuObject` construction returns NULL (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_makeobject.c:69-78`). It continues through later `NM_ITEM` entries and, if a `MenuitemObject` succeeds, calls `DoMethod(menu, MUIM_Family_AddTail, ...)` without checking `menu` (`:94-115`). The selected `DoMethod()` helper treats a NULL receiver as a no-op and returns zero (`compiler/alib/domethod.c:60-68`), so that item is unattached and undisposed. This covers failed `NM_TITLE` creation as well: the following item is orphaned, and later `NM_SUB` entries can be attached beneath that orphan before the partial strip is returned (`mui_makeobject.c:69-79,94-126`). The function also leaves `menuitem` pointing at the last successfully created `NM_ITEM` if a later `MenuitemObject` construction fails; following `NM_SUB` entries still satisfy the stale non-NULL check and are appended under that earlier item (`mui_makeobject.c:94-126`). `NM_SUB` is a child of the current item in the selected GadTools NewMenu semantics (`workbench/libs/gadtools/createmenusa.c:250-355`). The default Wanderer menu tables include multiple `NM_TITLE`/`NM_ITEM` sequences and item/subitem groups (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:3834-3952`), so an allocation failure followed by successful later construction can leave a section absent, leak orphan entries, or put a submenu under an orphan/previous item. **Trigger:** a transient allocation failure during `MUIO_MenustripNM` conversion, followed by successful later item construction. **Consequence:** the returned menu is incomplete or has incorrect hierarchy, and detached menu objects are not disposed. Abort/dispose the partial menu or track and validate the current parent after each failed constructor. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `muimaster` and calling `MUI_MakeObjectA(MUIO_MenustripNM, ...)`, including the default Wanderer menu path (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:3890,3952`; `workbench/system/Wanderer/mmakefile.src:38`). **Confidence:** high for the constructor-result state handling and selected menu nesting semantics; manifestation requires the stated allocation-success/failure sequence. No allocation failure or GUI was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#muimaster-menu-constructors-and-mui_makeobjecta-full-bodycaller-pass-gd9768-gd9769).

## GD9770

**MUI Group OM_SET leaves filtered attributes overwritten in the caller's tag list.** After calling the superclass, `Group__OM_SET()` scans `msg->ops_AttrList` and changes `MUIA_HelpLine`, `MUIA_UserData`, `MUIA_Frame`, `MUIA_ShowMe`, `MUIA_Weight`, and other filtered tags to `TAG_IGNORE` before forwarding the message to children (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:577-620`). It restores the `ops_AttrList` pointer, but never restores the modified `ti_Tag` values. Intuition `SetAttrsA()` assigns the exact caller-supplied `tagList` pointer to `ops_AttrList` and dispatches it directly (`rom/intuition/setattrsa.c:77-82`), so this mutation is observable by any caller that retains that array. The nearby `MUIA_Disabled` path explicitly saves and restores its original tag (`:560-562`), showing that the incoming list is otherwise retained. **Trigger:** an `OM_SET` call on a Group with child forwarding enabled includes any filtered attribute in a tag list that its caller later reuses or inspects. **Consequence:** later iteration of the caller's original list silently skips those attributes, and reusing the list for another Set applies different attributes than requested. This is conditional on tag-list reuse; ephemeral temporary lists only incur mutation with no later visible effect. Preserve original tags while filtering, or forward through a copied list. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `muimaster` Group; callers passing reusable OM_SET tag arrays. **Confidence:** high for the in-place mutation and missing restoration; caller-visible effect depends on reuse, and no OM_SET call was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9771

**Wanderer can lose drawer ToolTypes or omit the new sort preference after a snapshot-copy allocation failure.** `IconWindow_StoreSettings()` allocates a cleared pointer array, then assigns each `StrDup(oldtooltypes[i])` result without checking it; it continues copying and appends the `WNDRRSRT` preference after a failed entry (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow.c:213-234`). `StrDup()` returns NULL when its `AllocVec()` fails (`compiler/alib/strdup.c:50-56`), so a failed copy of an existing ToolType becomes an early terminator even though later entries are copied after it. The new sort preference is also duplicated without checking the result (`iconwindow.c:229-232`); failure there leaves all existing ToolTypes serializable but omits the updated sort setting. The function installs the new array and calls `PutDiskObject()` (`:234-238`). The selected writer opens the icon in `MODE_NEWFILE`, whose DOS contract deletes the old file and creates a new one (`workbench/libs/icon/puticontaglist.c:124-132`; `workbench/libs/icon/support.c:17-48`; `rom/dos/open.c:40-48`). The AOS `ProcessToolTypes()` writer counts entries only until the first NULL (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjio.c:878-898`); the PNG `icOn` chunk writer likewise emits ToolTypes only while each pointer is non-NULL (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjPNGio.c:900-912`). The snapshot menu reaches `IconWindow__MUIM_IconWindow_Snapshot()`, which calls `IconWindow_StoreSettings()` and returns TRUE regardless of whether it snapshots all icons or just the window (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:1428-1435`; `iconwindow.c:1611-1669`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds including `workbench-system-wanderer-app`, when snapshotting a drawer with an existing icon and either a `StrDup()` of an existing ToolType fails or the new `WNDRRSRT` duplication fails, followed by a successful `PutDiskObject()` write. **Consequence:** failure copying an existing entry causes that entry and every later ToolType to be omitted from the replacement `.info` file; failure copying the new sort preference leaves the prior ToolTypes but omits the current sort setting. Check all string-copy results and abort the save before replacing the existing icon if any duplication fails. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked nullable copies, NULL-terminated-prefix serialization and overwrite path; requires a string-allocation failure followed by a successful write. No allocation failure or icon write was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9772

**SysExplorer's Properties action dereferences missing tree-node userdata after a construct-hook allocation failure.** Its NListtree construct hook allocates an `ObjectUserData` record with `AllocPooled()` and returns the result, including NULL on allocation failure (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/sysexp_main.c:200-210`). NListtree's `MUIM_NListtree_Construct` passes that hook result through unchanged (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:6479-6490`); when the later node and name allocations succeed, `_NListtree_Insert()` stores the NULL result in `tn_User` and continues inserting the node (`:7101-7124`). SysExplorer's Properties hook retrieves `node->tn_User` and dereferences `data->win` without a NULL check (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/sysexp_main.c:266-270`). The hook is reachable from both the Properties menu and NListtree double-click notification (`:367-385`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the build-selected SysExplorer app, when `constructFunc()`'s pooled userdata allocation fails for a node, the subsequent NListtree node/name allocations succeed, and the user invokes Properties on that node or double-clicks it. **Consequence:** the Properties hook dereferences NULL and faults the application. Handle construct-hook allocation failure before publishing the node or make the property path tolerate absent userdata. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked NULL propagation and dereference; requires the userdata allocation to fail while later insert allocations succeed. No allocation failure or GUI action was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9773 — withdrawn duplicate

This duplicate candidate is consolidated into [GD9954](AROS-graphics-desktop.md#gd9954), which records the built-in string-hook allocation failure and the `TRUE` return after the old row is removed. Keep GD9954 as the sole active report entry; preserving the old row on custom-hook failure remains medium-confidence because the public documentation does not specify rollback semantics.

## GD9774

**Wanderer snapshot can replace a drawer icon with incomplete output when the settings write fails.** `IconWindow_StoreSettings()` updates the loaded drawer icon and calls `PutDiskObject(dir_name, drawericon)` without checking its BOOL result (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow.c:139-166,195-243`). The selected `PutDiskObject()` wrapper returns `PutIconTags()`'s result (`workbench/libs/icon/putdiskobject.c:42-50`); for this full write, `PutIconTagList()` opens the existing `.info` path through `OpenIcon(..., MODE_NEWFILE)` before invoking `WriteIcon()` (`workbench/libs/icon/puticontaglist.c:124-133`; `support.c:17-57`). DOS defines `MODE_NEWFILE` as deleting the old file and creating a new one (`rom/dos/open.c:45-48`). Both selected serialization paths propagate output failure: PNG writing checks short `Write()` results (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjPNGio.c:959-983`), while the AOS `WriteStruct()` walk aborts when a primitive write or special ToolTypes/DrawerData hook fails (`compiler/arossupport/writestruct.c:98-141,274-285,319-324`; `workbench/libs/icon/diskobjio.c:875-898,943-949`). `__WriteIcon_WB()` returns that failure to `PutIconTagList()` (`support.c:396-415`; `puticontaglist.c:126-155`). The `Snapshot` method ignores the void settings-save path and returns TRUE (`iconwindow.c:1611-1669`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds including `workbench-system-wanderer-app`, when a user snapshots a drawer with an existing `.info` file, the new-file open succeeds, and icon serialization then fails. **Consequence:** the previous drawer icon has already been replaced; the resulting file may be empty or partial, and Wanderer reports the Snapshot method as successful. Check and propagate the save result, and preserve the existing file until a complete replacement is ready. **Confidence:** high for the open mode, return-value propagation gap, and unconditional Snapshot success; requires a post-open write failure. This is distinct from GD9771, where a failed ToolType duplication followed by a successful serialization writes a valid but truncated ToolType prefix. No filesystem failure or icon write was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9775

**Wanderer snapshot-all ignores failed in-place icon-position updates.** The snapshot-all branch updates each visible icon's in-memory coordinates and calls `PutIconTagList()` with `ICONPUTA_OnlyUpdatePosition`, but discards the returned BOOL (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow.c:1620-1649`). In this mode `PutIconTagList()` opens the existing icon with `MODE_OLDFILE` and propagates the `WriteIcon()` result (`workbench/libs/icon/puticontaglist.c:124-133,152-155`). The selected non-PNG fast path writes the X and Y fields separately at fixed offsets and returns FALSE if either four-byte `Write()` is short; it does not roll back a completed first-field write (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:335-348`). DOS `Write()` returns the actual byte count, so a short write can modify only part of a coordinate (`rom/dos/write.c:28-43`). The snapshot loop continues and the enclosing method later returns TRUE regardless of those per-icon results (`iconwindow.c:1661-1669`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds including `workbench-system-wanderer-app`, when the user runs Snapshot All on a window containing an existing non-PNG icon and one of its position-field writes returns fewer than four bytes. **Consequence:** the icon may retain stale coordinates or a partially updated X/Y value, while Wanderer reports the snapshot method as successful and continues with the remaining icons. Check each result and report/abort on failure; an atomic temporary-file replacement would avoid partial coordinate writes. **Confidence:** high for the discarded return, two-write update, and short-write contract; requires an I/O short write. This is distinct from GD9774's drawer-settings full rewrite through `MODE_NEWFILE`. No filesystem failure or icon write was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9776

**Position-only icon writes ignore a failed initial seek and can overwrite the icon header.** In the non-PNG `ICONPUTA_OnlyUpdatePosition` path, `__WriteIcon_WB()` seeks to the X-coordinate field at offset `0x3a` but discards the `Seek()` result, then writes four bytes; it likewise ignores the Y-field seek result (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:335-348`). `PutIconTagList()` selects this fast path after opening the existing icon with `MODE_OLDFILE` (`puticontaglist.c:124-133`). DOS `Seek()` may fail and returns `-1` on error (`rom/dos/seek.c:25-40`); if the initial seek fails without moving the file position while writes remain accepted, the first coordinate write begins at the file's current offset instead of `0x3a`. The fast path can then report success because it checks only the two four-byte `Write()` results.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** callers using `PutIconTagList()` with `ICONPUTA_OnlyUpdatePosition` on an existing non-PNG icon through a handler that rejects the initial seek without repositioning the file but accepts writes. **Consequence:** X/Y bytes are written at the wrong offset (commonly the file start), corrupting unrelated icon data while the API may report success. Check both seek results before writing. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked seek and subsequent writes; trigger depends on a filesystem/device handler's failed-seek position behavior. No icon file or handler operation was used. This is distinct from GD9775's short-write result being ignored by Wanderer, and from GD9774's full drawer-settings overwrite path. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9777

**An empty icon name makes the icon library read before the supplied string.** `GetIconTagList()` documents a path argument and permits `NULL` for default-icon retrieval; a non-NULL name reaches `OpenIcon()` (`workbench/libs/icon/geticontaglist.c:29-32,177-179`). `PutIconTagList()` likewise routes a non-NULL name to `OpenIcon()` (`workbench/libs/icon/puticontaglist.c:120-133`). The shared `__OpenIcon_WB()` helper calls `strlen(name)` and immediately evaluates `name[nameLength - 1]` (`workbench/libs/icon/support.c:17-23`). For an empty string, `nameLength` is zero and the unsigned subtraction underflows, so the helper reads outside the string before attempting the `.info` path.

There is a checked-in caller path in the optional IconInject utility: a five-character `SOURCE` or `TARGET` argument takes the suffix branch's `else`, allocates a name buffer, and copies `strlen(name) - 5` bytes, which is zero; the resulting empty name is passed to `GetIconTags()` (`workbench/tools/IconInject/main.c:40-65,77-89`). The same argument normalization defect is separately covered by GD6109.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds including `icon.library`; directly, any caller passing a non-NULL empty object path without selecting a default. The checked-in trigger is the explicitly buildable optional `workbench-tools-injecticon` target when either argument has exactly five characters; both normalized buffers must allocate for execution to reach the icon lookup. **Consequence:** an out-of-bounds read while checking for a volume-name suffix; behavior is undefined and may fault or continue with an invalid path. Reject empty names before indexing or check `nameLength` first. **Confidence:** high for the underflow and read, and for the five-character IconInject normalization path; actual runtime outcome was not exercised. This is distinct from GD4801's wrong normalization and short-name oversized copy. No icon API or filesystem operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9778

**Zune timer-handler cleanup passes an invalid request to `CheckIO` after timer allocation failure.** Clock registers its timer input handler during Setup and later removes it during Cleanup (`workbench/classes/zune/clock/clock.c:178-186,219-232`). Busy has the same Setup/Cleanup and Show/Hide lifecycle (`workbench/classes/zune/busy/busy.c:120-184`), and Graph registers from Setup or its periodic attribute and removes on teardown/disable (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:331-342,425-441,545-559`). NList adds its timer handler in `mNL_Setup()` and unconditionally removes it from `mNL_Cleanup()` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc.c:1578-1583,1601-1614`). TextEditor configuration initializes `BlinkSpeed` to pending state 1 when blinking is enabled (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/InitConfig.c:206-216`). On activation, `mGoActive()` calls `MUIM_Application_AddInputHandler` and then unconditionally sets the state to 2; deactivation and `FreeConfig()` remove the handler when the state is 2 (`Dispatcher.c:578-582,615-619`; `InitConfig.c:437-441`). The separate input-trigger handler is also added and removed through RequestInput/RejectInput (`Dispatcher.c:86-105,609-619`). Thus timer-request allocation failure in MUI still advances TextEditor into the cleanup path with the request field unset.

MUI Application allocates a `timerequest_ext` and stores it in the input node only on allocation success, but returns TRUE even on failure (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1474-1502`). The removal path reads that node field and calls `CheckIO()` without validating the request (`:1509-1520`); Exec `CheckIO()` dereferences it (`rom/exec/checkio.c:48-58`). **Trigger:** any of these clients registers a timer handler while the request allocation fails, then reaches its matching removal path. **Consequence:** removal passes an unset or stale request pointer to `CheckIO()` and can fault instead of completing cleanup. Propagate allocation failure from AddInputHandler and have each caller track successful registration before removal. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting Zune Clock, Busy, Graph, NList, or TextEditor with the relevant timer handlers active; Graph/NList/TextEditor are optional class targets in this source tree. **Confidence:** high for the shared failure path and the traced add/remove pairs; allocation failure and client teardown were not induced. This shares MUI's invalid-request root cause with GD5191's Area rearm/cleanup path; GD5191 retains that separate callback rearm sequence. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9779

**Graph InfoText parsing dereferences an unchecked line allocation.** `Graph__ParseInfoText()` allocates a node for each parsed line and immediately writes `infoLine->ln_Name` without checking the `AllocVec()` result (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:119-145`, especially :138-141). `Graph__OM_SET()` calls the parser for `MUIA_Graph_InfoText` (`:302-305`). **Trigger:** setting non-NULL InfoText while a line-node allocation fails. **Consequence:** a NULL dereference during construction or attribute update, after the previous text has already been freed. Check the allocation and preserve a valid empty/old state or report failure. **Affected configuration and checked-in caller:** optional Graph.mcc clients using InfoText, including the explicitly buildable SysExplorer Power support module. Its battery-property constructor creates `GraphObject` with non-NULL `MUIA_Graph_InfoText` set to the empty string (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/Modules/Power/power_window_cl.c:452-457`); Graph initialization passes that attribute through `SetAttrsA()` and `Graph__ParseInfoText()` (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:233,302-305`), so the line-node allocation is attempted during battery-window construction. The Power module edge is commented out of SysExplorer's default aggregate (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/mmakefile.src:77-84`), so this caller requires selecting that optional module. **Confidence:** high for unchecked allocation and immediate dereference; the caller path is source-confirmed, while allocation failure is conditional and was not induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9780

**Graph source-handle lookup can return an invalid slot after growth failure or index overflow.** `Graph__MUIM_Graph_GetSourceHandle()` calls `Graph__UpdateSourceArray()` when the requested index exceeds the current count, ignores its return value, and then returns `&graph_Sources[SourceNo]` (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:849-862`). Growth publishes a new array only if `AllocMem()` succeeds (`:43-70`); on failure the old pointer/count remain. A caller requesting the next source therefore receives a pointer outside the old allocation and may pass it to `Graph__MUIM_Graph_SetSourceAttrib()`, which dereferences it (`:865-890`). The selected SysMon single-graph path requests one source for each reported CPU, starting from Graph's one-source initial array, and immediately installs pen/read-hook attributes for indices 1 and above (`workbench/system/SysMon/processor_graph.c:116-119,157-195`; processor count comes from the selected processor query at `processor.c:43-80`). A failed growth on that path makes those subsequent attribute writes use the invalid slot. There is also an independent index-wrap route: `MUIP_Graph_GetSourceHandle.SourceNo` is `ULONG` (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.h:35`), so `SourceNo == ULONG_MAX` makes `SourceNo + 1` wrap to zero before the `IPTR` parameter receives it. `Graph__UpdateSourceArray(data, 0)` requests a zero-byte `AllocMem()`, which returns NULL by contract (`rom/exec/allocmem.c:90-92`); because the helper initialized `newSourceArray` to the old pointer and does not update the array/count on failure, `GetSourceHandle()` then indexes the old array with `ULONG_MAX`. This second trigger does not require allocation failure and is limited to a client supplying that extreme source number; no checked-in caller does so. **Trigger:** request a source index beyond the current count while the source-array allocation fails, then use the returned handle; the checked-in SysMon caller reaches this path when single-graph mode is active and more than one processor is reported. Alternatively, call the exposed method with `SourceNo == ULONG_MAX`, then use its returned handle. **Consequence:** invalid memory access and possible graph-state corruption. Return a failure/NULL handle when growth fails and have callers check it. **Affected configuration:** optional Graph.mcc clients that add sources dynamically, including the selected SysMon single-graph caller when configured for multiple processors. **Confidence:** high for the ignored growth failure, unchanged old allocation, immediate caller write, and ULONG addition wrap; no allocation failure or extreme-index call was made. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9781

**Graph can publish an entry count larger than per-source buffer capacity.** `Graph__UpdateSourceEntries()` allocates a replacement array only when the requested count exceeds the current count; on `AllocMem()` failure it leaves `gs_Entries` at its old allocation but still returns the source pointer (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:76-101`). `Graph__OM_SET()` ignores that outcome and unconditionally commits the new `graph_EntryCount` after the per-source attempts (`:357-373`). With periodic updates enabled and a source read hook installed, `Graph__MUIM_Graph_Timer()` continues to advance `graph_EntryPtr` against the larger count and passes `&gs_Entries[graph_EntryPtr]` to the hook (`:924-963`). Once that index reaches the old capacity, the hook writes beyond the old allocation. The draw path also reads entries up to the current pointer (`:777-800`), and disposal later frees the old allocation using the larger committed size (`:258-267`). The same unchecked helper is used for the initial nonzero entry count: the selected SysMon Graph constructor sets a 1000 ms interval (`workbench/system/SysMon/processor_graph.c:102-111`), and Graph `OM_NEW` applies it with `SetAttrsA()` after creating the initial source (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:219-233`). The interval sets a nonzero count, so if this first entry-buffer allocation fails, `gs_Entries` remains NULL while the count is committed. SysMon subsequently installs `GraphReadProcessorValueFunc` (`processor_graph.c:182-195`), which writes through the timer-supplied `storage` pointer (`:53-70`); a later timer tick therefore writes through a pointer derived from NULL. This is the initial-allocation form of the same per-source capacity publication bug, not a separate finding. There is also a successful-allocation capacity mismatch on 32-bit builds: `IPTR` is unsigned pointer-sized and `sizeof(IPTR) * count` is unchecked (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:83-85`; `compiler/include/aros/cpu.h:88-90`). For example, `MUIA_Graph_EntryCount = 0x40000001` wraps a 32-bit four-byte element-size product to four bytes; `AllocMem()` can then succeed and publish that buffer while `OM_SET` commits the requested count. With periodic sampling enabled, the timer eventually indexes beyond the one-element allocation. The checked-in search found no caller supplying an extreme entry count; this route is limited to an external Graph client or future caller on a 32-bit target. **Trigger:** a per-source entry-buffer allocation fails while Graph sets its initial nonzero count or grows an existing count, followed by a timer tick, drawing, or disposal that uses the published count. **Consequence:** out-of-bounds source-hook writes or graph reads. Disposal passes the committed size for the retained old allocation; any additional effect of that mismatch is unverified. Update the count only if every source resize succeeds, or preserve per-source capacities. **Affected configuration:** optional Graph.mcc with one or more allocated sources and dynamic/fixed entry-count growth; periodic sampling requires a configured handler/source read hook. **Confidence:** high for the failed resize retaining the old pointer, unconditional count publication, and later indexed consumers; no allocation failure or graph update was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9782

**Graph marks its timer handler registered even when MUI cannot allocate the timer request.** Graph sets `GRAPHF_HANDLER` before calling `MUIM_Application_AddInputHandler()` in its periodic attribute and Setup paths (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:331-342,425-441`) and does not check the result. The selected MUI Application method returns success even when its `AllocVec()` for `timerequest_ext` fails, leaving the handler node without a request (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1474-1502`). Graph then suppresses registration retries, while cleanup later attempts removal (`graph.c:545-559`), reaching the shared invalid-request cleanup described by GD9778. **Trigger:** enable Graph periodic updates while the Application timer-request allocation fails. **Consequence:** periodic graph updates are silently lost; later cleanup passes the unset request into the removal path. Clear the registered flag or report failure when registration did not create a request, and make the Application method report allocation failure. **Affected configuration:** optional Graph.mcc under MUI when periodic updates are enabled. **Confidence:** high for the caller's unchecked registration and selected allocation path; no timer or allocation failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9783

**AboutWindow leaks its pool, catalog strings, and duplicated attributes when base-object construction fails.** `AboutWindow__OM_NEW()` creates a pool, opens a catalog, and duplicates each supplied title/version/copyright/description string before calling `DoSuperNewTags()` (`workbench/classes/zune/aboutwindow/aboutwindow.c:185-248,271-309`). When that call returns NULL, the error path closes only the catalog and returns (`:311-376`); it neither deletes `pool` nor frees any successful `StrDup()` allocations. **Trigger:** construction reaches `DoSuperNewTags()` with at least one owned allocation and base object construction fails, for example under memory pressure. **Consequence:** every failed attempt leaks the pool and all successfully duplicated strings, so repeated failed opens accumulate memory loss. Release all locally owned resources on this path (and any locally created child object not transferred to a parent). **Affected configuration:** optional AboutWindow.mcc builds, including its caller QuickPart, during failed window construction. **Confidence:** high for the allocated resources and incomplete error cleanup; no allocation failure or GUI was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9784

**Aboutbox dereferences the optional credits attribute when it is omitted.** `MUIA_Aboutbox_Credits` is described as optional in the class documentation (`workbench/classes/zune/aboutbox/MCC_Aboutbox.doc:86-92`). The constructor leaves `data->credits` unset when the tag is absent (`workbench/classes/zune/aboutbox/Aboutbox.c:498-519`), but every successful Window Setup calls `ParseCredits()` (`:616-634`, specifically :627-628). That function assigns the NULL field to `credits` and immediately evaluates `*credits++` in its loop condition (`:163-178`), causing an invalid read. **Trigger:** construct and set up an Aboutbox without supplying the documented optional Credits tag. **Consequence:** setup can fault instead of showing the remaining application information; treat absent credits as an empty string and skip parsing. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting Aboutbox.mcc and omitting `MUIA_Aboutbox_Credits`, as the documented API permits. **Confidence:** high; the NULL default, unconditional call, and dereference are direct; no GUI was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9785

**Calltips applies the left-margin flag to vertical positioning and ignores the top-margin flag.** `setRectangle()` subtracts the root group's top margin only when `data->marginLeft` is true (`workbench/classes/zune/calltips/Calltips.c:21-25`). The constructor stores `MUIA_Calltips_MarginLeft` and `MUIA_Calltips_MarginTop` in separate fields (`:80-93,119-126`), but `marginTop` is never consulted by the positioning code. **Trigger:** construct Calltips with different left/top margin settings, or change the rectangle while the root group has nonzero top margin. **Consequence:** vertical window placement follows the left-margin setting, so disabling top-margin compensation has no effect and disabling left-margin compensation also disables it vertically. Use `marginTop` for the top coordinate. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting optional Calltips.mcc. **Confidence:** high for the field mismatch and resulting coordinate calculation; no MUI window was opened. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9786 — Duplicate of GD6061

This is the same file-backed IconImage DiskObject ownership leak documented under [GD6061](#gd6061), including the constructor-failure path. GD6061 is the canonical finding; GD9786 is not a separate defect.

## GD9787

**MUI PenSpec acquisition failures become foreground byte 0xff in Lamp, NList, NListtree, BetterString, and TextEditor (wrong or unsupported drawing color; high source confidence).** In Lamp, `Lamp__MUIM_Draw()` assigns the result of `MUI_ObtainPen()` to `lmp_PenNr` but does not check its failure value `-1`; it masks the result with `MUIPEN()` and calls `SetAPen()` (`workbench/classes/zune/lamp/lamp.c:316-324`). NListtree's `ObtPen()` stores the result directly (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:824-834`), and its line/shadow/glow paths mask the pen before `SetAPen()` (`:274-306,335-374,405-444,473-504`); configurable PenSpecs are acquired during setup and config changes (`:5497-5524,4272-4303`). NList's `obtain_pen()` does the same (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc.c:243-257`), and `DrawText()` passes `MUIPEN(mypen)` into `SetABPenDrMd()` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc6.c:747-770`). BetterString's `GetCol()` returns `MUI_ObtainPen()` without checking (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/InitConfig.c:37-45`); its string renderer masks the selected text/cursor colors before `SetAPen()` (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/PrintString.c:256-281`). TextEditor's `SetCol()` stores the result without checking (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/InitConfig.c:86-100`), and style/separator rendering masks these colors before `SetAPen()` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/PrintLineWithStyles.c:62-97,229-265,307-310`). The selected MUI implementation returns `-1` when pen setup fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_obtainpen.c:55-77`), and `MUIPEN(-1)` is `0xffff` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui.h:175-177`). The low byte passed to `SetAPen()` or stored by `SetABPenDrMd()` is `0xff`; the RastPort foreground field is a signed `BYTE` (`rom/graphics/graphics.conf:97`; `rom/graphics/setapen.c:16-20,50-55`; `setabpendrmd.c:17-23,60-67`; `compiler/include/graphics/rastport.h:63`). Lamp's RGB branch checks its `ObtainBestPen()` result, while the listed PenSpec consumers do not. **Trigger:** use any listed class with a PenSpec whose MUI acquisition fails before its drawing path runs; for NListtree, the affected line path requires a normal line type. **Consequence:** drawing proceeds with foreground byte 0xff; this can select the wrong color or an unsupported index on a colormap with fewer than 256 entries. Check the return and use a safe fallback color. **Affected configuration:** the separately buildable Lamp, NList, NListtree, BetterString, and TextEditor class targets when using PenSpec colors (`workbench/classes/zune/lamp/mmakefile.src:8-18`; `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/mmakefile.src:4-37`; `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/mmakefile.src:4-19`; `workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/mmakefile.src:4-37`; `workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/mmakefile.src:4-48`). **Confidence:** high for unchecked `-1`, low-byte narrowing, and drawing continuing; whether byte 0xff is unsupported or visibly wrong depends on the active colormap and was not run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9788

**Calendar accepts invalid date fields in date conversion.** `Calendar__OM_SET()` copies `MUIA_Calendar_Month` and `MUIA_Calendar_Year` directly into `clockdata`, and adds one to `MUIA_Calendar_Month0`, without validating the values (`workbench/classes/zune/calendar/calendar.c:150-163`). It then calls `NumMonthDays()` and `Date2Amiga()` on that state (`:179-194`; `NumMonthDays()` calls `Date2Amiga()` at `:114-121`). For an invalid month, `Date2Amiga()` indexes its 12-entry `dayspermonth` table with `date->month - 1` without a bounds check (`rom/utility/date2amiga.c:55-64`); month 0 or Month0 12 therefore indexes outside the table. For the lower year bound, `CheckDate()` explicitly rejects years before 1978 (`rom/utility/checkdate.c:76-78`), but Calendar bypasses that validator. A direct `MUIA_Calendar_Year=1977` set with January 1 reaches `Date2Amiga()`; its leap-day calculation yields zero elapsed seconds for this input, and the subsequent `Amiga2Date(0, ...)` changes the displayed date to January 1, 1978 (`calendar.c:192-194`; `date2amiga.c:84-98`; `amiga2date.c:86-107,177-183`). Day zero is also accepted: the setter only clamps values above the month's maximum (`calendar.c:179-190`), so `MUIA_Calendar_MonthDay=0` reaches `Date2Amiga()`; for January 1978, `mday - 1` becomes -1 and the day-offset addition wraps the unsigned seconds result to a large timestamp (`date2amiga.c:60-64`). The following `Amiga2Date()` normalizes that wrapped value to a distant future date. The `MUIA_Calendar_Date` constructor/setter path also copies client `ClockData` without validation (`calendar.c:77-82,145-148`), so invalid month/year/day values can enter through that API as well.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting Calendar.mcc when a direct client supplies a month outside 1–12, Month0 outside 0–11, day 0, or a year before 1978 through the attributes or `ClockData`. The checked-in Time preferences client uses its 12-entry month cycle and clamps the year to 1978–2099 (`workbench/prefs/time/main.c:48-63,272-303,639-652`); no in-tree invalid month or year caller was found. **Consequence:** invalid months cause an out-of-bounds table read; day zero wraps the timestamp to a distant future date; pre-1978 years can be silently normalized to a different date (for the stated 1977 example, January 1 becomes January 1, 1978). Validate the complete date before conversion. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked fields, month-table access, explicit utility year minimum, 1977 conversion path, and unsigned day-offset wrap; triggers are limited to invalid direct-client input and no UI behavior was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9789

**LoginWindow supplies authentication methods after the Poplist has already been constructed.** `LoginWindow__OM_NEW()` creates `PoplistObject` with the string object and button but without `MUIA_Poplist_Array` (`workbench/classes/zune/loginwindow/loginwindow.c:251-268`). The checked-in debug caller supplies three distinct `MUIA_LoginWindow_Method` entries (`developer/debug/test/Zune/loginwindow.c:63-68`), but the popup has no selectable authentication methods; with multiple methods, the returned method string remains unset unless some other caller supplies it. ## GD9791

## GD9795

**NListviews MCP leaks opened libraries when an AmigaOS 4 interface lookup fails.**

On AmigaOS 4, `ClassInit()` stores the result of `OpenLibrary("commodities.library", 37L)` in `CxBase` and combines it with `GETINTERFACE(ICommodities, ...)` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlistviews_mcp/library.c:170-171`). Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD4390

**Concurrent AmigaGuide startup can publish duplicate ARexx port names on ExecSMP.** Each AmigaGuide process chooses the first unused numbered port name by calling `FindPort()` in a loop, then assigns the name to its newly created port and calls `AddPort()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/process.c:225-239`). The whole check-and-publish sequence is wrapped in `Forbid()`, but Exec documents that on ExecSMP this only prevents scheduling on the calling CPU (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-60`). `FindPort()` takes and releases the port-list read lock for the lookup (`rom/exec/findport.c:48-57`); `AddPort()` later takes the write lock and enqueues the port without checking whether another port with the same name was added in between (`rom/exec/addport.c:50-75`). Thus two concurrently starting AmigaGuide instances on different CPUs can both observe a free suffix and publish separate ports with the same name. The class exposes the per-instance port name through `DTA_ARexxPortName` (`amigaguideclass.c:431-434`), and each process consumes ARexx messages from its own port (`process.c:312-339`); external clients addressing the duplicate name can reach whichever matching port `FindPort()` returns, rather than reliably reaching the intended document instance. Make the suffix reservation and publication atomic across CPUs, or retry the uniqueness check while holding a cross-CPU lock.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** ExecSMP builds selecting the AmigaGuide datatype, when two instances with the same port-name stem start concurrently and both select the same free suffix before either calls `AddPort()`. **Consequence:** duplicate public ARexx names make name-based commands ambiguous and can route a request to the wrong AmigaGuide instance. **Confidence:** high for the split lookup/publication, local-only `Forbid`, and absence of duplicate-name validation in `AddPort`; manifestation requires the stated concurrent startup interleaving and a client addressing the duplicated name. No datatype, port, ARexx request, or concurrent startup was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD4020

**Concurrent ConClip startup can publish duplicate rendezvous port names on ExecSMP.** `checkport()` wraps `FindPort(CONCLIP_PORTNAME)` and the subsequent `CreatePort(CONCLIP_PORTNAME, 1)` in `Forbid()` (`workbench/c/ConClip.c:153-172`). On ExecSMP, `Forbid()` prevents task switches only on the calling CPU (`rom/exec/forbid.c:55-60`), so two concurrent ConClip starts on separate CPUs can both observe no port before either publishes. `CreatePort()` publishes the named port with `AddPort()` (`compiler/alib/createport.c:32-52`), and `AddPort()` enqueues it under the port-list write lock without checking for an existing equal name (`rom/exec/addport.c:50-75`). Both processes then install their edit hook and enter their own message loops (`ConClip.c:275-278,428-445`), but later `FindPort(CONCLIP_PORTNAME)` calls resolve only the first matching list node (`rom/exec/findport.c:48-57`). As a result, both instances advertise the same rendezvous name, so copy/paste requests can be routed to only one of them; a later `ConClip OFF` invocation likewise signals whichever duplicate `FindPort()` returns and may leave the other instance running.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** ExecSMP builds selecting `workbench/c/ConClip`, when two instances start concurrently and both complete the absent-port lookup before either `CreatePort()` publishes. **Consequence:** the intended singleton can become multiple active processes with an ambiguous shared public port name; rendezvous clients and the OFF command cannot reliably address the intended instance. **Confidence:** high for the non-atomic lookup/publication and duplicate-tolerant `AddPort`; occurrence requires the stated cross-CPU startup interleaving. No ConClip process, message port, clipboard operation, or concurrent startup was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9801

**The TextEditor SpellChecker frees an in-flight ARexx request when Ctrl-C interrupts its reply wait.** `SendRexx()` creates a reply port and a `RexxMsg` pointing to it, allocates the command argstring, and posts the message to the public `REXX` port (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/SpellChecker.c:132-152`). When `Wait()` returns only `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C`, the reply branch is skipped, but execution still deletes the command argstring and `RexxMsg`, then deletes the reply port (`:154-177`). The `RexxMsg` contract identifies this port as the destination for the eventual reply (`workbench/libs/rexxsyslib/createrexxmsg.c:25-34,56-64`); deleting the port frees its storage without replying pending messages (`rom/exec/deletemsgport.c:23-27,48-56`). The same stale-message interval also exposes the argstring to the Rexx service after it has been freed.
