No Rexx command, signal, or task was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9802

**TextEditor SpellChecker drops the final character of suggestion lines without a newline and splits long lines into separate entries.** The `T:Matches` reader calls `FGets(fh, entry, 128)` and unconditionally overwrites `entry[strlen(entry)-1]` before inserting the buffer into the suggestion list (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/SpellChecker.c:527-536`). DOS `FGets()` stops at newline, EOF, or `buflen-1` characters; it includes a newline only when one was read and always terminates the buffer (`rom/dos/fgets.c:24-28,52-75`). Thus an unterminated final line loses its last actual byte. A line at least 127 bytes long is returned in chunks; every chunk loses its last byte and is inserted as an independent suggestion.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting `texteditor.mcc`, when the configured suggestion command writes `T:Matches` with a final line lacking `\n` or any suggestion line reaching the 127-byte `FGets()` payload limit. **Consequence:** the displayed suggestion is truncated; long suggestions are split and cannot be selected as the original value. **Confidence:** high for the read/strip behavior and DOS `FGets()` contract; occurrence depends on the external suggestion output. No suggestion command or file was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9803

**VideoCore VCGfx publishes its GPU memory header without the Exec SMP memory-list lock.**

After initializing `vcsd_GPUMemManage`, `InitMem()` wraps `AddTail(&SysBase->MemList, ...)` in `Disable()`/`Enable()` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/vcgfx_memory.c:225-248`). On ExecSMP, `Disable()` only suppresses scheduling/interrupts on the current CPU; it does not acquire `MemListSpinLock` (`rom/exec/disable.c:54-70`; `rom/exec/memory.h:14-18`). The selected Exec allocator list walkers take that lock in shared mode (`rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:27-34,324-333`; `rom/exec/memory.c:26-37`), while `AddTail()` publishes the node through separate link stores without synchronization (`rom/exec/addtail.c:49-61`). The writer therefore bypasses the lock that is meant to serialize MemList access. A potential in-tree reader candidate in the same coldstart phase is: the Raspberry Pi package includes `input.device` before VCGfx (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:122,143`). `krnRomTagScanner()` sorts the initial resident array by descending priority while building `ResModules` (`rom/kernel/kernel_romtags.c:311-339`; assigned at `rom/kernel/prepareexecbase.c:51`). The input device's priority 30 therefore precedes VCGfx's priority 9 (`rom/devs/input/input.conf:4`; `vcgfx.conf:5`). `InitKickTags()` only sorts again if it adds a non-NULL KickTag list (`rom/exec/initkicktags.c:273-275`), so it is not the basis for this ordering. Input initialization starts `ProcessEvents()` with `NewCreateTask()` (`rom/devs/input/input.c:66-80`); that task creates message ports and I/O requests before its first `Wait()`, and these constructors call `AllocMem()` (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:157-194`; `rom/exec/createmsgport.c:48-52`; `createiorequest.c:59-69`). `AllocMem()` walks `SysBase->MemList` under `MemListSpinLock` shared mode (`rom/exec/memory_nommu.c:20-40`). On ExecSMP, the boot task is pinned to CPU 0 and secondary cores are released before COLDSTART resident initialization (`arch/arm-native/kernel/platform_init.c:84-107,260-280`). The input worker does not establish cross-CPU overlap: `NewCreateTask()` supplies no affinity override, `Exec_InitETask()` inherits the creating task's mask (`rom/exec/exec_util.c:126-164`), and the boot task is pinned to CPU 0 (`arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:260-280`). Since `input.device` creates the worker while its resident initializer runs on the boot task, both execute on CPU 0; this one-CPU-at-a-time path cannot overlap the later VCGfx initializer. A race still requires some other allocator walk on a different active CPU during `InitMem()`, which this review has not established for the selected boot path.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the optional BCM2708 VideoCore HIDD is included in the Raspberry Pi ARM boot package (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:143`). Its `residentpri 9` gives it `RTF_COLDSTART` under genmodule's resident-flag rule (`vcgfx.conf:5`; `tools/genmodule/writeinclibdefs.c:31-45`), and `InitCode(RTF_COLDSTART)` invokes matching residents (`rom/exec/initcode.c:57-96`). Exec's COLDSTART initialization enables multitasking before later COLDSTART residents (`rom/exec/exec_init.c:53-61`); the Raspberry Pi SMP kernel has released secondary cores by then (`arch/arm-native/kernel/platform_init.c:84-107`; `arch/arm-native/exec/platform_init.c:248-288`). The race requires an Exec memory-list walk on another active CPU while VCGfx's `InitMem()` publishes the node. **Consequence:** that walk can race the tail-link write and miss or observe the new GPU header before the append is coherently visible, yielding an inconsistent memory-list result for that operation. Use the MemList write-lock protocol used by `AddMemList()` around publication. **Confidence:** high that the writer bypasses Exec's MemList lock; low that this is a reachable race in the selected package because no concurrent in-tree reader has been established. The input worker route is specifically excluded by inherited CPU-0 affinity. No concurrent list operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).



## GD9804

**Selected bitmap conversions pass widths that do not fit the signed `ReadPixelLine8()` API and then consume rows the API did not read.** The picture datatype's ILBM BMHD stores `bmh_Width` as `UWORD` (`compiler/include/datatypes/pictureclass.h:30`). `ConvertBitmap2Chunky()` copies that width into `ULONG`, allocates an uncleared `MEMF_ANY` buffer, then passes it to the public `ReadPixelLine8()` whose width parameter is signed `WORD`; it ignores the returned pixel count (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/colorhandling.c:316-325,501-530`; `rom/graphics/graphics.conf:173`). For widths 32,769–65,535, a target that narrows to a negative signed 16-bit value makes `ReadPixelLine8()` derive an endpoint before `xstart`, so `ReadPixelArray8()` returns zero (`rom/graphics/readpixelline8.c:59-66`; `rom/graphics/readpixelarray8.c:100-111`). Picture conversion still returns success and feeds the uncleared buffer to `ConvertCM2CM()` or `ConvertCM2TC()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:983-1000`). At the boundary width 32,768, `ReadPixelLine8()` narrows its width to -32,768, but endpoint arithmetic can wrap the resulting stop coordinate back to 32,767; `rp8_render()` then narrows the inclusive 32,768-pixel rectangle width to -32,768 (`rom/graphics/readpixelline8.c:59-66`; `rom/graphics/readpixelarray8.c:21-32`). The selected PlanarBM `GetImageLUT()` implementation also uses a signed `WORD x` loop against that negative width, so it copies no row pixels (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:662-704`). The returned pixel count may be negative in this boundary case, but the picture and animation callers ignore it. Thus the affected signed-width boundary begins at 32,768 for the selected planar path; larger widths can instead return zero at the invalid-range check.

The same signed-width/ignored-result pattern occurs in the selected animation conversion: `ad_BitMapHeader.bmh_Width` is passed to `ReadPixelLine8()` and then read from `tmpline` without checking the result (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:573-599,680-700`). It also occurs in MUI's bitmap remapper: the public LONG `data->width` is passed to `ReadPixelLine8()` and the `linebuffer` is immediately consumed for masking/remapping (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bitmap.c:24-45,120-150,164-195`). Both row buffers are allocated without `MEMF_CLEAR`; MUI only rejects nonpositive widths and does not cap the value to `WORD_MAX` (`:49,72-74`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** include and use `picture.datatype`, `animation.datatype`, or MUI's bitmap class with an indexed/planar bitmap width 32,768 through 65,535, on a target whose unsigned-to-signed narrowing yields the corresponding negative `WORD`. Picture and animation are explicit module targets; no checked-in parent aggregate edge to either was found (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/mmakefile.src:4-14`; `animation/mmakefile.src:4-12`). MUI's `bitmap` class is included in `CLASSES` and the generated `workbench-libs-muimaster` module (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:58-83,428-439`). **Consequence:** row reads can return zero while callers continue using uninitialized bytes as pixel indices, producing incorrect remapped images or animation frames. Reject unsupported dimensions or process rows in chunks that fit the signed API, and check the returned pixel count. **Confidence:** high for the mismatched types, unchecked results and subsequent reads; medium for the exact negative conversion on the target ABI. No image, animation, MUI object, or pixel read was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9805

**MUI bitmap remapping uses signed-WORD loop counters for LONG bitmap dimensions.** `MUI_BitmapData.width` and `.height` are `LONG`, accepted from the public constructor/set tags, and `remap_bitmap()` rejects only values below one before allocating its line buffer and output bitmap (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bitmap.c:24-49,72-83,248-303`). The function declares both loop variables `x` and `y` as `WORD` (`:45`). Its remap, mask, and output loops compare those signed counters with the LONG dimensions (`:125-180,202-224`). When a supported bitmap dimension exceeds `WORD_MAX`, incrementing the corresponding counter past 32,767 narrows it outside the signed-WORD range. On the usual wrap behavior it becomes negative, so indexing `linebuffer[x]`/`mask` can address before the row and the loop condition stays true rather than terminating. The width path also passes the same over-range width to `ReadPixelLine8()` (GD9804).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** a MUI Bitmap object that reaches `remap_bitmap()` with either `data->mappingtable` or `data->sourcecolors` set (the helper returns early when both are NULL), and has a positive width or height above 32,767; the corresponding `AllocBitMap()` must succeed and the target must narrow the loop increment to a negative `WORD`. A transparency tag by itself is insufficient to enter the remapping loops. This does not require a very large pixel area: a 16-by-32,768 standard bitmap uses 64 KiB per plane, and the `BitMap` fields can represent it (`Rows` and `BytesPerRow` are `UWORD`). The selected `AllocBitMap()` stores `Rows = sizey` and computes the row stride from `sizex` (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:485-496`), so height 32,768 is representable; the loop variable `y` nevertheless passes 32,767 and can wrap negative. This height-only case avoids the separate signed-width `ReadPixelLine8()` issue in GD9804. The same class supports width 32,768 with height 1 (a few KiB per plane), which crosses the `x` bound but also overlaps GD9804. These examples establish modest-area in-tree bitmap representations, conditional on successful source/destination allocations and the target signed conversion. `bitmap.c` is included in the base `CLASSES` list for the generated `workbench-libs-muimaster` module (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:58-83,428-439`). **Consequence:** remapping can read or write before the line/mask buffer and fail to terminate. Use counters wide enough for `data->width`/`data->height` and validate representable bitmap dimensions. **Confidence:** high for the signed counter/dimension mismatch, the `UWORD` bitmap metadata limits, and the unchecked range; medium for the exact wrap manifestation on a given target and allocation success. No MUI object or bitmap was created; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9807

**MUI Bitmap ignores a transparent-pen request when no palette remapping is configured.** `remap_bitmap()` returns immediately when both `data->mappingtable` and `data->sourcecolors` are NULL (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bitmap.c:47-50`), before its separate transparency-mask allocation and construction at `:94-98`. `Bitmap__OM_SET()` accepts and stores `MUIA_Bitmap_Transparent`, but does not rebuild the mask or invoke remapping (`:332-381`). `MUIM_Draw()` selects the source bitmap when no remapped bitmap exists and, when `data->mask` is NULL, uses the opaque `BltBitMapRastPort()` path (`:523-550`).

A checked-in caller requests exactly this combination: PPP ModemManager creates a plain `BitmapObject` without mapping-table or source-color tags (`workbench/devs/networks/ppp/ModemManager/ModemManager.c:653-656`), opens its window, then `MakeBitmap()` sets `MUIA_Bitmap_Transparent` to 0 and assigns a new source bitmap before drawing (`:77-100,706,713`). Later, `UpdateModemInfo()` clears the backing bitmap to pen 0 before drawing the signal indicator (`:274-305`). The Bitmap class therefore has no mask for the direct draw, and pen-0 pixels are copied over the window instead of being transparent.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable PPP ModemManager target (`workbench/devs/networks/ppp/ModemManager/mmakefile.src:6-12`) using the selected muimaster Bitmap class, when it draws the `MUIA_Bitmap_Transparent=0` source bitmap without `MUIA_Bitmap_MappingTable` or `MUIA_Bitmap_SourceColors`. **Consequence:** the bitmap background is opaque and can cover the window's existing background. Build a transparency mask independently of palette remapping, and refresh derived bitmap state when the public transparent attribute changes. **Confidence:** high for the early return, missing mask, and opaque draw; medium-high for the intended visible result, which is supported by the public settable attribute and this caller's explicit transparent-pen setup. No GUI or bitmap operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9808

**NListtree's built-in pointer-match hooks can report distinct pointers as equal on 64-bit builds.** The built-in name and user-data pointer-comparison hooks subtract pointer-width `SIPTR` values and return the difference as 32-bit `LONG` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:3141-3145,3171-3175`; `LONG` is explicitly 32-bit while `SIPTR` is pointer-width in `compiler/include/exec/types.h:38,83-91`). The public hook documentation describes these modes as pointer comparison and says a zero result means a match (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:758-770,806-818`). Both forward and reverse search treat a zero hook result as a match (`NListtree.c:2409,2451,2494,2536`). On a 64-bit build, distinct addresses whose difference is a multiple of 2^32 therefore narrow to zero and can select the wrong node.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS NListtree class on a 64-bit target when a client selects either public `MUIV_NListtree_FindNameHook_PointerCompare` or `MUIV_NListtree_FindUserDataHook_PointerCompare` mode and searches across distinct node/user pointers separated by a multiple of 2^32. A checked-in caller search found no use of those built-in modes; this is a public API candidate with external-client reachability. **Consequence:** FindName/FindUserData may return a different node whose pointer is not equal to the requested pointer. Compare pointer identity directly or preserve a nonzero result for every unequal pointer. **Confidence:** high for the narrowing and zero-as-match path; medium for practical reachability of the address spacing and absence of checked-in users. No tree search or 64-bit allocation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9809

**NListtree resolves active-node sentinels by overwriting the caller's tag list.** `SetAttributes()` writes the resolved node pointer directly into `tag->ti_Data` for `MUIV_NListtree_Active_Parent`, `_First`, `_FirstVisible`, and `_LastVisible` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:4381-4415`). The public `SetAttrsA()` implementation passes its caller's `TagItem *` directly to `OM_SET` (`rom/intuition/setattrsa.c:77-82`), and NListtree's `_Set()` forwards that same list to `SetAttributes()` (`NListtree.c:5370-5377`). The public header and docs define these values as reusable special values for selecting a parent, first item, or visible endpoint (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mui/NListtree_mcc.h:95-99`; `docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:156-170`). After the first call, the caller's array contains a node pointer instead of its sentinel; a later call does not reevaluate the requested special value. If that node has since been removed, the stale pointer is passed to `GetParent()` during the next set.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when a caller uses `SetAttrsA()` with a retained tag list containing one of these active-node sentinels and reuses the list. This is a public API case; the checked-in demo uses varargs `DoMethod()` rather than a retained `SetAttrsA()` list. **Consequence:** repeated calls can activate the formerly resolved node instead of the then-current parent/first/visible node, and removing that node before reuse can leave a stale node pointer for the setter to dereference. Resolve the sentinel in a local variable and leave the incoming `TagItem` unchanged. **Confidence:** high for direct mutation and raw-list dispatch; the wrong repeated-call result follows from the changed tag value, while the stale-pointer consequence requires removal before reuse. No `SetAttrsA()` call or tree mutation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9810

**NListtree double-click tracking truncates row indices above 65,535.** The input handler declares the previous clicked entry as a function-local static `UWORD`, compares it with `tpres.entry` and then stores the current entry there (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:5819,5852,5893`). `UWORD` is unsigned 16-bit, while `MUI_NList_TestPos_Result.entry` and the NList entry count are `LONG` (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:58-62`; `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mui/NList_mcc.h:121,434-437`). The double-click condition is therefore false for a repeated click on an entry whose index exceeds 65,535 after its first index has been truncated. Indices that differ by 65,536 can also compare equal after the narrowing. The public NListtree contract says double-click opens/closes the clicked node and reports that node through the notification (`docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:543-581`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when a tree has more than 65,535 visible rows and a user double-clicks a row above that index. For example, row 65,537 is stored as 1, so a second click on row 65,537 fails the same-row comparison; clicking row 1 instead can satisfy it. The NList API and NListtree entry counts use 32-bit `LONG`, so the index is representable. **Consequence:** configured double-click open/close and notification behavior can be missed or associated with a different row. Store the previous entry in a `LONG` and keep the state per NListtree instance. **Confidence:** high for the type narrowing and comparison; medium for practical use of trees with this many simultaneously visible rows. No tree or input event was created; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9811

**NListtree dereferences a failed duplicated-name allocation during insertion.** With `NLTF_DUPNODENAMES` enabled, `_NListtree_Insert()` allocates `tn->tn_Name` and immediately passes it to `strlcpy()` without checking for NULL (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:7111-7116`). `AllocVecPooled()` returns NULL when the pool cannot satisfy the request (`rom/exec/allocvecpooled.c:68-86`), and the class enables duplicated names by default (`NListtree.c:5144-5146`). The later `if (tn->tn_Name)` failure path does not protect this earlier copy.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when a public `MUIM_NListtree_Insert()` call uses the default duplicated-name setting and the node-record allocation succeeds but the following name-copy allocation fails. The checked-in SysExplorer and Storage enumerators issue direct Insert calls without setting `MUIA_NListtree_DupNodeName` (`sysexp_main.c:347-355`; `storage_enum.c:105-106`); SysExplorer does not declare the MCC as a build dependency, so this in-tree pairing requires the class to be separately installed and loaded. Disabling `MUIA_NListtree_DupNodeName` avoids this particular allocation. **Consequence:** insertion dereferences a NULL destination instead of returning failure or leaving the tree unchanged. Check the copied-name allocation before `strlcpy()`, then free the unlinked node and invoke the matching destruct hook on failure. **Confidence:** high for the nullable allocation and immediate copy; memory pressure and this allocation ordering were not induced. No tree insertion was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9812

**NListtree InsertStruct continues at the root after an intermediate insertion fails.** `_NListtree_InsertStruct()` initializes `lasttn` to the root-list sentinel, then assigns each `MUIM_NListtree_Insert()` result to it without checking for NULL; it continues parsing the next path component (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:7417-7445`). The public root-list sentinel is zero (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mui/NListtree_mcc.h:543`), and `MUIM_NListtree_FindName()` interprets that value as the root list (`NListtree.c:8799-8822`). When an intermediate `_NListtree_Insert()` returns NULL because its tree-node record allocation fails (`:7093,7284-7294`), the next component is consequently searched/inserted at the root instead of under the missing parent.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when `MUIM_NListtree_InsertStruct()` receives multiple path components and an intermediate component's node-record allocation fails while later allocations succeed. The optional checked-in NListtree demo makes two multi-component calls using slash delimiters (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/demo/NListtree-Demo.c:245-246`; `demo/mmakefile.src:20-34`); no default aggregate selection for this demo was found. The public method is documented to insert a hierarchy and return its last entry (`docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:2148-2194`). **Consequence:** later path components can be created or reused at the wrong level, leaving a partial, incorrectly structured path while the method may return a non-NULL final node. Stop and return failure when an intermediate insertion returns NULL. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked result, root-sentinel alias, continuation, and optional in-tree caller; the required allocation failure was not induced. No path insertion was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9813

**NListtree Exchange resolves the second head/tail selector from the first list.** In `_NListtree_Exchange()`, the `MUIV_NListtree_Exchange_TreeNode2_Head` and `_Tail` cases call `GetHead()`/`GetTail()` on `ln1->ln_List`, even though `ln2` was resolved from `ListNode2` and the public method contract says these selectors choose from that second list (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:8000-8008`; `docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:1648-1665`). The selected `tn2` then flows through removal and reinsertion using `ln2` (`NListtree.c:8030-8062,8069-8111`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when a client calls `MUIM_NListtree_Exchange()` with distinct source/destination lists, a source list with at least two entries, and selects `TreeNode2_Head` or `_Tail` such that the selected node differs from `TreeNode1`. The checked-in caller search found no use of these second-list selectors, so reachability is through the public API. **Consequence:** Exchange selects a node from `ln1` instead of `ln2`. It then calls `NLRemoveFromTable()` on `ln2` for this `ln1` node; `NLFindInTable()` returns -1, so the node remains in `ln1`'s table even as `Remove()` unlinks it from the `ln1` list. The method later reinserts the node into `ln1` and calls `NLAddToTable()` there again, duplicating its table entry. The other exchanged node is inserted into `ln2`, using a predecessor saved from `ln1`; list chains and lookup/index behavior can therefore also become inconsistent. An empty source list, or a one-entry source list where both selectors resolve to the same node, skips the exchange. Resolve the second selector from `ln2`. **Confidence:** high: the wrong-list lookup, table miss, unlink, and duplicate insertion sequence are explicit; no Exchange call or tree mutation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9814

**NListtree Rename discards existing user data when the construct hook rejects replacement data.** With `MUIV_NListtree_Rename_Flag_User`, `_NListtree_Rename()` calls the destruct method on the node's current `tn_User` before it calls the construct method with `msg->NewName`; it assigns the construct result directly to `tn->tn_User` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:8671-8683`). The public construct-hook contract explicitly says that a `NULL` return means nothing is added (`NListtree.c:3445-3459`), and the dispatcher returns the hook result unchanged (`:6480-6493`). Rename does not check that result or restore the old user data.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when a client calls `MUIM_NListtree_Rename()` with the User flag and a construct hook returns `NULL` for the replacement. **Consequence:** the old user object has already been destructed, and the existing node is left with `tn_User == NULL` even though the rename method returns the node as if the operation succeeded. Construct replacement data before destroying the old value, and leave the node unchanged when construction fails. **Confidence:** high for the call order and documented failure contract; no hook or rename was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9815

**NListtree Rename dereferences a failed duplicated-name allocation after freeing the existing name.** With `NLTF_DUPNODENAMES` enabled, `_NListtree_Rename()` frees `tn->tn_Name`, allocates replacement storage, then calls `strlcpy()` without checking whether `AllocVecPooled()` returned `NULL` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:8687-8694`). The pool allocator returns `NULL` on allocation failure (`rom/exec/allocvecpooled.c:68-86`), and duplicated names are enabled by default (`NListtree.c:5144-5146`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when a public rename uses the default duplicated-name setting and the replacement-name allocation fails. **Consequence:** rename dereferences a NULL destination after releasing the node's old owned name; the existing name is also no longer available to preserve. Allocate and validate the replacement before releasing the old name, then leave the node unchanged on failure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked nullable result and operation order; no rename or allocation failure was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9816

**NListtree's built-in clipboard copier mishandles display escape sequences and mutates bracketed names.** The default `_NListtree_CopyToClip()` path copies `tn_Name` to a temporary buffer, but on ESC it skips two bytes and then uses `while(++*s != ']')` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:10051-10072`). For a simple documented two-byte formatting code such as `ESC b`, the unconditional `s++` skips the first ordinary character after the code too: a name like `ESC bHello` is copied beginning at `e`, dropping `H`. NList's built-in copy-hook contract says it skips the ESC and following character (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NList.doc:466-481`). For bracketed sequences, this increments the character at the opening bracket until it becomes `]`; it does not advance the source pointer through the sequence. The loop then advances once and copies the sequence payload, including its closing bracket, to the clipboard. The opening `[` in the stored node name has also been changed to `]`. The public CopyToClipHook documentation says the built-in hook skips all ESC sequences (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:415-445`), and NList documents bracketed `ESC P[...]` image sequences (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/NList_mcc.doc:757-760`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when the default clipboard path copies a node name containing a supported bracketed display sequence such as `ESC P[...]`; a custom CopyToClip hook bypasses this path. **Consequence:** clipboard text includes display-only sequence parameters and the node's stored name is modified in place. When duplicated names are disabled, that stored pointer may belong to the caller, so the write can also modify caller-owned storage. Traverse with a separate source pointer and never write into the original name. **Confidence:** high for the pointer/character operation and documented sequence shape; the resulting copy and source mutation were not run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9817

**NListtree Select Visible also selects hidden descendants, which become selected when expanded.** `TreeNodeSelectVisible()` checks that each current node is visible, selects it, then calls `TreeNodeSelectAll()` for every visible node with a child list (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:1589-1606`). `TreeNodeSelectAll()` recursively selects every descendant without checking `TNIF_VISIBLE` (`:1568-1582`). For an invisible node, `TreeNodeSelectOne()` sets its `TNF_SELECTED` flag directly (`:1513-1562`). The public Select method documents `MUIV_NListtree_Select_Visible` as applying to “all visible entries” (`docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:2773-2783`). When the hidden node is later expanded, `InsertTreeVisible()` sees that flag and selects its newly inserted NList row (`:1764-1800`). Thus Select Visible's hidden-node side effect persists and appears in the list when the user expands the branch. This finding is limited to the unintended hidden selection; hidden-node selected-table bookkeeping is shared with the explicit Select All path and is not separately attributed here.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when a caller selects `MUIV_NListtree_Select_Visible` and a visible list node contains descendants hidden beneath a closed child node. **Consequence:** the operation selects hidden descendants despite its visible-only contract, and those nodes appear selected when exposed later. Recurse with the visible-only traversal rather than `TreeNodeSelectAll()`. **Confidence:** high for the traversal, public contract and expansion path; no in-tree Select_Visible caller was found, so reachability is through the documented public API and external clients. No selection or tree operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**Legacy Listtree dereferences a failed image-wrapper allocation.** `Listtree__MUIM_List_CreateImage()` allocates a compatibility `ListImage` with `AllocPooled()` and immediately writes its links and fields without checking the result (`workbench/classes/zune/listtree/listtree.c:750-784`). ## GD9821

**The shared Zune MCC startup leaks `muimaster.library` when its AmigaOS 4 interface lookup fails.** In the AmigaOS 4 branch, `mccLibInit()` opens `muimaster.library` and calls `GETINTERFACE(IMUIMaster, ...)` in the same `if` condition (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mccinit.c:735-736`). `DROPINTERFACE(IMUIMaster)` and `CloseLibrary(MUIMasterBase)` are only reached inside that condition's body (`:789-791`). Close `MUIMasterBase` on the failed-interface path and clear it. **Confidence:** high for the conditional cleanup and failure return; this interface failure was not induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**Workbench program launch leaks its cloned process tags when startup argument construction fails.** `WB_LaunchProgram()` allocates a three-item `wbcm_Tags` list when the supplied launch tags contain `NP_StackSize` or `NP_Priority` (`workbench/libs/workbench/openworkbenchobjecta.c:509-525`). All checked-in `WB_LaunchProgram()` callers construct both tags (`:657-663,764-771`), so this allocation path is selected. If the later `WB_BuildArguments()` call fails—for example, its `WBArg` allocation, `DupLock()`, or `StrDup()` fails (`:375-390,412-437`)—control goes to `WB_LaunchProgram()`'s error block (`:528-533,545-548`). That block calls `DestroyWBCM()`, whose implementation frees only the message allocation and does not release `wbcm_Tags` (`handler_support.c:28-36`). The normal receiving path frees the copied tags in `__HandleLaunch_WB()` (`handler.c:287-302`), but no message is sent on this failed argument-build path.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Workbench Tool/Project launch through `OpenWorkbenchObjectA()` when the three-item tag allocation succeeds but a subsequent argument-array or argument-duplication operation fails. **Consequence:** the cloned process-tag array remains allocated for each failed launch attempt. Free `message->wbcm_Tags` in the pre-send cleanup path, or make `DestroyWBCM()` own it consistently. **Confidence:** high for the allocation, failure branch and missing cleanup; no allocation failure or launch was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9824

**Failed software-cursor replacement leaves the previous cursor erased until a later refresh.** `Display__Hidd_Display__SetCursorShape()` calls `cursor_Erase()` before allocating the new ARGB image (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1422-1425,1453-1461`). The method stores the requested hotspot offsets before allocation (`:1427-1428`). If `AllocVec()` fails, it releases the semaphore and returns `FALSE`; the old `cursor_argb`, dimensions, and save-under buffer are still retained, but `cursor_drawn` remains false and the offsets now belong to the failed request. `MonitorClass__MM_SetPointerShape()` only updates its selected `data->pointer` and calls `SetPointerPos()` when the HIDD method succeeds (`rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:1954-1960`), so failure leaves the prior Intuition pointer selected without immediately redrawing it. The generic `SetCursorPos()` path calls `cursor_Refresh()` and can redraw the retained image when the pointer next moves (`gfx_displayclass.c:1584-1595`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** any display subclass that inherits the generic software cursor implementation, including the LinuxFB display class (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx.conf:48-60`), when a visible cursor shape is being replaced and allocation of the new `width * height * 4` ARGB buffer fails. **Consequence:** the previously selected pointer disappears until a later position/refresh operation; when redrawn, it uses the failed request's hotspot offsets. The failed request does not switch Intuition's selected pointer. Commit hotspot offsets only with the replacement image, and keep or redraw the old cursor if allocation fails. **Confidence:** high for the allocation and caller state transitions; failure is conditional on memory exhaustion and was not induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9825

**AmigaVideo's aligned chunky-to-planar conversion left-shifts high-bit pixels as signed integers.** `write_aligned_planes()` assembles each 8-pixel chunk using expressions such as `src[0] << 24` and `src[1] << 16` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_bitmapclass.c:604-665`, especially `:626-633`). `UBYTE` values are promoted to `int`; a value of 128 or greater shifted into a position where the mathematical result exceeds `INT_MAX` has undefined behavior under C's signed-left-shift rules. The path is selected by `AmigaVideoBM__Hidd_BitMap__PutImageLUT()` for fully aligned chunks (`:712-759`). The checked-in public `WritePixelArray8()` reaches it through `write_pixels_8()` and `wp8_render()` (`rom/graphics/writepixelarray8.c:16-45,71-76`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:680-691`), and its documented input is an array of byte-valued pens.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected m68k Amiga `amigavideo` HIDD when `WritePixelArray8()` writes at an 8-pixel-aligned destination with at least one complete 8-pixel chunk containing a source byte of 128 or greater. **Consequence:** the conversion has C undefined behavior; exact output depends on the selected compiler/code generation, so pixel corruption is a source-level risk rather than a reproduced result. Cast each source byte to an unsigned 32-bit value before shifting. **Confidence:** high that the source expression can exceed signed `int` range and that the public path supplies byte values; exact target output was not built or run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9826

**`writepixelarrayalpha` reports setup failures with a successful process exit status.** Its shared `cleanup(msg)` prints the diagnostic when `msg` is non-NULL, releases any acquired bitmap/window/screen/library resources, then unconditionally calls `exit(0)` (`developer/debug/test/graphics/writepixelarrayalpha.c:36-52`). All startup failures—from opening a required library through screen lock or window creation—use this path (`:58-106`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** explicitly built optional `test-graphics/writepixelarrayalpha` when any required startup operation fails. **Consequence:** the program emits an error but returns success to a shell script or test runner, which can incorrectly count the test as passed. Preserve a failure status when `msg` is non-NULL while retaining zero for normal completion. **Confidence:** high from the direct cleanup call sites and unconditional exit; no failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9827

**NListtree ignores the documented numeric double-click column setting and can notify with a stale entry.** The `MUIA_NListtree_DoubleClick` documentation says callers normally set the column number and defines the `Tree` and `All` values as special alternatives (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:3618-3644`; public sentinel definitions in `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mui/NListtree_mcc.h:123-126`). The setter stores ordinary values and the getter returns them unchanged (`NListtree.c:4652-4660,5021-5025`). But `_NListtree_HandleEvent()` records `LDClickEntry` and `LDClickColumn` only for `MUIV_NListtree_DoubleClick_Tree` on the tree column or `MUIV_NListtree_DoubleClick_All` (`:5863-5875`). The NList double-click notification still calls `_NListtree_GetDoubleClick()`; that routine suppresses only `NoTrigger`, then uses the stored entry to invoke the method and emit the public notification (`:912-913,10376-10395`). For a documented nonnegative column value, the event branch never stores the clicked entry. `_New()` zeroes the instance data, including `LDClickEntry`, before processing the construction tags (`NListtree.c:5100-5103`); absent a prior supported double-click, the notification therefore looks up entry 0, and later such clicks can reuse stale entry state.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** direct NListtree API clients that set `MUIA_NListtree_DoubleClick` to a nonnegative column number, as the class documentation directs, and then double-click an entry. The legacy Listtree wrapper exposes a separate BOOL-typed `MUIA_Listtree_DoubleClick` (`workbench/classes/zune/listtree/Listtree_mcc.h:14`) and does not establish this numeric trigger. Checked-in direct NListtree clients use `Tree`, `All`, or the default; none uses a numeric column, so the finding applies to external clients of the documented NListtree API. **Consequence:** the clicked column/entry does not receive the documented double-click handling; the notification can report the first row on the initial event and stale entry state on subsequent events. Handle nonnegative values by matching `tpres.column` and updating the stored entry before the notification. **Confidence:** high for the documented numeric contract and missing implementation branch; no GUI event was sent. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9828

**NListtree preferences parse imported numeric values as unterminated C strings.** `NListtreeP_ConfigToGadgets()` passes values returned by `MUIM_Dataspace_Find()` directly to `atoi()` for LineType, IndentWidth, RememberStatus, OpenAutoScroll and UseFolderImage (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcp/NListtree.c:823-881`). Dataspace records are length-delimited: `Dataspace__MUIM_ReadIFF()` checks that each record fits the IFF chunk and passes its exact length to `MUIM_Dataspace_Add()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/dataspace.c:221-240`); Add allocates `sizeof(node) + len` and copies exactly `len` bytes, without adding a string terminator (`:93-126`), while Find returns the data pointer without the length (`:147-163`). A numeric record consisting only of digits and lacking a NUL therefore makes `atoi()` continue reading beyond that record. Zune's file-open path loads a selected prefs file and then calls `ConfigToGadgets` for each page (`workbench/prefs/Zune/zune.c:630-655`); the NListtree MCP manifest selects this class as the optional `classes-zune-nlisttree-mcp` target (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcp/mmakefile.src:11-15`). The ordinary GadgetsToConfig writer includes a NUL, so the trigger is malformed or manually edited settings data.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the optional NListtree preferences page when a user imports a settings file with one of these numeric records lacking a terminating NUL and containing only numeric characters through the record boundary. **Consequence:** `atoi()` reads beyond the stored record, invoking undefined behavior and potentially faulting or applying an unintended value. Validate each record's length/content and parse a bounded, terminated copy. **Confidence:** high for the length-delimited storage and unbounded conversion path; no malformed file was loaded. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9829

**Raspberry Pi framebuffer mode construction shifts a 32-bit `int` by 32.** `FBGfxDisplay__Root__New()` unconditionally evaluates `(1 << XSD(cl)->data.depth) - 1` for the `aHidd_PixFmt_CLUTMask` tag (`arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_displayclass.c:97`). The selected `initFBGfxHW()` path sets `data->depth = 32` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_support.c:51-57`), and the driver root constructor creates this display object during initialization (`fbgfx_hiddclass.c:52-59`). Because the left operand is the 32-bit `int` literal `1`, shifting it by 32 is undefined under the C shift rules. The expression is evaluated even though this mode is configured as truecolor (`fbgfx_displayclass.c:93-96`). The generic pixel-format parser consumes `CLUTMask` only for palette models and reads the truecolor masks/shifts instead (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_init.c:97-118,120-136`), so no visible effect from this tag value is established for the selected mode.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected AArch64 Raspberry Pi `hidd-fbgfx` when its driver/display object is constructed. **Consequence:** mode construction evaluates undefined behavior; the resulting CLUT mask or surrounding compiler-generated behavior is not portable, although this tag is not used as the active color model for the selected truecolor mode. Use a width-safe mask expression or set the CLUT mask only for palette modes. **Confidence:** high for the selected depth and out-of-range shift; no AArch64 build or display initialization was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9830

**Withdrawn as a duplicate of GD9831.** The FBGfx attribute-base leak described here is the same registration-failure defect now covered by GD9831, which also records the selected EFIFBGfx and VESAGfx variants. Keep this heading only as the disposition of the former candidate; do not count GD9830 as an active finding.


## GD9831

**EFI, Raspberry Pi, and VESA framebuffer initialization leak acquired OOP attribute-base references when graphics-driver registration fails.** The selected `EFIFBGfx_Init()`, `FBGfx_Init()`, and `VESAGfx_Init()` obtain eight entries in their static `xsd->attrBases` arrays before calling `AddDisplayDriver()` (`rom/hidds/efifbgfx/efifbgfx_init.c:34-55,103-133`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_init.c:32-57,90-108`; `rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_init.c:31-54,77-127`). Their `GetAttrBases()` helpers release the acquired prefix only when an obtain itself fails. If all eight obtains succeed and `AddDisplayDriver()` returns an error, each initializer returns FALSE without releasing those references; closing graphics.library does not release them, and none of the three modules has an expunge hook that releases `attrBases`. The generated module-init rollback then frees the failed module base (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:54-76`; `tools/genmodule/writestart.c:1158-1180`), leaving the references without a reachable owner. `AddDisplayDriverA()` can fail on configuration allocation, duplicate monitor IDs, or failed driver setup (`rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:181-184,270-297`); for these boot-mode drivers, failure to allocate the deferred boot-queue entry is a concrete setup-failure route (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:397-412`). `OOP_ObtainAttrBase()` increments the interface-bucket reference count (`rom/oop/obtainattrbase.c:130-136`), and `release_idbucket()` frees a bucket only when its count reaches zero (`rom/oop/support.c:181-205`); repeated failed initialization attempts can accumulate references. Release all acquired interfaces on every post-acquisition initialization failure.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** RISC-V64 OpenSBI selects `efifbgfx` (`arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:109-117`); AArch64 Raspberry Pi selects `fbgfx` (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:220-226`); i386-PC and x86_64-PC select `vesagfx` in their HIDD packages (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:75`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:68`). In any of these configurations, the trigger requires successful framebuffer initialization and all eight attribute-base acquisitions, followed by a nonzero `AddDisplayDriver()` result. **Consequence:** eight OOP interface references remain held after the failed module load; retries accumulate references and keep those interface buckets from reaching zero. **Confidence:** high for both acquisition/error/rollback paths and the missing release; no registration or allocation failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
## GD9832

**Generic 8-bit bitmap CopyBox can issue unaligned longword accesses when source and destination alignments differ on 68k.** `BM__Hidd_BitMap__CopyMemBox8()` decides its backward-copy alignment phase from the source end address alone (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapmemblit.c:215-295`). It then performs the bulk transfer with `ULONG *` loads and stores at both source and destination pointers. For an overlapping same-bitmap copy with an aligned base, `srcX=0`, `destX=1`, `width=4`, and `height=1`, the backward path sets source/destination end pointers to `base+4` and `base+5`; source-derived phase is zero, so the bulk loop decrements them by four and stores a `ULONG` at `base+1`. The adjacent source comment explicitly warns that these long writes can trap on 68k. The same alignment defect also occurs for separate, non-overlapping buffers: with aligned bitmap bases, `srcX=0`, `destX=1`, and width at least four, the forward branch computes zero phase from the aligned source but writes a longword at the odd-address destination. The generic `CopyBox` wrapper dispatches same-format 1-byte chunky copies to this routine and documents overlapping copies as supported (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1040-1070`; `:900-980`). The maintained `BltBitMap()` path accepts HIDD bitmaps, calls `int_bltbitmap()`, and reaches `HIDD_Gfx_CopyBox()` for the ordinary copy draw mode (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:130-190`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:469-490,620-649`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected m68k-Amiga build includes the generic `gfx` HIDD in both ROM and the other-memory module list (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:158,375`), and its `gfx` module selects the generic HIDD bitmap and memory-blit bodies (`rom/hidds/gfx/mmakefile.src:8-25`). The bug is reachable through `BltBitMap()` when same-format 8-bit chunky HIDD bitmaps are used and source and destination start addresses have different modulo-four alignment. Either a one-pixel rightward overlapping shift of a four-pixel region in one longword-aligned bitmap or a non-overlapping copy from `srcX=0` to `destX=1` between separate longword-aligned bitmap buffers is sufficient. No particular in-tree screen mode or workload is asserted. **Consequence:** the bulk transfer performs an odd-address 32-bit access and can raise an address error on 68k instead of completing the bitmap copy. Align both pointers before the longword loop or use byte accesses when their alignments differ. **Confidence:** high for the pointer arithmetic, generic dispatch, both copy-direction cases and explicit 68k trap note; the operation was not run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
