## GD9833

**Generic chunky bitmap template drawing reads one word past an exact-width raster row.** `BM__Hidd_BitMap__PutMemTemplate8/16/24/32()` advances the bit mask after every processed pixel and unconditionally loads the next `UWORD` when the current word is exhausted (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapmemblit.c:819-963,964-1109,1110-1317,1318-1463`). For a valid 16-pixel row with `srcx=0`, the sixteenth iteration advances `array` and reads its next word even though no subsequent pixel needs it. The generic ChunkyBM `PutTemplate` method dispatches all four pixel widths to these helpers (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:756-817`). `BltTemplate()` forwards its caller template and row modulo to that HIDD method (`rom/graphics/blttemplate.c:20-35,87-106`); the public contract defines `srcMod` as bytes per row and `AllocRaster()` allocates exactly `RASSIZE(width,height)` bytes (`rom/graphics/blttemplate.c:43-58`; `rom/graphics/allocraster.c:48-53`). Thus a one-row 16-pixel raster needs only two bytes, while the generic chunky helper reads two bytes beyond that payload. The hosted SDL bitmap class also dispatches each 1/2/3/4-byte `PutTemplate()` case to these same shared helpers (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_bitmapclass.c:743-758`), so the overread applies to SDL-backed bitmaps as well. `Text()` is another selected caller: it constructs a width-16 mask for a two-character fast-font run, allocates `RASSIZE` bytes when no sufficiently large `TmpRas` is available, and calls `BltTemplate()` with the exact raster width and height (`rom/graphics/text.c:137-154,381-388`); the final row reaches the same extra-word read.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** a generic ChunkyBM destination using `BltTemplate()` with a valid 16-pixel-wide, one-row allocated mask, `xSrc=0`, and `xSize=16` (or any call whose last processed bit is the last bit of its final allocated word). The generic HIDD module selects the relevant class bodies (`rom/hidds/gfx/mmakefile.src:9-25`); Raspberry Pi ARM and AArch64 packages include `gfx` (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:187`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:226`). The same public `BltTemplate()` trigger applies when the standalone hosted SDL target is explicitly built (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/mmakefile.src:3-19`); its parent dependency in the hosted boot aggregate is commented out. `Text()` also reaches the case for a two-character fast-font run with a 16-pixel raster width when it uses its exact-size allocation fallback. **Consequence:** the helper performs an unnecessary out-of-bounds 16-bit read after the final source bit; the value is unused, but the access has undefined behavior and can fault if the following address is inaccessible. Stop fetching mask words once the final requested bit has been consumed. **Confidence:** high for loop behavior, method dispatch, selected caller, public modulo contract and exact `AllocRaster()` sizing; no raster or drawing operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9834

**VCGfx CopyBox copies four-byte pixels without converting different pixel formats.** `MNAME_GFX(CopyBox)` obtains each bitmap's `PixFmt` and queries only `BytesPerPixel` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/vcgfx_hiddclass.c:575-587`). When both formats use four bytes per pixel, it computes row pointers with a fixed four-byte pixel stride and copies the bytes through DMA or `neon_copyline()` without comparing the format objects or converting pixels (`:589-665`). The generic HIDD implementation checks whether the `PixFmt` objects match and calls `HIDD_BM_ConvertPixels()` when they differ (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1045-1118`). The HIDD CopyBox contract permits source and destination bitmaps from different drivers (`:912-945`), and `AllocBitMap()` can request distinct 32-bit `BMF_SPECIALFMT` values including ARGB32, BGRA32 and RGBA32 while retaining a VCGfx friend driver (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:26-40,278-310`). VCGfx's display `CreateObject()` routes its friend bitmaps through the offscreen class while preserving those tags (`vcgfx_hiddclass.c:667-709`); the active offscreen implementation is a ChunkyBM system-RAM buffer (`vcgfx_offbitmap.c:53-67`). The public HIDD `BltBitMap()` path selects a bitmap's graphics driver and calls that driver's `CopyBox` (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:177-225`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** ARM32 and AArch64 Raspberry Pi packages selecting `vcgfx` (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:187`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:220-226`), for Copy-mode copies involving two chunky buffers whose pixel formats differ but both have four bytes per pixel, when VCGfx's graphics HIDD is selected. For example, copying a VCGfx-friend RGBA32 offscreen bitmap to an ARGB32 destination bypasses the format conversion performed by the generic implementation. **Consequence:** destination bytes retain the source channel ordering and are interpreted using the destination format, producing incorrect colors. Check format identity and delegate mismatched formats to the superclass/conversion path. **Confidence:** high for the missing format comparison, generic conversion behavior and selected bitmap route; no bitmap copy or display operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9835

**FreeType glyph-map allocation failure is dereferenced instead of returned as an error.** `GetGlyph()` sets `ge->GMap` to the result of `AllocVec(sizeof(struct GlyphMap), MEMF_PUBLIC | MEMF_CLEAR)` when the requested character maps to a nonzero glyph index (`workbench/libs/freetype2/glyph.c:354-361`). It calls `RenderGlyph()` only when that allocation succeeds, but then unconditionally reads `ge->GMap->glm_Width` (`:367-373`). If the structure allocation fails, this dereferences NULL. The call is reachable from `ObtainInfoA()` for `OT_GlyphMap` and `OT_GlyphMap8Bits` (`workbench/libs/freetype2/obtaininfoa.c:95-114`); diskfont requests glyph maps for characters while constructing an outline font (`workbench/libs/diskfont/bullet.c:418-432`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** diskfont opening an OFCH font whose `.otag` selects the FreeType2 engine, when a requested character resolves to a glyph and allocation of its `GlyphMap` structure fails. **Consequence:** the font-open path dereferences a NULL pointer instead of returning an allocation error; the process or system may fault. Check `ge->GMap` and set an appropriate error before reading its fields. **Confidence:** high for the null allocation result and unconditional dereference; allocation failure was not induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD5718

**Source and trigger:** In the Workbench argument path, `ReadArguments()` changes the process current directory to the dropped icon's `wa_Lock` and saves the previous directory lock returned by `CurrentDir()` (`workbench/prefs/boingiconbar/args.c:39-43`). If `GetDiskObject()` fails, it reports the error and returns FALSE without restoring the saved lock (`:64-70`). `main()` calls `FreeArguments()`—the only caller that restores `olddir`—only when `ReadArguments()` succeeds (`workbench/prefs/boingiconbar/main.c:34-80`; `args.c:76-80`). `CurrentDir()` returns the previous lock without releasing it (`rom/dos/currentdir.c:24-61`), while process teardown unlocks the current `pr_CurrentDir` (`rom/dos/createnewproc.c:964-965`), which is now the Workbench argument lock.

**Affected configuration:** Workbench launch with a dropped icon argument carrying a nonzero `wa_Lock` and nonempty `wa_Name`, when `GetDiskObject()` cannot read that icon's DiskObject.

**Consequence:** The process exits without releasing the separately saved prior current-directory lock; the process cleanup releases the Workbench argument lock instead. This leaves a DOS lock reference unreleased. Restore the old directory on the failure path, or centralize cleanup so it runs after either `ReadArguments()` result.

**Confidence:** High for the changed directory, skipped restore, and lock ownership; no Workbench launch or icon-read failure was induced. Source-only.

**Review state:** Full-body source pass of the selected BoingIconBar Preferences C units and their argument/import/export callers. This is distinct from the previously reported IControl Workbench lock leak (GD5703): a separate program and argument path.


## GD5719

**Source and trigger:** The selected IControl Preferences target builds its preview images from four `.ilbm` assets using the `ILBMTOC` generator (`workbench/prefs/icontrol/mmakefile.src:15-28`). That generator emits each color map as `const ULONG image_pal[]` containing `0xRRGGBB` values (`tools/ilbmtoc/ilbmtoc.c:610-625,716-729`). `InitImages()` passes those arrays to `InitImagePal()`, which casts away `const` and rewrites each palette in place as packed RGB bytes (`workbench/prefs/icontrol/icontroleditor.c:86-102,160-163`). All four checked-in image assets have multi-entry color maps (6 or 16 colors). On little-endian builds where the generated static data is writable, while converting palette entry 1 the green-byte store overwrites the low byte of `pal[1]` before the blue-byte expression reads it; the second preview color is therefore emitted with blue equal to green. If the generated `const` data is placed in read-only memory, the first conversion write can instead fault. `ChunkyImage` consumes the resulting byte triples as palette RGB (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/libraries/muiaros.h:2221`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/chunkyimage.c:43-64`).

**Affected configuration:** The optional IControl Preferences target on little-endian builds, when its editor initializes the preview images. The exact result depends on the target's placement/protection of generated const data; the palette-value corruption follows from the selected little-endian byte layout if writes are permitted.

**Consequence:** The editor can fail during preview initialization on protected const storage; on writable storage, preview color two can be wrong. Convert into a separate writable RGB buffer or copy each source color to a temporary before writing.

**Confidence:** High for the const write and little-endian overlap; runtime placement/protection is target-dependent and was not established. The four ILBM assets were inspected for CMAP counts; no image generation, build or GUI was run. Source-only.

## GD5720

**Source and trigger:** `Prefs_ExportFH()` sets `retval = TRUE` immediately after a complete ICTL payload write, then ignores the results of `PopChunk()` for ICTL and the enclosing unknown-size FORM, and also ignores `CloseIFF()`'s result (`workbench/prefs/icontrol/prefs.c:168-203`). `PopChunk()` can fail while seeking back to patch an unknown chunk size, writing that size, seeking to the end, writing a pad byte, or flushing the buffered stream (`workbench/libs/iffparse/popchunk.c:77-145`; `bufferingfuncs.c:552-580`). The selected DOS stream handler reports failed seeks and short writes to IFFParse (`dosstreamhandler.c:40-55`). The interactive `IControlEditor__MUIM_PrefsEditor_ExportFH()` returns `Prefs_ExportFH()`'s Boolean directly (`workbench/prefs/icontrol/icontroleditor.c:599-612`), so a finalization failure after the payload write is reported as success.

**Affected configuration:** Interactive IControl PrefsEditor export when chunk-size patching, stream flushing, or IFF close fails after the ICTL payload has been written. The CLI path has a separate ignored-export-result issue already covered by GD5702.

**Consequence:** The caller can accept a malformed or incomplete preference file as successfully exported. Propagate the chunk-finalization and close errors before returning TRUE.

**Confidence:** High for the unchecked finalization results and false-success return; no seek, flush or file-write failure was induced. Source-only.

**Review state for GD5719/GD5720:** Found during a full selected-target pass of IControl's six C bodies and five local headers, including generated palette provenance, image assets' color-map counts, and the interactive export caller. The explicit target is optional and its default aggregate inclusion is not claimed.


## GD9836

**Graphics enables a display without its required software compositor after object creation fails.**

`display_Setup()` marks a display `DF_SoftComposit` when no mode reports native composition but at least one truecolor mode can be composed in software (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:118-149,180-191`). When the compositor class is registered after a display, `compositor_Install()` calls `compositor_Setup()` for each such enabled display; when the display registers later, `display_Register()` makes the same call (`rom/graphics/graphics_compositor.c:48-58`; `graphics_display.c:366-395`). `compositor_Setup()` stores the return of `OOP_NewObjectTags()` without checking it and has no result to return (`rom/graphics/graphics_compositor.c:61-72`), so a failed object construction leaves `display_compositor` NULL while the display/class registration continues as successful.

The visible consequence is in the selected `LoadView` path: if the display HIDD does not implement `ShowViewPorts`, `display_LoadViewPorts()` gives the entire chain to the compositor when one exists. Without a compositor, it either returns early when the front viewport bitmap is already displayed, or calls `HIDD_Display_Show()` with only that front bitmap (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:511-565`). Neither branch forwards the viewport chain for composition. On a display that requires software composition, overlapping/additional viewports therefore are not composed even though the display remains enabled. Check compositor construction and propagate failure or keep the affected display disabled until setup succeeds.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** a build loading the software Compositor HIDD and a display whose mode requires software composition; per-display `OOP_NewObjectTags()` fails during either registration ordering; a later multi-viewport `LoadView` reaches a display HIDD whose `ShowViewPorts` method returns unsupported. The LinuxFB display is a concrete eligible path: its class inherits `CLID_Hidd_Display` and does not override `ShowViewPorts` (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx.conf:45-60`), while its mode construction exposes truecolor when the host framebuffer visual is `FB_VISUAL_TRUECOLOR` (`linuxfbgfx_displayclass.c:87-102`). The base `ShowViewPorts` returns `FALSE` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1351-1355`). This establishes a selected LinuxFB fallback path when the software compositor class is loaded; it does not claim the compositor module is part of every Linux image. **Consequence:** additional/overlapping viewport layers are omitted from the composed display; the fallback either leaves the already displayed front bitmap as-is or submits only the new front bitmap. **Confidence:** high for the ignored construction result, successful registration, and compositor-bypass branches; medium for visible impact, which requires the stated display and viewport configuration. No allocation failure or rendering was run; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9837

**NListtree sends OM_DISPOSE an invalid object when construction fails before the superclass object exists.** `_New()` creates its private and tree pools before calling `DoSuperNew()` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:5110-5135,5164`). Every unsuccessful path falls through to `CoerceMethod(cl, obj, OM_DISPOSE)` (`:5306-5312`). `NewObjectA()` invokes OM_NEW with the class pointer as the initial `obj` (`rom/intuition/newobjecta.c:139-143`; `rom/intuition/rootclass.c:72-91`). Thus failure to create either pool reaches the cleanup call with the class pointer, and a failed `DoSuperNew()` overwrites `obj` with NULL before reaching it. The NListtree `_Dispose()` method immediately derives instance data from `obj` and calls a method on it (`NListtree.c:5316-5329`); `INST_DATA` is just pointer-plus-offset (`compiler/include/intuition/classes.h:64`), so neither invalid value is a partially constructed instance safe to dispose. The cleanup can fault while handling the original allocation failure, and the first-pool-success/second-pool-failure path also leaves the already-created private pool unreleased. Only call object disposal after a superclass object exists; explicitly release any pools created before then.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable optional `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/mmakefile.src:1-26`), when either pre-superclass pool creation fails, or when `DoSuperNew()` fails. **Consequence:** invalid instance-data access in the cleanup method; the second-pool failure additionally leaks the first pool if execution survives. **Confidence:** high for the cleanup control flow and invalid inputs; no allocation failure or object construction was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9838

**NListtree forward selection iteration skips the active entry when nothing is selected.** The documented `MUIM_NListtree_NextSelected` contract says that when no entries are selected but one entry is active, the active entry is returned (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:9762-9795`; `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:2354-2420`). On the start sentinel, `_NListtree_NextSelected()` sets `curr` to zero, but enters the branch containing its active-entry fallback only if `data->SelectedTable.tb_Entries` is nonzero (`NListtree.c:9837-9862`). When the selection table is empty, it therefore writes the end sentinel immediately and never returns `data->ActiveNode`. The active-off value is zero, so a non-NULL active node meets the method's intended fallback test (`private.h:126`). The reverse iterator does return the active node in this empty-table case (`NListtree.c:9951-9970`), confirming the forward/reverse mismatch.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target and its optional checked-in `classes-zune-nlisttree-demo` client (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/demo/mmakefile.src:15-33`), when iteration starts with no selected entries and a non-NULL active entry. The demo's Test button calls `testfunc()`, which iterates with `MUIM_NListtree_NextSelected` and removes each returned node while the active list contains more than one node (`NListtree-Demo.c:854-878,1159-1162`). In this state, the documented active-entry fallback would remove the active row; the implementation returns End before the loop body, so it leaves that row in place. The Selected button also enumerates the method for diagnostics (`:805-848,1129-1130`). The internal drag/drop caller is guarded by a positive `SelectedTable.tb_Entries` count (`NListtree.c:6307-6320`), so it does not reach this empty-selection case. The demo target is optional; no default inclusion is claimed. **Consequence:** callers following the documented active-entry fallback receive End instead of the active node; in the demo Test action, the active row is not removed. Handle the empty-selection active-entry case before requiring a nonempty selection table. **Confidence:** high for the contract/control-flow mismatch and the selected demo caller; no tree or iteration was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9839

**BltPattern drops a fully visible 32,768-pixel span after narrowing its clipped dimensions to signed WORD.** In the generic area-pattern path, `bltpattern_render()` computes the inclusive clipped width and height, then stores each in `WORD` (`rom/graphics/bltpattern.c:28-35`). The HIDD `PutPattern` interface also takes signed `WORD` dimensions. The base bitmap method returns immediately when either is non-positive (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:3553-3557,3811-3822`); the generic chunky-bitmap method forwards the same signed dimensions to `PutMemPattern*` (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:832-918`), and each pixel-width helper rejects non-positive extents (`gfx_bitmapmemblit.c:829,974,1122,1328,1474,1736,1999,2332`). A standard bitmap can be allocated at 32,768 pixels wide: `AllocBitMap()` rounds that width to 4,096 bytes per row, and `BMA_WIDTH` reports `BytesPerRow * 8` (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:495-498`; `rom/graphics/getbitmapattr.c:66-68`). Its valid X bounds are therefore 0 through 32,767, representable by the `Rectangle` endpoints. With a non-solid `AreaPtrn`, the generic route passes that valid full-width rectangle through `do_render_func()` to `bltpattern_render()` (`bltpattern.c:156-180`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:123-140`). The maintained `RectFill()` wrapper dispatches patterned fills directly to `BltPattern()` with the caller’s inclusive bounds (`rom/graphics/rectfill.c:49-55`), so the public `RectFill()` route reaches the same narrowing when the caller uses a 32,768-pixel bitmap extent and an area pattern. The source census found no checked-in `RectFill()` caller that supplies this exact span. The inclusive width is 32,768; on the usual two's-complement target conversion to signed `WORD` yields -32,768, and both the base and chunky software routes reject the request before drawing. LinuxFB's bitmap class inherits `CLID_Hidd_ChunkyBM` and overrides only `SetColors`, so this narrowed-size path is selected there as well (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx.conf:25-35`). The same issue applies to a 32,768-pixel height. This differs from GD9401: here the inclusive endpoint itself is valid, and the size conversion loses the full-range request after clipping.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Graphics library bitmap-pattern rendering on a target where out-of-range signed-`WORD` conversion yields a negative value, when `BltPattern()` uses its generic `AreaPtrn` path on a bitmap with an exactly 32,768-pixel clipped width or height. The solid masked-template fast path does not use this callback. The selected LinuxFB `CLID_Hidd_ChunkyBM` class inherits the generic chunky pattern method and is an in-tree implementation path. **Consequence:** the software HIDD bitmap method draws none of the requested span. **Confidence:** high for the width/height narrowing, allocator dimensions, and both software-method rejection paths; symptom depends on target signed-conversion behavior, and other accelerated overrides may differ. No bitmap was allocated and no pattern was drawn. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9840

**NListtree dereferences a missing drop target while a drag is reported over an empty tree.** The NList drag-report path explicitly sets the row to zero when the list contains no entries, then invokes `MUIM_NList_DropType` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func2.c:1974-1984`). NListtree's `_DragNDrop_DropType()` asks `MUIM_NList_GetEntry` for that row and stores the result in `data->DropTarget` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:6086-6094`). NList's getter initializes the output to NULL and leaves it NULL for an empty list (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func.c:1463-1483`). Although the empty-list geometry chooses the Above drop type, NListtree later evaluates `data->DropTarget->tn_Flags` before checking whether the drop type is Onto (`NListtree.c:6134`). A drag pointer in the NList tree's horizontal drop-report area therefore dereferences NULL while computing drag feedback. Guard the target checks or reject the drop before dereferencing it.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable optional `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/mmakefile.src:1-26`), with an empty NListtree receiving a drag report in its horizontal bounds. The checked-in `NListtree-Demo` target is also explicitly buildable, sets `MUIA_NListtree_DragDropSort=TRUE` (which enables the superclass NList drag type), and provides a Remove button that removes selected nodes (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/demo/mmakefile.src:20-21`; `NListtree-Demo.c:952,1059-1062`; `NListtree.c:5169-5173`). This establishes an in-tree receiver configuration and a way to empty it; the actual drag-report event remains a user interaction, and no specific source object is required by the failing target method. **Consequence:** the drag-report method faults during drop feedback instead of safely handling an empty tree. **Confidence:** high for the zero-entry caller path, NULL output, and unconditional dereference ordering; no drag event or GUI was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9841

**NListtree Clear leaves a NULL node pool after pool recreation fails, and the next insertion faults in Exec.** `_NListtree_Clear()` deletes the existing `TreePool`, then unconditionally assigns the result of `AllocSysObjectTags(ASOT_MEMPOOL, ...)` on AmigaOS 4 or `CreatePool()` on other targets without checking for failure (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:7801-7819`). It returns normally after resetting the tree (`:7821-7833`). On the next normal `MUIM_NListtree_Insert()`, the construct hook runs and the tree-node allocation calls `AllocVecPooled(data->TreePool, ...)` (`NListtree.c:7075-7094`). With `TreePool == NULL`, `AllocVecPooled()` evaluates `IsManagedMem(mhe)` before its later explicit NULL check (`rom/exec/allocvecpooled.c:56-73`); `IsManagedMem` dereferences `mh_Attributes` through the supplied pointer (`compiler/include/exec/memheaderext.h:57-60`). Thus a failed pool recreation turns the following insertion into a NULL dereference instead of a reported allocation failure.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable optional `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target on both the AmigaOS 4 `AllocSysObjectTags` branch and other-target `CreatePool` branch, when Clear removes the old pool and replacement-pool allocation fails, followed by an Insert call. **Consequence:** the next insertion faults while Exec checks whether the NULL pool is managed; Clear itself does not report that the tree is left without a usable pool. Preserve the old pool until replacement succeeds, or leave the object in a state where later methods reject the missing pool safely. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked replacement, allocator call sequence, and null dereference; no pool allocation failure or insertion was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9842

**NListtree's GetNr method dereferences the active-node sentinel in list queries.** `_NListtree_GetNr()` resolves `MUIV_NListtree_GetNr_TreeNode_Active` directly to `data->ActiveNode` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:9245-9246`). The class initializes that field to `MUIV_NListtree_Active_Off`, which is NULL, and Clear resets it to the same value (`NListtree.c:5138; 7827`; `private.h:126`). Both the `MUIV_NListtree_GetNr_Flag_ListEmpty` and `MUIV_NListtree_GetNr_Flag_CountList` branches unconditionally read `tn->tn_Flags` before determining whether `tn` names a list (`NListtree.c:9255-9264`). Thus either list query faults when its TreeNode argument is the Active selector and no node is active, such as immediately after construction or Clear. The public documentation includes the active ListEmpty combination (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:1974-2028`); CountList has the same unchecked dereference. Guard the active-node sentinel and return a defined non-list/empty result before reading its flags.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable optional `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/mmakefile.src:1-26`) when a client uses the documented active-node selector with `MUIV_NListtree_GetNr_Flag_ListEmpty` while `MUIA_NListtree_Active` is Off. **Consequence:** the method faults instead of returning a result for the no-active-node state. The checked-in GetNr callers also use the active selector; their CountAll, CountLevel, position, and Visible paths avoid the `tn->tn_Flags` dereference, while the ListEmpty and CountList branches do not. **Confidence: high** for the initialization/reset state and unguarded dereference; the method call was not run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9843

**NListtree clipboard copying reads past a node name with a truncated display escape.** The default `_NListtree_CopyToClip()` path treats every ESC byte as the start of a two-byte escape and advances `s` by two without checking whether the node-name terminator was reached (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:10058-10071`). For a node name ending in ESC, or ESC plus one byte, `s += 2` reaches or passes the terminating NUL; the subsequent `s++` and copy read `*s` outside the node-name allocation. The public Insert method accepts and duplicates the supplied NUL-terminated name using `strlen()+1` without validating display escapes (`NListtree.c:7064-7078,7105-7119`), so this input reaches the clipboard parser. This is separate from GD9816's mutation and retention of a complete bracketed escape sequence.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable optional `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when a client inserts a node name with a truncated ESC sequence and invokes the default `MUIM_NListtree_CopyToClip` path (including the built-in context-menu route, which passes the selected node pointer at `NListtree.c:6568-6578`). A custom copy hook bypasses this parser. **Consequence:** the copier reads beyond the stored node name; adjacent bytes may be copied as clipboard text, and the malformed input can also cause an invalid-memory fault. Check for a NUL terminator before skipping the two-byte escape and stop or preserve malformed text safely. **Confidence: high** for the unterminated pointer advance and out-of-object read; no malformed name or clipboard operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9844

**NListtree KeepStructure operations continue after a failed ancestor clone and insert through a NULL destination list.** When `_NListtree_Copy()` is asked to preserve structure, it calls `CreateParentStructure()` and then proceeds with `CreateChildStructure()` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:8563-8573`). `CreateParentStructure()` recursively clones source ancestors and assigns each recursive result to `*destlist`, but it does not stop when that result is NULL (`:2660-2666`). If `DuplicateNode()` then succeeds for the next ancestor as the recursion unwinds, the function calls `InsertTreeNode()` with that NULL destination (`:2673-2693`). `InsertTreeNode()` immediately stores the destination in `tn_Parent` and dereferences it to add the node to `ln_List` (`:2561-2585`). `DuplicateNode()` can return NULL when its node/name allocation fails or its construct hook returns NULL (`:2590-2655`), so a failed deeper clone followed by a successful outer clone reaches this unchecked insertion. The same helper serves `_NListtree_Move()`: a failed ancestor clone can leave `ln2` NULL; the outer `cnt == 0` Move frame returns the original selected node, and `_NListtree_Move()` then passes the NULL `ln2` to `InsertTreeNode()` after it has already removed that node from its source list (`:8334-8345`). The checked-in demo explicitly invokes KeepStructure copying (`NListtree-Demo.c:675-681`) and KeepStructure moving (`:623-635`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` when a caller copies or moves a nested entry with the corresponding KeepStructure flag and an ancestor clone fails. Copy faults if an outer clone succeeds after the deeper failure; Move can fault when the failed ancestor leaves `ln2` NULL, after the source node has already been detached. **Consequence:** copy can dereference a NULL list; Move can dereference it and lose the selected node from its original list. Propagate recursive failure before further insertion and leave the source tree intact. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked NULL propagation and invalid insertion paths; the trigger depends on clone failure. No copy, move, or allocation failure was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9845

**NListtree copy silently omits descendants when a child clone fails.** The public `MUIM_NListtree_Copy` documentation says the complete child structure is copied (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:8381-8382`). `CreateChildStructure()` duplicates each descendant and inserts/recurses only when `DuplicateNode()` returns non-NULL (`:2706-2739`). If a descendant clone fails, it returns NULL without inserting that node or its subtree; the parent loop ignores this result and proceeds to later siblings (`:2724-2735`). The top-level `_NListtree_Copy()` likewise does not propagate a descendant failure and refreshes the view after the partial copy (`:8563-8574`), then returns zero (`:8582`). `DuplicateNode()` can fail on its node/name allocations or when the construct hook returns NULL (`:2590-2655`). The checked-in demo exposes KeepStructure copying with a custom construct hook (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/demo/NListtree-Demo.c:678-682`); that hook returns NULL when its `AllocVec()` fails (`:295-316`). The demo sets its success message immediately after `DoMethod()` without checking for a partial result (`:678-682`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` when copying a node with children and a descendant clone fails while the containing parent clone succeeds. This failure is reachable in the checked-in demo’s KeepStructure path when its custom construct hook cannot allocate the cloned user data. **Consequence:** the copied tree omits that descendant subtree, while the demo still reports “successfully copied”; the method also returns zero regardless of whether a clone failed. Abort and roll back the copy, or propagate an explicit partial-copy failure that callers can display. **Confidence:** high for the dropped recursive result, hook allocation failure path, and unconditional success message; occurrence depends on allocation failure during a descendant clone. No copy or failure was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9846 — Withdrawn

**Withdrawn: the Move KeepStructure destination-path allegation was based on a recursion-count error.** Re-tracing `CreateParentStructure()` shows that for a nested source, recursion reaches each ancestor with `cnt > 0`; the `(method == MUIM_NListtree_Copy) || cnt` branch duplicates that ancestor and inserts it under the caller's original destination. The outer `cnt == 0` frame then returns the original selected node for insertion under the cloned path (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:2660-2701,8323-8345`). Thus overwriting `*destlist` during unwinding advances it to the newly created path under the requested destination; it does not revert to the source top-level ancestor. The checked-in demo's active destination is consistent with this behavior (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/demo/NListtree-Demo.c:623-635`). No wrong-destination defect is established. The earlier ledger note claiming GD9846 is superseded by the correction dated 2026-10-26. No move or tree mutation was run; source-only.


## GD9847

**NewIcon decode errors are ignored, so incomplete pixel data is accepted as a valid icon.** `DecodeNI()` returns an error when encoded NewIcon data ends before the requested palette or image entries are decoded, or when it encounters an invalid zero byte (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjNIio.c:54-85`). `ReadImageNI()` discards both decoder results and returns `TRUE` anyway (`:182-188`); if the second image is missing, `ReadIconNI()` can return `FALSE`, but the selected `ProcessIconNI` hook also discards that result and returns its default success value (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjio.c:1011,1017-1021,1033`). The destination buffers are allocated with `MEMF_PUBLIC`, without `MEMF_CLEAR` (`diskobjNIio.c:162-176`; `support.c:495-510`), so bytes after a failed partial decode are not initialized by these paths. Later `LayoutIconA()` consumes the full `width * height` image buffer (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:345-355`), and the icon can be returned to its caller as loaded.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** NewIcon support enabled (the default) while reading an icon whose NewIcon palette or image encoding is truncated or contains an invalid zero byte; later layout/render of the accepted icon. **Consequence:** incomplete image data is treated as valid and layout reads uninitialized tail bytes, producing incorrect pixels; values outside the palette can also reach the separate GD9542 pen-map bounds defect. **Confidence:** high for the ignored status returns and non-cleared allocations; the visible result depends on malformed/truncated NewIcon data and subsequent layout. No icon file or layout was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), NewIcon decode-status propagation recheck dated 2026-10-26.

## GD9848

**NListtree methods and the demo Sort hook can pass or dereference a NULL list before a row is active.** `_New()` zeroes its temporary instance data, sets `ActiveNode` to the off sentinel, and later copies the structure into the object (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:5104-5108,5135-5139,5182-5189`). It initializes the root list but does not assign `ActiveList` during construction (`:5260-5268`); the field is only set by the explicit Clear path (`:7827-7828`) or later active-node attribute processing (`:4440-4458`). FindName and FindUserData accept their Active-list selectors and assign `ln = data->ActiveList` (`:8815-8817,8952-8954`). Their forward and reverse paths pass that pointer to helpers that dereference `ln->ln_List` without a NULL check (`:8826-8834,8963-8971; helper starts at :2391-2398,2432-2442,2476-2483,2517-2526`). GetEntry also accepts its Active-list selector (`:9092-9094`); for Head/Tail it dereferences `ln->ln_Flags`, for Next/Previous it takes `&ln->ln_Node`, and for numeric positions it calls `GetEntryByTotalPos(ln, ...)`, whose first access is `&ln->ln_List` (`:9105-9146`; helper `:1307-1312`), all without checking whether that list exists. Parent, Root, and Active positions use separate NULL-safe paths. The public method contract says the requested node is returned if available and otherwise NULL (`MCC_NListtree.doc:1882-1960`). The public docs define the active list as off when no active entry exists (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:190-205`) and document the active-list search selectors (`:1735-1739,1824-1828`).

The same uninitialized state reaches additional list-dependent selectors in `_NListtree_Open()` and `_NListtree_Close()`: Active-list plus Head/Tail reads `ln->ln_List` while resolving the node, before the later `if (ln && tn)` check (`:6690-6709,6876-6895`), and Close's Parent selector directly reads `data->ActiveList->ln_Parent` (`:6872-6873`). The public method docs define Active as the active node's list and Head/Tail as nodes in the chosen list (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:1180-1203,2446-2472`), but do not specify the no-active result for Open/Close; the documented Active+Active examples reach the later guard safely. No checked-in caller uses Active+Head/Tail or Parent without an active entry. These Open/Close combinations are therefore a **medium-confidence conditional extension** to the documented lookup cases, rather than the basis for the high-confidence portion of this finding. `_NListtree_Sort()` has the same unguarded state: both Active-list and Active-tree-node selectors leave `ln` as the initially NULL `data->ActiveList` when no node is active (`:9369-9385`). It then calls `ListNode_Sort(ln, ...)` unconditionally (`:9397`), whose flag-zero path dereferences `ln->ln_Flags` (`:3113`) and whose recursive path accesses `ln->ln_List` (`:3103`). The public docs expose both selectors and the Active-list/flag-zero form as the example (`MCC_NListtree.doc:2860-2890`), but do not state behavior when no entry is active; this Sort case was initially a medium-confidence extension. A checked-in optional demo provides a concrete inactive-tree caller: `DrawSampleTree()` inserts its sample rows without `MUIV_NListtree_Insert_Flag_Active` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/demo/NListtree-Demo.c:191-237`; the flag is `1<<13`, while sample `TNF_OPEN`/`TNF_LIST` are bits 0/1), and NList starts with Active off (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc.c:401-402`). Its Sort hook initializes `lastactive` to zero, gets the Active attribute, then passes that value as `ListNode` (`NListtree-Demo.c:745-756`); the button invokes this hook (`:1009,1110-1112`). With no active row, Active is NULL/zero (`NListtree.c:5138-5139,5006-5010`), so `_NListtree_Sort()` takes its default pointer branch and passes NULL through to `ListNode_Sort()`, whose flag-zero path reads `ln->ln_Flags` (`:9369-9400,3112-3116`). This confirms a task-fault path in the explicitly buildable demo when Sort is pressed before selecting a row. The class API’s no-active behavior remains an additional conditional public-contract case.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable `classes-zune-nlisttree-class`, on a newly constructed tree with no active node, when a caller uses FindName/FindUserData with an Active-list selector, GetEntry with the Active-list selector and a list-dependent position, Open with Active-list plus Head/Tail, Close with Active-list plus Head/Tail or the Parent selector, or Sort with the Active-list or Active-tree-node selector, before setting an active node or clearing the tree. Independently, the explicitly buildable `classes-zune-nlisttree-demo` reaches the same NULL-list fault if its Sort button is pressed before a row is selected, because its hook passes the NULL Active value as the method’s list argument. **Consequence:** the lookup helper or method dereferences a NULL list pointer and the caller's task faults instead of returning a node/NULL or leaving the tree unchanged. No method or GUI was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9850

**BltClear documentation contradicts itself about the row-mode flag.** The `flags` description says bit 1 selects row/bytes-per-row mode (`rom/graphics/bltclear.c:28-30`), which matches both implementations: the generic body packs the low-16-bit bytes-per-row and high-16-bit row count when `flags & 2` is nonzero (`:61-63`), and the m68k override does the same (`arch/m68k-amiga/graphics/bltclear.c:26-27`). The following `bytecount` description reverses those conditions, saying bit 1 set means a flat even byte count and bit 1 clear means the packed row form (`bltclear.c:31-35`). The architecture implementation points back to this same documentation.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** callers reading the graphics.library `BltClear()` documentation, on generic targets or the m68k override, when selecting flat-count versus row/bytes-per-row mode. **Consequence:** the parameter format is ambiguous within the same API comment, so a caller following the contradictory branch description can supply a value in the wrong format and clear an unintended extent. Make the `bytecount` conditions agree with the flag description and implementation. **Confidence:** high that the documented flag conditions conflict with each other and both selected implementations; the runtime effect depends on which contradictory sentence a caller follows. No BltClear call or memory operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**MUI master initialization dereferences a failed default-pen table allocation.** The selected AROS initializer allocates storage for all `MPEN_COUNT` `MUI_PenSpec` entries and immediately assigns the result to `defaultPen` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/muimaster_init-aros.c:44-46`). It then writes the first entry through `defaultPen->buf` without checking it (`:48-50`). This is the AROS-specific initializer selected by the module rule (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:439`); the generic `muimaster_init.c` path does not replace it in this target.

**Trigger and consequence:** opening/initializing muimaster when the `AllocMem()` request for the default pen table fails. The initializer writes through NULL before it can return its success status, causing a fault during library initialization rather than a clean initialization failure. **Affected configuration:** AROS builds of muimaster. **Confidence:** high for the selected source, failed-allocation result and unchecked first write; occurrence depends on memory exhaustion. ## GD9852

**Diskfont continues parsing a descriptor after read-buffer cursor restoration fails.** `ReadFontDescr()` calls `Flush(fh)` and ignores its result before a relative `Seek()` at both fixed-width-name and tagged-list boundaries (`workbench/libs/diskfont/af_fontdescr_io.c:136-145,174-187`). For a read-mode handle with read-ahead, DOS `Flush()` clears `fh_Pos` and `fh_End` before asking the handler to seek back to the logical file position; it returns FALSE if that compensation seek fails (`rom/dos/flush.c:73-84`). The following `Seek(..., OFFSET_CURRENT)` then sees empty buffer state and applies its relative offset from the still-advanced physical position. `ReadFontDescr()` ignores that seek result too and continues reading tag counts, tag data, and font fields; those values can come from the wrong record offsets, and the routine can still return a populated descriptor if the bytes happen to parse (`af_fontdescr_io.c:147-198`). The selected diskfont callers consume a non-NULL descriptor into font entries or lookup results (`diskfontfunc.c:93-145,842-860,1345-1370`). Check both `Flush()` and `Seek()` results and fail the descriptor read when the logical cursor cannot be restored or repositioned. **Affected configuration and trigger:** builds that load the standalone `diskfont.library` module (`workbench/libs/diskfont/mmakefile.src:6-21`) when reading a font descriptor with buffered unread bytes and the read-buffer compensation seek fails, while a later relative seek or read succeeds. **Consequence:** a valid descriptor may be rejected, or later font sizes/styles/tag data may be interpreted from incorrect offsets and returned as metadata. **Confidence:** high for the DOS buffer/cursor state transition and ignored return values; the incorrect parse requires the stated handler error followed by later I/O success. No font file or seek failure was exercised; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9853

**AmigaGuide records node offsets and lengths after read-buffer cursor restoration fails.** On AROS, `ParseNodeLine()` calls `Flush()` before querying the current file position and subtracting the current line length to store `agn_Pos`; the `CMD_ENDNODE` path does the same before computing `agn_Length` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/file.c:109-115,403-410`). Both calls ignore the result. For a read-mode filehandle with unread read-ahead data, DOS clears `fh_Pos`/`fh_End` before attempting to seek back to the logical position and returns FALSE when that compensation seek fails (`rom/dos/flush.c:73-84`). The subsequent `DTIO_GetFilePosition()` then queries the still-advanced underlying position with the buffer already cleared (`workbench/classes/datatypes/dtio64.h:59-73`; `rom/dos64/getfileposition64.c:56-68`), so stored node offsets and lengths include the skipped read-ahead span. `AllocAGObjectNode()` later seeks to those fields and reads the recorded length as the node body (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/util.c:383-407`); if the computed range remains within the file, the read can succeed with content from the wrong location. Check `Flush()` and position results before publishing node metadata, and reject a scan whose cursor could not be restored. **Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting the explicitly buildable `amigaguide.datatype` module (`workbench/classes/datatypes/amigaguide/mmakefile.src:4-14`) when scanning a guide with unread buffered data and a failed read-buffer compensation seek, followed by a successful position query and node-body read. **Consequence:** node navigation can load incorrect content or fail because its stored range points at the wrong file offset. **Confidence:** high for the ignored flush and the DOS buffer-state transition; the user-visible result requires the stated later I/O success and in-range computed span. No guide file or seek failure was exercised; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9854

**Workbench registers AppWindow drop zones but never dispatches zone messages or hooks.** `AddAppWindowDropZoneA()` parses the zone geometry and hook, then only appends the object to `aw->aw_DropZones` (`workbench/libs/workbench/addappwindowdropzonea.c:128-212`). Its API documentation says drops in a zone produce `AMTYPE_APPWINDOWZONE` messages and describes the enter/leave hook (`:81-104`). The selected Workbench sender, `SendAppWindowMessage()`, only reads the AppWindow fields and constructs `AMTYPE_APPWINDOW` messages (`sendappwindowmessage.c:113-135`); repository-wide searches for `aw_DropZones`, `awdz_`, `AMTYPE_APPWINDOWZONE`, and `AppWindowDropZoneMsg` find no dispatch/geometry/hook consumer. No checked-in caller registers a zone, so impact is established at the public API contract rather than a maintained application path. **Consequence:** the registration is inert: the public sender path ignores zone geometry and hooks and emits the ordinary AppWindow message type, so clients cannot receive the documented zone message or hook callbacks. Implement zone hit-testing and dispatch, or remove/document the unsupported behavior. **Confidence:** high that the selected Workbench implementation contains no consumer of the registration and that its sender emits only `AMTYPE_APPWINDOW`; external integrations were not inspected. No drop or hook was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9855

**Failed Raspberry Pi FBGfx initialization permanently detaches framebuffer kernel debug output.** `initFBGfxHW()` calls `RawPutChar(0x03)` as soon as it accepts the kernel framebuffer, before populating the hardware state and before `FBGfx_Init()` acquires OOP attribute bases or registers the display (`arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_support.c:40-48`; `fbgfx_init.c:88-108`). On this target, `RawPutChar()` dispatches to `KrnPutChar()`, whose AArch64 implementation handles `0x03` by setting `ARMI_PutChar = NULL` (`rom/exec/rawputchar.c:49-52`; `rom/kernel/putchar.c:49-52`; `arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_debug.c:20-29`). If `GetAttrBases()` fails or `AddDisplayDriver()` returns an error, `FBGfx_Init()` returns FALSE without restoring the framebuffer output callback or undoing the detach. There is also a later failure path after `FBGfx_Init()` succeeds: with `DDRV_BootMode=TRUE`, `AddDisplayDriverA()` queues the driver rather than instantiating it (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:397-412`); `NextDisplayInfo()` and `BestModeIDA()` later call `driver_ReplayBootQueue()` (`rom/graphics/nextdisplayinfo.c:60-66`; `bestmodeida.c:250-255`). If `HW_AddDriver()` then fails to instantiate the HIDD, `driver_Setup()` requeues the entry (`graphics_driver.c:326-327,369-388`). The selected FBGfx constructor has fallible superclass and display-object creation (`arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_hiddclass.c:59-84`), so this queued failure is reachable after the callback has already been detached and the library init has succeeded. No later retry or module rollback restores the callback. Later kernel `bug()` output then goes only to the serial callback even though the fallback driver has not produced a display. Preserve the callback until registration succeeds or add a rollback mechanism that can restore it on failed initialization.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** AArch64 Raspberry Pi builds that select FBGfx as the framebuffer fallback (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:220-226`) without `DEBUGDISPLAY`, when kernel framebuffer attributes are present and the detach runs, followed by OOP attribute-base acquisition failure, an immediate `AddDisplayDriver()` error, or later queued HIDD-instantiation failure during `driver_ReplayBootQueue()`. The platform's separate serial debug callback remains enabled (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/platform_bcm2708.c:268-274`; `platform_bcm2711.c:275-280`; `platform_bcm2712.c:393-399`), so this finding is limited to loss of framebuffer debug output. **Consequence:** subsequent kernel debug/bug text is no longer mirrored to the framebuffer after the fallback driver failed to register. **Confidence:** high for the permanent callback clear and missing rollback; occurrence requires the stated initialization failure. No framebuffer, module-load failure, or debug output was exercised; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9858

**NListtree per-node Select Ask reports the request code instead of the node's selection state.** `TreeNodeSelectOne()` handles Toggle specially but otherwise copies `seltype` directly to `st`; for `MUIV_NListtree_Select_Ask` it never reads `TNF_SELECTED`. ## GD9867

**AArch64 Raspberry Pi FBGfx framebuffer handoff does not synchronize concurrent kernel debug output.** With `DEBUGDISPLAY` unset, `initFBGfxHW()` sends `0x03` through `RawPutChar()` while transferring the bootstrap framebuffer to FBGfx (`arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_support.c:40-48`). The selected AArch64 kernel backend responds by clearing the shared `ARMI_PutChar` function pointer, while ordinary output checks and invokes that same pointer without a lock or atomic handoff (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/kernel_debug.c:20-29`). Kernel `bug()` formatting reaches this backend for each emitted character (`rom/kernel/_bug.c:19-22`). The Raspberry Pi target supports ExecSMP and packages FBGfx (`configure.in:2195-2198`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:220-226`), so another CPU can be emitting diagnostics while FBGfx disables the boot-console writer. There is no writer quiescence before `RawPutChar(0x03)` returns; an in-flight boot-console callback can therefore continue writing to the framebuffer during FBGfx ownership.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** an AArch64 Raspberry Pi `smp` build with FBGfx selected and `DEBUGDISPLAY` unset, when a kernel diagnostic on another CPU overlaps FBGfx initialization's callback clear. **Consequence:** boot-console writes can interleave with framebuffer ownership transfer or a display update, producing transient stale characters or pixels. Synchronize and drain active writers before clearing the callback, or route output through an ownership-aware backend. **Confidence:** high for the shared unsynchronized callback and selected SMP/FBGfx paths; medium for occurrence and visible effect because the concurrent interval is conditional and was not run. This is distinct from GD9855's later-init-failure path, which leaves the callback permanently detached, and GD6316's reset-time unlocked clear. No display, diagnostic, or SMP overlap was exercised; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9860

**NListtree silently truncates long node display strings.** The class allocates a fixed 4,096-byte display buffer (`DATA_BUF_SIZE`, `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:141,5254`). `_NList_Display()` clears it, appends the generated tree-indicator markup, optional caller preparses, and the selected column string with `strlcat(..., DATA_BUF_SIZE)`, then gives that buffer to NList (`:6461-6472`; tree markup is appended at `:2806-2877`). `strlcat` bounds the writes but silently truncates once the accumulated string reaches 4,095 bytes. Use a growable display buffer or report/reject overlong rendered strings. **Confidence:** high for the fixed buffer and silent bounded append; medium for caller-visible impact because it requires unusually long but accepted input. No long string or GUI was used; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9861

**NListtree leaks the duplicated node name when insertion cannot resolve a destination list.** With the default `NLTF_DUPNODENAMES` setting, `_NListtree_Insert()` allocates `tn->tn_Name` as a separate pool allocation and marks it `TNIF_ALLOCATED` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:7111-7116`). No insertion or pool exhaustion was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9862

**NListtree publishes visibility and row metadata after the inherited NList construct hook rejects an entry.** `_NListtree_Insert()` links the tree node, calls `InsertTreeNodeVisible()`, then updates its sibling table and returns the node without checking the NList insertion result (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:7121-7252`). For a visible node, `InsertTreeNodeVisible()` sets `TNIF_VISIBLE` before calling `InsertNListEntry()` (`:1804-1828`). That helper discards `MUIM_NList_InsertSingle`'s result and then asks NList for the last inserted entry record, storing it in `tn_NListEntry` (`:1271-1285`). NList's InsertSingle returns the result of `NL_List_Insert()`, which excludes an item when `MUIM_NList_Construct` returns NULL (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func2.c:1798-1806,626-682,775-827`). NListtree passes the original attribute list to its NList superclass with `TAG_MORE` (`NListtree.c:5165-5186`), so an inherited NList construct hook can reach that rejection path. NList updates `NList_LastInserted` only after a successful construct (`NList_func2.c:642,793`) and resets it to -1 only on Clear (`:1075`); `GetEntryInfo(-3)` reads that saved index, or the last row when it is still -1 (`NList_func.c:1524-1529`). Thus, with an earlier row present, a rejected insertion preserves the previous index and the unchecked query assigns that row's `NListEntry` to the new tree node. NListtree's direct-entry path later trusts this pointer for the node's visual position (`:1375-1380`), and removal uses that position in `MUIM_NList_Remove` (`:1262-1268`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when a caller supplies an inherited `MUIA_NList_ConstructHook` that returns NULL for a visible inserted tree-node entry, with at least one earlier NList row present. **Consequence:** NListtree records a node as visible although no backing row was inserted; its direct-entry metadata can refer to the previous row, so later position-based operations may address the wrong entry. Check and propagate the NList insertion result before publishing visibility/table state, and only fetch entry metadata after successful insertion. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked result and stale last-inserted lookup; medium for reachability because it requires a rejecting inherited hook. This is distinct from GD9722/GD9723, which cover NList's own allocation-failure loop and rejected-entry allocation leak. No hook or insertion was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

The checked-in demo calls InsertStruct but ignores its return, so no in-tree dereference is claimed. No allocation failure or tree method was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9865

**Legacy Listtree BOOL quiet setter is forwarded into a nesting counter.** The public compatibility header declares `MUIA_Listtree_Quiet` as a set/get `BOOL` (`workbench/classes/zune/listtree/Listtree_mcc.h:13`). `Listtree__OM_SET()` forwards each assignment unchanged to `MUIA_NListtree_Quiet` (`workbench/classes/zune/listtree/listtree.c:395-401`). The NListtree setter treats every `TRUE` as a nesting acquire and every `FALSE` as one release; it only clears the underlying NList quiet state when the counter reaches zero (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:1143-1169,4895-4905`). Thus a legacy client that sets the BOOL attribute TRUE twice and then FALSE once leaves the child NList quiet, although the last assigned legacy attribute value is FALSE. The underlying `MUIA_NList_Quiet` handler itself implements TRUE as full quiet and FALSE as clearing quiet (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc1.c:517-525`; `NList_mcc5.c:796-806`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the `workbench-classes-zune-listtree` compatibility module, selected by active dependencies from `workbench-classes-zune` (`workbench/classes/zune/mmakefile:1`; `workbench/classes/zune/listtree/mmakefile.src:8-18`) and the complete AROS Workbench class aggregate (`workbench/classes/mmakefile:4-10`; `workbench/mmakefile.src:7-21`); the trigger is a client making repeated idempotent TRUE assignments but only one FALSE assignment. No checked-in client of `MUIA_Listtree_Quiet` was found. **Consequence:** visual updates and deferred list work can remain suppressed until an extra FALSE is sent. Normalize the legacy BOOL assignment to idempotent state or track transitions in the wrapper. **Confidence:** medium: the BOOL declaration and direct forwarding are clear, but the checkout has no legacy Listtree manual defining repeated-set semantics. No Listtree object or UI update was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9866

**NListtree Select All Ask undercounts selected hidden descendants.** The public contract says `MUIV_NListtree_Select_All` selects “all entries” and that the matching Ask request returns the “total number of selected entries” (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:2777-2788,2820-2822`). The Select All mutation path calls `TreeNodeSelectAll()` recursively over every tree node (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:9724-9733,1568-1582`). Visible nodes are added to the NList selection table through `_NListtree_SelectChange()`, while hidden nodes only have `TNF_SELECTED` set (`:1513-1562,10470-10528`). The Ask path returns `data->SelectedTable.tb_Entries` directly (`:9724-9729`), so it counts visible NList rows and omits selected descendants hidden below closed branches. Those flags become NList selections when branches are later expanded (`:1764-1800`). Count selected flags across the tree for this query, or document and implement the result as a visible-selection count. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when the tree contains a closed branch with descendants and a caller issues Select All On followed by Select All Ask. No in-tree caller of this Ask query was found; the trigger is the documented public API. **Consequence:** the returned total is lower than the number of tree entries selected by the preceding Select All operation. **Confidence:** high for the documented contract, recursive hidden-node flag updates, and visible-only table count; exact caller impact depends on clients relying on the documented total. No tree or selection operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9868

**NListtree clone failure runs the destruct hook on the source node's userdata.** `DuplicateNode()` calls the construct method with `nodetodup->tn_User` to make the copy's userdata. When that hook returns NULL, the failure branch calls `MUIM_NListtree_Destruct` with the same original `nodetodup->tn_User` pointer before discarding the new node (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:2617-2637`). The public contract permits a construct hook to return NULL to reject an entry and describes the destruct hook as freeing userdata allocated by construction (`docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:375-403,452-479`). The checked-in demo's construct hook allocates independent userdata for each node and returns NULL on allocation failure, while its destruct hook frees the supplied userdata (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/demo/NListtree-Demo.c:295-316,323-333`). Thus a failed clone frees the original node's userdata while leaving the original tree node's `tn_User` pointer unchanged. The ordinary Copy path calls `DuplicateNode()` directly (`NListtree.c:8563-8570`); afterward the original node remains in the source tree. Later display/use can dereference freed storage, and removing the source node can free the same allocation again.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` when a copy or KeepStructure operation attempts to clone a node whose construct hook returns NULL and a matching destruct hook releases its input. The checked-in demo supplies such construct/destruct hooks and exposes ordinary and KeepStructure copy actions (`NListtree-Demo.c:575-599,670-684`). **Consequence:** source-node userdata is freed although its node remains live, leaving a dangling pointer with subsequent invalid access or double-free potential. Do not call the source node's destruct hook when clone construction fails; clean up only resources owned by the failed clone. **Confidence:** high for the pointer passed to the failure-path destruct call, the hook contracts, and the demo's freeing destruct hook; the trigger depends on a clone rejection or allocation failure. No copy or allocation failure was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9869

**AreaEnd corrupts the flag table and writes past a full AreaInfo buffer while closing a polygon.** `AreaEnd()` calls `areaclosepolygon()` whenever the vector list is nonempty, without first checking that a vector slot remains (`rom/graphics/areaend.c:71-92`). The helper's own precondition requires `Count < MaxCount`; when the last record is an `AREAINFOFLAG_DRAW` point different from the first, it increments `Count` and writes two coordinates through `VctrPtr` and one flag through `FlagPtr` (`rom/graphics/areafill.c:409-425`). At `Count == MaxCount`, `VctrPtr` points to the start of `FlagTbl`, so the coordinates overwrite its first two flag entries; `FlagPtr` points one byte past the caller's `5 * MaxCount` buffer, and the closure flag write is out of bounds. The selected ReAction `drawlist.image` supplies a concrete setup: `IM_DRAW` allocates `UWORD areabuf[5 * 64 / 2]` and initializes 64 vectors (`workbench/classes/reaction/drawlist/drawlistclass.c:153-159`). With that raster allocated, an `AMOVE`, 63 `ADRAW` points filling all 64 entries, and an `AFILL` whose last point differs from the start reaches the unconditional close. `AreaDraw()` accepts points until `Count == MaxCount`, then reports failure without adding a point (`rom/graphics/areadraw.c:59-77`); DrawList ignores that result and also ignores `AreaEnd()`'s return (`drawlistclass.c:205-232`). The public `InitArea()` contract sizes the supplied buffer at five bytes per `maxvectors` entry (`rom/graphics/initarea.c:30-40`), and does not reserve an extra closure slot.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Graphics.library plus the explicitly buildable `drawlist.image` module, when `IM_DRAW` gets a nonclosed filled polygon that occupies all 64 AreaInfo entries and `AllocRaster()` succeeds. `reaction.library` registers `images/drawlist.image` for its link-time class auto-open set (`workbench/libs/reaction/reaction_classes_autoinit.c:46-50`). The same missing-capacity check also affects other valid `AreaEnd()` callers that fill their declared vector capacity. **Consequence:** the closure overwrites the beginning of the flag table and stores one flag byte beyond the declared buffer; in DrawList that byte is beyond a stack-local array. **Confidence:** high for the capacity arithmetic, helper precondition, unconditional call and out-of-bounds write. No image was rendered and no stack layout or runtime effect was tested; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9870

**ClearScreen skips the visible remainder when its text line begins above the bitmap.** `ClearScreen()` computes `ymin` from the signed RastPort cursor and unsigned baseline/font sizes, then stores the result in `ULONG` (`rom/graphics/clearscreen.c:56-62`; field types in `compiler/include/graphics/rastport.h:73,82` and `compiler/include/graphics/text.h:25`). `Move()` accepts signed-WORD coordinates and assigns `cp_y` directly (`rom/graphics/move.c:58`). If `cp_y - TxBaseline + Font->tf_YSize` is negative, conversion to `ULONG` yields a very large value, so `height >= ymin` is false and `ClearScreen()` never issues its lower-screen `RectFill()`. For ordinary font metrics and signed-WORD-representable endpoints, the preceding `ClearEOL()` only attempts to fill the offscreen text row, which generic `RectFill()` clips away (`cleareol.c:57-61`; `rectfill.c:61-66,94-100`; `gfxfuncsupport.h:23`; `gfxfuncsupport.c:123-140`). At the signed-WORD boundary, its own `WORD` arguments can also wrap that offscreen row onto the bottom of a tall bitmap: with `cp_y = -32768`, `TxBaseline = tf_Baseline = 2`, and `tf_YSize = 2`, `ClearEOL()` computes both Y endpoints as -32770 and -32769; conversion to `RectFill()`'s `WORD` parameters produces 32766 and 32767. On a bitmap 32,768 rows high, it therefore clears the final two rows even though the text row is wholly above the bitmap. In the same setup, `ClearScreen()` calculates `ymin` as -32768, converts it to a large `ULONG`, and skips the intended fill from row zero down. These effects share the public offscreen-cursor boundary and are kept under GD9870.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library builds, with a valid RastPort and font, when the cursor is positioned above the bitmap far enough that `cp_y - TxBaseline + Font->tf_YSize < 0`. This is independent of GD5766's incorrect chunky `BMA_WIDTH` result and can occur with a correctly sized bitmap. No checked-in direct C caller was found; `ClearScreen` remains a public graphics.library vector (`graphics.conf:48`). **Consequence:** the visible portion of the screen below the cursor is left uncleared. **Confidence:** high for the signed-to-unsigned conversion and skipped fill; no bitmap was cleared. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9871

**Finding:** `SetRGB4CM()` accepts a negative color index and writes before the colormap tables.

**Source and trigger:** `n` is a signed `WORD`, but the only check is `n < cm->Count` (`rom/graphics/setrgb4cm.c:17-21,59`). On the supported AROS targets where the `UWORD` count promotes to `int`, a negative `n` satisfies this comparison. The function then reads and writes `cm->ColorTable[n]`, and for colormaps newer than V1.2 also writes `cm->LowColorBits[n]` (`:63-68`). `GetColorMap()` allocates each table as a separate `entries * sizeof(UWORD)` block (`rom/graphics/getcolormap.c:73-78`), so `n == -1` accesses the UWORD immediately before each table allocation.

**Affected configuration and consequence:** graphics.library builds exposing the public `SetRGB4CM()` vector (vector 105 in `rom/graphics/graphics.conf`), when a caller supplies a valid ColorMap and a negative index. The call writes outside the ColorTable and, for V39 ColorMaps, outside LowColorBits; adjacent memory can be corrupted. No ordinary native C caller was found. The checked-in m68kemu compatibility bridge has a generated `SetRGB4CM` thunk that obtains `n` from guest D0 and forwards it without a lower-bound check (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:3658-3666`); it does not establish a valid in-tree negative-index producer, but a guest caller can reach this vector through the bridge. The negative-index trigger therefore remains a caller/API-condition, not a demonstrated valid-client path. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked signed lower bound and out-of-range table accesses on supported 32-bit-int targets. No invalid call was made. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9872

**IPrefs accepts legacy pointer preferences with an unsupported depth or incomplete bitmap payload.** The selected `PointerPrefs_Handler()` loads each `ID_PNTR` chunk using `LoadChunk(iff, sizeof(struct PointerPrefs), ...)` and passes the result to `InstallPointer()` (`workbench/c/iprefs/pointerprefs.c:135-158`). `LoadChunk()` checks only that the chunk contains the fixed header, then allocates and reads the whole declared chunk; it does not validate a depth-dependent payload size (`workbench/c/iprefs/misc.c:150-168`). `InstallPointer()` takes `pp_Depth` without a range check, derives the color count from it, reads that many color triples starting immediately after the header, and writes one plane pointer for each depth (`pointerprefs.c:41-70`). The public `BitMap` has exactly eight plane slots (`compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:33-41`). Thus a PNTR record declaring depth 9 is accepted and, if the color-table allocation succeeds, writes `bm.Planes[8]` beyond the local `BitMap`; if the chunk does not contain the implied color and plane data, the earlier color reads also pass the loaded chunk's end. Reject depths greater than the plane-slot count and validate the complete payload extent with checked size arithmetic before reading it. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-c-iprefs` target when its pointer-preference handler processes a legacy PNTR chunk with depth greater than eight or a chunk shorter than its declared depth/dimensions require. **Consequence:** the preferences load can read beyond its chunk and write beyond its local bitmap, disrupting IPrefs processing. **Confidence:** high for the missing checks and resulting accesses; occurrence depends on the contents of the preference record and successful allocation. No preference file was supplied or processed; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9873

**ASL eraser can paint over earlier gadgets when clipping-region subtraction runs out of memory.** During a full redraw, `AslEraser__GM_RENDER()` creates a region covering the requester interior, then calls `ClearRectRegion()` for each gadget rectangle without checking its Boolean result (`workbench/libs/asl/eraserclass.c:85-129`). `ClearRectRegion()` returns `FALSE` when `_DoOperationBandBand()` cannot allocate a result rectangle (`rom/graphics/clearrectregion.c:74-105`; allocation failure is propagated by `intregions.c:263-267`). On that failure the helper disposes the partial temporary list and leaves the original region unchanged (`intregions.c:748-756`), so the current gadget's rectangle remains in `clip`; the eraser then fills every rectangle still in the region with the background pen (`eraserclass.c:120-129`). Each affected requester creates the eraser with `GA_Previous` set to the preceding gadget (`filereqhooks.c:924-930`; `fontreqhooks.c:991-997`; `modereqhooks.c:748-754`); `GA_Previous` inserts it immediately after that gadget (`rom/intuition/gadgetclass.c:152-156`), and `RefreshGList()` walks the list forward and renders each gadget (`rom/intuition/refreshglist.c:147-162,239-263`). Therefore a failed subtraction for a gadget before the eraser can leave its area in the clip and then paint over it; a failed subtraction for a later gadget may be covered when that later gadget renders afterward. Check subtraction failure and skip the fill or use a safe fallback. **Affected configuration and trigger:** ASL builds that include the `eraserclass` source (`workbench/libs/asl/mmakefile.src:6-15`) when a full redraw subtracts an earlier-rendered gadget and region-rectangle allocation fails for that rectangle. The eraser is used by file, font and screen-mode requesters and is enabled by `AVOID_FLICKER`, defined as 1 in `asl_intern.h:69`. **Confidence:** high for the ignored failure, unchanged region, insertion/redraw order and subsequent fill; visible overpaint requires failure on an earlier gadget whose area overlaps the eraser fill. No requester, allocation failure, or redraw was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9874

**IPrefs selects the wrong legacy pointer image on little-endian systems when `WhichInFile` is nonzero.** The Pointer preferences editor serializes `npp_WhichInFile` as big-endian and converts it back to host order on import (`workbench/prefs/pointer/prefs.c:98-104,180-184`). IPrefs reads the NPTR chunk but passes `npp->npp_WhichInFile` directly to `LoadPointerFile()` without `AROS_BE2LONG()` (`workbench/c/iprefs/pointerprefs.c:162-170`). If the selected image file is not opened by the picture datatype, `LoadPointerFile()` falls back to the legacy IFF parser and forwards that ULONG as the WORD `which` argument to `LoadPointerPrefs()` (`pointerprefs.c:94-116,135-158`). The legacy filter then compares `which` with the raw, big-endian `pp->pp_Which` field rather than converting it (`:157-159`). On a little-endian target, a serialized `WhichInFile` value of 1 is read as `0x01000000`, narrowed to WORD zero, while a legacy `pp_Which` of 1 is read as `0x0100`; the requested image is skipped, and a file containing multiple PNTR chunks can instead install its index-zero image. The Preferences editor supports two pointer slots (`workbench/prefs/pointer/prefs.h:14`), so index 1 is a valid nonzero choice. Convert and range-check `WhichInFile` before narrowing, and compare host-order pointer IDs. **Affected configuration and trigger:** little-endian builds selecting `workbench-c-iprefs`, when an NPTR preference requests legacy PNTR image 1 from a file that falls back from `NewDTObject()` to `LoadPointerPrefs()`; normal pointer index 0 is unaffected. The target is explicitly buildable through `workbench/c/iprefs/mmakefile.src:27-32`. **Consequence:** the requested busy-pointer image may be omitted or replaced by the file's normal-pointer image. **Confidence:** high for the endian serialization, missing conversion, narrowing, and legacy filter comparison; manifestation requires a nonzero `WhichInFile` and datatype fallback. No preference file was loaded; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
