## GD9875

**Concurrent `ChangeVPBitMap()` and `LoadView()` can use a disposed viewport bitmap wrapper.** `ChangeVPBitMap()` publishes `vp->RasInfo->BitMap` and calls `MakeVPort()` before obtaining `ActiViewCprSemaphore` (`rom/graphics/changevpbitmap.c:63-70`). `LoadView()` holds that semaphore while it calls `display_LoadViewPorts()` (`rom/graphics/loadview.c:53-64`), which passes the shared viewport data to `HIDD_Display_ShowViewPorts()` or the fallback `HIDD_Display_Show()` path (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:511-568`). In `MakeVPort()`, ordinary planar-to-planar swaps update the backing bitmap through `HIDD_PlanarBM_SetBitMap()` and do not dispose the wrapper. Disposal occurs on a narrower representation-change path: when the new bitmap is a HIDD bitmap, `PreviousBitmap` is already non-NULL, and the current `vpd->Bitmap` is an owned planar wrapper, `MakeVPort()` disposes that wrapper before publishing the HIDD bitmap (`rom/graphics/makevport.c:119-169`). This state can follow a planar bitmap being wrapped, a first HIDD-bitmap swap establishing `PreviousBitmap`, and a return to a planar bitmap that creates a new owned wrapper. The public `ChangeVPBitMap()` contract requires matching depth, alignment and BytesPerRow but does not prohibit that planar/HIDD representation sequence; `AllocScreenBuffer()` also accepts caller-supplied bitmaps without checking their representation (`rom/graphics/changevpbitmap.c:32-38`; `rom/intuition/allocscreenbuffer.c:88-92,140-159`). If `LoadView()` has already read the wrapper while the unsynchronized swap disposes it, the selected P96 `ShowViewPorts()` path passes that object to `P96GFXDisplay__DoShow()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_hiddclass.c:934-947`), which calls `OOP_SetAttrs()` on it (`:862-878`). AmigaVideo also forwards the shared viewport chain to its compositor (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1500-1527`). The m68k Amiga boot HIDD selection includes P96 (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:187,375`). Serialize the bitmap publication, `MakeVPort()` update, and display reload under the same view semaphore, while preserving the required ordering with VBlank buffer replies.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library builds using an HIDD display backend, with an active viewport whose VPD currently owns a planar wrapper and has `PreviousBitmap` set; a caller then supplies a same-layout HIDD bitmap while another task is refreshing the active view. The direct public API permits caller-supplied bitmaps, but no maintained in-tree caller performing this mixed-representation sequence was established. The checked-in `ChangeScreenBuffer()` wrapper holds `LockIBase` across `ChangeVPBitMap()` (`rom/intuition/changescreenbuffer.c:74-83`), and selected Intuition display rebuild routes use the same lock (`rom/intuition/rethinkdisplay.c:50-73,136-162`; `rom/intuition/remakedisplay.c:48-62`); the candidate therefore remains conditional on external/direct graphics clients overlapping these operations. The selected m68k Amiga P96 backend demonstrates the stale-object consumer. **Consequence:** P96 can call `OOP_SetAttrs()` through the disposed wrapper during a concurrent view refresh; the resulting invalid access or display state was not runtime-verified. **Confidence:** high for the missing shared lock and the conditional wrapper disposal/use sequence; medium for reachability because the mixed-representation API input and required interleaving were not exercised. This is separate from GD4763's ignored `MakeVPort()` failure and GD5422's VBlank pending-list race. No bitmap swap, view refresh, or concurrent operation was performed; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9876

**ASL accepts a short preferences chunk and opens relative-size requesters at their minimum dimensions.** The packed `AslPrefs` structure is 26 bytes (`compiler/include/prefs/asl.h:20-33`), but `LoadPrefs()` ignores `ReadChunkBytes()`'s return value and unconditionally sets its loaded bit after parsing an `ASL ` chunk (`workbench/libs/asl/asl_init.c:279-294`). The selected `ReadChunkBytes()` implementation limits the read to the remaining chunk size and returns the actual number of bytes copied (`workbench/libs/iffparse/readchunkbytes.c:58-85`). Thus a structurally valid 20-byte chunk containing `ap_SizePosition` but omitting the final `ap_RelativeWidth` and `ap_RelativeHeight` leaves those fields at zero; the library base is allocated with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`rom/exec/makelibrary.c:108-109`). On first library open, `OpenBase()` invokes this loader (`asl_init.c:201-206`). `AllocAslRequest()` turns the saved `ap_SizePosition & 0x10` bit into `IF_SIZE_REL` (`workbench/libs/asl/allocaslrequest.c:85-88`), and `AslRequest()` calculates zero width and height from the missing percentages before clamping each to the requester minimum (`workbench/libs/asl/aslrequest.c:139-154`). The loaded marker then prevents later opens from retrying the preference read during the same library lifetime.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** explicit builds of the selected `workbench-libs-asl` module (`workbench/libs/asl/mmakefile.src:17-21`) when `ENV:Sys/Asl.prefs` contains a valid `FORM PREF` with an `ASL ` chunk of 20-23 bytes whose `ap_SizePosition` enables relative sizing. A physically truncated chunk can produce the same short read. **Consequence:** requesters using the saved relative-size option open at their minimum dimensions instead of the requested percentage for that library lifetime. Check that `ReadChunkBytes()` returned exactly `sizeof(struct AslPrefs)` before committing the settings or marking them loaded. **Confidence:** high for the short-read and zero-field path; occurrence requires a short preference chunk and the relative-size flag. No preference file or requester was used; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9877

**ASL copies an unchecked initial drawer path into a fixed stack buffer.** `FRNewPath()` copies its `path` argument with `strcpy()` into `char pathstring[MAX_PATH_LEN]` (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqsupport.c:892-900`; `MAX_PATH_LEN` is 1025 at `filereqhooks.h:38`). The public `ASLFR_InitialDrawer` tag is copied into the requester's pool without a length limit (`filereqhooks.c:265-273`), and file requester initialization passes that stored value to `FRNewPath()` (`filereqhooks.c:939-940`). The buffer size used by the path gadget does not constrain this independent public tag path. **Affected configuration and trigger:** selected `workbench-libs-asl` builds when an application supplies an initial drawer string of 1025 bytes or longer. **Consequence:** the copy writes past the stack buffer before path validation and directory lookup, potentially corrupting requester task state. Reject or safely truncate overlong drawer paths before copying. **Confidence:** high for the unbounded public tag and fixed-size destination; the caller controls whether the length condition occurs. No requester or path was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9878

**ASL directory scans retry non-EOF ExNext errors without yielding.** In `FRGetDirectory()`, an `ExNext()` failure other than `ERROR_NO_MORE_ENTRIES` sets `success = FALSE` and immediately continues the enclosing `for (;;)` loop (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqsupport.c:462-485`). If the filesystem keeps returning the same error, the scan never exits; the routine is synchronous, and it keeps the busy pointer and directory-scan indicator active until the loop ends (`:430-438,643-652`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** selected `workbench-libs-asl` builds when a locked filesystem directory returns a persistent non-EOF error from `ExNext()`. **Consequence:** the file requester stops processing its normal event flow while repeatedly retrying the failing enumeration. Exit or otherwise bound retries after a non-EOF error, while retaining the failure result. **Confidence:** high for the unbounded retry path; occurrence depends on a filesystem returning a persistent error. No filesystem error was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9879

**ASL list sorting can compare a null volume name after a pool allocation failure.** `FRGetVolumes()` allocates a list node, then assigns the result of `PooledCloneStringLen()` to `node->node.ln_Name` without checking it (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqsupport.c:732-741`). It then inserts the node through `SortInNode()` and `FRCompareVolumeNodes()` unconditionally passes both `ln_Name` fields to `Stricmp()` (`:661-697,795`). The list node allocation can succeed while the subsequent clone allocation fails; if a later volume/assign is inserted, comparison dereferences the missing name. The directory path has a related unchecked name clone, but its comparator only reads the name in name-sort mode (`:576-579,369-398`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** selected `workbench-libs-asl` builds when the volume list contains at least two entries and a name clone allocation fails after its node allocation succeeds. **Consequence:** volume-list construction can fault instead of displaying the available entries. Check clone results and skip/free incomplete nodes or propagate an allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked pointer and comparator; the allocation failure and subsequent comparison are conditional. No allocation failure or requester was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9880

**ASL font requester sizing reads one pointer past its fixed style-label array.** `BiggestTextLength()` tests `strarray[i]` before checking `i < numstrings` (`workbench/libs/asl/basicfuncs.c:865-880`). The font requester passes a three-element local array with all three entries populated and `numstrings == 3` (`workbench/libs/asl/fontreqhooks.c:824-840`). After processing entry 2, the next loop condition reads `strarray[3]` before the count check can terminate the loop. Other selected requester callers also pass fixed arrays with a count and no required terminator. **Affected configuration and trigger:** selected `workbench-libs-asl` builds when a font requester uses the style gadget (`FOF_DOSTYLE`) and reaches label sizing. **Consequence:** every such sizing pass performs an out-of-bounds stack pointer read; depending on adjacent stack contents and layout, this is undefined behavior and can fault. Test the count before reading the array element. **Confidence:** high for the evaluation order and exact three-element caller; no requester was opened; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9881

**ASL leaks an opened requester font when copying its name fails.** `GetRequesterFont()` opens a font, then allocates a separate copy of `usedattr->ta_Name`; it records the opened font in `ld->ld_Font` only inside the successful name-allocation branch (`workbench/libs/asl/basicfuncs.c:719-740`). If the name allocation fails, it returns FALSE without closing the local `font`. `AllocCommon()` then goes to its failure cleanup, but `FreeCommon()` closes only `ld->ld_Font`, which remains NULL (`:482-486,348-389`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** selected `workbench-libs-asl` builds when a requester font opens successfully but the subsequent font-name `AllocVec()` fails. **Consequence:** the font open reference is leaked on each such failed requester initialization. Close the local font on the allocation-failure path or store it in `ld` before returning. **Confidence:** high for the unmatched successful-open/failure-cleanup path; the allocation failure is conditional. No font allocation failure or requester was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9882

## GD9883

**ASL font size sorting can reverse entries when sizes differ by more than a signed word.** `FOCompareSizeNodes()` subtracts the numeric font sizes stored in `ln_Name` but returns the result as signed `WORD` (`workbench/libs/asl/fontreqsupport.c:133-137`). `FOGetFonts()` stores each `AvailFonts.af_Attr.ta_YSize` value, a `UWORD`, in those nodes and passes them to this comparator (`:278-288`; `compiler/include/graphics/text.h:72-78`). Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9884

## GD9885

**ASL screen-mode depth labels shift a 32-bit value by 32.** When a display mode reports `MaxDepth > 8`, `SMActivateMode()` formats its color count using `1UL << i`, where `i` is assigned that maximum depth (`workbench/libs/asl/modereqsupport.c:359-373`). `ULONG` is 32 bits in this ABI (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:38-43`), so a supported 32-bit display depth shifts by the type width, which is undefined in C. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9886

**ASL admits HAM modes with no depth choice inside the requested range.** `SMGetModes()` admits a HAM display mode when its `MaxDepth` is at least `ism_MinDepth` and the requested maximum is at least 6 (`workbench/libs/asl/modereqsupport.c:119-129`). ## GD9887

**Concurrent ASL property-window refreshes share a mutable iteration pointer.** `SMRefreshPropertyWindow()` declares both `pi` and `pitable` static, then uses `pi` as the mutable cursor for its property loop (`workbench/libs/asl/modereqsupport.c:795-829`). ## GD9888

**ASL color picker narrows its public color count to signed 16 bits before building the palette.** The public font-requester parser accepts `ASLFO_MaxFrontPen` as a `UWORD` (`workbench/libs/asl/fontreqhooks.c:286-287`; `asl_intern.h:175`), and passes that value to the picker as `ASLCP_NumColors` (`fontreqhooks.c:871-879`). `AslColorPicker__OM_SET()` assigns the `IPTR` tag value to `AslColorPickerData.numcolors`, which is a signed `WORD` (`colorpickerclass.c:215-217`; `asl_intern.h:572-602`). ## GD9889

## GD9890

**XorRectRegionND dereferences a failed region allocation for an empty rectangle.** For an evil/empty rectangle, the function allocates `ret = NewRegion()` and immediately passes it to `_CopyRegionRectangles()` without checking for NULL (`rom/graphics/xorrectregionnd.c:62-70`). `NewRegion()` returns NULL when either its pooled or direct backing allocation fails (`rom/graphics/newregion.c:56-68`), while `_CopyRegionRectangles()` passes `&R2->RegionRectangle` to `_LinkRegionRectangleList()`, which dereferences the destination pointer before copying (`rom/graphics/intregions.h:155-162`; `rom/graphics/intregions.c:224-241`). The documented result is NULL on allocation failure, but this branch instead dereferences NULL. The neighboring `OrRectRegionND()` checks its result allocation before copying, and `AndRectRegionND()` returns the allocation result directly for an empty rectangle.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library builds selecting `xorrectregionnd` (`rom/graphics/mmakefile.src:28-211`), when a caller supplies a valid region, an empty/evil rectangle, and `NewRegion()` cannot allocate the result. No checked-in C caller of `XorRectRegionND()` was found; the consequence applies to direct API clients. **Consequence:** a NULL dereference during an allocation-failure path instead of a clean NULL return. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked result and dereference; occurrence requires the specific allocation failure and empty-rectangle branch. **ASL file requester copies a long drawer path into a filename-sized stack buffer.** When Return or Tab is pressed in the file string gadget, the handler constructs a path if the filename contains a colon or slash (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqhooks.c:1320-1335`). For a relative path containing a slash but no colon, it copies the current drawer string into `checkstring[MAX_FILE_LEN]` with `strcpy()` before adding the relative path (`:1322,1356-1364`). `MAX_FILE_LEN` is 257, but the drawer gadget accepts up to `MAX_PATH_LEN`, which is 1,025 (`filereqhooks.h:38-39`; `filereqhooks.c:878-880,883-890`). No requester or path was used; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9892

**ASL file requester uses `NameFromLock()` output after that call fails.** The AppWindow handler calls `NameFromLock()` into local `firsticonpath` and `iconpath` arrays but ignores its Boolean result (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqhooks.c:1081-1092,1114`). ## GD9893

**ASL list-view selection narrows long row indices to signed 16 bits.** The list-view total and pixel positions are stored as `LONG`, but `findnode()` accepts a `WORD` index and `mouseitem()` also returns `WORD` (`workbench/libs/asl/asl_intern.h:467`; `workbench/libs/asl/listviewclass.c:130-142,273-319`). `mouseitem()` calculates the absolute row as `LONG`, passes it to `findnode()`, then assigns it to its signed 16-bit return; `GM_GOACTIVE()` and drag selection keep the returned row in `WORD` locals (`listviewclass.c:298-312,693-708,805-815`). Programmatic selection has the same narrowing: `OM_SET` casts `ASLLV_Active` to `WORD`, and `OM_GET` returns that narrowed field (`listviewclass.c:454-488,639-643`). The in-tree file, font, and display-mode requester consumers also cast the returned active index to `WORD` before `FindListNode()` (`filereqhooks.c:1480-1485`; `fontreqhooks.c:1161-1185`; `modereqhooks.c:926-935`). A row index above 32,767 therefore cannot be represented reliably by click, drag, or programmatic selection; on the selected AROS 16-bit `WORD` ABI, the first such index, 32,768, narrows to a negative value and is treated as an out-of-list sentinel or rejected by `findnode()`. In contrast, the list total is `LONG`, rendering walks nodes sequentially, and the file requester enumerates `ExNext()` entries until end-of-directory and appends each accepted row without a 32,767-entry cap (`filereqsupport.c:444-454,566-628`; `listviewclass.c:467,205-230`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** ASL builds using the selected file requester, when a directory contains more than 32,767 displayed entries and the user clicks or programmatically selects an entry whose zero-based list index is above 32,767. **Consequence:** high-index rows can be drawn but cannot be selected reliably, so the file requester may leave the active selection unchanged or return a different file. Use a wide signed index consistently for row lookup, hit testing, `ASLLV_Active`, and requester-side node lookup. **Confidence:** high for the type mismatch and absent enumeration cap; occurrence requires a very large directory. No directory with this many entries or UI operation was used; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9894

**ASL cycle gadget returns its disposed object when frame allocation fails.** `AslCycle__OM_NEW()` creates the superclass gadget, then allocates its frame image. If `NewObjectA(FRAMEICLASS, ...)` fails, the code calls `CoerceMethod(..., OM_DISPOSE)` but does not set `g` to NULL before returning it (`workbench/libs/asl/cycleclass.c:225-245`). `AslCycle__OM_DISPOSE()` delegates to the gadget superclass, and the root-class disposer frees the gadget allocation (`cycleclass.c:250-257`; `rom/intuition/gadgetclass.c:473-478`; `rom/oop/rootclass.c:137-150`). The caller therefore receives a non-NULL pointer to a freed gadget and treats construction as successful. The selected font and mode requester callers store the pointer and continue gadget setup after checking only `!gad` (`workbench/libs/asl/fontreqhooks.c:980-983`; `modereqhooks.c:635-638,711-714,736-739`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** builds selecting the ASL font or screen-mode requester, when superclass gadget creation succeeds but the nested FRAMEICLASS allocation fails. **Consequence:** requester setup retains the freed gadget in its gadget chain; later layout, rendering or disposal may read or write freed memory or fail to build the requester. Set the returned gadget pointer to NULL after disposal so callers take their existing construction-failure cleanup. **Confidence:** high for the dispose-and-return ordering, root-class free, and selected callers' non-NULL checks; manifestation requires frame allocation failure. No allocation failure, requester construction or UI operation was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9896

**ASL signed-WORD row counting overflows for large file lists and multi-selections.** `CountNodes()` accumulates matching nodes in signed `WORD` and returns that narrow type (`workbench/libs/asl/basicfuncs.c:959-969`); `WORD` is signed 16-bit (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:58-62`). File requester directory enumeration has no 32,767-row cap (`filereqsupport.c:566-628`). The ASL list view stores `CountNodes(labels, 0)` in its `LONG total`, then derives pixel/visible counts and builds its node table only when `total > 0` (`workbench/libs/asl/listviewclass.c:493-518,149-174`). With more than 32,767 rows, incrementing the signed counter overflows; the result is not representable and C behavior is undefined. On common 32-bit two's-complement behavior, the returned negative count prevents the node table from being built and corrupts the view's scroll/count state. The same helper counts selected rows for the multi-select result path (`filereqhooks.c:667,1813-1845`), where the `WORD` result sizes allocation and bounds the copy loop even though public `fr_NumArgs` is `LONG` (`compiler/include/libraries/asl.h:61-62`). Use a wider unsigned count and validate it against allocation and public API limits. **Confidence:** high for the 16-bit signed accumulator and both selected consumers; no large directory or selection was exercised. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
## GD9897

**ASL's MorphOS fallback reads beyond every cool-image palette on truecolor screens.** On MorphOS, `USE_SHARED_COOLIMAGES` is zero, so ASL includes its local `CoolImage` definition and static image tables (`workbench/libs/asl/asl_intern.h:63-66`; `buttonclass.c:28-32`). In that branch `SHARED_COOLIMAGES_LIBRARY` is not defined, so `AslButton__OM_NEW()` computes `numcols` as `1 << data->coolimage->depth` and reads three bytes from `pal` for every entry through that count (`buttonclass.c:79-96`). The constructor therefore reads 16 or 256 entries from those respective palettes. **Affected configuration and trigger:** `workbench-libs-asl` built for MorphOS, with a requester button using a local cool image on a truecolor screen where `CyberGfxBase` is available (`buttonclass.c:79`). **Consequence:** button construction performs out-of-bounds reads from static palette data and fills the remaining color table with unrelated bytes, making behavior undefined and potentially rendering incorrect colors or faulting. Use the actual palette-entry count in the fallback image metadata and bound conversion to that count. **Confidence:** high for the selected preprocessor branch, table sizes, and constructor loop; no MorphOS build or truecolor requester was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9898

**SDL event-task startup can accept an unrelated signal as its readiness handshake.** `sdl_event_init()` uses the caller's predefined `SIGF_BLIT` bit as its private completion signal, clears that bit with `SetSignal(0, sync)`, creates the event task, then calls `Wait(sync)` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/event.c:118-146`). The event task signals the creator with that same bit only after installing its stack-local VBlank interrupt (`:42-64`). `SIGF_BLIT` aliases the general `SIGF_SINGLE` bit (`compiler/include/exec/tasks.h:140-148`), and Exec `Wait()` returns immediately when any producer has already set a requested bit (`rom/exec/wait.c:76-80,128-138`). The new task runs at priority 50; the non-SMP `NewAddTask()` path only reschedules its creator when the new task priority is strictly greater than the creator's (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:55-76`). Thus, for a creator at priority 50 or higher, an asynchronous producer that sets bit 4 after the clear but before the child's readiness signal can leave the creator running; `Wait(sync)` then returns on that unrelated signal and `sdl_event_init()` publishes `eventtask` without proving that the child reached its ready point. On SMP, task placement and whether the worker reaches its signal first depend on scheduler timing. This defeats the caller's startup barrier; a later startup failure can then enter event-task cleanup while initialization may still be in flight, compounding the existing GD2620 interrupt-lifetime concern.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional hosted SDL HIDD startup when its creator is not preempted by the priority-50 worker and another signal source sets `SIGF_BLIT`/`SIGF_SINGLE` during the handshake window. The priority-at-least-50 case is explicit for the non-SMP `NewAddTask()` path; SMP timing is conditional. No maintained caller was found that deliberately signals the SDL startup task in this window, so normal in-tree occurrence is unestablished. **Consequence:** startup can proceed before the event worker confirms its VBlank registration and initialization point. Allocate a private signal with `AllocSignal()` and release it on every exit path, or use a handshake that cannot be satisfied by an unrelated task signal. **Confidence:** high that the bit is shared and `Wait()` accepts any matching pending signal; medium that external callers encounter the narrow window. No signal, startup or scheduling event was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9900

**Scrollbar preferences leaves custom-only image controls enabled for the default scrollbar type.** `ScrollbarsP_New()` registers notifications that disable the background and knob image gadgets when the cycle is set to Standard (0) or New Look (1), and enable them for Custom (2) (`workbench/prefs/Zune/scrollbarsp.c:178-186`). **Zune preferences leaks loaded configdata and can overrun the Save As pathname buffer.** Each successful Open-menu request creates a `MUIC_Configdata` object, loads the chosen file, and copies its values into the preference pages, but the object is never stored for later use or disposed (`workbench/prefs/Zune/zune.c:629-659`). No file requester, config load, allocation pressure, or Save As was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9905

**Zune's file requester helper leaks ASL resources on allocation failure or cancellation.** After `OpenLibrary("asl.library", 37L)` succeeds, `aslfilerequest()` returns without `CloseLibrary(AslBase)` if `AllocAslRequest()` fails; if the requester is allocated but `AslRequest()` returns FALSE (including user cancellation), the helper closes the library but omits `FreeAslRequest(fr)` (`workbench/prefs/Zune/zunestuff.c:34-67`). The selected Zune Open and Save As menu handlers both call this helper (`zune.c:629-633,713-715`), so repeated failed/cancelled requester use accumulates library opens and/or requester allocations. **Trigger:** invoke either menu when requester allocation fails, or cancel after successful requester allocation. **Consequence:** retained ASL library references can prevent expunging the library, and unreleased requester structures/pools accumulate. Close the library and free any allocated requester on every exit path. **Affected configuration:** Zune Preferences with ASL available and Open/Save As menu use. **Confidence:** high for both unmatched ownership paths; no requester cancellation or allocation failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9907

**MUI trusts the embedded window-position size without checking the stored chunk length or destination capacity.** Loading a preferences file stores each IFF subchunk using its actual `cn_Size` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/dataspace.c:208-243`). Configdata later finds `MUICFG_WindowPos`, reads the first four bytes as a declared size, byte-swaps that many bytes on little-endian builds, and passes the pointer to the Application class (`configdata.c:861-879`). The Application handler reads the declared byte count and copies it starting at `winposused` without checking it against the property length or the fixed `winpos[MAXWINS]` array (`application.c:1009-1021`; `application.h:256-267`). **Trigger:** load a damaged/truncated preferences file with a `MUICFG_WindowPos` property shorter than its four-byte size field, or a declared size larger than the stored property or application buffer. **Consequence:** the load path can read/write beyond the dataspace allocation during byte swapping and then copy beyond the Application instance's window-position storage. Validate the actual dataspace property length, the embedded size, and the destination capacity before swapping/copying; reject malformed records. **Affected configuration:** MUI applications loading Zune preferences containing window-position data; the byte-swap write applies on little-endian builds, and the unchecked copy applies on all builds. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked lengths and copy; no damaged preference file was loaded. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9908

**Legacy MUI Application Input can consume a handler signal without dispatching its callback.** `Application__MUIM_Input()` builds a value from registered nodes' `ihn_Flags` and passes it to `Application__MUIM_NewInput()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1861-1893`). `NewInput()` interprets that value as the signal set to dispatch against `ihn_Signals` (`application.c:1587-1595,1660-1671`), then overwrites it with the correct wait mask before returning (`:1826-1835`). Thus the wait can wake, but after `Wait()` consumes a handler's signal, the next legacy Input call does not present that received bit to dispatch; the callback may not drain the associated message port until a later unrelated event causes another dispatch opportunity. **In-tree trigger:** Wanderer's `AskChoice2()` calls legacy Input and waits in its modal loop (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems_utilities.c:263-309`). Wanderer's application registers signal-based command-port and filesystem-notify handlers (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:3355-3380`), and `DisplayIOError()` enters `AskChoice()` (`filesystems_utilities.c:346-365`), which is called from filesystem operations. While that modal error dialog runs, a command or filesystem notification can wake the loop yet leave its callback undispatched; queued work can remain pending until another event or dialog exit. **Recommendation:** pass the received signal set to NewInput or dispatch handler signals from the actual Wait result, and keep the returned wait mask separate. **Affected configuration:** Wanderer builds using this MUI implementation; other legacy Input users require their own registered signal-handler path. **Confidence:** high for the mask/dispatch mismatch and the in-tree call chain; no signal or GUI loop was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9909

**ARexx command dispatch continues with missing or invalid parsed arguments.** For a matching command with a template, `Application__MUIM_NewInput()` allocates an argument buffer and writes into it without checking `AllocVec()`; it also calls the command hook even when allocating `RDArgs` fails or `ReadArgs()` rejects the input (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1717-1754`). In the `RDArgs` allocation-failure case, the VLA `args` is not initialized before it is passed to the hook; in the argument-buffer failure case, `CopyMem()` and the subsequent terminator writes use a NULL destination. **Trigger:** a templated ARexx command arrives while argument-buffer or RDArgs allocation fails, or with syntax rejected by `ReadArgs()`. **Consequence:** low-memory input can fault while building arguments or invoke the handler with indeterminate/invalid arguments after parsing failed. Check each allocation and the `ReadArgs()` result, and return the corresponding command error without invoking the hook on failure. **Affected configuration:** MUI applications enabling ARexx command templates. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocations and parse result; no ARexx command or allocation failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9910

**MUI Application Save and Load can pass an unterminated stack pathname to DOS.** For caller-supplied names (rather than the ENV/ENVARC special values), both methods copy at most `sizeof(name)-1` bytes into a local `char name[1024]` with `strncpy()` but never set `name[sizeof(name)-1]` to NUL (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:2411-2416,2485-2489`). If the supplied name is at least 1,023 bytes, `strncpy()` does not terminate it and the following `Open()` reads beyond the local array while searching for a terminator. **Trigger:** call `MUIM_Application_Load` or `MUIM_Application_Save` with a non-special path of 1,023 bytes or longer. **Consequence:** DOS receives a path containing bytes beyond the caller's pathname and beyond the local buffer, potentially opening the wrong file or failing unpredictably. Reject overlong paths or explicitly terminate the buffer after a checked copy. **Affected configuration:** MUI applications using the public Save/Load methods with explicit pathnames. An in-tree direct-call census found all checked-in calls use the ENV or ENVARC special values; no checked-in long explicit-path trigger was established, so the candidate is limited to external/public API callers. **Confidence:** high for the fixed buffer and missing terminator; no long path was passed to the methods. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9911

**MUI Dataspace IFF import loops forever on a zero-length record.** `Dataspace__MUIM_ReadIFF()` advances past an eight-byte ID/length header, checks that the declared payload does not exceed the remaining chunk, calls `MUIM_Dataspace_Add()`, and then advances `p` by `len` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/dataspace.c:221-240`). A zero length passes the remaining-bytes check, but `Dataspace__MUIM_Add()` rejects lengths below one and returns without adding a node (`:100-108`). The reader ignores that result and `p += len` leaves the cursor unchanged. While at least eight bytes remain, the same header is processed indefinitely. The nested Add semaphore acquisition is reentrant for its owning task (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:91-98`), so the repeated call returns and does not break the loop.

The selected Configdata loader passes `MUIC` chunks to this reader (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/configdata.c:1259-1266`). **Trigger:** load an IFF preference file whose `MUIC` chunk contains a complete record header with `len == 0` and enough bytes for the reader's eight-byte loop condition. **Consequence:** the loading task spins indefinitely while holding the Dataspace semaphore; Zune Preferences or an application restoring MUI state can stop responding, and other tasks attempting to use that Dataspace can wait behind it. Reject zero-length records and return a parse error, or ensure the cursor advances past/rejects the malformed record. **Affected configuration:** MUI Configdata or Application Load paths that import the affected Dataspace chunk. **Confidence:** high for the cursor and Add behavior; the malformed serialized record is required and no file was loaded. No IFF file or UI operation was used; source-only.

**Review evidence:** Dataspace reader/Add bodies and Configdata caller are covered in [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3363`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L3363); the zero-length record boundary trace is in the latest Dataspace import review entry.

## GD9912

**ASL font requester narrows large AvailFonts counts to signed WORD before sorting and grouping.** `AvailFontsHeader.afh_NumEntries` is an unsigned 16-bit count, and diskfont increments it as each entry fits in the caller's buffer (`compiler/include/diskfont/diskfont.h:90-93`; `workbench/libs/diskfont/availfonts.c:210-219`). ASL retries `AvailFonts()` with a larger buffer until it reports no shortage, then `SortAvailFonts()` assigns that count to signed `WORD numentries` and passes it to `qsort()` (`workbench/libs/asl/fontreqsupport.c:153-165,182-204`). At 32,768 entries, the conversion to `WORD` is implementation-defined; on the conventional GCC/Clang AROS conversion it becomes -32,768, which converts to a huge `size_t` argument and makes the selected qsort calculate element addresses far outside the returned font array (`compiler/crt/stdc/qsort.c:73-80`; `compiler/crt/stdc/__qsort.h:87-120`). If sorting returns, `FOGetFonts()` also uses signed `WORD` for its outer and grouping indices (`fontreqsupport.c:176,208-222`), which cannot represent all entries and reaches signed overflow during traversal. The font requester calls `FOGetFonts()` during setup and on rescan (`workbench/libs/asl/fontreqhooks.c:427,1292-1294`). **Trigger:** the selected font requester sees at least 32,768 available font entries across memory and disk, with the caller's `AvailFonts()` buffer large enough to return them. The API count can represent this value and no 32,767-entry cap is applied in these paths. **Consequence:** on the stated compiler conversion, sorting reads or compares beyond the font array; subsequent signed-index overflow also makes font grouping invalid. Use a wide unsigned count/index type and validate it against the header's representable range. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting ASL's FontRequester and the usual AROS GCC/Clang integer conversion behavior, with an exceptionally large available-font set. **Confidence:** high for the width mismatch and absence of a count cap; the exact failure manifestation depends on the compiler's out-of-range unsigned-to-signed conversion, and no such font set or requester was exercised. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9914

**ASL ListView drops timer-driven selection repeat at the list edges.** `AslListView__GM_HANDLEINPUT()` sets `code = IECODE_NOBUTTON` for `IECLASS_TIMER` and then falls through to `IECLASS_RAWMOUSE`, where it overwrites `code` with `ie_Code` (`workbench/libs/asl/listviewclass.c:781-805`). The selected InputDevice timer producer initializes timer events with `ie_Class = IECLASS_TIMER` and `ie_Code = 0` (`rom/devs/input/processevents.c:438-448`), and Intuition forwards timer events to the active BOOPSI gadget's `GM_HANDLEINPUT` (`rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:2764-2768`). Thus the timer tick does not enter the `IECODE_NOBUTTON` branch that calls `mouseitem()` and steps the active row when the pointer is in the top or bottom edge margin (`listviewclass.c:805-810`). **Trigger:** an ASL ListView is active while the user holds a selection and leaves the pointer stationary in an edge margin that relies on timer repeats. **Consequence:** the expected repeated movement through the list stops until another pointer event; handle timer events as a no-button tick without replacing that value with the timer event's zero code. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `workbench-libs-asl` and its ListView class. **Confidence:** high for event construction, delivery, and the overwritten branch condition; no requester interaction was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9915

**Wanderer reports a successful file copy when destination metadata updates fail.** `CopyFileInfo()` calls DOS `SetComment()` and `SetProtection()` but discards both Boolean results, then returns `TRUE` whenever it obtained the source FileInfoBlock (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems_utilities.c:527-549`). Both DOS APIs document failure status (`rom/dos/setcomment.c:33-51`; `setprotection.c:31-45`); `SetComment()` can also reject comments longer than `MAXCOMMENTLENGTH` (`setcomment.c:62-68`). Its only caller invokes it after the data stream was copied and closed, and ignores its return value (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:231-236`). **Trigger:** copying a file whose comment or protection bits cannot be applied on the destination, for example a too-long comment or a destination handler that rejects one of the metadata actions. **Consequence:** the copied file contents remain, but its comment and/or protection differ from the source without an error or failed-operation result. Check each DOS result, report partial metadata failure, and propagate a failure/status distinct from data-copy failure. **Affected configuration:** Wanderer's file-copy operation when the destination does not accept one or both metadata updates; exact handler support varies by filesystem. **Confidence:** high that failures are discarded and success is reported; no destination filesystem failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9916

**Wanderer directory deletion can pass a null FileInfoBlock to DOS Examine after allocation failure.** `IsDirectoryEmpty()` stores `GetFileInfoBlock(path)` in `fib`, then calls `ReadFileInfoBlockAndLockPath(path, fib)` without checking whether `fib` is null (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems_utilities.c:93-104`). `GetFileInfoBlock()` returns null when `AllocDosObject(DOS_FIB, ...)` fails (`:386-425`); the lock helper still calls `Examine(nLock, fib)` whenever `Lock()` succeeds (`:435-453`). DOS `Examine()` requires a valid output FileInfoBlock and calls `fixfib(fib)` on successful packets (`rom/dos/examine.c:25-31,61-66`; `bstr_helper.c:20-24`). The selected directory-removal path calls `IsDirectoryEmpty()` after deleting directory contents (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:807-814`). **Trigger:** FileInfoBlock allocation fails during this final emptiness check, but the subsequent directory lock and Examine operation succeed. **Consequence:** DOS attempts to populate/normalize a null FileInfoBlock, so directory deletion can fail catastrophically during low-memory cleanup. Return immediately when allocation fails and make the helper reject a null output buffer. **Affected configuration:** Wanderer's recursive directory deletion on filesystems where the post-allocation-failure lock and Examine can still succeed. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked null flow and DOS contract; no allocation failure or deletion was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9917 — withdrawn

A caller recheck found that the recursive-copy path supplies a FileInfoBlock already initialized by an earlier successful `GetFileInfoBlock()` on the same directory (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:721-726`). The helper's later `Examine()` failure leaves that prior state available; the available source evidence does not establish that `ExNext()` necessarily uses invalid state or that the copy silently omits entries. The helper's error propagation remains inelegant, but no independent user-visible defect is established. No filesystem error or copy was induced.

## GD9918

**Wanderer leaks the destination path allocated for each move operation.** `MoveContent()` stores `CombinePath(FilePart(sourcePath), targetDir)` in `nextTargetFile` and uses it for the existing-destination check, but never calls `FreeVec(nextTargetFile)` on either the collision path or after a successful move (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:642-665`). `CombinePath()` allocates and returns a new vector (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems_utilities.c:489-514`). The selected drop handler calls `MoveContent()` for each dropped entry (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:345-349`). **Trigger:** move one or more entries through Wanderer's drop handler. **Consequence:** the Wanderer task retains one allocated path buffer per invocation; repeated moves steadily consume task memory and can contribute to later allocation failures. Free the constructed path after the collision check, including early-exit paths. **Affected configuration:** Wanderer builds using the filesystem drop handler. **Confidence:** high for allocation ownership and missing release; no moves or memory-pressure scenario were run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9919

**Wanderer can reject moving a standalone `.info` file because an unrelated same-basename file exists at the destination.** `infoFileSetup()` supports a source whose base file is absent but whose `.info` sidecar exists by setting `localSourcePath` to the sidecar and clearing `hasInfoFile` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:512-539`). `MoveContent()` nevertheless constructs its preliminary collision path from the original `sourcePath` (`:642-648`), so for source `foo` it checks `target/foo`. If that path exists, it aborts before `moveFile()` can check the actual destination `target/foo.info` (`:655`; `moveFile()` at `:309-336`). **Trigger:** move a standalone `foo.info` represented to `MoveContent()` by base path `foo`, while the destination contains `foo` but not `foo.info`. **Consequence:** the valid sidecar move is refused as a collision with the unrelated destination file. Build the preliminary target from `localSourcePath`, or remove the redundant preliminary collision check and rely on `moveFile()`'s actual-path check. **Affected configuration:** Wanderer's move operation for standalone `.info` entries. **Confidence:** high for the differing source paths and early exit; no files were moved. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9920

**Wanderer overwrites a failed `.info` FileInfoBlock setup and later dereferences the null pointer.** In `copySingleFile()`, failure to allocate/read the source sidecar's FileInfoBlock sets `stop = TRUE` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:434-448`). For a top-level copy (`inDir == FALSE`), the subsequent destination-existence check assigns to `stop` instead of preserving the earlier failure (`:451-455`). If the destination does not already exist, execution continues: after copying the main file it calls `performDataCopy()` for the `.info` sidecar with `infoFib == NULL` (`:457-463`), and that function dereferences `fib->fib_Size` immediately (`:150-165`). The top-level call sets `inDir` to `!first`, so this occurs for the initial single-file copy (`:754-760`). **Trigger:** copy a file with an existing `.info` sidecar, have `GetFileInfoBlock(sourceInfoFilePath)` fail, and have the destination collision check return false. **Consequence:** after the main file has already been copied, the follow-up sidecar copy dereferences a null FileInfoBlock and the operation does not complete cleanly. Preserve the earlier stop state or return immediately on sidecar setup failure, and validate the FIB at the copy helper boundary. **Affected configuration:** Wanderer's top-level file-copy path when sidecar FIB allocation or examination fails. **Confidence:** high for the overwritten error flag and null dereference path; no allocation failure or file copy was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9921 — withdrawn as a duplicate of GD5846

This describes the same `performDataCopy()` negative-`Read()` result being treated as EOF and reported as a successful copy. GD5846 is the retained finding for this root cause. The later entry adds no distinct trigger or consequence. See GD5846 for the active scope. No read error or copy was induced; source-only.

## GD9922

**Wanderer can report a move as successful when destination-path allocation fails.** `moveFile()` stores the result of `CombinePath()` in `to`, then performs `FileExists(to)` before checking whether `to` is null (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:309-336`). `CombinePath()` returns null after allocation failure (`filesystems_utilities.c:489-514`). DOS `Lock()` safely returns `BNULL` for a null name (`rom/dos/lock.c:66-68`), so `FileExists(NULL)` returns false; the later `if (to && !stop)` skips `Rename()` without setting `stop`. Both in-tree `MoveContent()` calls use `newDir == FALSE` (`filesystems.c:655-659`). **Trigger:** `CombinePath()` cannot allocate the destination string during a Wanderer move. **Consequence:** the source entry remains in place, but `moveFile()` returns its success value; a sidecar move may then proceed separately, leaving a partially moved pair. Check `to` immediately and set/propagate failure before testing destination existence. **Affected configuration:** Wanderer's move operation when destination-path allocation fails. **Confidence:** high for the allocation/NULL-lock/false-success path; no allocation failure or move was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9923

**Wanderer ignores a failed destination Close() and reports the file copy as successful.** After the read/write loop, `performDataCopy()` sets its result from `stop`, calls `Close(out)` without checking the returned Boolean, then proceeds with metadata copying and returns the earlier result (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:227-253`). DOS documents that `Close()` returns zero on error (`rom/dos/close.c:27-36`); the implementation returns the destination handler's `ACTION_END` status (`close.c:68-79`). **Trigger:** the destination handler reports an `ACTION_END` failure after the explicit `Write()` calls succeeded. **Consequence:** Wanderer can report success despite the handler reporting a close/finalization error; the destination's final state depends on handler behavior. Check and propagate the output Close result before copying metadata or reporting completion. **Affected configuration:** Wanderer file copies on filesystems that can fail during output close/finalization. **Confidence:** high for the ignored documented status; no close failure or copy was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9924

**Wanderer reads uninitialized copy timing and divides by zero for empty files.** Before opening or reading the source, `performDataCopy()` initializes `totallen` and `actlen` to zero and `filelen` from `fib_Size`, then immediately calls the display hook; it does not initialize `difftime` in this initial callback (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:172-180`). The selected Wanderer callback computes speed from `difftime` on every non-delete callback, including this initial one, and sets gauge progress by converting `32768.0 * totallen / filelen` to `ULONG` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:162-178`). Thus every copy using this progress hook reads an indeterminate timing field before the first read initializes it. For a zero-byte file, `filelen` is also zero, so the initial gauge expression is `0/0`; the later read loop reaches EOF without setting `difftime`. **Trigger:** any file copy using the selected progress hook reaches the uninitialized speed calculation; copying a zero-byte file additionally triggers the zero-denominator gauge calculation. The drop handler creates and passes the progress hook (`wanderer.c:332-345`). **Consequence:** speed text is based on indeterminate timing for all such copies; for empty files, converting the NaN gauge result to `ULONG` is undefined by the C rules. Initialize timing before the initial callback and avoid computing rate or percentage when elapsed time or file length is zero. **Affected configuration:** Wanderer copy operations using the selected progress display. **Confidence:** high for the callback order, uninitialized field read and zero-length division; no file was copied. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9925

**Wanderer recursive deletion can skip an entry when child-path allocation fails and report success.** `deleteDirectoryContents()` gets each child path from `CombinePath()`, but if that returns null it neither sets `stop` nor reports failure; it proceeds to the next directory entry (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:352-363`). `CombinePath()` returns null when its `AllocVec()` fails (`filesystems_utilities.c:489-514`). At the end, the helper only marks failure for an `ExNext()` error, so a skipped child followed by normal end-of-directory returns success (`filesystems.c:365-377`). The parent then sees the directory is not empty and leaves it in place, but propagates the false success (`:807-814,825-830`). **Trigger:** recursive deletion encounters a child for which `CombinePath()` cannot allocate its full path, then enumeration reaches normal end. **Consequence:** the child and parent directory remain, while `DeleteContent()` reports success. Treat a null child path as an operation failure and propagate it. **Affected configuration:** Wanderer's recursive delete path under path-allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the skipped-entry and success-return path; no allocation failure or deletion was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9926

**Wanderer recursive copy can pass a null child path into string handling after allocation failure.** `copyDirectory()` passes the result of `CombinePath()` directly to `CopyContent()` without checking for null (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:487-495`). On allocation failure, `CombinePath()` returns null (`filesystems_utilities.c:489-514`). `CopyContent()` forwards its path to `infoFileSetup()`, which calls `FileExists(NULL)` and then `ConstructInfofileName(NULL)`; the latter immediately evaluates `strlen(path)` (`filesystems.c:695-699`; `filesystems_utilities.c:523-526,577-580`). **Trigger:** recursive directory copy cannot allocate a child path. **Consequence:** the null path reaches `strlen()`, so the copy can fail catastrophically rather than returning an operation error. Check the child-path allocation before calling `CopyContent()` and mark the recursive copy failed. **Affected configuration:** Wanderer's recursive directory copy under path-allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the null propagation and dereference; no allocation failure or copy was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9927

**Zune non-single-task application base names can collide during concurrent startup, long-base truncation, or suffix exhaustion.** `Application__OM_NEW()` defaults `MUIA_Application_SingleTask` to FALSE, then searches for the first unused `<Base>.<n>` by calling `find_application_by_base()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:419-446`). The helper protects its scan of the published application list with `ZuneSemaphore` but releases the semaphore before returning (`:296-318`). The new application is not added to that list until after configdata, timer and app-port construction (`:473-479,490-510,758-771`). Two constructors for the same base can therefore both observe the same suffix as free, choose it, and later publish distinct applications with identical `app_Base` values.

There are also two sequential collision cases. The loop tests only suffixes 1 through 999; if each is already present, it exits with `portname` still set to the occupied `.999` name, then duplicates it without a final availability check (`:438-446`). In addition, `portname` is only 255 bytes and `snprintf()` truncates `<Base>.<n>` to 254 characters (`:435-440`). A valid `MUIA_Application_Base` of at least 253 bytes therefore loses some or all of its numeric suffix; all 999 probes produce the same truncated string. After one such app is published, a later non-single-task instance with the same Base scans 999 times and then adopts that already-used string. The public attribute is declared as `STRPTR` with no length restriction (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.h:202-203,232-233`); a repository search found no maintained caller supplying a Base this long. Wanderer’s copy application is an in-tree non-single-task caller (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:2508-2511`), while other MUI applications use the default FALSE setting. Since config paths are derived from `app_Base` (`application.c:352,817-819`), colliding instances can read, monitor and save the same per-application preferences; applications using ARexx may also request the same port name.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Zune applications using non-single-task mode when two tasks construct applications concurrently with the same requested Base and first available suffix, when all `.1` through `.999` suffixes for a Base are already in use, or when a Base of at least 253 bytes is reused after the first instance publishes its truncated name. **Consequence:** duplicate application identities and shared preference files/notifications; ARexx port naming may also collide when enabled. Reserve the name atomically with publication, check truncation, and reject or extend the suffix range when it is exhausted. **Confidence:** high for the unsynchronized check-to-publication window, deterministic long-base truncation, and unchecked exhaustion path; no maintained long-base caller was found. No application startup was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9928

**Zune can hide an application before creating its AppIcon and leave it inaccessible when icon creation fails.** `Application__OM_SET()` sets `app_Iconified` and hides the application family before looking up a user/default DiskObject (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1076-1084`). If the supplied icon and all fallback icons are unavailable, the method breaks with the windows still hidden and no AppIcon (`:1095-1127`). If `AddAppIconA()` fails, its NULL result is stored but the method likewise leaves the application marked iconified (`:1132-1135`). The callee documents NULL on failure and returns it when the icon, message port, or icon render object is missing, or when allocating its AppIcon node fails (`workbench/libs/workbench/addappicona.c:184-193,213-223`). Its documentation explicitly allows adding AppIcons when Workbench is not running, so Workbench absence alone is not the trigger. Repeating `MUIA_Application_Iconified=TRUE` then skips the body because the state already matches (`application.c:1078-1081`). The normal window iconify gadget and `MUIM_Window_ActionIconify()` both use this path (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:2493-2496,4393-4400`). Restore the windows or reset the iconified state when no icon can be installed.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** Zune applications using the standard iconify action without a supplied DiskObject, when all default icon lookups fail, when the selected DiskObject has no render image, or when AppIcon-node allocation fails. **Consequence:** the windows are hidden without an AppIcon to restore them; recovery then requires the application to uniconify itself or another external action. **Confidence:** high for the state ordering and documented NULL failure path; medium for practical impact because it requires icon lookup or AppIcon allocation failure. No iconification or Workbench operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9929

**MUI reports an unrecognized ARexx command as successful.** `Application__MUIM_NewInput()` scans `data->app_Commands` and only assigns `rmsg->rm_Result1` inside the matching-command branch (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1707-1762`). If no command name matches, it still replies the message without setting an error result (`:1768-1770`). `MUI_RXERR_UNKNOWNCOMMAND` is defined for the MUI ARexx interface but is not used in this dispatch path (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui.h:668-671`). The standard `CreateRexxMsg()` producer allocates the message with `MEMF_CLEAR`, so its result begins at zero (`workbench/libs/rexxsyslib/createrexxmsg.c:56-64`). **Trigger:** send a command whose first token is absent from a MUI application's configured command table through its enabled ARexx port. **Consequence:** the caller receives a success result for an unhandled command and cannot distinguish a typo or unsupported command from a successful command. Set `rm_Result1` to `MUI_RXERR_UNKNOWNCOMMAND` when the table scan finds no match. **Affected configuration:** applications that publish a MUI ARexx port and receive a command not present in their table. **Confidence:** high for the no-match reply path and the zero-initialized standard message; no ARexx message was sent. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9930

**SetOutlinePen returns a sign-extended old pen instead of its unsigned pen value.** The RastPort stores `AOlPen` as signed `BYTE` (`compiler/include/graphics/rastport.h:65`). `SetOutlinePen()` assigns that field directly to its `ULONG oldPen` before replacing it (`rom/graphics/setoutlinepen.c:52-59`), so when the previous valid pen is 128–255, the signed byte is promoted as a negative integer and then converted to `ULONG`. By contrast, `GetOutlinePen()` explicitly casts the same field to `UBYTE` (`rom/graphics/getoutlinepen.c:49`), and `SetOutlinePen()` documents its result as “Previous outline pen” (`setoutlinepen.c:31-32`). **Trigger:** call `SetOutlinePen()` after the RastPort's outline pen has been set to a value in the upper half of the byte range, then consume the returned old pen as a `ULONG`. **Consequence:** the method returns a sign-extended value (for example, a stored 200 returns the unsigned-long representation of -56) instead of 200; callers that compare or use the prior pen as an index receive the wrong value. Normalize the saved byte through `UBYTE` before returning it. **Affected configuration:** graphics.library clients using valid outline-pen values 128–255 on targets where `BYTE` is signed 8-bit; checked-in callers found in this source search ignore the setter's return, so maintained in-tree impact is not established. **Confidence:** high for the signed-byte-to-ULONG conversion and documented return mismatch; no pen operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9931

**A heavily shared palette pen can wrap its reference count to zero and be returned to the free list while clients still hold it.** `PalExtra_RefCnt_Type` is signed `WORD` (`rom/graphics/graphics_intern.h:71,74`). Shared acquisitions increment this field without a maximum check in both `ObtainPen()` (`rom/graphics/obtainpen.c:135-145,185-191,230-256`) and `ObtainBestPenA()` (`rom/graphics/obtainbestpena.c:92-106,119-154`); both operations serialize updates with the PaletteExtra semaphore. On the target's 16-bit `WORD` representation, 65,536 successful references to one shared pen wrap the stored count back to zero. `ReleasePen()` interprets a zero reference count as an exclusive pen (`rom/graphics/releasepen.c:57-61,74-85,147-155`), so the first subsequent release inserts that still-shared pen into the free list without removing it from the shared list or accounting for the other live users. Another acquisition can then reassign or recolor a pen still held by clients. **Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library clients sharing one ColorMap pen through 65,536 successful ObtainPen/ObtainBestPenA calls without corresponding releases, followed by a release; this can arise from many retained objects or repeated unbalanced acquisitions. The threshold is high and no checked-in single caller was found that establishes it. **Consequence:** a live shared pen can be misclassified and made available to another client, breaking palette ownership and potentially changing the color seen by existing users. Use a wider unsigned reference count or reject increments at a safe limit while preserving acquisition/release balance. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked WORD increment and zero-means-exclusive release path on supported two's-complement targets; the high reference count was not induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9932

**Indexed HIDD palette updates can change the software ColorMap while the display driver rejects the hardware update.** `internal_SetRGB32Colors()` calls `HIDD_BM_SetColors()` but ignores its Boolean result, then updates the HIDD bitmap's pixel translation table (`rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:14-53`). The generic bitmap method first expands/updates its software ColorMap through `HIDD_CM_SetColors()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:1319-1341`). The VESA, EFI framebuffer, SM502, Raspberry Pi framebuffer, VGA, VideoCore and VMware SVGA SetColors overrides reject ranges beyond the mode's `1 << bpp` capacity (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_bitmapclass.c:168-205`; `rom/hidds/efifbgfx/efifbgfx_bitmapclass.c:168-205`; `workbench/hidds/sm502gfx/sm502gfx_bitmapclass.c:194-231`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx_bitmapclass.c:168-205`; `arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_bitmapclass.c:180-206`; `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/vcgfx_bitmapclass.c:226-245`; `workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/vmwaresvga_bitmap_common.c:68-89`). Most call the generic SetColors first and then reject; LinuxFB rejects before the superclass call (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx_bitmapclass.c:45-57`). In either ordering, graphics.library ignores FALSE and commits the translation-table entry. The caller's `SetRGB32()`/`LoadRGB32()` path does not propagate that failure. A 4-bit screen provides a concrete mismatch: `OpenScreen()` creates a ColorMap with at least 32 entries even when the requested palette has fewer (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1393-1408`), while these drivers accept hardware indices only below 16. Updating entry 16 through 31 can therefore change the queried software ColorMap and translation table but leave the displayed hardware palette unchanged. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the listed indexed HIDD backends when using screens with `bpp < 8`, where a public color update uses a ColorMap-valid index beyond the mode's hardware palette capacity (for a 4-bit screen, entries 16-31). **Consequence:** callers observe a successful void API operation and updated ColorMap state although the displayed color register was not changed; subsequent software palette reads disagree with hardware. Propagate backend rejection before committing the ColorMap/translation-table update, or define and consistently enforce the viewport's hardware palette range. **Confidence:** high for the call ordering, ignored return, and driver capacity checks; no display or color update was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9933

**SDL HIDD color updates leak their temporary palette array and dereference it after allocation failure.** `SDLBitMap__Hidd_BitMap__SetColors()` allocates `msg->numColors` `SDL_Color` records with `AllocVec()` and immediately writes each entry without checking for NULL (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_bitmapclass.c:234-258`). On success it passes the array to `SDL_SetColors()` and returns without freeing it (`:260-264`); there is no other cleanup for the local allocation. The generic superclass color-map update has already succeeded before this allocation (`:249-250`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** explicitly built hosted SDL HIDD (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/mmakefile.src:3-20`) receiving an indexed bitmap color update. The SDL display wrapper automatically injects this bitmap class only for valid-mode bitmaps; enumerated SDL formats are truecolor. An indexed trigger therefore requires an offscreen object explicitly created with the SDL bitmap class and an indexed pixel format; no maintained in-tree caller creating that object was found. Each successful call leaks `sizeof(SDL_Color) * numColors`; if allocation fails, the conversion loop writes through NULL. Single-color `SetRGB32()` calls also allocate one record per update, so repeated updates accumulate the leak. **Consequence:** palette changes can exhaust memory over time, and allocation pressure can crash the process/kernel while converting the update. Check allocation failure and release the temporary array after SDL consumes it. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation, missing free, and immediate writes; external indexed-object reachability is conditional. No SDL display or allocation failure was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10114 — SDL HIDD reports success when SDL could not apply a palette update

`SDLBitMap__Hidd_BitMap__SetColors()` first commits the update through its superclass, then calls `SDL_SetColors()` but discards its integer result and returns `TRUE` unconditionally (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdlgfx_bitmapclass.c:249-264`). The HIDD `SetColors` contract requires FALSE when the update fails (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:1271-1293`). SDL 1.2 documents that `SDL_SetColors()` returns 0 when the surface is not palettized or when not all requested colors can be set as requested, and 1 only when all are set ([SDL 1.2.15 `SDL_SetColors`](https://www.libsdl.org/release/SDL-1.2.15/docs/html/sdlsetcolors.html)). Thus the software ColorMap can contain the requested values while the SDL surface palette is unchanged or only partly updated, yet callers of the HIDD method receive success.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly selected hosted SDL HIDD, with an indexed SDL bitmap whose `SDL_SetColors()` call returns 0. Like GD9933, an indexed SDL bitmap requires explicit offscreen construction using the SDL bitmap class and an indexed format; the automatic valid-mode class path uses enumerated truecolor formats, and no maintained in-tree indexed-object caller was found. **Consequence:** direct HIDD clients are told the update succeeded even though SDL did not fully apply it, and the superclass ColorMap has already been changed. Propagate the SDL result and define rollback or partial-update behavior. **Confidence:** high for the ignored result, HIDD return contract, and SDL 1.2 result contract; the indexed object and SDL rejection trigger are conditional. No display, palette operation, or SDL failure was exercised. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9934

**GetMonitorList returns monitor objects without keeping them alive after dropping the list lock.** `GetMonitorList()` copies raw `Object *` entries into its returned array while holding `MonitorListSem`, then releases the semaphore before returning (`rom/intuition/getmonitorlist.c:69-86`). The function documents that the caller owns only the array copy; `FreeMonitorList()` calls `FreeVec(list)` and does not retain or release any monitor object (`freemonitorlist.c:24-52`). The display-removal path can dispose a monitor after the snapshot lock is released: `graphics_display.c:241-243` calls Intuition's `DisplayDriverNotify(..., FALSE, ...)`, which calls `DisposeObject(obj)` (`rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:72-75`); `MonitorClass__OM_DISPOSE()` removes the node under `MonitorListSem` and then proceeds with object disposal (`:1080-1108`). Thus a caller that keeps or dereferences an entry while a display is removed can use an object that has already been disposed.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** clients of the public `GetMonitorList()` API on a system where a graphics display can be removed or its driver expunged while the caller is using the returned entries. The checked-in tree has a debug client that reads monitor attributes from each entry; no maintained concurrent caller was found. **Consequence:** the snapshot array can contain a stale BOOPSI object pointer during display removal. Provide a monitor-object lifetime pin/snapshot mechanism, or explicitly synchronize clients with display removal. **Confidence:** high for raw-pointer copying, lock release, and disposal ordering; the client-visible lifetime guarantee is not documented, so practical impact is conditional on callers treating returned objects as usable during concurrent removal. No display removal or monitor query was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9935

**NListtree GetEntry dereferences a missing active list.** `_NListtree_GetEntry()` maps `MUIV_NListtree_GetEntry_ListNode_Active` to `data->ActiveList`, then the Head and Tail cases immediately read `ln->ln_Flags` without checking whether `ln` is NULL (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:9092-9093,9105-9116`). `_New()` zero-initializes the instance data and does not initialize `ActiveList` before creating the superclass (`:5122-5163`); the active-state handler only assigns it on a non-initial active-state update (`:4437-4447`). Thus an early public GetEntry request using the Active list selector with Head or Tail can dereference NULL before any active-state update.
