A repository-wide direct `MUIM_NListtree_GetEntry` call search finds no in-tree caller using the Active selector. The separately explicitly buildable compatibility `Listtree.mcc` adapter maps its public Active sentinel to this same selector and forwards Head/Tail unchanged (`workbench/classes/zune/listtree/listtree.c:527-545`; `listtree.conf:22`; `mmakefile.src:8-18`); no checked-in call to that wrapper method was found, so an actual trigger still requires a client. The public method contract still requires NULL for an unavailable list. **Consequence:** the public query crashes instead of returning NULL for an unavailable active list. Check `ln` before reading its flags and return NULL when it is absent. **Confidence:** high for the nullable zero-initialized field and unchecked dereference; the caller must use this selector while no active list is available. No method call or GUI operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9936

**Radeon continues initialization after PCIPC fails to map its framebuffer or MMIO BAR.** The enumerator stores the framebuffer `MapPCI()` result in `sd->Card.FrameBuffer`, immediately casts it to `struct MemChunk *`, and stores the separate MMIO and VBIOS mapping results without checking them (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_init.c:129-160`). It then unconditionally calls the matched card's `sup->Init(sd)` (`:162`). `RADEONInit()` accesses MMIO registers through `sd->Card.MMIO` (the conditional R300 read is at `workbench/hidds/radeon/radeon_driver.c:2342`, the RS100/RS200/RS300 read at `:2358`, and the general-path read at `:2370`). If that returns successfully despite a failed framebuffer map, the enumerator also dereferences the framebuffer-derived `mc` to initialize its memory chunk (`ati_init.c:166-174`). The x86-64 PC PCIPC method returns NULL when `KrnMapGlobal()` fails to map a valid BAR above its 128-GiB identity window (`arch/all-pc/hidds/pcipc/pcipc_driverclass.c:225-258`; `arch/x86_64-pc/kernel/mapglobal.c:88-126,148-166`). No result is checked and no early rejection occurs. **Affected configuration and trigger:** an explicitly selected Radeon HIDD build on x86-64 PC with PCIPC, when the Radeon framebuffer or MMIO BAR lies outside the identity window and global mapping fails. Radeon is a buildable target, but the default Workbench and PC graphics aggregate edges are commented in this snapshot (`workbench/mmakefile.src:35-40`; `arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:9-14`), so it is not claimed as a default inclusion. **Consequence:** initialization can access chip registers through a null-derived address or dereference a null framebuffer chunk instead of rejecting the card, causing a fault or memory corruption. Validate all required mappings before chip initialization and unwind any successful mappings on failure. **Confidence:** high for unchecked results and the cited immediate consumers; occurrence requires the stated optional target and BAR mapping failure. No BAR mapping, build, allocation failure, or hardware operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9940

**OpenScreen reports success when its display rebuild fails.** `int_openscreen()` sets `msg->Success` from its initial `MakeVPort()` call, then calls `int_RethinkDisplay()` without copying or checking `rmsg.failure` (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:2476-2485`). The rebuild can fail independently: `int_RethinkDisplay()` calls `MakeVPort()` again for the newly linked screen and stores any error in `failure`; on failure it skips `MrgCop()` and `LoadView()` before publishing `msg->failure` (`rom/intuition/rethinkdisplay.c:138-158,212-217`). The m68k Amiga boot selects AmigaVideo (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:158,375`), whose `MakeViewPort()` can return `MVP_NO_MEM` when it cannot allocate the replacement copper list (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1214-1259`). Thus an initial successful viewport preparation followed by failure of the second copper-list allocation leaves the screen published in Intuition's screen chain, but the display rebuild is skipped; `int_openscreen()` still returns success and `OpenScreen()` returns the screen pointer.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** m68k Amiga builds selecting Intuition, graphics and AmigaVideo, when a screen's initial `MakeVPort()` succeeds but the subsequent `int_RethinkDisplay()` rebuild fails, for example because the second AmigaVideo copper-list allocation fails. **Consequence:** OpenScreen reports a usable/opened screen although the new viewport was not merged or loaded to the display; Intuition's active-screen state can disagree with the visible display until a later successful rethink. Propagate `rmsg.failure` into `msg->Success` and perform the appropriate screen rollback. **Confidence:** high for ignored failure status and the selected no-load path; occurrence requires the second rebuild failure. No screen, copper list or allocation failure was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9939

**OpenScreen underflows the sprite palette base for one- and two-plane screens.** `spritebase` is a `UWORD`, but the low-depth expression assigns `(1 << ns.Depth) - 8` when `ns.Depth < 5` (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:175,1585`). For depth one or two, the signed expression is -6 or -4 and converts to 65530 or 65532. OpenScreen then uses `k + spritebase` for the three pointer colors and routes these indices to `SetRGB32()` because each exceeds `numcolors` (`openscreen.c:1661-1683`). The screen bitmap remains at `ns.Depth` even though OpenScreen asks mode selection for a mode with minimum depth eight (`:896,1225-1238`); the DisplayID bitmap request selects the HIDD path (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:219-226,242-250`). `SetRGB32()` rejects the out-of-range index only in the ColorMap update, then continues to `internal_SetRGB32Colors()`, whose HIDD path writes to `HIDD_BM_PIXTAB[first+i]` without checking the table extent (`rom/graphics/setrgb32cm.c:61-76`; `rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:115-124,43-52`). The table has 256 entries (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:423-426`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h:109-110`), so opening such a screen writes well beyond it. **Affected configuration and trigger:** Intuition/graphics builds with a non-BINCOMPAT flavour (`standalone`, `native`, or `emulation`) that open a one- or two-plane screen on a display mode with `dimensions.MaxDepth <= 8`, producing a displayable HIDD bitmap at the requested depth. When the mode has depth greater than eight, OpenScreen instead allocates at that higher depth and this underflow path does not apply. **Consequence:** screen initialization can corrupt memory while assigning the pointer palette. Compute a representable base for the requested palette/depth and reject or skip unavailable pointer colors; the shared GD5910 bounds check remains necessary. **Confidence:** high for the UWORD conversion, selected `OpenScreen()` writes, HIDD dispatch, and fixed table extent. No screen was opened; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9938

**SetPointerColors decodes the low-depth sprite palette base to an oversized color index.** `OpenScreen()` chooses `spritebase = (1 << ns.Depth) - 8` below depth five, then packs the value into `SpriteBase_Even` as `((spritebase & 0x0F) << 8) | (spritebase >> 4)` (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1585,1588-1590`). At depth four, the value is 8 and the stored field becomes `0x0800`. `SetPointerColors()` attempts to decode that packed value using `(firstcol << 4) | (firstcol >> 8)` without masking the shifted high bits (`rom/intuition/misc.c:351-357`), producing `0x8008`, not 8. OpenScreen requests a displayable HIDD bitmap at `ns.Depth` for a mode whose maximum depth is at most eight (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1225-1238`); with `ns.Depth == 4`, this supplies the four-plane HIDD bitmap to the pointer update. It then calls `SetRGB32()` for entries `0x8009` through `0x800B`. The ColorMap setter correctly rejects these indices: OpenScreen creates a minimum 32-entry ColorMap for this low-depth screen (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1406`), still far below these indices, and `SetRGB32CM()` checks `n < cm->Count` (`rom/graphics/setrgb32cm.c:61-76`), but the public `SetRGB32()` continues to `internal_SetRGB32Colors()` (`rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:116-124`), which writes the pixel value to `HIDD_BM_PIXTAB(bitmap)[first+i]` without a bounds check (`:43-52`). The table is allocated as 256 entries (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:423-426`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h:109-110`), so this maintained pointer-color update writes far beyond its allocation. `MakePointerFromPrefs()` calls `SetPointerColors()`, and the selected IPrefs pointer-preference path calls `MakePointerFromPrefs()` (`rom/intuition/misc.c:267-271`; `rom/intuition/setiprefs.c:176-178`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** selected Intuition/graphics builds with a non-BINCOMPAT flavour (`standalone`, `native`, or `emulation`) when pointer preferences are loaded or updated while a four-plane HIDD-backed screen using a mode with `dimensions.MaxDepth <= 8` is active. The finding concerns Intuition's generated index; GD5910 separately covers the shared unchecked translation-table write for caller-supplied out-of-range indices. **Consequence:** an out-of-bounds pixel-table write can corrupt adjacent memory while updating pointer colors. Mask the decoded nibble fields or otherwise decode the packed base correctly, and retain the independent common range check from GD5910. **Confidence:** high for the arithmetic, selected call path, and fixed table extent; no pointer update or screen operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9937

**SetIPrefs offsets the Workbench's last four palette colors past the end of its palette.** In the `IPREFS_TYPE_PALETTE_V39`/`V37` handler, entries with `idx` 4 through 7 are sent to the open Workbench viewport at `lastcol + idx`, where `lastcol` is palette capacity minus four (`rom/intuition/setiprefs.c:262-269`). These entries represent the last four colors: `OpenScreen()` uses `lastcol + k` for preference color `p[k+4]`, with `k` from zero through three (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1638-1649`). The SetIPrefs path therefore needs the corresponding `lastcol + (idx - 4)` offset. The selected IPrefs `palette` handler reads a PALT chunk into 32 `ColorSpec` records and calls SetIPrefs (`workbench/c/iprefs/main.c:94-101`; `workbench/c/iprefs/paletteprefs.c:46-82`). The checked-in Palette preferences defaults define entries 0–7 and then a `ColorIndex == -1` terminator (`workbench/prefs/palette/prefs.c:41-49`), so ordinary saved palette data reaches entries 4–7. For an 8-bit Workbench screen, `lastcol` is 252 and those four calls use indices 256–259. `SetRGB32()` then reaches `internal_SetRGB32Colors()`'s unchecked HIDD pixel-table write at `first + i`, while displayable HIDD bitmaps allocate exactly 256 entries (`rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:14-53,116-124`; `rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:417-426`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h:109-110`; generic bounds issue GD5910).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** selected Intuition and IPrefs on a system with an open Workbench screen of depth 8 or greater, when a palette preference file supplies colors at indices 4–7; the checked-in Palette editor defaults supply those indices. **Consequence:** these colors are not applied to the intended last four display registers, and on an 8-bit-or-higher displayable HIDD bitmap the update writes four entries past the allocated 256-entry pixel translation table. Correct the index offset and keep a range check at the shared translation-table write (GD5910). **Confidence:** high for the offset mismatch and table extent; the exact adjacent state affected by the out-of-bounds writes depends on allocation layout. No palette file, display, or runtime operation was used; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9941

**CloseScreen frees a bitmap still linked into AmigaVideo's compositor after a display rebuild failure.** `int_closescreen()` first removes the screen from `FirstScreen` and updates `ActiveScreen` (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:360-407`). The outer `CloseScreen()` then calls `RethinkDisplay()` but ignores its return value and immediately calls `FreeVPortCopLists()` (`:188-191`). `RethinkDisplay()` rebuilds every surviving visible viewport; if any `MakeVPort()` fails, it skips both `MrgCop()` and `LoadView()` (`rom/intuition/rethinkdisplay.c:138-158,212-217`). A successful `RethinkDisplay()` reaches `MrgCop()` and then `LoadView()` (`rethinkdisplay.c:151-158`); `MrgCop()` prepares the viewports and calls `display_LoadViewPorts()` for the active view (`rom/graphics/mrgcop.c:113-120`), and `display_LoadViewPorts()` dispatches `HIDD_Display_ShowViewPorts()` (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:511-525`). AmigaVideo's `ShowViewPorts()` calls compositor `BitMapStackChanged()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1494-1523`); that method removes prior bitmap nodes from its visible and obscured lists before rebuilding them (`amigavideo_compositorclass.c:130-164,196-266`). If a surviving viewport fails `MakeVPort()`, `RethinkDisplay()` skips `MrgCop()` and `LoadView()`, so this stack refresh is skipped. The closing screen must have been present in the previously published compositor stack for its bitmap node to remain there. `FreeVPortCopLists()` then invokes driver `DeinitViewPort()` and disposes the wrapped HIDD bitmap (`rom/graphics/freevportcoplists.c:57-78`); AmigaVideo's deinitializer frees viewport copper/user data but does not unlink its bitmap node (`amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1319-1344`). The node is embedded in the bitmap's `amigabm_data`, which the compositor inserted into its list (`amigavideo_compositorclass.c:196-220,260-266`). The AmigaVideo VBlank handler continues walking `csd->compositedbms` and dereferencing bitmap state (`amigavideo_chipset.c:1806-1813`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** m68k Amiga with selected AmigaVideo, a screen being closed while at least one other visible viewport remains, and a surviving viewport's `MakeVPort()` failing during `RethinkDisplay()` (for example, AmigaVideo cannot allocate a replacement CopList). **Consequence:** CloseScreen proceeds to dispose the removed screen's wrapped bitmap while its intrusive node remains in the compositor list; a subsequent VBlank or compositor traversal can follow the freed node/data. CloseScreen should preserve the bitmap until a successful compositor publication or detach it from the compositor before disposal, and should handle the rebuild error. **Confidence:** high for the ordering, embedded node ownership, skipped refresh, disposal, and subsequent list traversal; manifestation requires the stated allocation failure and later display traversal. No screen close, allocation failure or VBlank was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9942

**CloseScreen can tear down a private screen after a concurrent OpenWindow passed the empty-window check.** `CloseScreen()` checks `screen->FirstWindow` and returns FALSE before acquiring `WindowLock` (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:105-112,116-125`). A concurrent `OpenWindow()` can then acquire that same lock, complete `int_openwindow()`, and publish its window into `screen->FirstWindow` (`rom/intuition/openwindow.c:1048-1085,1618-1622`). After it releases the lock, `CloseScreen()` proceeds; its locked validation only confirms that the screen remains in `FirstScreen`, and it never rechecks `FirstWindow` (`closescreen.c:123-163`). `int_closescreen()` rechecks both visitor count and `FirstWindow` only when `pubScrNode` is non-NULL; private custom screens skip that guard and are unlinked (`:331-372`). CloseScreen then releases `WindowLock` before tearing down the layer info, bitmap, ColorMap and screen object (`:220-253,273-300`), leaving the published window linked to the screen as its storage is dismantled; subsequent window operations may also use that freed screen state. On AROS, OpenScreen defaults `dowindowlock` to TRUE and marks ordinary-task screens as locked (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:146,2223-2231`); `OpenWindow()` takes the global window lock for ordinary tasks (`openwindow.c:1048-1085`). `WA_CustomScreen` selects the caller-supplied custom screen without taking a public-screen visitor reference (`openwindow.c:341-344,604-625`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** AROS Intuition, when another task opens a window on a private custom screen after CloseScreen's initial empty-window check but before its locked teardown; public screens that successfully acquire a visitor reference take the separate refusal path. **Consequence:** CloseScreen can return success and free the screen while the newly published window remains linked to it, leaving the window's `WScreen`, layers and bitmap references stale and bypassing CloseScreen's documented refusal for screens with windows. Recheck `FirstWindow` while holding `WindowLock` immediately before unlinking, and keep teardown serialized until the screen is no longer usable. **Confidence:** high for the check/lock/publication ordering and private-screen path; the task interleaving was not run. No window or screen was opened or closed; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9943

**SysExplorer's processor page formats strings through unchecked allocation results.** `ParseProcessorInformation()` allocates display strings with `AllocVec()` and immediately writes through the returned pointers: the architecture label and architecture/endianness text (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/computer_page_cl.c:189-203`), each CPU label and model string (`:230-244`), the optional speed string (`:253-266`), and the per-core feature buffer passed to its formatter (`:276-287`). A failed allocation therefore reaches `sprintf()`/`snprintf()` with NULL, or passes NULL into the architecture formatter which writes to its output buffer. The page is constructed when `ComputerWindow__OM_NEW()` finds `processor.resource` and later calls `ParseProcessorInformation()` (`:364-367,475-479`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected `workbench-tools-sysexplorer` target (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/mmakefile.src:6-14`) when a Computer/System Properties window is created with `processor.resource` available and any of these string-buffer allocations fails. **Consequence:** SysExplorer can fault while building the processor page rather than omit the unavailable field or abort page construction cleanly. Check each allocation before formatting or passing the buffer to a formatter, and unwind any objects already created on failure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation results and immediate write/call sites; no allocation failure or application run was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9944

**Radeon uses an unallocated VRAM offset for the hardware cursor after cursor-buffer allocation fails.** `ATI_Init()` stores the result of `AllocBitmapArea(sd, 64, 64, 4, TRUE)` in `sd->Card.CursorStart` without checking it, then writes that value to `RADEON_CUR_OFFSET` (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_init.c:176-182`). `BitmapAlloc()` returns `0xffffffff` when no contiguous range can be reserved (`workbench/hidds/radeon/bitmap.c:460-488`). The Radeon `SetCursorShape` method later adds `CursorStart` to the framebuffer mapping and writes 4096 ULONGs through the resulting pointer before submitting the shape (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_class.c:359-411`). The method is registered in the selected Radeon HIDD configuration (`radeon.conf:40`) and Intuition forwards pointer-shape changes to the active display (`rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:1954-1955`).

**Trigger and impact:** On the optional Sam440 or CHRP/Efika Radeon HIDD, the 64×64 cursor-buffer reservation fails and a client then sets a non-NULL pointer shape. The `0xffffffff` offset is programmed as cursor storage, and on the supported 32-bit targets its addition to the framebuffer base wraps to a pointer immediately before that base; the 4096-word clear and image copy then write through an invalid framebuffer address, which can fault or affect memory outside the mapped aperture. Check the reservation before publishing the display or reject cursor updates when it failed. **Confidence:** high for unchecked sentinel propagation and the write path; conditional on VRAM reservation failure followed by a cursor update. The default Workbench/PC aggregate does not select this optional Radeon HIDD. No allocation failure, pointer update, build or hardware was exercised; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**Radeon does not check its CPU conversion-buffer allocation before using it as a pixel destination.** After the family-specific hardware initialization succeeds, `ATI_Init()` allocates 16 KiB for `sd->cpuscratch` but does not check the `AllocPooled()` result (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_init.c:164-178`). In `ATIOnBM::PutImage`, the fallback conversion paths for 32-bit and 16-bit framebuffer bitmaps pass this pointer as the destination to `HIDD_BM_ConvertPixels()` (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_bitmap.c:1803-1811,1863-1871`). The selected generic converter writes converted pixels through its destination pointer in `true_to_true()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapconvertpixels.c:160-231`).

**Trigger and impact:** The optional Sam440 or CHRP/Efika Radeon HIDD initializes successfully but the 16-KiB pool allocation fails; a client then calls `PutImage()` on a 16- or 32-bit framebuffer bitmap using a source pixel format that takes the conversion fallback. The converter writes through NULL and the image operation faults. Check the allocation during startup and fail initialization cleanly or reject the conversion path if no scratch buffer is available. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation and downstream write; conditional on pool allocation failure and a non-native conversion request. The default Workbench/PC aggregate does not select this optional Radeon HIDD. No allocation failure, image operation, build or hardware was exercised; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9946

**Find can add search results after the user stops the scan.** The Find worker queues each matching result as `MUIM_FindGroup_AddEntry`, passing `self` as the destination, but stores each returned queue-node ID in the single variable `methodid2` (`workbench/system/find/findgroup_class.c:727-734`). At worker exit it calls `MUIM_Application_UnpushMethod` only for `methodid1` (the initial list clear) and the last value of `methodid2` (`:755-757`). `UnpushMethod()` removes only nodes matching that exact queue-node ID; the application later dispatches all remaining queued methods (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1940-1962,278-290`). The Stop button calls `MUIM_Process_Kill`, which sets the worker's kill flag and waits for it to terminate before returning (`findgroup_class.c:781-785`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/process.c:152-185`). Because that wait blocks the application task, any earlier result methods still queued when the scan stops remain pending when Stop returns. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the standalone Find utility target (`workbench/system/find/mmakefile.src`), when at least two matching result methods are pending as the user stops the scan. **Consequence:** all but the last pending result are still inserted into the results list after Stop, so the displayed result set changes after the user has stopped the search. Cancel every pending result method for the scan, or have the result method reject entries from a stopped scan. **Confidence:** high for the queue-ID overwrite, exact-ID removal, and synchronous worker join; no Find process or queued result was run. The parent `workbench-system` aggregation edge is commented in this snapshot, so this is scoped to builds that explicitly select the standalone target. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9948

**FTManager leaks font entries queued after the application's final event-loop drain.** `MUIM_Application_NewInput()` drains the pushed-method queue before returning a ReturnID (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1839-1852`). FTManager exits that loop on Quit and immediately disposes the application (`workbench/system/ftmanager/ftmanager.c:281-282,360-368`). Application disposal later disposes its child windows, but its `OM_DISPOSE` implementation contains no pushed-method-queue drain; it frees the ReturnID queue separately (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:781-982`). Meanwhile, FTManager's FontList scan task can still be running: shutdown of the FontList sends it a break signal and waits for it to finish (`workbench/system/ftmanager/fontlist_class.c:169-190`), and the worker queues each discovered font entry to the application (`:286-297`). If a worker enqueues after NewInput's final drain and before/during FontList disposal, no event loop remains to call `flAddEntry()`, which is where the queued `MUIS_FontList_Entry` is freed (`:371-375`). The abandoned queue node is separately allocated with `mui_alloc()`/`AllocVec()` and is normally released only by dispatch or Unpush (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:222-242,278-290,1940-1963`; `support.h:39-41`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** explicitly built FTManager with a font-directory scan still running as the user quits, and at least one scan result is pushed after the final NewInput drain. FTManager's parent aggregation edge is commented in this snapshot. **Consequence:** each such pending result leaks its entry buffer, and its queued method node remains allocated after application teardown. Stop/join producers before the final drain or drain and release queued method payloads as part of shutdown. **Confidence:** high for the asynchronous producer, queue ownership/free sites, and missing destructor drain; the exact shutdown interleaving was not run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9949

**`OpenMonitor()` can pin or return a `MonitorSpec` after Sync/display teardown frees it.** `OpenMonitor()` returns a `MonitorSpec` and increments `ms_OpenCount` (`rom/graphics/openmonitor.c:64-85`). For a named, non-default monitor, it finds the spec while holding `MonitorListSemaphore` but releases that semaphore at `:66-71` before incrementing the count at `:83-84`. The display-ID path is also unpinned: `OpenMonitor()` calls `GetDisplayInfoData()` and receives the internal `MonitorSpec *` in `MonitorInfo.Mspc` before incrementing its count (`openmonitor.c:74-79,83-84`; `getdisplayinfodata.c:146-169,350-366`). `GetDisplayInfoData()`/`FindDisplayInfo()` do not take `displaydb_sem`, which `AddDisplayDriverA()` holds while removing the display (`adddisplaydrivera.c:236-238,294`; `finddisplayinfo.c:65-80`). Thus teardown can race both the ID lookup and the later pin. For the generic graphics Sync class, when a driver does not provide a prebuilt spec, the class allocates the `MonitorSpec` itself and records `SYNC_FREE_MONITORSPEC` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_syncclass.c:132-149`). Disposing that Sync removes the spec while holding `MonitorListSemaphore`, releases the lock, and frees the spec without checking `ms_OpenCount` (`gfx_syncclass.c:295-315`). Thus a concurrent named lookup can be followed by Sync disposal/free before `OpenMonitor()` increments the count, making the increment itself access freed storage. Independently, an already returned default/display-ID reference can be retained across handover and outlive the spec. The generic Display destructor disposes its mode enumerator (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:463-471`), whose destructor disposes each Sync object (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:332-341`).

During display-driver handover, `driver_ExpungeBootDisplay()` refuses removal only if `mdd->display` or `mdd->frontbm` is non-NULL (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:262-282`); it does not check any open MonitorSpec count. `display_Expunge()` then disposes the display object (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:245-252`), following the chain above. A client holding a valid `OpenMonitor()` result across handover is therefore left with a pointer to freed storage; a later `CloseMonitor()` obtains `DisplayInfoDataBaseSemaphore` through that pointer (`rom/graphics/closemonitor.c:54-64`). The API provides no handover notification for these individual MonitorSpec references and the removal check ignores the count. The named-lookup interleaving also has no caller-side synchronization requirement in the public `OpenMonitor()` contract.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** generic graphics Sync/Display classes when (1) a named-spec lookup overlaps Sync disposal, (2) an ID-based `OpenMonitor()` lookup overlaps display removal, or (3) a client retains an open default/display-ID MonitorSpec for an otherwise unused boot display while native HIDD driver handover proceeds before `CloseMonitor()`. **Consequence:** subsequent MonitorSpec reads or `CloseMonitor()` can access the freed spec and its semaphore. Include open monitor references in the expunge refusal/lifetime protocol, or retain the spec until its open count reaches zero. **Confidence:** high for allocation, lookup/pin ordering, missing reader synchronization, ignored open count and disposal chain; occurrence requires external use of the public API concurrent with Sync/display teardown or across handover. No driver handover, monitor query or close was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9951

**Graphics.library `ChangeSprite()` changes the stored image pointer but never updates the displayed sprite shape.** The selected implementation assigns `newdata` to `s->posctldata`, saves the existing coordinates and calls `MoveSprite()` (`rom/graphics/changesprite.c:49-56`). The generic `MoveSprite()` path sends only the cursor coordinates to `HIDD_Display_SetCursorPos()` and returns without handling nonzero sprite numbers (`rom/graphics/movesprite.c:68-81`). The m68k graphics override similarly calls `HIDD_AMIGAGFX_SetSpritePos()` for nonzero sprites and does not consume `posctldata` (`arch/m68k-amiga/graphics/movesprite.c:76-94`). The shape-changing extended-sprite path does make a separate `HIDD_AMIGAGFX_SetSpriteShape()` call (`arch/m68k-amiga/graphics/changeextspritea.c:82-95`), but `ChangeSprite()` never does. Thus changing an allocated simple sprite's data pointer and calling this API cannot publish the new image to the display backend; it only requests a move at the existing location. Forward the new image through the backend's shape update path, or return an explicit unsupported result if simple-sprite image replacement is not implemented.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** an external client calls the selected graphics.library `ChangeSprite()` vector to replace an allocated nonzero simple sprite on the m68k-amiga target, whose architecture-specific `MoveSprite()` is selected by `arch/m68k-amiga/graphics/mmakefile.src:4` and supports nonzero sprite positions. The extended-sprite path in the same target demonstrates the backend shape-update operation. No checked-in C caller of `ChangeSprite()` was found; generic non-m68k `MoveSprite()` explicitly ignores nonzero sprite numbers, so this finding is limited to the m68k path with sprite-capable hardware. **Consequence:** the display continues showing the previous sprite shape (or no shape) after the request, despite the caller's data pointer changing. **Confidence:** high that the selected m68k `ChangeSprite()` path never submits the new shape; medium for external API impact because no maintained in-tree caller or local function-level semantic documentation was found. No sprite or display was used. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9952

**`TextLength()` and `TextExtent()` dereference optional font metric tables without checking each pointer.** Both routines enter their per-character metric path when `FPF_PROPORTIONAL` is set or either `tf_CharKern` or `tf_CharSpace` is non-NULL, but then unconditionally index both tables (`rom/graphics/textlength.c:57-75`; `rom/graphics/textextent.c:72,80-117`). The diskfont loader allocates and sets `tf_CharSpace` and `tf_CharKern` independently only when their respective chunks exist (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfont_io.c:346-383`), so a font with only one table leaves the other pointer NULL. For any positive character count, the first routine then dereferences that missing table; `TextExtent()` calls `TextLength()` before repeating the same unsafe accesses. Graphics text rendering already treats the tables independently, using zero kerning when `tf_CharKern` is absent and `tf_XSize` when `tf_CharSpace` is absent (`rom/graphics/text.c:253-255,324-328`); `FontExtent()` likewise checks each pointer (`rom/graphics/fontextent.c:77-93`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** selected graphics.library builds that include TextLength/TextExtent (`rom/graphics/mmakefile.src`), when a client measures one or more characters using a `TextFont` with exactly one of the two optional metric tables present. Diskfont fonts can represent the tables independently. **Consequence:** the measurement call reads through a NULL table pointer and can fault instead of returning text metrics. Apply the same per-table fallback as the rendering and FontExtent paths. **Confidence:** high for the conditional table allocation and unconditional accesses; no font or measurement call was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9953

**The graphics copper-list debug test continues after `UCopperListInit()` fails to allocate its instruction buffer.** The test allocates the `UCopList` header and checks that allocation, but ignores the return from `UCopperListInit()` before issuing `CWait()` (`developer/debug/test/graphics/copper.c:85-95`). When the list-header allocation inside `UCopperListInit()` succeeds but its `CopIns` allocation fails, the initializer returns NULL while leaving `ucl->CopList` pointing at the partial header with `CopPtr == NULL` (`rom/graphics/ucopperlistinit.c:68-83`). `CWait()` immediately dereferences `ucl->CopList->CopPtr` and writes the instruction (`rom/graphics/cwait.c:57-60`). The rest of the test similarly proceeds to emit and attach the list.

Check the initializer result and free the partial `CopList`/header before abandoning setup; the library initializer should also leave a safely recoverable state on failure. **Confidence:** high for the allocation sequence, ignored return, and NULL dereference; no allocation failure or test program was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9954

**NList `MUIM_NList_ReplaceSingle` deletes the existing row when replacement construction fails.** `NL_List_Replace()` first asks the configured construct method to duplicate the replacement, and if it returns `NULL`, calls `NL_List_Remove(data, ent)` on the existing row while returning the removal result (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func2.c:961-1008`). The method is dispatched directly to this function (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc0.c:658-661`). The built-in string construct hook can return `NULL` when its `AllocVecPooled()` call fails (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_mcc.c:129-147`), and user construct hooks can likewise reject or fail to allocate. Thus a failed replacement request can mutate the list by removing the old value and still return success: `NL_List_Remove()` returns `TRUE` after a successful deletion (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func2.c:1095-1108,1271-1273`). Construct the new entry before changing the list and leave the existing row intact when construction fails. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable Zune `classes-zune-nlist-class` target when `MUIM_NList_ReplaceSingle` is called with a non-NULL replacement and its construct hook returns NULL, including built-in string-hook allocation failure. No maintained direct caller was found that demonstrates this failure trigger; the method is part of the public NList API. **Confidence:** high for the allocation-failure path, deletion and success return; medium that preserving the old row is the intended failure contract because the method documentation does not explicitly specify construct-failure behavior. No hook or allocation failure was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9955

**Shared palette pen references can wrap to zero and return a still-held pen to the free list.** `PalExtra_RefCnt_Type` is signed 16-bit `WORD` (`rom/graphics/graphics_intern.h:71-75`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:58-62`). `ObtainPen()` sets a new shared pen's reference count to 1 and increments it for every subsequent same-color shared acquisition (`rom/graphics/obtainpen.c:135-145,185-191,230-256`); `ObtainBestPenA()` also increments an existing shared pen's count (`rom/graphics/obtainbestpena.c:140-153`). Neither path bounds the counter. In GNU-toolchain builds, GCC converts out-of-range integers to signed N-bit types by reducing modulo 2^N ([GCC integer implementation](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Integers-implementation.html)); after 65,536 outstanding acquisitions of the same shared pen, the 16-bit count therefore becomes zero. A `ReleasePen()` at that point interprets zero as an exclusive pen and inserts it into the free list without removing it from the shared list (`rom/graphics/releasepen.c:80-85,147-154`). If another same-color `ObtainPen()` happens first, its any-pen search can find the entry in the shared list and increment the zero count to one (`obtainpen.c:230-239`); a later release then reaches zero and moves the pen to the free list while the original references remain outstanding. Use a wider count or reject/saturate increments before the representable limit. **Affected configuration and trigger:** graphics.library builds using the GNU toolchain, when a client successfully acquires the same shared pen 65,536 times without releasing it, then releases a reference (with or without an intervening same-color acquisition). Repeated `ObtainPen()` calls with the same color and `n=-1` are sufficient. No checked-in caller reaching this count was identified. **Consequence:** the pen can be reallocated or recolored while prior clients still hold it; direct release at zero also leaves it in both free and shared lists. **Confidence:** high for the counter width, GNU narrowing behavior, wrap, and both zero-count release paths; the trigger requires the stated high reference count. No palette operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9956

**Optional Nouveau bitmap `PutPixel()`/`GetPixel()` can race with accelerated operations on an already-mapped bitmap.** Both methods read `bo->map` and take `bmdata->semaphore` only when that pointer is NULL; when it is non-NULL they skip the bitmap lock. Neither method takes the driver's `globalLock`. The BO map is retained by `nouveau_bo_map()` until the mapping is invalidated (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_bitmapclass.c:244-256,288-300`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/libdrm/nouveau/nouveau.c:756-773`). In contrast, accelerated drawing takes `globalLock` and the bitmap semaphore before submitting work, then sets the shared `gpu_dirty` flag in its EXA helper (`nouveau_bitmapclass.c:382-423`; `nouveau_hiddclass.c:783-839`; `xf86-video-nouveau/nv04_exa.c:464-475`, `nv50_exa.c:1053-1064`, `nvc0_exa.c:1289-1305`). Pixel access tests and clears `gpu_dirty` without either lock and waits only if it observes TRUE. If a pixel method overlaps an accelerated operation on the same already-mapped bitmap, it can pass the dirty test before the GPU operation is marked pending and read/write the mapped storage while GPU work is queued or executing. The explicit “optimistics synchronization” FIXME on both paths is consistent with this gap. Serialize pixel access with the same engine/bitmap locks and perform the dirty wait within that synchronization, or otherwise establish an equivalent ordering protocol.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** an explicitly enabled Nouveau HIDD build using the compatible Mesa target (the package edge is commented out by default in `workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-21`), when separate tasks invoke `PutPixel()`/`GetPixel()` and an accelerated drawing method on the same bitmap concurrently after it has been mapped. **Consequence:** pixel reads may observe incomplete drawing, and pixel writes may race with or be overwritten by GPU drawing. **Confidence:** high for the missing serialization and conditional dirty check; medium for user-visible occurrence because it requires concurrent access to one bitmap and no in-tree workload reproducing that interleaving was established. No GPU operation or build was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9957

**Optional Nouveau bitmap operations ignore failure to map the buffer before dereferencing it.** The shared `MAP_BUFFER` macro calls `nouveau_bo_map()` when `bo->map` is NULL but discards its error result (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_intern.h:300`). `nouveau_bo_map()` returns `-EINVAL` if `drmMMap()` fails to supply a mapping (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/libdrm/nouveau/nouveau.c:763-773`), and the AROS `drmMMap()` wrapper returns NULL when the file/handle lookup fails or the kernel mapping has no virtual address (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/libdrm/arosdrm.c:286-291`; `drm-aros/nouveau/nouveau_aros_drm.c:43-65`). Callers then continue as if mapping succeeded: `PutPixel()`/`GetPixel()` form and access an address from `bo->map` (`nouveau_bitmapclass.c:249-274,293-315`); `PutImage()`/`GetImage()` compute a buffer pointer and pass it to the conversion routine (`:474-483,539-548`); and `ObtainDirectAccess()` stores the possibly NULL pointer in `addressReturn` but returns TRUE (`:764-778`). The software fallback methods also dereference the mapping after this macro. Propagate mapping failure and release any held locks before returning an error; `ObtainDirectAccess()` must not report success without a usable address.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** explicitly enabled Nouveau HIDD builds, when a bitmap operation requiring CPU mapping runs and `drmMMap()` fails (for example, an invalidated/closed GEM handle or kernel mapping failure). **Consequence:** drawing/readback can access an invalid address and fault or corrupt state; direct-access clients are told mapping succeeded while receiving NULL. **Confidence:** high for the ignored error and subsequent dereferences/TRUE result; the trigger depends on the mapping failure described above. No mapping failure or GPU operation was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9958

**Edit's preference requester truncates long paths without a terminator.** `Path` is a 100-byte global buffer (`workbench/tools/Edit/Prefs.c:40`). Both `ask_save()` and `ask_load()` return the dynamically allocated result of `get_full_path()` (`workbench/tools/Edit/DiskIO.c:175-182,326-332`); that helper allocates a variable-size buffer and grows it until `NameFromLock()` or `GetCurrentDirName()` succeeds, then appends the filename (`:83-100`). `ask_prefs()` copies exactly `sizeof(Path)` bytes from that full path with `CopyMemQuick()` and does not append a NUL (`Prefs.c:391-405`). If the selected full path is 100 bytes or longer, `Path` is left unterminated. The same call immediately passes it to `load_prefs()` or `save_prefs()`; `open_prefs()` passes it to DOS `Open()` as a C path (`Prefs.c:140-171,272`). The path operation can therefore read beyond the `Path` array and use bytes from adjacent global storage as part of the filename. Bound the copy to `sizeof(Path)-1` and terminate it, with a clear error or truncation policy for paths that do not fit.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable Edit/editor target (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:6-15`; its parent inclusion is commented out at `:12`) when the user selects a preference-file path whose normalized full path is at least 100 bytes. **Consequence:** the immediate preference-file open can use a path assembled from bytes beyond the buffer, failing or addressing an unintended name; the unterminated string read also crosses the array boundary. **Confidence:** high for the fixed-size nonterminated copy and immediate C-string use; the selected target accepts long paths through `get_full_path()`'s expanding buffer, though no requester or file was used. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9959

**Edit's preference loader trusts record lengths and can write beyond its destination fields.** After allocating and reading the declared `PREF/JANO` chunk, `load_prefs()` loops while `ByteRead < cn->cn_Size`, reads a two-byte record header, indexes the field table for valid IDs, and copies the record's unvalidated one-byte length directly into that field (`workbench/tools/Edit/Prefs.c:191-227`). It never checks that the header and payload fit in the chunk or that the length fits the field's actual destination. For example, the string fields point into fixed buffers (`WordsSep[40]`, `FontName[60]`, and `FontName+30`), while other IDs target fields inside `PREFS`; the writer's expected lengths are held in `sizefields[]` but the reader does not enforce them (`:43,67-71`; `Prefs.h:54-57`). A malformed preference record can therefore read past the allocated chunk and/or overwrite adjacent preference/global storage. Validate the remaining chunk bytes and enforce each field's exact or maximum size before copying; reject invalid records.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable Edit target (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:6-15`) when startup auto-loads a malformed local/`ENVARC:` preference file or the user selects one; startup calls `load_prefs(&prefs, NULL)` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Jed.c:93`). **Consequence:** malformed preference data can corrupt editor state or adjacent memory and make preference loading fail unpredictably. **Confidence:** high for the missing bounds checks and fixed-size destinations; malformed files are required. No preference file was loaded or modified. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9960

**Edit's preference parser can loop indefinitely on a JANO chunk larger than its 16-bit cursor.** `load_prefs()` stores the chunk offset in `UWORD ByteRead` but compares it with the wider signed `LONG cn->cn_Size` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Prefs.c:204-217`; `compiler/include/libraries/iffparse.h:65`). For a chunk larger than 65,535 bytes, `ByteRead` cannot reach `cn->cn_Size`; additions wrap the cursor back to the beginning while the loop condition remains true. Parsing then repeats old records indefinitely without reaching the end of the declared chunk; for a 65,536-byte chunk, a wrapped record header can also read its second byte one past the allocation. Widen the cursor and check each two-byte header and payload against the remaining chunk length, with a bounded parse failure.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable Edit target when startup or a user-selected file supplies a `PREF/JANO` chunk larger than the `UWORD` range. **Consequence:** preference loading does not finish and can revisit old records indefinitely; at the exact 65,536-byte boundary a header read can also cross the allocated buffer end. **Confidence:** high for the width mismatch and loop condition; the oversized chunk is the required input. No preference file or parser was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9961

**Edit's file requester copies a long directory path beyond its shared buffer.** `split_path()` computes the directory prefix length from the adjacent `AskArgs.dir` and `.file` pointers. When a requester supplies a directory prefix of at least 256 bytes, it clamps that length to 255 for the directory copy, then sets the filename destination to `BufTxt + Len + 1`, which is one past the 256-byte `BufTxt` array. It copies the filename and terminator there (`workbench/tools/Edit/DiskIO.c:111-130`; `BufTxt[256]` is defined in `Jed.c:32`). Both save and load requesters call this helper with non-NULL directory and filename outputs (`DiskIO.c:159-160,306-307`). `get_full_path()` grows its allocation as needed rather than imposing a 256-byte total path limit (`:48-103`), and project names can retain that allocated path (`Project.c:244-251`). Keep the directory and filename in independently sized storage or reject paths that cannot fit before copying.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable Edit target (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:6-15`; aggregate inclusion is commented out at `:12`), when a project path with a directory prefix of 256 bytes or more is passed to either requester. **Consequence:** filename bytes are written beyond `BufTxt`, corrupting adjacent global state. **Confidence:** high for the clamp/one-past destination and callers; occurrence requires a sufficiently long directory path. No requester or long path was used. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9962

**Edit reports a failed save as successful and clears the modified state.** On a buffered write failure, `save_file()` displays the DOS error and breaks out of the line-writing loop, then unconditionally calls `FClose()`, sets protection, and sets `retval = 1` (`workbench/tools/Edit/DiskIO.c:274-299`). `ThrowDOSError()` only formats and displays `IoErr()` and returns (`Utility.c:239-250`), so the error branch does not abort the function. `myFClose()` can itself report a failed final buffer flush, but the return value is also ignored (`DiskIO.c:216-229,294`). `save_project()` interprets any nonzero return as success and clears the modified mark (`Project.c:285-291`). Return failure after any failed write/flush, and only clear the project state after the complete file has been written and closed successfully.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable Edit target when saving encounters a short/failed `Write()` (for example, a full or failing destination volume). **Consequence:** the output file may be truncated or incomplete while the editor reports success and discards its modified-state indication, risking loss of the unsaved edits. **Confidence:** high for the returning error display, unconditional success assignment, ignored close status, and caller behavior; a DOS write failure is required. No file was saved and no failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD9963

**Edit crashes when it cannot allocate a line node while loading a file.** `load_file()` reads the file into `args->buffer`, allocates an initial line node, then allocates a new node for each newline encountered (`workbench/tools/Edit/DiskIO.c:384-434`). If a later `new_line(new)` allocation fails, the code sets `new` to NULL and `err = ERR_NOMEM`, breaks the loop, and then unconditionally writes `new->size` and `new->stream` at lines 431-432. Thus an allocation failure after at least one newline dereferences NULL instead of returning the error. If the initial `new_line(NULL)` allocation fails, the function sets `ERR_NOMEM` but does not free the already allocated file buffer; `load_in_project()` also does not release `args.buffer` on the error path (`Project.c:82-98`). Handle the failed node allocation before the final-node initialization and release the read buffer on every failed load.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the Edit target selected by the active AROS Workbench tools aggregate (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:6-16`) when a file has at least one line break and a subsequent line-node allocation fails, or when the first line-node allocation fails. **Consequence:** the later allocation failure crashes the editor during load; the initial allocation failure leaks the file buffer. **Confidence:** high for both allocation-failure paths and the missing cleanup; memory exhaustion is required. No allocation failure or file load was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9964

**The shared Radeon BIOS fallback copies into a NULL buffer when its pool allocation fails.** When the initially mapped VBIOS does not begin with the expected `55 aa` signature, `RADEONGetBIOSInfo()` replaces `sd->Card.VBIOS` with the result of `AllocPooled(sd->memPool, 65536)` and immediately calls `CopyMemQuick(0x000c0000, sd->Card.VBIOS, 65536)` without checking the allocation (`workbench/hidds/radeon/radeon_bios.c:58-65`). If the pool allocation fails, the nonzero-size quick copy receives a NULL destination; its selected generic implementation writes through that destination. The function is called from `RADEONInit()` (`workbench/hidds/radeon/radeon_driver.c:2422`), which does not check its return before continuing initialization. **Affected configuration and trigger:** an explicitly built `hidd-radeon` target that selects the shared `radeon_bios.c` body (no same-name architecture replacement), when the mapped ROM signature is invalid and the 64 KiB pool allocation fails. The Radeon parent aggregate dependency is commented out at this snapshot; Sam440 uses an embedded-ROM replacement and CHRP/Efika use an OpenFirmware replacement, so those selected variants do not take this allocation path. **Consequence:** the fallback performs an invalid destination write and Radeon initialization cannot proceed. Check the allocation and return failure before copying. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation-to-copy path and conditional invalid destination; configuration is optional and the trigger requires both stated conditions. No allocation failure, BIOS read, card, or module build was exercised; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD9965

**Graph.mcc stores `MUIV_Graph_Source_FillPenSrc` in the line-pen slot.** In `Graph__MUIM_Graph_SetSourceAttrib()`, the `MUIV_Graph_Source_FillPenSrc` case assigns `msg->AttribVal` to `dataSource->gs_PlotPen`, a `WORD`, instead of `gs_PlotFillPenSrc`, an `IPTR` (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:884-886`; field declarations in `graph_intern.h:14-18`). No source here establishes whether that virtual target is connected to the default `workbench-classes-complete` chain. A full-tree search found no checked-in caller of this selector, so no in-tree trigger is claimed. **Consequence:** requested fill color is not acquired or used; if called after Show, plot-pen state is also replaced by a narrowed pointer value. Store the argument in `gs_PlotFillPenSrc`. **Confidence:** high for the field mismatch and resulting ignored fill source; external caller usage and display consequences have not been reproduced. ## GD9966

**NBitmap leaks acquired palette pens on non-AmigaOS4 high-color screens when CyberGraphics is unavailable.** `NBitmap_SetupImage()` creates a dithered representation and obtains 256 pens when `data->scrdepth <= 8 || CyberGfxBase == NULL` on non-AmigaOS4 builds (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nbitmap_mcc/NBitmap.c:770-803`). The corresponding `NBitmap_CleanupImage()` releases those entries only when `data->scrdepth <= 8` (`:905-911`). Thus, if the selected NBitmap class runs on a screen deeper than eight bits while `CyberGfxBase == NULL`, successful pen acquisitions are retained on every Cleanup/Setup cycle; entries whose allocation returned `-1` are correctly skipped, but successful shared/exclusive pen references are not returned. The setup and cleanup methods are dispatched through the class's `MUIM_Setup` and `MUIM_Cleanup` methods (`dispatcher.c:338-362`), so ordinary object removal and remapping exercise this unmatched lifecycle.

Repeated cycles consume palette references and can leave pens unavailable or colors reserved after the object is gone. **Affected configuration:** non-AmigaOS4 builds of the optional NBitmap MUI class. **Confidence:** high for the mismatched setup/cleanup predicates and leaked successful acquisitions; actual palette exhaustion depends on available colors and repeated object lifecycle. No MUI object, pen allocation, or screen was exercised; source-only.

**NList bitmap-image creation leaks palette pens if its image-record allocation fails.** In `NL_CreateImage()`, when a source bitmap has `MUIA_Bitmap_SourceColors`, the routine obtains one ColorMap pen per used source index and stores each in `obtainpens` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func4.c:619-679`). No allocation failure or image creation was induced; source-only.

**NBitmap silently renders an unconverted RGB24 buffer when its endian-conversion allocation fails.** On little-endian AROS, `NBitmap_NewImage()` allocates a replacement buffer for each supplied RGB24 state and calls `NBitmap_Convertbuffer()` only when that allocation succeeds (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nbitmap_mcc/NBitmap.c:349-366,503-538`). Construction still succeeds, and drawing that state displays red and blue channels reversed. **Affected configuration:** `__AROS__ && !AROS_BIGENDIAN`, the explicitly buildable `classes-zune-nbitmap-class`, and RGB24 raw-buffer input (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nbitmap_mcc/mmakefile.src:4-5,18-24`). **Confidence:** high for the unchecked conversion allocation and resulting source-format mismatch; occurrence requires that allocation to fail. No buffer allocation or image draw was run; source-only.

## GD9970

**DitherImage's ARGB mask stride truncates widths above 65,535 pixels.** The helper calculates mask bytes per row with `RAWIDTH(w)`, which first casts the public `uint32` width to `UWORD` before adding the row-rounding bias (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nbitmap_mcc/DitherImage.c:35`). For width 65,538 this macro returns 2, although a row requires 8,194 bytes after the helper's even-byte alignment. `DitherImageA()` allocates `RAWIDTH(width) * height` bytes for an ARGB mask, then indexes each row through `mPtr[x / 8]` up to the full 32-bit width (`:94-100,102-107,172-185`), writing beyond the allocated mask. **Trigger and consequence:** create an ARGB32 NBitmap wider than 65,535 pixels, with a nonzero height, and set it up where NBitmap selects indexed dithering (screen depth at most eight; on non-AmigaOS4 also when CyberGraphics is unavailable). If the mask allocation succeeds, the row-stride truncation makes the ARGB transparency loop write beyond its mask allocation, corrupting adjacent memory. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable NBitmap class with ARGB32 input on the stated screen/configuration path. **Confidence:** high for the `UWORD` truncation and unchecked full-width mask writes; occurrence also requires an unusually wide image and successful small mask allocation. No wide image or draw was used; source-only.

The per-pixel loop only sets mask bits when `mPtr != NULL`, but still returns the non-NULL chunky image (`:172-185,197-201`). NBitmap still reports setup success and draws the color-mapped pixels without transparency, so transparent areas become opaque. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable NBitmap class on paths that dither ARGB32 images. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked mask allocation and unmasked caller fallback; occurrence requires the stated allocation failure. No allocation failure or image draw was run; source-only.

## GD9972

**Chunky2Bitmap passes an unrepresentable row width to WritePixelLine8.** The helper accepts `ULONG width` and allocates bitmaps using that full value, then passes the same width to `WritePixelLine8()` for every row (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nbitmap_mcc/Chunky2Bitmap.c:55-84`). The Graphics API declares WritePixelLine8's `xstart`, `ystart`, and `width` as signed `WORD` (`rom/graphics/writepixelline8.c:13-20`). With xstart zero, a row wider than 32,768 pixels cannot be represented as a valid endpoint/width pair; for example width 32,769 narrows to -32,767 and produces an invalid negative endpoint in the wrapper's `xstart + width - 1` calculation. The rectangle renderer cannot write the intended full row.

**Trigger and consequence:** pass a non-NULL chunky image wider than 32,768 pixels to `Chunky2Bitmap()`; NBitmap does so for its dithered output on non-AmigaOS4 builds when the screen is indexed or CyberGraphics is unavailable (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nbitmap_mcc/NBitmap.c:770-776,812-824`). The destination bitmap may be allocated, but each wide row is not represented correctly by the WritePixelLine8 call, leaving output blank or incomplete. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable NBitmap class on non-AmigaOS4 indexed/no-CyberGraphics paths with wide dithered images (`nbitmap_mcc/mmakefile.src:4-5,18-24`). **Confidence:** high for the ULONG-to-WORD mismatch and unrepresentable coordinate range; actual visible extent depends on renderer clipping. No wide bitmap or draw was run; source-only.

**TextEditor block deletion can destroy text when its undo snapshot allocation fails.** `CutBlock()` records an `ET_DELETEBLOCK` undo action before calling `CutBlock2()` to delete the selected text, but it ignores the result of `AddToUndoBuffer()` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/BlockOperators.c:704-719`). `AddToUndoBuffer()` sets `success = FALSE` when `GetBlock()` returns NULL and reports `Error_NotEnoughUndoMem`, but does not create an undo step (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/UndoFunctions.c:447-466`). `CutBlock()` proceeds to `CutBlock2()` regardless, which frees the selected intermediate lines and removes the selected boundary characters (`BlockOperators.c:765-817`). If other selected content is exportable, `GetBlock()` can return a non-NULL but incomplete undo snapshot, which `AddToUndoBuffer()` accepts.

In the first case the editor still deletes the block without recording an undo step; in the second it records only part of the block, so a later undo restores incomplete text. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable AROS TextEditor MCC target (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/mmakefile.src:4-5,11-52`) when block deletion is performed with undo enabled. **Confidence:** high for both unchecked failure paths and the unconditional deletion; no allocation failure or edit/undo operation was run. **TextEditor ExportBlock validates the stop column against the start line.** In `MUIF_TextEditor_ExportBlock_TakeBlock` handling, `mExportBlock()` resolves `newblock.stopline`, but checks and stores `msg->stopx` using `newblock.startline->line.Length` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/ExportBlock.c:55-68`).
