The method therefore returns bytes beyond the logical end of that line instead of rejecting or clamping the coordinate. The adjacent SetBlock method validates its stop column against the resolved stop line (`SetBlock.c:75-84`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an external client calls `MUIM_TextEditor_ExportBlock` with `MUIF_TextEditor_ExportBlock_TakeBlock`, selecting a multi-line range without `MUIF_TextEditor_ExportBlock_FullLines`, where the start line is longer than the stop line and `stopx` is greater than the stop line's length but no greater than the start line's length. The exported text can include unrelated bytes following the stop line. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable AROS TextEditor MCC target; no in-tree TakeBlock caller was found, so the caller trigger is external to this checkout. **Confidence:** high for the start-line/stop-line validation mismatch and resulting oversized copy length; medium for practical reachability because no maintained in-tree caller uses this flag and the API documentation does not spell out invalid-coordinate handling. No export call was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7731), TextEditor ExportBlock full-body and public-API caller pass.


## GD9979

**TextEditor SplitLine inserts a new line after its content allocation fails.** `SplitLine()` allocates a `line_node`, then calls `Init_LineNode()` without checking its result (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/EditorStuff.c:780-788`). `Init_LineNode()` returns FALSE when the new line's contents allocation fails and leaves `Contents`, `Length`, `allocatedContents`, and `visual` unset (`MixedFunctions.c:99-135`). `SplitLine()` continues to populate only some fields, builds style/color state, inserts the node into the live list, and reports success (`EditorStuff.c:798-999,995-1136`). The newly linked node can therefore contain uninitialized line state, which subsequent layout, drawing, or editing consumes.

**Trigger and consequence:** a split operation allocates the node successfully but fails the subsequent line-content allocation. Ordinary Return handling records an undo step and calls `SplitLine()` without checking its result (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/HandleInput.c:1367-1373`); the split helper nevertheless inserts the incomplete node. This can leave the editor's line list inconsistent and cause later display or editing operations to use invalid line fields. The same helper is used for wrapping, insertion, and undo paths. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable AROS TextEditor MCC target under memory pressure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked FALSE path and unconditional insertion; no allocation failure or split was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7756), TextEditor EditorStuff full-body and caller pass.

## GD9980

**TextEditor PasteClip can report success after dropping clipboard lines on allocation failure.** For a TextEditor-generated clip, `PasteClip()` copies optional style/color arrays and then allocates a line node and content buffer (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/EditorStuff.c:220-277,328-364`). If either line allocation fails, the branch frees only the node when needed; it does not set an error or stop reading, and any already-copied style/color arrays are not attached to a node or freed. After a later EOF, any other successfully imported lines are committed (`:381-437`). `Key_Paste()` treats that TRUE result as a completed paste and records an undo action for only the inserted range (`HandleInput.c:1288-1302`). The clipboard server's selected writer includes these per-line styles/colors when present (`ClipboardServer.c:333-389`).

**Trigger and consequence:** paste a multi-line TextEditor clipboard selection containing style/color metadata while a per-line node or content-buffer allocation fails, but a later clipboard line can still be imported. The editor commits a partial paste as success, omits the failed line, and leaves copied style/color arrays unattached to the editor's pool-managed line list until pool destruction. Undo covers only the partial insertion. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable AROS TextEditor MCC when pasting its own styled/colored clipboard data under allocation pressure. **Confidence:** high for the continuation/commit and missing cleanup paths; no paste or allocation failure was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7756), TextEditor EditorStuff full-body and caller pass.


## GD9981

**TextEditor style updates discard the old style map when growth allocation fails.** `AddStyleToLine()` rebuilds a line's style-change array through `AddToGrow()`, then frees the old array and installs the new one without checking whether every entry was copied (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/StyleOperators.c:116-202`). `AddToGrow()` silently omits an entry when its pool allocation fails and has no error return (`Grow.c:65-95`). A failed growth can therefore remove existing style transitions and/or the requested style boundary from the replacement array.

**Trigger and consequence:** apply or remove bold, italic, or underline on text that already has style transitions while the TextEditor pool cannot grow the temporary array. The operation can silently lose or corrupt style formatting on that line; a multi-line selection can leave different lines with inconsistent style maps. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable AROS TextEditor MCC through `MUIA_TextEditor_StyleBold`, `MUIA_TextEditor_StyleItalic`, `MUIA_TextEditor_StyleUnderline` (`GetSetAttrs.c:522-532`) or `MUIM_TextEditor_SetBlock` style operations (`SetBlock.c:100-112`). **Confidence:** high for the ignored grow failure and unconditional replacement; no allocation failure or style operation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7761), TextEditor StyleOperators full-body and setter-caller pass.


## GD9982

**TextEditor search indexes its 256-byte skip table with signed character values.** `mSearch()` declares `BYTE map[256]`, then indexes it with `(int)*str` while building the case-sensitive map and `(int)*contents` during forward search (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/Search.c:73,94-108,149-163`). On targets where plain `char` is signed, any input or document byte from `0x80` through `0xff` can be promoted to a negative index instead of its unsigned byte value. The documented search API limits string length to 120 characters but does not restrict its character set (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/doc/MCC_TextEditor.doc:1560-1588`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run a forward search on a signed-char target when the query or scanned line contains a high-bit byte. The table access falls outside `map`, so the search can return incorrect results or fail while evaluating the skip table. **Affected configuration:** AROS TextEditor MCC builds whose C compiler uses signed plain `char`; the defect is conditional on target/compiler char signedness. **Confidence:** high for the signed-index mismatch and table bounds; no search was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7767), TextEditor Search full-body and public-API caller pass.


## GD9983

**TextEditor MIME import appends color transitions to the style array.** In `MimeImport()`, the `#` color-marker branch initializes `newColor` but passes `&newStyle` to `AddToGrow(&style_grow, ...)` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/ImportHook.c:714-724`). The color grow-array receives no corresponding transition, while the style array gains an unrelated or stale `newStyle` record. At line finalization, the two arrays are installed as `line->Styles` and `line->Colors` independently (`:839-855`).

**Trigger and consequence:** import MIME formatted text containing a recognized `#...#` color span. The intended color change is omitted; when the style array exists, it also receives a bogus transition that can corrupt subsequent style interpretation. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MCC MIME and quoted-MIME import hooks. **Confidence:** high; direct wrong-grow target and final array assignment. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7771), TextEditor ImportHook full-body and caller pass.

## GD9984

**TextEditor MIME soft-line joining leaves the recorded line capacity stale.** When quoted-printable soft-line joining reallocates `line->Contents`, `MimeImport()` updates the pointer but does not update `line->allocatedContents` from its initial `len+4` value (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/ImportHook.c:575-599,748-768`). `PasteChars()` later compares required length against that recorded capacity and calls `ExpandLine()` when it appears insufficient (`EditorStuff.c:1288-1293`); `ExpandLine()` sizes its replacement from the stale capacity and uses `strlcpy()` (`MixedFunctions.c:143-165`). For a sufficiently long joined line and edit, the nominal expansion may still be smaller than the actual current contents, truncating the line during the copy before the edit proceeds.

**Trigger and consequence:** import a MIME line extended by one or more soft breaks, then insert text when the required size exceeds the stale recorded capacity. `ExpandLine()` can copy only the prefix that fits its undersized allocation and free the original buffer, losing the joined line's suffix. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MIME and quoted-MIME import followed by editing. **Confidence:** high for stale capacity and undersized sizing formula; consequence follows from `strlcpy()` sizing and the edit path, not runtime reproduced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7771), TextEditor ImportHook full-body and caller pass.


## GD9985

**TextEditor import leaves continuation line state uninitialized.** `ImportText()` clears the first `line_node` but allocates each subsequent node without clearing it; it only copies `Flow` from the preceding node when `clearFlow` is false (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/ImportText.c:44-54,96-107`). The selected `AllocVecPooled()` wrapper adds a size header but does not zero the payload (`extrasrc/AllocVecPooled.c:29-44`). The built-in import hooks populate contents, length, styles/colors, and only conditionally set flow/highlight/separator fields; they do not initialize every line field (`ImportHook.c:232-253,420-520,575-617,837-857`). The importer also reads a continuation node's `clearFlow` to determine the following node's flow (`ImportText.c:102-107`).

**Trigger and consequence:** import multi-line text using the built-in plain or MIME hooks. Continuation nodes can retain indeterminate `Highlight`, `Flow`, `Separator`, `clearFlow`, and `visual` values. Those fields control rendering/export, flow inheritance, and line-merging geometry (`PrintLineWithStyles.c:130-140,384-402`; `ClipboardServer.c:152-172`; `ImportText.c:102-107`; `EditorStuff.c:477-496`). A MIME separator directive explicitly sets `clearFlow` on its line, causing the immediately following node's `Flow` not to be initialized by the importer. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MCC multi-line imports and reimports. **Confidence:** high for the uninitialized allocation and incomplete field writes; effects are dependent on allocator contents and subsequent field use. No import or rendering was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7776), TextEditor ImportText full-body and caller pass.

## GD9986

**TextEditor ImportText accepts a truncated document after line-node allocation failure.** After a hook returns a non-NULL continuation pointer, `ImportText()` links the current line into the result, then allocates the next `line_node`. If that allocation fails, it breaks out of the loop and returns `ContainsLines(lines)`, which is TRUE for the already-imported prefix (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/ImportText.c:94-112`). It does not free or mark the partial result as failed. `ReimportText()` treats TRUE as complete, frees the existing document, and moves the partial list into the live editor (`:118-148`). The content setter likewise replaces the live list on TRUE (`GetSetAttrs.c:830-840`).

**Trigger and consequence:** import/reimport text with at least one completed line followed by more input while allocation of the next line node fails. Callers accept the prefix as a successful import; during `ReimportText()` the prior full document is freed, causing silent text loss. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MCC import, content replacement, and tab-mode reimport under memory pressure. **Confidence:** high for the break-and-success return and destructive reimport caller; no allocation failure was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7776), TextEditor ImportText full-body and caller pass.


## GD9987

**TextEditor MUI edit shortcuts are gated by the read-only flag.** In `mHandleInput()`, `MUIKEY_CUT`, `MUIKEY_PASTE`, `MUIKEY_UNDO`, and `MUIKEY_REDO` each call their operation only when `FLG_ReadOnly` is set (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/HandleInput.c:703-739`). The flag is explicitly the read-only state (`private.h:704`; `GetSetAttrs.c:164,446-458`). The called `Undo()` and `Redo()` functions independently require the flag to be clear (`UndoFunctions.c:69,235`). `Key_Cut()` calls `EraseBlock(..., CUTF_CLIPBOARD)`, whose enabled-selection path calls `CutBlock()` with `CUTF_CUT` and removes the selected text (`HandleInput.c:1177-1187,1246-1255`; `BlockOperators.c:704-748`).

**Trigger and consequence:** in editable mode, the MUI Cut/Paste/Undo/Redo shortcuts are not handled by this class, so expected shortcut actions are unavailable through this dispatch path. In read-only mode, Cut is dispatched and can delete the selection despite the read-only setting; the other three are dispatched but Undo/Redo reject the operation and Paste reaches the editing path without a read-only guard. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MCC instances receiving these MUI key events; destructive Cut requires a selected block and `FLG_ReadOnly`. **Confidence:** high for the inverted dispatch conditions and Undo/Redo guard; Cut's destructive consequence follows the selected `Key_Cut` path. No key event or edit was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7781), TextEditor HandleInput full-body and edit-helper pass.


## GD9988

**TextEditor cannot reset an overridden tab size to the user preference.** The public `MUIA_TextEditor_TabSize` contract says `MUIV_TextEditor_TabSize_Default` resets to the value configured in MUI preferences, and valid explicit values are 2–12 (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/doc/MCC_TextEditor.doc:978-990`). In the setter, the special case tests the existing `data->TabSize` against the sentinel instead of testing the incoming `ti_Data` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/GetSetAttrs.c:780-799`). For a normal explicit value followed by the documented default sentinel, the code takes the explicit-value branch and clamps 0 to 2. The stored preference is separately maintained in `GlobalTabSize` by `InitConfig()` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/InitConfig.c:157-173`), but the reset branch is not reached.

**Trigger and consequence:** set a specific tab size, then set `MUIA_TextEditor_TabSize` to `MUIV_TextEditor_TabSize_Default`. The active tab width becomes 2 spaces instead of the user's configured size, and `FLG_ForcedTabSize` remains set. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MCC instances whose clients reset an explicit tab-size override to the documented default. **Confidence:** high; direct mismatch between documented input sentinel and setter comparison. No attribute operation or reimport was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7790), TextEditor GetSetAttrs full-body and attribute-caller pass.


## GD9989

**TextEditor SetBlock flow changes do not set HasChanged.** `mSetBlock()` updates the selected lines' `line.Flow` values and `data->Flow`, then redraws the affected area, but unlike the equivalent `MUIA_TextEditor_Flow` setter it never sets `data->HasChanged = TRUE` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/SetBlock.c:118-148`; compare `GetSetAttrs.c:711-719`). The dispatcher only emits `MUIA_TextEditor_HasChanged` notifications when that field changes (`Dispatcher.c:752,845-846`). The public attribute documents HasChanged as indicating that gadget contents have changed and supports notification (`MCC_TextEditor.doc:472-487`).

**Trigger and consequence:** apply `MUIF_TextEditor_SetBlock_Flow` to a valid block after clearing HasChanged. The text's alignment is modified and redrawn, but HasChanged remains false and observers receive no change notification. Applications that use this tag to decide whether to save or prompt can miss the formatting edit. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MCC clients using the documented SetBlock flow operation and HasChanged state/notifications. **Confidence:** high; direct mutation and dispatcher notification comparison. No method or notification was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7799), TextEditor SetBlock full-body and flow-state caller pass.


## GD9990

**TextEditor ARexx commands still execute in read-only mode.** The public `MUIA_TextEditor_ReadOnly` contract states that read-only mode has no ARexx support except `COPY` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/doc/MCC_TextEditor.doc:826-847`). `mHandleARexx()` does not reject commands when `FLG_ReadOnly` is set; `CallFunction()` only special-cases vertical scrolling, then falls through to the full command switch when the command did not change the scroll position (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/HandleARexx.c:96-138,140-193`). Commands including `CLEAR`, `CUT`, `PASTE`, `ERASE`, `TEXT`, `DELETE`, and `BACKSPACE` therefore reach editing operations. The demo dispatches its ARexx command directly to this method (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/demo/TextEditor-Demo.c:88-94`), illustrating the documented integration path.

**Trigger and consequence:** call `MUIM_TextEditor_ARexxCmd` with a modifying command on a read-only TextEditor object. The command changes or deletes content despite read-only mode, contrary to the published contract. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MCC clients that invoke the ARexx command method while `MUIA_TextEditor_ReadOnly` is TRUE. **Confidence:** high; explicit contract and direct dispatch path. No ARexx command was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7804), TextEditor ARexx full-body and read-only-contract pass.


## GD9991

**TextEditor word navigation passes signed bytes as locale character indexes.** `CheckSep()` accepts a plain `char` and passes it to `IsAlNum()` after conversion to `long` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/Navigation.c:606-616`). The Locale API takes a 32-bit `ULONG` character (`workbench/libs/locale/locale.conf:43`). The selected English language implementation indexes `__eng_ctype_array[chr]`, which is a 256-entry table, without range normalization (`workbench/locale/languages/templates/english.c:93,363-372,724`). On targets where plain `char` is signed, document bytes `0x80`–`0xff` are sign-extended to large unsigned character values before this table lookup. `CheckSep()` is used by next/previous word navigation and TextEditor word selection (`Navigation.c:432-438,520-538`; `HandleInput.c:1031-1051`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke word navigation or word selection on a signed-char target when the cursor reaches a high-bit byte. The locale classifier receives an out-of-range value instead of the byte value; the selected English implementation indexes beyond its classification table, so word movement can misclassify the character or read unrelated memory. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MCC builds with signed plain `char`, using a locale language function that indexes a byte table; the in-tree English implementation is one confirmed provider. **Confidence:** high for sign extension and table indexing; no navigation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7809), TextEditor Navigation full-body and locale-caller pass.


## GD9992

**TextEditor plain export reserves too little space for dense style and color control codes.** `ExportHookFunc()` estimates per-line expansion as `emsg->Length * 10` and only grows the buffer when that amount exceeds the remaining capacity (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/ExportHook.c:74-95`). `mExportText()` zero-initializes `ExportMessage` and never sets its private `data` field (`mcc/ExportText.c:37-51`), so the selected plain hook takes its non-pooled branch and starts with a 1,024-byte shared buffer (`ExportHook.c:60-64`). Plain export emits color escapes for transitions (`:270-277`) and style escapes for bold, italic, and underline transitions (`:280-325`), in addition to copied text. For a final line containing 100 visible characters plus the editor's stored newline, `ExportText` passes `Length == 100` after removing that newline; the estimate is 1,000, so the initial 1,024-byte allocation is not grown. Alternating three-digit color entries 254/255 and toggling all three style bits on alternating single-character ranges emits more than 1,024 bytes before the final NUL, exceeding that allocation. The documented default color map supports entries through 255 (`MCC_TextEditor.doc:137-165`), and the Pen attribute accepts UBYTE values (`:713-722`).

**Trigger and consequence:** create a 100-character line with dense per-character style/color transitions as described, then export using the plain hook. The hook writes past its allocated output buffer, which can corrupt adjacent memory and truncate or damage the export. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MCC plain-text export when a line's style/color metadata expands beyond the fixed estimate; the concrete case uses documented color-map indices 254 and 255 and toggles bold, italic, and underline per character. **Confidence:** high for the zeroed `data` field, 1,024-byte branch, estimate and emitted controls; export was not run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7814), TextEditor ExportHook full-body and export-caller pass.

<a id="gd10534"></a>
## GD10534 — TextEditor leaks its export-state allocation when export fails

`ExportHookFunc()` allocates a temporary `struct Buffer` with `AllocVecShared()` before allocating its output storage (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/ExportHook.c:49-72`). If the initial output-buffer allocation fails, the hook takes the `buf->buffer == NULL` failure branch and returns NULL without freeing the already allocated `Buffer` (`:74,409-418`); this leaks even when the first line is also the last. If a later growth allocation fails on a non-final line, the hook frees the previous output buffer but returns the `Buffer` record as `UserData` because `emsg->Last` is false (`:78-115,397-408`). On the next line, its NULL `buf->buffer` reaches the failure branch and the NULL return makes `mExportText()` stop without freeing the record (`ExportText.c:44-69`; `ExportHook.c:409-418`). A growth failure on the final line does free the record and is excluded. The default plain hook is selected during TextEditor initialization (`Dispatcher.c:156`), and the Info tool calls this export method when rebuilding tooltypes (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/Info/main.c:285`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a built-in TextEditor export allocates the temporary `Buffer` record, then either its initial output allocation fails, or a grown buffer allocation fails on a non-final line. The export returns NULL and leaks the small `Buffer` record on those paths; the prior output buffer is freed on the growth-failure path. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MCC's built-in export hooks when their shared or pooled output allocation fails after the temporary record allocation succeeds; Info's selected tooltype-save path is one maintained caller. **Confidence:** high for the allocation and missing cleanup paths; occurrence requires the stated allocation-failure order. Growth failure on the final line is cleaned up and is not part of this finding. Free the temporary record on every failed export path before returning NULL. No allocation failure, export, or save was run; source-only. See the [TextEditor ExportHook coverage pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#texteditor-exporthook-full-body-and-export-caller-pass-gd9992-corrected-and-gd10534).

<a id="gd10535"></a>
## GD10535 — Info leaks the exported text when the tooltype editor is empty

`BuildToolTypes()` obtains an allocated export buffer, then treats either a NULL pointer or an empty string as the same return path (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/Info/main.c:285-291`). For a non-NULL empty string, it deletes the temporary pool and returns without `FreeVec(contents)`. The selected TextEditor creates an initial line containing `"\n"` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/Dispatcher.c:139-146`); `mExportText()` removes that artificial final newline and passes a zero-length line to the built-in export hook (`ExportText.c:61-68`), which returns its allocated, NUL-terminated output buffer for the final line (`ExportHook.c:361-368,397-402`). Thus an empty editor produces a non-NULL empty string and reaches the leaking branch.

**Trigger and consequence:** save an icon through Info with its tooltype editor empty, either because the icon has no tooltypes or after the user removes them all. `BuildToolTypes()` frees the temporary pool but leaks the exported empty-string allocation on each save attempt. This is separate from GD6043: an empty list is an intentional result and is serialized as no tooltypes, while GD6043 concerns an actual export/allocation failure being mistaken for that result. **Affected configuration:** selected Wanderer Info build with `USE_TEXTEDITOR=1`. **Confidence:** high for the empty export construction and missing `FreeVec`; one output buffer is retained per empty-list save. Free `contents` before returning from the non-NULL empty-string branch. No icon save or allocation was run; source-only. See the [Info/TextEditor export coverage pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#texteditor-exporthook-full-body-and-export-caller-pass-gd9992-corrected-and-gd10534).


## GD9993

**TextEditor undo-buffer resize discards the old buffer after allocation failure.** When `MUIA_TextEditor_UndoLevels` is set, `GetSetAttrs.c` calls `ResizeUndoBuffer()` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/GetSetAttrs.c:747-750`). For any nonzero new size, `ResizeUndoBuffer()` attempts an allocation; regardless of whether it succeeds, it then frees `data->undoSteps` and installs `newUndoSteps`, which remains NULL on failure. It also retains nonzero `usedUndoSteps`/`nextUndoStep` values up to the new capacity (`UndoFunctions.c:535-582`). The next `Undo()` or `Redo()` sees those counts and indexes the NULL `undoSteps` pointer (`:69-89`; redo path `:235-256`). Additionally, `FreeUndoStep()` is called only for slots beyond the new capacity, so clip snapshots retained in the old slots are not freed when the old array is discarded (`:561-571`; clip cleanup in `:35-53`).

**Trigger and consequence:** with at least one undo action recorded, set `MUIA_TextEditor_UndoLevels` to a different nonzero value while allocation of the replacement array fails. The editor loses its undo storage but continues reporting undo/redo availability; a subsequent operation can dereference NULL, and retained clip snapshots leak. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MCC clients that resize a nonzero undo level under memory pressure. **Confidence:** high; direct failure path and subsequent guarded index access. No allocation failure or undo was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7823), TextEditor UndoFunctions full-body and resize-caller pass.


## GD9994

**TextEditor assigns zero visual lines when a leading tab cannot fit.** With wrapping enabled, `LineCharsWidth()` asks `TextFitNew()` how many characters fit in the inner width and leaves `c` at zero when none fit; the optional word-wrap search starts at `c-1` and also leaves it zero when there is no preceding whitespace (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/MixedFunctions.c:228-288`). A leading tab whose configured pixel width exceeds `_mwidth()` makes `TextFitNew()` return zero: the tab branch subtracts the full tab width and exits when no width remains (`NewGfx.c:91-120`). `VisualHeight()` stops when `LineCharsWidth()` returns zero, so it records zero for the line (`MixedFunctions.c:297-325`); `CountLines()` stores that value as `line->visual` and excludes it from the total (`:760-771`). `GetLine()` then advances past zero-height nodes while mapping display rows (`:686-709`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use a wrapping mode, disable tab-to-space conversion, set a tab size whose pixel width exceeds the editor's positive inner width, and place a retained tab at the start of a nonempty line. For example, a 12-space tab at 96 pixels in a narrower editor. That line receives visual height zero, is omitted from display-line totals, and can be skipped by drawing and cursor-to-line mapping. **Affected configuration:** TextEditor MCC with wrapping enabled, horizontal scrolling off, retained tab characters, and tab width greater than inner gadget width. **Confidence:** high for zero fit, zero visual count and skip behavior; no layout or render was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7827), TextEditor MixedFunctions full-body and wrapping-caller pass.


## GD9995

**TextEditor font setup frees an uninitialized pointer when its name allocation fails.** `GetFont()` declares `fontname` without initializing it, assigns it only in the successful branch of `AllocVecShared()`, and calls `FreeVec(fontname)` unconditionally whenever a font configuration string exists (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/InitConfig.c:48-54,77`). If that allocation returns NULL, the cleanup passes an indeterminate pointer to `FreeVec`. `InitConfig()` calls `GetFont()` for both normal and fixed fonts during object setup (`:165-166`; caller `Dispatcher.c:247-257`).

**Trigger and consequence:** configure a normal or fixed font and have the corresponding shared allocation fail during TextEditor setup. Cleanup then operates on an uninitialized address, which can corrupt allocator state or fault; the intended fallback to the superclass font may not be reached. **Affected configuration:** selected TextEditor MCC builds with configured font strings, under memory pressure or allocator failure. **Confidence:** high for the uninitialized failure-path pointer; runtime allocator consequences were not induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7835), TextEditor InitConfig full-body and setup-caller pass.


## GD9996

**TextEditor keeps rendering through a failed double-buffer allocation.** During `MUIM_Show`, `mShow()` stores the result of `MUIG_AllocBitMap()` in `data->doublebuffer` without checking it, then assigns the possibly NULL result to `data->doublerp.BitMap` and continues setup (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/Dispatcher.c:452-456`). The selected AROS wrapper returns the underlying `AllocBitMap()` result, including NULL on failure (`AllocBitMap.c:39-48`). Later `DumpText()` routes drawing through the double-buffer raster port when callers request buffering or the draw covers fewer than three lines (`MixedFunctions.c:614-627`); `PrintLine()` then blits from `rp->BitMap` (`PrintLineWithStyles.c:457-465`). The code draws with a raster port whose bitmap is NULL and passes that bitmap to the final blit, so the update can fault or fail to render. **Affected configuration:** selected AROS TextEditor MCC path when `AllocBitMap()` fails; the wrapper also has platform-specific branches, but this finding is scoped to AROS. **Confidence:** high that allocation failure is unchecked and the NULL bitmap reaches drawing/blit; exact manifestation depends on the selected graphics operation. No allocation failure or redraw was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7845), TextEditor bitmap allocator and dispatcher full-body/caller pass.


## GD9997

**TextEditor clipboard parsing tests an uninitialized text pointer after allocation failure.** In `ServerReadLine()`, `textline` is declared without initialization. For a nonempty `CHRS` chunk it is assigned only if `AllocVecShared()` succeeds, but the next condition tests it regardless (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/ClipboardServer.c:405,544-564`). If the allocation fails, the code reads an indeterminate pointer; if it appears non-NULL, it can pass that invalid address into a newly allocated line node, while the failure branch may also free it (`:563-585`). `PasteClip()` consumes a line only when the worker returns success and a non-NULL node, so an invalid pointer can reach the normal clipboard import path (`EditorStuff.c:203-214`).

The parser evaluates the uninitialized pointer and may install or free an invalid address, causing a fault or allocator corruption instead of reporting an incomplete clipboard read. **Affected configuration:** selected AROS TextEditor MCC clipboard reader under memory pressure. **Confidence:** high for the uninitialized pointer read on the allocation-failure path; runtime consequences were not induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7850), ClipboardServer full-body and paste-caller pass.


## GD9998

**TextEditor spell checking uses a reversed word-length bound and can overflow its stack buffer.** `SpellCheckWord()` stores the cursor position in `end`, moves backward to the word start, then tests `start-end < 256` before copying `end-start+1` bytes into `char word[256]` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcc/SpellChecker.c:567-586`). For a same-line word, `GoPreviousWord()` moves the cursor left, so `start-end` is negative and the condition remains true regardless of word length (`Navigation.c:511-540`). The selected `strlcpy()` copies up to the supplied size minus one and NUL-terminates (`compiler/crt/stdc/strlcpy.c:76-90`), so a word of 256 or more bytes supplies a size larger than the destination.

**Trigger and consequence:** enable TextEditor TypeAndSpell and finish typing an alphabetic word of at least 256 bytes on one line, for example by entering a delimiter or Return. `SpellCheckWord()` passes the oversized length for its 256-byte local buffer, writing past the stack array before invoking the configured lookup. **Affected configuration:** selected TextEditor MCC builds with TypeAndSpell enabled; the check is independent of whether lookup is configured to use CLI or ARexx. **Confidence:** high for the reversed bound, same-line backward cursor movement, and oversized copy length; no long-word spell check was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L7854), SpellChecker full-body bound recheck and input-caller trace.


## GD9999

**Boot-mode display registration defers writing DDRV_ResultID through the caller's pointer.** AddDisplayDriverA() stores the supplied DDRV_ResultID address directly in cfg->drv_idstore (rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:230-232). For DDRV_BootMode, driver_Setup(..., FALSE, ...) returns success after queueing the config without creating the HIDD (rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:284-297; rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:401-414). When a display is eventually registered, display_Register() writes the ID through that saved pointer (rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:346-348). Queue replay is deferred until display enumeration or mode selection (rom/graphics/nextdisplayinfo.c:60-65; rom/graphics/bestmodeida.c:248-255), and a failed instantiation can leave the pointer stored for a later replay (rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:310-320).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** a client uses both DDRV_BootMode and DDRV_ResultID, with the result location having a shorter lifetime than the deferred replay. The API documentation describes the result location but gives no lifetime requirement; no in-tree DDRV_ResultID caller was found. **Consequence:** replay writes the assigned ID through a stale pointer, potentially corrupting reused caller storage or faulting. Complete the output write before returning, or define and enforce a persistent output-storage lifetime. **Confidence:** high for the deferred write and retained pointer; practical reachability is limited to external callers combining these tags. No registration or replay was run; source-only.


## GD10000

**Boot-mode display handover retains the caller's DDRV_HWRanges array.** AddDisplayDriverA() stores the tag's array pointer directly in the persistent gfxdriver_data record (rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:226-228). display_Register() attaches that record to the registered display (rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:381-384). Later, driver_FindBootDisplay() reads the retained drv_ranges pointer while comparing an incoming driver's ranges against each boot display (rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:220-245). The public tag documentation specifies a zero-size-terminated array but does not state that the array must remain alive after AddDisplayDriverA() returns (compiler/include/graphics/driver.h:29-42; rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:56-64).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** an external caller registers a DDRV_BootMode display with a DDRV_HWRanges array whose storage expires before a later native driver's handover check. Copy the terminated range array into owned storage or document and enforce its required lifetime. **Confidence:** high for pointer retention and later dereference; practical reachability is limited to external callers that provide short-lived arrays. No display registration or handover was run; source-only.




## GD10001

**NList's ByteRun1 bitmap conversion advances the compressed input pointer during repeated runs.** In `NL_CreateImage()`, the Bodychunk ByteRun1 decoder saves a repeated value in `val` and tracks the remaining run in `num`, but still executes `body++` after every output byte (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func4.c:523-551`). After consuming a repeat control and its value, subsequent output bytes should reuse `val` without consuming additional compressed input. Instead the pointer skips bytes belonging to following packets. The mask-plane loop has the same unconditional increment while consuming a repeat run (`:558-581`). The selected Muimaster Bodychunk decoder demonstrates the expected pointer movement: repeat runs read one value and emit it repeatedly, advancing the source only for bytes actually consumed (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/bodychunk.c:73-100`).

**Trigger and consequence:** pass a compressed Bodychunk with ByteRun1 data containing a repeated run to `MUIM_NList_UseImage()` or `MUIM_NList_CreateImage()` on a set-up NList. After the run, subsequent pixels (and, when present, mask data) are read from the wrong offsets; the converted list image is corrupted and may read beyond the encoded chunk if the shifted pointer reaches the end. NList's public method accepts Bitmap/Bodychunk objects (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NList.doc:3480-3513`), and the maintained NList demo uses `MUIM_NList_UseImage()` for Bodychunk objects (`demo/NList-Demo.c:662-663`), but sets compression to `0` for both sample Bodychunks (`:151,199`) and therefore does not exercise this ByteRun1 path. The trigger requires another client to supply a compressed Bodychunk. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable optional `classes-zune-nlist-class` target when a compressed ByteRun1 Bodychunk is supplied. **Confidence:** high for incorrect input-pointer advancement and resulting decode corruption; the exact out-of-bounds reach depends on encoded data and chunk length, which the Bodychunk interface does not expose to this conversion routine. No image conversion or malformed chunk was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), NList bitmap conversion and caller recheck.


## GD10002

**`LayoutIconA()` skips scaling the selected ARGB image after scaling the normal image.** The `width` and `height` locals hold the source dimensions shared by both image states. When image 0 has ARGB data and scaling is needed, the successful normal-image scaling path updates those locals to `ni->ni_Width` and `ni->ni_Height` (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:224-229`). On a fresh layout, the next loop iteration's image 1 `FetchIconARGB()` may return its own original-size ARGB buffer or synthesize one from image 0 at the original face dimensions (`support.c:142-155`; ARGB chunks are allocated to the FACE width and height in `diskobj35io.c:235-260,571-579`). Because the shared locals now equal the destination dimensions, the `if (width != ni->ni_Width || height != ni->ni_Height)` test is false and `ARGBMap` is set directly to that unscaled source buffer (`layouticon.c:222-235`). `DrawIconStateA()` then passes `ni->ni_Width` as the source stride and writes `ni->ni_Width` by `ni->ni_Height` pixels from `ARGBMap` (`workbench/libs/icon/drawiconstate.c:169-175`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on a fresh layout, lay out an icon with normal ARGB data on a screen deeper than eight bits with CyberGraphics available, with scaling from the icon's source dimensions to different `ni_Width`/`ni_Height`; then draw its selected state. If the selected ARGB image is absent, `FetchIconARGB()` synthesizes it at the original FACE size, so it reaches the same path. On enlargement, the draw reads beyond the selected image's source allocation; on other size changes, the destination-sized stride and extents misinterpret the source buffer, producing incorrect selected imagery. Preserve the source dimensions across loop iterations and scale each state independently. **Affected configuration:** icon.library ARGB rendering on high-color screens when CyberGraphics is available and the icon scale box or screen resolution changes the output size. The selected Workbench icon-list caller draws selected icons through `DrawIconStateA()` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Classes/iconlist.c:6570-6577`). **Confidence:** high for shared-dimension mutation, skipped second-state scale, source allocation size, and destination-sized read; enlargement is required for the out-of-bounds read. No icon file, screen layout, or draw was run. Source-only.


## GD10003

**`LayoutIconA()` divides by a zero source width when applying a finite scale box.** If either native FACE dimension is zero, `LayoutIconA()` falls back to `icon->do_Gadget.Width` and `Height` (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:156-162`). The classic DiskObject reader deserializes those gadget fields directly from the file and does not validate nonzero dimensions (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjio.c:154-173,279-315`). For any scale-box value other than `ICON_SCALEBOX_AUTOSCALE`, layout calls `scaleToBounds()` (`layouticon.c:195-203`). That helper only rejects nonpositive maximum dimensions; with a positive finite scale box and `SrcWidth == 0`, it computes `SrcHeight * MaxWidth / SrcWidth` and divides by zero (`layouticon.c:488-505`).

**Trigger and consequence:** load or pass a DiskObject whose FACE dimensions do not both exist and whose gadget width is zero, request layout on a non-NULL screen, and configure a positive finite per-icon or global scale box. `GetIconTagList()` accepts a caller-supplied screen and unconditionally calls `LayoutIconA()` for initial layout (`workbench/libs/icon/geticontaglist.c:123-124,341-346`); `ICONCTRLA_SetGlobalScaleBox` and `ICONCTRLA_SetScaleBox` expose the finite scale-box settings (`workbench/libs/icon/iconcontrol.c:185-187,596-601`; constants and packing in `compiler/include/workbench/icon.h:169-179`). The zero divisor invokes undefined C behavior and commonly traps, aborting the caller's layout. Validate source dimensions before the calculation and leave the icon in a defined failure state. **Affected configuration:** icon.library clients laying out zero-width legacy or caller-created DiskObjects with finite scale-box sizing; the default scale-box value does not enter this division. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked input and zero-divisor arithmetic; the precise failure mode depends on the target/compiler. No icon file, scale-box operation, or layout was run. Source-only.

**MUI ARexx dispatch treats command prefixes as complete command names.** `Application__MUIM_NewInput()` isolates the incoming command token length, then calls `Strnicmp(commandstr, cmd->mc_Name, len)` without checking that the configured `mc_Name` ends at the same position (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1711-1718`). `Strnicmp()` returns equal as soon as the requested comparison length is exhausted (`rom/utility/strnicmp.c:51-70`). **Affected configuration:** the selected MUI Application class when external clients configure ARexx commands; a repository search found no maintained `MUIA_Application_Commands` caller that demonstrates this trigger. No ARexx message was sent. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10079

**NListtree clipboard export skips display text and edits bracketed escape sequences in the stored node name.** The built-in `_NListtree_CopyToClip()` path copies `tn_Name` into a temporary string and claims to remove formatting escapes (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:10050-10075`). ## GD10082

**Nouveau's 3D alpha-template upload applies inverted alpha to the blue byte instead of the alpha byte.** On the transparent-colour-expansion path, the bitmap caller passes `msg->invertalpha` to `HiddNouveauAccelAPENUpload3D()` for NV10–NV40 cards and sufficiently large transfers (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_bitmapclass.c:832-859`; `:25`). Because the caller packs foreground RGB into the low 24 bits, the result preserves the source alpha and forces the blue component to 255 rather than using the inverted alpha. The software equivalent first computes `alpha = (*pixarray++) ^ 255` before blending (`nouveau_accel.c:298-329`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use `PutAlphaTemplate` with transparent color expansion and `invertalpha` enabled on an NV10–NV40 Nouveau device, with GART available and a transfer of at least 1,024 pixels. The accelerated output uses the wrong transparency and blue values, producing visibly incorrect template blending. Invert the 8-bit alpha before shifting it into the high byte. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Nouveau HIDD; default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the caller arguments, branch expression, and software-path alpha inversion; no GPU transfer was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10083

**Nouveau's software alpha blending left-shifts negative signed values.** `do_alpha()` multiplies the alpha by a signed channel difference, then evaluates `(tmp << 8)` where `tmp` can be negative (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_accel.c:41-45`). The function is called by the software 16-bit and 32-bit alpha-image and alpha-template loops (`:110-112,192-194,284-286,323-325,503-505,542-544`). Whenever a partially transparent source channel is lower than the destination channel, `a * v` is negative and the left shift has undefined behavior under C.

**Caller path and trigger:** `NouveauBitMap::PutAlphaImage` reaches the per-pixel 16/32-bit helpers after the NVC0 staging path declines/fails, the NV10–NV40 GART path is inapplicable/fails, and the NV50 superclass path is inapplicable (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_bitmapclass.c:656-759`). `PutAlphaTemplate` similarly reaches the software helpers unless its Blackwell staging, older 3D alpha upload, or NV50 superclass route succeeds (`:812-908`). The staging callbacks also call the same per-pixel helpers (`:570-590`). Use partial alpha and at least one source channel below its destination value; then `tmp` is negative and its left shift has undefined behavior. The blended result depends on compiler behavior; an optimizing compiler may produce incorrect component values. Replace the signed left shift with defined fixed-point arithmetic using a sufficiently wide signed type and explicit division/rounding. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Nouveau HIDD configurations using these software alpha-image/template paths; the module is not claimed to be part of default images. **Confidence:** high for the reachable software paths and negative operand; the rendered difference depends on compiler output and was not reproduced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10084

**The P96 monitor launcher ignores CLI parse errors and can report success without loading a card.** In CLI mode, `main()` assigns `ReadArgs("CARD/K", ...)` to `rdargs` but never checks for a NULL result (`workbench/devs/monitors/P96/p96.c:88-92`). DOS `ReadArgs()` returns NULL when parsing fails (`rom/dos/readargs.c:917-934`). The launcher then treats a missing `args.card` as an omitted option and infers `Picasso96/<program-name>.card` (`p96.c:94-111`). If that inferred card is absent, the failure path suppresses the error because `deduced` is TRUE and `res` remains `RETURN_OK` (`:130-153`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke the CLI target with malformed syntax (for example, an unrecognized argument) and no `CARD` tooltype. The program ignores the parse failure, tries the filename-derived card, and can exit successfully despite loading nothing; if that guessed card exists, it may load it despite the invalid command. Treat a NULL `ReadArgs()` result as a command error before applying the filename fallback. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable P96/Z3660/ZZ9000 monitor launcher targets (`workbench/devs/monitors/P96/mmakefile.src:20-30`); their parent aggregate entries are commented out, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the NULL return, unchecked result, fallback, and suppressed missing-card status; no launcher or card was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10085

**NListtree reverse searches skip nested descendants.** The ordinary name and user-data search helpers recurse into each list node's child list unless `SameLevel` is set (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:2414-2418,2499-2507`). The reverse helpers do not recurse: they test the current node and walk `GetPred()` through siblings, then move to a parent (`:2432-2473,2517-2550`). Therefore a reverse search starting at the root list never tests descendants of its root children. The same omission occurs when starting at another list node. Both public methods dispatch to these helpers when their respective `Reverse` flag is set (`:8826-8834,8963-8971`; public flags in `workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mui/NListtree_mcc.h:505,516`).

**Trigger and consequence:** call `MUIM_NListtree_FindName` or `MUIM_NListtree_FindUserData` with the reverse flag, omit `SameLevel`, and have the only matching node nested below a child list of the selected list. The call returns NULL even though the forward recursive search can find the node. Add reverse-order recursion into child lists while preserving the selected traversal semantics.

**Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/mmakefile.src:4-18`); default aggregate inclusion is not established here. No checked-in caller of the reverse flag was found. **Confidence:** medium-high. The method docs explicitly define `SameLevel` as the restriction to nodes on the same level, and the forward helpers recurse into descendants when that flag is absent; the reverse helpers omit descendants even when it is absent. The precise reverse traversal order remains undocumented, so this is limited to the missing recursive search coverage rather than a claim about which node must match first. No method call or tree operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10086

**Graphics display handover can dispose a display that still owns live display-ID bitmaps.** The public `DisplayHandover` contract says `dho_ExpungeDisplay()` refuses removal while a display is still in use (`compiler/include/graphics/driver.h:70-76`). The graphics callback only checks `mdd->display` and `mdd->frontbm` (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:262-282`), even though `display_Expunge()` explicitly requires that no bitmaps belonging to the driver exist and then disposes the display object (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:214-216,245-252`). `AllocBitMap()` accepts `BMATags_DisplayID`, resolves the display's driver and mode, and creates a HIDD bitmap through that display object (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:219-226,345-349`). The base bitmap class stores the display pointer without obtaining a reference (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:931-933`), exposes that same pointer through `aHidd_BitMap_Display` (`:1215`), and later passes it to framebuffer updates and color-setting (`:1355,4549-4554,5125-5130`). Its disposal method releases the colormap and pixel format but does not release or otherwise account for the display object (`:1137-1157`). Thus a retained offscreen display-ID bitmap, or a bitmap allocated by an `OpenScreen()` still in progress, can outlive the tracked screen/front bitmap; a later overlapping boot-display handover removes the display object while the bitmap still refers to it, and later bitmap operations can pass the disposed object to display methods.

**Trigger and consequence:** there are two source-supported routes. An offscreen caller can allocate and retain a `BMATags_DisplayID` bitmap while no viewport is loaded for an overlapping boot display, then a handover-enabled driver invokes the expunge callback. More concretely, the selected `OpenScreen()` path allocates its display-ID bitmap at `rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1225-1238` before it calls `DoSyncAction()` to run `int_openscreen()` at `:2297-2303`; that action later builds and loads the viewport (`:2418-2486`; `rom/intuition/rethinkdisplay.c:105-162`; `rom/graphics/loadview.c:55-65`). `display_LoadViewPorts()` assigns `mdd->display` only during that later load (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:511-518`). If handover overlaps this interval, the callback sees both `mdd->display` and `mdd->frontbm` clear and expunges the display, while the in-flight screen bitmap already retains its raw display pointer. `OpenScreen()` does not hold `displaydb_sem` across this interval, so the handover's exclusive display-database lock does not serialize the bitmap construction with removal. The later screen setup can therefore use the disposed display object through the bitmap. On the ordinary completed path, `CloseScreen()` frees its allocated bitmap (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:238-250`); this finding requires the stated overlap before viewport publication, or an offscreen client retaining its bitmap. The compositor's other maintained `BMATags_DisplayID` bitmap is owned and disposed with its compositor. Track live bitmap references and refuse handover until they are released, or invalidate/migrate them as part of expunge. This post-construction object-lifetime issue is distinct from GD5908’s concurrent unpinned `DisplayInfoHandle` lookup and bitmap-construction window. **Affected configuration:** systems using graphics display handover with a boot-mode display; Nouveau contains a selected handover caller (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:310-323`), though its target is optional and default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked bitmap lifetime and the in-flight `OpenScreen()`/handover overlap; actual post-disposal behavior depends on the OOP object manager and whether the scheduling overlap occurs. No display, bitmap, handover, or build was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10087

**SDL keyboard events place the raw key in the flags half of the HIDD event.** `SDLKbd__Hidd_Kbd_SDL__HandleEvent()` writes the raw key and release bit through the ULONG `kbdevt` member (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdl_kbdclass.c:64-75`), while `pHidd_Kbd_Event` overlays that ULONG with `{ UWORD flags; UWORD code; }` (`rom/hidds/kbd/include/keyboard.h:28-37`). On little-endian hosted targets, including the selected Linux x86/x86-64 configurations, this stores the raw key in `flags` and leaves `code` zero. The callback enters keyboard.device's `keyCallback()`, which separately reads those fields, buffers the ULONG, and updates the key matrix using `code` (`rom/devs/keyboard/keyboard.c:608-640`). Its queued-event path later interprets the buffered ULONG as the same union and publishes `evtData.code` as `ie_Code` (`:430-455`). Therefore every SDL key-down and key-up is delivered as raw code zero (Escape), and the matrix treats every event as Escape-down; key releases do not clear the actual key or the Escape matrix bit. The SDL event task dispatches both transitions to this producer (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/event.c:102-109`). Set `flags` and `code` explicitly, as the selected Linux and X11 producers do.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** optional hosted SDL keyboard HIDD on little-endian targets, for any key event. **Consequence:** clients receive Escape instead of the actual raw key, and key state can remain incorrect after release. **Confidence:** high for the union layout and direct producer/consumer path; no SDL event was generated. Source-only.


## GD10088

**ReAction Glyph's CheckMark type draws an empty checkbox instead of a checkmark.** The public Glyph header defines `GLYPH_CHECKMARK` as “Checkmark,” and the Reaction macro aliases `CheckMark` to that value (`compiler/include/images/glyph.h:36`; `compiler/include/reaction/reaction_macros.h:399-404`). The selected `Glyph__IM_DRAW()` dispatches that value to `glyph_draw_checkbox()` (`workbench/classes/reaction/glyph/glyphclass.c:396-397`), whose complete drawing routine only draws the four border edges and optionally fills the interior; it never draws a tick or other check mark (`:145-166`). The selected state changes the foreground/background pens but does not alter that geometry. Render a `glyph.image` with `GLYPH_Glyph=GLYPH_CHECKMARK` and callers receive an empty checkbox outline instead of the advertised checkmark. Implement the check stroke for this glyph type or give checkbox rendering a separate glyph ID.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** explicitly buildable optional `workbench-classes-reaction-glyph` target, when a client renders the public `GLYPH_CHECKMARK`/`CheckMark` image. The target is not established as part of the default aggregate in this snapshot, and no checked-in caller requests it. **Consequence:** UI clients relying on the checkmark glyph cannot visually indicate checked state with this image. **Confidence:** high for the enum name, alias, dispatch and full helper geometry; no glyph was rendered. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10089

**MUI ARexx dispatch ignores argument-setup failures and can invoke a command hook with invalid arguments.** For a configured command with `mc_Template`, `Application__MUIM_NewInput()` allocates an argument buffer with `AllocVec()` and immediately passes the result to `CopyMem()` and writes through it without checking for allocation failure (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1726-1731`). If that succeeds but `AllocDosObject(DOS_RDARGS, NULL)` fails, the code skips initialization of the `args` VLA, then still calls the command hook with that uninitialized array (`:1733-1753`). If `ReadArgs()` fails, including for bad syntax or allocation failure, its NULL result is likewise ignored and the hook is still invoked with zeroed or partially parsed arguments (`:1744-1753`). The public MUI header defines `MUI_RXERR_OUTOFMEMORY` and `MUI_RXERR_BADSYNTAX`, but this path does not return those errors (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui.h:657-670`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an application configures a `MUIA_Application_Commands` entry with a non-NULL template and receives a matching ARexx command while argument-buffer/DOS-object allocation fails, or with arguments that fail `ReadArgs()` parsing. Allocation failure at the `AllocVec()` call can lead to a write through a NULL destination; failure to allocate `RDArgs` or parse arguments still invokes the hook, which may read invalid parameters or perform an action with incomplete values. Check each allocation and `ReadArgs()` result, and skip the hook or return the matching `MUI_RXERR_*` status on failure.

**Affected configuration:** the selected MUI Application class when an application configures ARexx commands through `MUIA_Application_Commands` and a command has an argument template (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.h:202-203`). A repository-wide search found no maintained caller of this attribute. **Confidence:** high that allocation/parse failures do not stop dispatch; the null write and invalid hook arguments require the corresponding failure and a hook that uses those arguments. No ARexx message or allocation failure was exercised. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10090

**The m68k emulator does not dispatch several public Intuition vectors.** The checked-in generated and manual Intuition tables omit these public functions, despite their declarations in `rom/intuition/intuition.conf`: `DrawBorder()` at byte offset 108 (line 70), `PrintIText()` at 216 (line 88), `IntuiTextLength()` at 330 (line 107), `BuildSysRequest()` at 360 (line 112), `AllocRemember()` at 396 (line 118), `FreeRemember()` at 408 (line 120), `EasyRequestArgs()` at 588 (line 152), `BuildEasyRequestArgs()` at 594 (line 154), and `OpenScreenTagList()` at 612 (line 158). `FreeMonitorList()` at -972 (the next six-byte vector after `GetMonitorList()` at -966) is also absent: the generated table ends this range at `{ 966, thunk_intuition_GetMonitorList }` (`rom/intuition/intuition.conf:215-216`; `m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:6112-6118,7895-7898`). Generated-table gaps are visible between DrawImage 114 and its predecessor, OpenWorkBench 210 and RefreshGadgets 222, SetPrefs 324 and WBenchToBack 336, BeginRefresh 354 and EndRefresh 366, RethinkDisplay 390 and AlohaWorkbench 402, and GetDefaultPubScreen 582 and SysReqHandler 600 (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:7780-7782,7793-7795,7809-7815,7819-7824,7850-7852`). `OpenScreenTagList()` is also absent between the manual OpenWindowTagList entry at 606 and generated DrawImageState at 618 (`m68kemu_thunks.c:1450-1461`; `m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:7851-7853`). None has a manual dispatch entry (`m68kemu_thunks.c:1450-1461`). The current generator `SKIP_FUNCTIONS` set does not include these names, and this source comparison does not establish whether their omissions originate in the upstream FD input or thunk-generation process. The separate `VOID_FUNCTIONS` set includes `DrawBorder()`, `PrintIText()`, and `FreeRemember()`, but that set only controls return-stub generation and does not explain why their wrappers are absent. The emulator's unimplemented-LVO path returns zero without calling the native function (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_moira.cpp:280-290`). Native implementations exist for the requester and screen-tag APIs (`rom/intuition/easyrequestargs.c:15-24,60-77`; `buildeasyrequestargs.c:58-63`; `buildsysrequest.c:14-23`; `openscreentaglist.c:15-21`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an emulated m68k client calls any listed Intuition vector. Drawing calls produce no output; `IntuiTextLength()` reports zero; `BuildSysRequest()` and `BuildEasyRequestArgs()` return NULL without creating a requester; `AllocRemember()` returns NULL and `FreeRemember()` does not release remembered allocations; `EasyRequestArgs()` does not show or handle a requester and returns zero (which its native contract also uses for a button choice/error); `OpenScreenTagList()` does not open a screen and returns NULL. `FreeMonitorList()` does not release the array returned by `GetMonitorList()`, retaining that allocation until process/system teardown if a guest can hold and pass the returned pointer. However, the paired `GetMonitorList()` thunk also returns a raw native pointer without guest shadow conversion (covered separately by EK9432), so a normal guest-side obtain/free path is not established. The requester/screen pointer returns would additionally require guest-compatible shadow conversion if wrappers were added. **Scope qualification:** the native `BuildSysRequest()` family is itself documented as unsupported by `FreeSysRequest()` and `SysReqHandler()`; that API's emulation omission may therefore be intentional or redundant with native limitations, and is retained only as a coverage candidate.

**Affected configuration:** the optional m68k emulator using the checked-in Intuition thunk tables. **Confidence:** high that the public declarations have no generated/manual dispatch and the unimplemented path returns zero; impact is conditional on guest use of each API. No emulated caller or GUI operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10091

**Generic HIDD construction publishes a display with no name when copying aoHidd_Name fails.** HIDDCl__Root__New() initializes hd_Name to the non-NULL unknown sentinel, but when a non-NULL aoHidd_Name tag is supplied it overwrites that field with StrDup()'s result without checking for allocation failure or failing object construction (rom/hidds/hidd/hiddclass.c:278-299). StrDup() returns NULL when its AllocVec() fails (compiler/alib/strdup.c:16-58), so the superclass constructor returns a live HIDD object with hd_Name == NULL. The generic display constructor supplies a non-NULL aHidd_Name (the caller's tag or its "Generic Display" fallback) to that superclass (rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:361-373). Intuition's MonitorClass__OM_NEW() copies the resulting attribute into IMonitorNode.MonitorName and publishes the node in MonitorList without checking it (rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:267-275). Name lookup uses Exec FindName(), which deliberately skips nodes whose ln_Name is NULL, so the published display cannot be resolved by monitor name (rom/intuition/findmonitor.c:48-55,111-133; rom/exec/findname.c:82-92).

**Trigger and consequence:** allocation failure while the generic HIDD superclass duplicates the non-NULL name of a display object that Intuition then registers. The display's modes may remain available by other identifiers, but name-based monitor selection such as OpenScreen() cannot find that display and can fail or select a fallback monitor. Reject the object when name duplication fails, or preserve a valid fallback name and propagate the allocation status. **Affected configuration:** systems using the generic HIDD and graphics display classes with Intuition monitor registration; the display constructor always provides a name unless the caller's tag supplies one. **Confidence:** high for the NULL publication and name-lookup behavior; occurrence and user-visible impact are conditional on the name-copy allocation failure. No allocation failure, display registration, or screen open was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10092

**The generic keyboard input subsystem can lose or corrupt events queued before its first consumer registers on ExecSMP.** The `CLID_HW_Input` instance initializes one shared pending count and a fixed event array (`rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:163-167`; layout in `rom/hidds/input/input.h:31-38`). When there are no consumers, both the injected driver callback and `PushEvent()` call `InputHW__BufferPendingEvent()` (`inputsubsystem.c:94-106,240-251`). That routine reads `ihd_pendingcnt` to choose a slot, copies the event, and increments the count without a lock or atomic operation (`:79-92`). `HW_AddDriver()` supports multiple producer objects and supplies the generic callback when a driver does not provide its own (`:204-237`; generic driver registration in `rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:135-205`). The keyboard HIDD documents that its callbacks run inside interrupts (`rom/hidds/kbd/kbdclass.c:28-56`). On ExecSMP, two producer callbacks on different CPUs can therefore read the same count and write the same slot, or lose one of their increments. The first consumer replays only the count and slots visible to `InputHW_FlushPendingEvents()` (`inputsubsystem.c:116-126`). Its registration uses `Disable()` around list insertion and replay, but Exec documents that Disable is processor-local on SMP (`rom/hidds/input/inputclass.c:197-204`; `rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`), so it does not serialize remote producers with the shared pending buffer.

**Trigger and consequence:** an ExecSMP build using the optional `kernel-hidd-input` target, with at least two keyboard hardware producers delivering events on different CPUs before the first input consumer registers (or while pending events are being replayed). Pending key events can overwrite one another or be replayed from an incomplete count, losing or corrupting early input. Protect pending-buffer updates and the replay/reset operation with an SMP-safe lock or equivalent serialization. **Affected configuration:** ExecSMP systems that select `kernel-hidd-input`; the Raspberry Pi package manifest lists this module as optional/commented, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high that the shared queue is unsynchronized and Disable is local on SMP; the event-loss manifestation requires overlapping producers during the no-consumer/replay window. No input event or SMP interleaving was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10093

**The generic input HIDD can free a consumer while another CPU is calling it from an input interrupt.** `InputHW__CallBackFunc()` walks the shared consumer list and calls each node's callback without a lock (`rom/hidds/input/inputsubsystem.c:94-113`); the `PushEvent()` method has the same unlocked traversal (`:240-256`). `Input__Root__Dispose()` removes a consumer under `Disable()` and then calls the superclass disposer (`rom/hidds/input/inputclass.c:240-252`), which ends the object's lifetime. The matching insertion path also uses only `Disable()` (`:197-204`). Exec documents that on ExecSMP, `Disable()` affects only the local processor and shared parallel state needs a spinlock (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`). The class API documents that input callbacks run in interrupt context (`inputclass.c:76-77`). Thus, while one CPU is traversing and has read a consumer node, another CPU can dispose that consumer; the first CPU can then read the freed node's successor or callback fields and invoke a stale callback/private pointer.

**Trigger and consequence:** an ExecSMP build selecting the optional `kernel-hidd-input` target, with an input event callback running on one CPU while another CPU disposes the corresponding `CLID_Hidd_Input` consumer. The fanout can access freed consumer state or invoke a callback after its owner has torn down. Serialize list traversal against insertion/removal with an SMP-safe mechanism and ensure disposal waits for active callbacks to finish. **Affected configuration:** ExecSMP systems that use this optional input HIDD; no default-image package inclusion or maintained in-tree concurrent-disposal sequence was established. **Confidence:** high for the unprotected cross-CPU list/lifetime window; manifestation requires callback/disposal overlap. No input event, dispose operation, or SMP interleaving was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

**`GenTaskName()` dereferences a NULL result when its name allocation fails.** The helper assigns `AllocVec(...)` directly to `newName` and unconditionally passes it as the destination of `sprintf()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationclass.c:116-122`). `AllocVec()` returns NULL when its underlying `AllocMem()` fails (`rom/exec/allocvec.c:48-61`). ## GD10096

**Ignored damage-region insertions can leave resized relative gadgets or window borders outside the redraw region.** Before resizing, `WindowSizeWillChange()` asks `EraseRelGadgetArea(..., onlydamagelist = FALSE)` to add each old relative-gadget rectangle and then erase it (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_actions.c:135-221`; `rom/intuition/gadgets.c:550-565`). After relayout, `WindowSizeHasChanged()` adds the new gadget bounds with `onlydamagelist = TRUE` (`inputhandler_actions.c:229-297`). Both calls ultimately ignore `OrRectRegion()`'s Boolean result in `EraseRelGadgetArea()` and set `LAYERREFRESH` anyway. The surrounding resize code also ignores `OrRectRegion()` when adding old right/bottom border areas before the resize and new right/top/bottom border areas after it (`inputhandler_actions.c:177-196,276-317`). `OrRectRegion()` returns FALSE when its rectangle/node allocation fails and leaves the destination region unchanged (`rom/graphics/orrectregion.c:87-107`).

The resize ends by calling `CheckLayers()`, which routes flagged layers through `WindowNeedsRefresh()` (`inputhandler_actions.c:103-119,552`). For a simple-refresh window, the refresh uses clip rectangles built from `DamageList`; it does not add a failed gadget or border rectangle itself (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_support.c:1203-1256`; `rom/hyperlayers/beginupdate.c:67-100`). If an omitted rectangle was not already damaged, the new relative gadget or resized border can be left stale/blank; the pre-resize gadget path can also erase its old bounds without a corresponding refresh. The failure does not affect `LAYERSUPER` gadget insertion, which is deliberately skipped.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** selected Intuition/layers builds, when a window resize inserts old/new relative-gadget or frame rectangles into a non-super simple-refresh layer and `OrRectRegion()` cannot allocate. **Consequence:** Intuition sets the refresh flag but the rectangle is absent from the damage/clip region, so erased old content or new gadget/frame bounds may not be repainted. **Confidence:** high for the ignored results and refresh route; visible impact depends on allocation failure and prior damage state. No resize or allocation failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10097

**64-bit Font datatype scans past the end of a malformed `.otag` file looking for `TAG_DONE`.** After allocating and reading exactly `FileLen` bytes into `tmptags`, the 64-bit path increments `tagcnt` until `tmptags[tagcnt << 1] == TAG_DONE` without checking that another complete tag remains in the file (`workbench/classes/datatypes/font/otag.c:129-150`). For a truncated or malformed `.otag` file with no terminator among its complete tag records, the parser reads successive words beyond the `FileLen` allocation while counting tags. A file shorter than one tag also enters the scan and reads from the undersized allocation.
