## GD10134 — Nouveau mode enumeration dereferences failed tag allocations

`HIDDNouveauCreateSyncTagsFromConnector()` allocates the outer mode-tag array, one 15-item sync-tag array per connector mode, and a 32-byte description string without checking any result (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:144-155,202-207,225-234`). The selected allocator returns NULL when its underlying `AllocMem()` fails (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_init.c:182-199`). With one or more connector modes, failure of the outer allocation reaches `syncs[i]`/`syncs[modescount]`; failure of a per-mode allocation reaches `sync[j]`; failure of a name allocation reaches `sprintf(syncname, ...)`. The caller's later NULL check (`nouveau_hiddclass.c:483-490`) cannot handle these failures because the helper has already dereferenced the failed pointer.

**Trigger and consequence:** while Nouveau constructs display mode tags for a connected connector with at least one mode, any of these allocations fails. The fault occurs synchronously inside `Nouveau::Root::New()`, which graphics.library reaches through `HW_AddDriver()` while processing `AddDisplayDriverA()` (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:369-398`). It therefore prevents the normal constructor-failure result from reaching the caller; the precise system-level response depends on the task context in which registration is requested. **Affected configuration:** explicitly enabled Nouveau HIDD builds using the selected source list; Nouveau is optional and excluded from the default aggregate (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-28,274-310`). **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocator results and subsequent writes; manifestation depends on allocation failure and a connector with modes. Check every allocation and unwind any already-created per-mode tags before returning failure. No allocation failure, display registration, or build was run; source-only.


## GD10135 — Nouveau leaks dynamically allocated display-mode tag lists

When the selected connector has modes, `HIDDNouveauCreateSyncTagsFromConnector()` allocates an outer `TagItem` list, a 15-item list for every mode, and a 32-byte description for every mode (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:144-155,202-234`). `Nouveau::Root::New()` passes the outer list through `TAG_MORE` in its local `modetags`, then supplies that list to `OOP_NewObject()` for the display (`:531-535,613-626`). The selected display constructor synchronously constructs its mode enumerator (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:418-445`); `register_modes()` walks the tag list and creates Sync objects (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:519-552`), and the Sync constructor copies the description text into its embedded `sync_data.description` buffer while parsing the scalar mode values (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_syncclass.c:199-250`). The Nouveau arrays and strings are therefore temporary inputs and are not retained by the created objects. The local `syncs` pointer is not stored in the Nouveau instance, and the constructor has no `HIDDNouveauFree()` cleanup for the outer array, per-mode arrays, or strings; the source itself labels the `TAG_MORE` list as leaking (`nouveau_hiddclass.c:534`). In the ordinary allocator implementation, `HIDDNouveauAlloc()` obtains these blocks with `AllocMem()` and only `HIDDNouveauFree()` releases them (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_init.c:178-205`). `Nouveau_Exit()` only deletes the separate allocator pool (`:84-91`), and the library config is `noexpunge` (`nouveau.conf:1-5`), so neither normal driver-object disposal nor ordinary library lifecycle reclaims the tag allocations.

**Trigger and consequence:** Nouveau mode-tag construction runs for a selected connector with one or more modes. Every such construction permanently retains the helper's outer list, each per-mode list, and each mode-name string after the display constructor has consumed them. Repeated driver construction/retry or teardown/reinitialization accumulates the allocations; even a single initialization leaves the corresponding memory unavailable. **Affected configuration:** explicitly enabled optional Nouveau HIDD builds; Nouveau is excluded from the default package graph (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-28,274-310`). **Confidence:** high for the allocations, synchronous copy/consumption, and absence of retained ownership or frees; frequency depends on how often the optional driver is constructed. Free the temporary allocations after the synchronous display/mode-enumerator construction returns, including constructor-failure paths. No display registration, teardown, allocation accounting, GPU operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10136 — Nouveau continues after client allocation fails and retains a NULL client

`Nouveau::Root::New()` initializes its local `nvclient` to NULL, calls `nouveau_client_new(nvdev, &nvclient)`, and ignores the return value (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:417-418,467`). The selected implementation returns `-ENOMEM` when its `calloc()` fails and does not write `*pclient` on that path (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/libdrm/nouveau/nouveau.c:531-541`), so the root constructor continues with `nvclient == NULL`. It later stores this pointer in `carddata->client` without a check (`nouveau_hiddclass.c:601-609`).

The next acceleration setup can dereference the null client if channel creation succeeds: `NVAccelCommonInit()` calls `nouveau_pushbuf_new(pNv->client, ...)` (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/xf86-video-nouveau/nv_accel_common.c:674-688`), and `nouveau_pushbuf_new()` reads `client->device` before checking any argument (`libdrm/nouveau/nouveau.c:1555-1565`). If acceleration setup returns failure earlier, Nouveau only logs that it will run unaccelerated and continues construction (`nouveau_hiddclass.c:705-708`). A later cursor-shape request is another selected path: `NouveauDisplay::SetCursorShape()` calls `nouveau_bo_map()` with `carddata->client` (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_displayclass.c:409-413`); `nouveau_bo_wait()` passes a write access into `cli_push_get()`, which dereferences the client (`libdrm/nouveau/nouveau.c:763-774,916-929; :872-879`).

**Trigger and consequence:** after Nouveau has opened the DRM device, allocation of `struct nouveau_client_priv` in `nouveau_client_new()` fails. The unchecked result leaves a null client in the graphics object; startup can fault during acceleration initialization, or a later cursor operation can dereference NULL. **Affected configuration:** explicitly enabled optional Nouveau HIDD when this client allocation fails; Nouveau is excluded from the default package graph (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-28,274-310`). **Confidence:** high for the allocator failure return, ignored status, stored null pointer and selected dereference paths; whether failure occurs before the constructor's other resource allocations is conditional. Check the result and unwind/abort object construction before publishing the client pointer. No allocation failure, display registration, cursor request, GPU operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10137 — Nouveau leaks DRM and connector resources when root construction fails

After opening the DRM device and creating a Nouveau device and client, `Nouveau::Root::New()` has several failure returns with no matching cleanup (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:451-477,483-490,597-775`). If connector/CRTC selection fails, the helper frees its temporary mode resources, but the root constructor returns without deleting `nvclient`/`nvdev` or closing the DRM file descriptor. If sync-tag creation returns NULL, the selected connector, client, device and DRM descriptor remain live. This includes a selected connector that is reported `DRM_MODE_CONNECTED` but has `count_modes == 0`: connector selection stops at the first connected connector without checking its mode count (`nouveau_hiddclass.c:71-85`), and the tag helper explicitly returns NULL for zero modes (`:144-151`). If the graphics superclass constructor returns NULL, the selected connector and dynamically allocated sync tags also remain allocated. The class explicitly notes that its `Dispose` cleanup is unimplemented (`nouveau_hiddclass.c:778-779`). `nouveau_device_del()` frees only the Nouveau device wrapper (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/libdrm/nouveau/nouveau.c:493-502`); the DRM descriptor is separately closed in the earlier, pre-device setup error path (`nouveau_hiddclass.c:455-461`), showing it requires its own cleanup.

**Trigger and consequence:** Nouveau has successfully opened DRM and created its device/client, then connector selection fails (for example, no connected connector), sync-tag construction returns NULL (including a connector with no modes), or the graphics superclass constructor fails. Root creation returns NULL while retaining those resources; retries or repeated registration attempts accumulate device/client allocations and open DRM references, and selected later failure branches additionally retain the connector and sync-tag allocations. **Affected configuration:** explicitly enabled optional Nouveau HIDD builds; Nouveau remains excluded from the default package graph (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-28,274-310`). **Confidence:** high for the missing cleanup on each listed post-open failure return and separate ownership of the DRM descriptor; accumulation depends on repeated failed construction. Route post-open exits through a cleanup path that frees resources according to which construction stages succeeded. No display registration, induced failure, descriptor count, GPU operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10138 — Gallium NULL screen destruction tears down live driver state

`gallium.library` documents that `DestroyPipeScreen(pipe, NULL)` ignores a NULL screen, but its vector always dispatches `moHidd_Gallium_DestroyPipeScreen` with `.screen = pscreen` (`workbench/libs/gallium/destroypipescreen.c:20-27,40-45`). The selected optional Raspberry Pi overrides guard only the screen-specific destroy: V3D then unconditionally decrements `sd->screen_count`, treats zero as the last screen, and calls `v3d_release_all_bos()` plus per-session reset (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/v3d/v3d_galliumclass.c:465-503`). With one live screen, a documented NULL no-op therefore sweeps that screen's BOs and resets state under it. VC4 similarly guards `screen->destroy()` but always calls `aros_drm_release_bridge()` (`vc4_galliumclass.c:338-385`); with one live screen, the bridge count reaches zero and the caller releases all BOs and resets shared V3D/scanout state while the screen remains live. With multiple screens, the bridge helper also clears shared overlay bookkeeping before decrementing (`aros_drm_vc4.c:790-819`), so a NULL call can disturb live presentation state even when it does not trigger the final sweep.

**Trigger and consequence:** a client invokes the public vector with a valid pipe and a NULL screen, as the API documentation explicitly permits. On either selected driver this can prematurely release resources belonging to still-live screens, corrupt their subsequent rendering/presentation, or leave bookkeeping inconsistent. The checked-in Mesa callers found in this pass guard against NULL, so no maintained in-tree NULL invocation is claimed. **Affected configuration:** optional native Raspberry Pi V3D and VC4 Gallium HIDD targets (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/v3d/mmakefile.src:249-253`; `.../vc4gallium/mmakefile.src:15-19,313-315`); their aggregate dependency edges are commented, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high that the documented NULL contract is violated by both overrides and that the one-live-screen bookkeeping paths reach shared teardown; whether an external or future client exercises the permitted NULL call is unverified. Return immediately for NULL before changing screen counts or shared driver state. No NULL call, display, allocation failure, GPU operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10139 — GL context setup dereferences a failed RastPort clone

Both selected GLA backends clone the selected RastPort in their standard setup helper and immediately dereference the returned pointer without checking it. `MESA3DGLStandardInit()` assigns `CloneRastPort(ctx->visible_rp)` then reads `ctx->visible_rp->Layer->bounds` (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa3dgl_support.c:237-256`); `HostGLStandardInit()` does the same (`arch/all-hosted/libs/hostgl/hostgl_support.c:100-118`). `CloneRastPort()` explicitly returns NULL when its `AllocMem()` fails (`compiler/arossupport/clonerastport.c:27-30,49-54`). In both backends, `glACreateContext()` reaches the helper after selecting a RastPort (`mesa3dgl_glacreatecontext.c:138-150`; `hostgl_glacreatecontext.c:138-150`), and `glASetRast()` frees its prior clone, selects the replacement RastPort, then calls the helper (`mesa3dgl_glasetrast.c:52-68`; `hostgl_glasetrast.c:62-74`). Neither caller handles clone failure before the helper dereferences NULL.

**Trigger and consequence:** allocation of the small RastPort structure fails during context creation or target replacement. The process faults while reading `visible_rp->Layer`, rather than returning a failed context or preserving a usable old target. In `glASetRast()`, the previously owned clone has already been freed, so the context has no valid visible RastPort before the fault. **Affected configurations:** explicitly built `mesa3dgl.library` and optional hosted `hostgl.library` targets; Mesa3DGL is outside the general Workbench aggregate dependency (`workbench/libs/mesa/mmakefile.src:27-31,65-97,114-119`), and HostGL's aggregate edge is optional/commented (`arch/all-hosted/libs/hostgl/mmakefile.src:6-10`), so default-image inclusion is not claimed for either. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked NULL result and selected create/set-raster callers; allocation failure is conditional. Check the clone result and return an ordinary setup failure, with `glASetRast()` retaining or restoring the previous target until replacement succeeds. No allocation failure, context operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10140 — Wanderer dereferences a missing AppIcon DiskObject during position propagation

`IconList__MUIM_IconList_PositionIcons()` calls the selected `MUIM_IconList_PropagateEntryPos` override for each visible entry (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Classes/iconlist.c:2203-2232`). The IconWindowVolumeList override checks `WBAPPICONA_PropagatePosition` and then calls `AppIcon_GetDiskObject()`; it unconditionally writes `do_CurrentX` and `do_CurrentY` through the returned pointer (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow_volumelist.c:1308-1324`). `AppIcon_GetDiskObject()` looks up the pointer under the Workbench lock and returns NULL if it is no longer in the AppIcon list (`workbench/system/Wanderer/appobjects.c:145-160`).

`RemoveAppIcon()` unlinks the AppIcon under that same lock and frees it immediately after unlocking (`workbench/libs/workbench/removeappicon.c:60-66`). Therefore removal can occur after `AppIcon_Supports()` returns true but before `AppIcon_GetDiskObject()` performs its lookup. The checked lookup then returns NULL and the position callback dereferences it. Sorting calls `PositionIcons()` after rebuilding the list (`iconlist.c:7548-7568`), so this callback is reached by a selected in-tree operation while an AppIcon entry remains in the list ahead of the asynchronous refresh.

**Trigger and consequence:** a visible root AppIcon advertises `WBAPPICONA_PropagatePosition`, and another task removes it between the support check and DiskObject lookup while sorting or positioning is in progress. Wanderer's position callback faults on the NULL DiskObject result. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting Workbench and Wanderer's IconList/VolumeList modules; requires concurrent AppIcon removal and a visible propagating AppIcon. **Confidence:** high for the nullable lookup, unchecked dereference, and selected PositionIcons caller; the interleaving is conditional. Check the getter result and coordinate updates against removal under a shared lifetime lock. No AppIcon operation, race, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10141 — Wanderer can leave an IconWindow stuck open when deferred close allocation fails

Wanderer installs a `MUIA_Window_CloseRequest` notification on non-workbench IconWindows that calls `MUIM_IconWindow_RequestClose` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:4044-4049`). The request handler returns early if `IWDFLAG_CLOSING` is already set, otherwise sets that flag and queues `MUIM_IconWindow_Remove` through `MUIM_Application_PushMethod` without checking the result (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow.c:1401-1423`). The MUI queue method returns zero when its `CreateMQNode()` allocation fails, before adding any method to the queue (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:1893-1918,222-234`). The only removal that closes the native window, removes the application member and disposes the object is the queued `MUIM_IconWindow_Remove` (`iconwindow.c:1427-1444`). MUI consumes `IDCMP_CLOSEWINDOW` and raises `MUIA_Window_CloseRequest`; it does not close the window automatically (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:1775-1779,3387-3389`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a user closes a non-workbench Wanderer IconWindow while allocation of the application's method-queue node fails. The window's `IWDFLAG_CLOSING` remains set, but no removal method is queued. Subsequent close requests hit the early return, so the window remains open and cannot be closed through this path until another application-level teardown occurs. Clear the flag if queuing fails or perform a safe synchronous close/removal fallback. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-system-wanderer-app` target with its IconWindow class; the parent `workbench-system` edge is commented in this revision (`workbench/system/Wanderer/mmakefile.src:23-37`), so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the ignored zero result, flag ordering, close-request dispatch, and missing retry path; manifestation requires method-node allocation failure during a close request. No allocation failure, window close, or build was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10142 — NListtree retains stale disclosure state after a canceled click

`_HandleEvent()` stores `data->OpenCloseEntry` when SELECTDOWN lands on a list node's tree image (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:5827-5842`). The mouse-button handling, including SELECTUP cleanup, is nested inside `_isinobject(mx, my)` (`:5784-5790`); a release outside the widget therefore does not clear the stored pointer. The SELECTUP path also does not check that the release is over the same entry: for any valid row it toggles `OpenCloseEntry`, then clears it (`:5899-5930`). A later in-widget click that does not hit a disclosure image leaves the old pointer untouched on SELECTDOWN, so its SELECTUP can open or close the node from the canceled click instead of the row clicked.

The stale value can also become a dangling pointer: `MUIM_NListtree_Remove` reaches `RemoveNodes()` and `RemoveNode2()`, which unlinks and frees the tree node from `TreePool` (`NListtree.c:2319-2351,7534-7667`). Neither removal nor the outside-release branch clears `OpenCloseEntry`; a subsequent valid in-widget SELECTUP reads `tn_Flags` through that freed pointer (`:5921-5926`). The node must be removed after the first release-outside gesture and before the later in-widget release for this lifetime consequence.

**Trigger and consequence:** in a build selecting `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/mmakefile.src:4-19`), press on a node disclosure image, release outside the widget, then later complete a mouse click inside the widget. The stale node may be toggled unexpectedly; if it was removed in between, the event handler dereferences freed pooled storage and may fault or act on reused memory. Clear the pending node on every button release/cancel and verify it is still a member before dereferencing. **Confidence:** high for the pointer assignment, missing cleanup, toggle path, and node free; the UI event sequence is conditional and was not run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10143 — EGL surfaceless and pbuffer contexts fail because no RastPort is supplied

The AROS EGL backend advertises `KHR_surfaceless_context` and configures surfaceless displays for `EGL_PBUFFER_BIT` (`workbench/libs/egl/egl_arosmesa.c:281-287,322-327`). Its pbuffer constructor stores the requested width/height but creates no bitmap or RastPort (`:231-253`). During `eglMakeCurrent`, the surfaceless branch builds GLA tags containing only width, height and rendering options (`:153-172`); it never supplies `GLA_RastPort`. `glACreateContext()` calls `MESA3DGLSelectRastPort()` and returns failure when `ctx->visible_rp` is NULL (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa3dgl_glacreatecontext.c:138-143`). The EGL callback then leaves `eglctx->amesactx` NULL and returns `EGL_FALSE` (`egl_arosmesa.c:153-204`). The same missing-target path applies to an EGL_NO_SURFACE surfaceless context, using its default 1x1 dimensions.

**Trigger and consequence:** initialize the explicitly built AROS EGL backend on `_EGL_PLATFORM_SURFACELESS`, create a pbuffer or surfaceless context, and call `eglMakeCurrent()`. The advertised configuration cannot become current, so offscreen EGL clients fail before rendering. **Affected configuration:** the optional `workbench-libs-egl` backend with its surfaceless platform enabled (`workbench/libs/egl/mmakefile.src:12-59`); no default aggregate inclusion is claimed because `workbench/libs/mmakefile:22` comments out the EGL edge. **Confidence:** high for the missing RastPort tag, the GLA NULL rejection and the false return. No pbuffer or context was created. Provide an offscreen bitmap/RastPort to GLA or stop advertising pbuffer/surfaceless support until that target exists. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10144 — EGL swap buffers uses one display-wide context for every task

`egl_arosmesa_makecurrent()` stores the selected task's `GLAContext` in `_EGLDisplay.DriverData` after `glAMakeCurrent()` (`workbench/libs/egl/egl_arosmesa.c:116-204`, especially `:196-200`); replacing or unbinding a context clears that same display field (`:129-150`). `egl_arosmesa_swapbuffers()` ignores its `draw` surface argument and passes the display field to `glASwapBuffers()` (`:103-112`). But Mesa's current GL context is task-local: the selected GLA `glAMakeCurrent()` uses the current state-tracker context, `glAGetCurrentContext()` reads the current context, and the Mesa AROS patch routes the GLAPI current-context slot through per-thread pthread keys (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa3dgl_glamakecurrent.c:38-60`; `glagetcurrentcontext.c:35-40`; `mesa-26.0.0-aros.diff`, `glapi.h` and `shared-glapi/core.c` hunks). A single pointer in the display object cannot represent those separate task-current contexts.

**Trigger and consequence:** two AROS tasks make distinct EGL contexts current on the same EGL display; after the second bind updates `DriverData`, the first task calls `eglSwapBuffers()`. The callback flushes and presents the other task's GLA context and RastPort instead of the caller's context. If either task unbinds, it clears the shared field and a still-bound task's subsequent swap is silently skipped. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built AROS EGL plus Mesa3DGL, with multiple tasks using contexts from one display; the EGL aggregate edge is commented out of the general library list. **Confidence:** high for the display-field write/read and task-local GL current-context model; the wrong-context result follows from the callback's explicit pointer use. No multi-task EGL operation was run. Resolve the context from the calling task's EGL current binding or pass the correct context into the swap callback; do not store it in display-wide state. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10145 — Destroying an unbound EGL context detaches a different current GLA context

When the EGL destroy callback releases its final `_EGLContext` reference, it checks only whether the context being destroyed has an AROS GLA context, then unconditionally calls `glAMakeCurrent(NULL)` before destroying that object (`workbench/libs/egl/egl_arosmesa.c:75-87`). `glAMakeCurrent(NULL)` detaches the calling task's current state-tracker/GLAPI context (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa3dgl_glamakecurrent.c:38-60`); it does not select by the `eglctx->amesactx` being destroyed. EGL `MakeCurrent` establishes the caller's own current binding separately (`egl_arosmesa.c:116-204`), and the AROS Mesa GLAPI current-context slot is task-local (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa-26.0.0-aros.diff`, `shared-glapi/core.c` hunk).

**Trigger and consequence:** a task initializes EGL context A by making it current, unbinds A, then makes a different context B current and destroys A. When the EGL core releases A's final reference and invokes this callback, `eglctx->amesactx` is non-NULL and the callback detaches B from the calling task before freeing A. Subsequent GL calls on B lose their current-context binding until B is made current again. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built AROS EGL and Mesa3DGL, when destroying an initialized context that is no longer current while another GLA context is current in the same task; neither optional library's general aggregate edge is enabled here. **Confidence:** high for the unconditional task-current detach and its target; medium-high for the callback trigger, which depends on the imported EGL core invoking destroy after the object's final unbound reference. The fetched Mesa EGL core implementation is not part of this checkout, so that reference-release contract was not independently source-audited here. No context was created or destroyed. Only detach the GLA context if the current task's context is the one being destroyed. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10146 — EGL initialization passes an unchecked config allocation into Mesa helpers [medium impact, medium confidence; optional EGL]

`create_configs()` allocates `_EGLConfig` with `calloc()` but never checks the result before passing it to `_eglInitConfig()`, setting its fields and keys, and finally `_eglLinkConfig()` (`workbench/libs/egl/egl_arosmesa.c:276-296`). It returns `void`; `egl_arosmesa_initialize()` continues to set client APIs/extensions and returns `EGL_TRUE` without receiving a config-creation result (`:317-332`).

**Trigger and consequence:** memory allocation fails while initializing an EGL display. A NULL config is passed through the config setup/registration sequence without a local failure path; if the imported Mesa helpers require a non-NULL config, initialization faults, and if they tolerate it, the backend can still report success without a usable config. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built optional AROS EGL backend. **Confidence:** medium for the unchecked allocation and missing local error propagation; the exact NULL behavior of `_eglInitConfig()`, `_eglSetConfigKey()` and `_eglLinkConfig()` is not confirmed because Mesa 26's EGL core implementation is fetched at build time and not present in this checkout. Return an initialization failure when config allocation or setup fails. No allocation failure, display initialization or build was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10147 — LayoutIconA publishes a partially flood-filled backfill image when Flood runs out of scanline slots

For selected gadget-backfill images, `LayoutIconA()` creates a bitmap with a one-pixel border, draws the selected image, then calls `Flood(&rp, 1, 0, 0)` to replace the connected border color before copying the result into the icon bitmap (`workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c:271-305`). `Flood()` uses a fixed 100-entry scanline stack (`rom/graphics/flood.c:362-369`). If the fill topology requires another pending span when the stack is full, `filline()` returns `FALSE` immediately (`:376-388,439-441,459-461,497-499,517-519`), leaving queued spans unprocessed after already writing part of the fill. `LayoutIconA()` ignores the return value and unconditionally copies the partially processed bitmap (`layouticon.c:304-305`), then continues through the success path and can return TRUE (`:476-482`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an icon with `GFLG_GADGBACKFILL` and a selected image whose connected backfill region requires more than 100 pending scanline spans. The remaining border-colored areas are copied into the generated icon image even though `LayoutIconA()` reports success. **Affected configuration:** AROS builds selecting `workbench/libs/icon/layouticon.c`; the path is conditional on the icon's backfill flag and image geometry. The only checked-in `Flood()` production caller uses a plain RastPort and does not establish this topology; the trigger is supplied through icon data/API use. **Confidence:** high for the fixed-capacity failure return, ignored result and unconditional copy; exact image geometry is conditional and was not constructed. Handle `Flood()` failure before copying, or make the traversal continue without dropping pending spans. No icon was laid out and no allocation or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10148 — BetterString hexadecimal conversion keeps only the final digit

`HexToDec()` scans the hexadecimal token around the cursor, but its accumulation loop computes `res = (result << 4) + DecimalValue(...)` (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/HandleInput.c:491-520`). `result` is a `BOOL` initialized to `FALSE` and is set to `TRUE` only after conversion and overwrite, so it remains zero throughout the loop. Each iteration therefore replaces `res` with the current digit instead of shifting the accumulated value. The explicit `MUIM_BetterString_DoAction_HexToDec` action reaches this helper through `mDoAction()` (`HandleInput.c:708-712`); the public action value is declared in `include/mui/BetterString_mcc.h:100`, and the class documentation promises conversion of the current hexadecimal number (`doc/MCC_BetterString.doc:285-286`). The `#` shortcut also calls the same helper (`HandleInput.c:1148-1153`).

**Trigger and consequence:** convert a multi-digit hexadecimal token whose final digit is the only value retained; for example, `1A` becomes decimal `10`, and `FF` becomes decimal `15`, then `Overwrite()` replaces the token with that incorrect value. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-classes-zune-betterstring-class` MCC target; the parent Zune aggregate edge is commented out in `workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mmakefile.src`, so this is not asserted to be present in every default image. **Confidence:** high; the accumulator and its delayed Boolean assignment are directly visible, and both method and shortcut call paths are selected in the class source. Accumulate into `res` with a four-bit shift. No conversion or GUI operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10149 — BetterString reverts to a truncated activation snapshot

`mGoActive()` allocates `Original` with space for the current string and then copies it with `strlcpy(data->Original, data->Contents, strlen(data->Contents+1))` (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/Dispatcher.c:513-515`). The size is the length starting one character into the source, so for an original length of *n* the copy can retain at most *n−2* characters. `RevertToOriginal()` swaps `Contents` and `Original` and sets the cursor from the copied string's length (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/HandleInput.c:372-385`); both the `MUIM_BetterString_DoAction_Revert` action and the `Amiga+q` shortcut reach it (`HandleInput.c:671-677,1162-1166`). The documentation says the shortcut reverts to the original string and can be pressed again to return to the modified string (`doc/MCC_BetterString.doc:132-136`).

**Trigger and consequence:** activate the gadget while it contains text, edit it, then invoke Revert. The saved snapshot is truncated: a one-character original becomes empty, and longer originals lose their last two characters. The gadget therefore restores the wrong value. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-classes-zune-betterstring-class` MCC target; its parent aggregate edge is commented out, so this is not asserted to affect every default image. **Confidence:** high; the size expression, bounded `strlcpy()` semantics, snapshot swap and documented caller are directly established in selected sources. Pass the allocated destination size (`strlen(data->Contents)+1`) to `strlcpy()`. No text edit, activation, revert action or GUI operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10150 — Secret BetterString text is drawn unmasked when masking allocation fails

`PrintString()` copies secret contents into a temporary buffer and replaces every character with `*` only when `SharedPoolAlloc(StrLength+1)` succeeds (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/PrintString.c:148-158`). If the allocation returns NULL, `contents` remains `data->Contents`; the function continues measuring and drawing that plaintext, then copies the offscreen bitmap to the displayed gadget (`:234-235,327-341`).

**Trigger and consequence:** draw a nonempty gadget with `MUIA_String_Secret` enabled while the temporary masking-buffer allocation fails. The secret value is rendered visibly instead of masked. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-classes-zune-betterstring-class` MCC target, on any supported platform where this drawing allocation can fail. **Confidence:** high; the failure branch leaves the original pointer in place and the selected drawing path consumes it. On allocation failure, suppress the secret text or render a mask without exposing the original value. No allocation failure or drawing operation was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10151 — BetterString selection can retain an out-of-range start and read past its contents

`mSet()` handles tags in order. `MUIA_String_BufferPos` stores the requested position in `BufferPos`, while `MUIA_BetterString_SelectSize` copies that position to `BlockStart`, enables selection, and clamps only `BlockStop` to the string length (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/GetSetAttrs.c:203-208,364-377`). After all tags, it clamps `BufferPos` but does not clamp `BlockStart` (`:435-439`). On the next draw, `PrintString()` derives the selection width from both endpoints and calls `TextLength(contents+Blk_Start, Blk_Width)` (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/PrintString.c:206-218`). For proportional fonts, `TextLength()` reads one source byte per requested character (`rom/graphics/textlength.c:57-75`).

**Trigger and consequence:** with contents `abc`, set `MUIA_String_BufferPos` to 100 followed by `MUIA_BetterString_SelectSize` to 1 in the same ordered attribute list. The setter records start 100 and stop 101, clamps stop to 3, then clamps the cursor to 3 but leaves start at 100. Drawing computes start 3 and width 97, then a proportional-font `TextLength()` reads 97 bytes from the terminator at `contents+3`, beyond the content allocation. This can fault or read unrelated memory during rendering. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable BetterString MCC target when callers set these attributes together in this order and the gadget uses a proportional font. **Confidence:** high for the state transition and bounded-count read; the out-of-bounds access follows for the stated short-string case. Clamp both selection endpoints whenever the cursor or contents are changed, and validate selection endpoints before drawing. No attribute set or draw was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10152 — BetterString Paste turns a negative remaining capacity into a huge copy length

The `MUIA_String_MaxLen` setter stores a new limit but does not truncate existing contents (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/GetSetAttrs.c:321-324`). When Paste receives clipboard text, it checks whether the resulting length exceeds `MaxLength-1`, then computes the allowed `length` as `MaxLength - 1 - strlen(Contents)` (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/HandleInput.c:317-326`). If the existing contents are already longer than the new limit, unsigned `strlen()` arithmetic underflows and this assignment produces a negative `LONG`. That value is then passed to `ExpandContentString()` as an unsigned extra length and to `memmove()`/`memcpy()` as size arguments (`HandleInput.c:328-332`).

**Trigger and consequence:** set a nonzero `MUIA_String_MaxLen` smaller than the existing string, then paste any nonempty clipboard text with no selection. For example, with contents `abcd`, set `MaxLen` to 4 and paste one character: the calculated paste length is -1 on the supported AROS integer ABIs. With the existing content allocation, expansion can report success after its size arithmetic wraps; `memcpy()` then receives the negative length converted to a huge unsigned size, causing an invalid read/write and likely a fault or data damage. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable BetterString MCC target when callers lower `MUIA_String_MaxLen` at runtime below current contents and then paste. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked limit update and negative-count flow on supported AROS ABIs; no paste or memory failure was induced. Clamp remaining capacity to zero and keep the existing contents within the newly set limit. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10153 — BetterString leaks a shared-pool buffer when a clipboard chunk read fails

`ReadFromClipboard()` allocates `cn->cn_Size + 1` bytes from the class shared pool before reading a nonempty `CHRS` chunk (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/ClipboardServer.c:258-268`). It publishes the buffer only when `ReadChunkBytes()` returns a positive count; for a zero or negative result it only logs the error and leaves the allocation unfreed (`:283-288`). The function initialized the returned string pointer to NULL (`:221-222`), so `ClipboardToString()` reports failure and the Paste caller has no pointer it could release (`ClipboardServer.c:130-143`; `HandleInput.c:317-339`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a nonempty clipboard text chunk is allocated successfully but its read returns zero or an error. The buffer remains allocated in the BetterString shared pool; repeated failed reads can accumulate leaked pool storage until class expunge. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable BetterString MCC target when reading a truncated or otherwise unreadable clipboard chunk. **Confidence:** high for the missing free and lost pointer; the read-failure condition is external to this source path. Free the buffer on every nonpositive read result. No clipboard file or read failure was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10154 — BetterString builds its selection pointer before selecting screen-matched colors

`mSetup()` calls `SetupSelectPointer()` before registering the mouse handler (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/Dispatcher.c:305-313`). In the AROS pointerclass path, `SetupSelectPointer()` creates `PointerObj` using `selectPointerBitmap` (`Pointer.c:327-336`). PointerClass immediately passes that bitmap to `AllocSpriteDataA()` (`rom/intuition/pointerclass.c:84-103`), which allocates a destination bitmap and copies/scales the source pixels into it (`rom/graphics/allocspritedataa.c:243-253`). Only later, on the first mouse event over the gadget, `ShowSelectPointer()` calls `IdentifyPointerColors()`, which changes the plane pointers in the original static bitmap (`Pointer.c:403-406,257-293`); the already-created sprite bitmap is not updated.

**Trigger and consequence:** use the custom selection pointer on an AROS screen whose pointer-color ordering differs from the bitmap's initial plane ordering. The pointer object was copied before the code selects the screen-matched planes, so it retains the initial pixel pattern and can have poor contrast against the pointer colors. **Affected configuration:** the AROS BetterString MCC pointerclass path when `MUIA_BetterString_SelectPointer` is enabled and the gadget's pointer type is normal. **Confidence:** high that the post-construction plane updates cannot change the sprite bitmap; medium for the visible contrast impact, which depends on the screen's pointer-color mapping. Identify the screen colors before constructing the pointer object, or rebuild/update its sprite bitmap after selecting the planes. No pointer, screen or mouse operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10155 — BetterString underallocates 64-bit ExAll frames

Filename completion allocates each `FNCData` frame with `SharedPoolAlloc(4100)` and passes `&fncframe->buffer` plus a 4096-byte capacity to `ExAll()` (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/FileNameCompl.c:301,317,321`). `FNCData` places a pointer before the buffer (`mcc/private.h:38-42`). On 64-bit AROS that pointer occupies 8 bytes, so the 4100-byte allocation leaves only 4092 bytes for the ExAll buffer. The ExAll contract allows the filesystem to use the supplied buffer capacity (`rom/dos/exall.c:35-55,73-77`).

**Trigger and consequence:** AROS 64-bit filename completion on a directory whose ExAll batch uses more than 4092 bytes. The filesystem can write into the four bytes beyond the frame allocation, corrupting adjacent pool storage. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable BetterString MCC target on 64-bit AROS while enumerating a sufficiently populated directory. **Confidence:** high for the 4-byte size mismatch; the overrun depends on a near-full batch. Allocate `sizeof(struct FNCData)-sizeof(struct ExAllData)+4096` bytes, or otherwise size the frame from the actual buffer offset. No directory enumeration or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10156 — BetterString AROS volume completion drops the final volume-name character

The selected module build defines `AROS_ABI_V1` (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/mmakefile.src:32`). In that branch, volume completion passes `AROS_BSTR_strlen()` as the `strlcpy()` destination size instead of adding space for the terminating NUL (`mcc/FileNameCompl.c:235-240`). `AROS_BSTR_strlen()` returns the string length in both BSTR layouts (`compiler/include/dos/bptr.h:72,77`), while `strlcpy()` uses its size argument as the full destination capacity. The temporary name therefore loses its final character before prefix matching and insertion (`FileNameCompl.c:249-259`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use filename completion on an AROS volume prefix, such as typing `S` for a volume named `SYS`. The temporary name becomes `SY`, and the completion inserts `SY:` instead of `SYS:`. **Affected configuration:** the selected AROS ABI_V1 BetterString MCC target when completing device, volume or assign names. **Confidence:** high; the size convention and selected build flag are explicit. Pass `AROS_BSTR_strlen(...) + 1` or use the full temporary-buffer size. No completion was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10157 — BetterString filename completion truncates names longer than 31 characters

`InsertFileName()` formats every ExAll entry name into `char tmpname[32]` with `snprintf()` and then overwrites the user's prefix with that temporary (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/FileNameCompl.c:140-148,181-183`). The 32-character check in `FileNameComplete()` limits only the already typed prefix, not the returned directory-entry name (`:293-296`). ExAll provides each entry name through `ed_Name` without a 31-character limit (`rom/dos/exall.c:52-64`; `compiler/include/dos/exall.h:19-27`).

**Trigger and consequence:** complete a directory entry whose name exceeds 31 characters. The inserted completion is truncated to 31 bytes (including any appended slash/space), so it does not identify the actual entry. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable BetterString MCC target on filesystems that permit names longer than 31 characters. **Confidence:** high for the fixed destination size and truncating `snprintf()` path. Size the temporary from the entry's actual name length or write it directly into the content buffer after a successful expansion. No directory was enumerated; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10158 — Invalid BetterString filename patterns fall back to listing every entry

`FileNameComplete()` leaves `control->eac_MatchString` unchanged when `ParsePatternNoCase()` returns `-1` (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/FileNameCompl.c:305-317`). `AllocDosObject(DOS_EXALLCONTROL)` zero-initializes the control object (`rom/dos/allocdosobject.c:87-90`), so the failed parse leaves the match string NULL. ExAll explicitly treats a NULL match string as all files (`rom/dos/exall.c:82-86`). The code then stores those results and inserts one as a valid completion (`FileNameCompl.c:326-337`).

**Trigger and consequence:** enter a malformed DOS pattern in the filename prefix, such as an unmatched opening parenthesis, and request completion. `ParsePatternNoCase()` rejects the generated pattern (`rom/dos/patternmatching.c:503-514,630`), but the NULL match filter makes ExAll enumerate all entries; the first entry can replace the user's prefix even though it did not match. **Affected configuration:** the BetterString MCC filename-completion path when typed wildcard syntax is malformed. **Confidence:** high for the parse failure, zero-initialized control, and ExAll NULL-filter behavior. Abort completion or report the pattern error when parsing fails. No malformed pattern or directory enumeration was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10159 — BetterString insertion copies text after content expansion fails

When replacement text is longer than the replaced range, `OverwriteA()` calls `ExpandContentString()` and performs the suffix `memmove()` only if expansion succeeds. If expansion fails, it logs the error but still calls `CopyMem()` with the full replacement length (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/FileNameCompl.c:47-66`). The public `MUIM_BetterString_Insert` method reaches this helper through `mInsert()` (`mcc/HandleInput.c:1573-1598`).

**Trigger and consequence:** insert text that requires the content allocation to grow, then have that allocation fail. For example, a 39-character string in the initial 40-byte content buffer followed by a two-character insert at the end makes expansion necessary; the unconditional copy writes beyond the unchanged allocation. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable BetterString MCC target when an insertion or other growing overwrite encounters allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the missing failure return and copy length; the overrun depends on the chosen insertion position and current allocation capacity. Return without copying when expansion fails. No allocation failure or insert was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10160 — BetterString filename replacement wraps a negative MaxLen remainder

`OverwriteA()` attempts to shorten an expanding replacement when it would exceed `MaxLength`, but computes the new pattern length using `(MaxLength-1)-strlen(Contents)` and stores the result back into `UWORD ptrn_length` (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/FileNameCompl.c:47-58`). The `MUIA_String_MaxLen` setter allows lowering the limit without truncating current contents (`mcc/GetSetAttrs.c:321-324`). If the old contents already exceed the new limit, this remaining-capacity subtraction underflows; the result can wrap to a large `UWORD` used by the following `memmove()` and `CopyMem()`.

**Trigger and consequence:** lower `MaxLen` below the existing string length, then perform a filename/volume completion that expands the matched prefix. The wrapped replacement length can direct the following memory operations far beyond the content buffer. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable BetterString MCC target when callers lower `MaxLen` at runtime and invoke a growing completion. **Confidence:** high for the unsigned subtraction, narrowing, and later use; no limit change or completion was run. Clamp remaining capacity to zero before converting it to the replacement length, and keep existing text within a newly set limit. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10161 — BetterString leaks its filename-completion frame when ExAll control allocation fails

Filename completion first allocates a 4100-byte shared-pool frame, then allocates the ExAll control object (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/FileNameCompl.c:301-305`). If `AllocDosObject(DOS_EXALLCONTROL)` returns NULL, there is no corresponding `SharedPoolFree(fncbuffer)`; the frame is not stored in `data->FNCBuffer`, and the function later restores the edited contents and returns (`:346-352`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the frame allocation succeeds but ExAll-control allocation fails during filename completion. The unreachable frame remains allocated in the class shared pool; repeated retries leak another 4100-byte block each time. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable BetterString MCC target under this allocation-failure ordering. **Confidence:** high for the unmatched allocation and return path. Free `fncbuffer` when ExAll-control allocation fails. No allocation failure or completion was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10162 — Zune classes leak dependency libraries when an OS4 interface lookup fails

`ClassInit()` combines each required `OpenLibrary()` with `GETINTERFACE()` in one condition for locale, layers, keymap and diskfont (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/library.c:92-103`). On AmigaOS 4, `GETINTERFACE()` calls `GetInterface()` and can fail (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/include/mccinit.c:291-296`). If a library opens but its interface lookup returns NULL, that condition skips the body containing its matching `CloseLibrary()`; the function then unwinds earlier dependencies and returns FALSE (`library.c:119-139`). The shared MCC startup rollback deletes the custom class but does not invoke `ClassExpunge()` on this ClassInit failure path (`include/mccinit.c:761-785`). The separately buildable HotkeyString MCC has the same ordering for `keymap.library`: `ClassInit()` opens it and tests `GETINTERFACE(IKeymap, ...)`, but returns FALSE without closing the opened base if that interface lookup fails (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/hotkeystring/library.c:83-91`). Its `ClassExpunge()` would release the base, but the shared rollback does not call it on this failure path. The HotkeyString target is explicitly buildable and is not connected to the package aggregate (`mcc/hotkeystring/mmakefile.src:5-7`). The separately buildable BetterString MCP repeats the same failure for `locale.library`: its `ClassInit()` opens the base and tests `GETINTERFACE(ILocale, ...)`, then returns FALSE without closing it on interface failure (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcp/library.c:153-177`); it also uses the shared `mccinit.c` rollback, which skips `ClassExpunge()` on this path. The MCP's standalone target is defined in `mcp/mmakefile.src`; its parent aggregate edge is commented out. The optional NBalance MCC has the same open-then-interface ordering for `layers.library`: `ClassInit()` stores a successful `OpenLibrary()` in `LayersBase`, then returns FALSE if `GETINTERFACE(ILayers, ...)` fails, without closing the base (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nbalance_mcc/library.c:80-89`). Its `ClassExpunge()` is the only local path that closes `LayersBase` (`:92-99`), but the selected shared NList `mccinit.c` failure branch deletes `ThisClass` and closes its own bases without calling `ClassExpunge()` (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mccinit.c:761-785`). The explicitly buildable target is `classes-zune-nbalance-class` (`nbalance_mcc/mmakefile.src:3-5,19-21`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an AmigaOS 4 MCC/MCP initialization where a required library opens but fails to provide its requested `main` interface. The failed dependency retains its open reference on each failed initialization attempt. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable BetterString MCC, BetterString MCP, HotkeyString MCC, and NBalance MCC targets on AmigaOS 4 under that library/interface failure ordering; AROS builds use the non-interface branch of `GETINTERFACE()` and are unaffected by this finding. **Confidence:** high for the opened-base/failed-interface path and skipped cleanup. Close and clear each base when its interface lookup fails before unwinding prior dependencies. No library or interface failure was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

## GD10163 — NListtree Open-All inserts descendants from a hidden list into the visible list.

`MUIM_NListtree_Open` accepts `MUIV_NListtree_Open_TreeNode_All` and calls `OpenTreeNodeListExpand(data, ln)` for the selected list (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:6702-6748`). The method documentation says the list node selects which list to open and that TreeNode_All opens all nodes in that list; it does not require that list to be visible (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:2447-2473`). For a non-root list, `OpenTreeNodeListExpand()` calls `OpenTreeNodeExpand()` for every child (`NListtree.c:1998-2030`). When a child node is hidden below a closed ancestor, `GetVisualPos()` returns -1 because its `TNIF_VISIBLE` flag is clear (`:1367-1389`); `OpenTreeNodeExpand()` increments that result to position 0, opens the child and inserts its descendants there (`:1964-1991`). `InsertTreeVisible()` marks those descendants visible and inserts them into the NList regardless of whether their ancestors are visible (`:1764-1800`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the explicitly buildable AROS `classes-zune-nlisttree-class` target when a caller requests Open with a node's list and TreeNode_All while that list is below a closed ancestor, and one of its child nodes has a closed nonempty sublist. The hidden descendants are inserted at the start of the flattened NList (or at its bottom when it has no rows) while their parent rows remain hidden. They can appear and participate in list selection/navigation without the ancestor path; later opening the ancestor sees their visibility flags already set and may leave the rows in the wrong position. Keep Open-All's tree-state update separate from visible-row insertion when the selected list is hidden. **Confidence:** high for the position fallback and unconditional insertion path; impact requires the stated nested closed-list shape and public method call. No tree, UI operation or build was run; source-only. See the [Open-All caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L9071).
