## GD10164 — Explicit MUI demos dereference a failed custom-class result

Both explicitly buildable test programs call `MUI_CreateCustomClass()` and store its nullable result in `mcc`, then evaluate `mcc->mcc_Class` without checking it: HotkeyString-Test constructs its first class object at `workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/hotkeystring/HotkeyString-Test.c:78-103`, and BetterString-Test does so while constructing the PopASL string at `workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/BetterString-Test.c:115-143,131-132`. The selected `MUI_CreateCustomClass()` implementation returns NULL when its structure allocation or `MakeClass()` fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_createcustomclass.c:66-76`).

**Trigger and consequence:** custom-class creation fails, for example because allocation or superclass setup fails. The relevant test program dereferences NULL during UI construction instead of reporting startup failure. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable HotkeyString-Test and BetterString-Test executables only; this does not affect either class library or ordinary clients. **Confidence:** high for the nullable API result and unchecked dereferences. Check `mcc` before constructing objects and release any acquired resources on that failure path. No class-creation failure or demo was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


<a id="gd10209"></a>
## GD10209 — BetterString demos leak a custom class when application creation fails

Both BetterString test programs create a custom class before constructing their MUI application (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/BetterString-Test.c:115-117`; `mcc/hotkeystring/HotkeyString-Test.c:78-79`). Their `MUI_DeleteCustomClass(mcc)` calls are nested inside `if (app)` (`BetterString-Test.c:267-303`; `HotkeyString-Test.c:120-151`). When custom-class creation succeeds but `ApplicationObject` returns NULL, the cleanup block is skipped and the created class is not deleted. The selected `MUI_DeleteCustomClass()` implementation frees the class and wrapper and releases its superclass reference (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_deletecustomclass.c:56-72`).

**Trigger and consequence:** MUI application-object construction fails after custom-class creation succeeds, such as an allocation failure while building the application tree. The test exits its UI block without deleting the custom class, retaining the class/wrapper and superclass reference for the remainder of the process. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable BetterString-Test and HotkeyString-Test executables only. **Confidence:** high for the cleanup nesting and delete implementation; no allocation failure was induced. Move custom-class deletion to an unconditional cleanup path after disposing any successfully created application. Source-only; see the [BetterString test-program audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L9102).

<a id="gd10210"></a>
## GD10210 — BetterString MCP touches disposed preference gadgets after tree construction fails

`CreatePrefsGroup()` constructs the complete nested MUI tree, retaining pointers to preference gadgets in `data->Objects`, then performs `SetAttrs()` on several of those pointers after the outer `VGroup` constructor returns (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcp/CreatePrefsGroup.c:143-160,180-252,278-298`). A constructor failure for a child makes the containing MUI `Group__OM_NEW()` mark `bad_children`, dispose the group, and return NULL (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:340-352,415-419`). Group disposal disposes its child Family, and Family disposal calls `MUI_DisposeObject()` for every child (`group.c:457-467`; `family.c:129-141`). The post-construction code does not first test `group`; its non-NULL `data->Objects[...]` entries still point to gadgets that the failed outer construction has just disposed.

**Trigger and consequence:** during MCP preference-group construction, a nested child constructor such as the final `CrawlingObject` or one of its text children fails after the preference gadgets have been created. The outer Group constructor then disposes the assembled tree and returns NULL; `CreatePrefsGroup()` proceeds to `SetAttrs()` on the stale `InactiveBack`, `ActiveBack`, `SelectOnActive`, or `SelectPointer` pointer. If `SelectPointer` is present, the same block also calls `xget(example, ...)`; `GetAttr()` only rejects a NULL object, so a non-NULL disposed `example` is passed to `DoMethod()` (`rom/intuition/getattr.c:69-76`). This can fault or corrupt object state during the allocation-failure cleanup path before the caller can handle the NULL result. **Affected configuration:** the separately buildable BetterString MCP target when a nested MUI constructor fails after one or more preference gadgets were created. **Confidence:** high for the disposal and subsequent stale-pointer calls; exact visible failure depends on allocator state and MUI dispatch behavior. Return immediately when `group` is NULL before accessing saved child pointers, and clear or otherwise invalidate the stored entries during failure cleanup. No allocation failure or GUI operation was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

<a id="gd10211"></a>
## GD10211 — Mesa3DGL drops stencil when depth is disabled

The public GLA tags define `GLA_NoDepth` and `GLA_NoStencil` as separate switches, both defaulting to FALSE (`workbench/libs/gl/gla.h:75-82`; `mesa3dgl_glacreatecontext.c:93-100`). In `MESA3DGLSelectDepthStencilFormat()`, `noDepth` immediately sets `PIPE_FORMAT_NONE` and returns TRUE before considering `noStencil` (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa3dgl_gallium.c:70-125`). But `MESA3DGLFillVisual()` still adds `ST_ATTACHMENT_DEPTH_STENCIL_MASK` whenever either buffer remains requested (`:163-165`). Thus a caller that disables depth but leaves stencil enabled gets a successful visual setup with no depth/stencil format and a requested depth/stencil attachment. The selected `MESA3DGLFrameBufferValidate()` then creates that attachment from the `PIPE_FORMAT_NONE` format and does not reject a NULL resource before returning TRUE (`:170-213,215-257`).

**Trigger and consequence:** create a GLA context with `GLA_NoDepth=TRUE` and `GLA_NoStencil` omitted or FALSE. The selected backend cannot supply the requested stencil attachment; framebuffer validation may report success while handing the state tracker a NULL depth/stencil resource, depending on imported Mesa handling of `PIPE_FORMAT_NONE` and failed resource creation. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built Mesa3DGL library targets using this visual builder; the Mesa aggregate edge is commented out of the general Workbench library list (`workbench/libs/mesa/mmakefile.src:65-77,114-121`; `workbench/libs/mmakefile:27-31`). **Confidence:** high that the two independent flags produce an inconsistent visual/attachment request; medium on the exact downstream rendering failure because the fetched Mesa state-tracker core is not present in the checkout. Choose a stencil-capable format when depth is disabled, or fail context creation instead of advertising the attachment. No context, stencil operation, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


## GD10212 — ReAction Layout ignores its declared child-modification tag

The public header defines `LAYOUT_ModifyChild` as “Modify existing child” and says child tags apply after either `LAYOUT_AddChild` or `LAYOUT_ModifyChild` (`compiler/include/gadgets/layout.h:74-76,118`). The selected `Layout__OM_SET()` passes the tag list to `layout_set()` (`workbench/classes/reaction/layout/layoutclass.c:368-376`), but `layout_set()` handles `LAYOUT_AddChild`, `LAYOUT_AddImage`, and `LAYOUT_RemoveChild` only; it has no `LAYOUT_ModifyChild` case (`:118-269`). The adjacent `process_child_tags()` helper handles child size/weight/label attributes, but no code consumes `CHILD_ReplaceObject` or `CHILD_ReplaceImage`; repository-wide searches find these symbols only in their header declarations (`layout.h:127-128`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a client of `layout.gadget` submits an OM_SET/SetAttrs list containing `LAYOUT_ModifyChild` and its child tags to change an existing child. The operation is silently ignored, so the child object and its stored layout constraints remain unchanged even though the public header advertises modification. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable optional `workbench-classes-reaction-layout` (`workbench/classes/reaction/layout/mmakefile.src:5-17`); its parent aggregate dependency is commented in this snapshot, and no checked-in caller of `LAYOUT_ModifyChild` was found. **Confidence:** high that the selected class does not implement the declared tag; effect requires an external or future client to use it. No layout object or GUI operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L9118).


## GD10213 — ReAction Layout succeeds while losing an inline child on wrapper-allocation failure

`LAYOUT_AddChild` first allocates a `LayoutChild` wrapper with `AllocVec()` (`workbench/classes/reaction/layout/layoutclass.c:33-44,218-230`). If that allocation fails, the branch simply skips publication and returns no error; `layout_set()` is `void`. During `Layout__OM_NEW()`, the class calls `layout_set()` after the superclass has created the parent, then returns the parent `retval` regardless of whether any child wrapper was allocated (`:271-339`). The child is disposed only through a wrapper in `ld_Children` during `Layout__OM_DISPOSE()` (`:344-355`). With nested object macros, the child `NewObject()` is supplied as the `LAYOUT_AddChild` tag value before the parent constructor runs; maintained AHI ReAction source uses this form (`compiler/include/reaction/reaction_macros.h:216-225`; `workbench/devs/AHI/AHI/gui_ca.c:811-817`).

**Trigger and consequence:** creating a `layout.gadget` with an inline `LAYOUT_AddChild` object when allocation of that child's `LayoutChild` wrapper fails. The parent still reports successful construction but omits the child; because it was never linked into `ld_Children`, disposing the parent cannot dispose it, so an inline-created child is leaked. This is distinct from GD10120: GD10213 loses the child before a wrapper enters the list, while GD10120 removes an existing wrapper and sets its no-dispose flag before freeing it. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable optional ReAction `layout.gadget`; maintained nested-child construction exists in the AHI ReAction UI, while no default-image inclusion is claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked wrapper-allocation failure, successful parent return, and list-only cleanup; occurrence requires a child object to be created followed by wrapper allocation failure. No allocation failure, layout object, or GUI operation was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L9118).


<a id="gd10214"></a>
## GD10214 — Vulkan dispatch can switch GPUs between calls using the same handles

`VulkanGetPreferredGPU()` selects the registered GPU with the lowest priority value, then breaks equal-priority ties using the lowest `use_count` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/vulkan_intern.h:314-339`). `GET_GPU` invokes that selection afresh in each Vulkan HIDD method (`vulkan_class.c:27-30`). `CreateDevice()` chooses the current GPU and increments its `use_count` after the driver returns a device (`vulkan_class.c:177-203`); methods such as `GetDeviceQueue()` and `DestroyDevice()` independently choose again (`:206-229`). The loader forwards `vkCreateDevice()` and `vkGetDeviceQueue()` as separate methods without a GPU/driver association (`vulkan_loader.c:554-608`). The class does not retain a device-to-GPU association.

**Trigger and consequence:** two distinct GPU entries have the same priority and are both available. The first `CreateDevice()` selects the earlier entry while both counts are zero, then increments that entry's count. A following call such as `GetDeviceQueue()` now selects the other entry because its count is lower, and passes the first driver's opaque device handle to the second driver's callback. Destruction can likewise reach the wrong backend and decrement a different entry's count. This can make valid Vulkan device operations fail or be mis-handled and leaves load accounting inaccurate; the exact effect depends on the driver callbacks.

**Affected configuration:** the `hidd-vulkan` target selected through the active `workbench-hidds` virtual edge, with registered Vulkan GPU providers. The HIDD supports up to 32 entries and documents multi-GPU registration, but the checked-in source tree contains no direct `VulkanHidd_RegisterGPU()` provider callsite; package/runtime provider availability is not established. **Confidence:** high for the selection/count behavior under the stated trigger; current in-tree provider reachability is unverified. No GPU, device, or API call was run; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L9122).

<a id="gd10215"></a>
## GD10215 — Vulkan loader latches incomplete initialization as complete

`vk_loader_init()` sets the process-global `vk_init_done` before obtaining the Vulkan attribute base or creating the HIDD object (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/vulkan_loader.c:198-220`). If either operation fails, it returns with `vk_init_done` still TRUE and `vk_obj` still NULL. Every later entry point calls this helper and then returns its no-object fallback or initialization error, so it never retries. The explicit `VulkanProbe` path calls `vkEnumerateInstanceVersion()` and then `vkCreateInstance()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/test/VulkanProbe.c:58-80`); the former reports Vulkan 1.0 success when no object exists, while the latter returns `VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED` (`vulkan_loader.c:270-289,326-345`).

There is also no synchronization for concurrent first calls. A second caller can observe the done flag before initialization finishes; `vk_obj` is stored before `vk_mbase`, so a caller that sees the object before the method base is published can dispatch with an unset method ID. Two racing initializers can also create more than one HIDD object while only the last pointer is retained.

**Trigger and consequence:** the first Vulkan call encounters a temporary attribute-base or HIDD-object creation failure, or multiple tasks make the first Vulkan calls concurrently. A failed attempt permanently disables later calls in that process even after the HIDD becomes available; concurrent calls can return fallback errors or dispatch through incomplete state, and a losing object can remain undisposed. **Affected configuration:** `hidd-vulkan-loader` and clients using it, including VulkanProbe, both selected through active `workbench-hidds` virtual edges; the loader and probe have active `#MM-` virtual edges from `workbench-hidds` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/mmakefile.src:29,32,58-59`). Thus they are build-selected through that aggregate; package/runtime availability is not established. **Confidence:** high for the failure latch and publication ordering; no allocation failure or concurrent call was induced. Source-only.

**Review evidence:** [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L9122).


<a id="gd10216"></a>
## GD10216 — Vulkan loader drops caller instance-create settings and allocation callbacks

`vkCreateInstance()` explicitly discards both `pCreateInfo` and `pAllocator`, then sends the HIDD only the hardcoded application name `"AROS Vulkan Loader"` and version 1 (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/vulkan_loader.c:327-347`). The public `CreateInstance` callback accepts only an application name, application version and driver data (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan_hidd.h:97-100`); it has no way to receive the caller's requested Vulkan API version, instance flags, requested layers/extensions, engine identity, or allocation callbacks. The selected explicit caller sets `VkApplicationInfo.apiVersion` to Vulkan 1.2 and its application name to `"VulkanProbe"`, but those fields are not forwarded (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/test/VulkanProbe.c:66-78`). `vkDestroyInstance()` also ignores its allocator (`vulkan_loader.c:350-363`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a client supplies non-default instance-creation fields or a custom `VkAllocationCallbacks`. The HIDD provider receives no instance settings and cannot honor or validate the requested API version, layers/extensions or flags; the loader can report successful creation of an instance that does not match the request. Custom allocation callbacks are ignored on create and destroy. The checked-in probe demonstrates that an explicit maintained caller requests Vulkan 1.2 and a distinct application identity, but no Vulkan provider implementation is present in this checkout to establish the backend's resulting behavior.

**Affected configuration:** `hidd-vulkan-loader` and clients linking `-lvulkan`, including VulkanProbe, selected through active `workbench-hidds` virtual edges; the loader and probe have active `#MM-` virtual edges from `workbench-hidds` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/mmakefile.src:32,58-59`). Thus they are build-selected through that aggregate; package/runtime availability is not established. **Confidence:** high that the loader and public callback contract drop these inputs; downstream effect depends on the optional provider and requested fields. No Vulkan application, instance, allocation callback, driver or build was run; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [Graphics/Desktop coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L9152).


<a id="gd10217"></a>
## GD10217 — Vulkan extension inspection can decrement before the dependency map begins

The public getExtensionDepends(version, extension) helper finds the first dependency-version key not less than version with lower_bound(). When that key is not an exact match, it unconditionally assigns std::prev(depIt) (workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_extension_inspection.hpp:3038-3064). The generated dependency table contains entries whose first key is later than 1.0; for example, VK_KHR_video_queue has keys VK_VERSION_1_1 and VK_VERSION_1_3 (:665-670). A call with the accepted VK_VERSION_1_0 token and that extension makes lower_bound() return begin(), and the subsequent std::prev(begin()) is undefined behavior. The debug assertion explicitly accepts VK_VERSION_1_0 (:3041-3043), and the function's boolean result path is designed to report when no prior dependency-version record exists (:3057-3060).

**Trigger and consequence:** a consumer queries dependencies for an extension whose table begins at 1.1 or later using an earlier accepted core-version token. The helper performs an invalid iterator decrement, so the result of extension-dependency inspection is undefined; no specific crash or returned value is asserted. **Affected configuration:** the Vulkan target copies this generated header into the public include tree (workbench/hidds/vulkan/mmakefile.src:10-23) and is selected through an active `workbench-hidds` virtual edge; repository search found no checked-in call to this overload. The trigger is therefore an external consumer of the explicitly built Vulkan-Hpp header, not a claimed default-image path. **Confidence:** high for the invalid iterator operation under the stated inputs; in-tree reachability is not established. Check for depIt == dependencies.begin() before decrementing and return the no-prior-version result. No Vulkan API call, generated output or build was run; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [Vulkan extension-inspection header coverage](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L9161).


<a id="gd10218"></a>
## GD10218 — Vulkan object-type conversion asserts on the unknown sentinel

`ObjectType` explicitly defines `eUnknown = VK_OBJECT_TYPE_UNKNOWN` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_enums.hpp:1765-1768`), and `DebugReportObjectTypeEXT` has a matching `eUnknown` value (`:5769-5774`). The generated `debugReportObjectType()` switch maps object kinds unsupported by the legacy debug-report enum to `DebugReportObjectTypeEXT::eUnknown`, but has no `case ObjectType::eUnknown`; the descriptor-template, sampler-YCbCr-conversion and private-data-slot extension aliases share values with cases already handled (`:9561-9700`). Passing the explicit sentinel therefore reaches the default `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT(false)` before the fallback unknown return. The header defines `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT` as standard `assert` unless overridden (`vulkan_hpp_macros.hpp:74-76`), so an assert-enabled consumer aborts on this valid enum value; a build with assertions disabled reaches and returns the fallback.

**Trigger and consequence:** a C++ consumer calls `debugReportObjectType(ObjectType::eUnknown)` with assertions enabled. The helper asserts instead of returning `DebugReportObjectTypeEXT::eUnknown`.

**Affected configuration:** clients using the copied generated Vulkan-Hpp `vulkan_enums.hpp`; the HIDD and loader targets are connected to `workbench-hidds` by active `#MM-` virtual edges (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/mmakefile.src:29,32`). No checked-in C++ caller is known, and package/runtime availability is not established. **Confidence:** high for the enum value, missing case, and assert/fallback behavior; repository-wide search found no in-tree helper call. Add an explicit `eUnknown` case (or otherwise bypass the assertion for this sentinel). No C++ call or runtime was exercised; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [Vulkan enum header coverage](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L9164).


<a id="gd10219"></a>
## GD10219 — Withdrawn: empty Vulkan-Hpp proxy `end()` uses a defined zero offset

**Disposition: withdrawn; no bug is asserted.** The default and null constructors of `ArrayProxy` and `ArrayProxyNoTemporaries` establish a zero count and null pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan.hpp:314-324,424-434`); their `end()` methods consequently evaluate null pointer plus zero (`:383-385,487-490`). `StridedArrayProxy` inherits those empty states, and its `m_stride` member is initialized to `sizeof(T)` (`:528-542,561-563`), so its empty `end()` also adds zero to a null pointer. The original report incorrectly treated that expression as undefined. The C++11 working draft says adding zero to a pointer compares equal to the original pointer ([N3337, §5.7/7](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2012/n3337.pdf)); C++14 and later explicitly specify that null plus zero yields a null pointer ([current `[expr.add]`](https://eel.is/c++draft/expr.add)). Thus these empty-proxy `end()` expressions do not establish a defect in the header's supported C++11 mode or later modes. No in-tree C++ caller was found, and no other issue is asserted under GD10219. Source-only; no C++ call or build was run.

**Review evidence:** [Vulkan-Hpp full-body coverage](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-full-body-pass).


<a id="gd10220"></a>
## GD10220 — Vulkan-Hpp dynamic initialization ignores the supplied device lookup callback

`DispatchLoaderDynamic` exposes constructor and `init()` overloads taking both `PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr` and an optional `PFN_vkGetDeviceProcAddr` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan.hpp:21452-21460,21495-21499`). The `getDeviceProcAddr` parameter is unnamed and unused. Instead, `init(Instance)` obtains the member `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` by calling the supplied instance lookup callback for the string `"vkGetDeviceProcAddr"` (`:21509-21527`); subsequent device initialization uses that member to resolve device commands (`:23096` onward). The `DynamicLoader` overload also retrieves `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` directly from the library, then forwards it to the overload that ignores it (`:24357-24364`).

**Trigger and consequence:** initialize the dispatcher for a device while supplying the next-layer `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` callback needed by a Vulkan layer, where that callback cannot be obtained through the supplied `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`. This overload ignores the explicit device callback, then resolves device commands through the instance callback (`:21509-21527,23096-23104`); command pointers can therefore come from the wrong layer or remain unavailable, breaking device-level Vulkan-Hpp calls. The Khronos Vulkan-Hpp project recorded this exact limitation for layered loaders in [issue #2578](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Hpp/issues/2578), and its [release notes](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Hpp/blob/main/README.md#breaking-changes) later state that the device callback is required for device-level initialization. No in-tree C++ caller was found. **Affected configuration:** downstream users of the copied Vulkan-Hpp dynamic dispatcher that initialize through Vulkan layers requiring an explicit next-layer device callback. **Confidence:** high for the ignored callback and the documented layered-loader consequence; this optional header has no checked-in C++ consumer. Use the supplied device callback when present. No Vulkan callback or runtime was invoked; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [Vulkan-Hpp full-body coverage](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-full-body-pass).

<a id="gd10221"></a>
## GD10221 — No-exceptions Vulkan-Hpp initialization can call a null lookup function

With `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS`, `detail::DynamicLoader` does not throw when its platform library load fails; it leaves `m_library` null and reports this only through `success()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan.hpp:20078-20084,20116-20130`). The default `DispatchLoaderDynamic::init()` creates a static loader and forwards it to `init(dl)` (`:21465-21476`), which obtains `vkGetInstanceProcAddr` with `getProcAddress` and passes the result to `init(PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr)` (`:21478-21492`). That overload only asserts the pointer before immediately calling it to resolve `vkCreateInstance` (`:21478-21492`). With assertions disabled and no globally available `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`, this calls a null function pointer. The no-exceptions convenience path does not expose the local loader's `success()` for the caller to check.

**Trigger and consequence:** a no-exceptions client calls `DispatchLoaderDynamic::init()` when the platform loader cannot open a Vulkan library and its procedure lookup returns null, in a build where assertions are disabled. The convenience overload keeps its `DynamicLoader` as a hidden static local, does not check `success()`, and forwards the null result to `init(PFN_vkGetInstanceProcAddr)`, which stores it and calls it on the next line. Initialization therefore invokes a null function pointer instead of reporting load failure. A caller using `init(dl)` with its own loader can check `dl.success()` first; a plain default-constructed dispatcher is not affected until an initialization overload is called. **Affected configuration:** optional Vulkan-Hpp clients defining `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` and calling the convenience `DispatchLoaderDynamic::init()` (or calling `init(dl)` without checking a caller-owned loader) when lookup returns null, with assertions disabled. **Confidence:** high for the null result propagation and subsequent call under these conditions; no such AROS client or build configuration was found. Return/report initialization failure before calling a null lookup function, or expose a checked no-exceptions initialization result. No loader failure or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [Vulkan-Hpp full-body coverage](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-full-body-pass).



## GD10222 — Vulkan-Hpp format traits omit `R16G16_S10_5_NV`

`Format::eR16G16S105NV` is declared for `VK_FORMAT_R16G16_S10_5_NV` in `workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_enums.hpp:2157`, but the copied generated `vulkan_format_traits.hpp` omits it from `getAllFormats()` (`:7215-9643`) and every canonical metadata switch. In particular, `blockSize()` (`:206-477`) asserts and returns zero for an unmatched format; `componentCount()` (`:2266-2538`) returns zero; and `compatibilityClass()`, `componentName()`, `componentNumericFormat()`, and `texelsPerBlock()` likewise assert and return their empty/zero fallbacks. The adjacent `eR16G16Sfixed5NV` format is included in these tables, so this is not the general handling of the NV format family. A source comparison of all 322 enum entries against the six full-format metadata tables and `getAllFormats()` found this as the sole non-alias, non-undefined omission; suffix aliases are represented by their canonical entries.

**Trigger and consequence:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp client passes `Format::eR16G16S105NV` to format enumeration or the affected metadata helpers. The format is absent from enumeration, while helper calls return invalid defaults and, with assertions enabled, invoke the assertion handler. This can produce incorrect format classification/sizing or abort an asserting client. **Affected configuration:** consumers of the copied optional Vulkan-Hpp headers; no in-tree AROS caller was found. **Confidence:** medium; the enum is explicit, distinct from its represented sibling, and omitted consistently from all format metadata, but no in-tree use or generated-registry source is available here to independently confirm intended trait semantics. No API call or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [full-body source review and coverage](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-format-traits-full-body-pass).


## GD10223 — Vulkan-Hpp result wrappers can read indeterminate outputs

Enhanced and RAII wrappers leave output scalars, pointers, and counts uninitialized, call the Vulkan function, and later read or move the output into a `ResultValue`. A structural scan found 114 same-function uninitialized local outputs passed to a dispatch call and then read after result handling (96 `uint32_t`, 10 `size_t`, four `uint64_t`, one `int32_t`, and three `void *`). A focused scan of the vector/data-returning wrappers separately found 102 count/size locals read after `resultCheck()`; these are a subset of the same error-output pattern, not a separate bug count. Per-command error-output contracts remain relevant to each claimed trigger. `enumerateInstanceVersion()` does this with `apiVersion` in both the enhanced wrapper (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:5738-5751`) and RAII `Context::enumerateInstanceVersion()` (`vulkan_raii.hpp:16811-16820`); the official command reference permits loader/layer allocation and other failures ([`vkEnumerateInstanceVersion`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkEnumerateInstanceVersion.html)). The RAII instance is conditional on `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` with result assertions disabled/nonfatal. `Instance::enumeratePhysicalDevices()` does it with `physicalDeviceCount` (`:127-145`); the default and allocator overloads of `enumerateInstanceExtensionProperties()` (`:561-619`) and `enumerateInstanceLayerProperties()` (`:739-797`) likewise leave `propertyCount` uninitialized, pass it to the dispatch call, and read it after `resultCheck()`. The default and allocator overloads of the deprecated `PhysicalDevice::enumerateDeviceLayerProperties()` do the same (`:823-885`), as do both `PhysicalDevice::enumerateDeviceExtensionProperties()` overloads (`:650-716`) and both `Instance::enumeratePhysicalDeviceGroups()` overloads (`:5882-5946`) and the two `enumeratePhysicalDeviceGroupsKHR()` alias overloads (`:13447-13511`, which call the extension command with the same documented return contract). The WSI vector overloads `getSurfaceFormatsKHR()`, `getSurfacePresentModesKHR()`, `getSwapchainImagesKHR()`, and `getPresentRectanglesKHR()` have the same uninitialized-count/error-check/use sequence (`:9167-9221,9258-9312,9454-9505,9678-9731`). The `getSurfaceFormats2KHR()` overloads and `getSurfacePresentModes2EXT()` overloads repeat it (`:15368-15544,21388-21460`); the RAII Win32 `getSurfacePresentModes2EXT()` does as well (`vulkan_raii.hpp:23500-23532`); the `StructureChain` format overload also indexes both vectors with the indeterminate count after the no-exceptions error check (`:15534-15544`). The enhanced `getDisplayPropertiesKHR()`, `getDisplayPlanePropertiesKHR()`, `getDisplayPlaneSupportedDisplaysKHR()`, and `getDisplayModePropertiesKHR()` overloads follow the same count/error-check/read pattern (`:9808-9858,9884-9944,9971-10031,10060-10122`). The `getDisplayProperties2KHR()`, `getDisplayPlaneProperties2KHR()`, and `getDisplayModeProperties2KHR()` overloads do too (`:15570-15632,15658-15720,15749-15903`); both `StructureChain` mode-property overloads use the count in a vector-indexing loop after the result check (`:15850-15858,15897-15905`). The Vulkan reference pages list failure returns for these enumeration/query commands, including allocation failures and, for extension enumeration, `VK_ERROR_LAYER_NOT_PRESENT` ([instance extension
