modes](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetDisplayModePropertiesKHR.html)); under the general `VkResult` error-output rule, those failure paths do not guarantee a count value. `Device::getPipelineCacheData()` does it with `dataSize` (`:3640-3661`). `Device::getExecutionGraphPipelineNodeIndexAMDX()` has the same scalar shape (`:16799-16808`); `Device::mapMemory()` and `mapMemory2()` similarly return an uninitialized local `void *` if a failed dispatch leaves it untouched (`:1120-1129,8475-8480`); the KHR alias has the same flow (`:22599-22613`), and `getMemoryMetalHandleEXT()` returns an uninitialized local handle pointer after the same result check (`:31987-31992`). The Vulkan `VkResult` contract says runtime errors leave output parameters undefined unless the command specifies otherwise ([`vkMapMemory`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkMapMemory.html), [`vkMapMemory2`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkMapMemory2KHR.html), [`VkResult`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkResult.html)); these commands list failure returns and specify no error-output value. The wrapper moves that pointer into `ResultValue` before the caller can inspect its result. This confirms the mapping-pointer cases in the existing candidate; it does not independently validate the output contract for every other command listed. All four enhanced `PhysicalDevice::getVideoFormatPropertiesKHR()` overloads leave `videoFormatPropertyCount` uninitialized before dispatch and read it after `resultCheck()` (`:11255-11435`). Both enhanced `Device::getVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR()` overloads have the same count flow (`:11572-11646`). The core and EXT `PhysicalDevice::getToolProperties()` / `getToolPropertiesEXT()` vector overloads likewise leave `toolCount` uninitialized and use it after `resultCheck()` (`:7507-7571,21070-21134`). The default and allocator overloads of `Device::getPipelineExecutablePropertiesKHR()`, `getPipelineExecutableStatisticsKHR()`, and `getPipelineExecutableInternalRepresentationsKHR()` repeat the pattern for their respective count locals (`:22118-22191,22219-22292,22324-22403`). The corresponding RAII overloads also leave `executableCount`, `statisticCount`, or `internalRepresentationCount` uninitialized and use it after `resultCheck()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:23870-23902,23904-23935,23938-23972). Both EXT and KHR `PhysicalDevice::getCalibrateableTimeDomains*()` vector overloads do likewise (`:19768-19832,30525-30588`). The default and allocator `PhysicalDevice::getFragmentShadingRatesKHR()` vector overloads also leave and reuse an uninitialized count after `resultCheck()` (`:20860-20927`). The RAII `PhysicalDevice::getFragmentShadingRatesKHR()` vector overload repeats this flow (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:23287-23315`), so an error that leaves the count unwritten reaches its assertion/resize path in no-exceptions builds with result assertions disabled. Both enhanced overloads of `getCooperativeMatrixPropertiesNV()`, `getCooperativeMatrixPropertiesKHR()`, and `getCooperativeVectorPropertiesNV()` repeat that count flow (`:21196-21261,29193-29258,29511-29577`). The RAII `PhysicalDevice::getToolPropertiesEXT()` method repeats the uninitialized-count flow (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:23375-23401`). The two `getCooperativeMatrixFlexibleDimensionsPropertiesNV()` overloads have the same unchecked count read (`:31889-31958`); the RAII `getCooperativeMatrixPropertiesNV()` method also has it (`vulkan_raii.hpp:23428-23456`). `getSupportedFramebufferMixedSamplesCombinationsNV()` and `getOpticalFlowImageFormatsNV()` likewise use uninitialized counts after `resultCheck()` (`:21289-21359,27689-27767`), as does the RAII `getSupportedFramebufferMixedSamplesCombinationsNV()` (`vulkan_raii.hpp:23463-23492`). Both enhanced `Device::getFramebufferTilePropertiesQCOM()` overloads do the same (`:29039-29103`). The default and allocator overloads of `enumerateQueueFamilyPerformanceQueryCountersKHR()` and `enumerateQueueFamilyPerformanceCountersByRegionARM()` do the same for `counterCount` before resizing both returned vectors (`:15114-15208,32070-32165`). The ARM data-graph queries `getDataGraphPipelineSessionBindPointRequirementsARM()`, `getDataGraphPipelineAvailablePropertiesARM()`, and `getQueueFamilyDataGraphPropertiesARM()` also read their uninitialized counts after `resultCheck()` (`:29902-29981,30184-30258,30304-30381`). Both enhanced `Device::getVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR()` overloads have the same count flow (`:11572-11646`). The two `StructureChain` overloads use it to index `structureChains` and `videoFormatProperties` after only an assertion bounds check (`:11348-11381,11402-11435`); if the API returns one of its documented errors without writing the count and assertions are disabled, execution can index beyond both vectors. The RAII `PhysicalDevice::getVideoFormatPropertiesKHR()` vector and `StructureChain` overloads repeat the same uninitialized count and post-`resultCheck()` use (`vulkan_raii.hpp:19155-19181,19193-19228`); the RAII `StructureChain` overload also uses the count as an unchecked loop bound at `:19225-19227` when result assertions are disabled. The Vulkan `VkResult` contract says that output parameters have undefined contents when a command returns a runtime error unless the command specifies otherwise ([VkResult reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkResult.html)). For ordinary error returns, `detail::resultCheck()` in no-exceptions mode only invokes `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT_ON_RESULT`, which defaults to `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT` (`vulkan.hpp:7551-7559`, `vulkan_hpp_macros.hpp:74-80`); when assertions are disabled, control continues and the output is read. `ResultValue<T>` immediately copies or moves its argument into its `value` member (`vulkan.hpp:7371-7385`), so caller-side result checking cannot defer that read. Separately, `Device::acquireNextImageKHR()` and `acquireNextImage2KHR()` leave `imageIndex` uninitialized, but their `resultCheck()` success-code sets explicitly accept `eTimeout` and `eNotReady` before unconditionally moving the index into `ResultValue` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:9535-9562,9758-9783`). The WSI specification says a successful `vkAcquireNextImageKHR` sets `pImageIndex`, while `VK_NOT_READY` means no image was available and `VK_TIMEOUT` means none became available within the interval ([WSI specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/VK_KHR_surface/wsi.html)). The `vkAcquireNextImage2KHR` reference also defines the index as the acquired image and lists those statuses, without specifying a valid image index when no image is acquired. Thus the wrapper can move an indeterminate value if the implementation leaves the output untouched on either status; the candidate remains conditional on that output behavior. With `VULKAN_HPP_HANDLE_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_AS_SUCCESS` defined, `getSwapchainCounterEXT()` and `getPastPresentationTimingGOOGLE()` similarly accept `eErrorOutOfDateKHR` before using their uninitialized `counterValue` or `presentationTimingCount` (`:14469-14482,14558-14591,14616-14649`); these uses also depend on the API leaving outputs unwritten for that status.

Further non-count output instances occur in four typed helpers: `Device::writeAccelerationStructuresPropertyKHR()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:17625-17645`), `getRayTracingShaderGroupHandleKHR()` / `getRayTracingCaptureReplayShaderGroupHandleKHR()` (`:18216-18231,18275-18290`), and NV `getRayTracingShaderGroupHandleNV()` (`:19431-19446`). Each declares `DataType data` without value initialization, passes its address to an error-returning Vulkan command, then moves it into the result after `resultCheck()`. The Vulkan commands list host/device allocation, unknown, and validation failures ([acceleration-structure property reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkWriteAccelerationStructuresPropertiesKHR.html), [shader group handle reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetRayTracingShaderGroupHandlesKHR.html), [capture-replay handle reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetRayTracingCaptureReplayShaderGroupHandlesKHR.html)). In a no-exceptions build, `resultCheck()` only calls `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT_ON_RESULT`; when that assertion is disabled, each helper returns a `ResultValue` containing the moved output despite failure. For scalar `DataType` instantiations, the returned value is indeterminate. These are further instances of the same result-output root cause, outside the earlier primitive count inventory.

The enhanced `Device::getSemaphoreCounterValueKHR()` also leaves its `uint64_t value` uninitialized before the query and moves it into `ResultValue` after `resultCheck()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:20201-20213`). The core command, to which the KHR command is equivalent, lists device-lost, allocation, and unknown failures ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetSemaphoreCounterValue.html)); the general `VkResult` error-output rule leaves this output unspecified on runtime errors. In no-exceptions builds with result assertions disabled, the error result is returned alongside the indeterminate value. The core enhanced `Device::getSemaphoreCounterValue()` overload has the same uninitialized `uint64_t value` and post-check move at `vulkan_funcs.hpp:7151-7165`; it uses the same core command/error contract and is another wrapper instance of this GD10223 path.

The two enhanced `Device::getValidationCacheDataEXT()` allocator overloads also leave `size_t dataSize` uninitialized before the first query and use it after `resultCheck()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:18728-18747,18763-18782`). The command can fail with host/device allocation, unknown, or validation errors ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetValidationCacheDataEXT.html)); in no-exceptions builds with result assertions disabled, the loop exits on the error and subsequent assertion/resize logic reads the indeterminate size. This is another command-specific instance of GD10223.

The two enhanced `Device::getCudaModuleCacheNV()` allocator overloads also leave `size_t cacheSize` uninitialized before the first query, then use it in the loop condition, vector resize, assertion, and final resize (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:23547-23579,23586-23618`). The command can return `VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED`, `VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN`, or `VK_ERROR_VALIDATION_FAILED` ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetCudaModuleCacheNV.html)); on such an error, the general Vulkan output rule leaves `pCacheSize` undefined unless specified otherwise ([`VkResult`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkResult.html)). In no-exceptions builds with assertions disabled, the wrapper continues after `resultCheck()` and reads the indeterminate size, potentially attempting a huge resize or otherwise invoking undefined behavior. This is another command-specific instance of GD10223.

Five enhanced opaque descriptor-data helpers repeat the typed-output case: `getBufferOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT()`, `getImageOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT()`, `getImageViewOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT()`, `getSamplerOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT()`, and `getAccelerationStructureOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT()` each declare `DataType data` without value initialization, pass its address to an error-returning command, call `resultCheck()`, and move it into `ResultValue` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:24242-24255,24276-24289,24310-24323,24344-24357,24377-24390`). Their references list device/host allocation, unknown, or validation errors ([buffer](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetBufferOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT.html), [image](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetImageOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT.html), [image view](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetImageViewOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT.html), [sampler](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetSamplerOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT.html), [acceleration structure](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetAccelerationStructureOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT.html)). In no-exceptions builds with result assertions disabled, scalar `DataType` instantiations can return an indeterminate value after a failed dispatch. These are additional instances of GD10223; callers still need to choose a `DataType` large enough for the queried descriptor data.

The enhanced `PhysicalDevice::getSurfaceSupportKHR()` overload declares `Bool32 supported` without initialization, passes its address to `vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceSupportKHR`, and moves it into `ResultValue` after `resultCheck()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:9093-9098`). The official reference lists out-of-device-memory, out-of-host-memory, surface-lost, unknown, and validation failures, and defines the boolean only as an output for the query ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceSupportKHR.html)). In no-exceptions builds with assertions disabled, a failed dispatch that leaves the output untouched therefore returns an indeterminate support value. This adds a `Bool32` alias instance to GD10223; it is not represented in the prior primitive-type structural-scan subtotal.

The enhanced NV `Device::getAccelerationStructureHandleNV<DataType>()` overload also declares `DataType data` without initialization, passes its address to `vkGetAccelerationStructureHandleNV`, and moves it into `ResultValue` after `resultCheck()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:19489-19501`). The command documents host/device-memory, unknown, and validation failures, and its output is an eight-byte opaque handle ([official command reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetAccelerationStructureHandleNV.html)). In a no-exceptions build with result assertions disabled, an error that leaves the output unwritten can therefore return indeterminate data for scalar `DataType` instantiations. The caller must still provide a `DataType` of at least eight bytes; undersized instantiations violate the command's `dataSize` requirement and are not needed to trigger this result-error case. This is another command-specific GD10223 instance.

The two enhanced vector overloads of `PhysicalDevice::getCalibrateableTimeDomainsEXT()` also leave `timeDomainCount` uninitialized before the first count query, then inspect it after `resultCheck()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:19776-19795,19813-19832`). The command permits host/device-memory, unknown, and validation failures; its count is meaningful for successful/incomplete enumeration ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetPhysicalDeviceCalibrateableTimeDomainsKHR.html)). In no-exceptions builds with result assertions disabled, if an error leaves the count unwritten, the wrappers read the indeterminate count in the condition, vector resize, assertion, or final resize. This adds the calibrated-time-domain count overloads to GD10223. The RAII `PhysicalDevice::getCalibrateableTimeDomainsKHR()` method has the same uninitialized `timeDomainCount` and post-`resultCheck()` assertion/resize sequence (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:27465-27494`), as does the corresponding `getCalibrateableTimeDomainsEXT()` method (`:22821-22847`). Both dispatch through their respective alias slots, so each can encounter the same documented error path and is an instance of GD10223.

**Trigger and consequence:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp client uses an enhanced result wrapper whose dispatch returns an error without writing its output, with `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` and assertions disabled; or it calls an acquire-image wrapper that returns `eTimeout`/`eNotReady` without writing the index; with `VULKAN_HPP_HANDLE_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_AS_SUCCESS`, it can also receive `eErrorOutOfDateKHR` from the swapchain counter/timing wrappers while their scalar/count outputs remain unwritten. The wrappers read or move the indeterminate scalar, pointer, count, or size value before the caller can inspect `ResultValue::result`, causing undefined behavior. The acquire-image path can occur even with exceptions enabled because those statuses are explicitly accepted. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced API clients; the general error path requires no-exceptions with assertions disabled, while the acquire-image and out-of-date paths depend on the relevant output contracts and the latter on `VULKAN_HPP_HANDLE_ERROR_OUT_OF_DATE_AS_SUCCESS`. No in-tree AROS C++ caller was found. **Confidence:** medium; wrapper control flow and macro defaults are direct, but per-command output validity on errors is an external API contract not independently verified in this source-only pass. No Vulkan call or runtime behavior was exercised.

The RAII wrappers for `PhysicalDevice::getCooperativeMatrixPropertiesNV()` (`vulkan_raii.hpp:23428-23454`), `getCooperativeVectorPropertiesNV()` (`:26963-26992`), and `getCooperativeMatrixPropertiesKHR()` (`:27088-27113`) repeat the cooperative-query count path: each leaves its count uninitialized, calls the Vulkan command, then reads the count after `resultCheck()`. The RAII ARM data-graph methods `Device::getDataGraphPipelineSessionBindPointRequirementsARM()` (`:27187-27219`), `Device::getDataGraphPipelineAvailablePropertiesARM()` (`:27286-27315`), and `PhysicalDevice::getQueueFamilyDataGraphPropertiesARM()` (`:27337-27369`) do the same. These are additional GD10223 instances for the optional NV cooperative-vector, KHR cooperative-matrix, NV cooperative-matrix, and ARM data-graph APIs; the corresponding enhanced-wrapper command error contracts and generic `VkResult` output rule are described above. Under no-exceptions with result assertions disabled, an error that leaves the count undefined reaches the assertion/resize use. No new finding ID is needed.

Two Fuchsia export helpers and the NV remote-address helper have the same output issue. The enhanced `getMemoryZirconHandleFUCHSIA()` and `getSemaphoreZirconHandleFUCHSIA()` leave `zx_handle_t` locals uninitialized, dispatch, then move them into `ResultValue` after `resultCheck()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:24837-24844,24947-24954`); both commands list host-allocation, too-many-object, unknown, and validation failures ([memory handle](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetMemoryZirconHandleFUCHSIA.html), [semaphore handle](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetSemaphoreZirconHandleFUCHSIA.html)). The enhanced `getMemoryRemoteAddressNV()` similarly moves an uninitialized `RemoteAddressNV` (`void *`) after a failed result (`:25268-25276`); the RAII overload repeats this at `workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:25189-25202`. The command lists invalid-external-handle, unknown, and validation failures ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/memory.html#memory-remote-device-external-memory)). These are further GD10223 cases in no-exceptions builds with result assertions disabled; the RAII output-packaging instance is also covered by GD10264.

The enhanced OHOS `getMemoryNativeBufferOHOS()` helper also leaves an `OH_NativeBuffer *` local uninitialized, then moves it into `ResultValue` after result handling (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:26667-26676`). The command lists host-allocation, unknown, and validation failures ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetMemoryNativeBufferOHOS.html)), so in no-exceptions builds with result assertions disabled the returned pointer can be indeterminate. This is another platform-specific GD10223 instance.

The ARM tensor and tensor-view opaque capture-data convenience overloads repeat the typed-output case: each leaves `DataType data` uninitialized, passes it to the `VkResult` command, and moves it after `resultCheck()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:27545-27557,27578-27591`). The official descriptor-buffer chapter lists device/host allocation, unknown, and validation failures for both commands ([tensor and tensor-view capture data](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/descriptorbuffers.html#descriptor-buffer-capture-replay)). In no-exceptions builds with assertions disabled, scalar `DataType` instantiations can return indeterminate data. These extend GD10223; callers must still choose storage large enough for the relevant opaque data.

The two enhanced `Device::getShaderBinaryDataEXT()` allocator overloads also leave `size_t dataSize` uninitialized before querying, then use it after the result check in assertions and vector truncation (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:28391-28447`). The command lists device/host allocation, unknown, and validation failures ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetShaderBinaryDataEXT.html)); if its first query fails without writing the size, no-exceptions builds with assertions disabled continue into those reads. This extends GD10223.

The two enhanced `Device::getShaderInfoAMD()` vector overloads have the same count-output case: each declares `size_t infoSize` without initialization, performs a count query, retries only `eIncomplete`, then calls `resultCheck()` and uses the count in an assertion and vector resize (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:12509-12572`). The command permits host/device-memory, unknown, and validation errors ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetShaderInfoAMD.html)); if such a first query fails without writing the size, no-exceptions builds with non-aborting result assertions continue into the indeterminate-size reads. This is another command-specific GD10223 case; the two allocator overloads share the same flow.

The enhanced OHOS `Device::getSwapchainGrallocUsageOHOS()` overload also declares `uint64_t grallocUsage` without initialization, passes its address to the result-returning command, and moves it after `resultCheck()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:31782-31794`). The command documents `VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED`, `VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN`, and `VK_ERROR_VALIDATION_FAILED`, with no failure output value ([official Vulkan reference](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.4.341.0/linux/antora/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetSwapchainGrallocUsageOHOS.html)); the general `VkResult` output rule leaves it undefined on runtime errors ([VkResult reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkResult.html)). In no-exceptions builds with assertions disabled, a failed call can therefore return an indeterminate Gralloc usage mask. This is another command-specific instance of GD10223, conditional on the OHOS platform wrapper being enabled; no OHOS caller was found in this tree.

The enhanced OHOS `Queue::signalReleaseImageOHOS()` helper also returns an uninitialized `int32_t nativeFenceFd` after `resultCheck()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:31845-31858`). The command can fail with initialization, unknown, and validation errors, while the reference defines the fence-FD output only as a success result ([official reference](https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.4.335.0/linux/antora/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkQueueSignalReleaseImageOHOS.html)); the general `VkResult` rule leaves outputs undefined on runtime errors. If a failed call does not write the output, no-exceptions builds with assertions disabled return the indeterminate descriptor. This is another OHOS-gated GD10223 instance; no in-tree OHOS caller was found.

The enhanced `Device::getVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR()` vector overloads also leave `memoryRequirementsCount` uninitialized before the first count query, then read it after `resultCheck()` in the bounds assertion and vector resize (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:11576-11606,11611-11642`). The official command reference permits `VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN` and `VK_ERROR_VALIDATION_FAILED` and defines count outputs for successful/incomplete queries ([reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetVideoSessionMemoryRequirementsKHR.html)); on a failure with no output write, no-exceptions builds with assertions disabled proceed to read the indeterminate count. This is another command-specific GD10223 instance. The allocator overload has the same control flow.

The enhanced Win32 `Device::getMemoryWin32HandleNV()` helper also leaves a `HANDLE` local uninitialized, passes it to the result-returning command, and moves it into `ResultValue` after `resultCheck()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:12775-12790`). The official reference lists `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY`, `VK_ERROR_TOO_MANY_OBJECTS`, `VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN`, and `VK_ERROR_VALIDATION_FAILED` ([command reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetMemoryWin32HandleNV.html)); on a failed call that leaves the output unwritten, no-exceptions builds with assertions disabled return an indeterminate handle. This is another platform-gated GD10223 instance; `VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR` must be enabled.

Two external-memory export helpers add further platform-specific instances. The enhanced Win32 `getMemoryWin32HandleKHR()` declares an uninitialized `HANDLE` and moves it after `resultCheck()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:13567-13582`); the enhanced `getMemoryFdKHR()` does the same with an `int fd` (`:13639-13653`). Their references list host-memory, too-many-object, unknown, and validation failures ([Win32](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetMemoryWin32HandleKHR.html), [FD](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetMemoryFdKHR.html)). If failure leaves the output unwritten, optional no-exceptions clients with result assertions disabled return an indeterminate native handle. Both helpers are included in GD10223; the Win32 path requires `VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR`, while the FD path requires the external-memory-FD wrapper to be enabled.

The enhanced external-semaphore exports repeat the same issue: Win32 `getSemaphoreWin32HandleKHR()` moves an uninitialized `HANDLE` after `resultCheck()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:13777-13789`), and `getSemaphoreFdKHR()` moves an uninitialized `int fd` (`:13838-13850`). The official references list host-memory, too-many-object, unknown, and validation errors ([Win32](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetSemaphoreWin32HandleKHR.html), [FD](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetSemaphoreFdKHR.html)). In no-exceptions builds with assertions disabled, a failure that leaves the output unwritten reaches the return with an indeterminate native handle. These are platform-gated GD10223 instances (`VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR` for Win32; external-semaphore-FD support for the FD path).

The display-control wrappers also move output handles after `resultCheck()`: enhanced `PhysicalDevice::getRandROutputDisplayEXT()` moves an uninitialized `DisplayKHR` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:14212-14226`), while `Device::registerEventEXT()` and `registerDisplayEventEXT()` move uninitialized `Fence` locals (`:14344-14351,14406-14414`). The official references list runtime failure codes for RandR display lookup and both fence-registration commands ([RandR](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetRandROutputDisplayEXT.html), [device event](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkRegisterDeviceEventEXT.html), [display event](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkRegisterDisplayEventEXT.html)). If a failure leaves the output unwritten, no-exceptions builds with assertions disabled return an indeterminate display/fence handle. These are additional GD10223 instances; RandR requires the Xlib/XRandR platform guard.

Enhanced fence export has the same output issue on both platforms: `getFenceWin32HandleKHR()` returns an uninitialized `HANDLE` after failed result handling (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:14991-15020`), and `getFenceFdKHR()` returns an uninitialized `int fd` (`:15053-15080`). The Vulkan references list host-memory, too-many-object, unknown, and validation failures ([Win32 fence](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetFenceWin32HandleKHR.html), [POSIX fence](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetFenceFdKHR.html)). A failure that leaves the output unwritten can therefore return an indeterminate native handle in no-exceptions builds with assertions disabled. These are platform-gated instances of GD10223.

The Android external-memory helper `Device::getMemoryAndroidHardwareBufferANDROID()` leaves its `AHardwareBuffer *` local uninitialized and moves it after `resultCheck()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:16511-16516`). The official reference lists host-memory, too-many-object, unknown, and validation failures ([command reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetMemoryAndroidHardwareBufferANDROID.html)); on an error that leaves the output unwritten, no-exceptions builds with assertions disabled return an indeterminate pointer instead of a valid acquired buffer reference. This is another GD10223 case, gated by `VK_USE_PLATFORM_ANDROID_KHR` and the Android external-memory extension.

The RAII `Framebuffer::getTilePropertiesQCOM()` wrapper repeats the existing enhanced-wrapper case: it leaves `propertiesCount` uninitialized before the count query, then after `resultCheck()` uses it in the assertion and possible resize (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:26905-26924`). `vkGetFramebufferTilePropertiesQCOM` can return documented errors without providing a valid output count; with `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` and non-aborting result assertions, the wrapper continues to read that indeterminate count. This optional `VK_QCOM_tile_properties` RAII path is an additional GD10223 instance, not a separate finding. The enhanced overloads at `vulkan_funcs.hpp:29039-29103` are already covered.

The four RAII property-enumeration helpers in `vulkan_raii.hpp` repeat this same error-output defect: `Context::enumerateInstanceExtensionProperties()` (`:15270-15300`), `PhysicalDevice::enumerateDeviceExtensionProperties()` (`:15301-15330`), `Context::enumerateInstanceLayerProperties()` (`:15333-15359`), and `PhysicalDevice::enumerateDeviceLayerProperties()` (`:15361-15387`) declare `propertyCount` uninitialized and compare it after `resultCheck()`. Under `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` with result assertions disabled, an error return that leaves the output undefined proceeds to that read before packaging the error-bearing `ResultValue`. These are additional GD10223 instances, not a separate finding. The Vulkan references list error returns, including `VK_ERROR_LAYER_NOT_PRESENT` for layer-specific enumeration ([instance extensions](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkEnumerateInstanceExtensionProperties.html), [instance layers](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/man/html/vkEnumerateInstanceLayerProperties.html), [device extensions](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkEnumerateDeviceExtensionProperties.html), [device layers](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/man/html/vkEnumerateDeviceLayerProperties.html)). No checked-in C++ caller of these RAII methods was found; external API reachability only is claimed.

**Review evidence:** [targeted result-output trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-funcs-result-output-trace), [mapping-pointer error-contract follow-up](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-memory-map-pointer-error-contract-follow-up).



Additional RAII error-output cases in the same generated-header family are `Device::getTensorOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataARM<DataType>()` and `getTensorViewOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataARM<DataType>()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:26390-26422`): both move an uninitialized local into `ResultValue` after result checking. The command references permit failures and only guarantee output on success; with no exceptions and non-aborting result assertions, failed scalar/trivially default-initialized instantiations can package untouched output. `PhysicalDevice::getOpticalFlowImageFormatsNV()` also leaves `formatCount` uninitialized and reads it after `resultCheck()` (`vulkan_raii.hpp:26456-26492`). These add RAII instances to GD10223; the typed tensor helper output cases also share GD10264.

Further RAII enumeration-count instances confirmed in this pass are `Framebuffer::getTilePropertiesQCOM()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:26894-26925`) and `PhysicalDevice::getCooperativeVectorPropertiesNV()` (`:26961-26992`): each leaves its count uninitialized before the first result-bearing query and reads it after `resultCheck()`. In no-exceptions builds with non-aborting result assertions, documented errors that leave the count undefined can reach the final assertion/resize; these are additional GD10223 instances. `ShaderEXT::getBinaryData()` has the same uninitialized-size path, but it is already tracked as GD10266 and is not a separate finding here.

Additional ARM data-graph RAII count instances are `PhysicalDevice::getCooperativeMatrixPropertiesKHR()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:27085-27114`), `Device::getDataGraphPipelineSessionBindPointRequirementsARM()` (`:27188-27222`), and `Device::getDataGraphPipelineAvailablePropertiesARM()` (`:27287-27319`). Each leaves the count uninitialized before the first result-bearing query, then reads it after `resultCheck()` in the assertion/resize path; error returns that leave outputs undefined therefore share GD10223 under no-exceptions with non-aborting result assertions. Their enhanced counterparts and other ARM data-graph count helpers are already listed above. The two-call `SwapchainKHR::getLatencyTimingsNV()` fill count is tracked separately under GD10274.
**Additional confirmed GD10223 site (2026-11-02):** both enhanced `PhysicalDevice::getFragmentShadingRatesKHR()` overloads leave `fragmentShadingRateCount` uninitialized before the count query, then use it in vector resize/assert/truncation after `resultCheck()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:20858-20920`). The Vulkan reference lists `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY`, `VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN`, and `VK_ERROR_VALIDATION_FAILED` in addition to success/incomplete, and only defines the count for successful/incomplete enumeration ([`vkGetPhysicalDeviceFragmentShadingRatesKHR`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetPhysicalDeviceFragmentShadingRatesKHR.html)). In `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` builds where result assertions are disabled or nonfatal, an error on the first count call reaches the post-check count use. This is another GD10223 enumeration instance, gated by `VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate`; no in-tree C++ consumer was established. No Vulkan query/build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd10224"></a>
## GD10224 — Vulkan-Hpp owning wrappers retain borrowed allocators and dispatchers

`Optional<RefType>` stores only `RefType *`; its reference constructor saves the address it receives (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan.hpp:565-606`). The unique creation wrappers accept `Optional<const AllocationCallbacks>` by value and copy it into `detail::ObjectDestroy` (for example, `createInstanceUnique()` at `vulkan_funcs.hpp:57-75`). `ObjectDestroy` keeps that `Optional` member and later passes it to the handle's destroy method (`vulkan.hpp:6723-6756`); `UniqueHandle::~UniqueHandle()` invokes the deleter when the handle still owns a value (`vulkan.hpp:896-901`), and `Instance::destroy()` obtains the callback through `allocator.get()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:88-98`). Because `Optional<const AllocationCallbacks>` can be implicitly constructed from a `const AllocationCallbacks&`, a temporary callback object can be passed to the unique-creation wrapper; the deleter then retains a pointer to an object that dies at the end of the creation expression. A stack callback object that goes out of scope before the unique handle has the same lifetime problem. The RAII handle classes use the same borrowed-callback representation: for example, `DeviceMemory` stores `static_cast<const AllocationCallbacks *>(allocator)` in `m_allocator` (`vulkan_raii.hpp:9714-9720`) and later passes it to `vkFreeMemory` in `clear()` (`:9770-9781`). `Device::allocateMemory()` forwards the `Optional` to that owning wrapper (`:15430-15445`). Thus `device.allocateMemory(info, AllocationCallbacks{...})` can return a live RAII owner whose saved callback pointer refers to the temporary destroyed at the end of the expression. `DeviceMemory` is representative; other RAII owning handles similarly retain their allocation callbacks for destruction. The custom dispatcher in the unique-handle `ObjectDestroy` path is also borrowed: it stores `&dispatch`, then dereferences it during handle destruction, so a temporary or shorter-lived dispatcher has the corresponding dangling-pointer path.

**Trigger and consequence:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp client creates a unique handle or ordinary RAII owning handle with a temporary/shorter-lived `AllocationCallbacks` object, or uses a temporary/shorter-lived custom dispatcher with a unique handle. When the object is later reset/destroyed, cleanup reads a dangling callback pointer or dereferences a dangling dispatcher pointer. This is a use-after-lifetime read; it can pass invalid allocator data or call through invalid dispatch state, causing undefined behavior or incorrect cleanup. The unique-handle path applies to wrappers retaining `Optional<const AllocationCallbacks>` in `ObjectDestroy` (77 construction expressions were found in `vulkan_funcs.hpp`); the RAII-owner path is confirmed at the `DeviceMemory` allocation/free pair above. The Vulkan specification requires implementations that need callbacks between create and destroy to save a copy of the allocator, while requiring the callback functions and their backing data to remain valid for the object lifetime ([Vulkan Memory Allocation](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/memory.html)). The wrapper instead retains the address of the C++ `AllocationCallbacks` struct and later passes that address to the destroy/free call; therefore passing a temporary struct is invalid independently of the separate requirement that the callbacks and their `pUserData` remain valid. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp RAII/enhanced APIs when a non-null allocator or custom dispatcher does not outlive its owning object; no in-tree C++ caller or lifetime contract at these declarations was found. **Confidence:** high for temporary/shorter-lived allocator structs and medium for shorter-lived custom dispatchers; both pointer retention and later dereference are direct, but the checked-in tree does not document a dispatcher lifetime contract. No handle was created/destroyed; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [unique-handle dependency lifetime trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-unique-handle-allocator-lifetime), [RAII owner allocator retention pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-raii-owner-allocator-retention-gd10224).


## GD10225 — Vulkan-Hpp batch pipeline wrappers can leak partial successes

Vulkan permits batch pipeline creation to return an error while still returning handles for the pipelines that succeeded; the failing elements are null, and the application is expected to destroy each non-null handle (Khronos Vulkan specification, Multiple Pipeline Creation). The enhanced vector result wrappers call `detail::resultCheck()` before returning their output arrays (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:3764-3773,3793-3802,4916-4925,4945-4954,16561-16605`). Their `Unique` overloads call `resultCheck()` before wrapping raw handles in `UniqueHandle` (`:3846-3862,3882-3898,4998-5014,5030-5050,16652-16670,16690-16708`). The optional RAII header has the same error ordering in its vector-returning compute, graphics, ray-tracing KHR/NV, data-graph ARM, and beta execution-graph wrappers (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:16215-16234,16486-16505,22031-22053,22531-22550,21414-21433,27126-27146`): ordinary error results throw before raw handles are adopted. These wrappers also accept `ePipelineCompileRequiredEXT` in `resultCheck()` but only adopt the output vector when `result == eSuccess` (`:16223-16234,16494-16505,22040-22053,22539-22550,21422-21433,27135-27146`); when that status applies to one item while other items succeed, they return an empty RAII vector and lose those successful handles. The Vulkan specification says batch creation normally continues after an individual pipeline fails unless early-return is requested. In exception-enabled builds, a batch with at least one ordinary failed and one successful pipeline likewise throws at `resultCheck()`; stack unwinding discards the raw handle vector without destroying its non-null entries. With `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS`, `resultCheck()` applies `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT_ON_RESULT` instead (`vulkan.hpp:7551-7576`); if that assertion is disabled or nonfatal (including the default `assert` under `NDEBUG`), the RAII wrapper continues and returns an empty vector for the non-`eSuccess` result, again leaving non-null native handles unowned. These paths affect compute, graphics, ray-tracing, and data-graph batches, plus the beta AMDX execution-graph batch where enabled. Single-item convenience overloads are not included because a one-element batch cannot produce a partial success. Separately, the RAII ray-tracing vector wrapper accepts `eOperationNotDeferredKHR` but only adopts outputs when `result == eSuccess`; a call completed immediately with the former status returns an empty vector and drops its valid pipeline handles (`vulkan_raii.hpp:22040-22053`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp client calls a batch pipeline wrapper with multiple create infos and the Vulkan call creates at least one pipeline while another fails. In exception-enabled enhanced and RAII wrappers, an ordinary failure `VkResult` makes `resultCheck()` throw before handles are returned/adopted, leaking the successful handles. In the RAII wrappers, `ePipelineCompileRequiredEXT` is accepted but the successful subset is only adopted for `eSuccess`, so a batch returning that status can also lose its successful handles without throwing. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced or RAII API. For ordinary error results, the enhanced and RAII paths leak in exception-enabled builds; the RAII path also leaks with `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` when result assertions are disabled or nonfatal. The RAII `ePipelineCompileRequiredEXT` and ray-tracing `eOperationNotDeferredKHR` paths are accepted statuses and skip adoption regardless of exception mode. The AMDX wrappers apply only with `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS`. No in-tree AROS C++ caller of these wrappers was found. **Confidence:** high; wrapper ordering is direct, the RAII status gate is explicit, and the Vulkan specification expressly allows partial creation and requires cleanup of non-null outputs. No API call or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [enhanced-wrapper partial-creation trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-funcs-pipeline-partial-creation) and [RAII wrapper trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-raii-pipeline-partial-creation).



The RAII `Device::createShadersEXT()` batch also converts raw outputs to owning wrappers only when the aggregate result is `eSuccess` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:26680-26702`). Vulkan guarantees that every output slot is either null or a valid shader handle even on failure, and returns `VK_INCOMPATIBLE_SHADER_BINARY_EXT` when a binary cannot be used ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCreateShadersEXT.html)). A batch containing an incompatible binary plus another successfully created shader can therefore return a non-null handle alongside the accepted non-success status; the wrapper skips RAII conversion and returns an empty vector, leaking the valid shader handle. The later `reserve()` allocation-failure window after an all-success batch is separately GD10263.
<a id="gd10226"></a>
## GD10226 — Vulkan-Hpp RAII shader batches drop valid outputs on binary incompatibility

The selected `vulkan_raii.hpp` implementation stores raw outputs from `vkCreateShadersEXT`, accepts both `eSuccess` and `eIncompatibleShaderBinaryEXT` in `resultCheck()`, but constructs the owning `ShaderEXT` vector only when the result equals `eSuccess` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:26684-26701`). The Vulkan reference specifies that every output array element is set to either `VK_NULL_HANDLE` or a valid shader handle even when creation does not succeed, and that callers clean up a failed call by destroying every non-null handle ([`vkCreateShadersEXT`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCreateShadersEXT.html)). Therefore a batch that has already created a shader and then encounters an incompatible binary returns `eIncompatibleShaderBinaryEXT`; the RAII wrapper returns an empty vector and drops ownership of the earlier valid shader. The adjacent enhanced wrapper correctly preserves the output vector for that accepted result (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:28212-28220`), which isolates the defect to the RAII vector conversion.

**Trigger and consequence:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp RAII client submits multiple shader create infos, with at least one valid shader created and a later binary shader incompatible with the device. The Vulkan call returns `eIncompatibleShaderBinaryEXT` and leaves one or more non-null handles; `resultCheck()` accepts the status, but the RAII wrapper skips adoption because the status is not `eSuccess`. The returned vector is empty and the valid shader handles leak. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp RAII API with `VK_EXT_shader_object`; the in-tree tree has no caller of this method. **Confidence:** high; the result gate and ownership omission are direct, and the Vulkan reference explicitly requires cleanup of every non-null output on this status. No API call or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [RAII shader batch output trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-raii-shader-batch-output).


## GD10227 — Vulkan-Hpp batch unique wrappers leak handles if RAII-vector allocation throws

The batch `Unique` wrappers create Vulkan objects into ordinary handle vectors, then allocate the destination vector of owning `UniqueHandle`s afterward. For example, `createComputePipelinesUnique()` dispatches into `std::vector<Pipeline>`, checks the result, and only then calls `uniquePipelines.reserve()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:3846-3862,3882-3898`). The same ordering appears in `allocateCommandBuffersUnique()`, `allocateDescriptorSetsUnique()`, `createGraphicsPipelinesUnique()`, `createSharedSwapchainsKHRUnique()`, `createShadersEXTUnique()`, and other batch wrappers (`:2593-2604,4506-4517,4998-5014,10396-10410,28285-28299,28724-28740,29720-29736`). The optional RAII header similarly creates raw handle vectors before `pipelinesRAII.reserve()` and the equivalent reservations for command buffers, descriptor sets, swapchains, shaders and pipeline binaries (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:15850-15870,16215-16234,16338-16358,16486-16505,18821-18838,26684-26701,26818-26830`).

If any destination `reserve()` throws `std::bad_alloc` after a successful Vulkan call, stack unwinding destroys only the ordinary handle vector; it does not invoke Vulkan destroy/free commands. The `UniqueHandle` deleter is the layer that invokes destruction when an owning handle has been constructed (`vulkan.hpp:896-901`), but at the failing reserve no such owners exist. A scan found 22 post-dispatch reserves in `vulkan_funcs.hpp`'s batch unique wrappers; this is scope evidence for the repeated pattern, not a claim that every API family was separately exercised.

**Trigger and consequence:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp client calls a batch unique/RAII creation or allocation wrapper with at least one object successfully returned, then the destination RAII vector allocation fails. If the caller catches the allocation exception and continues using the device, the created Vulkan object(s) remain allocated without an owning handle; pool objects continue consuming their pool allocation until pool/device teardown. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp `Unique`/RAII APIs in exception-enabled C++ builds under host allocation failure. The in-tree call sites for all batch wrappers have not been exhaustively audited. **Confidence:** high; the call/allocation order and lack of a cleanup guard are direct. No allocation failure or Vulkan operation was induced; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [batch ownership-transfer trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-batch-unique-allocation-failure).


## GD10228 — Vulkan-Hpp deferred ray-tracing wrappers return before output storage is safe to release

`vkCreateRayTracingPipelinesKHR` may return `eOperationDeferredKHR`. The Vulkan deferred-host-operations contract says command parameters may be accessed until completion, pointer parameters must not be freed or reallocated while pending, and output writes happen-before completion ([Deferred Host Operations specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/VK_KHR_deferred_host_operations/deferred_host_operations.html); [ray-tracing pipeline reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCreateRayTracingPipelinesKHR.html)). Several enhanced wrappers pass output storage whose lifetime ends when the wrapper returns while explicitly accepting that deferred status. The single-pipeline enhanced and `Unique` wrappers pass the address of a local `Pipeline` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:18038-18061,18148-18172`). The two batch `Unique` overloads pass `pipelines.data()` for a local vector, then copy its current contents into `UniqueHandle`s before that vector is destroyed (`:18072-18101,18111-18141`). The RAII vector and single-pipeline wrappers do the same with local storage (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:22026-22053,22059-22078`). Their `resultCheck()` calls accept `eOperationDeferredKHR`, so the wrappers return normally while Vulkan may still need those output pointers.

The ordinary enhanced vector overloads return their output vector to the caller and are not included; their caller must retain that returned storage through deferred completion. The raw pointer overload likewise leaves storage lifetime with its caller. `vkCreateDataGraphPipelinesARM` is excluded because its valid-usage rule requires `deferredOperation` to be null ([data-graph pipeline reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCreateDataGraphPipelinesARM.html)).

**Trigger and consequence:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp client passes a valid non-null deferred operation and the implementation returns `eOperationDeferredKHR`. The convenience wrapper then returns and destroys its stack/local output storage before the caller joins the operation to completion. The implementation may later write pipeline handles through a pointer whose storage lifetime has ended; the returned scalar or `UniqueHandle`s also contain only the pre-completion values. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced, `Unique`, or RAII KHR ray-tracing-pipeline APIs when actual deferral occurs; no checked-in AROS C++ call site of these methods was found. **Confidence:** high; the wrappers' automatic-storage pointers and accepted deferred result are direct, and the Vulkan specification explicitly requires pending-operation pointer storage to remain valid. No Vulkan operation, build, or runtime was used; source-only.

**Review evidence:** [deferred ray-tracing output-lifetime trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-deferred-ray-tracing-output-lifetime).


## GD10229 — Vulkan HIDD narrows `size_t` values on 64-bit targets

The public `GetQueryPoolResults` callback and method message declare `dataSize` as `ULONG` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan_hidd.h:256-260,1047-1058`), although Vulkan defines this argument as `size_t` ([Vulkan query reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/queries.html)). The same width mismatch exists for `CreateShaderModule`: its callback and message use `ULONG codeSize` (`vulkan_hidd.h:234-236,980-986`), while `VkShaderModuleCreateInfo::codeSize` is `size_t` ([Vulkan structure reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkShaderModuleCreateInfo.html); copied C++ wrapper at `workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:149873-149889`). AROS defines `ULONG` as unsigned 32-bit (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:38-44`) and `size_t` as `long unsigned int` by default (`compiler/crt/stdc/include/aros/types/size_t.h:11-14`), which is 64-bit on LP64 targets. The class forwards both fields unchanged to the registered driver callback (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/vulkan_class.c:617-623,695-702`), so either HIDD entry point cannot represent a valid value above `ULONG_MAX`.

The same proxy narrowing reaches the enhanced `CommandBuffer::setViewport()` and `setScissor()` overloads: each forwards `viewports.size()`/`scissors.size()` to the native `uint32_t` count while keeping the original proxy data pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:5331-5338,5355-5362`). An oversized source container is therefore dispatched with a truncated count, including zero at exactly 2^32 entries. These are additional uses of GD10233; the API count and device limits make such extents invalid inputs, and no non-generated in-tree callers were found.
The same enhanced-proxy count forwarding is present in `CommandBuffer::blitImage()`, `clearDepthStencilImage()`, `clearAttachments()`, and `resolveImage()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:5543-5563,5588-5604,5624-5637,5664-5683`). Each count is taken from an `ArrayProxy` while the original data pointer is forwarded; `clearAttachments()` forwards its two independent counts separately. Oversized source containers therefore follow the same GD10233 truncation boundary; these command counts/device constraints make such input invalid, and no non-generated in-tree caller was found.
**Trigger and consequence:** on a 64-bit target, a client passes a query-result buffer size or shader-module code size above 4 GiB through the corresponding public HIDD method. The callback receives the value truncated to 32 bits; a query driver sees a smaller output capacity, while a shader driver sees only a truncated code extent and may reject the module or process an incomplete shader. **Affected configuration:** 64-bit LP64 targets using the optional Vulkan HIDD and a registered driver; no in-tree HIDD-method caller or GPU registration was found, so reachability is through external HIDD clients/drivers. The 32-bit `ULONG` is sufficient on 32-bit targets. **Confidence:** high for the declared-width mismatch and direct forwarding; practical impact is conditional on a valid resource exceeding 4 GiB and an external caller/driver. No Vulkan call, allocation, or build was run; source-only.


## GD10230 — Vulkan `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` returns commands outside the device level

`vkGetDeviceProcAddr()` returns any match from `vk_loader_local_proc()` before checking the requested command's dispatch level (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/vulkan_loader.c:248-263`). That local table includes global and instance-level commands such as `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`, `vkEnumerateInstanceVersion`, `vkCreateInstance`, `vkDestroyInstance`, `vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices`, `vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties`, and `vkCreateDevice` (`:161-190`). The Vulkan specification requires `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` to return function pointers for requested core or enabled-extension **device-level** commands and NULL for other cases ([vkGetDeviceProcAddr reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetDeviceProcAddr.html)). If the name is not local, the HIDD class also falls back to `GetInstanceProcAddr(NULL, name)` when no device lookup callback is installed (`vulkan_class.c:937-946`); the callback contract explicitly permits a NULL instance for global functions (`vulkan_hidd.h:88-91`). Neither path filters out global, instance-level, or physical-device-level names.

**Trigger and consequence:** a client calls `vkGetDeviceProcAddr()` with a valid device and a name such as `vkCreateInstance`, `vkEnumerateInstanceVersion`, or `vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties`. The local path returns a non-NULL pointer although Vulkan requires NULL; for global names resolved by a driver's instance callback, the fallback can do the same. This violates the function-availability contract and can cause a caller treating the result as a device command to call it with an incompatible dispatchable handle. **Affected configuration:** the AROS Vulkan loader and Vulkan HIDD on all targets; the fallback portion also applies when a driver supplies `GetInstanceProcAddr` without `GetDeviceProcAddr`. No in-tree caller exercising an out-of-level query was found. **Confidence:** high for the unconditional local-table contract violation; actual client consequences depend on how the returned pointer is used. No Vulkan call or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.


## GD10231 — Vulkan-Hpp hashers dereference nullable string members

The generated `std::hash<ApplicationInfo>` specialization iterates through `pApplicationName` and `pEngineName` without null checks (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_hash.hpp:1175-1183`), although Vulkan explicitly permits either pointer to be `NULL` ([`VkApplicationInfo`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkApplicationInfo.html)). The same pattern occurs for `DebugUtilsObjectNameInfoEXT::pObjectName` at `:3851`, which may be `NULL` to remove an object name ([`VkDebugUtilsObjectNameInfoEXT`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkDebugUtilsObjectNameInfoEXT.html)), and for `DebugUtilsMessengerCallbackDataEXT::pMessageIdName` and `pMessage` at `:3868-3875`; the latter may be null for the device-address-binding message type ([`VkDebugUtilsMessengerCallbackDataEXT`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkDebugUtilsMessengerCallbackDataEXT.html)). The corresponding wrapper equality operators short-circuit on identical pointers before calling `strcmp` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:7009-7014,31896-31900,32173-32180`), so these null values are represented as valid wrapper state, but the hash functions dereference them.

**Trigger and consequence:** a C++ client hashes any of these valid structures while one of the nullable string members is `NULL`, for example by inserting it into an `unordered_set` or calling its `std::hash` specialization. The hasher dereferences the null pointer and the client process faults. **Affected configuration:** consumers that include the copied optional Vulkan-Hpp `vulkan_hash.hpp` header (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/mmakefile.src:10-23`); no in-tree C++ Vulkan-Hpp consumer was found. **Confidence:** high for the nullable API fields and unconditional dereferences; no hashing operation or runtime failure was exercised. Hash each nullable string conditionally, including a stable null representation. Source-only.

## GD10232 — Vulkan-Hpp release-backed unique handles have incompatible deleters

The `UniqueHandleTraits<DisplayKHR>` specialization selects `detail::ObjectDestroy<PhysicalDevice, Dispatch>` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_handles.hpp:2675-2683`), but three unique-returning helpers construct `UniqueHandle<DisplayKHR, Dispatch>` with `detail::ObjectRelease<PhysicalDevice, Dispatch>` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:14232-14244,23013-23026,24665-24678`). The `UniqueHandle` constructor accepts only its trait-selected `Deleter const &` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan.hpp:872-885`), and `ObjectRelease` is neither derived from nor convertible to `ObjectDestroy` (`:6804-6840`), so those helper instantiations cannot pass their deleter to the constructor. `UniqueHandleTraits<PerformanceConfigurationINTEL>` has the same `ObjectDestroy<Device, Dispatch>` trait (`vulkan_handles.hpp:2773-2781`), while `Device::acquirePerformanceConfigurationINTELUnique()` supplies `ObjectRelease<Device, Dispatch>` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:20545-20565`); `Device` exposes `release(PerformanceConfigurationINTEL)` but no matching `destroy()` (`vulkan_handles.hpp:15753-15780`). For `DisplayKHR`, a trait-selected `ObjectDestroy` calls nonexistent `PhysicalDevice::destroy(DisplayKHR, ...)`; the available API is `releaseDisplayEXT(DisplayKHR)` (`vulkan_handles.hpp:20032-20037`). Even the supplied generic `ObjectRelease` calls `PhysicalDevice::release(DisplayKHR)` (`vulkan.hpp:6830-6839`), which is also absent.

**Trigger and consequence:** a C++ consumer instantiates `getDrmDisplayEXTUnique`, `getRandROutputDisplayEXTUnique`, `getWinrtDisplayNVUnique`, or `acquirePerformanceConfigurationINTELUnique`, or uses either affected unique-handle alias in a context that instantiates its destructor. Compilation fails due to incompatible/missing deleter operations. **Affected configuration:** downstream C++ consumers of the copied optional Vulkan-Hpp headers that instantiate these helpers or unique-handle destruction. The wrappers are guarded by enhanced mode and `VULKAN_HPP_NO_SMART_HANDLE`; both are enabled by default, while `VULKAN_HPP_DISABLE_ENHANCED_MODE` also defines `VULKAN_HPP_NO_SMART_HANDLE` (`vulkan_hpp_macros.hpp:50-53`; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:14220-14229,20538-20548,23003-23012,24655-24664`). RandR and WinRT helpers additionally require their respective platform guards. A source-wide C++ include/call search found no in-tree Vulkan-Hpp client; the checked-in Vulkan HIDD implementation is C, so no default AROS build failure is claimed. **Confidence:** high for the type and member-function mismatches and the conditional wrapper exposure; no C++ client was compiled. Provide deleters that match each release API and use them consistently in unique-handle traits and factories. Source-only.

## GD10233 — Vulkan-Hpp array proxies truncate large container sizes

The enhanced `ArrayProxy` constructors accept container `.size()` values convertible to `std::size_t`, then silently cast the value to `uint32_t` for `m_count` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan.hpp:367-375`). The corresponding `ArrayProxyNoTemporaries` constructors do the same for `data()` and `begin()` containers (`:459-479`); initializer-list constructors also narrow `list.size()` (`:350-359`). These proxies feed the generated `ArrayProxy` overloads in `vulkan_handles.hpp`, which pass `proxy.size()` as the Vulkan `uint32_t` element count (for example `:5157-5161,5177-5181,5334-5341`).

The same narrowing applies to the enhanced `RenderPassCreateInfo` constructor and its `setAttachments()`, `setSubpasses()`, and `setDependencies()` methods (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:88-102,140-188`). `Device::createRenderPass()` forwards the structure directly as `VkRenderPassCreateInfo` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:5188-5197`). On the 64-bit API surface, a container larger than `UINT32_MAX` entries is retained by pointer while its count wraps; exactly 2^32 entries yields a zero count. This is another instance of GD10233, gated by the optional copied Vulkan-Hpp API; no in-tree C++ call site was found. The core `RenderPassCreateInfo2` enhanced constructor and paired array setters use the same count-narrowing pattern and forward to `vkCreateRenderPass2()` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:141984-142181`; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:7348-7357`). These are invalid/extreme input sizes beyond native count representation, not a demonstrated valid-call overrun.

The handwritten enhanced `CommandBuffer::setVertexInputEXT()` overload also accepts two `ArrayProxy` values and forwards both proxy sizes as the native `uint32_t` description counts (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:24798-24812`). A proxy implicitly constructed from a container larger than `UINT32_MAX` has already lost the high count bits before this call, so the driver receives a truncated binding or attribute count with the original data pointer. This is the same `ArrayProxy` narrowing root cause, not a separate defect. Repository search found no checked-in call site for this Vulkan-Hpp helper; external C++ consumers are the trigger.

The optional beta `Device::createExecutionGraphPipelinesAMDX()` overloads also pass `createInfos.size()` to the native `uint32_t createInfoCount` and allocate their result vectors from that already-narrowed proxy count (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:16551-16600`). A container above `UINT32_MAX` elements is therefore silently truncated before the dispatch; at 2^32 elements the call receives zero and returns an empty pipeline vector. This is another use of the same `ArrayProxy` conversion defect, gated by `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS` and `VK_AMDX_shader_enqueue`; no in-tree call was found.

The same narrowing reaches the enhanced and RAII `Device::bindTensorMemoryARM()` helpers, which forward `bindInfos.size()` to the native `uint32_t bindInfoCount` while retaining `bindInfos.data()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:27404-27413`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:26321-26328`). It also reaches enhanced/RAII `Device::writeMicromapsPropertiesEXT()` and `writeMicromapsPropertyEXT()` plus `CommandBuffer::writeMicromapsPropertiesEXT()`, which forward `micromaps.size()` as the native micromap count (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:25877-25916,26013-26029`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:25453-25506,25523-25535`). At a proxy size of exactly 2^32, those calls pass a zero count with the original nonempty data pointer; for other oversized sizes they pass a truncated count. These APIs are gated by `VK_ARM_tensors` or `VK_EXT_opacity_micromap`. Repository search found no non-generated in-tree C++ call sites for these helpers.

Further source-order checks found the same unchecked count forwarding in enhanced/RAII `Device::createShadersEXT()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:28212-28217,28239-28244`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:26682-26690`), `CommandBuffer::bindShadersEXT()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:28513-28523`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:26749-26764`), and `CommandBuffer::convertCooperativeVectorMatrixNV()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:29317`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:27012-27019`). Enhanced and RAII `Device::createDataGraphPipelinesARM()` overloads likewise size output storage and pass the narrowed proxy count (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:29623-29631,29656-29664`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:27121-27136`), and `Device::bindDataGraphPipelineSessionMemoryARM()` forwards proxy size as a native `uint32_t` count (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:30067-30068`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:27264-27272`). `bindShadersEXT()` compares already-narrowed proxy sizes, so its validation can fail to detect distinct oversized source lengths that truncate to the same count. These are additional uses of the same proxy-narrowing root cause, gated by `VK_EXT_shader_object`, `VK_NV_cooperative_vector`, or `VK_ARM_data_graph`; no non-generated in-tree C++ callers were found.

The same narrowing occurs in the enhanced `Device::getCalibratedTimestampsKHR()` overloads: `ArrayProxy<const CalibratedTimestampInfoKHR>::size()` is forwarded as native `uint32_t timestampCount` while the proxy retains the original data pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:30615-30656`). The corresponding RAII overload does the same (`vulkan_raii.hpp:27497-27511`). For a source container larger than `UINT32_MAX`, the query therefore covers only the truncated prefix; the returned timestamp vector is sized to that same truncated proxy count. The enhanced `Device::updateIndirectExecutionSetPipelineEXT()` and `updateIndirectExecutionSetShaderEXT()` overloads likewise forward `executionSetWrites.size()` as the native `uint32_t executionSetWriteCount` with the original pointer (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:31647-31660,31683-31696`). These add the optional `VK_KHR_calibrated_timestamps`/`VK_EXT_calibrated_timestamps` and `VK_EXT_device_generated_commands` call sites to this same root cause. A repository search found no non-generated in-tree C++ caller for these methods.

The OHOS `Queue::signalReleaseImageOHOS()` overloads also forward `waitSemaphores.size()` as native `uint32_t waitSemaphoreCount` while retaining the proxy's original semaphore pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:31845-31858`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:27939-27955`). A wait-semaphore container larger than `UINT32_MAX` therefore submits only the truncated prefix (zero waits at exactly 2^32). This adds the optional `VK_OHOS_native_buffer` queue call to the same root cause; its distinct uninitialized fence-FD result on error remains tracked under GD10223. No non-generated in-tree caller was found.

The EXT alias of the enhanced `Device::transitionImageLayout()` helper repeats the existing core count-forwarding case (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:22508-22520`; core at `:8720-8732`, also recorded in the earlier GD10233 follow-up). It passes `transitions.size()` and the original data pointer; the proxy has already narrowed oversized source sizes to `uint32_t`, so exactly `2^32` entries becomes a zero native count. This is another extreme-size GD10233 use, not a demonstrated valid-call overrun because the Vulkan count itself is `uint32_t`. No non-generated in-tree call site was found.

The enhanced `VideoBeginCodingInfoKHR` constructor and `setReferenceSlots()` setter also derive the native `referenceSlotCount` from `ArrayProxyNoTemporaries<const VideoReferenceSlotInfoKHR>::size()` and retain the original proxy pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:159089-159103,159148-159155`). `CommandBuffer::beginVideoCodingKHR()` forwards the resulting structure directly to `vkCmdBeginVideoCodingKHR()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:11848-11864`). A proxy created from a container larger than `UINT32_MAX` entries therefore carries a truncated reference-slot count with the original pointer; this is the same count-narrowing root cause, available in the optional `VK_KHR_video_queue` Vulkan-Hpp API. No non-generated in-tree C++ call site was found.

The enhanced `SwapchainTimeDomainPropertiesEXT` constructor and both `setTimeDomains()` and `setTimeDomainIds()` narrow an output-vector capacity from `size_t` to `uint32_t` while retaining the original output pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:155720-155726,155770-155775,155785-155790`). `Device::getSwapchainTimeDomainPropertiesEXT()` forwards that structure to the native query (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:20347-20357`). With a 64-bit client and more than `UINT32_MAX` output slots in either selected array, the implementation sees only the truncated capacity while the vector retains its larger extent; exactly `2^32` slots advertise zero. This is a separate instance of GD10233's count narrowing from GD10257's parallel-output-array mismatch. The type is part of the optional `VK_EXT_present_timing` API; no non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found.

The enhanced `VideoEncodeInfoKHR` constructor and `setReferenceSlots()` setter independently cast the reference-slot proxy size to `uint32_t` while retaining its original pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:169865-169882,169968-169973`). `CommandBuffer::encodeVideoKHR()` forwards the structure to `vkCmdEncodeVideoKHR()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:23449-23465`). Thus an optional downstream C++ caller with more than `UINT32_MAX` reference slots can submit a truncated count with the original pointer; this is another occurrence of the same GD10233 root cause, gated by the Vulkan video encode API. No non-generated in-tree caller was found.

The enhanced `PipelineLibraryCreateInfoKHR` constructor and `setLibraries()` narrow the proxy size to `libraryCount` while preserving the original library pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:46854-46857,46889-46894`). The structure extends `GraphicsPipelineCreateInfo` (`vulkan.hpp:14488`), which is forwarded by `Device::createGraphicsPipelines()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:4883-4923`). An optional downstream C++ caller with more than `UINT32_MAX` library handles therefore gets a truncated native count; this is another extreme-size instance of GD10233, with no non-generated in-tree constructor caller found.

Under `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS`, `ExecutionGraphPipelineCreateInfoAMDX`'s enhanced constructor and `setStages()` likewise narrow the stage proxy size while retaining `pStages` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:47002-47018,47056-47060`). The enhanced `Device::createExecutionGraphPipelinesAMDX()` accepts an `ArrayProxy` and forwards its size to the native `uint32_t` create-info count (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:16551-16570`). These beta-only count conversions are further GD10233 instances; no non-generated in-tree caller was found.

The enhanced `VideoEncodeAV1SessionParametersCreateInfoKHR` constructor and `setStdOperatingPoints()` setter narrow the operating-point proxy size to `uint32_t` while retaining its data pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:164823-164833,164880-164885`). This codec-specific structure can be chained through `VideoSessionParametersCreateInfoKHR::pNext`, which `Device::createVideoSessionParametersKHR()` forwards to native `vkCreateVideoSessionParametersKHR()` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:164792-164830,173258-173277`; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:11689-11700`). A downstream 64-bit C++ caller with more than `UINT32_MAX` operating points therefore gets a truncated native count with the original pointer, including zero at exactly `2^32`. This is another GD10233 occurrence in optional AV1 video encoding, limited to oversized input beyond the native count domain. No non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found.

The enhanced `VideoEncodeH264PictureInfoKHR` constructor and `setNaluSliceEntries()` setter narrow `naluSliceEntries_.size()` to `uint32_t` while retaining `naluSliceEntries_.data()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:165813-165823,165856-165862`). The enhanced `VideoEncodeH264SessionParametersAddInfoKHR` constructor and its `setStdSPSs()`/`setStdPPSs()` setters cast each proxy length to `uint32_t` while preserving the respective source pointers (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:166910-166917,166951-166977`). `VideoEncodeH264SessionParametersCreateInfoKHR` carries the add-info record through its pointer, and the H.264 create-info record is supplied on `VideoSessionParametersCreateInfoKHR::pNext`; `Device::createVideoSessionParametersKHR()` forwards the chain to native `vkCreateVideoSessionParametersKHR()` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:167060-167175,173258-173277`; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:11689-11700`). The enhanced `VideoEncodeH265PictureInfoKHR` constructor and `setNaluSliceSegmentEntries()` setter narrow the NAL slice-segment proxy size to `uint32_t` while retaining its original pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:168168-168175,168208-168215`). A downstream 64-bit C++ caller with more than `UINT32_MAX` slice-segment entries therefore gets a truncated native count paired with the full pointer, including zero at exactly `2^32`. The enhanced `VideoProfileListInfoKHR` constructor and `setProfiles()` setter similarly cast the profile proxy size to `uint32_t` while retaining the full source pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:172727-172729,172762-172767`). `PhysicalDeviceVideoFormatInfoKHR` carries this record through its input `pNext` chain, and `PhysicalDevice::getVideoFormatPropertiesKHR()` forwards that structure to `vkGetPhysicalDeviceVideoFormatPropertiesKHR()` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:123042-123090`; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:11235-11248`). For a profile container above `UINT32_MAX`, the enhanced wrapper therefore supplies a count describing only a truncated prefix. The enhanced `SwapchainCreateInfoKHR` constructor and `setQueueFamilyIndices()` setter also narrow `queueFamilyIndices_.size()` to the native `uint32_t queueFamilyIndexCount` while preserving the full proxy pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:154420-154447,154539-154544`). The enhanced `SwapchainPresentFenceInfoKHR` and `SwapchainPresentModeInfoKHR` constructors/setters independently narrow their proxy sizes into `swapchainCount`, retaining the full fence or present-mode pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:155167-155172,155202-155209,155305-155310,155340-155347`). `PresentInfoKHR` exposes a `pNext` chain, and `Queue::presentKHR()` forwards the complete record directly to `vkQueuePresentKHR()` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:135085-135107,135159-135162`; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:9555-9574`).
