These are further GD10233 instances; no non-generated in-tree C++ consumer was found. Practical reachability requires exceptionally large arrays on a 64-bit client. No present, swapchain creation, or build was run.

The copied `vulkan_structs.hpp` uses `ArrayProxyNoTemporaries` in enhanced constructors and setters for `RenderingAreaInfo`, `RenderingAttachmentLocationInfo`, `RenderingInfo`, `RenderingInputAttachmentIndexInfo`, and `ResolveImageInfo2` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:144617,144660-144663,145063,145099-145102,145566-145582,145640-145644,145783,145822-145825,145946-145963,146019-146022`). Each converts the proxy size to a `uint32_t` count but retains its original data pointer. A container larger than `UINT32_MAX` therefore creates a native-compatible structure whose count describes only a truncated prefix; passing that structure to a corresponding Vulkan operation processes fewer attachments, input indices, or resolve regions than supplied. This is another use of the same proxy narrowing, with no new finding ID; no non-generated in-tree C++ consumer was found.

The same `ArrayProxyNoTemporaries` narrowing appears in the enhanced `PipelineColorWriteCreateInfoEXT` and `PipelineCoverageModulationStateCreateInfoNV` constructor/setter pairs, `PipelineCreationFeedbackCreateInfo` constructor/setter pair, and `PipelineDiscardRectangleStateCreateInfoEXT` constructor/setter pair (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:128652-128654,128688-128691,128914-128919,128976-128979,129548-129554,129597-129601,129712-129718,129764-129768`). Each keeps the original pointer while storing a `uint32_t` count. These are further GD10233 instances for 64-bit downstream C++ clients with arrays larger than the native count domain; no separate root cause or checked-in non-generated consumer was found.


The enhanced `DecompressMemoryInfoEXT` constructor and `setRegions()` setter also narrow `regions_.size()` to `uint32_t` while retaining the region pointer (`vulkan_structs.hpp:32734-32741,32777-32781`). `CommandBuffer::decompressMemoryEXT()` forwards that structure directly to `vkCmdDecompressMemoryEXT()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:30939-30947`). A downstream 64-bit Vulkan-Hpp client supplying more than `UINT32_MAX` regions therefore records a truncated region count with the original pointer (zero at exactly `2^32`); this is another GD10233 instance, gated by optional `VK_EXT_memory_decompression`. Such a container exceeds the native count domain and is an invalid/extreme input boundary, not a demonstrated valid-call overrun. No non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found.

The `DependencyInfo` enhanced constructor independently narrows its memory, buffer-memory, and image-memory barrier proxy counts, and the three paired setters repeat those casts (`vulkan_structs.hpp:33848-33859,33900-33904,33921-33925,33942-33946`). `CommandBuffer::pipelineBarrier2()`, `setEvent2()`, and `waitEvents2()` forward this structure to native synchronization2 commands (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:7755-7762,8102-8110,8138-8157`). An oversized barrier array on a 64-bit downstream C++ client is therefore represented by a truncated count with the original pointer (zero at `2^32`); it is another GD10233 instance, available through Vulkan 1.3 or `VK_KHR_synchronization2`. These sizes exceed the native count domain and are invalid/extreme inputs, not a demonstrated valid-call overrun. No non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found.

Descriptor creation wrappers add three more occurrences: `DescriptorPoolCreateInfo` narrows its pool-size count (`vulkan_structs.hpp:35429-35434,35479-35484`), `DescriptorSetAllocateInfo` narrows set-layout count (`:35706-35710,35749-35753`), and `DescriptorSetLayoutBinding` uses immutable-sampler proxy size as `descriptorCount` (`:35975-35985,36029-36034`). The corresponding pool creation, set allocation and layout creation APIs forward these structures to Vulkan (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:4317-4332,4456-4479,4201-4220`). As with the other GD10233 sites, oversized arrays beyond `UINT32_MAX` silently truncate while retaining the original pointer; the resulting counts are outside the native count domain, so this is scoped to invalid/extreme input. These are optional Vulkan-Hpp C++ paths with no non-generated in-tree callers found.

The descriptor-set-layout chain has further paired count/pointer casts: `DescriptorSetLayoutBindingFlagsCreateInfo` narrows binding flags (`vulkan_structs.hpp:36128-36130,36164-36169`) and `DescriptorSetLayoutCreateInfo` narrows its bindings (`:36268-36275,36313-36318`). Their `StructExtends` relation allows the flags record in the layout-create `pNext` chain (`vulkan.hpp:10433`), and `Device::createDescriptorSetLayout()` forwards the containing create info (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:4201-4220`). `DescriptorSetVariableDescriptorCountAllocateInfo` similarly narrows its per-set count array (`vulkan_structs.hpp:36638-36640,36674-36679`); it extends `DescriptorSetAllocateInfo` (`vulkan.hpp:10469`) and reaches `vkAllocateDescriptorSets()` through the same device helper (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:4456-4479`). These are further GD10233 occurrences with the same extreme-size-only truncation scope; no in-tree C++ caller was found.

`DescriptorUpdateTemplateCreateInfo` also narrows `descriptorUpdateEntries_.size()` in its enhanced constructor and setter while preserving the pointer (`vulkan_structs.hpp:37040-37045,37091-37096`). `Device::createDescriptorUpdateTemplate()` forwards it to native dispatch (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:6803-6818`), adding another optional Vulkan-Hpp GD10233 occurrence with the same greater-than-`UINT32_MAX` input limitation. No non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found.

`DeviceQueueCreateInfo` narrows the queue-priority proxy size to its native `queueCount` in the constructor and setter while retaining `pQueuePriorities` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:37507-37516,37561-37566`). This record is embedded in `DeviceCreateInfo`, which `PhysicalDevice::createDevice()` forwards to `vkCreateDevice()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:478-492`). A downstream 64-bit C++ client supplying more than `UINT32_MAX` priorities therefore gets a truncated queue count; this is another GD10233 edge case outside the representable native count range. No non-generated in-tree Vulkan-Hpp caller was found.

`DeviceCreateInfo`'s enhanced constructor and setters also narrow queue-create-info and enabled-extension-name array sizes while retaining their pointers (`vulkan_structs.hpp:38408-38422,38479-38484,38522-38527`); `PhysicalDevice::createDevice()` forwards the result to native `vkCreateDevice()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:478-492`). Oversized arrays are further GD10233 count-truncation cases. The constructor also narrows deprecated enabled-layer-name count, but the current [Vulkan device-create contract](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/man/html/VkDeviceCreateInfo.html) marks those layer fields ignored, so no behavior claim is based on that field. No non-generated in-tree Vulkan-Hpp caller was found.

Device-group records add three more count casts: `DeviceGroupDeviceCreateInfo` narrows the physical-device proxy (`vulkan_structs.hpp:40139-40143,40176-40181`) and extends `DeviceCreateInfo` (`vulkan.hpp:9793`); `DeviceGroupPresentInfoKHR` narrows device masks (`:40384-40388,40421-40426`) and extends `PresentInfoKHR` (`vulkan.hpp:11669`), which reaches `Queue::presentKHR()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:9564-9575`); and `DeviceGroupRenderPassBeginInfo` narrows per-device render areas (`:40531-40541,40578-40583`), extending render-pass and dynamic-rendering begin records (`vulkan.hpp:10045,10054`). These are additional GD10233 cases for arrays larger than the native `uint32_t` count domain; no non-generated in-tree Vulkan-Hpp caller was found.

`GeneratedCommandsShaderInfoEXT` narrows its enhanced shader-array proxy in its constructor and `setShaders()` while retaining `pShaders` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:54326-54328,54361-54365`). The record extends both `GeneratedCommandsInfoEXT` and `GeneratedCommandsMemoryRequirementsInfoEXT` (`vulkan.hpp:19170-19185`), which are forwarded by the generated-command preprocess/execute helpers and `Device::getGeneratedCommandsMemoryRequirementsEXT()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:31264-31310,31320-31375`). `PipelineVertexInputStateCreateInfo` similarly narrows binding- and attribute-description arrays in its constructor and setters (`vulkan_structs.hpp:55005-55017,55055-55061,55079-55085`); it is carried by `GraphicsPipelineCreateInfo` (`:56906-56925,56952-56971`) into `Device::createGraphicsPipelines()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:4883-4923`). `PipelineViewportStateCreateInfo` adds the viewport and scissor arrays to the same count-narrowing family: its enhanced constructor and setters cast each proxy size to `uint32_t` while retaining the corresponding pointer (`vulkan_structs.hpp:55454-55469,55503-55509,55524-55530`). The same GD10233 pattern appears in `PipelineColorBlendStateCreateInfo::attachments` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:56583-56599,56647-56654`), `PipelineDynamicStateCreateInfo::dynamicStates` (`:56772-56779,56815-56821`), and the stage array in `GraphicsPipelineCreateInfo` (`:56949-56986,57024-57030`). These are additional extreme-size inputs outside the native count domain; no non-generated in-tree Vulkan-Hpp caller was found.

The NV graphics-shader-group structures carry three more count/pointer pairs: `GraphicsShaderGroupCreateInfoNV::stages` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:57388-57399,57430-57437`), and `GraphicsPipelineShaderGroupsCreateInfoNV::groups` and `pipelines` (`:57559-57570,57600-57607,57621-57628`). Image compression controls also narrow their fixed-rate array count in the enhanced constructor and setter (`vulkan_structs.hpp:58979-58989,59025-59031`). `ImageCompressionControlEXT` extends image creation, swapchain creation, and physical-device image-format queries (`vulkan.hpp:15359-15383`), each of which forwards the containing native structure (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:2144-2174,6283-6314,9322-9369`). Under `VK_USE_PLATFORM_FUCHSIA`, `ImageConstraintsInfoFUCHSIA` narrows its format-constraints proxy in its constructor and setter (`vulkan_structs.hpp:59433-59445,59476-59483`). The explicit and list DRM-format-modifier image-create records also narrow their enhanced arrays: plane layouts in `ImageDrmFormatModifierExplicitCreateInfoEXT` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:59854-59864,59901-59908`) and modifier values in `ImageDrmFormatModifierListCreateInfoEXT` (`:60006-60011,60041-60048`). `ImageFormatListCreateInfo` narrows the enhanced view-format array in its constructor and setter (`vulkan_structs.hpp:60239-60244,60274-60281`). It extends `ImageCreateInfo`, `SwapchainCreateInfoKHR`, and `PhysicalDeviceImageFormatInfo2` (`vulkan.hpp:10199-10224`), reaching image creation, swapchain creation and image-format queries. `DeviceGroupSubmitInfo` narrows wait-semaphore device indices, command-buffer device masks, and signal-semaphore device indices in its enhanced constructor and paired setters (`vulkan_structs.hpp:40691-40702,40735-40740,40756-40761,40777-40782`). It extends `SubmitInfo` (`vulkan.hpp:9757`), which is forwarded through `Queue::submit()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:928-940`). `ImageCreateInfo` narrows the queue-family-index proxy size in its constructor and setter (`vulkan_structs.hpp:41040-41058,41152-41157`). `Device::createImage()` forwards the structure to native image creation (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:2162-2175`), so an oversized concurrent-sharing family list has the same GD10233 truncation behavior. No non-generated in-tree Vulkan-Hpp caller was found.

The optional `DirectDriverLoadingListLUNARG` constructor and `setDrivers()` narrow the driver proxy length to `driverCount` while retaining the original pointer (`vulkan_structs.hpp:43140-43144,43183-43188`). The structure extends `InstanceCreateInfo` (`vulkan.hpp:16832`) and is forwarded to native `vkCreateInstance()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:40-52`), another GD10233 instance for downstream clients with more than `UINT32_MAX` entries. No non-generated in-tree Vulkan-Hpp caller was found.

The older enhanced `CommandBuffer::pushConstants()` overload has the same byte-count narrowing at `workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:4861-4878`: `values.size() * sizeof(ValuesType)` is passed to native `vkCmdPushConstants` `uint32_t size` without a range check, while `values.data()` remains the original pointer. If the byte extent exceeds `UINT32_MAX`, the command records only its low 32-bit size. Vulkan defines `size` as the byte count of `pValues` and requires it to fit `maxPushConstantsSize` ([command reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdPushConstants.html)); since this native size is itself `uint32_t`, such an input is outside valid usage. The helper silently truncates that oversized C++ input instead of rejecting it, so this is an invalid-input handling manifestation of GD10233, not a demonstrated valid-call corruption path or a separate ID. No non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found.

The RAII `CommandBuffer::pushConstants()` overload repeats the same byte-extent conversion (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:16465-16477`): it passes `values.size() * sizeof(ValuesType)` directly to native `vkCmdPushConstants`'s `uint32_t size`, while retaining `values.data()`. This adds the RAII surface to the same GD10233 invalid-input behavior, subject to the same `maxPushConstantsSize` valid-usage limit; it is not a separate root cause or valid-call corruption claim. No non-generated in-tree caller was found.

The enhanced `WriteDescriptorSetInlineUniformBlock` proxy constructor and `setData()` setter separately narrow the byte extent, computing `static_cast<uint32_t>(data_.size() * sizeof(T))` while retaining `data_.data()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:174635-174637,174670-174676`). On a 64-bit C++ consumer, a data range larger than `UINT32_MAX` bytes can therefore be represented as only its low 32-bit byte count; for example, an extent of `2^32 + 4` bytes becomes `dataSize == 4`, and an update using a matching four-byte inline-uniform descriptor count writes only the first four bytes. An exact multiple of `2^32` becomes zero and violates Vulkan's nonzero `dataSize` requirement. The Vulkan contract defines `dataSize` as the byte length at `pData`, requires it to be positive, and requires the enclosing inline-uniform descriptor count to equal it ([structure reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkWriteDescriptorSetInlineUniformBlock.html), [write-descriptor-set reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkWriteDescriptorSet.html)). This is the same unchecked large-container extent narrowing, though this wrapper narrows bytes directly rather than an ArrayProxy element count. It is available with core Vulkan 1.3 or `VK_EXT_inline_uniform_block`; no non-generated in-tree C++ consumer was found.

The same defect is present in the RAII command-buffer helpers `setColorBlendEnableEXT()`, `setColorBlendEquationEXT()`, `setColorWriteMaskEXT()`, `setColorBlendAdvancedEXT()`, `setViewportSwizzleNV()`, and `setCoverageModulationTableNV()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:25991-26012,26019-26035,26090-26103,26161-26174,26217-26224`). Each forwards `ArrayProxy::size()` to a native `uint32_t` count while the proxy keeps the original pointer. A 64-bit caller with an oversized source container therefore records only the truncated prefix, including a zero-element command at exactly 2^32 entries. These are optional Vulkan-Hpp RAII methods; repository search found no non-generated in-tree caller. The neighboring `setSampleMaskEXT()` checks its size against the bounded sample-count-derived requirement and is not included. The later RAII `bindTensorMemoryARM()` is already covered above. In the same reviewed interval, `getOpticalFlowImageFormatsNV()` leaves its count unset on a failed first query before the post-loop result check; this is an existing GD10223 result/count case, not a new root cause (line 26461-26488).

The core Vulkan 1.3 enhanced and RAII `Queue::submit2()` overloads also forward `ArrayProxy<const SubmitInfo2>::size()` to native `uint32_t submitCount` while keeping the original pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:7790-7802`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:17687-17696`). Oversized source containers therefore submit only the truncated prefix, including zero entries at a source size divisible by 2^32. This is the same proxy narrowing defect; no checked-in non-generated call site was found.

The same unchecked element-count conversion occurs in the enhanced `AccelerationStructureInfoNV` constructor and `setGeometries()` setter: both obtain `geometries_.size()`, cast it to `uint32_t`, and retain the proxy data pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:2173-2185,2234-2241`). `CommandBuffer::buildAccelerationStructureNV()` forwards the resulting `geometryCount` and `pGeometries` directly to `vkCmdBuildAccelerationStructureNV()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:19090-19127`). A downstream 64-bit caller with more than `UINT32_MAX` geometries therefore submits a truncated count with the original pointer; this is another occurrence of the same GD10233 root cause, gated by `VK_NV_ray_tracing`. No non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found.

The same `ArrayProxyNoTemporaries` size narrowing reaches four pNext descriptor-write records: `WriteDescriptorSetAccelerationStructureKHR` and `WriteDescriptorSetAccelerationStructureNV` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:174322-174395,174466-174539`), `WriteDescriptorSetPartitionedAccelerationStructureNV` (`:174750-174825`), and `WriteDescriptorSetTensorARM` (`:174895-174961`). Their enhanced constructors/setters pair the proxy's narrowed element count with its original data pointer. These records extend `VkWriteDescriptorSet`; `Device::updateDescriptorSets()` reinterprets and forwards that record and pNext chain to `vkUpdateDescriptorSets()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:4621-4650`; [KHR acceleration structure](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkWriteDescriptorSetAccelerationStructureKHR.html), [NV acceleration structure](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkWriteDescriptorSetAccelerationStructureNV.html), [partitioned acceleration structure](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkWriteDescriptorSetPartitionedAccelerationStructureNV.html), [ARM tensor](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkWriteDescriptorSetTensorARM.html), [descriptor update](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkUpdateDescriptorSets.html)). An oversized source container therefore supplies a truncated descriptor payload count with the original pointer, including zero at exactly 2^32 elements. **Scope qualification:** these are additional wrapper sites for GD10233, not a new root cause; descriptor arrays that large exceed Vulkan's valid descriptor limits, so this is an invalid/extreme-input handling candidate rather than a demonstrated valid-call fault. The extensions are `VK_KHR_acceleration_structure`, `VK_NV_ray_tracing`, `VK_NV_partitioned_acceleration_structure`, and `VK_ARM_tensors`. No non-generated in-tree Vulkan-Hpp caller was found.

The enhanced `VideoDecodeInfoKHR` constructor and `setReferenceSlots()` setter cast the reference-slot proxy size to `uint32_t` while retaining its data pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:162319-162343,162413-162419`). `CommandBuffer::decodeVideoKHR()` forwards that structure directly to `vkCmdDecodeVideoKHR()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:11919-11935`). A downstream 64-bit C++ caller with more than `UINT32_MAX` entries therefore gets a truncated native count paired with the original pointer. This is another GD10233 site in optional Vulkan video decoding; the size is beyond the native count and video API limits, so this records oversized-input truncation, not a valid-call overrun. A repository search found no non-generated in-tree C++ caller.

The enhanced `VideoDecodeH265SessionParametersAddInfoKHR` constructor and `setStdVPSs()`, `setStdSPSs()`, and `setStdPPSs()` setters narrow the three proxy sizes to `uint32_t` while retaining their respective pointers (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:161968-161980,162012-162060`). The enhanced `VideoDecodeH265PictureInfoKHR` constructor and `setSliceSegmentOffsets()` setter cast the slice-offset proxy size to `uint32_t` while retaining its pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:161692-161700,161738-161742`). The enhanced `VideoDecodeH264PictureInfoKHR` constructor and `setSliceOffsets()` setter cast the slice-offset proxy size to `uint32_t` while retaining its data pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:160745-160751,160788-160794`). The enhanced `VideoDecodeAV1PictureInfoKHR` constructor and `setTileOffsets()`/`setTileSizes()` setters also derive the shared `tileCount` from `ArrayProxyNoTemporaries::size()` and retain the array pointers (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:159855-159878,159929-159949`). The enhanced `ValidationFeaturesEXT` constructor and enabled/disabled setters narrow their two feature-array proxy sizes to `uint32_t` while retaining the original pointers (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:158112-158121,158153-158160,158176-158184`). These are additional GD10233 instances, limited to input beyond native/API limits; no non-generated in-tree C++ Vulkan-Hpp caller was found.

The enhanced `TimelineSemaphoreSubmitInfo` constructor and its wait/signal value setters narrow proxy sizes to `uint32_t` while retaining the array pointers (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:157431-157443,157472-157479,157493-157500`). An oversized downstream value array therefore reaches native submission with a truncated count and original pointer. This is another GD10233 instance for invalid oversized input beyond native/API limits; no non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found.

**Trigger and consequence:** on a 64-bit target, a C++ container or initializer list passed to one of these enhanced APIs has more than `UINT32_MAX` elements. The proxy count wraps/truncates, so the Vulkan call receives only the narrowed count while retaining the original buffer pointer; at exactly 2^32 elements it sends a count of zero. The call silently processes fewer elements than the caller supplied. The `PushConstantsInfo` and inline-uniform byte-extent wrappers have the corresponding trigger when their input range exceeds `UINT32_MAX` bytes; the narrowed push-constant `size` records only its prefix, while narrowed inline-uniform `dataSize` makes the descriptor update write only the prefix described by that value (or zero at an exact 2^32-byte extent). These routes are gated by core Vulkan 1.4 / `VK_KHR_maintenance6` and core Vulkan 1.3 / `VK_EXT_inline_uniform_block`, respectively. The same element-count failure applies to the ARM tensor bind and opacity-micromap property helpers named above, including their RAII forwards, when those extensions are enabled. It also applies to enhanced/RAII shader-object creation and binding, cooperative-vector conversion, ARM data-graph pipeline creation/session-memory binding, KHR calibrated-timestamp queries, enhanced indirect-execution-set update calls, OHOS release-image semaphore arrays, and the listed dynamic-rendering/resolve structure constructors and setters; `bindShadersEXT()` additionally compares only narrowed counts. **Affected configuration:** downstream C++ clients using the copied optional Vulkan-Hpp enhanced API on targets with `size_t` wider than 32 bits; no in-tree C++ Vulkan-Hpp caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked narrowing; practical exposure requires an exceptionally large container. Reject sizes above `UINT32_MAX` or document/enforce the representable-size precondition. Source-only.



The same implicit `size_t` to native `uint32_t` count narrowing occurs in RAII `CommandBuffer::setViewportWithCountEXT()` and `setScissorWithCountEXT()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:23691-23709`), `CommandBuffer::setExclusiveScissorEnableNV()` and `setExclusiveScissorNV()` (`:22933-22959`), and `Device::transitionImageLayoutEXT()` (`:24013-24025`). Each forwards the original proxy pointer alongside the narrowed native count. On a 64-bit downstream caller, an extent above `UINT32_MAX` is truncated (exactly 2^32 elements becomes zero); viewport/scissor counts also exceed Vulkan device limits at such sizes, while the transition array requires an exceptionally large valid host range. These are additional RAII instances of GD10233, with no in-tree C++ caller found.

Additional RAII proxies narrow `ArrayProxy::size()` to native `uint32_t` counts while preserving the original pointers in `CommandBuffer::waitEvents2KHR()` (`vulkan_raii.hpp:24557-24575`), `Queue::submit2KHR()` (`:24598-24609`), `CommandBuffer::bindDescriptorBuffersEXT()` (`:24666-24676`), `setDescriptorBufferOffsetsEXT()` (`:24678-24704`), `setVertexInputEXT()` (`:24986-25001`), `setColorWriteEnableEXT()` (`:25305-25314`), `Device::buildMicromapsEXT()` (`:25385-25400`), `CommandBuffer::setColorBlendEnableEXT()`, `setColorBlendEquationEXT()`, `setColorWriteMaskEXT()`, `setColorBlendAdvancedEXT()`, `setViewportSwizzleNV()`, and `setCoverageModulationTableNV()` (`vulkan_raii.hpp:25990-26029,26093-26106,26160-26171,26215-26220`), `CommandBuffer::copyMemoryToImageIndirectNV()` (`:25741-25760`), and `CommandBuffer::decompressMemoryNV()` (`:25762-25773`). On a 64-bit downstream client, counts above `UINT32_MAX` describe only a truncated prefix (zero at exactly 2^32); applicable Vulkan device limits or exceptionally large arrays constrain reachability. The descriptor-offset pair also remains subject to GD10279 when the two arrays differ in length under no-exceptions with `NDEBUG`.

The enhanced `PhysicalDeviceLayeredApiPropertiesListKHR` constructor also narrows `ArrayProxyNoTemporaries::size()` directly to `uint32_t` while retaining `data()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:96912-96916`). The structure is chainable from physical-device property queries. On a 64-bit C++ client with more than `UINT32_MAX` entries, the advertised count truncates; exactly 2^32 entries advertises zero despite a nonempty pointer. This is another GD10233 occurrence, limited to an impractically large and invalid extent beyond the native count domain; no non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found. No property query or build was run.


The enhanced `PhysicalDeviceImageDrmFormatModifierInfoEXT` constructor and `setQueueFamilyIndices()` setter narrow the proxy's `size()` to `uint32_t` while retaining `data()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:94883-94894,94937-94944`). The structure is passed through `PhysicalDevice::getImageFormatProperties2()` to the native image-format query (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:6286-6294`; the KHR alias path is at `:12944-12952`). A downstream 64-bit client with more than `UINT32_MAX` queue-family entries therefore supplies a truncated count with the original pointer, including zero for exactly 2^32 entries. This is another GD10233 occurrence for an exceptionally large extent beyond the native count domain; no non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found. No image-format query or build was run.


`PhysicalDeviceHostImageCopyProperties` also narrows both output-layout proxy capacities in its enhanced constructor and respective setters while retaining their output pointers (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:93887-93902,93932-93960`). The structure is returned through `PhysicalDevice::getProperties2()` / `getProperties2KHR()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:6191-6195,12846-12850`). On a 64-bit caller with a proxy extent above `UINT32_MAX`, the native query sees only the truncated capacity; at exactly 2^32 entries it sees capacity zero and cannot return the caller's allocated list data, even though the pointer is nonnull. This is another GD10233 occurrence, limited to exceptional output capacities beyond the native count representation; no in-tree non-generated C++ caller was found. This is output truncation, not a demonstrated buffer overrun. No query or build was run.

The enhanced `SpecializationInfo` constructor and `setMapEntries()` setter also narrow `mapEntries_.size()` to `uint32_t` while retaining `mapEntries_.data()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:21659-21660,21692-21694`). `PipelineShaderStageCreateInfo::pSpecializationInfo` carries this record in a shader stage (`:21795-21802,21853-21856`), and `GraphicsPipelineCreateInfo` retains the stages array passed to `Device::createGraphicsPipeline(s)`, which forwards the create info to `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines()` (`:56880-57027`; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:4908-4978`). A 64-bit downstream client with more than `UINT32_MAX` specialization map entries can therefore present a truncated map-entry count with the original pointer, including zero at exactly 2^32. This is another GD10233 instance; the native count domain and practical resource limits make the trigger extreme and invalid, not a demonstrated valid-call overrun. No non-generated in-tree C++ construction caller was found. No Vulkan call or build was run; source-only.

The enhanced `CopyBufferInfo2`, `CopyBufferToImageInfo2`, `CopyImageInfo2`, `CopyImageToBufferInfo2`, `CopyImageToImageInfo`, `CopyImageToMemoryInfo`, and `CopyMemoryToImageInfo` constructors and setters narrow proxy sizes to `uint32_t` while retaining their region pointers (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:23558-23560,23605-23609,23718-23730,23780-23784,24332-24346,24402-24406,24524-24536,24586-24590,24705-24721,24783-24787,25073-25085,25135-25139,26236-26247,26298-26302`). The enhanced `CopyMemoryToImageIndirectInfoKHR` constructor and `setImageSubresources()` similarly narrow the subresource proxy size into `copyCount` while retaining `pImageSubresources` (`:25879-25893,25949-25953`), then `CommandBuffer::copyMemoryToImageIndirectKHR()` forwards the structure (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:30912-30920`). `CustomResolveCreateInfoEXT` narrows its color-format proxy count in its constructor and setter while retaining the pointer (`:28316-28324,28363-28367`); its extension traits allow it in graphics-pipeline, command-buffer-inheritance, and shader-create chains (`vulkan.hpp:19875-19893`). A 64-bit downstream caller with more than `UINT32_MAX` regions or subresources therefore supplies a truncated count paired with the original pointer. These are GD10233 instances in optional Vulkan APIs; the D3D12 case is Windows-guarded and does not imply AROS target selection. Such counts exceed the native count domain and are not demonstrated valid-call overruns. No non-generated in-tree C++ call site was found; no command or build was run.

The enhanced data-graph `DataGraphPipelineCreateInfoARM` constructor and `setResourceInfos()` narrow resource-info proxy size to `uint32_t` while preserving the pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:29429-29439,29483-29489`); `Device::createDataGraphPipelinesARM()` forwards those records to native dispatch (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:29614-29661`). `DataGraphPipelineIdentifierCreateInfoARM` also narrows identifier byte-array size in its enhanced constructor and setter (`vulkan_structs.hpp:29706-29710,29741-29746`). The nested `DataGraphPipelineShaderModuleCreateInfoARM` constant-array constructor/setter and `DataGraphProcessingEngineCreateInfoARM` engine-array constructor/setter do the same (`:30633-30645,30696-30701,30928-30934,30965-30972`); their `StructExtends` traits permit these records in the data-graph pipeline `pNext` chain (`vulkan.hpp:17874,17892`), and pipeline creation forwards the chain (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:29614-29661`). `DebugUtilsMessengerCallbackDataEXT` also narrows its queue-label, command-buffer-label, and object array sizes in its enhanced constructor/setters while retaining all three pointers (`:31985-31990,32048-32053,32069-32074,32090-32095`). This callback-data wrapper is normally populated by Vulkan for callback delivery; the narrowing applies to downstream C++ clients that construct or edit the wrapper themselves, and no in-tree user was found. These are additional optional Vulkan-Hpp instances of GD10233, with oversized counts beyond the native count domain.

The enhanced `PipelineLayoutCreateInfo` constructor and `setSetLayouts()` / `setPushConstantRanges()` setters also cast each proxy size to `uint32_t` while retaining the corresponding pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:131040-131043,131085-131108`). `Device::createPipelineLayout()` forwards this record directly to `vkCreatePipelineLayout()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:3976-3988`). Thus an optional downstream C++ caller with more than `UINT32_MAX` layouts or push-constant ranges can pass a truncated count with the original pointer; this is the same GD10233 proxy-count narrowing pattern, limited to an extreme extent beyond native count representation. No non-generated in-tree caller was found.

The same enhanced-proxy narrowing appears in `PipelineRenderingCreateInfo` color formats, `PipelineShaderStageModuleIdentifierCreateInfoEXT` identifier bytes, vertex-binding divisors, NV coarse sample orders, NV exclusive scissors, nested NV shading-rate palettes, and the viewport shading-rate palette array (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:132094-132142,132647-132685,133251-133293,133403-133453,133792-133831,133926-133960,134058-134061`). These wrappers retain each original proxy pointer while narrowing its size into a native `uint32_t` count/size, another GD10233 occurrence. No non-generated in-tree use of these enhanced Vulkan-Hpp pipeline wrappers was found; the cases require extents above the native count domain.

The enhanced `Device::bindBufferMemory2()` and `Device::bindImageMemory2()` overloads pass `bindInfos.size()` to the native `uint32_t bindInfoCount` while forwarding the original proxy data pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:5778-5780,5808-5810`). On a 64-bit downstream client, a proxy larger than `UINT32_MAX` entries is narrowed at the dispatch boundary; exactly 2^32 entries produces a zero count with the original nonempty pointer. This is another GD10233 instance, gated by the optional Vulkan-Hpp enhanced API and limited to oversized input outside the native count domain. A repository search found no checked-in C++ call site for either helper. No memory-bind operation or build was run.


## GD10234 — Vulkan-Hpp debug-utils helpers fail to compile for 32-bit non-dispatchable handles

The copied Vulkan-Hpp macro header sets `VK_USE_64_BIT_PTR_DEFINES` to `0` when none of its listed 64-bit target macros is defined (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_hpp_macros.hpp:106-113`). In that configuration, Vulkan's non-dispatchable C handle types are integer types; `HandleType::CType` therefore has an integral type for wrappers such as `Buffer`. The enhanced `Device::setDebugUtilsObjectNameEXT(handle, name, dispatch)` and `Device::setDebugUtilsObjectTagEXT(handle, tagName, tag, dispatch)` templates cast that value to its `CType` and then use `reinterpret_cast<uint64_t>` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:16101-16113,16143-16157`). C++ `reinterpret_cast` does not provide an integral-to-integral conversion, so instantiating either helper for a non-dispatchable handle is ill-formed in this configuration. The helpers are available in enhanced mode, which is enabled by default.

**Trigger and consequence:** a 32-bit C++ consumer includes the optional copied Vulkan-Hpp headers with enhanced mode enabled and instantiates either helper with a non-dispatchable handle such as `Buffer` or `Image`. Compilation fails at the cast. Dispatchable handles remain pointer-based, and 64-bit targets use pointer-based non-dispatchable C handles, so this finding is limited to 32-bit non-dispatchable handle instantiations. No in-tree C++ Vulkan-Hpp consumer was found. **Confidence:** high for the platform macro and source-level type/cast mismatch; no 32-bit compile was run. Use a conversion that handles both pointer and integer C handle representations. Source-only.


<a id="gd10235"></a>
## GD10235 — Vulkan-Hpp typed output helpers can under-size buffers

Several typed convenience helpers pass a caller-selected local type as the output buffer while accepting runtime multi-item requests or descriptor data with a size defined outside the C++ type. `Device::writeAccelerationStructuresPropertyKHR()` accepts an `ArrayProxy` of acceleration structures, forwards its full size and the caller's stride, but passes only `sizeof(DataType)` in both enhanced and RAII APIs (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:17625-17645`; `workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:21868-21885`; declaration at `vulkan_handles.hpp:14929-14935`). Vulkan requires `dataSize >= accelerationStructureCount * stride` ([command reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkWriteAccelerationStructuresPropertiesKHR.html), VUID `dataSize-03452`). The RAII overload has the same local-buffer consequence: when the requested result extent exceeds `sizeof(DataType)`, it forwards too little storage for the count/stride the caller supplied. Likewise, the enhanced and RAII `getRayTracingShaderGroupHandleKHR()` and `getRayTracingCaptureReplayShaderGroupHandleKHR()` helpers, plus the enhanced and RAII NV `getRayTracingShaderGroupHandleNV()`, accept `groupCount` but pass only `sizeof(DataType)` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:18216-18231,18275-18290,19431-19446`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:22105-22120,22145-22164,22598-22613`); Vulkan requires space for `groupCount * shaderGroupHandleSize` or `groupCount * shaderGroupHandleCaptureReplaySize` ([shader group handle reference, also covering the equivalent NV command](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetRayTracingShaderGroupHandlesKHR.html), VUID `dataSize-02420`; [capture-replay reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetRayTracingCaptureReplayShaderGroupHandlesKHR.html), VUID `dataSize-03484`). The wrappers do not relate the runtime counts and strides to `sizeof(DataType)`. Both the enhanced `Device::getAccelerationStructureHandleNV<DataType>()` and RAII `AccelerationStructureNV::getHandle<DataType>()` create a local object of the selected type and pass only `sizeof(DataType)` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:19488-19504`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:22638-22650`). Vulkan specifies this opaque handle is eight bytes ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetAccelerationStructureHandleNV.html), VUID `dataSize-02240). Instantiating either helper with a type smaller than eight bytes supplies too little output storage; an implementation that writes the full handle can write beyond the local object. The enhanced helper's same scalar output also has the separate failed-result/uninitialized-value case in GD10223. The plural/vector overloads accept an explicit byte size and are not included in this fixed-local-size instance. `Device::writeMicromapsPropertyEXT()` repeats the same shape in both enhanced and RAII APIs: each accepts an array of micromaps and a runtime stride but passes only `sizeof(DataType)` as `dataSize` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:25895-25920`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:25474-25490`; RAII declaration at `vulkan_raii.hpp:5384-5388`). Vulkan requires `dataSize >= micromapCount * stride` (VUID `dataSize-07576`; [official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkWriteMicromapsPropertiesEXT.html)). With more than one micromap and an extent larger than the one local `DataType`, the wrapper sends undersized output storage. The plural overloads retain caller-sized output and can allocate enough records; this problem is specific to the singular typed helper.

The enhanced `Device::getDescriptorEXT<DescriptorType>()` helper has the same caller-sized output weakness for a single descriptor: it allocates a local `DescriptorType` and passes `sizeof(DescriptorType)` as `dataSize` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:24111-24125`). The RAII `Device::getDescriptorEXT<DescriptorType>()` overload does the same with its local `DescriptorType` (`vulkan_raii.hpp:24651-24664`). Vulkan requires `dataSize` to equal the descriptor-type-specific size reported by `VkPhysicalDeviceDescriptorBufferPropertiesEXT` (with specified special cases; [official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetDescriptorEXT.html), VUID `dataSize-08125`). A downstream caller instantiating a smaller type supplies undersized local storage for a descriptor whose required encoding is larger; an implementation that writes the full encoding can overrun the object, while any unequal size violates the command requirement. The raw pointer overload allows callers to supply the correct byte size. This extends GD10235 beyond its multi-item property helpers.

The five enhanced opaque descriptor-data helpers also pass an arbitrary `DataType` object directly as the output buffer without checking its size (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:24242-24255,24276-24289,24310-24323,24344-24357,24377-24390`). Vulkan requires each buffer to be at least the device-reported capture-replay size for its resource type ([buffer](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetBufferOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT.html), [image](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetImageOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT.html), [image view](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetImageViewOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT.html), [sampler](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetSamplerOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT.html), [acceleration structure](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetAccelerationStructureOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataEXT.html)). A scalar or struct `DataType` smaller than that value supplies undersized local storage; an implementation that writes the full opaque data can overrun it. The five RAII overloads likewise pass a local `DataType` directly as the output pointer without checking its extent (`vulkan_raii.hpp:24719-24802`); they have the same undersized-storage consequence. Their failed-result uninitialized-value case is separately covered by GD10264. The ARM `getTensorOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataARM<DataType>()` and `getTensorViewOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataARM<DataType>()` helpers repeat this pattern (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:27547-27565,27577-27595`; RAII counterparts at `vulkan_raii.hpp:26390-26422`): Vulkan requires at least `tensorCaptureReplayDescriptorDataSize` or `tensorViewCaptureReplayDescriptorDataSize` bytes respectively ([descriptor-buffer specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/descriptorbuffers.html#descriptor-buffer-opaque-capture-data)). A smaller `DataType` again supplies insufficient local storage. These extend GD10235 to the optional `VK_ARM_tensors` plus `VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer` configuration. The same helpers' failed-result uninitialized-value case remains separately tracked in GD10223.

The enhanced and RAII `ExternalComputeQueueNV::getData<DataType>()` helpers expose caller-selected output storage without a size parameter (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:31111-31124`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:27688-27699`). Both pass the address of one local `DataType` as `pData`. `vkGetExternalComputeQueueDataNV` requires `pData` to be at least `VkPhysicalDeviceExternalComputeQueuePropertiesNV::externalDataSize` bytes ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetExternalComputeQueueDataNV.html), VUID `pData-08134`); instantiating a smaller `DataType` gives the implementation an undersized local object. This extends GD10235 to both optional copied Vulkan-Hpp APIs under `VK_NV_external_compute_queue`.

**Trigger and consequence:** a caller uses one of the multi-item helpers with a count/stride whose required extent exceeds `sizeof(DataType)`, calls `getDescriptorEXT` with a `DescriptorType` whose size differs from the descriptor-specific required size, or instantiates an opaque descriptor-data helper with `DataType` smaller than the device-reported output size. The wrapper then violates Vulkan's data-size requirement; when the supplied storage is too small and the implementation writes the full output, it can write beyond the local object. Callers can select a sufficiently large aggregate type for a particular request, so the finding is limited to mismatched runtime extent or descriptor encoding size. **Affected configuration:** downstream consumers of the optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced or RAII API; no non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found. **Confidence:** medium; the forwarding and Vulkan size requirement are direct, but the trigger requires a multi-item extent larger than the chosen `DataType`, and no call or runtime behavior was exercised. Validate the byte extent against the runtime request or provide only the explicitly sized/vector overload for multi-item output. Source-only.

### GD10236 disposition — duplicate consolidated into GD10280

GD10236 described the enhanced `Device::getPipelinePropertiesEXT()` overload passing a default, undersized `BaseOutStructure` to Vulkan. The later GD10280 review traced the same root cause in both enhanced and RAII convenience overloads and has the fuller scope and references. GD10236 is withdrawn as a separate candidate; GD10280 is the canonical finding.

## GD10237 — Vulkan-Hpp unique display-mode factory has no valid destroy operation

`PhysicalDevice::createDisplayModeKHRUnique()` constructs a `UniqueHandle<DisplayModeKHR, Dispatch>` with `detail::ObjectDestroy<PhysicalDevice, Dispatch>` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:10169-10186`). `ObjectDestroy::destroy()` later calls `m_owner.destroy(handle, allocator, dispatch)` (`vulkan.hpp:6678-6721`), but the generated `PhysicalDevice` wrapper declares no `destroy(DisplayModeKHR, ...)` overload and `vulkan_funcs.hpp` defines no `PhysicalDevice::destroy()` operation for a display mode. Vulkan's `VK_KHR_display` specification explicitly says display modes, including created modes, cannot be destroyed and have instance lifetime; the extension has no destroy command ([official display specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/VK_KHR_surface/wsi.html#display-modes), [extension issue resolution](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VK_KHR_display.html)).

**Trigger and consequence:** a downstream C++ client uses `createDisplayModeKHRUnique()` and instantiates destruction/reset of its returned unique handle with smart handles enabled. The generated deleter attempts to call a nonexistent `PhysicalDevice::destroy(DisplayModeKHR, ...)`, so the client fails to compile when that deleter is instantiated. The raw `createDisplayModeKHR()` overload remains usable; the mode itself must not be destroyed under this extension.

**Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced API with smart handles enabled and `VK_KHR_display`; no in-tree C++ Vulkan-Hpp caller was found. **Confidence:** high; the unique factory/deleter path is explicit, no matching destroy API exists in the wrapper, and the Vulkan extension specifies instance lifetime with no destroy operation. No C++ client was compiled and no display mode was created.

**Review evidence:** [Vulkan-Hpp DRM/display-mode source pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-drm-display-mode-unique-handle-review).

### GD10223 addendum: query-pool scalar result reads unwritten output on `VK_NOT_READY`

The enhanced `Device::getQueryPoolResult<DataType>()` default-initializes `DataType data`, calls `vkGetQueryPoolResults`, explicitly accepts `eNotReady` in `resultCheck()`, and moves `data` into `ResultValue` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:2019-2038`; result-value constructor at `vulkan.hpp:7380-7386`). The Khronos Queries chapter states that when neither `VK_QUERY_RESULT_WAIT_BIT` nor `VK_QUERY_RESULT_PARTIAL_BIT` is set, no result value is written for an unavailable query and the command returns `VK_NOT_READY` ([Queries chapter](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/queries.html)). With a scalar `DataType`, the helper therefore copies an indeterminate value before returning the accepted result code. **Trigger and consequence:** a downstream enhanced-mode caller requests one unavailable query with default flags (or other flags lacking WAIT and PARTIAL); constructing the returned `ResultValue` reads an indeterminate scalar, which is undefined behavior before the caller can check `result`. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced API; no in-tree C++ caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the source flow and specified no-write path. No Vulkan call or runtime behavior was exercised. Initialize the local value or avoid packaging it when `result == eNotReady`. Source-only.

### GD10235 addendum: singular typed query helper accepts multi-query counts

The enhanced `Device::getQueryPoolResult<DataType>()` takes arbitrary `queryCount` and `stride`, but passes the address of one local `DataType` with `dataSize = sizeof(DataType)` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:2019-2038`; declaration at `vulkan_handles.hpp:11629-11633`). Vulkan requires `dataSize` to be large enough for every requested query result (VUID `dataSize-00817`; [official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetQueryPoolResults.html)). For example, two 64-bit query results with stride 8 require at least 16 bytes, while `DataType = uint64_t` supplies 8. **Trigger and consequence:** a caller requests multiple results whose byte extent exceeds the chosen `DataType`; the helper passes undersized output storage, violating the command's size requirement and potentially allowing writes past the local object. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced API; no in-tree C++ caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the size mismatch; no Vulkan call or runtime behavior was exercised. Restrict this overload to one result or validate the requested extent and provide adequate storage. Source-only.


<a id="gd10238"></a>
### GD10238: Vulkan-Hpp setters and constructors can populate mutually exclusive pointer arrays

Several generated wrappers expose two alternative pointer-array forms and allow helper calls to leave both populated:

- `AccelerationStructureBuildGeometryInfoKHR::setGeometries()` updates `geometryCount` and `pGeometries` without clearing `ppGeometries`; enhanced `setPGeometries()` updates `geometryCount` and `ppGeometries` without clearing `pGeometries` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:935-960`). Its enhanced constructor rejects both nonempty proxies (`:840-868`), but switching forms through the setters bypasses that check. The command wrapper forwards the structure (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:17316-17336`). Vulkan requires exactly one geometry pointer when `geometryCount` is nonzero (VUID `pGeometries-03788`; [official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkAccelerationStructureBuildGeometryInfoKHR.html)).
- `AccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV` has the same setter gap (`:4730-4755`). Its enhanced constructor also assigns both pointer forms when both proxies are supplied and only checks that their lengths match (`:4573-4615`); equal nonzero lengths therefore pass while violating the API's one-pointer rule (VUID `pUsageCounts-07992`; [official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkAccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV.html)).
- `AccelerationStructureTrianglesOpacityMicromapEXT` and `MicromapBuildInfoEXT` each check mutually exclusive proxies in their enhanced constructors, but their enhanced setters update one member without nulling the alternate (`vulkan_structs.hpp:4902-4929,4986-5015,72050-72078,72132-72155`). Their API contracts also require exactly one of `pUsageCounts` and `ppUsageCounts` (VUIDs `pUsageCounts-07335` and `pUsageCounts-07516`; [opacity structure reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkAccelerationStructureTrianglesOpacityMicromapEXT.html), [micromap build reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkMicromapBuildInfoEXT.html)).
- `WriteDescriptorSet` checks that at most one of its image-info, buffer-info, and texel-buffer-view proxies is nonempty in the enhanced constructor (`vulkan_structs.hpp:136888-136917`), but `setImageInfo()`, `setBufferInfo()`, and `setTexelBufferView()` independently update their pointer and shared `descriptorCount` without clearing the other pointers (`:136972-137009`). The resulting record is forwarded by `Device::updateDescriptorSets()` and `CommandBuffer::pushDescriptorSet()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:4638-4650,8754-8770`); the selected descriptor payload must match `descriptorType` ([`VkWriteDescriptorSet` reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkWriteDescriptorSet.html)).

**Trigger and consequence:** a downstream caller supplies both nonempty pointer forms to the displacement enhanced constructor with equal lengths, or switches from one form to the other through a setter on any listed structure without first clearing the old pointer. For `WriteDescriptorSet`, calling `setImageInfo()` and then `setBufferInfo()` leaves both pointers non-null, with `descriptorCount` set only from the latter array; submitting that record through descriptor update or push can violate the descriptor-type/payload contract and leave a stale shorter array alongside the new payload. The resulting structure is passed into acceleration-structure or micromap build input (including through a pNext chain) with both pointers non-null, violating Vulkan's valid-usage contract and causing validation failure or implementation-dependent handling. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced API, with the relevant ray-tracing/micromap extensions enabled. The target-local search found no in-tree C++ consumer; downstream use is not established. **Confidence:** high for the constructible invalid states and contract violations; downstream execution is conditional. The helpers should clear the alternate pointer or reject mutually supplied array forms. No Vulkan call, GPU, build, or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.


<a id="gd10239"></a>
<a id="gd10239-vulkan-hpp-string-comparisons-pass-null-names-to-strcmp"></a>
### GD10239 — Vulkan-Hpp string comparisons pass null names to `strcmp`

`ApplicationInfo` defaults `pApplicationName` and `pEngineName` to null (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:6891-6903,7023-7029`). Its equality operator treats identical pointers as equal, but otherwise calls `strcmp` without checking either pointer (`:7010-7014`). Under `VULKAN_HPP_HAS_SPACESHIP_OPERATOR`, its custom ordering operator likewise calls `strcmp` whenever the pointers differ (`:6985-6999`). The Vulkan-Hpp hash review already established these `VkApplicationInfo` name fields are nullable and its equality operator recognizes null as representable state (coverage ledger: `vulkan_hash.hpp` review at line 9328).

`PipelineShaderStageCreateInfo` has the same unsafe pattern for `pName`: the field defaults to null (`:21934`); equality calls `strcmp` when pointers differ (`:21917-21920`), and its spaceship operator does so when enabled (`:21907-21909`). Although a null shader entry-point name is not a valid Vulkan pipeline input, the wrapper's default value is representable and comparing it to a value with a non-null name invokes the wrapper comparison before any Vulkan call.

`CuFunctionCreateInfoNVX` repeats the pattern: `pName` defaults to null (`:27204`), while equality (`:27190-27193`) and the optional spaceship operator (`:27182-27184`) use `strcmp` whenever the pointers differ. As with the shader-stage wrapper, this concerns comparison of wrapper values; it does not require submitting an invalid structure to Vulkan.

When `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS` is defined, `CudaFunctionCreateInfoNV` has the same default-null `pName` and unsafe equality/spaceship paths (`:27821-27839,27848-27851`). `DataGraphPipelineCompilerControlCreateInfoARM` also defaults `pVendorOptions` to null (`:28993-28997`) and compares differing values with `strcmp` in equality and optional spaceship comparison (`:28974-28985`). `DataGraphPipelineShaderModuleCreateInfoARM` also defaults `pName` to null (`:30610-30618`), and its equality and optional spaceship operators call `strcmp` when pointers differ (`:30741-30767`). Vulkan requires a valid entry-point name when submitting this structure, so this instance concerns comparing wrapper values before submission; it does not establish an invalid Vulkan call. The same default-null comparison pattern occurs in `DebugMarkerMarkerInfoEXT::pMarkerName` (`:31054,31132-31155`), `DebugMarkerObjectNameInfoEXT::pObjectName` (`:31182-31298`), `DebugUtilsLabelEXT::pLabelName` (`:31672,31747-31770`), and `DebugUtilsObjectNameInfoEXT::pObjectName` (`:31797-31899`). In each case equality and optional spaceship ordering call `strcmp` when pointers differ; these cases concern wrapper comparison before API submission. `DebugUtilsMessengerCallbackDataEXT` defaults `pMessageIdName` and `pMessage` to null (`:31939-31954,32191-32193`) and compares differing pointers with `strcmp` (`:32149-32177`); these callback-data strings are nullable API fields, as noted in the Vulkan-Hpp hash review. `LayerSettingEXT` also defaults `pLayerName` and `pSettingName` to null (`:68423-68424`), while equality and optional spaceship ordering compare differing pointers with `strcmp` (`:68391-68398,68410-68414`); comparing a default wrapper with populated names triggers the same undefined behavior before any API submission. `DisplayPropertiesKHR` defaults `displayName` to null (`:45353-45360`) and has the same pointer-difference/`strcmp` behavior in equality and optional spaceship ordering (`:45322-45345`); comparing a default wrapper with one carrying a non-null display name likewise reaches `strcmp`.

**Trigger and consequence:** a downstream caller compares a default-constructed `ApplicationInfo` with one whose corresponding application or engine name is non-null, or compares a default-constructed `PipelineShaderStageCreateInfo` with one whose `pName` is non-null. The same failure occurs when a default-constructed `CuFunctionCreateInfoNVX` is compared with one whose `pName` is non-null. With `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS`, the same applies to a default-constructed `CudaFunctionCreateInfoNV`. A default-constructed `DataGraphPipelineCompilerControlCreateInfoARM` compared with a non-null vendor-options string has the same failure. A default-constructed `DataGraphPipelineShaderModuleCreateInfoARM` compared with a value having a non-null `pName` likewise passes null to `strcmp`; Vulkan requires a valid entry-point name only when the structure is submitted. The same trigger applies to default-constructed debug marker and debug-utils label/object-name wrappers compared with a value holding a non-null corresponding name. For `DebugUtilsMessengerCallbackDataEXT`, comparing default data with non-null message-name or message pointers triggers the same path even though those callback strings are nullable. `LayerSettingEXT` has the same trigger for either default-null name compared with a non-null name. `DisplayPropertiesKHR` has the same trigger for `displayName`. Equality, and ordering when enabled, passes the null pointer to `strcmp`, invoking undefined behavior and commonly terminating the process. Comparing two values with identical null pointers takes the pointer-equality branch and does not trigger this issue. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp header; equality is available in all supported language modes, ordering is additionally affected when `VULKAN_HPP_HAS_SPACESHIP_OPERATOR` is defined, and the `CudaFunctionCreateInfoNV` case is gated by `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS`. No in-tree C++ Vulkan-Hpp caller was found. **Confidence:** high; default null fields and the unguarded string calls are explicit. No comparison was executed. Handle null pointers before string comparison (for example, order null before non-null). Source-only.


#### GD10239 addendum — beta shader-node name is also compared without a null guard

With `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS`, `PipelineShaderStageNodeCreateInfoAMDX` defaults `pName` to null and exposes a setter that accepts null (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:132760-132803,132867-132870`). Its equality operator calls `strcmp(pName, rhs.pName)` whenever the pointers differ, and its optional spaceship operator does the same (`:132839-132858`). Comparing a default wrapper with one whose name is non-null therefore passes null to `strcmp` before any API submission. This is the same GD10239 root cause and is limited to the beta AMDX wrapper; no additional candidate number is needed.


#### GD10239 addendum — display-properties v2 delegates comparison to nullable nested name

`DisplayProperties2KHR` stores a `DisplayPropertiesKHR` by value and its equality operator compares that member directly (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:45432-45438`). Its default constructor initializes the nested record with `displayName == nullptr` through `DisplayPropertiesKHR`'s default member initializer (`:45353-45360`); the nested equality operator calls `strcmp` when the two name pointers differ (`:45340-45345`). Comparing a default `DisplayProperties2KHR` with a value whose nested display name is non-null therefore reaches the existing GD10239 null-string comparison defect. When spaceship comparison is enabled, the defaulted memberwise ordering also delegates to `DisplayPropertiesKHR::operator<=>`, which has the same unchecked `strcmp` path (`:45320-45324`). This is an additional wrapper path under GD10239, not a separate root cause. No wrapper comparison was executed.


### GD10240 — Vulkan-Hpp `TensorCopyARM` array helpers can produce inconsistent dimensions

The enhanced `TensorCopyARM` constructor sets `dimensionCount` only from `srcOffset_.size()`, but stores pointers from all three proxies (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:26766-26775`). Its mismatch checks run only when both compared proxies are nonempty (`:26777-26795`). Therefore an empty source-offset proxy with a nonempty destination-offset or extent proxy passes the checks while producing `dimensionCount == 0` and a non-null pointer. Vulkan requires `dimensionCount` to be greater than zero when any of these pointers is non-null, and requires each non-null array to contain `dimensionCount` values ([`VkTensorCopyARM` reference, VUID `dimensionCount-09955`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkTensorCopyARM.html)).

The enhanced `setSrcOffset`, `setDstOffset`, and `setExtent` setters each independently overwrite the shared `dimensionCount` with their own proxy size without checking the other stored pointer arrays (`:26829-26863`). For example, setting a two-element source offset and then a three-element destination offset leaves `dimensionCount == 3` while `pSrcOffset` still refers to only two elements. The resulting region violates the same array-length requirement. `CopyTensorInfoARM` accepts and stores such regions (`:26939-26972`), and `CommandBuffer::copyTensorARM` forwards that structure to `vkCmdCopyTensorARM` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:27471-27486`).

**Trigger and consequence:** with enhanced mode enabled, construct a `TensorCopyARM` using an empty source-offset proxy and nonempty destination-offset or extent proxy, or call the enhanced offset/extent setters in an order that leaves a non-null array shorter than the final `dimensionCount`. Passing the region to `copyTensorARM` creates invalid Vulkan input; validation can reject it, and an implementation consuming the advertised array length may read beyond the supplied array. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp header with `VK_ARM_tensors` and enhanced mode enabled; the empty-source constructor case passes both exception and `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` builds because the checks intentionally skip empty proxies. No in-tree C++ Vulkan-Hpp client was found. **Confidence:** high for the invalid count/pointer states; driver-side consequences depend on downstream use and implementation behavior. No command or array operation was executed. Validate the nonempty array lengths together, derive the count from a non-null array, and keep the setters' count synchronized with every populated pointer. Source-only.


### GD10241 — Vulkan-Hpp create-info equality forms end pointers from null

`DeviceCreateInfo::operator==` compares extension-name arrays with `std::equal(ppEnabledExtensionNames, ppEnabledExtensionNames + enabledExtensionCount, rhs.ppEnabledExtensionNames, predicate)` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:38615-38619`). Both fields default to null/zero (`:38644-38647`), so comparing two default-constructed `DeviceCreateInfo` values evaluates `nullptr + 0` while forming the end iterator. Pointer arithmetic requires a pointer into an array object, so this is undefined behavior even though the intended range is empty. Equality is available independently of any Vulkan API call. The optional spaceship operator avoids this specific expression by checking the count in a loop; it does not form a null end pointer for a zero count.

**Trigger and consequence:** compare two default-constructed values, or any pair with equal zero extension counts and null extension-name arrays. Equality evaluates null-pointer arithmetic; behavior is undefined and may be miscompiled under optimization. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp header; ordinary C++ equality path. No in-tree C++ Vulkan-Hpp caller was found. The same issue occurs in `InstanceCreateInfo::operator==`, which forms `ppEnabledLayerNames + enabledLayerCount` and `ppEnabledExtensionNames + enabledExtensionCount` for its two `std::equal` calls (`:67548-67556`). Both counts and pointers default to zero/null (`:67569-67572`), so equality of default instances forms null end pointers for both empty ranges. Its optional spaceship implementation uses count-bounded loops and does not form these end pointers. The deprecated device-layer count/name members in `DeviceCreateInfo` are marked `ignored` and are intentionally excluded. **Confidence:** high for the expressions and default field values; no comparison or compiler run was performed. Avoid forming end pointers from null bases, for example by skipping the algorithms when counts are zero. Source-only.


<a id="gd10242"></a>
### GD10242 — Vulkan-Hpp string setters can leave fixed arrays unterminated

The enhanced `PhysicalDeviceDataGraphOperationSupportARM` and `DeviceFaultVendorInfoEXT` string constructors/setters assert that the input is shorter than the fixed destination, then on non-Windows copy `min(destination capacity, input.size())` bytes with `strncpy` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:28655-28663,28692-28701,39429-39437,39458-39465`). When assertions are disabled and the input length is at least the capacity, `strncpy` writes the entire fixed array without a terminating NUL. These wrappers later compare those fields with unbounded `strcmp` (`:28746-28757,39513-39526`), which can scan beyond the array. There are two more routes to the same comparison failure: `DeviceFaultVendorInfoEXT::setDescription(std::array<...>)` copies every byte, so on non-Windows a subsequent shorter string setter preserves an unterminated old tail (`:39451-39465`); and `DeviceFaultInfoEXT` accepts an arbitrary fixed description array without checking termination (`:39557-39568`) before its equality and optional ordering operators call `strcmp` (`:39616-39639`). Vulkan defines device-fault descriptions as null-terminated strings ([`VkDeviceFaultVendorInfoEXT` reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkDeviceFaultVendorInfoEXT.html)).

**Trigger and consequence:** in enhanced mode on a non-Windows build with `NDEBUG` or a no-op assertion macro, construct or set either string with length equal to or greater than its fixed capacity, then compare the wrapper; or compare a `DeviceFaultInfoEXT` built with a non-terminated description array. The string field is unterminated and `strcmp` reads beyond the array, invoking undefined behavior. A `DeviceFaultVendorInfoEXT` can also be made unterminated through its array setter followed by a shorter valid-length string setter. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp header; oversized-string trigger additionally requires enhanced mode, non-Windows and assertions disabled. No in-tree C++ client was found. **Confidence:** high for the copy bounds and comparison paths; no comparison or build was run. Validate array inputs and clear/terminate the destination in each string setter. Source-only.

**Addendum — valid-length setter can preserve an unterminated tail:** `PhysicalDeviceDataGraphOperationSupportARM::setName(std::array<...>)` accepts and copies every byte without requiring a NUL (`:28684-28689`). On non-Windows, the enhanced `setName(std::string const&)` copies only `name_.size()` bytes with `strncpy` and does not clear the remaining destination (`:28691-28701`). A caller can first set an all-nonzero fixed array, then call the string overload with a shorter, valid-length name; the old nonzero tail remains, and the wrapper's equality/optional ordering `strcmp` can read beyond `name` (`:28741-28757`). This adds a trigger independent of assertion configuration and oversized strings. **Affected configuration:** optional Vulkan-Hpp API on non-Windows with enhanced setters; no in-tree consumer was found. **Confidence:** high for the stale unterminated tail and comparison path; no comparison was run. Clear the array and append an explicit NUL on every string setter call. Source-only.

**Addendum — device-fault wrappers:** the same array-then-short-string setter sequence applies to `DeviceFaultVendorInfoEXT` (`:39451-39465`), whose equality and optional ordering operators use `strcmp` (`:39510-39526`). Separately, `DeviceFaultInfoEXT`'s public fixed-array constructor accepts an unterminated description and its comparisons also use `strcmp` (`:39557-39568,39616-39639`). These are the same fixed-buffer termination defect; they do not require an in-tree caller to establish the unsafe wrapper behavior. Source-only.
