<a id="gd10268"></a>
### GD10268 — DataTypes startup leaks a held global NamedObject when a name collision blocks its list

`GetDataTypesList()` first calls `FindNamedObject(NULL, DATATYPESLIST, NULL)` and reads `no_Object` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/helpfuncs.c:60-63`). `FindNamedObject()` increments `no_UseCount` for a named match and its public contract requires the caller to later call `ReleaseNamedObject()` (`rom/utility/findnamedobject.c:96-100`; `compiler/include/utility/name.h`). When the matched object's `no_Object` is NULL, `GetDataTypesList()` allocates a replacement and later tries to add it to the global namespace (`helpfuncs.c:65-75,93-98`). This is a supported NamedObject state: `AllocNamedObjectA()` leaves `no_Object` NULL when `ANO_UserSpace` is absent or zero and initializes `no_UseCount` to one (`rom/utility/allocnamedobjecta.c:126-155`; `compiler/include/utility/name.h`). The Utility global namespace is initialized with `NSF_NODUPS` (`rom/utility/utility_init.c:22-24`), and `AddNamedObject()` rejects a same-name entry under that flag (`rom/utility/addnamedobject.c:100-111`). On that rejection, the caller frees the new object and sets `no = NULL`, losing the original held pointer; the final `if (no) ReleaseNamedObject(no)` therefore cannot release the reference it obtained at line 60 (`helpfuncs.c:93-103`). The DataTypes library initializer then returns failure when `GetDataTypesList()` returns NULL (`workbench/libs/datatypes/datatypes_init.c:43-47`).

**Trigger and consequence:** before `datatypes.library` initializes, another client has added a global Utility NamedObject named `DataTypesList` with `no_Object == NULL`. Initialization obtains a reference to that object, fails to publish its replacement because duplicate names are forbidden, and leaks the obtained reference. The DataTypes library fails initialization; the other object also retains an unbalanced use count. If its owner later calls `RemNamedObject()` with a reply message, removal is deferred until the use count reaches zero, so the leaked reference can leave the object linked and its removal message pending (`rom/utility/remnamedobject.c:87-124`; `rom/utility/releasenamedobject.c:65-80`). **Affected configuration:** targets that build/load `datatypes.library` and expose Utility's global NamedObject namespace; the trigger requires a prior exact-name collision. **Confidence:** high for the reference-count and initialization paths once triggered; medium overall because the required external collision is unusual and no runtime setup was exercised. Preserve and release the original lookup reference on every branch before replacing `no`, or detect the incompatible existing object and fail without allocating a replacement. Source-only.

<a id="gd10269"></a>
### GD10269 — AddDataTypes populates shared datatype lists without taking their semaphore

`AddDataTypes` calls `CreateDTList()` before its `main()` acquires `dtl_Lock` (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:265-269`). `CreateDTList()` finds the shared global `DataTypesList`, checks each built-in list with `__FindNameNoCase()`, and calls `CreateBasicType()` for missing `binary`, `ascii`, `iff`, and `directory` entries (`:535-577`). `CreateBasicType()` inserts into both the per-kind list and `dtl_SortedList` (`:639-642`); the latter is walked and modified by `AlphaInsert()`/`Insert()` without synchronization (`:1221-1232`). The library's `ObtainDataType()` traverses the same sorted list while holding `dtl_Lock` shared (`workbench/libs/datatypes/obtaindatatypea.c:91-93,175-200`), but `CreateDTList()` does not obtain the lock before or during its searches and insertions. Its later `main()` lock protects only descriptor scanning after the built-ins have already been added.

**Trigger and consequence:** `AddDataTypes` runs while another task calls the DataTypes API, especially while the shared lists still lack built-in entries. A reader can traverse a list while `Enqueue()`/`Insert()` is between link updates, observing inconsistent list links; concurrent `AddDataTypes` invocations can also both pass the missing-name check and insert duplicate built-ins. This can make list traversal unreliable or corrupt list state. **Affected configuration:** targets that build and run `AddDataTypes` with `datatypes.library`, including the i386 PC boot-floppy executable manifest when that image is selected (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:159-160`; `arch/i386-pc/boot/floppy/mmakefile.src:72-75`). **Confidence:** high that the writer bypasses the semaphore used by readers; medium for the runtime consequence, which depends on task interleaving and list state. Hold `dtl_Lock` exclusively across each check-and-insert sequence (or initialize the built-ins under an equivalent one-time synchronization scheme). No DataTypes operation, interleaving, or boot image was run; source-only.

<a id="gd10272"></a>
### GD10272 — AddDataTypes refresh records a directory timestamp before a failed scan

In `REFRESH` mode, `DateScan()` compares the current `DEVS:DataTypes` directory date with `dtl_DateStamp`; when it differs, it updates `dtl_DateStamp` and returns TRUE before `main()` calls `ScanDirectory()` (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:295-300,386-410`). `ScanDirectory()` is `void` and only traverses when allocating its `AnchorPath` succeeds; if `AllocVec(sizeof(struct AnchorPath), MEMF_CLEAR)` returns NULL, it silently returns without scanning (`:436-444`). The `REFRESH` branch does not receive a status and `main()` later sets `result = RETURN_OK` (`:295-301,348`). `DateScan()` returns FALSE when the next invocation sees the same directory timestamp (`:394-401`), so that retry skips `ScanDirectory()`.

**Trigger and consequence:** a change to the `DEVS:DataTypes` directory changes its date, then the `AnchorPath` allocation fails during `AddDataTypes REFRESH`. The command reports success without loading the newly added descriptor; a later refresh against the unchanged directory date skips the scan, so the missed descriptor remains unavailable until the directory date changes again or the descriptor is loaded another way. **Affected configuration:** the optional `workbench-c-adddatatypes` executable in `REFRESH` mode; the checked-in Security-Startup invocation uses `AddDataTypes REFRESH QUIET` (`workbench/c/security/AMUInit.c:97`). **Confidence:** high for the timestamp-before-scan ordering, silent allocation failure, and next-refresh skip; occurrence depends on low-memory allocation failure after a directory change. No allocation failure, refresh command, or datatype load was run. Commit the date only after a successful scan, or preserve a retry indication when traversal setup fails. Source-only.

<a id="gd10271"></a>
### GD10271 — AddDataTypes ignores failures to allocate built-in datatype entries

`CreateDTList()` checks for the built-in `binary`, `ascii`, `iff`, and `directory` entries, then calls `CreateBasicType()` without checking any of its return values (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:542-575`). `CreateBasicType()` returns NULL when its `AllocVec()` fails and only links the entry into its type list and the sorted list after allocation succeeds (`:611-645`). `CreateDTList()` nevertheless returns the non-NULL shared DataTypesList (`:535-540,579-585`), so `main()` treats initialization as successful and continues (`:265-269`); after successful argument parsing it sets `result = RETURN_OK` without knowing whether one or more built-ins were omitted (`:287-349`). These entries provide the generic fallback for `ExamineData()`: the ASCII, binary and IFF paths call `FindDtInList()` on those lists, which returns NULL when no entry matches (`workbench/libs/datatypes/helpfuncs.c:318-427,440-505`).

**Trigger and consequence:** while one or more of the four built-in entries are absent, `AllocVec()` fails for that entry during `AddDataTypes` startup. The command continues as though the shared list were initialized and may return success, but the corresponding generic classifier is absent; `ExamineData()` can then return NULL for content that should fall back to the built-in type. A later successful `AddDataTypes` invocation can retry missing entries. **Affected configuration:** the optional `workbench-c-adddatatypes` executable when built and run; it is listed in the i386 PC floppy executable archive (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:159-160`; `arch/i386-pc/boot/floppy/mmakefile.src:72-75`) and is also invoked by the checked-in Security-Startup script (`workbench/c/security/AMUInit.c:97`). **Confidence:** high for the ignored allocation result and incomplete classifier state; occurrence depends on low-memory allocation failure. No allocation failure, datatype query, command, or build was run. Propagate a failed `CreateBasicType()` result and report initialization failure, or roll back partial entries. Source-only.

<a id="gd10270"></a>
### GD10270 — Vulkan-Hpp `UniqueDisplayKHR` uses a destroy operation that `PhysicalDevice` does not provide

`UniqueHandleTraits<DisplayKHR, Dispatch>` declares its deleter as `detail::ObjectDestroy<PhysicalDevice, Dispatch>` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_handles.hpp:2677-2683`). `ObjectDestroy::destroy()` forwards to `m_owner.destroy(...)` (`vulkan.hpp:6678-6712`), but the selected `PhysicalDevice` wrapper has no `destroy(DisplayKHR, ...)` overload; it exposes `releaseDisplayEXT(DisplayKHR, ...)` instead (`vulkan_handles.hpp:18861-20990,20030-20037`). The three generated unique-result methods for displays correctly provide an explicit `detail::ObjectRelease<PhysicalDevice, Dispatch>` deleter (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:14244,23026,24678`), showing that release rather than destroy is required for these acquired-display handles.

**Trigger and consequence:** compile code that constructs or otherwise destroys a non-null `UniqueDisplayKHR` using the public alias with smart handles enabled. `UniqueHandle`'s destructor calls its inherited deleter's `destroy()` (`vulkan.hpp:872-897`); instantiating that path requires `PhysicalDevice::destroy(DisplayKHR, ...)`, which is not declared, so the alias cannot be used as its name promises and the client fails to compile. The generated unique-result overloads with their explicit release deleters are separate and are not affected by this default-alias mismatch. **Affected configuration:** copied Vulkan-Hpp header with smart handles enabled; no in-tree use of `UniqueDisplayKHR` was found. **Confidence:** high for the template/deleter mismatch from the declarations and forwarding bodies; no client compilation was run. Give the alias a release-based deleter or omit it when no default destroy deleter exists. Source-only.


<a id="gd10275"></a>
### GD10275 — Buffered IconList setup leaks its RastPort on layer setup failure

In `IconList__MUIM_Show()`, buffered setup allocates a bitmap and a new RastPort, stores the bitmap in that RastPort, then attempts to allocate layer info and create an upfront layer (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Classes/iconlist.c:3063-3080`). If `NewLayerInfo()` or `CreateUpfrontLayer()` fails, the failure branch overwrites `icld_BufferRastPort` with `icld_DisplayRastPort` (`:3093-3097`). The fallback cleanup frees the bitmap and disposes layer info when present, but never frees the newly allocated RastPort (`:3102-3108`). `CreateRastPort()` returns a separately allocated RastPort and `FreeRastPort()` is its release operation (`compiler/arossupport/createrastport.c:17-20`; `compiler/arossupport/freerastport.c:25-47`). Once its pointer is overwritten, later `MUIM_Hide()` cleanup cannot reach it.

**Trigger and consequence:** buffered rendering is enabled, bitmap and RastPort allocation succeed, and either layer-info allocation or upfront-layer creation fails. Each such setup attempt leaks the RastPort allocation; repeated failed setup can accumulate these leaks. **Affected configuration:** clients that select the IconList MUI class and enable `ICONLIST_DISP_BUFFERED` before show. Wanderer's own buffer-enabling code is guarded by `ICONWINDOW_BUFFERLIST`, whose definition is commented out in this snapshot (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow.c:930-947`), so this is not claimed for the default Wanderer path. **Confidence:** high for the lost allocation and missing release; no allocation failure or GUI operation was induced. Free the newly created RastPort on fallback before replacing its pointer. Source-only.


<a id="gd10274"></a>
### GD10274 — Vulkan-Hpp latency timing wrapper returns unwritten records

The RAII `SwapchainKHR::getLatencyTimingsNV()` wrapper and both enhanced `Device::getLatencyTimingsNV()` allocator overloads first call `vkGetLatencyTimingsNV` with `pTimings == nullptr`, resize a vector to the returned maximum `timingCount`, then make the fill call and return the vector without using its updated count (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:27059-27072`; `workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:29418-29464`). Vulkan specifies that the null-array call returns the maximum number of queryable frame records, while the fill call overwrites `timingCount` with the number of values actually written ([`VkGetLatencyMarkerInfoNV`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkGetLatencyMarkerInfoNV.html)). The wrapper record type default-initializes timestamp and ID fields to zero (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:54576-54593`), so vector elements beyond the fill count remain plausible-looking empty records.

**Trigger and consequence:** latency data changes between the count and fill calls and the fill call writes fewer records than the queried maximum. The returned vector then has a larger size than the number of valid records, and callers can treat the trailing default entries as actual frame timings. The API explicitly distinguishes maximum queryable count from actual values written; the precise changing-data condition was not reproduced or tied to a specific driver. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced or RAII C++ API with `VK_NV_low_latency2`; no non-generated in-tree consumer of these vector helpers was found. **Confidence:** high that the wrappers ignore the output count and return any unwritten vector tail; conditional on the permitted query/fill count being smaller on the second call. Resize the vector to the updated `latencyMarkerInfo.timingCount` before returning. Source-only.

<a id="gd10273"></a>
### GD10273 — Generic bitmap row alignment wraps at the UWORD width limit

`BM__Root__New()` defaults bitmap alignment to 16 pixels (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:897-899`). `GetBytesPerRow()` rounds `data->width` up using a `UWORD` temporary (`:849-870`). For a valid nonzero width from 65,521 through 65,535, the rounded width is 65,536 and narrows to zero. When no explicit `BytesPerRow` is supplied, the constructor stores that zero as the row stride (`:1033-1049`). In the generic chunky class, this yields a zero-sized `AllocVec()` request and bitmap-construction failure (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:70-79`; `rom/exec/allocvec.c:54-56`). In the generic planar class, `GetBytesPerRow()` returns `width >> 3` for planar pixels, also zero after the wrap; with positive depth, `PBM__Root__New()` requests zero bytes for each plane, `AllocMem(0)` returns NULL, and object construction fails (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:139-195`; `rom/exec/allocmem.c:90-92`). Both failures occur despite the dimensions fitting the public `AllocBitMap(ULONG, ULONG, ...)` inputs (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:52-54,253-254`).

The trigger is an offscreen chunky or planar bitmap with height greater than zero, width 65,521–65,535, default 16-pixel alignment, and no caller-supplied row stride; the planar path also requires positive depth. The selected generic `CreateObject()` path chooses the chunky or planar class from the pixel format when no specialized class is supplied (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1040-1068`). This is a large-dimension allocation failure, not evidence of an undersized successful buffer. **Affected configuration:** generic software chunky and planar bitmap allocation. **Confidence:** high for the arithmetic and both constructor failure paths; no such bitmap was allocated. Keep the rounded width and row-size arithmetic in a type wide enough to represent the rounded value, then validate any narrowing separately. Source-only.

The same wrap is present in the framebuffer mode-change path: `BM__Root__Set()` copies the selected mode's horizontal display size into `data->width` and recomputes `data->bytesPerRow` with `GetBytesPerRow()` (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:4454-4470`). The generic display `Show()` path sets the framebuffer's ModeID and then copies the newly shown bitmap into it (`gfx_displayclass.c:1230-1248`); generic chunky/planar Set methods forward to the root method, and the generic CopyBox fallback reads the resulting row-stride attribute (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:980-1004`; `gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:336-350`; `gfx_hiddclass.c:1040-1109`). Thus a custom enumerated framebuffer mode with the same horizontal width can leave the framebuffer row stride zero and make generic copy operations use incorrect row addresses. This additional path requires a display driver to enumerate such a mode and use the generic stride/copy methods; a checked-in mode with that width was not verified here, and driver-specific accelerated handling was not established. It remains conditional and source-only.

The framebuffer ModeID branch above only establishes the zero `BytesPerRow` state for a custom mode of that width. Its downstream display-copy effect is not proven: `CopyBox` exposes an unsigned width but the generic fallback uses signed `WORD` loop variables, and hardware drivers may override the operation. Treat this framebuffer route as unresolved, not as an established additional consequence of GD10273.


**Additional confirmed GD10264 sites (2026-11-01):** RAII `Device::getTensorOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataARM<DataType>()` and `getTensorViewOpaqueCaptureDescriptorDataARM<DataType>()` declare uninitialized `DataType` locals, call result-bearing Vulkan queries, then package those locals after `resultCheck()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:26390-26422`). The commands permit errors and write opaque bytes only on success; with no exceptions and disabled/nonfatal result assertions, scalar or trivially default-initialized `DataType` instantiations can package untouched storage. Requires `VK_ARM_tensors` with descriptor capture/replay support. No query/build was run.
<a id="gd10276"></a>
## GD10276 — EasyRequest body allocations are leaked on success and later setup failure

`BuildEasyRequestArgs()` allocates the formatted message with `buildeasyreq_formattext()` and allocates a separate `IntuiText` line array with `requester_makebodyplain()` (`rom/intuition/buildeasyrequestargs.c:155-159,186-187`; the latter uses `AllocVec()` in `rom/intuition/requesters.h:160-189`). If requester-body allocation succeeds but gadget creation or `OpenWindowTagList()` later fails, the builder frees `RawBody` and then the request data, but never frees the separate `ReqBody` allocation (`buildeasyrequestargs.c:189-214,252-267`). On successful window creation both pointers are retained in `IntRequestUserData`, attached to `req->UserData`, and the live requester is returned (`:216-249`). `FreeSysRequest()` reaches `freesysreq_intern()`, which closes the window and frees the gadgets, labels, and user-data structure, but the only `FreeVec()` calls for `RawBody` and `ReqBody` are inside a disabled `#if (0)` block (`rom/intuition/sysrequest_intern.c:314-356`). No other active release of those allocations exists. The `EasyRequestArgs()` convenience wrapper calls `FreeSysRequest()` after handling the requester (`rom/intuition/easyrequestargs.c:66-80`), so the successful path leaks both body allocations too. Direct `BuildEasyRequestArgs()` clients also use the documented cleanup path: Exec user alerts call `FreeSysRequest()` after `SysReqHandler()` (`rom/exec/useralert.c:33-58`), and the selected PFS3 formatter plus the standalone requester demo do likewise (`rom/filesys/pfs3/fs/format.c:270-290`; `developer/demos/easyreq.c:61-77`). These caller cleanups therefore do not avoid the leak.

**Trigger and consequence:** a successfully constructed requester followed by `FreeSysRequest()` leaks its formatted string buffer and line-array allocation; repeated requests steadily consume memory. Separately, if `ReqBody` allocation succeeds but later gadget creation or window opening fails, the builder leaks the line-array allocation on its failure path. **Affected configuration:** selected Intuition builds that include this implementation, with successful body allocation; the second leak additionally requires a later setup failure. **Confidence:** high for each allocation and the missing release paths; no requester or failure was induced. Free `ReqBody` on failed construction and release both retained body allocations after closing a successful requester, while preserving their shared-string lifetime until then. Source-only.

<a id="gd10281"></a>
## GD10281 — EasyRequest can open without its requested body text after allocation failure

`requester_makebodyplain()` returns `NULL` when its `AllocVec()` for the `IntuiText` line array fails (`rom/intuition/requesters.h:160-189`). `BuildEasyRequestArgs()` stores that result in `requserdata->ReqBody` but does not check it before proceeding to gadget creation and `OpenWindowTagList()` (`rom/intuition/buildeasyrequestargs.c:186-216`). If the window opens, it publishes the user data and calls `buildreq_draw()` with the NULL body pointer (`:220-249`). The drawing path passes it to `ReqPrintIText()` and then `int_PrintIText()`; the latter's `for (; iText; ...)` loop simply draws no body text for NULL (`rom/intuition/requesters.c:172-175`; `rom/intuition/printitext.c:93-95`). The requester dimensions were already calculated from the formatted `RawBody`, so the window still opens with the reserved body area and controls but omits the explanatory text.

**Trigger and consequence:** `RawBody`, labels, and gadgets are successfully allocated, but the `ReqBody` line-array allocation fails and window creation succeeds. `BuildEasyRequestArgs()` returns a live requester that lacks the message supplied by its caller; `EasyRequestArgs()` likewise handles and frees that textless requester as though construction succeeded. One concrete caller is the optional ASL file requester: its delete confirmation formats “Warning: you cannot get back what you delete! Ok to delete %s?” and uses `EasyRequestArgs()` before calling `DeleteFile()` when the first button is selected (`workbench/libs/asl/catalogs/asl.cd:34-39`; `filereqsupport.c:1325-1334`). Under this allocation failure, the “Delete File” title and “Delete|Cancel” buttons can still be shown without the warning or filename. **Affected configuration:** selected Intuition builds under the specific `ReqBody` allocation failure; the ASL consequence applies when the explicit optional `workbench-libs-asl` target is built and used. Its parent aggregate edges are disabled (`workbench/libs/asl/mmakefile.src:41-46`), so no default-image inclusion is claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation, NULL-tolerant rendering and caller's delete branch; the user-visible consequence requires allocation failure and a subsequent first-button selection. No allocation failure, requester, or file deletion was induced. Treat a missing body array as requester-construction failure, or provide a rendering fallback. Source-only.

<a id="gd10283"></a>
## GD10283 — First system-requester gadget allocation failure dereferences a NULL cleanup list

Both `buildeasyreq_makegadgets()` and `buildsysreq_makegadgets()` allocate a shared button-frame image before building a gadget list (`rom/intuition/buildeasyrequestargs.c:488-494`; `rom/intuition/sysrequest_intern.c:468-481`). On the first `FRBUTTONCLASS` `NewObject()` failure, each function is still on its first iteration, assigns NULL `thisgadget` to `gadgetlist`, and calls `intrequest_freegadgets(gadgetlist, ...)` (`buildeasyrequestargs.c:570-587`; `sysrequest_intern.c:483-512`). The shared cleanup helper dereferences `gadgets->GadgetRender` before its `while (gadgets)` loop (`rom/intuition/requesters.c:40-45`), so it faults instead of returning NULL. The already allocated `gadgetframe` is also not disposed on either first-button failure. `BuildEasyRequestArgs()` expects a NULL return to perform ordinary requester-construction cleanup (`buildeasyrequestargs.c:189-214,252-267`); `buildsysreq_intern()` likewise expects the helper to return NULL and unwind its requester data and screen lock (`sysrequest_intern.c:49-165`). But both callers are bypassed by the cleanup fault. `BuildSysRequest()` enters `buildsysreq_intern()`, and `AutoRequest()` calls `BuildSysRequest()` (`buildsysrequest.c:48-57`; `autorequest.c:48-57`), so the second path affects these public APIs too.

**Trigger and consequence:** frame-image creation succeeds, then allocation/construction of the first requester button fails in either builder. `BuildEasyRequestArgs()`, `BuildSysRequest()`, or `AutoRequest()` crashes while attempting cleanup and leaves the shared frame image allocated. This is distinct from a later-button failure, where a non-NULL gadget list exists and the cleanup helper can traverse it. **Affected configuration:** Intuition builds under first-button object creation failure; the public requester APIs all reach one of the two builders. **Confidence:** high for the NULL assignment, unconditional dereference and leaked frame; no allocation failure was induced. Handle an empty gadget list in the cleanup helper or dispose the frame and return NULL directly when the first button cannot be created. Source-only.

<a id="gd10282"></a>
## GD10282 — EasyRequest layout arithmetic wraps when gadget rows exceed screen height

`BuildEasyRequestArgs()` derives the gadget count from `|` separators in the caller's `es_GadgetFormat` (`rom/intuition/buildeasyrequestargs.c:302-305`) and arranges buttons into `nrows` based on the available screen width (`:496-523`). It computes `gadgetsheight` from those rows, clamps the requester height to `scr->Height` when the complete layout is too tall, then subtracts `gadgetsheight` and the fixed borders from that screen height into `dims->disptextheight` (`:533-553`). `disptextheight` is a `UWORD` (`rom/intuition/requesters.h:38-48`); if the buttons and borders alone exceed the screen, the subtraction is negative and conversion to `UWORD` wraps to a large positive value. The later `dims->textheight > dims->disptextheight` test consequently misses that the body has no remaining display height and does not create its text scrollbar (`buildeasyrequestargs.c:606-627`). The drawing path uses the wrapped value to form a WORD-based clip rectangle endpoint (`rom/intuition/requesters.c:163-169`), so the body clip region is also computed from an invalid height.

**Trigger and consequence:** `BuildEasyRequestArgs()` or `EasyRequestArgs()` receives enough gadget labels to make the arranged button rows taller than the screen, for example many wide choices on a low-height screen. The requester height is clamped, but the remaining body height wraps; the expected text scrollbar is omitted and the body clipping geometry is invalid, leaving message lines inaccessible or incorrectly clipped. **Affected configuration:** selected Intuition builds with a caller-supplied EasyStruct whose gadget rows exceed the selected screen's usable height. **Confidence:** high for the unsigned narrowing and missed scrollbar branch; exact on-screen rendering depends on the layer clip implementation. No requester was opened or layout rendered. Compute available text height in a signed wide type and reject or separately handle layouts where gadget rows leave no body area. Source-only.

<a id="gd10277"></a>
## GD10277 — Clipped CyberGraphics blur reads unwritten scratch pixels

The selected CyberGraphics blur allocates `src` with `AllocMem(..., MEMF_ANY)` and calls `ReadPixelArray()` for the full requested rectangle, but ignores its returned pixel count (`arch/x86_64-all/cgfx/processpixelarray_avx_opblur.c:475-486`). `ReadPixelArray()` routes through `DoRenderFunc()`, which clips the requested rectangle to the bitmap and adjusts the callback's source offset for the clipped intersection (`workbench/libs/cgfx/readpixelarray.c:142-147,157-168`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:123-140,1064-1082`; `rom/graphics/graphics_intern.h:41` enables the bitmap clip fallback). Its callback writes only the intersection at `data.array + modulo * srcy + bppix * srcx` (`readpixelarray.c:161-168`); no code initializes the unfilled scratch area. The AVX blur then processes every `w × h` scratch pixel (`processpixelarray_avx_opblur.c:51-145,151-241`) and `WritePixelArray()` clips the output again (`:513`; `workbench/libs/cgfx/writepixelarray.c:183-204`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on a layerless 640-pixel-wide HIDD bitmap, call `ProcessPixelArray()` with `POP_BLUR` for x=600, width=100, and a fully visible y-range. The read clips to 40 pixels per row and leaves `src[40..99]` uninitialized. With the minimum radius of one, the horizontal pass for output column 39 reads `src[40]`; that output column is within the visible bitmap and is written back, so its color depends on stale scratch contents. Larger radii can contaminate more pixels along the clipped edge. The generic selected blur implementation has the same partial-row issue in its `ReadPixelArray()`/full-width processing loop (`workbench/libs/cgfx/processpixelarray_opblur.c:57-79`).

**Affected configuration:** CyberGraphics library builds that select the generic blur or x86-64 AVX2 blur implementation, when a `POP_BLUR` rectangle is partially clipped at a RastPort edge. The CyberGraphics library is an optional target; this is not claimed for every default image. **Confidence:** high for the clipping offset, untouched scratch tail, full-width convolution, and visible clipped write; no pixel operation was run. Restrict processing to the returned intersection and adjust the blur edge policy, or initialize/fill the clipped scratch area before convolution. Source-only.

<a id="gd10278"></a>
## GD10278 — Dtpic state redraw can pass a failed clone bitmap to the blitter

`clone_bitmap()` returns `NULL` when its `AllocBitMap()` call fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/dtpic.c:195-219`). During datatype setup, both selected and highlighted clones are stored without checking either result, and `setup_datatype()` still returns success as long as the original image bitmap exists (`:275-285`). On a later draw, the selected or highlighted state replaces the valid source pointer with the corresponding clone pointer and passes it to `BltBitMapRastPort()` without a null check (`:604-621`). The blitter immediately evaluates `OBTAIN_HIDD_BM(srcBitMap)`; `IS_HIDD_BM(bitmap)` expands to `bitmap->pad == HIDD_BM_PAD_MAGIC`, so a null source is dereferenced before the blitter's later `srcbm_obj == NULL` check (`rom/graphics/bltbitmaprastport.c:116-119`; `rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:632`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional Dtpic class loads an image whose base bitmap succeeds, but allocation of either its selected or highlighted clone fails; a client enables the corresponding `MUIA_Dtpic_DarkenSelState` or `MUIA_Dtpic_LightenOnMouse` attribute; the image's mask mode is not `mskHasMask`; and the object is shown and enters that state. The next redraw can fault while the blitter checks the null bitmap. The class does not fail setup or fall back to the original bitmap after clone allocation failure. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly requested `workbench-classes-zune-dtpic` module, under clone-allocation failure and use of the corresponding state attribute. The pinned muimaster manifest sets `MAKE_BUILTIN_DTPIC := no`, and the Dtpic target is absent from the active parent class aggregate, so this is not claimed for the default build. No checked-in caller setting either state attribute was found; the trigger is available through the public Dtpic attributes in `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/dtpic.h:15-20`. **Confidence:** high for the missing allocation check and null dereference path; no allocation failure, state event, or GUI draw was induced. Keep the normal bitmap selected when a clone is unavailable, or reject setup if a requested state image cannot be created. Source-only.

<a id="gd10279"></a>
<a id="gd10279-vulkan-hpp-no-exceptions-helpers-can-dispatch-mismatched-parallel-arrays"></a>
## GD10279 — Vulkan-Hpp no-exceptions helpers can dispatch mismatched parallel arrays

Several enhanced Vulkan-Hpp wrappers check that parallel `ArrayProxy` values have equal lengths by throwing `LogicError` when exceptions are enabled, but reduce the same check to `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT` under `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS`. `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT` defaults to C `assert` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_hpp_macros.hpp:74-79`), so `NDEBUG` removes these guards. The wrappers then dispatch a count from one proxy with the other proxy's pointer unchanged.

Confirmed sites include `CommandBuffer::bindVertexBuffers()` (buffers/offsets; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:5450-5474`; RAII `vulkan_raii.hpp:16660-16674`), core and KHR `waitEvents2()` (events/dependency infos; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:8147-8164,23946-23963`; RAII `vulkan_raii.hpp:17853-17868,24563-24578`), and core and EXT `bindVertexBuffers2()` (buffers/offsets and optional nonempty sizes/strides; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:8342-8367,21835-21859`; RAII `vulkan_raii.hpp:17948-17975,23722-23745`). The transform-feedback helpers check buffers against offsets and optional sizes (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:11975-11993`; RAII `vulkan_raii.hpp:19378-19396`), while begin/end transform-feedback check nonempty counter-offset arrays against counter-buffer counts (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:12028-12040,12073-12085`; RAII `vulkan_raii.hpp:19407-19419,19430-19442`). `Device::setHdrMetadataEXT()` checks swapchains against metadata (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:14731-14745`; RAII `vulkan_raii.hpp:20627-20639`), and `CommandBuffer::setDescriptorBufferOffsetsEXT()` checks buffer indices against offsets (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:24194-24208`; RAII `vulkan_raii.hpp:24689-24703`). `bindShadersEXT()` also has an assertion-only stage/shader length comparison (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:28512-28524`; RAII `vulkan_raii.hpp:26753-26765`); a non-null shader proxy shorter than the stage list is invalid when that guard disappears, while the valid null-pointer form is covered separately by GD10284. The previously documented acceleration-structure build and indirect-build overloads have the same assertion-only pattern (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:17316-17399,17426-17449`; RAII `vulkan_raii.hpp:21692-21776`). `Device::getAccelerationStructureBuildSizesKHR()` has the same assertion-only companion-array check in both the enhanced and RAII overloads: each compares `maxPrimitiveCounts.size()` with `buildInfo.geometryCount`, then forwards `maxPrimitiveCounts.data()` to the native command (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:17864-17896`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:21975-21995`). The Vulkan reference defines `pMaxPrimitiveCounts` as an array of exactly `pBuildInfo->geometryCount` values ([`vkGetAccelerationStructureBuildSizesKHR`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetAccelerationStructureBuildSizesKHR.html)). In a no-exceptions build with `NDEBUG`, a shorter proxy bypasses the check and leaves the native function with fewer elements than its geometry count requires; this is another GD10279 site. The enhanced and RAII `CommandBuffer::setSampleMaskEXT()` wrappers also use assertion-only length checks in no-exceptions builds (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:26718-26742`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:25942-25960`). Their native `pSampleMask` extent is based on `samples` ([`vkCmdSetSampleMaskEXT`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdSetSampleMaskEXT.html)); with `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` and `NDEBUG`, a too-short `ArrayProxy` bypasses either check and the native command may read beyond the supplied words. Vulkan defines each companion array extent from the command's shared count ([vertex buffers](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdBindVertexBuffers.html), [vertex buffers2](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdBindVertexBuffers2.html), [wait events2](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdWaitEvents2.html), [HDR metadata](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkSetHdrMetadataEXT.html), [descriptor buffer offsets](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdSetDescriptorBufferOffsetsEXT.html)).

**Additional confirmed constructor sites (2026-11-02):** `SemaphoreWaitInfo` checks `semaphores_.size() == values_.size()` using `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT` in no-exceptions builds (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:148865-148872`); under `NDEBUG`, unequal arrays are accepted with `semaphoreCount` taken from the semaphore array and both pointers retained. The enhanced core/KHR wait wrappers forward the record to native dispatch (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:7182-7190,20231-20239`; RAII `vulkan_raii.hpp:17446-17455`). Similarly, `SetDescriptorBufferOffsetsInfoEXT` checks buffer-index/offset lengths with `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:149056-149064`); when removed, `setCount` comes from buffer indices and a shorter offsets pointer is passed by `CommandBuffer::setDescriptorBufferOffsets2EXT()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:30801-30809`; RAII `vulkan_raii.hpp:27580-27587`). `SubmitInfo` also compares wait-semaphore and wait-stage-mask lengths with `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT` in no-exceptions builds (`vulkan_structs.hpp:151114-151121`); with `NDEBUG`, its constructor retains the semaphore-derived count and independently sized stage-mask pointer, then `Queue::submit()` forwards the record (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:928-936`). `VideoDecodeAV1PictureInfoKHR` checks that tile-offset and tile-size proxy lengths match with `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT` in no-exceptions builds (`vulkan_structs.hpp:159854-159878`); when `NDEBUG` removes the check, it retains the tile count from the offsets and both pointers, and the enclosing `VideoDecodeInfoKHR` chain is forwarded to `vkCmdDecodeVideoKHR` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:11919-11935`). This constructor site joins the existing GD10279 assertion-only validation pattern; GD10258 separately records the independently reachable setter mismatch. These are not new root causes or IDs. The no-exceptions `NDEBUG` trigger is conditional on those macros and no in-tree C++ Vulkan-Hpp caller was found. No Vulkan operation or build was run. Source-only.

**Trigger and consequence:** an enhanced or RAII client uses unequal required arrays (or a nonempty optional companion array of the wrong length) in a build with `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` and `NDEBUG`. The assertion no longer stops the wrapper; it sends the count from the primary array with a shorter companion pointer, violating Vulkan's array-length requirements. An implementation that reads the missing elements can access beyond the supplied array or record invalid state. Exception-enabled builds reject these mismatches before dispatch. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced/RAII APIs with the relevant core version or extension enabled; no non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the compiled-out guards and mismatched native count/pointer pairs; no malformed call or Vulkan operation was run. Validate lengths with a non-asserting path before dispatch. Source-only.

<a id="gd10280"></a>
## GD10280 — Vulkan-Hpp pipeline-properties convenience wrappers pass undersized output storage

The enhanced `Device::getPipelinePropertiesEXT()` wrapper constructs a local `BaseOutStructure` and passes its address to `vkGetPipelinePropertiesEXT` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:25302-25314`). The parallel RAII overload does the same (`vulkan_raii.hpp:25208-25218`). `BaseOutStructure` contains only `sType` and `pNext`, and its default `sType` is `eApplicationInfo` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:8705-8718`). Vulkan requires `pPipelineProperties` to point to a `VkPipelinePropertiesIdentifierEXT` ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetPipelinePropertiesEXT.html)), whose layout also contains the 16-byte `pipelineIdentifier` field (`vulkan_structs.hpp:131193-131205`). Thus both convenience overloads pass the wrong structure type and do not allocate storage for the returned identifier. The raw overload accepts caller-provided output storage through `BaseOutStructure *` and can be used with a correctly sized `PipelinePropertiesIdentifierEXT` object.

**Trigger and consequence:** a Vulkan-Hpp enhanced or RAII client calls the convenience overload with `VK_EXT_pipeline_properties` and the `pipelinePropertiesIdentifier` feature enabled. The wrapper supplies its short base object rather than a `PipelinePropertiesIdentifierEXT`; validation can reject the call, while an implementation that writes the required identifier can write past the local object's storage. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced or RAII C++ API; no in-tree C++ call to the convenience overload was found. **Confidence:** high for the wrapper's local type/size and the API's required output type; the extent of any implementation write on invalid input is implementation-dependent. No Vulkan call or build was run. Return a typed `PipelinePropertiesIdentifierEXT` or provide a typed output overload. Source-only.


<a id="gd10284"></a>
## GD10284 — Vulkan-Hpp shader binding rejects the valid null-array unbind form

The enhanced `CommandBuffer::bindShadersEXT()` and RAII `CommandBuffer::bindShadersEXT()` require `stages.size() == shaders.size()` before dispatch. With exceptions enabled, a mismatch throws `LogicError`; with `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS`, the wrapper asserts the same equality (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:28505-28524`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:26748-26765`). `ArrayProxy` has a default/null constructor that stores count zero and a null pointer (`vulkan.hpp:301-309`). The native command explicitly permits `pShaders == NULL` and defines it as if an array of `stageCount` `VK_NULL_HANDLE` values had been supplied, which unbinds shaders from all listed stages ([`vkCmdBindShadersEXT` reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdBindShadersEXT.html)).

**Trigger and consequence:** with `VK_EXT_shader_object`, pass a nonempty stage list and a null/empty `ArrayProxy<const ShaderEXT>` to either enhanced or RAII `bindShadersEXT()`. The native Vulkan call is valid and unbinds those stages, but exception-enabled wrappers throw before dispatch; no-exceptions builds with assertions enabled stop at the assertion. With `NDEBUG`, the check disappears and the native call proceeds. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced or RAII API with `VK_EXT_shader_object`; no non-generated in-tree caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the wrapper guard and the native null-pointer behavior. No shader or command buffer was used and no C++ client was compiled. Permit the null-proxy case and retain length validation when a shader array is provided. Source-only.

<a id="gd10285"></a>
## GD10285 — TextEditor preferences initialization leaks partially created MUI subclasses

`CreateSubClasses()` creates the width slider, speed slider, and text subclasses in sequence, but returns `FALSE` on any later creation failure without deleting earlier successes (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcp/Dispatcher.c:107-145`). In the `TextEditor.mcp` library, `ClassInit()` returns `FALSE` when that helper fails and does not call `DeleteSubClasses()` (`mcp/library.c:184-193`). The shared startup path handles a failed `ClassInit()` by deleting only its outer `ThisClassP`, then closing `muimaster.library` and returning a failed library init; it does not call `ClassExpunge()` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/include/mccinit.c:761-791,820-821`). `ClassExpunge()` is where this module normally calls `DeleteSubClasses()` (`mcp/library.c:197-208`). The MUI creator allocates both a `MUI_CustomClass` record and an OOP class, and the matching delete path frees them (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_createcustomclass.c:57-82`; `mui_deletecustomclass.c:45-64`), so any earlier subclasses remain allocated after this failed initialization.

The separate `mcp/Preference.c` source has a similar cleanup gap: it calls `CreateSubClasses()` before creating the outer settings class and application, but calls `DeleteSubClasses()` only inside `if (app)` (`mcp/Preference.c:87-145`). However, the checked-in `mcp/mmakefile.src` does not include `Preference.c` in its `FILES`, and a repository-wide target/source-reference search found no build rule selecting this program. Treat this as an unselected-source lead, not as a build-selected TextEditor MCP defect. If an external build selects this source, a partial subclass failure leaves earlier subclasses allocated; if the parent settings class is created but application-object creation fails, the parent class and subclasses are also left allocated.

**Trigger and consequence:** for the selected MCP module, memory pressure causes the second or third `MUI_CreateCustomClass()` call in `CreateSubClasses()` to fail after an earlier one succeeded. The successful earlier MUI class(es) and their superclass references are not released. The analogous `Preference.c` trigger is conditional on an external build selecting that unreferenced source. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly selected optional `workbench-classes-zune-texteditor-mcp` module; the top-level aggregate edge is commented in this revision, so no default-image inclusion is claimed. The standalone preferences program is not shown selected by this checkout's build rules. **Confidence:** high for the MCP module's missing cleanup and leaked allocations; no later callback invocation or crash is claimed. No allocation failure, module load, MUI class creation, or build was induced. Roll back each successful subclass on every failed setup path, or use a single cleanup path before returning.

**Review evidence:** [TextEditor MCP subclass setup and rollback trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#texteditor-mcp-subclass-setup-and-rollback).


<a id="gd10286"></a>
## GD10286 — VulkanProbe leaks a successfully opened Radeon HIDD reference

The `VulkanProbe` program selected through an active `workbench-hidds` virtual edge opens `radeonsi.hidd` so its GPU registration remains active, stores the returned base only in a block-local variable, and deliberately keeps the reference for the probe's lifetime (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/test/VulkanProbe.c:45-56`). The program never calls `CloseLibrary()`; every later early return and the normal success return leave that open reference outstanding (`:78-83,90-101,144-147,171-196`). Exec's `OpenLibrary()` calls the library's Open vector and returns the reference (`rom/exec/openlibrary.c:73-92`); its API pairs this with an explicit `CloseLibrary()` (`rom/exec/closelibrary.c:35-40,64-83`) and does not register the reference for process-exit cleanup. **Trigger and consequence:** explicitly build and run `VulkanProbe` on a system where `OpenLibrary("radeonsi.hidd", 0)` succeeds. That run leaves one extra open count on the shared library; repeated runs accumulate references and can prevent expunge if the provider is unloadable. The repository at the reviewed commit contains no `radeonsi.hidd` provider, so successful-open reachability depends on a separately supplied provider; no default-image inclusion is claimed. Close the acquired base through a common cleanup path after Vulkan use. **Affected configuration:** the `VulkanProbe` program selected through the active `workbench-hidds` virtual edge (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/mmakefile.src:45-60`) when the named HIDD is available. The probe is build-selected; the provider is absent from this checkout, so successful-open runtime reachability requires a separately supplied provider. **Confidence:** high that a successful open is never balanced and Exec has no per-process open-reference cleanup; expunge impact is conditional on provider lifecycle flags. No probe or library load was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkanprobe-library-reference-lifetime-pass).
