**Trigger and consequence:** build or install the optional pass-through `gl.library` without building/configuring an implementation, then open `gl.library` before setting `SYS/GL` or `SYS/GL.default`. The pass-through library calls `OpenLibrary(NULL, version)` rather than returning NULL for the unavailable implementation; depending on assertion/build configuration and library-list contents, this raises the assertion or faults in name comparison. **Affected configuration:** optional `workbench-libs-gl` used without an implementation-selection variable; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/libs/gl/mmakefile.src:5`). **Confidence:** high that the missing configuration produces a NULL implementation pointer and violates `OpenLibrary()`'s name input requirement; the exact failure behavior depends on build assertions and runtime list state. Check for a NULL name and return NULL from `LibOpen()`. No library, configuration, or build was run; source-only. See the [GL pass-through library review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gl-pass-through-library-full-body-and-notification-setup-gd14813).

<a id="gd10448"></a>
## GD10448 — CursorFB direct access bypasses the software-cursor bracket

The CursorFB bitmap class brackets ordinary pixel/image reads and writes with the display cursor semaphore and removes/renders the pointer around overlapping operations (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_cursorfbclass.c:40-75,181-269`). Its method table instead maps both `ObtainDirectAccess` and `ReleaseDirectAccess` to `cursorfb_fwd`, which only calls the corresponding method on the wrapped real bitmap (`:68-70,481-482`). The display class wraps framebuffer or displayable bitmaps in CursorFB when it supplies a software cursor (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1074-1090`). The public `LockBitMapTagList()` path obtains direct access from the HIDD bitmap and returns the base address to the caller; its contract describes exclusive bitmap access and permits the caller to use that pixel address until unlock (`workbench/libs/cgfx/lockbitmaptaglist.c:30-45,96-108,144-148`). `UnLockBitMapTagList()` releases the HIDD direct-access lease (`workbench/libs/cgfx/unlockbitmaptaglist.c:99-103`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on a display without a hardware cursor, use a direct-access-capable, software-cursor-wrapped framebuffer while the pointer is visible; have a client write through the returned bitmap address to pixels under the cursor, then unlock. CursorFB does not hide the software pointer or take its cursor semaphore for the lease, so the client can overwrite the cursor pixels directly. Later cursor movement/removal can also restore the saved pre-write pixels over the client's update. The wrapper likewise does not serialize direct writes against cursor movement/redraw. **Affected configuration:** the optional m68k P96 HIDD when the detected board lacks the `BIB_HARDWARESPRITE` flag, plus any other display with both software-cursor fallback and direct-access-capable display bitmaps. P96 derives `SupportsHWCursor` from that board flag (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_hiddclass.c:1651,1735,736-738`), delegates cursor setup to the generic software cursor when it is clear (`:1184-1187`), and selects its P96 bitmap class for mode-ID bitmaps (`:705-714`); that bitmap class returns its direct video-memory address while holding `bmLock` (`p96gfx_bitmapclass.c:644-670`). The CursorFB wrapper is then selected by the generic display path (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:784-794,1074-1085`). The direct lock is reachable through the Cybergraphics bitmap-lock API. A maintained optional caller exists in the PNG image class: `PNG_Draw()` passes its supplied RastPort to `WriteRGBAPixels()`, whose Cybergraphics hook is selected for Cybergraphics bitmaps and obtains `LBMI_BASEADDRESS` before writing the decoded pixels directly (`workbench/devs/diskimage/png_image/class.c:179-208,229-250`; `writergbapixels_cgx.c:54-82,90-106`; `workbench/libs/cgfx/lockbitmaptaglist.c:144-158`). The package installs `png.image` (`workbench/devs/diskimage/Makefile:59,199`). This establishes an in-tree direct-write route when a truecolor PNG is drawn to an active wrapped framebuffer. On the P96 HIDD, generic GFX pixel formats expose mapped Cybergraphics formats for the supported 15/16/24/32-bit modes (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_pixfmtclass.c:96-120,204-205`), which pass `LockBitMapTagList()`'s non-`-1` format check. The P96 display reports no separate framebuffer, creates the displayable bitmap with its P96 bitmap class, and the generic Display class wraps that displayable object when software cursor support is needed (`p96gfx_hiddclass.c:705-714,739-741`; `gfx_displayclass.c:935-970,1074-1085`). Its no-framebuffer Show path targets that same bitmap for the software cursor (`gfx_displayclass.c:1183-1195`). The PNG class opens `Picasso96API.library` first and only attempts `cybergraphics.library` if P96 is unavailable (`png_image/init.c:159-167`), so the in-tree CGX writer can lock the public bitmap whose HIDD object is the active CursorFB wrapper in this fallback configuration. The generic image method may also receive offscreen or non-displayed RastPorts, which are not claimed as affected. **Confidence:** high for the P96 capability combination, forwarding path and direct-address contract, and for the PNG class direct-write route in its Cybergraphics fallback configuration; actual corruption requires the supplied RastPort to reference the active software-cursor framebuffer and the write to overlap the cursor. Bracket the complete direct-access lease with cursor removal/restoration and synchronization. No bitmap lock, cursor movement, write, or build was performed; source-only. See the [CursorFB caller and direct-access review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#cursorfb-direct-access-cursor-lifetime-pass).

<a id="gd10449"></a>
## GD10449 — BetterString filename completion truncates large directory result counts

`FileNameComplete()` accumulates `ExAllControl.eac_Entries` into local `UWORD entries`, then adds that truncated total back to the last `ULONG eac_Entries` and stores the result in `InstData.FileEntries`, also a `UWORD` (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/FileNameCompl.c:314-329`; `compiler/include/dos/exall.h:94-101`; `mcc/private.h:77-80`). The selected ExAll contract returns a count for each buffer and requires repeated calls until enumeration finishes (`rom/dos/exall.c:43-48,75-77`). The completion state uses `FileEntries` to wrap `FileNumber` when cycling candidates (`FileNameCompl.c:194-214`). `FileNumber` itself is a signed `WORD` (`private.h:77-80`); for 32,770–65,535 results, backward initialization stores `eac_Entries - 1` as a negative value, and the next backward step's `< 0` branch resets it to the same final index on two's-complement AROS targets.

**Trigger and consequence:** with 32,770–65,535 matching entries, repeatedly request backward completion; on AROS's two's-complement targets the signed `FileNumber` becomes negative, so the backward step resets it to `FileEntries - 1` each time and repeats the same final candidate. With more than 65,535 results, the 16-bit accumulation and stored total also wrap, so cycling cannot reliably enumerate the full set; at exact multiples of 65,536 the stored count becomes zero. This is a completion correctness failure; no buffer overrun is claimed. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable optional BetterString MCC target (`workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/mmakefile.src:5-45`) when a DOS filesystem returns a sufficiently large matching result set. **Confidence:** high for the narrowing and downstream count use; the wider triggers depend on a directory and filesystem capable of exceeding the respective 16-bit range, and the signed-index behavior is scoped to AROS's two's-complement targets. Accumulate and store the total and index in types wide enough for the supported directory size, or reject/cap the result set explicitly. No directory enumeration or build was run; source-only. See the [BetterString filename-completion review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#betterstring-filename-completion-large-directory-count-pass).


A direct-access caller census found three additional paths, but none establishes a direct write to the active software-cursor framebuffer. `AHIRecord` locks the public screen bitmap only to query `LBMI_BYTESPERPIX`, then immediately unlocks without requesting or writing the base address (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:322-346`). The font datatype allocates a new offscreen bitmap before locking it, then passes its pixels to `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY` and unlocks (`workbench/classes/datatypes/font/fontclass.c:316-343`). The Compositor obtains direct access to each alpha bitmap as a source for `HIDD_BM_PutAlphaImage()` and releases it after the draw (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:306-323`); the source-to-active-display alias is not established, and destination rendering goes through the HIDD method. GD10448 therefore remains limited to a client that writes directly through an obtained base address for the active wrapped bitmap; no new in-tree direct-write caller is claimed.
<a id="gd10451"></a>
## GD10451 — MUI applications can remain in their event loops when their only window fails to open

`AboutAROS__MUIM_Application_Execute()` sets `MUIA_Window_Open` to TRUE but does not query whether the window opened before delegating to the blocking `MUIM_Application_Execute` loop (`workbench/system/AboutAROS/aboutaros.c:461-468`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:2344-2359`). The MUI Window setter calls `WindowOpen()` but discards its FALSE result (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:3158-3170`). Window setup, root-object setup, or native `OpenWindowTags()` failure can therefore leave the object closed (`:3757-3795`). AboutAROS registers its only `MUIV_Application_ReturnID_Quit` notification on that window's close request (`aboutaros.c:436-440`), so a failed open leaves no window capable of producing the normal quit event. `main()` then cannot reach its `MUI_DisposeObject(application)` call (`workbench/system/AboutAROS/main.c:32-40`) until Execute returns.

**Trigger and consequence:** launch AboutAROS and have its only window fail during setup or native window creation. The program enters the application event loop with no visible window and has no ordinary close action; it remains active until it receives Ctrl-C or is otherwise terminated. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-system-aboutaros` target (`workbench/system/AboutAROS/mmakefile.src:5-29`) when MUI window opening fails; the parent `workbench-system` edge is commented, so default installation is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked open state and missing close event source; occurrence depends on the window failure. Check `MUIA_Window_Open` after setting it and exit/clean up when opening failed. No window failure or application loop was induced; source-only; related MUI setter failure behavior is tracked in GD5522.

The same failure is independently present in several other build-selected Workbench applications. In **Info**, `SetAttrs(window, MUIA_Window_Open, TRUE, ...)` is followed directly by a loop that exits only on `MUIV_Application_ReturnID_Quit` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/Info/main.c:1270-1272`); the ordinary quit notifications come from the window close gadget and the window's buttons (`:1143-1145` and the construction/notification setup), so failure to open leaves the loop without its normal user-controlled exit. **DiskInfo** registers quit on window close (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/DiskInfo/diskinfo.c:537-538`), sets the window open without checking, and then delegates to the blocking superclass execute loop (`:589-599`; `application.c:2344-2359`). **SysMon** similarly registers quit only on window close (`workbench/system/SysMon/main.c:276-277`), ignores the open result (`:407`), and continues its timer-driven input loop (`:409-420`); Ctrl-C remains an external escape. **ExecuteCommand** registers close and Cancel as its quit sources (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/ExecuteCommand/executecommand.c:169-180`) and its Execute method opens unchecked before the blocking superclass call (`:215-227`). **WBNewDrawer** registers close and Cancel as quit sources, opens unchecked and calls Application Execute (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/WBNewDrawer/main.c:130-142`); successful creation is another quit path but also requires the inaccessible dialog's OK button (`:146-150`). **WBRename** opens unchecked (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/WBRename/main.c:184-193`) and calls Application Execute from its main flow (`:117-119`); its normal quit notifications and successful rename action also require interaction with that window (`:184-209`). **Clock** registers close as its quit source, ignores the result of opening its window, and enters Application Execute (`workbench/utilities/Clock/main.c:158-172`). **AROSTCP SysLog** opens its main window without checking (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/syslog/main.c:177-184`); Quit is notified by the main window's close request or application menu (`:332-342`), so neither ordinary path is interactable after a failed open. Its explicit target is marked contrib and its parent edge is commented.

QuickPart adds the same caller pattern: `QP_Main()` sets its only main window open without checking the result, later enters a `MUIM_Application_NewInput` loop, and registers the normal Quit return only on that window's close request (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_Main.c:653-664,708-718`). A failed open therefore leaves no visible close action; the loop waits on the MUI window/timer/input signals plus Ctrl-C/Ctrl-D, and normal disposal remains after the loop (`:720`). The active `AROS` Workbench target selects `workbench-tools-quickpart` through `workbench-tools` (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`). This adds QuickPart as another selected caller; produced-image installation is not inferred.

The same condition also affects 17 standalone Preferences applications that share `SystemPrefsWindowObject`: ASL, ScreenMode, ReqTools, Input, IControl, Wanderer, Boot (PC targets), Locale, Palette, Pointer, Serial, Network, BoingIconBar, Printer, Font, Appearance and Firewall. Each application sets its SystemPrefsWindow open and immediately calls `MUIM_Application_Execute` without checking the resulting open state (for example, `workbench/prefs/asl/main.c:63-64`, `screenmode/main.c:66-68`, and `firewall/main.c:63-64`). The inherited `PrefsWindow` close notification calls `MUIM_PrefsWindow_Cancel` (`workbench/classes/zune/prefswindow/prefswindow.c:126-133`); `SystemPrefsWindow__MUIM_PrefsWindow_Cancel()` returns `MUIV_Application_ReturnID_Quit` after the editor cancel path (`workbench/classes/zune/systemprefswindow/systemprefswindow.c:385-403`). If the window failed to open, the window close request and Save/Use/Cancel controls are unavailable to send that return ID, so the app remains in Execute until Ctrl-C or external termination. Their individual `mmakefile.src` files define explicit `%build_prog` targets, while the `workbench-prefs` aggregate edges are commented; default packaging is not claimed. This raises the optional caller count to 28 beyond AboutAROS.

Two further standalone Preferences programs use the same failure-prone flow outside `SystemPrefsWindowObject`. **Time** sets its only window open without a readback and enters `HandleAll()`'s `MUIM_Application_NewInput` loop; its normal Quit paths are the Cancel button and Project/Quit menu, while Ctrl-C remains an escape (`workbench/prefs/time/main.c:631-635,673-688`). **Trackdisk** sets its main window open without a readback, then loops on `MUIM_Application_NewInput`; Cancel and `MUIA_Window_CloseRequest` return Quit, but its wait mask does not include Ctrl-C (`workbench/prefs/trackdisk/trackdisk_prefs.c:86-101`). On failed open, both lack their normal interactive exit; Trackdisk can remain waiting without a UI until an application signal or external termination. Their standalone targets are explicit and their `workbench-prefs` aggregate edges are commented (`workbench/prefs/time/mmakefile.src:8-14`; `trackdisk/mmakefile.src:8-14`), so default packaging is not claimed. WiFi Preferences checks `MUIA_Window_Open` before its loop, and Zune Preferences checks the main window before calling `loop()`; both are excluded.

RequestString is another caller: after successfully constructing its application, it registers Quit only on the window close request and string acknowledgement (`workbench/c/RequestString.c:157-169`), sets the window open without checking the resulting state, and immediately calls `MUIM_Application_Execute` (`:181-185`). If the window fails to open, neither normal user action is available and the command waits in the application loop; only Ctrl-C or external termination can release it. Its `%build_prog` target is explicit at `workbench/c/mmakefile.src:135-136`, but its parent `workbench-c` aggregate is commented at `:99-109`, so default packaging is not claimed. This raises the total to 29 additional targets beyond AboutAROS.

The `R` command's GUI dialog is another case: it registers Quit on the close request and Cancel gadget, opens unchecked, then blocks in `MUIM_Application_Execute` (`workbench/c/R/gui.c:333-371`). If opening fails, the shell command has no dialog action to return its result and waits until Ctrl-C or external termination. Its explicit target is `workbench-c-r` (`workbench/c/R/mmakefile.src:9-15`); the parent edge is commented. Snoopy also opens its only preferences window without checking (`workbench/system/Snoopy/gui.c:302-303`) and enters the application execute loop (`:324-327`); the only registered Quit path is the Cancel hook's confirmation sequence (`:111-133,320-321`). If that window fails, Snoopy remains active without its normal user exit. Its target is explicit and its parent aggregate is commented (`workbench/system/Snoopy/mmakefile.src:8-15`). Neither caller is claimed to be in default packaging. These two callers raise the total to 31 additional targets beyond AboutAROS. WiMP adds another standalone target: it registers Quit on the main Window close request and the application Quit menu (`workbench/tools/WiMP/WiMP.c:1073-1074,1086-1088`), opens the main window without checking, and enters `MUIM_Application_Execute` (`:1175-1178`). Its separate info window is only opened from the main-window action (`:878`), so it does not provide an independent startup exit. If the main window fails, its normal UI quit paths are unavailable and the app remains in the MUI loop until Ctrl-C or external termination. WiMP has an explicit `%build_prog` target while its parent aggregate is commented (`workbench/tools/WiMP/mmakefile.src:10-15`); default packaging is not claimed. This brings the total to 32 additional targets beyond AboutAROS.

These 32 additional targets each have a standalone `%build_prog` manifest, but their parent and default-package selection has not been reconciled consistently enough to classify all of them. The Wanderer tools and SysMon callers above are in the active Workbench target chain. The shared consequence is an application that remains in its event loop after its only interactive window fails to open, until Ctrl-C/Ctrl-D where supported or external termination (with SysMon continuing periodic updates). This expands GD10451's caller evidence; it does not add 32 separate root-cause findings. No open failure was induced and no program was run; source-only.

<a id="gd10452"></a>
## GD10452 — BHFormat proceeds without its progress and Stop window after that window fails to open

`btn_format_function()` closes the selection window, sets the progress window open, but never checks `MUIA_Window_Open` (`workbench/system/BHFormat/gui.c:423-424`). It then opens a separate confirmation requester and, if the user confirms, proceeds into the cylinder-format loop (`:432-456`). The selected `MUI_RequestA()` implementation creates and opens its own requester window and checks that requester's open state; its reference window is only used to position the requester (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_request.c:174-180,206-217,273-278`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:1094-1117`). The format progress window contains the gauge and Stop button (`gui.c:647-666`); the only Stop notification sets `formatwin`'s user data (`:683-684`), and the formatter checks that field during its cylinder loop (`:447-461`).

**Trigger and consequence:** while running the standalone GUI Format target, cause `formatwin` to fail opening while the independent confirmation requester still opens, then confirm a full format. BHFormat proceeds to format cylinders with its progress and Stop window unavailable; its loop does not detect the failed open, and the GUI Stop path cannot be used. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-system-format` target (`workbench/system/BHFormat/mmakefile.src`); its `workbench-system` aggregate edge is commented, so default inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high that the open result is ignored and that the progress/Stop controls live only in the failed window; the combined window-failure and confirmation-success trigger is conditional. Check `MUIA_Window_Open` and abort before confirmation/formatting if the progress window did not open. No device, requester, window failure, format operation, or build was exercised; source-only. This is distinct from the CLI EOF confirmation issue documented in GD format coverage: it concerns the GUI progress/cancellation path.

<a id="gd10453"></a>
## GD10453 — X11 framebuffer teardown can free a bitmap still referenced by the event task

`X11BM_DisposeFB()` allocates a temporary reply port before sending `NOTY_WINDISPOSE`. If `CreateMsgPort()` fails, it returns immediately, skipping both notification of the X11 event task and destruction of the host window, colormap and pixmap (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11gfx_onbitmap.c:322-364`). The caller does not preserve the object on this error: `X11BM__Root__Dispose()` calls `X11BM_DisposeFB()` and then unconditionally invokes the superclass disposer (`x11gfx_bitmapclass.c:128-146`), whose root method frees the object allocation (`rom/oop/rootclass.c:137-149`).

The event task's `xwinnode` retains the framebuffer object's `bmobj` pointer after `NOTY_WINCREATE` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11.c:442-464`). Only a processed `NOTY_WINDISPOSE` removes that node (`:551-568`). Until then, an X11 `Expose` event follows the retained pointer into `OOP_INST_DATA()` and `X11BM_ExposeFB()` (`:123-127`). Thus a failed reply-port allocation during disposal leaves the event task with a pointer to the freed bitmap object; later expose handling can access freed instance data. The early return also leaves the X window and associated server resources allocated.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the hosted `x11gfx` HIDD target (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/mmakefile.src:42-62`), when disposing an already registered framebuffer bitmap with a live drawable and `CreateMsgPort()` fails. `rom/exec/createmsgport.c:50-74` shows failure both when `AllocMem()` cannot allocate the port and when `AllocSignal(-1)` cannot obtain a signal bit (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:55-100`). **Consequence:** a later expose event can dereference the disposed bitmap object, and the host window/resources remain leaked. **Confidence:** high for the skipped notification, unconditional object free, and retained event-task pointer; manifestation requires the stated allocation failure followed by an event. On the successful path, `X11DoNotify()` waits for a reply (`x11.h:237-242`), and the event task removes/frees the node before replying (`x11.c:551-568`), so disposal does not race past that handshake. Preserve the bitmap until the event task has removed its node, or provide a teardown handshake that does not fail before detaching the object. No allocation failure, bitmap disposal, X11 event, or runtime operation was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#x11-framebuffer-dispose-reply-port-failure-gd10453).


<a id="gd10454"></a>
## GD10454 — Volumelist reads past non-terminated BCPL DOS-list names

`Volumelist__OM_NEW()` copies each device, volume and assign name using `strncpy(entry.name, AROS_BSTR_ADDR(actdl->dol_Name), sizeof(entry.name))` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/volumelist.c:168-171,192-195,236-239`). On configurations without `AROS_FAST_BSTR`, `AROS_BSTR_ADDR()` points one byte past the length-prefixed BSTR header; the BSTR length is available at `AROS_BSTR_ADDR(name)[-1]` (`compiler/include/dos/bptr.h:57-83`), and `DosList.dol_Name` is explicitly a BCPL string (`compiler/include/dos/dosextens.h:418-419`). `strncpy()` therefore scans up to 100 source bytes looking for NUL instead of stopping at the BSTR's declared length. A valid short BSTR with no trailing C NUL can be read past its allocation while the list entry is copied; the resulting bytes are then retained in `entry.name` and returned by the display hook. The DOS-list lock protects the entry's lifetime but does not bound the read. Use `AROS_BSTR_strlen()` and copy exactly the bounded name length before adding the colon. **Affected configuration and trigger:** m68k builds where `AROS_FAST_BSTR` is not defined, with Volumelist built into muimaster or loaded as `Volumelist.mui`, when a device, volume or assign entry has a short standard BCPL BSTR without an extra NUL terminator. A checkout-wide `AddDosEntry()` caller census found no selected in-tree producer of a valid non-terminated BSTR. DOS assign helpers, filesystem volume constructors (AFS, CDVDFS, PFS3, SFS, RAM, CDFS, SMBFS and hosted emulation), and the Workbench Mount path use `MakeDosEntry()` or create an explicitly terminated/padded name; `MakeDosEntry()` allocates a trailing NUL (`rom/dos/makedosentry.c:55-81`), and the standard Mount parser's non-fast BSTR allocation is cleared and reserves padding after the copied payload (`workbench/c/Mount.c:231-238,1508-1519`). FAT and NTFS copy `name[0]+2` bytes into the standard BSTR (`rom/filesys/fat/volume.c:1044-1056`; `workbench/fs/ntfs/disk.c:219-230`); SMBFS rename writes its trailing NUL explicitly (`workbench/network/smbfs/source_code/main.c:5607-5625`). PTP's `c2bstr()` does not write a terminator, but its DOS-list allocation comes from a cleared pool (`rom/usb/classes/ptp/ptp.class.c:561-582,4191-4192,4247-4251`). `AddBootNode()` and `CliInit()` reuse supplied DeviceNodes; their checked Workbench creation path is terminated/padded, but arbitrary external BootNodes remain outside the census. The public `AddDosEntry()` contract accepts a caller-supplied DosList and does not require C termination, so an external producer can still pass a valid short BCPL name without an extra NUL. **Consequence:** source overread and possible garbage in the displayed name; a fault depends on allocation/page boundaries. **Confidence:** high for the representation mismatch and unbounded copy under the stated valid BSTR input; current in-tree trigger reachability is unconfirmed. No DOS list, volume, MUI object or runtime operation was used; source-only.


<a id="gd10455"></a>
## GD10455 — HostGL continues after its X11 display connection fails

`HostGL_Ctx_Manager_Init()` stores the result of `XOpenDisplay(NULL)` in `global_x11_display` but does not test it and returns success unconditionally (`arch/all-hosted/libs/hostgl/hostgl_ctx_manager.c:95-101`). Its init hook runs after the priority-0 X11/GLX host-library hooks (`:112-114`; `x11_hostlib.c:101-102`; `glx_hostlib.c:148-149`), so this concerns failure to connect to the X server, not failure to load the host libraries. On a later `glACreateContext()`, the selected implementation reads the display pointer and calls `DefaultScreen(dsp)` without a null check (`hostgl_glacreatecontext.c:155-162`); the Xlib macro expands to a `dpy` field dereference (`/usr/include/X11/Xlib.h:89` in the review environment). Thus a failed display open is converted into a null dereference instead of the documented NULL context-creation result (`hostgl_glacreatecontext.c:91-94`). This is separate from GD10445, which covers the independent unchecked TLS allocation results in the same manager.

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional hosted X11 `hostgl` library is loaded while its X11 connection cannot be opened, and a client then calls `glACreateContext()`. The library reports successful initialization; context creation dereferences the null display pointer and can fault the calling task. **Affected configuration:** explicit `hosted-libs-hostgl` builds and clients using its GLA API; the parent aggregate dependency is optional/commented (`arch/all-hosted/libs/hostgl/mmakefile.src:9-13,20-36,54-55`). No in-tree HostGL client was established in this pass. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked failed result and the subsequent source-level dereference; occurrence requires the host display connection to fail and a context call. Check the display result during initialization, fail the init hook, or reject context creation before using the display. No host display, context, build or runtime call was used; source-only. See the [HostGL TLS and display-init caller recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hostgl-display-initialization-failure-pass-gd10455).


<a id="gd10456"></a>
## GD10456 — HostGL context-allocation failure dereferences the null context during cleanup

`glACreateContext()` initializes `ctx` to NULL, checks the initial `AllocVec()` result, and jumps to `error_out` on failure (`arch/all-hosted/libs/hostgl/hostgl_glacreatecontext.c:103-108,127-131`). The cleanup then unconditionally reads `ctx->HiddX11BitMapAB` and `ctx->framebuffer` before reaching the later `if (ctx) HostGLFreeContext(ctx)` guard (`:233-249`). Thus failure of the first context allocation dereferences NULL rather than returning the documented NULL result (`:91-94`). The X11-window and buffer cleanup branches already guard `ctx`, confirming that the common cleanup path is intended to handle absent context storage. This is distinct from GD10445's unchecked TLS allocations and GD10455's failed X11 display connection.

**Trigger and consequence:** a caller invokes `glACreateContext()` in the optional HostGL library and the first `AllocVec(sizeof(struct hostgl_context), ...)` fails. Error cleanup dereferences the NULL `ctx` pointer and can fault the caller instead of reporting context-creation failure. **Affected configuration:** explicit `hosted-libs-hostgl` builds and clients using its GLA API (`arch/all-hosted/libs/hostgl/mmakefile.src:20-36,54-55`); the parent aggregate dependency is optional/commented (`:9-13`). No in-tree HostGL client was established in this pass. **Confidence:** high for the allocation check, unconditional cleanup dereferences, and API's documented NULL failure result; occurrence requires allocation failure. Guard all `ctx` field cleanup behind a non-NULL check before returning NULL. No allocation failure, context, host display, or build was used; source-only. See the [HostGL context allocation cleanup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hostgl-context-allocation-failure-cleanup-pass-gd10456).


<a id="gd10458"></a>
## GD10458 — HostGL debug logging dereferences a NULL context while unbinding

`glAMakeCurrent()` documents an optional context pointer through its explicit `if (ctx)` / `else` detach behavior (`arch/all-hosted/libs/hostgl/hostgl_glamakecurrent.c:43-62`). Before that branch, however, its `D()` diagnostic evaluates `((struct hostgl_context *)ctx)->glXctx` (`:39-41`). In a build where `D()` expands its argument, calling the supported NULL detach path dereferences NULL before clearing the current context. The selected EGL backend calls `glAMakeCurrent(NULL)` when unbinding a context and when destroying one (`workbench/libs/egl/egl_arosmesa.c:76-85,129-137`), and that EGL target is explicitly compiled with `NDEBUG` but does not disable HostGL's separate debug macro (`workbench/libs/egl/mmakefile.src:33-38`). HostGL's target has a commented `-DDEBUG=1` build option (`arch/all-hosted/libs/hostgl/mmakefile.src:50-52`), showing the diagnostic-enabled configuration. **Affected configuration and trigger:** optional hosted HostGL built with its debug logging enabled, with the EGL backend or another client making a documented NULL detach call. **Consequence:** the context is not detached and the caller faults in the debug build. **Confidence:** high for the source-level dereference and checked-in EGL calls; restricted to debug-enabled HostGL configurations. Guard the context field in the diagnostic or log the raw pointer before entering the NULL-aware branch. No context, build, or runtime operation was used; source-only; see the [HostGL make-current review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hostgl-make-current-and-destruction-pass-gd10458).


<a id="gd10457"></a>
## GD10457 — HostGL exposes a context after framebuffer-buffer allocation fails

The selected HostGL renderer defines `RENDERER_BUFFER` and uses the pbuffer path when no X11 visual is available (`arch/all-hosted/libs/hostgl/hostgl_renderer_config.h:8-9`; `hostgl_glacreatecontext.c:181-189`). `HostGL_AllocateBuffer()` creates a pbuffer, then allocates the pixel and scanline buffers without checking either result (`hostgl_funcs.c:117-140`). Its caller does not receive a status; `glACreateContext()` continues to create the GLX context and reports success based only on `ctx->glXctx` (`hostgl_glacreatecontext.c:213-231`). `glASwapBuffers()` then passes `swapbuffer` to `glReadPixels()`, uses `swapbuffer`/`swapbufferline` in `CopyMem()`, and passes `swapbuffer` to `WritePixelArray()` without checking them (`hostgl_glaswapbuffers.c:75-125`). The same `HostGL_AllocateBuffer()` is used by `HostGL_ResizeBuffer()` after it frees the prior buffer/pbuffer (`hostgl_funcs.c:144-173,176-205`), and that resize path also ignores allocation failure.

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional HostGL renderer uses its pbuffer path for a positive-size context, either during creation or after resize, and allocation of the pixel buffer or scanline buffer fails. The context can still be returned as successful; a later `glASwapBuffers()` uses a NULL buffer for GL output, `CopyMem()`, or display output, so rendering can fault or fail. **Affected configuration:** explicit `hosted-libs-hostgl` builds using the selected `RENDERER_BUFFER` configuration, when no visual is available and the pbuffer fallback is selected; the GLA context and swap methods are exposed through the target's public vectors. No in-tree HostGL client was established in this pass. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocations, success publication, and unchecked swap-buffer use; occurrence requires allocation failure or resize-buffer allocation failure. Propagate buffer setup failure and reject/tear down the context or resize before publishing it. No allocation failure, context, display, rendering operation, or build was used; source-only. See the [HostGL buffer-allocation and swap pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hostgl-buffer-allocation-and-swap-pass-gd10457).

<a id="gd10459"></a>
## GD10459 — Sound datatype indexes sample-format tables with an unchecked public value

The public Sound datatype extension defines exactly four sample-type values, `SDTST_M8S` through `SDTST_S16S` (0–3) (`compiler/include/datatypes/soundclassext.h:16-23`). `parsetaglist()` stores any `SDTA_SampleType` tag directly into the instance's `UBYTE SampleType` field and reports the tag as handled without validating that it is in this range (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:1024-1027`; `classbase.h:66`). The AHI worker indexes the four-entry `sdtst2ahist` table with that field when starting playback (`dispatch.c:3595,3972`); the same file also indexes the four-entry `bytesPerPoint` table with `SampleType` in playback and write paths (`:204,2409,2423,2457,3697,3987-3998`).

**Trigger:** a Sound datatype client sets `SDTA_SampleType` to a value from 4 through 255 and reaches one of the table-indexing paths. On AROS, `GetSoundDTPrefs()` enables AHI by default (`dispatch.c:569-573`), `Sound_NEW()` selects `PlayerProcAHI` when that setting is active (`:871-874`), and `Sound_TRIGGER(STM_PLAY)` sends the request to that worker (`:2253-2284`). If the AHI library/device and audio allocation succeed, playback reads beyond `sdtst2ahist`; continuous playback and sample write paths also read beyond `bytesPerPoint`. No checked-in caller supplying an out-of-range value was found; the trigger is through the public attribute contract.

**Consequence:** the worker consumes an out-of-bounds byte as the AHI sample format. The exported `DTM_WRITE`/`DTM_COPY` methods also reach `Sound_WRITE()` (`dispatch.c:340-342,2653-2707`): AIFF output indexes `bytesPerPoint` when sizing the sample write, while SVX output does so when writing a selected range (`:2409,2423,2457`). These paths can use an incorrect byte count or format and read beyond the supplied sample buffer. Reject values outside 0–3 before storing the attribute, and keep a defensive bounds check at table use sites.

**Affected configuration and confidence:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatypes-sound` target (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/mmakefile.src:1-13`), when a client supplies an invalid public value and reaches playback/write processing; AHI playback additionally requires the selected AHI path to open and allocate audio successfully. High confidence in the unchecked store and fixed-size table indexing; no maintained invalid-value caller or runtime failure was established. No datatype object, AHI operation, malformed attribute, or build was exercised; source-only. See the [Sound datatype sample-format review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-sample-format-bound-pass-gd10459).


<a id="gd10460"></a>
## GD10460 — Sound datatype shifts by an unchecked signal-bit number

`parsetaglist()` accepts `SDTA_SignalBitNumber` and assigns its `IPTR` value directly to the signed-byte `InstanceData.SignalBit` field, with no check that it names one of the 32 Exec signal bits (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:1100-1102`; `classbase.h:64`). The value is later used as the shift count in `Sound_GET()` when returning `SDTA_SignalBitMask` (`dispatch.c:1189-1191`) and in the playback worker's completion/continuous notifications (`:3301-3302,3419-3420,4103-4104`). For example, setting bit number 32 reaches `1L << 32`. `ULONG` signal masks remain 32-bit on both 32- and 64-bit AROS (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:34-39`), but C `long` width follows the target ABI: on 32-bit targets this count is outside the shift type's width and has undefined behavior; on 64-bit targets the shift is representable but truncates to a zero `ULONG` when passed to `Signal()`, so the requested notification is lost. Values that narrow to negative signed-byte values other than the -1 sentinel produce invalid negative shift counts. On 32-bit targets even the valid bit number 31 uses signed `1L << 31`, whose result is not representable and is undefined by C.

**Trigger and consequence:** a client supplies an out-of-range `SDTA_SignalBitNumber`, then requests the mask attribute or starts a playback path that signals the configured task. The getter or worker forms a mask outside the 32-bit signal range. Depending on target ABI, this is an undefined shift or truncates to an empty signal mask; bit 31 also has signed-shift undefined behavior on 32-bit targets. The public numeric attribute is declared in `compiler/include/datatypes/soundclass.h:46`; no checked-in invalid-value caller was found. The in-tree `Play` command uses the valid `SIGB_SINGLE` value (`workbench/c/Play.c:81-85`). **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatypes-sound` target (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/mmakefile.src:1-13`), for public clients that set an invalid bit number; playback notification also requires a configured `SignalTask` and a completion/continuous notification path. The failure mode differs between 32- and 64-bit C `long` ABIs as described above. **Confidence:** high that the unchecked assignment and invalid shift are present; reachability requires an invalid public attribute value. Validate 0–31 (or the documented unset sentinel) before storing and guard the shift sites. No object, signal, playback, or build was run; source-only. See the [Sound datatype signal-bit range pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-signal-bit-range-pass-gd10460).


<a id="gd10461"></a>
## GD10461 — Long sound samples overflow the waveform scaling guard

`DrawWaveform()` copies the public `ULONG SampleLength` into signed `LONG samplelength`, then evaluates `samplelength << 8` in its width guard (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:1678-1687`). The comment describes a 25500% scaling limit, but for a valid positive sample length greater than 8,388,607 frames, shifting the signed value left by eight cannot be represented in AROS's signed 32-bit `LONG`; the C operation has undefined behavior on all AROS targets. A common two's-complement result is a negative guard operand, causing any positive drawing width to satisfy `w > (samplelength << 8)` and the function to return without rendering, but the exact result is compiler-dependent. The checked sound-class instance stores the length as `ULONG` (`classbase.h:58-60`), and the public `SDTA_SampleLength` setter accepts the tag value without narrowing (`dispatch.c:967-969`). A checked-in producer reaches this range: the selected 8SVX reader adds the two ULONG VHDR sample counts, requires the resulting size not exceed the BODY chunk, allocates and reads that many bytes, then supplies both the sample pointer and length to the Sound datatype (`workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/8svxclass.c:177-202`). No 8,388,607-frame limit is applied.

**Trigger and consequence:** a valid uncompressed 8SVX BODY contains more than 8,388,607 sample frames, allocation succeeds, and the Sound datatype receives a positive-width `GM_RENDER` or `DTM_DRAW`. The scaling check has signed-overflow undefined behavior and may suppress the waveform or vary with compiler behavior. This is distinct from GD6199, which covers small `DTM_DRAW` rectangles narrowed to `UWORD` and dimensions underflowing before this guard. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatypes-sound` target (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/mmakefile.src:1-13`); the threshold is about 8 MiB for 8-bit mono audio or 16 MiB for 16-bit mono audio, so the frame count is representable and not inherently exceptional. **Confidence:** high in the signed-width mismatch and overflow; the exact post-overflow guard result depends on compiler behavior. Compare width in a wider unsigned type or use division-based checked arithmetic. No long sample was loaded or drawn, and no build was run; source-only. See the [Sound datatype long-sample waveform pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-long-sample-waveform-pass-gd10461).


<a id="gd10462"></a>
<a id="gd10462-hyperlayers-omits-resize-backfill-strips-when-rectangle-union-fails"></a>
## GD10462 — Hyperlayers omits resize backfill strips when rectangle union fails

`MoveSizeLayer()` builds the region of newly exposed pixels from `rectw` and `recth` after a layer grows (`rom/hyperlayers/movesizelayer.c:402-411`). It clears the temporary region, calls `OrRectRegion()` for each positive dimension, ignores both Boolean results, then passes the resulting region to `_BackFillRegion()` and ultimately returns TRUE (`:433-439`). `OrRectRegion()` documents FALSE on allocation failure; for an existing destination it constructs a temporary result and only replaces the original after success, so a failed second union leaves the first strip as the destination (`rom/graphics/orrectregion.c:21-38,64-101`). `_BackFillRegion()` immediately returns for an empty region and otherwise invokes the layer backfill hook once per rectangle (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:1252-1268,1333-1361`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a layer is enlarged in both width and height, the first strip is added, and allocation for the second union fails. Only the first strip is backfilled; the other newly exposed strip is omitted while the layer resize continues and reports success. If the first union fails but a later union succeeds, the same omission applies to the failed strip. A client can observe incomplete background/backfill for that resize operation. The selected Intuition `DoMoveSizeWindow()` calls `MoveSizeLayer()` for window size changes without temporarily replacing the hook (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_actions.c:434-468,512-529`); the separate `smartresize()` path does suppress both hooks while changing size and is not claimed as a trigger (`rom/intuition/windowclasses.c:1002-1030`). Ordinary `OpenWindow()` defaults its backfill to `LAYERS_BACKFILL` and passes that value into layer creation (`rom/intuition/openwindow.c:100,1411-1415`); Hyperlayers interprets this sentinel as a `BltBitMap()` clear (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:110-140`). Thus the omitted strip misses the default clear even without a custom hook, although a later application redraw may repair it. **Affected configuration:** `kernel-layers` clients enlarging a layer with an active backfill hook, including ordinary selected Intuition windows using the default backfill. **Confidence:** high that failed union results are ignored and the omitted strip is not passed to the backfill/clear operation; persistence depends on later client redraw. Check both `OrRectRegion()` results and abort or preserve enough state to retry the missing backfill. No allocation failure, resize, or hook call was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#movesizelayer-growth-backfill-union-result-recheck).


<a id="gd10463"></a>
<a id="gd10463-changelayershape-installs-an-empty-layer-bound-when-rectangle-allocation-fails"></a>
## GD10463 — ChangeLayerShape installs an empty layer bound when rectangle allocation fails

`ChangeLayerShape()` disposes the current outer `l->shape`, allocates a replacement `Region`, and, when that allocation succeeds, adds the layer-bounds rectangle with `OrRectRegion()` (`rom/hyperlayers/changelayershape.c:128-141`). It ignores the Boolean result; the source comment explicitly leaves error handling as a FIXME. `OrRectRegion()` can return FALSE when it cannot allocate the region rectangle and leaves an initially empty destination empty (`rom/graphics/orrectregion.c:21-38,64-101`). The function then continues using the empty `l->shape`: its custom-shape intersection with the empty bound has no pixels, and `SetRegion(l->shape, l->visibleshape)` clears the derived visible shape (`changelayershape.c:143-151`; `rom/graphics/andregionregion.c:54-57`; `rom/graphics/setregion.c:25-39`). Unlike GD6179, this case has a valid Region object; the failure is the separate rectangle-node allocation.

The selected Intuition `ChangeWindowShape()` route calls `ChangeLayerShape()` under the screen refresh lock, stores its return value, and then calls `CheckLayers()` (`rom/intuition/changewindowshape.c:92-109`). Thus the shape-update path can publish/recalculate the now-empty layer bound after the rectangle insertion failed. Hyperlayers `ScaleLayer()` is another caller (`rom/hyperlayers/scalelayer.c:78-85`). **Trigger and consequence:** a shape change reaches this code, `NewRegion()` succeeds, and the following `OrRectRegion()` fails. The old outer shape has already been disposed; the replacement and derived visible shape remain empty for the layer check, so the shape update can remove the layer's visible/clipped area instead of retaining its rectangular bound. **Affected configuration:** `kernel-layers` shape changes through Intuition or `ScaleLayer()` during region-rectangle allocation failure. **Confidence:** high that the bounds-union failure is ignored and the empty destination flows into visible-shape construction; the extent of the rendered effect depends on subsequent layer redraw and recovery. Check the union result and preserve the old shape or unwind the operation. No shape change or allocation failure was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#changelayershape-outer-bound-union-failure-recheck).


<a id="gd10464"></a>
<a id="gd10464-hyperlayers-can-omit-exposed-simple-refresh-areas-after-damage-insertion-fails"></a>
## GD10464 — Hyperlayers can omit exposed simple-refresh areas after damage insertion fails

`_CopyClipRectsToClipRects()` ignores `OrRectRegion()` failures at both simple-refresh damage insertion sites (`rom/hyperlayers/basicfuncs.c:572-585,775-790`). `_BackFillRegion()` also sets `LAYERREFRESH` and ignores `OrRegionRegion(r, l->DamageList)` when `addtodamagelist` is true (`basicfuncs.c:1278-1287`). In backup mode, the first site adds the intersection to `DamageList` when an old clip rectangle was hidden. In the visible-area path, the second site calls the layer backfill hook and then adds the newly exposed rectangle to `DamageList`; a successful hook call does not itself perform the client redraw represented by the refresh list. `OrRectRegion()` returns FALSE on allocation failure and leaves its destination unchanged (`rom/graphics/orrectregion.c:64-101`). After the clip-copy loop, `_CopyClipRectsToClipRects()` derives `LAYERREFRESH` from whether `DamageList` is empty (`basicfuncs.c:952-960`). `BeginUpdate()` constructs refresh clipping from `DamageList` (`rom/hyperlayers/beginupdate.c:67-100`), so a failed insertion can leave the newly exposed area outside the client refresh. The selected `_BackupPartsOfLayer()` caller uses the backup-mode insertion during layer geometry changes (`basicfuncs.c:1018-1070`); `_ShowPartsOfLayer()` uses the visible-area insertion when revealing content (`:1078-1138`), with callers in visibility, shape, movement/resize, deletion and z-order operations.

**Trigger and consequence:** a simple-refresh layer enters one of these insertion paths and allocation for its rectangle or region union fails. The affected area is absent from `DamageList`; if no other damage remains, `LAYERREFRESH` is cleared, otherwise the client receives a refresh that still omits this area. During reveal, the backfill hook runs before the failed insertion, but the application redraw region is still lost. **Affected configuration:** `kernel-layers` simple-refresh layers undergoing operations that back up or reveal clip rectangles. **Confidence:** high for ignored failures and DamageList-driven refresh selection; visible stale content depends on the affected area requiring client redraw and not being repaired by later damage. Check all three insertion results and retain/retry the area on failure. This is separate from GD10096's Intuition resize-specific insertions. No allocation failure, layer transition, or refresh was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hyperlayers-damage-insertion-failure-recheck).

<a id="gd10465"></a>
<a id="gd10465-boingiconbar-can-leave-its-static-toolbar-hidden-after-window-creation-fails"></a>
## GD10465 — BoingIconBar can leave its static toolbar hidden after window creation fails

Both static-mode startup and Workbench screen restoration call `OpenMainWindow()` without checking its Boolean result (`workbench/tools/BoingIconBar/iconbar.c:488-493,1885-1892`). `OpenMainWindow()` returns FALSE when `OpenWindowTags()` fails and sets `Window_Open` only on success (`:1541-1570`). In the no-window main-loop path, the only retry is through `CheckMousePosition()` (`:603-638`), which calls `OpenMainWindow()` only when the pointer is within the bottom eight screen pixels and horizontal toolbar range (`:1590-1604`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional BoingIconBar target runs with `STATIC` enabled and a static startup or screen-restore `OpenMainWindow()` attempt fails while the pointer is outside that activation strip. The caller discards the failure; the toolbar remains closed and the idle loop does not retry until the pointer enters the strip. This can leave a configured static toolbar absent after startup or a Workbench screen reset. **Confidence:** high for the ignored result and conditional retry; no window-open failure or screen reset was induced. Source-only.

<a id="gd10466-v3d-can-keep-a-framebuffer-page-as-its-render-target-after-scanout-detach-allocation-fails"></a>
<a id="gd10466"></a>
## GD10466 — Failed scanout detach leaves the Gallium render target on a framebuffer page

`v3d_scan_unbind()` tries to allocate a private BO for the resource. It replaces `rsc->bo` only if allocation succeeds, but calls `v3d_scan_release()` regardless (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/v3d/v3d_galliumclass.c:277-291`). The caller invokes it after the exit-frame blit when leaving scanout (`:1117-1121`). If allocation fails, the resource retains its reference to the scanout BO while the global scanout record is cleared. Later presentation computes `bound` from that record and BO handle (`:707-708`), so it no longer recognizes the retained framebuffer-backed resource as scanout-bound. If overlay setup is unavailable or refuses the windowed target, subsequent rendering/blit handling continues with that framebuffer BO rather than a private render-target BO.

**Trigger and consequence:** an active V3D scanout resource leaves scanout and the `scanout-exit` BO allocation fails. The driver forgets the binding but leaves the resource attached to the framebuffer page; later rendering can modify a display page through the ordinary windowed path, contrary to the helper's stated detach invariant. Visible damage depends on whether that page is displayed or reused by the framebuffer path. **Affected configuration:** optional Raspberry Pi 3/4 AArch64 V3D Gallium HIDD (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/v3d/mmakefile.src`); its parent aggregate edge is commented, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high that failed allocation preserves the framebuffer BO while scanout state is cleared; the resulting visible corruption depends on subsequent render/presentation state. Preserve/retry the detach state or prevent reuse of the framebuffer BO after allocation failure. No allocation failure, display, GPU operation, or build was exercised; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-scanout-detach-allocation-failure-gd10466).

<a id="gd10467"></a>
<a id="gd10467-v3d-can-present-a-frame-discarded-by-timeout-recovery"></a>
## GD10467 — V3D can present a frame discarded by timeout recovery

`v3d_wait_for()` returns FALSE after a GPU timeout and calls `v3d_recover()` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/v3d/v3d_hw.c:610-615`). Recovery clears the running/queued job state and advances `finished_seqno` to the current `seqno` without replaying those jobs (`:561-569,582-584`). The sequence wrapper discards the wait result and returns no status (`:767-775`). In the overlay path, `DisplayResourceRP()` then unconditionally calls `v3d_show_overlay()` for the queued BO after `v3d_hw_wait_seqno()` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/v3d/v3d_galliumclass.c:888-896`); success rotates that BO into the on-plane state (`:949-956`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an overlay frame's queued render job does not complete before the GPU wait timeout. Recovery abandons the job, but the caller proceeds as though the queued frame had retired. The driver can therefore display and retain an incomplete or stale frame as the newly presented image. **Affected configuration:** optional Raspberry Pi 3/4 AArch64 V3D Gallium HIDD; the target's aggregate build edge is commented, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high that timeout recovery discards queued work and the wrapper suppresses the failure; medium that a given timed-out buffer contains visibly incomplete pixels. Return completion status and keep the previous displayed frame when the wait fails. No GPU timeout, recovery, display or build was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-wait-recovery-overlay-result-gd10467).


<a id="gd10468"></a>
<a id="gd10468-v3d-job-state-is-not-serialized-against-interrupts-in-execsmp"></a>
## GD10468 — V3D job state is not serialized against interrupts in ExecSMP

`v3d_service()` protects its state updates only with `Disable()/Enable()` and explicitly notes that this is sufficient on UP but requires a spinlock for SMP (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/v3d/v3d_hw.c:370-377`). The routine mutates the binner/render running flags, completion sequence numbers, overflow state, and the RCL queue (`:386-479`). It is called from the completion IRQ handler (`:487-495`) and from task-side submit/wait paths (`:593-607,662-739`). Those task paths hold `job_lock`, but the IRQ handler does not take it; `Disable()` only disables interrupts on the calling CPU in ExecSMP (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-60`). The selected driver registers GIC SPI 74 (`v3d_intern.h:195`). BCM2711 targets shared SPIs to CPU 0 (`arch/aarch64-native/kernel/platform_bcm2711.c:87-107`), while AArch64 SMP scheduling accepts tasks with no assigned affinity on any CPU (`kernel_scheduler.c:38-49`). The RasPi `smp` configure variant defines `__AROSEXEC_SMP__` (`configure:11356-11360`). Thus a task-side service call on a nonzero CPU can overlap the device IRQ handler on CPU 0; the handler does not acquire the task's `job_lock`.

**Trigger and consequence:** explicitly build the optional V3D HIDD for `raspi-aarch64` with variant `smp`, then use the driver while a submitting/waiting task is scheduled on a nonzero CPU as the V3D completion IRQ is dispatched on CPU 0. Both service invocations can consume the same completion status or RCL queue entry, update the queue head/count and render-running state, or access waiter fields concurrently. This can issue a duplicate or lost render transition, leave a queued frame unprocessed, or lose/wrongly deliver a waiter signal. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `hidd-v3d` with `raspi-aarch64` and variant `smp`; the module rule exists at `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/v3d/mmakefile.src:251-254`, while the aggregate dependency is commented at `:11,249`, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. The default UP variant is excluded. **Confidence:** high that the shared state has no cross-CPU serialization and that SPI delivery is targeted at CPU 0 in this configuration; the actual interleaving and visible rendering symptom remain conditional. Protect the service state with an IRQ-safe cross-CPU lock or defer IRQ work to a serialized context. No interrupt, interleaving, GPU operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-hardware-service-full-body-smp-race-gd10468).


<a id="gd10469"></a>
<a id="gd10469-changelayershape-ignores-custom-shape-intersection-failure"></a>
## GD10469 — ChangeLayerShape ignores custom-shape intersection failure

After constructing the layer's rectangular bound, `ChangeLayerShape()` intersects `l->shaperegion` into `l->shape` with `AndRegionRegion()` and ignores the result (`rom/hyperlayers/changelayershape.c:134-146`). `AndRegionRegion()` calculates into a temporary region; on allocation failure it returns FALSE before clearing or replacing its destination (`rom/graphics/andregionregion.c:57-87`). Therefore, when the requested custom shape is non-NULL and the Boolean operation needs region-rectangle allocation that fails, `l->shape` remains the full rectangular bound instead of the requested intersection. The function translates and installs this broader region and derives `visibleshape` from it (`changelayershape.c:143-149`).

The selected Intuition `ChangeWindowShape()` caller continues to `CheckLayers()` after the operation (`rom/intuition/changewindowshape.c:92-109`), so the incorrect bound is used in layer visibility/clipping calculations. **Trigger and consequence:** a custom-shape update reaches this path and intersection-region allocation fails; the layer can remain visible/clipped to its full rectangle outside the requested shape, causing incorrect layer exposure or drawing until a later successful shape update. **Affected configuration:** `kernel-layers` callers that change a layer to a non-NULL custom shape, including Intuition's selected window-shape path, during region Boolean allocation failure. **Confidence:** high that the failed operation preserves the rectangular destination and the caller proceeds; exact visual symptoms depend on subsequent drawing and layer changes. Check the Boolean result and unwind or retain the prior installed shape on failure. This is distinct from GD10463, where insertion of the rectangular bound itself fails and leaves an empty shape. No allocation failure or shape update was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#changelayershape-custom-intersection-failure-recheck).


<a id="gd10470"></a>
<a id="gd10470-palette-preferences-cannot-restore-very-large-color-maps-through-loadrgb4"></a>
## GD10470 — Palette Preferences cannot restore very large color maps through LoadRGB4

Palette Preferences snapshots the active screen's `ColorMap->Count` in unsigned `data->count`, allocates that many saved entries, and sets `restore = TRUE` (`workbench/prefs/palette/paleditor.c:376-388`). During cleanup it passes the full count to `LoadRGB4()` (`:402-412`). `ColorMap->Count` is `UWORD` (`compiler/include/graphics/view.h:148-153`), but the `LoadRGB4()` vector takes signed `WORD count` and immediately returns for `count <= 0` (`rom/graphics/loadrgb4.c:14-20,64-65`). `GetColorMap(ULONG entries)` can construct a map with 32,768 entries and stores that count in the `UWORD` field; its documentation says the result may be stored in a viewport (`rom/graphics/getcolormap.c:14-29,59-69`). OpenScreen does not provide this trigger through `SA_ColorMapEntries`: its local `numcolors` is signed `WORD` (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:174`), so on the affected 16-bit two's-complement targets the value 32,768 narrows to -32,768 before the call and the `numcolors < 32 ? 32 : numcolors` expression creates a 32-entry map instead (`:685-688,1393-1406`). The supported external producer is therefore a client that obtains a 32,768-entry map through `GetColorMap()` and installs it in a viewport. Palette Preferences can be directed to a public screen and selects it when its bitmap depth exceeds four (`workbench/prefs/palette/main.c:50-73,105-112`); no checked-in producer of such an installed map was found.

**Trigger and consequence:** on a target where conversion of UWORD 32768 to signed WORD yields -32768, run Palette Preferences on a public screen with a 32,768-entry `ColorMap` created through `GetColorMap()`, allow its snapshot allocation to succeed, change palette colors, and close/clean up the editor. `LoadRGB4()` receives a nonpositive count and returns without restoring the snapshot, so the screen retains the edited palette. This is not reachable by requesting 32,768 through `SA_ColorMapEntries`, because OpenScreen narrows that tag to signed `WORD` and creates a 32-entry map on those targets. **Affected configuration:** Palette Preferences explicitly directed to a depth-greater-than-four public screen whose client-installed `ColorMap` has more than `WORD_MAX` entries, on targets with the usual 16-bit two's-complement signed conversion. No in-tree producer of such a map was identified. **Confidence:** high for the unsigned-to-signed narrowing and early return on those targets; medium for practical reachability because the required map must be supplied and installed by a client. Use a count type able to represent `ColorMap->Count` or restore in bounded chunks. This is separate from GD5910's pixel-table bounds issue for positive counts above 256. No screen, preference editor, or color-map update was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#palette-preferences-large-colormap-restore-recheck).

<a id="gd10472"></a>
<a id="gd10472-openscreen-reduces-large-sa_colormapentries-requests-to-32-entries"></a>
## GD10472 — OpenScreen reduces large `SA_ColorMapEntries` requests to 32 entries

`OpenScreen()` stores the `SA_ColorMapEntries` tag value in local `WORD numcolors` (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:174,685-688`). On the selected 16-bit two's-complement targets, requesting 32,768 entries converts to -32,768. The defaulting check (`if (!numcolors)`) does not run, and the later minimum expression treats the negative value as less than 32, so `GetColorMap()` is called with 32 (`:1393-1406`). The call succeeds and installs a 32-entry map rather than rejecting the unsupported request or providing the requested size. The public tag documentation describes the value as the number of ColorMap entries and states a default, but no maximum (`rom/intuition/openscreentaglist.c:208-211`). `GetColorMap()` accepts an `ULONG`, stores `entries` in a `UWORD` count, and documents that the returned map may be stored in a viewport (`rom/graphics/getcolormap.c:14-29,59-69`), so 32,768 is representable by the ColorMap API.

**Trigger and consequence:** an external client opens a screen with `SA_ColorMapEntries` set to 32,768 on an affected target. The screen opens with only 32 ColorMap entries, so the caller's requested palette capacity is silently lost. An exact repository-wide C/C++/header search found no checked-in caller of `SA_ColorMapEntries`, so this remains an exported-API candidate with no maintained in-tree trigger. **Affected configuration:** selected Intuition builds on targets with 16-bit signed `WORD` conversion behavior; the same narrowing affects requests above `WORD_MAX` that convert to negative values. **Confidence:** high for the narrowing and resulting 32-entry map; medium for the exact intended upper bound because the tag documentation states no maximum and no in-tree caller demonstrates the expected range, though the adjacent public ColorMap API accepts an unsigned count through 65,535. Keep the request in an unsigned type through validation and reject values above the representable `ColorMap->Count` range before allocation. This is distinct from GD10470, which concerns restoration through the signed `LoadRGB4()` count when a large map is already installed. No screen was opened and no map allocation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#openscreen-large-colormap-tag-narrowing-gd10472).


<a id="gd10471--vulkan-hpp-dynamic-dispatch-loses-the-ext-fallback-for-vkcmdendrendering2khr"></a>
<a id="gd10471"></a>
## GD10471 — Vulkan-Hpp dynamic dispatch loses the EXT fallback for `vkCmdEndRendering2KHR`

The generated dynamic-dispatch initializers copy EXT pointers into KHR slots when the KHR slot is empty, but later perform a separate KHR-name lookup and assign its result unconditionally. This erases a valid EXT fallback when the KHR lookup returns null. The affected commands are `vkGetPhysicalDeviceCalibrateableTimeDomainsKHR` (RAII `InstanceDispatcher`: `vulkan_raii.hpp:293-296,386-387`; `DispatchLoaderDynamic::init(Instance)`: `vulkan.hpp:22316-22319,22990-22992`), `vkGetCalibratedTimestampsKHR` (RAII `DeviceDispatcher`: `vulkan_raii.hpp:1286-1288,1878-1879`; dynamic instance/device init: `vulkan.hpp:22320-22322,22992-22993,23675-23678,24268-24269`), `vkReleaseSwapchainImagesKHR` (RAII: `vulkan_raii.hpp:1472-1474,1833-1834`; dynamic instance/device init: `vulkan.hpp:22539-22541,22933,23861-23864,24223`), and `vkCmdEndRendering2KHR` (RAII: `vulkan_raii.hpp:1954-1963`; dynamic instance/device init: `vulkan.hpp:23084-23093,24344-24353`). The enhanced and RAII KHR wrappers accept either the EXT or KHR extension as availability, then dispatch through the KHR slot: calibrated time-domain query (`vulkan_raii.hpp:27463-27485`), calibrated timestamps (`:27497-27513`), swapchain image release (`:26949-26957`), and rendering end (`:28100-28106`; non-RAII wrappers in `vulkan_funcs.hpp:29144-29165,30507-30548,30594-30629,32222-32240`).

**Trigger and consequence:** initialize a dynamic dispatcher on an implementation that returns an EXT command pointer but null for its KHR name, then call the corresponding KHR-named wrapper: `getCalibrateableTimeDomainsKHR()`, `getCalibratedTimestampsKHR()`, `releaseSwapchainImagesKHR()`, or `endRendering2KHR()`. The Vulkan specification explicitly says alias function pointers must be retrieved separately and an alias pointer is available only when the extension/version that introduced that alias is supported and enabled; an EXT pointer with a null KHR lookup is therefore a supported case ([Vulkan specification, Command Function Pointers](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html#initialization-functionpointers)). The KHR slot is left null. Assertion-enabled enhanced/RAII builds stop at the wrapper assertion; with assertions disabled, or through raw overloads that do not check the slot, the wrapper calls through null and can fault. The EXT-named wrappers retain their separately loaded pointers. **Affected configuration:** clients of the bundled optional Vulkan-Hpp API using dynamic dispatch, including RAII, on implementations exposing an affected EXT command name without its KHR name. The optional `hidd-vulkan` target stages these headers through its `%copy_includes` rule (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/mmakefile.src:6-21`); no in-tree C++ Vulkan-Hpp caller was found, so affected use is downstream. No effect on the C Vulkan API is claimed. **Confidence:** high for each overwrite and wrapper use; occurrence depends on the implementation's proc-address results and client choosing the KHR wrapper. Preserve each fallback by applying it after the KHR lookup or only assigning the KHR slot when that lookup succeeds. No Vulkan call, build, or runtime reproduction was performed; source-only; see the [dynamic dispatch fallback review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-end-rendering2-dispatch-fallback-gd10471).

<a id="gd10473"></a>
<a id="gd10473-videocore-cursor-setup-leaks-firmware-memory-after-partial-allocation"></a>
## GD10473 — VideoCore cursor setup leaks firmware memory after partial allocation

`InitCursor()` asks the VideoCore firmware for a 64×64×4-byte cursor allocation and stores the returned handle in `vcsd_CurBufHandle` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/vcgfx_hiddclass.c:294-323`). It then returns `FALSE` if `LOCKMEM` fails (`:325-340`), or if the returned bus address lacks the GPU alias bits (`:342-354`), without issuing `FREEMEM` for the allocated handle; the latter branch also leaves the allocation locked. The adjacent offscreen bitmap setup explicitly releases its firmware allocation when its address validation fails (`vcgfx_offbitmap.c:99-132`), and the general GPU-memory free helper pairs unlock and free (`vcgfx_memory.c:163-187`). `vcgfx_init.c` ignores `InitCursor()`'s return value and continues driver initialization (`:154-160`), so this partial cursor failure does not enter the module-wide failed-init cleanup already covered by GD6256.

**Trigger and consequence:** firmware successfully returns an `ALLOCMEM` handle, then `LOCKMEM` fails or returns a bus address rejected by the alias check. The firmware retains the cursor allocation (16 KiB); repeated attempts can consume additional GPU memory. In the invalid-alias case the hardware cursor stays unavailable, as later methods return `FALSE` when `vcsd_CurBuf` is NULL (`vcgfx_hiddclass.c:386-393`). **Affected configuration:** Raspberry Pi builds selecting `vcgfx`, including the supported BCM283x and BCM2711 packages; the rejected bare-address case is specifically described for QEMU by the source comment. **Confidence:** high for the acquired handle, early returns, and absence of a matching release on these paths; occurrence depends on the stated firmware response. No firmware allocation or cursor setup was run; source-only; see the [cursor setup review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#videocore-cursor-setup-failed-lockmem-allocation-leak-gd10473).

<a id="gd10474"></a>

## GD10474 — Vulkan-Hpp RAII Context calls a missing loader entry point in no-exceptions builds

With the default `VULKAN_HPP_ENABLE_DYNAMIC_LOADER_TOOL=1`, the RAII default `Context()` obtains `vkGetInstanceProcAddr` from its private `DynamicLoader` and immediately constructs `ContextDispatcher` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_hpp_macros.hpp:86-88`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:3139-3140,3210-3212`). `DynamicLoader` throws when loading fails only when exceptions are enabled; under `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS`, it leaves the failed load unreported (`vulkan.hpp:20021-20024,20052-20080`). `getProcAddress()` does not check either the library handle or returned function pointer (`:20115-20123`). `ContextDispatcher` immediately invokes the supplied pointer to retrieve the global commands (`vulkan_raii.hpp:29-36`), and `Context` exposes neither the loader's `success()` status nor a no-exceptions error result (`:3173-3177,3208-3212`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a downstream client builds the bundled header with dynamic loading enabled and `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS`, no Vulkan loader library can be loaded, and `getProcAddress("vkGetInstanceProcAddr")` resolves to null. The RAII `Context` constructor then calls through that null pointer while constructing its dispatcher, before the client can inspect a status. The precise lookup result can depend on platform symbol lookup and other globally loaded libraries; this report does not claim every missing-library case necessarily returns null. With exceptions enabled, the loader failure instead throws from `DynamicLoader` construction. **Affected configuration:** downstream C++ users of the copied optional Vulkan-Hpp headers; no in-tree RAII Context client was found. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked null call path when lookup returns null; conditional on no-exceptions configuration and lookup result. Provide a checked Context initialization result or validate the loader/proc pointer before constructing the dispatcher. No Vulkan library failure, Context construction, build, or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only; see the [loader failure trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-raii-context-loader-failure-gd10474).

<a id="gd10475"></a>

## GD10475 — Vulkan-Hpp constructs a device dispatcher after failed device creation

`PhysicalDevice::createDevice()` declares a default `vk::Device`, calls `vkCreateDevice()`, and passes the result through `resultCheck()`; it then unconditionally constructs the RAII `Device` from that output handle (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:15255-15264`). The default `vk::Device` contains a null native handle (`vulkan_handles.hpp:18739`); if the failed call leaves its output untouched, the wrapper passes null to `Device(PhysicalDevice const &, VkDevice, ...)`, which stores the handle and constructs `DeviceDispatcher` (`vulkan_raii.hpp:4231-4235`). That dispatcher immediately calls the parent dispatcher's `vkGetDeviceProcAddr` with the supplied device for each command (`:709-730`). Under `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS`, `resultCheck()` uses `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT_ON_RESULT`; the default maps to `assert`, so in a build with `NDEBUG` the failed result does not stop construction (`vulkan_hpp_macros.hpp:75-80`; `vulkan.hpp:7551-7562`). The function then returns a `ResultValue<Device>` containing the error and the wrapper, instead of gating wrapper construction on success (`vulkan.hpp:7526-7545`).

**Trigger and consequence:** downstream code uses the copied RAII API with `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` and `NDEBUG`; `vkCreateDevice()` returns an error without writing a device handle. The wrapper continues and calls `vkGetDeviceProcAddr(VK_NULL_HANDLE, ...)` during dispatcher construction, even though no device was created. This violates the resolver's valid-device input contract; driver behavior on the invalid call is implementation-dependent. The caller cannot inspect the returned error until after this resolver sequence finishes. **Affected configuration:** downstream C++ users of the optional copied Vulkan-Hpp RAII API; no in-tree caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the unconditional dispatcher construction after a failed result and null output; the trigger depends on the API failure leaving the output untouched and on the assertion being disabled. Return the error result before constructing the RAII wrapper when creation fails. No Vulkan call, failed creation, build, or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only; see the [failed device-creation trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-raii-device-create-failure-gd10475).

<a id="gd10476"></a>

<a id="gd10476-sysexplorer-keeps-removed-hidd-objects-in-its-hardware-tree"></a>
## GD10476 — SysExplorer keeps removed HIDD objects in its hardware tree

SysExplorer's enumeration callbacks pass borrowed HIDD object pointers in `InsertObjectMsg`; the NListtree construct hook copies each pointer into persistent `ObjectUserData` without obtaining an object reference, and the destruct hook only frees that wrapper (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/sysexp_main.c:80-85,193-222`). The Storage and ATA module callbacks retain the same kind of controller pointer (`Modules/Storage/storage_enum.c:51-60,92-111`; `Modules/ATA/ata_enum.c:122-129`). The Gfx module also stores each display object: `gfxEnum()` obtains `aHidd_Gfx_DisplayList` or `aHidd_Gfx_DisplayDefault`, and `addGfxDisplay()` passes the borrowed display pointer through `InsertObjectMsg` (`Modules/Gfx/gfx_enum.c:56-82,85-109`). None of these tree rows is invalidated when its source object is removed.

For hardware-driver rows, `HW_EnumDrivers()` holds its shared list semaphore only during callbacks; `HW_RemoveDriver()` removes and disposes the object after releasing the exclusive-lock operation (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:276-295,353-375`). A concrete in-tree removal route is ATA `ata_expunge()` (`rom/devs/ata/ata_init.c:296-313`). After a cached ATA controller is removed, a later properties action passes the stale pointer to `GenericWindow`/`DevicePage`, whose constructor calls `OOP_GetAttr()` (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/sysexp_main.c:265-283`; `Modules/Storage/device_page_cl.c:47-60`). OOP attribute dispatch reads the object's class pointer (`rom/oop/getattr.c:57-72`; `rom/oop/include/oop.h:96-101`).

There is a separate graphics-display route through the same retained-pointer defect. `graphics_display.c::display_Expunge()` unlinks and disposes `display_obj` (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:221-253`). During driver setup, graphics.library supplies `driver_ExpungeBootDisplay()` as the handover callback to an incoming driver; a matching unused boot-mode display can therefore be expunged during hardware takeover (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:212-280,320-345`). SysExplorer's optional Gfx module stores that display object in a tree row, and a later double-click or Properties menu action passes it to `MonitorWindow__OM_NEW()`, which immediately calls `OOP_GetAttr(display_obj, aHidd_Name, ...)` (`workbench/tools/SysExplorer/sysexp_main.c:265-283,368-385`; `workbench/tools/SysExplorer/Modules/Gfx/gfxmonitor_window_cl.c:41-55`). The graphics path does not require ATA removal; it requires the Gfx module to have enumerated the boot display before a compatible driver takes it over while SysExplorer remains open.
