The `Native32` special case later overrides `BytesPerPixel` to four, but the four 32-bit formats without alpha (`0RGB32`, `BGR032`, `RGB032`, `0BGR32`) take the ordinary branch and do not receive that override. The selected standard-format definitions give these formats depth 24 and storage width four bytes (`rom/hidds/gfx/stdpixfmts_le.h:141-165`; corresponding big-endian definitions are in `stdpixfmts_be.h`). The SDL constructor itself uses `BytesPerPixel * 8` when creating an ordinary bitmap precisely to preserve this distinction (`sdlgfx_bitmapclass.c:93-110`).

The mismatch is reachable through the selected CyberGraphX pixel-array wrappers: `RECTFMT_0RGB32` and its sibling formats are documented as four bytes per pixel (`workbench/libs/cgfx/writepixelarray.c:106-117`); their mappings provide both four-byte `bppix` and the corresponding HIDD standard format (`gfxfuncsupport.c:37-43,56-75`). `WritePixelArray()` forwards that format and byte-row modulo to `HIDD_BM_PutImage()` (`writepixelarray.c:176-202`), and `ReadPixelArray()` does the same for `HIDD_BM_GetImage()` (`readpixelarray.c:135-166`). The SDL method instead constructs a 24-bit, three-byte-per-pixel temporary surface, so SDL reads or writes pixels at three-byte intervals while the caller's array stores them at four-byte intervals.

**Trigger and consequence:** use the optional hosted SDL HIDD for a display bitmap and call `WritePixelArray()` or `ReadPixelArray()` with `RECTFMT_0RGB32`, `RECTFMT_BGR032`, `RECTFMT_RGB032`, or `RECTFMT_0BGR32`. Writes sample misaligned component groups after the first pixel; reads return a packed three-byte sequence into rows that callers interpret as four-byte pixels, leaving padding bytes unstored and subsequent pixel components misaligned. Create the temporary surface with the pixel format's storage width, as the bitmap constructor does. **Affected configuration:** an explicitly selected `hidd-sdlgfx-yes` target and CyberGraphX pixel-array use on an SDL-backed bitmap; the SDL aggregate edge is commented in the checked-in hosted boot manifest. **Confidence:** high for the 24-bit/4-byte format definitions, wrapper mappings, and the SDL surface-depth argument; no SDL pixel-array operation was run. Source-only; see the [SDL 32-bit pixel-array format trace](AROS-other-drivers-coverage.md#sdl-32-bit-pixel-array-format-trace-gd10510).

<a id="gd10511--negative-decoration-barheight-can-produce-a-zero-system-image-height"></a>
<a id="gd10511"></a>
## GD10511 — Negative Decoration BarHeight can produce a zero system-image height

`LoadSystemConfig()` parses `BarHeight` with `atol()` and stores the signed result without range validation (`workbench/libs/decortheme/themeconfig.c:27-32,367-369`); `DecorConfig.BarHeight` is a `LONG` (`workbench/libs/decortheme/decortheme.h:54-57`). In `windecor_getdefsizes()`, title-gadget images start with a nonzero image height, then scale it when the reference font height plus two exceeds `BarHeight` (`workbench/c/Decoration/windowdecorclass.c:1816-1859`). The output height is `ULONG *`, while the divisor is signed `LONG`; with a negative configured bar height, the divisor is converted to a large unsigned value. For ordinary small image/font dimensions the scaled height therefore truncates to zero.

Intuition's `SYSICLASS` sizing path requests the window decorator's dimensions (`rom/intuition/sysiclass.c:230-255`). `CreateStdSysImage()` is used for window depth, zoom, close, and extra system gadgets (`rom/intuition/intuition_misc.c:310,376,476,926`); after creating the image it reads `IA_Height` and divides by that value to preserve the preferred aspect ratio (`:173-203`). Thus opening a window that requests one of those gadgets with a negative-BarHeight Decoration theme can reach division by zero during gadget image construction. This is a separate trigger from GD6008's zero value, which divides directly in `windecor_getdefsizes()`.

**Trigger and consequence:** select a custom Decoration theme whose `System/Config` sets a negative `BarHeight`, then open a window requesting a system gadget with a valid corresponding theme image. The decoration size result can be zero and `CreateStdSysImage()` divides by that zero height. Reject nonpositive `BarHeight` values when parsing/loading the theme, and guard zero dimensions before aspect-ratio division. **Affected configuration:** Decoration-enabled builds using a custom theme with negative `BarHeight` and a window requesting a relevant system gadget; bundled themes were not checked for negative values in this pass. **Confidence:** high for signed parsing, unsigned size calculation, and the zero-height divide path; no custom theme or window was exercised. Source-only; see the [negative BarHeight caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#negative-decoration-barheight-system-image-path-gd10511).

**GD10242 addendum — `LayerProperties` accepts unterminated fixed arrays:** Its public constructor copies caller-provided `layerName` and `description` arrays verbatim without enforcing a terminator (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:68085-68094`). The equality and optional ordering operators pass both arrays to `strcmp` (`:68139-68157`). A caller can construct either field as a fully nonzero array and compare the wrapper, causing `strcmp` to read beyond the fixed array. This is the same fixed-array termination defect as the existing GD10242 cases. **Affected configuration:** optional Vulkan-Hpp header; constructor/comparison path (spaceship ordering is conditional on `VULKAN_HPP_HAS_SPACESHIP_OPERATOR`). **Confidence:** high for the unchecked fixed-array copy and unbounded comparison; no comparison or build was run. Ensure supplied arrays are terminated or compare them with bounded operations. Source-only.

Caller-created arrays with no NUL byte can make these comparisons read beyond the array. This is the same fixed-array termination defect as the existing GD10242 cases. **Affected configuration:** optional Vulkan-Hpp header; comparisons are available in the standard wrapper configuration, with spaceship ordering conditional on `VULKAN_HPP_HAS_SPACESHIP_OPERATOR`. **Confidence:** high for unchecked copies and unbounded comparisons; no comparison or build was run. Use bounded comparison or ensure termination in the wrapper boundary. Source-only.

Equality and optional spaceship ordering pass both arrays to `strcmp` (`:87634-87657`). Comparing a wrapper containing either full nonzero array can read past that array. This is the same fixed-array termination defect as the existing GD10242 cases. **Affected configuration:** optional Vulkan-Hpp header; spaceship ordering requires `VULKAN_HPP_HAS_SPACESHIP_OPERATOR`. **Confidence:** high for unchecked array copy and unbounded comparison; no comparison or build was run. Bound comparisons to the fixed array or ensure termination at construction. Source-only.

**GD10242 addendum — `PhysicalDeviceProperties::deviceName` accepts unterminated arrays:** the public `PhysicalDeviceProperties` constructor copies a caller-supplied `std::array<char, VK_MAX_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_NAME_SIZE>` verbatim (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:97805-97820`); the public `deviceName` member can likewise be assigned directly (`:97917-97924`). Its equality operator calls `strcmp(deviceName, rhs.deviceName)` (`:97905-97910`), and its optional spaceship operator does the same (`:97880-97893`). Constructing or mutating a wrapper with a full nonzero array and comparing it can make `strcmp` read beyond the fixed array, invoking undefined behavior. `PhysicalDeviceProperties2` embeds this type and delegates equality to it (`:97995-98005`). This is the same fixed-array termination defect as the existing GD10242 cases. **Affected configuration:** optional Vulkan-Hpp header; spaceship ordering additionally requires `VULKAN_HPP_HAS_SPACESHIP_OPERATOR`. A valid Vulkan properties query should produce a terminated device name; the direct trigger is caller-created or caller-mutated wrapper data. **Confidence:** high for the public unchecked array and unbounded comparison. No comparison or build was run. Validate/terminate the fixed array or use bounded comparison. Source-only.

<a id="gd10512--physical-device-memory-property-equality-can-compare-memoryheap-padding"></a>
<a id="gd10512"></a>
## GD10512 — Physical-device memory-property equality can compare `MemoryHeap` padding

`MemoryHeap` contains a 64-bit `DeviceSize size` followed by 32-bit `MemoryHeapFlags flags`; its own equality and optional spaceship operators compare those fields semantically (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:70556-70610`; `DeviceSize` is `uint64_t` at `vulkan.hpp:6888`, and `MemoryHeapFlagBits` is based on `VkMemoryHeapFlags` at `vulkan_enums.hpp:2388-2397`). On ABIs where `sizeof(MemoryHeap) > sizeof(DeviceSize) + sizeof(MemoryHeapFlags)` (tail padding), those bytes are padding, not value fields. `PhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties::operator==` instead `memcmp`s each active heap as `sizeof(MemoryHeap)` bytes (`vulkan_structs.hpp:101256-101260`), so padding can make equality false for heaps whose `size` and `flags` are equal. This also makes equality disagree with the fieldwise element comparisons used by the optional spaceship operator (`:101234-101253`). The ordinary `PhysicalDevice::getMemoryProperties()` wrapper writes Vulkan output directly into the wrapper object (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:398-406`), and the properties wrapper constructor also accepts caller-supplied heap arrays (`vulkan_structs.hpp:101175-101184`); neither source path establishes padding bytes as value data. `PhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties2` delegates its equality to this embedded value (`vulkan_structs.hpp:101336-101350`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on an ABI with tail padding in `MemoryHeap`, compare two `PhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties` values with equal active counts and equal heap `size`/`flags`, but differing padding bytes in any active heap. `operator==` can report false even though each corresponding `MemoryHeap` compares equal; the result can vary with object construction or output-buffer contents and can disagree with the enclosing spaceship comparison. This is distinct from GD10250's over-count out-of-bounds reads: counts here remain within Vulkan's fixed array capacities. **Affected configuration:** optional Vulkan-Hpp API on ABIs where `MemoryHeap` has tail padding, with at least one active heap. No maintained in-tree C++ caller of this equality operator was found. **Confidence:** high that the outer comparison includes padding on such ABIs; manifestation depends on the padding bytes differing. No comparison or build was run. Compare active elements with `MemoryHeap::operator==` or compare fields explicitly. Source-only.

<a id="gd10514"></a>
### GD10514 — Vulkan-Hpp displacement-micromap constructor accepts both alternative usage-count arrays

The enhanced `AccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV` constructor (defined outside the `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS` guard) accepts both a `usageCounts` array and a `pUsageCounts` array-of-pointers (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:4573-4617`). It stores both data pointers in `pUsageCounts` and `ppUsageCounts` and sets the shared count from the first array. Its validation only throws (or asserts in `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` mode) when both arrays are nonempty **and their lengths differ** (`:4606-4615`); equal-length nonempty arrays pass and leave both native alternatives non-NULL. Vulkan requires only one of `pUsageCounts` and `ppUsageCounts` to be valid (`[VkAccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV valid usage](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkAccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV.html)`, VUID `...-pUsageCounts-07992`). The wrapper is chainable under `AccelerationStructureGeometryTrianglesDataKHR` (`vulkan.hpp:16159-16167`), so the malformed record can be submitted through the selected generated acceleration-structure build wrappers. The selected `CommandBuffer::buildAccelerationStructuresKHR()` and `Device::getAccelerationStructureBuildSizesKHR()` wrappers forward the containing `AccelerationStructureBuildGeometryInfoKHR` directly to native dispatch (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:17299-17310,17845-17862`), so this record form reaches both command paths.

**Trigger and consequence:** a downstream Vulkan-Hpp client uses `VK_NV_displacement_micromap` and constructs this wrapper with both arrays nonempty and equal in length. Construction succeeds, but passing the record in the geometry `pNext` chain violates the Vulkan valid-usage rule; validation may reject the acceleration-structure build, and behavior after submitting invalid input is not specified. This finding is distinct from GD10233's count narrowing: the shared count is correctly sized for the equal-length arrays, but the two mutually exclusive pointers are both populated. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp headers used by a client of `VK_NV_displacement_micromap`; no in-tree C++ callsite was found. **Confidence:** high for the constructor behavior, chain registration, and Vulkan valid-usage requirement; driver consequences are not claimed. Reject any case where both proxies are nonempty (and keep the count paired with the selected array). No Vulkan structure, build, or command was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd10515"></a>
## GD10515 — Vulkan-Hpp displacement-micromap constructor drops the pointer-array usage count

The enhanced `AccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV` constructor, defined outside the `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS` guard, accepts the pointer-array form as its second array proxy, `pUsageCounts_`. It assigns `usageCountsCount` from `usageCounts_.size()` unconditionally, while assigning the pointer-array data to `ppUsageCounts` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:4583-4604`). The corresponding `setPUsageCounts()` overload correctly derives the shared count from that proxy's size (`:4749-4753`); the neighboring `AccelerationStructureTrianglesOpacityMicromapEXT` enhanced constructor also selects the nonempty proxy when deriving its count and rejects simultaneous nonempty alternatives (`:4902-4927`). Vulkan defines `usageCountsCount` as the number of usage-count structures consumed; when it is zero, the supplied non-NULL pointer array contributes no entries ([structure reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkAccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV.html), members 58-62).

**Trigger and consequence:** a downstream client constructs the enhanced wrapper with an empty `usageCounts` proxy and a nonempty pointer-array proxy. Construction succeeds with `usageCountsCount == 0` and a non-NULL `ppUsageCounts`, so the requested usage-count entries are silently omitted from the native structure. This differs from GD10514, where both nonempty alternatives are stored simultaneously and violate VUID `...-pUsageCounts-07992`. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp API with `VK_NV_displacement_micromap`, when a client uses the pointer-array constructor form; no in-tree C++ callsite was found. **Confidence:** high for the count assignment and API field meaning. No Vulkan command, build, or runtime operation was performed; source-only. Derive the count from whichever single proxy is selected and reject simultaneous nonempty forms.

<a id="gd10516"></a>
## GD10516 — Vulkan-Hpp `ApplicationInfo` comparisons pass null names to `strcmp`

The `ApplicationInfo` constructor defaults both `pApplicationName` and `pEngineName` to null (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:6891-6902`). Its `operator==` handles identical pointers, including two null pointers, but when only one side is null it calls `strcmp` with that null argument (`:7009-7015`). Under `VULKAN_HPP_HAS_SPACESHIP_OPERATOR`, `operator<=>` similarly calls `strcmp` whenever the pointers differ, without checking either pointer (`:6986-7005`). `strcmp` requires both arguments to point to null-terminated strings.

**Trigger and consequence:** a Vulkan-Hpp client compares a default-constructed `ApplicationInfo` with one whose application or engine name is non-null, or compares two such records whose corresponding name pointers differ with one null. The comparison has undefined behavior and can fault. Comparing two default-constructed values does not trigger this path because the corresponding pointers are equal. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp API; the spaceship path is additionally gated by the C++20 spaceship-operator configuration. A repository search found no in-tree comparison callsite. **Confidence:** high for the null defaults and unguarded comparison paths. No comparison or build was run; source-only. Handle null/null as equal and order null separately before calling `strcmp`.


<a id="gd10517"></a>
## GD10517 — Graph source-array growth leaves skipped entries uninitialized

`Graph__MUIM_Graph_GetSourceHandle()` grows the source array directly to `SourceNo + 1` when the requested index is beyond the current source count (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.c:849-860`). `Graph__UpdateSourceArray()` allocates with `MEMF_ANY` and copies the existing prefix, but on growth it clears and initializes only the final slot at `count - 1` (`:33-70`). Any indices between the old count and that final slot remain uninitialized even though `graph_SourceCount` is then advanced to include all of them. The public method message accepts an arbitrary `ULONG SourceNo` and documents no sequential-only requirement (`graph.h:35`).

With the initial one-source graph, a request for source index 2 grows the array to three entries, copies slot 0, initializes slot 2, and leaves slot 1 uninitialized. The draw method iterates over every index below `graph_SourceCount` and reads each source's entry buffer and pen fields (`graph.c:675-693,766-800`). If the graph has a nonzero entry count, drawing therefore uses the uninitialized `gs_Entries` pointer in the skipped slot; stale contents can produce invalid reads or a fault, and the pen state is also indeterminate. `Graph__UpdateSourceEntries()` can likewise inspect the uninitialized entry pointer when a later count change reaches that slot (`:76-100`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an optional Graph.mcc client requests a source handle that skips one or more indices, then draws or resizes a graph with a nonzero entry count. The skipped records are published as active without initialization, so graph rendering or resizing can read invalid state and may fault. Initialize every new record in the grown range, including its pen sentinels and entry buffer, or reject skipped indices. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable optional `workbench-classes-zune-graph` target (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/mmakefile.src:6-14`); its local `#MM-` edge actively contributes to the virtual `workbench-classes-zune` target; default aggregate inclusion is not established. No checked-in caller was found that skips indices: SysMon requests CPU sources in increasing order (`workbench/system/SysMon/processor_graph.c:167-195`), so that caller is not claimed as a reproducer. **Confidence:** high that successful sparse growth leaves intermediate records untouched and that draw/resize paths consume every published slot; manifestation depends on a downstream caller requesting a gap and the uninitialized contents. No graph object, drawing, resize, or build was performed; source-only. See the [coverage trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graph-sparse-source-index-growth-gd10517).


<a id="gd10518"></a>
## GD10518 — Graph.mcc ignores its aggregate attribute while drawing

The public header defines `MUIA_Graph_Aggregate` as a boolean attribute (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/graph.h:17-20`). `Graph__OM_SET()` handles it by setting or clearing `GRAPHF_AGGR`, and its comment describes aggregate mode as plotting the sources' combined values (`graph.c:294-300`). However, the complete `graph.c` body has no read of `GRAPHF_AGGR` after this setter. `Graph__MUIM_Draw()` instead iterates over `graph_SourceCount` and plots each source independently in both the fill and line paths (`:675-719,766-800`); the aggregate flag does not affect the output.

**Trigger and consequence:** an optional Graph.mcc client sets `MUIA_Graph_Aggregate` to TRUE and supplies multiple data sources. The graph continues to render separate series, so the requested aggregate display is not produced; setting the attribute has no rendering effect. Implement aggregation in the draw path or remove/mark the unsupported attribute. **Affected configuration:** downstream clients of the explicitly buildable optional `workbench-classes-zune-graph` target (`workbench/classes/zune/graph/mmakefile.src:6-14`); its local `#MM-` edge actively contributes to the virtual `workbench-classes-zune` target; default aggregate inclusion is not established. A repository-wide exact-name search found no in-tree caller, so no stock application consequence is claimed. **Confidence:** high that the attribute is public, the setter changes only a flag, and no draw code reads it. No graph object, draw, or build was run; source-only. See the [coverage trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graph-aggregate-attribute-gd10518).

<a id="gd10519"></a>
## GD10519 — VBlank may traverse a DBufInfo after Safe reply releases it

`TOF_VBlank()` removes a due queue entry and advances the queue link before replying to the embedded `dbi_SafeMessage` and then `dbi_DispMessage` (`rom/graphics/graphics_init.c:180-188`). `ReplyMsg()` enqueues the message and signals its reply task before returning (`rom/exec/replymsg.c:50-64`; `rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-106`). On ExecSMP, a task on another CPU can therefore run while the VBlank handler continues through the queue.

The selected `FreeScreenBuffer()` path can release a different `DBufInfo` that is still queued. `ChangeScreenBuffer()` synchronously updates the public screen bitmap and returns after `ChangeVPBitMap()` enqueues the buffer's `sb_DBufInfo`; it does not wait for VBlank (`rom/intuition/changescreenbuffer.c:74-83`; `rom/graphics/changevpbitmap.c:98-105`). If the caller frees that currently displayed screen buffer before the next VBlank, `FreeScreenBuffer()` queues the screen-owned `RestoreDBufInfo` at the head, waits for its Safe message, and then immediately frees the ScreenBuffer's own `sb_DBufInfo` (`rom/intuition/freescreenbuffer.c:65-108`; `rom/intuition/allocscreenbuffer.c:96-108`). `FreeDBufInfo()` is only a null check followed by `FreeMem()`; it neither waits for queue completion nor removes a queued node (`rom/graphics/freedbufinfo.c:53-61`). Both queue entries are due on the next VBlank. The handler removes RestoreDBufInfo first; its Safe reply can wake the caller on another CPU, which frees the older `sb_DBufInfo` while the handler's queue link already points to that still-pending record. The handler then dereferences the freed record on its next loop iteration.

A related path can free the current entry itself: after the Safe reply wakes `FreeScreenBuffer()`, the caller may close the screen; `CloseScreen()` sends a synchronous action to the Intuition input task, but its `LockIBase()` protects screen-list changes rather than the graphics pending queue, and it frees `RestoreDBufInfo` after the action (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:147-152,183-186,353-400`; `rom/intuition/inputhandler_actions.c:583-637`). If that close completes on another CPU before the VBlank handler posts the Disp message, the handler accesses the freed restore record.

**Trigger and consequence:** on an ExecSMP target with the graphics VBlank server active, a task on a non-VBlank CPU calls `ChangeScreenBuffer()` and then `FreeScreenBuffer()` for that displayed allocated buffer before the next VBlank. When the VBlank handler replies Safe for the newly queued RestoreDBufInfo, the other CPU can free the still-queued per-buffer DBufInfo before the handler reaches it. The later loop reads that freed node's count/link and may reply through its stale embedded messages, causing invalid memory access or corruption. The related prompt-CloseScreen path can free the currently processed RestoreDBufInfo before its second reply. The affected selected topologies are x86-64 PC and Raspberry Pi 2/3/4/5 ExecSMP, where GD10508 traces the VBlank producer to CPU 0; explicit PC IRQ affinity may alter the producer CPU. **Confidence:** high for queue order, immediate owner frees, and handler access; medium for the required cross-CPU scheduling overlap. Keep each DBufInfo alive until it has been dequeued and both replies posted, or cancel/remove a pending entry before freeing it. No screen, VBlank, free/close sequence, or SMP interleaving was run; source-only. This is distinct from GD10508's unsynchronized queue-head mutation.


<a id="gd10520"></a>
## GD10520 — V3D page-rounding overflow retains an empty arena after BO creation fails

The optional Raspberry Pi V3D DRM shim accepts `drm_v3d_create_bo.size` as `__u32` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/v3d/drm-stubs/drm-uapi/v3d_drm.h:251-265`) and passes it to `v3d_gpu_mem_alloc()` (`v3d_drm_shim.c:158-175`). `ULONG` is a 32-bit unsigned type on AROS, including AArch64 (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:39-43`). The allocator rounds with `size = (size + V3D_PAGE_MASK) & ~(ULONG)V3D_PAGE_MASK` without checking the addition (`v3d_mem.c:179-186`). For `size == UINT32_MAX`, the addition wraps to 4094 and masking yields zero.

The allocator scans existing arenas, but `Allocate()` explicitly returns NULL for a zero-byte request (`rom/exec/allocate.c:125-127`). It then calls `arena_new()` with the 32 MiB minimum (`v3d_mem.c:198-202`). `arena_new()` allocates and maps the arena, links it into `sd->arenas`, and accounts its usable size before returning (`v3d_mem.c:73-143`). The subsequent zero-byte `Allocate()` still returns NULL; the failure branch reports the error and releases the semaphore without removing the new arena (`v3d_mem.c:205-210`). Thus each repeated maximum-size CREATE_BO request that can successfully allocate/map another arena retains another 32 MiB of usable GPU memory (34 MiB raw allocation including alignment slack) despite returning failure. The empty arenas are released only by the final session cleanup (`v3d_mem.c:256-272`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional shim receives repeated CREATE_BO requests with `size == UINT32_MAX`, and each `arena_new()` succeeds. Each request fails, but leaves an additional empty mapped arena allocated until session teardown, allowing repeated failed requests to consume system memory. **Affected configuration:** explicitly enabled AArch64 Raspberry Pi V3D HIDD; its package edge is commented in `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/v3d/mmakefile.src`, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. No checked-in Mesa request producer was available in this checkout, and the dependency's internal size calculation was not verified. **Confidence:** high for the 32-bit wrap and local retention path; conditional on a caller issuing the near-maximum size and arena allocation/mapping succeeding. Reject zero/overflowing rounded sizes before arena creation, and release an arena created for a request if its first allocation fails. No ioctl, allocation failure, build, or GPU operation was exercised; source-only. See the [allocator and UAPI trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-bo-size-rounding-overflow-and-failed-allocation-arena-retention-gd10520-added-prior-size-narrowing-wording-corrected-2026-11-01).

<a id="gd10521"></a>
## GD10521 — System requester dimensions ignore per-line `IntuiText.ITextFont`

`buildsysreq_calculatedims()` calls `ReqITextSize()` to measure the body, but that helper measures every string with `TextLength(&scr->RastPort, ...)` and uses `scr->RastPort.Font->tf_YSize` for its height (`rom/intuition/sysrequest_intern.c:367-385,530-555`). The drawing path goes through `ReqPrintIText()` to `int_PrintIText()` (`rom/intuition/requesters.c:59-80,166-175`); `int_PrintIText()` opens and selects each non-NULL `ITextFont` before drawing that entry (`rom/intuition/printitext.c:94-125`). Thus dimension calculation and rendering use different fonts when a caller supplies a per-line font. The computed width also determines the text-box width, and the computed height contributes to requester height (`sysrequest_intern.c:367-434).

**Trigger and consequence:** a caller passes body `IntuiText` entries with a `TextAttr` whose opened font has different width or height metrics from the screen RastPort font. The requester is sized using the screen font but rendered with the custom font. Larger custom metrics can extend beyond the calculated box or be clipped by its text region; smaller metrics can be overestimated and cause the screen-fit check to reject a requester that would fit. **Affected configuration:** Intuition system requesters using `BuildSysRequest()`/`AutoRequest()` with custom per-entry fonts; no checked-in caller was found that supplies such a font on this path. **Confidence:** high for the measurement/rendering mismatch; visible clipping or false rejection depends on metric differences, entry coordinates, and available screen space. Measure each entry with its selected font and include that font's baseline/height in the requester dimensions. No requester, custom-font open, or build was run; source-only. See the [requester font-metrics trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#system-requester-ignored-itextfont-metrics-gd10521).

<a id="gd10522"></a>
## GD10522 — `int_PrintIText()` carries a custom entry's soft style into following plain text

`int_PrintIText()` saves the incoming RastPort font and `AlgoStyle` once before traversing the linked `IntuiText` list (`rom/intuition/printitext.c:90-94`). For an entry with `ITextFont`, it opens/selects that font and calls `SetSoftStyle()` with the entry's `TextAttr.ta_Style` (`:102-110`). After drawing, it restores the original font and closes the temporary font (`:117-125`) but does not restore `AlgoStyle` until after the entire list has been processed (`:129-136`). `SetFont()` updates the font and metrics but does not reset `AlgoStyle` (`rom/graphics/setfont.c:57-67`); `SetSoftStyle()` directly changes `rp->AlgoStyle` (`rom/graphics/setsoftstyle.c:63-65`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a linked `IntuiText` chain contains an entry with non-NULL `ITextFont`, followed by an entry with `ITextFont == NULL`. The latter is drawn with the original RastPort font but retains soft-style bits set for the preceding custom font, so it can appear bold/italic or otherwise styled contrary to the caller's RastPort state. The original style is restored after the complete chain, so the effect is limited to later entries in that same call. **Affected configuration:** Intuition callers of `PrintIText()` or requester drawing that pass mixed-font `IntuiText` chains. A targeted in-tree census of Intuition, GadTools, ReqTools and AHI font/list assignments did not establish a maintained chain with this exact mixed-font sequence; the candidate therefore remains conditional on public or future callers. **Confidence:** high for the style mutation and missing per-entry restoration; visible effect depends on the requested style bits, font support, and a subsequent unfonted entry. Restore the saved RastPort soft style after each custom-font entry when restoring the original font, then preserve the existing final state restoration. No text rendering or build was run; source-only. See the [IntuiText soft-style trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#itext-custom-font-soft-style-carries-forward-gd10522).


<a id="gd10523"></a>
## GD10523 — `StridedArrayProxy` exposes contiguous-pointer iteration for strided records

`StridedArrayProxy<T>` publicly re-exports `ArrayProxy<T>::begin()`, which returns a raw `T const *`, and defines `end()` by advancing the byte address by `size() * m_stride` and casting it back to `T const *` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan.hpp:525-542`). Its constructor explicitly permits `stride > sizeof(T)` (`:530-535`). A range-based `for` over this class uses its `begin()` and `end()` members and increments the raw pointer by one `T` per iteration ([C++ range-for translation](https://eel.is/c++draft/stmt.ranged), [pointer arithmetic](https://eel.is/c++draft/expr.add)); that step is `sizeof(T)` bytes, not `m_stride`.

**Trigger and consequence:** a downstream C++ caller constructs a strided proxy with `stride > sizeof(T)` and traverses it with range-based `for` or an algorithm using its exposed `begin()`/`end()`. The traversal does not visit the logical records at their declared stride; it can treat padding/gap bytes as `T`, visit the wrong number of elements, or perform invalid pointer arithmetic over storage that is not a contiguous `T` array. `front()` and the custom `back()` are separate accessors and do not make the raw-pointer iteration stride-aware. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp headers for downstream C++ clients; repository search found no checked-in `StridedArrayProxy` use outside the generated headers. **Confidence:** high for the iterator/stride mismatch; manifestation requires a caller to traverse a non-packed proxy. Provide a stride-aware iterator, or do not expose ordinary raw-pointer `begin()`/`end()` for non-packed strides. No iteration, compilation, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="gd10524"></a>
## GD10524 — `StridedArrayProxy` byte-offset arithmetic wraps at 4 GiB

`ArrayProxy::size()` returns `uint32_t`, and `StridedArrayProxy::m_stride` is also `uint32_t` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan.hpp:405-408,561-562`). The `size() * m_stride` expression in `end()` and `(size() - 1) * m_stride` in `back()` are therefore evaluated in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic before pointer addition (`:539-550`). Unsigned arithmetic wraps modulo 2^32 ([C++ unsigned integer arithmetic](https://eel.is/c++draft/basic.fundamental)).

**Trigger and consequence:** a 64-bit client on an ABI where the two `uint32_t` operands remain 32-bit has a valid backing region whose strided extent exceeds `UINT32_MAX` bytes while the element count itself still fits `uint32_t`. For example, count `268435457` and stride `16` produce an intended extent of 2^32 + 16 bytes; the `end()` offset wraps to 16, and the `back()` offset wraps to zero. Consequently range traversal can stop near the beginning, and `back()` can return the first record instead of the last. This is separate from GD10233's element-count conversion: the count is representable here, but its byte-offset product is not. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp header used by a downstream 64-bit C++ client with a multi-gigabyte strided region; no in-tree `StridedArrayProxy` caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the 32-bit product and resulting wrong offsets; practical exposure depends on a backing region larger than 4 GiB. Widen the multiplication before computing either offset and check representability in the pointer-difference domain. No multi-gigabyte allocation, proxy call, or build was performed; source-only.

## GD10525 — withdrawn duplicate of GD10479

The `DisplayModeKHR` copy-construction and copy-assignment parent-handle defect is already documented as GD10479, with the same source locations and consequence. GD10525 adds no distinct trigger or root cause; use [GD10479](#gd10479-vulkan-hpp-displaymodekhr-copies-lose-their-physical-device-association) as the canonical finding. This duplicate ID is retained only for historical cross-reference and is not an additional bug.
<a id="gd10526"></a>
## GD10526 — Radeon cursor visibility can race display activation and leave cursor state inconsistent

The selected Radeon class exposes `SetCursorVisible` and `SetCursorShape` in its HIDD display method list (`workbench/hidds/radeon/radeon.conf:37-42`). `SetCursorVisible()` updates the cursor enable bit through `ShowHideCursor()` and then writes `sd->Card.cursorVisible`, without taking the driver's `HWLock` (`ati_class.c:427-431`; register update at `radeon_driver.c:1615-1632`). The `SetCursorShape(NULL)` path performs the same hardware/state update without the lock (`ati_class.c:359-367`). For a non-NULL shape, the method does take `HWLock` (`:384-421`).

The display `Show()` path does take `HWLock`, loads a new mode, then restores cursor visibility from the shared `cursorVisible` field (`ati_class.c:98-122`). The maintained visibility route is `ActivateMonitor()` → `SetAttrs(..., MA_PointerVisible, ...)` → the monitor class setter → `HIDD_Display_SetCursorVisible()` (`rom/intuition/misc.c:69-115`; `rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:1041-1057`). `ActivateMonitor()` is called from the Intuition input handler as well as screen lifecycle paths (`rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:1956,2166`; `rom/intuition/openscreen.c:2465`; `rom/intuition/closescreen.c:412`). On the other side, `LoadView()` takes `ActiViewCprSemaphore` and reaches `display_LoadViewPorts()` and Radeon `Show()` (`rom/graphics/loadview.c:59-69`; `rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:506-565`; `ati_class.c:98-122`). These paths do not share the Radeon `HWLock` at the caller boundary: Radeon `Show()` holds it, but `SetCursorVisible()` and the NULL-shape route do not. Thus they are not serialized by this source-level lock structure. For example, a visibility update can enable the register, a concurrent `Show()` can load the mode and reapply the old `FALSE` state, and the visibility call can then publish `TRUE`; the software state and final hardware bit disagree until a later cursor/mode operation. This is a source-derived interleaving; no scheduler trace was run. Similar ordering is possible while hiding the pointer.

**Trigger and consequence:** on a Radeon display, a pointer visibility change or NULL cursor-shape update overlaps `HIDD_Display_Show()` on another task. The unlocked read-modify-write register access and shared state publication can leave the hardware cursor visibility inconsistent with `sd->Card.cursorVisible`. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `hidd-radeon` on supported Radeon hardware; its parent aggregate edge is optional in this checkout. **Confidence:** high for the lock asymmetry and state update order; medium for manifestation because it requires overlapping display calls from separate tasks. Protect all cursor enable/state transitions with `HWLock`. No display, cursor operation, interleaving or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd10527"></a>
## GD10527 — Radeon cursor position overflows its signed horizontal-offset field at `WORD_MIN`

The HIDD display cursor-position method takes signed `WORD` coordinates (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1543-1566`). The maintained `graphics.library/MoveSprite()` caller forwards the signed coordinates for cursor sprite zero (`rom/graphics/movesprite.c:70-87`). Radeon stores them in `WORD x, y`; for negative x it computes `xoff = -x`, then forms the register value with `(xoff << 16)` (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_class.c:437-455`, also `:467-470` for the secondary display).

When x is the minimum signed `WORD` value (-32768), its mathematical negation, 32768, is not representable in `WORD`. On the usual 16-bit two's-complement `WORD` conversion, `xoff` becomes negative again; the subsequent left shift of a negative signed value is undefined in C. The offset therefore is not reliably encoded for this representable cursor coordinate. The equivalent y case stores the negated value in `yoff` and masks it into the low register half (`:448-455,467-470`), so this finding is limited to horizontal positioning.

**Trigger and consequence:** `MoveSprite()` or a direct HIDD caller positions Radeon cursor sprite zero at x = -32768, after viewport-offset addition. The signed negation cannot be represented in `xoff`, and the register expression can invoke undefined behavior, leaving the horizontal cursor offset/compiler result unreliable. A conditional in-tree route also exists: the `IECLASS_NEWPOINTERPOS` pixel path adds the screen origin to the signed local position and calls `ActivateMonitor()` (`rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:2159-2168`); that routine replaces only the `-1` sentinel and clamps only the upper edge before forwarding the stored coordinates to the monitor HIDD (`rom/intuition/misc.c:87-115; :21-33`). Ordinary raw-mouse coordinates are clamped nonnegative earlier (`inputhandler.c:1545-1549`). The source does not establish that a selected Radeon screen bitmap can retain a `LeftEdge` of `WORD_MIN`, so this route is possible from the checked-in call chain but not confirmed for the target driver. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `hidd-radeon` on targets with 16-bit signed `WORD` and 32-bit `int`; the public `MoveSprite()`/HIDD boundary is reachable to callers, and the in-tree pixel-event route additionally depends on accepted screen geometry. **Confidence:** high for the narrowing boundary and source expression; medium for in-tree reachability and the target compiler's out-of-range signed conversion. Compute in an unsigned or wider type and encode the register field without shifting a negative signed operand. No cursor operation or build was run; source-only.


<a id="gd10528"></a>
## GD10528 — `MUIO_ImageButton` silently truncates long image paths

`INTERNAL_ImageButton()` first calls `Lock(imagePath, ACCESS_READ)` on the complete caller-supplied path. If that succeeds, it builds the image specification in `TEXT imageSpec[512]` by appending `"3:"` and `imagePath` with `strlcat()`, but ignores both return values (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_makeobject.c:133-145`). `strlcat()` copies at most 511 bytes including the terminator, so a path longer than 509 bytes is shortened. The full-path lock is then released, and the shortened spec is passed as `MUIA_Image_Spec` (`:146-160`). The selected image class duplicates that string (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/image.c:104-126`); the `3:` parser interprets ordinary paths as brush filenames (`workbench/libs/muimaster/imspec.c:179-183,375-377`) and later attempts to load that stored filename (`:496-520`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a `MUIO_ImageButton` caller supplies a path longer than 509 bytes and the complete path can be locked. The image object receives only the prefix, so setup can fail to load the requested image or load a different file if the truncated path resolves to one. The lock check does not protect against this because it checked the untruncated path. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting `muimaster` and calling `MUI_MakeObject(MUIO_ImageButton, label, imagePath)`; the public `ImageButton()` macro forwards the path without a documented length limit (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/include/libraries/muiaros.h:5410-5411`). The maintained in-tree callers found use short fixed theme paths, so no current in-tree manifestation was established. **Confidence:** high that the helper truncates paths above the fixed bound and passes the prefix to image setup; practical manifestation is conditional on a public/future caller supplying such a path. Allocate the spec to fit the input or detect truncation and use the simple-button fallback. No long path or GUI was exercised; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mui-imagebutton-path-length-recheck-gd10528).

<a id="gd10529"></a>
## GD10529 — AmigaVideo `UpdateRect()` leaves cached pixels unwritten

`AmigaVideoBM::PutPixel()` stores the requested pixel in its per-object cache and sets a bit in `writemask`; it writes the planar memory only when `flushpixelcache()` runs (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_bitmapclass.c:389-433,435-453`). The bitmap's installed `UpdateRect()` method is empty (`:1029-1031`), and the selected AmigaVideo compositor's `BitMapRectChanged()` method is also empty (`amigavideo_compositorclass.c:474-477`). The HIDD contract says `UpdateRect()` runs after drawing so the changed image becomes visible (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:5027-5063`).

The public `WritePixel()` path writes through `HIDD_BM_PutPixel()` and then calls `update_bitmap()` for the one-pixel rectangle (`rom/graphics/writepixel.c:65-71,77-82`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:218-232`). `AllocBitMap()` creates an HIDD bitmap object for a bitmap with a display ModeID (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:219-220,335-350`), and the selected m68k Amiga boot manifest includes the AmigaVideo HIDD (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:158,375`). Therefore the normal `WritePixel()` update notification does not drain this driver's deferred cache.

A second selected route changes the backing planes without draining that cache. `ChangeVPBitMap()` assigns the replacement bitmap and calls `MakeVPort()` (`rom/graphics/changevpbitmap.c:66-68`); when the viewport owns a wrapped bitmap object, `MakeVPort()` reuses it with `HIDD_PlanarBM_SetBitMap()` (`rom/graphics/makevport.c:135-142`). AmigaVideo's setter replaces `data->pbm` and its layout fields, then commits same-layout plane changes, but does not clear `writemask` or `pixelcache` (`amigavideo_bitmapclass.c:1035-1068`). A later cache drain can therefore apply a queued old-bitmap pixel to the newly attached planes. The selected AmigaVideo display path explicitly handles same-layout classic `ChangeVPBitMap()` through this in-place setter (`amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1245-1254`). Intuition's maintained `ChangeScreenBuffer()` caller passes `screenbuffer->sb_BitMap` to `ChangeVPBitMap()` before updating the Screen RastPort (`rom/intuition/changescreenbuffer.c:74-80`). Its `AllocScreenBuffer()` API stores a non-NULL caller-supplied bitmap directly in the ScreenBuffer (`rom/intuition/allocscreenbuffer.c:109-115,141`), without checking whether it is a classic planar bitmap; such a same-layout caller-supplied bitmap reaches the AmigaVideo setter. `LockIBase()` around the change does not drain the bitmap's private pixel cache.

**Trigger and consequence:** a `WritePixel()` targets an AmigaVideo HIDD bitmap and no later operation on the same cached four-byte planar word invokes `flushpixelcache()`. The pixel remains absent from the underlying planes after the update call; if the bitmap is disposed before another cache-flushing operation, the write is lost. If `ChangeVPBitMap()` replaces the wrapped bitmap first, a later drain can instead write the queued old pixel into the new buffer. A later read from the same cached word can report the queued value, masking stale plane contents. Flush the cache before returning from `UpdateRect()` and before replacing the bitmap's backing planes. **Affected configuration:** the selected m68k Amiga `amigavideo` HIDD, for HIDD display-mode bitmaps using the public graphics `WritePixel()` path. **Confidence:** high for the deferred write, empty installed update methods, and selected caller path; visibility and final loss depend on whether another operation flushes the cache. No pixel operation, bitmap disposal, display or build was run; source-only. See the [coverage trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-pixel-cache-update-boundary-gd10529).

<a id="gd10530"></a>
## GD10530 — AmigaVideo pixel-cache mask uses a signed shift for bit 31

`AmigaVideoBM__Hidd_BitMap__PutPixel()` stores the pixel in `pixelcache[bit]`, then sets its dirty mask with `data->writemask |= 1 << bit` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_bitmapclass.c:449-451`). `bit` is an unsigned byte, but integer promotion leaves the literal `1` as signed `int`; AROS `ULONG` and the cache mask are 32-bit (`amigavideo_bitmap.h:73-76`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:35-39`). A valid 32-pixel-wide bitmap write at `(31,0)` computes `bit == 31`: `offset` is 3, the aligned cache offset is 0, and the low three x bits are 7. Shifting signed `1` by 31 is undefined under the configured C standards through C17 because the result is not representable in `int` ([WG14 C17 ballot N2176 §6.5.7p4](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg14/www/docs/n2176.pdf)). The later `flushpixelcache()` tests bit 31 of the mask when deciding whether to copy `pixelcache[31]` into the planar word (`:409-428`).

**Trigger and consequence:** write pixel x=31 in a row whose first 32 pixels are in bounds, then invoke an operation that flushes this cache word. If the selected compiler does not produce the expected high mask bit for the undefined shift, the cached pixel is skipped when planar memory is updated. **Affected configuration:** m68k Amiga builds selecting the AmigaVideo bitmap HIDD; the trigger is a valid pixel at cache slot 31. **Confidence:** high for the signed shift and reachable bit index; medium for a visible missed pixel because the actual compiler result for this expression was not established. Use an unsigned mask operand (`1UL << bit`). No drawing operation, compiler output, or build was exercised; source-only. See the [cache-mask trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-pixel-cache-mask-bit31-gd10530).


<a id="gd10531"></a>
## GD10531 — Nested `ObtainGIRPort()` skips setup for a different layer

`ObtainGIRPort()` locks `GadgetLock` and each returned RastPort's layer, but its clip/scroll backup and nesting counter live in one `IntuitionBase::BackupLayerContext` (`rom/intuition/obtaingirport.c:73-89`; `rom/intuition/intuition_intern.h:343-348,506-511`). Only the acquisition that changes `nestcount` from zero saves the layer state, zeros `Scroll_X`/`Scroll_Y`, and installs a NULL clip region. `GadgetLock` is a recursive Exec semaphore for its owning task (`intuition_intern.h:243-246`; `rom/exec/obtainsemaphore.c:59-62`; `rom/exec/semaphores.c:100-113`), so a custom hook can acquire another GIRPort synchronously while retaining the first.

**Trigger and consequence:** a custom gadget hook holds a GIRPort for layer A and synchronously invokes a render hook for a gadget on layer B, whose hook also calls `ObtainGIRPort()`. The second call sees a nonzero shared nesting count, so it returns a clone for B without clearing B's clip region or scroll offsets. Drawing through that nested RastPort therefore uses B's preexisting layer context instead of the setup the helper otherwise establishes; when B has a non-NULL clip region or nonzero scroll, nested output may be clipped or displaced. Releasing B decrements the count but cannot restore or adjust B's context; the outer release restores A's saved state (`releasegirport.c:50-68`). **Affected configuration:** Intuition builds with custom gadget clients that nest rendering across distinct layers. The public function documentation asks callers to obtain a port for each hook and does not specify a same-layer-only or non-nesting restriction (`obtaingirport.c:29-45`). The checked-in direct-call search did not establish a maintained cross-layer nested caller, so reachability is external/future-client only. **Confidence:** high for the shared-counter and skipped-setup behavior; medium for caller reachability and visible effect, which require nested hooks on distinct layers with non-default clip/scroll state. A per-layer nesting context or an explicit restriction enforced/documented by the API would avoid the mismatch. No nested render, GUI operation, or build was run; source-only. See the [GIRPort nesting trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#girport-nested-layer-context-gd10531).

<a id="gd10532"></a>
## GD10532 — V3D treats a partial MMU setup as an active page table

v3d_hw_init() allocates the page table and scratch page independently, then configures the V3D MMU only if both handles are nonzero (arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/v3d/v3d_hw.c:206-232). If page-table allocation succeeds but the scratch-page allocation fails, initialization logs that it is running unprotected and still sets powered = TRUE and returns success (:260-264). However, v3d_mmu_map() decides whether the MMU is available by checking only mmu_pt_handle (:295-302). It therefore writes entries to the driver's page table and returns the unmasked physical address through V3D_GPU_VA, even though this initialization path did not install that table or enable the MMU. The actual unprotected fallback, used only when the page-table handle is null, returns V3D_GPU_ADDR(paddr), which masks the address to 30 bits (v3d_intern.h:299-300). The allocator permits arena addresses anywhere below 4 GiB, not just below 1 GiB (v3d_mem.c:67-71,93-101). The driver also does not establish that translation is disabled before taking its fallback path: `V3D_Init()` calls `v3d_reset_deassert()`, which only writes the reset bit when it was asserted (`v3d_init.c:125-134,257-264`); an already-running block is not reset there. `v3d_hw_init()` logs the entry `MMU_CTL` and page-table base (`v3d_hw.c:139-145`), but that observation does not control initialization. If either MMU allocation fails, it leaves the firmware's previous MMU state untouched, still sets `powered` and returns TRUE (`:206-232,260-264`). The `v3d_galliumclass` initializer then accepts the usable hardware state and proceeds with screen creation (`v3d_galliumclass.c:519-523`).

**Trigger and consequence:** either (a) page-table allocation succeeds but the following 4 KiB scratch-page allocation fails, and a later BO lands at an address from 1 GiB to below 4 GiB; or (b) an MMU allocation fails while the V3D MMU was already enabled on entry. In case (a), BO mapping treats the newly allocated but uninstalled table as active and returns an unmasked address; in case (b), the fallback masks the physical address even though the previously active firmware translation has not been disabled or replaced. In both cases the submitted GPU address does not match the translation state established by this initialization path, so BO access and rendering can fail. The second trigger depends on firmware leaving the MMU enabled; this source pass confirms that startup preserves an already-deasserted block and does not act on the logged enable state, but does not establish the firmware's state on every board. This is the same readiness/state mismatch as the partial-allocation case, not a separate finding. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable optional Raspberry Pi AArch64 hidd-v3d; its parent aggregate edge is commented out, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high that the partial allocation state is accepted and the mapper selects the wrong branch; the rendering consequence depends on the stated allocation failure, BO address range, and hardware address path. Track MMU readiness separately from allocation handles, and use the unprotected mapping unless the driver has actually installed and enabled its table. No allocation failure, GPU operation, build, or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only; see the [V3D hardware-service review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-hardware-service-source-order-and-mm-mapping-findings-gd10532-gd10533).

<a id="gd10533"></a>
## GD10533 — V3D submission sequence wrap skips the completion wait

The V3D submission counter is an AROS ULONG (32-bit unsigned) and increments without wrap handling at each accepted submission (v3d_intern.h:364-365; v3d_hw.c:676; compiler/include/exec/types.h:38-39). The counter is retained across screen sessions: last-screen teardown sets finished_seqno and bin_flushed_seqno to the current seqno, but does not reset seqno (v3d_galliumclass.c:500-510). When the counter wraps to zero, v3d_hw_wait_seqno() skips its wait because of the explicit seqno && condition (v3d_hw.c:767-775). The selected overlay presentation path records the current sequence with a queued frame and calls this wait before showing that frame (v3d_galliumclass.c:879-896). The service machine also uses ordinary unsigned ordering to decide whether a queued render has had its bin flushed (v3d_hw.c:460-479), so a wrapped low sequence can compare as already flushed against the previous high bin_flushed_seqno.

**Trigger and consequence:** after the 32-bit counter wraps, the overlay queues a frame with sequence zero. Its later presentation does not wait for that submission to retire; if the binner is still working, the render queue can also treat the wrapped sequence as already flushed. The driver may present incomplete frame contents or start rendering before its bin data is ready. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable optional Raspberry Pi AArch64 hidd-v3d; its parent aggregate edge is commented out, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the counter wrap, skipped wait, and non-wrap-safe queue comparison; visible corruption depends on a wrapped submission reaching the overlay path while its GPU work remains outstanding. Use wrap-safe sequence comparisons or reset/rebase the counter only after draining all jobs. No sequence wrap, GPU submission, display, build, or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only; see the [V3D hardware-service review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#v3d-hardware-service-source-order-and-mm-mapping-findings-gd10532-gd10533).

<a id="gd10536"></a>
## GD10536 — Nouveau destroys an MST manager after initialization fails

`nv50_mstm_new()` allocates and publishes `*pmstm` before calling `drm_dp_mst_topology_mgr_init()`; if initialization returns an error, it returns without clearing or freeing that pointer (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/dispnv50/disp.c:1601-1621`). The selected DRM helper can fail while creating its ordered workqueue or allocating the initial topology state (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/display/drm_dp_mst_topology.c:5710-5758`). In the latter case it has initialized locks and work items but has not called `drm_atomic_private_obj_init()`; in the earlier case it returns before initializing the work items, manager device fields, or private object. `nv50_sor_create()` propagates this error after the encoder has been registered and attached to the connector, while `nv50_display_create()` only logs the per-output error and continues (`disp.c:1998-2040,3070-3085`). On later encoder teardown, `nv50_sor_destroy()` calls `nv50_mstm_del()` for the non-NULL pointer; that helper unconditionally calls `drm_dp_mst_topology_mgr_destroy()`, which tears down work and the atomic private object as if initialization had succeeded (`disp.c:1579-1600`; `drm_dp_mst_topology.c:5772-5795`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an explicitly enabled Nouveau display with a non-eDP MST-capable DP output encounters allocation failure during `drm_dp_mst_topology_mgr_init()`, then reaches normal encoder teardown or a later display-creation failure cleanup. Teardown operates on a partially initialized manager; depending on which allocation failed, it can flush uninitialized work and finalize an uninitialized DRM private object, causing invalid cleanup or a crash. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable optional `nouveau.hidd` with a detected non-eDP DP MST output; the target is not included by the default package graph. **Confidence:** high for the published pointer, propagated error, and unconditional destroy path; failure and subsequent teardown are conditional. Clear/free the manager on init failure or track successful initialization and only run the matching destroy path. No allocation failure, encoder teardown, GPU/display operation, or build was run; source-only. See the [Nouveau display full-body and MST-init trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nouveau-nv50-display-full-body-and-mst-init-failure-gd10536).

<a id="gd10537"></a>
## GD10537 — SDL startup disposes input objects while its event task can still dispatch to them

`SDLKbd__Root__New()` and `SDLMouse__Root__New()` publish the created input objects in `xsd.kbdhidd` and `xsd.mousehidd` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/sdl_kbdclass.c:44-53`; `sdl_mouseclass.c:44-52`). `sdl_Startup()` may then fail while registering the keyboard or mouse hardware driver: `HIDD_Input_AddHardwareDriver()` can return NULL if driver-node allocation, object creation, or driver setup fails (`rom/hidds/hidd/hwclass.c:174-216`). Its `!msdriver` cleanup removes a successfully registered keyboard driver and immediately disposes the mouse and keyboard HIDD objects (`startup.c:97-126`; `OOP_DisposeObject()` reaches `root_dispose()`, which frees the object allocation at `rom/oop/rootclass.c:137-150`), but leaves the global object pointers intact and does not stop or synchronize with the event task.

That task was already started before `sdl_hidd_init()` and `sdl_Startup()` (`startup.c:275-299`). While the cleanup is disposing the input objects, `sdl_event_task()` can process a queued or newly received matching event and call `Hidd_Mouse_SDL_HandleEvent()` or `Hidd_Kbd_SDL_HandleEvent()` through the stale global pointer (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/sdl/event.c:88-107`). The event worker releases `sdl_lock` before iterating the copied event batch and dispatching input events (`event.c:71-75,88-107`), so that semaphore does not serialize dispatch against startup cleanup. The helpers call `OOP_DoMethod()` on the supplied object (`sdl_mouseclass.c:121-124`; `sdl_kbdclass.c:80-88`); that macro reads `o_Class` from the OOP object header immediately preceding the freed object pointer (`rom/oop/include/oop.h:94-101`), with no NULL or lifetime check. The caller stops the event task only after `sdl_Startup()` returns FALSE (`startup.c:296-300`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional hosted SDL HIDD reaches input-object creation, a later input-driver registration fails, and a mouse or keyboard event is dispatched after the object is disposed but before the event task is stopped. Because OOP dispatch reads the freed object's preceding class-pointer header, it can use stale object/class state and fault. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the optional hosted SDL HIDD, under the stated registration-failure and event timing. **Confidence:** high for pointer publication, cleanup order, and the absence of synchronization around dispatch; low-to-medium for event reachability. This failure branch runs before `AddDisplayDriverA()`. `sdl_hidd_init()` has already called `SDL_Init(SDL_INIT_VIDEO)`, so the uncertainty is not whether SDL's video subsystem was initialized; checked-in code does not establish whether the host SDL backend can deliver matching input events before display-driver registration succeeds. Retain this as a conditional candidate pending that backend contract. Stop and synchronize the event task before disposing input objects, or clear and protect the published pointers while draining in-flight dispatches. This is separate from GD2620's stack-local VBlank server left registered during task removal and GD5721's retained registered driver instances after display-registration failure. No registration failure, event, object disposal, or build was induced; source-only; see the [SDL event lifecycle review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sdl-event-task-startup-input-object-disposal-pass-gd10537).

<a id="gd10538"></a>
## GD10538 — V3D recovery can orphan successful MMU scratch allocations

`v3d_hw_init()` enters the MMU allocation block only when `mmu_pt_handle` is NULL, then independently assigns both `mmu_pt_handle` and `mmu_scratch_handle` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/v3d/v3d_hw.c:206-211`). If page-table allocation fails while scratch allocation succeeds, the function leaves the driver powered and returns success (`:214-264`). A later GPU recovery calls `v3d_block_reset()` and `v3d_hw_init()` again (`:583-584`). If the page-table allocation still fails and the next scratch allocation succeeds, its handle overwrites the prior live allocation without freeing it. If the page-table allocation succeeds on retry, the new scratch allocation also overwrites the prior handle. `v3d_gpu_mem_free()` is used for client BOs, but not these private allocations; session cleanup only releases arenas whose entire allocator is empty (`v3d_drm_shim.c:120-149`; `v3d_mem.c:256-275`). The orphaned block therefore pins its arena after the session sweep and can accumulate on successive qualifying recovery attempts.

**Trigger and consequence:** in the optional Raspberry Pi AArch64 V3D HIDD, page-table allocation fails but scratch allocation succeeds during initialization, then a GPU hang causes recovery and the scratch allocation succeeds again. Each retry loses the prior scratch handle and permanently consumes its suballocation; enough repeated failures can retain otherwise releasable arenas and reduce RAM available to GPU BOs. Recovery is capped at four attempts per session (`v3d_hw.c:570-581`), limiting accumulation in one session. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable optional `raspi-aarch64` V3D module; default aggregate inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the overwritten handle and unreclaimed allocation on the stated path; occurrence depends on the allocator failure pattern and subsequent recovery. Retain/reuse an existing scratch allocation independently of page-table readiness, and free it if replacing it. No allocation failure, GPU recovery, build or runtime operation was exercised; source-only.
<a id="gd10539"></a>
## GD10539 — DoGadgetMethodA drops the gadget RastPort's pen state during GM_RENDER

`DoGadgetMethodA()` initializes its reusable RastPort, then copies only `Layer` and `BitMap` from `gi->gi_RastPort` before replacing `gi_RastPort` with the reusable object (`rom/intuition/dogadgetmethoda.c:106-113`). `InitRastPort()` zeroes the structure and sets `FgPen` to `-1` and `BgPen` to `0` (`rom/graphics/initrastport.c:60-71`). The `GM_RENDER` path changes write mask and draw mode but does not restore the source RastPort's foreground or background pen (`dogadgetmethoda.c:130-162`). Before the reusable-port optimization, this branch passed the complete `ObtainGIRPort()` clone to the method (`07eb4e69d5^:rom/intuition/dogadgetmethoda.c`); `ObtainGIRPort()` clones the complete RastPort before setting rendering attributes (`rom/intuition/obtaingirport.c:67-92`), and Intuition's clone copies the complete structure (`rom/intuition/misc.c:145-155`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a custom gadget is rendered through `DoGadgetMethodA()` with a window/requester whose RastPort has nondefault `FgPen` or `BgPen`, and its `GM_RENDER` implementation relies on those inherited values before setting its own pens. The callback instead sees `FgPen == -1` and `BgPen == 0`, which can produce incorrect pixels or incorrect pen-dependent drawing. The only checked-in direct `DoGadgetMethodA()` `GM_RENDER` caller found is `animation.datatype`'s playback refresh (`workbench/classes/datatypes/animation/animationplayback.c:335-340`): its renderer blits a frame bitmap, or explicitly sets the foreground color before its fallback fill (`animationclass.c:1620-1640`); its nested TapeDeck renderer selects explicit draw pens from `DrawInfo` (`workbench/classes/gadgets/tapedeck/tapedeckclass.c:348-405`). Thus no in-tree caller depending on the lost inherited pen state was established. The visible-impact claim remains conditional on external/custom classes using the documented render RastPort. Copy the caller RastPort state into the reusable port before applying the deliberate rendering overrides. **Affected configuration:** selected Intuition builds when a downstream custom `GM_RENDER` method relies on inherited `FgPen`/`BgPen`; no checked-in trigger was found. **Confidence:** high for the regression and lost pen state, medium for visible impact because it depends on a callback consuming that state. No gadget was rendered or runtime behavior exercised; source-only. See the [coverage record](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#dogadgetmethoda-render-rastport-pen-state-pass-gd10539-added).

## GD10543

**WBRename can overflow its relabel-path buffer for a long valid DOS name.** `doRelabel()` uses `TEXT buff[128]`, then appends the volume name and `:` with `strcat()` before looking up its device (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/WBRename/main.c:280-285`); it later clears the buffer and appends the device name and `:` the same way (`:286-289`). Either name needs at most 126 bytes to fit with the colon and terminator, but DOS-list names are not limited to that size: `MakeDosEntry()` allocates according to `strlen(name)` and copies the full input in the selected `AROS_FAST_BPTR` representation (`rom/dos/makedosentry.c:54-80`); the BSTR representation also accepts a 255-byte name. WBRename obtains the old volume name from its Workbench lock and the device name from `dol_Name`, without imposing a shorter bound (`main.c:95-103,252-278`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** build-selected WBRename target; relabel a volume whose volume or device name is at least 127 bytes. **Consequence:** unchecked concatenation writes beyond the 128-byte stack buffer, causing undefined behavior and likely process corruption or a fault. **Confidence:** high for the buffer arithmetic and unbounded DOS-name construction; no long-name DOS-list entry or relabel was created. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


<a id="gd10544"></a>
## GD10544

**Workbook dereferences a missing GadTools VisualInfo during window construction.** `WBWindowNew()` successfully opens a window and creates its menu, then calls `GetVisualInfo(my->Window->WScreen, TAG_END)` and passes the result directly to `LayoutMenus()` without checking it (`workbench/system/Workbook/wbwindow.c:797-803`). `GetVisualInfoA()` returns NULL when allocating the `VisualInfo` fails (`workbench/libs/gadtools/getvisualinfoa.c:58-64`), while `LayoutMenusA()` immediately dereferences `vi->vi_dri` before any null check (`workbench/libs/gadtools/layoutmenusa.c:58-61`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-system-workbook` target (`workbench/system/Workbook/mmakefile.src:11-18`), when VisualInfo allocation fails for a successfully opened Workbook window and its menu was created. **Consequence:** the Workbook task faults during window construction instead of taking the `WBWindowNew()` error path; the menu allocation and opened window are not released by that error path. Check `vis` before layout and route failure through cleanup that also frees the menu. **Confidence:** high for the nullable return, immediate dereference, and missing caller check; allocation failure was not induced. The parent aggregate edge is commented, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#workbook-gadtools-visual-info-failure-gd10544).

**GD9858 caller-scope recheck:** repository-wide search at the reviewed commit finds no checked-in call asking about an individual node. The one actual `MUIV_NListtree_Select_Ask` call is the optional NListtree demo's `MUIM_NListtree_Select_All` request (`workbench/classes/zune/nlist/demo/NListtree-Demo.c:809-811`), which `_NListtree_Select()` handles separately by returning `SelectedTable.tb_Entries` (`NListtree.c:9724-9729`). GD9858 therefore remains a public API contract defect, but its individual-node trigger is limited to external callers; the checked-in demo does not exercise it.
