<a id="gd10547"></a>
## GD10547 — VulkanProbe can miss compute queues beyond its fixed family array

`VulkanProbe` first asks Vulkan for the total queue-family count, then clamps that count to 16 before filling its fixed `qprops[16]` array (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/test/VulkanProbe.c:127-135`). It searches only the returned prefix for `VK_QUEUE_COMPUTE_BIT` and reports that the physical device has no compute-capable family if none is found (`:136-147`). For a device exposing more than 16 queue families with a compute-capable family only at index 16 or later, the probe reports a false failure and never attempts device creation even though such a family exists.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable optional `VulkanProbe` target (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/mmakefile.src:32,58-59`) running against a device whose queue-family list exceeds 16 entries and whose compute-capable families occur only beyond the first 16. The probe prefers the RX 9060 XT but falls back to physical device zero if that exact ID is not enumerated (`VulkanProbe.c:104-125`); no in-tree GPU provider or matching device was found, so occurrence on intended hardware is unverified.

**Confidence:** high for the 16-entry bound and resulting false-negative control flow; practical reachability depends on a Vulkan implementation exposing the stated family layout. Query and allocate the full family list, or continue enumeration through a mechanism that preserves all returned entries. No device, queue family, or build was exercised; source-only.


<a id="gd10548"></a>
## GD10548 — VulkanProbe can report success on a different GPU as success on the 9060

The probe searches the enumerated physical devices for vendor/device ID `1002:7590`, but when it does not find that ID it sets `amdIndex = 0` and continues with the first physical device (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/test/VulkanProbe.c:104-125`). The physical-device array has capacity eight, and the probe accepts `VK_INCOMPLETE` without retrying or distinguishing a truncated list (`:38-41,88-95`). After any device-zero logical-device and compute-queue success, it unconditionally logs that radv created the device and queue “on the 9060” (`:171-189`). Therefore, when device zero is another compute-capable GPU and the 9060 is absent or beyond the first eight entries, the success line identifies the wrong GPU.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** explicitly buildable optional `VulkanProbe` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/mmakefile.src:32,58-59`); the 9060 is not in the first eight returned physical devices, while device zero supports the subsequent compute-device creation calls. The probe does print a preceding note that it will use device zero, but its terminal success line still makes the 9060-specific claim. No in-tree Vulkan GPU provider was found, so this configuration is unverified.

**Consequence and confidence:** high that fallback selection and the hardcoded success text can disagree; medium that a particular driver/device setup reaches the success path. The result can falsely report the requested GPU path as validated. Preserve the selected device identity in the result message, and treat `VK_INCOMPLETE` as an enumeration that needs another pass if the target is not found. No device or build was exercised; source-only.


<a id="gd10549"></a>
## GD10549 — MUI Register title counting wraps its signed 16-bit index

`Register_DATA.numitems` is a signed `WORD` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/register.c:45-64`). `Register__OM_NEW()` counts the caller-provided, NULL-terminated `MUIA_Register_Titles` array by incrementing that field directly in the loop condition (`:383-395`). `WORD` is explicitly signed 16-bit (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:58-62`), while the public attribute is documented only as `STRPTR *` and gives no maximum count (`classes/register.h:15-19`; copied public header `workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/include/libraries/mui.h:2585-2588`). With 32,768 non-NULL title entries, the increment from 32,767 wraps to a negative `WORD` on the supported two's-complement targets; the next loop condition indexes `labels[-32768]` instead of testing the valid terminator at `labels[32768]`.

**Trigger and consequence:** an explicitly built default `muimaster` Register object receives a valid NULL-terminated title array with at least 32,768 entries. Counting reads before the caller's pointer array and can fault or produce an invalid count before the class can reject or allocate the register. The later `WORD`-typed active/column/item fields also make this class unable to represent that many tabs, so the count needs a checked upper bound before incrementing, not just a wider temporary. Checked-in Register title arrays are small; no maintained caller near this limit was found.

**Affected configuration:** default `muimaster` builds selecting Register (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:58-87`). **Confidence:** high for the signed-width mismatch and pre-terminator negative indexing on supported targets; reachability is limited to unusually large external/custom title arrays. No object, title array, or GUI was created; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

<a id="gd10550"></a>
## GD10550 — Nouveau drawing reports success after acceleration initialization partially fails

`NVAccelCommonInit()` creates the channel, push buffer, buffer context and scratch buffer before creating the architecture-specific engine objects (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/xf86-video-nouveau/nv_accel_common.c:674-707`). A scratch-buffer/map failure returns `FALSE` without calling `NVAccelCommonFini()`. Later `INIT_CONTEXT_OBJECT(...)` failures also return `FALSE` directly (`:598-606,710-783`). For Tesla, `NVAccelInit2D_NV50()` returns false if `nouveau_object_new()` fails or if the subsequent `PUSH_SPACE(push, 64)` fails (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/xf86-video-nouveau/nv50_accel.c:92-103`); the macro propagates that result without calling cleanup. In these paths the channel and push-buffer state created earlier remain live, while the NV50 2D object or its channel-binding/setup commands may be absent. Only push-buffer or buffer-context creation failures explicitly call the cleanup routine (`:682-695`).

The selected Nouveau root constructor logs an acceleration setup failure and continues operating in unaccelerated mode (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_hiddclass.c:707-708`). However, Tesla bitmap Clear/FillRect still dispatch to `HIDDNouveauNV50FillSolidRect()` (`nouveau_bitmapclass.c:327-376,382-431`), whose only readiness check is a non-NULL channel (`xf86-video-nouveau/nv50_exa.c:1051-1067`). Tesla `CopyBox` similarly dispatches to `HIDDNouveauNV50CopySameFormat()` (`nouveau_hiddclass.c:783-835`); its channel and push-buffer checks also pass after the scratch-buffer or context-object failures because those branches leave both pointers live (`nv50_exa.c:1072-1095`). Both wrappers call NV50 preparation, which emits 2D methods and validates the push buffer without establishing that the NV50 2D context object was initialized (`nv50_exa.c:201-228,257-282`). On a successful prepare, the fill wrapper marks the bitmap GPU-dirty and returns TRUE, while the copy wrapper marks source and destination GPU-dirty and returns TRUE. These results prevent their caller paths from using the superclass/software fallback (`nouveau_bitmapclass.c:372-376,426-430`; `nouveau_hiddclass.c:838-850`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an explicitly enabled Nouveau build encounters a scratch-buffer or later context-object initialization failure after channel creation. On Tesla, subsequent Clear, FillRect, or same-format CopyBox calls can submit through the incomplete NV50 channel. On Fermi-through-pre-Blackwell NVC0 configurations, a failed NVC0 2D setup can leave the channel and push buffer live without the 2D object's binding/defaults. The wrappers can report these operations as handled, suppressing the intended unaccelerated fallback; drawing may be lost or leave bitmap contents stale while the wrappers mark affected bitmaps GPU-dirty. The package edge is commented out in the checked-in default aggregate (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-29`), so this is scoped to explicitly enabled Nouveau configurations.

The same partial-readiness defect also affects NVC0 2D setup. On architectures from Fermi up to Blackwell, `NVAccelCommonInit()` invokes `NVAccelInit2D_NVC0()` (`nv_accel_common.c:736-738`). That routine creates `Nv2D`, then can return FALSE if `PUSH_SPACE(push, 64)` fails, before binding the object or programming the 2D defaults (`nvc0_accel.c:201-244`). `INIT_CONTEXT_OBJECT` propagates the failure without cleanup (`nv_accel_common.c:598-606`), and the HIDD constructor logs it but continues (`nouveau_hiddclass.c:707-708`). `HIDDNouveauNVC0FillSolidRect()` checks only that `channel` exists before calling `NVC0EXAPrepareSolid()`; the latter can later reserve space, validate, and return TRUE without checking that the setup-time 2D binding/defaults were sent. The wrapper then returns success and marks the bitmap dirty (`nvc0_exa.c:204-230,1248-1308`). `HIDDNouveauNVC0CopySameFormat()` likewise sees the still-live push buffer/channel and can report success after its prepare/copy path (`nvc0_exa.c:258-310,1313-1432`). This extends the same incomplete-acceleration-state root cause to NVC0 setup; it is not a separate finding.

**Confidence:** high that the described failures leave channel/push-buffer state live and accelerated wrappers remain callable; medium that this produces lost/stale drawing on hardware, since command execution was not observed. Make initialization failure tear down all partial state and/or gate accelerated methods on a complete acceleration-ready state. No allocation failure, GPU command, drawing operation, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd10552"></a>
## GD10552 — Nouveau NV10–NV40 alpha uploads discard 3D prepare failures

`HiddNouveau3DCopyBoxFromGART()` dispatches the old-architecture GART-to-bitmap render to `HIDDNouveauNV103DCopyBox()`, `HIDDNouveauNV303DCopyBox()`, or `HIDDNouveauNV403DCopyBox()` for NV10/20, NV30, or NV40, but ignores each Boolean result and itself returns `VOID` (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_accel.c:871-909`). The three wrappers return FALSE when their corresponding `*EXAPrepareComposite()` fails (`xf86-video-nouveau/nv10_exa.c:904-925`; `nv30_exa.c:981-1003`; `nv40_exa.c:1033-1055`). Those prepare routines can fail push-buffer-space, surface/texture setup, or BO-validation checks (`nv10_exa.c:548-600`; `nv30_exa.c:474-550`; `nv40_exa.c:462-534`). Their FALSE results are discarded by the shared helper. I rechecked the apparent draw-stage failure too: the selected GART wrappers pass a NULL mask, so the NV40 prepare path sets up one texture and emits fewer than 64 dwords after its 128-dword reservation; NV10 and NV30 also emit fewer than 64 in these selected paths. Consequently the immediate `PUSH_SPACE(push, 64)` does not need a new buffer segment after successful prepare, and its failure is not included as a trigger here (`nv10_exa.c:548-636,904-925`; `nv30_exa.c:474-589,981-1003`; `nv40_exa.c:462-573,1033-1055`).

Both `HiddNouveauAccelARGBUpload3D()` and `HiddNouveauAccelAPENUpload3D()` call the void helper for each staged GART chunk and continue their loops, then return TRUE (`nouveau_accel.c:915-995,1001-1064`). Their bitmap callers treat TRUE as completion and skip the superclass/software path (`nouveau_bitmapclass.c:677-704,832-867`). Thus a failed NV10–NV40 composite can leave one or more uploaded chunks undrawn while the public bitmap method reports success.

**Trigger and consequence:** explicitly enabled Nouveau on NV10–NV40, an alpha-image/template transfer that selects the GART/3D path, and that architecture's prepare routine failing to reserve push-buffer space, set up a supported surface/texture, or validate the target. The shared helper discards the wrapper's FALSE result; the outer upload then reports success, omits that chunk, and suppresses software fallback. Nouveau is optional in the default package graph (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-29`).

**Confidence:** high that prepare failures are discarded and the outer path returns success; medium for visible partial-image consequences because no failure was induced. Return and propagate the per-chunk render status so the bitmap method can use its normal fallback. No GPU operation, failure injection, or build was performed; source-only.

<a id="gd10553"></a>
## GD10553 — Nouveau NV10–NV40 alpha uploads omit GPU-dirty synchronization state

The NV10–NV40 alpha upload helpers queue GART-to-bitmap rendering through the shared push buffer, but do not set the destination bitmap's `gpu_dirty` flag (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_accel.c:871-909,915-995,1001-1064`). The successful bitmap callers invoke `MAP_BUFFER` after the helper (`nouveau_bitmapclass.c:697-702,862-864`), but that macro maps only when `bo->map` is NULL and waits for GPU work only when `gpu_dirty` is true (`nouveau_intern.h:300-301`). If the bitmap already has a CPU mapping, the return path skips both mapping/wait and the false dirty flag prevents the wait. Later `GetPixel()` also skips the synchronization when a mapping already exists and `gpu_dirty` is false (`nouveau_bitmapclass.c:288-306`), so it can read before the queued rendering completes. Disposal likewise kicks pending push-buffer work only when `gpu_dirty` is true (`nouveau_bitmapclass.c:136-154`), so this path can leave queued work unsubmitted when the bitmap is released.

**Trigger and consequence:** explicitly enabled Nouveau on NV10–NV40, an alpha-image or transparent alpha-template upload using the GART/3D route, and a destination bitmap whose BO is already mapped when the upload returns. Subsequent mapped CPU reads can observe stale pixels; disposing before another operation submits the channel can leave queued work without the lifecycle kick used by other accelerated writers. Nouveau is optional in the default package graph (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-29`).

**Confidence:** high that these paths omit the dirty-state publication and that the mapped fast path skips the wait; medium for timing-dependent stale reads or pending-command disposal effects. Publish the bitmap's GPU-dirty state when a chunk is successfully queued and propagate failed submissions separately. No mapped bitmap, GPU operation, disposal, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd10554"></a>
## GD10554 — Nouveau NV10–NV40 alpha-image upload converts beyond its GART chunk

`HiddNouveauAccelARGBUpload3D()` sizes each GART chunk as `line_count = GART->size / line_len`, caps it at 2,047 rows and the remaining `height`, and then maps the GART BO (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_accel.c:925-940,949-952`). Both input-copy branches mistakenly pass the full remaining `height` to the row-copy/conversion operation instead of `line_count` (`:953-984`). The next statement advances `src` by only `line_count` rows, and the GPU copy and outer-loop decrement also consume only `line_count` (`:987-994`). On supported little-endian targets, `ConvertPixels` dispatches the BGRA32-to-ARGB32 pair to the registered `convert_BGRA32_ARGB32_generic()` function (`rom/hidds/gfx/colorconv_init.c:19-31`; `rgbconv.c:42-45`; `colorconv/rgbconv_bgra32.h:100-106`). Its `SWAP32CODE` loop iterates the passed `height` and writes every pixel at the destination pitch (`colorconv/rgbconv_rgbswap.h:1-14`). The alternate big-endian `CopyMemBox32` call is passed the same excessive row count.

**Trigger and consequence:** explicitly enabled Nouveau on NV10–NV40, `PutAlphaImage()` selecting the GART path, and an image height greater than `GART->size / (width * 4)`. The GART allocation is capped at 12 MiB (`nouveau_hiddclass.c:49,710-718`). For example, a 4,096 × 2,048 32-bit upload has a 16,384-byte row and at most 768 rows fit in that BO, but the first conversion is asked to write all 2,048 remaining rows. This writes beyond the mapped GART buffer before the code submits only the first 768 rows. The out-of-range write can corrupt adjacent mapped memory or fault; no hardware or allocation behavior was exercised. The upload method selects this route for NV10–NV40 when the bitmap is chunky with more than one byte per pixel and `width * height >= 1,024` (`nouveau_bitmapclass.c:25,677-700`). Nouveau remains optional in the default package graph (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-29`).

**Affected configuration:** explicitly enabled `nouveau.hidd` targeting its checked-in i386, x86-64, or RISC-V 64-bit builds (`mmakefile.src:25-28`), with an NV10–NV40 GPU and the stated image dimensions. **Confidence:** high for the row-count mismatch and write extent; the memory fault/corruption consequence depends on the runtime mapping layout. Pass `line_count` to the conversion/copy call. No image upload, memory failure, GPU operation, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd10555"></a>
## GD10555 — Generic HIDD alpha blending left-shifts negative signed values

Unless `EXACT_ALPHA` is defined, the shared `do_alpha()` helper computes `tmp = a * (f - b)` and evaluates `(tmp << 8)` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:2944-2956`). There is no in-tree definition of `EXACT_ALPHA`, so the shift-based branch is selected by the checked-in build configurations. For any positive alpha and a source/foreground channel below the destination/background channel, `tmp` is negative; left-shifting a negative signed integer has undefined behavior in C. `PutAlphaImageBuffered()` and its allocation-failure slow path both call this helper for nonzero, non-255 alpha values (`:3057-3150`). `JAM1AlphaTemplateBuffered()` also calls it for each mask pixel (`:3421-3439`).

**Selected caller path and trigger:** `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` dispatches to `HIDD_BM_PutAlphaImage()` (`workbench/libs/cgfx/writepixelarrayalpha.c:117-128`); the Compositor calls the same method when compositing alpha bitmaps (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:302-322`). `BltTemplateAlpha()` reaches `PutAlphaTemplate()` through its render hook (`workbench/libs/cgfx/blttemplatealpha.c:91-115`), which selects the JAM1 helper for transparent color expansion unless draw mode is invert. A partially transparent source with any channel lower than the destination triggers the negative shift. The generic implementation also serves inheriting HIDD bitmap classes; classes that override the methods may use different arithmetic.

**Consequence and scope:** the blend result is compiler-dependent and may be incorrect under optimization. This affects checked-in generic HIDD builds that do not define `EXACT_ALPHA`; the repository contains no such definition. It is a separate implementation site from GD10083's Nouveau helper, although the undefined arithmetic is analogous. **Confidence:** high for the negative operand and selected callers; any visible pixel difference is compiler-dependent and was not reproduced. Replace the signed shift with defined signed arithmetic that preserves the intended fixed-point rounding. No blend, build, or runtime operation was performed; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14615`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14615).

<a id="gd10556"></a>
## GD10556 — `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` ignores its global alpha argument

`WritePixelArrayAlpha()` accepts `globalalpha` as its tenth argument, and its documentation says this value is applied to every source pixel (`workbench/libs/cgfx/writepixelarrayalpha.c:37-63`). The implementation never reads the argument: it stores only the source array and modulo in `render_data`, then forwards unchanged ARGB pixels to `HIDD_BM_PutAlphaImage()` (`:71-110,112-130`). The source file explicitly lists “The globalalpha parameter is currently ignored” in its BUGS section (`:80`).

**Maintained caller and trigger:** the MUI Pixmap class accepts `MUIA_Pixmap_Alpha`, defaults it to `0xffffffff`, stores values supplied on object creation or update, and passes `data->alpha` when drawing ARGB32 data (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/pixmap.c:147-178,670-684,750-762`). A Pixmap caller that sets a non-full alpha requests global attenuation, but the API drops that value and blends using only the source pixels' alpha. The class is an explicitly buildable external module (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:58,420-425`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/mmakefile.src:318-323`). Any other API caller passing a value other than `0xffffffff` encounters the same mismatch; `globalalpha == 0` also fails to suppress blending. This finding covers the `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` path; the MUI Pixmap class's separate <=8-bit rendering path is GD10557.

**Affected configuration and confidence:** CyberGraphX `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` users on builds with the function selected; the explicit MUI Pixmap module and external clients are affected when they request a non-full global alpha. High confidence that the parameter is unused and the documented contract is not implemented. The resulting visual difference depends on source alpha and destination pixels; no rendering was run. Apply the global factor to each source alpha before dispatch, preserving the API's documented endpoint behavior. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14623`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14623).

<a id="gd10557"></a>
## GD10557 — Low-depth MUI Pixmap drawing ignores its global alpha

For screens with depth at most eight, `Pixmap__MUIM_Setup()` creates a dithered image and, for ARGB32, a one-bit transparency mask (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/pixmap.c:529-560`). `DitherImage()` sets each mask bit solely from the source pixel's alpha threshold (`:275-280,323-338`); it does not consult `data->alpha`. `DrawPixmapSection()` then takes the dithered-bitmap branch and draws through that mask (or draws opaque if no mask exists), without applying the configured global alpha (`:644-665`). The high-depth ARGB32 path instead passes `data->alpha` to `WritePixelArrayAlpha()` (`:680-683`).

**Caller, trigger, and consequence:** the external MUI Pixmap class accepts and updates `MUIA_Pixmap_Alpha` (`:147-178,757-760`), and its Setup explicitly recognizes non-full `data->alpha` as additional transparency (`:566-581`). On a screen of depth at most eight, draw an ARGB32 Pixmap with a non-full global alpha; for example, with `data->alpha == 0` and source alpha 255, the dither mask still marks the pixel opaque and the low-depth path draws it. The requested global opacity is therefore ignored on this rendering path. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable MUI Pixmap external module on low-depth screens (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:58,420-425`; `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/mmakefile.src:318-323`). **Confidence:** high for the setup/draw dispatch and missing alpha input to mask generation; no low-depth display was used. Fold the global factor into the transparency decision or otherwise preserve opacity in the low-depth renderer. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14627`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14627).

<a id="gd10551"></a>
## GD10551 — Nouveau GART image transfer can loop forever when a row exceeds the scratch buffer

The AROS upload and download helpers compute `tmp_pitch = width * cpp`, then clamp the per-iteration line count to `GART->size / tmp_pitch` (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/xf86-video-nouveau/nouveau_exa.c:571-605,657-676`). If the allocated scratch BO is non-NULL but smaller than one row, integer division yields zero and sets `lines` to zero. The helpers pass that zero height to `NVAccelM2MF()` and leave their positive outer `height` unchanged.

Every selected M2MF destination accepts zero height as success. NV04, NV50 and NVC0 M2MF routines skip their `while (h)` bodies and return TRUE (`nv04_exa.c:402-449`; `nv50_exa.c:948-1037`; `nvc0_exa.c:988-1077`). The NVE0 path delegates to the A0B5 copy-engine rectangle routine, which submits the supplied height and returns TRUE without a zero-height check (`nvc0_exa.c:1080-1091`; `nouveau_copya0b5.c:30-83`). The installed 85B5 and 90B5 rectangle callbacks likewise emit the given height and return TRUE (`nouveau_copy85b5.c:31-86`; `nouveau_copy90b5.c:31-87`). `NVAccelM2MF()` dispatches to an enabled copy-engine callback first, then to the NVE0, NVC0, NV50, or NV04 path according to architecture (`nouveau_exa.c:47-76`). Thus the zero-progress result is not limited to the Tesla/NV50 fallback; it applies across the selected dispatch routes when they receive zero height.

**Selected caller and trigger:** `NouveauBitMap::PutImage` and `GetImage` select the GART helpers when `width * height >= 32 * 32` and `carddata->GART` is non-NULL (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_bitmapclass.c:25,433-465,492-531`). A 1,025-pixel-wide, one-row 32-bit transfer meets that threshold and has a 4,100-byte packed row; if the successfully allocated GART BO is smaller than that row, both helpers can enter the zero-line loop. Upload advances `y` by zero and cannot reduce `height`; download likewise leaves `height` unchanged. The `PutImage`/`GetImage` methods hold the engine and bitmap locks, and the transfer holds `gartsemaphore` for the duration of the helper call, so the non-progressing loop blocks later operations needing those locks. The GART allocation uses the device-reported GART size minus a 512-KiB reserve when below 12 MiB, and its return is not checked (`nouveau_hiddclass.c:710-726`); source alone does not establish that a particular supported GPU returns a BO in the failing size range.

**Affected configuration and confidence:** explicitly enabled Nouveau HIDD with successful GART setup that supplies a BO smaller than a requested row; the checked-in default package edge is commented out (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-29`). High confidence in zero-line/no-progress behavior across the inspected dispatch routes; medium confidence in practical reachability because actual small-GART allocation behavior is hardware/driver dependent. Reject a zero line count and fall back before issuing M2MF. No allocation failure, transfer, GPU operation, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd10558"></a>
<a id="gd10559"></a>
## GD10559 — Sound.datatype uses an uninitialized MaxPlaySamples result

In continuous AHI playback, `PlayerProcAHI()` declares `playsamples` without initialization and ignores the BOOL result of `AHI_GetAudioAttrs()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:3975-3987`). The value is then used in mix-rate scaling and playback-buffer sizing. AHI documents this query as fallible; its implementation returns FALSE if the audio-mode database, matching mode tags, or subdriver library cannot be obtained, and does not write the requested value on those failure paths (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/modeinfo.c:414-446,568-572`; the value is written only in the successful tag loop at `:507-509`). The configured AHI `AddAudioModes REFRESH` command removes existing IDs one by one and then reloads descriptors (`workbench/devs/AHI/AddAudioModes/AddAudioModes.c:163-207`; documented at `workbench/devs/AHI/Docs/ahiusr.texinfo:420-435`). AHI serializes each database operation, but there is no lock spanning `AHI_AllocAudio()` and the later `AHI_GetAudioAttrs()` call; a refresh can remove the selected ID in between, making `GetDBTagList()` fail.

**Trigger and consequence:** build the Sound datatype and AHI tools/device, then run `AddAudioModes REFRESH` concurrently with `SDTA_Continuous` playback during the interval after `AHI_AllocAudio()` succeeds but before `AHI_GetAudioAttrs()` queries the selected mode. If refresh has removed that ID before reloading it, the query returns FALSE without setting `playsamples`. The datatype nevertheless uses that indeterminate value for its two dynamic-sample buffer sizing. This can produce an invalid allocation size or make playback fail; size arithmetic can also wrap and leave the allocation shorter than the sample extents submitted or copied. Check the query result and abort or use a validated fallback before reading `playsamples`. **Confidence:** high that a failed lookup leaves the output untouched and the caller unconditionally consumes it; medium for the concurrent refresh window. The Sound datatype and AHI subsystem are optional configured targets; the Sound-to-AHI dependency edge is commented (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/mmakefile.src:4-13`; `workbench/devs/AHI/mmakefile.src:5-9,55`), while AHI's configured `SUBDIRS` includes `AddAudioModes` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Makefile.in:46`). No mode refresh, playback, allocation failure, or build was exercised. Source-only; see the [Sound datatype continuous-buffer caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-ahi-attribute-query-failure-gd10559).

## GD10558 — AROS VMM marks a nonresident page-table address as a table pointer

The AROS VMM startup initializes the private root-table entries for the managed range as `LOCUNUSED`/`PAGED_OUT` (`workbench/system/VMM/pagehandler.c:31-41`). When a fault has no resident table, `HandleMissingTable()` reaches `GetNewTable()`; the fresh-table path calls `InstallNewTable()` and then `MakeTableResident()` (`workbench/system/VMM/fault.c:525-555`). `MakeTableResident()` derives `TableStart` by interpreting the current root-table descriptor as a pointer-table address, then unconditionally passes that address to `MarkPage()` (`:196-218`). For an invalid/paged-out descriptor, this value is a paging marker, not a pointer to a live table. `MarkPage()` follows it as a pointer-table and page-table address and reads/writes the resulting entries without validating the descriptor (`workbench/system/VMM/mmu_table.c:1055-1105`).

The code that installs the page-table descriptors at `TableStart` and flushes them is excluded under `#if !defined(__AROS__)` (`fault.c:211-218`), while the `MarkPage()` call remains active. On AROS, `MarkAddress()`'s page-table construction body is likewise excluded and the function returns success (`mmu_table.c:145-239`). Thus the table fault path can both walk an address derived from a nonresident marker and return without installing a mapping that resolves the original fault.

**Trigger and consequence:** an explicitly built AROS VMM handler receives a user-mode page fault inside its configured range for an address whose root-level table is marked nonresident. `MakeTableResident()` can access descriptors through the paging-marker-derived address; that access can itself fault or update unrelated descriptor memory. Even if it returns, the AROS-compiled path has not installed the requested table entries, so retrying the original access can fault again. **Affected configuration:** Workbench-selected `workbench-system-vmm-handler` builds for i386/x86-64, whose manifest selects the common `fault.c` plus `x86/traphandler_x86.c`; reaching the page-fault path still requires launching VMM and a configured paging range. m68k is excluded from this caller claim because the current manifest omits its trap-entry assembly (GD6336). The AROS `AllocAddressRange()`/startup defect GD9419 leaves practical startup reachability uncertain, so this is a conditional source candidate for a handler that reaches the stated fault path, not a claim of normal boot impact. **Confidence:** high for the invalid marker-to-pointer use and the compiled-out table installation; operational reachability is uncertain. No VMM handler, fault, or MMU operation was run. Source-only; see the [AROS VMM table-fault recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#aros-vmm-table-fault-gd10558).

<a id="gd10562"></a>
## GD10562 — QuickPart writes beyond its DOS device-name buffer

When a leaf partition object is constructed, `QPPartition__OM_NEW()` scans DOS device entries with a handler task and startup message. It copies each BCPL device name into `char devNmBufTmp[64]` with `strncpy(..., 64)`, but then indexes that buffer using the full `AROS_BSTR_strlen()` result (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartition.c:317-331`). `dol_Name` is a BSTR (`compiler/include/dos/dosextens.h:418-419`); a 64-character BSTR is representable, and `MakeDosEntry()`/`AddDosEntry()` do not impose a smaller device-name limit (`rom/dos/makedosentry.c:55-78`; `rom/dos/adddosentry.c:70-105`). At length 63, the colon fits at index 63 but the terminator is written out of bounds at index 64. At length 64 or greater, both the colon and terminator are written out of bounds. Longer names also cause out-of-bounds writes. These writes occur before the `IsFileSystem()` check and before the later comparison against the selected disk's device, so any qualifying long device entry encountered during the scan reaches the bad indexing.

**Trigger and consequence:** explicitly build and run QuickPart with a disk whose leaf partition is being displayed, while the DOS device list contains a `DLT_DEVICE` entry with a handler task/startup and a valid name of 63 or more characters. Constructing the leaf partition scans that entry and writes beyond a stack buffer; adjacent stack state can be corrupted or the task can fault. **Affected configuration:** `workbench-tools-quickpart` selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`); produced-image installation is not inferred. **Confidence:** high for the out-of-bounds writes at the stated valid BSTR length; practical reachability depends on such a long handler entry being present during QuickPart's partition scan. Bound the length before copying and reserve space for the colon and NUL. No long device entry, QuickPart scan, or runtime memory failure was used; source-only.

<a id="gd10563"></a>
## GD10563 — QuickPart dereferences a failed selection-region allocation

When the partition object is the active selection, `QPPartition__MUIM_Draw()` constructs a nonempty inset clip rectangle from the object's margins, calls `NewRegion()`, and immediately passes the result to `OrRectRegion()` without checking it (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartition.c:527-565`). `NewRegion()` returns NULL when its allocation fails (`rom/graphics/newregion.c:56-68`). For an ordinary nonempty clip rectangle, `OrRectRegion()` reads `Reg->RegionRectangle` without a NULL check (`rom/graphics/orrectregion.c:62-65`). The partition container creates these partition objects while enumerating the opened partition table (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:213-218,428-440`), and the selected partition is drawn through the class's active-selection branch.

**Trigger and consequence:** QuickPart draws an active leaf partition while the graphics Region allocation fails. The subsequent union dereferences NULL and can fault the GUI task instead of skipping or recovering from the selection outline. **Affected configuration:** selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`); this establishes build selection, not produced-image installation. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation and callee dereference; occurrence requires the allocation failure and a valid, nonempty clip rectangle. Check `NewRegion()` and omit or safely recover from the outline if it fails. No allocation failure, partition drawing, or GUI operation was induced; source-only.

<a id="gd14946"></a>
## GD14946 — QuickPart displays an incorrect partition capacity

`QPPartition__OM_NEW()` calculates the displayed partition capacity as `(((de_HighCyl - de_LowCyl + 1) * de_Surfaces * de_BlocksPerTrack) - 1) * dg_SectorSize` (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartition.c:293`). The geometry members and intermediate arithmetic are `ULONG` (32-bit unsigned); assignment to `UQUAD adjustedsize` occurs only after this expression has already been evaluated. The displayed value therefore wraps modulo 2^32 for sufficiently large extents, even when the true byte count fits in `UQUAD`. For every nonempty extent, subtracting one before multiplying also makes the displayed byte count one sector smaller. `adjustedsize` is formatted into the capacity label at `:301-309`, which the application presents as the selected partition's capacity (`QP_ccApp.c:330-342`). That `sprintf()` uses `%u` for the `UQUAD` argument (`:300`); `%u` requires `unsigned int`, so this is also a variadic format/type mismatch with undefined behavior, and the emitted label can depend on the target ABI. This affects the display only; this path does not use the value to set partition boundaries or perform I/O.

**Trigger and consequence:** open QuickPart on a partition whose geometry exceeds the 32-bit intermediate range, or any nonempty partition for the one-sector undercount. The UI reports a wrapped or understated capacity; the `%u`/`UQUAD` mismatch can independently misformat it on affected ABIs. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable QuickPart target selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate; default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the arithmetic and display path. Widen each operand before multiplication, compute the inclusive sector count without subtracting one, and use a format specifier matching `UQUAD`. No partition scan, UI operation or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd10564"></a>
## GD10564 — QuickPart does not handle failed partition-node allocations

The partition container allocates its initial free-space node and immediately dereferences it without checking for NULL (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:663-679`). During partition insertion, `InsertPartEntry()` does test the `newPartNode` allocation, but continues after failure and unconditionally takes `&newPartNode->PCCN_Node` when `MUIM_Group_InitChange` succeeds (`:128-144,167-177`). The selected muimaster `Group__MUIM_InitChange()` returns TRUE for a valid group (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:855-864`), so a failed node allocation reaches the null dereference on the normal insertion path. A third allocation is silently treated as optional: when a post-partition free-space node allocation fails, the existing free node has already been shortened or marked for deletion, but the code skips adding the trailing free region (`QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:261-277,146-165,183-187`).

**Trigger and consequence:** memory allocation fails while constructing a partition container or inserting a partition, causing the GUI task to dereference NULL; if instead the trailing spacer allocation fails during insertion, the tail free region is omitted from the displayed partition model. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable QuickPart target selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate; default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for both NULL dereferences and the lost-tail state under the stated allocation failures. Abort construction/insertion and restore the prior free-space state whenever a required node allocation fails. No allocation failure, partition scan or GUI operation was induced; source-only.

<a id="gd10561"></a>
## GD10561 — BHFormat leaves the DOS device-list read lock held after a volume lookup fails

When Workbench starts BHFormat on a volume, the GUI calls `Info()` on the supplied lock, then acquires `LockDosList(LDF_DEVICES | LDF_READ)` and searches only `DLT_DEVICE` entries for a handler whose task matches the volume lock (`workbench/system/BHFormat/gui.c:516-542`). If no match exists, it reports `ERROR_DEVICE_NOT_MOUNTED` and jumps to `cleanup` without calling `UnLockDosList()` (`gui.c:538-541,713-722`). The RAM filesystem is a checked-in example: its startup creates and publishes a `DLT_VOLUME` node with `dol_Task = proc_port`, and does not add a `DLT_DEVICE` node (`rom/filesys/ram/commands.c:127-146`). Therefore opening BHFormat on `RAM:` reaches the unmatched-device branch after a successful `Info()`. `main()` then calls `FreeAll()` and returns, but Exec's shared semaphore has no automatic task-exit release: `LockDosList()` obtains the shared `di_DevLock`, `UnLockDosList()` is the release path, and `RemTask()` contains no DOS-list/semaphore cleanup (`rom/dos/lockdoslist.c:60-74`; `rom/dos/unlockdoslist.c:47-59`; `rom/exec/remtask.c:39-176`). The global device-list semaphore remains held in shared mode. Subsequent operations that request it exclusively, including `RemDosEntry()`, can block indefinitely (`rom/dos/remdosentry.c:56-84`).

**Trigger and consequence:** launch the Workbench GUI Format target on `RAM:`. Its handler answers `Info()`, but only a volume entry matches the task; BHFormat exits its GUI error path while retaining the DOS device-list read lock. A later DOS-list writer can then wait indefinitely. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-system-format`; its parent aggregate edge is commented, so default-image inclusion is not claimed (`workbench/system/BHFormat/mmakefile.src:4-15`). **Confidence:** high for the branch, RAM volume-only registration, process exit, and missing automatic shared-lock cleanup; the writer hang follows the exclusive semaphore contract. Unlock on every path after successful acquisition. No GUI, DOS-list operation, or runtime lock contention was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [BHFormat source-order review and lock-cleanup recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#bhformat-volume-handler-dos-list-lock-gd10561).

<a id="gd10560"></a>
## GD10560 — FTManager GUI installs to the wrong directory when a destination lock fails

`Init()` opens Codesets and initializes FreeType and the GUI classes, then stores `Lock("Fonts:", ACCESS_READ)` in `destdir` without checking the result; it returns success either way (`workbench/system/ftmanager/ftmanager.c:73-102`). `ftmanager_gui()` proceeds whenever `Init(TRUE)` returns nonzero (`:168-174`). The GUI Install notification calls `MUIM_FontInfo_WriteFiles` (`fontwindow_class.c:100-103`), whose handler passes a relative font basename and a NULL `target_dir` to `fiWriteFiles()` (`fontinfo_class.c:727-738`). That function sets the process current directory to `destdir`, then opens `<basename>.otag` and `<basename>.font` with `MODE_NEWFILE` (`:741-765,873-885`). If the initial `Fonts:` lock failed, `destdir` is NULL; `CurrentDir()` stores that NULL current directory (`rom/dos/currentdir.c:52-58`), and DOS resolves a relative `Open()` with no current-directory lock through `dl_Root->rn_BootProc` with a NULL lock (`rom/dos/open.c:191-203`). The later destination-change handler has the same state mismatch: it updates `destdir` only when `Lock(name, ACCESS_READ)` succeeds, but leaves the entered destination text unchanged when the lock fails (`ftmanager.c:301-315`). In that case, installs continue under the previous `destdir` (or the NULL-current-directory fallback) while the GUI displays the rejected path.

**Trigger and consequence:** in the selected FTManager GUI, either the initial `Lock("Fonts:")` fails or the user enters/selects a destination that `Lock(name, ACCESS_READ)` cannot open. A source font can be added from another available directory (`ftmanager.c:197-226,256-274`). If the user installs with the displayed destination unchanged, a failed initial lock sends relative output through the boot process's namespace; a failed destination change retains the prior `destdir`, so output goes to that previous location. With write access, either case creates or overwrites the `.otag` and `.font` files somewhere other than the destination shown or implied by the UI. This is distinct from GD6024's ignored output error: these opens can succeed at the wrong path. The CLI path supplies an explicit `target_dir` and is not included in this trigger. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected `workbench-system-ftmanager` GUI target (`workbench/system/ftmanager/mmakefile.src:4-13`; `workbench/system/mmakefile.src:10-14`; `workbench/mmakefile.src:7-30`). **Confidence:** high for the unchecked initial lock, stale `destdir` on failed change, and DOS fallback; successful misplaced output depends on the selected prior/boot directory allowing creation. Update the stored lock and displayed path atomically, and reject installation when the destination lock is invalid. No font was installed and no lock failure or file operation was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [FTManager selected-source review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#ftmanager-selected-target-source-pass-2026-10-22) and [destination-lock recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#L14661).

<a id="gd10565"></a>
## GD10565 — QuickPart leaves a disk-device open reference behind

`QPDisk__OM_NEW()` creates an I/O request and calls `OpenDevice()` to validate the discovered disk, then stores that still-open request in the new object without closing it (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:397-400,467-480`). The disk-discovery caller immediately invokes `MUIM_QPart_Disk_ScanForParts` on the object (`QP_FindDisks.c:235-240,257-273`). That method calls `OpenDevice()` again on the same request and, after identifying the drive, calls `CloseDevice()` only once (`QP_ccDisk.c:183-202`). AROS `OpenDevice()` dispatches the device Open vector on each successful call (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-120`); `CloseDevice()` dispatches one Close vector and invalidates the request's device field (`rom/exec/closedevice.c:67-86`). The subsequent object disposer deletes the request and message port without another close (`QP_ccDisk.c:593-608`). Thus the constructor's first open is left unmatched. QuickPart obtains its device name from each selected storage-unit object's `Hidd_StorageUnit_Device` attribute (`QP_FindDisks.c:99-117`); the selected AHCI unit returns `ahci.device` (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_unitclass.c:92-103`). AHCI's successful Open increments `sim_UseCount` and Close decrements it (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_init.c:200-251`); its unit cleanup waits for that count to reach zero (`rom/devs/ahci/ahci_cam_aros.c:200-210`). Therefore, when QuickPart scans and later disposes an AHCI-backed disk object, the unmatched constructor open can leave the AHCI unit-use count elevated and make its cleanup wait indefinitely. The ATA, SCSI, NVMe and VirtIO unit handlers also increment per-unit open counters on successful Open and decrement on Close (`ata_busclass.c:1060-1069` / `ata_init.c:363-378`; `scsi_busclass.c:1022-1031` / `scsi_init.c:351-366`; `nvme_busclass.c:703-711` / `nvme_init.c:192-207`; `virtio_busclass.c:292-297` / `virtio_init.c:167-175`), but no further consequence is claimed for those counters here. If the scan's second open fails, the initial open is likewise not closed. The I/O request is also deleted while its first device open remains outstanding.

**Trigger and consequence:** run the explicitly built QuickPart disk discovery on a disk whose device successfully opens in `QPDisk__OM_NEW()`. The immediate scan opens the same request a second time and closes once; later disposal frees the request/port without balancing the constructor open. This leaves one successful device open outstanding for each discovered disk object. **Affected configuration:** the active `AROS` Workbench target selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`; this establishes build selection, not produced-image installation (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34). **Confidence:** high for the unmatched successful Open/Close sequence; the exact resource retained depends on the selected device's Open/Close implementation. Close the validation open before publishing the object, or reuse it for the scan and close it exactly once before deleting the request. No disk device, QuickPart scan, or runtime operation was used; source-only.

<a id="gd10566"></a>
## GD10566 — QuickPart dereferences unchecked disk-scan allocations

The disk constructor passes the result of `CreateMsgPort()` directly to `CreateIORequest()`, then passes the result of `CreateIORequest()` to `OpenDevice()` without checking either (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:397-400`). `CreateMsgPort()` can return NULL when its memory or signal allocation fails (`rom/exec/createmsgport.c:50-74`), and `CreateIORequest()` returns NULL for a NULL port or failed allocation (`rom/exec/createiorequest.c:57-76`). `OpenDevice()` immediately dereferences its request argument before dispatch (`rom/exec/opendevice.c:92-98`), so either allocation failure reaches a NULL dereference. The constructor also has no cleanup of its temporary request or port on either later failure branch: a failed `OpenDevice()` sets `self = NULL` and falls through to return without deleting them (`QP_ccDisk.c:400,465-518`); if the device opens but `DoSuperNewTags()` fails, it likewise returns NULL without closing the device or deleting the request and port (`:400-465,518`). After a successful object construction, it also fails to check the `AllocVec()` result for `qpd_Disk_Handler` before `CopyMem()` uses it as the destination (`:467-480`). In the scan method, both the replacement copy of a pre-supplied drive name and the first drive-name buffer are allocated and then immediately passed to `strcpy()`, drive identification, or `sprintf()` without checking the result (`QP_ccDisk.c:187-200`); failure on the supplied-name branch also loses the original pointer when the field is overwritten.

**Trigger and consequence:** memory or signal allocation fails during QuickPart disk-object creation or its initial partition scan. Depending on the failure point, the GUI task can dereference NULL in `OpenDevice()`, `CopyMem()`, `strcpy()`, drive identification, or `sprintf()`. Separately, a failed device open leaks the allocated request and message port; a failed superclass construction after a successful open leaks those objects and leaves the device open reference outstanding. The supplied-name scan branch additionally loses its prior allocated string if the replacement allocation fails. **Affected configuration:** selected by the active `AROS` Workbench tools aggregate (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`); this establishes build selection, not produced-image installation. **Confidence:** high for each unchecked result and the corresponding callee dereference; occurrence requires the stated resource failure. Check each allocation before use, preserve the old name until replacement succeeds, and unwind any already-created request/port/device resources on constructor failure. No allocation failure, device open, partition scan, or GUI operation was induced; source-only.


<a id="gd10567"></a>
## GD10567 — QuickPart leaks disk-object strings and localization state on disposal

A successfully constructed disk object allocates and stores a private copy of its handler name (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:472-480`), a localization `Hook` and separate hook data (`:484-494`), and a drive-unit display string (`:508-513`). Its initial scan allocates or replaces the drive name and later allocates the verbose-name and capacity strings (`:187-200,241-258`). These pointers are retained in `QPDisk_DATA` (`QP_ccDisk.h:56-72`). `QPDisk__OM_DISPOSE()` only calls `DeleteIORequest()` and `DeleteMsgPort()` before delegating to its superclass; it never frees any of those allocations or the hook data (`QP_ccDisk.c:593-608`). QuickPart's normal exit calls `MUI_DisposeObject(AQPart_App)` (`QP_Main.c:720`); the selected MUI application/window/group/family disposal chain reaches each child object's `OM_DISPOSE` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:856-878`; `window.c:3091-3100`; `group.c:457-467`; `family.c:129-141`). Thus every disk object successfully constructed and scanned leaves its own allocations live after QuickPart tears the UI down; reopening QuickPart in the same system can accumulate these leaked allocations per enumerated disk.

**Trigger and consequence:** run the explicitly built QuickPart tool, allow one or more disks to be enumerated and scanned, then close the application normally. Recursive MUI teardown invokes the disk class disposer, which releases its I/O request and port but not its privately allocated handler/name/capacity strings, localization hook, or hook data. Memory use therefore grows by the surviving allocations for each disk object and can accumulate across repeated launches. The initial `MUIA_QPart_Disk_Name` may be borrowed from the storage unit, but the strings listed above are independently allocated by the disk class; the report does not claim ownership of that borrowed input. **Affected configuration:** the active `AROS` Workbench target selects `workbench-tools-quickpart`; this establishes build selection, not produced-image installation (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34). **Confidence:** high for the allocations, absent frees, and selected recursive teardown path. Release the class-owned allocations during disposal after child objects no longer need their text pointers. No QuickPart app, MUI object, or memory-pressure scenario was run; source-only.

<a id="gd10568"></a>
## GD10568 — MUI_MakeObject ignores the Menuitem_CopyStrings flag

`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui.h` declares `MUIO_Menuitem_CopyStrings` as a flag for `MUIO_Menuitem` (:142-143). The constructor forwards the supplied title and shortcut pointers directly to `MUIA_Menuitem_Title` and `MUIA_Menuitem_Shortcut`, decodes only the standard NewMenu check/toggle/disabled bits from `params[2]`, and leaves a `/* flags NYI */` comment without handling `MUIO_Menuitem_CopyStrings` (`mui_makeobject.c:489-499`). The Menuitem class stores those pointers directly in its instance data (`classes/menuitem.c:210-217`); no copy is made on construction or attribute update (`:340-349`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a client sets `MUIO_Menuitem_CopyStrings` and expects the constructor to retain copies of temporary or subsequently modified title/shortcut strings. The returned menu item instead borrows the original pointers, so later reads can observe changed text or access storage after its owner releases it. **Affected configuration:** applications using the selected muimaster library and this public flag. The repository-wide source search found no in-tree use of `MUIO_Menuitem_CopyStrings`, so no maintained caller is claimed as a trigger. **Confidence:** high that the declared flag is ignored and the strings are stored by pointer; medium that the flag promises copy ownership, inferred from its public name and declaration as a flag for this constructor. Implement the flag by copying and owning the strings, or remove/document it as unsupported. No menu operation or temporary-string lifetime was exercised; source-only; see the [caller and parameter-contract census](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mui-makeobject-maintained-caller-census-gd10568).

With `MUIO_MenustripNM_CommandKeyCheck` enabled, `CreateMenuString()` reads `label[1]` whenever the entry is not the `NM_BARLABEL` sentinel, but does not first check whether `nm_Label` is NULL (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_makeobject.c:82-92`). The MUI MiamiPanel caller passes that flag with an `appMenu` whose `MTITLE` and `MITEM` macros deliberately initialize `nm_Label` to NULL and carry catalog IDs in `nm_UserData` (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/MUI.MiamiPanel/muimiamipanel.h:432-435`; `Classes/muimiamipanel_class_app.c:65-90,139`). The caller uses the menu strip in application construction and then searches its user-data IDs to attach menu notifications (`:126-140,193-231`).

<a id="gd10571"></a>
## GD10571 — SMP-SmallPT does not handle startup task or port creation failures

The optional SMP-SmallPT application does not propagate failures through its startup handshakes. `main()` does not check its `CreateMsgPort()` result for `mainPort` (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/main.c:201`); if it is NULL, the later `WaitPort(mainPort)` reaches Exec's direct message-list dereference (`rom/exec/waitport.c:62-76`). `main()` also assigns the `NewCreateTask()` result for the renderer to `renderer`, discards it, then blocks in `WaitPort(mainPort)` for the renderer's welcome message (`main.c:242-255`). If renderer task creation fails while `mainPort` is valid, no task can send that message. Inside `Renderer()`, a failed `CreateMsgPort()` leaves the outer port-guarded initialization body skipped without notifying the main task (`renderer.c:64-66,117-125`). For each render worker, the renderer stores `NewCreateTask()`'s result but never checks it (`renderer.c:147-164`), then waits indefinitely for `workers[i].port` to become non-NULL (`:166-170`). A failed worker task never starts `RenderTile()` and cannot write the port. Even when a worker starts, `RenderTile()` writes the result of its own `CreateMsgPort()` through `myPort` and proceeds with startup signaling only inside the non-NULL port branch (`smallpt.cc:322-330,337-350`); port allocation failure therefore leaves the parent waiting on the unchanged NULL value.

**Trigger and consequence:** explicitly build and run SMP-SmallPT when creation of `mainPort`, the renderer task/port, any worker task, or a worker port fails. A NULL `mainPort` reaches `WaitPort()`'s port dereference; a failed renderer or worker startup can leave a parent waiting without timeout for a message or port that cannot be published. Workers created before a later worker failure may remain alive without the renderer completing its setup. The configured `RAYDEPTH` also scales each worker's requested stack (`renderer.c:59,162`), so a large setting can make worker task allocation fail more readily. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable `SMP-SmallPT` program target (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/mmakefile.src:28-30`); its edges from the SMP test aggregate are commented (`developer/debug/test/smp/mmakefile.src:5-6`), so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked task/port results and the startup waits/null port use; occurrence depends on the stated resource failure. Check each creation result and send an explicit startup-failure message that lets the parent unwind already created workers. No allocation failure, task, GUI, or build was exercised; source-only; see the [SMP-SmallPT startup failure pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#smp-smallpt-startup-failure-gd10571).

<a id="gd10572"></a>
## GD10572 — SMP-SmallPT leaks a public-screen lock when its window cannot open

`createMainWindow()` calls `LockPubScreen(0)` and, when it succeeds, reads the screen dimensions before trying `OpenWindowTags()` (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/main.c:37-53,61-76`). It calls `UnlockPubScreen()` only inside the successful-window branch (`:77-80`). If window construction fails, it returns NULL while retaining the lock. The caller then skips the `if (displayWin)` body and returns from `main()` without another unlock (`:192-195,443-444`). `LockPubScreen()` explicitly pins a public screen until the matching unlock (`rom/intuition/lockpubscreen.c:26-31,52-65`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run the explicitly buildable SMP-SmallPT program when `LockPubScreen()` succeeds but `OpenWindowTags()` fails, for example because window construction cannot allocate its resources. The failed launch leaves the public screen locked after the application exits, potentially preventing its closure or lifecycle transition. **Affected configuration:** the optional `SMP-SmallPT` target (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/mmakefile.src:28-30`); it is not selected by the commented parent test aggregate. **Confidence:** high for the successful lock, window-failure return, and missing release; occurrence depends on window construction failure after screen lock. Unlock the screen on both window-open outcomes. No window or allocation failure was induced; source-only.

<a id="gd10573"></a>
## GD10573 — SMP-SmallPT leaves timer.device open and calls GetSysTime after a failed open

`main()` creates `timerPort` and `tr` before its resource checks, then opens `timer.device`; it assigns the local `TimerBase` only when `OpenDevice()` succeeds, but does not handle a nonzero return (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/main.c:103-105,118-139`). The program later calls `GetSysTime()` after startup and while updating the window title (`:277,352`). The selected vector implementation dereferences its `TimerBase` argument through `GetTimerBase()` (`rom/timer/getsystime.c:58-61`), so a failed open leaves the base NULL for those calls. On the normal success path, the application closes its window and frees image resources but never calls `CloseDevice(tr)`, `DeleteIORequest(tr)`, or `DeleteMsgPort(timerPort)` (`main.c:409-414`); the timer open reference and these public allocations remain outstanding. Early `OpenResource()` or request-allocation returns likewise do not unwind any previously created timer port/request (`:118-139`).

**Trigger and consequence:** explicitly build and run SMP-SmallPT when opening `timer.device` fails; a later `GetSysTime()` call dispatches through a NULL base and can fault. On ordinary successful runs, each exit leaves the timer device open and its request/port allocated. **Affected configuration:** the optional SMP-SmallPT executable target (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/mmakefile.src:28-30`). **Confidence:** high for the open-result handling, direct-base vector behavior, and missing success-path close/free; failure depends on timer-device availability and the leak occurs on normal exit. Abort startup if the timer open fails, then close and delete all timer resources on every exit path. No device open, application run, or build was performed; source-only.

<a id="gd10574"></a>
## GD10574 — SMP-SmallPT dereferences a failed presentation RastPort allocation

After opening its window, `main()` calls `CreateRastPort()` and immediately writes `outBMRastPort->BitMap` without checking the result (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/main.c:224-225`). `CreateRastPort()` returns NULL when its `AllocMem(sizeof(struct RastPort), MEMF_ANY)` fails (`compiler/arossupport/createrastport.c:47-53`). Thus a presentation-RastPort allocation failure in this selected startup path reaches a null member write before the renderer task is started.

**Trigger and consequence:** explicitly build and run SMP-SmallPT when the display window opens but `CreateRastPort()` cannot allocate its RastPort. Startup dereferences NULL and fails instead of closing the window and releasing the already allocated bitmap. **Affected configuration:** the optional `SMP-SmallPT` executable target (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/mmakefile.src:28-30`). **Confidence:** high for the nullable helper contract and immediate dereference; occurrence requires the stated memory failure. Check the returned pointer and unwind the bitmap/window resources on failure. No allocation failure, GUI operation, or build was induced; source-only.

<a id="gd10575"></a>
## GD10575 — SMP-SmallPT renderer dereferences failed workspace allocations

After receiving the GUI startup message, `Renderer()` allocates the tile-work array, the shared message pool, and the worker array without checking any result (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/renderer.c:125,134,141`). With a positive tile count, it immediately writes every `workPackages[i]` (`:129-132`). For a positive CPU count, it indexes `messages[i]` while populating the message pool (`:134-138`) and later indexes `workers[i]` while creating workers (`:147-155`). `AllocMem()` may return NULL; each failed allocation therefore reaches a dereference before the renderer sends the GUI's startup acknowledgement. `main()` is already waiting for that acknowledgement on `mainPort` (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/main.c:271-273`), so the renderer task can fail and strand the GUI during startup.

The main task also ignores failure to allocate the shared pixel buffer (`main.c:227`), immediately passes it to `WritePixelArray()` (`:229-234`), and includes it in the worker startup message (`:259-267`). A worker later writes rendered pixels through that pointer (`smallpt.cc:441-445`). Each `RenderTile()` worker dereferences `syncPort` with `FreeSignal()` without checking the allocation result (`smallpt.cc:322-334`); its `Vec` tile buffer and 20-entry message pool are also allocated unchecked and indexed (`:328,340-342`). The tile buffer is written during rendering (`:408-432`). These failures can stop a worker before it sends work, or later during rendering, after the renderer has accepted its published port as ready (`:330,166-171`).

**Trigger and consequence:** explicitly build and run SMP-SmallPT with a nonzero render size and CPU count when allocation of a renderer array, shared pixel buffer, worker `syncPort`, tile buffer, or message pool fails. The affected task dereferences NULL or sends a missing buffer into the rendering path. A worker can stop before sending work or while rendering after its port has been published; startup or shutdown can then wait for a message that cannot arrive, and earlier resources/tasks are not unwound. **Affected configuration:** the optional SMP-SmallPT executable target (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/mmakefile.src:28-30`), not selected by the commented parent aggregate. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocations, immediate dereferences/indexing, and missing buffer validation; occurrence depends on memory exhaustion at one of these allocations. Check each allocation, unwind initialized arrays/workers, and report startup failure before publishing readiness. No allocation failure, renderer task, GUI, or build was induced; source-only; see the [SMP-SmallPT full target pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#smp-smallpt-full-target-pass-gd10571-gd10575).


<a id="gd10576"></a>
## GD10576 — SMP-SmallPT RAYDEPTH can overflow the worker stack-size calculation

`main()` parses `RAYDEPTH/N` into a `LONG` and only clamps values below 2 (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/main.c:85,152-157`). `ReadArgs()` converts `/N` values using `StrToLong()`; that routine explicitly does not check whether the number is too large (`rom/dos/readargs.c:843-845,879-881`; `rom/dos/strtolong.c:35-37`). `Renderer()` calculates `ULONG workerStack = AROS_STACKSIZE + maximal_ray_depth * 1000` with signed `int` arithmetic before conversion to `ULONG` (`renderer.c:59`). For x86-64, `AROS_STACKSIZE` is 40960 (`arch/x86_64-all/include/aros/cpu.h:176`): at `RAYDEPTH=2147443`, the mathematical sum is 2147483960, 313 greater than `INT_MAX`; the signed expression overflows. The value is then passed to `NewCreateTask()` as `TASKTAG_STACKSIZE` (`renderer.c:155-163`), so the requested stack size is not represented reliably and may be invalid or too small, with later stack exhaustion possible depending on compiler/build behavior. Larger valid `LONG` values also overflow the multiplication.

**Trigger and consequence:** explicitly run the optional SMP-SmallPT target with `RAYDEPTH` at or above the x86-64 overflow boundary. The stack-size expression has signed overflow, so C behavior is undefined and the worker stack request may be corrupted; a resulting worker creation failure also reaches the unchecked startup wait described in GD10571. **Affected configuration:** SMP-SmallPT on x86-64; the threshold depends on the target's `AROS_STACKSIZE` and integer model. **Confidence:** high for the missing upper bound and signed-overflow condition on x86-64; downstream stack/failure symptoms depend on compiler behavior and allocation outcome. Bound the accepted depth and calculate the stack size in a checked unsigned/wider type before narrowing. No target execution, stack allocation, or build was performed; source-only; see the [SMP-SmallPT full target pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#smp-smallpt-full-target-pass-gd10571-gd10575).


<a id="gd10577"></a>
## GD10577 — SMP-SmallPT applies its minimum HEIGHT clamp before parsing HEIGHT

`main()` tries to enforce a 128-pixel minimum for `req_height` before it reads the `HEIGHT/N` argument (`developer/debug/test/smp/smp-smallpt/main.c:176-181`). At that point `req_height` is still its initialized zero, so the check does nothing for a supplied value. `createMainWindow()` accepts any nonzero requested height below its normal screen-derived height, then rounds it down to a multiple of 32 (`main.c:44-47`). As a result, values such as `HEIGHT=127` produce an inner height of 96, and values from 1 through 31 round to zero and may cause window creation to fail or choose implementation-defined/default sizing behavior. This can also leave the renderer with a window too short for the intended minimum tile/render area.

**Trigger and consequence:** run the explicitly buildable SMP-SmallPT program with a `HEIGHT` value below 128 and below the normal screen-derived height. The requested minimum is not applied; the resulting height is reduced to the preceding multiple of 32 (or zero), affecting the window and rendering dimensions. **Affected configuration:** the optional SMP-SmallPT target on systems where a public screen is available and the requested height is below the computed default. **Confidence:** high that the clamp runs before assignment and that the window helper rounds down; whether zero height causes open failure or fallback dimensions depends on Intuition behavior. Parse the height first, then clamp it before calling `createMainWindow()`. No window or rendering operation was run; source-only; see the [SMP-SmallPT full target pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#smp-smallpt-full-target-pass-gd10571-gd10575).

<a id="gd10578"></a>
## GD10578 — WinGDI keyboard HIDD uses an incompatible callback function type

The WinGDI keyboard instance stores its callback as `InputIrqCallBack_t` (`arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/gdi.h:73-76`), whose second argument is `InputIrqData_t` (`rom/hidds/input/include/input.h:16,33`). But `GDIKbd__Root__New()` casts the tag value to `VOID (*)(APTR, UWORD)` before assigning it to that field (`arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/wingdi_kbdclass.c:133`). These function-pointer types are incompatible: `UWORD` is a 16-bit integer, while the callback data is a pointer. The selected event path later calls the correctly typed field with `&kEvt` (`wingdi_kbdclass.c:78`), so the mismatch is at callback installation rather than the event invocation. A compiler that diagnoses incompatible function-pointer assignment will reject this source when warnings are errors. AROS defaults to `-Wall -Werror` when supported (`configure.in:1169-1178`; compiler feature detection in `config/features.in:887-901`). Store the tag value as `InputIrqCallBack_t` directly instead of casting through the obsolete scalar prototype.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** a MinGW32 build compiling the selected `kernel-hidd-wingdi` module (`arch/all-mingw32/hidd/wingdi/mmakefile.src:4,9-11`) with a compiler that supports the default warning flags; the MinGW32 boot package lists `wingdi` in its HIDD set (`arch/all-mingw32/boot/mmakefile.src:9-14`). **Consequence:** the incompatible function-pointer assignment is diagnosed and, under default `-Werror`, prevents the keyboard HIDD translation unit and module from building. No runtime callback failure is claimed from this cast because the stored field is subsequently called with the pointer-based typedef. **Confidence:** high for the source-level type mismatch; compiler diagnostic and build outcome were not tested. Source-only.

<a id="gd10579"></a>
## GD10579 — AmigaVideo compositor accepts a missing display-rethink task

`AmigaVideoCompositor::Root::New()` stores the result of `NewCreateTask()` in `compdata->housekeeper` but does not check it; its later creation-failure branch checks only `dodispose`, which is set for attribute-base or display-object failure (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_compositorclass.c:66-110`). Exec documents that `NewCreateTaskA()` returns NULL on failure and frees its partial task allocation (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:188-191,249-270`). The compositor can therefore be returned without the worker. Later, when `gfx_vblank_attachbm()` encounters an interlaced bitmap while the display is not interlaced, it signals `csd->svcTask` only if non-NULL and returns FALSE (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_chipset.c:1327-1335`). The worker is the only checked-in caller of `RethinkDisplay()` in this HIDD (`amigavideo_compositorclass.c:502-525`). In this state the requested rebuild is not queued and the bitmap is not attached by that attempt; compositor setup has already reported success.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected m68k Amiga AmigaVideo HIDD, if compositor housekeeper task allocation fails and a later display-stack update needs the non-interlaced-to-interlaced rethink path. **Consequence:** the display-stack update remains incomplete; the compositor should fail construction or otherwise retain/retry the rethink request when no worker exists. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked nullable task and missing request path; the user-visible display consequence is conditional on the described mixed-interlace transition. No task-creation failure, display update, or hardware operation was induced; source-only.


<a id="gd10580"></a>
## GD10580 — Vulkan-Hpp latency timing helpers return unused timing slots

The optional Vulkan-Hpp vector helpers for `Device::getLatencyTimingsNV()` (default and custom allocator overloads) and RAII `SwapchainKHR::getLatencyTimingsNV()` first query a count with `pTimings == NULL`, resize the result vector to that capacity, then call `vkGetLatencyTimingsNV()` again with the vector as output storage (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:29425-29439,29448-29463`; `vulkan_raii.hpp:27059-27072`). The Vulkan contract says the second call overwrites `timingCount` with the number of timing records actually written; the wrappers return the vector without resizing it to that updated count ([`VkGetLatencyMarkerInfoNV`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkGetLatencyMarkerInfoNV.html)). `LatencyTimingsFrameReportNV` value-initializes its timestamp fields, so any allocated tail not written by the second call is returned as zero-valued records (`vulkan_structs.hpp:54437-54505`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the maximum count from the preliminary query exceeds the number actually written by the fill call. The helpers then return a vector whose size overstates the number of valid timing reports; callers can mistake default-initialized tail entries for real frame timing data. The specification permits the output count to be the number actually written, and the two calls are separate, so equality is not guaranteed. **Affected configuration:** downstream C++ clients using the optional copied Vulkan-Hpp headers and `VK_NV_low_latency2`; no maintained in-tree C++ caller of these helpers was found. **Confidence:** high for the missing resize and count-output contract; occurrence depends on the second call reporting fewer records than the first call's capacity. Resize the vector to the `timingCount` returned by the fill call. No timing query, Vulkan call, build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only; see the [latency timing count recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-low-latency-timing-result-count-gd10580).

<a id="gd10581"></a>
## GD10581 — Nouveau GH100 recovery modes use fixed board GPIO/UART addresses across targets

The AROS GH100 GSP recovery code dispatches `NvGfwReset` mode bit 8 to `gh100_gsp_aros_perst()` and bit 32 to `gh100_gsp_aros_ec_cycle()` after GFW boot times out (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/gsp/gh100.c:681-695`). Those helpers access fixed physical addresses `0x20200000` and `0x20310000` (`:298,420`), with no architecture or platform capability check. `compat_map_mmio()` maps the address only on ARM/AArch64/RISC-V, but returns the same numerical address directly on other targets (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_mmio.c:14-25`). The optional Nouveau target has selectable i386, x86-64, and RISC-V64 aliases (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:22-28`); the two recovery modes are compiled into the selected GH100 source on all of them.

**Trigger and consequence:** an operator supplies `NvGfwReset` with bit 8 or bit 32 on a supported GH100 configuration where GFW boot times out, but the machine does not implement the board-specific GPIO or embedded-controller UART at those addresses. The helper then performs MMIO reads/writes through an unverified physical address: the access can fault or reach unrelated mapped memory/device registers, and the recovery sequence cannot perform its intended reset. This is conditional on both the explicit recovery option and a nonmatching hardware map; mode 0 is the default. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable optional `nouveau.hidd` on its i386, x86-64, or RISC-V64 targets when those reset bits are selected; default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** medium-low. The cross-target calls and fixed addresses are direct, but this source does not document which board owns the addresses or whether the option is intended to be used only there. Gate these modes on a verified platform mapping/capability and reject them elsewhere. No device, reset, MMIO access, build, or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

#### GD10233 addendum — ARM striped-render-pass semaphore proxy narrows its element count

`RenderPassStripeSubmitInfoARM`'s enhanced constructor and `setStripeSemaphoreInfos()` cast `ArrayProxyNoTemporaries::size()` to `uint32_t` while retaining the original semaphore-info pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:144024-144029,144060-144068`). The extension declaration permits this structure in `CommandBufferSubmitInfo::pNext` (`vulkan.hpp:16421-16427`); `SubmitInfo2` is forwarded through enhanced `Queue::submit2()` to `vkQueueSubmit2` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:151282-151681`; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:7776-7802`). The Vulkan contract defines the count as the pStripeSemaphoreInfos array length and requires it to equal the total stripe count for non-resuming render-pass instances recorded in the submitted command buffer ([ARM render-pass-striped specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/features/latest/features/proposals/VK_ARM_render_pass_striped.html), [command-buffer submit reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkCommandBufferSubmitInfo.html)).

**Trigger and consequence:** an enhanced-mode caller supplies a stripe-semaphore proxy larger than `UINT32_MAX` and chains the wrapper through a command-buffer submit record.
