<a id="gd14327"></a>
## GD14327 — VESA framebuffer fallback keeps the last PCI display match

When bootloader `VesaInfo.FrameBuffer` is zero, `initVesaGfxHW()` calls `Find_PCI_Card()` (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx_support.c:64-67`). The helper enumerates PCI devices matching only interface 0, display class `0x03`, and VGA subclass `0x00` (`:250-264`). Its callback maps each match's BAR0 and assigns the result directly to the same `sd->framebuffer` field (`:205-223`). The selected PCI `EnumDevices` implementation walks the entire device list and invokes the callback for every match; it has no stop-on-success return (`rom/hidds/pci/pciclass.c:421-445`). Thus a later matching device replaces the earlier mapping, regardless of which adapter supplied the boot mode.

The bootloader can publish a zero framebuffer address when the VBE mode-information version is below 2.0; it sets `FrameBuffer` from `phys_base` only for version 2.0 or newer (`rom/bootloader/bootloader_init.c:165-196`). VESAGfx then clears the selected buffer using the boot mode's height and pitch and later copies display updates through it (`vesagfx_support.c:96-100,119-180,291-302`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a PC boots a VESA graphics mode with `VesaInfo.FrameBuffer == NULL` and has two or more PCI devices matching the helper's display/VGA filter, with a later enumerated device different from the adapter whose VESA mode is active. Initialization retains the later device's BAR0, so clearing and refresh writes target the wrong adapter's aperture; the active display may remain stale, and writes may affect unrelated BAR0 state. **Affected configuration:** the build-selected i386-PC or x86-64-PC VESAGfx path when its zero-address PCI fallback is taken; both boot manifests list VESAGfx (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:75`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:68`). No in-tree machine inventory establishes that this multi-display/old-VBE combination is currently deployed. **Confidence:** high for enumerating every matching device and retaining the last BAR0 mapping; medium for practical manifestation because it requires the stated boot mode and multiple matching adapters. Associate the boot framebuffer with a specific PCI device or reject ambiguous fallback instead of overwriting the selected mapping. No VESA boot, PCI enumeration, mapping, display write, or build was performed; source-only.

## GD14328 — Reentrant `DoGadgetMethodA()` calls overwrite the outer dispatch state

<a id="gd14328"></a>

`DoGadgetMethodA()` uses the single `IntuitionBase::DoGadgetMethodGI` and `DoGadgetMethodRP` records for every invocation (`rom/intuition/intuition_intern.h:591-592`). It obtains `GadgetLock`, clears and rebuilds the shared GadgetInfo with `SetupGInfo()`, and initializes the shared RastPort before dispatching the custom method (`rom/intuition/dogadgetmethoda.c:95-113`; `rom/intuition/gadgets.c:684-727`). For `GM_RENDER`, it places pointers to those shared records into the callback message and calls `Custom_DoMethodA()` while still holding the lock (`dogadgetmethoda.c:130-162`). Exec semaphores permit recursive acquisition by their owning task (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:94-109`), so a custom method can synchronously invoke `DoGadgetMethodA()` again. The nested call's `SetupGInfo()` zeroes and repopulates the same GadgetInfo, and `InitRastPort()` resets the same RastPort; the nested call then returns without restoring either record. The outer callback's message therefore still points to records now describing the nested gadget/window, and the outer RastPort's layer/bitmap may have changed. This is separate from GD10531's shared cross-layer clip/scroll setup: the dispatch-context overwrite also applies when nested calls use the same layer.

**Trigger and consequence:** a custom gadget method dispatched by `DoGadgetMethodA()` synchronously calls `DoGadgetMethodA()` for another gadget and then resumes using its original `gpr_GInfo` or `gpr_RPort`. Those pointers now expose the nested call's state, so subsequent outer drawing or gadget-context reads can use the wrong bitmap, layer, screen, or gadget metadata. **Affected configuration:** Intuition builds when a custom/public gadget method reenters this vector; no checked-in in-tree reentrant caller was established, so the trigger is conditional on external/custom clients. **Confidence:** high for shared-state overwrite and recursive lock behavior; medium for visible consequences, which depend on the callback's post-reentry use. Use per-invocation state or explicitly reject/guard reentry. No gadget method, render, or build was run; source-only. See the [reentrant dispatch trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#dogadgetmethoda-reentrant-dispatch-state-gd14328-added-2026-11-02).


<a id="gd14329"></a>
## GD14329 — `ObtainDataTypeA()` ignores `DTA_GroupID` for a named RAM datatype

`ObtainDataTypeA()` documents `DTA_GroupID` as the group to match (`workbench/libs/datatypes/obtaindatatypea.c:45-52`) and reads it into `grpid` (`:88-89`). For `DTST_RAM` with a NULL handle, enumeration filters each candidate by that group (`:175-187`). For a non-NULL RAM handle, however, the function looks up the supplied datatype name and returns that node directly without comparing its `dth_GroupID` to `grpid` (`:188-196`); it then increments `OpenCount` and returns it (`:218-222`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a caller invokes the public `ObtainDataTypeA(DTST_RAM, name, attrs)` API with both a datatype name and a nonzero `DTA_GroupID` that disagrees with the named datatype. The function returns and opens the mismatched datatype instead of rejecting it or returning no match, so the caller can proceed under an incompatible group assumption. **Affected configuration:** any build including datatypes.library; consequence requires a direct public API caller supplying this combination. The selected `NewDTObjectA()` RAM-plus-group path maps the group to its built-in name and does not establish this mismatch, and a repository search found no direct in-tree `ObtainDataTypeA(DTST_RAM, ...)` caller. **Confidence:** high for the inconsistent branch behavior against the function's documented filter; caller-visible impact is conditional on an external or future caller using both selectors. Apply the same group check to named lookup or define/document name selection as overriding the group. No datatype query or build was run; source-only; see the [named-RAM group-filter caller recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#obtaindatatypea-named-ram-group-filter-gd14329).


<a id="gd14330"></a>
## GD14330 — Datatypes file probe widens a failed `Read()` into an out-of-bounds scan length

`ExamineLock()` allocates `CheckArray` with `CheckSize + 1` bytes, where the initial `CheckSize` is at least 64, then assigns the `Read()` result directly to the `UWORD CheckSize` variable (`workbench/libs/datatypes/helpfuncs.c:232-244`). DOS `Read()` returns a signed `LONG` and documents `-1` on error (`rom/dos/read.c:32-43,50-76`). If the read fails, conversion to `UWORD` yields 65,535, which passes the `> 0` test. The function then forwards that length to `ExamineData()` (`helpfuncs.c:274-282`); its classifier reads the supplied length while scanning `CheckArray` (`:434-505`). When the initial probe size is below 65,534 bytes (the normal 64-byte case), the allocation is smaller than the resulting 65,535-byte scan, so the error path reads past the probe buffer.

**Trigger and consequence:** a file opens successfully but its probe read returns `-1` (for example, a filesystem or device read error), its initial probe size is below 65,534 bytes, and its initial bytes do not take the IFF-specific shortcut. `ExamineLock()` interprets the error as a 65,535-byte successful read and the datatype classifier scans beyond the allocated buffer, causing invalid memory reads and potentially a fault or incorrect classification. **Affected configuration:** any target using the selected `workbench/libs/datatypes` implementation for `DTST_FILE`; exact device/filesystem conditions that produce a read error are environment-dependent. **Confidence:** high for signed-to-unsigned narrowing and the downstream scan bound; triggering requires `Read()` to return its documented error value. Keep the read result in a signed `LONG`, reject negative results, and only then convert a positive byte count. No read error or datatype query was induced; source-only; see the [file-probe read-result caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#datatypes-file-probe-read-result-gd14330).
<a id="gd14331"></a>
## GD14331 — m68kemu `GetRPAttrsA()` writes native-width results into 32-bit guest slots

The generated Graphics thunk clones the guest TagItem list and maps pointer-valued `ti_Data` entries into host addresses inside the guest memory buffer (`rom/m68kemu/m68kemu_thunks_gen.c:4238-4245`; `m68kemu_shadow.c:139-163`; `m68kemu_intern.h:108-112`). It then calls native `GetRPAttrsA()`. That implementation treats `ti_Data` as a pointer to an output cell and stores each result through `IPTR *`, explicitly documenting that outputs are IPTR-sized (`rom/graphics/getrpattrsa.c:30-35,95-119`). In the 64-bit m68kemu build, native `IPTR` is 64 bits (`compiler/include/aros/cpu.h:88-90`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:82-86`), while the emulated m68k caller provides 32-bit result storage and the thunk reads each guest TagItem as 32-bit tag/data words (`m68kemu_shadow.c:152-160`; `rom/m68kemu/INTERNALS.md:306`). A normal four-byte output variable is therefore overwritten by an eight-byte store; a pointer-valued result also cannot be represented in the guest's 32-bit slot without an explicit guest-pointer translation.

**Trigger and consequence:** an emulated m68k program calls Graphics `GetRPAttrsA()` with an output tag such as `RPTAG_APen` whose `ti_Data` points to a four-byte guest variable. The getter stores the requested value plus four bytes into adjacent guest memory; `RPTAG_Font` also returns a native host pointer rather than a guest/shadow pointer. **Affected configuration:** the optional x86-64 `m68kemu.library` target (`rom/m68kemu/mmakefile.src:8-10,14-17,25-44`); its package edge is disabled by default, but the library target is explicitly buildable. **Confidence:** high for the host/guest width mismatch, mapped output address and native write width; caller reachability depends on guest software using this graphics API. Use a guest-width output marshaller and translate pointer-valued results back into guest/shadow handles. No emulator, guest program, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="gd14333"></a>
## GD14333

**Reaction Label ignores the documented pen mapping for its embedded image.** The public Reaction image header defines `LABEL_Mapping` as a `UWORD *` “Pen mapping for next image” (`compiler/include/images/label.h:40`). `label_set()` accepts the tag but only stores the pointer in `ld_Mapping` (`workbench/classes/reaction/label/labelclass.c:57-59`); `OM_GET` returns that stored pointer (`:305-307`). The complete class body contains no read of `ld_Mapping`. When the label is drawn, it calls `DrawImageState()` with the child image, state and `DrawInfo`, but does not apply the stored map (`:376-388`). A repository-wide exact-symbol search found no in-tree caller setting `LABEL_Mapping`; the class is an explicitly buildable module target (`workbench/classes/reaction/label/mmakefile.src:1-15`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a client builds or sets a Reaction Label with both `LABEL_Mapping` and a child image whose pen indices require remapping. Drawing the label ignores the requested mapping and renders the child image with the mapping available from the image/DrawInfo path, which can produce incorrect colors. **Affected configuration:** builds that include `workbench-classes-reaction-label`; caller-visible effect requires a client to use the documented tag and an image for which the mapping changes rendered pens. **Confidence:** high that the tag is accepted but never consumed and omitted from the image-draw call; medium that the current implementation violates the intended “next image” contract, since no checked-in caller or fuller in-tree contract clarifies the expected mapping semantics. Apply the mapping to the child image's draw operation according to the Reaction image contract, or remove/deprecate the unsupported attribute if it is not intended to be honored. No image was drawn and no build was run; source-only; see the [LABEL_Mapping contract recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#label-mapping-pen-map-contract-gd14333).


<a id="gd14334"></a>
## GD14334

**Reaction Label does not implement the public `LABEL_Key` getter.** The public header defines `LABEL_Key` as a `UWORD` OM_GET attribute for the underscore key (`compiler/include/images/label.h:42`). `Label__OM_GET()` handles `LABEL_Underscore` and other label attributes but has no `LABEL_Key` case, so it delegates the query to its ImageClass superclass (`workbench/classes/reaction/label/labelclass.c:212-318`). ImageClass returns FALSE for attributes outside its recognized `IA_*` set (`rom/intuition/imageclass.c:162-205`); therefore a `LABEL_Key` query fails and does not write the caller's output storage. A repository-wide search found no in-tree `LABEL_Key` query, so impact is limited to external users of the explicitly buildable Reaction class (`workbench/classes/reaction/label/mmakefile.src:1-18`). **Confidence:** high that the documented attribute is unimplemented; caller impact requires a client to query it and rely on the documented result.

**Trigger and consequence:** a client calls `GetAttr(LABEL_Key, label, &key)` or sends the equivalent `OM_GET` to a Reaction Label object. The query reports failure instead of returning the underscore key described by the public API, so clients cannot obtain the shortcut key from the label object. **Affected configuration:** builds that include `workbench-classes-reaction-label`; caller-visible impact requires a client to query this public attribute. **Confidence:** high that the attribute is declared but unhandled and that the superclass returns FALSE for it; no maintained caller or more detailed in-tree key-extraction contract was found. Implement `LABEL_Key` using the documented underscore-key semantics, or correct the public declaration if the attribute is intentionally unsupported. No object query or build was run; source-only; see the [LABEL_Key OM_GET contract recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#label-key-om-get-contract-gd14334).


<a id="gd14338"></a>
## GD14338 — TensorDescriptionARM::setStrides replaces the tensor dimension count

`TensorDescriptionARM::setStrides()` assigns `dimensionCount` from `strides_.size()` while updating only `pStrides` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:42605-42611`). This is inconsistent with the enhanced constructor, which derives `dimensionCount` from `dimensions_.size()` and treats an empty strides proxy as “no stride array” (`:42524-42546`). For proxies larger than `UINT32_MAX`, its cast is also covered by the general size-narrowing finding GD10233; GD14338 records the distinct wrong-field update that breaks ordinary valid setter sequences. The Vulkan contract requires `dimensionCount > 0`, requires `pDimensions` to point to `dimensionCount` values, and permits `pStrides == NULL`; when strides are non-null they must also cover that same dimension count ([VkTensorDescriptionARM reference](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/man/html/VkTensorDescriptionARM.html)).

**Trigger and consequence:** a client creates a valid description with nonempty dimensions and no strides, then calls `setStrides({})` to clear/retain the optional null stride array. The setter changes `dimensionCount` to zero but leaves `pDimensions` unchanged. Passing this description to `Device::createTensorARM()` forwards it through `TensorCreateInfoARM::pDescription` to `vkCreateTensorARM()` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:42709-42718,42738-42742`; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:27142-27155`), yielding an invalid zero-dimensional description, so creation can fail validation or be rejected by the implementation. Other nonmatching stride lengths likewise replace the dimension count with a value that no longer describes `pDimensions`. `TensorDescriptionARM` is also permitted in `DataGraphPipelineResourceInfoARM` and `DataGraphPipelineConstantARM` chains (`vulkan.hpp:16842-16851`), so the same bad state can reach data-graph pipeline creation. **Affected configuration:** downstream C++ consumers of the optional copied Vulkan-Hpp `VK_ARM_tensors` / `VK_ARM_data_graph` APIs; no non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the setter mismatch, invalid resulting count, and native forwarding; no tensor or data-graph operation was run. Keep `dimensionCount` tied to `dimensions` when changing optional strides, and reject any nonempty stride array whose length differs from the existing dimension count. Source-only.

<a id="gd14339"></a>
## GD14339 — Vulkan-Hpp display-property comparison and hashing dereference a null name

`DisplayPropertiesKHR` defaults `displayName` to null and its enhanced constructor also accepts a null name (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:45256-45270,45364-45375`). Its equality operator compares pointer identity first, then calls `strcmp(displayName, rhs.displayName)` whenever the pointers differ (`:45340-45345`); this is the non-reflection implementation, since `VULKAN_HPP_USE_REFLECT` selects tuple equality. The C++20 three-way comparison likewise calls `strcmp` when the pointers differ (`:45317-45324`). Therefore, when reflection is disabled, comparing wrappers with the same `display` but a default-null name and a non-null name reaches `strcmp` with a null argument; passing a null pointer to `strcmp` has undefined behavior. Separately, the `std::hash<DisplayPropertiesKHR>` specialization iterates `displayName` through its terminating NUL without checking for null (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_hash.hpp:5285-5301`); hashing a default-constructed wrapper dereferences null. `hash<DisplayProperties2KHR>` hashes its nested `displayProperties` and reaches the same path (`:5304-5314`).

**Trigger and consequence:** with reflection disabled, an optional Vulkan-Hpp C++ client compares wrappers with the same `display`, one default-constructed (null `displayName`) and one with a non-null name. Equality, inequality, or C++20 ordering can invoke undefined behavior instead of returning a result. Hashing a default-constructed wrapper or an enclosing `DisplayProperties2KHR` likewise dereferences null. **Affected configuration:** downstream clients of the optional copied Vulkan-Hpp headers; a repository-wide exact-type search found no non-generated in-tree use. **Confidence:** high for the nullable default and unchecked string operations; no comparison, hash operation, Vulkan call or build was run. Handle null names explicitly in comparison and hashing. Source-only.

<a id="gd14337"></a>
## GD14337 — Vulkan-Hpp TensorCopyARM can leave a non-null offset with zero dimensions

The enhanced `TensorCopyARM` constructor sets `dimensionCount` exclusively from `srcOffset_.size()` but stores `dstOffset_.data()` and `extent_.data()` independently (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:26766-26775`). Its size checks explicitly allow either array to be empty (`:26776-26795`). When `srcOffset_` is empty and `dstOffset_` is nonempty, construction succeeds with `dimensionCount == 0`, `pSrcOffset == nullptr`, and non-null `pDstOffset`. The Vulkan structure contract permits a null source offset but defines `dimensionCount` as the length of each non-null offset/extent array and requires a nonzero count if any such pointer is non-null ([`VkTensorCopyARM`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkTensorCopyARM.html)). `CopyTensorInfoARM` carries the record in `pRegions`, and `CommandBuffer::copyTensorARM()` forwards the native structure (`:26950-27005`; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:27482-27489`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp C++ client constructs `TensorCopyARM({}, dstOffsets)` (or supplies only a nonempty extent). The wrapper produces a structure whose `dimensionCount` contradicts its non-null array pointer; submitting it through `copyTensorARM()` violates the Vulkan parameter contract and can be rejected by validation/driver handling rather than representing the intended region. **Affected configuration:** downstream C++ consumers of the copied optional Vulkan-Hpp API with `VK_ARM_tensors`; no in-tree C++ construction caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the constructor behavior, forwarding path, and specification mismatch. Derive the count from the nonempty array(s) and validate all nonempty arrays agree, while retaining the permitted null-array semantics. No tensor command or build was run; source-only.


## GD14336 — GELS clear-path recursion treats standalone VSprites as Bobs

`DrawGList()` builds `ClearPath` links between every consecutive sprite it visits, without filtering for Bobs (`rom/graphics/drawglist.c:192-207`). When a Bob is followed in the sorted list by a standalone VSprite, the traversal stores that VSprite in the Bob's `ClearPath`. On a later redraw, `DrawGList()` calls `_ClearBobAndFollowClearPath()` for the Bob (`:80-93`); the helper recurses through `ClearPath` and immediately dereferences `CurVSprite->VSBob->Flags` on each node (`rom/graphics/gels_internal.c:181-203`). A standalone VSprite has no Bob (`VSprite.VSBob` at `compiler/include/graphics/gels.h:99`; `AddVSprite()` only links the VSprite, while `AddBob()` initializes the Bob's waiting flag and links its `BobVSprite`, `rom/graphics/addvsprite.c:54-85; addbob.c:53-68`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a client uses the public GELS APIs to place a Bob before a standalone VSprite in sort order, calls `DrawGList()` once so the Bob's `ClearPath` is populated, then redraws the list or removes the Bob with `RemIBob()`. The recursive clear reaches the standalone VSprite and dereferences its NULL `VSBob`, faulting the graphics operation. A repository-wide call-site check found no maintained client that builds this mixed list; the trigger is conditional on external or future GELS clients. Restrict `ClearPath` construction/traversal to Bobs or handle non-Bob VSprites explicitly. **Affected configuration:** graphics.library GELS clients using both Bobs and standalone VSprites; no default application impact is established. **Confidence:** high for the pointer flow and NULL dereference under the stated mixed-list sequence; no GELS operation or fault was run. Source-only; see the [clear-path caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gels-clear-path-bob-vsprite-mix-gd14336).

<a id="gd14345"></a>
## GD14345 — Vulkan-Hpp platform external-handle wrappers default to OpaqueFd

Six Win32-specific Vulkan-Hpp structures use `eOpaqueFd` as the default for their `handleType`: `ImportFenceWin32HandleInfoKHR` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:62957-62962`), `FenceGetWin32HandleInfoKHR` (`:51617-51619`), `ImportMemoryWin32HandleInfoKHR` (`:63601-63604`), `MemoryGetWin32HandleInfoKHR` (`:70315-70317`), `ImportSemaphoreWin32HandleInfoKHR` (`:64816-64821`), and `SemaphoreGetWin32HandleInfoKHR` (`:148352-148354`). The corresponding enum definitions distinguish `eOpaqueFd` from `eOpaqueWin32` (`vulkan_enums.hpp:4320-4324,4413-4417,4501-4505`). The import structures carry Win32 `HANDLE` values; the get structures are passed to Win32 getter functions that return `HANDLE`s.

The affected wrappers pass these structures through without translating the handle type: fence and semaphore imports go directly to `vkImportFenceWin32HandleKHR` and `vkImportSemaphoreWin32HandleKHR` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:14962-14983,13734-13757`); the memory import structure extends `MemoryAllocateInfo` and is forwarded through `Device::allocateMemory()` (`vulkan.hpp:12350-12356`; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:995-1019`). The getters likewise pass each info structure directly to its Win32 API (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:13557-13580,13764-13787,14991-15014`). The RAII getter/import wrappers also reinterpret and forward the same structures without changing `handleType` (`vulkan_raii.hpp:20123-20129,20211-20217,20226-20233,20733-20738,20746-20752`).

The same wrong default is used by `ImportMemoryHostPointerInfoEXT` and `ImportMemoryMetalHandleInfoEXT` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:63555-63563,63467-63480`; fields at `:63446-63450,63568-63573`). The host-pointer import requires a host-allocation or host-mapped-foreign-memory type, represented by `eHostAllocationEXT` and `eHostMappedForeignMemoryEXT` in the local enum (`vulkan_enums.hpp:4333-4334`). The Metal import's handle-type enum values are `eMtlbufferEXT`, `eMtltextureEXT`, and `eMtlheapEXT` (`:4345-4348`). Both structures extend `MemoryAllocateInfo` (`vulkan.hpp:13301,19545`) and are forwarded in its pNext chain by `Device::allocateMemory()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:995-1021`). Omitting the constructor argument therefore selects a POSIX-FD handle type for host-pointer or Metal-handle imports too; these are additional wrong-default cases in the same root cause.

Fuchsia has the same mismatch in `ImportMemoryZirconHandleInfoFUCHSIA`: its constructor and member default `handleType` to `eOpaqueFd` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:63856-63863,63956-63960`), although the local Fuchsia memory-handle enum is `eZirconVmoFUCHSIA` (`vulkan_enums.hpp:4336`). It extends `MemoryAllocateInfo` (`vulkan.hpp:15595`) and reaches the native allocation call through `Device::allocateMemory()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:995-1021`). `SemaphoreGetZirconHandleInfoFUCHSIA` likewise defaults to `eOpaqueFd` in its constructor and member (`vulkan_structs.hpp:148475-148483,148566-148570`), while the local Fuchsia semaphore-handle enum is `eZirconEventFUCHSIA` (`vulkan_enums.hpp:4510`); the getter forwards the structure directly to `vkGetSemaphoreZirconHandleFUCHSIA` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:24930-24956`). Thus omitting the handle-type argument on any of these Fuchsia wrappers supplies the wrong platform handle bit.
`ImportSemaphoreZirconHandleInfoFUCHSIA` has the same default in its constructor/member (`vulkan_structs.hpp:64975-64984,65064-65070`), instead of `eZirconEventFUCHSIA` (`vulkan_enums.hpp:4510`). The import wrapper forwards it directly to `vkImportSemaphoreZirconHandleFUCHSIA` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:24902-24924`), adding another Fuchsia import path to the same mismatch.

The export-side `MemoryGetMetalHandleInfoEXT`, `MemoryGetRemoteAddressInfoNV`, and `MemoryGetZirconHandleInfoFUCHSIA` constructors and members also default to `eOpaqueFd` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:69961-69969,70054-70058; :70194-70201,70285-70289; :70438-70446,70529-70533`). Their corresponding handle types are Metal's `eMtlbufferEXT`/`eMtltextureEXT`/`eMtlheapEXT` (`vulkan_enums.hpp:4345-4348`), RDMA's `eRdmaAddressNV` (`:4338`), and Fuchsia's `eZirconVmoFUCHSIA` (`:4336`). The getters forward the structures directly to `vkGetMemoryMetalHandleEXT`, `vkGetMemoryRemoteAddressNV`, and `vkGetMemoryZirconHandleFUCHSIA` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:31965-31990,25252-25278,24820-24846`), so omitted type arguments pass the mismatched default to these APIs too.

Five capability-query wrappers share the same default. `PhysicalDeviceExternalBufferInfo` defaults its memory handle type to `eOpaqueFd` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:89349-89357,89449-89453`) and `getExternalBufferProperties()` forwards it directly (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:6668-6676,6682-6696`). `PhysicalDeviceExternalImageFormatInfo` does likewise (`vulkan_structs.hpp:89925-89931,90008-90010`) and is passed in the `pNext` chain supplied unchanged to `getImageFormatProperties2()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:6286-6295,6301-6317`). `PhysicalDeviceExternalTensorInfoARM` defaults the same way (`vulkan_structs.hpp:90478-90486,90582-90588`) and `getExternalTensorPropertiesARM()` forwards it directly (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:27496-27503,27511-27522`). The fence and semaphore query records also default to their respective `eOpaqueFd` bits (`vulkan_structs.hpp:89584-89590,89667-89669; :90364-90369,90446-90449`); `getExternalFenceProperties()` and `getExternalSemaphoreProperties()` forward those records directly (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:6703-6711,6717-6729; 6738-6746,6752-6766`). These query APIs report capabilities for the supplied type, so on a platform where the intended type is Win32, Metal, Zircon, or another non-FD type, omitting the argument queries the FD type and can return capabilities unrelated to the intended sharing path.

**Trigger and consequence:** a Vulkan-Hpp client omits `handleType` when constructing one of the affected import/export wrappers or capability-query records. Import/export calls receive a mismatched handle-type bit and may fail; capability queries return properties for `eOpaqueFd` rather than the intended platform type and can mislead later sharing decisions. **Affected configuration:** consumers compiling the copied headers with the corresponding Win32, host-pointer, Metal, RDMA, Fuchsia, external-memory/fence/semaphore capability, or ARM-tensor declarations and using a non-FD handle type. The Vulkan HIDD target is optional, and no non-generated in-tree C++ use of these wrappers was found. **Confidence:** high for the recorded defaults and direct forwarding; caller impact is conditional on omitting `handleType` while intending a different type, and no API call was run. Require callers to set the corresponding platform handle type or provide a correct type-specific default. Source-only; see the [platform handle-default source and caller pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-external-handle-defaults-and-queries-gd14345).

<a id="gd14346"></a>
## GD14346 — Vulkan-Hpp create-info equality forms null array endpoints

When `VULKAN_HPP_USE_REFLECT` is not defined, `DeviceCreateInfo::operator==()` calls `std::equal()` with `ppEnabledExtensionNames + enabledExtensionCount` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:38611-38619`). A default-constructed object has `enabledExtensionCount == 0` and `ppEnabledExtensionNames == nullptr` (`:38382-38390,38635-38637`), so comparing two default objects forms `nullptr + 0` before the empty range is passed to `std::equal()`. `InstanceCreateInfo::operator==()` does this for both layer and extension arrays (`:67544-67556`); its default counts and pointers are zero/null (`:67565-67572`). Pointer arithmetic is only defined within an array object or one past it, so the null-plus-zero endpoint expression has undefined behavior even though the intended range is empty. Enabling `VULKAN_HPP_USE_REFLECT` selects tuple-based comparison instead; the optional spaceship operator also uses count-bounded loops and does not form these endpoints.

**Trigger and consequence:** a client using the copied Vulkan-Hpp C++ wrappers compares two default-constructed `DeviceCreateInfo` objects or two default-constructed `InstanceCreateInfo` objects with `operator==` (or `operator!=`) while `VULKAN_HPP_USE_REFLECT` is not defined. The equality implementation evaluates the null pointer endpoint expression and has undefined behavior; compiler optimization may make the comparison appear to work, but the operation is not defined by the language. **Affected configuration:** consumers compiling the copied headers without `VULKAN_HPP_USE_REFLECT`; no non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the null pointer/count state and endpoint expression; no equality operation or build was run. Return early for zero counts before forming array endpoints. Source-only; see the [create-info equality source pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-create-info-equality-source-pass-gd14346).

<a id="gd14347"></a>
## GD14347 — Vulkan-Hpp tool-properties equality and hash disagree on trailing array bytes

Five copied Vulkan-Hpp records have the same mismatch. `PhysicalDeviceToolProperties::operator==` compares its four fixed-size character arrays with `strcmp()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:120974-120977`), and its hash combines every byte of those arrays (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_hash.hpp:14700-14725). `PhysicalDeviceVulkan12Properties` compares `driverName` and `driverInfo` with `strcmp()` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:124861-124865`), while its hash walks both full arrays (`vulkan_hash.hpp:15147-15165`). `PipelineExecutableInternalRepresentationKHR` compares `name` and `description` as C strings (`vulkan_structs.hpp:130064-130068`), while its hash walks both complete arrays (`vulkan_hash.hpp:15804-15825`). `PipelineExecutablePropertiesKHR` has the same mismatch (`vulkan_structs.hpp:130191-130195`; `vulkan_hash.hpp:15828-15850`). `RenderPassSubpassFeedbackInfoEXT` compares its fixed-size `description` using `strcmp()` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:144211-144214`), while its hash combines every byte of the `VK_MAX_DESCRIPTION_SIZE` array (`vulkan_hash.hpp:17351-17363`). All five types have `std::hash` specializations in namespace `std`; the pipeline executable query wrappers also return these records in vectors (`vulkan_raii.hpp:23870-23895,23940-23963`).

**Trigger and consequence:** two values of any of these types have equal non-string fields and identical C-string prefixes, but different bytes after at least one terminating NUL in a compared array. Equality reports them equal, while the hash incorporates the differing suffix and can produce different hash values. Such keys violate the equal-keys/same-hash requirement used by unordered associative containers, so lookup, insertion, and duplicate detection can behave incorrectly. The public constructors accept complete fixed-size arrays for the original four records (`vulkan_structs.hpp:120885-120895,124486-124594,129976-129990,130109-130120`); `RenderPassSubpassFeedbackInfoEXT::description` is public and initialized as a fixed-size array, so differing trailing bytes are also representable. The Vulkan 1.2 properties query and pipeline-executable RAII wrappers return these records as values, and downstream callers can also construct them directly. **Affected configuration:** downstream C++ consumers including the copied Vulkan-Hpp hash header and using any affected type as an unordered-container key; no in-tree consumer was found. **Confidence:** high for the source-level equality/hash mismatch; the concrete hash collision behavior depends on the standard-library hash implementation, and no container operation or build was run. Hash only the NUL-terminated string contents (or make equality compare all array bytes consistently). Source-only; see the [tool-properties equality/hash trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-tool-properties-equality-hash-gd14347).

<a id="gd14348"></a>
## GD14348 — Generic truecolor-to-palette conversion reuses cached pens after colormap replacement

`true_to_pal()` stores each nearest palette index in the destination bitmap's `data->invlut`, keyed by the source RGB555 bucket (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapconvertpixels.c:237-275,292-305,331-344`). The cache is consulted before the current colormap is searched. `BM__Hidd_BitMap__SetColors()` clears the table after updating that bitmap's own colormap (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:1336-1346`), but `BM__Hidd_BitMap__SetColorMap()` only replaces `data->colmap` and returns the old pointer (`:4597-4608`); it leaves `invlut` intact.

A maintained route temporarily changes that pointer. When `int_bltbitmap()` copies from a truecolor source with a colormap into a palettized destination without one, it attaches the source colormap to the destination (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:563-576`). For differing pixel formats, `HIDD_Gfx_CopyBox()` passes the destination object and a NULL LUT to `HIDD_BM_ConvertPixels()`, which therefore uses that attached colormap (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1107-1118`). Afterward `int_bltbitmap()` resets the destination colormap to NULL (`gfxfuncsupport.c:657-662`). The bitmap-owned inverse cache survives both pointer changes. A later conversion using a different source colormap can therefore hit the earlier map's cached pen for the same RGB555 key instead of finding the nearest pen in the current map. `BitMapScale()` has the same temporary attach/reset pattern (`rom/graphics/bitmapscale.c:164-173,226-229`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a generic-base HIDD bitmap with a palettized destination format receives a truecolor-to-palette conversion that populates `invlut`, then its colormap is replaced (including the selected temporary blit/scaling path) and a subsequent source color maps to a different nearest pen under the new colormap. The stale pen index is written to the destination, producing incorrect colors. **Affected configuration:** generic graphics HIDD bitmap classes that inherit these base methods and perform truecolor-to-palette conversion with a bitmap colormap; the in-tree `BltBitMap()` and `BitMapScale()` temporary-colormap routes establish maintained callers. **Confidence:** high for cache retention across `SetColorMap()` and selected caller sequencing; a visible wrong pen requires the new colormap to choose a different index for the cached color bucket. Invalidate `invlut` when the colormap pointer changes, or associate cached entries with a colormap generation. No bitmap conversion, colormap mutation, scaling, or build was run; source-only; see the [cache lifetime and caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#generic-hidd-inverse-palette-cache-colormap-lifetime-gd14348).

<a id="gd14349"></a>
## GD14349 — AmigaVideo writes user copper instructions past the fixed copper buffer

The selected AmigaVideo build defines `USE_UCOP_DIRECT` as 1 (`amigavideo_intern.h:9`). `MakeViewPort()` allocates the destination copper list using `bmcl->MaxCount << 2` bytes, where `MaxCount` is `get_copper_list_length() >> 2`; that helper returns 2,000 bytes for the base list, i.e. a fixed capacity of 500 32-bit copper instructions (`amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1142-1160,1274`; `amigavideo_chipset.c:486-495`). It populates the system instructions into that buffer and sets the user list's `CopLStart` to the resulting tail (`amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1182-1188`). `AmigaVideo_ParseCopperlist()` then emits each accepted user MOVE/WAIT instruction directly at this tail via `COPPEROUT`, without checking the remaining allocation or growing the buffer (`:1363-1478`; `amigavideo_intern.h:11-13`). Thus a user list whose emitted instructions plus system copper instructions exceed the fixed 500-instruction allocation writes past the chip-memory allocation. `CBump()` supports linked extension segments and imposes no total-list cap (`rom/graphics/cbump.c:56-97`), so this is reachable through the public API.

The same parser sums `Count` from the first user `CopList` and every extension in its `Next` chain into a local `WORD count`, then uses that total to size the list and set `bmdata->bmuclsize` (`amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1363-1387`). `CopList.Count` is itself a signed `WORD` (`compiler/include/graphics/copper.h:44-55`). There is no aggregate bound; sufficiently many extension segments make the compound assignment convert an out-of-range `int` sum back to signed `WORD`. This can wrap on common two’s-complement targets and compound the invalid size/tail calculation described above.

In the non-direct-copy path, the out-of-range count can also produce an invalid allocation and copy extent; however, the selected build uses direct copper-list output, so the confirmed primary issue is writing beyond the fixed allocation. On the selected build, `bmuclsize` also advances the copper tail by `count << 2` with no capacity check; after count narrowing or simply an over-capacity user list, later list construction can use an invalid tail. The exact arithmetic after narrowing is implementation-defined/undefined as described above.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** m68k Amiga builds selecting the AmigaVideo HIDD (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:158,375`) when an external or future public user-copper client emits more instructions than remain in the fixed system copper buffer during viewport rebuild. The checked-in active graphics copper test uses only seven instructions; the larger 2View SHAM/MacroPaint producer is under `#if 0` and is not compiled. Because total capacity is only 500 and system instructions already occupy part of it, the actual user-list threshold is lower than 500 and depends on display mode. **Consequence:** `COPPEROUT` writes beyond the allocated chip-memory buffer; later copper-tail calculations may also point outside it. Bound user output against the remaining capacity before writing, and reject/roll back an oversized viewport list. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked destination extent and segmented public producer; reaching the limit depends on a sufficiently large user list. The separate signed aggregate narrowing can further corrupt sizing at large counts; exact behavior after narrowing is implementation-defined/undefined. No copper list, viewport, allocation failure, or build was exercised; source-only; see the [aggregate-count and copy caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-copperlist-aggregate-count-overflow-gd14349).

<a id="gd14350"></a>
## GD14350 — AmigaVideo's inserted line-wrap wait can make the published user-list tail one instruction short

In the selected direct-output build, `AmigaVideo_ParseCopperlist()` inserts an additional `COPPEROUT(0xFFDF, 0xFFFE)` the first time a valid user `COPPER_WAIT` maps past line 256 (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1418-1444`). The output pointer `copl` advances for that inserted instruction and for the user's wait, but `bmdata->bmuclsize` remains derived from the input `Count` sum (`:1383,1450-1478`). For a count-exhausted user list without a `CEND` end-wait, every input entry is emitted, plus the inserted line-wrap wait, so `bmuclsize` is one instruction shorter than the emitted output.

`MakeViewPort()` initializes `csd->starty` to `STANDARD_VIEW_Y` (`0x2c`, 44; `amigavideo_chipset.c:1958`; `compiler/include/graphics/monitor.h:100`). A user wait with `VWaitPos` greater than 212 and less than the bitmap's `displayheight` therefore enters the line-wrap branch. If this is followed by one or more user instructions and the bounded list ends by exhausting its count, `AmigaVideo_ParseCopperlist()` sets `copld.copper2_tail` one 32-bit instruction before the actual output end. The selected compositor later calls `setcopperlisttail()` at that published tail (`amigavideo_chipset.c:1420-1426,1440-1474`), replacing the final user instruction with a copper-list link/end sequence. The final user register write or wait is consequently omitted. A trailing `CEND` sentinel supplies one counted entry that the parser skips, balancing the extra line-wrap wait. The checked-in graphics copper test does not call the `CEND()` macro, but it appends `CWait(uCop, 10000, 0xFF)` (`developer/debug/test/graphics/copper.c:109-110`); with the selected display height below that value, the parser treats this final out-of-range wait as a terminator and skips the counted entry, so that caller does not trigger the short-tail case. No checked-in count-exhausted list without an equivalent skipped terminal entry was found. The public `UCopperListInit()`/`CMove()`/`CWait()` documentation does not state that a terminator is mandatory, and the parser supports count exhaustion, so the no-terminator path remains a conditional public-API candidate.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** m68k Amiga builds selecting AmigaVideo, with a user copper list that omits the optional `CEND()` sentinel, contains a valid wait mapping above line 256, then has a final instruction, and is attached during viewport rebuild. No maintained in-tree caller without an equivalent skipped terminal wait was found. **Consequence:** `setcopperlisttail()` overwrites the last emitted user instruction, so the requested copper effect is missing. Keep output and published tail accounting synchronized, or require and validate a terminal sentinel. **Confidence:** high for the one-instruction output/tail mismatch and link write at the stored tail; public exposure depends on whether external clients rely on count-exhausted lists without `CEND()`. No copper list or viewport was run; source-only; see the [line-wrap output/tail caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-linewrap-wait-tail-accounting-gd14350).

<a id="gd14351"></a>
## GD14351 — FKey submits an ARexx request when command-string allocation fails

`ExecuteArexx()` stores the result of `CreateArgstring(ki->param, strlen(ki->param))` in `rm_Args[0]` without checking it, then unconditionally sets the argument count to one and sends the `RexxMsg` to RexxMaster (`workbench/tools/commodities/FKey.c:1074-1077`). `CreateArgstring()` returns NULL when its `AllocMem()` fails (`workbench/libs/rexxsyslib/createargstring.c:54-58`). The request therefore reaches RexxMaster marked as a one-argument command even though the command pointer is NULL; the configured command is not delivered, and FKey waits for a reply instead of reporting the local allocation failure. `ClearRexxMsg()` safely skips NULL argument entries, so this finding is limited to the lost command and misleading request completion, not a cleanup dereference (`workbench/libs/rexxsyslib/clearrexxmsg.c:50-56`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the optional `workbench/tools/commodities/FKey` target when a configured ARexx hotkey runs and allocation of the command argstring fails. The target is selected as an explicit Commodities program, not through the commented parent aggregate edge (`workbench/tools/commodities/mmakefile.src:10-20`).

**Consequence:** the requested ARexx command is submitted without its required command string and is not executed as configured; the user receives no direct indication that FKey failed to allocate it. Check `CreateArgstring()` and abort/clean up before `PutMsg()` on failure.

**Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation result and the NULL-return contract; the ARexx request consequence follows from the submitted one-argument message fields. No allocation failure or ARexx request was induced.


<a id="gd14352"></a>
## GD14352 — Graphics copper test dereferences a failed list initialization

The optional `test-graphics` copper utility allocates its `UCopList` header, then calls `UCopperListInit(uCop, 7)` without checking the return value before its first `CWait()` (`developer/debug/test/graphics/copper.c:82-96`). `UCopperListInit()` can return NULL if allocation of the first `CopList` fails; in that case `uCop->CopList` remains NULL (`rom/graphics/ucopperlistinit.c:59-78`). It can also allocate the `CopList` but fail to allocate its instruction buffer, leaving `CopPtr` NULL before returning (`:72-78`). `CWait()` immediately evaluates `ucl->CopList->CopPtr` and writes through the resulting `copIns` without a null check (`rom/graphics/cwait.c:57-63`). Thus either initialization allocation failure faults the test process instead of reporting/handling an unavailable user copper list. Check the initialization result and release any partial list/header before continuing or exiting.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** explicitly build and run the optional `test-graphics` utility with the `USERCOPPER` argument when either `UCopperListInit()` allocation fails after the header allocation succeeds. The target is available through `developer/debug/test/graphics/mmakefile.src:5-28`; it is not built by default. **Consequence:** the utility dereferences NULL during copper-list construction. **Confidence:** high for both nullable allocation paths, the ignored return and immediate dereference. No allocation failure or program run was induced; source-only; see the [caller initialization trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-copper-test-list-init-failure-gd14352).

GD9615 selected-backend supplement: the explicitly buildable IntelGMA monitor target selects `intelgma_hiddclass.c` in `IGMA_HIDD_SOURCES` (`workbench/devs/monitors/IntelGMA/mmakefile.src:13-26,65-67`), although its parent aggregate edges are disabled (`:60-63`; `arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:11`; `workbench/devs/monitors/mmakefile.src:9`). Its registered `Hidd_Gfx::CopyBox` method (`intelgma_hiddclass.c:795,1038-1048`) takes the blit-engine path when both bitmaps are in framebuffer memory and their depths match; it packs `msg->destY` using `msg->destY << 16` (`:820-865`). The explicitly buildable Radeon HIDD also has its aggregate edges disabled (`workbench/hidds/radeon/mmakefile.src:4,12-15`; `arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:9`); its same-depth framebuffer blit path packs signed `WORD yb` and `ya` using `<< 16` (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_class.c:293-340`). NVIDIA's explicitly buildable HIDD has its aggregate edge disabled (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/mmakefile.src:4,10-14`; `arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:7-13`) and its `Hidd_Gfx::CopyBox` method is selected by `nvidia.conf:15-21`; both the same-depth blit and different-depth stretch paths left-shift signed `msg->destY` when packing the destination (`nvidiaclass.c:539-542,617-623`). In these methods the public CopyBox contract supplies signed `WORD` coordinates (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:396`), while generic `BltBitMap()` forwards negative destination coordinates without low-edge clipping (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:142-162`). A negative destination Y whose rectangle still intersects the bitmap therefore reaches a left shift of a promoted negative `int`, which is undefined behavior in C before the GPU command is submitted. This is an additional source-level consequence of GD9615 for these explicitly built backend paths; GPU clipping behavior is not established and is not needed for the signed-shift finding. The SAGA override always delegates CopyBox to its superclass, so it adds no separate hardware path (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/sagagfx/sagagfx_hiddclass.c:647-678`).

GD9615 Raspberry Pi VCGfx backend supplement: the VCGfx HIDD selects this `CopyBox` method in `vcgfx.conf:16-23` and is included in the packaged HIDD lists for ARM32 and AArch64 Raspberry Pi (`arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:187`; `arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:226`; selected body in `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/mmakefile.src:8-25`). For Copy draw mode and source/destination buffers with four bytes per pixel, `MNAME_GFX(CopyBox)` computes `drow_base = dst_buf + msg->destY * dst_pitch + msg->destX * 4` without checking either destination coordinate against bitmap bounds (`vcgfx_hiddclass.c:559-598`), then writes each row through `drow_base` (`:656-664`). The signed `WORD` destination fields (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:396`) reach this method unadjusted from the HIDD path when negative (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:142-162`). A negative destination origin with an intersecting rectangle therefore forms an out-of-range destination pointer and writes the copied rows before the bitmap buffer. This establishes a maintained Raspberry Pi driver path for GD9615, in addition to its public API and optional test-layer caller. No blit or framebuffer operation was run; source-only.

No target, blit or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.


<a id="gd14355"></a>
<a id="gd14355-dir-discards-malformed-pattern-template-errors"></a>
## GD14355 — Dir discards malformed pattern-template errors

For a supplied directory argument, `Dir` passes the result of `ParsePattern()` into `iswild` but only tests whether it equals `1` (`workbench/c/Dir.c:209-235`). The selected parser returns `-1` and sets `ERROR_BAD_TEMPLATE` for malformed patterns such as an unterminated character class (`rom/dos/parsepattern.c:17-47`; `rom/dos/patternmatching.c:439-442,558-574,630-633`). Since `-1` is not `1`, `Dir` calls `doDir()` with the original template as a literal path; the subsequent `Lock()` failure replaces the parser's useful error with the path lookup error.

**Trigger and consequence:** run `Dir` with a malformed wildcard template. The command reports a path lookup failure instead of the invalid-template error, obscuring the cause and making callers unable to distinguish invalid syntax from a missing path. Handle negative `ParsePattern()` results as parse failures and preserve `IoErr()`. **Affected configuration:** explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` builds with malformed supplied pattern arguments. **Confidence:** high for the parser return contract and the unchecked `-1` branch; no command was run. This is distinct from GD10410's allocation-failure NULL dereference and GD10409's post-match enumeration status handling. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#dir-shell-command-full-body-enumeration-and-allocation-pass).


<a id="gd14356"></a>
<a id="gd14356-dirs-all-files-option-does-not-recurse-into-subdirectories"></a>
## GD14356 — Dir's `ALL FILES` option does not recurse into subdirectories

In `doDir()`, both recursion and directory-name display are inside `if (error == 0 && doDirs)` (`workbench/c/Dir.c:601-655`). When `all` is true, the loop recursively visits children; when `doDirs` is false, that entire block is skipped. The final file-output block only prints files from the current directory (`:657-665`). The command documentation says `ALL` displays files recursively while `FILES` selects file-only output (`:62-64`), and the option parser permits both switches together (`:139-150,175-196`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run `Dir <directory> ALL FILES` on a tree containing subdirectories. The command lists files in the starting directory but never visits its children, so it silently omits the requested recursive files. Decouple traversal from whether directory names are displayed: recurse whenever `all` is set, and gate only `showdir()` on `doDirs`. **Affected configuration:** explicit optional `workbench-c-sh` builds using `ALL` with `FILES` and without `DIRS`. **Confidence:** high for the documented option semantics and branch gating; no directory listing was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#dir-shell-command-full-body-enumeration-and-allocation-pass).


<a id="gd14357"></a>
<a id="gd14357-search-suppresses-file-open-and-file-io-errors"></a>
## GD14357 — Search suppresses file-open and file-I/O errors

`FindString()` ignores a failed `Open()` and returns `FALSE`; its `Read()` loops stop on any nonpositive result without distinguishing EOF from `-1`, and the initial and current-position `Seek()` results are not checked (`workbench/c/Search.c:453-510`). These operations set `IoErr()` on failure (`rom/dos/open.c:17-40`; `rom/dos/read.c:17-40`; `rom/dos/seek.c:17-38`). The caller does not mark `success` false when `FindString()` fails to open or read a file (`Search.c:333-356`), and after ordinary traversal it clears `IoErr()` whenever `success` remains true (`:365-368`).

**Trigger and consequence:** Search reaches a matching file that cannot be opened, or a read/seek fails while scanning it, while directory matching itself completes normally. The command treats the file as a nonmatch and can return the ordinary “not found” warning without reporting the I/O failure, so users cannot tell an incomplete search from a complete one. Propagate `FindString()` access/read/seek failures separately from “no match” and preserve the DOS error. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds when a traversed file handler reports an open, read, or seek error. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked results, DOS error contract and final `IoErr()` clearing; no handler failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#search-command-file-io-error-propagation-pass).

<a id="gd14360"></a>
<a id="gd14360-delete-hides-unmatched-arguments-after-any-earlier-match"></a>
## GD14360 — Delete hides unmatched arguments after any earlier match

`doDelete()` initializes `firstmatch` once before iterating the `/M` file arguments, then clears it permanently on the first result (`workbench/c/Delete.c:211,218-242`). At function exit, it reports a non-`ERROR_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`/non-`ERROR_NO_MORE_ENTRIES` match error only while `firstmatch` is still true (`:355-361`). Therefore an unmatched later pattern is ignored if any earlier argument matched; `deletedfile` may already be true from an earlier successful deletion and the command returns `RETURN_OK` (`:363-368`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke `Delete` with an existing first argument followed by a nonexistent literal or no-match pattern. The existing object is processed, but the missing requested argument is silently skipped and the overall command can report success. Track match status per argument and preserve an aggregate warning/failure when any requested argument has no match. **Affected configuration:** selected `workbench-c` builds with multiple `FILE/M` arguments where an earlier one matches and a later one does not (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:5-45`). **Confidence:** high for the once-only state and final status gate; no files were deleted. This is distinct from GD10344's success return for a protection-skipped matched object. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#delete-command-multi-argument-match-status-pass).


<a id="gd14361"></a>
<a id="gd14361-delete-reads-before-an-empty-file-argument"></a>
## GD14361 — Delete reads before an empty file argument

For each `/M` item, `doDelete()` computes `lastIndex = strlen(files[i]) - 1` and immediately reads `files[i][lastIndex]` to check for a trailing colon (`workbench/c/Delete.c:218-224`). `ReadItem()` accepts a quoted empty token and returns it as an item containing only the NUL terminator (`rom/dos/readitem.c:136-163`), so this input can reach the code with length zero. The index then becomes negative (or an implementation-defined narrowing of the unsigned underflow) and the colon check reads before the string.

**Trigger and consequence:** pass an empty quoted `FILE/M` argument, such as `Delete ""`. The command reads outside that argument while testing for a device-name suffix; it may misclassify the input or fault, instead of rejecting an empty path cleanly. Check for an empty string before calculating the last-character index. **Affected configuration:** selected `workbench-c` builds with an empty quoted Delete argument. **Confidence:** high for empty-token acceptance and the unchecked `strlen()-1` access; no command was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#delete-command-empty-argument-bounds-pass).


<a id="gd14362"></a>
<a id="gd14362-makedir-all-clears-filesystem-errors-on-several-failure-paths"></a>
## GD14362 — MakeDir ALL clears filesystem errors on several failure paths

`CreateDirAll()` initializes its local `error` to zero and sets it only for a repeated volume prefix or an existing non-directory component (`workbench/c/MakeDir.c:143,153-160,205-213`). If the root `Lock()` fails, an intermediate `CreateDir()` fails, or `Examine()` fails, the function breaks with `error` still zero and unconditionally calls `SetIoErr(error)` before returning `BNULL` (`:220-252`). DOS documents that failed `Lock()`, `CreateDir()`, and `Examine()` set `IoErr()` (`rom/dos/lock.c`, `createdir.c:17-39`, `examine.c:17-42`). The caller uses that value for its final `PrintFault()` (`MakeDir.c:101-121`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use `MakeDir ALL` when the volume/root cannot be locked, an intermediate directory cannot be created (for example, because of protection or storage failure), or examining an existing component fails. The command reports an error return but overwrites the specific DOS cause with zero, typically printing a misleading “No error” diagnostic. Preserve the operation's `IoErr()` on failure, assigning a local error only for synthesized cases. **Affected configuration:** selected `workbench-c` builds using `ALL` on a handler that returns one of these failures. **Confidence:** high for the unassigned local error, unconditional `SetIoErr(0)`, and caller behavior; no filesystem failure was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#makedir-all-error-preservation-pass).


<a id="gd14457"></a>
<a id="gd14457-allocspritedataa-does-not-bound-old-format-sprite-height"></a>
## GD14457 — AllocSpriteDataA does not bound old-format sprite height

`SPRITEA_OutputHeight` is copied to the `ULONG height` local, but the old-data conversion narrows it to `UWORD height2` for the temporary bitmap and plane allocation, then iterates using a `UWORD k` against the original `ULONG height` (`rom/graphics/allocspritedataa.c:155-177,180-189`). No upper-bound check precedes this conversion. For `SPRITEA_OldDataFormat` with `SPRITEA_OutputHeight=65537`, `height2` becomes 1 and only four bytes are allocated for the two temporary planes, while the conversion attempts to process the requested 65,537 rows. The UWORD loop counter wraps at 65,535 and remains less than the ULONG height, so it does not terminate; writes proceed beyond the allocation.

**Trigger and consequence:** an `AllocSpriteDataA()` caller supplies old-format data with output height above 65,535. Intuition’s selected `SetPointer()` wrapper also accepts a signed `WORD` height, passes it to `MakePointerFromData()`, and does not reject negative values (`rom/intuition/setpointer.c:20-34,57-62`; `rom/intuition/misc.c:250-268`); a negative value is converted to a large ULONG tag and reaches the same branch. The conversion writes past its temporary plane allocation and loops without reaching the scaling/return path. Reject heights that cannot fit the `SimpleSprite.height`/temporary bitmap fields before allocating or copying. **Affected configuration:** graphics.library plus Intuition’s selected PointerClass/SetPointer path when a caller supplies a negative height; `MakePointerFromPrefs()` uses the safe 16-by-16 dimensions, and no ordinary in-tree caller supplies an out-of-range height. **Confidence:** high for the narrowing, undersized allocation, wrapping loop counter and absent validation; no sprite data or allocation was created. Source-only; see the [old-format sprite height pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#allocspritedata-old-format-height-boundary-pass).


<a id="gd14363-shader-module-identifier-comparisons-trust-an-unchecked-identifiersize"></a>
<a id="gd14363"></a>
## GD14363 — ShaderModuleIdentifierEXT comparisons trust an unchecked identifierSize

`ShaderModuleIdentifierEXT` stores identifier bytes in a fixed `VK_MAX_SHADER_MODULE_IDENTIFIER_SIZE_EXT` array (32 bytes), but its public constructor accepts any `uint32_t identifierSize` without checking that bound (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:150027-150035`). The public field can also be changed after construction. Equality passes `identifierSize` directly to `memcmp`, and the optional C++20 three-way comparison loops to the same unchecked size (`:150081-150104`). Vulkan requires a returned identifier size in the range 1 through 32 ([`VkShaderModuleIdentifierEXT` reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkShaderModuleIdentifierEXT.html)), but that contract is not enforced by this wrapper constructor or field.

**Trigger and consequence:** construct or mutate two wrapper values with the same `identifierSize` greater than 32, then compare them. Both comparison implementations read beyond the fixed identifier arrays, invoking undefined behavior. This concerns invalid wrapper state; compliant Vulkan query results do not trigger it. Bound the comparison length to the array size or reject invalid sizes at construction and mutation. **Affected configuration:** optional Vulkan-Hpp header; C++20 ordering requires `VULKAN_HPP_HAS_SPACESHIP_OPERATOR`, while equality is unconditional. No in-tree C++ caller constructing an oversized identifier was found. **Confidence:** high for fixed capacity and unchecked comparison bounds; no comparison or build was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#shader-module-identifier-comparison-bounds-pass).

<a id="gd14364"></a>
<a id="gd14364-vcgfx-skips-overlapping-vertical-copies-when-dma-is-unavailable"></a>
## GD14364 — VCGfx skips overlapping vertical copies when DMA is unavailable

VCGfx treats DMA as optional: InitDMA() can fail, but its return value is ignored and the display driver continues initialization (arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/vcgfx_init.c:148-176). The bitmap CopyBox method selects its DMA path for a large-enough copy between its own framebuffer bitmaps (vcgfx_hiddclass.c:634-643). If vc4_dma_copy() returns false, it falls through to a CPU copy except when source and destination share a buffer and the vertical rectangles overlap; in that case it returns without copying (vcgfx_hiddclass.c:645-658).

When InitDMA() could not acquire a channel, it leaves vcsd_DMAChannel at -1 (vcgfx_dma.c:56-60). The overlapping-copy request reaches vc4_dma_copy_band(), which immediately returns false without starting a transfer (vcgfx_dma.c:200-212,303-341). The HIDD nevertheless takes the overlap early return as if DMA had partially overwritten the source and destination. For example, a 64-by-16 32-bit scroll moves 4,096 bytes, exceeds the 2,048-byte threshold, and a one-row vertical overlap satisfies the early-return condition. No pixels move, so the requested copy is silently lost. The same problem applies to other DMA helper failures detected before starting a transfer; PutImage and GetImage have separate full-rectangle CPU fallbacks, so this finding is limited to CopyBox. Keep the no-transfer and partial-transfer outcomes distinct, or run the CPU copy when DMA did not start.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the VCGfx HIDD packaged for ARM32 and AArch64 Raspberry Pi (arch/arm-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:187; arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:226), when DMA initialization cannot provide a channel and a Copy-mode 32-bit copy between VCGfx buffers is at least 2,048 bytes with overlapping vertical ranges. No DMA resource, framebuffer, scroll, or build was exercised. **Confidence:** high for the optional initialization result, no-channel early return, and skipped fallback; occurrence depends on DMA availability and the stated copy. Source-only; see the [VCGfx no-DMA overlapping-copy pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vcgfx-no-dma-overlapping-copy-pass).

<a id="gd14365"></a>
<a id="gd14365-generic-hidd-copybox-uses-signed-word-counters-and-coordinates-for-uword-extents"></a>
## GD14365 — Generic HIDD CopyBox uses signed WORD counters and coordinates for UWORD extents

The Hidd_Gfx CopyBox method accepts UWORD width and height, but the generic implementation stores its pixel counters and loop sentinels in signed WORD variables and passes per-pixel coordinates through WORD GetPixel/DrawPixel interfaces (rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:396,526; rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:972-979; rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_intern.h:431-441). In the forward direction it assigns endX = msg->width and endY = msg->height to those signed WORDs (gfx_hiddclass.c:991-1007). A forward extent of 32,768 cannot be represented by the signed loop sentinel. With width=32,768 and srcX >= destX, the forward loop starts at zero and increments x from 32,767, overflowing signed WORD before the loop can test the narrowed end sentinel again. The backward loop also fails for extents greater than 32,768: `width - 1` cannot be represented by signed WORD when assigned to `startX`, and its decrementing counter can overflow. Height has the corresponding forward and backward cases. On AROS two’s-complement targets the out-of-range sentinel/start conversion wraps; the subsequent signed counter overflow is undefined behavior and can lead to incorrect traversal or compiler-dependent behavior. Independently, coordinates can cross the signed WORD limit even for a small rectangle: with `srcX=32767` and `width=3`, the third source pixel expression `srcX + x` is 32769 before conversion to the WORD GetPixel argument, which wraps negative on these targets. The generic planar GetPixel then calculates a negative row-byte offset and a negative remainder used as a right-shift count (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:396-422`), causing an invalid plane access and undefined shift behavior.

The affected code is the generic per-pixel fallback, reached when the direct-buffer bulk copy/conversion paths do not apply (gfx_hiddclass.c:1031-1129,1135-1247). The fast Copy-mode same-format chunk-buffer helpers use separate LONG counters and are not included. Two caller paths demonstrate representability: the optional HIDDCompositorRedrawBitmap() derives width from inclusive WORD Rectangle endpoints as an ULONG and passes it to HIDD_Gfx_CopyBox(); x=0 through x=32767 yields width=32,768 (workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:283-304). Public `BltBitMap()` also clips against the bitmap’s UWORD width and can retain a small in-bounds rectangle crossing x=32767; it then dispatches to HIDD CopyBox (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:142-175`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:642-650`). A generic planar bitmap can represent such a width, and its GetPixel implementation uses the narrowed WORD directly (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:396-422`). The HIDD bitmap width itself is UWORD (rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:491), so a 32,768-pixel bitmap is representable. The compositor target is explicitly buildable but its parent aggregate edge is disabled (workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/mmakefile.src:3-14).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected generic GFX HIDD, when the generic per-pixel fallback handles an extent at the signed WORD boundary or a source/destination rectangle crosses coordinate 32,767; the public HIDD bitmap API and checked-in callers can express those UWORD extents. No bitmap, compositor, or build was run. **Confidence:** high for signed loop overflow and the planar coordinate narrowing/negative-shift path on AROS two’s-complement targets; the exact manifestation of loop-counter overflow depends on compiler behavior. Use unsigned or wider counters and bounds that preserve the UWORD extent. Source-only; see the [generic CopyBox extent-width pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#generic-copybox-extent-width-pass).


<a id="gd14366"></a>
<a id="gd14366-generic-hidd-copybox-buffer-fast-paths-ignore-the-gc-color-mask"></a>
## GD14366 — Generic HIDD CopyBox buffer fast paths ignore the GC color mask

`copybox_impl()` takes the direct chunky-buffer path whenever both bitmap buffers are exposed and the GC draw mode is Copy (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1024-1045`). For matching pixel formats it calls `HIDD_BM_CopyMemBox8/16/24/32()` with no GC or color-mask argument (`:1050-1101`); for differing formats it calls `HIDD_BM_ConvertPixels()` with no mask (`:1103-1118`). These paths are selected without checking `GC_COLMASK(msg->gc)`. In the generic per-pixel fallback, the same Copy mode copies source pixels into `GC_FG` and then uses `DrawPixel()`, whose implementation preserves destination bits excluded by `GC_COLMASK` (`gfx_hiddclass.c:1152-1168,1177-1191`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:1447-1509`). The GC attribute documentation says ColorMask prevents selected color bits from changing (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:622`).

There is a maintained caller. `BltBitMap()` combines the caller-supplied plane mask with any source-depth limit in `GC_COLMASK` for non-truecolor destinations (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:483-534`). The explicit mask alone is sufficient to make it partial. For a palette destination, the source-to-truecolor pen helper is not selected; the ordinary HIDD CopyBox branch is reached (`:613-649`). HIDD chunky LUT8 bitmaps are supported: `AllocBitMap()` selects `LUT8` for `BMF_SPECIALFMT|PIXFMT_LUT8` allocations (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:26-40,243-310`), the standard format is palette/chunky (`rom/hidds/gfx/stdpixfmts_le.h:178-189`), and display class dispatch selects the generic ChunkyBM class, which exposes its backing buffer (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1005-1050`; `gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:43-70,964-975`). Matching LUT8 bitmaps enter the raw byte-copy path. The HIDD bitmap reports the pixel format's real depth, so this finding does not rely on a smaller requested allocation depth to establish the caller's mask.

**Trigger and consequence:** on the generic GFX HIDD, call `BltBitMap()` in Copy mode between same-format chunky LUT8 palette bitmaps with a partial public plane mask (for example, `mask=0x0f`). The caller sets the GC color mask, but the fast path copies the full byte, overwriting destination bits selected out by the mask. The per-pixel fallback preserves those bits. The unlike-format `ConvertPixels` omission remains an additional direct-HIDD/API case; the maintained same-format caller establishes reachability. **Affected configuration:** generic GFX HIDD with exposed chunky LUT8 buffers, including special-format HIDD allocations. **Confidence:** high for the public mask setup, selected CopyBox dispatch, and unmasked byte copy. No bitmap operation or build was run. Honor `GC_COLMASK` in the optimized paths or bypass them when it is partial. Source-only; see the [generic CopyBox color-mask pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#generic-copybox-color-mask-pass).


<a id="gd14367"></a>
<a id="gd14367-copybox-cursor-intersection-check-narrows-unsigned-extents-to-word"></a>
## GD14367 — CopyBox cursor-intersection check narrows unsigned extents to WORD

Both CopyBox and CopyBoxMasked cursor de-masquerade wrappers compute source/destination intersection bounds through signed `WORD w = msg->width, h = msg->height`, then pass `x + w - 1` and `y + h - 1` as `WORD` endpoints to `GfxDisplay_CursorIntersects()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1270-1276,1616-1624`; both method widths/heights are `UWORD`, `gfx.conf:396-397`). For a width of 32,768 at `destX=1`, `w` narrows to a negative value on AROS two’s-complement targets; the computed inclusive right edge then narrows to a negative `WORD` instead of the actual coordinate 32,768. `GfxDisplay_CursorIntersects()` rejects the rectangle when that right edge is less than the cursor's nonnegative bitmap-space X position (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:296-310`). The same arithmetic applies to source checks and height.

**Trigger and consequence:** a CopyBox call involving a CursorFB-wrapped display bitmap, extent at or above the signed-WORD limit, and a cursor positioned inside the actual rectangle but beyond the wrapped endpoint can skip cursor removal. The blit then reads or overwrites the composited cursor pixels; the cursor backup can subsequently restore stale pixels when the pointer moves. **Affected configuration:** generic GFX HIDD's software-cursor wrapper path with UWORD extents that produce an unrepresentable signed endpoint; no in-tree caller at the boundary was established in this pass. **Confidence:** high for the narrowed endpoints and false-negative intersection check; visible corruption requires the cursor to overlap the actual region and subsequent cursor restore. No cursor, bitmap operation, or build was run. Compute rectangle endpoints in a wider signed type and clip before passing to the WORD-based intersection helper. Source-only; see the [CopyBox cursor-bound pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#copybox-cursor-bound-pass).


<a id="gd14369"></a>
## GD14369 — NVIDIA CopyBox uses signed shifts to pack GPU command fields

The NVIDIA `Hidd_Gfx::CopyBox` override packs Y coordinates and extents with signed left shifts: the same-depth blit path uses `msg->srcY << 16`, `msg->destY << 16` and `msg->height << 16` (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/nvidiaclass.c:539-542`); the stretch path uses `msg->destY << 16`, `msg->height << 16` and `msg->srcY << 20` (`:617-633`). The method declares its coordinates as signed `WORD` and its extents as `UWORD` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:396`). C promotes these fields to signed `int` before the shifts. A negative destination Y therefore invokes undefined behavior in either path. A positive stretch-source Y of 2,048 or more, or a direct-HIDD height of 32,768 or more, also shifts a positive value beyond `INT_MAX` and invokes undefined behavior. `graphics.library`'s HIDD `BltBitMap()` path forwards a negative destination coordinate without low-edge clipping (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:142-162,207-216`), so a partially intersecting call with `destY=-1` reaches the NVIDIA method when its bitmaps select the relevant accelerated path. The direct `Hidd_Gfx::CopyBox` method accepts the full UWORD height range, beyond the signed WORD size accepted by `BltBitMap()`. Cast each operand to an unsigned command-word type before packing, and clip or reject invalid rectangles before dispatch. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the explicitly buildable NVIDIA HIDD (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/nvidia.conf:18-21`; its parent aggregate edge is commented in `workbench/hidds/nvidia/mmakefile.src:4`), when NVIDIA-owned framebuffer bitmaps select the same-depth blit or supported stretch path with negative destination Y; additionally, direct HIDD callers can trigger the extent/source-Y cases described above. **Consequence:** the packed command value is not defined by C for these inputs; the exact rendering result is compiler- and target-dependent. This is separate from GD9615's unresolved question about GPU handling of the resulting coordinates. **Confidence:** high for the field types and undefined arithmetic; branch reachability depends on bitmap ownership, format and caller inputs. No blit, GPU, or build was run. Source-only; see the [NVIDIA CopyBox signed-field pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#nvidia-copybox-negative-coordinate-shift-gd14369).



#### GD14369 addendum — ATI Radeon CopyBox also shifts a negative Y coordinate

The optional ATI Radeon `Hidd_Gfx::CopyBox` override packs `ya` and `yb` with `(ya << 16)` and `(yb << 16)` before writing the source and destination coordinate registers (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_class.c:330-340`). These locals are signed `WORD`s. In the same-depth, framebuffer-resident branch, a negative `destY` that reaches this code remains negative in `yb` for ordinary source-above-destination copies, so `yb << 16` has undefined behavior under C's signed-left-shift rules. `BltBitMap()`'s selected HIDD path forwards negative destination coordinates without low-edge clipping (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:142-162,207-216`), and the ATI class registers this `CopyBox` method (`workbench/hidds/radeon/radeon.conf:20-22`).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** explicitly built ATI Radeon HIDD, when two Radeon framebuffer bitmaps of the same depth are copied with a negative destination Y through `BltBitMap()` or a direct HIDD call. The module has a standalone build target, while its parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/hidds/radeon/mmakefile.src:4-14`); no default-image trigger is claimed. **Consequence:** the packed destination coordinate is not defined by C and may vary with compiler and target. This supplements GD14369's NVIDIA instance; it does not establish how Radeon hardware clips the submitted rectangle under GD9615. **Confidence:** high for signed promotion/shift and method reachability; no blit, GPU, or build was run. Source-only.


<a id="gd14460"></a>
<a id="gd14460-amigavideo-setbitmapnull-dereferences-the-detached-bitmap"></a>
## GD14460 — AmigaVideo `SetBitMap(NULL)` dereferences the detached bitmap

`AmigaVideoBM__Hidd_PlanarBM__SetBitMap()` first forwards the request to its `CLID_Hidd_PlanarBM` superclass, then dereferences `msg->bitMap` in its layout comparison and again while refreshing cached width, height and depth (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_bitmapclass.c:1035-1067`).
