The generic `PBM_SetBitMap()` explicitly accepts NULL as a detach request: it frees the wrapper's pixel format, clears the stored bitmap, resets the bitmap attributes and returns TRUE (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:265-283`). Therefore an AmigaVideo bitmap object receiving `HIDD_PlanarBM_SetBitMap(object, NULL)` reaches a NULL dereference after the superclass has already detached its backing bitmap and pixel format. The object is left with superclass state detached but AmigaVideo's cached `data->pbm` and layout state not updated. Guard the NULL detach path in the override and clear its cached bitmap/layout state consistently.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** m68k Amiga systems selecting the AmigaVideo HIDD (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:158,375`) when a caller invokes the public PlanarBM SetBitMap method with NULL on an AmigaVideo bitmap object. `AmigaVideoBM` is the displayable bitmap subclass selected by `AmigaVideoDisplay::CreateObject()` for the generic bitmap class when a valid mode ID is supplied (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:763-782`; class declaration `amigavideo.conf:94-110`). The repository's generic planar-wrapper release does call SetBitMap(NULL), but it uses the separate cached `CLID_Hidd_PlanarBM` object created by graphics.library, not this displayable AmigaVideo subclass (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:33-62`; cache setup `rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:138-144`). The selected `MakeVPort()` setter call supplies its current non-NULL classic bitmap (`rom/graphics/makevport.c:135-142`); no checked-in caller was found that sends NULL to an AmigaVideo bitmap object, so the reported trigger is an external HIDD method client relying on the superclass-supported detach behavior.

**Confidence:** high that the override dereferences NULL after its superclass accepts the request; medium that NULL-detach behavior is a required subclass contract, because the method interface does not separately document NULL semantics. No object, method call, display or build was exercised. Source-only; see the [SetBitMap caller and superclass trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-setbitmap-null-gd14460).

<a id="gd14459"></a>
<a id="gd14459-test-layers-scroll-command-dereferences-an-empty-layer-slot-after-reporting-it-missing"></a>
## GD14459 — `test-layers` scroll command dereferences an empty layer slot after reporting it missing

`scrolllayer()` reads an interactive layer ID and checks whether `layers[i]` is NULL. When the slot is empty, it prints “No layer with id” but does not return (`developer/debug/test/layers/layerstest.c:354-362`). After asking for the scroll deltas, it dereferences `layers[i]->Flags` and passes the same pointer to `ScrollLayer()` (`:364-375`). Thus choosing a valid in-range slot 0–9 that has not been populated or was already deleted causes a NULL dereference after the warning. The unchecked out-of-range index is a separate existing finding, GD10889.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** explicitly buildable `test-layers` (`developer/debug/test/layers/mmakefile.src:3-7`), when a user selects an in-range empty layer slot in the `scrolllayer` command. **Consequence:** the diagnostic process faults instead of reporting that the requested layer does not exist. Return immediately from the NULL branch before prompting for deltas or using the slot. **Confidence:** high for the missing return and subsequent dereference; no command or layer operation was run. Source-only; see the [test-layers scroll command pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#test-layers-scrolllayer-empty-slot-gd14459).

<a id="gd14458"></a>
<a id="gd14458-mesa3dgl-drawable-size-subtraction-underflows-for-a-collapsed-window-layer"></a>
## GD14458 — Mesa3DGL drawable-size subtraction underflows for a collapsed window layer

`MESA3DGLRecalculateBufferWidthHeight()` stores the visible RastPort dimensions, margins, and destination dimensions in `ULONG` fields/locals (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa3dgl_types.h:26,44-47`; `mesa3dgl_support.c:303-323`). It subtracts `left` and `right` (and `top` and `bottom`) before checking whether the result is negative. Unsigned arithmetic wraps instead, so both `< 0` checks at `:325-326` can never clamp an undersized layer to zero. The implementation itself documents that a window can temporarily have layer bounds around one pixel while the window remains fully sized (`:314-319`); with nonzero window borders, subtracting those margins from the one-pixel layer dimensions wraps to a near-maximum `ULONG`.

**Trigger and consequence:** a Mesa3DGL context uses a window whose layer bounds are temporarily narrower/shorter than its left+right or top+bottom margins, a state explicitly noted in this source. `MESA3DGLCheckAndUpdateBufferSize()` calls this calculation during make-current, set-RastPort and swap-buffer updates (`mesa3dgl_gallium.c:312-324`; `mesa3dgl_glamakecurrent.c:43-50`; `mesa3dgl_glasetrast.c:52-74`; `mesa3dgl_glaswapbuffers.c:63-70`). The wrapped dimensions are stored in the framebuffer and passed to Gallium resource creation as `templ.width0/height0` (`mesa3dgl_gallium.c:181-185`). If the backend rejects those dimensions, validation still returns success without checking the created attachment (`:236-245`), leaving the render resource NULL; `glASwapBuffers()` then skips presentation (`mesa3dgl_glaswapbuffers.c:61-67`). **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable optional Mesa3DGL library, when a window-backed context is updated while its layer bounds are smaller than the configured margins. **Confidence:** high for the unsigned underflow and unchecked propagation; a failed resource allocation and lost presentation depend on the selected Gallium backend. Calculate in a signed type before clamping, then convert to `ULONG`. No context, window resize, resource allocation, or build was run; source-only; see the [drawable-size arithmetic recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mesa3dgl-drawable-size-arithmetic-gd14458).

<a id="gd14461"></a>
<a id="gd14461-amigavideo-loses-the-current-sprite-when-replacement-allocation-fails"></a>
## GD14461 — AmigaVideo loses the current sprite when replacement allocation fails

`new_setsprite()` handles a sprite shape whose width or height differs from the stored shape by calling `new_resetsprite()` before allocating the replacement chip-memory buffer (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_chipset.c:938-945`). `new_resetsprite()` first redirects the sprite's copper pointer to the null sprite, frees the old buffer, and clears the stored dimensions (`:125-132`). If the subsequent `AllocMem()` fails, `new_setsprite()` returns `FALSE` without restoring the old buffer or shape (`:941-943`). The AmigaVideo `SetSpriteShape` method propagates that failure (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:980-1000`), and the selected m68k `ChangeExtSpriteA()` returns the failed method result to its caller (`arch/m68k-amiga/graphics/changeextspritea.c:31-49`). The legacy cursor converter has the same order: `setsprite()` calls `resetsprite()` and frees/nulls the current cursor buffer before allocating the new one, then returns `FALSE` on allocation failure (`amigavideo_chipset.c:858-863`; `resetsprite()` at `:116-122`). `AmigaVideoDisplay__Hidd_Display__SetCursorShape()` propagates this result, and `ChangeExtSpriteA()` uses that method for sprite number zero (`amigavideo_hiddclass.c:956-977`; `changeextspritea.c:84-89`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on the m68k Amiga AmigaVideo path, replace an existing cursor or hardware sprite with a different-sized shape while the required chip-memory allocation fails. The operation reports failure, but the previously installed shape has already been removed and the cursor/sprite points at the null data. Allocate the replacement before releasing the old buffer, then swap state only after successful initialization. **Confidence:** high for the ordering and failure propagation; requires an allocation failure during a size-changing shape replacement. No sprite or allocation failure was induced; source-only. See the [AmigaVideo replacement allocation trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-sprite-replacement-allocation-failure-gd14461).

<a id="gd14462"></a>
<a id="gd14462-amigavideo-selects-the-sprite-display-band-from-a-truncated-y-coordinate"></a>
## GD14462 — AmigaVideo selects the sprite display band from a truncated Y coordinate

Both AmigaVideo position handlers copy the incoming `WORD` Y coordinate into `UBYTE cursy` while scanning `compositedbms` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:1010-1058`). The assignment truncates the coordinate modulo 256 before the band comparison; optional interlace adjustment is then applied to this truncated value. The actual untruncated `msg->y` is later passed to `setspritepos()` or `new_setspritepos()`, so the coordinate used to choose `res` and `interlace` can refer to an earlier display band than the coordinate programmed into the sprite registers (`amigavideo_chipset.c:1007-1034`). The display-band list is built from screen `topedge` and `displayheight` (`amigavideo_chipset.c:1339-1359`), and the handlers stop at the first matching band.

**Trigger and consequence:** on the m68k Amiga AmigaVideo path, position a hardware cursor or sprite at a Y coordinate of 256 or greater while multiple vertically stacked composited displays have different resolution/interlace settings. The modulo-256 comparison can select an earlier band's settings, then program the actual lower-band coordinate using those settings, misplacing the sprite or selecting the wrong horizontal resolution/interlace encoding. Keep the comparison in a type wide enough for the incoming coordinate and band limits. **Confidence:** high for the narrowing and inconsistent coordinate use; visible mispositioning depends on the selected stacked-display modes and hardware. No sprite, display, or hardware operation was run; source-only. See the [AmigaVideo sprite-band coordinate trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-sprite-band-coordinate-gd14462).

<a id="gd14463"></a>
<a id="gd14463-amigavideo-shifts-negative-sprite-coordinates-as-signed-integers"></a>
## GD14463 — AmigaVideo shifts negative sprite coordinates as signed integers

The AmigaVideo sprite position encoders keep X/Y in signed `WORD` locals and pack them using left shifts before assigning the result to `UWORD` register fields (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_chipset.c:987-1003,1017-1034`). In particular, `x <<= (2 - res)` shifts a negative promoted `int` when a sprite is positioned left of the physical display, and `y << 8` shifts a negative promoted `int` when positioned above it. Left-shifting a negative signed value is undefined in C. The public `MoveSprite()` and HIDD `SetCursorPos(WORD, WORD)` interfaces accept signed coordinates, and the display method describes them as positions relative to the physical origin without excluding off-screen positions (`rom/graphics/movesprite.c:24-35`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:462`). Both the cursor encoder and numbered-sprite encoder contain the same packing operations.

**Trigger and consequence:** on the m68k Amiga AmigaVideo path, pass a negative X or Y coordinate to position a hardware cursor or sprite, such as a partially off-screen position. The C implementation does not define the packed register value for that input; compiler optimization may alter the intended two's-complement bit-field encoding, causing incorrect placement. Convert to an unsigned register-width value before field shifts and mask the packed fields explicitly. **Confidence:** high for the signed-shift undefined behavior; the visible outcome depends on compiler and target. No negative-coordinate operation, hardware action or build was run; source-only. See the [AmigaVideo signed-coordinate packing trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-sprite-signed-coordinate-packing-gd14463).

<a id="gd14464"></a>
<a id="gd14464-amigavideo-accepts-wide-sprites-while-encoding-only-16-pixels"></a>
## GD14464 — AmigaVideo accepts wide sprites while encoding only 16 pixels

The numbered-sprite `SetSpriteShape` method advertises and accepts width up to 64 whenever the detected chipset is AGA (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:982-1000`; `GetMaxSpriteSize()` uses the same `csd->aga` check at `:1002-1007`). But `new_setsprite()` switches to the 64-pixel fetch mode only when both `csd->aga` and `csd->aga_enabled` are true (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_chipset.c:930-935`). When AGA hardware is present but its features are disabled, it forces `width = 16` while retaining the original bitmap width separately (`:909,935-937`). The conversion loop therefore visits only 16 pixels per row even if the accepted input bitmap is wider (`:955-977`), then returns success after programming that truncated sprite.

**Trigger and consequence:** on AGA hardware while `aga_enabled` is false, call the AmigaVideo numbered-sprite shape method with width 17–64. The public size query and method validation permit it, but the displayed hardware sprite contains only the leftmost 16 pixels while the method reports success. Reject widths above the active fetch capability or enable the required AGA fetch mode before accepting the shape. **Confidence:** high for the validation/conversion mismatch; the trigger requires an AGA-capable device before AGA mode has been enabled. No sprite, hardware operation or build was run; source-only. See the [AmigaVideo wide-sprite fetch-mode trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-wide-sprite-fetch-mode-gd14464).

<a id="gd14465"></a>
<a id="gd14465-amigavideo-uses-one-sprite-fetch-mode-for-buffers-with-different-layouts"></a>
## GD14465 — AmigaVideo uses one sprite fetch mode for buffers with different layouts

`csd->fmode_spr` is shared state. Each call to `new_setsprite()` overwrites it from only the shape currently being installed: AGA-enabled shapes wider than 16 select mode 2, while other shapes select mode 0 (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_chipset.c:930-936`). Each sprite buffer is then allocated and populated using that call's `fetchsize` (`:938-977`). However, the VBlank handler writes every active sprite's control word at `p[1 << csd->fmode_spr]` using the one current global value (`:1844-1851`), and `setfmode()` likewise programs that shared sprite fetch mode into the copper list (`:134-145`). Thus later installing a different-width sprite changes the mode and control-word offset used for already allocated buffers.

**Trigger and consequence:** on AGA-enabled AmigaVideo, install two numbered sprites with different widths such that one needs the 64-pixel fetch mode and the other uses 16 pixels. The second shape update changes the shared fetch mode; VBlank then uses its control-word offset for both buffers, which does not match at least one buffer's allocated layout. The wide sprite can be fetched in the wrong mode and the VBlank control-word write can overwrite image data instead of the control word. Keep a common buffer layout for all sprites at the active hardware fetch mode, or recalculate all buffers atomically when the shared mode changes. **Confidence:** high for the per-shape global update and global VBlank use; the visible/corrupt result requires mixed-width active sprites and was not exercised. No sprite, VBlank, hardware operation or build was run; source-only. See the [AmigaVideo shared sprite fetch-mode trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-shared-sprite-fetch-mode-gd14465).

<a id="gd14466"></a>
<a id="gd14466-amigavideo-never-publishes-numbered-sprite-buffers-into-the-copper-list"></a>
## GD14466 — AmigaVideo never publishes numbered sprite buffers into the copper list

`initcustom()` initializes all eight hardware sprite pointer pairs in the startup copper list to `csd->sprite_null`, but records a patch location only for sprite 0 in `csd->copper1_spritept` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_chipset.c:2004-2010`). Numbered sprites use a separate `csd->new_copper1_spritept[8]` array (`amigavideo_intern.h:149`). A source-wide search of the selected AmigaVideo implementation finds no assignment to any element of this array; its only uses are NULL checks and writes in `new_setnullsprite()` and `new_setspritevisible()` (`amigavideo_chipset.c:107-112,1070-1088`). Consequently, after a numbered sprite shape is converted and stored in `new_sprite[spritenum]`, `new_setspritevisible()` skips updating the copper-list pointer because the corresponding patch location is NULL. The initialized copper list continues to point that sprite channel at the null sprite. Position methods update the position/control registers but do not publish the sprite data pointer.

**Trigger and consequence:** on the selected m68k Amiga AmigaVideo HIDD, call `ChangeExtSpriteA()` with a nonzero sprite number and a valid shape for a viewport using this driver. The selected m68k graphics implementation calls `HIDD_AMIGAGFX_SetSpriteShape()` and, on success, `SetSpriteVisible(TRUE)` (`arch/m68k-amiga/graphics/changeextspritea.c:87-96`). The AmigaVideo methods can return success after updating an unreferenced buffer, but the copper list remains pointed at `sprite_null`, so the numbered sprite image is not displayed. Initialize each channel's copper pointer patch location when building the copper list and update it on shape/visibility changes. **Confidence:** high for the unassigned patch-location array and the selected success path; no chipset operation or hardware display was run. See the [AmigaVideo numbered-sprite copper-pointer trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-numbered-sprite-copper-pointer-gd14466).

GD14466 initialization follow-up: the AmigaVideo resident is created through `InitResident()`'s `MakeLibrary()` path (`rom/exec/initresident.c:93-94`), and `MakeLibrary()` allocates the full library base with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`rom/exec/makelibrary.c:109`). Thus `new_copper1_spritept[]` starts as NULL; the result does not depend on stale allocator contents. `initcustom()` then explicitly records only the channel-0 patch location.

<a id="gd14467-planar-bltbitmap-downward-overlap"></a>
<a id="gd14467"></a>
## GD14467 — Planar `BltBitMap()` corrupts downward overlapping copies

**`BltBitMap()` copies overlapping bitmap rows in the wrong order when the destination is below the source (conditional image corruption; high source confidence).** In the generic planar path, rows are always processed from `y = 0` upward (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:287-320`). The overlap check only detects address overlap between the current source and destination scanlines and copies that one row to `temp`; it does not choose a reverse row order when a later destination row aliases an earlier source row (`:291-312`). For a same-bitmap copy of rows 0–3 to rows 1–4, row 0 overwrites row 1 before row 1 is read, and the overwritten data then propagates down the remaining rows. The public description says the routine moves part of a bitmap around (`:57-60`), and its implementation explicitly permits the same bitmap as source and destination in its overlap handling (`:78-83`).

The maintained `MoveRaster()` caller makes the downward-copy direction reachable: with negative `dy`, it calls `BltBitMap()` using the upper source area and a lower destination area (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:842-852`). This affects the generic planar software path; HIDD bitmap backends dispatch to `CopyBox` and are not included in this finding. A fix should copy rows bottom-to-top when the destination starts below an overlapping source, while retaining the current horizontal overlap handling. **Confidence:** high for the generic planar path and the `MoveRaster()` route. No bitmap or scroll operation was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14468-findcolor-unextended-colormap"></a>
<a id="gd14468"></a>
## GD14468 — `FindColor(..., -1)` walks past an unextended colormap

**`FindColor()` treats the `-1` maximum as unbounded when the colormap has no `PalExtra` (conditional out-of-bounds palette reads; high source confidence).** `GetColorMap()` allocates a zeroed `ColorMap`, initializes its `Count` and color tables, and leaves `PalExtra` NULL (`rom/graphics/getcolormap.c:61-92`; the zeroing allocation is at `:61-62`). `FindColor()` only replaces `maxpen == -1` when `cm->PalExtra` is non-NULL (`rom/graphics/findcolor.c:64-67`). It then compares an unsigned `ULONG index` with signed `LONG maxpen` in `while(index <= maxpen)` (`:71-73`); with `maxpen == -1`, the usual integer conversion turns the bound into `ULONG_MAX`. The loop consequently calls `color_distance()` with indices beyond `cm->Count`, reading past `ColorTable` and, for V39 maps, `LowColorBits` (`rom/graphics/color_support.c:16-46`).

**Trigger and consequence:** call the selected Graphics.library `FindColor()` vector with a valid `GetColorMap()` result that has not had `AttachPalExtra()` applied and pass `maxpen = -1`. `GetColorMap()` itself leaves this state, and `AttachPalExtra()` is a separate API. The result is an out-of-bounds read that may fault or return a meaningless pen. The checked-in ColorWheel and MUI callers also pass `-1`, but their colormaps are associated with screens; this review did not establish a maintained unextended-colormap caller. Resolve `-1` to `cm->Count - 1` when no palette extra is attached, then bound the search. **Confidence:** high for the conditional and unsigned loop bound; no call or memory access was run. Source-only.


<a id="gd14470-wanderer-leaks-copy-window-tree-if-application-setup-fails"></a>
<a id="gd14470"></a>
## GD14470 — Wanderer leaks its copy-window tree if Application setup fails

`CreateCopyDisplay()` constructs the Window and its nested Group/Gauge/Text/Button objects as arguments to `MUI_NewObject(MUIC_Application, ...)` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:2506-2561`). The Application class does not process `MUIA_Application_Window` until after Configdata, timer port/request creation, and `OpenDevice(TIMERNAME, ...)` succeed (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/application.c:473-510,516-576`). On any of those later timer-setup failures, it disposes its partially built Application and returns NULL before adding the supplied Window to `app_WindowFamily`; disposal only walks that family (`:847-878`), so the separately created Window tree is not owned or freed.

The caller checks only `d->copyApp`; when it is NULL, `CreateCopyDisplay()` returns FALSE without disposing `d->win` or its child tree (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:2563-2580`). The enclosing copy operation runs `DisposeCopyDisplay()` only when `displayCreated` is TRUE (`:333-363`), so it does not clean this failure path either.

**Trigger and consequence:** use Wanderer's file-copy drop path while creation of the Application's timer port/request fails or `timer.device` cannot be opened, after the nested display objects have been constructed successfully. The Application constructor returns failure, but the Window and its child objects remain allocated with no owning Application; repeated failures retain each tree. **Affected configuration:** Workbench Wanderer copy-display path using the selected MUI Application class. **Confidence:** high for object-construction order, delayed Window attachment, and missing cleanup in both caller levels; the resource failure is conditional. Dispose the constructed Window tree when Application construction fails, or construct and attach it only after Application setup succeeds. No GUI, allocation failure, timer-device operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [Wanderer copy-display trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-copy-display-setup-failure-gd14470).


<a id="gd14469"></a>
<a id="gd14469-amigavideo-dereferences-a-missing-pixel-format-descriptor-for-truecolor-sprites"></a>
## GD14469 — AmigaVideo dereferences a missing pixel-format descriptor for truecolor sprites

Both `setsprite()` and `new_setsprite()` read a truecolor shape bitmap's `aHidd_PixFmt_StdPixFmt`, pass it to `HIDD_DMEnum_GetPixFmt()`, and store the result without checking for NULL (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_chipset.c:842-848,922-928`). The generic DMEnum implementation returns NULL for the pseudo format `vHidd_StdPixFmt_Native` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:1321-1335`; the pseudo-format range is defined at `rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:205-216`). This is a valid descriptor for a truecolor HIDD pixel-format object; the Gfx HIDD's own documented truecolor format example uses `vHidd_StdPixFmt_Native` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:309-326`). When the conversion reaches `ALPHA_COMP`, `RED_COMP`, `GREEN_COMP`, or `BLUE_COMP`, `GET_COLCOMP` dereferences the unchecked format pointer (`amigavideo_chipset.c:885-886,965-966`; `rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:299-305`). `ChangeExtSpriteA()` dispatches sprite number zero to `HIDD_Display_SetCursorShape()` and nonzero numbers to `HIDD_AMIGAGFX_SetSpriteShape()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/graphics/changeextspritea.c:80-95`), so both the legacy cursor and numbered-sprite paths reach the affected converters. `AllocSpriteDataA()` documents its truecolor HIDD source path and preserves the source bitmap as the friend so the created sprite bitmap takes its format (`rom/graphics/allocspritedataa.c:194-215,240-253`); the Gfx HIDD documented truecolor pixel-format example uses `vHidd_StdPixFmt_Native` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:307-326`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** m68k-Amiga builds selecting the optional AmigaVideo HIDD, when `ChangeExtSpriteA()` receives a truecolor HIDD sprite bitmap whose pixel format uses the valid `Native` pseudo standard-format code. **Consequence:** sprite-shape conversion dereferences NULL and faults instead of converting the source or returning failure; the existing cursor/numbered sprite state may already have been reset if dimensions changed. **Confidence:** high for the valid pseudo format, NULL return, unchecked macro dereference, and selected public dispatch paths; occurrence requires the stated truecolor source format. Use the shape bitmap's actual `HIDDT_PixelFormat` object for component extraction or reject unsupported standard-format codes before processing. No sprite operation, fault, build, or hardware access was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


<a id="gd14471-reqtools-shared-idcmp-port-walk-omits-smp-lock"></a>
<a id="gd14471"></a>
## GD14471 — ReqTools shared-port teardown walks the IDCMP queue without its SMP lock

`RTFuncs_CloseWindowSafely()` prevents local task switching with `Forbid()`, then traverses the shared window port’s `mp_MsgList` and removes/replies messages belonging to the closing window (`workbench/libs/reqtools/rtfuncs.c:617-641`). On ExecSMP, `Forbid()` does not serialize another CPU. Exec’s `InternalPutMsg()` and `GetMsg()` protect that list with `mp_SpinLock` (`rom/exec/putmsg.c:83-92`; `rom/exec/getmsg.c:64-72`), and `Disable()`’s documentation explicitly requires a spinlock for cross-CPU shared data (`rom/exec/disable.c:58-61`). The ReqTools walk and `Remove()` take no such lock, so concurrent message publication or consumption can invalidate its current/next node pointers or race queue removal.

The helper is used by ReqTools’ shared-IDCMP close path (`workbench/libs/reqtools/general.c:427`) and is exposed as `rtCloseWindowSafely()`. The same lock omission appears in `StopTimer()`: after `Wait()`, it scans `reqwin->UserPort->mp_MsgList` and removes the timer reply under `Disable()`/`Enable()` alone (`workbench/libs/reqtools/filereq.c:450-475`). On ExecSMP, an IDCMP producer or another port consumer can mutate the list on another CPU during either traversal. **Trigger and consequence:** close a ReqTools window sharing another window’s UserPort while another CPU sends or removes a message, or run the file requester timer-reply scan while other messages arrive on its UserPort. The unlocked traversal can corrupt the message list or skip/mis-handle queued messages. **Affected configuration:** ExecSMP with the ReqTools shared-port teardown path. **Confidence:** high for the lock mismatch and caller reachability; no concurrent queue operation or window close was run. Source-only.


<a id="gd14472-rtlockwindow-reads-private-tail-of-requesters"></a>
<a id="gd14472"></a>
## GD14472 — `rtLockWindow()` reads past ordinary requester objects

`RTFuncs_rtLockWindow()` walks `window->FirstRequest` as a list of `struct rtWindowLock *`, then reads `rtwl_Magic` and `rtwl_RequesterPtr` to decide whether a lock already exists (`workbench/libs/reqtools/rtfuncs.c:368-390`). The private `rtWindowLock` embeds a public `struct Requester` first and places those fields after it (`:22-31`), but Intuition permits ordinary Requester objects in the same list; the public structure ends at `ReqPad2` (`compiler/include/intuition/intuition.h:420-449`). Thus a window with any unrelated requester attached causes the duplicate-lock scan to read private fields beyond that requester’s allocation before it can allocate and install its own lock.

**Trigger and consequence:** call `rtLockWindow()` on a window whose `FirstRequest` chain contains a normal `struct Requester` that is not a ReqTools lock. The scan reads beyond the object; depending on adjacent memory, it can fault or accidentally treat unrelated data as a lock and return a bogus pointer/refcount. Only the zero-requester path avoids this read. Walk requesters using a safe registered/private-object discriminator that does not read beyond the public object, or track ReqTools locks separately. **Confidence:** high for the layout and unconditional field reads; no requester was attached and no call was run. Source-only.


<a id="gd14473-nfloattext-align-tag-accesses-instance-before-super-new"></a>
<a id="gd14473"></a>
## GD14473 - NFloattext constructor accesses instance data before superclass allocation

In the NFloattext OM_NEW method, when MUIA_NFloattext_Align is present, the code evaluates INST_DATA(cl, obj) and writes the alignment before calling DoSuperNew() (workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nfloattext_mcc/NFloattext.c:133-139,144-148). On the selected AROS object path, NewObjectA() dispatches OM_NEW with the class pointer as the initial obj argument; the actual object is allocated by the superclass construction (rom/intuition/newobjecta.c:133-145; workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_newobject.c:49-55). INST_DATA adds cl_InstOffset to this class pointer, so the pre-super write does not address an allocated NFloattext object's instance data. After DoSuperNew succeeds, mNFT_New assigns NFloattext_Align from its local Align value, initially ALIGN_LEFT (NFloattext.c:70-72,150-158), overwriting the requested value as well.

**Trigger and consequence:** build/load the optional NFloattext.mcc target and create an object with the public MUIA_NFloattext_Align attribute (compiler/include/mui/NFloattext_mcc.h:70). The constructor writes through an instance-data pointer derived from the class object before allocation, which can corrupt memory or fault; if that write happens not to fail, the requested alignment is reset to the default. No checked-in caller passes this attribute, so the trigger is an external or future client using the public attribute. The class target itself is explicitly buildable, but its parent aggregate edge is commented out (workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nfloattext_mcc/mmakefile.src:4,13-15). **Confidence:** high for the object-construction order and overwritten value; no object creation or build was run. Source-only.


<a id="gd14474-nfloattext-getentry-returns-unwrapped-tail-on-allocation-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14474"></a>
## GD14474 - NFloattext returns the unwrapped text tail when wrapped-line allocation fails

For a wrapped row, mNFT_GetEntry obtains the source entry, character offset, and wrapped character count from MUIM_NList_GetEntryInfo. It allocates a temporary string, copies exactly gei.charlen characters from entry[gei.charpos], and appends a terminator. If allocation fails, however, it returns &entry[gei.charpos] directly (workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nfloattext_mcc/NFloattext.c:287-316). That pointer continues through the rest of the original entry, not just this wrapped line. The public MUIP_NFloattext_GetEntry result contains only an entry pointer, with no length field (workbench/classes/zune/nlist/include/mui/NFloattext_mcc.h:72-73); MUIM_List_GetEntry likewise returns a string pointer (workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlist_mcc/NList_func.c:1456-1474). The fallback therefore cannot preserve the intended wrapped-line boundary.

**Trigger and consequence:** use the explicitly buildable NFloattext class with an entry that wraps to multiple lines, request a wrapped line through MUIM_List_GetEntry or MUIM_NFloattext_GetEntry, and have the temporary AllocVecShared allocation fail or need to grow and fail. The method returns the selected line plus the remaining original text instead of a NUL-terminated copy of that line; consumers can display or parse text belonging to subsequent wrapped rows as part of the selected entry. Return failure on allocation failure or provide a lifetime-safe terminated representation. **Affected configuration:** optional NFloattext MCC when used for wrapped entries. **Confidence:** high for the character-count copy and unbounded-tail fallback; no allocation failure or GUI operation was run. Source-only.

<a id="gd14475"></a>
<a id="gd14475---nlisttree-open-all-dereferences-the-table-of-an-empty-child-list"></a>
## GD14475 - NListtree Open-All dereferences the table of an empty child list

**Indexed summary:** NListtree's Open-All method reads the first table entry before checking whether a non-root list is empty.

**Source and trigger:** The public Open method maps MUIV_NListtree_Open_TreeNode_All to the supplied list node and unconditionally calls OpenTreeNodeListExpand() for that list (workbench/classes/zune/nlist/nlisttree_mcc/NListtree.c:6716-6718,6731-6747). For a non-root list, OpenTreeNodeListExpand() evaluates tb->tb_Table[0] for its redraw position before entering the loop that would naturally do zero iterations for an empty table (:1998-2030). Empty list tables have a NULL pointer: removal of the final child explicitly frees the table and stores NULL in tb_Table (:1084-1092); newly allocated tree-pool nodes are also drawn from a MEMF_CLEAR pool. The dereference therefore faults when a caller requests Open-All on an empty child list. The public method documentation describes Open-All as opening all nodes in the supplied list and does not exclude empty lists (workbench/classes/zune/nlist/docs/MCC_NListtree.doc:2423-2474). **Affected configuration and trigger:** an explicitly built/loaded NListtree MCC client calls MUIM_NListtree_Open with a concrete non-root empty list node and MUIV_NListtree_Open_TreeNode_All. The legacy Listtree compatibility MCC forwards its Open selectors directly to MUIM_NListtree_Open without validating the list contents (workbench/classes/zune/listtree/listtree.c:687-718), so its clients can reach the same path. The checked-in direct Open-All calls use the root sentinel; no in-tree child-list trigger is claimed. Both NListtree and Listtree have disabled parent aggregate edges in this snapshot, so no default inclusion is claimed. **Consequence:** the Open method faults instead of treating the empty list as a no-op. Check tb_Entries before indexing the table, or use a safe redraw position for an empty list. **Confidence: high** for the NULL table state and unconditional index; no GUI method or runtime operation was run. Source-only.

**Review state:** Traced the public method dispatch, empty-table teardown, documented Open-All contract, checked-in root-list callers, and the legacy Listtree wrapper's direct forwarding path. No checked-in caller supplies a child list to Open-All; scope includes external clients of either explicitly built optional class.


## GD10253 — Vulkan-Hpp resolve-attachment setters can desynchronize subpass array counts

The enhanced `SubpassDescription` and `SubpassDescription2` constructors check that a nonempty resolve-attachment array has the same length as the color-attachment array (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:140894-140923,141532-141570`). Their `setResolveAttachments()` methods do not preserve that invariant: each overwrites the shared `colorAttachmentCount` with the resolve proxy's size and updates `pResolveAttachments`, while leaving `pColorAttachments` unchanged (`:140996-141003,141655-141662`). The render-pass creation wrappers forward the resulting native structures (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:5188-5218,7348-7376`).

**Trigger and scope:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp client changes a subpass's resolve attachments to a length different from its existing color array, then submits the subpass through `createRenderPass()` or `createRenderPass2()`. **Consequence:** the native count no longer matches the color array and can describe invalid or mismatched subpass attachment data. The constructor guard does not protect the later setter mutation. **Confidence:** high for the count/pointer mismatch; no in-tree C++ consumer was found. No render pass or build was run; source-only.

## GD10264 — Vulkan-Hpp no-exceptions result wrappers package uninitialized outputs

Several enhanced/RAII wrappers declare output locals without initialization, pass their addresses to a result-returning Vulkan command, call `resultCheck()`, and then package the local into `ResultValue<T>`. For example, `Semaphore::getCounterValue()` uses an uninitialized `uint64_t value` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:17432-17442`); `PhysicalDevice::getSurfaceSupportKHR()` does the same with `Bool32 supported` (`:18362-18373`). On a failed first validation-cache query, `ValidationCacheEXT::getData()` can also use its uninitialized `dataSize` after result checking (`:22315-22338`). The same pattern appears in the indexed mapping, surface-support, external-handle, platform-native-buffer, ray-tracing, descriptor, acceleration-structure/micromap, and tensor-property output wrappers summarized in the master index.

`resultCheck()` reports failure through `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT_ON_RESULT`; its default is `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT` (`vulkan.hpp:7551-7572`; `vulkan_hpp_macros.hpp:74-79`). In `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` builds where that assertion is disabled or configured not to abort, control continues and `createResultValueType()` packages the untouched output. **Trigger and scope:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp enhanced or RAII API query fails without writing its output in a no-exceptions build with non-aborting result assertions. **Consequence:** the returned error result carries an indeterminate value; reading that value has undefined behavior. **Confidence:** high for the representative source paths and shared wrapper pattern; no in-tree C++ consumer was found. No Vulkan call or build was run; source-only.

## GD10266 — Vulkan-Hpp no-exceptions enumeration wrappers read counts after failure

Generated RAII enumeration wrappers leave the count local uninitialized before the first count-only query, then use it after `resultCheck()` even if that query failed. `PhysicalDevice::enumerateDeviceExtensionProperties()` declares `uint32_t propertyCount`, performs the count query, and after result checking compares and may resize using `propertyCount` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:15301-15335`). `PhysicalDevice::enumerateQueueFamilyPerformanceCountersByRegionARM()` similarly uses an uninitialized `counterCount` after result checking (`:28038-28075`). The same count-after-error structure occurs across the extension/layer, WSI, pipeline-cache, video-query, display, performance-counter, shader-info, and other optional enumeration wrappers listed in the master index.

When a first query returns a failure other than the explicitly retried `eIncomplete`, the vector remains empty and the native API need not write the output count. In a no-exceptions configuration where `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT_ON_RESULT` does not abort, the wrapper then reads that indeterminate count in assertions or comparison/resize logic. **Trigger and scope:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp RAII enumeration call receives such a failed count-only query under a no-exceptions, non-aborting-result-assertion configuration. **Consequence:** the wrapper reads an indeterminate count and may perform an invalid vector resize before returning the error result. **Confidence:** high for the cited wrappers and repeated generated pattern; no in-tree C++ consumer was found. No Vulkan query or build was run; source-only.


<a id="gd14477"></a>
## GD14477 - Vulkan-Hpp DisplayKHR RAII releases display handles it only queried

The RAII `DisplayKHR::clear()` calls `vkReleaseDisplayEXT()` whenever its stored display handle is non-null (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:9934-9942`). However, the RAII `PhysicalDevice::getDisplayPlaneSupportedDisplaysKHR()` wraps each handle returned by the display-support query in an owning `DisplayKHR` (`:18703-18732`). The Xlib `getRandROutputDisplayEXT()`, DRM `getDrmDisplayEXT()`, and WinRT `getWinrtDisplayNV()` query methods also return owning wrappers (`:20406-20415`, `:24222-24231`, `:24942-24951`); convenience constructors expose the RandR, DRM, and WinRT query paths directly (`:9859-9880`). These functions retrieve/identify display handles; they do not acquire display control. Vulkan defines separate acquire calls for Xlib, DRM, and WinRT, while `vkReleaseDisplayEXT` releases previously acquired display access ([WSI display acquisition](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/VK_KHR_surface/wsi.html#_acquiring_and_releasing_displays), [`vkReleaseDisplayEXT`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkReleaseDisplayEXT.html)).

**Trigger and scope:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp RAII client obtains one of these queried `DisplayKHR` wrappers and lets it clear/destruct without acquiring the display, or obtains another wrapper for a display whose control has been acquired through the same Vulkan instance. **Consequence:** the wrapper issues a release for unacquired display state; if the same display was acquired elsewhere, this can release that control prematurely while the other owner still expects it. Subsequent direct-display operations can fail or the display can return to the native display system. **Affected configuration:** clients of the optional copied Vulkan-Hpp RAII header using `VK_KHR_display`, `VK_EXT_acquire_xlib_display` with the Xlib platform guard, `VK_EXT_acquire_drm_display`, or `VK_NV_acquire_winrt_display` with its Win32 platform guard. No checked-in C++ caller was found; no default runtime inclusion is claimed. **Confidence:** high that the query paths produce release-on-destruction wrappers and acquisition is a separate API operation; the exact driver response to a release without a matching acquisition is implementation-dependent. Return a non-owning display handle from query methods, or track whether this wrapper performed/owns acquisition before releasing. No Vulkan call, display, build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd14479"></a>
## GD14479 - Vulkan-Hpp latency timings return unused vector entries

`SwapchainKHR::getLatencyTimingsNV()` performs a count query, resizes `timings`, passes that capacity into the fill call through `GetLatencyMarkerInfoNV::timingCount`, and returns the vector without shrinking it to the count written by the fill call (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_raii.hpp:27059-27073`). The structure contract says the fill call overwrites `timingCount` with the number of values actually written ([`VkGetLatencyMarkerInfoNV`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkGetLatencyMarkerInfoNV.html)).

**Trigger and scope:** an optional Vulkan-Hpp client calls the wrapper while the number of retained latency reports changes between the count and fill calls. **Consequence:** the returned vector contains default-initialized trailing entries that were not written by Vulkan, and its length overstates the number of valid reports. This timing data describes newest collected frames, so report count can vary as the queue advances. **Affected configuration:** clients using `VK_NV_low_latency2` through the optional copied Vulkan-Hpp RAII header; no checked-in C++ caller was found. **Confidence:** medium-high for the missing trim and count contract; the timing queue changing between the calls is runtime-dependent. Resize to the returned `timingCount` before returning. No Vulkan swapchain, call, build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd14480"></a>
## GD14480 - Nouveau compatibility I²C adapter rejects single-message reads

The Nouveau compatibility adapter advertises `I2C_FUNC_I2C` (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_i2c.c:157-162`), and its `i2c_master_recv()` wrapper submits one `I2C_M_RD` message (`:188-193`). However, `i2c_bit_xfer()` handles only (a) a two-message one-byte register probe, (b) a two-message write/read where at least one message is longer than one byte, and (c) a single message with flags zero (`:123-151`). A single read therefore falls into the unsupported-case branch and returns `-EOPNOTSUPP`. This conflicts with both the advertised functionality and the provided receive helper.

The in-tree CH7006 and SIL164 encoder code uses `i2c_master_recv()` after writing the register address (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/dispnv04/i2c/ch7006_drv.c:393-404`; `ch7006_mode.c:380-390`; `sil164_drv.c:120-130`). These calls receive `-EOPNOTSUPP`, and the encoder read helpers take their error path. The adapter's single-message write path does work, so this defect specifically prevents the read half of those helpers from succeeding. **Affected configuration and trigger:** an explicitly built Nouveau HIDD accesses an encoder through these compatibility helpers; Nouveau is excluded from the default aggregate in this checkout (`workbench/mmakefile.src:36-41`; `arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:7-13`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-28`). **Consequence:** encoder register reads fail even though the adapter advertises generic I²C support. Support single-message reads or stop advertising the unsupported capability and avoid the helper path. **Confidence:** high for dispatch behavior and direct helper/caller correspondence; optional/unselected build limits default-tree impact. No I²C transfer, Nouveau build, or hardware operation was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14481"></a>
## GD14481 - Nouveau compatibility I²C transfer dereferences an unallocated device

Both `i2c_writeread()` and `i2c_write()` call `OOP_NewObject()` to create a temporary `CLID_Hidd_I2CDevice`, then unconditionally pass that result to `OOP_DoMethod()` and `OOP_DisposeObject()` (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_i2c.c:24-52,58-90`). There is no NULL check or error return between construction and dispatch. `OOP_DoMethod` expands to dereferencing the object's class pointer (`rom/oop/include/oop.h:101`), so if device-object construction fails, either transfer path dereferences NULL instead of returning a failed transfer. The `i2c_bit_xfer()` caller selects these helpers for supported write/read forms (`linux_i2c.c:131-142`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** the optional Nouveau HIDD uses the compatibility adapter and allocation of a temporary I²C device object fails during a write or combined write/read transfer; this module is excluded from the default aggregate in this checkout (`workbench/mmakefile.src:36-41`; `arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:7-13`; `workbench/hidds/nouveau/mmakefile.src:18-28`). **Consequence:** the I²C caller faults during memory pressure rather than receiving an error. Check the allocation result and return an appropriate negative transfer error before method dispatch or disposal. **Confidence:** high for unchecked construction result and macro dereference; occurrence requires allocation failure. No allocation failure, I²C transfer, Nouveau build or hardware operation was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14482"></a>
## GD14482 - Nouveau internal I²C bit-bang truncates message lengths to eight bits

The compatibility `struct i2c_msg` declares `len` as `__u16` (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/include/linux/i2c.h:58-63`), but `nvkm_i2c_bit_xfer()` copies each message length into `u8 remaining` before its read/write loops (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/i2c/bit.c:183-204`). Any length divisible by 256 becomes zero; other lengths above 255 are truncated modulo 256. For a 256-byte message, the function sends the address and then skips the data loop, yet returns `num` as success if no earlier error occurred (`:186-207`). The path is installed in `nvkm_i2c_bus_algo` through `nvkm_i2c_bus_xfer()` (`bus.c:75-104`) when bus construction chooses its internal bus function (`bus.c:214-250`). **Affected configuration and trigger:** an explicitly built Nouveau HIDD configured to use the internal bit-bang implementation receives a message longer than 255 bytes. The source has an `CONFIG_NOUVEAU_I2C_INTERNAL` guard around this implementation; the default external `i2c.hidd` bit-bang route is separate. No checked-in caller with a transfer above 255 bytes was found in the inspected Nouveau I²C call sites. **Consequence:** data is silently omitted or truncated while transfer reports success. Use a counter wide enough for `i2c_msg.len` or reject unsupported lengths before starting the transaction. **Confidence:** high for width mismatch and resulting loop bound; low for current in-tree occurrence because no qualifying caller was found and the internal implementation is optional. No I²C transfer, build or hardware operation was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14483"></a>
## GD14483 - Nouveau compatibility I²C adapter treats one-byte register reads as probes

The first branch in `i2c_bit_xfer()` treats any two-message transaction with equal addresses, one-byte write and one-byte read, and the expected flags as a probe; it calls `HIDD_I2C_ProbeAddress()` and reports two messages completed (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm-compat/linux_i2c.c:123-129`). A probe only emits the address and checks its acknowledgement: generic `Hidd_I2C::ProbeAddress()` creates a temporary device, calls `I2C_Address()`, and stops without sending the write byte or reading a data byte (`workbench/hidds/i2c/i2cclass.c:178-205`). The following general write/read branch requires at least one message length greater than one (`linux_i2c.c:131-136`), so the normal one-byte register-read transaction never reaches `i2c_writeread()`.

Nouveau's `nvkm_rdi2cr()` constructs exactly this pair: a one-byte register write followed by a one-byte read, and returns the receive buffer when `i2c_transfer()` reports two messages (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/nouveau/include/nvkm/subdev/i2c.h:91-103`). Through the adapter, the probe branch reports success without modifying that buffer, so the helper returns an uninitialized/stale byte as if it were the register value. **Affected configuration and trigger:** the optional Nouveau HIDD uses the AROS bit-banged adapter for a one-byte register read; bus setup selects `i2c_bit_algo` when GPIO callbacks are present and `NvI2C` is false (`drm/nouveau/nvkm/subdev/i2c/bus.c:214-250`; default false option is established at `:214-217`). Nouveau remains excluded from the default aggregate here (`workbench/mmakefile.src:36-41`; `arch/all-pc/drivers/mmakefile.src:7-13`). **Consequence:** register reads can return stale data while claiming a successful transfer, breaking the numerous NVKM register-read helpers. Distinguish the probe API from generic write/read transactions and dispatch the latter through `i2c_writeread()`. **Confidence:** high for the exact message shape, branch ordering, probe semantics and success return; optional target limits default-tree impact. No I²C transaction, Nouveau build, or hardware operation was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14484"></a>
## GD14484 - ColorMap SetColors can wrap its required size and write out of bounds

`CM__Hidd_ColorMap__SetColors()` computes the required entry count as `msg->firstColor + msg->numColors` in `ULONG` without checking addition overflow (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_colormapclass.c:247-250`). It only grows the color array when that wrapped result exceeds the current entry count; it then forms `&data->clut.colors[msg->firstColor]` and writes `numColors` entries (`:254-283`). The HIDD method accepts both indices as `ULONG` (`:200-205`), and `ColorMap::New()` accepts arbitrary `NumEntries` values despite only logging a diagnostic above 256 (`:68-80`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a client calls the public HIDD ColorMap `SetColors` method with a `firstColor` near `ULONG_MAX` and a positive `numColors` such that their sum wraps to a value no larger than the existing entry count (for example `firstColor = ULONG_MAX`, `numColors = 1`). The growth check is bypassed, but the subsequent indexed pointer and write still use the huge starting index, causing an out-of-bounds write. **Affected configuration:** builds including the generic `hidd.gfx` ColorMap class. The checked-in direct callers found are the bitmap wrapper (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:1337-1340`, whose public first/count arguments are `UWORD`) and the Amiga P96 sprite path (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/p96gfx/p96gfx_hiddclass.c:1377`, count one); neither establishes an in-tree overflow trigger. The finding therefore concerns direct HIDD clients or future callers using the method's full-width arguments. Reject ranges where `numColors > ULONG_MAX - firstColor` before computing the end or touching the allocation. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked arithmetic and write path; no maintained triggering caller found. No ColorMap method, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only; see the [SetColors range trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#colormap-setcolors-overflow-gd14484).

<a id="gd14485"></a>
## GD14485 - Display Show ignores framebuffer palette-copy failures

`copy_bm_and_colmap()` reads the source bitmap's ColorMap entry count, then loops over the entries and calls `HIDD_CM_GetColor()` and `HIDD_BM_SetColors()` one entry at a time without checking either result (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:50-61`). `HIDD_BM_SetColors()` can fail when it must grow the destination ColorMap and `AllocMem()` fails (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:1315-1345`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_colormapclass.c:247-264`). Both `Show()` call paths ignore the helper's lack of status: copy-back to the old bitmap at `gfx_displayclass.c:1217`, and copying a newly shown bitmap into the framebuffer at `:1248`; the latter proceeds into the pixel CopyBox and then commits the shown bitmap state.

**Trigger and consequence:** a display transition copies a bitmap whose palette has more entries than the destination map, and allocation of the expanded destination map fails. The failed entry and subsequent entries are silently omitted, while `Show()` continues; the new framebuffer or copied-back bitmap can therefore retain stale/missing palette colors while the display transition is treated as successful. **Affected configuration:** the generic framebuffer-backed display class when source/destination palette sizes differ and palette expansion fails. **Confidence:** high that the boolean failure is discarded on both paths; conditional on palette growth being needed and allocation failing for the visible color mismatch. Propagate palette-copy errors and abort or roll back the transition before reporting success. No display transition, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only; see the [framebuffer palette-copy trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#display-show-palette-copy-failure-gd14485).

<a id="gd14486"></a>
## GD14486 - SetRGB32 writes beyond the HIDD bitmap pixel lookup table

`internal_SetRGB32Colors()` passes the supplied `first` and `count` to `HIDD_BM_SetColors()`, then writes every returned `colors[i].pixval` into `HIDD_BM_PIXTAB(vp->RasInfo->BitMap)[first + i]` without checking the index (`rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:14-53`). HIDD bitmap pixel tables allocated by `AllocBitMap()` contain exactly `AROS_PALETTE_SIZE` entries, 256 (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h:109-110`; `rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:424-425`). `SetRGB32()` accepts an `ULONG n` and invokes this helper with `(n, 1)` (`setrgb32.c:114-124`). It first calls `SetRGB32CM()`, which ignores indices at or above `ColorMap.Count`, but that check does not gate the later HIDD helper call (`rom/graphics/setrgb32cm.c:68-78`). The same helper is called for complete `LoadRGB32()` and `LoadRGB4()` batches (`rom/graphics/loadrgb32.c:102`; `rom/graphics/loadrgb4.c:98`); those APIs accept caller-supplied counts and do not cap them at the 256-entry PixTab size.

**Trigger and consequence:** call `SetRGB32()` for a HIDD RastPort bitmap with `n >= 256`, or call `LoadRGB32()`/`LoadRGB4()` with a batch extending beyond entry 255, on a palette or truecolor pixel format. Even when the public ColorMap says an index is out of range, the helper still invokes the HIDD setter and writes to PixTab index `n`; index 256 is already one element beyond the allocated table. The batch APIs also apply their entire count through this helper without a 256-entry clamp. This can corrupt adjacent memory. **Affected configuration:** graphics.library's HIDD bitmap path with its fixed 256-entry PixTab. **Confidence:** high for the fixed table size, selected helper call paths, and out-of-range write; no checked-in caller using such a range was found. Validate the index range against `AROS_PALETTE_SIZE` before both HIDD palette update and PixTab write, preserving the documented ignore behavior. No palette API call, memory fault, or build was run; source-only; see the [SetRGB32 PixTab bounds trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#setrgb32-pixtab-bounds-gd14486).

<a id="gd14487"></a>
## GD14487 - Wanderer reports a successful copy when destination close fails

`performDataCopy()` checks the byte count returned by each `Write()`, but ignores the result of `Close(out)` and then continues to `CopyFileInfo()` and returns `quit`, which remains FALSE when no earlier error was noticed (`workbench/system/Wanderer/filesystems.c:197-236,253`). The DOS `Close()` contract explicitly permits failure and returns zero on error (`rom/dos/close.c:27-36`). A selected FAT handler can reject `ACTION_END`: it runs `TestLock()` and returns `DOSFALSE` when the volume is no longer mounted (`rom/filesys/fat/packet.c:375-390`; `lock.c:55-72`). On disk removal with outstanding locks, FAT clears `glob->sb` and retains the old volume in its spare list (`disk.c:64-67`; `volume.c:1114-1128`), so a still-open destination handle can reach that failing close path.

**Trigger and consequence:** a destination operation reaches `Close(out)` and its filesystem reports an `ACTION_END` failure, for example if a removable FAT volume is removed after the final successful write but before the close packet is handled. FAT's removal path explicitly detaches the volume while open locks remain, and its subsequent close packet rejects the old volume as not mounted. Wanderer discards the close status and returns success, so the copy result does not tell the caller that the destination handle failed to close; the destination may be incomplete or not finalized. This is separate from GD5846's negative `Read()` result and the existing `CopyFileInfo()` metadata-result finding. **Affected configuration:** Wanderer file-copy operations on filesystems that can fail the close packet; the FAT handler is one selected implementation. **Confidence:** high for the ignored result and FAT failure path; the exact copy/remove interleaving is conditional. No close failure, media removal, file copy, or build was induced; source-only; see the [close-result trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-copy-close-result-gd14487).

<a id="gd14488-copytopar-reports-success-after-a-short-parallel-device-write"></a>
<a id="gd14488"></a>
## GD14488 - CopyToPAR reports success after a short parallel-device write

`CopyToPAR`'s `WritePAR()` sets the request's `CMD_WRITE`, buffer and requested length, then decides success solely from `DoIO()`'s returned `io_Error`; it never compares `io_Actual` with the requested `size` (`workbench/c/CopyToPAR.c:150-157`). The copy loop treats every non-error completion as a complete chunk and continues until the file is exhausted (`:170-186`). The USB printer worker sets `io_Actual` to `psdStreamWrite()`'s byte count but obtains the error from `ncp_EPInStream` after writing to `ncp_EPOutStream` (`rom/usb/classes/printer/printer.class.c:705-720`). Poseidon reports a USB OUT transfer error in the OUT stream's error field and can return a byte count smaller than the requested length (`rom/usb/poseidon/poseidon.library.c:5235-5266,5410-5464`); `psdGetStreamError()` reads the passed stream's field (`:5537-5549`).

**Trigger and consequence:** `CopyToPAR FILE USB` reaches a short OUT transfer while the optional IN stream reports no error. The device request then completes with fewer bytes than requested and a clear `io_Error`, so `WritePAR()` reports success and the utility advances to the next chunk or exits successfully. This can silently omit part of the file from the printer output. The printer class's separate cross-stream error handling is already tracked as OD3367; this finding records the additional in-tree caller consequence and `CopyToPAR`'s independent failure to check the byte count. **Affected configuration:** the selected `CopyToPAR` command with its USB option and a printer-class device exposing an IN stream; `CopyToPAR` is in the Workbench C command manifest (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:13`). **Confidence:** high for the missing count check and class/stream data flow; an actual short transfer was not induced. No USB request, print job, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#copytopar-short-write-gd14488).

<a id="gd14489-copy-can-delete-a-moved-source-after-destination-close-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14489"></a>
## GD14489 - Copy can delete a moved source after destination close failure

After `CopyFile()` reports success, the normal file-copy path calls `Close(out)` and ignores its return, then closes the input and, in MOVE mode, deletes the source (`workbench/c/Copy.c:2067-2085`). Its direct path likewise ignores `Close(out)` after copying (`:914-921`); the non-filesystem streaming path does so at `:1761-1778`. DOS documents that `Close()` can fail and returns zero on error (`rom/dos/close.c:27-36`). The selected FAT handler can reject `ACTION_END` when the volume has been detached (`rom/filesys/fat/packet.c:375-390`); disk removal with outstanding locks detaches the volume and retains its old superblock (`disk.c:64-67`; `volume.c:1114-1128`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a copy or move finishes its explicit writes, then the destination handler reports an `ACTION_END` failure. In MOVE mode, the normal path still treats `CopyFile()`'s zero result as success and calls `KillFile()` on the source; if that succeeds, `Copy` reports the move as successful despite the destination close failure. In ordinary copy mode it can also report success for a destination that the handler did not successfully finalize. **Affected configuration:** the selected Workbench `Copy` command (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:72`) when writing to a filesystem that can fail close/finalization; the removable FAT path is a concrete conditional implementation. This is a separate caller from GD14487, which tracks Wanderer's ignored close result. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked close and MOVE deletion sequence; the filesystem close failure is conditional. No file was copied or moved and no close failure was induced; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#copy-command-full-body-and-close-metadata-version-review-gd14489-gd14491).

<a id="gd14492-join-reports-success-when-closing-its-destination-fails"></a>
<a id="gd14492"></a>
## GD14492 - Join reports success when closing its destination fails

`main()` opens the destination with `MODE_NEWFILE`, runs `doJoin()`, then ignores `Close(destfile)`'s return and returns the unchanged `rc` (`workbench/c/Join.c:110-118`). DOS documents that `Close()` can fail and returns zero on error (`rom/dos/close.c:31-36`). A selected FAT handler can reject its `ACTION_END` packet after the volume has detached while locks remain (`rom/filesys/fat/packet.c:375-390`; `disk.c:64-67`; `volume.c:1114-1128`).

**Trigger and consequence:** all source appends complete, but the destination handler fails when `Join` closes its output. `doJoin()` has returned `RETURN_OK`, and `main()` neither changes `rc` nor removes the file because cleanup only runs for an earlier error. The command therefore reports success even though the filesystem rejected final close. **Affected configuration:** the selected Workbench `Join` command (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:25`) writing to a filesystem that can fail close/finalization; removable FAT is one conditional path. **Confidence:** high for the ignored return and selected handler path; no close failure was induced. Propagate close failure and remove or report the incomplete destination. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#join-full-body-review-gd14492-gd14494).

<a id="gd14495-diskchange-suppresses-the-missing-device-argument-error"></a>
<a id="gd14495"></a>
## GD14495 - DiskChange suppresses the missing-device argument error

`ReadArgs("DEVICE/A", ...)` failure leaves the local `error` at its initial zero because `main()` has no parse-failure branch (`workbench/c/DiskChange.c:63-75`). It still calls `PrintFault(error, "DiskChange")`. `PrintFault()` explicitly emits no text when its error code is zero (`rom/dos/printfault.c:65-71`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke the selected `DiskChange` command without its required `DEVICE` argument or with an argument parse error. `ReadArgs()` fails and sets `IoErr()`, but the command returns `RETURN_FAIL` without displaying the parse diagnostic because it passes zero to `PrintFault()`. Copy `IoErr()` into `error` on the failure path before reporting. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench C `DiskChange` command (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:17`) when argument parsing fails. **Confidence:** high for the missing assignment and zero-code PrintFault behavior. No command was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#checkmem-and-diskchange-command-full-body-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14493-join-ignores-wildcard-enumeration-errors-after-matching-a-file"></a>
<a id="gd14493"></a>
## GD14493 - Join ignores wildcard enumeration errors after matching a file

`doJoin()` loops while `MatchNext(ap)` returns zero, but after the loop it checks only Ctrl-C and whether `numfiles` is zero; it never inspects the final `match` result (`workbench/c/Join.c:167-195`). The DOS `MatchNext()` contract returns zero on success or an error code on failure (`rom/dos/matchnext.c:17-27,438`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a wildcard has yielded at least one file and a later `MatchNext()` fails, for example on a filesystem enumeration error. Since `numfiles` is already nonzero, the no-files branch does not run, and `rc` remains `RETURN_OK`. `Join` can then close and retain a destination missing the remaining matching files while reporting success. **Affected configuration:** the selected Workbench `Join` command with a patterned source and an enumeration failure after one or more matches. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked error result and return path; no enumeration failure was induced. Treat `ERROR_NO_MORE_ENTRIES` as normal and propagate other `MatchNext()` errors. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#join-full-body-review-gd14492-gd14494).

<a id="gd14494-join-labels-source-read-errors-as-write-errors"></a>
<a id="gd14494"></a>
## GD14494 - Join labels source read errors as write errors

When `Read()` returns -1, `append()` prints the `STR_ERR_READING` message (`workbench/c/Join.c:232-237`). `getstring(STR_ERR_READING)` returns the literal `"Error while writing"`, the same wording as the distinct write-error case (`:288-296`).

**Trigger and consequence:** reading a source file fails. The command prints the correct `IoErr()` via `PrintFault()`, followed by a contradictory “Error while writing” label, which misidentifies the failed operation during diagnosis. **Affected configuration:** all selected `Join` invocations that encounter a source `Read()` error. **Confidence:** high; the return string and caller are direct. Correct the read-error text. No read error or command was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#join-full-body-review-gd14492-gd14494).

<a id="gd14490-copy-reports-success-when-requested-metadata-updates-fail"></a>
<a id="gd14490"></a>
## GD14490 - Copy reports success when requested metadata updates fail

The successful-operation path sets `COPYFLAG_DONE`, prints the success result, then calls `SetData()` without using a return value (`workbench/c/Copy.c:2124-2136`). `SetData()` discards the results of `SetProtection()`, and, when requested, `SetFileDate()` and `SetComment()` (`:2316-2338`). These DOS calls return Boolean success indicators and document `IoErr()` on failure (`rom/dos/setprotection.c:25-36`; `setfiledate.c:31-45`; `setcomment.c:25-45`). `SetComment()` also rejects comments longer than `MAXCOMMENTLENGTH` (`setcomment.c:58-62`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a file's data copy succeeds, then the destination handler rejects a requested protection, date, or comment update, or the source comment exceeds the DOS limit. The command has already recorded its success and does not change its result when `SetData()`'s operation fails; the destination therefore differs from the requested clone/metadata state while `Copy` reports success. Protection is requested by default unless `NOPRO` is set; dates and comments are requested by `DATES`/`COM` or `CLONE`. **Affected configuration:** the selected Workbench `Copy` command with a destination filesystem that rejects one of the requested metadata actions, or a too-long source comment under `COM`/`CLONE`. **Confidence:** high for discarded status and success ordering; no metadata failure was induced. Propagate the metadata status and report a partial copy result. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#copy-command-full-body-and-close-metadata-version-review-gd14489-gd14491).

<a id="gd14491-copy-newer-version-parsing-can-scan-beyond-its-fixed-buffer"></a>
<a id="gd14491"></a>
## GD14491 - Copy NEWER version parsing can scan beyond its fixed buffer

With `NEWER`, `VersionFind()` reads file data into a fixed 4096-byte allocation, searches for `$VER:`, then calls `makeversionfromstring()` without passing the valid byte count or adding a terminating NUL (`workbench/c/Copy.c:2522-2552`). The allocation is initially zeroed, but a successful 4096-byte read fills it completely. `makeversionfromstring()` calls `skipnonspaces()`, whose loop stops only at NUL or a space and has no buffer limit (`:2570-2589,2673-2681`).

**Trigger and consequence:** `Copy NEWER` examines a source or destination file containing `$VER:` followed by a malformed, non-space run that fills the version buffer. When the 4096-byte read has no NUL terminator and the run reaches the allocation boundary, `skipnonspaces()` continues reading beyond the allocated buffer while attempting to find the expected separator. This can fault or otherwise make version comparison unreliable instead of rejecting the malformed version string. **Affected configuration:** the selected `Copy` command's `NEWER` option and a file with a `$VER:` marker whose following token is not separated by a space within the read buffer. **Confidence:** high for the missing length/termination and unbounded scan; the malformed input was not run. Carry the available buffer length through parsing and reject unterminated tokens. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#copy-command-full-body-and-close-metadata-version-review-gd14489-gd14491).
<a id="gd14497-makedir-all-discards-create-error"></a>
<a id="gd14497"></a>
<a id="gd14497-makedir-all-clears-the-error-when-creating-a-path-component-fails"></a>
## GD14497 — MakeDir ALL clears the error when creating a path component fails

`CreateDirAll()` attempts `CreateDir(name)` after locking a path component fails, but if that creation also fails it exits the loop without saving the resulting `IoErr()` (`workbench/c/MakeDir.c:145-164`). The common failure cleanup then calls `SetIoErr(error)` with the still-zero local value (`:208-220`). The same loss can occur when changing the new directory's mode fails and the retrying `Lock()` also fails (`:165-171`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke `MakeDir ALL` for a path whose missing component cannot be created, for example because the parent is not writable or storage is exhausted. The command returns failure with `IoErr()` reset to zero, so scripts and callers cannot identify the actual cause and `PrintFault()` emits no useful fault text. Preserve the failing operation's error before cleanup. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds when `ALL` is used and a component creation/permission retry fails. **Confidence:** high; no directory operation or filesystem error was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#makedir-all-path-creation-and-error-preservation-pass-gd14497).

<a id="gd14498"></a>
<a id="gd14498-list-leaks-pattern-buffers-when-pattern-parsing-fails"></a>
## GD14498 — List leaks pattern buffers when pattern parsing fails

For `SUB`, `main()` allocates `subpatternStr` and returns from the parse-error branch without freeing it (`workbench/c/List.c:1194-1204`). For `PAT`, it similarly allocates `parsedPattern` and omits its free when `ParsePatternNoCase()` returns `-1` (`:1215-1223`). The DOS parser documents `-1` on error and sets `IoErr()` for malformed syntax (`rom/dos/parsepattern.c:39-51`; `rom/dos/patternmatching.c:440-443,463-518`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run List with a malformed `PAT` (for example an unmatched pattern delimiter), or a malformed `SUB` string that makes its wrapped pattern invalid. The command reports failure but leaves the allocated parse buffer allocated; repeated invocations retain memory. Free the successfully allocated buffer on the parse-error branches. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds with invalid `PAT`/`SUB` syntax after the corresponding allocation succeeds. **Confidence:** high for both allocation/error/return paths and parser error contract; no pattern command or allocation failure was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#list-command-full-body-pattern-and-cleanup-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14499-list-all-leaks-unvisited-recursion-nodes-after-a-traversal-error"></a>
<a id="gd14499"></a>
## GD14499 — List ALL leaks queued directories after a traversal error

With `ALL`, `listFile()` queues child directories in `DirList` and moves each directory it processes to `FreeDirNodeList` (`workbench/c/List.c:992-1007,1048-1061`). If a later `MatchFirst()`/`MatchNext()` fails, the loop breaks, but cleanup drains only `FreeDirNodeList`; remaining nodes and their `StrDup()`-allocated path strings stay allocated (`:1064-1068`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use `ALL` on a tree where multiple child directories are queued, then a queued directory fails to match or traverse (for example it is removed or becomes inaccessible before its turn). List reports the traversal error but leaks the unvisited queue nodes and path strings. Drain and free both lists on every exit. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds with recursive listing and a traversal error while queued siblings remain. **Confidence:** high for the queue insertion, error break and one-list-only cleanup; the race/permission trigger is conditional. No directory traversal or filesystem error was induced. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#list-command-full-body-pattern-and-cleanup-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14500-assign-leaves-utility-library-open-on-argument-errors"></a>
<a id="gd14500"></a>
## GD14500 — Assign leaves utility.library open on argument-validation errors

`Main()` opens `utility.library` and then `dos.library` (`workbench/c/Assign.c:229-234`). The mutually exclusive-option and invalid-device-name branches close DOS, free parsed arguments, then return directly without reaching the common `CloseLibrary(UtilityBase)` (`:248-255,260-276,315-318`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke Assign with incompatible operation switches or a malformed device name after both libraries open. The command returns failure but leaves the utility.library open reference outstanding; repeated invalid invocations accumulate references. Route these exits through common cleanup or close UtilityBase before returning. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c-sh` builds where utility.library opens and one of these argument-validation branches is taken. **Confidence:** high for the open and bypassed close; no invalid invocation or library state was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#assign-shell-command-full-body-initialization-and-output-pass).

<a id="gd14501-assign-reports-success-after-deferred-output-is-cancelled"></a>
<a id="gd14501"></a>
## GD14501 — Assign reports success after Ctrl-C stops deferred output

`_DeferFlush()` consumes `SIGBREAKF_CTRL_C`, sets only its local `broken` flag, stops writing and prints `ERROR_BREAK` (`workbench/c/Assign.c:913-938`). It returns `void`; `showAssigns()` also returns `void`, and `Main()` retains its existing `error` value when the output was a successful listing (`:283-308,319-321`).

**Trigger and consequence:** interrupt deferred assign listing with Ctrl-C while `_DeferFlush()` is writing. The remaining buffered text is discarded, a break diagnostic is printed, but Assign can exit with `RETURN_OK`, so scripts cannot detect the interrupted listing. Return and propagate a cancellation status such as `RETURN_WARN`. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c-sh` builds when Ctrl-C is received during deferred output. **Confidence:** high for the consumed signal, truncated buffer-drain path and unchanged result; no signal or listing was run. Source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#assign-shell-command-full-body-initialization-and-output-pass).



<a id="gd14502-adddatatypes-workbench-argument-loop-never-advances"></a>
<a id="gd14502"></a>
## GD14502 — AddDataTypes loops past Workbench startup arguments

The Workbench startup loop initializes `num` to 1 and tests it against `sm_NumArgs`, but its increment expression advances only `wa`; `num` is never changed (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:273-281`). `wa` starts at `sm_ArgList[1]`, the first argument after the command itself.

**Trigger and consequence:** launch AddDataTypes from Workbench with at least one argument.
