The first descriptor is loaded, then the loop condition remains true and the argument pointer advances beyond the argument array. The command continues reading invalid `WBArg` entries and may load unintended names or fail unpredictably instead of terminating after the supplied arguments. Increment `num` alongside `wa` (or iterate directly using the bounded index). **Affected configuration:** the optional `workbench-c-adddatatypes` executable launched through Workbench with a nonempty argument list. **Confidence:** high; the loop counter is invariant in the source. No Workbench launch or descriptor load was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#adddatatypes-command-full-body-descriptor-and-startup-review-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14503-adddatatypes-leaks-allocation-on-header-decode-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14503"></a>
## GD14503 — AddDataTypes leaks the descriptor allocation when header decoding fails

`CreateDataType()` allocates `cdt` after finding a DTHD property, then enters the success path only if `ReadStruct()` succeeds (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:796-810`). If decoding fails, the function falls through and returns `cdt` without linking or freeing it; the caller ignores the return value (`LoadDataType()`, `:493-510`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a DTHD property is present but its fixed header cannot be decoded, including a truncated or malformed header. Each such descriptor attempt retains the allocated `CompoundDataType` block. Free `cdt` on the decode-failure path and return NULL. **Affected configuration:** AddDataTypes processes an invalid datatype descriptor with a DTHD property. **Confidence:** high for allocation ownership and the unchecked failure path; the malformed descriptor was not run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#adddatatypes-command-full-body-descriptor-and-startup-review-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14504-adddatatypes-reads-fixed-header-from-short-dthd-property"></a>
<a id="gd14504"></a>
## GD14504 — AddDataTypes decodes a fixed header without checking the DTHD property size

`CreateDataType()` allocates `cdt` using `sizeof(struct CompoundDataType) - 32 + prop->sp_Size`, then passes `prop->sp_Data` to `ReadStruct()` without checking that the DTHD property contains the fixed 32-byte `FileDataTypeHeader` (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:796-810`). `FileDataTypeHeaderDesc` declares a 32-byte destination, and its `MemStreamHook()` reads and advances the source pointer for every requested byte without a length parameter or boundary check (`:103-121,707-731`). `ReadStruct()` issues all descriptor reads and treats the hook's returned byte as valid (`compiler/arossupport/readstruct.c:85-112`). Thus a DTHD chunk shorter than 32 bytes can make the decoder read beyond `sp_Data`; because the destination allocation also shrinks with `sp_Size`, the fixed-width writes can extend beyond `cdt` as well.

**Trigger and consequence:** AddDataTypes processes a descriptor whose DTHD property size is below 32 bytes. Header decoding accesses bytes outside the property data, and the destination may be undersized for the fixed header. Reject undersized DTHD properties before allocation/decoding and bound the stream hook by the property length. **Affected configuration:** AddDataTypes processes a malformed datatype descriptor. **Confidence:** high for the missing size check, fixed read size and size-derived allocation; no malformed descriptor was run; source-only. This is distinct from GD14503's allocation leak when a decode fails.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#adddatatypes-command-full-body-descriptor-and-startup-review-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14505-adddatatypes-does-not-validate-dthd-payload-offsets"></a>
<a id="gd14505"></a>
## GD14505 — AddDataTypes trusts DTHD offsets and lengths outside the property payload

After copying the bytes following the fixed header into `cdt + 1`, `CreateDataType()` converts the file's name, base-name, pattern, and mask offsets directly into pointers, without checking them against the copied payload length (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:818-829,854-856`). The descriptor generator defines these offsets relative to the payload after the 32-byte header (`tools/dtdesc/createdtdesc.c:510-524,553-580`). No validation ensures the string offsets land inside the payload and reach a NUL before its end, or that `maskOffset + 2 * maskLen` remains within it. The resulting pointers are used in debug string output and, with DEBUG disabled as checked in, by `AddDataType()`'s `Stricmp()`, `strlen()` and pattern parsing (`:968-1001`). The mask pointer is read for `dth_MaskLen` words during byte-order conversion and again when matching data (`:849-856`; `workbench/libs/datatypes/helpfuncs.c:343-351`).

**Trigger and consequence:** process a DTHD property with an out-of-range offset, unterminated name/pattern, or mask range extending past the payload. The loader can read outside the allocated descriptor data while converting or comparing the descriptor, causing a fault or invalid datatype state. Validate each offset, bounded string terminator and mask extent against `prop->sp_Size - 32` before constructing or using the pointers. **Affected configuration:** AddDataTypes processes a malformed descriptor. **Confidence:** high for unchecked offsets and subsequent length-driven accesses; no malformed descriptor was run. This concerns fields inside a sufficiently large DTHD chunk and is separate from GD14504's short fixed header. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#adddatatypes-command-full-body-descriptor-and-startup-review-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14506-adddatatypes-returns-success-after-descriptor-processing-failures"></a>
<a id="gd14506"></a>
## GD14506 — AddDataTypes reports success after descriptor processing fails

`LoadDataType()` returns `void` and silently skips work when `AllocIFF()`, `Open()`, `OpenIFF()`, chunk setup, `ParseIFF()`, or `CreateDataType()` fails (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:662-703,791-913`). `ScanDirectory()` also returns `void`; it prints `MatchFirst()`/`MatchNext()` errors but does not expose them to `main()` (`:431-497`). After successful CLI argument parsing, `main()` unconditionally assigns `RETURN_OK` after either the file scan or refresh branch (`:285-349`), and the Workbench path similarly reports success after calling the void loader (`:273-284`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke AddDataTypes with a valid command line but a missing, unreadable, malformed, or unloadable descriptor, or use `REFRESH` when traversal or descriptor loading fails. Diagnostics may be printed, but the command exits successfully, so scripts and startup callers cannot distinguish a complete activation from a failed or partial one. Propagate processing status through `LoadDataType()` and `ScanDirectory()` and preserve a failure result when any requested item fails. **Affected configuration:** the optional AddDataTypes command in CLI, `REFRESH`, or Workbench startup mode. **Confidence:** high for the unconditional success assignment and void processing APIs; no command or file error was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#adddatatypes-command-full-body-descriptor-and-startup-review-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14507-datatype-open-count-mutates-under-shared-lock"></a>
<a id="gd14507"></a>
## GD14507 — DataType reference counts are mutated under a shared semaphore

`ObtainDataTypeA()` increments `cdt->OpenCount` before releasing `dtl_Lock` acquired with `ObtainSemaphoreShared()` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/obtaindatatypea.c:103-107,213-218`). `LockDataType()` performs the same non-atomic increment under the shared semaphore (`lockdatatype.c:58-65`), and `ReleaseDataType()` decrements under a shared acquisition (`releasedatatype.c:56-68`). Shared holders are allowed to overlap, so concurrent read/modify/write operations can lose increments or decrements. The consumer uses `OpenCount` to refuse replacement only when it is nonzero (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:1024-1034`); a lost count can therefore allow replacement and freeing of a descriptor while another caller still holds it.

**Trigger and consequence:** two tasks concurrently obtain/lock or release references to the same datatype, and their `OpenCount` updates overlap. The count may understate outstanding references; a later AddDataTypes replacement can treat the datatype as unused and free it while a caller retains the pointer. Protect count changes with exclusive synchronization or an appropriate atomic operation, while preserving the replacement/list lifetime contract. **Affected configuration:** concurrent DataTypes API use and AddDataTypes descriptor replacement; interleaving is possible on SMP and may also occur with task preemption. **Confidence:** high for shared-lock use, non-atomic updates and the replacement consumer; no concurrent call or replacement was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#datatype-api-wrapper-and-reference-count-full-body-pass-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14510-obtainbestpena-overflows-color-distance-scaling"></a>
<a id="gd14510"></a>
## GD14510 — ObtainBestPenA overflows its color-distance scaling calculation

The tolerance decision multiplies `best_distance` by `pe_NFree` in 32-bit `ULONG` arithmetic (`rom/graphics/obtainbestpena.c:119-124`). `best_distance` is the squared 8-bit RGB distance (up to 195,075; `color_support.c:16-55`), while `pe_NFree` and `pe_SharableColors` are 16-bit values (`compiler/include/graphics/view.h:264-276`). A concrete public setup reaches a large enough palette: `OpenScreen()` accepts the documented `SA_ColorMapEntries` tag into a signed `WORD` and passes positive values through to `GetColorMap()` (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:174,685-687,1393-1406`; tag documentation `rom/intuition/openscreentaglist.c:204-218`). A depth-8-or-greater screen with `SA_ColorMapEntries=32767` therefore gets a 32,767-entry ColorMap. `AttachPalExtra()` does not cap shareable colors for depth 8 or above, so `pe_NFree` starts at 32767; one existing shared pen leaves it at 32766 (`rom/graphics/attachpalextra.c:71-109`; `rom/graphics/obtainpen.c:210-224`).

With `OBP_Precision=PRECISION_GUI` (32), suppose that one shared pen is black and the requested color is (109, 236, 252). `color_distance()` yields 131,081. The intended left side is 131,081 × 32,766 = 4,295,000,046, which wraps to 32,750 in 32-bit arithmetic. The right side is 32² × 32,766 = 33,552,384. Since the wrapped left side is smaller, `ObtainBestPenA()` accepts and increments the distant shared black pen instead of attempting to allocate a closer color. The comparison must widen before multiplication.

**Trigger and consequence:** a client uses a depth-8-or-greater screen with at least 32,766 free/shareable entries, has a distant shared color available, and calls `ObtainBestPenA()` with a nonzero precision such as `PRECISION_GUI`. The overflow can make a color outside the requested tolerance appear acceptable, so the function returns a poor color match instead of allocating a new pen or failing under `OBP_FailIfBad`. **Affected configuration:** palettes large enough for the product to wrap below the tolerance threshold; ordinary 256-entry palettes are unaffected. **Confidence:** high for the operand widths, accepted OpenScreen palette size, and arithmetic example; no screen or pen was created. Source-only.

<a id="gd14511-compositor-selects-mode-with-stale-dimensions"></a>
<a id="gd14511"></a>
## GD14511 — Compositor mode selection can pair one mode ID with another mode's dimensions

`FindBestHiddMode()` assigns a difference of `1` when an axis exactly matches the requested dimension (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/displaymode.c:39-41`). Consequently, an exact `800×600` candidate and an `801×601` candidate both score `delta == 1`. If the latter has greater depth and appears later, the equal-delta depth tie-break replaces `found_mode` (`:53-74,76-84`) but does not update `found_width` or `found_height`, which are updated only in the strictly-smaller-delta branch (`:44-51`). The function then stores the stale dimensions in `displayrect` (`:89-94`). The selected ID is passed to bitmap allocation while dimensions come from `displayrect` (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:636-642,692-695`); in the framebuffer path it is also applied directly to the framebuffer (`:680-683`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the selected mode enumeration contains an exact-size truecolor mode and a deeper truecolor mode one pixel larger in both dimensions, with the exact-size mode encountered first. The compositor can allocate or configure a display bitmap using the deeper mode ID but the exact mode's dimensions, causing a failed mode/bitmap match or incorrect clipping/composition. Update the saved dimensions whenever a tied candidate replaces the selected mode, and score exact matches as zero. **Affected configuration:** explicit builds that include the Compositor monitor and a display-mode set with such tied candidates. The Compositor target is opt-in (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/mmakefile.src:4-13`). **Confidence:** high for the stale state pairing and its consumers; no display mode was enumerated or changed. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#compositor-display-mode-selection-full-body-pass-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14512-compositor-rebuilds-regions-under-shared-lock"></a>
<a id="gd14512"></a>
## GD14512 — Compositor rebuilds bitmap regions while holding a shared lock

`BitMapPositionChange()` acquires `LOCK_COMPOSITOR_READ` (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:1357-1365`), but when a displayed bitmap moves it changes the stack node's `leftedge`/`topedge` and invokes `HIDDCompositorToggleCompositing()` or `HIDDCompositorRedrawVisibleRegions(..., NULL)` (`:1411-1431`). The latter calls `HIDDCompositorRecalculateVisibleRegions()`, which mutates shared flags and region state; it clears each node's existing `screenregion` before rebuilding it (`:147-181`). `ClearRegion()` disposes the current rectangle list (`rom/graphics/clearregion.c:56-59`). Meanwhile `BitMapRectChanged()` also takes `LOCK_COMPOSITOR_READ` and traverses the same `screenregion` rectangle nodes (`compositor_class.c:1264-1296,1338-1346`). These methods are reached through the normal Graphics.library wrappers: `ScrollVPort()` calls `compositor_ScrollBitMap()` and `UpdateBitMap()` calls `compositor_UpdateBitMap()` (`rom/graphics/scrollvport.c:68-91`; `rom/graphics/updatebitmap.c:24-40`; `rom/graphics/graphics_compositor.h:30-54`). Those wrappers issue the OOP method directly and add no outer serialization. The lock macros map READ to `ObtainSemaphoreShared()` and WRITE to exclusive `ObtainSemaphore()` (`compositor_intern.h:83-85`); Exec's shared-semaphore path permits concurrent shared holders (`rom/exec/semaphores.c:50-81`), so it does not exclude these mutations from another read-locked caller.

**Trigger and consequence:** on an ExecSMP system, a bitmap position change for a non-top displayed bitmap overlaps a bitmap-rectangle redraw for a displayed bitmap. The position path can free/rebuild region rectangles while the redraw walks them, and concurrent position changes can also race on stack coordinates and compositor mode state. The redraw may use stale region data or observe inconsistent visibility. Use the exclusive compositor lock for position changes and any redraw path that recalculates shared regions. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the optional Compositor monitor on ExecSMP, with concurrent graphics position and bitmap-update calls. **Confidence:** high that a mutating recalculation runs under a shared semaphore while other callers use that semaphore to read the same state; the overlap is conditional and was not scheduled or run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#compositor-position-and-bitmap-redraw-lock-pass-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14513-waitx-fails-to-carry-month-overflow-into-year"></a>
<a id="gd14513"></a>
## GD14513 — WaitX loses the year carry when a recurring month crosses December

Both month-advance sites add `interval->months`, then reduce an over-12 month with `% 12` before computing the year carry (`workbench/c/WaitX.c:341-345,442-449`). After the modulo, `clock->month / 12` is always zero. A one-month advance from December therefore becomes January of the same year; a twelve-month advance produces month zero and does not advance the year. These paths run when advancing a past DATE/TIME schedule and when calculating later recurring executions (`:333-379,440-477`); `MN=MONTHS/K/N` is accepted by the command template (`:136`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke WaitX with a recurring month interval that crosses December, such as `MN=1` starting in December or `MN=12`. The next scheduled date can be interpreted in the wrong year or rejected by `CheckDate()`, causing WaitX to report an invalid/past date or schedule an execution at the wrong time. Compute the carry from the pre-modulo month value and normalize month into 1–12. **Affected configuration:** explicit builds of the shell-command target `workbench-c-sh`; its parent aggregate edge is commented out in this snapshot (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:80-105,142-144`). **Confidence:** high for the arithmetic order and recurrence callers; no date schedule was run. Source-only.

<a id="gd14514-waitx-never-closes-utility-library"></a>
<a id="gd14514"></a>
## GD14514 — WaitX leaks its utility.library open reference

`MainEntry()` opens `utility.library` and stores the result in `UtilityBase` (`workbench/c/WaitX.c:122-124,161-164`), but the command does not call any Utility function and its common exit cleanup closes only DOS (`:497-517`). Every successful Utility open therefore leaves the library open after WaitX exits; the later error paths after the open share the same cleanup omission.

**Trigger and consequence:** run the explicitly built WaitX command once with `utility.library` available. Its open count remains elevated after the process returns, preventing the library from expunging when otherwise unused; repeated invocations retain repeated opens. Remove the unused open or close it in common cleanup. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c-sh` builds; the aggregate parent edge is commented out in this snapshot (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:80-105,142-144`). **Confidence:** high for unmatched open/close ownership; no library lifecycle was exercised. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#waitx-full-body-recurrence-and-resource-pass-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14515-logger-discards-buffer-after-flush-error"></a>
<a id="gd14515"></a>
## GD14515 — Logger discards buffered entries after failed or partial writes

`FlushLogBuffer()` seeks to end of the selected log file and writes the buffered bytes, but ignores both results and sets `logBufUsed` to zero unconditionally (`workbench/c/Logger.c:198-207`). DOS `Seek()` reports `-1` on error (`rom/dos/seek.c:38-40`), and `Write()` can return a short count or `-1` (`rom/dos/write.c:40-43`). The function is called periodically during the logger loop and again during shutdown for each configured file (`Logger.c:536-540,590-598`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the target volume reports a seek/write error or accepts only part of a flush. Logger drops the entire buffer, permanently losing entries that were not written; a failed seek can also leave the write at the prior file position. Check the seek and write results, retain or retry unwritten bytes, and report a flush failure. **Affected configuration:** explicit builds of `workbench-c-logger`; its dependency edge is commented out in this snapshot (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:150-153`). **Confidence:** high for discarded buffer state on unchecked I/O outcomes; no file or write failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sayargs-and-logger-full-body-pass-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14516-psi-does-not-clear-text-mode-info"></a>
<a id="gd14516"></a>
## GD14516 — Public Screen Inspector leaves stale mode details when selection becomes invalid

`DispIDinfo_Set()` resets its text fields with `MUIA_String_Contents` (`workbench/prefs/PSI/displayidinfo_class.c:163-172`), but those objects are created with `TextObject` and use `MUIA_Text_Contents` (`:62-68,101-107,111-117`). These are distinct attributes (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/text.h:19-20`; `classes/string.h:26-27`), so the reset does not clear the displayed text objects. The selected edit-panel caller sets `MUIA_DispIDinfo_ID` to `INVALID_ID` when a display mode query fails (`workbench/prefs/PSI/editpanel_class.c:691-704,741-746`). `FindDisplayInfo()` explicitly returns NULL for `INVALID_ID` (`rom/graphics/finddisplayinfo.c:61-63`), and `GetDisplayInfoData()` returns zero for that missing handle (`rom/graphics/getdisplayinfodata.c:146-159`); consequently none of the later field updates run.

**Trigger and consequence:** PSI shows details for one mode, then its selected mode becomes invalid (for example, the mode list entry is removed or its query fails). The panel reports “unknown mode” elsewhere but retains the prior mode's dimensions, color depth and scan rates. Clear these TextObjects with `MUIA_Text_Contents`. **Affected configuration:** explicit builds of the optional `workbench-prefs-psi` program (`workbench/prefs/PSI/mmakefile.src:6-15`). **Confidence:** high for the mismatched attribute IDs and selected invalid-mode caller; no GUI or mode change was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#psi-display-mode-details-and-system-pen-widgets-full-body-pass-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14517-compositor-continues-mode-selection-after-stack-allocation-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14517"></a>
## GD14517 — Compositor uses an uninitialized sync object after bitmap-stack allocation fails

`BitMapStackChanged()` sets `ok = FALSE` and breaks when allocating the first `StackBitMapNode` fails (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:1145-1159`), leaving the just-purged bitmap stack empty. It nevertheless calls `UpdateDisplayMode()` unconditionally before checking `ok` (`:1217-1218,1247-1252`). On a newly created compositor, `flags` is zero-cleared by OOP Root::New and the constructor only adds `COMPSTATEF_DEEPLUT` (`rom/oop/rootclass.c:115-120`; `compositor_class.c:956-984`), so the non-alpha `CalculateParametersRegular()` path runs. Its reverse stack loop does not execute for the empty list, leaving local `sync` uninitialized, then passes it to `OOP_GetAttr()` for display dimensions (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/displaymode.c:174-221).

**Trigger and consequence:** the first bitmap-stack node allocation fails while Graphics.library loads a non-NULL ViewPort chain. `UpdateDisplayMode()` performs attribute reads through an indeterminate object pointer before the intended reset-and-fallback branch, so the compositor can fault or otherwise fail instead of falling back to a single bitmap. The normal caller is `LoadView()`'s display update through `compositor_LoadViewPorts()` (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:544-553`; `graphics_compositor.h:18-28`). Skip mode selection when stack construction fails, or explicitly handle an empty stack before reading `sync`. **Affected configuration:** explicit builds selecting the optional Compositor monitor (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/mmakefile.src:1-14`). **Confidence:** high for the empty-stack/uninitialized-object path; the allocation failure and resulting OOP behavior were not induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#compositor-stack-allocation-failure-full-caller-pass-gd14517-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14518-compositor-does-not-handle-failed-bitmap-mode-lookup"></a>
<a id="gd14518"></a>
## GD14518 — Compositor dereferences a NULL pixel format for compositable bitmaps with no own ModeID

`CalculateParametersRegular()` obtains each stack bitmap's own ModeID and calls `HIDD_DMEnum_GetMode()` without checking its Boolean result (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/displaymode.c:194-200`). The selected DMEnum implementation sets both output pointers to NULL when the lookup fails (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:1006-1038`), after which this function immediately evaluates `OOP_GET(pf, aHidd_PixFmt_ColorModel)` and later reads attributes through `sync` (`displaymode.c:200-221`).

A compositable bitmap may legitimately have an invalid own ModeID while its friend has a valid one. `AllocBitMap()` retains the friend but, when a special pixel format is requested, explicitly sets the bitmap ModeID back to `vHidd_ModeID_Invalid` (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:256-273,284-313`). The generic bitmap class's compositable setter deliberately resolves the compositing mode from the friend when present and accepts it if that lookup succeeds (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:5170-5206`). OpenScreen's custom-bitmap path consults the display's compositor callbacks and enables a validated HIDD bitmap (`rom/intuition/openscreen.c:1165-1189`; `compositor_class.c:1440-1465`), so the compositor can receive such a bitmap in its ViewPort stack.

**Trigger and consequence:** use an accepted custom HIDD bitmap with a valid friend mode and `ModeID == vHidd_ModeID_Invalid` on a non-alpha compositor path. The mode lookup returns NULL outputs, and the compositor attempts attribute dispatch through NULL rather than using the friend mode or handling lookup failure; loading the ViewPort can fault before display-mode selection completes. Resolve the effective mode through the friend bitmap (as the generic compositable setter does), or handle the failed lookup before using either output. **Affected configuration:** explicit builds selecting the optional Compositor monitor and a graphics/HIDD path supporting such compositable custom bitmaps (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/mmakefile.src:1-14`). **Confidence:** high for the failed-lookup NULL outputs and unchecked uses; no bitmap, OpenScreen call or display update was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#compositor-mode-lookup-failure-custom-friend-bitmap-pass-gd14518-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14519-compositor-retains-alpha-state-across-bitmap-stack-replacement"></a>
<a id="gd14519"></a>
## GD14519 — Compositor carries the prior stack's alpha state into the next mode selection

`BitMapStackChanged()` purges the old stack but does not clear `COMPSTATEF_HASALPHA` (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:816-831,1124-1127`). While building the replacement stack it only sets the flag when it encounters an alpha bitmap (`:1170-1198`); it does not clear a prior value when the new stack contains no alpha bitmap. It then calls `UpdateDisplayMode()` before the later redraw/recalculation (`:1217-1218,1243-1244`). `UpdateDisplayMode()` therefore can run `CalculateParametersAlpha()` against a non-alpha stack. That routine chooses the maximum dimensions among displayable stack bitmaps, whereas the regular path follows the topmost bitmap's mode (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/displaymode.c:100-170,173-222`). `HIDDCompositorRecalculateVisibleRegions()` is where HASALPHA is actually cleared (`compositor_class.c:159-164`), after mode choice; when the replacement top bitmap permits passthrough, the redraw/recalculation path is skipped (`:741-752`).

**Trigger and consequence:** replace a composited stack containing an alpha screen with a non-alpha stack whose topmost bitmap has a smaller mode than a lower displayable bitmap. Mode selection uses the alpha algorithm's maximum-size rule instead of the regular top-screen rule, so it can retain or select a mode and display rectangle that do not match the new topmost screen. If the replacement goes directly to passthrough, HASALPHA also remains set and the old intermediate alpha bitmap is not released by the cleanup guarded on that flag (`:778-795`). Clear HASALPHA when replacing the stack, then derive it solely from the new stack before mode selection and cleanup. **Affected configuration:** explicit builds selecting the optional Compositor monitor; the visible mode mismatch requires multiple displayable bitmaps with differing modes during an alpha-to-non-alpha stack transition. **Confidence:** high for stale flag ordering and skipped cleanup; wrong mode depends on the stated stack/mode combination. No display transition or allocation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#compositor-alpha-flag-stack-replacement-transition-gd14519-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14520-compositor-accepts-composition-bitmap-allocation-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14520"></a>
## GD14520 — Compositor treats failed display-bitmap allocation as a successful stack update

In the non-framebuffer path, `HIDDCompositorToggleCompositing()` calls `AllocBitMap()` for the new display/composition bitmap when `composit` is true and `displaybitmap` is NULL (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:632-648`). If that allocation returns NULL, the branch does not set `ok = FALSE` or otherwise report failure. It skips the new-screen `HIDD_Display_Show()` because `newsdispbitmap` remains NULL, then clears `modeschanged` and returns TRUE (`:748-813`). The caller therefore skips its reset and single-bitmap fallback; it returns the previous `screenbitmap` and reports `active` based on the still-NULL `displaybitmap` (`:1247-1265`).

The maintained Graphics.library caller treats a non-NULL returned bitmap as the requested display update: it updates `frontbm` to the new ViewPort bitmap and, only for displays flagged `DF_DirectFB`, may install the framebuffer into that bitmap (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:552-604`; `display_FBInstall()` checks `DF_DirectFB` at `:452-475`). If an earlier screen bitmap is still returned, Graphics.library records the new top bitmap as frontmost although the old screen remains displayed. If no earlier screen bitmap exists, the caller instead records `frontbm = NULL`, but still returns success while the requested stack was never shown. In neither case does it invoke the documented Compositor failure fallback because `ok` remained TRUE.

**Trigger and consequence:** a ViewPort stack needs software composition on a selected no-framebuffer display, and allocation of the compositor's display bitmap fails. The compositor does not show the requested stack and reports success. With a previous non-NULL screen bitmap, stale front-bitmap bookkeeping is additionally recorded; with no prior screen bitmap, Graphics.library records an empty display while returning success. Propagate the allocation failure through `ok` so the existing reset/single-bitmap fallback runs. **Affected configuration:** explicit builds selecting the optional Compositor monitor, on a no-framebuffer display, when the stack requires composition and display-bitmap allocation fails. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked NULL branch and caller bookkeeping; allocation failure and resulting display state were not induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#compositor-display-bitmap-allocation-failure-caller-pass-gd14520-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14521-compositor-silently-skips-redraw-when-region-allocation-fails"></a>
<a id="gd14521"></a>
## GD14521 — Compositor shows an unrendered composition bitmap when redraw-region allocation fails

`HIDDCompositorRedrawVisibleRegions()` returns immediately if its `NewRegion()` call returns NULL (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:424-427`); the function has no status result. `NewRegion()` returns NULL when its region allocation fails (`rom/graphics/newregion.c:58-68`). When composition is first enabled, `HIDDCompositorToggleCompositing()` invokes this redraw routine before calling `HIDD_Display_Show()` for the new composition bitmap (`compositor_class.c:734-739,757-766`). It does not learn that the redraw was skipped, so it displays the newly allocated bitmap without drawing the viewport stack or its background into it. The outer `BitMapStackChanged()` path then reports the compositor active based on the non-NULL display bitmap and returns the display's non-NULL screen bitmap (`:1247-1265`), so Graphics.library accepts the update (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:552-604`).

**Trigger and consequence:** enabling composition requires an initial full redraw, and either allocating the temporary region or adding the display rectangle to it fails. The new composition bitmap is still shown without its initial contents, producing a blank or stale display until a later redraw succeeds. Return and propagate a redraw failure so the existing reset/single-bitmap fallback runs instead of showing the unrendered buffer. **Affected configuration:** explicit builds selecting the optional Compositor monitor when a ViewPort stack requires software composition and either region allocation fails. **Confidence:** high for both ignored failure paths and the subsequent Show ordering; allocation failure and resulting visual state were not induced. Source-only.

**Additional failure route:** after `NewRegion()` succeeds, `OrRectRegion()` is called on the empty region to add the display rectangle, but its BOOL result is ignored (`compositor_class.c:427-430`). The implementation returns FALSE when allocation of the first region rectangle fails and leaves the region empty (`rom/graphics/orrectregion.c:86-98`); the redraw loops then render nothing. This has the same unrendered-bitmap consequence and is included in GD14521. `BitMapRectChanged()` also invokes this helper for incremental alpha-bitmap damage (`compositor_class.c:1317-1322`); failure there suppresses reconstruction of the damaged composition area, while the caller continues its update/copy path. This caller consequence is also in the GD14521 coverage trace.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#compositor-initial-redraw-region-allocation-failure-pass-gd14521-2026-11-03).

**GD14508 duplicate reconciliation (2026-11-03):** removed GD14508 as a separate finding because it is identical to GD9618 in the `BestModeIDA()` GreenBits tag parser. Expanded GD9618 to capture both under-enforcement for requested minima above four and over-enforcement for minima below four. GD9618 is the canonical entry; no new defect or body/path/LOC credit is added.


<a id="gd14522"></a>
## GD14522 — DisplayInfo palette-size calculation shifts by the full int width [low impact, high source confidence; conditional HIDD format]

`GetDisplayInfoData()` counts the set bits in the pixel format's red, green, and blue masks, then computes `1 << (RedBits + GreenBits + BlueBits)` before clamping values above 65,535 (`rom/graphics/getdisplayinfodata.c:233-253`). The left operand is an `int`; for a 32-bit total RGB mask, the shift count equals the operand width and the C expression has undefined behavior. The following clamp therefore cannot reliably enforce the documented-in-code 65,535 ceiling; on common x86 shift lowering the masked count can produce 1, which is returned as `PaletteRange`.

**Trigger and consequence:** a HIDD exposes a display mode whose red, green, and blue masks contain 32 bits in total (for example, a 32-bit RGB format with no alpha bits), and a client queries that mode with `DTAG_DISP`. `DisplayInfo.PaletteRange` can be nonsensical instead of saturating at 65,535. The explicit in-tree pixel-format tables reviewed here use at most 30 RGB bits. The optional LinuxFB HIDD forwards host `fb_var_screeninfo` red/green/blue lengths into its pixel-format masks (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx_displayclass.c:48-90`), so a 32-bit total is not ruled out; no such host mode or in-tree consumer of `PaletteRange` is established. **Affected configuration:** any target exposing such a 32-bit RGB mode through the graphics HIDD API, including optional LinuxFB builds if the host framebuffer reports that layout. **Confidence:** high that the expression is undefined at the stated input; medium that a given compiler returns an incorrect value, and low for current in-tree impact. Saturate by checking the total bit count before shifting. No mode was queried and no build was run; source-only. See the [DisplayInfo query review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#displayinfo-palette-range-full-width-shift-gd14522).


<a id="gd14523"></a>
## GD14523 — Headless graphics driver reports successful registration without a display after allocation failure [conditional]

`HeadlessGfx__Root__New()` publishes the new HIDD in `XSD(cl)->headlessgfxhidd`, then attempts to create its required display object. If `OOP_NewObject()` fails, the constructor still returns the non-NULL graphics HIDD and leaves `headlessgfxdisplay` NULL (`rom/hidds/gfx/headless/headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:301-307`). `HeadlessGfx__Root__Get()` consequently returns NULL for `aHidd_Gfx_DisplayDefault` (`:328-338`). The selected Graphics.library `driver_Setup()` treats a non-NULL HIDD object as successful even when its default display is NULL: it only logs the missing-display condition and reaches its unconditional TRUE return (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:372-399,414`). Therefore `AddDisplayDriverA()` returns `DD_OK` (`rom/graphics/adddisplaydrivera.c:284-297`), and the disk monitor loader returns `RETURN_OK` (`rom/hidds/gfx/headless/disk_startup.c:174-189`) although no headless display was registered. The HIDD's duplicate-instance guard sees the published pointer and prevents a retry (`headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:175-178`).

**Trigger and consequence:** allocation of the Headless display object fails while constructing the graphics HIDD. The monitor launch reports success but provides no display, and this class instance cannot retry display creation. Check the display-object allocation and unwind the partially constructed HIDD, or propagate the failure so `AddDisplayDriverA()` reports `DD_DRIVER_ERROR`. **Affected configuration:** optional Headless Gfx HIDD builds, for either disk-loaded monitor or resident registration; requires display-object creation failure. **Confidence:** high for source-level return and registration flow; the allocation failure was not induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [headless HIDD allocation-failure and registration trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#headless-gfx-full-body-registration-failure-pass-gd14523-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14524"></a>
## GD14524 — Calculator decimal-key input does not start a new operand after an operator or result

The digit branch of `mAddCalcKey()` changes `STATE_OP` to `STATE_RIGHTVAL` and clears the edit buffer, and changes `STATE_EQU` to `STATE_LEFTVAL` and clears it (`workbench/tools/Calculator.c:444-459`). The decimal-key branch only appends `.` and redraws; it does not perform either transition (`:461-465`).

**Trigger and consequence:** enter `1`, `+`, `.`, `5`, `=`. The decimal is appended to the old left operand while the state remains `STATE_OP`; entering `5` then clears that edit buffer and starts the right operand as `5`, producing `6` rather than `1.5`. The same stale-buffer behavior occurs when decimal is the first key after a result. Apply the numeric-entry state transition and initialize the new operand before appending the decimal point. **Affected configuration:** the selected Calculator desktop tool. **Confidence:** high from the complete state-machine path; no GUI interaction was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Calculator full-body state-machine pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#calculator-full-body-decimal-and-tape-input-pass-gd14524-gd14525).

<a id="gd14525"></a>
## GD14525 — Calculator does not terminate a maximum-length tape filename copy

`get_arguments()` copies the user-supplied `TAPE/K` string with `strncpy(tapename, ..., CALC_TAPENAME_MAX)` where the destination is exactly 320 bytes (`workbench/tools/Calculator.c:584-603`). For an input at least 320 bytes long, `strncpy()` does not append a terminator. Later `strlen(tapename)` and `Open(tapename, ...)` consume it as a C string (`:649-653`; `:606-625` for the alternate tape path).

**Trigger and consequence:** pass a `TAPE/K` argument of at least 320 characters. Subsequent length/path handling reads beyond the fixed `tapename` array and may treat adjacent memory as part of the filename, causing an invalid open or an out-of-bounds string read. Copy at most `sizeof(tapename)-1` and terminate explicitly, or reject overlong input. **Affected configuration:** selected Calculator CLI target; the oversized-argument condition depends on the command-input path accepting that length. **Confidence:** high for the missing-terminator condition; reachability of a 320-character CLI argument was not verified. Source-only.


<a id="gd14526"></a>
## GD14526 — GraphicDump indexes its error-name table with the signed device error

After the asynchronous `PRD_DUMPRPORT` request completes, GraphicDump uses `PIO->iodrp.io_Error` directly as an index into a 12-entry `ErrorText` array (`workbench/tools/GraphicDump.c:168-170`). `io_Error` is a signed `BYTE` (`compiler/include/exec/io.h:19-28`), and standard I/O errors are negative (`compiler/include/exec/errors.h:12-18`); printer errors also include positive values through 31 and custom values through 126 (`compiler/include/devices/printer.h:214-227`). Thus a negative I/O error indexes before the array, while printer error values of 12 or more index past it.

**Trigger and consequence:** the printer request completes with a negative I/O error or a printer-specific error value at least 12. The error-report path reads an invalid pointer from outside `ErrorText` and passes it to `Printf()`, so diagnostics can be wrong or the tool can fault while reporting the original printer error. Map known codes explicitly and provide a bounded fallback for unknown values. **Affected configuration:** selected GraphicDump tool with a printer.device implementation returning one of these valid/possible request errors. **Confidence:** high for the signed field, table extent, and unchecked index; no printer operation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [GraphicDump full-body printer/error/input pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphicdump-full-body-printer-error-input-pass-gd14526-gd14527).

<a id="gd14527"></a>
## GD14527 — GraphicDump turns a negative delay into a multi-year wait

The CLI `/N` `DELAY` argument is read through `LONG *` and assigned to the unsigned `ULONG delay`; the program then multiplies it by 50 and passes the result to `Delay()` (`workbench/tools/GraphicDump.c:382-400`). `Delay()` interprets its `ULONG` argument as ticks at 50 ticks per second (`rom/dos/delay.c:19-24`). A negative input therefore converts to a large unsigned value, and multiplication can wrap to another very large wait.

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke GraphicDump with a negative `DELAY` value. Instead of rejecting it or waiting no time, the tool requests an extremely long timer delay before starting the printer operation. Validate the signed value as nonnegative and bound it before converting seconds to ticks. **Affected configuration:** selected GraphicDump CLI invocation. **Confidence:** high for the conversion and unit path; no delay was run. Source-only.


<a id="gd14528"></a>
## GD14528 — PrintFiles exits successfully after printer or file-printing failures

`initdevice()` reports failure when the printer cannot be opened, and `printfile()` prints a message when `DTM_PRINT` fails, but neither records a process result (`workbench/tools/PrintFiles.c:24-57,76-111`). Both the CLI and Workbench paths eventually reach `return 0`; in the CLI path a failed `initdevice()` simply skips the print loop, while individual failures are swallowed by the void `printfile()` helper (`:142-227`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run PrintFiles with a printer unit that cannot open, or a file whose datatype print method fails. The tool emits an error or skips printing but reports success to its caller and scripts. Propagate failure from initialization/printing to `main()` and return an error status. **Affected configuration:** selected `workbench-tools` PrintFiles target, CLI and Workbench launches. **Confidence:** high for the return flow; no printer or file was used. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [PrintFiles and printer utilities full-body pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#printer-utilities-and-printfiles-full-body-pass-gd14528).

<a id="gd14529-mount-readfile-can-loop-forever-after-short-read"></a>
<a id="gd14529"></a>
## GD14529 — Mount can loop forever after a zero-byte short read [conditional]

`readfile()` determines the file length with `Seek()`, then repeatedly calls `Read()` until its cached `rest` count reaches zero (`workbench/c/Mount.c:1243-1278`). A zero-byte `Read()` result is not treated as EOF or failure: it subtracts zero from `rest` and advances `buf` by zero, so the loop repeats without progress. DOS documents that `Read()` returns zero at end of file (`rom/dos/read.c:31-36`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the mount definition is shortened after `readfile()` measures its length but before the read loop finishes, or a selected file handler returns zero before the measured byte count is satisfied. `Mount` then spins indefinitely instead of reporting a short/incomplete read. The function is used both for named mount files and for `DEVS:MountList` (`Mount.c:1013-1016,1115-1118`). Stop on zero progress and report an incomplete file. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds when a mount definition changes during reading or its handler returns an early EOF. **Confidence:** high for the zero-progress loop and DOS return contract; the concurrent file-change trigger was not induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Mount parser, handler and full-body pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mount-command-full-body-parser-and-handler-pass).

<a id="gd14530-version-misindexes-arm-floating-point-attributes"></a>
<a id="gd14530"></a>
## GD14530 — Version mislabels ARM floating-point attributes and indexes past the table [conditional]

`ARM_ParseAttrs()` stores the numeric `Tag_FP_arch` value directly in `pv_arm_fpu` (`workbench/c/Version.c:1730-1733`). `printverstring()` then indexes `arm_fpus` with that raw value and rejects only values greater than 6 (`:855-863,944-947`). The local ELF definitions assign values 1 through 6 to FP ISA levels v1, v2, v3, v3-D16, v4 and v4-D16 (`compiler/include/dos/elf.h:397-404`); the Arm ABI also defines those values as the corresponding permitted FP ISA levels ([AAELF32 Addenda, `Tag_FP_arch`](https://github.com/ARM-software/abi-aa/blob/main/addenda32/addenda32.rst#L725-L734)).

**Trigger and consequence:** run the explicitly built `Version ARCH` on an ARM ELF file with a valid `Tag_FP_arch` value. Values 1–5 are displayed one slot too high (for example, v2 is printed as v3); value 6 passes the bound check and reads `arm_fpus[6]`, one element beyond the array. The architecture report is incorrect and the out-of-range lookup may produce garbage or a fault. Map nonzero ABI values to the table with the correct offset and use a bound matching the table. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds with `ARCH` on ARM targets and an ELF file containing the respective attribute. **Confidence:** high for the valid numeric values, shifted mapping and value-6 table overrun. No ELF file was read by Version; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Version full-body file-scanner and ELF pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#version-full-body-file-scanner-and-elf-pass).

<a id="gd14531-version-trusts-elf-section-header-entry-size"></a>
<a id="gd14531"></a>
## GD14531 — Version trusts the ELF section-header entry size [conditional]

`arm_read_cpudata()` allocates the section-header block as `int_shnum * shentsize`, where `shentsize` comes from the ELF header, but then traverses it as an array of the fixed local `struct sheader` type (`workbench/c/Version.c:1751-1772,1789`). The command forces that local definition to the 32-bit ELF layout (`Version.c:46`); `struct sheader` is 40 bytes on this build (`compiler/include/dos/elf.h:250-262`). No check requires the file's `e_shentsize` to cover that structure before the array indexing.

**Trigger and consequence:** use `Version ARCH` on an ARM ELF with multiple section headers and an `e_shentsize` smaller than the local structure size. `load_block()` reads only the smaller declared table allocation, while a later `sh[i]` access walks 40-byte elements and can read beyond that allocation. Validate the ELF class and section-entry size against the parser's layout (and check the count-times-size calculation) before loading or indexing the table. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds with `ARCH` on ARM targets, when the input ELF has malformed section-header metadata. **Confidence:** high for the fixed-size indexing and absent entry-size validation; no malformed ELF file was read. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Version full-body file-scanner and ELF pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#version-full-body-file-scanner-and-elf-pass).


<a id="gd14532-install-uses-a-device-node-after-unlocking-the-dos-list"></a>
<a id="gd14532"></a>
## GD14532 — Install uses a DeviceNode after releasing the DOS-list lock [conditional]

`initVolume()` obtains a read lock, calls `FindDosEntry()`, and releases the lock before using the returned `DeviceNode *` (`workbench/c/Install.c:408-417`). It then dereferences `dn->dn_Startup` and follows the startup message fields, retaining the startup-message pointer in its `Volume` object (`:417-19,436-39,447-58`). `FindDosEntry()` documents that the DOS list must be locked for lookup (`rom/dos/finddosentry.c:28-42`); the returned list node is not retained by a reference-counting operation. The selected `Assign DISMOUNT` path takes the write lock, removes the matching node, and calls `FreeDosEntry()` before unlocking (`workbench/c/Assign.c:504-533`); `FreeDosEntry()` frees the node and its name (`rom/dos/freedosentry.c:44-50`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on an ExecSMP system, dismount the same device after Install releases its read lock and before it finishes reading the node's startup fields. `Assign DISMOUNT` can free the node in that interval, leaving Install to read a freed `DeviceNode` and potentially freed startup data. Install may fault or use incorrect device parameters. Copy the needed startup fields while holding the list lock, with an appropriate lifetime guarantee for referenced data. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` Install target on ExecSMP, with a concurrent dismount of the same device. **Confidence:** high for the unlocked borrowed-pointer use and freeing dismount path; the interleaving was not run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Install command full-body device and blocklist pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#install-command-full-body-device-and-blocklist-pass).


<a id="gd14533-planarbm-fill-can-loop-forever-at-the-largest-row"></a>
<a id="gd14533-planarbm-fill-can-loop-forever-at-the-largest-row-coordinate"></a>
<a id="gd14533"></a>
## GD14533 — PlanarBM fill can loop forever at the largest row coordinate [conditional]

The optimized Copy-mode `PBM__Hidd_BitMap__FillRect()` stores its inclusive Y loop variable in signed `WORD` and continues while `y <= y2` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:443-504`). A planar bitmap can have 32,768 rows: `BitMap.Rows` is `UWORD`, and the public `AllocBitMap()` path accepts the height before storing it in that field (`compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:33-41`; `rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:49-54,485-499`). The maximum valid row is therefore 32,767, also the largest positive `WORD`.

**Trigger and consequence:** issue a Copy-mode `RectFill()` covering a planar bitmap's final row when it has 32,768 rows. The normal clip rectangle permits `MaxY == 32767` (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:1064-1088`), and the selected generic PlanarBM fill method receives the inclusive bounds (`:330-335`). After processing row 32,767, incrementing signed `WORD y` wraps to -32,768; every representable `WORD` remains `<= 32767`, so the loop never terminates and continues writing successive invalid row addresses. Use a wider loop counter or an end condition that does not increment past the inclusive maximum. **Affected configuration:** graphics.library's generic PlanarBM adapter on a 32,768-row planar bitmap, Copy draw mode, and a fill that reaches row 32,767. **Confidence:** high for the loop boundary and public dimension/coordinate ranges; no such bitmap or fill was created. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [ChunkyBM and PlanarBM full-body pixel, allocation and bounds pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#chunkybm-and-planarbm-full-body-pixel-allocation-and-bounds-pass).

<a id="gd14534-planarbm-image-loops-do-not-advance-past-constant-planes"></a>
<a id="gd14534-planarbm-image-loops-do-not-advance-past-constant-one-planes"></a>
<a id="gd14534"></a>
## GD14534 — PlanarBM image loops do not advance past constant-one planes [conditional]

`PBM_PutImage_Native()` and `PBM_PutImage_Native32()` keep a pointer to the current plane and advance it at the end of each iteration, but the `continue` for a constant-one plane skips that advance (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:519-562,572-616`). `PBM__Hidd_BitMap__GetImageLUT()` repeats the same pattern (`:688-739`). These methods otherwise explicitly support the `(UBYTE *)-1` plane sentinel: `GetImageLUT()` pre-fills those bits as one, and the pixel and fill methods also recognize the sentinel (`:378-389,411-429,473-504`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use a planar bitmap with a constant-one plane followed by a backed plane in `GetImageLUT()` or a native `PutImage`/`PutImageLUT` operation. Once the loop encounters the sentinel, it rereads that same plane pointer on later iterations; the backed planes after it are ignored. Reads return pixels missing those higher-plane bits and writes leave those planes unchanged. This affects public paths that dispatch to these methods, including `ReadPixel()`'s one-pixel LUT read and `WritePixelArray8()`'s LUT write (`rom/graphics/readpixel.c:99-115`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:680-691`). Advance the plane pointer even when skipping a constant plane. **Affected configuration:** selected generic PlanarBM adapters for bitmaps containing a `-1` plane before one or more backed planes. **Confidence:** high for pointer progression and the constant-plane convention; no bitmap transfer was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [ChunkyBM and PlanarBM full-body pixel, allocation and bounds pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#chunkybm-and-planarbm-full-body-pixel-allocation-and-bounds-pass).

<a id="gd14535-chunkybm-truncates-its-owned-buffer-size"></a>
<a id="gd14535"></a>
## GD14535 — ChunkyBM truncates its owned buffer size [conditional]

`CBM__Root__New()` computes `height * bytesperrow` and stores it in `chunkybm_data.bufsize`, whose type is `ULONG`, before passing the stored size to `AllocVec()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:27-86`; `gfx_intern.h:76-85`). The mode-change resize path repeats the narrowing by assigning `height * bpr` to `ULONG newsize` before allocating and recording it (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:1045-1061`). On 64-bit targets the product can be computed at pointer width but is still truncated at either ULONG assignment; on 32-bit targets the product itself can wrap. The HIDD bitmap dimensions are `UWORD`; `AllocBitMap()` accepts `ULONG` dimensions, routes depths above eight through HIDD bitmap creation, and its default format for depth 32 is ARGB32 (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:491-502`; `rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:49-54,237-255,293-310`). The generic display class selects ChunkyBM for chunky pixel formats (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1040-1054`).

**Trigger and consequence:** allocate an HIDD-backed 32-bit bitmap of width 32,768 and height 32,769. With the default 16-pixel alignment its row is 131,072 bytes, so the backing storage requires 4,295,098,368 bytes (4 GiB + 128 KiB). Storing that size in 32-bit `ULONG` truncates it to 131,072 bytes, and either the constructor or a later resize can succeed with only that much memory. A valid two-row native image write at (0,0) then writes its second row at offset 131,072, at the end of the allocation (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:285-353`; the HIDD method takes signed `WORD` coordinates/extents in `gfx.conf:518-525`). Reject products that do not fit `bufsize`/the allocator size type before allocation, or retain and validate the full size. **Affected configuration:** generic ChunkyBM bitmap allocation on 32-bit and 64-bit AROS targets when the required product exceeds 32-bit `ULONG` and narrows to a nonzero size. `ULONG` is fixed at 32 bits; on 32-bit targets the product may wrap during multiplication, while on 64-bit targets the wide product is truncated when stored in `bufsize` before `AllocVec()`. **Confidence:** high for the type truncation in both initial allocation and resize, concrete arithmetic and unchecked row access; no large bitmap or image write was performed. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [ChunkyBM and PlanarBM full-body pixel, allocation and bounds pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#chunkybm-and-planarbm-full-body-pixel-allocation-and-bounds-pass).


<a id="gd14536-getvpmodeid-dereferences-an-unassigned-viewport"></a>
<a id="gd14536"></a>
## GD14536 — GetVPModeID dereferences an unassigned viewport's RasInfo [conditional]

`InitVPort()` initializes a valid `ViewPort` by copying defaults in which both `ColorMap` and `RasInfo` are NULL (`rom/graphics/initvport.c:11-25,65-72`). `GetVPModeID()` checks `ColorMap`, then immediately reads `vp->RasInfo->BitMap` without checking `RasInfo` (`rom/graphics/getvpmodeid.c:58-69`). Its documented result includes `INVALID_ID` when the viewport has no associated display mode (`:29-38`).

**Trigger and consequence:** initialize a standalone viewport with `InitVPort()` and query it with `GetVPModeID()` before attaching raster information or a ColorMap. The function dereferences NULL instead of returning `INVALID_ID`. Check `RasInfo` and its bitmap before testing for an HIDD bitmap. **Affected configuration:** graphics.library clients querying a valid but not-yet-attached ViewPort. **Confidence:** high for the initialized field values, missing guard and documented invalid-mode result; no viewport operation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Graphics helper vectors full-body mode, region and GELS pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-helper-vectors-full-body-mode-region-and-gels-pass).


<a id="gd14539"></a>
<a id="gd14539-iconx-resolves-workbench-arguments-relative-to-the-script-directory"></a>
## GD14539 — IconX resolves Workbench arguments relative to the script directory

`main()` changes the process current directory to the script's `wa_Lock` before calling `BuildCommandLine()` (`workbench/c/IconX.c:241-244,299`). The builder then processes every Workbench argument from index 1 by calling `Lock(wa_Name)` without first switching to that argument's `wa_Lock` (`:155-168,181-197`). `WBArg` carries a separate lock and name for each argument (`compiler/include/workbench/startup.h:32-36`); the Workbench library duplicates the lock independently for each `WBOPENA_ArgLock` (`workbench/libs/workbench/openworkbenchobjecta.c:386-425`), and the AppWindow sender constructs each argument as `FilePart(path)` plus a lock to its containing directory (`workbench/libs/workbench/sendappwindowmessage.c:106-117`).

**Trigger and consequence:** launch an IconX script with a project argument from another drawer. IconX resolves that argument's basename under the script directory instead of the directory recorded in its `WBArg`; if no same-named file exists, the argument is silently omitted, and if one does exist, the script receives that other file's path. Resolve each name against its corresponding `wa_Lock`. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds when an IconX Workbench launch includes one or more extra arguments whose directory differs from the script's directory. **Confidence:** high for the independent per-argument lock contract and the builder's use of process current directory; no Workbench launch or script was run. Source-only.

<a id="gd14540-gfxfree-leaves-a-color-map-view-extra-pointer-stale"></a>
<a id="gd14540"></a>
## GD14540 — GfxFree leaves a ColorMap's ViewPortExtra pointer stale [conditional]

`VideoControl()` accepts `VTAG_VIEWPORTEXTRA_SET` by assigning the supplied node to `cm->cm_vpe` (`rom/graphics/videocontrol.c:70-75`). The API explicitly permits that tag and `VTAG_ATTACH_CM_SET` to be supplied separately or in either order (`:386-395`). If the ColorMap has no attached ViewPort yet, `GfxNew(VIEWPORT_EXTRA_TYPE)` leaves `vpe->ViewPort` NULL (`rom/graphics/gfxnew.c:87-96`). `GfxFree()` clears the owning ColorMap's `cm_vpe` only by following `vpe->ViewPort->ColorMap` (`rom/graphics/gfxfree.c:72-80`), then frees the node (`:87-100`); with no ViewPort back-pointer, it cannot clear the direct `cm_vpe` reference. Later `FreeColorMap()` sees the stale non-NULL field and calls `GfxFree()` on that freed node (`rom/graphics/freecolormap.c:63-65`).

**Trigger and consequence:** create a ColorMap and ViewPortExtra, set only `VTAG_VIEWPORTEXTRA_SET`, explicitly free the extra with `GfxFree()`, then free the ColorMap. The second cleanup receives a dangling node pointer and can fault or corrupt memory instead of completing safely. Clearing `cm_vpe` when the extra is explicitly freed requires retaining or otherwise locating the owning ColorMap even before `cm_vp` is attached. **Affected configuration:** clients of graphics.library using the supported separate `VideoControl()` tag sequence and explicit `GfxFree()` before `FreeColorMap()`. **Confidence:** high for the stored pointer, absent back-pointer, and later cleanup call; no caller sequence or memory reuse was exercised. This is separate from GD5919's constructor-failure leak. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [GfxFree and VideoControl association lifetime recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gfxfree-videocontrol-color-map-association-lifetime-recheck-gd14540).

<a id="gd14541-readpixelarray8-declares-a-word-result-for-a-long-pixel-count"></a>
<a id="gd14541"></a>
## GD14541 — ReadPixelArray8 declares a WORD result for a LONG pixel count [conditional]

The Graphics vector declaration in `rom/graphics/graphics.conf` gives `ReadPixelArray8()` a `WORD` return type (`:175`), while its implementation entry and local result are `LONG` (`rom/graphics/readpixelarray8.c:40,94-96,125`). Its API documentation says the result is the number of pixels read (`:85-86`), and the renderer accumulates and returns `width * height` (`:24-32,120-125`). `ReadPixelLine8()` declares a `LONG` result and forwards this value (`rom/graphics/readpixelline8.c:35,57-66`; `graphics.conf:173`).

**Trigger and consequence:** read an area whose pixel count exceeds the signed `WORD` range, such as a sufficiently large valid bitmap region. A client compiled against the vector declaration can observe the result narrowed to a signed 16-bit value even though the implementation computed the full `LONG` count; the returned count can wrap or become negative, and `ReadPixelLine8()` inherits the mismatched declaration through its call. Align the public vector declaration and implementation with the documented count type, or explicitly constrain and document the supported count. **Affected configuration:** clients using Graphics.library's `ReadPixelArray8()` / `ReadPixelLine8()` declarations on regions with more than 32767 pixels. **Confidence:** high for the declaration/definition/documentation mismatch; the large-region behavior was not exercised. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Graphics function-list declaration and implementation signature reconciliation](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-conf-selected-function-list-signature-and-vector-reconciliation-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14542-which-all-skips-later-search-categories"></a>
<a id="gd14542"></a>
## GD14542 — Which `ALL` skips later search categories [conditional]

`Which` documents `ALL` as finding “all locations” of a command and separately searches resident commands, the shell command path, and the `C:` multiassign (`workbench/c/Which.c:20-26,145-185`). The main routine gates each later category on `!found` even when `checkAll` is true (`:167-185`). Thus a resident match suppresses all filesystem searches, and any path match suppresses the separate `C:` multiassign search. The helper-level `checkAll` loops cannot recover matches in a category the caller never invokes.

**Trigger and consequence:** run `Which ALL <name>` where the command is resident and also exists in a searched directory, or where it exists in a command-path directory and in a distinct `C:` multiassign member. The command prints only the earlier category's match(es) and exits successfully, omitting valid locations despite `ALL`. Preserve the accumulated `found` result for final status while allowing subsequent categories to run when `checkAll` is set. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` target; its aggregate parent edge is not claimed as selected. **Confidence:** high for the category guards and documented `ALL` behavior; the separate C: scan and command-path scan are explicit in the implementation. No command or filesystem operation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Which full-body and ALL-category traversal pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#which-full-body-and-all-category-traversal-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14543-setclock-never-closes-timer-device"></a>
<a id="gd14543"></a>
## GD14543 — SetClock never closes its timer.device open [conditional]

After `OpenDevice("timer.device", UNIT_VBLANK, ..., 0)` succeeds, `SetClock` performs the selected LOAD/SAVE/RESET operation, then deletes the I/O request and message port without calling `CloseDevice()` (`workbench/c/SetClock.c:101-178`). The only `CloseDevice()` on the path is absent; nearby selected commands such as `Wait` close the device before deleting their request (`workbench/c/Wait.c:154-190`). Thus each successful invocation leaves the timer device's open reference outstanding while freeing the request used to open it.

**Trigger and consequence:** run `SetClock LOAD`, `SAVE`, or `RESET` when `timer.device` opens successfully. The operation may complete, but the unmatched open accumulates across invocations and the request is destroyed while its device association remains open. Close the device on every successful-open path before deleting the request. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` target; its parent aggregate edge is not claimed as selected. **Confidence:** high for the successful open and missing close on the cleanup path; no command or device operation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [SetClock full-body and process/device cleanup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#setclock-full-body-and-process-state-pass).

<a id="gd14544-setdefaultfont-screen-replacement-leaks-previous-font"></a>
<a id="gd14544"></a>
## GD14544 — SetDefaultFont leaks the previous default screen font [conditional]

On its `SCREEN` branch, `SetDefaultFont` opens a new font and passes it to `SetDefaultScreenFont()` without closing the font previously stored by Intuition (`workbench/c/SetDefaultFont.c:126-136`). The setter only replaces `IntuitionBase`'s `ScreenFont` pointer under `Forbid()` and does not release the old font (`rom/intuition/setdefaultscreenfont.c:47-54`). `CloseFont()` decrements `tf_Accessors` and removes a non-ROM font when its last accessor closes (`rom/graphics/closefont.c:55-60`). Thus replacing a previously installed disk font drops the only global pointer to its outstanding open reference.

**Trigger and consequence:** after installing a non-ROM screen font, invoke `SetDefaultFont SCREEN` again with another available font. The old font remains registered/open with its accessor count unreleased and can accumulate across replacements. Close the previous screen-font reference as part of replacing it, preserving the old pointer until the setter has completed. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` target; its parent aggregate edge is not claimed as selected. **Confidence:** high for the open, pointer replacement and `CloseFont()` reference behavior; no font replacement or allocation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [SetDefaultFont full-body and screen-font replacement pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#setdefaultfont-full-body-and-screen-font-replacement-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14545-rename-continues-after-break-between-source-patterns"></a>
<a id="gd14545"></a>
## GD14545 — Rename continues processing sources after Ctrl-C [conditional]

The multi-source rename loop accepts `ERROR_BREAK` from the current source pattern, calls `MatchEnd()`, then advances to the next `from[i]` without leaving the outer loop (`workbench/c/Rename.c:290-296,331-351`). The DOS matcher records a detected break in `ap_FoundBreak` and returns `ERROR_BREAK` (`rom/dos/matchnext.c:110-119`); `CheckSignal()` clears the signal it returns (`rom/dos/checksignal.c:53-65`). `MatchFirst()` does not reset `ap_FoundBreak` before starting another pattern (`rom/dos/matchfirst.c:60-80`), but its first `MatchNext()` sets it from `CheckSignal()` again. With the signal already consumed, that later call overwrites the prior break with zero. Rename checks `ap_FoundBreak` only after all source patterns finish (`workbench/c/Rename.c:353-362`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run `Rename FROM/A/M ... TO` with an existing destination directory and at least two source arguments; after one match of the first source is renamed, press Ctrl-C while its scan is active. Rename ends that pattern but processes later source arguments anyway, and a later matcher can clear the saved break state so the command returns success instead of warning. Stop the outer source loop as soon as the current scan reports `ERROR_BREAK`, while retaining that status through cleanup. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds using multiple FROM arguments, a destination directory, and Ctrl-C during a source scan. **Confidence:** high for the loop/status transition and DOS signal/match contracts; no file was renamed or signal generated. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Rename full-body pattern/cleanup and Ctrl-C pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#rename-full-body-pattern-cleanup-and-ctrl-c-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14546-sort-uses-examined-size-after-short-read"></a>
<a id="gd14546"></a>
## GD14546 — Sort processes uninitialized bytes after a short input read [conditional]

`Sort` allocates an uninitialized buffer sized to `fib->fib_Size`, calls `Read()` once, and treats every result except `-1` as a complete input (`workbench/c/Sort.c:335-357`). It then passes the original examined size to `sort()` regardless of the actual returned byte count. DOS defines `Read()` as returning the number of bytes actually read, with short positive reads possible (`rom/dos/read.c:24-46`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the input is shortened after `Examine()` but before `Read()`, or its filesystem returns a short read for the requested length. `Sort` parses and writes the unread tail of the uninitialized allocation as if it belonged to the file, producing corrupted output and potentially copying unrelated stale memory into the destination. Require the requested byte count or retry/resize based on the actual input length before sorting. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` target when the input changes between size query and read or a selected handler returns a short read. **Confidence:** high for the API byte-count contract and caller's use of the stale FIB size; the trigger requires a short read. No input file, concurrent write, or command was used. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Sort full-body I/O, allocation, and short-read pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sort-full-body-io-allocation-and-short-read-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14547-sort-null-fib-after-allocation-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14547"></a>
## GD14547 — Sort may examine through a null FIB after allocation failure [conditional]

After opening the output, `Sort` allocates a `DOS_FIB`. If that allocation returns NULL, it assigns `IoErr()` to `error`; when the current IoErr value is zero, execution still enters the `error == 0` block and calls `Examine(lock_in, fib)` with the null pointer (`workbench/c/Sort.c:316-324,335-337`). The `AllocDosObject(DOS_FIB)` implementation returns `AllocVec()` directly and does not set IoErr on this path (`rom/dos/allocdosobject.c:68-69`). The selected RAM filesystem's `ExamineObject()` writes fields through the supplied FIB (`rom/filesys/ram/filesystem.c:1069-1109`), reached by its `CmdExamineObject()` handler (`rom/filesys/ram/commands.c:1281-1286`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run Sort on a RAM filesystem when FIB allocation fails and IoErr is zero. The unchecked null FIB is passed to Examine and the RAM handler dereferences it, crashing the command instead of returning an allocation error. Treat a null FIB as an unconditional failure with a defined error, and skip Examine. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` plus RAM filesystem; requires FIB allocation failure with IoErr equal to zero. **Confidence:** high for the null flow and RAM handler writes; conditional on allocator failure and prior IoErr state. No allocation failure or command was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Sort full-body I/O, allocation, and short-read pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sort-full-body-io-allocation-and-short-read-pass).

<a id="gd14548-run-drops-continuation-after-allocation-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14548"></a>
## GD14548 — Run launches a truncated command when continuation buffering fails [conditional]

For buffered shell continuation input, `Run` allocates a new buffer for the original command plus the remaining input. If `AllocMem()` fails, it sets `cmdsize` to zero but leaves `command` pointing at the original command text; execution then proceeds to `SystemTagList(command, ...)` without reporting that the continuation was lost (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Run.c:94-121,151-165`). The continuation handling is explicitly described as support for `+` style input (`:86-92`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run a command with buffered continuation text while the concatenation allocation fails. Run starts the incomplete first portion as a background command and returns success, so requested later command text is silently omitted. Treat the allocation failure as an error and do not launch the shortened command. **Affected configuration:** selected `workbench-c` shell command when continuation input is buffered and the combined-buffer allocation fails. **Confidence:** high for the fallback control flow; requires allocation failure. No command, shell input, or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Run shell-command full-body continuation and handle pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#run-shell-command-full-body-continuation-and-handle-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14549-execute-drops-continuation-after-allocation-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14549"></a>
## GD14549 — Execute silently drops buffered continuation arguments on allocation failure [conditional]

When `Execute` finds buffered input remaining after `ReadArgs()`, it allocates a combined `arguments` buffer to append that text. If `AllocVec()` fails, `extraargs` remains NULL and `arguments` still points to the initial parsed arguments; execution continues and injects only that shortened string into the script input (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Execute.c:64-87,209-229`).

**Trigger and consequence:** execute a script with buffered `+` continuation arguments while the combined-buffer allocation fails. The script runs with only the initial arguments and the command reports success, silently omitting the remaining input. Treat allocation failure as an error and do not start the incomplete script. **Affected configuration:** selected shell `Execute` command with buffered continuation text and allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the fallback path; requires allocation failure. No script, continuation input, or allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Execute shell-command full-body continuation and cleanup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#execute-shell-command-full-body-continuation-and-cleanup-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14550-execute-leaks-combined-continuation-buffer"></a>
<a id="gd14550"></a>
## GD14550 — Execute leaks its combined continuation buffer [conditional]

When buffered continuation input is successfully combined, `Execute` stores the allocation in `extraargs` and points `arguments` at it (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Execute.c:64-82`). The later argument-injection path copies those bytes into the CLI standard-input buffer (`:209-229`), so the temporary allocation is no longer needed. Neither the successful return nor the `SetVBuf()` failure return frees `extraargs`; only earlier file-open and temporary-file error exits do so (`:91-99,130-142,156-166,179-184`).

**Trigger and consequence:** execute repeatedly with buffered continuation input. Each successful combined-buffer allocation remains allocated after its contents have been copied, causing memory use to grow with each invocation. Free `extraargs` after the input-buffer copy and on all later exits. **Affected configuration:** selected shell `Execute` command when buffered continuation text causes the allocation to succeed. **Confidence:** high for allocation, copy, and missing cleanup paths. No script or repeated invocation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Execute shell-command full-body continuation and cleanup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#execute-shell-command-full-body-continuation-and-cleanup-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14551-path-reset-frees-the-next-list-node"></a>
<a id="gd14551"></a>
## GD14551 — Path RESET frees the next entry before traversing it [conditional]

The RESET loop saves `cur->next` as `next`, unlocks `cur`, then frees `BADDR(cur->next)` rather than `cur` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Path.c:104-121`). It advances to the saved pointer and dereferences that entry on the next iteration. For a list with at least two entries, the second node has already been freed; traversal reads its `next` and `lock` fields after free, while the first node is leaked. The final node is also not freed because its `next` is null.

**Trigger and consequence:** run `Path RESET` with at least two command-path entries. The command traverses freed list memory, may unlock an invalid lock or fault, leaks the former head entry, and leaves the CLI path empty only if traversal completes.
