Free the current node after saving the next pointer. **Affected configuration:** selected `workbench-c` shell command with a CLI path containing two or more entries. **Confidence:** high from the explicit list traversal and `FreeVec()` target. No path was modified. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Path shell-command full-body list and allocation pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#path-shell-command-full-body-list-and-allocation-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14552-path-can-examine-a-null-fib-after-allocation-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14552"></a>
## GD14552 — Path may pass a null FIB to Examine after allocation failure [conditional]

`IsDirectory()` passes the result of `AllocDosObject(DOS_FIB, NULL)` directly to `Examine()` without checking it (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Path.c:339-350`). `AllocDosObject(DOS_FIB)` returns `AllocVec()` directly (`rom/dos/allocdosobject.c:68-69`), so allocation failure is not converted into a DOS error by this allocator. The selected RAM filesystem's `ExamineObject()` fills fields through its FIB pointer (`rom/filesys/ram/filesystem.c:1069-1109`).

**Trigger and consequence:** add a candidate path while DOS FIB allocation fails and the lock resolves to the RAM filesystem. `Examine()` can pass the null FIB to the handler, which writes through it instead of cleanly rejecting the path. Check the allocation before calling `Examine()` and return false with a defined error. **Affected configuration:** selected shell `Path` command and RAM filesystem, conditional on FIB allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the null flow and selected handler writes; no failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Path shell-command full-body list and allocation pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#path-shell-command-full-body-list-and-allocation-pass).

<a id="gd14553-path-leaks-fib-when-examine-fails"></a>
<a id="gd14553"></a>
## GD14553 — Path leaks its FIB when Examine fails [conditional]

`IsDirectory()` frees the allocated FIB only inside the `if (Examine(lock, fib))` success block (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Path.c:345-388`). If `Examine()` fails for a valid lock because the handler reports an I/O or metadata error, the false return bypasses `FreeDosObject()` and the caller simply rejects that path.

**Trigger and consequence:** add a path whose lock succeeds but whose filesystem `Examine()` fails. Each such attempt leaks one `FileInfoBlock`. Move FIB cleanup after the conditional so both Examine outcomes release it. **Affected configuration:** selected shell `Path` command on a filesystem that can fail Examine for a locked path. **Confidence:** high for the allocation and missing failure cleanup; the trigger requires an Examine failure. No path or filesystem error was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Path shell-command full-body list and allocation pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#path-shell-command-full-body-list-and-allocation-pass).

<a id="gd14554-setenv-hides-global-variable-listing-failures"></a>
<a id="gd14554"></a>
## GD14554 — Setenv and UnSetEnv report success when global-variable listing fails [conditional]

In its no-argument listing path, `Setenv` initializes the result to success, then silently skips listing if `AllocDosObject(DOS_FIB)` fails (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Setenv.c:81-109`). If the FIB exists but `Examine(lock, FIB)` fails, it also frees the FIB and returns success without preserving or reporting the DOS error (`:93-105`). `UnSetEnv` repeats the same allocation and Examine handling and also leaves its result at success (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Unsetenv.c:113-145`). Both commands also end their `ExNext()` loops without distinguishing normal `ERROR_NO_MORE_ENTRIES` from another enumeration error, leaving a partial listing reported as successful.

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke `Setenv` or `UnSetEnv` without arguments while `ENV:` can be locked but FIB allocation or `Examine()` fails. The command prints no list and reports success, so scripts cannot distinguish the failed listing from an empty environment. Return a failure and preserve/report allocation, Examine, and non-terminal ExNext errors. **Affected configuration:** selected shell `Setenv` command on the listing path; requires the stated allocation or filesystem failure. **Confidence:** high for both unchecked failure paths and unchanged result. No environment listing or failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Setenv shell-command full-body listing and status pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#setenv-shell-command-full-body-listing-and-status-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14555-resident-leaves-forbid-active-on-removal-and-replace-paths"></a>
<a id="gd14555"></a>
## GD14555 — Resident leaves task switching forbidden on several resident-command paths [conditional]

The REMOVE branch calls `Forbid()` before `FindSegment()`. When a segment is found, neither the successful `RemSegment()` path nor the failed-removal path calls `Permit()` before returning (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Resident.c:115-143`). The same imbalance occurs when REPLACE finds no user segment: it calls `Forbid()`, `FindSegment()` returns NULL, and the code falls through without `Permit()` before continuing to `AddSegment()` or any later return (`:187-229`). DOS `RemSegment()` does not balance Exec's forbid count, and Exec requires one `Permit()` for each `Forbid()` (`rom/dos/remsegment.c:48-89`; `rom/exec/forbid.c:33-43`; `rom/exec/permit.c:34-35`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use `Resident NAME REMOVE` for an existing segment, or `Resident NAME REPLACE FILE` when no user segment with that name exists. The command exits with the forbid count still elevated; task switching remains disabled on the local processor until a matching Permit occurs, and nested caller operations can inherit the forbidden state. Balance every acquired forbid on all exits. **Affected configuration:** selected shell `Resident` command and the specified operations. **Confidence:** high for the missing Permit and Exec nesting contract. No resident list or scheduling operation was changed; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Resident shell-command full-body resident-list and cleanup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#resident-shell-command-full-body-resident-list-and-cleanup-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14556-resident-leaks-snapshot-nodes-on-list-allocation-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14556"></a>
## GD14556 — Resident leaks earlier snapshot nodes when list construction fails [conditional]

The no-argument listing path allocates a copied `SegNode` for each resident and appends it to a temporary list. If a later `NewSegNode()` fails, it sets `ERROR_NO_FREE_STORE`, breaks, calls `Permit()`, and returns from the error branch without removing or freeing nodes already added to the local list (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Resident.c:237-260`). Each node owns both a structure and a duplicated name (`:309-324`).

**Trigger and consequence:** list resident commands when allocation fails after at least one snapshot node was created. All earlier nodes and names leak. Drain and free the partial list before returning the allocation error. **Affected configuration:** selected shell `Resident` command with at least one resident and a later snapshot allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for the partial-list ownership and early return. No allocation failure or listing was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Resident shell-command full-body resident-list and cleanup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#resident-shell-command-full-body-resident-list-and-cleanup-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14557-resident-can-skip-purity-check-when-fib-allocation-fails"></a>
<a id="gd14557"></a>
## GD14557 — Resident can skip its pure-file check after FIB allocation failure [conditional]

Unless FORCE is requested, `Resident` performs the protection check only inside `if (!FORCE && AllocDosObject(DOS_FIB, NULL))`. If the FIB allocation returns NULL, the check is skipped; the preceding `SetIoErr(0)` leaves no failure, and the code proceeds to `LoadSeg(file)` and can add the command as resident (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Resident.c:114,163-185`). `AllocDosObject(DOS_FIB)` returns `AllocVec()` directly without setting IoErr (`rom/dos/allocdosobject.c:68-69`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke Resident without FORCE on a non-PURE file while FIB allocation fails but `LoadSeg()` succeeds. The explicit safety check is bypassed, and an ineligible command can be installed as resident even though FORCE was not supplied. Treat FIB allocation failure as an error and do not load or add the segment. **Affected configuration:** selected shell `Resident` command with FORCE omitted; requires allocation failure and a successful subsequent load. **Confidence:** high for skipped check/control flow and allocator behavior; manifestation depends on memory state. No segment was loaded or added. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Resident shell-command full-body resident-list and cleanup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#resident-shell-command-full-body-resident-list-and-cleanup-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14558-if-val-ignores-invalid-numeric-operands"></a>
<a id="gd14558"></a>
## GD14558 — If VAL treats nonnumeric operands as zero [conditional]

The numeric comparison path calls `StrToLong()` for both operands but ignores its return value (`workbench/c/shellcommands/If.c:217-223`). `StrToLong()` returns `-1` when no digits are present and sets the output value to zero (`rom/dos/strtolong.c:54-68`); `doeval()` then compares those values normally.

**Trigger and consequence:** use a numeric condition with a nonnumeric operand, for example `If abc EQ 0 VAL`. The invalid operand becomes zero and the condition evaluates true instead of reporting an invalid numeric expression, so the wrong script branch can run. Check both parse results and reject invalid operands before comparison. **Affected configuration:** selected shell `If` command using `VAL` and a malformed numeric operand. **Confidence:** high for the ignored error result, conversion behavior, and comparison. No script or branch was executed. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [If shell-command full-body comparison and skip pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#if-shell-command-full-body-comparison-and-skip-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14559-cd-ignores-current-directory-name-update-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14559"></a>
## GD14559 — CD reports success when the shell directory name cannot be updated [conditional]

After changing the process's current directory, `CD` calls `GetLockName()` and passes the resulting full path to `SetCurrentDirName()`, but ignores the setter's return value and leaves `error` unchanged if `GetLockName()` returns NULL (`workbench/c/shellcommands/CD.c:64-75`). The selected setter rejects names longer than 255 bytes and returns false without updating the CLI name (`rom/dos/setcurrentdirname.c:55-74`). `GetLockName()` can produce a longer path because it grows its buffer until `NameFromLock()` succeeds (`workbench/c/shellcommands/CD.c:116-137`).

**Trigger and consequence:** change to a directory whose full path exceeds 255 bytes, or trigger a `GetLockName()` allocation/path-resolution failure after the `CurrentDir()` change. The process's lock changes, but the shell's saved current-directory name remains stale and `CD` reports success. Check `SetCurrentDirName()` and propagate name-resolution failure, or define a consistent display-name fallback. **Affected configuration:** selected shell `CD` command with a path beyond the DOS CLI name limit or a failed name-resolution allocation. **Confidence:** high for the changed lock, 255-byte setter limit and ignored result; requires the stated path/failure. No directory was changed. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [CD shell-command full-body directory and name pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#cd-shell-command-full-body-directory-and-name-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14560-echo-first-on-empty-string-reads-before-argument"></a>
<a id="gd14560"></a>
## GD14560 — Echo FIRST reads before an empty string argument [conditional]

When `FIRST` is nonzero and its one-based offset is greater than or equal to the argument length, Echo advances by `l - 1` to select the last character (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Echo.c:98-112`). For an empty string, `l` is zero and this forms a pointer one byte before the argument. The output loop then dereferences that pointer while its length limit is nonzero (`:119-127`).

**Trigger and consequence:** pass an empty string argument with a positive FIRST value, for example `Echo "" FIRST 2`, if the shell preserves that empty argument. Echo reads and may print bytes preceding the argument instead of producing empty output. Avoid moving before the buffer when the string length is zero. **Affected configuration:** selected shell Echo command with an empty argument and positive FIRST. **Confidence:** high for the pointer arithmetic and dereference; depends on the shell passing an empty argument through `/M`. No command was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Echo shell-command full-body slicing and output pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#echo-shell-command-full-body-slicing-and-output-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14561-getenv-truncates-long-global-values"></a>
<a id="gd14561"></a>
## GD14561 — Getenv, Get, Alias, Set and Unset silently truncate long variable values [conditional]

`Getenv` asks `GetVar()` to copy into a fixed 256-byte stack buffer and prints the result whenever the return is not `-1` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Getenv.c:65-85`). The DOS contract explicitly says a value longer than the buffer is truncated and the copied length is returned (`rom/dos/getvar.c:40-52`). `SetVar()` accepts null-terminated strings with `size == -1` and stores their full `strlen()` length for local variables or writes the complete string to ENV (`rom/dos/setvar.c:184-194,211-227`), with no 255-byte limit. The `Get` command also reads a local value into a 256-byte buffer and prints the returned prefix (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Get.c:65-84`). `Alias` also uses fixed 160-byte buffers for both named lookup and list display and prints the truncated prefix (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Alias.c:90,103-116,143-153`); `Unalias` uses the same 160-byte buffer for its no-argument alias listing (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Unalias.c:65-108). The no-argument `Set` and `Unset` listings have the same issue for local values: each calls `GetVar()` with a 160-byte buffer and prints the returned prefix without checking whether the value was truncated (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Set.c:101-119`; `Unset.c:93-111`).

**Trigger and consequence:** retrieve a global variable whose first line exceeds 255 bytes with `Getenv`, retrieve a local variable whose first line exceeds 255 bytes with `Get`, or retrieve/list aliases whose first lines exceed 159 bytes with `Alias`/`Unalias`, or list local variables whose first lines exceed 159 bytes with `Set` or `Unset`. These commands print only the buffer prefix and report success. Size the buffers from each value length or stream the full value. **Affected configuration:** selected shell commands with oversized global/local variable values. **Confidence:** high for the fixed destination, truncation contract and unbounded SetVar input. No variable was created or read. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Getenv shell-command full-body value-length pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#getenv-shell-command-full-body-value-length-pass-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14562-alias-mistakes-getvar-failure-for-success"></a>
<a id="gd14562"></a>
## GD14562 — Alias treats GetVar failure as a successful lookup [conditional]

The named lookup path assigns `GetVar()`'s `LONG` result to `BOOL Success`, then considers only zero to mean failure (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Alias.c:103-116`). DOS `GetVar()` returns `-1` when the requested variable is not defined (`rom/dos/getvar.c:170-177`); conversion to `BOOL` keeps it nonzero, so the command enters the success branch and prints `Buffer`, which was not populated by that failed lookup.

**Trigger and consequence:** query a name that is not defined as a local alias. Alias treats the failure sentinel as success, prints uninitialized stack-buffer contents, and returns `RETURN_OK` instead of warning that the alias does not exist. Keep the result in `LONG` and compare it with `-1`. **Affected configuration:** selected shell Alias command with a missing named alias. **Confidence:** high for the return type, conversion and branch flow. No alias query was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Alias shell-command full-body lookup and value pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#alias-shell-command-full-body-lookup-and-value-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14563-cut-dereferences-before-malformed-boundary-string"></a>
<a id="gd14563"></a>
## GD14563 — Cut reads before malformed range text [conditional]

`getBoundaries()` advances its input pointer by the return value of `StrToLong()` without checking for `-1` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Cut.c:213-229`). DOS `StrToLong()` returns `-1` when no numeric prefix is present (`rom/dos/strtolong.c:54-68`). For a range such as `CHAR nope`, the pointer is moved one byte before the range string; the subsequent `*buffer` test dereferences that out-of-bounds address (`Cut.c:220-225`).

**Trigger and consequence:** pass a nonnumeric CHAR or WORD range. Cut reads memory before the argument while attempting to parse it and may then mis-handle the range or access further invalid data. Check the parse result and reject malformed boundaries before pointer arithmetic. **Affected configuration:** selected shell Cut command with malformed range text. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked `-1` offset and immediate dereference; the byte's value determines subsequent parsing. No command was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Cut shell-command full-body range and output pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#cut-shell-command-full-body-range-and-output-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14564-cut-ignores-output-write-errors"></a>
<a id="gd14564"></a>
## GD14564 — Cut ignores output errors and can return success with missing text [conditional]

Both WORD and CHAR output loops call `FPutC()` without checking its result, and the final newline write is also unchecked (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Cut.c:149-163,174-185`). DOS `FPutC()` returns a negative value on output failure. Once a range parses, the command sets `rc = RETURN_OK` regardless of failed writes.

**Trigger and consequence:** Cut writes to an output stream or handler that fails during a selected range. The command can emit only part of the requested text, ignore the write error, and return success. Check every `FPutC()` result and propagate the DOS error. **Affected configuration:** selected shell Cut command when Output() fails to accept a character or newline. **Confidence:** high for ignored results and success assignment; requires a write failure. No output failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Cut shell-command full-body range and output pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#cut-shell-command-full-body-range-and-output-pass).

<a id="gd14565-pathpart-directory-branch-copies-no-terminator"></a>
<a id="gd14565"></a>
## GD14565 — PathPart passes a non-terminated copy to PathPart() [conditional]

The DIR branch allocates exactly `strlen(DIR)` bytes and copies that many bytes, omitting the input string's NUL terminator (`workbench/c/shellcommands/PathPart.c:68-74`). DOS `PathPart()` scans until it finds NUL (`rom/dos/pathpart.c:63-78`), so it reads past the allocation when processing this copy. The branch then uses the resulting pointer difference as an index into the same allocation.

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke `PathPart DIR <nonempty-path>`. PathPart() reads beyond the allocated buffer while searching for separators and the terminator; its returned pointer and the subsequent output can depend on adjacent memory. Allocate room for and copy the NUL terminator before calling PathPart(). **Affected configuration:** selected shell PathPart command using DIR. **Confidence:** high for the allocation/copy extent and callee scan. No command or path was processed. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [PathPart shell-command full-body copy and output pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#pathpart-shell-command-full-body-copy-and-output-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14566-pathpart-ignores-output-errors"></a>
<a id="gd14566"></a>
## GD14566 — PathPart ignores output errors [conditional]

On every successful DIR, FILE, or ADD path, the command ignores the result from `PutStr(outstr)` and from the final `FPutC(Output(), '\\n')`, then returns `RETURN_OK` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/PathPart.c:105-111`). DOS output routines report write failure through their return values.

**Trigger and consequence:** the selected output stream fails during the path or newline write. PathPart can emit a partial or empty result while reporting success. Check both output operations and return an error when either fails. **Affected configuration:** selected shell PathPart command with a failing Output() handler. **Confidence:** high for discarded results and unconditional successful return; requires output failure. No output operation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [PathPart shell-command full-body copy and output pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#pathpart-shell-command-full-body-copy-and-output-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14567-skip-accepts-eof-without-endskip"></a>
<a id="gd14567"></a>
## GD14567 — Skip reports success when no matching EndSkip exists [conditional]

Without LABEL, `Skip` sets `quit` only when it reads `ENDSKIP`, but after EOF or `ReadItem()` error it exits the loop without recording whether that terminator was found (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Skip.c:76-118`). The final error check is gated on `SHArg(LABEL) != NULL`, so the no-label path returns `RETURN_OK` even when it never found `ENDSKIP` (`:120-131`). The command documentation says a missing Lab/EndSkip target returns an error (`:31-35`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run `Skip` without a LABEL in a script that reaches EOF or encounters a read error before an `EndSkip`. Skip reports success although it did not find the requested block terminator, making malformed script flow indistinguishable from a successful skip. Track whether EndSkip was found and return an error on EOF/read failure. **Affected configuration:** selected shell Skip command using the no-label form. **Confidence:** high for loop exits and final result condition. No script was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Skip shell-command full-body target and EOF pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#skip-shell-command-full-body-target-and-eof-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14568-info-overflows-filter-vector-while-adding-assignment-entries"></a>
<a id="gd14568"></a>
## GD14568 — Info can overrun its fixed filter vector while expanding assignments [conditional]

When `DEVICES/M` is supplied, `ScanDosList()` allocates exactly `MAX_MULTIARGS` pointers (128) for `strray`, then copies every ReadArgs result without checking the count (`workbench/c/Info.c:281-295`). It subsequently appends one task-name entry for each matching volume or directory assign and an empty placeholder for every lock in a matching directory assign's `AssignList`, with no capacity check (`:303-348`). The DOS assign-list is a linked list with no 128-entry bound in the selected `AssignAddToList()` implementation (`rom/dos/assignaddtolist.c:67-110`). The final scan walks the vector looking for a NULL terminator (`Info.c:355-376`).

**Trigger and consequence:** pass a pattern matching a directory assign whose linked path list, together with the initial filter and entries from other matched assigns/volumes, fills or exceeds the 128-pointer allocation. A full vector has no NULL terminator; further entries are written past the pooled allocation, and the subsequent terminator search also reads out of bounds. Size the vector for the combined count with overflow checks, or append with an explicit capacity and report excess entries. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds with `DEVICES/M` and a DOS list containing sufficiently expanded matching directory assigns. **Confidence:** high for the fixed allocation, unbounded linked-list expansion and unchecked writes; occurrence depends on the DOS-list configuration. The direct 128-argument trigger is not claimed because the selected CLI input path is bounded to 256 bytes (`rom/dos/readargs.c:205,304`). No DOS-list, command or allocation was exercised. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Info filter expansion and volume-list full-body recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#info-filter-expansion-and-volume-list-full-body-recheck-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14569-info-dereferences-unmounted-volume-task-in-filter-pass"></a>
<a id="gd14569"></a>
## GD14569 — Info dereferences a missing handler task for an unmounted volume [conditional]

In the filtered DOS-list pass, `ScanDosList()` matches volume and directory assigns, then handles every `DLT_VOLUME` by dereferencing `ndl->dol_Task->mp_SigTask` without checking `dol_Task` (`workbench/c/Info.c:310-328`). The later volume snapshot explicitly copies `dol_Task` as optional and prints a mounted marker only when it is non-NULL (`:365-375`; `:860-869`), so an unmounted volume node is an accepted state.

**Trigger and consequence:** run Info with a `DEVICES` pattern matching an unmounted volume. The volume passes the filter, then Info dereferences its null handler task while building the expanded filter list. Skip task-name collection for unmounted volumes or represent the volume name directly. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds with a matching unmounted volume node. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked dereference and the command's handling of null volume tasks; no DOS-list state or command was used. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Info filter expansion and volume-list full-body recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#info-filter-expansion-and-volume-list-full-body-recheck-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14571-waitforport-deletes-an-outstanding-timer-request"></a>
<a id="gd14571"></a>
## GD14571 — WaitForPort deletes an outstanding timer request on break [conditional]

After starting `TR_ADDREQUEST`, WaitForPort exits its wait loop immediately when CTRL-C or CTRL-D is returned by `Wait()` (`workbench/c/WaitForPort.c:107-119`). Its cleanup closes the timer device and deletes the I/O request and reply port without checking or aborting the request (`:152-168`). Exec documents that outstanding I/O must be finished before `CloseDevice()` (`rom/exec/closedevice.c:37-40`); the selected timer device queues `UNIT_VBLANK` requests and later replies through the request message (`rom/timer/lowlevel.c:187-220,365-375`). The break checks take precedence over the timer-port check, even when both signals are returned.

**Trigger and consequence:** if CTRL-C or CTRL-D arrives while the one-second request remains queued, timer completion can later reply through the freed request and port. If the timer and break signals are both active, the break branch can instead leave an already-completed `NT_REPLYMSG` linked on the reply port; `DeleteIORequest()` directly frees that message storage (`rom/exec/deleteiorequest.c:45-47`), and `DeleteMsgPort()` frees the port without draining remaining messages (`rom/exec/deletemsgport.c:48-53`). `WaitIO()` explicitly removes a completed reply message from its port (`rom/exec/waitio.c:57-76`). Finish or abort the request and call `WaitIO()` before closing and deleting the request/port. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds when WaitForPort is interrupted during an active timer interval. **Confidence:** high for the active request, immediate break and missing finish/abort sequence; no signal or I/O was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [WaitForPort full-body timer lifecycle and timeout pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#waitforport-full-body-timer-lifecycle-and-timeout-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14573-search-prefix-table-loop-wraps-for-long-literal"></a>
<a id="gd14573"></a>
## GD14573 — Search's prefix-table loop wraps for long literal searches [conditional]

For non-pattern, non-file searches, Search builds a Knuth–Morris–Pratt prefix table with `for (q = 1; q < pat_length; q++)`, but `q` is an 8-bit `UBYTE` while `pat_length` is a `UWORD` (`workbench/c/Search.c:140-141,171,204-230`). If the literal search string is at least 256 bytes, `q` wraps from 255 to zero and remains less than `pat_length`; the table-building loop does not terminate. There is no break check in this loop.

**Trigger and consequence:** run Search with a literal `SEARCH` string of at least 256 bytes and without PATTERN or FILE. The command remains stuck building its prefix table and does not reach the file search or its later Ctrl-C handling. Use an index type wide enough for the accepted string length and add an explicit bound/check. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds with a long literal search argument. **Confidence:** high for the type widths and loop condition; no command was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Search full-body pattern and file-I/O pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#search-full-body-pattern-and-file-io-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14575-load-command-sends-eject-operations"></a>
<a id="gd14575"></a>
## GD14575 — Load sends eject operations on the selected ATA devices [conditional]

The shared Eject/Load implementation computes `load` from the CLI command name, but `SCSIEject()` ignores it and always sends a START STOP CDB with LOEJ set and START clear (`workbench/c/Eject.c:106-110,129-136`). The follow-up `TrackdiskEject()` changes `io_Length` for Load, but the selected ATA `TD_EJECT` handler ignores that field and invokes `unit->au_Eject()` (`:140-149`; `rom/devs/ata/ata.c:430-438`). The ATA and ATAPI eject callbacks also issue eject-only operations (`rom/devs/ata/lowlevel.c:2298-2320,2474-2492`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke the compiled `Load` command for an eject/load-capable ATA or ATAPI device. The preliminary SCSI sequence requests eject, and the subsequent trackdisk command also requests eject; media is not loaded. Generate START STOP parameters based on `load` and provide a trackdisk path that honors the requested direction. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds on selected ATA/ATAPI units that support media load/eject. **Confidence:** high for command-name detection and the unconditional eject operations in the selected driver path; no media command was sent. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Eject/Load full-body DOS-list, command and device pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#eject-load-full-body-dos-list-command-and-device-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14577-automount-returns-success-after-pref-or-mount-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14577"></a>
## GD14577 — Automount returns success after preference or mount failures [conditional]

After creating its pool, `main()` records the result from `LoadPrefs()` and prints an error for some nonzero failures, but reaches an unconditional `RETURN_OK` (`workbench/c/Automount.c:258-271,339-345`). The mount loop also stores `ERROR_NO_FREE_STORE` when `CreateBSTR()` or its startup path allocation fails, then falls through to that successful return (`:300-305,319-324`). A malformed preferences file returns `-1` and skips mounting without changing the final result.

**Trigger and consequence:** encounter a preferences parse/read error or a mount-loop allocation failure. Automount may print a diagnostic or stop processing devices, yet its process status remains success, so Startup-Sequence and other callers cannot detect that automatic mounting did not complete. Preserve the error result and return an appropriate DOS status after cleanup. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds when preferences or mount setup fail. **Confidence:** high for the recorded failures and unconditional success return; no file, mount or allocation failure was exercised. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Automount full-body preference and mount-status pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#automount-full-body-preference-and-mount-status-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14578-requestchoice-leaks-gadget-buffer-if-body-format-allocation-fails"></a>
<a id="gd14578"></a>
## GD14578 — RequestChoice leaks the gadget buffer if body formatting allocation fails [conditional]

`Do_RequestChoice()` allocates `GadgetText` first, then calls `FilterBodyText()`. If the second allocation fails, it immediately returns `RETURN_FAIL` without freeing the already allocated gadget string (`workbench/c/RequestChoice.c:135-148`). The caller has no reference to that buffer and cannot release it.

**Trigger and consequence:** `ComposeGadgetText()` succeeds but `FilterBodyText()` cannot allocate its formatted body. The command exits with its gadget buffer still allocated; repeated failures leak one buffer per invocation. Free `GadgetText` on this early return or use a shared cleanup path. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds under memory pressure during RequestChoice body formatting. **Confidence:** high for the allocation and missing cleanup path; no allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [RequestChoice full-body requester and buffer pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#requestchoice-full-body-requester-and-buffer-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14579-symboldump-calls-debug-library-after-failed-open"></a>
<a id="gd14579"></a>
## GD14579 — SymbolDump calls debug.library after an unchecked open [conditional]

`OpenLibraries()` stores the result of `OpenLibrary("debug.library", 0L)` but does not validate it; `main()` unconditionally calls `EnumerateSymbolsA()` afterward (`workbench/c/SymbolDump.c:68-70,79-94`). The generated debug-library vector call requires a valid `DebugBase`.

**Trigger and consequence:** run SymbolDump where `debug.library` is unavailable or cannot be opened. The command calls its library vector with a null base and can fault instead of reporting that symbol enumeration is unavailable. Check the open result and return a diagnostic error before making the call. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds without an openable `debug.library`. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked open and unconditional vector call; no library was removed or command run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [SymbolDump full-body library and output pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#symboldump-full-body-library-and-output-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14580-symboldump-reports-success-when-output-is-unavailable"></a>
<a id="gd14580"></a>
## GD14580 — SymbolDump reports success when it cannot write the symbol file [conditional]

`main()` silently skips enumeration when `Open("SYS:symbols.out", MODE_NEWFILE)` fails, then returns zero (`workbench/c/SymbolDump.c:85-100`). On the open-success path, the symbol callback ignores every `FPrintf()` result and `main()` also ignores `Close()`'s result (`:55-65,87-98`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the destination cannot be created, or a write/close fails while the symbols are being emitted. SymbolDump exits successfully even though `SYS:symbols.out` is absent or incomplete, making the Callgrind input unusable without a failure status. Report the DOS error and return failure when open, write or close fails. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds when the destination path or output handler fails. **Confidence:** high for the ignored results and unconditional success; no file was opened or written. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [SymbolDump full-body library and output pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#symboldump-full-body-library-and-output-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14576-eject-finds-device-node-without-locking-dos-list"></a>
<a id="gd14576"></a>
## GD14576 — Eject reads a DOS device entry without locking the device list [conditional]

Eject calls `LockDosList(LDF_READ)`, then passes the returned list to `FindDosEntry(..., LDF_DEVICES)` and later reads `dev_node->dn_Startup` (`workbench/c/Eject.c:225-245`). `LockDosList()` accepts `LDF_READ` alone and still returns the non-NULL pseudo-list handle, but it obtains the device-list semaphore only when `LDF_ALL` is present; `LDF_READ` alone therefore locks no list (`rom/dos/lockdoslist.c:55-66,87`; flag definitions in `compiler/include/dos/dosextens.h:488-495`). `FindDosEntry()` explicitly requires the list to remain locked (`rom/dos/finddosentry.c:28-39`). The matching `UnLockDosList(LDF_READ)` releases no lock because it likewise has no list-selection flag (`rom/dos/unlockdoslist.c:49-56`). A selected console-handler shutdown path takes the device-list write lock while iterating/changing a device node (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:1232-1245`), confirming this list has concurrent writers; it does not prove that the particular Eject node is freed.

**Trigger and consequence:** run Eject while the device list is being changed or the selected node is removed/replaced after lookup. The command traverses and dereferences an unprotected DOS-list entry, so it can use stale startup data or a stale node. Lock with `LDF_DEVICES | LDF_READ` and retain the lock through copying the startup fields needed for `OpenDevice()`. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds during concurrent DOS device-list mutation. **Confidence:** high for the flags and selected API contract; no list mutation or command was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Eject/Load full-body DOS-list, command and device pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#eject-load-full-body-dos-list-command-and-device-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14574-search-silently-skips-file-after-long-line-buffer-allocation-fails"></a>
<a id="gd14574"></a>
## GD14574 — Search silently skips a file when its longest-line buffer cannot be allocated [conditional]

`FindString()` initially allocates a buffer based on the file size, reducing the requested size until an allocation succeeds. If it discovers a line at least as long as that buffer, it frees the working buffer and makes a single larger allocation for the longest line (`workbench/c/Search.c:451-499`). If that allocation fails, `buffer` is NULL, so the line-scanning block is skipped (`:502-505`); `FindString()` returns its initial `FALSE` value without setting an error (`:436,626`), and the caller can report the file as not containing the requested string.

**Trigger and consequence:** search a file containing a line larger than the largest initial buffer available under memory pressure, then fail the exact longest-line allocation. Search silently omits that file and may return the no-match warning even if the line contains the requested text. Retain the smaller buffer and implement chunked line matching, or propagate allocation failure as an error. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds with a long-line file and the stated allocation pressure. **Confidence:** high for the free-then-single-allocation path and skipped scan; no allocation failure or search was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Search full-body pattern and file-I/O pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#search-full-body-pattern-and-file-io-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14572-waitforport-times-out-after-eleven-seconds"></a>
<a id="gd14572"></a>
## GD14572 — WaitForPort waits an extra timer interval before timing out [conditional]

The command sets `wait_limit` to ten times its one-second interval, then increments `wait_time` after each timer reply and stops only when `wait_time > wait_limit` (`workbench/c/WaitForPort.c:107-108,123-145`). At exactly ten elapsed intervals the comparison is false, so it queues an eleventh one-second request; timeout occurs after that request completes.

**Trigger and consequence:** wait for a port that does not appear. The documented ten-second wait can continue for roughly eleven seconds, delaying callers such as the checked-in Rexx startup paths. Stop at the limit (`>=`) or schedule the remaining interval directly. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds when the requested port remains absent for the full timeout. **Confidence:** high for the counter/comparison and repeated one-second requests; no timer or port wait was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [WaitForPort full-body timer lifecycle and timeout pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#waitforport-full-body-timer-lifecycle-and-timeout-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14570-info-tests-before-the-first-byte-of-empty-assignment-filter"></a>
<a id="gd14570"></a>
## GD14570 — Info reads before an empty assignment filter string [conditional]

For each entry in a matched directory assign's lock list, `ScanDosList()` appends the empty string as a placeholder to `strray` (`workbench/c/Info.c:330-342`). The later device-filter pass feeds each non-NULL vector element to `myMatchPatternNoCase()`, which computes `len = strlen(p)` and tests `p[len - 1]` without handling `len == 0` (`:235-252,355-376`). The placeholder is a non-NULL pointer, so it is processed as a filter entry.

**Trigger and consequence:** filter Info by a directory assign that has at least one lock in its assign list, then let the device scan evaluate the expanded filter vector. Pattern matching reads one byte before the empty string while deciding whether to append a colon; the invalid read can affect the branch and may fault for an unsuitable address. Skip empty placeholders or handle zero-length patterns before indexing. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds when a matched directory assign has an assign-list entry. **Confidence:** high for the empty-string insertion and unchecked `len - 1` read; the resulting byte value and fault behavior are address-dependent. No command or DOS-list state was used. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Info filter expansion and volume-list full-body recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#info-filter-expansion-and-volume-list-full-body-recheck-2026-11-03).


<a id="eject-doslist-read-flag-implementation-and-writer-recheck-gd14576"></a>
Eject DOS-list read-flag implementation and writer recheck (GD14576 confirmed; no new finding or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): inspected the selected Eject lookup (`workbench/c/Eject.c:225-253`) against the actual `LockDosList()`, `UnLockDosList()`, and `FindDosEntry()` implementations. `LockDosList(LDF_READ)` passes the mode validation and returns the non-NULL pseudo-list pointer, but the device semaphore is acquired only under `flags & LDF_ALL` (`rom/dos/lockdoslist.c:55-66,87`); `UnLockDosList(LDF_READ)` similarly releases none (`rom/dos/unlockdoslist.c:49-56`). `FindDosEntry()` requires the DOS list to remain locked (`rom/dos/finddosentry.c:28-39`). The selected console handler provides a concrete concurrent device-list mutation path, acquiring `LDF_DEVICES | LDF_WRITE` during shutdown while walking and updating `dn_Task` (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:1232-1245`). This confirms the missing synchronization in Eject and that the null check on the returned handle does not detect it. Eject reads `dn_Startup` only after the no-op unlock (`Eject.c:240-253`); whether the specific node's storage is reclaimed in an overlapping path remains unproven, so the finding retains a conditional stale-node consequence and does not claim a reproduced use-after-free. No list mutation, Eject command, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="waitforport-break-and-timer-signal-overlap-recheck-gd14571"></a>
WaitForPort break/timer signal overlap and request teardown recheck (GD14571 expanded; no new ID or body/path/LOC credit; 2026-11-03): traced the break loop against Exec `Wait()`, `WaitIO()`, `DeleteIORequest()`, `DeleteMsgPort()` and timer completion/abort (`workbench/c/WaitForPort.c:110-168`; `rom/exec/wait.c:128-135`; `rom/exec/waitio.c:57-76`; `deleteiorequest.c:45-47`; `deletemsgport.c:48-53`; `rom/timer/lowlevel.c:187-220,365-375`; `rom/timer/abortio.c:69-83`). `Wait()` returns every currently active requested bit; WaitForPort checks Ctrl-C/D first and can skip `GetMsg()` when the timer bit is also set. Thus the original pending-request case remains: the timer list can still reference the request when teardown frees it. A second completion race is supported: if the timer has already replied, the early break leaves the request as `NT_REPLYMSG` in the reply-port queue, then `DeleteIORequest()` frees the linked message and `DeleteMsgPort()` discards the remaining queue. `WaitIO()` is the selected API that removes an already replied request from the port. Expanded GD14571 to record both states; the post-reply case does not require claiming later timer access, and no signal, timer request, or build was exercised. Source-only.

<a id="gd14582-gpio-command-accepts-unsupported-pin-numbers"></a>
<a id="gd14582"></a>
## GD14582 — GPIO command reports success for unsupported pin numbers [conditional]

`GPIO` parses the requested `LONG` pin and immediately converts it to `ULONG`, without checking the signed value or the pin range supported by the opened resource (`workbench/c/GPIO.c:108-110`). The selected Raspberry Pi `gpio.resource` methods silently do nothing outside their implemented pin ranges: RP1 operations handle pins 0–27 and the legacy peripheral path handles pins 0–53 (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/gpio/gpio_init.c:56-79,95-145,152-169,180-209`). `GPIOGet()` initializes its result to zero and returns it unchanged when neither path handles the pin (`:148-169`). The command never receives an operation status and returns `RETURN_OK` after any requested operation (`workbench/c/GPIO.c:111-138`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use a negative pin or a pin beyond the active resource's supported range. The command reports a low reading for GET, or reports success after SET/MODE/PULL even though the resource performed no operation. Reject unsupported values before calling the void resource vectors and return an error. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `workbench-c` command on a system with the Raspberry Pi `gpio.resource` available. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked conversion, no-op resource paths and success return; no GPIO was accessed. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [GPIO full-body range and resource-contract pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gpio-full-body-range-and-resource-contract-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14585-requeststring-never-frees-readargs-state"></a>
<a id="gd14585"></a>
## GD14585 — RequestString never frees its ReadArgs state [conditional]

After `ReadArgs()` succeeds, every path proceeds without calling `FreeArgs(rdargs)` (`workbench/c/RequestString.c:99-213`). This includes the normal requester completion path after `MUI_DisposeObject(app)` and the application-construction failure path. `ReadArgs()` returns an owned RDArgs structure and any parser allocations for the caller to release with `FreeArgs()`.

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke RequestString with successfully parsed arguments. Its DOS argument state is left allocated when the command exits; repeated invocations can accumulate the RDArgs and parser-owned storage. Free the successful `ReadArgs()` result on both the normal and failed-application paths. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c-requeststring` builds. **Confidence:** high for successful allocation and absent cleanup; no requester or allocation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [RequestString full-body MUI and argument-lifetime pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#requeststring-full-body-mui-and-argument-lifetime-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14588-clip-wait-ignores-startnotify-failure"></a>
<a id="gd14588"></a>
## GD14588 — Clip GET WAIT blocks after StartNotify fails [conditional]

In the `GET WAIT` path, Clip calls `StartNotify(clipUnitNR)` without checking its Boolean result, then unconditionally waits for the notification signal or Ctrl-C (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Clip.c:101-116`). DOS documents StartNotify as returning success/failure, and its implementation returns false when it cannot resolve the device path or register the notification (`rom/dos/startnotify.c:48-60,73-86,166-197`). On that failure path Clip has no notifier that can signal `waitSig`, but still blocks in `Wait()`.

**Trigger and consequence:** use `Clip GET WAIT` when the `CLIPS:<unit>` path has no usable handler or notification registration fails. The command waits indefinitely for a signal that will never be sent, unless the user interrupts it. Check `StartNotify()` and return its DOS error before waiting. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c-shellcommands` builds when GET WAIT is used and DOS notification setup fails. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked failure and unreachable signal source; no clipboard handler or wait was exercised. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Clip full-body notification, IFF and count pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#clip-full-body-notification-iff-and-count-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14589"></a>
## GD14589 — Clip overflows the accumulated clipboard buffer size [conditional]

`fromClip()` stores both `filebuffer_size` and `ContextNode.cn_Size` in 32-bit `ULONG`/`LONG` fields (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Clip.c:245-247`; `compiler/include/exec/types.h:35-39`; `compiler/include/libraries/iffparse.h:59-66`). When it appends a later `CHRS` chunk, `filebuffer_size + cn->cn_Size + 1` is evaluated at 32 bits before `AllocVec()` receives it (`Clip.c:284-295`). Once the total exceeds `ULONG_MAX`, the allocation wraps to a smaller size, but `CopyMem()` still copies the full previous `filebuffer_size` into that allocation (`:292`); the subsequent `ReadChunkBytes()` is also given the full current chunk size (`:297-303`). The IFF reader limits that read to the declared chunk extent, not to the destination allocation (`workbench/libs/iffparse/readchunkbytes.c:58-85`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on a 64-bit build with sufficient memory, read clipboard data containing multiple `FTXT/CHRS` chunks whose combined text exceeds 4 GiB (for example, three positive 1.5 GiB chunks). The accumulated allocation expression wraps; the next `CopyMem()` writes the previous multi-gigabyte buffer into the undersized allocation, corrupting adjacent heap memory. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c-shellcommands` builds on a 64-bit AROS system with a correspondingly large clipboard payload; no checked-in caller or fixture establishes such a payload. **Confidence:** high for 32-bit arithmetic and the allocation/copy size mismatch; conditional on a clipboard larger than 4 GiB and sufficient memory. Use checked wide arithmetic and reject totals not representable by the allocation/read interfaces. Source-only; no clipboard data or command was used.

**Coverage evidence:** [Clip full-body notification, IFF and count pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#clip-full-body-notification-iff-and-count-pass-2026-11-03).



<a id="gd14590"></a>
## GD14590 — Sound datatype disposal retries failed shutdown allocations forever [conditional]

When a Sound object has a player process, `Sound_DISPOSE()` loops until it can create a reply message port and then loops until it can allocate the exit `IORequest`; both loops only call `Delay(25L)` after failure (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:1427-1437`). `CreateMsgPort()` can return NULL when its message-port allocation or signal-bit allocation fails (`rom/exec/createmsgport.c:50-74`), and `CreateIORequest()` returns NULL when its `AllocMem()` fails (`rom/exec/createiorequest.c:59-76`). There is no retry bound, resource-release attempt, or failure return from this method before it can send `COMMAND_EXIT` and finish disposal (`dispatch.c:1439-1445`).

**Trigger and consequence:** dispose a Sound object with a running player while the required signal bit or memory remains unavailable. The disposal method delays and retries indefinitely, never sending the worker's exit command or releasing the object's remaining resources; a caller waiting for disposal can hang. A temporary shortage may eventually clear, but persistent exhaustion has no termination path. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built and installed `workbench-datatypes-sound` when an object with an active player is disposed under persistent signal or memory exhaustion; the target's parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/mmakefile.src:4-13`). **Confidence:** high for the unbounded retry and allocation failure returns; conditional on sustained resource exhaustion during disposal. Provide a bounded failure path or reuse an already-owned shutdown/reply resource. Source-only; no allocation failure, datatype disposal, or audio operation was induced.

**Coverage evidence:** [Sound datatype dispose allocation-retry pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-dispose-allocation-retry-gd14590).


<a id="gd14591"></a>
## GD14591 — RequestString compares the encrypted hash instead of entered text [conditional]

`RequestString` saves the string gadget contents in `returntext`, replaces that pointer with the result of `ACrypt()` when `ENCRYPT` is set, and only then evaluates `COMPARE` using `strcmp(returntext, args[ARG_COMPARE])` (`workbench/c/RequestString.c:185-211`). The command documentation says `COMPARE` tests whether the input string equals the supplied argument (`:35-39`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke RequestString with both `ENCRYPT` and `COMPARE`, and enter text that matches the `COMPARE` argument. The comparison uses the encrypted hash, so it returns `RETURN_WARN` instead of success; conversely, a compare value matching the hash can succeed despite different entered text. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly built `workbench-c-requeststring` target (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:135-136`) when both options are supplied. **Confidence:** high; the substitution precedes the comparison and the documented operands differ. Preserve the original input for `COMPARE`, or perform the comparison before replacing it with the encrypted output. Source-only; no command or build was run.

**Coverage evidence:** [RequestString option-interaction caller pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#requeststring-encrypt-compare-interaction-gd14591).


<a id="gd14592"></a>
## GD14592 — RequestFile passes an unterminated drawer buffer to AddPart [conditional]

`main()` allocates a 512-byte path buffer and copies `fr_Drawer` into all 512 bytes with `strncpy()` (`workbench/c/RequestFile.c:81,130,165,183`). When the drawer string is at least 512 bytes, `strncpy()` does not append a terminator. The ASL drawer gadget accepts up to 1024 characters (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqhooks.h:38`; `filereqhooks.c:879`), and `FRGetSelectedFiles()` clones the selected drawer path into dynamically sized storage (`filereqhooks.c:1772-1777`). `RequestFile` then calls `AddPart()` on the copied buffer; the selected DOS implementation calls `strlen(dirname)` before it checks whether the resulting path fits (`rom/dos/addpart.c:115-130`).

**Trigger and consequence:** select a drawer path of 512 or more bytes in either single-select or multiselect mode. `AddPart()` scans past the allocated command buffer looking for a NUL terminator, so it may read adjacent memory and compute or reject the combined path using bytes outside the copied drawer. Ensure the buffer is terminated or reject paths that do not fit before calling `AddPart()`. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:5-45`) when a long drawer can be selected. **Confidence:** high for the fixed-size copy, ASL's larger accepted path, and `AddPart()`'s pre-check `strlen()`; the specific adjacent bytes read depend on runtime allocation layout. No requester or long path was used; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [RequestFile full-body path handling pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#requestfile-full-body-path-handling-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14593"></a>
## GD14593 — RequestFile reports success when a selected path cannot be joined [conditional]

In both single-select and multiselect handling, `RequestFile` assigns the result of `AddPart()` to `Success` but does not change `Return_Value` when it is false (`workbench/c/RequestFile.c:168-175,185-195`). The selected DOS `AddPart()` returns false and sets `ERROR_LINE_TOO_LONG` when the joined path exceeds the supplied 512-byte capacity (`rom/dos/addpart.c:127-139`). In single-select mode this suppresses the path output; in multiselect mode that selected item is skipped, and the command continues printing other items and a newline. The initial `Return_Value` remains `RETURN_OK` (`RequestFile.c:125`).

**Trigger and consequence:** select a file whose drawer and name together exceed 511 path bytes (or select such an item in a multi-selection). The command omits the path, or returns only a subset of selected paths, yet exits with success. Check the `AddPart()` result and report a DOS error or an incomplete selection. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-c` builds when the selected path exceeds the command's 512-byte buffer. **Confidence:** high for the helper's failure return and the caller's unchanged exit status/output flow. No long path or requester was used; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [RequestFile full-body path handling pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#requestfile-full-body-path-handling-pass-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14594"></a>
## GD14594 — Font Preferences treats an IFF open failure as a successful import [conditional]

`Prefs_ImportFH()` initializes `success` to TRUE. If `OpenIFF()` fails, it displays an error but leaves `success` unchanged and returns TRUE (`workbench/prefs/font/prefs.c:170-174,185-185,228-235`). For command-line `FROM=... USE` or `SAVE`, `Prefs_Load()` propagates that value; `Prefs_HandleArgs()` then continues with its uninitialized stack array `fp` and opens `ENV:SYS/font.prefs` and, for SAVE, `ENVARC:SYS/font.prefs` with `MODE_NEWFILE` before exporting the array (`:89-100,118-144`).

**Trigger and consequence:** supply an existing file that DOS can open but `OpenIFF()` rejects, together with `USE` or `SAVE`. The import is accepted as successful and the command writes indeterminate stack contents as font preferences, replacing the current ENV settings and potentially the persistent ENVARC settings. Return FALSE when IFF initialization fails and do not save unless the import completed. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `workbench-prefs-font` when its CLI `FROM` path names a non-IFF or malformed file and USE/SAVE is requested (`workbench/prefs/font/mmakefile.src:4-14`; the parent Preferences edge is disabled). **Confidence:** high for the unchanged TRUE result and caller's uninitialized local array flowing to truncating output opens; no file or preferences operation was performed. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Font Preferences selected-body and IFF import pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#font-preferences-selected-body-and-iff-import-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14595"></a>
## GD14595 — Font Preferences imports short FONT chunks from an uninitialized record [conditional]

For each `ID_FONT` chunk, `Prefs_ImportFH()` declares an uninitialized `FileFontPrefs`, asks `ReadChunkBytes()` to fill the full structure, and only treats a negative result as an error (`workbench/prefs/font/prefs.c:190-210`). The selected `ReadChunkBytes()` implementation caps the requested byte count to the chunk's remaining size and returns the number actually read (`workbench/libs/iffparse/readchunkbytes.c:58-85`). A truncated but nonnegative result therefore still flows through `FileFontPrefs2FontPrefs()`, which copies every field, including all 128 font-name bytes, from the partly initialized local record (`workbench/prefs/font/prefs.c:32-50`; `workbench/prefs/font/prefs.h:11-25`). The importer can return success, and the CLI caller can subsequently save those values (`prefs.c:89-100,118-144`).

**Trigger and consequence:** import an IFF preferences file containing an `ID_FONT` chunk shorter than `sizeof(struct FileFontPrefs)` but otherwise found by `ParseIFF()`. Missing bytes come from uninitialized stack storage and are copied into the resulting settings; `USE`/`SAVE` can persist them, while the GUI import can display the corrupted fields. Require an exact structure-sized read and reject the file before converting the record. **Affected configuration:** explicit `workbench-prefs-font` builds when importing a truncated FONT chunk. **Confidence:** high for the short-read contract and unconditional full-structure copy; no malformed file was created or read. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Font Preferences selected-body and IFF import pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#font-preferences-selected-body-and-iff-import-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14596"></a>
## GD14596 — Font Preferences saves invalid font strings after ignoring conversion errors [conditional]

`FontString2FontPrefs()` returns FALSE when the font name will not fit `fp_Name`, but it also accepts an invalid size suffix: it ignores `StrToLong()`'s `-1` result and stores the zero value that DOS writes on conversion failure (`workbench/prefs/font/fpeditor.c:51-74`; `rom/dos/strtolong.c:43-80`). `Gadgets2FontPrefs()` ignores each conversion result, always sets the entry type, and returns TRUE (`fpeditor.c:77-98`). The ExportFH method then serializes these fields (`:213-225`; `workbench/prefs/font/prefs.c:268-289`).

**Trigger and consequence:** enter an overlong font name or a nonnumeric size in a font gadget, then save or use the preferences. An overlong name leaves the old name in place; a nonnumeric size is stored as zero. The editor reports successful conversion and exports settings different from the entered values, potentially making the selected font unavailable to subsequent consumers. Validate the complete string, propagate conversion failure, and prevent export until all entries parse. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `workbench-prefs-font` when users enter strings outside the supported name/size format. **Confidence:** high for the ignored parse return and `StrToLong()` failure behavior; downstream font selection depends on the consuming client. No GUI or preference save was performed. Source-only.


<a id="gd14597"></a>
## GD14597 — Font Preferences reports export success after a write failure [conditional]

`Prefs_ExportFH()` discards the results from several structural writes (`PushChunk()`, header `WriteChunkBytes()`, and `PopChunk()`). For each font record it assigns the `WriteChunkBytes()` result to `error`, immediately overwrites it with `PopChunk()`, and only prints the latter result; no write error sets `success` FALSE (`workbench/prefs/font/prefs.c:238-302`). Its command-line caller ignores the helper's return value as well (`:118-142`). `WriteChunkBytes()` returns the actual byte count or a negative error (`workbench/libs/iffparse/writechunkbytes.c:30-44`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a DOS write or IFF chunk operation fails while creating `ENV:SYS/font.prefs` or `ENVARC:SYS/font.prefs`, for example because the destination becomes full or unwritable. Export can leave a truncated or structurally invalid preferences file while reporting success, and the caller gives no failure result to the user. Check every IFF operation, return failure on short/error writes, and preserve the previous preference file when export fails. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `workbench-prefs-font` when an ENV or ENVARC export encounters a write/stream error. **Confidence:** high for discarded API results and unconditional success after opened-stream writes; no file or write failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Font Preferences selected-body and IFF import pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#font-preferences-selected-body-and-iff-import-pass-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14598"></a>
## GD14598 — Firewall Preferences skips a persistent rules file when ENV contains only the other rule type [conditional]

Startup reads both rule files from `ENV:AROSTCP`, then loads `ENVARC:AROSTCP` only when both rule counts are zero (`workbench/prefs/firewall/main.c:31-34`; `prefsdata.c:21-25`). Each reader updates only its own count when its file opens (`filter.c:284-304`; `nat.c:215-235`). If the ENV directory contains filter rules but no NAT rules, the nonzero filter count prevents loading the persistent NAT rules; the reverse applies when ENV has only NAT rules.

**Trigger and consequence:** start Firewall Preferences with a nonempty ENV `ipf.rules`, an empty or absent ENV `ipnat.rules`, and nonempty ENVARC `ipnat.rules` (or the converse). The editor loads only one half of the effective saved configuration; later Use/Save can write and apply that incomplete set. Load each rule file from ENVARC independently when its ENV counterpart has no usable rules. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `workbench-prefs-firewall` when runtime ENV and persistent ENVARC contain different, partially populated rule sets (`workbench/prefs/firewall/mmakefile.src:4-14`; the parent Preferences edge is disabled). **Confidence:** high for the combined-count fallback condition and independent readers; no firewall preferences or command was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Firewall Preferences selected-body, rule I/O and apply pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#firewall-preferences-selected-body-rule-io-and-apply-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14599"></a>
## GD14599 — Firewall Preferences reports rules applied without checking ipf or ipnat results [conditional]

`ApplyFirewallRules()` synchronously calls `SystemTags()` to flush and reload filter and NAT state, but ignores every return value and unconditionally returns TRUE (`workbench/prefs/firewall/prefsdata.c:31-53`). The selected DOS `SystemTagList()` contract returns the command's return code or `-1` if it cannot run (`rom/dos/systemtaglist.c:31-40`); these calls explicitly request synchronous execution with `SYS_Asynch, FALSE` (`prefsdata.c:35-50`). `SaveFirewallPrefs()` and `UseFirewallPrefs()` then return success, and the Preferences editor clears its changed/testing state (`prefsdata.c:60-89`; `fweditor.c:904-937`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a flush or load command cannot start, rejects the file, or returns a failure. The UI still treats Use/Save as successful; because flush precedes load, active rules may also be left cleared or only partly applied. Check each command's result, preserve the failure for the caller, and report which stage failed. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built Firewall Preferences with the `ipf` or `ipnat` command missing or failing during Use/Save. **Confidence:** high for ignored synchronous command results and unconditional success; no command or firewall state was exercised. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Firewall Preferences selected-body, rule I/O and apply pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#firewall-preferences-selected-body-rule-io-and-apply-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14600"></a>
## GD14600 — Firewall Preferences reports successful rule-file writes after FPuts fails [conditional]

`WriteFilterConf()` and `WriteNATConf()` check whether `Open(..., MODE_NEWFILE)` succeeds, but ignore the return from every subsequent `FPuts()` and `Close()` and then return TRUE (`workbench/prefs/firewall/filter.c:310-334`; `nat.c:241-265`). The selected DOS `FPuts()` returns `-1` when its underlying write is short or fails (`rom/dos/fputs.c:31-41,58-62`). The orchestration uses these Boolean results to decide whether to apply the files and report success (`workbench/prefs/firewall/prefsdata.c:59-89`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a rule-file write or buffered close fails after the destination has been opened, such as on a full or write-protected filesystem. The writer reports success with a truncated or incomplete file, so Save/Use can proceed as if the rules were stored correctly. Propagate write and close failures and avoid replacing the prior file until a complete new copy is ready. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built Firewall Preferences when writing either ENV or ENVARC rule files encounters an I/O failure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked writes and DOS result contract; no file or write failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Firewall Preferences selected-body, rule I/O and apply pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#firewall-preferences-selected-body-rule-io-and-apply-pass-2026-11-03).


<a id="gd14601"></a>
## GD14601 — ASL Preferences accepts a failed IFF open and saves zeroed settings [conditional]

`Prefs_ImportFH()` starts with `success = TRUE`. When `OpenIFF()` fails, it displays an error but never sets `success` to FALSE, then returns TRUE (`workbench/prefs/asl/prefs.c:53-56,68,104-110`). The command-line `FROM` path treats that result as a successful load; its global `aslprefs` storage is zero-initialized, and `USE`/`SAVE` then creates `ENV:SYS/Asl.prefs` and optionally `ENVARC:SYS/Asl.prefs` with `MODE_NEWFILE` and exports those zeroed values (`:33,189-243`). The MUI PrefsEditor also relies on a false import result to try ENVARC after ENV (`workbench/classes/zune/prefseditor/prefseditor.c:65-75`).

**Trigger and consequence:** open a non-IFF or malformed file with `FROM=... USE` or `SAVE`, or have an invalid ENV preference file while a valid ENVARC file exists. The invalid import is treated as successful, so command-line Use/Save can replace existing settings with zeros, and the GUI does not fall back to the persistent file. Return failure for OpenIFF failure so callers can stop or try their fallback. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `workbench-prefs-asl` when an opened preference file is not a valid IFF stream (`workbench/prefs/asl/mmakefile.src:6-15`; parent Preferences edge disabled). **Confidence:** high for the success flag and both caller behaviors; no preference file or command was used. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [ASL Preferences selected-body and IFF persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#asl-preferences-selected-body-and-iff-persistence-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14602"></a>
## GD14602 — ASL Preferences copies a short ASL chunk from an uninitialized record [conditional]

For a parsed `ID_ASL` chunk, `Prefs_ImportFH()` declares an uninitialized `struct AslPrefs loadprefs`, reads the full structure, checks only for a negative result, then copies and byte-swaps the whole structure regardless of how many bytes were read (`workbench/prefs/asl/prefs.c:73-88`). The selected `ReadChunkBytes()` caps the request to the chunk's remaining bytes and returns the actual count (`workbench/libs/iffparse/readchunkbytes.c:58-85`); a short nonnegative count is therefore accepted. The result is used as a successful import and is later saved by the CLI path or exposed to the editor (`prefs.c:189-243`; `asleditor.c:337-350`).

**Trigger and consequence:** import an IFF file whose `ID_ASL` chunk is shorter than `sizeof(struct AslPrefs)`. Missing bytes are copied from the uninitialized local record into the global settings and can be displayed or persisted as preferences. Require an exact structure-sized read and reject incomplete chunks. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `workbench-prefs-asl` when importing a truncated `ID_ASL` chunk. **Confidence:** high for the short-read contract and unconditional full-size copy; no file was read or created. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [ASL Preferences selected-body and IFF persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#asl-preferences-selected-body-and-iff-persistence-pass-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14603"></a>
## GD14603 — ASL Preferences reports success when preference writes fail [conditional]

`Prefs_ExportFH()` ignores the results of the FORM/PRHD chunk pushes, header write, ASL data write and final FORM pop; it only prints some chunk errors and leaves `success` TRUE after an opened write stream (`workbench/prefs/asl/prefs.c:116-184`). The selected `WriteChunkBytes()` returns the actual count written or a negative error (`workbench/libs/iffparse/writechunkbytes.c:30-44`). The command-line caller ignores `Prefs_ExportFH()`'s result and closes the destination after opening it with `MODE_NEWFILE` (`prefs.c:217-243`); the PrefsEditor method returns the helper result directly (`asleditor.c:355-369`).

**Trigger and consequence:** writing or finalizing `ENV:SYS/Asl.prefs` or `ENVARC:SYS/Asl.prefs` fails after the file is opened. The export can leave a truncated IFF file while returning success; command-line Use/Save also suppresses the failure. Propagate short writes, chunk errors and close errors, and preserve the prior file until a complete replacement is available. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `workbench-prefs-asl` when the destination filesystem reports a write/finalization error. **Confidence:** high for discarded write results and unconditional success; no file or write failure was induced. Source-only.

<a id="gd14604"></a>
## GD14604 — ReqTools CLI ignores preference export and close failures [conditional]

`Prefs_ExportFH()` detects a short or failed `Write()` and returns FALSE (`workbench/prefs/reqtools/prefs.c:65-98`; DOS `Write()` returns the number actually written or -1 on error, `rom/dos/write.c:35-55`). However, `Prefs_HandleArgs()` discards that result for both ENV and ENVARC outputs, ignores `Close()`'s result, and returns TRUE regardless (`prefs.c:113-158`). DOS `Close()` can report a buffered write/flush failure (`rom/dos/close.c:24-34`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run the explicitly built ReqTools Preferences CLI with `USE` or `SAVE` when the target filesystem short-writes, fails a buffered flush, or fails close. The command still reports success to its caller even though the active or persistent preferences file can be incomplete. Propagate both export and close failures through `Prefs_HandleArgs()` and `main()`. **Affected configuration:** `workbench-prefs-reqtools` CLI invocation when ENV or ENVARC writes fail; its explicit target is enabled while the parent `workbench-prefs` aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/prefs/reqtools/mmakefile.src:8-14`). **Confidence:** high for the discarded results and DOS return contracts; no file operation or build was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [ReqTools Preferences full-body and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#reqtools-preferences-full-body-and-persistence-pass).

<a id="gd14605"></a>
## GD14605 — Printer Preferences uses imported fixed-width names as unterminated C strings [conditional]

The IFF importer accepts an exactly sized `PTXT`, `PUNT`, or `PDEV` chunk and copies the complete record, but never requires a NUL byte in the fixed-width `pt_Driver[30]`, `pu_DeviceName[32]`, or `pd_UnitName[32]` fields (`workbench/prefs/printer/prefs.c:118-155`; definitions in `compiler/include/prefs/printertxt.h:28-34,78-90`). The GUI import path then passes these arrays as string pointers and calls `strcmp()` on `pu_DeviceName` (`workbench/prefs/printer/editor.c:708-742`). The C-string operations can read beyond the corresponding field, including beyond the end of the local `unit` record, when a structurally sized preference chunk contains no terminator.

**Trigger and consequence:** import a Printer preferences IFF file with a full-width, unterminated driver, device, or unit name. Opening/synchronizing the GUI can read past the field while comparing or displaying the value, causing invalid display data or a fault; later export also consumes UI strings into fixed-width fields. Validate termination (or copy into bounded terminated buffers) before using imported names as strings. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built Printer Preferences GUI when loading such a malformed `PTXT`, `PUNT`, or `PDEV` chunk. **Confidence:** high for missing validation and subsequent C-string use; no file or GUI was used. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Printer Preferences full-body import, editor and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#printer-preferences-full-body-import-editor-and-persistence-pass).

<a id="gd14606"></a>
## GD14606 — Printer Preferences reports successful persistence after IFF finalization or file writes fail [conditional]

`Prefs_ExportFH()` sets `retval = TRUE` after writing its data chunks, then calls `CloseIFF()` without observing errors; `CloseIFF()` automatically pops remaining chunks, including the outer FORM, but its implementation logs and discards `PopChunk()` errors (`workbench/prefs/printer/prefs.c:262-310`; `workbench/libs/iffparse/closeiff.c:74-82`). The command-line caller also ignores `Prefs_ExportFH()` and DOS `Close()` results for ENV and ENVARC writes and returns TRUE (`workbench/prefs/printer/prefs.c:346-372`). DOS `Close()` can report buffered flush failure (`rom/dos/close.c:24-30,74-80`). The GUI PrefsEditor path does return the export helper result (`workbench/prefs/printer/editor.c:792-804`), but cannot detect the ignored IFF finalization failure.

**Trigger and consequence:** an IFF chunk/FORM finalization or destination-file write fails after the output is opened. The GUI helper or CLI can report success while leaving an incomplete preference file; the CLI suppresses even the helper's detected chunk-write failures. Propagate IFF finalization/write errors and check CLI export and DOS close results. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `workbench-prefs-printer` GUI export or `USE`/`SAVE` when destination I/O/finalization fails; its parent Preferences aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/prefs/printer/mmakefile.src:8-14`). **Confidence:** high for the discarded return paths and selected close contract; no file operation or build was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Printer Preferences full-body import, editor and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#printer-preferences-full-body-import-editor-and-persistence-pass).

<a id="gd14607"></a>
## GD14607 — Locale Preferences overflows fixed locale-name storage for long resource filenames [conditional]

`ScanDirectory()` allocates each `node.ln_Name` to the full discovered filename length, removes the extension, then copies the resulting base name into `entry->realname` with `strcpy()` (`workbench/prefs/locale/prefs.c:215-242`). `realname` is a fixed 30-byte array (`workbench/prefs/locale/prefs.h:38-52`). The scan covers country and language resources (`prefs.c:675-676`), so a base filename longer than 29 bytes writes beyond the entry allocation; language entries end immediately after this fixed array.

**Trigger and consequence:** Locale initialization encounters a country or language resource whose extension-stripped filename is 30 bytes or longer. The copy overwrites adjacent entry storage and can corrupt the locale list or later allocations. Bound the copy or reject overlong resource names before constructing an entry. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built Locale Preferences when such a resource is installed in `LOCALE:Countries` or `LOCALE:Languages`. **Confidence:** high for the allocated source length, fixed destination size, and unbounded copy; no directory contents were changed or scanned at runtime. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Locale Preferences full-body resource, editor and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#locale-preferences-full-body-resource-editor-and-persistence-pass).

<a id="gd14608"></a>
