## GD14608 — Locale Preferences dereferences a missing preferred-language list entry [conditional]

`Language__OM_GET(MUIA_Language_Preferred)` loops over all ten preference slots and initializes `langNative` to NULL before each `MUIM_List_GetEntry()` call. It then passes the result to `Stricmp()` without checking it (`workbench/prefs/locale/page_language.c:601-619`). The `MUIC_List` superclass is implemented by `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c`; its `MUIM_List_GetEntry` documents and stores NULL for an out-of-range index (`list.c:3020-3057`). `Stricmp()` dereferences both arguments (`rom/utility/stricmp.c:59-62`). `Gadgets2LocalePrefs()` requests this attribute during Use/Save (`workbench/prefs/locale/registertab.c:228-240`).

**Trigger and consequence:** save or use Locale preferences when fewer than ten languages are in the Preferred list, including the normal case of selecting only one language. The first unused slot reaches `Stricmp(NULL, ...)` and can fault instead of completing the preference operation. Stop at the first missing list entry before comparing it. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built Locale Preferences GUI. **Confidence:** high for the selected list's null result, the null-unsafe compare, and the export caller; no GUI operation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Locale Preferences full-body resource, editor and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#locale-preferences-full-body-resource-editor-and-persistence-pass).

<a id="gd14609"></a>
## GD14609 — Locale Preferences truncates half-hour city offsets to whole hours [conditional]

The city-list hook converts a signed `±HHMM` value with `CityArray[sel].timediff / 100 * 60` before matching it against the timezone table (`workbench/prefs/locale/page_timezone.c:561-587`; `CityArray` values are in `workbench/prefs/locale/cities.h:16-86`). Integer division discards the minute component. For example Adelaide's `+930` becomes 540 minutes, selecting the table's +09:00 zone instead of +09:30; the resulting value is stored as the selected GMT offset and can be saved (`page_timezone.c:581-587`; the selected value is read and stored by `registertab.c:249,263-268,309`).

**Trigger and consequence:** select a city with a half-hour offset from the city list, such as Adelaide, Bombay, or Calcutta. Locale Preferences stores a whole-hour offset and can apply a system time offset that is wrong by 30 minutes. Convert hours and minutes separately while preserving the sign. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built Locale Preferences GUI when choosing a city whose offset contains nonzero minutes. **Confidence:** high for the arithmetic and checked-in city values; no timezone selection or system clock was changed. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Locale Preferences full-body resource, editor and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#locale-preferences-full-body-resource-editor-and-persistence-pass).

<a id="gd14610"></a>
## GD14610 — Locale Preferences makes system-clock correction depend on the selected character set [conditional]

`Gadgets2LocalePrefs()` retrieves the selected character-set string into `tmp` (`workbench/prefs/locale/registertab.c:242-246`), then later uses `if (tmp)` to decide whether to subtract the previous locale GMT offset while synchronizing the system clock (`:270-299`). `tmp` therefore reflects whether a character set is selected, not the GMT-clock mode or timezone state that caused `sync_clock` to be set (`:251-268`). The Language class explicitly returns NULL for its “not specified” character-set entry (`workbench/prefs/locale/page_language.c:622-629`).

**Trigger and consequence:** change the GMT-clock setting or change timezone while GMT clock is active. The system-time correction then depends on whether a character set is selected: with no selected charset it skips the offset adjustment; with a selected charset it applies it. The character-set choice can therefore change the clock result for the same timezone operation. Gate the conversion on the relevant clock/timezone state instead of the charset pointer. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built Locale Preferences GUI when clock synchronization is requested; the battclock resource and timer device must be available for the correction path. **Confidence:** high that the unrelated pointer controls the adjustment branch; no clock or device operation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Locale Preferences full-body resource, editor and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#locale-preferences-full-body-resource-editor-and-persistence-pass).

<a id="gd14611"></a>
## GD14611 — Locale Preferences uses imported fixed-width names without checking for terminators [conditional]

`Prefs_ImportFH()` accepts a full-size `LocalePrefs` record and copies it without validating string termination (`workbench/prefs/locale/prefs.c:418-468`; the country name is 32 bytes and preferred-language fields are ten 30-byte arrays in `compiler/include/prefs/locale.h:62-67`). The GUI subsequently passes the country array into the Region setter, which compares it as a C string, and passes preferred-language fields into `Stricmp()` (`registertab.c:315-323`; `page_language.c:653-665`). A full-width field with no NUL is therefore consumed by unbounded string routines.

**Trigger and consequence:** import a structurally valid `locale.prefs` whose country or preferred-language field fills its fixed-width field without a terminator. GUI synchronization can read past the field while looking up the selected country or language, causing incorrect settings or a fault. Validate termination or use bounded comparisons/copies before string operations. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built Locale Preferences GUI when importing such a record. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked record copy and selected string consumers; no preferences file was read. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Locale Preferences full-body resource, editor and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#locale-preferences-full-body-resource-editor-and-persistence-pass).


<a id="gd14612"></a>
## GD14612 — Input Preferences reports success when the KMSW export fails [conditional]

`Prefs_ExportFH()` sets `retval = TRUE` after writing the `INPT` chunk. It then tries to push and write the `KMSW` chunk, but neither a failed `PushChunk()` nor a short/failed `WriteChunkBytes()` clears `retval`; on successful KMSW write it only evaluates `retval = retval && TRUE` (`workbench/prefs/input/prefs.c:424-458`). The GUI export method returns this helper result (`workbench/prefs/input/ipeditor.c:585-596`), while CLI Use/Save ignores it and also ignores DOS `Close()` failures (`workbench/prefs/input/prefs.c:529-551`).

**Trigger and consequence:** exporting when the INPT write succeeds but KMSW chunk creation or writing fails. The caller receives success and may treat a file missing the alternate-keymap preferences as complete. Make KMSW failure clear the overall result and propagate finalization errors. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-prefs-input` GUI export and CLI Use/Save; its parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/prefs/input/mmakefile.src:4-12`). **Confidence:** high for the result-flow defect; no IFF write failure or build was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Input Preferences full-body import, editor and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#input-preferences-full-body-import-editor-and-persistence-pass).

<a id="gd14613"></a>
## GD14613 — Input Preferences imports short KMSW chunks from uninitialized storage [conditional]

`Prefs_ImportFH()` declares `loadkmsprefs` without initializing it. For a KMSW chunk, it caps the requested size at the struct size, accepts any read for which `ReadChunkBytes()` returns that size, then copies every KMSW field into global preferences (`workbench/prefs/input/prefs.c:268-273,332-352`). Thus a short chunk can leave the unread tail indeterminate while still satisfying the equality check and being consumed as settings. Unlike the adjacent `loadprefs`, this local struct is not cleared before the read.

**Trigger and consequence:** import a KMSW chunk shorter than the current `FileKMSPrefs` layout, including an empty chunk. Unread fields can be loaded from stack contents and displayed or later saved as key-switch settings. Reject undersized records or zero-initialize and version the compatibility handling. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Input Preferences GUI or CLI import. **Confidence:** high for the uninitialized destination and subsequent field copies; no malformed file was imported. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Input Preferences full-body import, editor and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#input-preferences-full-body-import-editor-and-persistence-pass).

<a id="gd14614"></a>
## GD14614 — Input Preferences compares unterminated imported keymap fields as C strings [conditional]

The INPT and KMSW import paths copy the fixed-width `ip_KeymapName[64]` and `kms_AltKeymap[64]` fields directly into global preference structures without checking for a NUL terminator (`workbench/prefs/input/prefs.c:327,350`; public field sizes: `compiler/include/prefs/input.h:26-53`). On GUI import, `InputPrefs2Gadgets()` passes these arrays to `stricmp()` while searching the scanned keymap list (`workbench/prefs/input/ipeditor.c:526-535`).

**Trigger and consequence:** import a full-width malformed keymap name with no NUL byte and then construct/update the editor. The comparison reads beyond the fixed array, potentially matching garbage or accessing unrelated memory. Validate or terminate imported strings before using them as C strings. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Input Preferences GUI when importing a malformed INPT/KMSW record. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked fixed-width copies and string comparisons; no malformed file or GUI was used. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Input Preferences full-body import, editor and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#input-preferences-full-body-import-editor-and-persistence-pass).


<a id="gd14615"></a>
## GD14615 — ScreenMode Preferences accepts failed and short IFF imports [conditional]

`Prefs_ImportFH()` initializes `success` to TRUE. If `OpenIFF()` fails, its branch leaves that value unchanged; if `ReadChunkBytes()` returns a negative error, the code prints a message but likewise leaves success TRUE. Any nonnegative read count, including a short record, is treated as success and the zero-initialized record is copied into global preferences (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/prefs.c:52-117`). The GUI import method then updates the gadgets on that success result (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/smeditor.c:207-224`).

**Trigger and consequence:** import an unreadable IFF stream or an `SCRM` chunk shorter than `ScreenModePrefs`. The editor accepts the import and applies stale/default or partly zeroed settings instead of rejecting it or allowing fallback. Mark every open/read/short-record failure as failure and validate the record size. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable ScreenMode Preferences GUI and CLI import (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/mmakefile.src:4-14`). **Confidence:** high for return-path handling; no malformed file was used. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [ScreenMode Preferences full-body selector, editor and IFF pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#screenmode-preferences-full-body-selector-editor-and-iff-pass).

<a id="gd14616"></a>
## GD14616 — ScreenMode Preferences reports success after IFF chunk writes fail [conditional]

`Prefs_ExportFH()` initializes `success` to TRUE and checks `PushChunk()` results only to decide subsequent control flow. It ignores the `WriteChunkBytes()` and `PopChunk()` results for both `PRHD` and `SCRM`, and only changes `success` for `OpenIFF()` or `AllocIFF()` failure (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/prefs.c:122-198`). The GUI export method returns the helper result; CLI callers also ignore it (`smeditor.c:226-238`; `prefs.c:231-257`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an IFF chunk write or finalization fails after the output is opened. Export can report success with a truncated/incomplete screen-mode preference file, and CLI Use/Save suppresses the helper failure as well. Propagate every write/pop/finalization failure and check the CLI close result. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable ScreenMode Preferences GUI or CLI Use/Save (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/mmakefile.src:4-14`). **Confidence:** high for discarded result paths; no IFF operation or build was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [ScreenMode Preferences full-body selector, editor and IFF pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#screenmode-preferences-full-body-selector-editor-and-iff-pass).

<a id="gd14617"></a>
## GD14617 — ScreenMode Preferences indexes the mode array with an inactive-list value [conditional]

The active-selection notification calls `SelectFunc()` for every `MUIA_List_Active` change, and the hook directly indexes `ids_array` by that value without checking for `MUIV_List_Active_Off` (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/smselector.c:41-55,168-169`). The off value is -1 (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.h:270-274`). The selector's custom OM_GET methods likewise index both arrays directly by the active value (`smselector.c:251-265`). The editor explicitly sets the list active value to off in its Set Defaults method (`smeditor.c:476-490`).

**Trigger and consequence:** clear the mode selection or use Set Defaults. The selection hook reads before the allocated ID array; a later Mode/Active attribute query can also index before the arrays. Guard inactive selection and return an explicit invalid mode value. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable ScreenMode Preferences GUI. **Confidence:** high for the -1 value, callback registration, unguarded indexing and selected off-setting caller; no GUI operation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [ScreenMode Preferences full-body selector, editor and IFF pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#screenmode-preferences-full-body-selector-editor-and-iff-pass).

<a id="gd14618"></a>
## GD14618 — ScreenMode test leaks its temporary RastPort on every successful test [conditional]

The Test method allocates a RastPort with `CreateRastPort()`, attaches the test screen bitmap, draws the preview and closes the screen, but never calls `FreeRastPort()` (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/smeditor.c:320-347,462-465`). The selected `CreateRastPort()` implementation allocates the RastPort with `AllocMem()`, and `FreeRastPort()` releases it (`rom/intuition/misc.c:131-142,161-170`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run the screen-mode Test action successfully. Each test leaves a RastPort allocation behind; repeated tests accumulate leaked memory. Free the temporary RastPort on every path after it is created. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable ScreenMode Preferences GUI when Test opens a screen. **Confidence:** high for the selected allocation/free contract and missing cleanup; no test screen was opened. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [ScreenMode Preferences full-body selector, editor and IFF pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#screenmode-preferences-full-body-selector-editor-and-iff-pass).

<a id="gd14619"></a>
## GD14619 — ScreenMode test dereferences a failed RastPort allocation [conditional]

After opening the test screen, the Test method calls `CreateRastPort()` and immediately writes `rp->BitMap` without checking whether allocation returned NULL (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/smeditor.c:320-347`). The selected implementation returns NULL when its `AllocMem()` fails (`rom/intuition/misc.c:131-142`).

**Trigger and consequence:** memory allocation fails while the Test action is opening a valid mode. The preferences process dereferences NULL instead of abandoning/cleaning up the test screen and timer resources. Check the allocation and use the normal cleanup path. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable ScreenMode Preferences GUI under memory pressure during Test. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation and NULL-return contract; no allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [ScreenMode Preferences full-body selector, editor and IFF pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#screenmode-preferences-full-body-selector-editor-and-iff-pass).

<a id="gd14620"></a>
## GD14620 — ScreenMode selector allocation failure dispatches disposal before object construction [conditional]

`ScreenModeSelector__OM_NEW()` allocates its arrays before constructing the BOOPSI object, but its allocation-failure path calls `CoerceMethod(CLASS, self, OM_DISPOSE)` (`workbench/prefs/screenmode/smselector.c:102-111,178-180`). At that point `self` is still the incoming, unconstructed object pointer. `ScreenModeSelector__OM_DISPOSE()` immediately reads instance data from `self` (`smselector.c:183-200`). If the ID-array allocation fails after the mode array succeeds, the allocated mode array also has not been attached to instance data and cannot be freed by that disposer.

**Trigger and consequence:** either pre-object array allocation fails while constructing the selector. The error path invokes disposal with no initialized instance data and may fault; when the second allocation fails, the first allocation is leaked as well. Release local allocations directly before returning, and dispatch disposal only after an object exists. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable ScreenMode Preferences GUI under allocation failure. **Confidence:** high for allocation/disposal ordering; no allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [ScreenMode Preferences full-body selector, editor and IFF pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#screenmode-preferences-full-body-selector-editor-and-iff-pass).


<a id="gd14621"></a>
## GD14621 — Serial Preferences defaults encode eight data bits as an invalid value [conditional]

`Prefs_Default()` sets `sp_BitsPerChar` to 8 and `sp_StopBits` to 1 (`workbench/prefs/serial/prefs.c:306-319`). The selected IPrefs consumer interprets these fields as offsets: it logs `8 - sp_BitsPerChar` data bits and `1 + sp_StopBits` stop bits, then packs the raw fields into the system preferences nibble fields (`workbench/c/iprefs/serialprefs.c:62-72`; the system preference contract documents those encodings in `compiler/include/intuition/preferences.h:94-100`). The serial CLI fallback calls `Prefs_Default()` when neither ENV nor ENVARC settings can be loaded, then exports those values on USE/SAVE (`prefs.c:259-301`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run Serial Preferences CLI USE/SAVE with no readable existing serial preference file. The fallback writes 8 and 1 as encoded values, which IPrefs interprets as zero data bits and two stop bits rather than the intended defaults of eight data bits and one stop bit. Set defaults using the encoded values (0 and 0). **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-prefs-serial` CLI fallback path; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/prefs/serial/mmakefile.src:4-12`). **Confidence:** high for the field encodings, defaults and CLI path; no preferences file or serial device was used. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Serial Preferences full-body editor and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#serial-preferences-full-body-editor-and-persistence-pass).

<a id="gd14622"></a>
## GD14622 — Serial Preferences reports export success despite IFF finalization failures [conditional]

`Prefs_ExportFH()` checks the exact byte count for the preference-data chunk but discards the `PRHD` write result and all `PopChunk()` results; it also cannot report `CloseIFF()` finalization errors. It returns TRUE once the `SERL` data write succeeds (`workbench/prefs/serial/prefs.c:180-242`). The GUI export method propagates that helper result, while CLI callers ignore both export and DOS `Close()` results (`sereditor.c:293-307`; `prefs.c:275-301`).

**Trigger and consequence:** export when the header write, chunk/FORM finalization or destination-file close fails after the `SERL` payload is written. GUI or CLI Use/Save can report success with a malformed or incomplete preference file. Check header writes and chunk pops, expose finalization status, and check CLI export/close results. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Serial Preferences GUI or CLI Use/Save (`workbench/prefs/serial/mmakefile.src:4-12`). **Confidence:** high for discarded result paths; no IFF operation or build was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Serial Preferences full-body editor and persistence pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#serial-preferences-full-body-editor-and-persistence-pass).


<a id="gd14623"></a>
## GD14623 — Palette Preferences rejects legacy ILBM CMAP imports after reading them [conditional]

`Prefs_ImportFH()` has a legacy `ID_ILBM:ID_CMAP` branch that reads color registers into `paletteprefs.pap_Colors`, but never sets its return value `retval` to TRUE (`workbench/prefs/palette/prefs.c:151-186`). The editor only calls `PalPrefs2Gadgets()` when that result is true (`workbench/prefs/palette/paleditor.c:307-321`).

**Trigger and consequence:** import an ILBM file with a CMAP chunk through the Palette Preferences editor. Colors are copied into the global preference state, but the import is reported as failed and the editor leaves the displayed palette unchanged. Mark a successfully parsed CMAP as success before returning. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Palette Preferences GUI (`workbench/prefs/palette/mmakefile.src:4-16`). **Confidence:** high for the copied data, false return and guarded caller; no ILBM file was imported. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Palette Preferences full-body editor, import/export and color ownership pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#palette-preferences-full-body-editor-import-export-and-color-ownership-pass).

<a id="gd14624"></a>
## GD14624 — Palette Preferences reads outside its three-channel RGB array when refreshing a selection [conditional]

When `PEPalette__OM_SET()` handles updated palette entries, it stores the selected red, green and blue values in `data->rgb[0..2]`, but then uses the active palette-list index as the subscript for all three color-adjustment attributes (`workbench/prefs/palette/palette.c:392-421`). The active index is only bounded by `data->numentries`, which is the number of entries in the supplied palette array (`palette.c:347-350`). `PalPrefs2Gadgets()` sends this setter on imported or default palette updates (`paleditor.c:283-304,307-321,350-361`).

**Trigger and consequence:** refresh palette entries while the selected pen-list row is 3 or higher. The code reads past `rgb[3]` and supplies the same out-of-range value for red, green and blue; the color-adjustment display can be corrupted and the read can extend into adjacent instance fields. Use fixed channel indices 0, 1 and 2. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Palette Preferences GUI after selecting a later pen row and importing or restoring defaults. **Confidence:** high for the array size, active-index range and setter caller; no GUI operation was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Palette Preferences full-body editor, import/export and color ownership pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#palette-preferences-full-body-editor-import-export-and-color-ownership-pass).

<a id="gd14625"></a>
## GD14625 — Palette Preferences can dereference an uninitialized color-field pointer after setup [conditional]

`PEPalette__OM_NEW()` allocates `colorfieldentries` with `AllocMem(MEMF_ANY)` and does not initialize the pointer slots. `PEPalette__MUIM_Setup()` fills only the slots for the color fields it creates (four on a 2-bit screen, eight on a deeper screen). Later, `PEPalette__OM_SET()` checks up to eight slots and calls `NNSET()` on every non-NULL value (`workbench/prefs/palette/palette.c:347-360,392-408,497-548,600-607`). The screen setup chooses the four- or eight-field count based on bitmap depth (`palette.c:363-389`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on a 2-bit-or-lower screen, Palette Preferences receives a `MUIA_Palette_Entries` update after setup, as happens when the editor imports or restores preferences. Slots 4–7 were never initialized or assigned, so random pointer contents can be passed to `NNSET()`. Clear the pointer array and bound refreshes to the number of created fields. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Palette Preferences GUI on a low-depth screen. **Confidence:** high for allocation/initialization and refresh bounds; no low-depth GUI was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Palette Preferences full-body editor, import/export and color ownership pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#palette-preferences-full-body-editor-import-export-and-color-ownership-pass).

<a id="gd14626"></a>
## GD14626 — Palette Preferences crashes if it cannot allocate the screen-color backup [conditional]

`PalEditor__MUIM_Setup()` records a nonzero ColorMap count, assigns `AllocVec()` to `data->origcols`, sets `restore = TRUE`, and immediately writes every saved color through the pointer without checking allocation (`workbench/prefs/palette/paleditor.c:365-391`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the Palette Preferences editor sets up on a screen with a nonempty ColorMap while the backup allocation fails. Setup writes through NULL and can fault instead of continuing without a preview backup or returning a setup failure. Check the allocation before filling the backup and restore only when it exists. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Palette Preferences GUI under memory pressure. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation and write loop; no allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Palette Preferences full-body editor, import/export and color ownership pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#palette-preferences-full-body-editor-import-export-and-color-ownership-pass).

<a id="gd14627"></a>
## GD14627 — Palette Preferences leaks pen-map buffers when its editor is disposed [conditional]

`PalEditor__OM_NEW()` allocates `penmap4` and `penmap8` and stores them in instance data on successful object construction (`workbench/prefs/palette/paleditor.c:187-199,231-239`). `PalEditor__OM_DISPOSE()` frees `data->pens` but never frees either pen-map allocation (`paleditor.c:255-261`).

**Trigger and consequence:** dispose a successfully constructed Palette Preferences editor. Both `MAXPENS`-sized pen-map allocations remain allocated. Free the two buffers in the editor's disposal path. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Palette Preferences GUI. **Confidence:** high for allocation and disposal ownership; no GUI lifecycle was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Palette Preferences full-body editor, import/export and color ownership pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#palette-preferences-full-body-editor-import-export-and-color-ownership-pass).

<a id="gd14628"></a>
## GD14628 — Palette Preferences leaks its color-field pointer table on disposal [conditional]

`PEPalette__OM_NEW()` allocates `data->colorfieldentries` to track the created color-field objects (`workbench/prefs/palette/palette.c:355-362`). `PEPalette__OM_DISPOSE()` only delegates to the superclass and never frees that table (`palette.c:472-474`).

**Trigger and consequence:** dispose the custom palette editor object after it has been constructed. The pointer table remains allocated for the life of the process. Free the table during disposal. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Palette Preferences GUI. **Confidence:** high for the allocation and missing release; no GUI lifecycle was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Palette Preferences full-body editor, import/export and color ownership pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#palette-preferences-full-body-editor-import-export-and-color-ownership-pass).

<a id="gd14629"></a>
## GD14629 — Palette Preferences export hides IFF finalization and CLI write failures [conditional]

`Prefs_ExportFH()` sets success after writing the PALT payload but discards every `PopChunk()` result and the `CloseIFF()` finalization status (`workbench/prefs/palette/prefs.c:266-305`). `Prefs_HandleArgs()` also ignores both `Prefs_ExportFH()` and DOS `Close()` results for ENV and ENVARC output, then returns TRUE (`prefs.c:338-364`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an IFF chunk/FORM finalization or destination flush fails after opening the output. GUI export can report success after incomplete finalization, and CLI Use/Save suppresses detected helper and close failures. Propagate IFF finalization status and check CLI export/close results. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Palette Preferences GUI or CLI Use/Save (`workbench/prefs/palette/mmakefile.src:4-16`). **Confidence:** high for unchecked paths; no write or build was run. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Palette Preferences full-body editor, import/export and color ownership pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#palette-preferences-full-body-editor-import-export-and-color-ownership-pass).


<a id="gd14631"></a>
## GD14631 — Appearance theme import accepts a theme-name prefix as a different theme [conditional]

`AppearanceEditor__MUIM_PrefsEditor_ImportFH()` compares each available theme name against the imported path's final component using `strncmp(themeName, tmpThemeFile, strlen(themeName))` (`workbench/prefs/appearance/appearanceeditor.c:644-659`). It does not require the imported component to end at the same position, so a shorter available theme matches a longer imported name sharing its prefix. The loop stops on that first match and selects it.

**Trigger and consequence:** import a theme path whose final component begins with an installed theme name but has additional characters, where the shorter theme sorts first in enumeration. The editor silently selects the shorter, wrong theme and derives its option files and preview from that selection. Compare complete names (and account for any intended suffix) before accepting a match. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Appearance Preferences GUI importing a `theme.var` path with an ambiguous prefix. **Confidence:** high for the prefix comparison and immediate selection; no preference file was imported. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Appearance Preferences full-body editor and preview pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#appearance-preferences-full-body-editor-and-preview-pass).


<a id="gd14635"></a>
## GD14635 — Pointer Preferences negates unsigned hotspot coordinates in the editor [confirmed]

`NewPointerPrefs.npp_X` and `npp_Y` are documented as unsigned hotspot coordinates (`compiler/include/prefs/pointer.h:49-55`), and the selected IPrefs consumer passes the decoded values directly to `LoadPointerFile()` and then `InstallBitMap()` (`workbench/c/iprefs/pointerprefs.c:96-127,161-171`). The editor negates those values when populating the preview (`workbench/prefs/pointer/pteditor.c:69-78,235-248`), where the preview stores them in `UWORD` fields and only draws hotspot guides when each value is less than the bitmap dimension (`ppreview.c:31-34,197-210,405-426`). When a user clicks to choose a hotspot, the preview stores the positive mouse-relative coordinates, but `StoreEntry()` negates them before writing the unsigned preference fields (`pteditor.c:212-222`).

**Trigger and consequence:** open Pointer Preferences with a nonzero imported hotspot, or click to set a hotspot. Imported coordinates wrap to large unsigned values and the preview omits the guides; clicked coordinates are saved as `0 - coordinate` modulo 65,536, so IPrefs later installs the pointer with a different hotspot. Pass positive coordinates through the editor and store them without negation. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Pointer Preferences GUI and its exported `NPTR` records. **Confidence:** high for the declared unsigned fields, preview bounds check, editor conversions and selected consumer; no GUI or pointer settings were changed. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Pointer Preferences hotspot sign and imported-name recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#pointer-preferences-hotspot-sign-and-imported-name-recheck).


<a id="gd14636"></a>
## GD14636 — Pointer Preferences can read past a full-width imported filename [conditional]

`Prefs_ImportFH()` zeroes a fixed `ExtPointerPrefs` stack record, reads up to its full `filename[NAMEBUFLEN]` member from an `NPTR` chunk, and passes that member to `Strlcpy()` without first checking for a NUL within the member (`workbench/prefs/pointer/prefs.c:67-109`; `prefs.h:14-25`). The selected `Strlcpy()` implementation copies up to the destination limit and then scans the rest of the source until it finds a NUL (`rom/utility/strlcpy.c:80-102`). A chunk with a complete 1,024-byte non-NUL filename therefore makes that scan continue beyond the stack record.

**Trigger and consequence:** import an `NPTR` chunk whose filename occupies all 1,024 available bytes without a terminator. `Strlcpy()` reads adjacent stack memory while searching for the end of the source string, with behavior depending on the bytes beyond the record. Validate/terminate the chunk filename within its recorded size before treating it as a C string. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Pointer Preferences GUI importing a crafted or malformed `NPTR` record. **Confidence:** high for the fixed field, missing validation and selected `Strlcpy()` scan; no IFF file was imported. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Pointer Preferences hotspot sign and imported-name recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#pointer-preferences-hotspot-sign-and-imported-name-recheck).


<a id="gd14637"></a>
## GD14637 — Appearance theme description without a newline dereferences NULL [conditional]

The theme description readers call `strstr(buffer, "\n")` but do not check whether it found a newline before passing `&line2[1]` to the second text gadget (`workbench/prefs/appearance/appearanceeditor.c:183-190,696-703,1149-1156`). A nonempty EOF-terminated description can therefore leave `line2 == NULL` and form a pointer from NULL.

**Trigger and consequence:** select, import or restore a theme whose nonempty `Description` has no newline. The callback forms an invalid second-line pointer while updating the UI and may fault. Check for a newline and use an empty second line when absent. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Appearance Preferences GUI with such a theme description. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked search result and all three callers; no theme file or GUI was used. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Appearance Preferences full-body editor and preview pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#appearance-preferences-full-body-editor-and-preview-pass).


<a id="gd14638"></a>
## GD14638 — Editor Preferences trusts file-provided field lengths while loading preference records [conditional]

`load_prefs()` allocates the complete `JANO` payload, then walks records using a one-byte field ID and one-byte length. It checks only that the field ID is below `MAX_NUMFIELD`; it does not require two bytes to remain for the record header, constrain the payload length to the remaining chunk, or clamp it to the destination field's declared size (`workbench/tools/Edit/Prefs.c:208-227`). For variable-size `wordssep`, the destination is the fixed `WordsSep[MAX_SPLIT]` array (40 bytes), but a file record can request up to 255 bytes (`Prefs.c:64-75,223-226`; `Prefs.h:65`).

**Trigger and consequence:** import a malformed `JANO` preference chunk with an oversized field length, truncated record header/payload, or an oversized `wordssep` field. The parser reads past the chunk or writes past a fixed field, corrupting state and potentially adjacent memory. Validate each complete record against the remaining chunk and the destination capacity before copying. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Editor Preferences loading an externally edited or damaged preference file. **Confidence:** high for the missing bounds checks and fixed destination sizes; no file was loaded. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Editor Preferences selected-source and shared serializer pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-preferences-selected-source-and-shared-serializer-pass).


<a id="gd14647"></a>
## GD14647 — Vulkan loader reports zero process memory use for every memory-budget query

The loader handles `VkPhysicalDeviceMemoryBudgetPropertiesEXT` itself while servicing `vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties2()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/vulkan_loader.c:463-492`). For every heap it writes `heapBudget[i]` as the physical heap size and unconditionally writes `heapUsage[i] = 0`; it has no accounting path from the driver or Vulkan memory allocations. The HIDD callback interface exposes only base physical-device memory properties for this query (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan_hidd.h`; `vulkan_class.c:100-107`), so this loader shim cannot obtain the current process's memory use from the provider.

**Trigger and consequence:** a client queries the EXT memory-budget structure after allocating device memory. It receives zero usage regardless of allocations, and a budget equal to the full heap size; software using these values to choose allocation sizes can overestimate available VRAM and make allocation decisions that fail or cause avoidable pressure. Return provider-backed accounting, or do not advertise/serve the extension structure with fabricated values. **Affected configuration:** clients using the in-tree Vulkan loader's `VK_EXT_memory_budget` output-chain shim with a provider that reports physical memory heaps. **Confidence:** high that the shim returns these constants and that its callback path contains no accounting; no allocation or query was run, and the downstream allocation effect depends on client policy. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Graphics/Desktop Vulkan loader and consumer pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-loader-consumer-pass).


<a id="gd14639"></a>
## GD14639 — Editor Preferences leaks the DOS file handle when OpenIFF fails [conditional]

`open_prefs()` opens a DOS file, stores its handle in `iff_Stream`, and returns the IFF handle only if `OpenIFF()` succeeds. If `OpenIFF()` fails, it calls `FreeIFF()` without closing the already-open DOS stream (`workbench/tools/Edit/Prefs.c:145-179`). The common `close_prefs()` path does close that stream, but the failed-open path bypasses it (`:182-188`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a DOS file opens successfully but `OpenIFF()` rejects the stream, such as an unsupported/truncated IFF header, or IFF setup fails after Open. Repeated attempts retain one DOS file handle each for the process lifetime. Close the stream on every `OpenIFF()` failure. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Editor Preferences loading or saving a file. **Confidence:** high for the open/cleanup ordering; no IFF error was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Editor Preferences selected-source and shared serializer pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-preferences-selected-source-and-shared-serializer-pass).


<a id="gd14640"></a>
## GD14640 — Editor Preferences reports Save success after serialization or finalization fails [conditional]

`save_prefs()` checks `PushChunk()` and each pair of `WriteChunkBytes()` calls only to break the record loop; it ignores `PopChunk()` and `CloseIFF()` results and returns zero unconditionally (`workbench/tools/Edit/Prefs.c:266-306`). The Save gadget and keyboard shortcut call it without checking a result (`workbench/prefs/Editor/JanoPrefs.c:365-368,407-411`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a preference save encounters a chunk push/pop, short write, or finalization error. The method returns the same zero value as a successful save, and its GUI callers do not display a failure; the selected file can be partial or malformed. Propagate serialization and close errors and have callers report failure. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Editor Preferences during Save or Save As. **Confidence:** high for discarded results and return value; no file error was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Editor Preferences selected-source and shared serializer pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-preferences-selected-source-and-shared-serializer-pass).


<a id="gd14641"></a>
## GD14641 — Editor Preferences sample drawing discards and fails to restore the previous layer clip region [conditional]

`clipWindow()` returns the region it displaced when installing the sample's clipping rectangle (`workbench/prefs/Editor/SampleEd.c:52-80`). `render_sample()` discards that return value (`:135-142`); `unclipWindow()` then installs NULL and disposes the currently installed region instead of reinstalling the displaced region (`:36-45,171`). The selected `InstallClipRegion()` contract returns the old region to the caller, transfers the supplied region, and requires callers to manage region lifetime (`rom/hyperlayers/installclipregion.c:21-33,60-67`).

**Trigger and consequence:** render the preview while the window layer already has a non-NULL clip region installed. The previous region is detached and lost rather than restored, and its allocation is not released; subsequent drawing uses the wrong clipping state. Preserve the displaced region and reinstall it after rendering, or dispose it when replacement is intentional. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Editor Preferences when preview drawing overlaps an existing layer clip region. **Confidence:** high for the local API ownership contract and discarded return; no non-NULL prior region was installed. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Editor Preferences selected-source and shared serializer pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-preferences-selected-source-and-shared-serializer-pass).


<a id="gd14642"></a>
## GD14642 — Editor Preferences dereferences failed GadTools context and gadget allocations [conditional]

After opening the window, `setup_guipref()` does not check `CreateContext()` before building the gadget list. It also dereferences the first two `CreateGadgetA()` results through `GetSI(gad)->Buffer`, dereferences checkbox gadgets through `gad->Flags`, and continues creating later gadgets without checking their results (`workbench/prefs/Editor/JanoPrefs.c:238-322`).

**Trigger and consequence:** GadTools allocation fails during window setup. The code dereferences NULL and may fault instead of abandoning the partially built window and releasing its resources. Check each constructor and unwind the already-created GUI objects. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable Editor Preferences under memory pressure. **Confidence:** high for unchecked return/use paths; no allocation failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Editor Preferences selected-source and shared serializer pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-preferences-selected-source-and-shared-serializer-pass).

<a id="gd14643"></a>
## GD14643 — Vulkan-Hpp parallel-array setters can desynchronize shared counts [conditional]

`SemaphoreWaitInfo::setSemaphores()` sets the shared `semaphoreCount` from the semaphore proxy and updates only `pSemaphores`; `setValues()` independently overwrites that count from the values proxy and updates only `pValues` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:148911-148915,148926-148930`). The core and KHR enhanced `Device::waitSemaphores()` overloads forward the resulting structure to Vulkan (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:7182-7190,20231-20239`; RAII `vulkan_raii.hpp:17446-17455`). Vulkan requires both pointers to reference arrays of `semaphoreCount` elements ([official `VkSemaphoreWaitInfo` reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkSemaphoreWaitInfo.html)).

`SubmitInfo::setWaitSemaphores()` and `setWaitDstStageMask()` likewise each update shared `waitSemaphoreCount` from one proxy while changing only the corresponding pointer (`vulkan_structs.hpp:151155-151175`). `Queue::submit()` forwards the record to `vkQueueSubmit()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:928-936`), and Vulkan requires both arrays to match `waitSemaphoreCount` ([official `VkSubmitInfo` reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkSubmitInfo.html)).

`SetDescriptorBufferOffsetsInfoEXT::setBufferIndices()` and `setOffsets()` have the same defect: each independently sets shared `setCount` from its proxy and updates only its own pointer (`vulkan_structs.hpp:149115-149119,149130-149134`). The enhanced `CommandBuffer::setDescriptorBufferOffsets2EXT()` forwards that structure to the native command (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:30801-30809`; RAII forwarding at `vulkan_raii.hpp:27580-27587`). The Vulkan contract requires both arrays to contain `setCount` entries ([official `VkSetDescriptorBufferOffsetsInfoEXT` reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkSetDescriptorBufferOffsetsInfoEXT.html)).

`VideoDecodeAV1PictureInfoKHR::setTileOffsets()` and `setTileSizes()` likewise each overwrite shared `tileCount` while retaining the other pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:159929-159949`). `CommandBuffer::decodeVideoKHR()` forwards its `VideoDecodeInfoKHR` to Vulkan (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:11919-11931`), and the AV1 picture info can be carried in that structure’s `pNext` chain. Vulkan defines `tileCount` as the extent of both arrays ([official `VkVideoDecodeAV1PictureInfoKHR` reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkVideoDecodeAV1PictureInfoKHR.html)).

`PresentInfoKHR::setSwapchains()`, `setImageIndices()`, and `setResults()` independently overwrite the shared `swapchainCount` while changing only one pointer (`vulkan_structs.hpp:135085-135255`). The enhanced `Queue::presentKHR()` forwards the structure to `vkQueuePresentKHR()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:9555-9578`). Vulkan defines the same count for the swapchain and image-index arrays, and for the optional results array when non-null ([official `VkPresentInfoKHR` reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPresentInfoKHR.html)).

`SwapchainTimeDomainPropertiesEXT::setTimeDomains()` and `setTimeDomainIds()` also independently update shared `timeDomainCount` while changing only their respective pointer (`vulkan_structs.hpp:155693-155760`). `Device::getSwapchainTimeDomainPropertiesEXT()` forwards the structure to Vulkan (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:20347-20365`); Vulkan requires both arrays to follow the same count and both pointers to be null or non-null together ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkSwapchainTimeDomainPropertiesEXT.html)). This overlaps GD14644’s separate constructor case, where the enhanced constructor accepts mismatched empty/nonempty proxies.

`TensorCopyARM::setSrcOffset()`, `setDstOffset()`, and `setExtent()` similarly each rewrite shared `dimensionCount` and only their own pointer (`vulkan_structs.hpp:26740-26905`). The enhanced `CommandBuffer::copyTensorARM()` forwards a containing region to Vulkan (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:27473-27490`); `dimensionCount` is the extent of each non-null array ([official `VkTensorCopyARM` reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkTensorCopyARM.html)). `TensorDescriptionARM::setDimensions()` and `setStrides()` also each rewrite `dimensionCount` independently (`vulkan_structs.hpp:42491-42635`). A description is forwarded through `TensorCreateInfoARM` to `Device::createTensorARM()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:27126-27157`); when `pStrides` is non-null it must have `dimensionCount` elements ([official `VkTensorDescriptionARM` reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkTensorDescriptionARM.html)).

`IndirectCommandsLayoutTokenNV::setIndexTypes()` and `setIndexTypeValues()` share `indexTypeCount` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:65988-66195`); its enhanced constructor checks equal lengths, and the structure is passed through `Device::createIndirectCommandsLayoutNV()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:22807-22835`). Vulkan requires both arrays to use the shared count ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkIndirectCommandsLayoutTokenNV.html)). `IndirectExecutionSetShaderInfoEXT::setInitialShaders()` and `setSetLayoutInfos()` do the same to `shaderCount` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:66760-66875`); the record is passed through `Device::createIndirectExecutionSetEXT()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:31507-31535`). Vulkan requires `pInitialShaders` and any non-null `pSetLayoutInfos` array to have that count ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkIndirectExecutionSetShaderInfoEXT.html)).

`PipelineBinaryKeysAndDataKHR::setPipelineBinaryKeys()` and `setPipelineBinaryData()` independently rewrite `binaryCount` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:127319-127425`). `PipelineBinaryCreateInfoKHR` can carry that record into `Device::createPipelineBinariesKHR()` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:127556-127680`; `vulkan_funcs.hpp:28562-28621`). Vulkan defines `binaryCount` as the size of both arrays ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPipelineBinaryKeysAndDataKHR.html)).

The platform-gated `Win32KeyedMutexAcquireReleaseInfoKHR` and `Win32KeyedMutexAcquireReleaseInfoNV` repeat the pattern: their acquire-array setters independently overwrite shared `acquireCount` for the sync, key, and timeout arrays; their release sync/key setters independently overwrite `releaseCount` (`vulkan_structs.hpp:173752-173816,173803-173833,174026-174110`). Both structures extend `VkSubmitInfo` and are forwarded by `Queue::submit()`. The official Vulkan references define the shared array extents ([KHR](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkWin32KeyedMutexAcquireReleaseInfoKHR.html), [NV](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkWin32KeyedMutexAcquireReleaseInfoNV.html)).

**Trigger and consequence:** after constructing one of these records with matching arrays, call one setter with a proxy of a different length from its paired retained array, then pass it to the matching API: `Device::waitSemaphores()`, `Queue::submit()`, the descriptor-offset command, AV1 decode (picture info in the decode info chain), `Queue::presentKHR()`, swapchain time-domain query, ARM tensor copy/create, indirect-command layout or execution-set creation, or pipeline-binary creation. For Win32 keyed-mutex records, attach the structure to `VkSubmitInfo`'s pNext chain. The last setter determines the count while the other pointer retains its old extent. This violates the native array contract and can make the Vulkan operation fail or process the wrong array entries. Keep paired proxies equal in length and prevent setter sequences from desynchronizing their shared count. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp enhanced or RAII API using `VkSemaphoreWaitInfo`, `VkSubmitInfo`, AV1 video decode, `VK_KHR_swapchain`, `VK_EXT_present_timing`, `VK_ARM_tensors`, `VK_NV_device_generated_commands`, `VK_EXT_device_generated_commands`, `VK_KHR_pipeline_binary`, `VK_KHR_maintenance6` with `VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer`, or Win32 builds with `VK_KHR_win32_keyed_mutex`/`VK_NV_win32_keyed_mutex`; no in-tree C++ caller of these generated APIs was found. **Confidence:** high for count/pointer mutation and native forwarding; no Vulkan call or malformed structure was exercised. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Vulkan-Hpp shared-count setter census](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-shared-count-setter-census-gd14643).

<a id="gd14644"></a>
### GD14644 withdrawn — duplicate of GD10257

GD14644 described the constructor-side null/non-null output-array mismatch in `SwapchainTimeDomainPropertiesEXT`. That case is now included with the shared-count setter mismatch and unequal-capacity constructor case under canonical GD10257; no separate finding is retained. The source review and trigger details remain in GD10257.

<a id="gd14645"></a>
## GD14645 — Vulkan-Hpp enhanced setters can retain mutually exclusive array pointers [conditional]

Several generated structures support two mutually exclusive native pointer representations for the same array. `AccelerationStructureBuildGeometryInfoKHR::setGeometries()` fills `pGeometries` and the shared count, while `setPGeometries(ArrayProxy<...>)` fills `ppGeometries` and the count; neither clears the alternate pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:802-970`). The enhanced constructor explicitly rejects having both proxies nonempty, but a later setter bypasses that check. Vulkan requires exactly one of the two pointers to be valid when the geometry count is nonzero ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkAccelerationStructureBuildGeometryInfoKHR.html)); `CommandBuffer::buildAccelerationStructuresKHR()` forwards the structure to the driver (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:17299-17315`).

The same setter pattern occurs in `MicromapBuildInfoEXT` and the `AccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV` and `AccelerationStructureTrianglesOpacityMicromapEXT` pNext records: `setUsageCounts(ArrayProxy<...>)` fills `pUsageCounts`, while the pointer-array overload `setPUsageCounts(ArrayProxy<...>)` fills `ppUsageCounts`; the setter does not clear the alternate member (`vulkan_structs.hpp:4519-4785,4864-5035,72002-72160`). Vulkan specifies that only one of `pUsageCounts` and `ppUsageCounts` may be valid in each record ([`VkMicromapBuildInfoEXT`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkMicromapBuildInfoEXT.html), [`VkAccelerationStructureTrianglesOpacityMicromapEXT`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkAccelerationStructureTrianglesOpacityMicromapEXT.html), [`VkAccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkAccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV.html)). Micromap build info is forwarded by `CommandBuffer::buildMicromapsEXT()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:25692-25710`); the triangle pNext records are consumed through the acceleration-structure build path above.

**Trigger and consequence:** construct one of these records using one pointer representation, then call the enhanced setter for the alternate representation without first clearing the original. Both native pointers remain non-null, violating the Vulkan contract; implementations may reject the structure or interpret it inconsistently. Each representation setter should clear its alternate pointer. **Affected configuration:** optional Vulkan-Hpp enhanced/RAII consumers using acceleration structures, opacity/displacement micromaps, or micromap builds. No in-tree C++ caller of these generated APIs was found. **Confidence:** high for setter behavior, native structure layout, and official pointer exclusivity; no Vulkan build or runtime operation was performed. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Vulkan-Hpp mutually exclusive array representation review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-exclusive-array-representation-setters-gd14645).

<a id="gd14646"></a>
## GD14646 — Vulkan-Hpp TensorCopyARM constructor permits non-null arrays with zero dimensions [conditional]

The enhanced `TensorCopyARM` constructor derives `dimensionCount` only from `srcOffset_`, but its size checks intentionally skip comparisons when either input is empty. It therefore accepts an empty `srcOffset_` together with a nonempty `dstOffset_` and/or `extent_`, leaving `dimensionCount == 0` while one or more corresponding pointers are non-null (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:26768-26799`). Vulkan requires `dimensionCount` to be greater than zero whenever any of those pointers is non-null ([official `VkTensorCopyARM` reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkTensorCopyARM.html)). `CommandBuffer::copyTensorARM()` forwards a containing `CopyTensorInfoARM` to the native command (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:27482-27490`).

**Trigger and consequence:** construct `TensorCopyARM` with an empty source-offset proxy and a nonempty destination-offset or extent proxy, then include it in a copy command. The resulting region violates the API's dimension-count and array-extent contract. Reject such partial proxy combinations or derive the count from a mandatory nonempty array. **Affected configuration:** optional Vulkan-Hpp enhanced API with `VK_ARM_tensors`. **Confidence:** high for constructor behavior, the specification condition, and native forwarding; no tensor-copy call was made. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [TensorCopyARM constructor and dispatch trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-tensorcopy-constructor-gd14646).
<a id="gd14648-compositor-single-bitmap-fallback-leaks-bitmap-wrapper"></a>
<a id="gd14648"></a>
## GD14648 — Compositor single-bitmap fallback leaks its allocated bitmap wrapper

`HIDDCompositorShowSingle()` switches to the requested top bitmap and disposes the old compositor display bitmap with `OOP_DisposeObject()` only (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:831-844`). The non-framebuffer display bitmap is created through `AllocBitMap()` and retained as `HIDD_BM_OBJ(tmpBM)` (`:638-648`); `AllocBitMap()` allocates a separate `struct BitMap` wrapper (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:339-377,445-475`). `FreeBitMap()` is the matching destructor: for an HIDD bitmap it disposes the HIDD object, frees an owned screen pixel table when present, and frees the wrapper (`rom/graphics/freebitmap.c:50-72`). Directly disposing the object in `HIDDCompositorShowSingle()` therefore leaks the wrapper. The regular `HIDDCompositorToggleCompositing()` cleanup retrieves `aHidd_BitMap_BMStruct` and calls `FreeBitMap()` when available (`compositor_class.c:778-803`), showing that the compositor has a wrapper-aware cleanup path.

`HIDDCompositorShowSingle()` is called when the viewport stack is cleared and when stack-node allocation fails (`compositor_class.c:1128-1140,1247-1252`). If either occurs while a non-framebuffer composed display bitmap exists, the fallback disposes its HIDD object but loses the only pointer to the allocated `BitMap` wrapper when it sets `displaybitmap = NULL`.

**Trigger and consequence:** a non-framebuffer composition bitmap is active and either the viewport stack is removed or rebuilding its node list fails. The display switches to a single bitmap, but the allocated `BitMap` wrapper remains allocated. Use the same `aHidd_BitMap_BMStruct` / `FreeBitMap()` cleanup used by the toggle path. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the optional Compositor monitor on a display without a framebuffer, followed by a screen close or stack-node allocation failure while composition is active. **Confidence:** high for allocation/destruction ownership and both selected callers; no allocation failure or screen transition was induced. Source-only.

<a id="gd14649-compositor-reuses-alpha-intermediate-bitmap-after-mode-change"></a>
<a id="gd14649"></a>
## GD14649 — Compositor reuses an alpha intermediate bitmap after a mode change

`HIDDCompositorToggleCompositing()` allocates `intermedbitmap` only when the current stack has alpha and the pointer is NULL (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/compositor_class.c:719-730`). The allocation uses the current display rectangle, depth, and mode tags. When an intermediate already exists, there is no check of its dimensions or ModeID and no replacement on a later mode change. `UpdateDisplayMode()` updates `displaymode`, `displaydepth`, and `modeschanged` when a different composition mode is selected (`workbench/devs/monitors/Compositor/displaymode.c:232-260`); Toggle handles the mode change for `displaybitmap`, but not for `intermedbitmap` (`compositor_class.c:625-641,778-795`). With alpha active, `HIDDCompositorRedrawVisibleRegions()` uses the retained intermediate as its render target and copies the full current display rectangle into the current display bitmap (`:421-422,510-540`). The generic `CopyBox` fallback does not clip that request to source bitmap bounds: its same-format chunky path forwards the full rectangle dimensions to `HIDD_BM_CopyMemBox*()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:972-1088`), whose copy implementation derives source addresses from the requested coordinates and dimensions without checking bitmap width/height (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapmemblit.c:300-342`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional compositor already has an alpha intermediate bitmap, then a replacement alpha stack or screen selects a mode requiring a larger display rectangle. The new display bitmap is created or switched for the new mode, but rendering continues through the smaller old intermediate; on the generic `CopyBox` path the full-display copy reads beyond the old intermediate's image bounds, so the displayed composition can be corrupted. A different pixel format can also make the retained target unsuitable for the new stack. Recreate the intermediate when the mode or required dimensions change, and dispose the old bitmap after the display switch. **Affected configuration:** Compositor-enabled builds when alpha composition remains active across a mode change that increases required bounds or changes pixel format, with a generic `CopyBox` implementation for the out-of-bounds read case. **Confidence:** high that the old intermediate is retained without validation and the generic copy path does not clip the requested source rectangle; occurrence requires the stated mode transition. No mode transition or display operation was run. Source-only.

<a id="gd14650-linuxfb-16-bit-directcolor-gamma-table-wraps-to-zero"></a>
## GD14650 duplicate reconciliation — covered by GD5977 (withdrawn)

**Disposition:** withdrawn as a duplicate. GD5977 already records the 16-bit `scale_size` narrowing to zero, skipped `FBIOPUTCMAP` loop, and success return; GD14650 adds no independent root cause.

In `LinuxFBDisplay__Root__New()`, DIRECTCOLOR formats enable gamma support and set `data->scale_size = 1 << bits`, where `bits` is the maximum red/green/blue channel length (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx_displayclass.c:271-310`). `scale_size` is a `UWORD` (`linuxfbgfx_display.h:22-25`). If a host reports a DIRECTCOLOR channel length of 16, the computed count 65,536 converts to zero in that field. `LinuxFBDisplay__Hidd_Display__SetGamma()` loops from zero while `i < data->scale_size`; with a zero count it performs no `FBIOPUTCMAP` calls but returns TRUE (`linuxfbgfx_displayclass.c:390-432`). The graphics HIDD exposes this method as the display's gamma capability (`linuxfbgfx_displayclass.c:311-322`).

**Trigger and consequence:** LinuxFB detects a DIRECTCOLOR framebuffer with at least one RGB channel length of 16, then a client sets gamma. The driver reports success while leaving the host gamma table unchanged. Use a count type that represents 65,536 entries and ensure its loop index can reach the count, or reject the unsupported format/gamma request. **Affected configuration:** optional LinuxFB HIDD on a host exposing a 16-bit DIRECTCOLOR component and a caller using the HIDD gamma method. **Confidence:** high for the field narrowing, empty loop, and success return; no framebuffer or gamma request was used. Source-only.

<a id="gd14651-linuxfb-32bpp-setcolors-shifts-past-int-width"></a>
## GD14651 duplicate reconciliation — covered by GD9395 (withdrawn)

**Disposition:** withdrawn as a duplicate. GD9395 already records the 32-bpp signed shift, LinuxFB `SetColors()` rejection, and ignored-return effects in pixel-table initialization and display color-map copying; GD14651 adds only a caller trace, not an independent defect.

`LinuxFBBM__Hidd_BitMap__SetColors()` checks `firstColor + numColors` against `(1 << data->bpp)` before forwarding to the superclass (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx_bitmapclass.c:45-56`). The HIDD bitmap pixel format supplies `data->bpp` from `aHidd_PixFmt_BitsPerPixel` (`:24-31`), so for a 32-bpp framebuffer the expression shifts a signed `int` by its width, which is undefined in C. The check is reached from the generic display `copy_bm_and_colmap()` path: `Display::Show()` iterates the source color map and calls `HIDD_BM_SetColors()` on the framebuffer (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:40-62,1210-1249`). With common x86 shift lowering the limit becomes 1, and valid color indices above zero are rejected before the superclass can copy the map. The generic copy helper ignores the return value, so the display update continues with an incomplete destination color map.

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional LinuxFB HIDD exposes a 32-bpp framebuffer, and `Show()` copies a source bitmap whose color map has more than one entry to that framebuffer. The range check has undefined behavior; on common x86 lowering, only the first entry is accepted, so indexed colors can be displayed incorrectly. Compare against the representable API index range without shifting by 32 (or special-case bpp values at or above the index width). **Affected configuration:** optional LinuxFB 32-bpp displays using the generic direct-framebuffer Show/copy-back path with a multi-entry source color map. **Confidence:** high for the width-matched shift and caller path; the exact result of undefined behavior depends on compiler lowering, and no framebuffer display was exercised. Source-only.

<a id="gd14652-directfb-failed-show-leaves-null-front-bitmap"></a>
<a id="gd14652"></a>
## GD14652 — Failed direct-framebuffer Show leaves a NULL front bitmap for uninstall [conditional]

In graphics.library's `display_LoadViewPorts()`, a NULL return from the display/compositor Show path falls into the “screen is empty” branch and sets `mdd->frontbm = NULL`, then returns success (`rom/graphics/graphics_display.c:552-604`). The generic framebuffer-backed `Display::Show()` can return NULL when it rejects the requested bitmap's ModeID; it returns before changing its retained `data->shownbm` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1210-1249`). On direct-framebuffer displays, an earlier successful update can have installed the framebuffer object into the old front bitmap and saved that bitmap's original fields in `mdd->bm_bak` (`graphics_display.c:452-475`). The failed Show path does not call `display_FBUninstall()` before clearing `frontbm`. Before attempting the mode change, generic `Display::Show()` also erases its software cursor (`gfx_displayclass.c:1215-1218`). If `OOP_SetAttrs()` rejects the framebuffer ModeID, the method returns without calling `cursor_SetTarget()` or `cursor_Draw()` (`:1230-1238`); `cursor_visible` remains set but `cursor_drawn` remains FALSE, so the pointer disappears until a later cursor refresh.

**Trigger and consequence:** on a direct-framebuffer display with a previously installed front bitmap, request a bitmap whose ModeID the generic Show method rejects. `display_LoadViewPorts()` sets `frontbm` to NULL but leaves `bm_bak` non-NULL and the old bitmap's framebuffer installation active. On a later successful Show, `display_LoadViewPorts()` calls `display_FBUninstall()` before assigning the new `frontbm`; uninstall takes `oldbm = mdd->frontbm` and writes the saved object/color fields through it (`graphics_display.c:478-500,576-594`). Because `oldbm` is NULL, the recovery path dereferences NULL. The current failed call may also return success to its caller despite not switching the display.

**Affected configuration:** the `frontbm`/`bm_bak` failure requires generic framebuffer-backed direct-FB with `DF_DirectFB`, a prior successful `display_FBInstall()`, and a later failed ModeID switch followed by another successful Show. The cursor consequence additionally requires the display to use the generic software cursor methods (LinuxFB does). Optional Compositor can pass the Show failure through, but is not required for the graphics.library state bug. **Confidence:** high for the retained `bm_bak`, cleared `frontbm`, and subsequent NULL dereference; occurrence requires the described sequence. Preserve/uninstall the old front bitmap on Show failure, and only call `display_FBUninstall()` when its saved front-bitmap pointer remains valid.

No mode switch, framebuffer failure, display operation, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="gd14653"></a>
<a id="gd14653-truecolor-to-palette-cache-omits-alpha"></a>
## GD14653 — Truecolor-to-palette cache omits alpha

`true_to_pal()` compares source alpha along with RGB when selecting the nearest colormap entry (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapconvertpixels.c:292-296,326-331`). `color_distance()` explicitly weights alpha differences four times more heavily (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_intern.h:396-414`). But the cached pen key contains only the top five bits of red, green, and blue (`gfx_bitmapconvertpixels.c:298-305`), so pixels with the same RGB and different alpha reuse one cached palette index. HIDD colormaps retain caller-supplied `HIDDT_Color` values, including alpha (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_colormapclass.c:234-275`), and ARGB source pixel formats provide per-pixel alpha.

**Trigger and consequence:** generic truecolor-to-palette conversion without a caller-supplied pixel LUT, using an alpha-bearing source and a destination colormap with entries whose alpha differs. A pixel caches the nearest palette index for its RGB; a later pixel with the same RGB but different alpha hits that entry without running the alpha-aware distance search. It can be written with the wrong transparency/color-map index. Intuition's pointer construction creates a palette with alpha zero for pen 0 and `PointerAlpha` for the remaining pens (`rom/intuition/pointerclass.c:132-139`), establishing an in-tree alpha-varying colormap producer. A generic caller route also exists: `PutAlphaImage()` reads a palette destination as ARGB32, blends, and sends ARGB32 back through `PutImage()`, whose non-native path reaches `true_to_pal()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:79-114,2899-2931,3098-3112`; `gfx_bitmapconvertpixels.c:575-642`). The generic software cursor uses `PutAlphaImage()` on its framebuffer target (`gfx_displayclass.c:187`), but I did not establish that the selected framebuffer colormap has alpha-varying entries; the trigger remains conditional on such a palette and an alpha-dependent nearest-entry ranking. **Affected configuration:** generic-base graphics HIDD bitmaps using the inverse palette cache (`invlut`) with alpha-aware colormaps; caller-supplied `pixlut` paths do not use this cache. **Confidence:** high for the alpha-sensitive comparison and RGB-only cache key; the wrong entry requires palette candidates whose ranking changes with alpha and an inverse-conversion call on that bitmap. Include alpha in the cache key or use a cache that preserves alpha distinctions. No bitmap conversion or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14654"></a>
## GD14654 withdrawn — contiguous `ConvertPixels()` pointer advancement is not an established contract

The implementation advances the source and destination pointers in its row-copy branch and other conversion helpers, but the checked-in method declaration specifies only `APTR *` parameters and does not say the returned positions must advance (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:545`). A source search found 16 direct in-tree calls; the selected callers and the two conversion test clients do not read the pointer variables after the call. The outputs therefore do not establish an observable defect or a documented external contract. Withdraw GD14654 from the active candidate list. No body, path, or LOC credit changed. No pixel conversion or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14655-vmwaresvga-leaks-mode-registration-tags"></a>
<a id="gd14655"></a>
## GD14655 — VMware SVGA HIDD leaks dynamic mode-registration arrays [optional target]

`VMWareSVGA_CreateSyncTags()` allocates the outer mode-tag array, then allocates a 12-entry tag array and a description string for each unique connector mode (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/vmwaresvga_hiddclass.c:114-194`). It frees the temporary `order` array, and frees a just-failed tag/string pair, but the successful mode arrays are only freed when there are no usable modes (`:225-230`). On success, `VMWareSVGA__Root__New()` passes the outer array to the display object (`:281-291`). The generic display constructor passes those tags synchronously to a new mode enumerator (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:418-445`); `register_modes()` creates one Sync object per nested tag list (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:519-550`), and the Sync constructor copies the description into its own fixed-size `description` field (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_syncclass.c:199-267`). The mode database retains the created objects, not the supplied tag arrays. Neither successful construction nor the HIDD's `Root::Dispose` frees the outer array, nested arrays, or strings.

**Trigger and consequence:** construct the optional VMware SVGA HIDD when the connector reports at least one unique mode. The HIDD permanently loses the outer tag allocation and, for every unique mode, its nested tag array and description buffer. Failed superclass/display construction after `VMWareSVGA_CreateSyncTags()` also leaves the allocations behind. This is a per-HIDD-instance leak proportional to the number of distinct display sizes. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable VMware SVGA HIDD (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/mmakefile.src:157-195`); its parent `workbench-drivers` aggregate is commented out in `workbench/mmakefile.src`, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for allocation, synchronous value-copying, and absent release paths; no module construction or expunge was run. Free the temporary tag arrays and strings after the mode enumerator has consumed them, including constructor failure paths. Source-only.


<a id="gd14656-vmwaresvga-reports-noop-gamma-support"></a>
<a id="gd14656"></a>
## GD14656 — VMware SVGA advertises gamma support but ignores gamma updates [optional target]

`VMWareSVGADisplay::Get()` reports `aHidd_Display_SupportsGamma = TRUE` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/vmwaresvga_displayclass.c:42-53`), but its `SetGamma()` method ignores the three supplied 256-entry tables and returns `TRUE` without programming the display or forwarding to the superclass (`:132-136`). The HIDD contract defines `SetGamma()`'s success result as “driver supports gamma correction” (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1721-1744`). Intuition checks `SupportsGamma` when constructing a monitor and allocates its gamma table (`rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:244-259`); its gamma-setting and default-table paths later call `HIDD_Display_SetGamma()` with the selected tables (`:1850-1874,1990-2012`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use the explicitly buildable VMware SVGA display with Intuition gamma control or an HIDD client that submits gamma tables. The capability query and method report success, but the requested gamma is ignored, so the display remains at its previous/default color response while callers treat the update as applied. **Affected configuration:** optional VMware SVGA HIDD when used by Intuition or another gamma-table client; no default-image inclusion is claimed. **Confidence:** high for the capability flag, success return, empty method body, and Intuition caller path; no VMware display or gamma update was run. Either implement the gamma table or report gamma support as false and return false. Source-only.


<a id="gd14657-vmwaresvga-onscreen-set-invalid-mode-dereferences-null-sync"></a>
<a id="gd14657"></a>
## GD14657 — VMware SVGA on-screen bitmap Set dereferences an invalid mode lookup [optional target]

`VMWareSVGAOnBM::Set()` rejects only the `vHidd_ModeID_Invalid` sentinel. For any other ModeID it calls `HIDD_DMEnum_GetMode()` but ignores the Boolean result, then passes `sync` to `OOP_GetAttr()` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/vmwaresvga_onbitmapclass.c:205-220`). The generic mode enumerator returns false and explicitly sets both outputs to NULL for an unregistered or invalid mode ID (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:1006-1036`). `OOP_GetAttr()` dispatches through `OOP_DoMethod()`, whose `OOP_OCLASS(o)` dereferences the object pointer (`rom/oop/getattr.c:58-79`; `rom/oop/include/oop.h:95-102`). The superclass bitmap setter already handles this condition by checking the GetMode result and returning FALSE (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4454-4475`), but the VMware override dereferences `sync` before it reaches that validation.

**Trigger and consequence:** call `Root::Set` on a VMware SVGA on-screen framebuffer bitmap with a `ModeID` other than the invalid sentinel that is not registered by that display's enumerator. The lookup returns NULL outputs, and the first `OOP_GetAttr(sync, ...)` dispatch dereferences NULL instead of rejecting the tag; the generic error return is never reached. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable VMware SVGA HIDD when a client submits an unsupported/stale ModeID to an on-screen bitmap. **Confidence:** high for the invalid lookup result and null-object dispatch path; no OOP Set call or display operation was run. Check `HIDD_DMEnum_GetMode()` and return FALSE before reading the Sync attributes. Source-only.


<a id="gd14658-vmwaresvga-marks-kms-ready-when-its-render-worker-cannot-run"></a>
<a id="gd14658"></a>
## GD14658 — VMware SVGA marks KMS ready when its render worker cannot run [optional target]

`VMWareSVGA_KMS_Init()` stores the result of `NewCreateTask()` in `render_task` but never checks it, then sets `ready = TRUE` and returns success (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/vmwaresvga_kms.c:463-477`). `NewCreateTaskA()` can return NULL when task creation/context setup fails (`rom/exec/newcreatetaska.c:257-261`). The task is the only caller of `VMWareSVGA_KMS_DamageFlush()` (`vmwaresvga_kms.c:238-260`); bitmap writes merely queue damage.

The worker also returns without cleaning up its successfully created message port/request if timer request allocation or `OpenDevice()` fails (`:243-249`). In either startup-failure case, KMS remains advertised ready and modes can be used, but queued screen updates are never flushed to the host; the timer setup path additionally leaks whichever timer resources were allocated.

**Trigger and scope:** optional VMware SVGA HIDD initialization when task creation fails, or when its render task cannot allocate/open the timer. **Consequence:** a display that reports ready but does not propagate later drawing updates; timer setup failure also retains local resources. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked result and sole flush path; manifestation depends on startup resource failure. Check the task result before setting ready and unwind timer resources on worker setup failure. No task or timer failure was induced; source-only.



<a id="gd14659-vmwaresvga-keeps-the-pre-modeset-cpu-mapping-when-remapping-fails"></a>
<a id="gd14659"></a>
## GD14659 — VMware SVGA keeps the pre-modeset CPU mapping when remapping fails [optional target]

After `drmModeSetCrtc()` succeeds, `VMWareSVGA_KMS_SetMode()` obtains the buffer's current CPU mapping. The code replaces `fb->map` only when `drmMMap()` succeeds, but sets `curfb`/`curmode` and returns success either way (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/vmwaresvga_kms.c:134-154`). The adjacent comment says scanout may move the buffer and retire its prior CPU view (`:138-143`).
