A valid packet with a full-width field makes the parser read past that field, potentially consume subsequent packet bytes as part of the string, and continue beyond the supplied packet while searching for a terminator. Copy the bounded field lengths during unpack instead. No in-tree caller of `hdmi_infoframe_unpack()` was found, so this is a defect in the exported compatibility API without demonstrated active use in this checkout. Source-only; no packet was parsed.

<a id="gd14725"></a>
## GD14725 — Failed log-worker creation is reported as successful and cannot be retried

`vmwgfx_log_init()` sets `nlog.started` before allocating its ring buffer, and returns `TRUE` without checking the result of `CreateNewProcTags()` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm-compat/linux_printk.c:501-512`). If worker creation fails, later calls immediately return success, while `nlog.buf` remains non-null and `nlog.flusher` remains null. Normal informational `printk` output is then appended to a buffer that is never flushed and is not mirrored to the serial log (`:515-529`); the allocated 2 MiB buffer also remains stranded. This affects diagnostics rather than display operation. Source-only; no task-creation failure was induced.

<a id="gd14728"></a>
## GD14728 — VMware SVGA cursor setup leaks the dumb buffer when mapping fails [optional target]

When no cursor buffer exists, VMWareSVGA_KMS_SetCursorShape() creates a dumb buffer and, on successful creation, immediately attempts drmMMap() (workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/vmwaresvga_kms.c:271-279). If creation succeeded but mapping returns NULL, the shared failure branch clears kms->cursor.handle and returns FALSE without calling drmModeDestroyDumb() (:280-285). The mapping helper simply returns the vmwgfx mapping result and does not destroy the GEM handle (libdrm/arosdrm.c:246-250). The neighboring framebuffer helper explicitly destroys a dumb handle on this same create-success/map-failure path (vmwaresvga_kms.c:51-58). The selected display method propagates the failure and switches to software cursor rendering (vmwaresvga_displayclass.c:176-183).

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional VMware SVGA HIDD receives a non-NULL cursor shape, dumb-buffer creation succeeds, and CPU mapping fails. Hardware cursor setup fails and falls back to software rendering, but the created DRM buffer handle has been discarded without destruction. A later cursor-shape attempt can repeat the allocation and leak another buffer until the DRM file is closed. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built VMware SVGA HIDD when cursor mapping fails after successful buffer creation. **Confidence:** high for the cleanup omission and discarded handle; occurrence depends on the stated mapping failure. Destroy the dumb buffer before clearing its handle on this branch. No mapping failure, cursor update, device, or build was exercised; source-only.


<a id="gd14729"></a>
## GD14729 — The full vmwgfx shutdown path leaves its PCI wrapper and bus state allocated

`vmwgfx_init_findcard()` allocates and caches a `struct pci_dev` in the static `found_pdev`, while `drm_aros_pci_init()` retains the PCI bus object and attribute bases (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm-aros/drm_drv.c:552-562`; `drm_aros_pci.c:180-189`). The AROS full-shutdown helper calls `vmw_aros_remove()` but only clears `current_drm_device` (`drm_drv.c:607-614`); it does not free/reset `found_pdev`, clear `vmwgfx_aros_pdev`, or call `drm_aros_pci_shutdown()` to dispose the bus and release its attribute bases (`drm_aros_pci.c:194-216`). A full unload therefore retains the PCI wrapper and PCI enumeration resources, and a later initialization reuses the cached wrapper state. No in-tree caller of `vmwgfx_shutdown()` was found, so this is scoped to the explicit full-shutdown entry point rather than the reset callback. Source-only; no unload/reload was run.

<a id="gd14730"></a>
## GD14730 — DRM ELD SAD helpers accept negative descriptor indices

Both `drm_eld_sad_get()` and `drm_eld_sad_set()` reject only indices greater than or equal to `drm_eld_sad_count()` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_eld.c:21-29,44-52`). Their `int sad_index` parameter is then used directly in `DRM_ELD_CEA_SAD(mnl, sad_index)`, whose offset is `20 + mnl + 3 * sad_index` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/include/drm/drm_eld.h:69`). A negative index therefore passes the check and points before the SAD array; the getter reads that location as a descriptor, while the setter writes three bytes there. This is an exported compatibility API defect; a search found no in-tree caller of either helper, so no active trigger in this checkout is established. Reject negative indices before computing the pointer. Source-only; no ELD buffer was accessed.

<a id="gd14731"></a>
## GD14731 — DRM SCDC helpers truncate transfer lengths to the I2C message field

`drm_scdc_read()` and `drm_scdc_write()` accept a `size_t size` but assign it (or `1 + size`) to `struct i2c_msg.len`, which is `u16` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/display/drm_scdc_helper.c:70-86,110-124`; `workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/include/linux/i2c.h:58-63`). No range check rejects values above the message field's maximum. For reads of at least 65,536 bytes, the requested length wraps when stored; for writes, the offset byte plus payload length wraps. If the adapter accepts the truncated message, these helpers can return success after transferring fewer bytes than requested. No checked-in caller of the block helpers was found, so this is an exported API defect without an established active call path in this checkout. Validate the size against the I2C message limit before allocation or transfer. Source-only; no bus transfer was run.

<a id="gd14732"></a>
## GD14732 — Legacy CRTC initialization leaves a published CRTC with a freed primary plane on CRC setup failure

With `CONFIG_DEBUG_FS`, `drm_crtc_crc_init()` can return `-ENOMEM` when allocating `crtc->crc.source` fails (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_crtc.c:138-147`). This call occurs after `__drm_crtc_init_with_planes()` has linked the CRTC into `mode_config.crtc_list`, incremented `num_crtc`, and assigned its `primary` pointer (`:283-296`). The error path only unregisters the mode-object ID; the legacy `drm_crtc_init()` wrapper then cleans up and frees the primary plane without removing the CRTC from the list (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_modeset_helper.c:145-175`). The device is left with a listed CRTC whose `primary` points to freed storage and with a consumed CRTC index. Later initialization/validation or teardown can traverse this inconsistent partial object. The trigger requires the optional debugfs configuration and the CRC-source allocation failure. No checked-in caller of the legacy wrapper was found, so this is an exported helper defect without established active use in this checkout. Roll back the CRTC list/count and associated initialization before freeing the plane. Source-only; no allocation failure or initialization was induced.

<a id="gd14733"></a>
## GD14733 — DRM refresh calculation overflows before its denominator check

`drm_mode_vrefresh()` passes `mode->htotal * mode->vtotal` to `check_mul_overflow()`, but both fields are `u16` and undergo integer promotion to signed `int`; the product can overflow before the checked helper receives it (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_modes.c:1287-1307`; `include/drm/drm_modes.h:252-263`). DisplayID detailed timings independently supply 16-bit active and blanking values, which are combined into the 16-bit totals (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_edid.c:6793-6818`). A mode with both totals above 46,340 can therefore overflow this multiplication. Basic mode validation checks timing order but not total magnitude, and the connector probe sorts surviving modes using `drm_mode_vrefresh()` (`drm_modes.c:1629-1665,1841-1860`; `drm_probe_helper.c:559-712`). Such a mode can receive an incorrect refresh estimate and be ordered incorrectly; the supposed overflow check does not guard the product. Widen at least one operand before multiplication and check that result. Trigger is limited to unusual but representable timing totals; no display or EDID was used. Source-only.

<a id="gd14734"></a>
## GD14734 — GEM device teardown never destroys the object-name IDR

`drm_gem_init()` initializes `dev->object_name_idr` with `idr_init_base()` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_gem.c:95-101`), but its registered managed cleanup only destroys the VMA offset manager (`:82-87,114`). The device-wide IDR is used by GEM flink/open operations and entries are removed as object handles disappear (`:275-282,933-938,958-972`); unlike each per-file object IDR, no device teardown path calls `idr_destroy()` for it (`:1090-1097`; repository search). The AROS IDR implementation's destroy routine removes residual entries, frees cached IDR layers and destroys its mutex (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm-compat/linux_idr.c:214-229`). Thus every initialized GEM device leaves the IDR's lock resources alive, and use of GEM names can retain its cached IDR storage at device teardown. vmwgfx enables `DRIVER_GEM` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/vmwgfx/vmwgfx_drv.c:1599`), so this path is active for the optional VMware driver. Add `idr_destroy(&dev->object_name_idr)` to the managed cleanup after object/name users are quiesced. Source-only; no device teardown or GEM name operation was run.

<a id="gd14735"></a>
## GD14735 — vmwgfx ignores failure to allocate its legacy gamma table

`drm_mode_crtc_set_gamma_size()` returns `-ENOMEM` and resets `crtc->gamma_size` to zero when allocating the gamma store fails (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_color_mgmt.c:208-220`). All three vmwgfx CRTC implementations ignore that return value (`drm/vmwgfx/vmwgfx_scrn.c:899`, `vmwgfx_ldu.c:510`, `vmwgfx_stdu.c:1625`) and proceed with CRTC setup. The selected CRTC callbacks implement `gamma_set`, but the legacy gamma ioctl first checks `gamma_size` through `drm_crtc_supports_legacy_gamma()` and returns unsupported when it is zero (`drm_color_mgmt.c:244-257,371-378`). Under allocation failure, device initialization therefore succeeds with gamma correction silently unavailable on the affected CRTC. Propagate the initialization error or explicitly treat gamma as an optional capability and report that degradation. Conditional on gamma-store allocation failure; no allocation failure or device initialization was run. Source-only.

<a id="gd14736"></a>
## GD14736 — vmwgfx advertises cursor hotspot support when hotspot properties fail to initialize

vmwgfx enables `DRIVER_CURSOR_HOTSPOT` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/vmwgfx/vmwgfx_drv.c:1599`). During cursor-plane initialization, `__drm_universal_plane_init()` calls `drm_plane_create_hotspot_properties()` but discards its return value (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_plane.c:476-480`). That helper can fail with `-ENOMEM` while allocating either signed-range property, and cleans up the first property if creating the second fails (`:330-357`). Plane setup then returns success without publishing `HOTSPOT_X/Y`, despite the driver-wide hotspot feature remaining enabled. The vmwgfx cursor atomic update adds `plane_state->hotspot_x/y` to cursor position and forwards them to the virtual display (`drm/vmwgfx/vmwgfx_cursor_plane.c:838-842`); atomic clients that enable virtualized cursor-plane support cannot set the missing properties and lose the hotspot positioning needed to predict pointer location. Propagate property-creation failure so cursor-plane setup can roll back. Conditional on property allocation failure during one of the three vmwgfx cursor-plane initializers; no allocation failure or cursor operation was run. Source-only.

<a id="gd14737"></a>
## GD14737 — vmwgfx ignores suggested-position property allocation failure and dereferences NULL during connector setup

`drm_mode_create_suggested_offset_properties()` can return `-ENOMEM` with either `mode_config.suggested_x_property` or `suggested_y_property` still NULL (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_connector.c:2692-2707`). `vmw_kms_init()` ignores that return and proceeds to initialize a display unit (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/vmwgfx/vmwgfx_kms.c:1177-1184`). Each of the three connector constructors later passes both fields to `drm_object_attach_property()` without checking them (`vmwgfx_scrn.c:904-906`, `vmwgfx_stdu.c:1627-1632`, `vmwgfx_ldu.c:512-517`). The core helper immediately reads `property->dev` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_mode_object.c:238-241`), so failure to allocate either property causes a NULL dereference during vmwgfx display initialization rather than a clean initialization error. Propagate the property-creation error from `vmw_kms_init()` before creating connectors, or guard the attachment and fail connector initialization. Trigger requires allocation failure while creating these properties. No failure was induced and no driver was initialized; source-only.

<a id="gd14738"></a>
## GD14738 — DP AUX backlight callback hides AUX errors and records a failed enable as enabled

When the optional backlight-class integration is compiled, `dp_aux_backlight_update_status()` ignores the return from `drm_edp_backlight_enable()`, sets `bl->enabled = true`, and returns success (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/display/drm_dp_helper.c:4368-4383`). The enable helper can return an AUX read/write error, so on an unplugged or temporarily unresponsive panel the backlight remains unconfigured while the backlight core sees a successful update. Subsequent unblanked updates take the `enabled` branch and only write the brightness level; they do not retry enabling the control mode, so recovery waits for another blank/unblank cycle. The blank path similarly discards disable errors and reports success (`:4384-4391`). The `drm_panel_dp_aux_backlight()` wrapper documents that it creates this managed interface for panels that use standard DP AUX backlight control (`:4398-4420`); no checked-in caller of the wrapper was found, so this is a conditional exported-helper defect, gated by the backlight-class configuration, rather than an established AROS panel failure. Propagate the operation error and update `enabled` only after a successful AUX operation. Source-only; no panel, AUX transfer, or backlight operation was run.

**GD14738 also appears in the copied Nouveau DRM helper:** `workbench/hidds/nouveau/drm/display/drm_dp_helper.c:4371-4391` contains the same optional callback and ignored enable/disable results. Its `sources.drm.mak` selects the helper. No checked-in caller of `drm_panel_dp_aux_backlight()` was found there either; the same configuration and trigger limitations apply.

<a id="gd14739"></a>
## GD14739 — Mesa GLAPI ignores pthread-key exhaustion and aliases GL state to key zero

The Mesa 26 AROS patch declares `aros_dispatch_key` and `aros_context_key` as zero-initialized statics, then ignores both `pthread_key_create()` results in its one-time initializer (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa-26.0.0-aros.diff:728-743`). The default Mesa configuration selects 26.0.0 and applies this patch when present (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa.cfg:15-16,32-38`). AROS pthread supports 64 keys; `pthread_key_create()` returns `EAGAIN` without writing the output key when all are in use (`compiler/pthread/pthread.h:189`; `compiler/pthread/pthread_key_create.c:38-58`). GLAPI then ignores `pthread_setspecific()` errors and reads the resulting keys as its per-thread dispatch/context slots (`mesa-26.0.0-aros.diff:754-790,793-810`).

If only one TLS slot remains, GLAPI creates one key and the other stays at its static value 0; if no slots remain, both stay 0. Key 0 is already allocated in either case. GLAPI stores its dispatch table or context pointer in that unrelated key's per-thread value, overwriting another library's TLS value; with both keys aliasing, dispatch and context also overwrite one another. The pthread implementation writes the value for any allocated key (`compiler/pthread/pthread_setspecific.c:34-51`). This can corrupt the other key owner's thread state and make Mesa GL dispatch/context lookup return the wrong object. Scope: applications using the patched Mesa 26 GLAPI after exhausting nearly all or all 64 pthread TLS keys. Check both key-creation results and fail or retain a safe no-op path without using an uninitialized key. Source-only; no key exhaustion or GL call was run.

<a id="gd14740"></a>
## GD14740 — VC4 render-scale patch stores viewport and scissor values in framebuffer-dependent units

The Mesa 26 AROS patch divides `glViewport` x/y/width/height by `mesa3dgl_render_scale` only when `ctx->DrawBuffer->Name == 0` at the time the call is made (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa-26.0.0-aros.diff:981-1007`). The same conditional conversion is applied when `glScissor` stores its rectangle (`:1018-1045`). Mesa3dgl enables this scale when the VC4 scaler is available and a valid environment variable or per-program tooltype requests scale 2–4; it also reduces the drawable dimensions by that factor (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa3dgl_support.c:29-35,120-134,328-337`).

Viewport and scissor are persistent context state. Binding a different draw framebuffer does not itself repeat the application's viewport/scissor calls, so values stored while framebuffer 0 is bound remain divided when an application later renders to a full-size FBO; values stored while an FBO is bound remain undivided when it returns to the smaller scaled default drawable. The former can confine FBO rendering to a smaller region, while the latter can make default-framebuffer rendering use an oversized viewport/scissor. Applications that explicitly reset both states after every framebuffer switch avoid this case. **Affected configuration:** Mesa 26 VC4 builds with render scaling enabled and applications switching between framebuffer 0 and an application FBO while reusing viewport/scissor state. **Confidence:** high for state persistence and the conversion being conditional on the current target; affected behavior follows from the values supplied to GL state storage. Imported Mesa implementation bodies are not present in this checkout, so this is based on the patch and GL state contract; no runtime reproduction or build was performed. A robust fix needs to retain unscaled API values and derive target-specific values when framebuffer state changes, or otherwise restore/recompute the values on target switches.

<a id="gd14741"></a>
## GD14741 — Mesa 26 `CPU_TO_LE32` unconditionally byte-swaps little-endian AROS values

The Mesa 26 AROS patch defines `CPU_TO_LE32(x)` as `__builtin_bswap32(x)` for every `__AROS__` target (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa-26.0.0-aros.diff:679-690`). AROS explicitly supports little-endian targets, including i386 and AArch64 (`arch/i386-all/include/aros/cpu.h:43`; `arch/aarch64-all/include/aros/cpu.h:25`, both define `AROS_BIG_ENDIAN` as 0). On those targets host-to-little-endian conversion is identity, but this macro reverses every byte. Any Mesa code using the macro to prepare little-endian GPU data or command fields will submit byte-swapped values; big-endian AROS is the only architecture for which the definition has the expected effect. The older in-tree AROS Mesa patches used `AROS_BE2LONG`, which is explicitly endian-dependent (`mesa-20.0.8-aros.diff:715-720`, likewise 20.3.2/21.0.2). **Affected configuration:** Mesa 26 AROS builds on little-endian targets, for call paths that use `CPU_TO_LE32`. **Confidence:** high that the conversion definition is incorrect on little-endian; exact affected call sites in the imported Mesa source cannot be enumerated because the Mesa checkout is absent from this repository. Correct the definition to branch on `AROS_BIG_ENDIAN` or use an available host-to-little-endian conversion. Source-only; no build or GPU operation was run.

<a id="gd14742"></a>
## GD14742 — MST stream-encryption status parser accepts truncated replies

`drm_dp_sideband_parse_query_stream_enc_status()` reads the assembled reply at offsets 1, 2 and 3 but never checks `raw->curlen` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/display/drm_dp_mst_topology.c:1002-1034`). The receive object is reset to zero before each message (`:3862-3864`), and the message length is tracked separately in `curlen` (`include/drm/display/drm_dp_mst_helper.h:170-179`). A reply that contains the matching request-type byte but omits some or all status bytes can therefore pass `verify_rx_request_type()` and be parsed from zero-filled missing bytes. The transaction handler also ignores `drm_dp_sideband_parse_reply()`'s return value (`:4011`), marks the transaction received, and wakes the waiter. `drm_dp_send_query_stream_enc_status()` then returns success and copies the resulting status to its caller (`:3251-3261`).

**Trigger and scope:** an MST branch returns a CRC-valid but truncated `QUERY_STREAM_ENC_STATUS` response whose first payload byte matches the request type. **Consequence:** the caller receives an apparently successful status with missing fields treated as zero, potentially reporting authentication/encryption as incomplete or unsupported. **Affected configuration:** external clients of the optional DisplayPort MST helper that call its stream-encryption status API. A repository-wide caller search found no checked-in call to `drm_dp_send_query_stream_enc_status()`; the selected vmwgfx driver has no MST connector path, and the parallel Nouveau helper is in an optional target excluded from the default build graph. Both vendored copies contain the same unchecked parser and ignored parse result. **Confidence:** high for the parser and transaction behavior in the vmwaresvga copy and the identical Nouveau function; a visible caller consequence requires an external API client and malformed short reply from the MST branch. Validate the complete response length before reading fields and propagate parse failure to the transaction waiter. No MST device, sideband message or build was used; source-only.

<a id="gd14745"></a>
## GD14745 — AMDX pipeline-node equality can pass a null name to `strcmp`

With `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS`, `PipelineShaderStageNodeCreateInfoAMDX` initializes `pName` to null (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:132760-132773,132867-132870`). Its `operator==` accepts equal pointers directly, but for unequal pointers calls `strcmp(pName, rhs.pName)` without checking either pointer (`:132856-132859`). Consequently, comparing a default-constructed wrapper with a wrapper whose name is set can call `strcmp(nullptr, nonnull)`, which has undefined behavior and commonly faults. The generated spaceship comparison has the same issue at `:132839-132850` when names differ and one pointer is null.

**Trigger and scope:** C++ code that includes this vendored Vulkan-Hpp header with `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS` and compares two `PipelineShaderStageNodeCreateInfoAMDX` values with different `pName` pointers where either is null; the default constructor provides a direct null-valued case. **Consequence:** comparison has undefined behavior rather than a defined ordering/equality result. **Affected configuration:** clients using the optional AMDX beta extension wrapper; this is not part of the ordinary Vulkan HIDD runtime path, and no checked-in caller of this wrapper was found in the inspected tree. **Confidence:** high for the null-pointer comparison path in both operators. This is a source-level C++ wrapper candidate; no comparison was executed and no build was run. A null-aware comparison (e.g. compare nullness before string contents) would preserve safe value comparisons.

<a id="gd14746"></a>
## GD14746 — VC4 overlay teardown releases its scanout BO before the HVS list latches

`vc4_aros_clear_overlay()` sends a NULL overlay descriptor and immediately drops `overlay_pinned_handle` under `bo_lock` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vc4gallium/vc4_galliumclass.c:749-772`). On HVS4, `vc4_hvs_overlay(NULL)` clears `hvs_OvlActive`, writes a rebuilt display list, and returns without arming or waiting for the latch (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vcgfx/vcgfx_hvs.c:939-948`). The BCM2711 HVS5 implementation has the same ordering: `vc4_hvs5_overlay(NULL)` rebuilds the list and returns at `vcgfx_hvs5.c:711-720`, while its replacement path explicitly says the old buffer stays on screen until the update latches and calls `hvs5_latch_wait()` (`:739-742`). The regular HVS4 replacement path likewise documents and waits for the old buffer's latch (`vcgfx_hvs.c:1032-1038`). The teardown path therefore permits the BO to reach its final unref and firmware free while the old display list may still be scanning it, risking a transient invalid display read or corruption during overlay removal/driver teardown. This is exercised by the maintained VC4 bridge when `vc4_aros_release_all_bos()` removes a live overlay before sweeping BOs (`vc4_drm_aros.c:3004-3015`). The affected hardware configurations are the optional Raspberry Pi VC4 Gallium HIDD using HVS4 and the HVS5 dispatch used on BCM2711. Have overlay removal wait for the display-list latch before releasing the pin, using a bounded wait/recovery path consistent with the replacement path. High confidence in the ordering gap; hardware-visible manifestation depends on whether the list update takes effect before the BO is freed. No display, teardown, or hardware operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

<a id="gd14747"></a>
## GD14747 — VC4 BO allocation retry can overwrite a concurrently allocated handle

Both `ioctl_create_bo()` and `ioctl_create_shader_bo()` select a free handle while holding `bo_lock`, but do not mark that slot reserved before allocating GPU memory. If the first allocation fails, each drops `bo_lock` while `gpu_mem_reclaim()` runs, then retries using the original handle without checking it again (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vc4gallium/vc4_drm_aros.c:798-829,854-902`; `bo_alloc_handle()` treats any zero-refcount slot as free at `:241-260`). A concurrent BO create can claim and populate the same slot during that unlocked interval. When the first request's retry succeeds, it overwrites the table entry while the other BO's allocation remains live and its returned handle aliases the new BO; later close/unref can free the wrong allocation or leak the overwritten one. This is reachable through concurrent Gallium contexts sharing the HIDD static BO table when mailbox allocation fails and reclaim is attempted. Reserve the slot across the unlocked reclaim interval, or reacquire a fresh handle and revalidate before publishing. High confidence in the unreserved slot and overwrite ordering; occurrence requires the OOM/reclaim branch to overlap another create. No allocation failure, concurrent create, or GPU operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

<a id="gd14748"></a>
## GD14748 — VC4 OOM reclaim frees frame pools outside the submission lock

`gpu_mem_reclaim()` waits for the current `seqno` through `v3d_wait_seqno()` and then frees and clears every pooled tile, exec, RCL, and overflow BO (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vc4gallium/vc4_drm_aros.c:473-510`). That wait releases `render_lock` before returning. The reclaim caller (`ioctl_create_bo()` or `ioctl_create_shader_bo()`) then frees the pool entries without reacquiring that lock, while `ioctl_submit_cl()` uses and mutates those same pool entries only under `render_lock` (`:2137-2144,2713-2720`). A concurrent submission can therefore begin after the wait completes and race the reclamation: pool pointers/handles may be cleared or freed while `do_submit_cl()` is selecting or using them, potentially submitting freed memory or corrupting the pool bookkeeping. Trigger requires GPU allocation failure to enter reclaim while another context submits. Hold the submission lock across the complete wait-and-free operation, or otherwise serialize pool reclamation with submission. High confidence in the missing common lock and shared pool state; no OOM, submission race, or GPU operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

<a id="gd14749"></a>
## GD14749 — VC4 dirty-exit reclaim frees BOs while the previous GPU job may still run

When a new process creates a VC4 screen after a different task exits without GL teardown, `vc4_aros_create_screen()` explicitly invokes `bridge->release_all_bos()` to reclaim the previous task's leaked allocations (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vc4gallium/aros_drm_vc4.c:688-711`). That callback reaches `vc4_aros_release_all_bos()`, which clears the overlay, waits for display DMA, then frees every live BO and all frame-pool BOs, but does not wait for V3D completion (`vc4_drm_aros.c:2989-3056`; `vc4_aros_bridge.c:55-59`). A task exiting does not retire an already submitted V3D job, so an outstanding job can still fetch its command lists, shader/uniform buffers, textures, render targets, or pool memory when the reclaim frees them. The new app can then also submit into the reset pool state. Before a dirty-exit sweep, drain or reset V3D and confirm all in-flight references are quiescent before freeing the GPU allocations. High confidence that the explicit abandoned-session reclaim lacks a V3D wait; manifestation requires the prior process to exit with GPU work outstanding. No process exit, GPU submission, reclaim, or hardware operation was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

<a id="gd14750"></a>
## GD14750 — Generic HIDD bitmap stride rounds wide dimensions to zero

`GetBytesPerRow()` stores both the aligned width and `data->width + data->align - 1` result in `UWORD` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:849-870`). With the default 16-pixel alignment, any bitmap width from 65,521 through 65,535 rounds to 65,536 pixels, which truncates to zero in that `UWORD`; the constructor then accepts and stores a zero `bytesPerRow` (`:1033-1050`). The selected `ChunkyBM` subclass multiplies height by this stride and calls `AllocVec(0)`, which is explicitly guaranteed to return NULL (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:68-86`; `rom/exec/allocvec.c:50-57`). A maintained public path accepts the width as `ULONG` and forwards it as the HIDD Width tag; depths above eight select the HIDD bitmap path and RGB15/16/24/32 formats (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:49-56,242-254,294-302`). Therefore valid wide true-color `AllocBitMap()` requests at the top of the HIDD `UWORD` width range fail as though memory were unavailable, even when sufficient memory exists. Keep the aligned width in a wider type and check the resulting byte stride before narrowing or allocation. High confidence in the arithmetic and clean allocation failure; scope is generic HIDD/ChunkyBM allocations with depth above eight (or another route selecting the chunky class), positive height, default alignment, and width 65,521–65,535. No bitmap or allocation was created; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

<a id="gd14751"></a>
## GD14751 — BMP loader drops trailing pixels in packed low-depth rows [medium impact, high source confidence; optional datatype]

`LoadBMP()` computes the number of source bytes for 1-, 2-, and 4-bit rows with floor division (`biWidth >> 3`, `>> 2`, and `>> 1`) and expands only those complete bytes (`workbench/classes/datatypes/bmp/bmpclass.c:555-605`). When the pixel width is not a multiple of 8, 4, or 2 respectively, it skips the remaining row bytes without decoding their partial final byte. It then passes `biWidth` pixels from the line buffer to `PDTM_WRITEPIXELARRAY` (`:615-624`). The allocated line buffer is not cleared (`:446-451`), so the trailing pixels are not initialized by this row's decode and the right edge of the decoded image is wrong. For widths smaller than one packed byte, the row decodes zero source bytes.

**Trigger and consequence:** load a valid uncompressed BMP at 1, 2, or 4 bits per pixel with a width not divisible by its packed-pixel group size. The last 1–7, 1–3, or 1 pixel(s) on each row are missing/incorrect. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatype-bmp`; its local manifest selects this loader (`workbench/classes/datatypes/bmp/mmakefile.src:6-13`). **Confidence:** high for the floor division and omitted remainder; no image was loaded. Decode the partial last byte and stop at the declared pixel width. Source-only.

<a id="gd14752"></a>
## GD14752 — BMP writer produces invalid output for 1- and 4-bit images [medium impact, high source confidence; optional datatype]

`SaveBMP()` explicitly accepts bitmap depths 1 and 4 and writes them into the BMP `biBitCount` field (`workbench/classes/datatypes/bmp/bmpclass.c:690-716,746-761`). Its row-padding calculation then uses `pixelElements = depth / 8` (`:731-743`), which is zero at both supported depths. For every width the first branch selects `alignwidth = width * 0`, so `biSizeImage` is zero; the later line-buffer allocation and `PDTM_READPIXELARRAY`/`FWrite` operations consequently use a zero-byte row (`:748-754,817-870`). No packed source pixels are emitted, although the file header advertises nonzero dimensions and 1- or 4-bit data.

**Trigger and consequence:** request `DTM_WRITE` in raw mode for a picture.datatype object whose bitmap depth is 1 or 4. The writer returns success after producing a BMP with an empty pixel array and inconsistent image size, so it cannot be decoded as the requested picture. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatype-bmp`; `BMP__DTM_WRITE()` routes raw writes to `SaveBMP()` (`:915-929`). **Confidence:** high for the zero divisor-derived byte count and zero-length writes; no file was written. Compute packed row bytes from bit depth and width, and report write failures. Source-only.

<a id="gd14753"></a>
## GD14753 — BMP loader returns success after pixel data ends early [medium impact, high source confidence; optional datatype]

For each supported pixel-depth branch, `LoadBMP()` sets `cont = 0` when `LoadBMP_FillBuf()` cannot provide a complete row (`workbench/classes/datatypes/bmp/bmpclass.c:462-468,488-494,518-522,571-575`). This exits the row loop, but the function then follows its normal cleanup path, sets `IoErr` to zero, and returns `TRUE` (`:631-636`). The partial picture object is therefore accepted as a successfully loaded BMP.

**Trigger and consequence:** load a BMP whose pixel array ends before all declared rows are present. The datatype reports success and exposes an incomplete image instead of reporting an invalid/truncated file. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatype-bmp`. **Confidence:** high for the early-end branch and unconditional success return; no file was loaded. Treat an incomplete row as a load failure and dispose the partial object. Source-only.

<a id="gd14754"></a>
## GD14754 — BMP writer ignores header and palette write failures [low impact, high source confidence; optional datatype]

`SaveBMP()` ignores the return values from all file-header and info-header `FWrite()` calls (`workbench/classes/datatypes/bmp/bmpclass.c:775-813`); `WriteBMP_Colormap()` also discards its palette `FWrite()` result (`:206-224,815-821`). Later pixel-row writes are checked and cause `SaveBMP()` to return `FALSE` on failure (`:875-881`), but if the header or palette write fails and all later operations succeed, it still reaches the success return (`:907-911`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a raw BMP save encounters a short or failed header/palette write, followed by successful later writes. The datatype reports success even though the output lacks required header or palette bytes and is not a complete BMP. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatype-bmp`, through `BMP__DTM_WRITE()` raw mode. **Confidence:** high for ignored results and later success return; no output failure was induced. Check every `FWrite()` result and fail the save on incomplete output. Source-only.

<a id="gd14755"></a>
## GD14755 — BMP loader underflows a too-small pixel offset before validating it [medium impact, high source confidence; 32-bit ABI, optional datatype]

`LoadBMP()` parses `bfOffBits` as `ULONG`, then subtracts the 14-byte file header, 40-byte info header, and palette size in place (`workbench/classes/datatypes/bmp/bmpclass.c:269-272,418-428`). If the declared pixel offset is smaller than those preceding structures, the unsigned subtraction wraps. The following `bfOffBits < 0` check cannot detect that wrapped value. On a 32-bit ABI, where the relevant `ULONG` and C `long` are both 32 bits, the subsequent subtraction from signed `filebufbytes` also uses unsigned arithmetic; it can leave the count nonnegative and skip the attempted-read validation before advancing `filebufpos` by the wrapped offset. Row decoding then reads from that invalid position (`:455-480` and subsequent depth branches).

**Trigger and consequence:** load a BMP with `bfOffBits` before the end of its file/info header and palette. On 32-bit builds, the invalid offset is not rejected before row decoding, so the loader can read from outside its buffered input and produce a failed or corrupted load. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatype-bmp` on 32-bit targets. **Confidence:** high for the unsigned wrap and skipped negative check; the exact downstream manifestation depends on ABI arithmetic and the supplied file. Validate the original offset against the minimum header/palette end before subtracting. No file was loaded; source-only.

<a id="gd14756"></a>
## GD14756 — BMP loader accepts a file when only one signature byte matches [low impact, high source confidence; optional datatype]

`LoadBMP()` rejects the file signature only when both byte comparisons are true: `filebuf[0] != 'B' && filebuf[1] != 'M'` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/bmp/bmpclass.c:290-297`). Therefore a first byte of `B` with a non-`M` second byte, or a non-`B` first byte with a second byte of `M`, passes this check. `BMP__OM_NEW()` calls `LoadBMP()` directly for the new object, with no other signature-identification gate in this class (`:145-161`). The parser then interprets bytes 2 onward as BMP size, offset and info header.

**Trigger and consequence:** open a non-BMP file through the BMP datatype whose first two bytes have exactly one of the expected signature bytes, and whose following bytes happen to satisfy enough of the BMP header checks. The datatype may accept and render unrelated content as a BMP or return a later misleading parse result instead of rejecting its file type. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatype-bmp`; its target selects this class (`workbench/classes/datatypes/bmp/mmakefile.src:6-13`), though that target is not included by the default datatype aggregate in this checkout. **Confidence:** high for the boolean condition and absence of another class-local signature check; low practical impact because the remaining header must also look plausible. Reject when either signature byte differs. No file was opened; source-only.

<a id="gd14757"></a>


## GD14757 — BMP loader treats valid top-down image heights as unsigned [medium impact, high source confidence; 32-bit optional datatype]

The BMP info-header declaration correctly types `biHeight` as signed `LONG`, but `LoadBMP()` parses the field into `ULONG biHeight` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/bmp/bmpclass.c:80-93,226-238,315-323`). The loader accepts uncompressed `BI_RGB` (`:326-330`), sets the picture height from this unsigned value into the 16-bit `BitMapHeader.bmh_Height` (`:389-392`; `compiler/include/datatypes/pictureclass.h:28-38`), and begins decoding with `for (y=biHeight-1; y>=0; y--)` where `y` is signed `long` (`bmpclass.c:236,454-455`). A negative BMP height is the specified representation for a top-down uncompressed RGB bitmap, whose rows are stored from top to bottom ([Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/wingdi/ns-wingdi-bitmapinfoheader)).

**Trigger and consequence:** load a valid top-down `BI_RGB` BMP with a negative height whose absolute value fits the picture datatype's dimensions. On 32-bit builds, the unsigned parsed height is narrowed into `bmh_Height` (for example, `-4` becomes 65532), while the loop's initial unsigned value converts to a negative `long` on the target's usual two's-complement ABI; the row loop is skipped and the loader returns success with no decoded rows and a bogus height. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatype-bmp` on 32-bit targets; the datatype accepts `BI_RGB`, which permits top-down RGB images. **Confidence:** high for the signed/unsigned and destination-width mismatch; no image was loaded. Parse the field as signed, distinguish orientation, use its absolute row count, and decode rows in the correct order. No file or datatype operation was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14758"></a>
## GD14758 — Generic HIDD bitmap alignment calculation assumes a power of two [medium impact, high source confidence]

The `aoHidd_BitMap_Align` documentation describes a requested pixel alignment and does not restrict it to powers of two (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:765-800`). The base class accepts the tag directly into `data->align` (`:923-924`), but `GetBytesPerRow()` rounds with `(width + align - 1) & ~(align - 1)` (`:849-854`), a bit-mask expression that is correct only for power-of-two alignments. For example, width 8 with alignment 3 yields 8 pixels rather than the required 9; the generic class publishes that byte stride as `aoHidd_BitMap_BytesPerRow` and ChunkyBM uses it as the row step and allocation layout (`:1038-1050`; `gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:50-75,117-118`).

**Trigger and consequence:** create a generic bitmap with a non-power-of-two alignment. Its reported row stride does not satisfy the requested alignment; consumers relying on aligned row starts, including hardware-oriented subclasses or wrapped buffers, can receive an unsuitable layout. **Affected configuration:** HIDD bitmap subclasses using the generic base-class stride calculation and accepting non-power-of-two `aoHidd_BitMap_Align`. **Confidence:** high that the arithmetic fails the documented alignment for such inputs; medium that this is a practical caller-visible defect because current in-tree users may only request power-of-two values. Either reject non-power-of-two values explicitly or use division-based round-up. No bitmap was created; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


<a id="gd14759"></a>
## GD14759 — BMP loader decodes the third 2-bit palette index incorrectly [medium impact, high source confidence; optional datatype]

`LoadBMP()` accepts `biBitCount == 2`, sets the palette size to four entries, and expands each packed byte into four `PBPAFMT_LUT8` indices (`workbench/classes/datatypes/bmp/bmpclass.c:346-353,395-410,595-600`). For the third pixel, it stores `(byte & 0x0C)` without shifting the two-bit field down. That produces indices 0, 4, 8, or 12 instead of 0 through 3. The selected picture.datatype LUT8 path treats each byte as a color-register index (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.c:1291-1310`); the picture object's fixed 256-entry `SrcColRegs` array is zero-initialized, and only the first four entries are loaded (`workbench/classes/datatypes/picture/pictureclass.h:20`; `pictureclass.c:165`; `bmpclass.c:395-410`). The wrong indices therefore use zero-filled color entries rather than the BMP's palette. This remains distinct from GD14751, which covers missing pixels when the width leaves a partial final packed byte: a four-pixel-wide row exercises this bad third index with no partial byte.

**Trigger and consequence:** load a 2-bit-per-pixel BMP row whose third packed pixel is nonzero. That pixel is mapped using the wrong palette index, so the decoded image has incorrect colors (the decoded index selects an unpopulated, zero-valued color-register entry). **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatype-bmp`; this finding is limited to the 2-bit mode that its loader explicitly accepts. **Confidence:** high for the bit-mask/shift mismatch and wrong index; no image was loaded. Shift the masked field right by two before storing it. Source-only; see the [BMP packed-pixel review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#bmp-packed-pixel-index-review-gd14759).


<a id="gd14760"></a>
## GD14760 — BMP loader ignores a reduced `biClrUsed` palette [medium impact, high source confidence; optional datatype]

For indexed BI_RGB images, `biClrUsed` specifies the color-table length; zero selects the depth's maximum palette size ([Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/wingdi/ns-wingdi-bitmapinfoheader#members)). `LoadBMP()` parses `biClrUsed` but chooses `numcolors` solely from `biBitCount` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/bmp/bmpclass.c:315-323,336-360`). It then asks `LoadBMP_Colormap()` to read that maximum count before decoding pixels (`:175-198,393-413`).

**Trigger and consequence:** load a valid indexed BI_RGB BMP with nonzero `biClrUsed` smaller than the maximum palette, such as an 8-bit image with two palette entries and `bfOffBits` immediately after those entries. For a small file, the palette reader requests 1,024 bytes and fails at EOF although the file contains the complete declared palette and pixel array; larger pixel arrays can instead be consumed as if they were palette entries. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatype-bmp`, limited to indexed images whose declared palette is smaller than the depth maximum. **Confidence:** high for the parsed-but-ignored count and resulting over-read/failure; the reduced-palette size rule is specified by the linked BITMAPINFOHEADER documentation. Honor nonzero `biClrUsed`, use the maximum only when it is zero, and validate pixel indices against the resulting palette. No image was loaded; source-only.


<a id="gd14761"></a>
## GD14761 — VC4 emulates NPOT repeat with clamp and loses linear-filter wrap at the texture seam [medium impact, high source confidence; optional Mesa 26 VC4 target]

The AROS Mesa 26 patch detects `PIPE_TEX_WRAP_REPEAT` on a non-power-of-two base texture in `vc4_program.c`, then applies `ntq_ffract()` to the normalized coordinate. In `vc4_uniforms.c`, it forces that axis’s P1 hardware wrap field to `1` (clamp-to-edge) (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa-26.0.0-aros.diff:1100-1154,1165-1182`). This avoids sampling the padded power-of-two storage, but it does not preserve repeat filtering at the 0/1 boundary: with linear filtering, a coordinate just below the repeat seam should blend the last logical texel with the first. After `fract()` and clamp, the hardware instead clamps both filter taps to the first texel; just below 1 it clamps to the last texel. The result is a visible discontinuity/seam for linearly filtered NPOT repeat textures. The patch checks the base width/height and applies the same transformation without a filter-mode condition.

**Trigger and consequence:** on a VC4 Mesa 26 build, sample an NPOT texture with REPEAT and linear filtering at coordinates near an integer wrap boundary. The image can show a seam or incorrect edge colors instead of blending across the repeated boundary. **Affected configuration:** optional Raspberry Pi VC4 Gallium/Mesa 26 path; its parent dependency is commented out in `arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vc4gallium/mmakefile.src:15-19`, so this is not claimed to occur in the default build. Mesa’s `mesa.cfg` selects the checked-in AROS patch when fetching Mesa 26 (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa.cfg:13-36`). **Confidence:** high for the coordinate and clamp transformation; no imported Mesa runtime, texture sampling, or build was exercised. A correct emulation needs to preserve cross-edge filtering, for example by supplying wrapped edge data or implementing the filter across the logical texture boundary. Source-only; see the [patch review trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mesa-26-vc4-npot-repeat-filtering-gd14761).


<a id="gd14762"></a>
## GD14762 — VC4 submission drain timeout proceeds with the prior job still pending [medium impact, high source confidence; optional VC4 HIDD]

Before starting a binning job, `do_submit_cl()` waits for `CT0CS.CTRUN` to clear and for `pending_render` to be handed off (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vc4gallium/vc4_drm_aros.c:2512-2535`). If the loop exceeds 100,000,000 spins, it only logs a timeout and breaks. The function then clears error state, overwrites the pending CT1 addresses and marks `pending_render = TRUE` for the new submission before writing the next CT0 start/end addresses (`:2538-2542,2634-2648`); it also assigns and publishes another seqno (`:2663-2668`). The separate `v3d_wait_seqno()` timeout path resets both control threads and reconciles sequence counters (`:1125-1230`), but this drain timeout does not call that recovery.

**Trigger and consequence:** when the previous bin job or FLDONE handoff remains stuck beyond the drain loop, this path continues without resetting or reconciling the old work. It can replace the pending RCL handoff and submit bookkeeping while the old job remains active; the new job can be ignored or lose its render handoff, and later waits may observe inconsistent completion state. **Affected configuration:** optional Raspberry Pi VC4 Gallium target; its parent dependency edge is commented out in the module makefile. **Confidence:** high that timeout breaks into submission without recovery, and that the same pending state and registers are then reused; the exact hardware-visible outcome requires a stuck/draining-failure state. Abort the new submission and route through the same reset/bookkeeping recovery used by `v3d_wait_seqno()` before reusing pipeline state. No GPU stall or submission was induced; source-only.

<a id="gd14763"></a>
## GD14763 — CVT descriptors never add the reduced-blanking 60 Hz mode [medium impact, high source confidence; VMware and Nouveau DRM]

`drm_cvt_modes()` enumerates CVT 3-byte timing flags with `for (j = 1; j < 5; j++)` and tests `1 << j` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_edid.c:4022,4051-4060`). The rate table includes a 60 Hz entry at index zero, and the call passes `j == 0` as the reduced-blanking argument, but the loop never reaches zero. The CVT 3-byte descriptor's bit zero denotes 60 Hz reduced blanking; `add_cvt_modes()` dispatches these descriptors for EDID revision 3 or later, and `_drm_edid_connector_add_modes()` invokes that parser during mode discovery (`:4078-4089,6940-6965`). The same file is byte-identical in the Nouveau copy.

**Trigger and consequence:** a monitor advertises a CVT 3-byte timing with the 60 Hz reduced-blanking flag (including a descriptor whose only supported bit is bit zero). This parser adds none of the bit-zero modes, so the probed mode list omits an advertised supported timing. **Affected configuration:** VMware SVGA and Nouveau paths using these vendored DRM EDID parsers. **Confidence:** high for the skipped bit and parser reachability; no display or mode enumeration was exercised. Iterate from bit zero and pass the corresponding reduced-blanking flag. Source-only; see the [EDID parser review trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vmware-nouveau-drm-edid-review-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14764"></a>
## GD14764 — HDR minimum luminance is calculated as zero for every EDID value [medium impact, high source confidence; VMware and Nouveau DRM]

`drm_calculate_luminance_range()` reduces the 8-bit `min_cll` value with `DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(min_cll, 255)`, which can only produce zero or one, then computes `DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(q * q, 100)`, which is zero for either result (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_edid.c:5405,5433-5438`). Consequently `luminance_range.min_luminance` is always zero. The function's own comment gives the intended formula as `maxLum * (CV/255)^2 / 100`; for the valid maximum code CV=255, this should be one percent of max luminance, not zero. `drm_parse_hdr_metadata_block()` calls the calculation when the metadata block provides the minimum-luminance byte (`:5460-5477`), and the result is stored in the connector's documented EDID-derived luminance-range field (`include/drm/drm_connector.h:426-438`). The same implementation is present in the byte-identical Nouveau copy.

**Trigger and consequence:** a connector receives HDMI static type-1 HDR metadata containing the minimum-luminance field. The reported panel minimum is always zero, even when the EDID code specifies a nonzero value; consumers of `drm_display_info.luminance_range` therefore receive incorrect HDR display information. **Affected configuration:** VMware SVGA and Nouveau DRM EDID consumers. **Confidence:** high for the integer-rounding collapse and metadata-parser reachability; no display was queried. Preserve precision through the complete formula (for example, multiply before dividing with sufficient width). Source-only; see the [EDID parser review trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vmware-nouveau-drm-edid-review-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14765"></a>
## GD14765 — HDR maximum luminance is derived from the MaxFALL field [medium impact, high source confidence; VMware and Nouveau DRM]

The CTA HDR static-metadata parser stores the desired content maximum-luminance byte from `db[4]` in `hdr_metadata->max_cll`, and the separate maximum frame-average light-level byte from `db[5]` in `max_fall` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/drm/drm_edid.c:5460-5474`; `include/linux/hdmi.h:379-386`). The luminance-range routine then assigns `max_avg = hdr_metadata->max_fall` and applies the desired maximum-luminance conversion `50 * 2**(CV/32)` to that value (`drm_edid.c:5410,5413-5431`). The two metadata quantities are separately defined in CTA static HDR metadata; MaxFALL is a frame-average content limit, while the encoded desired maximum luminance is the input to the panel maximum-luminance calculation. The result is stored as the connector's EDID-derived maximum panel luminance (`include/drm/drm_connector.h:426-438`). The same code is present in the byte-identical Nouveau copy.

**Trigger and consequence:** a display advertises differing desired maximum luminance and MaxFALL values. The reported `display_info.luminance_range.max_luminance` is calculated from MaxFALL, so it can substantially understate or otherwise misstate the display's supported maximum luminance. **Affected configuration:** VMware SVGA and Nouveau DRM EDID consumers. **Confidence:** high for field assignment and formula input mismatch; no display was queried. Use the desired maximum-luminance code for this conversion and keep MaxFALL as content metadata. Source-only; see the [EDID parser review trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vmware-nouveau-drm-edid-review-2026-11-03).
<a id="gd14766"></a>
## GD14766 — VC4 submission accepts invalid BO handles and builds GPU addresses from zero

**Source and trigger:** `bo_bus_addr()` logs and returns zero when a GEM handle index is outside `bo_handle_count`, or when the selected BO handle is zero, out of range, or no longer referenced (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vc4gallium/vc4_drm_aros.c:513-531`). In `process_bin_cl()`, the `VC4_PACKET_GEM_HANDLES` case assigns that return to `exec->current_bo[0]` and continues without propagating an error (`:1455-1469`). A later `VC4_PACKET_GL_INDEXED_PRIMITIVE` is copied and its index-buffer address is patched as `current_bo[0] + ib_offset` (`:1513-1524`). Unlike `relocate_shader_recs()`, which checks the handle and returns failure (`:1650-1678`), this parser does not stop on an invalid GEM handle. `do_submit_cl()` treats a nonzero transformed command-list size as success and proceeds to construct the RCL and write the V3D command-thread start registers (`:2316-2323,2615-2635`); the ioctl dispatcher returns this path to the Mesa bridge (`:2713-2720,2777-2786`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a submitted command list or surface descriptor names an absent or stale BO. The HIDD continues and can submit an indexed draw, render target, or depth/stencil operation whose GPU address is based at zero (plus any supplied offset), instead of returning a submission error. The operation can fail or corrupt rendering and may leave the GPU processing an invalid address. No claim is made that the checked-in Mesa producer emits such a packet during normal operation; local Mesa sources are linked externally, and this malformed-input path was not induced.

**Affected configuration:** explicit optional Raspberry Pi VC4 Gallium HIDD target; the parent `workbench-hidds-raspi` dependency is commented out in this checkout (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vc4gallium/mmakefile.src:15-19`). No default-image inclusion is claimed.

**Confidence:** high that the parser logs but accepts the invalid handle and submits the resulting address; ordinary rendering impact is conditional on a malformed/stale command list reaching this internal ioctl. Reject the command list when either required handle resolution fails, before submitting any GPU work. Source-only; no command list, GPU operation, or build was run. See the [VC4 command-list follow-up](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vc4-bin-cl-invalid-handle-follow-up-gd14766).


<a id="gd14768"></a>
## GD14768 — Legacy network-browser backdrop parser allocates no byte for the path terminator

`IconWindowIconList__Func_ParseBackdrop()` allocates `linelen + strlen(bdrp_dir)` bytes for `bdrp_fullfile`, then formats the concatenated directory and entry name with `sprintf()` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow_networkbrowserlist.c:488-493`). After dropping the leading colon and newline, the formatted path needs `strlen(bdrp_dir) + linelen` characters plus one NUL byte. The allocation omits that final byte, so a valid `:name` entry writes one byte past the requested allocation. The function is called while scanning `.backdrop` files in the root-list update path (`:915-933`).

**Trigger and consequence:** if this legacy function is built and a root volume has a `.backdrop` entry, formatting its full path writes the terminator beyond the requested buffer. The allocator may round the request internally, so the precise adjacent-memory effect is not established. **Reachability:** this is not in the current Wanderer app `FILES` list (`workbench/system/Wanderer/mmakefile.src:7-21`) or any class module `files=` list (`Classes/mmakefile.src:25-54`); no checked-in consumer references its class symbol. Treat as a dormant-source candidate, not a current shipped Wanderer defect. **Confidence:** high for the size arithmetic; runtime impact untested. Allocate one extra byte or use a bounded formatter. Source-only; see the [legacy source review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-networkbrowserlist-full-body-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14769"></a>
## GD14769 — AVX RGB24 conversion processes eight pixels while advancing four

`convert_RGB24_XRGB32_AVX()` enters its vector loop when `x + 4 <= width` and advances `x` by four (`arch/i386-all/hidd/gfx/rgbconv_avx.c:142-155`), but loads two overlapping 16-byte source vectors, shuffles eight pixels, and stores eight 32-bit outputs (`:156-171`). For a four-pixel row it reads through source byte 27 although the row has 12 pixel bytes, then writes eight outputs into a four-pixel destination. Wider rows also overlap writes and process beyond the requested width. **Trigger and consequence:** if this AVX kernel is registered and used for an RGB24-to-XRGB32 conversion, the vector path can read past the source row and overwrite destination pixels/buffer beyond the requested width. **Affected configuration:** optional i386 AVX HIDD graphics conversion code. **Reachability:** the current i386 `SetArchRGBConversionFunctions()` has all registrations inside `#if (0)` (`arch/i386-all/hidd/gfx/rgbconv_arch.c:15-25`), and no other in-tree reference to this converter was found; therefore this is a dormant implementation defect, not an active conversion-path claim. **Confidence:** high for the loop/batch mismatch; no conversion was run. Advance by eight and use a batch bound consistent with the actual source and destination extents. Source-only.

<a id="gd14770"></a>
## GD14770 — AVX RGB24 shuffle mask duplicates a source channel

The final four entries of `AVX_ABCtoDABC_MASK` are `0xFF, 0x02, 0x01, 0x01` (`arch/i386-all/hidd/gfx/rgbconv_avx.c:132-140`). With `_mm256_set_epi8()` ordering, the lowest output pixel therefore selects source byte 1 twice and never selects source byte 0. The corresponding SSE RGB24-to-XRGB32 mask ends in `0xFF, 0x02, 0x01, 0x00` (`rgbconv_sse.c:245-258`), matching the expected distinct component selection. **Trigger and consequence:** if registered, pixels handled by the AVX RGB24 vector path have one color component replaced by a duplicate of another. **Affected configuration and reachability:** same dormant optional i386 AVX kernel and disabled in-tree registration described for GD14769. **Confidence:** high for the mask discrepancy; no conversion was run. Correct the final shuffle index and keep it aligned with the SSE/generic channel mapping. Source-only.

<a id="gd14771"></a>
## GD14771 — AVX BGR15 conversions mis-map red and blue channels

The AVX `BGRA32 -> BGR15` and `ARGB32 -> BGR15` kernels overwrite the extracted blue vector with `red << 10`, while also retaining red in the low bits (`arch/i386-all/hidd/gfx/rgbconv_avx.c:312-348,436-472`); this duplicates red and discards blue. The `BGR15 -> ARGB32` kernel treats the low five bits as blue and the high five bits as red (`:498-533`), but the format definitions specify `BGR15_RMASK = 0x001F` and `BGR15_BMASK = 0x7C00` (`rom/hidds/gfx/colorconv/rgbconv_macros.h:100-115`). Thus its output reverses those channels relative to the generic `UPSHIFT16()` conversion. **Trigger and consequence:** if any of these AVX kernels is registered for a conversion with distinct red and blue values, output colors are wrong. **Affected configuration and reachability:** optional i386 AVX HIDD graphics conversion code; current in-tree architecture registration is disabled under `#if (0)` and no other caller was found, so these remain dormant implementation defects. **Confidence:** high for the channel mapping; no conversion was run. Align the vector extraction/shifts with the format masks and generic fallback. Source-only.


<a id="gd14772"></a>
<a id="gd14772-workbench-handler-dereferences-a-failed-close-relay-allocation"></a>
## GD14772 — Workbench handler dereferences a failed close-relay allocation

In `__HandleIntuition_WB()`, the `WBENCHCLOSE` branch assigns `CreateIWBHM(WBHM_TYPE_HIDE, ...)` to `iwbhm` and immediately writes `iwbhm->iwbhm_Data.Hide.imsg` without checking for NULL (`workbench/libs/workbench/handler.c:401-406`). `CreateIWBHM()` returns NULL when its `AllocMessage()` allocation fails (`workbench/libs/workbench/support_messages.c:67-81`). The handler's Intuition-message loop invokes this function directly (`handler.c:180-184`) and relies on it to reply to the incoming message; on the successful close-relay path, the reply is intentionally deferred until the Workbench application responds (`handler.c:151-169,403-414`).

**Trigger and scope:** a `WBENCHCLOSE` event reaches the active Workbench handler while allocation of the `IntWBHandlerMessage` fails. **Consequence:** the handler dereferences NULL before replying; the Workbench handler task can terminate, and Intuition's synchronous close caller waits indefinitely for the original message reply (`rom/intuition/wbtasktalk.c:60-101`; caller `rom/intuition/closeworkbench.c:92`). This is distinct from GD5833, which covers a successfully allocated relay leaked when the Workbench application port is absent. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked nullable allocation and blocked-reply path; requires allocation failure during a close event. Reply the original message or report the allocation failure before leaving the handler path. No allocation failure, Workbench close, or task was induced; source-only.


<a id="gd14773"></a>
<a id="gd14773-concurrent-closeworkbench-calls-can-dereference-a-disposed-screen"></a>
## GD14773 — Concurrent `CloseWorkBench()` calls can dereference a disposed screen

`CloseWorkBench()` reads `IntuitionBase->WorkBench` before acquiring the public-screen-list lock, then calls `FireScreenNotifyMessage(..., SNOTIFY_BEFORE_CLOSEWB, ...)` before taking that lock (`rom/intuition/closeworkbench.c:53-59`). After acquiring the lock, it dereferences the saved pointer to read `pubScrNode` and `psn_VisitorCount` without checking whether the current `WorkBench` pointer still matches it (`:71-79`). Another task can complete a concurrent `CloseWorkBench()` in the notification/scheduling interval: its `CloseScreen()` path disposes the screen object (`rom/intuition/closescreen.c:290-291`) and clears `IntuitionBase->WorkBench` before releasing the same public-screen-list lock (`closeworkbench.c:94-113`). The first caller then resumes with a pointer to the disposed screen.

**Trigger and scope:** two tasks call `CloseWorkBench()` concurrently while a Workbench screen is open, and one caller is delayed after reading the screen pointer but before its visitor-count dereference. **Consequence:** the delayed caller reads `pubScrNode` through a disposed screen object; allocator reuse can turn this into a fault or incorrect visitor-count decision. **Affected configuration:** Intuition with concurrent public `CloseWorkBench()` callers. **Confidence:** high for the unsynchronized read/notify/lock ordering and disposal path; the task interleaving was not run. Revalidate the Workbench pointer under the screen-list lock before dereferencing it, while preserving the notification ordering and lifetime across the unlocked callback interval. No screen operation, notification or concurrent caller was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14774"></a>
## GD14774 — Workbench handler can send through a port after it is unregistered and freed

`RegisterWorkbench()` and `UnregisterWorkbench()` protect `WorkbenchBase->wb_WorkbenchPort` only while assigning or clearing the pointer (`workbench/libs/workbench/registerworkbench.c:82-94`; `unregisterworkbench.c:57-72`). The handler reads the field without that semaphore and sends through it in both relay and Intuition-event paths (`handler.c:370-379,413-416`); in each path the non-NULL guard and `PutMsg()` argument are separate reads, so unregister can also clear the field between them and pass NULL to `PutMsg()`. The explicitly buildable Wanderer teardown removes its input handlers, calls `UnregisterWorkbench()`, then deletes `wd_CommandPort` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:3401-3422`); Workbook likewise unregisters and later deletes `AppPort` (`workbench/system/Workbook/wbapp.c:323-379,128-129`). Both parent `workbench-system` dependency edges are commented out in this snapshot (`workbench/system/Wanderer/mmakefile.src:23-29`; `Workbook/mmakefile.src:15-17`), so neither is claimed as default-image selection. Exec `DeleteMsgPort()` immediately frees the signal bit and port allocation, while `PutMsg()` dereferences the port to lock and update its message list (`rom/exec/deletemsgport.c:48-55`; `rom/exec/putmsg.c:71-88`).

**Trigger and scope:** a handler relay or `WBENCHOPEN`/`WBENCHCLOSE` event overlaps the selected Workbench application's unregistration and port deletion, with the handler having read the old pointer before it is cleared. **Consequence:** the handler can call `PutMsg()` on freed port storage, causing a fault or message-list corruption; the relay may also remain unreplied if delivery is lost. The registration semaphore does not pin the port because the sending path never acquires it. **Affected configuration:** an explicitly built Workbench library handler and Workbench application, including the checked Wanderer and Workbook targets; their parent aggregate edges are commented out in this snapshot. **Confidence:** high for the send/teardown ordering and immediate port free; the overlapping task schedule was not run. Synchronize port lookup and send against unregister/port destruction, or otherwise retain the destination port's lifetime through delivery. No application teardown or message send was run; source-only.


<a id="gd14775"></a>
<a id="gd14775-editor-include-path-parsing-writes-past-its-fixed-scratch-buffer-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14775 — Editor include-path parsing writes past its fixed scratch buffer [explicit optional target]

`GetIncludeFile()` composes the include path directly in the global `BufTxt` array (`workbench/tools/Edit/Utility.c:120-145`), declared as only 256 bytes (`Jed.c:32`). Angle-bracket includes start with `INCLUDE:` and then copy every remaining include-name byte; quoted includes first copy the entire directory prefix from `prj->path` and then copy the include-name bytes. Neither copy loop checks the remaining `BufTxt` capacity, and the terminating NUL is also written through the unbounded destination pointer (`Utility.c:137-145`). The line length comes from the loaded file: `load_file()` records the complete span up to each newline in `LINE.size` without a 256-byte limit (`DiskIO.c:392-416`). The selected Ctrl+Enter event path calls `GetIncludeFile()` on the current line and then tries to open the returned path (`Events.c:153-164`).

**Trigger and consequence:** in the Editor, Ctrl+Enter on an `#include` line whose directory prefix plus include name exceeds `BufTxt` capacity (or an angle include name exceeding the remaining capacity after `INCLUDE:`). The path construction writes past the global 256-byte array before `get_full_path()` is called, potentially corrupting adjacent static state or producing a damaged path. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor` target; its dependency from `workbench-tools` is commented out (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`; `workbench/tools/mmakefile.src:7-10`), so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked write and unlimited loaded line length; requires a long include path. Bound both the directory-prefix and filename copies to the destination capacity and reject or safely truncate paths that do not fit. No file, include path, Editor session, or build was used; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor Utility full-body and include-path pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#edit-include-path-fixed-buffer-overflow-gd14775).


<a id="gd14776"></a>
<a id="gd14776-editor-selected-line-indentation-ignores-allocation-failures-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14776 — Editor selected-line indentation ignores allocation failures [explicit optional target]

In the selection branch of `indent_by()`, each applicable line is forced to `WHOLESEL` and passed to `add_char()`, but its Boolean result is discarded; the loop continues and then closes the undo group (`workbench/tools/Edit/Edit.c:376-389`). `add_char()` returns `FALSE` when growing a line buffer fails, without inserting the character (`workbench/tools/Edit/Memory.c:48-64,87-109`). The equivalent non-selection branch checks that result and reports `ERR_NOMEM` (`Edit.c:405-417`), but the selected branch does neither. After the loop, the function unconditionally updates the cursor byte position by `method` for nonzero positions (`:390-410`), even if insertion into the active line failed. Selected indentation is reachable from the Amiga-key+Space/Tab commands and menu Indent (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:66-74,389-393`).

**Trigger and consequence:** indent a selection containing lines that need buffer growth, and an `AllocMem()` for one of those lines fails. That line remains unchanged while other successful line edits stay committed in the undo group; the command gives no allocation error or rollback. If the failed line is the active line and the cursor is past column zero, cursor accounting still advances as if the character had been inserted, so it no longer points to the same text position. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; its parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for the ignored return and mutation/cursor path; requires a line-buffer allocation failure during selected indentation. Check each result and abort/report or roll back the grouped operation before updating cursor state. No edit, allocation failure, Editor session, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor Edit.c full-body and indentation pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#edit-selected-indent-allocation-failure-gd14776).


<a id="gd14777-editor-selected-text-deletion-keeps-failed-line-mutations-in-its-undo-count-path-explicit-optional-target"></a>
<a id="gd14777"></a>
## GD14777 — Editor selected-text deletion keeps failed line mutations in its undo/count path [explicit optional target]

`del_block()` ignores the Boolean results of `rem_chars()` and `join_lines()` for partial-line selections, clears the selection flags, and increments `nbrem` after the join call regardless of its result (`workbench/tools/Edit/Edit.c:302-317`). It later subtracts `nbrem` from `p->max_lines` (`:326-339`). Loaded lines have `max == 0` because `new_line()` initializes it to zero and `load_file()` assigns only `size` and `stream` (`Memory.c:35-43`; `DiskIO.c:407-416`). A partial `rem_chars()` therefore attempts a new line-buffer allocation; it can record the removal in the undo journal before returning `FALSE` if growth fails (`Memory.c:247-260`; `workbench/tools/Edit/UndoRedo.c:218-273`). `join_lines()` likewise records a JOIN_LINE undo entry before trying to grow the first line, and returns `FALSE` on allocation failure without unlinking the second line (`Memory.c:327-352`; `UndoRedo.c:293-307`).

If the join allocation fails after the undo record was made, the original second line remains linked. `del_block()` nevertheless decrements the model's line count. Undo then treats the recorded JOIN_LINE as completed and reinserts `buf->old` after `buf->line` (`UndoRedo.c:531-547`); because that node is already the next line, `InsertAfter()` can create a self-linked node (`Utility.c:160-170`). A failed `rem_chars()` can also leave its recorded deletion inconsistent with the unchanged text, so a later undo may restore duplicate characters. **Trigger and consequence:** cut/delete a multi-line selection with at least one partial boundary, then a line-buffer allocation fails while applying a partial removal or joining the boundary lines. The Editor can show an incorrect line count; if the failed join was journaled, a subsequent undo can corrupt the line list. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; its parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for ignored returns, pre-allocation undo logging, and unconditional line-count adjustment; requires the stated allocation failure. Propagate failures and commit undo records only for mutations that actually complete. No selection, allocation failure, undo operation, Editor session, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor Edit.c full-body and deletion-failure pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#edit-selected-delete-allocation-failure-gd14777).


<a id="gd14778"></a>
<a id="gd14778-editor-case-conversion-dereferences-the-end-of-an-empty-file-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14778 — Editor case conversion dereferences the end of an empty file [explicit optional target]

`read_file()` leaves `args->buffer` NULL when the opened file has size zero, then returns success (`workbench/tools/Edit/DiskIO.c:341-380`). `load_file()` still creates one line and assigns its `stream` from the null `q` pointer with a zero size (`:392-430`); `load_in_project()` accepts that line list and makes it the current project (`workbench/tools/Edit/Project.c:80-95`). With no selection, `change_case()` unconditionally reads `ln->stream[p->nbc]` and passes the result to `change_casechar()` before writing it back (`workbench/tools/Edit/Edit.c:464-468`). The new project cursor starts at character offset zero, and the Editor exposes Upper/Lower/Toggle menu actions (`workbench/tools/Edit/Project.c:64-75,80-95`; `workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:393-395`).

**Trigger and consequence:** open a zero-byte file in the Editor and invoke Upper, Lower, or Toggle with no selection. The current line has a NULL text pointer, so the case command reads through NULL and faults instead of leaving the empty line unchanged. The same unchecked end position also reads/writes past the logical line when invoked with the cursor at `p->nbc == ln->size`; for a loaded final line without a newline, that is one past the file buffer. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; its parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for the zero-length file path and unconditional NULL dereference; requires invoking case conversion on the empty file. Return without changing when the cursor is not on a character, and handle empty loaded buffers without storing a NULL text pointer. No file, Editor command, session, or build was used; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor case-conversion empty-file pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#edit-case-conversion-empty-file-gd14778).


<a id="gd14779"></a>
<a id="gd14779-editor-case-conversion-bypasses-undo-and-modified-state-tracking-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14779 — Editor case conversion bypasses undo and modified-state tracking [explicit optional target]

`change_case()` mutates selected text through `replace_chars()` and a single character through `replace_char()` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Edit.c:438-468`). Both helpers write directly to line storage and do not record an undo operation (`workbench/tools/Edit/Memory.c:230-244`). Unlike normal `add_char()`/`rem_chars()` paths, case conversion does not call the undo registration helpers that run `PRE_CHECK` and set `MODIFIED` (`workbench/tools/Edit/UndoRedo.c:28-33,218-224`). The Upper/Lower/Toggle menu actions dispatch directly to `change_case()` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:393-395`). `close_project()` asks whether to save only through `warn_modif()`, which prompts only when `p->state & MODIFIED` is set (`workbench/tools/Edit/Project.c:480-495`; `Utility.c:324-343`).

**Trigger and consequence:** change the case of at least one letter in a clean project, then close that project without another journaled edit. The text changes in memory but the project remains unmarked and the undo log has no corresponding action; closing it therefore skips the modified-file prompt and discards the case changes. If another edit was already journaled, Undo still skips the case conversion. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; its parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for the direct mutation, missing undo registration and close-prompt state check. Record the old/new bytes in the undo journal and mark the project modified when case conversion changes any character. No edit, undo, close, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor memory helper and case-change tracking pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#edit-memory-helper-case-change-gd14779).


<a id="gd14780"></a>
<a id="gd14780-editor-reload-clears-the-unsaved-marker-before-checking-whether-reload-succeeded-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14780 — Editor Reload clears the unsaved marker before checking whether reload succeeded [explicit optional target]
