`reload_project()` saves the cursor position, calls `unset_modif_mark(p, TRUE)`, then ignores the return from `load_in_project(p, p->path)` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Project.c:189-201`). `unset_modif_mark()` commits and clears the undo state and sets `p->state = 0` (`:368-380`). `load_in_project()` changes the project contents only when `load_file()` succeeds (`:67-83`), so on a read or allocation error the old in-memory text remains while its dirty state and undo history have already been discarded. The Reload menu action is reachable from Open with Shift after `warn_modif()` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:311-320`). Closing a project prompts only when `MODIFIED` is set (`Project.c:480-495`; `Utility.c:324-343`).

**Trigger and consequence:** confirm Reload for a modified project, then have reading the backing path fail (for example, it was removed or became unreadable). The previous in-memory edits remain visible, but the Editor has cleared their undo history and modified marker; a later close can discard them without a save prompt. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for operation ordering and failure behavior; requires reload failure. Preserve the modified state and undo history until a replacement load succeeds, then commit the reload. No reload, file change, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor project lifecycle pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-project-lifecycle-and-file-io-pass-gd14780).

<a id="gd14781"></a>
<a id="gd14781-editor-save-as-clears-the-dirty-state-before-the-save-succeeds-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14781 — Editor Save As clears the dirty state before the save succeeds [explicit optional target]

When Save As or saving a project without a path obtains a destination, `save_project()` calls `set_project_name()` and immediately sets `p->state = 0` before calling `save_file()` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Project.c:263-293`). `save_file()` can fail opening the destination or report write errors and return false (`workbench/tools/Edit/DiskIO.c:232-285`); nevertheless, the project has already lost its `MODIFIED` flag. Closing checks that flag before prompting (`Project.c:480-495`; `Utility.c:324-343`).

**Trigger and consequence:** choose a Save As destination for modified text, then make the write fail, such as by exhausting disk space. The operation reports failure, but the project remains associated with the new destination and is considered clean; closing it can discard the unsaved contents without a prompt. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for the state update before the write and the failure return path; requires a failed Save As. Keep the dirty state until `save_file()` succeeds, and restore/retain the original project path if failure should leave Save As uncommitted. No save, I/O failure, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor project lifecycle pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-project-lifecycle-and-file-io-pass-gd14780).

<a id="gd14782"></a>
<a id="gd14782-editor-save-reports-success-after-a-write-failure-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14782 — Editor save reports success after a write failure [explicit optional target]

In `save_file()`, failures from buffered `FWrite()` calls jump to `wrterr`, display an error, and break the loop; the function then calls `FClose()` without checking its return and unconditionally sets `retval = 1` (`workbench/tools/Edit/DiskIO.c:263-282`). `myFClose()` itself returns false if the final buffered `Write()` fails (`:207-219`), but that result is discarded. The caller `save_project()` treats any nonzero result as success and clears the modified marker (`workbench/tools/Edit/Project.c:286-293`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a disk-full or other write error occurs during a save, including while flushing the final buffer. The Editor displays an I/O error but reports the save as successful to its caller, which clears the dirty state; closing can then discard unsaved text without another prompt, and the destination may contain a truncated file. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for both ignored failure returns and unconditional success; requires a write failure. Propagate write and close errors through `save_file()` and clear the project dirty state only after a complete successful write. No save or I/O failure was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor project lifecycle pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-project-lifecycle-and-file-io-pass-gd14780).

<a id="gd14783"></a>
<a id="gd14783-editor-cut-deletes-selected-text-after-a-failed-clipboard-write-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14783 — Editor Cut deletes selected text after a failed clipboard write [explicit optional target]

`CBWriteFTXT()` checks that `OpenIFF()` succeeded, but ignores `PushChunk()`, every `WriteChunkBytes()`, `PopChunk()`, and `CloseIFF()` result, then returns `TRUE` (`workbench/tools/Edit/ClipLoc.c:115-155`). The IFF writer reports byte counts/errors from `WriteChunkBytes()`; other AROS callers check those results (for example `workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:2385-2386`). The Cut menu action calls `del_block()` whenever `CBWriteFTXT()` returns true (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:358-365`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a clipboard chunk write fails after `OpenIFF()` succeeded. The Editor still treats the clipboard copy as successful and removes the selected text, losing it from the document while the clipboard contains incomplete data. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for ignored writer status and unconditional success; requires an IFF/clipboard write failure. Check each IFF operation and return success only after all selected bytes and chunk finalization succeed. No clipboard operation or failure was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor clipboard and cursor pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-clipboard-and-cursor-pass-gd14783).

<a id="gd14784"></a>
<a id="gd14784-editor-join-and-strip-deletes-the-next-line-after-insertion-fails-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14784 — Editor “join and strip” deletes the next line after insertion fails [explicit optional target]

`join_strip()` attempts to append the non-whitespace part of the next line with `insert_str()`. On failure it displays an out-of-memory error, but then unconditionally calls `del_line()` on that next line and decrements `p->max_lines` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Cursor.c:464-487`). `insert_str()` returns false without inserting when line-buffer growth fails (`workbench/tools/Edit/Memory.c:117-139`).

**Trigger and consequence:** join two nonempty lines where appending the second line requires line-buffer growth, and that allocation fails. The existing first line remains unchanged, but the second line is deleted, losing its content. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for the unchecked failure branch and subsequent deletion; requires allocation failure during append. Abort the operation before deleting the next line when insertion fails, and roll back any preceding inserted separator. No edit or allocation failure was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor clipboard and cursor pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-clipboard-and-cursor-pass-gd14783).

<a id="gd14785"></a>
<a id="gd14785-editor-word-selection-reads-one-byte-past-an-unterminated-final-line-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14785 — Editor word selection reads one byte past an unterminated final line [explicit optional target]

Word-selection adjustment calls `backward_word(ln, find_nbc(ln, p->ccp.startsel))` without ensuring the resulting character index is less than the line length (`workbench/tools/Edit/Edit.c:109-112`). When the mouse endpoint is at or beyond the end of the line, `find_nbc()` returns `ln->size` (`Cursor.c:45-53`). `backward_word()` then forms `ln->stream + pos` and reads `TypeChar[*str]` before reducing the index (`Cursor.c:76-84`). Loaded lines are spans into the exact file buffer, and the final unterminated line ends at the buffer boundary (`DiskIO.c:392-430`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use word-selection mode and place/drag its start endpoint at the end of an unterminated final line. The backward word scan reads one byte beyond the allocated file buffer; the resulting selection boundary is undefined and may fault or select incorrectly. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for the one-past-end index and dereference; requires the stated endpoint on a final line without an EOL byte. Handle `pos == ln->size` by moving to the last valid character before reading, and make the helper enforce its own bounds. No selection or file was used; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor clipboard and cursor pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-clipboard-and-cursor-pass-gd14783).

<a id="gd14786"></a>
<a id="gd14786-editor-paste-reports-success-and-reads-uninitialized-line-counts-after-partial-insertion-failure-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14786 — Editor paste reports success and reads uninitialized line counts after partial insertion failure [explicit optional target]

`CBReadCHRS()` ignores the return from `add_string()`/`add_block()` and sets `ret = TRUE` regardless (`workbench/tools/Edit/ClipLoc.c:189-195`). `add_string()` can return false after inserting earlier parts of a multiline paste if a later `break_line()` or `insert_str()` fails; `buf[2]` is only assigned at the successful end of `add_string()` (`Memory.c:143-170`). The Paste handler trusts the true result, then adds `buf[2]` to `edit->max_lines` and uses the other output fields (`Events.c:367-380`).

**Trigger and consequence:** paste multiline clipboard text and an allocation fails after one or more lines were already inserted. The operation is reported as successful despite partial content, and the caller reads an uninitialized `buf[2]` for the line-count update; the project line count and display/cursor state can become inconsistent. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for the ignored Boolean result and output initialization order; requires allocation failure during a multiline paste. Propagate insertion failure, initialize all output fields, and either roll back the partial paste or return accurate committed counts. No paste or allocation failure was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor clipboard and cursor pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-clipboard-and-cursor-pass-gd14783).

<a id="gd14787"></a>
<a id="gd14787-editor-text-rendering-can-overrun-its-fixed-scratch-buffer-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14787 — Editor text rendering can overrun its fixed scratch buffer [explicit optional target]

The Editor's shared render buffer is `BufTxt[256]` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Jed.c:32`). Its `write_text()` implementation is in `Jed.c:397-440`. It writes visible text and expands tabs with `memset(buf, ' ', ts)` (`:426-434`), but bounds the loop only by `gui.nbcol` and remaining source bytes; it does not cap writes by the remaining `BufTxt` capacity. `gui.nbcol` is calculated from window width and selected font width (`workbench/tools/Edit/Gui.c:214-230`), while the window template allows widths up to `0xffff` and setup can size it to the screen (`Gui.c:127-141,448-461,537-547`). The fixed-width font requester has no width restriction and recalculates the viewport after selection (`Prefs.c:315-329,409-422`). Loaded line spans retain their full length without a 256-byte cap (`DiskIO.c:392-430`).

**Trigger and consequence:** show a line with enough visible characters, or tab-expanded spaces, to reach beyond 256 bytes while the viewport is wider than 256 text columns. `write_text()` then writes beyond `BufTxt`; the tab case can overshoot the viewport as well because the tab expansion is not clipped to the remaining columns. This is an out-of-bounds write in the Editor's render path. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for the unchecked writes and fixed buffer; requires a sufficiently wide viewport and line content reaching the buffer boundary. Bound rendering by both the visible columns and remaining `BufTxt` capacity. No window, font or file was opened; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor GUI, startup, preferences, printing and search pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-gui-startup-preferences-print-and-search-pass-gd14787).

<a id="gd14788"></a>
<a id="gd14788-editor-whole-word-search-reads-past-an-unterminated-final-line-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14788 — Editor whole-word search reads past an unterminated final line [explicit optional target]

After a pattern match, `HilitePattern()` checks `TypeChar[search[len]]` to decide whether the following character is part of a word (`workbench/tools/Edit/Search.c:596-601`). A match that ends exactly at the end of an unterminated final line makes `search + len` point one byte beyond the file buffer: `load_file()` stores line spans directly into the exact-size read buffer and does not add a terminator (`workbench/tools/Edit/DiskIO.c:392-430`). This check is reached when whole-word matching is enabled.

**Trigger and consequence:** enable whole-word search and search for a pattern that ends at the end of an unterminated final line. The boundary check reads past the allocated file contents; the result is undefined and can fault or misclassify the match. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for the one-past-end boundary and unchecked read; requires the stated match at EOF. Treat the line end as a word boundary before accessing the following byte. No search or file was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor GUI, startup, preferences, printing and search pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-gui-startup-preferences-print-and-search-pass-gd14787).

<a id="gd14789"></a>
<a id="gd14789-editor-bracket-matching-dereferences-the-cursor-position-without-checking-line-length-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14789 — Editor bracket matching dereferences the cursor position without checking line length [explicit optional target]

`match_bracket()` reads `p->edited->stream[p->nbc]` before checking whether the cursor is on a character (`workbench/tools/Edit/Search.c:679-687`). The cursor can validly sit at `p->edited->size` at end-of-line; horizontal End sets that position, and loaded final unterminated lines have no storage byte beyond their contents (`Cursor.c:341-360`; `DiskIO.c:392-430`). An empty line can also have a NULL stream.

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke Find Bracket with the cursor at the end of an unterminated final line, or on an empty line. The command reads one byte beyond the line/file buffer, or through a NULL stream, before it can report that no bracket is present. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for the unchecked cursor index; requires the stated cursor position. Check for a valid line buffer and `p->nbc < line->size` before reading. No command or file was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor GUI, startup, preferences, printing and search pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-gui-startup-preferences-print-and-search-pass-gd14787).

<a id="gd14790"></a>
<a id="gd14790-editor-preferences-always-replace-a-selected-parent-screen-with-the-default-public-screen-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14790 — Editor preferences always replace a selected parent screen with the default public screen [explicit optional target]

The parent-screen validation loop initializes both `list` and `first` to `IntuitionBase->ActiveScreen`, then uses `list && list != first` as its loop condition (`workbench/tools/Edit/Prefs.c:449-459`). Since `list == first` at initialization, the body never runs. `first` therefore remains non-NULL and the fallback locks the default public screen, assigning it to `tmpprefs.parent` (`:461-465`) even when the selected parent screen is still present. `update_prefs()` applies this modified preference structure to the Editor (`:487-500`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use a preference set that selects a non-default parent/public screen, then apply preferences while the Editor is using a public screen. The validation path skips checking the selected screen and silently substitutes the default public screen, so the Editor opens on the wrong screen. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for the loop's false initial condition and unconditional fallback; requires selecting a non-default screen. Iterate the screen list starting after the sentinel/current screen, or use a loop whose first iteration checks the initialized entry. No screen or preferences were changed; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor GUI, startup, preferences, printing and search pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-gui-startup-preferences-print-and-search-pass-gd14787).

<a id="gd14791"></a>
<a id="gd14791-editor-preferences-parser-trusts-field-lengths-from-the-file-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14791 — Editor preferences parser trusts field lengths from the file [explicit optional target]

`load_prefs()` walks the preference chunk using a 16-bit `ByteRead`, reads each record's field ID and byte length, and copies `src[1]` bytes into the destination selected by the field ID without validating either the record bounds or the destination field capacity (`workbench/tools/Edit/Prefs.c:204-227`). The known field sizes are available in `sizefields[]`, but the parser does not use them (`:68-76`). A short/corrupt record can also make the parser read the length or data beyond the allocated chunk.

**Trigger and consequence:** load a truncated or malformed Editor preferences file whose record length exceeds its destination field or remaining chunk size. The parser can overwrite adjacent preference state or read beyond the chunk and fail unpredictably while loading preferences. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for unchecked record and field lengths; requires malformed preferences input. Validate each header and payload against remaining chunk bytes and the corresponding field capacity before copying. No preferences file was opened or modified; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor GUI, startup, preferences, printing and search pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-gui-startup-preferences-print-and-search-pass-gd14787).

<a id="gd14792"></a>
<a id="gd14792-editor-search-window-dereferences-gadgets-after-unchecked-allocation-failures-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14792 — Editor search window dereferences gadgets after unchecked allocation failures [explicit optional target]

`setup_winsearch()` checks whether `OpenWindowTags()` succeeds but does not check the results of `CreateContext()` or any `CreateGadget()` call. It immediately passes the first string-gadget pointer to `GetSI()`/`CopyMem()` and later dereferences checkbox gadget pointers (`workbench/tools/Edit/Search.c:170-171,192-204,212-231,240-253`). GadTools creation can fail under memory pressure.

**Trigger and consequence:** open Search or Replace while gadget allocation fails. A NULL gadget is dereferenced during initialization, so the Editor can crash instead of reporting an allocation failure and closing the partial search window. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for unchecked return values and immediate dereferences; requires a failed gadget allocation. Check each creation result and unwind the partially created gadget list and window on failure. No allocation failure or search window was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor GUI, startup, preferences, printing and search pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-gui-startup-preferences-print-and-search-pass-gd14787).

<a id="gd14793"></a>
<a id="gd14793-editor-replace-all-can-loop-forever-when-deletion-fails-for-an-empty-replacement-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14793 — Editor Replace All can loop forever when deletion fails for an empty replacement [explicit optional target]

`ReplaceAllPat()` ignores the return from `rem_chars()` and, when the replacement string is empty, does not advance the cursor before searching again (`workbench/tools/Edit/Search.c:499-524`). `rem_chars()` records the removal before attempting a shrinking reallocation and returns false without changing the text if that allocation fails (`workbench/tools/Edit/Memory.c:247-260`). The next quiet `HilitePattern()` therefore finds the same occurrence again and leaves the cursor at the same offset (`Search.c:505-523,650-653`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run Replace All with an empty replacement on a loaded file while removal-buffer reallocation fails. The matching text remains in place, the search finds it again, and the replacement loop can continue indefinitely without making progress. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-tools-editor`; the parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`). **Confidence:** high for the no-progress loop and failure behavior; requires the stated allocation failure. Stop on mutation failure and report it, or ensure failed deletion advances/aborts rather than retrying the same match. No replacement or allocation failure was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Editor GUI, startup, preferences, printing and search pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#editor-gui-startup-preferences-print-and-search-pass-gd14787).


<a id="gd14794"></a>
<a id="gd14794-icon-35-writer-leaks-an-iffhandle-on-every-serialization-explicit-optional-target"></a>
## GD14794 — Icon 3.5 writer leaks an IFFHandle on every serialization [explicit optional target]

`WriteIcon35()` allocates an `IFFHandle` with `AllocIFF()` and then returns from the function without calling `FreeIFF()` on any path after that allocation (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobj35io.c:947-1066`). `AllocIFF()` allocates and clears an `IntIFFHandle` with `AllocMem()` and documents that its default context node persists until `FreeIFF()` (`workbench/libs/iffparse/allociff.c:25-36,51-72`); `FreeIFF()` releases the context items and that allocation (`freeiff.c:48-75`). The selected `ProcessIcon35()` write hook calls `WriteIcon35()` when `WriteStruct()` serializes OS 3.5 icon data (`workbench/libs/icon/diskobjio.c:991`). The read counterpart frees its allocated handle at `diskobj35io.c:555`, while the writer has no corresponding cleanup.

**Trigger and consequence:** repeatedly save icons that take the OS 3.5 IFF serialization path while `AllocIFF()` succeeds. Each call retains an `IntIFFHandle` allocation, so repeated saves consume memory until the system has less memory available for later operations. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-libs-icon`; its aggregate dependency is commented (`workbench/libs/icon/mmakefile.src:54-66`), so inclusion in a default image is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unmatched allocation and reachable writer call; the amount leaked per save is `sizeof(struct IntIFFHandle)` plus any context allocations not released by the absent `FreeIFF()`. Free the IFF handle on every post-allocation exit, closing the parser first when required. No icon save, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Icon IFF writer allocation cleanup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#icon-iff-writer-allocation-cleanup-pass-gd14794).



<a id="gd14795"></a>
<a id="gd14795-diskfont-cache-entry-count-can-wrap-its-allocation-on-32-bit-builds"></a>
## GD14795 — Diskfont cache entry count can wrap its allocation on 32-bit builds

`ReadDirEntry()` opens the cached font index and passes it to `StreamInFileList()` without validating the records first (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfontfunc.c:576-589`). The reader loads `fe2.Numentries` from the cache as a `ULONG` (`:413-416`), then allocates `fe2.Numentries * sizeof(struct TTextAttr)` bytes (`:420-423`). On a 32-bit target, that multiplication is performed at 32-bit width and can wrap to a small nonzero size. If the small allocation succeeds, the next loop still iterates the original count and writes `attrs[i].tta_Tags` for every entry (`:425-427`), overrunning the allocation before it checks whether the cache contains corresponding attribute records. The cache filename is `FONTS:fontcache` on the AROS path (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfont_intern.h:69-74`); `AllocVec()` can return a non-NULL block for a small nonzero wrapped size (`rom/exec/allocvec.c:40-65`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on a 32-bit build of diskfont.library, font enumeration reads a corrupt `FONTS:fontcache` whose entry count makes the allocation-size multiplication wrap to a small nonzero value. The initialization loop writes beyond the allocated `TTextAttr` array and can corrupt memory or fault before the cache is rejected and rebuilt. **Affected configuration:** 32-bit targets that explicitly build and load `workbench-libs-diskfont` (`workbench/libs/diskfont/mmakefile.src:6-21`); its aggregate edges are commented, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked 32-bit multiplication, allocation result use, and count-controlled initialization loop; requires a malformed cache count and a wrapped allocation that succeeds. Validate the count against the cache's remaining record data and use checked multiplication before allocation. No cache file, font scan, allocation, or build was used; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Diskfont cache parser count-bound pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#diskfont-cache-parser-count-bound-pass-gd14795).



<a id="gd14796"></a>
<a id="gd14796-diskfont-iterator-allocation-failure-leaves-the-font-semaphore-held"></a>
## GD14796 — Diskfont iterator allocation failure leaves the font semaphore held

`AllocResources()` obtains `DiskfontBase->fontssemaphore` before allocating its `DF_Data` iterator state (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfontfunc.c:737-747`). If `AllocMem()` fails, it returns the still-NULL pointer without releasing the semaphore. `DF_IteratorInit()` propagates that NULL (`:895-906`). The selected `OpenDiskFont()` caller detects the failed initialization but only logs it and skips the iterator cleanup branch (`workbench/libs/diskfont/opendiskfont.c:112-117`); consequently no cleanup releases the semaphore. Other diskfont operations that need this semaphore can then remain blocked indefinitely.

**Trigger and consequence:** a diskfont iterator initialization under memory pressure when the semaphore acquisition succeeds but allocation of `DF_Data` fails. The font semaphore remains owned by the caller's task after `OpenDiskFont()` returns, preventing later font-directory scans or opens that need it from progressing. **Affected configuration:** builds that explicitly build and load `workbench-libs-diskfont` (`workbench/libs/diskfont/mmakefile.src:6-21`); default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the acquire-before-allocation ordering, missing release, and selected caller's lack of cleanup; requires the stated allocation failure. Release the semaphore on the allocation-failure path. No allocation failure, font operation, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Diskfont iterator allocation and caller failure paths](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#diskfont-iterator-allocation-and-caller-failure-paths-gd14796).

<a id="gd14797"></a>
<a id="gd14797-diskfont-directory-enumeration-passes-failed-exall-allocations-to-dos"></a>
## GD14797 — Diskfont directory enumeration passes failed ExAll allocations to DOS

`GetFileList()` allocates an `ExAllControl` and a 1,024-byte `ExAllData` buffer, then immediately writes `eac->eac_LastKey` and calls `ExAll()` without checking either allocation (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfontfunc.c:216-231`). `ReadDirEntry()` reaches `GetFileList()` for each font directory while building or refreshing the diskfont directory cache (`:534-573`). If either allocation fails, the function dereferences a NULL control structure or passes a NULL data buffer to `ExAll()` rather than returning a clean enumeration failure.

**Trigger and consequence:** a font-directory scan during memory pressure when `AllocDosObject(DOS_EXALLCONTROL, ...)` or `AllocMem(1024, ...)` fails. The scan can fault in diskfont code or invoke `ExAll()` with an invalid buffer, disrupting font enumeration instead of reporting the failed scan. **Affected configuration:** builds that explicitly build and load `workbench-libs-diskfont` (`workbench/libs/diskfont/mmakefile.src:6-21`). **Confidence:** high for the unchecked nullable results and immediate use; requires either allocation to fail. Check both results and unwind any successful partial allocation before returning failure. No directory scan, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Diskfont iterator allocation and caller failure paths](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#diskfont-iterator-allocation-and-caller-failure-paths-gd14796).

<a id="gd14798"></a>
<a id="gd14798-failed-diskfont-descriptor-reread-leaves-the-process-in-the-fonts-directory"></a>
## GD14798 — Failed diskfont descriptor reread leaves the process in the Fonts directory

In the `DF_FONTSDATA` path, `DF_IteratorRememberOpen()` changes the task's current directory to the remembered font's directory before rereading its descriptor (`workbench/libs/diskfont/diskfontfunc.c:1157-1164`). If `ReadFontDescr()` fails, `RememberAttr` remains NULL and the function returns immediately (`:1164-1179`), bypassing the later `CurrentDir(olddir)` restoration and descriptor cleanup (`:1247-1257`). `OpenDiskFont()` calls this routine after selecting a disk font (`workbench/libs/diskfont/opendiskfont.c:145-153`). Thus a descriptor that cannot be reread after selection causes the caller's task to retain the font directory as its current directory after `OpenDiskFont()` returns.

**Trigger and consequence:** a selected font descriptor becomes unreadable or a read/allocation failure occurs between enumeration and `DF_IteratorRememberOpen()`'s second read. The font open fails and subsequent relative DOS operations in that task resolve from the font directory instead of the caller's prior directory. **Affected configuration:** builds that explicitly build and load `workbench-libs-diskfont` (`workbench/libs/diskfont/mmakefile.src:6-21`). **Confidence:** high for the changed-directory early return and selected call path; requires the descriptor reread to fail after the directory change. Route all post-`CurrentDir()` exits through cleanup that restores the saved directory and frees any partial descriptor state. No font was opened and no current directory was changed; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Diskfont iterator allocation and caller failure paths](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#diskfont-iterator-allocation-and-caller-failure-paths-gd14796).


<a id="gd14799"></a>
## GD14799 — More writes before its buffer after a non-seekable read error [selected Workbench utility]

`OpenFile()` treats a failed end seek as a non-seekable stream and requests up to 65,536 bytes (`workbench/utilities/More/more.c:357-364`). It only rejects a short or failed `Read()` when `seekable` is true (`:384-390`). DOS `Read()` returns `-1` on failure (`rom/dos/read.c:47-68`). If a non-seekable handler returns that error, execution assigns `-1` to `new_filelen` and writes the terminator at `new_filebuffer[-1]` (`more.c:392-393`); the subsequent `while (flen--)` also starts from a negative count (`:397-404`).

**Trigger and consequence:** open a non-seekable source in More whose read operation fails before returning data. The error is treated as a length, causing an out-of-bounds byte write before the allocated buffer and then invalid negative-length processing, so the viewer can corrupt memory or fail while opening the source. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected `workbench-utilities-more` program (`workbench/utilities/More/mmakefile.src:11-16`); selected through the active `workbench-utilities` and `workbench-complete` dependencies. **Confidence:** high for DOS's `-1` error result and the unchecked non-seekable branch; requires an underlying read error. Reject every negative `Read()` result before using it as a length. No stream or read failure was exercised; source-only.

**Coverage:** [More file input, line indexing and event-loop review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#more-file-input-line-indexing-and-event-loop-review-gd14799).

<a id="gd14800"></a>
## GD14800 — More line-array allocation can wrap on 32-bit builds

`OpenFile()` counts every newline into signed 32-bit `new_num_lines` (`workbench/utilities/More/more.c:399-404`) and allocates `new_num_lines * sizeof(struct LineNode)` without checked multiplication (`:406`). `LineNode` contains a 32-bit pointer and two `UWORD`s plus a `BOOL` (`:96-102`); on 32-bit AROS its aligned size is 12 bytes. For a file with enough lines, the 32-bit allocation-size product wraps; if the wrapped nonzero allocation succeeds, the initialization loop still writes one `LineNode` per original line (`:423-446`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on a 32-bit build, open a sufficiently large newline-dense file for which `new_num_lines * 12` exceeds the 32-bit allocation-size range and wraps to a small nonzero size. The line-initialization loop then writes beyond the undersized array and can corrupt memory or fault. **Affected configuration:** 32-bit builds of the Workbench-selected `workbench-utilities-more` target (`workbench/utilities/More/mmakefile.src:11-16`); selected through the active `workbench-utilities` and `workbench-complete` dependencies. **Confidence:** high for unchecked multiplication and the count-controlled writes; requires a file large enough for wraparound and successful allocation of the wrapped size. Check the multiplication before allocation and reject unrepresentable line counts. No large file, allocation, or build was used; source-only.

**Coverage:** [More file input, line indexing and event-loop review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#more-file-input-line-indexing-and-event-loop-review-gd14799).

<a id="gd14801"></a>
## GD14801 — More discards keyboard commands while tracking a scrollbar

`HandleScrollGadget()` waits on the window port and drains every queued `IntuiMessage`, but its switch handles only gadget-up, mouse-move and (when compiled) refresh events; every other message is replied to and discarded (`workbench/utilities/More/more.c:1150-1183`). The window explicitly requests `IDCMP_VANILLAKEY`, and the normal `HandleWin()` loop treats Escape as a quit command (`:806-819,1315-1321,1400-1414`). `HandleWin()` calls the nested tracker after a scrollbar gadget-down (`:1332-1341`).

**Trigger and consequence:** press Escape while a horizontal or vertical scrollbar is being dragged, before the gadget-up ends the nested tracking loop. The Escape message is consumed by `HandleScrollGadget()` instead of reaching `HandleWin()`, so the documented keyboard quit action is lost for that keypress and the viewer remains open. Other unrelated IDCMP classes queued during tracking are likewise dropped. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected `workbench-utilities-more` target (`workbench/utilities/More/mmakefile.src:11-16`); selected through the active `workbench-utilities` and `workbench-complete` dependencies. **Confidence:** high for the nested queue drain and outer Escape handling; requires Escape to be delivered during scrollbar tracking. Preserve or dispatch non-tracking messages instead of replying to them as unhandled. No GUI input was generated; source-only.

**Coverage:** [More file input, line indexing and event-loop review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#more-file-input-line-indexing-and-event-loop-review-gd14799).


<a id="gd14802"></a>
## GD14802 — More Find requester copies a 257-byte string into a 256-byte buffer [selected Workbench utility]

The Find requester creates its string gadget with `GTST_MaxChars, 256` (`workbench/utilities/More/req.c:303-304`) and later copies the gadget string into the static `searchtext[256]` array (`:62,383-389`). GadTools converts `GTST_MaxChars` to `STRINGA_MaxChars` by adding one for the terminating NUL (`workbench/libs/gadtools/stringclass.c:80-88`); its comment explicitly distinguishes the character count from the trailing zero. A 256-character search string is therefore accepted as 257 bytes including NUL, and `strcpy()` writes that terminator one byte beyond `searchtext`.

**Trigger and consequence:** enter exactly 256 characters in More's Find field and activate Find/Next. The copy writes one byte past the static search buffer, corrupting adjacent program data and potentially changing subsequent search or UI behavior. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected `workbench-utilities-more` target (`workbench/utilities/More/mmakefile.src:6-16`); selected through the active `workbench-utilities` and `workbench-complete` dependencies. **Confidence:** high for the buffer sizes, GadTools max-character semantics and unbounded copy; requires a maximum-length search. Allocate `GTST_MaxChars + 1` bytes or copy with an explicit destination bound and terminator. No requester input was entered; source-only.

**Coverage:** [More selected companion sources: requesters, locale and menus](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#more-selected-companion-sources-requesters-locale-and-menus-gd14802).

<a id="gd14803"></a>
## GD14803 — More truncates long paths returned by its file requester [selected Workbench utility]

`GetFile()` stores the selected full path in a static 108-byte `filebuffer`, copies at most 107 bytes from the ASL drawer, and calls `AddPart()` with a capacity of 107 without checking its result (`workbench/utilities/More/misc.c:103-108,133-138`). The selected ASL requester supports a drawer buffer of `MAX_PATH_LEN` 1,025 bytes and a filename buffer of `MAX_FILE_LEN` 257 bytes (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqhooks.h:37-39`; requester gadgets at `filereqhooks.c:878-880`). The helper then returns the possibly truncated path; the Open menu passes it to `OpenFile()` (`workbench/utilities/More/more.c:1555-1560`).

**Trigger and consequence:** select a valid path whose drawer plus filename exceeds 107 bytes. `GetFile()` returns a truncated path, so More attempts to open a different or nonexistent name instead of the selected file; the caller does not report that the returned path was shortened. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected `workbench-utilities-more` target (`workbench/utilities/More/mmakefile.src:6-16`); selected through the active `workbench-utilities` and `workbench-complete` dependencies. **Confidence:** high for the 108-byte destination, larger ASL path capacities and unchecked `AddPart()` result; requires a selection exceeding the helper buffer. Build the result in a buffer sized for the ASL contract or detect and report truncation. No file requester was opened; source-only.

**Coverage:** [More selected companion sources: requesters, locale and menus](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#more-selected-companion-sources-requesters-locale-and-menus-gd14802).

<a id="gd14804"></a>
<a id="gd14804-sound-datatype-indexes-past-its-validity-flags-when-one-shot-playback-ends"></a>
## GD14804 — Sound datatype indexes past its validity flags when one-shot playback ends

`SoundFunc()` uses `sfd->Sound` as an index into the two-element `Valid` array, then assigns `AHI_NOSOUND` to `snd` for non-continuous playback and immediately checks `sfd->Valid[snd]` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:3544-3552`). `AHI_NOSOUND` is `0xffff` (`workbench/devs/AHI/Include/C/devices/ahi.h:288`), so this terminal one-shot branch reads far beyond `Valid[2]` from the AHI sound callback. The callback is invoked when a sample reaches end of sound (`workbench/devs/AHI/Device/mixer.c:721-727`), and `PlayerProcAHI()` installs this hook for non-continuous samples with nonzero `SDTA_Cycles` (`dispatch.c:3958-3963`).

**Trigger and consequence:** play a non-continuous sample with `SDTA_Cycles` nonzero until the callback reaches its stop branch. The out-of-range read can use unrelated memory as the validity flag and may fault; it also makes the subsequent stop/restart decision depend on data outside the array. Guard `AHI_NOSOUND` before indexing `Valid`, or represent the no-sound state separately. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatypes-sound` when AHI playback is selected; its parent aggregate edge is commented, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the sentinel value, two-element array and callback path; no playback was run. Source-only.

**Coverage:** [Sound datatype AHI worker recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-ahia-worker-recheck-gd14804).

<a id="gd14805-stereo-sound-datatype-playback-truncates-large-cycle-counts"></a>
<a id="gd14805"></a>
## GD14805 — Stereo Sound.datatype playback truncates large cycle counts

`SDTA_Cycles` is stored as a `UWORD` in `InstanceData`, and the AHI worker initializes both `SoundFuncData.Cycles` and `CyclesLeft` from `UMult(id->Cycles, numCh)` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:990-994,3918-3923`). Both destination fields are also `UWORD` (`:3511-3512`). For stereo, `numCh` is 2, so any accepted cycle count above 32,767 exceeds the counter range; 32,768 wraps the product to zero. `SoundFunc()` uses this counter to decide when to stop or switch sounds (`:3544-3561`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use AHI playback for a stereo sample with `SDTA_Cycles` greater than 32,767. The per-channel callback count wraps before playback starts; at 32,768 the first end-of-sound callback takes the counter's zero branch, so playback can stop far earlier than requested. Use a counter wide enough for the product or validate/reject cycle counts that cannot be represented. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-datatypes-sound` when stereo AHI playback is selected; the module's parent aggregate edge is commented, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the input narrowing, product, counter widths and callback use; exact callback timing is delegated to AHI. No playback or build was run. Source-only.

**Coverage:** [Sound datatype AHI worker recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#sound-datatype-ahia-worker-recheck-gd14804).


<a id="gd14806"></a>
<a id="gd14806-vc4-mesa-bo-cache-timeout-uses-adjustable-wall-time-conditional"></a>
## GD14806 — VC4 Mesa BO-cache timeout uses adjustable wall time [conditional]

The Raspberry Pi Mesa shim defines `clock_gettime()` at `workbench/libs/mesa/aros_drm_shim.c:282-291`. It ignores `clk_id`, calls DOS `DateStamp()`, and converts that value into `timespec` (`:284-289`). `DateStamp()` obtains its value from `GetSysTime()` (`rom/dos/datestamp.c:59-68`), which is the settable system clock; AROS's POSIX implementation instead implements `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` with `GetUpTime()` (`compiler/crt/posixc/clock_gettime.c:78-86`), whose contract says it cannot be changed (`rom/timer/getuptime.c:34-41`). The shim itself says this clock is used for BO-cache timeout (`aros_drm_shim.c:275-276`).

**Trigger and consequence:** in the Raspberry Pi VC4 Mesa path, a BO-cache timeout is measured across a system-clock adjustment. A backward adjustment makes elapsed time appear shorter and can retain cached buffers past their timeout; a forward adjustment makes them expire early, causing unnecessary resource churn. This is a timeout/caching correctness issue; no data-corruption consequence is established. The fetched Mesa caller that chooses the clock is outside this checkout, so the exact call sequence remains conditional. Honor `clk_id` and use `GetUpTime()` for monotonic requests.

**Affected configuration:** optional Raspberry Pi ARM `mesa3dgl`/`vc4gallium` target; `aros_drm_shim.c` is included under the `raspi` Mesa source gate (`workbench/libs/mesa/mmakefile.src:43-54`) and directly in the VC4 HIDD source list (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vc4gallium/mmakefile.src:99-106`). Default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the wall-clock/monotonic mismatch and medium for caller impact because the fetched Mesa caller source is absent. No clock adjustment, BO operation, build, or runtime test was performed; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [VC4 Mesa clock shim source and clock-contract trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vc4-mesa-bo-timeout-clock-source-review-gd14806).


<a id="gd14807"></a>
<a id="gd14807-mesa-stdc-base-resolver-races-across-concurrent-tasks-conditional"></a>
## GD14807 — Mesa StdC base resolver races across concurrent tasks [conditional]

`__aros_getbase_StdCBase()` in `workbench/libs/mesa/aros_drm_shim.c:129-144` caches one `stdcbase` and one `stdctask` in unsynchronized static variables. When the caller changes, it opens a per-task `stdc.library` base and writes the two globals separately, then returns the shared `stdcbase`. There is no lock, interrupt exclusion, or per-task slot. This resolver is called by ordinary StdC functions such as `strtok()` and `rand()` (`compiler/crt/stdc/strtok.c:72-82`; `rand.c:42-47`), whose base contains task-specific state such as `last` and `srand_seed` (`compiler/crt/stdc/__stdc_intbase.h:45-51,73-75`). The shim comment says it exists to redirect Mesa's libc calls through the correct per-task base (`:118-127`).

**Trigger and consequence:** two AROS tasks concurrently call Mesa paths that use StdC. If task A is preempted after writing `stdcbase`/`stdctask` but before the helper returns, task B can replace the pair; when A resumes, it returns B's base. A's subsequent StdC call then reads or updates B's supposedly per-task state, so operations such as `strtok()` can continue another task's tokenization state and `rand()` can share the other task's sequence. Keep the resolver state per task or synchronize lookup, update, and returned-base selection. **Affected configuration:** optional Raspberry Pi ARM Mesa3DGL/VC4, for external clients using the shared GL module concurrently from multiple tasks; no default-image inclusion or checked-in concurrent client is claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unsynchronized shared-state race and wrong-base return; medium for external concurrent-client reachability. No task schedule, GL call, build, or runtime test was exercised; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Mesa StdC resolver concurrency trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mesa-stdc-base-resolver-concurrency-recheck-gd14807).

<a id="gd14808"></a>
## GD14808 — chunky pixel writes can read before the source array after clipping [conditional]

`do_render_with_gc()` keeps the source-array x/y offsets in signed `WORD` variables and adds the distance clipped from the requested rectangle (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:110,123-140,169-180`). The shared write callback uses that offset directly in pointer arithmetic on the caller's buffer (`:680-689`; `CHUNKY8_COORD_TO_BYTEIDX` at `rom/graphics/graphics_intern.h:295-296`). For example, `WritePixelArray8()` can be called with `xstart=-32768`, `xstop=0`; the API documents a padded source row of 32,784 bytes for that 32,769-pixel range (`rom/graphics/writepixelarray8.c:16-45,71-74`). A layerless destination bitmap is clipped to its own bounds even without an explicit clip: `BITMAP_CLIPPING` is enabled and `GetRPClipRectangleForBitMap()` substitutes the bitmap rectangle when the RastPort has no clip rectangle (`rom/graphics/graphics_intern.h:41`; `gfxfuncsupport.c:1064-1087`). Thus a one-pixel-wide bitmap clips this request to x=0, and the 32,768 offset is assigned back to signed `WORD srcx`, which becomes -32768 on targets that retain the low 16 bits. The callback then forms `array - 32768` and passes it to `HIDD_BM_PutImageLUT()`. The selected generic HIDD method reads from `pixarray[0]` when converting the one-pixel clipped rectangle (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:3924-3951`). `WriteChunkyPixels()` and the CGFX `WritePixels8()` vector share the same helper (`rom/graphics/writechunkypixels.c:61-70`; `rom/graphics/cgx_support.c:16-25`). The transparent text-rendering callback has the same pointer arithmetic shape (`gfxfuncsupport.c:743-754`; `text.c:739-743`), but its raster width and destination extent are held in signed `WORD` values (`text.c:561-563,582-589`), so this trace did not establish a clipped offset greater than `WORD_MAX` for that caller. This source-side read-before-array defect is distinct from GD2662, where the analogous narrowed offset makes `ReadPixelArray8()` write before its output buffer.

**Trigger and consequence:** a chunky pixel write has a clipped source offset greater than `WORD_MAX`; a destination bitmap beginning at x=0 and a request beginning at -32768 provide a source-supported example. On conventional targets where conversion to `WORD` keeps the low 16 bits, the HIDD reads bytes before the caller's array to draw the visible clipped pixels. This can select incorrect pen values or fault if the computed source address is inaccessible. **Affected configuration:** graphics.library's shared chunky-write path, including `WritePixelArray8()`, `WriteChunkyPixels()`, and `WritePixels8()` callers, on targets with the described signed-WORD narrowing. The tracked caller census did not establish an in-tree caller using this extreme clipped offset; public API clients can supply it. **Confidence:** high for the narrow-before-index source path and selected generic HIDD read; medium for exact manifestation because conversion and address accessibility depend on target/compiler and allocation placement. Preserve clipped offsets in a wide type and validate source row bounds before forming the pointer. No pixel transfer, bitmap, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#graphics-chunky-pixel-write-clipped-source-offset-gd14808).



<a id="gd14809"></a>
## GD14809 withdrawn — duplicate Vulkan-Hpp query helper coverage

GD14809 duplicated two earlier findings: its unwritten scalar on `VK_NOT_READY` case is covered by the GD10223 query-pool addendum, and its unrestricted `queryCount` with one-object storage case is covered by the GD10235 typed-output helper addendum. Those entries retain the command contract, triggers, and consequences. This ID remains as a compatibility anchor for prior ledger and index links; do not count it as a separate bug.

<a id="gd14811"></a>
## GD14811 — Vulkan GPU re-registration replaces callbacks behind live handles [conditional]

`VulkanRegisterGPU()` treats an entry with the same PCI BDF/vendor/device as an idempotent match, then overwrites its `callbacks`, `driver_data`, `class_id`, and other mutable fields without checking `use_count` or requiring the incoming provider to match the current one (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/vulkan_intern.h:134-148,160-187`). The existing entry keeps its `use_count` and remains eligible for selection. Vulkan HIDD methods resolve the preferred entry for each call (`vulkan_class.c:27-30`); for example, `CreateDevice()` creates a handle using the selected callback, while `DestroyDevice()` later invokes whichever `DestroyDevice` callback is currently stored in the selected entry (`:177-217`). The loader passes the opaque handle through and carries no provider identity (`vulkan_loader.c:554-608`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a Vulkan driver registers a card, creates Vulkan objects/devices, and then another registration for the same BDF/vendor/device refreshes that registry entry with different callbacks or `driver_data`, while that entry remains the preferred entry for subsequent calls (for example, it is the only registered GPU). Later operations on the existing handles are routed to the replacement provider; destruction can be sent to a backend that did not create the handle, and the original provider may retain its resources. This differs from GD10214: that finding covers selection moving between distinct GPU entries as use counts change, while this one covers mutation of the same registry entry during re-registration.

**Affected configuration:** optional `hidd-vulkan` plus one or more external/provider HIDDs calling the exported `VulkanHidd_RegisterGPU()`; repository-wide search found no checked-in provider callsite, so no current in-tree trigger or default-image exposure is claimed. The registration routine explicitly supports repeated scans of the same BDF, but the source tree does not establish that a live device exists when a replacement registration occurs.

**Confidence:** high that the existing slot's dispatch state can be replaced while its use count remains nonzero, and that subsequent methods re-read that state; medium that a provider/client sequence reaches this state and causes handle misuse. Reject provider replacement while `use_count != 0`, or retain provider identity per Vulkan object/device and dispatch destruction through its creator. No registration, GPU object, Vulkan call, or build was exercised; source-only; see the [registration and dispatch recheck](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-registry-live-handle-reregistration-gd14811).

<a id="gd14812"></a>
## GD14812 — MUIScreen can miss AutoClose registration before its worker initializes [conditional]

`libInit()` launches the AutoClose task with `AddTask()` and returns success without waiting for the task to create `muisb_taskMsgPort` (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/muiscreen_init.c:20-53,56-96`). The task initializes that field only when it starts and successfully calls `CreateMsgPort()` (`:70-71`). `MUIS_OpenPubScreen()` allocates an AutoClose node and supplies `SA_PubTask`/`SA_PubSig` only when that field is already non-NULL (`workbench/libs/muiscreen/openpubscreen.c:60-75`); otherwise it still opens and returns the public screen without any AutoClose registration (`:89-118`). `AddTask()` makes the worker ready but does not guarantee that an equal- or higher-priority caller yields to it before the next library call (`rom/exec/newaddtask.c:25-75,325-329`). Thus a caller can open an AutoClose screen immediately after MUIScreen initialization but before the worker publishes its port, and that screen is permanently omitted from `muisb_autocScreens` and lacks the owner task/signal setup.

**Trigger and consequence:** MUIScreen is initialized, then an `AutoClose` screen is opened before the worker has created and published its message port. The screen opens successfully but never receives AutoClose tracking, so it can remain open after its windows and visitors are gone. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting MUIScreen and using `MUIS_OpenPubScreen()` with `AutoClose` during this startup window. **Confidence:** high for the missing readiness handshake and conditional behavior; the startup interleaving was not run. Initialize and publish the port before `libInit()` reports success, or make open wait/fail until the worker is ready. No screen, task, or build was run; source-only; see the [worker readiness trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#muiscreen-autoclose-worker-startup-readiness-gd14812).



<a id="gd14813"></a>
## GD14813 — GL library initialization dereferences a failed notification-path allocation [explicit optional target]

`GetGLVarPath()` allocates storage for the filesystem notification path, then unconditionally formats into the returned pointer (`workbench/libs/gl/gl_init.c:91-108`). When `ENV:SYS` exists and `NameFromLock()` succeeds, an `AllocVec()` failure leaves `GLB(base)->glb_Notify.nr_Name` NULL and the following `sprintf()` writes through NULL. The helper is called during `LibInit()` via `SetupGLVarNotification()` (`:154-185,190-228`), before the library reports successful initialization. The explicit GL target selects this body; its parent aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/libs/gl/mmakefile.src:1-31`).

**Trigger and consequence:** initialize the optional pass-through `gl.library` with an accessible `ENV:SYS` directory and fail the notification-path allocation. The initialization path calls `sprintf(NULL, ...)`, so library initialization can fault instead of completing cleanly. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-libs-gl`, when the directory lookup succeeds and the path allocation fails. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation and immediate write; requires that conditional allocation failure. Check the allocation result before formatting and leave notification setup disabled if storage is unavailable. No allocation failure, library initialization or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage:** [GL pass-through library full-body and notification setup pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gl-pass-through-library-full-body-and-notification-setup-gd14813).


<a id="gd14814"></a>
## GD14814 — Lamp draws with pen 255 when MUI cannot obtain its PenSpec pen [conditional]

`Lamp__MUIM_Draw()` stores the result of `MUI_ObtainPen()` in `lmp_PenNr` and unconditionally passes `MUIPEN(lmp_PenNr)` to `SetAPen()` in the `PCH_NEWSPEC` branch (`workbench/classes/zune/lamp/lamp.c:316-320`). `MUI_ObtainPen()` initializes its return value to `-1` and returns that value when PenSpec conversion or setup fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_obtainpen.c:52-60`). The `MUIPEN` macro masks to the low 16 bits (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui.h:175-177`), and `SetAPen()` accepts a `UBYTE` and stores it as the RastPort foreground pen (`rom/graphics/setapen.c:16-23,53-55`), so `MUIPEN(-1)` becomes pen 255. `Lamp__MUIM_Draw()` then immediately calls `RectFill()` using that RastPort (`lamp.c:327-338`).

**Trigger and consequence:** while the Lamp is set up, set `MUIA_Lamp_PenSpec` to a PenSpec that cannot be converted or resolved (the setter marks `PCH_NEWSPEC` and requests redraw at `lamp.c:178-182`), or one whose RGB pen cannot be allocated/found, then draw the Lamp. The failure value is not checked, so the lamp background is drawn with foreground pen 255 rather than retaining or choosing a valid fallback pen. The visible result depends on the screen depth and graphics backend; the source establishes the invalid fallback selection, not a particular hardware rendering artifact. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable `workbench-classes-zune-lamp` target (`workbench/classes/zune/lamp/mmakefile.src:1-17`); no default-image inclusion is claimed. **Confidence:** high for unchecked failure propagation and pen narrowing; medium for user-visible rendering because backend handling of pen 255 varies. Check for `-1` before `SetAPen()` and define a fallback or skip drawing. No PenSpec failure or draw was run; source-only; see the [MUI pen caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#lamp-mui-penspec-failure-caller-gd14814).

**Coverage:** [Lamp MUI PenSpec failure caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#lamp-mui-penspec-failure-caller-gd14814).


<a id="gd14815"></a>
## GD14815 — Window render-info storage drops MUI pen allocation flags and leaks allocated pens [conditional]

`MUI_ObtainPen()` encodes an allocation marker in bit 16 of its `LONG` result when the underlying PenSpec setup allocated a colormap pen (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_obtainpen.c:61-68`). `MUI_ReleasePen()` calls graphics `ReleasePen()` only when that marker remains set (`mui_releasepen.c:45-51`). Window setup stores these results directly into `mri_PensStorage`, whose element type is `UWORD` (`classes/window.h:380`), and cleanup later passes those narrowed values back to `MUI_ReleasePen()` (`classes/window.c:368-409,582-599`). The marker therefore cannot survive storage in this array. The generated half-shine and half-shadow RGB specs are passed through `MUI_ObtainPen()` when their configured specs are empty (`:383-407`), so successful `ObtainBestPenA()` allocations have this lifetime mismatch.

**Trigger and consequence:** set up a Window whose half-shine or half-shadow RGB PenSpec causes `ObtainBestPenA()` to allocate a colormap pen. Its encoded result is truncated to 16 bits in `mri_PensStorage`; on Window cleanup, `MUI_ReleasePen()` sees no allocation marker and does not release it. Repeated Window setup/cleanup can retain allocated colormap pens. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable muimaster; the default half-shine/half-shadow RGB-spec path is selected when those preference specs are empty. **Confidence:** high for marker truncation and skipped release; allocation depends on the active colormap and `ObtainBestPenA()` result. Preserve the allocation marker in storage or track allocation state separately, while keeping the public `mri_Pens` values limited to pen numbers. No Window, pen allocation, cleanup, or build was run; source-only; see the [Window render-info pen ownership trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#window-render-info-pen-ownership-gd14815).

**Coverage:** [Window render-info pen ownership trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#window-render-info-pen-ownership-gd14815).


<a id="gd14816"></a>
## GD14816 — VulkanProbe can report the RX 9060 XT milestone after testing another GPU [explicit optional target]

`VulkanProbe` searches the enumerated physical-device properties for vendor/device `1002:7590`, but when none matches it logs that the 9060 XT was not found and sets `amdIndex = 0` anyway (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/test/VulkanProbe.c:104-125`). It then queries queue families and creates the logical device using `devs[amdIndex]` (`:127-172`). If that fallback device has a compute queue and device creation succeeds, the unconditional success message still says the logical device and queue were created “on the 9060” (`:188-190`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional probe runs on a configuration where Vulkan enumerates at least one non-9060 device that supports compute and accepts device creation, but the RX 9060 XT is absent. The program exits successfully while falsely claiming that the 9060-specific driver path was validated. **Affected configuration:** explicitly building/running `hidd-vulkan-vulkanprobe`; the target exists in `workbench/hidds/vulkan/mmakefile.src:45-56`, while its aggregate edge is commented at `:58`, so no default-image inclusion is claimed. **Confidence:** high for the false-success control flow; the alternative-GPU condition is configuration-dependent. Treat missing target hardware as failure (or clearly report a generic fallback result) and gate the 9060 success message on a matching device. No Vulkan call, GPU, or build was exercised; source-only; see the [VulkanProbe source review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkanprobe-device-selection-and-library-lifetime-gd14816-gd14817).

<a id="gd14817"></a>
## GD14817 — VulkanProbe leaves its `radeonsi.hidd` library reference open [explicit optional target]

`main()` calls `OpenLibrary("radeonsi.hidd", 0)` and stores the returned base only in a block-local variable (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/test/VulkanProbe.c:50-56`). There is no `CloseLibrary()` call on either the success or any later early-return path in the function (`:34-196`). Exec's `OpenLibrary()` invokes the library's Open vector (`rom/exec/openlibrary.c:81-92`), while `CloseLibrary()` is the corresponding operation that invokes its close vector (`rom/exec/closelibrary.c:64-83`). DOS `Exit()` explicitly closes its own DOS library reference, not arbitrary libraries opened by the process (`rom/dos/exit.c:83-91`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional probe successfully opens `radeonsi.hidd` and then returns through any path. Its open reference remains outstanding after process termination, so the driver may remain resident and its close/expunge lifecycle is not completed; repeated probe runs can retain additional opens. **Affected configuration:** explicitly building/running `hidd-vulkan-vulkanprobe` when `radeonsi.hidd` can be opened; no default-image inclusion is claimed. **Confidence:** high that the successful open is never paired and normal DOS exit does not close arbitrary library references; whether that prevents unloading depends on the driver's lifecycle and load configuration. Retain the base for cleanup and close it on all return paths after Vulkan objects that depend on it are destroyed. No library was opened and no build was run; source-only; see the [VulkanProbe source review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkanprobe-device-selection-and-library-lifetime-gd14816-gd14817).


<a id="gd14818"></a>
## GD14818 — Gallium HIDD exposes a WinSys attribute macro with no backing attribute ID [conditional]

`workbench/hidds/gallium/include/gallium.h` declares only `aoHidd_Gallium_InterfaceVersion` and `aoHidd_Gallium_CoreAPI` in its attribute enum (`:51-57`), but then defines `aHidd_Gallium_WinSys` in terms of the undeclared `aoHidd_Gallium_WinSys` (`:59-61`). A checkout-wide search found no in-tree use of either WinSys identifier; the concrete Gallium classes and `gallium.library` use the declared InterfaceVersion/CoreAPI attributes.

**Trigger and consequence:** a consumer uses the advertised `aHidd_Gallium_WinSys` macro. The preprocessor expands it to an undeclared C identifier and compilation fails; if a consumer supplies its own coincidentally named definition, it can instead calculate an attribute ID not represented by this interface's `num_Hidd_Gallium_Attrs`. **Affected configuration:** consumers including the Gallium HIDD header from an explicitly selected Gallium-capable build; the generic `hidd-gallium` aggregate edge is commented in `workbench/hidds/gallium/mmakefile.src:25-26`, so default inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the header inconsistency and compile failure when the macro is used without an external definition; no current checked-in callsite was found. Either declare and implement the WinSys attribute as part of the interface or remove the stale macro. No build was run; source-only; see the [Gallium interface and subclass pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#gallium-hidd-interface-and-subclass-pass-gd14818).


<a id="gd14819"></a>
## GD14819 — CreatePipe can return a stale caller-supplied driver pointer after creation fails [conditional]

`CreatePipe()` uses the caller's `CPS_PipeScreenDriver` storage when supplied (`workbench/libs/gallium/createpipe.c:76-84`), but never initializes `*driver` before trying the display-specific and fallback creation paths. If neither path assigns a new object, the final `return *driver` at `:116-140` returns whatever value the caller's storage held on entry. The documented tag is an output location (“where to store the driver”), not an input driver handle (`:48-51`). The checked-in Mesa caller uses a zero-cleared context allocation before passing `&ctx->driver` (`workbench/libs/mesa/mesa3dgl_glacreatecontext.c:129-135`), so that client does not establish the stale-value trigger.

**Trigger and consequence:** an external caller supplies a valid output pointer whose current value is non-NULL, then driver selection and fallback object construction both fail. `CreatePipe()` returns the stale pointer as if it were a successfully created pipe; subsequent callers may dispatch methods or destroy it as a live object. **Affected configuration:** clients of the explicitly buildable `gallium.library` that pass pre-populated driver output storage and encounter pipe-creation failure; the library's aggregate edge is commented, so default availability is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the uninitialized output and returned stale value; no checked-in client with nonzero initial storage was found. Set `*driver = NULL` immediately after validating the output pointer, before any path can fail. No object construction or build was run; source-only; see the [CreatePipe output and failure-path trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#createpipe-output-pointer-and-failure-path-recheck-gd14819).


<a id="gd14820"></a>
## GD14820 — Mesa frees GL contexts without disposing their Gallium driver objects [conditional]

`mesa3dgl_glacreatecontext.c` creates a Gallium HIDD object through `CreatePipeV()` and stores it in `ctx->driver` (`:115-155`). The active context teardown destroys the state tracker and pipe screen, then frees the Mesa context (`mesa3dgl_gladestroycontext.c:59-66`; `mesa3dgl_gallium.c:351-362`), but never calls `DestroyPipe(ctx->driver)`. A checkout-wide search finds only one Mesa `DestroyPipe()` call, in `glacreatecontext.c:177` inside `#if (0)`. The creation error path after pipe creation also frees the context without disposing the driver (`glacreatecontext.c:153-167,216-219`); even the state-manager allocation failure explicitly destroys the pipe screen but leaves the `DestroyPipe()` call disabled (`:172-179`). Concrete Gallium HIDD `Root.Dispose` methods inspected for LLVMPipe, Softpipe and VMware SVGA delegate to their superclass; they do not provide implicit cleanup in lieu of `OOP_DisposeObject()`.

**Trigger and consequence:** a GL context is created far enough for `CreatePipeV()` to return a driver object, and then the context is normally destroyed or a later creation stage fails. The driver OOP object is never disposed, so its object allocation and associated class/object lifetime remain retained; repeated context create/destroy cycles accumulate these objects. **Affected configuration:** Mesa3DGL builds with Gallium support and any selected Gallium HIDD, including the checked-in normal context path; no claim is made for builds that omit Mesa3DGL. **Confidence:** high that creation is paired with no active disposal call and that `DestroyPipe()` is the public disposal API; the exact retained memory/class-reference consequence follows from the OOP object's undisposed lifetime. Dispose the driver after its pipe screen on both normal and every post-creation failure path. No GL context or build was run; source-only; see the [Mesa Gallium pipe lifetime trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mesa-gallium-pipe-lifetime-and-context-teardown-gd14820).


<a id="gd14821"></a>
## GD14821 — Jano Editor frees a queued startup request when its Ctrl-C wait is interrupted [conditional; explicit optional target]

When a Jano Editor instance is already running, `find_janoed()` allocates a private reply port and I/O request, stores the second instance's `StartUpArgs *` in the request, posts it to the public Jano port, then waits on either the reply-port signal or Ctrl-C (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:437-455`). If Ctrl-C wakes the wait before the running instance replies, the following `GetMsg(port)` can return no message, but `find_janoed()` still returns true and `main()` calls `cleanup()` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Jed.c:64-67`). `close_port()` immediately calls `DeleteExtIO(cmd)` and then removes/deletes the private reply port (`Events.c:495-500`); `DeleteExtIO()` frees the request storage (`compiler/alib/deleteextio.c:42-52`). Cleanup also frees `args.sa_ArgLst` (`Jed.c:120-128`). The running instance later dequeues the still-published request in `handle_port()`, reads its `CMD_NEWEDIT` argument pointer, operates on it, and replies (`Events.c:503-537`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a second Editor instance finds the running Jano port, queues `CMD_NEWEDIT`, and receives Ctrl-C before the first instance dequeues and replies. The sender frees both the queued request and its referenced startup argument list; the receiver may then read freed request/argument storage and eventually reply to a deleted port. **Affected configuration:** explicitly building/running `workbench-tools-editor` with another Jano Editor instance active and Ctrl-C interrupting the duplicate-instance wait; the target is not connected to the aggregate tool target by an active edge (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`), so default inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the cancellation cleanup sequence and continued receiver ownership of the queued message; the timing interleaving was not run. On interruption, remove/cancel the message from the remote queue if still pending and wait for completion before freeing its request or arguments; alternatively keep all referenced storage alive until the reply is received. No Editor, message, signal, or build was run; source-only; see the [Jano startup request and cancellation trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#jano-editor-startup-request-cancellation-gd14821).


<a id="gd14822"></a>
## GD14822 — Jano cleanup reuses its freed IPC request and reply port to notify Preferences Editor [conditional; explicit optional target]

`cleanup()` destroys the Editor's IPC objects before calling `CloseMainWnd()` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Jed.c:120-124`). `close_port()` frees `cmd` with `DeleteExtIO()` and removes/frees `port` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:495-500`; `compiler/alib/deleteextio.c:42-52`; `compiler/alib/deleteport.c:42-46`). `CloseMainWnd()` then unconditionally calls `send_pref(&prefs, CMD_KILL)` (`workbench/tools/Edit/Gui.c:578-582`). If `FindPort(JANOPREFS_PORT)` succeeds, `send_pref()` writes through the stale `cmd`, copies the preferences into it, posts it, and reads the stale `port->mp_SigBit` to wait (`Events.c:480-492`).

The same unguarded call occurs on the required-library-open failure path before `create_port()` has run (`workbench/tools/Edit/Jed.c:76-95,111-124`); if the Preferences port exists then, `send_pref()` dereferences the still-NULL `cmd`.

**Trigger and consequence:** Jano Editor enters `cleanup()` while the Preferences Editor still publishes `JANOPREFS_PORT`. The cleanup frees the private request and reply port, then the later shutdown notification dereferences those freed objects; this can fault or send through invalid message storage before the Editor exits. **Affected configuration:** explicitly building/running `workbench-tools-editor` with the Preferences Editor active at cleanup; the Editor target's aggregate edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`), so default inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for cleanup ordering, the frees, and the later stale-pointer dereferences; no cleanup path was run. Send the notification before freeing the IPC objects, or guard/recreate a valid request/reply port for the shutdown message. No Editor or message port was used; source-only; see the [Editor IPC cleanup-order trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#jano-editor-cleanup-ipc-use-after-free-gd14822).


<a id="gd14823"></a>
## GD14823 — Jano Editor retries deletion of a port freed after request allocation fails [conditional; explicit optional target]

`create_port()` stores the new message port in the global `port`, publishes it with `AddPort()`, and then allocates the `JPacket` request (`workbench/tools/Edit/Events.c:463-474`). If `CreateIORequest()` fails, it calls `DeletePort(port)` but leaves the global pointer unchanged. `DeletePort()` removes a port only when `mp_Node.ln_Name` is non-NULL, then calls `DeleteMsgPort()` to free its signal and storage (`compiler/alib/deleteport.c:42-46`). `AddPort()` enqueues every port regardless of name (`rom/exec/addport.c:49-71`). On normal startup, `PortName` is non-NULL, so the rollback removes and frees the port but leaves global `port` stale; the caller ignores the zero return (`workbench/tools/Edit/Jed.c:94-97`), and common cleanup calls `RemPort(port)` and `DeleteMsgPort(port)` again (`Jed.c:120-124`; `Events.c:495-500`). On the duplicate-instance path, `find_janoed()` first sets `PortName = NULL` (`Events.c:441-445`); if request allocation then fails, `DeletePort()` frees the still-enqueued private port without unlinking it, leaving a freed node in Exec's port list until cleanup attempts to remove it.

**Trigger and consequence:** Jano Editor creates its message port but `CreateIORequest()` cannot allocate the request. The first cleanup path then operates on the already-freed port, risking invalid list manipulation and a second free; cleanup may be reached after project setup or GUI setup fails as well as after normal execution. **Affected configuration:** explicitly building/running `workbench-tools-editor` with message-port creation succeeding and request allocation failing; the target's aggregate makefile edge is commented (`workbench/tools/Edit/mmakefile.src:12-17`), so default inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the stale global pointer and duplicate deletion; allocator and runtime behavior were not exercised. Clear `port` after `DeletePort()` or centralize ownership so cleanup only deletes a successfully created port. No allocation failure, port operation, or build was run; source-only; see the [Jano port-allocation rollback trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#jano-editor-port-allocation-rollback-gd14823).


<a id="gd14824"></a>
## GD14824 — clippingtest reports setup failures with a successful exit status [conditional; explicit test target]

`Cleanup()` prints a supplied error message, closes any opened window/libraries, frees parsed arguments, then unconditionally calls `exit(0)` (`developer/debug/test/layers/clippingtest.c:35-50`). All setup failures use this path: required library-open failures in `OpenLibs()`, argument parsing failure, `OpenWindowTags()` failure, and `NewRegion()` failure (`:59-83,85-106,126-127`). The normal path also calls `Cleanup(0)` and exits with the same status (`:189-196`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run the explicit `test-layers` `clippingtest` program in a context that judges success from its process status, then cause one of its startup or region-allocation steps to fail. The program prints an error but exits zero, so a script or test harness can count a test that never ran as passed. **Affected configuration:** the optional `test-layers` target (`developer/debug/test/layers/mmakefile.src:3-7`); no claim is made that a checked-in harness invokes this program or relies on its exit status. **Confidence:** high that all error paths return status zero; medium for downstream impact because no selected automated caller was found. Return a nonzero status for error cleanup while preserving zero for normal completion. No program, failure, or build was run; source-only; see the [test-layers helper re-review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#test-layers-helper-re-review-gd14824).


<a id="gd14825"></a>
## GD14825 — PopupMenu can wait forever when Intuition cannot queue a resize action
