PM_ResizeWindow() enables IDCMP_NEWSIZE, calls ChangeWindowBox(), then waits unconditionally on the window's UserPort (workbench/libs/popupmenu/window.c:132-143). The public Intuition function posts its resize action asynchronously through DoASyncAction() but ignores the Boolean result (rom/intuition/changewindowbox.c:67-83). For callers outside the InputDeviceTask, DoASyncAction() must allocate an action record from ActionsMemPool; on allocation failure it returns FALSE without queueing or executing the resize (rom/intuition/inputhandler_actions.c:642-672). The normal resize action is what calls DoMoveSizeWindow(..., TRUE, ...), which publishes IDCMP_NEWSIZE (changewindowbox.c:90-112; inputhandler_actions.c:528-538). Therefore no message arrives to release PopupMenu's WaitPort().

The resize path is reached when a popup submenu/window already exists: PM_OpenPopupWindow() calls PM_ResizeWindow() for an existing pull-down or submenu (workbench/libs/popupmenu/pm.c:406-431), while PM_OpenPopupMenuA() runs PM_DoPopup() synchronously in the caller (:921-924,1081-1084).

**Trigger and consequence:** on an explicitly built PopupMenu library, a non-InputDeviceTask caller opens a nested menu that resizes an existing popup window while Intuition's action-pool allocation fails and the popup UserPort has no earlier queued message. ChangeWindowBox() returns without a queued resize/NEWSIZE message and PM_ResizeWindow() blocks indefinitely in WaitPort(), leaving the menu caller stuck. **Affected configuration:** explicit workbench-libs-popupmenu module builds; its aggregate build edge is commented, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the ignored failure result and unconditional wait; requires the resize path and action-pool allocation failure. Check ChangeWindowBox()'s result or use a completion mechanism with failure handling before waiting. No allocation failure, popup, window resize or build was exercised; source-only.


<a id="gd14826"></a>
## GD14826 — PopupMenu sorted insertion never finds an insertion point [conditional; explicit optional library]

`PM_FindSortedInsertPoint()` tests `PM_String_Compare(pm->Title, fm->Title) < 0` (`workbench/libs/popupmenu/pmfind.c:163-173`). `PM_String_Compare()` is declared and defined to return `ULONG`, accumulating character differences in an unsigned value (`pmmem.h:27`; `pmmem.c:66-75`). In C, that unsigned result cannot be less than zero, so the condition is always false. `PM_InsertMenuItemA()` uses this search for `PM_InsertSub_Sorted`; when it returns NULL, the insertion branch does nothing but the function still increments and returns its insertion count (`pm.c:1188-1197`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a caller uses `PM_InsertSub_Sorted` to insert a menu item. The API reports the item as inserted although it is not linked into the menu, and sorted insertion never takes effect. A repository-wide search found the API implementation and public declaration but no checked-in caller of this tag, so no current in-tree menu behavior is claimed. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built PopupMenu library, when used by an external or future client; its aggregate build edge is commented, so no default-image inclusion is claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unsigned comparison and false success count; caller reachability is external-only in the current tree. Return a signed comparison result or test its sign without relying on a negative `ULONG`. No PopupMenu call or build was run; source-only; see the [support-helper source pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-support-helpers-sorted-insertion-and-shadow-list-pass).

<a id="gd14829"></a>
## GD14829 — PopupMenu truncates custom image heights when sizing rows [conditional; explicit optional library]

For checkmark, submenu, and command-key images, `PM_ItemHeight()` stores `PM_Image_Height()` in a `UBYTE` before comparing it with the row height (`workbench/libs/popupmenu/pmlayout.c:26-36`). The backing image height is a `UWORD`, so a height above 255 wraps modulo 256; for example 256 becomes zero. The row is then sized from the font and spacing, while `PM_NewDrawItem()` draws the full custom image.

**Trigger and consequence:** a PopupMenu item has a custom image or icon taller than 255 pixels. Layout underestimates the row height, so the image can overlap adjacent items or be clipped. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built PopupMenu library. **Confidence:** high for the narrowing and layout/draw mismatch; the trigger requires unusually tall client-supplied image data. Use a `UWORD` temporary for image height. No menu layout or drawing was run; source-only; see the [layout and topology calculation pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-layout-and-topology-calculation-pass).

<a id="gd14830"></a>
## GD14830 — PopupMenu pull-down layout underflows when item minimums exceed the available bar height [conditional; explicit optional library]

`PM_LayoutMenu()` first computes the full minimum height of a vertical menu, but then replaces the pull-down root height with the screen bar height (`workbench/libs/popupmenu/pmlayout.c:398-424,435-445`). In `PM_LayoutGroup()`, the remaining distributable height is a `UWORD`; it subtracts each fixed-size or minimum-size child height without checking whether the total exceeds the available height (`:254-279`). If the menu has more minimum-height content than the bar can hold, this subtraction wraps. The subsequent equal-distribution pass assigns the wrapped remainder to flexible items (`:298-319`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a pull-down menu contains enough fixed/minimum-height content that its total minimum height exceeds the selected screen bar height. The available-height calculation wraps, and flexible rows can receive incorrect oversized heights and positions. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built PopupMenu library with a pull-down menu. **Confidence:** high for the unsigned subtraction and violated capacity condition; the amount of visible layout damage depends on menu contents and screen geometry. Detect the over-capacity case before distribution and apply a defined clipping/overflow policy. No menu layout or GUI operation was run; source-only; see the [layout and topology calculation pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-layout-and-topology-calculation-pass).


<a id="gd14832"></a>
## GD14832 — PopupMenu real-shadow shading swaps red and blue fields for BGR 15/16-bit pixels [conditional; non-AROS CyberGraphX path]

In `shadefunc()`, the `PIXFMT_BGR16` branch reads the low 5-bit field with `M16BLUE()` into `tr`, adds the red adjustment, then writes it to the high red-position field; it reads the high `M16RED()` field into `tb`, adds the blue adjustment, and writes that into the low field (`workbench/libs/popupmenu/pmdrawshadow.c:200-219`). The documented BGR16 layout places blue in the high field and red in the low field (`workbench/libs/cgfx/include/cybergraphics.h` pixel-format documentation in `writepixelarray.c:88-92`). The BGR15 branch repeats the same field reversal (`pmdrawshadow.c:284-303`; format definition at `writepixelarray.c:80-84`). The 24/32-bit BGR branches keep channel offsets in their corresponding byte positions.

**Trigger and consequence:** build/run PopupMenu on a non-AROS target where the CyberGraphX `DoCDrawMethodTagList()` real-shadow branch is enabled, with a BGR15/BGR16 bitmap and a real shadow. Each shaded pixel has its red and blue fields exchanged in addition to applying the configured offsets, producing incorrect shadow colors. **Affected configuration:** non-AROS builds of the optional PopupMenu library with CyberGraphX real shadows; the AROS build excludes this branch with `#ifndef __AROS__`. **Confidence:** high for the packed-field mismatch; the platform path is explicitly conditional. Keep channel extraction, adjustment, and packing in the same format positions. No bitmap or shadow was rendered; source-only; see the [real-shadow pixel-format pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-real-shadow-pixelformat-pass).


<a id="gd14833"></a>
## GD14833 — Clearing PopupMenu disabled state also clears an independent no-select setting [conditional; explicit optional library]

`PM_NoSelect` records its state in `NPM_NOSELECT` (`workbench/libs/popupmenu/pmtags.c:100-106`), while `PM_Disabled` also sets `NPM_NOSELECT` when disabling an item. Setting `PM_Disabled` to FALSE clears both `NPM_DISABLED` and `NPM_NOSELECT` (`:169-173`), with no check for an independently requested no-select state. The public tag describes `PM_NoSelect` as making the item unselectable, and `PM_Disabled` separately as disabling it (`compiler/include/libraries/pm.h:105-106`).

**Trigger and consequence:** create or configure an item with `PM_NoSelect=TRUE`, then clear/set `PM_Disabled=FALSE`. The item loses its independent unselectable state and can be selected. The same occurs when re-enabling an item that was both disabled and explicitly no-select. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built PopupMenu library. **Confidence:** high for the overlapping flag mutation and distinct public tag meanings. Track disabled and no-select state independently, or preserve no-select when only clearing disabled state. No tag operation or popup was run; source-only; see the [attribute-vector review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-item-attribute-full-body-and-aliasing-pass).


<a id="gd14835"></a>
## GD14835 — CyberGraphX initialization failure releases HIDD attribute bases twice [conditional; explicit optional library]

`cgfx_init()` obtains six HIDD attribute bases. If any acquisition fails or the shared pixel buffer cannot be allocated, it calls `ReleaseAttrBases()` and returns FALSE (`workbench/libs/cgfx/cybergraphics_init.c:35-42,47-70`). AROS library-init rollback then calls registered EXPUNGELIB callbacks after an INITLIB callback fails (`compiler/autoinit/functions.c:60-69`). The registered `cgfx_expunge()` calls `ReleaseAttrBases()` again, and the global base pointers are not cleared after the first release (`cybergraphics_init.c:12-26,69-78`). `OOP_ReleaseAttrBase()` decrements a shared IID refcount and removes/frees its bucket when the count reaches zero (`rom/oop/releaseattrbase.c:56-59`; `rom/oop/support.c:181-203`).

**Trigger and consequence:** CyberGraphX initialization partially acquires one or more bases, then a later base or `pixel_buf` allocation fails, while another subsystem holds one of the same HIDD bases. Rollback decrements the other subsystem's reference a second time and can remove the shared attribute-ID bucket prematurely, leaving that subsystem's HIDD attribute IDs invalid. **Affected configuration:** explicit CyberGraphX library initialization failure with shared HIDD attribute-base users. **Confidence:** high for the two cleanup calls and shared refcount behavior; the effect requires a partial initialization failure and another holder. Clear each successfully released base or rely on the expunge callback for rollback, but not both. No library initialization failure or HIDD user was induced; source-only; see the [CyberGraphX init rollback pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#cybergraphics-library-init-rollback-pass).

<a id="gd14836"></a>
## GD14836 — TextEditor demo indexes before its file buffer on read error [optional demo]

Both TextEditor demo variants store the result of `Read()` in signed `LONG size` and immediately write `text[size] = '\0'` without checking for `-1` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/demo/TextEditor-Demo.c:385-396`; `TextEditor-Demo-Toolbar.c:264-274`). `Read()` explicitly returns `-1` on an I/O error (`rom/dos/read.c:29-34,59-64`). In that case the terminator write targets one byte before the allocated 300 KiB buffer, and the value is subsequently used as the file content length/bound. **Trigger and consequence:** launch either demo with a readable file whose read operation fails after open (for example, a device/filesystem read error); the demo writes out of bounds and can corrupt adjacent memory or fault. The AROS demo target selects `TextEditor-Demo.c`; the toolbar variant is a separate legacy source and is not selected by its current `mmakefile.src`. **Confidence:** high for the negative return contract and unchecked signed index; manifestation depends on the failed-read context. Check for `size < 0` before indexing or processing. No read failure or demo execution was induced; source-only.

<a id="gd14837"></a>
## GD14837 — TextEditor demo's SkipHeader option scans past a file with no newline [optional demo]

When `SkipHeader` is enabled, both demo variants first test `buffer < &text[size]` in the outer loop but the nested loop advances until it sees `\n` without checking the same bound (`TextEditor-Demo.c:397-403`; `TextEditor-Demo-Toolbar.c:276-282`). For a non-empty file containing no newline, the nested scan passes the buffer's terminating NUL and continues reading beyond the input allocation until an unrelated newline is found. **Trigger and consequence:** run the demo with `SkipHeader` and a file whose contents have no newline. The scan reads out of bounds and can fault; if it finds a later newline, the subsequent import begins at an unrelated address. The AROS demo target selects `TextEditor-Demo.c`; the toolbar variant is a separate legacy source not selected by its current `mmakefile.src`. **Confidence:** high for the unbounded inner loop and no-newline condition. Bound the inner scan and handle end-of-buffer. No demo or malformed file was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14838"></a>
## GD14838 — TextEditor MCP fails to parse the AmigaOS 4 Menu key name

On AmigaOS 4, `key_menu` is included in the `enum Keys` and `menu/S` is present in the `ReadArgs()` template (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcp/KeyStorage.c:83-87,120-125`). `ConvertKeyString()` checks that argument under the misspelled preprocessor condition `__amigso4__` rather than the defined `__amigaos4__` (`:241-248`), so the `RAWKEY_MENU` assignment is compiled out. `KeyToString()` does emit the `menu` token for `RAWKEY_MENU` on AmigaOS 4 (`:403-407`), and the preferences update path reparses that string through `ConvertKeyString()` (`CreatePrefsGroup.c:229-270`). **Trigger and consequence:** on an AmigaOS 4 build of the optional TextEditor MCP, select a keybinding for the Menu raw key and acknowledge it or change its action. The displayed `menu` token parses to the initialized zero key instead of `RAWKEY_MENU`, so the saved keybinding is lost or changed. **Confidence:** high for the conditional typo and asymmetric parse/format mapping; the optional target's active build selection depends on the external AmigaOS 4 build. Use the matching `__amigaos4__` condition. No AmigaOS 4 build or preferences operation was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14839"></a>
## GD14839 — TextEditor MCP leaks LocaleBase when AmigaOS 4 interface acquisition fails [conditional; optional MCP]

`ClassInit()` assigns the successful `OpenLibrary("locale.library", 38)` result to `LocaleBase` and then tests `GETINTERFACE(ILocale, ...)` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcp/library.c:154-158`). On AmigaOS 4, the selected macro calls `GetInterface()` and can fail (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/include/mcc_common.h:52-53`). If that happens, the `if` body is skipped and the function returns `FALSE` without closing `LocaleBase` (`library.c:188-193`). The shared MCP startup then deletes the outer custom class and closes its own dependencies but does not call `ClassExpunge()` on failed `ClassInit()` (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/include/mccinit.c:761-791,794-818`); normal `LocaleBase` cleanup exists only in `ClassExpunge()` (`mcp/library.c:197-208`). **Trigger and consequence:** on an AmigaOS 4 build of the optional TextEditor MCP, `OpenLibrary()` succeeds but `GetInterface()` fails during initialization. The failed module initialization retains one Locale library reference per attempt. This does not apply to the AROS branch, where `GETINTERFACE` is a `TRUE` macro. **Confidence:** high for the unbalanced open and failed-init rollback path; requires the interface-acquisition failure. Close the opened base on the failed-interface branch. No AmigaOS 4 initialization or interface failure was induced; source-only.


<a id="gd14841"></a>
## GD14841 — TextEditor MCP debug memory tracker truncates long allocation aliases [conditional; DEBUG build]

`matchAllocFunc()` splits each `|`-separated free-function list into `char tmp[16]`, truncating aliases longer than 15 characters before exact comparison (`workbench/classes/zune/texteditor/mcp/Debug.c:518-528`). In the AmigaOS 4 debug wrappers, this affects more than directory contexts (`mcp/Debug.h:162-174`): `AllocDosObjectTags` and `ExamineObjectTags` are both in the `FreeDosObject` alias list, `AllocSysObjectTags` is in the `FreeSysObject` alias list, and `ObtainDirContext`/`ObtainDirContextTags` are in the `ReleaseDirContext` alias list. Each listed long alias is truncated before comparison, so correctly paired frees of those tracked allocations fail the exact-name check. The MorphOS branch has the same failure for `AllocSysObjectTags`/`FreeSysObject` and the directory-context wrappers (`:381-424`); its `FreeDosObject` wrapper has the long alias in its free list but does not wrap a corresponding `AllocDosObjectTags` call. `_UNMEMTRACK()` removes the tracking node but increments `DbgUnsuitableFreeCount` and emits a false unsuitable-free warning (`Debug.c:553-575`); cleanup reports the count (`:640-643`).

**Trigger and consequence:** in a DEBUG TextEditor MCP build with memory tracking enabled, release an object tracked through any affected long alias, such as a directory context or an AllocDosObjectTags, ExamineObjectTags, or AllocSysObjectTags allocation, then clean up debugging. The tracker emits a false warning and reports an incorrect unsuitable-free count; the underlying allocation/release API pair remains correct. **Affected configuration:** optional TextEditor MCP `DEBUG` builds using the AmigaOS 4 or MorphOS wrapper branch, with `DBC_MTRACK` enabled (it is enabled in the default debug-class mask). **Confidence:** high for the alias truncation and false diagnostic. Compare alias lengths without truncation (or size the buffer from the token length). No debug build or directory operation was run; source-only; see the [debug memory-tracker pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#texteditor-mcp-debug-memory-tracker-pass).


<a id="gd14842"></a>
## GD14842 — BetterString and HotkeyString demos dereference failed custom-class creation

The optional test program assigns the result of MUI_CreateCustomClass() to mcc but does not check it before using mcc->mcc_Class in the first custom-string gadget (workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/BetterString-Test.c:115-132; further uses follow at lines 143 and later). The selected implementation explicitly returns NULL when the requested superclass is unavailable or its custom-class/class allocation fails (workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_createcustomclass.c:49-70); another checked-in custom-class caller checks the result before proceeding (workbench/libs/muimaster/customclasses.h:35-54).

The separate optional HotkeyString test has the same unchecked result and dereferences mcc->mcc_Class while building its first custom gadget (workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/hotkeystring/HotkeyString-Test.c:78-99); its own test target is explicit in mcc/hotkeystring/mmakefile.src:23 and the parent aggregate edge is commented. The same MUI_CreateCustomClass() failure condition therefore affects both test executables.

**Confidence:** high for the unchecked nullable result and dereference; occurrence requires the class creation failure. Check mcc and take the normal cleanup/exit path before building the object tree. No class creation failure, demo run, or build was induced; source-only.

<a id="gd14843"></a>
## GD14843 — BetterString and HotkeyString demos skip class cleanup after application creation fails

After successfully creating its Area.mui custom class, the demo constructs the application object (workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/BetterString-Test.c:115-117). It only calls MUI_DeleteCustomClass(mcc) inside if(app) (:300-303). If ApplicationObject returns NULL, control skips both application disposal and custom-class deletion, then closes the library and returns (:305-311). The selected MUI_DeleteCustomClass() implementation frees the custom class and its superclass reference (workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_deletecustomclass.c:45-64); the class is a separately allocated object created through MUI_CreateCustomClass().

**Trigger and consequence:** custom-class creation succeeds, but ApplicationObject construction fails. The test exits without deleting the custom class, leaving its registered class and associated allocation unreleased by this code path. **Affected configuration:** explicit BetterString test-program target when MUI application construction fails. 
The separate optional HotkeyString test also encloses MUI_DeleteCustomClass(mcc) inside if(app) (workbench/classes/zune/betterstring/mcc/hotkeystring/HotkeyString-Test.c:78-79,148-151), so successful custom-class creation followed by application-construction failure skips the same cleanup. Its target is explicit in mcc/hotkeystring/mmakefile.src:23.

**Confidence:** high for the omitted cleanup and corresponding release operation; lifetime of the retained class past the subsequent MUI library close was not exercised. Move custom-class cleanup to a common exit path after any successfully created application has been disposed. No allocation failure, class lifecycle, demo run, or build was induced; source-only.

<a id="gd14846"></a>
## GD14846 — X11 clipboard reader does not validate returned text type [candidate]

The X11 reader requests `UTF8_STRING` in `XConvertSelection()` but does not validate the type/encoding of the selection owner's response. In both the initial `SelectionNotify` path and the INCR `PropertyNotify` path, it requests `AnyPropertyType` and checks only `actual_format == 8` before copying bytes and replying success (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11_clipboard.c:108-120,190-262,321-343`). A response carrying an unsupported or inconsistent 8-bit type is therefore returned to the caller as though it were UTF-8 text. ICCCM requires a selection conversion to return a type appropriate to the requested target, but that type need not always equal the target atom; the reader needs to validate the allowed result types rather than assume any 8-bit property is text in the requested encoding.

**Trigger and consequence:** hosted X11 receives a clipboard conversion response whose property has format 8 but an unsupported type/encoding for the requested `UTF8_STRING` target (or `INCR` for the initial marker). The read completes successfully with bytes whose encoding/meaning does not match the requested target. The only checked-in client of the `HOST_CLIPBOARD` port is the `hostcb` debug program, which copies a successful result into the AROS text clipboard (`developer/debug/test/misc/hostcb.c:118-121,146-184`; the explicit test target is listed in `developer/debug/test/misc/mmakefile.src:17`). MUI’s ordinary text clipboard uses `OpenClipboard()` directly (`workbench/libs/muimaster/clipboard.c:64-95`), so no standard MUI paste consequence is claimed. **Affected configuration:** hosted X11 HIDD with an external `HOST_CLIPBOARD` client; the checked-in client is an explicit diagnostic target. **Confidence:** high for the missing type validation and success path; whether an external owner emits such a protocol-invalid response is conditional. Validate the property type against the supported encodings on normal and incremental paths and fail the request on a mismatch. No clipboard owner or transfer was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd14847"></a>
## GD14847 — X11 incremental clipboard reader rejects a valid empty transfer [conditional]

In the INCR `PropertyNotify` path, the reader treats a property with `bytes_after == 0` as the final chunk and reports success only when `hostclipboard_incrbuffer` is non-NULL (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11_clipboard.c:302-316`). It allocates that buffer only in the other branch, when `bytes_after != 0` (`:318-345`). Thus, if an owner sends an empty 8-bit final property before any nonempty chunk, the reader replies failure even though the transfer completed successfully with zero bytes. ICCCM's INCR requestor procedure uses a zero-length property to signal completion ([ICCCM §2.7.2](https://www.x.org/archive/current/doc/xorg-docs/icccm/icccm.pdf)).

**Affected configuration and trigger:** hosted X11 receives a valid INCR response for an empty text selection, with the first data property zero-length. **Consequence:** the async clipboard read reports failure instead of returning an allocated empty string; the checked-in `hostcb` consumer treats this as a command failure (`developer/debug/test/misc/hostcb.c:139-181`). **Confidence:** high for the branch behavior and protocol completion marker; availability of an empty INCR response depends on the external selection owner choosing INCR for that transfer. Treat an initial zero-length chunk as a successful empty buffer and terminate the transfer normally. No owner or transfer was exercised; source-only.


<a id="gd14848"></a>
## GD14848 — Rectangle image titles leak image-spec state on repeated size queries [conditional]

`zune_text_get_bounds()` assigns a newly created image-spec object directly to `chunk_node->image` whenever it measures an image chunk (`workbench/libs/muimaster/textengine.c:583-592`). It does not clean up an existing `image` first. The only cleanup for this state is in `zune_text_destroy()`, which calls `zune_imspec_cleanup()` for the currently stored pointer (`textengine.c:181-200`). The Rectangle class constructs and retains its parsed title text at Setup, calls `zune_text_get_bounds()` from `MUIM_AskMinMax`, and destroys the text at Cleanup (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/rectangle.c:149-164,205-209`). `zune_imspec_setup()` allocates the spec and may load datatype pictures or pens; cleanup disposes those resources (`workbench/libs/muimaster/imspec.c:463-490,573-625`). The text parser accepts embedded `\33I[...]` image specs (`textengine.c:323-342`), while `MUIA_Rectangle_BarTitle` is a string attribute (`classes/rectangle.h:19`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a Rectangle bar title contains an image spec and its persistent text object is measured repeatedly. Each measurement replaces the prior image-spec pointer, so the prior parsed spec and any resources it owns become unreachable and remain allocated. **Affected configuration:** MUI Rectangle objects using image-spec title strings and receiving repeated `MUIM_AskMinMax` calls; a source-wide census of all 15 direct `zune_text_get_bounds()` call sites found Rectangle is the only caller that remeasures the same retained `ZText`; checked-in `MUIA_Rectangle_BarTitle`/`MUIO_BarTitle` callers use plain text, so no in-tree image-title trigger was established. **Confidence:** high for the overwrite and missing release; use of an image spec in a bar title is conditional. Reuse the existing image-spec state or clean it up before replacing it. No Rectangle object, image decode, allocation or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd14849"></a>
## GD14849 — MUI text clients dereference failed parsed-text allocations [conditional]

`zune_text_new()` returns `NULL` when allocating its `ZText` object or duplicated content fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/textengine.c:120-130`). Several selected callers retain or immediately use that result without handling failure:

- Rectangle setup assigns the result and still returns `TRUE`; `MUIM_AskMinMax` passes the NULL pointer to a bounds helper that returns safely, then dereferences it for width and height (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/rectangle.c:149-155,205-210`).
- MUI Text's `setup_text()` assigns the result and calls the bounds helper; its `MUIM_AskMinMax` later unconditionally reads `data->ztext->height` and `->width` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/text.c:237-254,313-336`).
- Register setup assigns each label's result and calls the bounds helper. When `register_truncate_titles` is false, the same setup then dereferences each `items[i].ztext->width` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/register.c:499-519`). With truncation enabled, this trace did not establish a subsequent dereference of the failed label object.

**Trigger and consequence:** allocation of a displayed title or label fails, followed by the corresponding size/setup path. Rectangle and Text can dereference NULL during sizing; Register can do so during setup when title truncation is disabled. These failures can fault before the MUI object is laid out. **Affected configuration:** MUI Rectangle, Text, and Register classes; Register's direct setup fault additionally requires `register_truncate_titles == FALSE`. **Confidence:** high for the checked failure returns and use sites; trigger requires allocation failure. Propagate parse/allocation failure or make each caller handle a missing `ZText` before reading it. Source-only; no allocation failure, object setup, layout or build was exercised.

<a id="gd14850"></a>
## GD14850 — MUI text parser returns incomplete objects after internal allocation failure [conditional]

`zune_text_parse_line()` returns `NULL` if allocating its `ZTextLine` fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/textengine.c:480-494`), but `zune_text_new()` treats every NULL as normal end-of-input, breaks its parse loop, and returns the allocated `ZText` containing only the earlier lines (`textengine.c:157-175`). The parser also ignores failures from `zune_text_chunk_new()`: that helper silently returns when allocating the chunk fails and frees the chunk without reporting failure when its string allocation fails (`textengine.c:218-227,254-265`). `zune_text_parse_line()` continues and returns the line, so the enclosing `ZText` remains non-NULL with the failed chunk missing. Callers therefore cannot use the existing NULL result to distinguish a fully parsed string from a truncated one.

The image escape has another unchecked allocation. For `\33I[...]`, `parse_escape_code()` temporarily terminates the image spec at `]`, assigns `StrDup(s)` to `zc->imspec`, restores the bracket, and creates the chunk without checking whether the duplication succeeded (`textengine.c:323-342`). If it fails, `zune_text_chunk_new()` takes its ordinary-text branch; because `text_start` still points at the opening `[`, it copies the text only up to `zc->text` (the closing bracket), leaving a literal `[` and spec text while omitting `]` and the image. This is a silent malformed-text fallback.

**Trigger and consequence:** while parsing nonempty text, allocation of a line, chunk, chunk string, or image-spec copy fails. `zune_text_new()` can return a non-NULL object with later input or a chunk silently absent; image-spec duplication failure instead turns the marker into truncated literal text. Callers proceed to size or draw incomplete or malformed content. **Affected configuration:** all MUI classes using the shared text engine; image-spec consequence requires `\33I[...]`; triggers require internal allocation failure. **Confidence:** high that these failure branches and fallback are present; runtime visibility was not exercised. Propagate internal allocation failure to `zune_text_new()` and release partially built lines/chunks, and check `StrDup()` before creating the image chunk. Source-only; no allocation failure or MUI rendering was exercised.


<a id="gd14851"></a>
## GD14851 — MUI text parser mishandles a trailing or line-final HiCharIdx marker [conditional]

When `zune_text_parse_line()` sees the configured `ZTEXT_ARG_HICHARIDX` marker, it advances `s` twice to skip the marker and the following character (`workbench/libs/muimaster/textengine.c:529-540`). The ordinary loop tail then advances `s` once more at line 543. If the marker is the final byte, the first advance reaches the string terminator and the next two move beyond the allocated `dup_content` buffer. The next loop condition reads through that out-of-bounds pointer. If the marker is immediately before a newline, the branch consumes the newline as the highlighted character and the common loop tail then skips the first character on the next line; the newline is never seen by the line-splitting logic, so the lines are merged. The text class passes `MUIA_Text_HiCharIdx` directly as this marker (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/text.c:242-248`); checked-in callers set it to `'_'` (for example `external/openurl/prefs/utils.c:196-203`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a Text object uses HiCharIdx and its content ends in the marker, or the marker is immediately before a newline. At end-of-string, parsing reads beyond its copied buffer and may misparse adjacent bytes or fault during setup. Before a newline, it merges lines and drops the first character after that newline. **Affected configuration:** MUI Text with `MUIA_Text_HiCharIdx` enabled; in-tree examples use underscore. **Confidence:** high for pointer advancement and subsequent read; runtime behavior was not exercised. Check for the terminator before consuming the character after the marker and avoid advancing past the input end. Source-only; no MUI object setup or build was run.


<a id="gd14852"></a>
## GD14852 — MUI Text constructor replaces failed attribute copies with empty defaults [conditional]

`Text__OM_NEW()` duplicates nonempty `MUIA_Text_Contents` and `MUIA_Text_PreParse` values with `StrDup()` but does not remember whether a supplied value failed to copy (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/text.c:76-97`). It then treats either NULL field as though the caller omitted the attribute and allocates an empty default. The constructor only disposes the object if those fallback allocations also fail (`:99-104`). Thus, if allocation of a supplied larger string fails while allocation of the empty string succeeds, construction succeeds with empty content or without the requested preparse formatting instead of reporting failure.

**Trigger and consequence:** creation of a Text object with a supplied content or preparse string whose duplication fails, followed by a successful small empty-string allocation. The object silently displays empty text or loses formatting. **Affected configuration:** MUI Text construction under allocation pressure; this requires a failed larger allocation followed by a successful fallback allocation. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked fallback logic; the allocator sequence and user-visible result were not exercised. Track whether each attribute was supplied and fail object creation when its copy fails. Source-only; no allocation failure or object construction was run.


<a id="gd14853"></a>
## GD14853 — Software cursor shape updates mishandle allocation failures [conditional]

`Display__Hidd_Display__SetCursorShape()` acquires `fbsem`, erases the currently drawn cursor, and immediately stores the requested hotspot offsets before validating the new shape or allocating its ARGB buffer (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1414-1447`). A zero-sized shape or failed `AllocVec()` then releases the semaphore and returns `FALSE` without redrawing the old shape or restoring its prior offsets (`:1449-1465`). The old `cursor_argb`, dimensions, and visibility remain, but `cursor_drawn` was cleared by `cursor_Erase()`. The selected Intuition MonitorClass caller updates its `data->pointer` only when the method succeeds (`rom/intuition/monitorclass.c:1954-1960`), so a failed replacement leaves Intuition believing the old pointer remains installed while the generic software cursor has been erased. `ChangeExtSpriteA()` also propagates the failure without any recovery (`rom/graphics/changeextspritea.c:86-96`).

There is also a false-success path after the new ARGB image is installed: the setter calls `cursor_AllocBackup()` but ignores its result (`gfx_displayclass.c:1468-1477`). That helper first frees the existing save-under, then can return FALSE when the pixel format has no byte size or the replacement `AllocVec()` fails (`:209-233`). The setter still returns TRUE. `cursor_Draw()` requires a non-NULL backup and returns without drawing when it is absent (`:137-140`), so Intuition records the new pointer as installed while it remains invisible.

**Trigger and consequence:** on a generic software-cursor display, replacement validation or ARGB allocation fails after the old cursor is erased, or save-under allocation fails during shape replacement or framebuffer target change. The first case returns FALSE while leaving the old pointer invisible and its hotspot changed; shape/target backup failures can leave the new pointer invisible while the operation proceeds (shape replacement reports TRUE). **Affected configuration:** displays using the generic software cursor implementation. The checked subclasses with no `SetCursorShape()` override are VESA, EFI framebuffer, AArch64 Raspberry Pi framebuffer, and LinuxFB. VESA is selected in the i386-PC and x86-64-PC packages, EFI framebuffer in the OpenSBI package, and fbgfx in the AArch64 Raspberry Pi package; LinuxFB is separately buildable but absent from the inspected default Linux aggregate. The first case requires an existing drawn cursor, and the second requires an active framebuffer target plus save-under allocation/format failure. **Confidence:** high for the state transitions and selected callers; no allocation failure or cursor update was induced. Prepare replacement image and save-under storage before changing current state, check all allocation results, and restore/redraw the previous state when returning failure. Source-only; no display operation or build was run.


<a id="gd14854"></a>
## GD14854 — Generic software cursor ARGB allocation size can wrap on 32-bit targets [conditional]

`Display__Hidd_Display__SetCursorShape()` reads the source bitmap's Width and Height into `IPTR` variables, then allocates `width * height * 4` bytes before asking `HIDD_BM_GetImage()` to convert all `width × height` pixels to ARGB32 (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1420-1421,1444-1463`). On 32-bit targets, `IPTR` is unsigned 32-bit (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:82-86`), so the ARGB allocation product wraps modulo 2^32 when the requested byte count exceeds that range. The shared bitmap attributes permit each dimension to be a `UWORD` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:491-492`); no pixel-count or multiplication-overflow check precedes allocation or conversion. If the wrapped allocation succeeds, `GetImage()` is still asked to write the full ARGB32 rectangle into the undersized buffer. The save-under allocation has a second unchecked product: `cursor_w` and `cursor_h` are `UWORD`, so their product is evaluated as signed `int` before it is multiplied by `IPTR bpp` (`gfx_displayclass.c:222-233`). Large dimensions can therefore overflow the signed intermediate on both 32-bit and 64-bit builds, before the result is passed to `AllocVec()`. The checked display subclasses with no `SetCursorShape` override inherit this implementation: VESA (`rom/hidds/vesagfx/vesagfx.conf:2-23`), EFI framebuffer (`rom/hidds/efifbgfx/efifbgfx.conf:2-23`), Raspberry Pi framebuffer (`arch/aarch64-raspi/hidd/fbgfx/fbgfx.conf:2-23`), and LinuxFB (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx.conf:44-60`). The active i386-PC package selects VESA (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:75`), making the 32-bit ARGB-size wrap applicable to a checked package; x86-64 PC, OpenSBI RISC-V, and AArch64 Raspberry Pi select VESA, EFI framebuffer, and framebuffer HIDDs respectively, so the signed save-under overflow remains applicable there. LinuxFB is separately buildable but omitted from the inspected default Linux aggregate.

**Trigger and consequence:** a generic software-cursor display receives a nonzero bitmap whose ARGB byte count exceeds the 32-bit allocation-size range, or whose pixel-count product exceeds `INT_MAX` before save-under sizing. If the resulting wrapped/overflowed allocation succeeds, the subsequent full-image or save-under transfer can write beyond its buffer. **Affected configuration:** the ARGB wrap is selected by i386-PC VESA; LinuxFB is an additional separately buildable inheritor. The save-under overflow applies to the selected i386-PC and x86-64-PC VESA, OpenSBI EFI framebuffer, and AArch64 Raspberry Pi framebuffer targets. Both cases require unusual bitmap dimensions and a successful undersized allocation. **Confidence:** high for the arithmetic types, missing overflow validation, and full-rectangle transfer requests; actual bitmap feasibility and allocator outcomes were not exercised. Validate each multiplication in a sufficiently wide unsigned type, reject unrepresentable sizes, and ensure the conversion dimensions fit the allocation. Source-only; no bitmap or conversion was run.


<a id="gd14855"></a>
## GD14855 — Generic software cursor narrows computed coordinates before clipping [conditional]

`cursor_Draw()` computes the pointer's framebuffer coordinates in `LONG`, including the mouse position, signed hotspot offset, and bitmap LeftEdge/TopEdge, but stores the result in `cursor_drawX`/`cursor_drawY` before copying it back to the local `LONG x/y` used for off-screen checks and clipping (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:152-164`). Both stored fields are `WORD` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_display.h:50-55`). The input position and hotspot are also `WORD` in the selected `SetCursorPos`/`SetCursorShape` methods (`gfx_displayclass.c:1365,1545`); bitmap LeftEdge/TopEdge are `WORD` HIDD attributes (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:489-490`). Their combined result can be outside signed 16-bit range even though each input is representable. Narrowing wraps the coordinate before the code decides whether the cursor is off-screen, potentially drawing it at an unrelated in-range location or clipping it incorrectly.

**Trigger and consequence:** a generic software cursor receives signed position/hotspot/bitmap-offset values whose computed bitmap coordinate is outside `[-32768,32767]`, and the narrowed value falls within the framebuffer bounds. The cursor can appear at the wrong edge or position instead of being clipped at its actual location. **Affected configuration:** displays using generic software cursor methods with a framebuffer dimension and coordinate combination that makes the wrapped value visible; the HIDD Width/Height attributes allow values above 32767. **Confidence:** high for the narrowing and subsequent use, conditional on the coordinate combination and visible wrapped result; no cursor operation was run. Keep the computed coordinate in `LONG` through clipping and store only after any required representability check. Source-only; no display operation or build was run.


<a id="gd14857"></a>
## GD14857 — Palette changes do not refresh the software cursor [conditional]

The CursorFB method table forwards `Hidd_BitMap::SetColors` straight to the wrapped bitmap (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_cursorfbclass.c:153-158,422-426`); it neither brackets the change with cursor removal nor redraws the cursor afterward. The normal graphics.library `SetRGB32()` path resolves the HIDD bitmap associated with a ViewPort and invokes `HIDD_BM_SetColors()` (`rom/graphics/setrgb32.c:14-53,116-124`). MakeVPort stores the displayable HIDD bitmap object in ViewPortExtra (`rom/graphics/makevport.c:132-168`), and the generic display class wraps displayable bitmaps when their driver does not advertise hardware-cursor support (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:784-795,1078-1085`). The generic bitmap SetColors implementation updates the bitmap ColorMap and, when visible, forwards the palette update to the display framebuffer (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:1308-1355`). LinuxFB's explicit HIDD target supports `FB_VISUAL_PSEUDOCOLOR` by advertising `vHidd_ColorModel_Palette` and programming the framebuffer colormap (`arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/linuxfbgfx_displayclass.c:98-109`; `linuxfbgfx_bitmapclass.c:45-79`); it inherits the generic no-hardware-cursor behavior.

The software cursor is alpha-composited into the bitmap as native pixels and keeps a save-under (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:105-123,127-190`). On a mutable palette target, changing a palette entry used by a currently composited cursor pixel immediately changes that pixel's displayed color, but the cursor is not recomposited against the updated palette. The old cursor image can therefore remain visibly tinted or otherwise wrong until a later operation redraws it, such as pointer movement or shape replacement.

**Trigger and consequence:** a software cursor is visible on a mutable indexed/pseudocolor display, and `SetRGB32()` changes a palette entry currently used by a cursor pixel. The pointer can display the newly assigned palette color rather than the color produced by alpha-compositing its ARGB shape against the current background and palette; it is repaired only when the cursor is next erased and drawn. **Affected configuration:** graphics builds using the generic software-cursor wrapper with mutable palette bitmaps; LinuxFB's optional `kernel-hidd-linuxfb` target is an in-tree example when the host framebuffer reports `FB_VISUAL_PSEUDOCOLOR` (`arch/all-linux/mmakefile.src:6`; target-specific module manifest at `arch/all-linux/hidd/linuxfb/mmakefile.src:18-21`). This mode is not asserted to be in the default aggregate. **Confidence:** medium. The unbracketed palette route is source-confirmed, but the visible mismatch depends on whether the software cursor is expected to preserve its ARGB composite after the indexed palette changes; indexed framebuffer contents generally remap with the palette. No palette or cursor operation was run. If cursor color fidelity across palette updates is part of the display contract, recompose the current cursor around palette changes while holding the cursor semaphore. Source-only; no display operation or build was run.

<a id="gd14858"></a>
## GD14858 — Palette updates race truecolor-to-palette conversion [conditional]

`BM__Hidd_BitMap__SetColors()` updates the bitmap's color map through `HIDD_CM_SetColors()` and then clears `data->invlut`, but it holds no bitmap semaphore across either operation (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:1308-1359`). `CM__Hidd_ColorMap__SetColors()` can grow the map by allocating a replacement array, copying the old entries, freeing the old array, and publishing the new pointer (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_colormapclass.c:234-264`). The truecolor-to-palette converter reads the bitmap's `colmap` entries directly while searching (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapconvertpixels.c:237-275,308-344`); it also reads and writes `data->invlut` without locking. When the caller has not supplied a pixel LUT, the cache entry is keyed only by the source color and retains a palette index selected from the current color map.

A conversion concurrent with `SetColors()` can therefore read the color array while it is being replaced/freed. Even when the update does not resize the map, a conversion can calculate an index from the old palette, then write that index into `invlut` after `SetColors()` has invalidated the cache; subsequent conversions can keep using that stale index. The selected generic bitmap `PutImage()` path invokes `ConvertPixels()` for non-native formats (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:2899-2931`); neither that path nor `BM__Hidd_BitMap__ConvertPixels()` takes `data->lock`. The lock is used for visible-state/display updates, not as a general bitmap-operation lock (`gfx_bitmapclass.c:4542-4556,5088-5132,5246-5253`). These paths are reachable through normal HIDD bitmap operations.
A selected backend confirms that its own bitmap mutex does not serialize the palette update with conversion: VMware's shared on/off-bitmap implementation wraps `PutImage()` (including its non-native `HIDD_BM_ConvertPixels()` call) in `LOCK_BITMAP` (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/vmwaresvga_bitmap_common.c:172-184,238-257,249-252`), while its selected `SetColors()` method invokes the generic superclass update without taking that lock (`:68-99`). The superclass mutates the colormap and invalidates `invlut` without `data->lock`, as above. Thus the VMware bitmap lock cannot protect the shared generic palette/cache state for a concurrent SetColors/PutImage pair. The class configuration selects both methods (`vmwaresvga.conf:66-74,96-103`), and both bitmap classes include the shared implementation (`vmwaresvga_onbitmapclass.c:50`; `vmwaresvga_offbitmapclass.c:48`).

Two conversions can also race on first cache creation: each can observe `data->invlut == NULL`, allocate and initialize a separate table, then publish its pointer. The last store wins, so the other allocation becomes unreachable; each invocation continues using its own local pointer. This leaks one 64 KiB cache allocation for that race. It is the same missing synchronization around the bitmap-owned conversion cache, not a separate finding.

**Trigger and consequence:** two tasks concurrently convert truecolor pixels into the same palette bitmap, with or without a concurrent palette update. Expansion of the color map can make a conversion read the old array while it is freed; a non-expanding update can leave stale cached palette indices after invalidation; two initial conversions can leak one cache allocation. The conversion can choose incorrect pens, read invalid storage, or leak the unreachable cache. **Affected configuration:** generic HIDD graphics bitmap classes with a mutable color map and concurrent `SetColors` plus truecolor-to-palette conversion; no particular display backend is required. **Confidence:** high that these paths share mutable state without a common lock; the visible consequence depends on task interleaving. Serialize color-map updates against conversion and protect cache invalidation/fill with the same synchronization. No concurrent operation or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14859"></a>
## GD14859 — Sound.datatype AHI startup leaks its timer resources on init failure [conditional]

`PlayerProcAHI()` makes a best-effort timer port and request, then opens `timer.device` before it processes the initial `COMMAND_INIT` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:3612-3627`). The `COMMAND_INIT` branch creates the worker's command port; if `CreateMsgPort()` fails, it clears the message's return data, replies to the constructor, and returns immediately (`:3731-3740`). That return bypasses the `COMMAND_EXIT` cleanup that closes the timer device and deletes the timer request and port (`:3777-3786`). The parent `Sound_NEW()` treats the NULL handshake data as startup failure and disposes the datatype object, but it has no references to or cleanup for the worker's timer resources (`:871-907`).

The child exits and the object construction fails, but the timer request/port and open `timer.device` reference are leaked. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `workbench-datatypes-sound` with AHI playback enabled and `timer.device` available; the Sound datatype's parent aggregate edge is commented, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the resource acquisition, early-return bypass, and missing parent cleanup; manifestation depends on the command-port allocation failure occurring after timer setup succeeds. Route this failure through the worker's timer cleanup before replying/exiting. No allocation failure or audio/device operation was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14862"></a>
## GD14862 — AHI sound cursor time wraps after about 71 minutes [conditional]

The AHI play-position timer subtracts `cursorStart` from `GetSysTime()` and computes `elapsed_us` as `now.tv_secs * 1000000UL + now.tv_micro` in `ULONG` before widening it to `UQUAD` for the sample-position multiplication (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:3641-3655`). `ULONG` is explicitly unsigned 32-bit in the public type definitions (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:39-43`), so elapsed microseconds wrap modulo 2^32 after roughly 4,294.97 seconds (71 minutes 35 seconds). The subsequent cast cannot recover the lost high bits. In continuous playback, the cursor's sample offset is computed from this wrapped value and modulo `SampleLength` (`dispatch.c:3666-3673`), so it jumps backward and then repeats its position cycle. For a sufficiently long finite sample/cycle duration, the wrapped elapsed value can also keep the displayed cursor tracking after the audio has ended.

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional AHI cursor timer remains active during playback for more than about 71 minutes. Its displayed playhead then derives from a wrapped elapsed time and no longer tracks elapsed playback. **Affected configuration:** Sound.datatype's AHI playback path when timer.device is available and the play cursor is enabled; continuous playback is the direct selected case. **Confidence:** high for the 32-bit arithmetic wrap and wrong cursor time; the exact visible redraw cadence follows the existing roughly 25 fps timer. Compute elapsed time in a 64-bit type before multiplying. No audio, timer, cursor, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="gd14863"></a>
## GD14863 — More wraps long-line lengths before applying its display cap [selected Workbench utility]

`LineNode` stores both the source byte count and rendered text width in `UWORD` fields (`workbench/utilities/More/more.c:96-101`). The line parser increments `stringlen` for every source byte (`:423-435`), while `CalcTextLen()` accumulates expanded columns in another `UWORD` and applies the 4,096-column cap only after the scan (`:316-333`). For a line of exactly 65,536 ordinary characters, both counters wrap to zero before the cap/check. The drawing path therefore treats the line as empty (`:655-678`), the horizontal extent calculation sees no text width, and `FindString()` uses the wrapped source length as its search bound (`:1188-1212`). Other lengths whose low 16 bits are small similarly display/search only that truncated prefix.

**Trigger and consequence:** open a file in More containing a line at least 65,536 bytes long, with its length modulo 65,536 below the 4,096-column display limit. The viewer renders only the truncated width (zero for exactly 65,536 bytes), loses the corresponding horizontal-scroll range, and Find cannot search beyond the truncated source length. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected `workbench-utilities-more` target (`workbench/utilities/More/mmakefile.src:6-16`); selected through the active `workbench-utilities` and `workbench-complete` dependencies; no specific generated image was checked. **Confidence:** high for the 16-bit counter wrap and its direct rendering/search consumers; requires a long line in the opened file. Accumulate source/display lengths in a wider type and clamp only the rendered width. No file, search, UI operation or build was run; source-only.


<a id="gd14864"></a>
## GD14864 — More overflows its title buffer for long AppWindow paths [selected Workbench utility]

`filenamebuffer` is 300 bytes, and the AppWindow drop handler builds a path into it with `NameFromLock(..., 299)` and `AddPart(..., 299)`, then assigns it to `filename` (`workbench/utilities/More/more.c:118,1294-1303`). After a successfully opened dropped file, `HandleFileChange()` calls `SetWinTitle()` (`:1310-1311,755-759`), where `strcpy(s, filename)` copies that path into the separate 256-byte `s` buffer (`:132,737-748`). A valid path longer than 255 bytes therefore overwrites adjacent static storage before `Lock()` or `NameFromLock()` can replace/truncate the title text. The same function then formats the name and two decimal values into a 256-byte `wintitle` with unbounded `__sprintf()` (`:739-750`); even when `s` itself fits, a long name plus the title suffix can overflow `wintitle` (the English format has 26 bytes of non-name text with one-digit counts). The file requester supports 1,025-byte paths and 257-byte names (`workbench/libs/asl/filereqhooks.h:38-39`), while this AppWindow branch itself accepts paths up to its 299-byte destination limit.

**Trigger and consequence:** drop a valid file onto More's AppWindow with an assembled path longer than 255 bytes, or with a shorter path long enough that the formatted title exceeds 255 characters. Opening succeeds, then title update writes beyond `s` or `wintitle`, corrupting adjacent static state and potentially disrupting later UI or file operations. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected `workbench-utilities-more` program (`workbench/utilities/More/mmakefile.src:6-16`); selected through the active `workbench-utilities` and `workbench-complete` dependencies. **Confidence:** high for both unbounded writes, path construction, and the direct caller route; requires a valid sufficiently long path. Bound the title formatting and size the buffers for the accepted path and suffix. No file was dropped or opened; source-only.


<a id="gd14865"></a>
## GD14865 — More command formatting overflows its buffer for long paths [selected Workbench utility]

More has two unbounded command-formatting paths into the shared `s[256]` buffer (`workbench/utilities/More/more.c:132`). Project/Save As and Project/Print combine the source `filenamebuffer[300]` (up to 299 bytes from startup/AppWindow paths; `:118,287,1294-1303`) with a destination returned in `filebuffer[108]` (`workbench/utilities/More/misc.c:103-107,133-139`) before passing the result to `System()` (`more.c:1535-1544`). **Trigger and consequence:** invoke Print/Save As with sufficiently long source and destination paths, or use the editor shortcut when the `editor` variable and current filename are long enough. `__sprintf()` writes past `s`, corrupting adjacent stack/static data before command submission. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected `workbench-utilities-more` program (`workbench/utilities/More/mmakefile.src:6-16`); selected through the active `workbench-utilities` and `workbench-complete` dependencies. **Confidence:** high for the fixed buffer sizes, input limits and unbounded formatting calls; each combined-length condition is available through the selected paths. <a id="gd14866"></a>
## GD14866 — More mishandles Read errors on non-seekable inputs [selected Workbench utility]

`OpenFile()` uses a 65,536-byte read limit for inputs where seeking to end fails, and only rejects a short read when `seekable` is true (`workbench/utilities/More/more.c:356-399`). DOS `Read()` returns `-1` on error (`rom/dos/read.c:40-43`). On a non-seekable input that returns this error, the condition `flen != new_filelen && seekable` is false, so the function proceeds with `new_filelen = flen` and writes `new_filebuffer[new_filelen] = '\0'` at offset -1. It then enters `while (flen--)` with a negative value while counting lines, advancing through memory beyond the allocation; signed decrement eventually overflows as well. The line-index allocation is never reached safely on this path.

**Trigger and consequence:** More opens a non-seekable DOS file/device and its first `Read()` fails. The load path writes before the allocated buffer and then scans with a negative length, causing memory corruption and undefined behavior rather than reporting the I/O error. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected `workbench-utilities-more` program (`workbench/utilities/More/mmakefile.src:6-16`), when invoked on a non-seekable source whose DOS handler returns a read error. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked error path and consequences; no checked-in caller or specific device was established. Reject negative `Read()` results before updating the length or indexing the buffer. No device, read failure, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd14867"></a>
## GD14867 — More underallocates its line index after 32-bit size overflow [selected Workbench utility]

`OpenFile()` counts every newline into signed 32-bit `LONG new_num_lines`, then passes `new_num_lines * sizeof(struct LineNode)` directly to `AllocVec()` without checking multiplication overflow (`workbench/utilities/More/more.c:399-407`). On 32-bit builds `struct LineNode` is 12 bytes (32-bit pointer, two `UWORD`s, and 16-bit `BOOL`; definition at `more.c:91-98`). With 357,913,942 lines, the requested byte count wraps from 4,294,967,304 to 8. `AllocVec()` may therefore return a small non-NULL block, after which the loop writes one node per line (`more.c:416-435`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on a 32-bit build, More loads a newline-dense file with at least 357,913,942 lines (roughly 358 MB if each line is empty). If the wrapped allocation succeeds, filling the line index writes far beyond it and corrupts memory. The input is within the signed `LONG` file-size range, while the allocation expression exceeds the 32-bit address-size range. **Affected configuration:** 32-bit builds of the Workbench-selected `workbench-utilities-more` program; 64-bit builds do not have this multiplication wrap at the same line count. **Confidence:** high for arithmetic wrap and underallocation; manifestation depends on availability of the wrapped allocation. Check the multiplication against the allocator's maximum size before allocating. No large file, allocator behavior, or build was exercised; source-only.


<a id="gd14871"></a>
## GD14871 — Chunky bitmap mode-change allocation failure leaves new dimensions over the old buffer

`CBM__Root__Set()` invokes the base bitmap setter first, which commits the new framebuffer ModeID, dimensions, pixel format and row size. The subclass then updates its cached bytes-per-pixel before trying to grow an owned buffer (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:1018-1046`; base mutation at `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:4444-4478`). If `AllocVec()` fails, the method returns without restoring the base attributes or updating cached `bytesperrow`; the old buffer and `bufsize` remain, while the pixel size is new (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:1046-1065`). Later pixel writes use the new pixel size with the old cached stride to compute their address (`:109-150`), and other inherited consumers can observe the new base row size.

**Trigger and consequence:** a generic ChunkyBM framebuffer with an owned buffer changes to a larger or deeper mode whose `height * BytesPerRow` exceeds its current allocation, and the attempted replacement allocation fails. After the setter returns, drawing within the newly published dimensions can calculate addresses beyond the retained old allocation, corrupting adjacent memory or faulting. Roll back the base mode/dimensions/pixelformat on allocation failure, or keep the object inaccessible until a correctly sized buffer is installed. **Affected configuration:** the optional HeadlessGfx display target creates displayable bitmaps as `HeadlessGfxBM`, whose constructor delegates to ChunkyBM without supplying an external buffer (`rom/hidds/gfx/headless/headlessgfx.conf:45-51`; `headlessgfx_bitmapclass.c:34-43`; `headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:344-375`). The HeadlessGfx target is explicitly buildable but commented out of its aggregate target (`headless/mmakefile.src:4-5,23-24`). The buffer-growth failure is still required. **Confidence:** high that the failure path leaves inconsistent base and subclass state and that subsequent pixel addressing can exceed `bufsize`; medium for practical manifestation because the optional target and allocation failure are both conditional. No mode switch or allocation failure was induced; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


<a id="gd14872"></a>
## GD14872 — CursorFB direct bitmap access does not protect the borrowed buffer across mode changes [conditional]

CursorFB wraps the generic ChunkyBM framebuffer when the display needs a software cursor. Its ordinary drawing methods acquire the display semaphore through `CFB_INIT`, but its `ObtainDirectAccess` and `ReleaseDirectAccess` entries both use the plain forwarding method `cursorfb_fwd` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_cursorfbclass.c:43-75,481-482`). That forwards to `CBM__Hidd_BitMap__ObtainDirectAccess()`, which returns the current `data->buffer` pointer and dimensions; the generic ChunkyBM `ReleaseDirectAccess()` is empty (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:932-960`). Cybergraphics `LockBitMapTagList()` uses this method and documents exclusive access until `UnLockBitMap()` (`workbench/libs/cgfx/lockbitmaptaglist.c:31-45,100-118`; `unlockbitmap.c:45-66`). This path does not implement that contract: ChunkyBM returns the pointer without acquiring a lock, and release does not wait for outstanding access (`gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:932-960`). The selected Nouveau and Radeon bitmap implementations instead acquire bitmap/engine locks in ObtainDirectAccess and release them in ReleaseDirectAccess (`workbench/hidds/nouveau/nouveau_bitmapclass.c:764-781`; `workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_bitmap.c:1176-1219`). The in-tree decorator hook also holds this lock across direct pixel writes: `ShadeLine()` obtains it for `rp->BitMap`, uses `HIDD_BM_PutPixel()` while the handle is live, and unlocks only after the draw (`workbench/libs/decorator/drawfuncs.c:958,1018-1024,1085-1105,1144-1161`). AHIRecord only probes bytes-per-pixel and unlocks immediately (`workbench/tools/AHIRecord/AHIRecord.c:331-341`), while the font datatype locks a newly allocated offscreen bitmap (`workbench/classes/datatypes/font/fontclass.c:314-342`); those two call paths do not establish a concurrent display-mode trigger.

A display mode switch follows a different synchronization interval: `Display__Hidd_Display__Show()` holds the display semaphore while calling `OOP_SetAttrsTags()` on the framebuffer (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_displayclass.c:1199-1240`), but the direct-access method does not retain that semaphore for the caller's lock interval. The generic `CBM__Root__Set()` grows an owned buffer by allocating a replacement and freeing the old pointer (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:1045-1064`). A mode change from another task can therefore replace and free the allocation while a direct-access client still holds the borrowed address; that client may continue reading or writing freed storage before it unlocks.

**Trigger and consequence:** a client obtains direct access to a CursorFB-wrapped, owned-buffer ChunkyBM framebuffer, and another task shows a mode whose required buffer is larger. The mode change frees the old allocation without waiting for the outstanding direct-access lease, leaving the first client with a stale pointer. **Affected configuration:** optional HeadlessGfx displayable bitmaps use `HeadlessGfxBM` (a ChunkyBM subclass) and the generic graphics class reports no hardware cursor support by default, selecting CursorFB for the framebuffer (`rom/hidds/gfx/headless/headlessgfx.conf:45-51`; `headlessgfx_bitmapclass.c:34-43`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:860-869`; `gfx_displayclass.c:519-531`). HeadlessGfx advertises LUT8, RGB15_LE, RGB16_LE and BGRA32 modes, each represented in the Cybergraphics pixel-format mapping (`headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:66-126`; `gfx_pixfmtclass.c:96-120`). The target is optional (`headless/mmakefile.src:4-5,23-24`). Direct access plus an overlapping growth mode switch are required. **Confidence:** high for the raw-pointer return, missing semaphore retention in the wrapper, and old-buffer free; manifestation requires the described cross-task overlap and a growth mode. Hold the display semaphore for the direct-access lease or otherwise prevent framebuffer replacement until all leases are released. No bitmap lock, mode change, concurrent access, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

<a id="gd14873"></a>
## GD14873 — X11 clipboard INCR reader leaves requests pending for non-8-bit chunks [conditional]

The hosted X11 reader processes an incremental clipboard property only when `actual_format == 8` (`arch/all-hosted/hidd/x11/x11_clipboard.c:302-397`). If a `PropertyNewValue` arrives with another format, it skips both the data accumulation and the terminal reply, then deletes the property (`:399-404`). The request remains stored in `hostclipboardmsg` and the read state remains `HOSTCLIPBOARDSTATE_READ_INCR`; `x11clipboard_handle_commands()` immediately returns whenever that message is non-NULL (`:88-92`). The caller waiting for the asynchronous read therefore receives no reply, and subsequent clipboard commands remain unprocessed.

**Trigger and consequence:** an X11 selection owner sends a non-8-bit property during a UTF8_STRING INCR transfer. The hosted clipboard task deletes the chunk without terminating the outstanding request, leaving its caller blocked and the clipboard command queue stalled. **Affected configuration:** optional hosted X11 HIDD, with an external selection owner providing an invalid-format chunk. **Confidence:** high that this branch neither replies nor clears the outstanding request; occurrence requires the described nonconforming response. On an unsupported property, terminate the transfer with failure, clear the accumulated buffer, restore event selection, and reply to the waiting request. No X11 selection transfer, caller wait, or build was run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

<a id="gd14870"></a>
## GD14870 — Generic 16-bit bitmap copies accept odd row strides and fault on strict-alignment CPUs

The generic bitmap constructor documents that an explicit `aHidd_BitMap_BytesPerRow` overrides `aHidd_BitMap_Align`, and accepts any supplied stride at least as large as the computed minimum; it does not validate alignment to the pixel size (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapclass.c:776-803,923-929,1038-1050`). The generic ChunkyBM subclass uses that stride as its row pitch and allocates `height * bytesperrow` bytes (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_chunkybitmapclass.c:50-75`). The same-format CopyBox fast path dispatches 2-byte chunky formats to `BM__Hidd_BitMap__CopyMemBox16()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1024-1074`), which forms each row address from `srcY * srcMod` / `destY * dstMod` then dereferences `UWORD *` and `ULONG *` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_bitmapmemblit.c:300-383`). Thus an accepted odd stride moves every other row to an odd address.

**Trigger and consequence:** a direct HIDD client creates two 16-bit generic chunky bitmaps of height at least two with the default 16-pixel alignment and explicit `BytesPerRow=33` (the width-one default minimum is 32 bytes), then copies a pixel from row 1 using the generic CopyBox path. The constructor accepts the stride, but the helper accesses the row at base+33 through `UWORD *`; on m68k CPUs that require even alignment, the copy can raise an address error. Require row strides to preserve pixel alignment, or use byte-safe accesses for unsupported strides. **Affected configuration:** the generic `gfx` HIDD when selected on m68k-Amiga (`arch/m68k-amiga/boot/mmakefile.src:158,375`; `arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/gfx/mmakefile.src:1-14`), with a direct HIDD client supplying the documented explicit stride. No checked-in producer of an odd-stride generic bitmap was established. **Confidence:** high for constructor acceptance, row-address calculation, typed access and the strict-alignment consequence; medium for in-tree reachability because the trigger requires a direct HIDD client with an odd explicit stride. No bitmap or copy was created or run; source-only; see the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).


<a id="gd14869"></a>
## GD14869 — NVIDIA CopyBox packs tall extents with undefined signed shifts [explicit optional target]

`Hidd_Gfx::CopyBox` declares `height` as `UWORD` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:396`). On AROS, `UWORD` promotes to signed `int` for the expressions in the NVIDIA implementation. The same-depth blit packs `(msg->height << 16)` into its extent word (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/nvidiaclass.c:542`); the different-depth stretch path does the same for both destination and source extent words (`:621,626`). For `height >= 32768`, shifting the positive promoted `int` left by 16 produces a value outside the signed-int range, which is undefined behavior before `NVDmaNext()` receives the packed value. `struct BitMap.Rows` is also a `UWORD`, so this height is within the public bitmap dimension representation (`compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:33-40`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an NVIDIA `CopyBox` call selects either hardware engine and supplies a height of at least 32,768. The C expression has undefined behavior and the emitted GPU extent may be wrong or compiler-dependent. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable `hidd-nvidia` target (`workbench/hidds/nvidia/mmakefile.src:5-13`); its aggregate edge is commented, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. The same-depth path requires matching bitmap depths; the stretch path handles differing depths. No checked-in caller passing this height was established in this pass. **Confidence:** high for the signed promotion and undefined shift; practical manifestation depends on compilation and a sufficiently tall bitmap/request. Cast to `ULONG` before shifting and mask each packed field. No blit, bitmap allocation, GPU operation or build was run; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).
