## GD14868 — Headless boot-driver replay retains a pointer to its caller's stack tags [optional target]

The disk-started HeadlessGfx monitor builds its HIDD attributes in the automatic `attrs[6]` array and passes that array to `AddDisplayDriverA()` (`rom/hidds/gfx/headless/disk_startup.c:51,150-174`). It marks the registration `DDRV_BootMode` in a second local tag array (`:53-57`). When there is no display yet, `driver_Setup()` takes the boot-mode queue branch and stores the `attrs` pointer directly in the queue node (`rom/graphics/graphics_driver.c:401-410`); it does not instantiate the driver during that call. The startup routine then releases the HeadlessGfx attribute base and returns, ending the lifetime of `attrs` (`disk_startup.c:174-184`).

The queue is replayed later when `BestModeIDA()` or the first `NextDisplayInfo()` query finds the display database empty (`rom/graphics/bestmodeida.c:248-255`; `nextdisplayinfo.c:60-65`). Replay passes the stored pointer to `driver_Setup()`, which forwards it to `HW_AddDriver()` and the HeadlessGfx constructor (`graphics_driver.c:296-323,329-350`). That constructor reads width, height, nominal depth and depth limits from the tag list (`rom/hidds/gfx/headless/headlessgfx_hiddclass.c:188-189,232-254`). The stack tag records may already have been overwritten when those reads occur, so configured dimensions/depths can be lost or interpreted from unrelated stack contents; tag traversal itself also relies on the stale terminator.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the optional disk-started HeadlessGfx monitor, registered with `DDRV_BootMode` while no display is registered, followed by the later normal boot-time replay. The resident HeadlessGfx init path passes `NULL` attributes and is not affected. **Consequence:** HeadlessGfx can be constructed with incorrect settings or read beyond the original tag-list storage while searching for `TAG_DONE`. **Confidence:** high for pointer retention past the caller's automatic-storage lifetime and later constructor reads; exact manifestation depends on stack reuse. Copy the tag items into queue-owned storage or construct the driver before returning. No monitor launch, stack overwrite, display replay, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only. See the [coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md).

<a id="gd14874"></a>
## GD14874 — Optional VMM startup leaks its queued launch message on early manager exit [conditional]

The MUI starter allocates a `VMMsg`, sends it to the new manager process's `pr_MsgPort`, then waits on the separate starter port (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/aloha.c:288-302,335-357`). The manager calls `Init_VM_Manager()` before it reads that process-port message (`workbench/system/VMM/VM_Manager.c:604-607`). If `OpenLibs()` fails, `Init_VM_Manager()` returns before reaching its later `WaitPort()`/`GetMsg()` startup-message receive (`workbench/system/VMM/VM_Manager_Init.c:424-438`). The manager then sends a separate `VMCMD_InitFailed` reply, cleans up, and returns (`VM_Manager.c:614-644`). The MUI starter consumes and frees that reply, then returns without freeing its original launch `VMMsg`; its local pointer has been overwritten with the reply pointer (`aloha.c:347-357`). There is a second early exit in the same pre-receive window: if allocation of the manager's reply fails, it signals the starter and exits without consuming the queued startup message (`VM_Manager.c:614-620`). The starter wakes, `GetMsg()` returns `NULL`, and the assignment overwrites its pointer to the launch message (`aloha.c:347-357`). No selected path releases the queued launch-message payload on either exit, so the allocation is leaked in both cases.

**Trigger and consequence:** the optional VMM manager exits before consuming its queued launch message, either because `OpenLibs()` fails or because allocating the manager's reply message fails. In the first case the caller receives the failure response; in the second it wakes to an empty starter port. Both paths lose the sender's pointer to the queued public-memory `VMMsg`, leaking one allocation per attempt. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable optional VMM MUI starter and handler; the default parent aggregate does not select this VMM target (`workbench/system/VMM/MUI/mmakefile.src`; `workbench/system/VMM/mmakefile.src`). **Confidence:** high for the early receive ordering, queued sender allocation, both exits, and missing release; no allocation or library failure or VMM launch was induced. Consume and release the launch request on every manager-startup path, or have the sender reclaim it after a failure reply. Source-only; see the [startup failure trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vmm-manager-early-library-failure-leaves-start-message-gd14874).


<a id="gd14875"></a>
## GD14875 — Generic pixel CopyBox narrows large unsigned widths to signed loop bounds [conditional]

The generic GFX HIDD's `copybox_impl()` receives `width` as the public HIDD method's `UWORD`, but stores loop start/end/direction and the per-pixel loop counters in signed `WORD` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx.conf:396`; `rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:979-988,1135-1148`). The direct-buffer fast path can return before these loops, but the pixel fallback is used when one or both bitmaps do not expose a chunky buffer, and for supported draw modes/formats not handled by the fast path (`:1018-1020,1112-1133`).

For a width of 32,769 pixels, the forward path assigns `msg->width` to signed `endX`; conversion to the supported 16-bit `WORD` is implementation-defined and commonly produces a negative bound. With that narrowing result, the `WORD` loop counter `x` must pass its positive maximum while incrementing toward the bound, invoking signed-overflow undefined behavior. Under wraparound code generation, the counter becomes negative and those coordinates reach the planar bitmap `GetPixel()`/`PutPixel()` methods, which use them to derive an unsigned plane offset without bounds checks (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:356-425`); such execution can read or write outside the requested row. Other compiler outcomes may truncate the operation or fail to terminate. The HIDD contract allows a `UWORD` width and bitmap widths are also `UWORD`, so the request is representable, though it requires a very wide bitmap and the generic per-pixel fallback.

**Trigger and consequence:** a direct HIDD client requests a valid CopyBox rectangle wider than 32,767 pixels on a bitmap route that reaches the generic pixel fallback. Narrowing plus signed overflow makes loop behavior undefined; on wraparound target code generation, negative coordinates can produce out-of-range pixel accesses. The public `BltBitMap()` vector instead takes a signed `WORD` width and clips it against bitmap bounds, so it cannot supply a positive width above 32,767 (`rom/graphics/bltbitmap.c:27-38,128-174`). No other checked-in wide-width caller was established. **Affected configuration:** generic GFX HIDD bitmap paths using this fallback, including planar bitmaps; no default display configuration or in-tree direct caller with such a width was established. **Confidence:** high for the narrowing and signed-overflow UB, and for the planar methods' lack of coordinate bounds checks; the concrete out-of-range effect depends on compiler/target code generation and an external direct HIDD call. Keep counters and endpoints in an unsigned or wider type, or reject widths not representable by the loop variables. Source-only; no bitmap operation or build was run.

## GD14879 — Radeon PCI size queries overwrite a 32-bit stack local on 64-bit targets [optional HIDD]

`RadeonEnumerator()` declares the PCI-region `size` destination as `ULONG` (`workbench/hidds/radeon/ati_init.c:101-104`), then passes its address to `OOP_GetAttr()` for BAR0 size, BAR2 size, and ROM size (`:131-159`; the size is queried again during failure cleanup at `:192-196`). The optional HIDD target is not connected to the default graphics aggregate in this snapshot. **Affected configuration:** 64-bit builds of the explicit `hidd-radeon` target selecting shared `ati_init.c`; no default display configuration or actual Radeon device is claimed. **Confidence:** high for the 32-bit destination, pointer-sized output contract, and out-of-object write; the adjacent-local effect depends on target stack layout. Use `IPTR size` for OOP output, then validate/narrow explicitly where the mapper's `ULONG` length requires it. No build, PCI enumeration, or device operation was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Radeon PCI size-attribute caller type trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#radeon-pci-size-attribute-caller-type-trace-2026-11-05).


<a id="gd14882"></a>
## GD14882 — WAV export ignores failure to write the RIFF pad byte [optional datatype]

`WAVE__DTM_WRITE()` checks each RIFF header, format, data-chunk header, and encoded sample write, converting short/error results into failure. For mono output with an odd `totalFrames`, it sets `pad_byte` to one and includes that byte in the RIFF container size, then calls `Write(file, &null_byte, 1)` without checking the result (`workbench/classes/datatypes/wav/wave_class.c:105-110,175-184`). It leaves `Error == OK`, so the method returns TRUE even if this final write returns zero or -1 (`:187-194`). `SaveDTObjectA()` uses the DTM_WRITE result to decide whether to delete the output (`workbench/libs/datatypes/savedtobjecta.c:108-127`), so a successful close can retain a file missing its required word-alignment byte and one byte shorter than its declared RIFF size. The selected WAV reader stops after decoding the data chunk, so this review does not establish that this module rejects its own such output.

**Trigger and consequence:** save a mono WAV object with an odd sample count to a destination where the final one-byte `Write()` fails or is short after all preceding writes succeeded. `DTM_WRITE` reports success and `SaveDTObjectA()` can retain a file whose RIFF size field exceeds its actual size by one byte. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built/installed WAV datatype; its local target has no active aggregate/package edge in this snapshot. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked final write, odd-frame condition, success return and caller handling; the downstream effect of the malformed RIFF length depends on the consumer. No write failure was induced. Check the pad-byte result and propagate the error. No file operation or build was run; source-only. See the [WAV datatype caller review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wav-dtm-write-pad-byte-review-gd14882).

<a id="gd14883"></a>
## GD14883 — WAV export reads sample length through a signed 32-bit slot [optional datatype]

`WAVE__DTM_WRITE()` declares `totalFrames` as `LONG` and passes `&totalFrames` as the storage for `SDTA_SampleLength` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/wav/wave_class.c:48,68-76`). The DataTypes getter contract treats every attribute storage address as `IPTR *` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/getdtattrsa.c:84-88`), and the Sound datatype stores its `ULONG SampleLength` in that slot through `*opg->opg_Storage = data` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:1160-1162,1357`). On 64-bit targets, `IPTR` is pointer-sized while `LONG` remains 32-bit (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:37-43,83-87`; `compiler/include/aros/cpu.h:63-66,74-80`), so the getter writes an `IPTR` through the address of a 4-byte object, overwriting adjacent stack storage. On 32-bit targets, a valid sample length at or above `0x80000000` becomes negative in `LONG`; the writer's loop condition `frame > 0` then skips all sample output while later chunk sizes are calculated from that value (`wave_class.c:156-177`). The 8SVX loader obtains sample lengths from unsigned voice-header fields and stores them as `ULONG` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/8svx/8svxclass.c:120-215`; `sound/classbase.h`), so this value range is representable when memory and input size permit.

**Trigger and consequence:** export a Sound datatype object whose sample length is at least `0x80000000`. On 64-bit builds, the attribute read writes beyond `totalFrames`; on 32-bit builds, the signed value prevents the sample loop and can produce a WAV with inconsistent or empty data and sizes. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built WAV datatype; the 64-bit storage-width mismatch applies to its 64-bit builds, while the signed-range error applies to 32-bit builds. The optional target has no active aggregate/package edge in this snapshot. **Confidence:** high for the API storage width, destination type, Sound getter write, and signed loop behavior; the large sample trigger requires a correspondingly large in-memory Sound object. Use pointer-sized storage for the attribute read, validate its range, and use an unsigned frame counter with checked RIFF-size arithmetic. No large file, WAV export, or build was exercised; source-only. See the [WAV datatype sample-length type trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wav-sample-length-type-trace-gd14883).

<a id="gd14884"></a>
## GD14884 — Sound datatype leaks its previously owned sample on replacement [conditional]

`Sound_NEW()` sets `FreeSampleData` to TRUE for each created instance (`workbench/classes/datatypes/sound/dispatch.c:839-858`). Later `SetDTAttrsA()` forwards to `SetGadgetAttrsA()`, whose contract sends `OM_SET` (`workbench/libs/datatypes/setdtattrsa.c:54-60`; `rom/intuition/setgadgetattrsa.c:62-65`). The Sound `OM_SET` handler calls `parsetaglist()`, where `SDTA_Sample` and `SDTA_LeftSample` overwrite `id->Sample` directly (`dispatch.c:1368-1381,959-965,1085-1091`); no old pointer is released or retained. Disposal frees only the current `id->Sample` and `id->RightSample` (`:1452-1459`). Therefore, replacing an owned sample buffer on a non-continuous object loses the only reference to the old allocation, which is not freed at disposal.

**Trigger and consequence:** load or create a non-continuous Sound object with an owned `AllocVec` sample, let playback finish, then replace it through `SetDTAttrs()` with another owned sample. The old allocation becomes unreachable and remains leaked for the rest of the process lifetime. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `workbench-datatypes-sound` and its Sound datatype subclasses; no checked-in caller replacing a sample on an existing object was found, so the trigger is through the public datatype API. **Confidence:** high for the default ownership flag, pointer overwrite, and final disposal behavior; no replacement or allocation measurement was run. Retain and release replaced owned buffers after they are no longer in use, or make ownership transfer explicit. Source-only.

<a id="gd14877"></a>
## GD14877 — AmigaVideo masked blits ignore the requested draw mode [conditional; m68k-Amiga]

`AmigaVideoCl__Hidd_Gfx__CopyBoxMasked()` reads `GC_DRMD(msg->gc)` and passes it as `mode` to `blit_copybox_mask()` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_hiddclass.c:935-951`). The helper never reads that parameter. Once both bitmaps pass `canblit()`, it always programs the blitter with minterm `0xCA` (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_blitter.c:245-258,386-418`), the fixed masked-copy operation. In contrast, the generic `CopyBoxMasked` fallback implements `vHidd_GC_DrawMode_AndInverted` by complementing the source pixel under set mask bits before writing it (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1518-1547`). For that mode, the AmigaVideo hardware path therefore copies the unmodified source where the mask is set instead of the inverted source. The public `BltMaskBitMapRastPort()` conversion maps minterm `0x20` to `vHidd_GC_DrawMode_AndInverted` (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h:84-89`; `rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:374`), and forwards it to the HIDD method (`rom/graphics/bltmaskbitmaprastport.c:27-38,127-139`).

**Trigger and consequence:** issue a masked copy on AmigaVideo bitmaps with GC draw mode `AndInverted` (for example, through the public masked-blit vector with minterm `0x20`) while both bitmaps are AmigaVideo drawables and their planes pass the Chip RAM blitter check. The selected hardware path returns success after applying ordinary masked copy, so pixels selected by the mask have the wrong value. When `canblit()` fails, the method falls back to the generic implementation, which handles this mode. **Affected configuration:** m68k-Amiga AmigaVideo HIDD hardware-blitter path; no checked-in caller using minterm `0x20` was found, so the trigger is an API/HIDD client condition. **Confidence:** high that `mode` is unused and the fixed `0xCA` operation differs from the generic AndInverted result. Dispatch the mode-specific minterm or delegate unsupported modes. No graphics operation or build was run; source-only; see the [AmigaVideo masked draw-mode audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-masked-draw-mode-audit).


<a id="gd14878"></a>
## GD14878 — AmigaVideo blitter drops oversized operations while reporting success [conditional; OCS-class chipsets]

`startblitter()` returns without programming the blitter when an OCS-class chipset request exceeds 64 words horizontally or 1,024 rows vertically (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_blitter.c:53-65`). The helper returns `void`, so its callers cannot distinguish this rejection. `blit_copybox_mask()` calls it for each destination plane and then returns `TRUE` (`:386-424`); `blit_copybox()` and `blit_fillrect()` likewise call it and return success (`:228-240,474-497`). The HIDD dispatchers propagate that success rather than retrying the generic implementation. OCS selection is represented by `ecs_agnus == FALSE`; chipset initialization sets that field from the hardware VPOSR bit (`amigavideo_chipset.c:1892`). For example, an in-bounds 1,025-row masked copy in an offscreen AmigaVideo bitmap reaches the helper, which skips each hardware operation, while the HIDD method reports success. The selected AmigaVideo bitmap constructor obtains dimensions from its superclass without imposing these blitter limits (`amigavideo_bitmapclass.c:75-112`).

**Trigger and consequence:** on an OCS-class system, submit an AmigaVideo blit/fill whose computed hardware width exceeds 64 words or whose height exceeds 1,024 rows, using Chip RAM bitmaps that pass `canblit()`. The operation is silently skipped (or a multi-part operation is partially applied) and the HIDD method reports success. This applies to the `startblitter()` callsites in copy, masked-copy, fill, and pattern paths; screen-mode bounds alone do not cover larger offscreen bitmaps. **Affected configuration:** m68k-Amiga AmigaVideo on OCS-class chipsets; ECS Agnus uses the extended size registers instead. No in-tree oversized AmigaVideo operation was established. **Confidence:** high for the silent limit check and success propagation; practical reachability depends on a client creating a sufficiently large Chip RAM bitmap/operation. Split operations into supported chunks or propagate failure so callers can fall back. No operation or build was run; source-only; see the [AmigaVideo blitter-size limit audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#amigavideo-blitter-size-limit-audit).


<a id="gd14880"></a>
## GD14880 — Generic masked-copy fallback writes an IPTR past its 32-bit pixel-format local [conditional; 64-bit targets]

`copyboxmasked_impl()` declares `pixfmt` as `ULONG` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_hiddclass.c:1380-1384`). When both bitmap pixel formats are truecolor and the source and destination use different pixel-format objects, it passes `&pixfmt` cast as `IPTR *` to `OOP_GetAttr()` for `aHidd_PixFmt_StdPixFmt` (`:1416-1433`). `OOP_GetAttr()`'s storage contract is `IPTR *` (`rom/oop/include/oop.h:164-169`); the generic pixel-format getter writes `pf->stdpixfmt` through the full-width storage pointer (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_pixfmtclass.c:123-126,185-190`). `HIDDT_StdPixFmt` is `IPTR` (`rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:90`), while `ULONG` remains 32-bit (`compiler/include/exec/types.h:37-43`). Thus on a 64-bit build the getter writes four bytes beyond `pixfmt`; the adjacent stack effect depends on compiler layout. The resulting pixel-format value is then passed to the source `GetImage()` and destination `PutImage()` operations (`gfx_hiddclass.c:1490-1498,1580-1583`).

**Trigger and consequence:** perform a masked copy through the generic `Hidd_Gfx::CopyBoxMasked` fallback with two truecolor bitmaps whose pixel-format objects differ. On 64-bit targets, the valid operation overwrites four bytes outside the local `pixfmt` object and can corrupt neighboring stack state; the exact subsequent effect depends on local layout. The generic fallback is registered in `kernel-hidd-gfx` (`rom/hidds/gfx/mmakefile.src:12-40`) and is reachable through the public `BltMaskBitMapRastPort()` bridge (`rom/graphics/bltmaskbitmaprastport.c:27-38`); target manifests select it on AArch64 Raspberry Pi and RISC-V64 OpenSBI (`arch/aarch64-raspi/boot/mmakefile.src:152`; `arch/riscv64-opensbi/boot/mmakefile.src:50`). **Affected configuration:** 64-bit builds selecting the generic GFX HIDD and its fallback; a driver-specific override can avoid this implementation. **Confidence:** high for the pointer-width write and four-byte overrun; neighboring-state corruption is layout-dependent. Store the result in `IPTR` and narrow only at an API boundary that requires `ULONG`. No masked blit or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Generic masked-copy pixel-format output-width check](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#generic-masked-copy-pixel-format-output-width-gd14880).

<a id="gd14885"></a>
## GD14885 — Locale Preferences dereferences failed pooled allocations during resource scanning [conditional]

`ScanDirectory()` checks the `AllocPooled()` result for its entry, but does not check the following `AllocVecPooled()` for `entry->node.ln_Name` before calling `strcpy()` (`workbench/prefs/locale/prefs.c:232-242`). Country entries also allocate a fallback `displayflag` and immediately pass it to `sprintf()` without checking the result (`:247-251`). The called metadata readers contain the same unchecked allocation pattern: `GetAROSRegionAttribs()` frees the prior resource-name string, allocates `cn->cn_Size`, then passes that pointer to `ReadChunkBytes()` and debug string output; the FLAG branch allocates `lockFlag` and immediately writes through it (`:109-124`). `GetAROSLanguageAttribs()` frees the old name, allocates its replacement, and immediately copies into it (`:156-163,185-192`). `Prefs_Initialize()` also checks the `AllocPooled()` for the built-in English entry but not its subsequent name allocation (`:681-686`).

**Trigger and consequence:** the Locale Preferences memory pool is created successfully, but one of these later pooled allocations fails while country/language resources are being scanned or metadata is being parsed. The affected path dereferences or writes through NULL and can terminate the preferences process instead of skipping the entry or returning an initialization error. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable optional `workbench-prefs-locale` target (`workbench/prefs/locale/mmakefile.src:6-18`); its parent dependency is commented out. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocation results and immediate uses; no allocation failure was induced. Check each allocation before freeing/replacing or writing through the associated pointer, and unwind or skip the affected entry on failure. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Locale Preferences resource-scan allocation failure trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#locale-prefs-resource-scan-allocation-failure-gd14885).

<a id="gd14886"></a>
## GD14886 — Locale Preferences reports successful export after IFF or file-close errors [conditional]

`Prefs_ExportFH()` sets success after the locale payload write, ignores both `PopChunk()` results and `CloseIFF()` finalization (`workbench/prefs/locale/prefs.c:467-548`), while the IFF implementation logs and discards failures closing pending chunks (`workbench/libs/iffparse/closeiff.c:74-82`). The CLI caller ignores `Prefs_ExportFH()` and DOS `Close()` results for both ENV and ENVARC writes (`prefs.c:620-650`; `rom/dos/close.c:24-30,74-80`). The GUI export method does return the helper result (`registertab.c:345-361`), but cannot observe finalization errors hidden by `CloseIFF()`.

**Trigger and consequence:** an IFF chunk/FORM finalization or destination flush fails after opening a locale preferences output. GUI export can report success after failed IFF finalization; CLI Use/Save suppresses detected helper failures and close/flush failures, potentially leaving an incomplete preferences file while reporting success. Propagate chunk-finalization status from the IFF layer and check export and close results in the CLI caller. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-prefs-locale` GUI or CLI Use/Save (`workbench/prefs/locale/mmakefile.src:11-19`); its parent aggregate edge is disabled. **Confidence:** high for discarded error results; no IFF or DOS write failure was induced. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Locale Preferences export finalization and caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#locale-preferences-export-finalization-and-caller-trace).

<a id="gd14881"></a>
## GD14881 — Text datatype reports successful `DTM_WRITE` after output errors

The selected text datatype maps `DTM_WRITE` to `DT_Write()` (`workbench/classes/datatypes/text/text.conf:37-38`; `mmakefile.src:4,11-12`). In `DTWM_RAW` mode, `DT_Write()` ignores `Write()` when saving the full buffer and delegates selected-text output to `CopyTextNowDOS()` (`textclass.c:2997-3012`). That helper ignores every `FWrite()` and `FPutC()` result (`:1658-1729`). In `DTWM_IFF` mode it ignores `PushChunk()`, `CopyTextNowIFF()`'s `WriteChunkBytes()` results, both `PopChunk()` results and `CloseIFF()` (`:3013-3039`; `CopyTextNowIFF()` at `:1563-1655`). `DT_Write()` then returns `TRUE` unconditionally (`:3045`). `SaveDTObjectA()` uses the method result as its return value and deletes the output only when `DTM_WRITE` returns zero (`workbench/libs/datatypes/savedtobjecta.c:51-58,108-127`).

**Trigger and consequence:** save a text.datatype object through `SaveDTObjectA()` in raw mode to a destination whose DOS `Write()` returns a short count or error. The datatype still reports success; if `Close()` itself succeeds, `SaveDTObjectA()` retains the partial file instead of deleting it or reporting failure. IFF-mode output also discards its chunk-write and finalization results. **Affected configuration:** explicitly built `workbench-datatypes-text`; the text datatype target is optional, and this finding makes no default-package inclusion claim. **Confidence:** high for the ignored write results, unconditional success, and `SaveDTObjectA()` handling; no write failure was induced. Propagate every raw and IFF write/finalization error through `DT_Write()` as a zero result. No file or datatype object was saved; source-only.
<a id="gd14887"></a>
## GD14887 — More treats unsupported stream-seek responses as file lengths [selected Workbench utility]

`OpenFile()` treats any nonnegative `Seek(..., OFFSET_END)` result as evidence that the input is seekable, then uses the result of a second seek as the exact byte count to read (`workbench/utilities/More/more.c:357-364`). DOS documents `Seek()` as returning the previous position or `-1` on error (`rom/dos/seek.c:34-41`), but `InternalSeek()` returns the handler's `dp_Res1` status without translating `dp_Res2` when that status is nonnegative (`rom/dos/internalseek.c:18-35`). The console handler reports unsupported `ACTION_SEEK` as `DOSTRUE` with `ERROR_ACTION_NOT_KNOWN` (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:1211-1215`), so both seeks appear to succeed with position 1. More then requests one byte and treats that as the whole input (`more.c:384-399`). In line mode, the console read returns at most the requested length (`rom/filesys/console_handler/support.c:1166-1180`), so More consumes at most one input character before closing the handle.

The same caller error affects a named pipe. The selected pipe handler has no `ACTION_SEEK` case; its default reply is `dp_Res1 = 0` plus `ERROR_ACTION_NOT_KNOWN` (`workbench/fs/pipe/pipe-handler.c:346-352`). The shell's `Pipe()` helper demonstrates a named reader endpoint: it opens `PIPE:*` for writing, obtains its name with `NameFromFH()`, then opens that name for reading (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Pipe.c:115-123`). `OpenPipe()` resolves existing names and permits one reader endpoint (`workbench/fs/pipe/pipecreate.c:95-139,167-209`). With such a read endpoint, More's two seeks appear to succeed at position zero, so it allocates a one-byte buffer and requests a zero-byte read. If the pipe is empty while its writer remains open, that read waits until data arrives; when `CheckWaiting()` sees data, the zero-length request completes without moving any bytes (`workbench/fs/pipe/pipesched.c:149-167,211-229`). Closing More's reader then clears `OPEN_FOR_READ` (`pipecreate.c:333-353`); if the producer continues past the pipe-buffer capacity, the writer queue is not drained while the buffer is full (`pipesched.c:171-181`), so its write can remain pending. Thus More displays no stream data and may leave the producer blocked.

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke the Workbench-selected More utility with `CON:` as its input path and enter text, or open a named `PIPE:` endpoint for reading while a writer is active. On `CON:`, More displays at most the first character and closes the handle without displaying the rest. On `PIPE:`, it interprets the unsupported seek's zero result as a zero-byte length, waits for data or writer EOF if needed, and then returns without consuming or displaying the pipe data; closing its reader can leave a sufficiently large producer write blocked on a full pipe. **Affected configuration:** `workbench-utilities-more` (`workbench/utilities/More/mmakefile.src:11-16`); selected through the active `workbench-utilities` and `workbench-complete` dependencies. **Confidence:** high for the nonnegative unsupported-action responses, More's resulting one-byte/zero-byte read lengths, and the pipe queue behavior; manifestation requires a non-seekable stream path and, for the blocked-writer consequence, enough subsequent output to fill the pipe. Test the documented error result, or stream reads without inferring total length from a nonnegative seek response. No console input, pipe data, or build was used; source-only.

**Coverage:** [More console input and seek-contract reconciliation](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#more-console-input-and-seek-contract-reconciliation-gd14887).

<a id="gd14888"></a>
## GD14888 — `Skip /BACK` ignores failed rewinds on non-seekable scripts

`Skip` documents `/BACK` as restarting its search at the beginning of the script, but ignores the result of `Seek(Input(), 0, OFFSET_BEGINNING)` and continues its `ReadItem()`/`FGetC()` scan regardless (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Skip.c:25-30,90-98,128-144`). The built-in `Execute` command accepts an input path and, when invoked from the normal shell input, assigns the opened handle to `cli_CurrentInput` (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Execute.c:108-122`). Shell defines script input by `cli_CurrentInput != cli_StandardInput`, reads through that current handle (`workbench/c/Shell/Shell.c:47,51-63,100-106`; `workbench/c/Shell/readLine.c:54`), and closes/restores it when the stream ends (`Shell.c:159-177`). Thus `Execute CON:` supplies a console-backed script stream, while `Execute PIPE:name` can supply a named pipe reader; Shell's selected `Pipe()` helper demonstrates creating a writer endpoint, obtaining its name with `NameFromFH()`, then opening that name for reading (`workbench/c/shellcommands/Pipe.c:115-123`). The console handler does not implement `ACTION_SEEK` (`rom/filesys/console_handler/con_handler.c:1211-1215`), and the pipe handler's unknown-action reply for the absent seek case is zero plus `ERROR_ACTION_NOT_KNOWN` (`workbench/fs/pipe/pipe-handler.c:346-352`). Neither stream can be rewound, but `Skip` proceeds with its forward scan.

**Trigger and consequence:** execute a console-backed or named-pipe-backed script containing a `Skip LABEL BACK` command whose matching `Lab` appeared earlier in the stream. `Skip` cannot revisit that earlier input; it consumes subsequent console/pipe input until the label appears again or the stream ends, then reports the label missing if it was not encountered. This differs from GD14887: More misinterprets unsupported seek results as file lengths, while `Skip` independently ignores the failed rewind result. **Affected configuration:** the `Skip` command is in the shell-command source list and built-in resource list (`workbench/c/shellcommands/mmakefile.src:1-39,55-98`); the trigger requires a non-seekable stream as script input. **Confidence:** high for the ignored seek result and forward-only scan; conditional on using `Execute` with a console or pipe stream. Check the rewind result and return an error when the input cannot seek. No console script, pipe data, or build was used; source-only.

**Coverage:** [Skip non-seekable `/BACK` caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#skip-back-console-script-caller-trace-gd14888).

<a id="gd14889"></a>
## GD14889 — VMware SVGA LUT8 palette updates overrun the bitmap color cache [optional HIDD]

The shared VMware bitmap instance stores only 16 entries in its local color cache (`workbench/hidds/vmwaresvga/vmwaresvga_bitmap.h:32-44`). The selected `VMWareSVGAOffBM` class includes the shared `SetColors()` method (`vmwaresvga.conf:86-103`; `vmwaresvga_offbitmapclass.c:50`), and its constructor accepts the bitmap pixel-format depth, storing one byte per pixel for depths up to eight (`vmwaresvga_offbitmapclass.c:78-104`). `AllocBitMap()` can select the standard `LUT8` format, whose pixel format is an 8-bit palette (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:27,285-302`; `rom/hidds/gfx/stdpixfmts_le.h:177-188`). The VMware display class routes displayable non-framebuffer bitmaps to this offscreen class (`vmwaresvga_displayclass.c:78-83`).

For palette formats, the VMware `SetColors()` override first calls the generic superclass, then allows updates through `(1 << data->bpp)` (`vmwaresvga_bitmap_common.c:80-90`). At depth eight, that accepts palette indices 0 through 255, but the subsequent loop writes each updated color to `data->cmap[xc_i]`, whose capacity is only 16 (`:90-96`; `vmwaresvga_bitmap.h:40-44`). A valid update that includes any index 16 or greater therefore writes beyond the array into adjacent bitmap instance data.

The path is reachable through the selected graphics.library allocator as well as direct HIDD updates. `BMF_REQUESTVMEM` includes `BMF_DISPLAYABLE` (`compiler/include/graphics/gfx.h:78`); `AllocBitMap()` sets `aHidd_BitMap_Displayable` from those flags and defaults a depth-at-most-eight bitmap without a friend or mode to `LUT8` (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:290-302,323-325`). With the VMware display selected, its display class routes a displayable non-framebuffer bitmap to `VMWareSVGAOffBM` (`vmwaresvga_displayclass.c:78-83`). Because `BMF_REQUESTVMEM` also selects color-table initialization, `AllocBitMap()` calls `HIDD_BM_SetColors()` once for every palette entry (`allocbitmap.c:399-446`). The selected offscreen method therefore writes beyond `cmap[16]` during initialization of an 8-bit palette bitmap.

**Trigger and consequence:** allocate a depth-eight `BMF_REQUESTVMEM` bitmap through the VMware display path with no friend bitmap or mode ID. The LUT8 palette initialization reaches entry 16 and writes beyond the backend's 16-entry array, corrupting adjacent bitmap instance data during allocation. Direct HIDD `SetColors()` updates covering index 16 or greater have the same defect. **Affected configuration:** the optional `workbench-hidd-vmwaresvga` target with the graphics.library HIDD allocator selecting its display class; no default-image inclusion is claimed. **Confidence:** high for the selected method, 256-entry initialization loop, and undersized array. Size the cache for the supported palette depth or bound the backend loop to its actual capacity. No bitmap allocation, palette update, failure injection, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="gd14890"></a>
## GD14890 — Vulkan-Hpp displacement-micromap constructor drops pointer-array usage counts [optional beta API]

The enhanced `AccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV` constructor derives `usageCountsCount` only from `usageCounts_.size()` while initializing `ppUsageCounts` from the separate pointer-array argument (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:4585-4605`). Passing an empty `usageCounts_` and a nonempty pointer-array argument therefore stores a non-NULL `ppUsageCounts` but sets `usageCountsCount` to zero, so the supplied usage records are not included when Vulkan consumes the structure. The official Vulkan reference defines `usageCountsCount` as the number of records and allows exactly one of `pUsageCounts` or `ppUsageCounts` to be valid ([VkAccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkAccelerationStructureTrianglesDisplacementMicromapNV.html)). The same constructor's check permits both arrays when their lengths match, producing both non-NULL fields despite that one-pointer requirement (`:4607-4616`). The neighboring enhanced `AccelerationStructureTrianglesOpacityMicromapEXT` constructor handles either representation by deriving the count from the nonempty array and rejects both being present (`:4901-4929`).

**Trigger and consequence:** with `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS` and enhanced constructors enabled, construct the displacement-micromap wrapper with an empty direct `usageCounts_` array and a nonempty pointer-array argument, then pass it to Vulkan. The wrapper reports zero usage entries despite retaining the supplied pointer array; Vulkan therefore receives an incomplete geometry usage description and may reject or mis-size the associated build. Supplying both arrays of equal length instead creates invalid input with both pointer fields set. **Affected configuration:** consumers of the optional Vulkan HIDD headers copied by `workbench/hidds/vulkan/mmakefile.src:9-23`, when they opt in to the beta extension; no checked-in caller or default-image inclusion was found. **Confidence:** high for the constructor state and the Vulkan pointer/count contract; runtime effect depends on a downstream beta-extension caller. Derive the count from whichever single array is supplied and enforce the one-array constraint. No C++ instantiation, Vulkan operation, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14891"></a>
## GD14891 — Vulkan-Hpp reflection cannot compile for bit-field wrappers [optional configuration]

`vulkan_structs.hpp` has several wrappers with C++ bit-field members whose reflection methods pass those members to `std::tie`: acceleration-structure instance records (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:3425-3428,3585-3588,4226-4229`), cluster geometry flags (`:17723-17725`), cluster build and template records (`:18001-18005,18331-18335`), and cluster instantiate records (`:19530-19531`). For example, `ClusterAccelerationStructureGeometryIndexAndGeometryFlagsNV::reflect()` promises a tuple of references and passes its bit-fields to `std::tie` (`:17697-17701`). `std::tie` takes lvalue references, and C++ bit-fields cannot bind to references, so enabling `VULKAN_HPP_USE_REFLECT` makes these function definitions ill-formed; downstream code that reaches equality through `reflect()` has the same conditional compile failure. The default non-reflection equality implementations compare fields directly and do not have this problem.

**Trigger and consequence:** compile a translation unit that includes the Vulkan-Hpp headers with `VULKAN_HPP_USE_REFLECT` defined. Compilation fails in this wrapper's `reflect()` definition (and, if reached, the reflected equality path); consumers cannot use the optional reflection configuration with this generated header. **Affected configuration:** optional consumers of `workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp` that define `VULKAN_HPP_USE_REFLECT`; the selected AROS tree has no in-tree definition of this macro, so no default build impact or in-tree caller is claimed. **Confidence:** high for the C++ bit-field/reference incompatibility and local source path; conditional impact is clear, but no compiler run was performed. Return a tuple of values for these bit-fields (or otherwise avoid binding them by reference). Source-only; no build or C++ instantiation was run.

<a id="gd14892"></a>
## GD14892 — Vulkan-Hpp tensor-copy helpers can emit mismatched dimension arrays [optional ARM API]

The enhanced `TensorCopyARM` constructor always initializes `dimensionCount` from `srcOffset_.size()` but independently stores all three array pointers (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:26665-26675`). Its checks permit an empty `srcOffset_` alongside nonempty `dstOffset_` or `extent_` because each mismatch check is skipped when either side is empty (`:26776-26795`). The Vulkan contract defines `dimensionCount` as the number of entries in all three arrays; each pointer may independently be NULL, but if any is non-NULL then `dimensionCount` must be greater than zero, and each non-NULL array must have `dimensionCount` entries ([VkTensorCopyARM specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/copies.html#VkTensorCopyARM)). Thus an empty source-offset proxy with a nonempty destination-offset or extent proxy produces `dimensionCount == 0` with a non-NULL array pointer and invalid Vulkan input.

The enhanced `setSrcOffset()`, `setDstOffset()`, and `setExtent()` setters each update the shared `dimensionCount` from only the array being set and do not check the other stored pointers (`:26828-26864`). Setting one proxy to a different length after setting another therefore leaves a non-NULL array whose length does not match `dimensionCount`.

**Trigger and consequence:** with enhanced mode enabled, construct `TensorCopyARM` with empty `srcOffset_` and a nonempty `dstOffset_` or `extent_`, or call the individual enhanced setters with different nonempty lengths. Passing the resulting record to `vkCmdCopyTensorARM` supplies inconsistent `dimensionCount`/array state; validation must reject it, and implementations cannot interpret the requested copy region according to the declared arrays. **Affected configuration:** downstream consumers of the optional `VK_ARM_tensors` Vulkan-Hpp API with enhanced mode enabled; checked-in Vulkan wrappers expose `copyTensorARM`, but no AROS call site constructing this record was found. **Confidence:** high for the constructor/setter state and Vulkan's count/pointer contract; no runtime validation was performed. Select a common dimension count from the nonempty arrays and reject inconsistent lengths in both construction and setters. No C++ instantiation, Vulkan operation, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14893"></a>
## GD14893 — Vulkan-Hpp tensor-description setters can desynchronize dimension arrays [optional ARM API]

`TensorDescriptionARM` represents both `pDimensions` and optional `pStrides` using one shared `dimensionCount`. Its enhanced constructor sets the count from `dimensions_.size()`, stores both arrays, and checks that nonempty strides have the same length (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:42523-42547`). The enhanced `setDimensions()` instead updates `dimensionCount` from only the dimensions proxy (`:42590-42596`), while `setStrides()` overwrites that same count from only the strides proxy (`:42605-42611`); neither validates the other currently stored array. For example, set a three-element dimensions proxy followed by a two-element strides proxy: the wrapper retains a non-null three-element `pDimensions`, a non-null two-element `pStrides`, and `dimensionCount == 2`. Reversing the order or setting either proxy empty can likewise produce arrays inconsistent with the shared count.

The Vulkan contract defines `dimensionCount` as the number of dimensions, requires `pDimensions` to point to that many elements, and, when non-null, requires `pStrides` to point to that many elements ([VkTensorDescriptionARM reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkTensorDescriptionARM.html)). Therefore these enhanced setter sequences create an invalid tensor description that may be rejected or interpreted using truncated/mismatched array data when passed through `TensorCreateInfoARM` to `vkCreateTensorARM`.

**Trigger and consequence:** with enhanced mode enabled, invoke `setDimensions()` and `setStrides()` with differing proxy lengths on the same wrapper, then pass it to tensor creation. The resulting shared count cannot describe both non-null arrays, violating the API pointer/count contract. **Affected configuration:** downstream consumers of the optional `VK_ARM_tensors` Vulkan-Hpp wrapper; repository search found generated `createTensorARM` wrappers but no AROS code constructing `TensorDescriptionARM`. **Confidence:** high for wrapper state and the documented array contract; no validation-layer or runtime operation was performed. Preserve the established dimension count and reject a setter proxy of a different nonempty length, or make the setter update/clear related arrays consistently. Source-only; no C++ instantiation or build was run.

<a id="gd14894"></a>
## GD14894 — External-handle Vulkan-Hpp wrappers default to the POSIX FD type [optional/conditional APIs]

Four Vulkan-Hpp wrapper constructors guarded by `VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR` select the POSIX `eOpaqueFd` value as their default handle type: `FenceGetWin32HandleInfoKHR` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:51617-51619`), `ImportFenceWin32HandleInfoKHR` (`:62957-62962`), `ImportSemaphoreWin32HandleInfoKHR` (`:64816-64821`), and `SemaphoreGetWin32HandleInfoKHR` (`:148352-148354`). These records are passed directly to the corresponding Win32 Vulkan commands by the generated wrappers in `vulkan_funcs.hpp`. The Vulkan specification's supported-type tables for the Win32 fence and semaphore APIs enumerate Win32 handle types, not `OPAQUE_FD` ([fence import rules](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/synchronization.html), [semaphore import rules](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/synchronization.html)); the corresponding get-handle commands likewise request Win32 handle types ([fence get info](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkFenceGetWin32HandleInfoKHR.html), [semaphore get info](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkSemaphoreGetWin32HandleInfoKHR.html)). Thus the default-constructed or partially initialized wrapper carries an enum invalid for its Win32 operation.

A further scan found the same mismatched default in ten other handle-specific records: `ImportMemoryHostPointerInfoEXT` (`:63355-63358`), `ImportMemoryMetalHandleInfoEXT` (`:63477-63480`), `ImportMemoryWin32HandleInfoKHR` (`:63600-63604`), `ImportMemoryZirconHandleInfoFUCHSIA` (`:63855-63859`), `ImportSemaphoreZirconHandleInfoFUCHSIA` (`:64979-64984`), `MemoryGetMetalHandleInfoEXT` (`:69960-69963`), `MemoryGetRemoteAddressInfoNV` (`:70194-70196`), `MemoryGetWin32HandleInfoKHR` (`:70314-70317`), `MemoryGetZirconHandleInfoFUCHSIA` (`:70437-70440`), and `SemaphoreGetZirconHandleInfoFUCHSIA` (`:148474-148478`). These defaults conflict with the handle contracts: host-pointer imports require `HOST_ALLOCATION` or `HOST_MAPPED_FOREIGN_MEMORY` ([host pointer import rules](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkImportMemoryHostPointerInfoEXT.html)); Metal memory import/get operations use MTL buffer/texture/heap types ([Metal import rules](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkImportMemoryMetalHandleInfoEXT.html), [Metal extension](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VK_EXT_external_memory_metal.html)); Win32 memory import requires a Win32 NT or global-share handle type ([Win32 memory import rules](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/memory.html)); Fuchsia memory/semaphore APIs use Zircon VMO/event types ([Fuchsia external memory](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VK_FUCHSIA_external_memory.html), [Fuchsia external semaphore](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VK_FUCHSIA_external_semaphore.html)); and the NV remote-address getter requires an export handle type declared when memory was created, with the extension specifying `RDMA_ADDRESS_BIT_NV` ([remote-address rules](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkMemoryGetRemoteAddressInfoNV.html), [NV RDMA extension](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VK_NV_external_memory_rdma.html)). The FD default may therefore make default or partially initialized records invalid across these optional platform APIs too.

**Trigger and consequence:** under `VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR`, construct one of these records while omitting `handleType` (including the common form that supplies only the fence/semaphore and, for imports, flags/handle). Pass it to the associated `vkGet*Win32HandleKHR` or `vkImport*Win32HandleKHR` wrapper. The command receives `OPAQUE_FD`, which is not in the Win32 operation's supported handle-type set; validation rejects the call, or the operation fails. Supplying an explicit supported Win32 type avoids the constructor-default defect. **Affected configuration:** downstream Vulkan-Hpp consumers compiling the optional Win32 platform API; repository search found generated dispatch wrappers but no AROS application call site using these records, so no default AROS runtime impact is claimed. **Confidence:** high for the four constructor defaults and the specification mismatch; runtime/API validation was not run. No C++ instantiation, Windows build, or Vulkan operation was performed; source-only.

<a id="gd14895"></a>
## GD14895 — Vulkan-Hpp NV indirect-command setters can desynchronize paired index arrays [optional enhanced API]

`IndirectCommandsLayoutTokenNV` has one `indexTypeCount` for both `pIndexTypes` and `pIndexTypeValues`. The enhanced constructor checks that the two proxy arrays have equal lengths, but the enhanced setters update the shared count independently: `setIndexTypes()` sets it from `indexTypes_.size()` and replaces only `pIndexTypes` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:66164-66170`); `setIndexTypeValues()` does the same from the other array while replacing only `pIndexTypeValues` (`:66179-66185`). After setting unequal-length arrays, the wrapper contains a non-null array whose actual length differs from the shared count. The Vulkan contract says both arrays must each contain `indexTypeCount` entries when the count is nonzero ([VkIndirectCommandsLayoutTokenNV reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkIndirectCommandsLayoutTokenNV.html)).

**Trigger and consequence:** with enhanced mode enabled, call the two setters on one wrapper with different nonzero array lengths, then pass it through `vkCreateIndirectCommandsLayoutNV`. The produced token violates the Vulkan array/count contract and is invalid input; validation should reject it, and the requested custom index-type mapping cannot be represented correctly. **Affected configuration:** downstream users of the optional `VK_NV_device_generated_commands` enhanced Vulkan-Hpp API; no AROS application call site constructing this wrapper was found. **Confidence:** high for the setter state and documented count contract; no runtime validation was performed. Keep the paired arrays consistent in both setters, or provide a combined setter that validates equal lengths. Source-only; no C++ instantiation, Vulkan operation, or build was run.

<a id="gd14896"></a>
## GD14896 — Vulkan-Hpp shader-layout setter overwrites the initial-shader count

The enhanced constructor for `IndirectExecutionSetShaderInfoEXT` initializes `shaderCount` from `initialShaders_` and checks that a nonempty `setLayoutInfos_` has the same length (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:66803-66829`). **Trigger and consequence:** with enhanced mode enabled, create the wrapper with a nonempty initial-shader array, then call `setSetLayoutInfos()` with a different nonzero length and pass the result in an indirect execution set creation request. The structure violates the Vulkan array/count contract and is invalid input; validation should reject it, and the initial shader list cannot be interpreted according to the declared count. **Affected configuration:** downstream users of the optional `VK_EXT_device_generated_commands` enhanced Vulkan-Hpp API; no AROS application call site constructing this structure was found. **Confidence:** high for the setter behavior and documented count contract; no runtime validation was performed. Preserve the initial shader count and validate layout-info length, or update both arrays together. Source-only; no C++ instantiation, Vulkan operation, or build was run.

<a id="gd14897"></a>
## GD14897 — Vulkan-Hpp micromap usage-count setters can leave both alternative arrays set

`MicromapBuildInfoEXT` exposes two alternative representations for usage counts: `pUsageCounts` and `ppUsageCounts`. Its enhanced constructor accepts the alternatives separately and checks that at most one proxy is nonempty (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:72048-72076`). The enhanced `setUsageCounts()` updates `usageCountsCount` and `pUsageCounts`, but leaves `ppUsageCounts` untouched (`:72132-72139`); `setPUsageCounts()` updates the same count and `ppUsageCounts`, but leaves `pUsageCounts` untouched (`:72147-72154`). Switching representations via setters can therefore leave both pointers non-null. Vulkan requires exactly one of these alternatives to be valid and the other to be null ([VkMicromapBuildInfoEXT reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkMicromapBuildInfoEXT.html)).

**Trigger and consequence:** with enhanced mode enabled, initialize a `MicromapBuildInfoEXT` using one nonempty usage-count representation, then call the setter for the other representation. Passing the result to `vkBuildMicromapsEXT` or `vkCmdBuildMicromapsEXT` violates the mutually exclusive pointer contract; validation should reject the structure, and the selected usage list is ambiguous. **Affected configuration:** downstream users of the optional `VK_EXT_opacity_micromap` enhanced Vulkan-Hpp API; no AROS application call site constructing this wrapper was found. **Confidence:** high for setter behavior and the Vulkan contract; no runtime validation was performed. Each setter should clear the other pointer and preserve a coherent count, or expose a single validated choice. Source-only; no C++ instantiation, Vulkan operation, or build.

<a id="gd14898"></a>
## GD14898 — MUI gradient parser narrows accepted angles to 16 bits

`zune_gradient_string_to_intern()` accepts numeric angles through `StrToLong()` without checking the documented internal angle range, stores the parsed value in a temporary `ULONG`, then assigns it to `spec->u.gradient.angle`, which is a `UWORD` documented as holding values in `[0,360)` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/imspec_gradient.c:34-67,117-118`; `imspec_intern.h:93-95`). The narrowing silently keeps only the low 16 bits. The renderer later treats the stored value as a nonnegative angle and applies modulo 360 in `FillPixelArrayGradient()` (`imspec_gradientdraw.c:510-612`), so an accepted `-1` becomes 65535 and renders using 15 degrees instead of being rejected or following the negative-angle normalization path; an accepted 65536 becomes zero and takes the vertical fast path instead of 16 degrees. The earlier signed-minimum drawing claim is withdrawn: because the field is `UWORD`, `INT_MIN` cannot be passed intact to the renderer. `StrToLong()` also has unchecked signed overflow for that extreme input, but its post-UB result is not used to substantiate this finding.

**Trigger and consequence:** supply a scaled or tiled gradient spec with a numeric angle outside the representable/documented range (for example `-1` or `65536`) and render it on a CyberGraphX truecolor target. The parser reports success but the 16-bit assignment changes the angle before drawing, producing an unintended direction rather than rejecting or consistently normalizing the input. **Affected configuration:** MUI consumers that accept numeric gradient specs; no in-tree caller supplying these boundary values was found. **Confidence:** high for successful parse, `UWORD` narrowing, and resulting values; medium for expected handling of out-of-range angle syntax because the internal field comment specifies `[0,360)` while the renderer also contains normalization for arbitrary angles. Validate the input range or normalize in a sufficiently wide signed type before storing. No gradient was rendered or build run; source-only.

<a id="gd14899"></a>
## GD14899 — Tall MUI gradients overflow signed intersection arithmetic

`FillPixelArrayGradient()` computes the per-row intersection accumulator in signed `int` using products of rectangle dimensions and 8-bit direction components (`workbench/libs/muimaster/imspec_gradientdraw.c:328-425`). For a 180-degree gradient, the normal `libm` values produce `vx = 255` and `vy = 0`; the setup chooses `yw = -height`, `ystart = height`, and `r = 0`. On the first row, with `y = height`, `y1_mul_t_accu = r - yw * vx * y` is therefore `255 * height * height`. At height 3,000 this is 2,295,000,000 when `vx` truncates to 255; even `vx = 254` yields 2,286,000,000, still above signed 32-bit `INT_MAX` (2,147,483,647). `height` is computed from the inclusive draw endpoints (`:344-345`), which arrive as `WORD` values and can represent this size (`imspec_gradientdraw.c:617-622`). The overflow occurs before pixel interpolation and is undefined signed arithmetic; the subsequent color values can be incorrect or compiler-dependent. This is separate from GD9657's zero-denominator case at 135 degrees.

**Trigger and consequence:** draw a numeric 180-degree scaled or tiled gradient over a truecolor rectangle at least 3,000 pixels high, such as a tall MUI Image object on a CyberGraphX truecolor screen. The `Image` class records itself as the gradient object during `MUIM_Show` and draws its image spec through `zune_imspec_draw()` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/image.c:434-440,536-545`; `imspec.c:858-872,877-885`); truecolor mode is set for screen bitmaps with depth at least 15 (`classes/window.c:514-517`). The renderer executes signed overflow during accumulator initialization, so gradient interpolation is not well-defined and may visibly produce incorrect colors. **Affected configuration:** muimaster with CyberGraphX truecolor rendering and a caller-supplied large gradient region; no in-tree 180-degree/3,000-pixel caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the 32-bit arithmetic bound and source path; medium for practical reachability and visible manifestation on a configured large truecolor surface. Use a wider accumulator or checked arithmetic. No gradient, bitmap, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="gd14900"></a>
## GD14900 — OpenWindow cleanup dereferences a failed BorderRPort allocation

For a non-GimmeZeroZero window, `intui_OpenWindow()` first creates `w->WLayer`, then allocates a separate `BorderRPort`. If that allocation fails, the error branch calls `intui_CloseWindow()` (`rom/intuition/openwindow.c:1499-1520`). The `IntWindow` was allocated with `MEMF_CLEAR` (`openwindow.c:645`), and this failed allocation leaves `w->BorderRPort` null. In the non-GZZ branch, `intui_CloseWindow()` deletes the layer and unconditionally calls `DeinitRastPort(w->BorderRPort)` (`rom/intuition/closewindow.c:465-471`). `DeinitRastPort()` immediately reads `rp->RP_Extra` (`compiler/arossupport/deinitrastport.c:52-59`), so this error cleanup dereferences NULL before reaching `FreeMem()`.

**Trigger and consequence:** open an ordinary non-GZZ window under memory pressure where layer creation succeeds but allocation of the extra BorderRPort fails. The intended graceful `OpenWindow()` failure path instead faults during cleanup, leaving the partially created window state and layer cleanup incomplete. **Affected configuration:** Intuition window creation on all targets using this non-GZZ path; the failure requires the specific allocation ordering. **Confidence:** high for the NULL assignment, unconditional call and dereference. Guard the deinitialization/free operations when no BorderRPort was allocated, or initialize the port before entering shared cleanup. No allocation failure, window operation, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14901"></a>
## GD14901 — ReAction Label can dereference a missing RastPort font after its fallback fails

When a label has text and the supplied RastPort has no font, `Label__IM_DRAW()` attempts to borrow the default public-screen font. If `LockPubScreen(NULL)` returns NULL, the code continues without setting a font and calls `SetSoftStyle()` (`workbench/classes/reaction/label/labelclass.c:396-420`). `AskSoftStyle()` explicitly returns zero for a RastPort whose `Font` is NULL (`rom/graphics/asksoftstyle.c:56-59`), but `SetSoftStyle()` later unconditionally evaluates `rp->Font->tf_Style` for its return value (`rom/graphics/setsoftstyle.c:63-67`), dereferencing NULL. The Intuition contract permits `LockPubScreen()` to return NULL on failure, and its implementation can have no default public or Workbench screen (`rom/intuition/lockpubscreen.c:30-48,143-158`). `DrawImageState()` forwards the caller's RastPort directly to an image's `IM_DRAW` method (`rom/intuition/drawimagestate.c:98-104`), and Layout renders image children that way (`workbench/classes/reaction/layout/layoutclass.c:922-943`). When Layout obtains a port from `GadgetInfo`, `ObtainGIRPort()` clones `gi_RastPort`, while `CloneRastPort()` copies the entire structure without installing a default font (`rom/intuition/obtaingirport.c:60-97`; `compiler/arossupport/clonerastport.c:51-55`). This preserves a fontless input port, although no checked-in caller establishes the simultaneous public-screen lookup failure.

**Trigger and consequence:** draw a text-bearing `label.image` to a valid RastPort with `rp->Font == NULL` while `LockPubScreen(NULL)` fails (for example, when no default/Workbench screen can be obtained). The attempted fallback does not initialize the RastPort, and `SetSoftStyle()` faults on its NULL font before the label can use its later zero-height fallback. **Affected configuration:** optional ReAction `label.image` consumers, including the AHI and DiskImage GUI targets; no checked-in caller was found that proves the combined null-font/failed-screen-lock trigger, so this remains a public direct-call candidate. **Confidence:** high for the NULL dereference when the branch conditions hold; medium for trigger reachability in an ordinary GUI session. Return before the style call when no font is available, or establish a valid default font on the RastPort. No image was drawn and no build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14902"></a>
## GD14902 — FTManager publishes an incomplete grayscale preview after required allocation failures

The grayscale path has three required allocations whose failures are not propagated. First, if the temporary pixel `array` allocation fails, the body that allocates and renders `gray_bitmap` is skipped (`workbench/system/ftmanager/fontbitmap_class.c:160-166,231-255`). If `array` succeeds but destination `AllocBitMap()` fails, `gray_bitmap` remains NULL and no render occurs (`:231-253`). In both cases construction continues; the MUI Bitmap object is created and receives the NULL `gray_bitmap` attribute (`:303-318,326-348`). If those allocations succeed but the one-row scratch bitmap allocation fails, the `WritePixelArray8()` call is skipped (`:239-252`) while the destination remains uninitialized: `AllocBitMap()` was called without `BMF_CLEAR`, and its standard raster allocation does not clear planes (`rom/graphics/allocbitmap.c:74-76,193,523-532`; `rom/graphics/allocraster.c:57`). The constructor still publishes that bitmap.

In each case `fbNew()` returns the MUI object instead of failure. `fiUpdatePreview()` treats any non-NULL object as success, removes/disposes the old preview, and adds the new one (`workbench/system/ftmanager/fontinfo_class.c:697-724`). A NULL bitmap draws nothing; the scratch-allocation case exposes uncleared raster contents instead of the requested glyphs.

**Trigger and consequence:** use FTManager's GUI with grayscale preview selected and encounter allocation failure in the grayscale pixel array, destination bitmap, or row-work bitmap. The first two failures replace the previous preview with a blank object; failure of the row-work allocation publishes an unrendered destination whose pixels are not initialized. **Affected configuration:** the selected `workbench-system-ftmanager` GUI, grayscale mode, and any of these allocation failures. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked branches and publication path; contents shown after the scratch failure depend on raster memory contents. Check all three allocations and fail preview construction if any required buffer is unavailable; initialize the destination before writing when appropriate. No allocation failure, preview, or build was induced; source-only.
