`fbNew()` initializes its bounding-box extrema to `INT_MAX`/`INT_MIN` (`workbench/system/ftmanager/fontbitmap_class.c:89-90`). For each input character, a NULL result from `ObtainInfo(... OT_GlyphMap ...)` or `OT_GlyphMap8Bit` takes the explicit missing-glyph branch, advances the pen and skips all four extrema updates (`:102-151`). The selected FreeType2 wrapper returns NULL when `FT_Get_Char_Index()` finds no character mapping, and also explicitly rejects zero-width glyphs such as SPACE (`workbench/libs/freetype2/glyph.c:43-52,354-373`). If every character lacks a glyph map, `xmin`/`ymin` and `xmax`/`ymax` remain at their sentinels. The code then evaluates `xmax - xmin + 1` and `ymax - ymin + 1` as signed `int` (`:152-153`), which overflows the signed range before the positive/size checks (`:159`). The GUI obtains the preview string from the editable test-string field and passes it directly to `FontBitmapObject` (`workbench/system/ftmanager/fontinfo_class.c:690-706`); a non-NULL returned object replaces the previous preview (`:713-722`).

**Trigger and consequence:** use a font with no glyph-map entry for any character in the preview string (including an empty string if the zero-length glyph allocation is accepted). The unmodified extrema feed signed-overflowing dimensions; depending on compiler behavior, this can lead to invalid dimensions or a small blank preview being allocated and published instead of reporting that no glyphs could be drawn. **Affected configuration:** the selected FTManager GUI in either preview mode, for strings whose glyph lookups all fail. **Confidence:** high that the sentinel values reach signed-overflowing arithmetic when the branch conditions hold; medium for the downstream result because signed overflow is undefined behavior. Track whether any drawable glyph updated the bounds, and return an empty/failed preview before calculating dimensions if none did. No font or preview was loaded and no build was run; source-only.


<a id="gd14905"></a>
## GD14905 — FreeType2 glyph retrieval dereferences a failed GlyphMap allocation

`GetGlyph()` allocates a `struct GlyphMap` into `ge->GMap` and calls `RenderGlyph()` only when the allocation succeeds (`workbench/libs/freetype2/glyph.c:354-361`). It then unconditionally reads `ge->GMap->glm_Width` (`:367-372`). If the allocation returned NULL for a character that maps to a glyph, the assignment leaves `ge->GMap` NULL and this read dereferences it before the caller can receive an allocation error. `ObtainInfoA()` reaches this helper for both `OT_GlyphMap` and `OT_GlyphMap8Bits` requests (`workbench/libs/freetype2/obtaininfoa.c:93-115`). The selected FTManager target requests one of those maps for every preview character (`workbench/system/ftmanager/fontbitmap_class.c:91,117-122`), and its makefile links `freetype2` (`workbench/system/ftmanager/mmakefile.src:13`).

**Trigger and consequence:** request a mapped glyph through the FreeType2 library while allocation of the per-glyph `GlyphMap` fails. The library dereferences the NULL pointer, faulting the calling task instead of returning an allocation failure. **Affected configuration:** consumers of the selected AROS FreeType2 wrapper that request either glyph-map tag; FTManager is one confirmed in-tree caller. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked NULL dereference and call path under the stated allocation failure. Return the allocation error immediately when `AllocVec()` fails. No allocation failure, glyph request, or build was induced; source-only.


<a id="gd14906"></a>
## GD14906 — Planar image transfers misindex after a NULL or constant plane

`PBM__Hidd_BitMap__GetImageLUT()` starts each scanline at `data->bitmap->Planes`, then skips a NULL or `(UBYTE *)-1` entry with `continue` before reaching the `plane++` at the bottom of the loop (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_planarbitmapclass.c:692-733`). If any earlier plane is absent, each later depth iteration rereads that same absent slot and never samples the later plane. The generic `PBM_PutImage_Native()` and `PBM_PutImage_Native32()` writers have the same skip-before-increment structure (`:520-562,565-616`), and `PutImageLUT()` forwards to `PBM_PutImage_Native()` (`:648-658`). `WritePixelArray8()` reaches `HIDD_BM_PutImageLUT()` through `write_pixels_8()` (`rom/graphics/writepixelarray8.c:68-77`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:680-691,696-731`). The m68k AmigaVideo GetImageLUT and PutImage overrides repeat this loop pattern (`arch/m68k-amiga/hidd/amigavideo/amigavideo_bitmapclass.c:795-842,855-980`).

A maintained caller can create sparse source bitmaps: `DrawImageState()` constructs a temporary bitmap with each plane assigned from `ImageData`, NULL, or `(PLANEPTR)-1` according to `PlanePick` and `PlaneOnOff` (`rom/intuition/drawimagestate.c:162-200`). For an image whose data is picked into a higher plane while a lower plane is absent, a selected-state blit uses minterm `0x30`; the minterm conversion maps this to `CopyInverted`, and the palette-to-truecolor pen conversion path calls `HIDD_BM_GetImageLUT()` for modes other than Copy/NoOp/Invert (`rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.h:85-90`; `rom/graphics/gfxfuncsupport.c:613-621,432-436`). The planar reader therefore returns a pixel value omitting the selected higher image plane (or retaining only `PlaneOnOff` prefill bits), producing incorrect selected-image colors. For writers, a sparse planar destination similarly causes `PutImage()` to miss writes to later planes when a preceding slot is NULL or constant; `WritePixelArray8()` is one public path to that writer, though no checked-in client passing such a sparse destination was established in this pass.

**Trigger and consequence:** render an `Image` through `DrawImageState()` with a sparse `PlanePick` that maps image data above a NULL or constant lower plane, in a selected-state draw routed through the pen-conversion path; or write pixel data to a sparse planar destination. The display/readback omits higher source planes, and the writer leaves higher destination-plane data unchanged or misapplied. **Affected configuration:** the generic planar HIDD path with an applicable palette-to-truecolor destination or sparse planar write target; equivalent loops are present in the m68k AmigaVideo bitmap class. **Confidence:** high for the plane-pointer control-flow defect; medium for reaching the read/write paths, which depends on draw mode, destination format and sparse bitmap layout. Advance the plane pointer for every plane index, including skipped entries. No image, pixel-array operation or build was run; source-only.

**GD10484 caller/wrapper follow-up (2026-11-06):** the `PhysicalDevices(Instance const&)` convenience constructor (`vulkan_raii.hpp:4190-4196`, available in exception-enabled builds) delegates to the same `Instance::enumeratePhysicalDevices()` implementation and inherits its result. The constructed RAII `PhysicalDevice` stores both the passed native handle and the parent dispatcher (`:3522-3535`); it does not reject null handles. Methods such as `getFeatures()` dispatch that stored handle directly (`:15138-15145`), so a trailing null wrapper reaches the driver with `VK_NULL_HANDLE`. A repository-wide C++ caller search found no in-tree use of this RAII enumeration; the Vulkan HIDD's device enumeration path and the test probe use the C API. This confirms the null-handle consequence while keeping the finding scoped to downstream RAII consumers. No device-set change, query, or build was exercised.

**GD10233 continuation — graphics-pipeline batch counts:** the enhanced `Device::createGraphicsPipelines()` vector overloads, including the `Unique` form, pass `createInfos.size()` directly to Vulkan's `uint32_t createInfoCount` while forwarding the original proxy data (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:4905-4925,4933-4954,4987-5014`; allocator-customized unique form begins at `:5022`). A proxy above `UINT32_MAX` entries truncates at the native boundary, with exactly 2^32 entries becoming a zero count. This is beyond Vulkan's native count representation and practical pipeline limits, so it is recorded as an extreme-size instance of GD10233 rather than a valid-call overrun. No in-tree C++ caller was found. The associated unique-wrapper post-dispatch allocation ordering remains GD10227. See the [coverage entry](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-graphics-pipeline-wrapper-implementation-and-neighboring-command-pass-gd10227gd10233gd10228-rechecked-gd10233-expanded-2026-11-06-no-bodypathloc-credit). No Vulkan call/build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14907"></a>
## GD14907 — Toggle-select buttons return an uninitialized gadget-up code

`ButtonGClass__GM_GOACTIVE()` returns `GMR_NOREUSE | GMR_VERIFY` for a `GACT_TOGGLESELECT` button, but this branch never stores a value through `msg->gpi_Termination` (`rom/intuition/buttongclass.c:291-335`). The public `gpInput` contract requires gadget classes returning `GMR_VERIFY` to set that field; Intuition uses its low 16 bits as the `IDCMP_GADGETUP` Code (`compiler/include/intuition/gadgetclass.h:260-270,289-295`). `DoGPInput()` supplies the address of an uninitialized local `ULONG termination` and passes it to `HandleCustomGadgetRetVal()` (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_support.c:756-780`). When the gadget also has `GACT_RELVERIFY`, that handler emits `IDCMP_GADGETUP` with `termination & 0xffff` (`:639-665`), so the application receives an indeterminate code. The same class explicitly writes `IDCMP_GADGETUP` in its separate `GM_HANDLEINPUT` release branch (`buttongclass.c:376-382`), showing the missing initialization is specific to the toggle-select `GM_GOACTIVE` return. Both activation tags are supported by the base gadget class (`rom/intuition/gadgetclass.c:288-300,350-366`); the selected reqtools file requester creates a toggle-select button (`workbench/libs/reqtools/filereqsetup.c:430-438`), while the generic custom-gadget path is selected by Intuition's input handler (`inputhandler.c:783-789`).

**Trigger and consequence:** activate a custom ButtonGClass gadget configured with both `GACT_TOGGLESELECT` and `GACT_RELVERIFY`. Its immediate `GMR_VERIFY` causes Intuition to send `IDCMP_GADGETUP`, but the message's Code is taken from an uninitialized stack value rather than a defined termination code. The gadget selection state still toggles; consumers that inspect the Code receive an unpredictable value. **Affected configuration:** the selected Intuition ButtonGClass and consumers using toggle-select with release verification. **Confidence:** high for the uninitialized value and its use in the documented output field. Initialize the termination field on this branch to the intended code (or initialize the local before method dispatch). No gadget event or build was run; source-only.

**Additional selected entry point:** Intuition's `DoActivateGadget()` independently constructs `GM_GOACTIVE` with another uninitialized `termination` local and passes it to the same handler (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_support.c:1024-1046`). It is reached by public `ActivateGadget()` (`rom/intuition/activategadget.c:145`) and by input-handler tab cycling (`inputhandler.c:2407`). Thus the missing class write also yields an indeterminate gadget-up Code for these activation paths when the gadget has release verification; this is the same root cause, not a separate finding.

<a id="gd14908"></a>
## GD14908 — Custom gadget removal can race with post-dispatch input handling

`DoGPInput()` calls the custom gadget's `GM_GOACTIVE` or `GM_HANDLEINPUT` method through `Locked_DoMethodA()`, which acquires `GadgetLock` only around `Custom_DoMethodA()` and releases it before `HandleCustomGadgetRetVal()` processes the result (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_support.c:431-452,756-780`). The post-dispatch handler then reads gadget fields, may call `GM_GOINACTIVE`, changes `Activation`, and may traverse the gadget list for tab cycling (`:639-747`). The selected `RemoveGList()` path acquires the same `GadgetLock` while unlinking gadgets (`rom/intuition/removeglist.c:83-137`); it deliberately supports removing an active gadget and defers only while the left button is still down (`:155-183,196-272`).

Because post-processing continues after `Locked_DoMethodA()` releases the lock, another task can remove the gadget in this gap. A definite entry point is `DoActivateGadget()`: it dispatches custom `GM_GOACTIVE`, processes the return, and only then publishes `iihd->ActiveGadget` (`rom/intuition/inputhandler_support.c:1024-1060`). The selected tab-cycle path calls `FindCycleGadget()` and `DoActivateGadget()` while handling the prior gadget's transition (`rom/intuition/inputhandler.c:2395-2408`), so the next gadget is not yet `ActiveGadget` during its `GM_GOACTIVE` callback/result handling. If another task removes that target in the interval, `RemoveGList()` sees it as inactive and takes the direct unlink path (`rom/intuition/removeglist.c:100-120`) instead of deferring removal. A selected MUI caller illustrates teardown ownership: `Boopsi__MUIM_Hide()` calls `RemoveGadget()` and immediately `DisposeObject()` on its embedded gadget (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/boopsi.c:415-432`). This does not establish that MUI always overlaps tab cycling, or that every embedded object is a custom gadget, but it confirms a maintained remove-and-free pattern. The left-button retry defers mouse removal while the button remains down, but does not apply to programmatic/tab-cycle activation. If the caller frees the gadget during this interval, post-processing uses a stale pointer; even without freeing it, Intuition can publish an active pointer to an object no longer in the window list. **Trigger and consequence:** concurrent UI management removes a custom gadget during the interval after its input method returns and before Intuition finishes handling that return. This can cause stale-object access or leave Intuition's active-gadget state inconsistent. **Affected configuration:** windows with custom BOOPSI gadgets where one task processes input while another calls `RemoveGList()`/`RemoveGadget()` and releases the gadget storage. **Confidence:** high for the unprotected interval and removal lock interaction; the race requires task interleaving. Keep gadget lifetime/list membership protected through result processing or revalidate under `GadgetLock` before dereferencing and publishing the result. No input/removal interleaving or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd10244"></a>
## GD10244 — Vulkan-Hpp rasterization default leaves `lineWidth` zero [conditional]

The vendored Vulkan-Hpp `PipelineRasterizationStateCreateInfo` constructor gives its `lineWidth_` parameter `{}` by default and copies it directly to the member (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:55621-55645`). The public member initializer also uses `{}` (`:55812-55824`), so both default construction and zero-initialization leave `lineWidth == 0.0f`. `setLineWidth()` is available but is not applied automatically (`:55731-55735`). Conversion to native Vulkan passes the wrapper's memory directly through reinterpret-cast conversion operators (`:55737-55755`); `GraphicsPipelineCreateInfo` stores the rasterization-state pointer unchanged and likewise exposes native reinterpret-cast conversion (`:56910-56956,57123-57140`). No wrapper normalization replaces zero with a valid line width.

**Trigger and consequence:** a client default-constructs the rasterization state, supplies it to a graphics-pipeline create info, and creates a pipeline where wide-line support or dynamic line-width state does not exempt the static value. The native call receives `lineWidth = 0.0f`, violating the valid-usage requirement for rasterization and causing pipeline creation validation/failure or invalid driver behavior. **Affected configuration:** clients using the optional `hidd-vulkan` C++ header API and constructing a rasterization state without explicitly setting a valid line width; the HIDD target has no default `workbench-hidds` dependency edge in this snapshot, and the in-tree VulkanProbe does not create a graphics pipeline. **Confidence:** high for the default value and unchanged native pass-through; no pipeline or validation layer was run. Default `lineWidth` to `1.0f`, or require callers to set a valid value before native conversion. Source-only.

<a id="gd10241"></a>
## GD10241 — Vulkan-Hpp create-info equality adds zero to null array pointers [conditional]

`DeviceCreateInfo::operator==` forms `ppEnabledExtensionNames + enabledExtensionCount` before calling `std::equal()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:38608-38618`). The wrapper's default member initializer sets `ppEnabledExtensionNames` to null and the count to zero (`:38634-38637`); default construction therefore evaluates null-pointer-plus-zero when two default objects are compared. `InstanceCreateInfo::operator==` repeats the same pattern for both layer and extension name arrays, whose default pointers/counts are also null/zero (`:67543-67556,67567-67574`). The equality operators are present even when the optional spaceship operator is enabled; the latter uses count-bounded loops and does not form these end pointers.

**Trigger and consequence:** a C++ client compares default `DeviceCreateInfo` or `InstanceCreateInfo` objects with `operator==`. The pointer arithmetic is undefined even though the range count is zero and `std::equal()` would otherwise process no elements; behavior is not guaranteed by the language. **Affected configuration:** clients using these optional Vulkan-Hpp struct wrappers and equality operators. The checked-in VulkanProbe uses the C API and no in-tree caller of these C++ comparisons was found. **Confidence:** high for null/zero defaults and the equality expression; no C++ comparison was executed. Guard each array comparison when its count is zero, or use a zero-count-safe comparison path. No C++ client, comparison, or build was run; source-only.

The enhanced `CommandBuffer::setViewportWScalingNV()` overload also forwards `viewportWScalings.size()` to the native `uint32_t viewportCount`, retaining the proxy data pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:14128-14138`). On a 64-bit client, a source container larger than `UINT32_MAX` elements is narrowed by `ArrayProxy` construction; the dispatched count truncates while the pointer remains unchanged. This is another GD10233 call site, gated by `VK_NV_clip_space_w_scaling`; such a list exceeds the native count representation and Vulkan viewport limits, so this is an invalid/extreme-input case rather than a demonstrated valid-call overrun. Repository search found only generated declarations/definitions and no non-generated in-tree call site.

Two additional enhanced proxy-count sites occur in the legacy `VK_NV_shading_rate_image` wrappers. `CommandBuffer::setViewportShadingRatePaletteNV()` forwards `shadingRatePalettes.size()` as native `uint32_t viewportCount`, and `setCoarseSampleOrderNV()` forwards `customSampleOrders.size()` as native `uint32_t customSampleOrderCount` while retaining each original pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:18823-18824,18854-18857`). On a 64-bit client, a proxy built from more than `UINT32_MAX` elements truncates its count while keeping the data pointer; these lists also violate native/device limits, so this is an invalid/extreme-input GD10233 case rather than a demonstrated valid-call overrun. Both are gated by `VK_NV_shading_rate_image`; repository search found only generated declarations/definitions, not non-generated in-tree callers.

The enhanced `Device::bindAccelerationStructureMemoryNV()` wrapper forwards `bindInfos.size()` to native `uint32_t bindInfoCount` with the original proxy pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:19060-19073`). Oversized source containers therefore narrow at the proxy/native boundary, with a zero count at exactly `2^32`; such arrays exceed API/device limits, so this is an invalid/extreme-input GD10233 instance, not a demonstrated valid-call overrun. It is gated by `VK_NV_ray_tracing`; no non-generated in-tree caller was found.

`Device::createRayTracingPipelinesNVUnique()` also follows GD10227's raw-handle-then-owner-vector allocation order: both allocator forms create raw pipelines, then the default-allocator form reserves the destination unique vector and the custom-allocator form constructs/reserves it after dispatch (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:19309-19321,19346-19360`). If that allocation throws after one or more pipeline handles were created, stack unwinding destroys only the raw handle vector and leaks those Vulkan pipelines until device teardown. This is an additional `VK_NV_ray_tracing` instance of GD10227; no allocation failure or Vulkan call was induced.

The enhanced (non-RAII) `CommandBuffer::setExclusiveScissorEnableNV()` and `setExclusiveScissorNV()` wrappers also forward `ArrayProxy::size()` as their native `uint32_t exclusiveScissorCount`, preserving the proxy data pointer (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:19993-20003,20014-20023`). Containers above `UINT32_MAX` therefore truncate, with exactly `2^32` entries becoming a zero count; such counts exceed the relevant device limits and are invalid/extreme inputs, not demonstrated valid-call overruns. These are the enhanced counterparts to the RAII GD10233 sites already listed. No non-generated in-tree call site was found.

**Additional GD10223 instance (2026-11-06):** both enhanced `Device::getCudaModuleCacheNV()` vector overloads leave `cacheSize` uninitialized before the initial count query, then inspect it after `resultCheck()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:23547-23574,23582-23609`). The command documents `VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED`, `VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN`, and `VK_ERROR_VALIDATION_FAILED`, while its size-output description only covers successful/incomplete retrieval ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetCudaModuleCacheNV.html)). In `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` builds with result assertions disabled or non-aborting, a failed first call that leaves `cacheSize` unwritten reaches `cacheSize <= cacheData.size()` and potentially `resize(cacheSize)`, reading an indeterminate value. **Affected configuration:** beta Vulkan-Hpp clients enabling `VK_ENABLE_BETA_EXTENSIONS` and `VK_NV_cuda_kernel_launch`, using either enhanced vector overload in no-exceptions mode with non-aborting result assertions. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked use and documented error returns; dependent on error behavior leaving the output untouched, which the command does not specify. No CUDA module call or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd14909"></a>
## GD14909 — Vulkan-Hpp property helpers pass scalar output storage for arrays [conditional]

The enhanced singular `Device::writeAccelerationStructuresPropertyKHR<DataType>()` accepts an `ArrayProxy` of acceleration structures, forwards the full proxy size as `accelerationStructureCount`, but advertises only `sizeof(DataType)` bytes of output and returns a single `DataType` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_handles.hpp:14925-14934`; definition at `vulkan_funcs.hpp:17625-17646`). The adjacent plural helper allocates caller-selected output storage and passes its full byte size; the singular overload instead passes one element regardless of the number of input structures. The native command's valid-usage rule requires `dataSize >= accelerationStructureCount * stride` ([Vulkan reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkWriteAccelerationStructuresPropertiesKHR.html#VUID-vkWriteAccelerationStructuresPropertiesKHR-dataSize-03452)). For a multi-element proxy and normal nonzero result stride, the fixed one-element output size violates that rule; the call is invalid and validation may reject it. The scalar return also cannot expose one result per input structure. **Trigger and consequence:** a client supplies more than one acceleration structure to this enhanced helper expecting results for the whole proxy; results beyond the first are unavailable, and native output semantics are inconsistent with the forwarded count. **Affected configuration:** optional Vulkan-Hpp C++ clients using `VK_KHR_acceleration_structure`; no non-generated in-tree caller was found. **Confidence:** high that the wrapper forwards N inputs with only one result's storage and returns one scalar; intended usage for N>1 is inferred from the array parameter and neighboring plural overload. No Vulkan call, C++ instantiation, build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

**Additional GD14909 instance (2026-11-06):** `Device::writeMicromapsPropertyEXT<DataType>()` has the same array/scalar mismatch: it accepts an `ArrayProxy<const MicromapEXT>`, forwards `micromaps.size()`, but passes `sizeof(DataType)` output storage and returns a scalar (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_handles.hpp:17071-17073`; definition at `vulkan_funcs.hpp:25903-25919`). The adjacent plural `writeMicromapsPropertiesEXT()` accepts explicit output size and returns a vector. This is conditional on optional `VK_EXT_opacity_micromap` C++ clients using multiple micromaps; no in-tree caller was found. The N-input intent is inferred from the array parameter and plural overload. The command's valid-usage rule requires `dataSize >= micromapCount * stride` ([Vulkan reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkWriteMicromapsPropertiesEXT.html#VUID-vkWriteMicromapsPropertiesEXT-dataSize-07576)); with multiple micromaps and normal nonzero result stride, the fixed one-element output size makes this call invalid, and validation may reject it. No Vulkan operation or build was run; source-only.

**Additional GD10227 instance (2026-11-06):** both enhanced `Device::createPipelineBinariesKHRUnique()` overloads call Vulkan into a local `std::vector<PipelineBinaryKHR>`, then allocate/reserve the destination vector of `UniqueHandle<PipelineBinaryKHR>` only after result checking (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:28687-28729,28747-28790`). If that allocation throws after Vulkan has returned handles, unwinding destroys only the raw vector and leaves the pipeline binaries unowned. Conditional on optional `VK_KHR_pipeline_binary` C++ clients and host allocation failure; no in-tree caller was found. No allocation failure or Vulkan call was induced; source-only.


**Additional GD14909 instances (2026-11-07):** The enhanced singular `Device::getRayTracingShaderGroupHandleKHR<DataType>()` and `getRayTracingCaptureReplayShaderGroupHandleKHR<DataType>()` both accept `groupCount`, pass that full count to Vulkan, but provide only `sizeof(DataType)` output bytes and return one `DataType` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:18218-18229,18277-18288`; declarations at `vulkan_handles.hpp:15092-15130`). Their RAII equivalents repeat the same mismatch (`vulkan_raii.hpp:22105-22120,22149-22163`). The Vulkan reference specifies that each call writes `groupCount` handles and requires `dataSize` to cover the per-handle size multiplied by `groupCount` ([shader handles](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetRayTracingShaderGroupHandlesKHR.html#VUID-vkGetRayTracingShaderGroupHandlesKHR-dataSize-02420), [capture/replay handles](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetRayTracingCaptureReplayShaderGroupHandlesKHR.html#VUID-vkGetRayTracingCaptureReplayShaderGroupHandlesKHR-dataSize-03484)). If a caller requests multiple groups with a `DataType` sized for one handle, the wrapper issues an invalid undersized-output call and cannot return all handles; a driver that writes the requested group array could exceed that object. The vector overloads accept an explicit byte size and allocate matching storage. No non-generated in-tree caller was found. This remains conditional on optional Vulkan-Hpp clients using the scalar helper with `groupCount > 1`; caller intent is inferred from the count argument and adjacent plural/vector overloads. No Vulkan call, build or C++ instantiation was run; source-only.
<a id="gd14910"></a>
## GD14910 — Vulkan loader reads the output-only instance-version pointer

When the HIDD object exists, `vkEnumerateInstanceVersion()` initializes its local `apiVersion` by reading `*pApiVersion` before dispatch (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/vulkan_loader.c:270-288`). Vulkan defines this parameter as an output value: the supported version is written to it, and callers need only pass a valid pointer ([official reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkEnumerateInstanceVersion.html)). The HIDD message also explicitly describes the field as output (`vulkan_hidd.h:1252-1257`), and the class callback forwards the pointer to the provider or writes Vulkan 1.0 itself (`vulkan_class.c:953-961`). Thus the loader reads an indeterminate value for a normal caller that passes an uninitialized output variable, before the provider gets a chance to write it; this is undefined behavior in the loader and can also feed arbitrary prior contents to a provider that treats its pointer as output-only. **Trigger and consequence:** a client calls this entry point with a valid pointer to an uninitialized `uint32_t` after loader initialization succeeds. **Affected configuration:** clients using the AROS Vulkan loader with a constructed Vulkan HIDD object; the no-object fallback bypasses the read. **Confidence:** high for the output-only contract and unconditional read on the dispatched path. No Vulkan call or build was run; source-only.


**Caller/configuration recheck (2026-11-06):** exact-symbol search found only the checked-in VulkanProbe call in `workbench/hidds/vulkan/test/VulkanProbe.c:59`; its local `apiVersion` is explicitly initialized to zero (`:37`), so this caller does not trigger the uninitialized-value case. The loader is built as an explicit `hidd-vulkan-loader` link library (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/mmakefile.src:41-43`); its aggregate dependency is commented out (`:32-33`), and the probe is a separate explicit target. Therefore retain GD14910 as a public-loader contract defect for callers that pass a normal uninitialized output variable, with no checked-in call-site manifestation established. The loader's no-HIDD fallback writes Vulkan 1.0 and bypasses the read; the defect is on the HIDD-present dispatch path. No call or build was run.

<a id="gd14912"></a>
## GD14912 — Vulkan-Hpp pipeline-cache helper reads an undefined size after error [conditional]

Both enhanced `Device::getPipelineCacheData()` overloads declare `size_t dataSize` without initialization, call the dispatch function with `pData == nullptr`, and use `dataSize` after `resultCheck()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:3633-3659,3668-3694`; declarations at `vulkan_handles.hpp:12168-12178`). In `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` builds, `resultCheck()` invokes `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT_ON_RESULT`; the default macro maps to `assert` (`vulkan_hpp_macros.hpp:78-80`), which is disabled by `NDEBUG`. The Vulkan command permits runtime errors including out-of-device-memory, out-of-host-memory, unknown, and validation failures ([`vkGetPipelineCacheData`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetPipelineCacheData.html)); Vulkan specifies that, unless otherwise stated, output parameters have undefined contents on runtime error ([`VkResult`](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkResult.html)). The command does not define a special size output for those error returns. Thus a runtime error can leave `dataSize` undefined, after which the wrapper evaluates it in the size assertion and comparison and may resize its vector based on an indeterminate value.

**Trigger and consequence:** an optional C++ client calls either enhanced overload in a `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS`, `NDEBUG` build and the initial pipeline-cache query returns a runtime error. The helper reads the undefined `dataSize` after the nonfatal result check, causing undefined behavior and potentially an invalid vector resize before returning the error. **Affected configuration:** copied optional Vulkan-Hpp public headers; no non-generated in-tree caller of this helper was found. **Confidence:** high for the source flow and applicable API contract; actual occurrence depends on a runtime error. No Vulkan call, C++ instantiation, build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd14913"></a>
## GD14913 — Vulkan-Hpp mapMemory may return an uninitialized pointer on failure [conditional]

The enhanced `Device::mapMemory()` declares `void * pData` without initialization, passes its address to `vkMapMemory`, checks the result, then moves the pointer into `ResultValue<void *>` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_funcs.hpp:1113-1131`; declaration at `vulkan_handles.hpp:11279-11284`; result construction at `vulkan.hpp:7459-7480,7527-7540`). In `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS` builds, `resultCheck()` only invokes `VULKAN_HPP_ASSERT_ON_RESULT`; if that assertion is disabled or configured away, execution continues for an error result, and `ResultValue` copies the still-indeterminate pointer. The Vulkan specification describes `ppData` as the pointer returned on success and lists `VK_ERROR_MEMORY_MAP_FAILED`, `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY`, `VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_HOST_MEMORY`, `VK_ERROR_UNKNOWN`, and `VK_ERROR_VALIDATION_FAILED` as failures without defining a failure value for `ppData` ([Khronos Vulkan specification, `vkMapMemory`](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/man/html/vkMapMemory.html)). **Trigger and consequence:** an enhanced-overload caller builds with `VULKAN_HPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS`, the result assertion does not abort, and `vkMapMemory` returns an error without writing `ppData`; constructing the returned `ResultValue` reads an indeterminate pointer, which is undefined behavior even if the caller checks the error before accessing `.value`. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp public headers; no non-generated in-tree C++ caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the unsafe result construction under the stated failure behavior; whether a particular implementation writes `ppData` on failure is unspecified, so that remains implementation-dependent. No Vulkan call, C++ instantiation, build or runtime behavior was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd14911"></a>
## GD14911 — Info dereferences a failed fallback `.info` path allocation [selected Workbench tool]

When `MatchFirst(file, ap)` fails, Info allocates a buffer for the alternate `file + ".info"` path, then immediately passes the pointer to `sprintf()` without checking it (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/Info/main.c:793-801`). `AllocVec()` can return NULL when that allocation fails. The initial failed `MatchFirst()` resets `ap_Base` and the pattern builder frees any partial chain on its own error path (`rom/dos/matchfirst.c:63-77`; `rom/dos/match_misc.c:84-92,283-303`), so this is distinct from GD6051, which covers a successful match chain later freed without `MatchEnd()`.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** the selected `workbench-system-wanderer-tools-info` program (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/Info/mmakefile.src:6-16`) receives a file/icon name whose direct `MatchFirst()` fails, followed by failure to allocate the fallback `.info` path buffer. **Consequence:** `sprintf()` writes through NULL and Info can fault instead of reaching the fallback result handling. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked nullable allocation and immediate write; no allocation failure or Info launch was induced. Check the allocation and report/return a recoverable failure. Source-only.

Sources: `workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/Info/main.c:782-814`; `rom/dos/matchfirst.c:63-77`; `rom/dos/match_misc.c:84-92,283-303`. See the [Info coverage ledger](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#info-texteditor-exporthook-full-body-and-export-caller-pass-gd9992-corrected-and-gd10534). Source-only review.

<a id="gd14914"></a>
## GD14914 — DiskInfo can index past its size-suffix table for extremely large reported sizes [conditional]

`FormatBlocksSized()` has five suffix pointers (`K`, `M`, `G`, `T`, `P`) but indexes `suffixes[divcount]` on every division without bounding `divcount` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Tools/DiskInfo/support.c:19,65-82`). Its size is the `UQUAD` product of the 32-bit `blocks` and `bytesperblock` parameters, converted to `DOUBLE` (`:67`); while that size is greater than 1024, each iteration consumes another suffix. If the product exceeds `1024^6` bytes (1 EiB), five iterations leave the value above 1024 and the sixth reads `suffixes[5]`, past the array. The resulting invalid pointer is passed as the `%s` argument to `snprintf()` (`:84-87`). The existing GD6053 count narrowing and percentage overflow are separate defects in this helper.

**Trigger and consequence:** DiskInfo formats a size from DOS `InfoData` whose block count and block size produce more than 1 EiB after the helper's `ULONG` parameter conversions. The code can read an out-of-bounds suffix pointer while formatting the size; the displayed text or call outcome depends on adjacent data. **Affected configuration:** selected Wanderer DiskInfo when a filesystem reports such extreme metadata. No checked-in filesystem configuration producing this size was identified, so this remains a conditional candidate. **Confidence:** high for the unbounded array access and threshold; practical reachability is unestablished. Clamp the suffix index or handle larger units explicitly. No volume query or GUI operation was performed; source-only. See the [DiskInfo formatter review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#diskinfo-main-support-full-body-2026-11-03).

<a id="gd14915"></a>
## GD14915 — Scrollgroup ignores FreeHoriz and FreeVert movement limits [conditional]

The Scrollgroup API declares `MUIA_Scrollgroup_FreeHoriz` and `MUIA_Scrollgroup_FreeVert` as initialization booleans (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/scrollgroup.h:19-23`), and the MUI Scrollgroup contract describes them as controlling whether the group is horizontally or vertically moveable ([MUI Royale Scrollgroup reference](https://hollywood-mal.com/docs/pdf/muiroyale.pdf), sections 43.2-43.3). The class constructor reads `MUIA_Scrollgroup_Contents` and `MUIA_Scrollgroup_UseWinBorder`, but never reads either Free attribute (`scrollgroup.c:293-348`). The Scrollgroup layout hook decides and shows bars solely from content and viewport min/max dimensions (`:133-177,188-215`); its bar notification hook always forwards both horizontal and vertical positions into the Virtgroup (`:285-324`). OM_GET also exposes only Contents, HorizBar and VertBar (`:367-384`). Consequently, setting either movement attribute to FALSE does not prevent the corresponding bar from being shown or the content from moving on that axis when it overflows.

**Trigger and consequence:** create a Scrollgroup with `MUIA_Scrollgroup_FreeHoriz, FALSE` or `MUIA_Scrollgroup_FreeVert, FALSE` and content whose minimum size exceeds the corresponding viewport. The class still creates and lays out both scrollbars, and the notification path still moves the content on both axes. Maintained-tree callers set these attributes to FALSE in QuickPart, InstallAROS, SysMon, SysExplorer, Aboutbox, MiamiPanel, PSI, Wanderer Preferences, and Zune Navigation Preferences (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_Main.c:472`; `workbench/tools/InstallAROS/ia_main.c:686,745`; `workbench/system/SysMon/main.c:135`; `workbench/tools/SysExplorer/computer_page_cl.c:434`; `workbench/classes/zune/aboutbox/Aboutbox.c:473`; `workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/MUI.MiamiPanel/Classes/muimiamipanel_class_mgroup.c:97` and `.../muimiamipanel_class_prefs.c:270,300,337`; `workbench/prefs/PSI/editpanel_class.c:487`; `workbench/prefs/wanderer/wpeditor.c:1186-1187`; `workbench/prefs/Zune/navigationp.c:66`). The exact content minimum-size overflow condition for these callers has not been established, so these references document use of the ignored option and do not demonstrate a caller-specific visual regression. **Affected configuration:** MUI Scrollgroup users relying on a false movement limit when content exceeds the viewport; Scrollgroup is included in muimaster for the `tiny` variant or built as its separate MUI class (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src:4-30,300-305`; `classes/mmakefile.src:203-209`). **Confidence:** high that the attributes are ignored in this implementation; visible unwanted movement requires overflow and user interaction. No GUI layout or scrolling operation was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md), MUI Scrollgroup attribute and caller pass dated 2026-11-07.

<a id="gd14916"></a>
## GD14916 — LogView installs a failed pattern parse as its active filter [malformed pattern; selected on x86-64 PC]

The LogView task-name filter allocates `patternBuf`, calls `ParsePatternNoCase()`, ignores its return value, frees the prior valid filter, and stores the new buffer as `logfilt` (`workbench/system/LogView/logview.c:476-488`). The parser returns `-1` for malformed templates before guaranteeing a terminating NUL: for example, a trailing `#` returns `ERROR_BAD_TEMPLATE` at `rom/dos/patternmatching.c:454-467`, and an unclosed group returns at `:628-633`. On the next list rebuild, `CreateLogEntryList()` passes `logfilt` to `MatchPatternNoCase()` (`workbench/system/LogView/logclass.c:45-81`); the matcher consumes the parsed pattern as a NUL-terminated token stream (`rom/dos/matchpatternnocase.c:53`; `rom/dos/patternmatching.c:326-430`).

**Trigger and consequence:** enter a malformed wildcard expression such as a trailing `#` in LogView's task filter and apply the filter. The parser failure is ignored, so LogView replaces its prior filter with an uninitialized or partially written buffer and uses it for matching. Results may be incorrect; matching may also read beyond the valid parsed text, with failure behavior dependent on allocator contents. **Affected configuration:** `workbench-system-logview` is selected by the Workbench aggregate when `TARGET_USELOGRES=yes` (`workbench/system/LogView/mmakefile.src:4-12`). `configure.in:1649` forces `with_log_resource=yes` for x86-64 PC, and `workbench-complete` depends on `workbench-system` (`workbench/mmakefile.src:9-21`), so the target is selected in x86-64 PC Workbench builds. Other configurations select it when log.resource is enabled. This proves build-target selection, not package/image inclusion or runtime launch. **Confidence:** high that parser failure is ignored and the failed output is installed and consumed; exact visible or fault outcome is conditional. Check the parse result and retain the prior filter or reject the input on failure. No malformed filter or GUI operation was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14917"></a>
## GD14917 — VMM stores and compares task patterns after parse failure [malformed pattern; optional target]

`EnterTask()` allocates a token buffer and calls `ParsePatternNoCase()` without checking its result, then stores that buffer in the task table as a pattern (`workbench/system/VMM/forbidden_tasks.c:310-360`). A malformed template can make the parser return before writing its terminator (`rom/dos/patternmatching.c:454-467,628-633`). The selected `ExtCheckVirtMem()` path later passes the stored pattern to `MatchPatternNoCase()` (`forbidden_tasks.c:134-211`). `RemoveTask()` has the same unchecked parser call into a 200-byte stack buffer, then compares the result with `strcmp()` (`:365-397`); it documents that the buffer is assumed to be NUL-terminated. Rexx `ADD_PROG` and `REM_PROG` pass the supplied task name to these functions (`workbench/system/VMM/rexx.c:66-104`), and configuration loading also reaches `EnterTask()` (`workbench/system/VMM/config.c:22-55`).

**Trigger and consequence:** add or remove a VMM task entry with a malformed wildcard expression, such as a trailing `#`. The failed parse is treated as success: add stores an uninitialized or partial pattern that is later matched against task names; remove compares an uninitialized or unterminated stack buffer. Task matching/removal can produce incorrect results and may read beyond valid pattern text. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-system-vmm-handler` (`workbench/system/VMM/mmakefile.src:4-50`); its aggregate dependency is commented, so default inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high that parse errors are ignored and failed output is consumed; exact outcome depends on allocator/stack contents. Reject malformed patterns before publishing or comparing them. No Rexx command, configuration load, task, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14918"></a>
## GD14918 — ReqTools Select All matches an unvalidated pattern buffer [malformed user pattern; optional target]

`SelectAll()` allocates an uninitialized `selpat`, calls `ParsePatternNoCase()` without checking the result, then passes `selpat` to `MatchPatternNoCase()` for each eligible entry (`workbench/libs/reqtools/filereqextra.c:533-557`). The user can reach this path through the Match Pattern dialog (`workbench/libs/reqtools/filereqmain.c:1016-1026`). A malformed expression such as a trailing `#` makes the shared parser return `ERROR_BAD_TEMPLATE` before writing a NUL (`rom/dos/patternmatching.c:454-467`); `MatchPatternNoCase()` then interprets the uninitialized allocation as a terminated token stream (`rom/dos/matchpatternnocase.c:53`; `patternmatching.c:326-430`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke Select All by Pattern, enter a malformed wildcard expression, and accept it. The parser error is ignored and matching proceeds on uninitialized or partially written pattern data. Selection can be incorrect; matching may read beyond valid pattern text, with the exact failure dependent on allocator contents. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable `workbench-libs-reqtools` module (`workbench/libs/reqtools/mmakefile.src:53`); the aggregate edge is commented, so default inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high that the failure result is ignored and the buffer is consumed; exact visible or fault outcome is conditional. Check the parse result and abort selection on failure. No requester, pattern, or build was run; source-only.

**Additional ReqTools file-filter path for GD14918:** the initial requester setup and later PATSTR update also ignore `ParsePatternNoCase()`'s result when writing `glob->matchpat` (`workbench/libs/reqtools/filereq.c:85`; `filereqmain.c:1042-1045`). `SkipEntry()` then applies that buffer while filtering files (`filereqextra.c:477-501`). The initial `GlobData` is cleared, so a malformed pattern with a valid prefix can become a silently truncated filter; subsequent failures can leave prior bytes in the reused buffer. This gives the same parse-error handling defect a second user-visible path. The Select All route above remains the direct uninitialized-allocation case.


<a id="gd14920"></a>
## GD14920 — Info overruns the local buffer while normalizing long device patterns [selected Workbench command]

`myMatchPatternNoCase()` stores each candidate pattern length in `len`, then reads `p[len - 1]` before checking whether the pattern is empty. For a valid empty pattern this reads one byte before the string. For nonempty patterns not ending in `:`, it copies the full pattern into `name[32]` and appends `:` plus a NUL without checking the combined length (`workbench/c/Info.c:235-254`). A 31-character pattern writes the colon at `name[31]` but the terminator at `name[32]`, one byte past the array; longer patterns overwrite further adjacent stack storage.

The `DEVICES/M` argument path validates each input pattern with a 128-byte output buffer and then calls `ScanDosList()` (`Info.c:571-609,618-621`). `ParsePatternNoCase()` accepts the empty string by writing a NUL and returning success (`rom/dos/patternmatching.c:440-444`); ReadArgs accepts quoted empty items (`rom/dos/readitem.c:132-164`). Thus `DEVICES=""` reaches the under-read. A 31-character literal also parses successfully, so validation does not reject it. `ScanDosList()` invokes `myMatchPatternNoCase()` while comparing filters against DOS assign/volume names and again for active device names (`:310-318,355-369`); it reaches the unsafe normalization before deciding whether the candidate matches. ReadArgs' command input buffer permits these inputs (`rom/dos/readargs.c:205,303-304`).

**Trigger and consequence:** run Info with `DEVICES=""` and a DOS-list scan that reaches an assign, volume, or active device; the matcher reads one byte before the empty string. Alternatively, use a non-colon-terminated pattern of at least 31 characters; the matcher writes beyond `name[32]` (at exactly 31 characters, the NUL is one byte out of bounds). These reads/writes can corrupt adjacent stack data or fault during filtering. Check for zero length before indexing, and bound or dynamically size colon normalization. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected `Info` command in `workbench-c` (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:5-24`), selected through `workbench-complete` (`workbench/mmakefile.src:9-24`). This is separate from GD14568's expanded-filter-vector capacity, GD14569's unmounted-volume task dereference, and GD14570's empty-assignment placeholder read. **Confidence:** high for both boundary conditions and accepted caller inputs; no command, DOS-list scan, or build was run. Source-only.

**Review evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#info-rename-pattern-caller-recheck-gd14920-added).

<a id="gd14922"></a>
## GD14922 — H.264 decode setter updates the SPS limit instead of the PPS limit [optional copied Vulkan-Hpp API]

`VideoDecodeH264SessionParametersCreateInfoKHR::setMaxStdPPSCount()` assigns its argument to `maxStdSPSCount` instead of `maxStdPPSCount` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:161219-161222`). The constructor and public fields keep the SPS and PPS limits separate (`:161151-161161,161285-161290`), and the generated setters for the paired H.264 add-info structure also maintain independent SPS/PPS values (`:161070-161098`). This create-info is carried in the video-session-parameters creation chain (`vulkan.hpp:12184`); `Device::createVideoSessionParametersKHR()` forwards that chain to `vkCreateVideoSessionParametersKHR()` (`vulkan_funcs.hpp:11689-11700`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a C++ client initializes an H.264 decode session-parameter create-info, then calls `setMaxStdPPSCount(n)`. The wrapper changes the SPS maximum to `n` and leaves the PPS maximum at its previous value, often zero. The driver receives unintended SPS/PPS capacity limits and may reject later parameter additions or accept an incorrect configuration. **Affected configuration:** consumers of the optional copied Vulkan-Hpp header using this setter; no maintained-tree C++ caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the wrong assignment and native forwarding; exact driver response depends on its validation and subsequent parameter additions. Assign to `maxStdPPSCount`. No Vulkan call or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-video-decode-h264-session-parameter-setter-gd14922).

<a id="gd14923"></a>
## GD14923 — H.265 encode enhanced constructor initializes PPS from the SPS proxy [optional copied Vulkan-Hpp API]

The enhanced `VideoEncodeH265SessionParametersAddInfoKHR` constructor initializes `pStdPPSs` with `stdSPSs_.data()` rather than `stdPPSs_.data()` (`workbench/hidds/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_structs.hpp:169253-169263`). The declared member is `const StdVideoH265PictureParameterSet *`, while `stdSPSs_` is an `ArrayProxyNoTemporaries<const StdVideoH265SequenceParameterSet>`; these are distinct record pointer types. The same constructor's count initializer correctly uses `stdPPSs_.size()`, and the adjacent `setStdPPSs()` setter stores `stdPPSs_.data()` (`:169337-169343`).

**Trigger and consequence:** compile a C++ translation unit that includes this copied Vulkan-Hpp header with enhanced mode enabled (the default unless `VULKAN_HPP_DISABLE_ENHANCED_MODE` is defined). The non-template constructor body contains an invalid conversion from a sequence-parameter-set pointer to a picture-parameter-set pointer, so conforming C++ compilers should reject the header even if the constructor is not called. **Affected configuration:** optional copied Vulkan-Hpp headers with the H.265 video types available and enhanced mode enabled; disabling enhanced mode avoids this constructor. **Confidence:** high for the incompatible pointer types and source typo; no compiler was run. Initialize `pStdPPSs` from `stdPPSs_.data()`. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [`AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md`](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vulkan-hpp-h265-encode-session-parameter-constructor-gd14923).

<a id="gd14925"></a>
## GD14925 — Wanderer leaks prepared objects when IconWindow construction fails

`Wanderer__MUIM_Wanderer_CreateDrawerWindow()` creates an owned menustrip before constructing the `IconWindowObject` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/wanderer.c:3994-4010`). If the window constructor returns NULL, the function skips all success-path setup and returns `window` without disposing `_NewWandDrawerMenu__menustrip` (`:4018-4109`). This failure can occur after the strip was successfully created: the IconWindow class delegates to the selected muimaster Window class (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow.c:674-718`), whose `Window__OM_NEW()` allocates `wd_MemoryPool` before it processes caller tags, and explicitly disposes the partial window and returns NULL when `CreatePool()` fails (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:2853-2872,2902-2906`). The failed Window constructor therefore has not adopted either the caller's `MUIA_Window_Menustrip` or the `MUIA_Window_RootObject` group constructed inline as the `WindowContents` argument (`iconwindow.c:699-718`). The root group and any children it adopted are lost when IconWindow's `DoSuperNew()` returns NULL and its constructor falls through to `return self` without cleanup (`:720-827`). The optional `_newIconWin__BackFillHook` allocation is also not freed on this failure path; it is only stored in instance data after successful superclass construction and freed later by `IconWindow__OM_DISPOSE()` (`:450-456,720-787,830-860).

**Trigger and consequence:** create a Wanderer drawer/root window when NewMenu conversion succeeds but the subsequent Window instance-pool allocation fails. The menustrip, prepared WindowContents object tree, and optional backfill hook remain allocated with no retained owner. **Affected configuration:** the full Workbench target selects `workbench-system-wanderer-app`: `AROS` depends on `workbench-complete`, which includes `workbench-system`, and the active MetaMake virtual-target edge adds Wanderer to that aggregate (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-21`; `workbench/system/mmakefile.src:10-14`; `workbench/system/Wanderer/mmakefile.src:23-39`). The path uses the selected muimaster Window class. **Confidence:** high for the ownership and early Window-construction failure path; manifestation requires the stated allocation sequence. Unwind the menustrip, the temporary WindowContents tree, and the optional backfill hook when superclass construction fails, while transferring ownership on success. No allocation failure or GUI was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Wanderer prepared-object ownership on failed IconWindow construction](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-menustrip-failed-window-construction-gd14925).

<a id="gd14926"></a>
## GD14926 — Wanderer leaks DiskObjects loaded by drawer settings operations

Two drawer-settings paths acquire DiskObjects without releasing them. For every non-root IconWindow, `IconWindow__OM_NEW()` loads the drawer icon with `GetIconTags()` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow.c:488-512`), reads its DrawerData/ToolTypes and passes it to `IconWindow_RestoreSettings()` (`:514-587`), but never retains or frees the pointer. `IconWindow_StoreSettings()` separately loads another DiskObject with `GetIconTags()` before updating DrawerData/ToolTypes and calling `PutDiskObject()` (`:139-247`); it restores the original ToolTypes pointer after writing but never frees the loaded DiskObject. For an existing `.info` file, `GetIconTagList()` calls `ReadIcon()`, which creates a new DiskObject and returns it on successful AOS or PNG parsing (`workbench/libs/icon/geticontaglist.c:177-186`; `workbench/libs/icon/support.c:279-315`). `PutDiskObject()` serializes the supplied structure and does not consume caller ownership (`workbench/libs/icon/putdiskobject.c:42-50`; `workbench/libs/icon/puticontaglist.c:124-155`). `FreeDiskObject()` releases the DiskObject and layout-specific allocations created by icon loading (`workbench/libs/icon/freediskobject.c:25-67`).

**Trigger and consequence:** open or recreate a non-root drawer window whose `.info` icon loads successfully, or snapshot a drawer whose icon loads successfully. Each window construction and each settings-save call loses its loaded DiskObject, including mapped/layout resources; repeated drawer opens and snapshots leak memory. **Affected configuration:** the full Workbench target selects `workbench-system-wanderer-app`, whose source list includes `iconwindow.c` (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-21`; `workbench/system/mmakefile.src:10-14`; `workbench/system/Wanderer/mmakefile.src:23-39`). **Confidence:** high for the successful owned `ReadIcon()` result and the missing release/retained owner in both settings paths; the leak occurs for each successful load. Call `FreeDiskObject(drawericon)` after the last settings read, including all exits after acquisition. No icon load, window, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [IconWindow drawer DiskObject ownership trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-iconwindow-drawer-diskobject-ownership-gd14926).

<a id="gd14927"></a>
## GD14927 — Wanderer silently constructs IconWindows without their IconList

Both root and non-root branches of `IconWindow__OM_NEW()` create `_newIconWin__IconListObj` with `NewObject()` and do not check whether it returned NULL (`workbench/system/Wanderer/iconwindow.c:459-464,581-587`). The constructor then passes the possibly NULL pointer to `IconListviewObject` (`:659-663`). `IconListview__OM_NEW()` explicitly treats a NULL list as optional by omitting it from its child group, still constructs and returns the scrollbar wrapper, and stores the NULL `iconlist` (`workbench/system/Wanderer/Classes/iconlistview.c:188-231,240-265`). IconWindow then accepts a successful superclass construction, stores the NULL list pointer, and returns a usable window object without checking it (`iconwindow.c:720-827,1037-1045`). Its setup path later sends Update/Sort to the NULL list and continues (`:930-952`); there is no retry or failure propagated to the `CreateDrawerWindow()` caller.

**Trigger and consequence:** an IconList class construction fails during root or non-root window creation, but the later IconListview/Window constructions succeed. Wanderer still adds and opens the window, which has no IconList content; the failed open is silently presented as an empty drawer/window. **Affected configuration:** the full Workbench target selects Wanderer's app and IconList classes through active MetaMake edges (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-21`; `workbench/system/mmakefile.src:10-14`; `workbench/system/Wanderer/mmakefile.src:23-39`; `Classes/mmakefile.src:5-9,30-48`). **Confidence:** medium-high for the unchecked NULL propagation and empty-view construction; manifestation requires an IconList construction failure followed by successful parent-object construction. Abort IconWindow construction when the IconList is unavailable and unwind any already-created objects. No allocation failure or GUI was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [IconList construction-failure propagation through IconListview](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#wanderer-iconlist-failure-through-iconlistview-gd14927).


<a id="gd14928"></a>
## GD14928 — MiamiPanel dereferences an unallocated interface message port during startup

`MiamiPanelProc()` assigns the result of `CreateMsgPort()` to `mpb_port` but does not check it before constructing the application (`workbench/network/stacks/AROSTCP/MUI.MiamiPanel/muimiamipanel_proccess.c:38-43`). The selected app constructor creates the main window and its interface group, then calls `openWindow()` before returning (`Classes/muimiamipanel_class_app.c:143-177,245-262`; `muimiamipanel_misc.c:157-171`). Opening the window runs the interface group's setup method, which evaluates `1 << MiamiPanelBaseIntern->mpb_port->mp_SigBit` without validating the port (`Classes/muimiamipanel_class_ifgroup.c:183-199`). Thus, if `CreateMsgPort()` fails and the window otherwise reaches setup, startup dereferences NULL and the panel cannot complete construction.

**Trigger and consequence:** start the MiamiPanel application while allocation of its private message port fails, with subsequent app/window construction succeeding far enough to run interface-group setup. This can fault during startup instead of reporting allocation failure cleanly. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable optional `arostcp-libs-muimiamipanel` module; its alias and AROSTCP aggregate edges are commented (`MUI.MiamiPanel/mmakefile.src:10-14,42-45`), so default inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked dereference and call sequence; conditional on the message-port allocation failure. Check the port before constructing/opening the app and return the startup failure through the existing message result path. No allocation failure, panel, or GUI was run; source-only; see the [startup allocation-failure trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#miamipanel-startup-message-port-allocation-failure-gd14928).

<a id="gd14929"></a>
## GD14929 — Long proportional color-font strings can write before the temporary glyph raster

`TextExtent()` keeps the running horizontal position and its extrema in signed `WORD` variables (`rom/graphics/textextent.c:80-123`). `ColorFontBasedText()` then stores the raster width, row stride, and per-glyph position in signed `WORD` variables (`rom/graphics/text.c:564,587-593,617-636`) and does not check glyph destinations against the allocated raster before writing rows (`:638-654`).

**Trigger and consequence:** call the selected `Text()` vector with a proportional color font whose `tf_CharSpace`/glyph advances take the cumulative position beyond 32,767, while the positive `WORD` count remains in range. For example, a 32,767-character string of two-pixel glyphs crosses the boundary after 16,384 characters on toolchains that narrow out-of-range signed-word conversions by retaining the low 16 bits. `TextExtent()` then records a negative minimum; `ColorFontBasedText()` narrows its computed positive width back to `WORD`, initializes `x` from `-MinX`, and forms `raster + wx` with the wrapped negative glyph position. The subsequent glyph loop writes before the temporary raster allocation. This is conditional on the compiler's signed narrowing behavior and a long proportional color-font string; no checked-in caller providing such a string was established. **Affected configuration:** builds selecting the standard Graphics library and color-font support. **Confidence:** medium; the source data flow is direct, while conversion of out-of-range `int` values to signed `WORD` is implementation-defined and no target compiler run was made. Keep the raster geometry and glyph positions in a sufficiently wide signed type, and reject or clip positions outside the allocated extent. No text, font, allocation, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14930"></a>
## GD14930 — QuickPart leaks a constructed disk object when its list spacer fails

`FindDisks()` successfully constructs a `QPDisk` object, then separately constructs the spacer `HGroup` used beside that object in the drive list (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_FindDisks.c:235-253`). If the spacer construction returns NULL, the `if (diskObj && qpt_VOID_spacer2)` insertion block is skipped. The drive record is then freed at the end of the loop, but the already-created `diskObj` is neither inserted into a group nor disposed (`:253-279`). `QPDisk__OM_NEW()` retains its message port and I/O request in the object after a successful device open (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:397-400,467-480`); those fields are only released by the object's later disposal path (`:593-608`). The object and those resources therefore remain allocated after this failed row construction.

**Trigger and consequence:** QuickPart disk discovery successfully constructs a disk object, but the following spacer `HGroup` allocation fails. That disk object is orphaned when `FindDisks()` frees the drive record and advances to the next disk; each such failure retains the object and its constructor-owned storage/device request. **Affected configuration:** the Workbench-selected QuickPart target (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`). **Confidence:** high for the missing object cleanup; spacer-allocation failure incidence is conditional. Dispose `diskObj` on every path where it was not inserted into the drive group. No allocation failure, disk discovery, GUI operation, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="gd14931-adddatatypes-exclusion-pattern-overflows-parse-buffer"></a>
<a id="gd14931-adddatatypes-ignores-an-undersized-exclusion-pattern-buffer-and-misses-x86_64-files"></a>
## GD14931 — AddDataTypes ignores an undersized exclusion-pattern buffer and misses `.x86_64` files

`main()` clears `StackVars`, then parses the fixed `ExcludePattern` into `ExclPat` without checking the return value (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:170-171,211-215,262-268`). The source pattern is 42 bytes long, and its parsed representation also needs 42 bytes including the final NUL: `#?` becomes one `P_ANY` token, the alternatives retain 31 literal bytes and six `P_ORNEXT` tokens, with `P_ORSTART`, `P_OREND`, the dot, and NUL. `ExclPat` is only `2*EXCL_LEN+3`, or 39 bytes, because `EXCL_LEN` is 18. The shared parser checks destination capacity and returns `-1` before writing past it (`rom/dos/patternmatching.c:439-442,633-635`). It has already reserved `P_OREND` in the last destination byte when it sees `(`, so that marker remains present when the final close token cannot fit; the emitted alternatives reach only `x86_` before the overflow.

`ScanDirectory()` ignores this parse failure and later passes `ExclPat` to `MatchPatternNoCase()` for every file (`workbench/c/AddDataTypes.c:436-477`). The matcher finds the saved `P_OREND` at the end of the array, so the source does not establish the earlier claimed unbounded OR scan through adjacent fields. It then reads the pattern terminator just beyond the array; in the selected natural-alignment layout this is zeroed padding from the `memset(&vars, 0, ...)` at `:262`. The concrete mismatch is that the final alternative is `x86_`, not `x86_64`, so a file with the intentionally excluded `.x86_64` suffix is not filtered and reaches `LoadDataType()`.

**Trigger and consequence:** run AddDataTypes with `FILES` or `REFRESH` so `ScanDirectory()` processes a directory containing a valid datatype file with the `.x86_64` suffix. The fixed exclusion fails to match that file, and `LoadDataType()` may parse and register it alongside the intended datatype. The actual presence and registration effect of such an installed file were not established. Size `ExclPat` for the complete compiled representation and check the parser result before matching.

**Affected configuration:** the `workbench-c-adddatatypes` target, included by the `workbench-c` aggregate (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:99-105,159-160`); the mismatch applies to CLI directory or refresh scans.

**Confidence:** high for the 42-byte required representation, 39-byte capacity, parser failure, and incomplete final alternative; medium for a visible registration effect, which depends on a matching datatype file being present. No command, file scan, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [AddDataTypes exclusion-pattern capacity and matcher caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#adddatatypes-exclusion-pattern-capacity-gd14931).

<a id="gd14932-copy-misreports-malformed-destination-pattern"></a>
## GD14932 — Copy reports malformed destination patterns as storage failures

`IsPattern()` returns the result of `ParsePattern()`, but replaces `IoErr()` with `ERROR_NO_FREE_STORE` for every `-1` result (`workbench/c/Copy.c:1471-1489`). The selected DOS parser uses `ERROR_BAD_TEMPLATE` for malformed syntax, and its autodoc directs callers to `IoErr()` for the specific failure (`rom/dos/parsepattern.c:27-31,50-55`; `rom/dos/patternmatching.c:439-442,628-633`). In the normal copy path, `main()` calls `IsPattern(args.to, cd)`; a `-1` result enters the truthy branch, skips the wildcard-destination diagnostic, and leaves the command's failure result in place (`Copy.c:597,984-995`). Final return handling publishes the overwritten `cd->IoErr` with `SetIoErr()` (`:1201-1209`).

**Trigger and consequence:** invoke Copy with a malformed pattern in `TO`, such as an unterminated character class. The command returns failure without performing the copy, but callers receive `ERROR_NO_FREE_STORE` instead of the parser's `ERROR_BAD_TEMPLATE`, obscuring the cause. Preserve the parser's `IoErr()` when the buffer allocation succeeded and distinguish parse failure from allocation failure.

**Affected configuration:** the `Copy` command is in `SH_FILES` and selected by the `workbench-c-sh` target, which is a dependency of `workbench-c` (`workbench/c/mmakefile.src:67-80,99-109,138-144`).

**Confidence:** high for the error-code overwrite and return path; no command or malformed pattern was run. This is an error-reporting defect; the checked path returns failure and does not proceed with the copy. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [Copy pattern-result and IoErr caller trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#copy-malformed-destination-pattern-error-trace-gd14932).

<a id="gd14933"></a>
## GD14933 — Disabling an active menu entry leaves its highlight until the menu session closes

`OffMenu()` clears `MENUENABLED` on an attached menu or clears `ITEMENABLED` on an item/subitem (`rom/intuition/offmenu.c:56-94`). If the disabled entry is currently highlighted, its `HIGHITEM` flag and pixels remain set. On pointer movement, `HandleMouseMove()` calls `HighlightMenuTitle()` for the old title before switching titles (`rom/intuition/menutask.c:349-368`), or calls `HighlightItem()` for the old item/subitem before selecting the new one or clearing the active selection (`:323-343,385-399`). Both renderers gate their toggle and redraw on enabled state: `HighlightMenuTitle()` requires `MENUENABLED` (`:604-608`), while `HighlightItem()` requires the item, parent menu, and (for a subitem) parent item to remain enabled (`:1768-1774`). Thus the corresponding old-title or item redraw returns without removing the highlight. The menu bar/menu window remains open during this transition, leaving the stale entry visibly selected until the menu session ends and its windows close (`:490-503,951-970,1245-1277`).

**Trigger and consequence:** call `OffMenu()` for the currently highlighted menu, item or subitem during an open menu session, then move the pointer so Intuition attempts to clear that active selection. The now-disabled entry remains visibly highlighted until the menu session closes. **Affected configuration:** Intuition menu handling; the missing redraw follows the shared enabled-state logic in both title and item renderers. **Confidence:** high for the state transition and stale pixels; conditional on disabling an active entry during an open menu session. The old entry should be redrawn/unhighlighted independently of whether it remains enabled. No menu operation, GUI, or build was run; source-only; see the [Intuition menu drawing-mode and highlight trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#intuition-menutask-setdrmd-caller-trace).


<a id="gd14934-locale-timezone-constructor-failure-leaks-city-listview"></a>
## GD14934 — Locale Timezone constructor failure leaks its city Listview

`Timezone__OM_NEW()` constructs `data->city_name` as a Listview containing a List object before it creates the GMT checkmark and label (`workbench/prefs/locale/page_timezone.c:706-729`). The children are not added to the parent Group until all four constructions succeed (`:731-734`). If `MUI_MakeObject(MUIO_Checkmark, NULL)` or `Label1()` fails, the constructor calls `handle_New_error()`. That cleanup disposes `gmt_label`, `gmt_switch`, and `zone_name`, frees `city_select_names`, and disposes the parent object, but it never disposes the already-created `data->city_name` (`:593-624,723-730`). Because the Listview has not yet been added to the parent, disposing the parent does not own or release that unattached child.

**Trigger and consequence:** creation of the GMT checkmark or label fails after the city Listview succeeds. The Timezone constructor returns NULL while retaining the Listview and its nested list object; repeated failed attempts leak those objects. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable Locale Preferences target (`workbench/prefs/locale/mmakefile.src:6-18`); its parent Preferences dependency is commented out. **Confidence:** high for the missing cleanup and unattached-child ownership; the trigger depends on a later MUI object allocation failing. Dispose `data->city_name` in the partial-construction cleanup before disposing the parent. No GUI, allocation failure, or build was run; source-only.


<a id="gd14935-locale-timezone-failed-setup-keeps-event-handler-registered"></a>
## GD14935 — Locale Timezone keeps its event handler registered after setup failure

`Timezone__MUIM_Setup()` first completes the Group setup, then registers `data->ehn` with the window, and only afterward calls the fallible `timezone_init()` (`workbench/prefs/locale/page_timezone.c:775-785`). On a bitmap depth below 15, `timezone_init()` can return FALSE when its `earthmap_chunky_remapped` allocation fails (`:197-204`). The parent Group setup treats the Timezone object as the failed child and sends `MUIM_Cleanup` only to preceding siblings, not to that child (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/group.c:1047-1068`). The Window open failure path then calls `MUIM_Window_Cleanup`, which only cleans render information and does not clean the root object (`window.c:3768-3771,4046-4059`). Thus the failed Timezone setup does not reach its own cleanup method, which is where the event handler would be removed (`page_timezone.c:788-798`).

The window's AddEventHandler implementation unconditionally inserts the supplied node into its intrusive event-handler list (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/window.c:3994-4005`). If the same window/object retries setup after the allocation failure, the still-linked `data->ehn` is inserted a second time; the insertion routine does not first unlink or detect an already-linked node (`:273-293`). Re-inserting a node already in the list can break the list links.

**Trigger and consequence:** on a low-color screen, fail the remapped-earth allocation after the Timezone object has registered its handler, then retry opening the same MUI window. The setup returns failure while retaining the event-handler registration; retry can insert the same node again and corrupt the window's event-handler list. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable Locale Preferences target on a screen with bitmap depth below 15; the parent Preferences aggregate edge is disabled (`workbench/prefs/locale/mmakefile.src:6-18`). **Confidence:** high for the failure order and missing rollback; the consequence requires allocation failure followed by retry. Remove the handler and unwind successful superclass setup before returning FALSE. No allocation failure, window retry, event, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14936-locale-preferences-tests-character-set-pointer-instead-of-clock-mode"></a>
## GD14936 — Locale Preferences gates clock conversion on the character set pointer

`Gadgets2LocalePrefs()` decides whether to synchronize the system clock from the battery clock when the GMT Clock option changes or when the timezone changes while GMT Clock is enabled (`workbench/prefs/locale/registertab.c:263-268`). In the synchronization block it reads the battery clock and conditionally adjusts it by `localeprefs.lp_GMTOffset` (`:284-292`). That condition tests `tmp`, which was last assigned by `GetAttr(MUIA_Language_Characterset, ...)` at `:238-241`; it does not test the clock-mode value `gmtclock` or the GMT flag. A configured character-set string therefore causes the timezone adjustment regardless of the selected clock mode. The surrounding comment describes the offset conversion as dependent on the GMT clock setting, and the same function explicitly computes `gmtclock` from the timezone gadget before deciding when synchronization is needed.

**Trigger and consequence:** change the GMT Clock option while the character-set attribute returns a non-NULL string, or change timezone while GMT Clock is enabled. The battery-clock synchronization then uses the stored timezone offset based on the unrelated character-set pointer, potentially shifting system time when that conversion should not apply or using the old stored offset after a timezone change. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable Locale Preferences target; its parent Preferences aggregate edge is disabled (`workbench/prefs/locale/mmakefile.src:6-18`). **Confidence:** medium; the unrelated condition is definite, while the intended transition math for changing between local-clock and GMT-clock modes needs confirmation against the project’s clock policy. Gate conversion on the intended old/new clock-mode state and use the offset appropriate to that transition. No preferences UI, battery clock, timer request, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14937-locale-language-list-allocation-failure-is-not-checked"></a>
## GD14937 — Locale language-list construction dereferences failed allocations

`init_language_lists()` counts the installed language entries, then allocates the available and preferred pointer arrays (`workbench/prefs/locale/page_language.c:61-68`). It does not check either result before filling them in the following `ForeachNode` loop or writing their terminating NULL pointers (`:70-98`). `Language__OM_NEW()` calls this helper without a status result and proceeds to use both arrays as list source arrays (`:419-421,437-454`). The constructor's later object-allocation checks do not cover these buffers.

**Trigger and consequence:** either pointer-array allocation fails while creating Locale Preferences. The helper then writes through a NULL array while distributing language entries or adding a terminator, causing a crash instead of reporting construction failure. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable Locale Preferences target; its parent Preferences aggregate edge is disabled (`workbench/prefs/locale/mmakefile.src:6-18`). **Confidence:** high for the unchecked allocations and subsequent writes; trigger requires allocation failure.
