Check both allocations and return through constructor cleanup before populating either array. No allocation failure, preferences UI, or build was run; source-only.

<a id="gd14938-mui-list-clear-writes-freed-active-entry"></a>
## GD14938 — MUI List clear writes the freed active entry while resetting selection

`MUIM_List_Clear` frees every `ListEntry` but leaves `entries_active` at its previous selected index. It then sets `MUIA_List_Entries` to zero and, when a row had been active, sets `MUIA_List_Active` to Off (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:2266-2294`). The active setter records the old index and, for a writable list, writes `data->entries[old]->flags` before completing the selection change (`:1510-1537`). Since `FreeListEntry()` already returned that entry to the pool (`:520-525`), this is a write through a stale freed entry pointer during a normal clear of a selected writable list.

A selected in-tree route is the public-screen picker in Zune Preferences. Its `PopPublicScreenStrObjFunc()` clears and repopulates the interactive `InputListFrame` list when the popup opens (`workbench/prefs/Zune/systemp.c:72-125,147-155`). On a successful prior popup close, `PopPublicScreenObjStrFunc()` reads the active entry into the associated StringObject (`:128-140`; the close hook is called from `workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/popobject.c:227-234`). Reopening after selecting a public screen therefore clears a list that still has an active row and reaches the stale-entry write. The `systemp.c` target is explicitly buildable through `workbench/prefs/Zune/mmakefile.src:8-17`; this establishes the source route, not default image inclusion.

A second route is LogView. `CreateLogEntryList()` clears and rebuilds its list (`workbench/system/LogView/logclass.c:45-86`), and the Apply-filter hook invokes it after filter changes (`workbench/system/LogView/logview.c:743-755,499-500`). It selects the last row after repopulating; `MUIA_List_Quiet` does not suppress the stale write because the active setter dereferences the old entry before checking the quiet flag. LogView is selected in the standard x86_64 configuration through `TARGET_USELOGRES` (`configure.in:1647-1649`, `config/target.cfg.in:43`, `workbench/system/LogView/mmakefile.src:4-12`).

**Trigger and consequence:** select a public screen in the Zune Preferences picker, close it successfully, then reopen it; or load nonempty LogView entries, change a filter, and press Apply. Clearing the still-selected row writes its render flag through the freed `ListEntry` pointer; this can corrupt the list pool or crash the UI interaction. The same defect applies when `MUIM_List_Clear` is called on any writable list with an active entry.

**Affected configuration:** `muimaster.library` List class (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mmakefile.src`) and any caller clearing an active writable list; concrete callers include the explicitly buildable Zune Preferences target and LogView in the standard x86_64 configuration when `TARGET_USELOGRES` is enabled.

**Confidence:** high for the free-before-active-reset ordering and stale-pointer write; no UI, allocator failure, or runtime behavior was exercised. Reset or detach the old active index before freeing its entry, or avoid dereferencing it during the clear transition. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [MUI List clear ordering and public-screen picker caller](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#mui-list-clear-active-entry-lifetime-gd14938).

<a id="gd14939-quickpart-zero-largest-drive-divides-by-zero"></a>
## GD14939 — QuickPart divides by zero when every enumerated disk has zero measured capacity

`unitenumFunc()` adds every fixed disk, SSD, or RAID unit to `FoundDrives` even when `OpenRootPartition()` fails; in that case the `MEMF_CLEAR`-initialized `qpfd_Size` remains zero and `qped_DriveLargest` is unchanged (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_FindDisks.c:95-131`). `OpenRootPartition()` can return NULL after its device open or geometry query fails (`rom/partition/openrootpartition.c:50-94`). If the found-drive list is nonempty but all entries retain zero size, `FindDisks()` leaves `qped_DriveLargest` zero, then divides each disk's size by it while setting `MUIA_UserData` (`QP_FindDisks.c:230-258`). The division occurs before the insertion guard, so a failed `QPDisk` object does not avoid this path.

**Trigger and consequence:** QuickPart enumerates one or more supported storage units, but root-partition opening or geometry acquisition fails for every unit. Each drive record is still queued with size zero, and processing the first record divides by zero while computing the scale percentage. QuickPart can fault before completing the disk list.

**Affected configuration:** QuickPart, selected through the Workbench aggregate (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`). **Confidence:** high for the zero-initialized sizes, unconditional enqueue and unchecked denominator; the trigger depends on enumeration succeeding while all root handles or geometry queries fail. Skip records without valid geometry or guard the denominator before computing percentages. No device enumeration, geometry failure, GUI operation, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [QuickPart disk discovery full-body and zero-capacity scale trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-disk-discovery-full-body-zero-capacity-gd14939).

<a id="gd14940-quickpart-never-closes-scanned-root-partition-handle"></a>
## GD14940 — QuickPart never closes the root partition handle retained by a disk object

`QPDisk__MUIM_QPart_Disk_ScanForParts()` stores the result of `OpenRootPartition()` in `data->qpd_Disk_PH` (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccDisk.c:204-206`). The handle owns a separate device open, I/O request, message port, and partition-handle allocation; `OpenRootPartition()` allocates these and opens the device before returning the handle (`rom/partition/openrootpartition.c:50-79`). The scanner may open and close the handle's partition table while populating the UI (`QP_ccDisk.c:263-324`; `QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:428-454`), but neither `QPDisk__OM_DISPOSE()` nor the container disposer calls `CloseRootPartition()` (`QP_ccDisk.c:593-608`; `QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:771-781`). `ClosePartitionTable()` only tears down the table and does not free the root handle or close its device (`rom/partition/closepartitiontable.c:31-58`); `CloseRootPartition()` is the API that releases the device request, port, and handle (`rom/partition/closerootpartition.c:47-62`).

**Trigger and consequence:** scan a disk whose root partition handle opens, then dispose its QuickPart disk object, including during normal application shutdown. The retained `qpd_Disk_PH` is never closed, leaving its partition-handle storage, request, message port, and device open reference allocated. Repeated calls to the scan method can overwrite the stored handle and retain additional handles. This is independent of GD10565's unmatched extra open on the QPDisk object's own I/O request.

**Affected configuration:** QuickPart, selected through the Workbench aggregate (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`). **Confidence:** high for root-handle acquisition, ownership cleanup API, and its absence from the object/container disposal paths. Close the retained root handle after dependent partition containers are disposed and before the disk object's storage is released. No disk scan, device open, application shutdown, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [QuickPart disk class full-body and root-handle lifetime audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-disk-class-full-body-root-handle-gd14940).

<a id="gd14941-quickpart-scans-nested-partitions-only-for-last-sibling"></a>
## GD14941 — QuickPart recursively scans nested partitions only for the final sibling

`QPPartitionContainer__MUIM_QPart_ccPartitionContainer_FindParts()` assigns each result of `MUIM_QPart_ccPartitionContainer_AddPart` to the single `newPartObj` variable inside the partition loop, then checks for and recursively updates a nested container only once, after the loop (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:421-449`). Each `AddPart` constructs a partition object, and `QPPartition__OM_NEW()` creates a nested partition-container child when that partition itself has a partition table (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartitionContainer.c:207-218`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccPartition.c:247-271`). Therefore, when an earlier sibling has subpartitions but the final sibling does not, the earlier sibling's nested container is never sent `MUIM_QPart_ccPartitionContainer_UpdateParts`; it remains empty. If the final `AddPart` returns NULL, the same post-loop recursion is skipped even if an earlier sibling has a nested container. The partition library explicitly supports recursively opening tables for partitions (`rom/partition/openpartitiontable.c:25-29`).

**Trigger and consequence:** scan a table with multiple partition entries where a non-final partition contains a nested partition table and the last entry does not. QuickPart creates the earlier partition's nested container but never populates it, so its subpartitions are absent from the displayed model. Recurse on each successfully created partition object during the loop, while the table handles remain valid.

**Affected configuration:** QuickPart, selected through the Workbench aggregate (`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25`; `workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34`). **Confidence:** high for the one-variable/post-loop recursion and nested-container construction; trigger depends on a nested table in a non-final sibling. No partition table, scan, GUI operation, or build was used; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [QuickPart partition-container full-body nested-recursion trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-partition-container-full-body-nested-recursion-gd14941).

<a id="gd14942-quickpart-omits-primary-from-mbr-partition-description"></a>
## GD14942 — QuickPart omits “primary” from primary MBR partition descriptions

The active-partition details formatter initializes \`ContainerSubStr\` to the non-NULL empty string, then the MBR-parent branch tests \`if (!ContainerSubStr)\` before assigning \`"primary"\` (\`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccApp.c:232-234,268-274\`). For ordinary MBR primary partition type IDs, the earlier type-ID switch leaves the string unchanged, so this condition is false and the details pane formats the entry as an MBR partition without identifying it as primary.

**Trigger and consequence:** select a primary partition in an MBR table and view its details in QuickPart. The details label omits the “primary” qualifier that the source intends to add. This is a presentation-only error; partition geometry and table data are unaffected. **Affected configuration:** QuickPart, selected through the Workbench aggregate (\`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25\`; \`workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34\`). **Confidence:** high for the non-NULL initialization and unreachable condition. Test for an empty string or use a separate flag to distinguish an unset subtype. No partition selection, GUI operation, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [QuickPart application class full-body active-part details audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-application-class-full-body-details-gd14942).

<a id="gd14943-quickpart-operation-group-leaks-spacer-on-parent-construction-failure"></a>
## GD14943 — QuickPart leaks its operation-group spacer when parent construction fails

\`QPOpGrp__OM_NEW()\` creates a \`RectangleObject\` spacer before calling \`DoSuperNewTags()\` to construct the parent group, and only attaches the spacer after the parent constructor succeeds (\`workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_ccOpGrp.c:59-84\`). If the parent construction fails and returns NULL, the method returns NULL without disposing the already-created spacer.

**Trigger and consequence:** allocation or child construction fails while creating a QuickPart pending-operation group after its initial spacer has been created. The group constructor returns failure, but the unattached spacer object remains allocated. **Affected configuration:** QuickPart, selected through the Workbench aggregate (\`workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25\`; \`workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34\`). **Confidence:** high for the allocation order and missing cleanup; occurrence requires parent-group construction failure. Dispose the spacer on the failed-parent path. No allocation failure, operation group, GUI, or build was used; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [QuickPart operation-group full-body constructor and ownership audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-operation-group-full-body-spacer-gd14943).

<a id="gd14944-quickpart-calls-uuid-unparse-after-uuid-open-fails"></a>
## GD14944 — QuickPart calls UUID_Unparse even when opening uuid.library fails

main() stores the result of OpenLibrary("uuid.library", 0) in UUIDBase but does not check it before continuing to construct and run the application (workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_Main.c:350-353,368-381). When the user selects a GPT partition, QPApp__OM_SET() calls UUID_Unparse() for every 16-byte partition type ID without checking UUIDBase (QP_ccApp.c:313-320). The UUID implementation is a library vector (workbench/libs/uuid/uuid_parse.c:109-122), so dispatch requires a valid library base. The partition GPT parser has its own UUID helpers and explicitly avoids depending on uuid.library during partition-table use (rom/partition/partitiongpt.c:107-110), so GPT discovery does not guarantee that this separate display library open succeeded.

**Trigger and consequence:** uuid.library cannot be opened during QuickPart startup, but the tool continues and enumerates a GPT disk. Selecting a GPT partition calls the UUID library vector with UUIDBase == NULL, which can fault while building the details pane. **Affected configuration:** QuickPart with GPT partitions and an unavailable uuid.library; selected through the Workbench aggregate (workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25; workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34). **Confidence:** high for the unchecked open and unconditional vector call; occurrence requires the library open to fail and a GPT partition to be selected. Abort startup with a clear error or skip UUID formatting when the library base is unavailable. No library-open failure, partition selection, GUI operation, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [QuickPart startup and UUID library lifecycle audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-startup-full-body-uuid-gd14944-gd14945).

<a id="gd14947-quickpart-portuguese-translates-bytes-as-characters"></a>
## GD14947 — QuickPart's Portuguese catalog labels bytes as characters

The Portuguese QuickPart catalog maps `WORD_Bytes` to `caracteres` (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/catalogs/portuguese.ct:5-7`), while the catalog definition says the source string is `bytes` (`catalogs/quickpart.cd:2-4`). The selected caller inserts this translation after the formatted disk capacity value (`QP_ccDisk.c:257`). In Portuguese, `caracteres` means characters, not the byte unit used by the capacity label.

**Trigger and consequence:** use QuickPart with the Portuguese catalog selected and view a disk capacity. The unit label describes the displayed byte quantity as characters, misleading the user about the capacity unit. This is a presentation/catalog defect; it does not affect the stored capacity or disk operations. **Affected configuration:** QuickPart catalog build includes Portuguese (`catalogs/mmakefile.src:6-12`); the application and catalog are selected through the Workbench QuickPart aggregate (`workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:20-26`). **Confidence:** high that the catalog entry is semantically inconsistent with `WORD_Bytes`; no locale rendering or catalog build was run.

**Coverage evidence:** [QuickPart source, GUI stub and catalog review](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-gui-and-catalog-review).

<a id="gd14948-hdtoolbox-inquiry-skips-standard-firmware-revision"></a>
## GD14948 — HDToolBox skips the firmware revision in standard SCSI INQUIRY data

`identify()` computes the available response length as `4 + data[4]`, then appends the four-byte firmware revision only when that value is at least 36 (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/harddisks.c:57-66`). Standard INQUIRY byte 4 reports the number of bytes following byte 4; a standard 36-byte response therefore has an additional length of 31, and the computed value is 35. A standards-conforming target returning that response has valid revision bytes at offsets 32–35, but HDToolBox omits them from the drive label. The in-tree ATA SCSI emulation uses 32 for this field (`rom/devs/ata/scsiemu.c:64-65`), which masks the boundary issue for that implementation.

**Trigger and consequence:** probe a device that returns the standard 36-byte INQUIRY response with Additional Length 31. HDToolBox displays its vendor and product fields but omits the firmware revision from the drive name. This is a presentation-only error and does not affect device selection or I/O. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable HDToolBox target (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/mmakefile.src:4-22`) when a probed SCSI device reports the standard field value. **Confidence:** high for the response-length arithmetic and conditional; no physical device or inquiry command was exercised. Interpret Additional Length as bytes after byte 4 (or check for at least 31) before appending offsets 32–35. The SCSI Commands Reference Manual describes the standard response as at least 36 bytes and byte 4 as `N-4` ([Seagate manual](https://knowledge.seagate.com/files/staticfiles/support/docs/manual/Interface%20manuals/100293068m.pdf)).

**Coverage evidence:** [HDToolBox device-probing full-body audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hdtoolbox-device-probing-full-body-audit-gd14948).

<a id="gd14949-hdtoolbox-frees-linked-node-after-add-failure"></a>
## GD14949 — HDToolBox leaves a freed partition node linked when backend creation fails

`addPartition()` inserts its newly allocated UI node into the parent model list before calling `AddPartitionTags()` (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/partitions.c:291-320,344-350`). If the backend returns NULL, the function calls `freePartitionNode(partition)` and returns NULL (`:375-379`), but does not first remove the node from the parent list. `freePartitionNode()` releases the node and its list sentinel without unlinking the node itself (`:194-205`). The GUI caller reports the failure and does not insert anything into the MUI list (`gui.c:392-411`), leaving the parent model list with links to freed storage. Backend partition creation can return NULL when it cannot allocate its native handle; for example, the MBR backend restores the slot and returns NULL if `PartitionMBRNewHandle()` fails (`rom/partition/partitionmbr.c:282-308`).

**Trigger and consequence:** create a partition in HDToolBox when the selected partition-table backend fails after the GUI node has been linked, such as a native handle allocation failure. The failure path frees the linked node but leaves its address in the parent list; later list traversal, cleanup, or another partition operation can follow invalid links and fault or corrupt the in-memory model. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable HDToolBox target with a backend that can fail after model-node insertion. **Confidence:** high for insertion-before-backend-call and free-without-unlink; no allocation failure was induced. Unlink the provisional node before freeing it, or link it only after backend creation succeeds.

**Coverage evidence:** [HDToolBox partition-model full-body and caller audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hdtoolbox-partition-model-full-body-audit-gd14949-gd14950).

<a id="gd14951-hdtoolbox-erases-model-before-table-destroy-succeeds"></a>
## GD14951 — HDToolBox discards the partition model before table destruction is confirmed

When replacing an existing table, `makePartitionTable()` first frees every child model node, then calls `DestroyPartitionTable()` without checking its result, and immediately attempts `CreatePartitionTable()` (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/partitiontables.c:83-106`). A destroy failure leaves the backend table open: the public API closes it only when the backend destroy method returns success (`rom/partition/destroypartitiontable.c:48-54`), and the MBR destroy method returns failure when its write fails (`rom/partition/partitionmbr.c:454-467`). `CreatePartitionTable()` rejects a root whose table is still open (`rom/partition/createpartitiontable.c:55-82`). HDToolBox then reports table creation failure but retains an empty child model for the still-existing table.

**Trigger and consequence:** choose to replace an existing table in HDToolBox and have the backend fail while writing the destruction update. The tool reports failure after freeing its displayed partition model, while the old table remains open and its partition handles remain in the backend list. Reopening or editing that table from the empty model can misrepresent existing partitions. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable HDToolBox on a writable table backend when destruction I/O fails. **Confidence:** high for the order and backend return/close behavior; no write failure was induced. Check and propagate destruction failure before discarding child nodes; rebuild or retain the model on failure. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [HDToolBox partition-table lifecycle and backend error trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hdtoolbox-partition-table-lifecycle-audit-gd14951).

<a id="gd14952-hdtoolbox-preferences-do-not-bound-partition-id-copy"></a>
## GD14952 — HDToolBox does not bound partition IDs read from preferences

`parsePrefs()` reads preference tokens into a 256-byte `ident` buffer and passes table-type IDs to `parseType()` (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/prefs.c:175-183,294-301,364-369`). For non-GPT tables, `parseType()` decodes the whole token with `strcpyESC()` into `tn->type.id`, whose fixed capacity is 32 bytes (`prefs.c:126-132`; `rom/partition/include/libraries/partition.h:54-58`; `hdtoolbox_support.c:87-121`). Neither the decoded ID length nor the configured `IDLen` is checked against that capacity. The same unchecked copy is used for a table's `Default` value (`prefs.c:270-274`). The shipped preference file uses short IDs and does not reach the condition.

**Trigger and consequence:** load an `ENV:hdtoolbox.prefs` entry whose non-GPT ID or `Default` string decodes to more than 32 bytes. The parser writes past the fixed ID field into adjacent type/list state, which can corrupt the preference model and make later type lookup or UI use fail. **Affected configuration:** HDToolBox when its editable preferences file contains an oversized non-GPT ID/default entry. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked decoder and fixed destination; the checked-in default entries fit. Reject decoded IDs and IDLen values beyond the destination capacity before copying. No malformed preference was loaded; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [HDToolBox preferences and type-map full-body audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hdtoolbox-preferences-full-body-audit-gd14952-gd14953).

<a id="gd14954-hdtoolbox-size-parser-treats-leading-zero-decimals-as-octal"></a>
## GD14954 — HDToolBox parses leading-zero size input as octal

`sizeStrToUL()` passes base `0` to `strtoul()` for both the integer and fractional portions (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/hdtoolbox_support.c:144-155`). The resize size gadget accepts decimal digits, a decimal point, and `M`/`G` suffixes (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/gui.c:2063-2071`), and its change handler passes the entered string to this helper before converting it to cylinders (`gui.c:729-731`). A leading-zero value is therefore interpreted as octal: for example, `08M` stops parsing at the `8`, falls into the “assume bytes” branch, and converts to zero kilobytes; `010M` is interpreted as 8M rather than 10M.

**Trigger and consequence:** enter a size such as `08M` or `010M` in the resize dialog. HDToolBox computes the wrong cylinder count (for `08M`, the conversion falls to its minimum one-cylinder result), so the displayed and requested partition size do not match the user's decimal input. **Affected configuration:** HDToolBox resize dialog, selected Workbench tool target. **Confidence:** high for base-0 parsing and the decimal-only gadget acceptance; no resize or table write was performed. Parse these user-entered quantities with base 10.

**Coverage evidence:** [HDToolBox support helpers and resize-size caller audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hdtoolbox-support-and-resize-size-audit-gd14954).

<a id="gd14955-hdtoolbox-never-deletes-custom-listview-class"></a>
## GD14955 — HDToolBox never deletes its custom Listview class

`initGUI()` creates a custom Listview class and stores it only in the local `listcc` variable (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/gui.c:1797-1815`). The class is used to create `gadgets.leftlv`, but `deinitGUI()` disposes the application, frees `ptclass`, and closes `muimaster.library` without calling `MUI_DeleteCustomClass()` for `listcc` (`gui.c:2571-2579`). `MUI_CreateCustomClass()` allocates both a custom-class descriptor and an Intuition class; `MUI_DeleteCustomClass()` is the API that frees the class/descriptor and releases its superclass reference (`workbench/libs/muimaster/mui_createcustomclass.c:64-88`; `mui_deletecustomclass.c:48-64`). The superclass lifetime consequence is also explicit in Intuition: `MakeClass()` increments `cl_SubclassCount` for the superclass (`rom/intuition/makeclass.c:153-160`), and `FreeClass()` refuses to free a class while that count is nonzero (`rom/intuition/freeclass.c:96-105`). Leaving this custom subclass registered therefore pins the Listview superclass as well as retaining the custom class and descriptor.

**Trigger and consequence:** launch and exit HDToolBox after `MUI_CreateCustomClass()` succeeds. Its Listview custom-class descriptor and class are left without their matching deletion call; repeated launches can retain class resources and a superclass reference. The same leak occurs if later GUI initialization fails after the class was created. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable HDToolBox target. **Confidence:** high for the successful creation and missing delete path; no application launch or class-expunge behavior was exercised. Retain the class pointer in cleanup state and call `MUI_DeleteCustomClass()` after disposing all objects of that class.

**Coverage evidence:** [HDToolBox startup, locale and GUI class-lifecycle audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hdtoolbox-startup-locale-class-lifecycle-audit-gd14955-gd14956).

<a id="gd14957-hdtoolbox-partition-gadget-leaks-frame-image"></a>
## GD14957 — HDToolBox's partition gadget leaks its frame image object

`pt_new()` allocates a `FRAMEICLASS` image with `NewObjectA()` and saves it in `data->frame` after successful superclass gadget construction (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/ptclass.c:226-245`). The failure path disposes the image, but `pt_dispose()` releases pens and delegates to the superclass without disposing `data->frame` (`:1051-1068`). The selected Intuition gadget-class dispose method frees notification state and delegates; it does not own or dispose the `GA_Image` pointer (`rom/intuition/gadgetclass.c:473-478`). Other in-tree classes that allocate a frame image explicitly call `DisposeObject()` from their dispose methods, e.g. ColorWheel (`workbench/classes/gadgets/colorwheel/colorwheelclass.c:439-440`).

**Trigger and consequence:** create and dispose HDToolBox's partition-table gadget, including normal application shutdown. The separately allocated frame-image object remains allocated for each successful gadget construction; Add Partition and Resize/Move each construct one such gadget. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable HDToolBox target. **Confidence:** high for image allocation, ownership storage and missing disposal; no GUI lifecycle was run. Dispose `data->frame` in `pt_dispose()` after the gadget no longer uses it.

**Coverage evidence:** [HDToolBox partition-table gadget full-body audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hdtoolbox-partition-gadget-full-body-audit-gd14957).

<a id="gd14956-hdtoolbox-returns-success-after-startup-failure"></a>
## GD14956 — HDToolBox returns success after initialization fails

`main()` prints the initialization error when `initEnv()` fails, then performs cleanup and unconditionally returns `0` (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/main.c:103-117`). `initEnv()` returns distinct nonzero `ERR_*` values for failures opening required libraries or creating the GUI (`:35-55`).

The selected C startup stores `main()`'s return in `__startup_error` and returns that value from its program entry (`compiler/startup/startup.c:127-142,86-118`). DOS `CallEntry()` returns the entry's result (`rom/dos/exit.c:101-130`), and `RunCommand()` returns it to the Shell (`rom/dos/runcommand.c:154-167,185-187`). The maintained Shell caller stores it in `cli_ReturnCode` (`workbench/c/Shell/Shell.c:555-556`), so the zero result is observable as command success through that path.

**Trigger and consequence:** launch HDToolBox when a required library or GUI resource cannot be initialized. The tool reports the failure text but exits with a success status, so scripts or callers cannot distinguish startup failure from a normal exit using the process result. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable HDToolBox target on startup failure. **Confidence:** high for the failure return and unconditional process status; no startup failure was induced. Return a nonzero result when initialization fails.

**Coverage evidence:** [HDToolBox startup, locale and GUI class-lifecycle audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hdtoolbox-startup-locale-class-lifecycle-audit-gd14955-gd14956).

<a id="gd14953-hdtoolbox-preference-type-list-allocation-failure-null-dereference"></a>
## GD14953 — HDToolBox dereferences missing type-map nodes after allocation failure

`getTableTypeList()` silently skips a partition-table entry if either allocation for its `TableTypeNode` or nested type list fails (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/prefs.c:84-112`). After preferences are parsed, `parsePrefs()` unconditionally looks up EBR and MBR nodes and dereferences both results to make EBR share the MBR type list (`:414-416`). If allocation failure omitted either entry, that lookup returns NULL and initialization dereferences it. `LoadPrefs()` calls `getTableTypeList()` immediately before `parsePrefs()` (`:421-430`), and `main()` invokes `LoadPrefs()` during startup (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/main.c:58`).

**Trigger and consequence:** HDToolBox startup experiences an allocation failure while building the table-type map. Initialization later reaches the unconditional EBR/MBR list alias and can fault instead of reporting or recovering from the allocation failure. **Affected configuration:** HDToolBox startup under memory pressure. **Confidence:** high for the skipped allocations and unchecked lookups; no allocation failure was induced. Propagate allocation failure and verify both lookups before dereferencing.

**Coverage evidence:** [HDToolBox preferences and type-map full-body audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hdtoolbox-preferences-full-body-audit-gd14952-gd14953).

<a id="gd14950-hdtoolbox-overlap-check-allows-last-sector"></a>
## GD14950 — HDToolBox's overlap check accepts another partition's final sector

`validValue()` represents an existing partition's sector interval as `LowCyl * spc` through `(HighCyl + 1) * spc - 1`, inclusive, but tests the candidate with `value < (((HighCyl + 1) * spc) - 1)` (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/partitions.c:248-265`). That strict comparison excludes the existing partition's final sector from the overlap test. The selected callers supply inclusive endpoint sectors: the resize dialog computes its proposed high endpoint as `(value + 1) * spc - 1` (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/gui.c:618-623`), and the drag path computes the active partition's inclusive start/end and checks the shifted endpoint (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/ptclass.c:806-813`).

**Trigger and consequence:** resize or move a partition so its proposed endpoint lands exactly on the final sector of a different partition. `validValue()` accepts that endpoint, allowing a one-sector overlap in the pending model; saving the table can then describe overlapping partitions and their data ranges conflict. **Affected configuration:** explicitly buildable HDToolBox when the selected table backend permits the edit and the user chooses that boundary. **Confidence:** high for the inclusive endpoint convention and strict comparison; no partition edit or table write was performed. Compare against the exclusive end `(HighCyl + 1) * spc`, or use `<=` for the inclusive end. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [HDToolBox partition-model full-body and caller audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#hdtoolbox-partition-model-full-body-audit-gd14949-gd14950).

<a id="gd14945-quickpart-does-not-close-uuid-library"></a>
## GD14945 — QuickPart leaves its opened UUID library reference outstanding

main() successfully opens uuid.library into the global UUIDBase before entering the program's main work (workbench/tools/QuickPart/QP_Main.c:350). Its cleanup closes MUIMasterBase and ExpansionBase, then frees the allocated signal, but never calls CloseLibrary(UUIDBase) (:728-734). The successful OpenLibrary() increments the library's open reference through its Open vector; CloseLibrary() is the matching release operation (rom/exec/openlibrary.c:86-100; rom/exec/closelibrary.c:58-94). Task termination does not close arbitrary library references on behalf of the caller (rom/exec/remtask.c:39-176).

**Trigger and consequence:** run QuickPart when uuid.library opens successfully, then exit the tool. Its UUID library open count is left elevated, preventing normal expunge while the reference remains and accumulating one outstanding reference per launch where the library supports unload. **Affected configuration:** QuickPart when uuid.library is available; selected through the Workbench aggregate (workbench/mmakefile.src:7-25; workbench/tools/QuickPart/mmakefile.src:28-34). **Confidence:** high for the successful open and missing close on the normal return path. Close UUIDBase during cleanup. No application launch, library expunge, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [QuickPart startup and UUID library lifecycle audit](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#quickpart-startup-full-body-uuid-gd14944-gd14945).

<a id="gd14958-popupmenu-exclusion-varargs-failure-frees-uninitialized-pointer"></a>
## GD14958 — PopupMenu's exclusion-list wrapper frees an uninitialized pointer after allocation failure

In the `NO_LINEAR_VARARGS` implementation of `PM_ExLst()`, `values` is declared without initialization, then assigned only if `AllocVec()` succeeds (`workbench/libs/popupmenu/staticlib/pm_exlst.c:48-66`). The function calls `FreeVec(values)` unconditionally after the allocation branch (`:84-86`). If the temporary array allocation fails, `values` is indeterminate and `FreeVec()` receives it. Exec's `FreeVec()` only treats NULL as safe; for a non-NULL value it subtracts the allocation header and passes the resulting address to `FreeMem()` (`rom/exec/freevec.c:45-52`).

**Trigger and consequence:** call the variadic `PM_ExLst()` wrapper on a `NO_LINEAR_VARARGS` target while its temporary ID-array allocation fails. Cleanup can pass an arbitrary stack value to `FreeMem()`, causing invalid memory-list manipulation or a fault instead of returning the initialized NULL result. **Affected configuration:** consumers of the separately built PopupMenu static library on targets defining `NO_LINEAR_VARARGS`, including x86-64; the static library is an explicit link-library target and its aggregate link edges are commented out, so default-image use is not claimed. **Confidence:** high for the uninitialized failure path and `FreeVec()` behavior; no allocation failure was induced. Initialize `values` to NULL or call `FreeVec()` only when allocation succeeded. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [PopupMenu static-library wrapper pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#popupmenu-static-library-wrapper-audit-gd14958).

<a id="gd14959-vgagfx-init-failure-leaks-attr-bases-and-mode-list"></a>
## GD14959 — VGAGfx leaks initialization resources when display setup fails

`VGAGfx_Init()` obtains nine OOP attribute bases and allocates the default mode-list nodes before opening `graphics.library` (`arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_init.c:34-96`). If `OpenLibrary("graphics.library", 41)` returns NULL, the initializer exits at lines 98-101 without calling `OOP_ReleaseAttrBases()` or freeing the nodes already linked into `csd->modelist`. The later `AddDisplayDriver()` failure path also closes the library but returns without releasing either resource (`:118-137`). There is no VGAGfx expunge/deinit hook that releases these bases or walks the modelist; the module manifest selects only this initializer and the HIDD implementation files (`arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/mmakefile.src:7-18`). `OOP_ObtainAttrBases()` obtains one base per interface ID (`rom/oop/obtainattrbases.c:49-67`), and each successful `OOP_ObtainAttrBase()` increments that interface bucket’s reference count (`rom/oop/obtainattrbase.c:130-134`); `OOP_ReleaseAttrBases()` releases the corresponding references (`rom/oop/releaseattrbases.c:50-57`).

**Trigger and consequence:** load the VGAGfx module when its subsequent graphics.library open fails, or when `AddDisplayDriver()` rejects registration. Initialization returns FALSE, but the acquired OOP attribute-base references remain elevated; any successfully allocated mode-list nodes are also orphaned when the failed library base is discarded. Repeated failed module initialization can accumulate these resources. **Affected configuration:** native i386-PC and x86-64-PC packages that include VGAGfx (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:75-78`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:62-69`), only when one of the stated init operations fails. **Confidence:** high for the missing cleanup and OOP reference accounting; no failed library open or registration was induced. Add a single failure cleanup path that frees the mode-list nodes and releases the bases acquired by this init before returning FALSE. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [VGAGfx initialization rollback and OOP attribute-base ownership pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vgagfx-init-failure-rollback-gd14959).

<a id="gd14960-vgagfx-constructor-removes-unregistered-reset-callback"></a>
## GD14960 — VGAGfx constructor failure removes an unregistered reset callback

After the superclass creates the VGAGfx object, `VGAGfx__Root__New()` tries to create its display object. It initializes and registers `data->ResetInterrupt` only if that display creation succeeds (`arch/all-native/hidd/vgagfx/vgagfx_hiddclass.c:102-110`). If display creation returns NULL, the failure branch coerces the partially constructed HIDD through its Dispose method (`:111-114`), and `VGAGfx__Root__Dispose()` unconditionally calls `RemResetCallback()` (`:120-126`). The generic OOP root constructor allocates and clears the full instance data (`rom/oop/rootclass.c:115-126`), so the reset node's `ln_Pred` and `ln_Succ` remain NULL on this path. `RemResetCallback()` forwards it to `Remove()` (`rom/exec/remresetcallback.c:45-49`); `Remove()` dereferences both links without checking whether the node belongs to a list (`rom/exec/remove.c:45-64`). Thus display-object construction failure reaches a NULL-link dereference during rollback. This is the same unmatched-registration pattern already documented for VESA, EFI framebuffer, and Raspberry Pi framebuffer HIDDs, but occurs in the separate VGAGfx class.

**Affected configuration and trigger:** native i386-PC and x86-64-PC boot packages include VGAGfx (`arch/i386-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:75-78`; `arch/x86_64-pc/boot/mmakefile.src:62-69`). The failure occurs when `OOP_NewObject()` cannot construct the VGA display after the VGAGfx object itself has been created. **Consequence:** the rollback can fault in `Remove()` rather than dispose the partial HIDD and return NULL cleanly. **Confidence:** high for the constructor branch, zeroed reset-node links and unconditional list removal; no display allocation failure was induced. Track whether the callback was registered and remove it only on the successful-registration path. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [VGAGfx partial-construction reset-callback rollback pass](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#vgagfx-unregistered-reset-callback-rollback-gd14960).


<a id="gd14961-pixfmt-constructor-discards-parsed-attributes"></a>
## GD14961 — Generic PixFmt constructor discards successfully parsed attributes [external caller conditional]

`PF__Root__New()` lets the Root superclass allocate the object, then parses a non-NULL attribute list into a local `HIDDT_PixelFormat pf` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_pixfmtclass.c:52-71`). When parsing succeeds, it sets `ok = TRUE` and returns the object, but never copies `pf` into the instance's `struct pixfmt_data::pf` (`gfx_intern.h:59-65`). The Root constructor clears newly allocated instance data (`rom/oop/rootclass.c:115-126`), so subsequent `PF__Root__Get()` calls return zeroed defaults rather than the supplied format attributes (`gfx_pixfmtclass.c:123-205`). The internal standard-format path avoids this constructor branch by copying prebuilt data into the object, and the selected DMEnum registration path creates an empty object and then copies its parsed format manually (`gfx_init.c:186-207`; `gfx_dmenumclass.c:1200-1215`).

**Trigger and consequence:** an external or future client directly constructs the generic PixFmt class with valid non-NULL format tags. Construction reports success, but getters expose the zeroed instance fields instead of those tags, so the object does not describe the requested pixel format. **Affected configuration:** targets selecting the generic `kernel-hidd-gfx`; no direct in-tree attribute-bearing constructor caller was found. **Confidence:** high for the ignored parsed value and returned object; practical occurrence is conditional because the generic class is used internally through separate initialization paths. Copy `pf` into the instance data before returning. No object was constructed or queried; source-only.

<a id="gd14962-pixfmt-cgx-lookup-index-is-not-bounded"></a>
## GD14962 — PixFmt `CgxPixFmt` getter indexes its map with an unchecked standard-format value [conditional]

The generic `Hidd_PixFmt` Get method indexes the fixed `hidd2cgx_pixfmt` table directly with `pf->stdpixfmt` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_pixfmtclass.c:204-206`). The table has 23 entries for the declared standard-format values 0 through `num_Hidd_AllPf - 1` (`rom/hidds/gfx/include/gfx.h:205-263`); no range check protects the lookup. `parse_pixfmt_tags()` stores any supplied `StdPixFmt` value at or above `num_Hidd_PseudoStdPixFmt` without checking it against `num_Hidd_AllPf` (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_init.c:84-87`). Display mode registration reaches that parser with driver-provided PixFmt tags (`rom/hidds/gfx/gfx_dmenumclass.c:518-535,1091-1105`), then stores the parsed descriptor for mode queries. A malformed external/future driver tag can therefore place an out-of-range value in a descriptor before a later `CgxPixFmt` attribute query indexes beyond the table.

**Trigger and consequence:** a display driver supplies a PixFmt tag with `StdPixFmt >= num_Hidd_AllPf`, and a client queries `aoHidd_PixFmt_CgxPixFmt` on the registered descriptor. The getter reads beyond the map and returns an unrelated byte; if the bad index is sufficiently large, the read can fault. **Affected configuration:** targets using the generic GFX HIDD and a driver/client combination that supplies and queries the malformed format; no in-tree caller of the CgxPixFmt attribute was found. **Confidence:** high for the missing parser bound and direct table index; trigger is conditional on invalid driver metadata and a query. Reject out-of-range standard-format values and bound the getter lookup. No driver or attribute query was run; source-only.


<a id="gd14963-vc4-vblank-signals-stale-task-after-waiter-release"></a>
## GD14963 — VC4 vblank IRQ can signal a released waiter on SMP [conditional]

The VC4 `INTB_VERTB` handler independently loads `vblank_waiter` and then reads `vblank_waiter_sig` before calling `Signal()` (`arch/arm-native/soc/broadcom/2708/hidd/vc4gallium/vc4_init.c:47-54`). The waiter-side `vc4_wait_leave()` clears the task pointer, executes a memory barrier, frees the signal bit, and releases `wait_gate` (`:82-93`); it does not synchronize with an interrupt handler that already loaded the old task pointer. The registered server is reached from the Raspberry Pi system-timer interrupt through `core_Cause(INTB_VERTB, ...)` (`arch/arm-native/kernel/platform_bcm2708.c:570-575`), and BCM2836/2837 routes the shared GPU IRQ to core 0 (`:327-333`). Raspberry Pi target configuration supports the `smp` variant (`configure.in:2186-2199`), so a wait caller scheduled on another core can execute `vc4_wait_leave()` concurrently with the core-0 vblank server. Both selected wait paths use this registration and release it after `Wait()` (`vc4_galliumclass.c:422-488`; `vc4_drm_aros.c:1142-1230`).

If the interrupt reads the old task and signal bit before the waiter clears them, it can call `Signal()` after `FreeSignal()` has made the bit available for reuse by that same task. `Signal()` sets `tc_SigRecvd` without checking `tc_SigAlloc` (`rom/exec/signal.c:296-302`); `AllocSignal()` sets the allocation bit but does not clear a stale received bit (`rom/exec/allocsignal.c:113-123`); and `Wait()` returns immediately when its requested bit is already received (`rom/exec/wait.c:75-77`). Thus the next wait using the reused signal bit can return spuriously. The memory barrier orders the pointer clear against the signal-bit free, but it does not wait for a concurrent handler to finish; the independent task and signal loads also do not form one atomic registration snapshot. The handler may additionally retain the task pointer until after the waiting call proceeds, though no task-free consequence is asserted here.

**Trigger and consequence:** on an SMP Raspberry Pi build with the optional VC4 Gallium target enabled, a vblank interrupt on core 0 overlaps a GPU wait caller on another core as it leaves the waiter slot. The handler can signal the old task with a bit that the task has already freed and may have reused, causing a spurious wake in later code. **Affected configuration:** Raspberry Pi BCM2836/2837 SMP plus the optional VC4 Gallium module; its parent build edge is commented out, so default-image inclusion is not claimed. **Confidence:** high that the two sides lack an interrupt-quiescence handshake and that the shared IRQ is routed to core 0; conditional on the waiter running on another CPU during the narrow interval and reusing the signal bit. No interrupt interleaving, signal allocation, build, or hardware operation was run. Source-only.


<a id="gd14964-hdtoolbox-device-unit-scan-count-is-unbounded"></a>
## GD14964 — HDToolBox accepts an unbounded device-unit scan count [conditional]

`addDevice()` parses the text after the first colon with `atoi()` and stores the result as `maxunits` (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/devices.c:30-55`). It invokes `findHDs()` synchronously before publishing the new device entry (`:55-67`). `findHDs()` uses at least eight units, but raises the loop limit to every larger positive `maxunits` value and attempts each unit in turn (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/harddisks.c:86-90`). An unavailable unit does not end the scan: the loop continues after `OpenDevice()` fails and releases its per-unit node before the next iteration (`:92-138`). The unit-count suffix is accepted from `[Devices]` preference entries, icon `DEVICE=` ToolTypes, and the interactive Add Device string (`workbench/tools/HDToolBox/prefs.c:214-227,397-408`; `gui.c:375-383`).

**Trigger and consequence:** a device entry has a large positive, `int`-representable suffix such as `disk.device:1000000`. Preference loading or the Add Device callback then probes that many units synchronously, including continuing through unavailable units, making startup or the GUI unresponsive for an impractical duration. Nonpositive or `atoi()`-to-zero suffixes retain the default eight-unit scan. **Affected configuration:** the optional HDToolBox target when a configured or entered device string contains a large positive unit count. **Confidence:** high for the unbounded loop and synchronous callers; the duration depends on the device's `OpenDevice()` failure cost. Validate and cap the suffix before scanning. No device, preferences file, GUI action, or build was used; source-only.

<a id="gd14965-ftmanager-partial-class-init-skips-cleanup"></a>
## GD14965 — FTManager skips cleanup after partial custom-class initialization [conditional]

`Init(TRUE)` opens `codesets.library`, initializes FreeType, then creates the GUI custom classes in sequence (`workbench/system/ftmanager/ftmanager.c:73-97`). Each successful initializer stores its `MUI_CreateCustomClass()` result in a global, but if any later initializer fails, `Init()` returns false without unwinding earlier classes or the two successfully acquired library resources. `ftmanager_gui()` immediately returns `RETURN_FAIL` on that false result (`ftmanager.c:168-169`); the normal `Cleanup()` call is only on later paths (`:181,375`). `Cleanup()` contains the matching `CloseLibrary(CodesetsBase)` and `FT_Done_Library(ftlibrary)` calls (`:54-65`). The four `CleanupFont*Class()` helpers each call `MUI_DeleteCustomClass()` for a non-NULL class and clear the global, so staged rollback can release the earlier acquisitions.

**Trigger and consequence:** GUI startup successfully creates one or more early custom classes, then a subsequent `MUI_CreateCustomClass()` fails. The process exits its GUI entry path while those class objects and their MUI superclass references remain, and Codesets/FreeType resources acquired before class setup remain open. This is a partial-startup resource leak; a failure at the first class has no earlier class to leak. **Affected configuration:** the FTManager GUI path when custom-class creation fails after at least one prior class succeeded. **Confidence:** high for the short-circuit return and absent class/library cleanup; no class-creation failure was induced. Unwind only the resources successfully acquired so far, in reverse initialization order. Source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [FTManager partial custom-class initialization cleanup trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#ftmanager-partial-class-init-gd14965).

<a id="gd14966-ftmanager-empty-list-press-dereferences-null-entry"></a>
## GD14966 — FTManager dereferences a NULL font entry when its list has no active row

The FTManager listview maps `MUIA_Listview_DoubleClick` to an application return ID (`workbench/system/ftmanager/ftmanager.c:224-225`). In the `ID_ShowFont` branch, it declares `entry`, calls `MUIM_List_GetEntry` for `MUIV_List_GetEntry_Active`, ignores the result, and immediately reads `entry->FileName` (`:316-322`). The List class initializes `entries_active` to `MUIV_List_Active_Off` (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/list.c:1130`), and `MUIM_List_GetEntry` explicitly writes NULL when the requested position is invalid (`:3051-3062`). The selected List keyboard handler handles `MUIKEY_PRESS` by setting `MUIA_Listview_DoubleClick` without checking whether an active row exists (`:4097-4103`); Listview forwards notifications for that attribute to its underlying List (`workbench/libs/muimaster/classes/listview.c:172-194`). FTManager allows the font list to be empty when its initial Fonts directory scan finds no entries.

**Trigger and consequence:** focus the FTManager font list while it contains no active entry and invoke the configured `MUIKEY_PRESS` action. The resulting `ID_ShowFont` handling receives NULL from `MUIM_List_GetEntry` and dereferences it at `entry->FileName`, terminating the GUI path with a NULL-pointer fault. **Affected configuration:** the FTManager GUI when its font list is empty and the configured press key is invoked. **Confidence:** high for the handler, invalid-index NULL result, and keyboard notification route; no GUI input was run. Check both the `DoMethod()` result and `entry` before constructing the font window. Source-only.

<a id="gd14967-ftmanager-cli-short-font-copy"></a>
## GD14967 — FTManager CLI accepts a short font-file copy as complete [conditional]

`copy_file_handle()` treats only `Write() == -1` as failure and never compares the returned count with the bytes read (`workbench/system/ftmanager/cli.c:94-112`). DOS `Write()` returns the actual number of bytes written, including a nonnegative short count (`rom/dos/write.c:36-43`). After a short or zero-byte write, the helper reads the next source block and can reach EOF and return TRUE with part of the current block omitted. `copy_file()` deletes the destination only when the helper returns FALSE (`cli.c:117-150`), so this path leaves the incomplete `.ttf` in place. In CLI `COPY` mode, the caller then uses that destination as `dat->Filename`; if `FT_New_Face()` rejects it, the error path returns without deleting the copied file (`cli.c:212-240,253-259`). This is distinct from GD6024, which concerns failures writing the generated `.otag` and `.font` outputs.

**Trigger and consequence:** run FTManager CLI with `COPY` enabled and a DOS filesystem returns a nonnegative count smaller than the requested chunk length. The copy helper reports success and leaves a truncated font file in the target directory; a later FreeType rejection still leaves that file behind. **Affected configuration:** the FTManager CLI `COPY/S` path and a filesystem that returns a short `Write()` result. **Confidence:** high for the unchecked byte count, success propagation, and missing partial-file cleanup; occurrence depends on a short nonnegative filesystem write. Require the full requested byte count and remove the partial target on failure. No copy, file write, font parse, or build was run; source-only.

**Coverage evidence:** [FTManager CLI copy short-write trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#ftmanager-cli-copy-short-write-gd14967).

<a id="gd14972-ftmanager-cli-failed-copy-replaces-existing-font"></a>
## GD14972 — FTManager CLI failed font copy destroys an existing target [conditional]

`copy_file()` opens its destination with `MODE_NEWFILE` before copying (`workbench/system/ftmanager/cli.c:117-145`). DOS documents that this mode deletes an existing file and creates a new one (`rom/dos/open.c:37-48`); it does not preserve the old contents while the copy is in progress. If a subsequent source `Read()` fails or destination `Write()` returns `-1`, `copy_file_handle()` returns FALSE (`cli.c:94-112`), and `copy_file()` attempts to delete the destination as cleanup (`:135-145`). The previous target has already been replaced by the new, incomplete file, so a failed CLI copy can leave no usable version of that font. This is independent of GD14967, where a nonnegative short write is incorrectly treated as success and the truncated copy is retained.

**Trigger and consequence:** run FTManager CLI with `COPY` enabled and a destination file of the same basename already present; after `Open(..., MODE_NEWFILE)` replaces it, the source read or destination write fails. The copy reports failure but the previously valid target is lost; cleanup may delete the incomplete replacement. **Affected configuration:** FTManager CLI `COPY/S` path when overwriting an existing target and the filesystem reports a read/write error. **Confidence:** high for `MODE_NEWFILE` replacement semantics and the failure cleanup path; occurrence depends on an I/O error after the destination opens. Copy to a temporary sibling and replace the destination only after successful transfer and close. No file, copy operation, error, or build was exercised; source-only.

<a id="gd14969-ftmanager-cli-readargs-leak"></a>
<a id="gd14970-ftmanager-font-scan-list-publication-race"></a>
## GD14970 — FTManager scan-task list publication and disposal race on ExecSMP [conditional]

`flAddDir()` allocates `ScanDirTaskInfo` with `MEMF_CLEAR`, starts `ScanDirTask` while holding `Forbid()`, and only links `info->Node` into `ScanDirTasks` after `CreateNewProcTags()` returns (`workbench/system/ftmanager/fontlist_class.c:334-351`). The worker can start at `ScanDirTask()` immediately; even when `FT_Init_FreeType()` fails, it reaches unconditional cleanup that calls `REMOVE(&info->Node)` and frees `info` (`:207-224,321-324`). Before the parent publishes the node, its cleared `ln_Pred` and `ln_Succ` are NULL, and `REMOVE` dereferences both links (`compiler/include/exec/lists.h:136-145`). Exec documents that `Forbid()` on ExecSMP blocks task switching only on the calling processor; it does not serialize the worker on another CPU (`rom/exec/forbid.c:58-60`). `AddTask()` publishes the created task as ready before returning (`rom/exec/addtask.c:22-35,80-88`; `rom/exec/newaddtask.c:25-42`), so an ExecSMP scheduler can run the worker before `ADDTAIL()`. The same list is also read in `flDispose()` while it signals tasks (`fontlist_class.c:168-188`); worker cleanup removes and frees records at `:321-324`. Those operations likewise rely only on processor-local `Forbid()`, so disposal can read a record after a worker has freed it or traverse links during mutation.

**Trigger and consequence:** on an ExecSMP build, another CPU schedules a new scan process and it exits quickly before the creator inserts the record, for example because FreeType initialization fails. The worker's cleanup then removes a zero-linked node and can fault on a NULL dereference. Separately, closing the FTManager window while a scan is finishing can overlap `flDispose()`'s record traversal with the worker's remove/free, letting disposal dereference freed task metadata or follow a concurrently changed list. **Affected configuration:** the explicitly buildable FTManager target on ExecSMP; the FTManager edge in the Workbench:System aggregate is commented in `workbench/system/ftmanager/mmakefile.src`. **Confidence:** high for the publication order, cleanup path, and unsynchronized list accesses; occurrence depends on a cross-CPU schedule. No allocation failure, task schedule, GUI action, or build was run. Gate workers until publication and protect all list access/removal with cross-CPU synchronization. Source-only review.

## GD14969 — FTManager CLI does not release successful ReadArgs allocations

`ftmanager_cli()` calls `ReadArgs(..., NULL)`, which allocates the `RDArgs` structure and parser buffers and marks the structure as owned by ReadArgs (`workbench/system/ftmanager/cli.c:172`; `rom/dos/readargs.c:238-250,936-941`). After a successful parse, the function has several error returns and a normal return, but none calls `FreeArgs()`. The FreeArgs contract and implementation release the argument buffers, internal list, and ReadArgs-allocated structure (`rom/dos/freeargs.c:23-35,55-81`). Parse failures are cleaned within ReadArgs and are not included.

**Trigger and consequence:** run FTManager in CLI mode with arguments that parse successfully. Each invocation retains the parser structure and its allocations after returning, including early failures after parsing. **Affected configuration:** FTManager's CLI entry path (`argc > 1`); the GUI path does not call `ftmanager_cli()` (`ftmanager.c:389-397`). **Confidence:** high for successful allocation and missing cleanup; no command or memory-pressure scenario was run. Call `FreeArgs(rdargs)` on all post-parse exits after the argument values are no longer needed. Source-only review.

**Coverage evidence:** [FTManager CLI ReadArgs ownership trace](AROS-graphics-desktop-coverage.md#ftmanager-cli-readargs-ownership-gd14969).
